prs.title: fix(core): cap grep_search output size and tell the model to narrow broad searches
prs.body:
## Summary

A broad `grep_search` can still send the model far more text than it can use. The match cap limits how many lines come back, not how big they are: with the default 100 matches over long log or minified lines, the tool builds about 150K characters today. The executor's generic 64KB cap then cuts that mid-line and tells the model to read the full output from a file, which is the opposite of what you want after a search that's too broad. This PR bounds grep output by size inside the tool and tells the model to narrow the search instead.

## Details

- `formatGrepResults` stops adding lines once the output would pass `MAX_GREP_OUTPUT_CHARS` (40,000 characters). It always cuts on a whole line and closes the file block, so the result stays well formed.
- When it cuts, it adds a short notice saying how many matches (or files, for `names_only`) were shown out of how many, and suggests a more specific pattern, `include_pattern`, `dir_path`, or `names_only`.
- If context lines are what doesn't fit, it drops them first and keeps the matches. That matters for the 1 to 3 match auto-context case on files with long lines, where 50 context lines can push the match itself out.
- 40,000 is the default `tools.truncateToolOutputThreshold` and the distillation threshold (10,000 tokens x 4), and it's under `MAX_STORED_TOOL_OUTPUT_BYTES`, so for normal text the generic truncation no longer fires on grep.
- Results under the budget are byte-for-byte the same as before, and the existing grep and ripgrep tests pass unchanged. The `(limited)` summary also shows when output was cut for size.

This complements #29822, which caps `total_max_matches` and rewords the overflow message. They don't overlap: 5000 matches of 120-character lines is still about 640K characters, and this is what bounds that.

## Related Issues

Related to #17448

The core of that report (one search sending ~41M tokens) can't happen on main anymore. The default match cap (#17146), per-line truncation (#21147) and the 64KB tool output cap (#29451) bound it, and the pre-send check has blocked oversized requests since #10459. This PR covers the "agent should refine its search" part; the UI wording is in #29822, which should be the one that closes the issue.

## How to Validate

1. `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/tools/grep-utils.test.ts src/tools/grep.test.ts src/tools/ripGrep.test.ts`
2. On main, the new tests fail. The two end-to-end ones report 151,330 and 152,905 characters for a default search over long lines.
3. Manual: in a folder with a few files of long lines that share a word, ask the agent to search for it. The result ends with "Output truncated: showing N of 100 matches..." and stays under 40,000 characters.

prs.title: fix(core): exclude evicted binary payloads from exempt retrieval byte budget
prs.body:
## TLDR

Fixes #30446.

`collapseOlderFunctionResponses` now sizes older retrieval turns using their retained byte size (after evicted sibling `inlineData` and nested `functionResponse.parts` are excluded) instead of `calculateHistoryByteSize([turn])`, preventing a single older image `read_file` from exhausting the 64 KB `MAX_EXEMPT_RETRIEVAL_HISTORY_BYTES` budget and collapsing earlier text reads.

## Dive Deeper

- **Root cause:** `collapseOlderFunctionResponses` always evicts binary payloads from older turns (replacing sibling `part.inlineData` with `OMITTED_BINARY_MESSAGE` and stripping nested `part.functionResponse.parts`), even for preserved exempt retrieval turns. However, the budget loop measured each candidate turn with `calculateHistoryByteSize([turn])`, which counts those evicted binary bytes. One >64 KB screenshot `read_file` exhausted the entire exempt retrieval budget and caused older text `read_file` / `grep` outputs to collapse to 2 KB previews.
- **Fix:** Added a private `calculateRetainedTurnByteSize(turn)` helper in `packages/core/src/context/chatCompressionService.ts` used only in the exempt-budget loop. It counts `OMITTED_BINARY_MESSAGE_BYTES` for sibling `inlineData` parts and omits nested `functionResponse.parts`, while leaving `calculateHistoryByteSize` untouched so memory-pressure thresholds continue measuring full binary size.
- **Tests:** Added a parameterized regression test in `packages/core/src/context/chatCompressionService.test.ts` covering both `nested` (`functionResponse.parts[].inlineData`) and `sibling` (`part.inlineData`) layouts. Both cases fail on `main` and pass with this fix.

## Reviewer Test Plan

```bash
npx vitest run packages/core/src/context/chatCompressionService.test.ts packages/core/src/agents/memory-leak-regression.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false
```

- `packages/core/src/context/chatCompressionService.test.ts`: 38/38 passed
- `packages/core/src/agents/memory-leak-regression.test.ts`: 18/18 passed
- `prettier --check` & `eslint --max-warnings 0` on modified files: passed

prs.title: fix(extensions): allow unsafe config paths for extension git operations
prs.body:
## Summary

Since 0.70.0, `gemini extensions install <git-url>` and `gemini extensions update` fail for every Git-based extension with `Use of "GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM" is not permitted without enabling allowUnsafeConfigPaths`. This PR enables the simple-git `unsafe` categories that `getSafeGitEnv()` needs in `GIT_EXTENSION_OPTIONS`, so extension clone and update checks work again. It also adds regression tests that run the real simple-git guard.

## Details

- **Root cause:** #30356 moved to simple-git 4.x. Its unsafe-option guard checks the environment passed via `.env()` as well as the arguments. `getSafeGitEnv()` sets several values on purpose to harden git, and the guard flags them:
  - `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` (and a user-provided `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`) → `allowUnsafeConfigPaths`
  - `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` → `allowUnsafeConfigEnvCount`
  - `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n` entries that blank out `credential.helper`, `core.fsmonitor` and `core.hooksPath` → `allowUnsafeCredentialHelper`, `allowUnsafeFsMonitor`, `allowUnsafeHooksPath`

  `GIT_EXTENSION_OPTIONS` only enabled askpass, editor, pager and ssh, so `cloneFromGit()` and `checkForExtensionUpdate()` threw before git ever ran.
- **Adding only `allowUnsafeConfigPaths` (the fix proposed in the issue) is not enough.** simple-git stops at the first violation, so the guard then rejects `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, then `credential.helper`, `core.fsmonitor` and `core.hooksPath` in turn. I checked this one flag at a time against simple-git 4.0.2. The new tests also fail with `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT ... allowUnsafeConfigEnvCount` when only that one flag is added.
- **Security:** these flags only relax simple-git's own pre-spawn guard for values we set ourselves. The hardened environment git receives is unchanged: system config disabled, and credential helper, fsmonitor, hooks path, ssh command, pager and editors blanked. The argument-level protections we don't need stay on, for example `allowUnsafePack`, `allowUnsafeProtocolOverride` and `allowUnsafeExec`. The shadow checkpoint repo in `gitService.ts` (`SHADOW_REPO_GIT_OPTIONS`) already enables these categories.
- **Scope:** `github.ts` holds the only two `simpleGit()` call sites that use `getSafeGitEnv()` outside the shadow repo. The fix covers install (`ExtensionManager` → `cloneFromGit`), update checks and updates (`checkForExtensionUpdate`), and skill installs from Git (`skillUtils` → `cloneFromGit`). Other `getSafeGitEnv()` users call `git` through `execa` or `spawnAsync`, so they aren't affected.
- **Forward compatibility:** I also checked the fixed option set against simple-git 4.1.0, the version in the open dependabot bump #30423. It passes there too, while the current set still fails on `credential.helper`.
- **Downstream impact:** this is already affecting other projects. bastgau/ha-dev-environment#32 pinned its Gemini review workflow to 0.68.0 because 0.70.0 fails to install the extension. monochrome-muncher/hivemind#496 documents that 0.70.0 through 0.71.1 can't install or update from a Git URL and tells users to clone and `gemini extensions link` as a workaround.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30416

## How to Validate

1. Unit tests (the three new tests fail on `main` and pass with this change):
   ```bash
   npm run build
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/config/extensions/github.test.ts
   ```
   Expected: `Tests 67 passed (67)`. On `main`, the three `should configure simple-git so the safe git env passes its guard` tests fail with `Use of "GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM" is not permitted without enabling allowUnsafeConfigPaths`. The `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` case fails with `Use of "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL" ...`.
2. Manual repro, using an isolated HOME and an extension repo with no GitHub releases so install falls back to `git clone`:
   ```bash
   npm run build
   export HOME=$(mktemp -d)
   node packages/cli/dist/index.js extensions install https://github.com/gemini-cli-extensions/cloud-run --consent
   node packages/cli/dist/index.js extensions update cloud-run
   ```
   Expected with this PR: `Extension "cloud-run" installed successfully and enabled.`, then `Extension "cloud-run" is already up to date.` with no error.
   On `main`: install fails with `Failed to clone Git repository from ... Use of "GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM" is not permitted without enabling allowUnsafeConfigPaths`. Update prints `Failed to check for updates ...` with the same error.
3. Edge case: a user-provided `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` is still honoured and accepted by the guard. This is covered by the parameterised update test.
4. `npm run preflight`

prs.title: fix(cli): skip piped-stdin read before the sandbox hop in ACP mode
prs.body:
## Summary

With a sandbox enabled, `gemini --acp` doesn't answer an `initialize` request sent at startup, so ACP clients hang. This PR skips the pre-sandbox stdin read in ACP mode, as suggested in the issue.

Before relaunching inside the sandbox, `main()` in `packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx` reads stdin whenever it isn't a TTY, so it can forward piped input to the sandboxed CLI as `--prompt`. In ACP mode, stdin is the client's JSON-RPC stream. `readStdin()` clears its 1 s no-input timer when the first chunk (the `initialize` request) arrives, then waits for an EOF that never comes while the session is open, so `start_sandbox` is never reached. Without a sandbox the bug doesn't happen, because that path hands off to `runAcpClient` before it reaches its own `readStdin()` call.

## Details

- Skip the pre-sandbox `readStdin()` when `partialConfig.getAcpMode()` is true. Stdin is left untouched for the sandboxed process, which inherits it: every sandbox command is spawned with `stdio: 'inherit'`, and Docker/Podman/runsc also get `run -i`.
- `getAcpMode()` covers both `--acp` and the deprecated `--experimental-acp`. It is the same check the non-sandbox path uses before `runAcpClient`.
- Unchanged: outside ACP mode, piped stdin is still read and forwarded to the sandbox as `--prompt`. A new test covers this, since the pre-sandbox stdin forwarding (the `readStdin()` call and the `--prompt` branch of `injectStdinIntoArgs`) had no test coverage before.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30398

Same symptom as the earlier #23959, which was auto-closed for missing information without a fix; the fix suggested there was also to avoid reading stdin during early initialization in ACP mode. The issue also points to #22782 as likely the same cause.

## How to Validate

1. `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/gemini.test.tsx`: 51 passed, 1 skipped. Locally I had to set `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true` (as CI does) because of the pre-existing folder-trust test dependency tracked in #30383.
2. Revert the one-line guard in `gemini.tsx` and run `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/gemini.test.tsx -t "sandbox hop with piped stdin"`. `should not read stdin before the sandbox hop in ACP mode` fails with `expected "readStdin" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times`.
3. End to end on macOS with the Seatbelt sandbox, after `npm run build`:
   ```sh
   (printf '%s\n' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":1,"clientCapabilities":{}}}'; sleep 20) \
     | HOME="$(mktemp -d)" GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true GEMINI_SANDBOX=sandbox-exec node packages/cli/dist/index.js --acp
   ```
   - Before: no output; the process sits in the pre-sandbox `readStdin()`.
   - After: `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"result":{"protocolVersion":1,"authMethods":[...` comes back from the sandboxed CLI.

prs.title: fix(acp): surface BeforeAgent hook denial and stop reasons (#30114)
prs.body:
Fixes #30114, #30132

### Problem
When Gemini CLI is running in ACP mode (`gemini --acp`), if a `BeforeAgent` (or `AfterAgent`) hook denies a prompt or stops execution (`continue: false` / `AgentExecutionStopped` / `AgentExecutionBlocked`), the ACP stream consumer in `acpSession.ts` dropped these events in the `switch (event.type)` default block. As a result, the ACP client received an empty turn ending with `end_turn` and no message or explanation.

### Solution
- Handle `GeminiEventType.AgentExecutionStopped` and `GeminiEventType.AgentExecutionBlocked` in `acpSession.ts`.
- Emit an `agent_message_chunk` with the effective reason or `systemMessage` so the ACP client/IDE clearly sees why execution stopped or was blocked.
- Added unit regression tests in `acpSession.test.ts`.

prs.title: fix(acp): standardize token usage tracking and quota metadata (#24280, #27985)
prs.body:
### Description
This PR resolves two token tracking discrepancies in ACP mode:
1. **Preserve `PromptResponse.usage` on cancelled turns (#24280)**: Previously, early aborts or cancellations returned `{ stopReason: 'cancelled' }` without `usage` or `_meta`. This caused ACP clients to lose token usage metrics on cancelled prompts. Cancellation paths now return `buildPromptResponse('cancelled')` with preserved turn usage.
2. **Track cached and thought tokens in model quota metadata (#27985)**: Per-model quota breakdowns in `_meta.quota.model_usage` previously only tracked input and output tokens, omitting cached and thought tokens. We now track all four token dimensions (`input`, `output`, `cached`, `thought`) across all models and multi-turn tool loops.

### Changes
- `packages/cli/src/acp/acpSession.ts`:
  - Updated `modelUsageMap` type to include `cached` and `thought` tokens.
  - Added `cached_tokens` and `thought_tokens` to `_meta.quota.token_count` and `_meta.quota.model_usage`.
  - Added helper `recordTurnUsage()` to ensure tokens parsed before abort are preserved.
  - Updated abort and `AbortError` return paths to return `buildPromptResponse('cancelled')`.
- `packages/cli/src/acp/acpSession.test.ts`:
  - Added unit tests for mid-stream prompt aborts, immediate aborts, `AbortError` handling, and multi-turn multi-model token accumulation.

issues.body:
Build: 1.0.115.

**Repro:**
1. Start an attached async shell task whose child spawns a long-lived grandchild (e.g. a polling waiter).
2. Kill the wrapper (session teardown / supervisor reap).

**Actual:** the agent is notified "command completed with exit code 143" while the grandchild may still run (observed: live waiter with zero polls recorded under that sess), and conversely exit-3-style "duplicate guard" early-exits are indistinguishable from real termination without reading stdout. The disposition (drained vs killed vs detached-survived) is not part of the completion signal.

**Expected:** completion telemetry should include: signaled-vs-exited, whether descendants survived, and stdout-available flag. Adjacent prior: #4144 (terminal reasons hidden for startup/turn failures).

type.name: Feature

issues.body:
Build: 1.0.115.

**Repro / observation:** long-lived sessions rely on background-task completion notifications to wake idle turns. Across a week of instrumented operation (1070 events journaled on one machine via our own hook, plus cross-machine ledger comparisons), every wake was accounted for — but historical incidents exist where a notification was marked seen by the runtime and never surfaced to the model turn (external symptom identical to a dead consumer; our forensic example involved a 20-minute gap that self-resolved, and a documented 43-minute class). See also #5508 (notification held 60s while another background task runs) and #5370 (agent output withheld until next user turn).

**Actual:** no API/hook/log exposes per-notification disposition (queued / surfaced-at / dropped-with-reason). External tooling can only infer liveness indirectly (heartbeat ledgers), which cannot distinguish "notification lost", "held by queue", or "turn consumed it without acting".

**Expected:** expose disposition: (a) include a monotonic notification id in hook payloads so ledgers can join send↔surface, (b) emit a `NotificationDiscarded`-style event (reason: queue-retention, session-state, etc.), (c) document retention semantics. This turns a class of "silent wedge" bug reports (incl. #5508/#5370/#4755) into measurable, joinable evidence for both users and the team.

issues.title: ahp.connections.refresh retries forever with 30s timeouts and no backoff or circuit breaker

labels.name: area:networking
labels.description: Proxy, SSL/TLS, certificates, corporate environments, and connectivity issues

issues.body:
Build: 1.0.115 (packaging-agnostic: observed on both snap and standalone Windows installs, two machines).

**Repro / observation (passive, log-based):**
1. Leave a CLI host process running with stale remote AHP environment connections whose compute hosts no longer exist.
2. Tail the host process log.

**Actual:** `ahp.connections.refresh` requests fail continuously: each attempt ends after a ~30s timeout (JSON-RPC code -32603, "Connection recovery has not succeeded after 60 seconds. Background retries continue.") and the loop re-fires every ~4s indefinitely. Aggregated counts from two independent machines over ~18h: ~23,000 failed refresh requests on one host, plus a steady ~300 failures/10min rate after the dead connections were removed from user config but before the host process restarted (the retry loop keeps its in-memory snapshot).

**Expected:** exponential backoff with a cap; a circuit breaker after N consecutive failures; surfacing dead connections to the user (e.g. `/status` or one-time notice) instead of silent background churn. A shared request path with 30s-timeout retries every 4s risks event-loop pressure that plausibly contributes to user-visible latency complaints (interactions with notification-surfacing latency were inconclusive from our side and are reported separately, honestly labeled).

Related pattern: #4907 (MCP reconnect notification flood) — same class: unbounded background retry loops with user-visible side effects.

issues.title: Local sandbox blocks `git submodule update`, even as a no-op (worked in 1.0.99-2)

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

With local sandboxing on, `git submodule update` cannot run in a repository that has initialized submodules, even when every submodule is already at its recorded commit. Any install or build script that calls it fails, so the agent cannot build such a repository inside the sandbox.

This is a change in behavior: 1.0.99-2 runs the same command in the same repository with sandboxing on. I found no changelog entry for it.

The failure:

```
error: could not write config file <repo>/.git/modules/<submodule>/config: Operation not permitted
fatal: could not set 'core.worktree' to '../../../<submodule>'
```

Two things combine:

- The effective sandbox policy lists every Git `config` file and `hooks` directory under `<repo>/.git` as read-only, including those of each submodule (`.git/modules/<submodule>/config`) and of each linked worktree.
- `git submodule update` rewrites `core.worktree` in each submodule's config on every run, whenever the key is already set, so it needs that write even when it has nothing to update. See [`ensure_core_worktree`](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.54.0/builtin/submodule--helper.c#L2717-L2746); Git's `master` has the same code.

The documentation does not mention this protection, and says the opposite:

- "Read/write permission to everything in and below the repository's `.git` directory." ([Configuring local sandbox settings](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/cloud-and-local-sandboxes/configuring-local-sandbox-settings#configuring-filesystem-settings))
- "In a Git repository, the repository's Git metadata is also writable" ([Using local sandboxing](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/cloud-and-local-sandboxes/using-local-sandboxing))

### Affected version

1.0.117-3. Not affected: 1.0.99-2. Also seen in a VS Code 1.148.0 Agents-window session.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Open a repository that has at least one initialized submodule, with local sandboxing enabled.
2. Ask Copilot to run `git submodule update --init`.
3. The command exits 128 with the error above, although `git submodule status` shows every submodule at its recorded commit. With sandboxing off, or on 1.0.99-2 with it on, the same command exits 0.

Seen in [open-telemetry/opentelemetry.io](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry.io) (ten submodules), where the install, build and test scripts all run `git submodule update --init` first.

Excerpt of the effective sandbox policy for that repository, from the VS Code session, paths shortened:

```
## Working directory

### Read-only paths (153)

- <repo>/.git/config
- <repo>/.git/hooks
- <repo>/.git/modules/<submodule>/config
- <repo>/.git/modules/<submodule>/hooks
- <repo>/.git/worktrees/<worktree>/commondir
- <repo>/.git/worktrees/<worktree>/modules/<submodule>/config
- <repo>/.git/worktrees/<worktree>/modules/<submodule>/hooks
- <repo>/<submodule>/.git

### Read-write paths (1)

- <repo>
```

### Expected behavior

One of:

- `git submodule update` works inside the sandbox, at least when it has nothing to update, as it did in 1.0.99-2.
- The documentation says that Git config files and hook directories under `.git` stay read-only, those of submodules and linked worktrees included, and what that means for commands that write them.

### Additional context

- macOS 27.2.1 (26B131), Apple silicon, zsh
- git 2.54.0 (Apple Git-157)
- From the same policy report: sandbox bypass allowed; MCP servers, LSP servers and extensions sandboxed
- No bypass prompt was offered when the command failed, although "Allow sandbox bypass" is on
- Asked about the failure, the CLI agent said its sandbox guidance marks `.git/config`, `.git/hooks` and the configured hooks directory as read-only inside the working directory; it does not name the configs of submodules or linked worktrees, and the user documentation mentions none of these
- Git's side reproduces without Copilot: with a submodule's config file made immutable (`chflags uchg`), `git submodule update --init` prints the same two lines in a scratch repository
- Workaround in use: read `git submodule status`, skip the update when every submodule is in sync, and run the update outside the sandbox when a recorded commit has moved

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

I'm driving the CLI from the Python SDK over stdio. One of my sessions got really big (events.jsonl is ~808 MB, lots of screenshots in it). If I resume it and call `session.get_events()`, about 6 seconds later the CLI log shows:

```
[ERROR] Rust JSON-RPC transport error: Error: write EINVAL
```

After that the CLI never writes anything to stdout again. The getMessages call never comes back, ping / status.get time out, but the process is still alive, so the SDK has no idea the connection is gone. `client.stop()` hangs too, and the process ignored SIGTERM, so I had to kill -9 it.

Smaller sessions are fine. I truncated the same events.jsonl to check:

- 100 MB: getMessages returns in ~2s
- 300 MB: ~4s
- 808 MB: write EINVAL, connection dead

Resuming the 808 MB session without calling getMessages works fine.

### Affected version

1.0.116 (saw it on 1.0.115 too), macOS arm64. The log says "Starting CLI in stdio mode (Rust JSON-RPC engine)".

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Have a session with a very large events.jsonl (800 MB+).
2. From the Python SDK over stdio: `session = await client.resume_session(session_id, ...)`
3. `await session.get_events()`
4. `await client.get_status()` never returns.

### Expected behavior

getMessages either returns or fails with an error, and the connection keeps working. Or, if the transport does break, the CLI exits or closes stdout so the client can tell.

### Additional context

My guess is the whole response goes out in one write and hits the macOS limit where write(2) returns EINVAL above INT_MAX bytes. Chunking the write, or letting getMessages page, would probably fix it.

For now I work around it by not calling getMessages on big sessions (I read events.jsonl directly instead), plus timeouts and restarting the CLI when it stops answering.

issues.title: Copilot CLI floods Windows Credential Manager with copilot-mcp-oauth / copilot-keychain-chunk entries, causing CredWrite error 8 for other apps

labels.name: area:authentication
labels.description: Login, OAuth, device auth, token management, and keychain integration

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
## Summary

Copilot CLI accumulated hundreds of entries in Windows Credential Manager and never removed them. The vault reached a state where no application could write a credential. For example, `az devops login` failed, and so did `cmdkey /add` from the command line.

## Environment

- Copilot CLI 1.0.116
- Windows, Entra ID (AzureAD) user account

## Symptoms

```
Unable to use secure credential store in this environment.
(8, 'CredWrite', 'Not enough memory resources are available to process this command')
```

- `cmdkey /add:x /user:u /pass:abc` fails with "Not enough memory resources are available".
- The error occurs even for 1-character values, and for the SESSION, LOCAL_MACHINE and ENTERPRISE persistence modes.
- Adding entries through the Credential Manager UI still worked.
- Event Viewer showed nothing relevant (no Vault, DPAPI or LSA errors).
- No policy blocks credential storage (`DisableDomainCreds` = 0).

## Evidence

`cmdkey /list` showed 332 entries. 268 were Copilot's:

- 135 x `*.copilot-mcp-oauth`
- 133 x `copilot-keychain-chunk.<n>.<n>.<n>`

The other 64 entries were from other applications. The `Credentials` vault folder held about 120 KB.

## Confirmation

I deleted only the 268 Copilot entries. Credential writes worked again immediately, using the same Python keyring `WinVaultKeyring` call that failed before.

## Expected behavior

- Update or overwrite existing entries instead of creating new ones.
- Remove entries when an MCP server's auth is cleared or no longer needed.
- Store tokens more compactly, with fewer chunked entries.
- Handle `CredWrite` failures gracefully.

## Workaround

```powershell
cmdkey /list | Select-String 'Target:' | % {($_ -replace '.*Target:\s*','').Trim()} |
  ? { $_ -match 'copilot-mcp-oauth$|copilot-keychain-chunk\.' } | % { cmdkey /delete:$_ }
```

Then re-authenticate MCP servers.

## Open question

It's unclear which limit was hit (entry count, total size, or something else). UI saves still worked while API writes failed.

issues.title: Gemini 4 Neon: buffered tool calls >60s hit /chat/completions idle timeout (unexpected EOF during chunk size line / Incomplete response)

labels.name: area:networking
labels.description: Proxy, SSL/TLS, certificates, corporate environments, and connectivity issues

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When using `gemini-4-neon` in Copilot CLI (which routes exclusively through `/chat/completions`), any turn that generates a large single tool call (roughly >25–30 KB, e.g., creating a medium-to-large file with `create`) fails deterministically with:

- `Incomplete response` shown in the UI after the model's brief intro text
- Automatic retries (5 retries, ~5s total backoff wait), all failing the same way
- Final error:
  ```
  Execution failed: Failed to get response from the AI model; retried 5 times (total retry wait time: 5.00 seconds) Last error: Failed native model HTTP request: error decoding response body: error reading a body from connection: unexpected EOF during chunk size line
  ```

**Root cause confirmed via `--log-level all` controlled probes:**

1. `gemini-4-neon` on `/chat/completions` does **not** stream `tool_call_delta` arguments incrementally—it buffers the entire tool call JSON on the server and delivers it in a single `assistant.tool_call_delta` event once generation finishes, sending **zero SSE chunks** while generating the tool-call arguments.
2. The `/chat/completions` streaming connection enforces an exact **60.0-second inter-chunk idle timeout**. Once tool-call argument generation takes >60s after the last text/reasoning chunk, the server/proxy abruptly closes the HTTP chunked stream without the terminating chunk (`unexpected EOF during chunk size line`, telemetry `model_stream_interruption`).
3. Because each retry attempts the exact same single large tool call, all 6 attempts (1 initial + 5 retries) fail deterministically at `prefill/intro + 60.0s`, even after compacting conversation history.

In addition, at large contexts (~430K–467K input tokens), `gemini-4-neon` occasionally hits the same 60.3s `transport` drop **before response headers arrive** (no `request_id`), as well as transient HTTP `503` responses on `/chat/completions`.

### Affected version

```
GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.116.
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Run a standalone prompt asking `gemini-4-neon` to stream a short intro sentence and then call `create` with a ~28–40 KB file payload:

```powershell
copilot --model gemini-4-neon --reasoning-effort low --log-level all --log-dir .\logs --no-ask-user --allow-all -s -p "First write a single short sentence saying you are creating the file. Then call the create tool to create sample.md containing a markdown table with 220 numbered rows (rows 1 to 220), where each row has columns: Row, Topic, Description (about 12 words of realistic technical text per row). Do not use powershell; use the create tool directly."
```

(Using 300+ rows / ~40 KB reproduces a 100% 6-of-6 retry failure; 220 rows / ~28 KB sits right on the 60s cliff and fails on Attempt 1.)

#### Controlled comparison (same machine, same CLI build, `--log-level all`)

| Probe on `gemini-4-neon` | Total duration | Streamed deltas | Max silent gap | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ~28 KB `create` tool call (Attempt 1) | 69.23s | 0 `tool_call_delta` | **60.001s** (after last `message_delta`) | **Failed** (`failure_kind: "transport"`, `model_stream_interruption`) |
| ~28 KB `create` tool call (Retry 1) | 61.92s | **1** `tool_call_delta` (all 28,239 B at once) | **57.15s** | **Barely passed** (2.85s under 60s cutoff) |
| 48.7 KB plain text (no tool call, `low`) | **109.05s** | 350 `message_delta` | **0.62s** | **Passed, 0 retries** |
| Heavy `xhigh` reasoning (no tool call) | **159.11s** | 33 `reasoning_delta` + 93 `message_delta` | **9.68s** | **Passed, 0 retries** |

This rules out a general 60s total-turn limit or `xhigh` reasoning itself: long text and long reasoning turns stream incremental chunks and succeed cleanly well past 100–159s, while any single tool call whose buffered generation exceeds 60.0s is killed mid-stream.

### Expected behavior

Large tool calls (such as `create`/`edit` writing a 30–50 KB file) on `gemini-4-neon` should complete reliably without hitting a 60-second mid-stream EOF—either by streaming incremental `tool_call` argument chunks on `/chat/completions`, sending periodic SSE keepalive comments/heartbeats while buffering a tool call, or raising the upstream idle timeout.

### Additional context

- **Synthetic repro debug-log timeline (220-row `create` probe, 2026-11-26):**
  - Attempt 1 (`request_id: DE1C:214584:4357216:4662549:6B08548E`):
    - `15:47:27.032Z` — `POST /chat/completions` sent
    - `15:47:36.261Z` — last `assistant.message_delta` dispatched
    - `15:48:36.262Z` — **60.001s later**: `[WARNING] [rust:model_events::producer] Model provider request failed {"stage":"inference","api_endpoint":"/chat/completions","failure_kind":"transport","request_id":"DE1C:214584:4357216:4662549:6B08548E"}` followed by `model_stream_interruption` and `assistant.turn_retry`
  - Retry 1 (`Request-ID: 0d7d8c80-47b2-47bf-bef3-6de98c0c678f`):
    - `15:48:37.350Z` — retry sent
    - `15:48:41.791Z` — last `assistant.message_delta` dispatched
    - `15:49:38.940Z` — **57.149s later**: single `assistant.tool_call_delta` carrying the entire 28,239-byte `create` argument payload
- **Catalog endpoint difference:** `gemini-4-neon` advertises `supported_endpoints: ["/chat/completions"]`, whereas `claude-opus-5.5` uses `/v1/messages` and `gpt-6.2-sol` uses `ws:/responses`.
- **Environment:**
  - OS: Windows 11 (build 26300)
  - Architecture: x86_64
  - CLI: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.116
  - Shell: PowerShell

issues.title: CLI repeatedly ignores commit instruction, tool rejections and reminders to check its rules

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Copilot CLI repeatedly proposed adding a `Co-authored-by` trailer despite the user explicitly instructing it not to. Even after the user rejected commands and repeatedly told it to check its rules, the assistant failed to find and apply the instruction until after a third rejection.

### Affected version

1.0.114

### Steps to reproduce / observed sequence

1. The user had explicitly instructed the assistant not to add `Co-authored-by` trailers to commits, then asked it to commit work in a continued session after history had been summarized.
2. The assistant proposed staging and committing with the prohibited trailer. The user rejected the command.
3. The assistant guessed that the problem was the length of the staging command and retried a shorter command with the same trailer. The user rejected it and reminded the assistant to check its rules.
4. Rather than finding the instruction, the assistant asked the user to identify the rule. The user told it to read the rules and figure it out.
5. The assistant searched repository instruction files, attempted a history search that did not return the relevant local result, and then guessed that the problem was the combined shell command. It staged the changes and again proposed a commit with the trailer. The user rejected it a third time.
6. Only then did the assistant search local session history successfully, find the explicit prior instruction, and commit without the trailer.

### Expected behavior

The assistant should honor the explicit instruction when preparing the commit. After a rejection and reminders to check its rules, it should review relevant available instructions and conversation history, rather than repeatedly guessing or asking the user to restate them.

### Additional context

Observed on macOS. The prior instruction was available in local session history, and a successful search resolved the issue. This report describes one observed session; reproducibility under other session and memory configurations has not been established.

labels.name: area:non-interactive

labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

ACP should allow reading your account limits on all operating systems

### Proposed solution

**Context.** T3 Code runs Copilot CLI over ACP (`copilot --acp`) and shows the user's subscription limits next to other agents' limits.

**Today (1.0.115, Windows):**
- `quotaSnapshots` (for example `premium_interactions`: entitlement, used, reset date) arrive only in the `assistant.usage` session event, so only after a model call.
- `session/new` with `session.quota_observation` opted in emits nothing.
- `/usage` over ACP returns only the session's counters ("Requests: 0 AI Credits"), not account quotas.
- `account.getQuota` exists (see #4504) but is not exposed over ACP.

Clients therefore cannot show limits until the user runs a turn. The only workaround is to read the CLI's OAuth token from the OS credential store and call the undocumented `copilot_internal/user` endpoint. That is fragile and should not be needed.

**Request (any one of these would work):**
1. An ACP extension method, for example `github.com/copilot/getQuota`, returning the same shape as `quotaSnapshots`.
2. A `session.quota_observation` account reading after `session/new` for clients that opt in.
3. A documented, public REST endpoint for the authenticated user's Copilot quota.

Related: #5029 asks for the same account quota data in the status line payload, and #1240 and #4233 cover session usage over ACP.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. A user opens T3 Code (an ACP client) and goes to its Usage → Limits page before starting any Copilot session, to decide whether to use a premium model today. The page cannot show Copilot's premium request allowance yet.
2. The user runs one Copilot turn. `assistant.usage` arrives with `quotaSnapshots`, and the limit appears.
3. After the client restarts, the limit is unknown again until the next turn.

### Additional context

- Copilot CLI 1.0.115 on Windows, `copilot --acp`, protocol v1.
- Related: #5029 asks for the same account quota data in the status line payload. #1240 and #4233 cover session usage over ACP, not account quota.
- T3 Code already uses `assistant.usage` → `quotaSnapshots` for this, so a reply from option 1 or 2 in the same shape would need almost no client change.

issues.title: Windows: existing UNC paths are denied by content exclusion on 1.0.114 (regression from 1.0.108)

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

On Windows, Copilot CLI 1.0.114 rejects shell tool calls that reference an **existing UNC path** during preflight, with:

```text
Access denied: "\\localhost\C$\Temp\plain" is excluded by organization content policy. Do not attempt to access this file.
```

No configured exclusion rule matches these paths. The same folder accessed via its drive-letter path (`C:\Temp\plain`) is allowed in the same session. A UNC path to a non-existent host is also allowed. The denial happens before PowerShell starts (no shell ID or exit code is recorded), so Windows/SMB permissions are never involved. The user can open the same network folders in File Explorer.

The same organization policy did not produce these denials on 1.0.108. This looks like a regression in how 1.0.114 classifies Windows UNC paths for content exclusion, and it may be related to #5521 (Perforce `//depot/...` paths misclassified as UNC paths on Linux, also 1.0.114).

### Affected version

```text
GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.114-unstable.r45286541461.g05667ac (via VS Code 1.148.0, Windows x64)
```

Not reproduced on 1.0.108-0 (also via VS Code, Windows x64).

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Use Windows with an organization account that has content exclusions enabled. Both machines below log `[ContentExclusionService] Loaded 2 exclusion rule(s) for 1 repo(s)`, and the rules are for an unrelated repository.
2. Create a local folder: `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\Temp\plain`
3. Ask Copilot to run each command below through its PowerShell tool, as separate tool calls:

| Command | 1.0.114 result |
|---|---|
| `Test-Path -LiteralPath 'C:\Temp\plain'` | allowed (`True`) |
| `Test-Path -LiteralPath '\\localhost\C$\Temp\plain'` (same folder via UNC) | **denied** (code `denied`) |
| `Test-Path -LiteralPath '\\nonexistent-host.invalid\share\plain'` | allowed (`False`) |
| `Test-Path -LiteralPath 'C:\Temp\SAV\x'` (local control) | allowed (`True`) |

On 1.0.114, an existing directory on a corporate DFS share and its parent folder were both denied with the same message. The user can open both in File Explorer.

On 1.0.108-0, a different machine using the same organization policy could list that same corporate share directory through the PowerShell tool. `Test-Path '\\localhost\C$\Temp'`, `Test-Path '\\nonexistent-host.invalid\share\plain'` and `Test-Path 'C:\Temp\SAV\x'` were also allowed. Caveat: on 1.0.108 the PowerShell sandbox was disabled for these runs. With it enabled, every command failed earlier with an unrelated `Invalid sandbox host rule` error. The sandbox state of the 1.0.114 machine was not recorded.

### Expected behavior

UNC paths that don't match any configured exclusion rule should not be denied. The same folder should get the same decision regardless of whether it's referenced by drive letter or UNC path.

### Additional context

- In the session log, the `preToolUse` hook completes without a decision or output before each denial. The tool result carries error code `denied`.
- In the 1.0.114 process log, no `ContentExclusion`, `rt_git`, or `denied` lines appear around the local, allowed calls. Process log lines around the denied UNC calls have not been collected yet.
- `git -C '\\localhost\C$\Temp' rev-parse --show-toplevel` (and the `\\?\UNC\localhost\C$\Temp` form) returns the normal `not a git repository` result, the same as for `C:\Temp`, so repository discovery via git does not appear to fail on these paths.

issues.title: Org-level custom agents ignore `model`; a model list drops the agent

labels.name: area:agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Org-level custom agents (`agents/*.md` in `<org>/.github-private`) ignore the `model` frontmatter field. The same file honours `model` when placed in `.github/agents/` of the repo.

The API returns the model correctly, so it is dropped client-side:

```
GET https://api.githubcopilot.com/agents/swe/custom-agents/<org>/<repo>?exclude_invalid_config=true&include_sources=org,enterprise
→ { "name": "test-writer", ..., "model": "claude-haiku-5.5" }
```

Related: a `model` list (supported locally since v1.0.83, #2133) makes the server exclude the org agent as invalid, so it silently disappears (`No such agent`).

### Reproduce

1. Add to `<org>/.github-private/agents/test-writer.md`:
   ```yaml
   ---
   name: test-writer
   description: Writes unit tests.
   model: claude-haiku-5.5
   model-policy: required
   ---
   ```
2. In a clone of any repo in `<org>`, without a local copy of the agent:
   `copilot -p "Reply: ready" --agent test-writer --output-format json`

| Agent source | `model` used |
|---|---|
| `.github/agents/` in the repo | `claude-haiku-5.5` ✅ |
| org `.github-private` | `claude-sonnet-5.5` (session default) ❌ |
| org, with `model: [claude-haiku-5.5, gpt-6-luna]` | agent not loaded ❌ |

`model-policy: required` makes no difference for org agents.

### Expected

Org agents honour `model` and `model-policy` like repo-level agents, and accept a model list.

### Environment

Copilot CLI 1.0.116, Linux (Docker, `node:24-slim`), github.com

issues.title: OTel file not written for BYOK -p runs without GitHub sign-in (regression in 1.0.115)

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Since 1.0.115, `copilot -p` with a BYOK provider and no GitHub sign-in doesn't write the OTel file. The run succeeds and exits 0, but the file at `COPILOT_OTEL_FILE_EXPORTER_PATH` is never created, and there's no warning or error.

The log shows OTel being configured (`OpenTelemetry enabled: exporter=file`), but `OTel session policy applied` and `OpenTelemetry tracker created for session` never show up. On 1.0.114 both lines appear and the file is written. 1.0.116 also writes the file once a GitHub account is available (e.g. after `gh auth login`).

### Affected version

1.0.115 and 1.0.116 (1.0.114 works), Linux x64, installed via npm

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Save a minimal OpenAI-compatible stub as `server.py`:

```python
import json
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):  # model list
        self.send_response(200)
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b'{"data": []}')

    def do_POST(self):  # one streamed chat completion with usage
        self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
        self.end_headers()
        base = {"id": "1", "object": "chat.completion.chunk", "created": 0, "model": "gpt-4o"}
        for extra in (
            {"choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {"role": "assistant", "content": "Done"}}]},
            {"choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}],
             "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 10, "completion_tokens": 1, "total_tokens": 11}},
        ):
            self.wfile.write(f"data: {json.dumps({**base, **extra})}\n\n".encode())
        self.wfile.write(b"data: [DONE]\n\n")

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass


HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 18080), Handler).serve_forever()
```

2. Run this from the same directory, without any GitHub credentials:

```bash
d=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$d/gh" "$d/home"
python3 server.py & sleep 1
cd "$d" && env -u GH_TOKEN -u GITHUB_TOKEN -u COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN \
  GH_CONFIG_DIR="$d/gh" COPILOT_HOME="$d/home" \
  COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE=openai COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18080/v1 \
  COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY=test COPILOT_MODEL=gpt-4o \
  COPILOT_OTEL_ENABLED=true COPILOT_OTEL_EXPORTER_TYPE=file \
  COPILOT_OTEL_FILE_EXPORTER_PATH="$d/otel.jsonl" \
  copilot -p "Reply with just: Done" --no-auto-update --log-level all --log-dir "$d/logs"
echo "exit: $?"; ls -l "$d/otel.jsonl"
grep -h "rust:otel" "$d"/logs/*.log
kill $!
```

3. On 1.0.115 and 1.0.116, `otel.jsonl` doesn't exist and the log only has:

```
[INFO] [rust:otel] OpenTelemetry enabled: exporter=file, source=github.copilot ...
[INFO] [rust:otel] OpenTelemetry configured from managed settings: exporter=file, source=github.copilot ...
[DEBUG] [rust:otel] Stopping OpenTelemetry session
```

On 1.0.114 the file is written, and the log also has `OTel session policy applied` and `OpenTelemetry tracker created for session <id>`.

### Expected behavior

The OTel file is written whether or not a GitHub account is signed in, as in 1.0.114.

### Additional context

Possibly the same cause as #5376 (no session tracker in ACP mode).

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Expose Copilot CLI's built-in assisted approval safety judge in ACP mode. ACP clients such as T3 Code should be able to use Copilot's assisted permission policy, automatically approving actions the judge considers safe and requesting human approval for the remaining actions.

In Copilot CLI 1.0.91, I could not enable assisted approval in a direct ACP session. This was reproduced without T3 Code involved.

### Proposed solution

- Expose an assisted permission mode through ACP session configuration and document the supported way to enable it, including any experimental flags or policy requirements.
- Use Copilot's existing safety judge in ACP sessions, forwarding requests that still require human approval through `session/request_permission`.
- Preserve the ACP client's rejection and cancellation decisions for requests sent to it.

If an existing supported configuration already enables this, please document it in the ACP server reference.

### Example prompts or workflows

- An ACP editor session can use assisted approval for routine code changes and verification commands.
- Actions the safety judge does not approve automatically appear in the client's approval UI for the user to decide.
- Users can select assisted approval without requiring each ACP client to implement its own model reviewer.

### Additional context

Environment: Copilot CLI 1.0.91, macOS, ARM64.

Starting the ACP server with assisted approval:

```sh
copilot --acp --experimental --assisted-approval
```

exits before ACP initialization with:

```text
--assisted-approval is only supported in non-interactive prompt mode or direct workflow mode.
```

Starting with `copilot --acp --experimental`, completing `initialize` and `session/new`, and sending `/permissions assisted` as a text prompt through `session/prompt` returns:

```text
Failed to run /permissions: Error: Assisted mode is disabled. Run `/experimental on`, start with `--experimental`, or set `enabledFeatureFlags.AUTO_APPROVAL` to true before using `/permissions assisted`. An explicit false override takes precedence over experimental mode.
```

A subsequent `/permissions show` reports:

```text
Permission policy: Manual Approval for this session. Tool, path, and URL requests require individual approval.
```

The same result occurred with an isolated `COPILOT_HOME` containing `experimental: true` and `enabledFeatureFlags.AUTO_APPROVAL: true` in both `settings.json` and `config.json`. The permission configuration advertised by `session/new` exposed only `allow_all` on/off; the advertised `/permissions` command hint was `[default|allow-all|show]`.

ACP reference: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/acp-server

issues.title: /mcp <server-name> fails due to case sensitive matching

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

`/mcp <server-name>` finds a server name only with an exact-case match. For a server with the name `MyServer`, `/mcp myserver` and `/mcp myServer` fail with `Server "myserver" not found. Use /mcp to open the MCP server list.`

### Proposed solution

Make the server-name lookup case-insensitive for the `/mcp` slash commands (`/mcp <name>`, `/mcp edit`, `/mcp enable`, `/mcp disable`) and for `--disable-mcp-server`.

1. Try the exact-case match first.
2. If no exact match exists, use the one server whose name matches without case.
3. If two or more servers match without case, show the error with the list of matching names.

This change helps users who do not remember the exact case of a server name. Brand names with mixed case cause this error frequently.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. A plugin declares the server `MyServer`. The user types `/mcp myserver` to sign in again. Today the command fails. With this change, it opens the detail view for `MyServer`.
2. A user starts `copilot --disable-mcp-server myserver`. Today the CLI does not disable the `MyServer` server. With this change, it disables that server.
3. A user types `/mcp disable MYSERVER`. With this change, the CLI disables `MyServer`.

### Additional context

- Version: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.91 on Windows.
- Workaround: run `/mcp` with no name, then select the server from the list.
- Related: #1062. That fix made `/mcp enable` and `/mcp disable` reject unknown names. Thus a name with the wrong case now gets the "not found" error.

issues.title: OTel metrics have no service.instance.id, so concurrent sessions write to the same metric streams
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Copilot CLI exports cumulative metrics (`gen_ai.client.token.usage`, `github.copilot.tool.call.count`, ...) with only `service.name` and `service.version` on the resource. There is no `service.instance.id` or any other attribute that is unique per process.

When several CLI processes export to the same backend, their metric streams have the same identity. That breaks the OTel [single-writer](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/metrics/data-model/#single-writer) rule. In Prometheus and Mimir, `service.instance.id` becomes the `instance` label, so every session writes to the same series. Each process starts its counters from zero, and the backend sees resets and out-of-order values. Sums and rates across users are wrong.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.88

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. `COPILOT_OTEL_FILE_EXPORTER_PATH=/tmp/otel.jsonl copilot -p "Reply with: pong"`
2. Check the `resource` of the metric lines in `/tmp/otel.jsonl`. It only has `service.name` and `service.version`.
3. Run two sessions at the same time with `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` pointing at a collector that writes to Prometheus. Both sessions update the same series.

### Expected behavior

Each process sets `service.instance.id` on the resource. A random UUID at startup is what the [semantic conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/registry/attributes/service/) recommend. The session ID would also work.

### Additional context

We can't work around this with `resourceAttributes` in enterprise managed settings, because that value is the same for every user. Right now we drop the CLI metrics in our collector and build our own metrics from the spans instead.

Linux (WSL2), x86_64.

issues.title: Tool approvals sometimes silently lost when copilot CLI is used in parallel sessions

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

labels.name: area:configuration
labels.description: Config files, instruction files, settings, and environment variables

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When two or more `copilot` CLI sessions run simultaneously and each persists a tool approval (the "Always allow" prompt), one session's approval seems to sometimes silently overwrite the other's in `~/.copilot/permissions-config.json`. The loss is not limited to the same directory — approvals for *other* directories in the file can also be dropped, because the entire `locations` object appears to be replaced rather than merged.

This makes "Always allow" feel unreliable: user repeatedly re-approves the same commands, MCP tools, and extensions after seemingly random sessions.

The same read-modify-write pattern appears to be reused for other config files, so we suspect (but did not isolate repros for) related races affecting:

- `config.json` → `trustedFolders` (re-prompted to trust folders that were previously trusted)

Filing this against the most reproducible case; if the team confirms a shared root cause, fixing the underlying config store should resolve the others.

### Affected version

1.0.55-7

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Seems intermittent but, variations of:

1. Open two terminals.
2. In Terminal A: `cd <dirA>`, run `copilot`, trigger a tool that prompts for approval (e.g., any shell command), choose **Always allow**. Leave the session running.
3. In Terminal B: `cd <dirB>` (a *different* directory), run `copilot`, trigger a tool that prompts for approval, choose **Always allow**. Exit the session.
4. Back in Terminal A: trigger another tool that prompts for approval, choose **Always allow**. Exit the session.
5. Inspect `~/.copilot/permissions-config.json`.

Observed: `locations[<dirB>]` is missing entirely. Only Terminal A's view of the world survives, because Terminal A's final write replaced the on-disk `locations` object with its in-memory copy — which never knew about `<dirB>`.

### Expected behavior

`locations` in `permissions-config.json` should contain entries for both `<dirA>` and `<dirB>`, with the approvals granted in each session preserved. Concurrent sessions should merge their changes, not overwrite each other.

### Additional context

 ## Environment
 
 - OS: Windows 11
 - CPU architecture: x86_64
 - Terminal emulator: Windows Terminal
 - Shell: PowerShell 7
 - Multiple parallel CLI sessions across different cwds (worktrees, separate projects) is the normal workflow that triggers this.

issues.title: Stdio MCP server fails to connect when `server/discover` times out: legacy `initialize` fallback on the same connection is rejected with -32022

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
## Summary

When a stdio MCP server takes longer than ~10 s to start, Copilot CLI gives up waiting for its `server/discover` probe and sends a legacy `initialize` **on the same stdio connection**. A server built on the MCP Python SDK 2.3.0 then processes the queued `server/discover` first, locks the connection to the 2026-07-28 protocol, and rejects the `initialize` with `-32022`. Copilot CLI reports the server as failed and does not retry, even though both sides support 2026-07-28.

In the same situation, Claude Code (2.1.308) and the MCP Python SDK client re-probe with `server/discover` and connect successfully.

## Environment

- Copilot CLI 1.0.103 (linux-x64)
- MCP server: any stdio server on `mcp` (Python SDK) 2.3.0 with a slow cold start. Observed with `analytics-mcp` 0.8.0 (Google Analytics MCP server) and `serena-agent` 2.1.0.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Save this as `slow_server.py`:

   ```python
   # /// script
   # dependencies = ["mcp==2.3.0"]
   # ///
   import time

   time.sleep(12)  # simulate a slow cold start

   from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer

   server = MCPServer("slow-start-repro")


   @server.tool()
   def ping() -> str:
       return "pong"


   server.run("stdio")
   ```

2. Run `uv run --script slow_server.py < /dev/null` once so the dependencies are cached.
3. Start Copilot CLI with the server:

   ```sh
   copilot -p "List the tools of the slowrepro MCP server. Do not call them." \
     --additional-mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{"slowrepro":{"type":"local","command":"uv","args":["run","-q","--script","/path/to/slow_server.py"],"tools":["*"]}}}'
   ```

## Actual behavior

The server is not connected. The log shows:

```
[WARNING] [rust:rt_mcp_connection] MCP server connection failed {"server_name":"...","raw_error":"failed to initialize MCP client: JSON-RPC error: -32022: connection is serving the 2026-07-28 protocol; the initialize handshake is not accepted({\"supported\":[\"2026-07-28\"],\"requested\":\"2025-11-25\"})"}
```

Frames captured between Copilot CLI and the server (seconds since spawn):

```
 0.007 C->S {"id":0,"method":"server/discover","params":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion":"2026-07-28",...}}}
 9.797 C->S {"id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-11-25",...}}
13.813 S->C {"id":0,"result":{"supportedVersions":["2026-07-28"],...}}
13.814 S->C {"id":1,"error":{"code":-32022,"message":"connection is serving the 2026-07-28 protocol; the initialize handshake is not accepted","data":{"supported":["2026-07-28"],"requested":"2025-11-25"}}}
```

Servers that normally start within 5 s also hit this right after the machine boots (cold disk cache, many processes starting at once). In that case, `/mcp reload` or restarting Copilot CLI connects them.

## Expected behavior

The connection succeeds over 2026-07-28, as it does when the server starts within the timeout. Any of these would work:

- When the fallback `initialize` gets `-32022` and `data.supported` contains a version the client supports, re-probe with `server/discover` at that version. The MCP Python SDK client does this (`mcp/client/_probe.py`: "The fallback handshake itself can be answered with -32022 … That code is itself positive modern evidence … so it triggers one re-probe at a mutual version instead of failing the connect."), and so does Claude Code.
- Accept a late `server/discover` response that arrives after the fallback was sent.
- For stdio, restart the server process before falling back, so the fallback does not share a connection with the unanswered probe.

## Workaround

Make the server start faster than the probe timeout. In our case the venv is read-only at runtime, so `.pyc` files were never written. Installing the server with `uv tool install --compile-bytecode` brought startup down to ~3.5 s, and Copilot CLI then connected over 2026-07-28. This still fails occasionally right after the machine boots, as described above.

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Copilot CLI  1.0.109  on Windows blocks a direct TCP connection to an internal Nexus server, even though outbound and local networking are enabled and both its hostname and resolved IP are allowed.

The connection fails with  SocketErrorCode: AccessDenied , Windows error  10013 , for  <ip_address>:443 . Maven also reports  Permission denied: getsockopt  when resolving dependencies. Adding the IP and restarting the CLI did not resolve it.

### Affected version

Copilot CLI  1.0.109  on Windows

### Steps to reproduce the behavior
1. Enable the sandbox and allow outbound and local networking.
2. Add the Nexus hostname and its resolved IP to allowed hosts.
3. Have Copilot run a PowerShell TCP connection to the hostname on port 443:

```
$client = New-Object System.Net.Sockets.TcpClient
try {
    $client.ConnectAsync('nexus.mycompany.com', 443).Wait(10000)
} finally {
    $client.Dispose()
}
```

### Expected behavior

The direct TCP connection succeeds under the displayed policy.

### Additional context

curl  to the same HTTPS hostname succeeds from the sandbox. The effective policy lists both the hostname and IP in allow layer 1, says outbound and local networking are allowed, and identifies the host filter as the local proxy.

releases.body:
**Added**
- Add sandbox.userPolicy.network.extraCaCertificates, in user or managed settings, to trust custom CA certificates for sandboxed commands through TLS-intercepting proxies

**Fixed**
- Fix Page Down stalling at a pinned prompt in a 10-row terminal with tabs enabled.

**Improved**
- Assisted Permissions can avoid unnecessary confirmation prompts when Copilot stops a process it started in the same session by process ID.

**Fixed**
- Approving an MCP server's tools for the session or for a location no longer also approves Copilot's built-in requests, such as shell commands or memory stores, when the server's name matches a built-in permission type. The approval still covers that server's tools, including after the session is resumed.
- Starting in autopilot now asks before launching each extension, instead of denying every extension with "no one to approve"
- Restore original binary skill assets when rejecting a Forge draft and preserve edits made after generation.
- `/mcp search` explains why a registry server can't be installed instead of showing an endless installation spinner.
- Quitting a local CLI session with /exit or Ctrl+D discards queued prompts so they don't run after the exit summary.
- Copilot CLI starts without plugins when it cannot read or parse config.json, leaving the file unchanged.
- Match MCP server names regardless of capitalization in `/mcp` commands and `--disable-mcp-server`, with exact matches taking precedence.
- Answering a permission prompt keeps the composer draft unchanged.
- On Linux and macOS, stop child processes of a GITHUB_ASKPASS sign-in helper that is still running when it times out.
- Keep existing repository settings files read-only for sandboxed commands and agent edits in writable Git worktrees on macOS and Linux.
- Git commits, branch creation, and stashing work again in linked worktrees the Copilot CLI sandbox can write to.
- Fix indexed search results for regular expressions that join groups of alternatives.
- Stopping Copilot CLI in ACP mode with Ctrl+C no longer reports a false shutdown error or exits with a failure status.
- Prevent repeated notices about organization-required plugins when resuming a session or when authentication refreshes.
- Use a recognizable Copilot CLI name for voice input in Windows microphone privacy settings.

issues.title: tui: live reload ignores edits to symlinked cli.json

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/tui
labels.description: Terminal interface

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

issues.body:
## Summary

When `~/.config/opencode/cli.json` is a symlink to a file in another directory, editing the target file does not trigger TUI live reload. Reproduced on `opencode v2.4.2`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Put a `cli.json` file in another directory, such as `/tmp/dotfiles/cli.json`.
2. Symlink `~/.config/opencode/cli.json` to `/tmp/dotfiles/cli.json`.
3. Open `opencode` in a terminal.
4. Edit `/tmp/dotfiles/cli.json`, for example set `"tabs": { "mode": "off" }` or change `theme.name`.

## Expected

The TUI reloads `cli.json` and applies the change right away.

## Actual

Nothing updates in the running TUI. Running `touch -h ~/.config/opencode/cli.json` triggers the reload immediately.

## Cause

- [`packages/cli/src/config/config.ts#L31`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/e702df9e74d2821d7c4ef587ae25dae4c26b6e68/packages/cli/src/config/config.ts#L31) sets the config path to `path.join(global.config, "cli.json")` without resolving symlinks.
- [`packages/tui/src/config/index.tsx#L368-L375`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/e702df9e74d2821d7c4ef587ae25dae4c26b6e68/packages/tui/src/config/index.tsx#L368-L375) passes `path.dirname(host.path)` to `safeWatch`, which calls `node:fs` `watch` on `~/.config/opencode` at [`packages/tui/src/util/watch.ts#L10-L15`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/e702df9e74d2821d7c4ef587ae25dae4c26b6e68/packages/tui/src/util/watch.ts#L10-L15).
- Editing the symlink target emits an event in the target's directory, not in `~/.config/opencode`, so `ConfigProvider` never reloads.
- The Rust client watches only `self.config` in the same way at [`packages/cli-rs/crates/local/src/cli_config.rs#L584`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/e702df9e74d2821d7c4ef587ae25dae4c26b6e68/packages/cli-rs/crates/local/src/cli_config.rs#L584).

Watching the `realpath` target's parent directory as well as `~/.config/opencode` when they differ would catch edits to the symlinked file.

Related issue #45067 covers the write side, where saving settings from the TUI replaces a symlinked `cli.json` with a regular file.

labels.name: platform/linux
labels.description: Linux

issues.body:
## Summary

When the background service fails a scripted `opencode run` session server-side (observed with `AI.Error.QuotaExceeded` on plan usage limits), the CLI exits 1 with a completely empty stderr and no usable error on stdout. Scripted/CI consumers cannot see why the run failed — the cause only exists in the server log (`~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`).

## Environment

- opencode version: v2.4.1 (also reproduced in the wild on v2.2.5 and v2.3.2)
- OS: Ubuntu, Linux main 7.0.0-43-generic x86_64
- Terminal: Unavailable (headless server, cron/automation context)
- Shell: bash (calling script) / fish (interactive)
- Install/channel: latest, background service (`opencode serve --service` as a systemd user unit)
- Active plugins: none configured

## Reproduction

1. Run a scripted call through the shared background service:
   `opencode run --format json -m <provider>/<model> "<prompt>"`
2. Have the provider/session fail server-side during the drain — concretely observed when the OpenCode Go plan's weekly/monthly usage limit is exhausted, so the server aborts the session before/while draining.
3. Observe the process exit code and stderr.

## Expected Behavior

The failure reason (e.g. `AI.Error.QuotaExceeded: OpenCode Go usage limit reached (weekly, resets in ...)`) should be printed to stderr (and/or surfaced as an error event in `--format json` stdout), so scripted consumers can log, classify, and react to it.

## Actual Behavior

Process exits 1 with empty stderr, and the NDJSON stdout carries no content the consumer can act on. The only trace is in the server log:

```
timestamp=... level=ERROR run=... message="Failed to drain Session" cause="AI.Error: OpenCode Go usage limit reached (weekly, resets in 1d 21h). To keep going now, turn on Extra Usage or upgrade to Go Plus at https://opencode.ai/console/wrk_****/go." role=server sessionID=ses_...
```

(full JS stack frames follow in the log line; trimmed here)

## Additional Context

- Hit 4 times over one month in a production nightly email-classification job (gmail-tracker digest, `cwd` on a server): Nov 8 02:30 UTC (v2.2.5), Nov 21, 22, 25 02:30 UTC (v2.3.2). Every failure showed `opencode run exited 1:` with an empty stderr string while the server log held the full quota error.
- Frequency: intermittent — happens whenever the plan quota is exhausted at run time; all other runs behave normally.
- Workaround: tail the server log for the last `level=ERROR` line when `run` exits 1 with empty stderr (implemented in the consumer). A first-class stderr/error-event would remove the need.
- The quota error message itself is great — it just never reaches the CLI caller.

issues.body:
## Summary

A `SKILL.md` whose frontmatter fails to parse is dropped with `Effect.logDebug` only, so at the default
log level the skill simply does not exist: no warning, no error, no event. The model then works without
instructions the user believes are loaded. This is the same class as #45876 (agent markdown silently
skipped), whose fix covered agents — the skill path still logs at debug.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.4.2
- Client: TUI / shared service
- Model and provider: Not relevant
- OS: Linux 6.x x86_64
- Terminal: xterm-kitty, truecolor
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: latest (release)
- Active plugins: none

## Reproduction

1. Create a skill with malformed frontmatter — the YAML parses into an error rather than a mapping, e.g.
   an unterminated quoted scalar:

   ```markdown
   ---
   name: repro
   description: "unterminated
   ---
   body
   ```

   at `~/.config/opencode/skills/repro/SKILL.md` (a project `.opencode/skills/` source behaves the same).

2. Start opencode and open the skills list (`/skills`).
3. The skill is absent.
4. Look at `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`: there is no line at the default level mentioning
   the file or the parse failure. With `OPENCODE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` the line appears as
   `message="skill file skipped" reason=frontmatter`.

## Expected Behavior

A warning at the default log level naming the file and the reason — the behaviour #45876 established for
agent definitions ("inconsistent with skill loading, which logs an error"). A skill that fails to load is
a configuration error the user must be able to see, exactly like an agent that fails to load.

## Actual Behavior

Silence. The loader skips the file:

```ts
// packages/core/src/config/plugin/skill.ts (v2.4.2, lines 133-139)
if (parsed._tag === "Skipped") {
  yield* Effect.logDebug("skill file skipped", {
    filepath,
    reason: parsed.reason,
    ...(parsed.reason === "frontmatter" ? { issue: parsed.issue } : {}),
  })
  continue
}
```

## Additional Context

Why this matters more for skills than for most settings: the model's behaviour changes with the skill,
and nothing else reports the loss. In the session that produced this report, the project ships 24 skills
(8 runtime + 16 reference documents registered as skill sources); one malformed frontmatter would remove
one of them silently, and the only way to notice is to know the expected list by heart.

Related: #45876 (closed) fixed the agent path and states that skills log an error — they do not, at least
not at the default level. If the intent is that `logDebug` is enough, the issue can be closed with that
rationale; the request is the same visibility the agent loader now has.

issues.title: V2: GET /api/vcs boots a cold location per directory, so a client sweeping its project list loads every project's MCP servers

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/sdk-api
labels.description: SDK and HTTP API

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/linux
labels.description: Linux

issues.body:
### Description

A request to `GET /api/vcs` for a directory whose location is not loaded boots the full location, local stdio MCP servers included, just to answer a git status read. A client that asks for the VCS state of every project it knows therefore boots every project at once. The idle eviction (60 minutes by default) cannot keep up with that.

What we saw on one `opencode serve` with about 80 known project directories (git worktrees), a handful of local stdio MCP servers (each location starts its own copy of all of them) and one local plugin in the config:

- Several times in one evening, the server booted nearly every known directory, roughly in path order, within a minute or two: 29, 31, 51 and 69 `location services booted` lines per minute.
- During one sweep the MCP server processes went from 3 sets to about 63 sets in two minutes. The service reached 5.3 GB (cgroup peak) and other API calls timed out.
- A later sweep booted 83 locations in four minutes (62 in the first two) and started about 80 MCP sets.
- In the sweep window almost all HTTP responses were `GET /api/vcs`: 177 of them in under two minutes. They took 28 ms to 72 s (median 0.6 s; 21 took over 2 s) and ended with status 404, or 499 when the client gave up. A clean server returns 200 for the same route, so we do not know why ours answered 404; the log lines carry no directory, so we cannot tie each request to a boot.

Related: #53918 (the form and permission reads boot cold locations in the same way, confirmed below), #51173 (`/api/vcs` waits for the location's plugins, so it depends on a booted location) and #63336 (MCP processes outlive the client).

Narrowing:

- Deleting a session while a TUI is attached to it did not cause this in a clean repro. The attached client made its normal startup reads once, refreshed one location about a minute later, and booted nothing new in two minutes.
- `GET /api/session/:id/permission` and `GET /api/session/:id/form` on three cold sessions booted all three locations, one MCP set each, as #53918 says.
- A request for a route the server does not have boots nothing.

Expected: a VCS read for a cold location reads the git state without constructing the location graph (watchers, MCP servers), or at least without starting MCP servers. A sweep over N projects should not leave N MCP sets running for an hour.

### Plugins

None in the repro.

### OpenCode version

2.0.32

### Steps to reproduce

1. Put one local stdio MCP server in `opencode.json`. Any small server works; we used a 20-line Node script that answers `initialize` and `tools/list`.
2. Make three git repositories, `p1`, `p2` and `p3`.
3. Start `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD=secret opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096 --print-logs --log-level debug` from another directory.
4. For each repository, run `curl -u opencode:secret "http://127.0.0.1:4096/api/vcs?location%5Bdirectory%5D=/abs/path/to/pN"` (an absolute path). Passing the directory in the `x-opencode-directory` header does the same.
5. Count the MCP processes: `pgrep -fc <mcp script>`.

Result: three MCP processes, and three `location services booted` lines, one per repository. Each request returns 200 within 0.4 s. In the same setup, `GET /api/no-such-route` with the same directory returns 404 and boots nothing.

### Operating System

Linux (Fedora 44, kernel 7.3), x64.

### Terminal

Not terminal specific. We could not identify the sweeping client from the server log, and the repro uses curl.
