- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A terminal whose shell exits on its own (the user types `exit`, or the command finishes) never releases its pty pair. Each one leaks 2 fds. After about 500, `POST /api/pty` fails with `PTY spawn failed`, and on macOS the pty limit (`kern.tty.ptmx_max` = 511) is shared by the whole machine. This PR adds a carried patch for `bun-pty@0.4.11` that closes the native handle when the child exits.

**Cause.** In bun-pty, only `kill()` calls `bun_pty_close(handle)`. When the read loop sees the child exit (`n === -2`), it fires `onExit` and stops without closing. `Pty` in `packages/core/src/pty.ts` only calls `kill()` while the session is `running`, so a session that exited by itself is never closed. This is still unfixed in bun-pty 0.6.2.

**Change** (`patches/bun-pty@0.4.11.patch`, `Terminal._startReadLoop`):

```diff
 } else if (n === -2) {
   // flush decoder, fire remaining onData
   const exitCode = lib.symbols.bun_pty_get_exit_code(this.handle);
-  this._onExit.fire({ exitCode });
+  this._closing = true;
+  try {
+    this._onExit.fire({ exitCode });
+  } finally {
+    lib.symbols.bun_pty_close(this.handle);
+  }
   break;
```

**Why it's safe:**
- `main` is `./src/index.ts` and the package has no `exports`; `dist/` only ships `.d.ts` files. So `src/terminal.ts` is the only JS that runs, in dev and in compiled binaries.
- The exit code is read before the close. `bun_pty_close` (rust-pty `lib.rs` at the v0.4.11 tag) only removes the handle from the registry, which drops the registry's `Arc<Pty>`. Every other FFI call looks the handle up in that registry and returns `-1` if it's missing, and handle ids are never reused. So calling it again would be a no-op, not a use-after-free.
- `kill()` already makes this same call on every terminal that's closed while running, so this code path is already used in production.
- `_closing = true` is set before `onExit` fires. `write`, `resize` and `kill` all return early when it's set, and the read loop breaks right after. So nothing touches the handle after the close, and a listener that calls `kill()` during the event no longer signals a pid that's already been reaped and fires a second `onExit` with code 0 (that's what happens today). `pid` is a cached field. OpenCode's own `onExit` handler only updates session state, notifies subscribers and publishes events. After it runs, `write`/`resize`/teardown all check `status === "running"` first.
- `try/finally` keeps the handle from leaking if a listener throws.
- On Unix, dropping the `Pty` closes the master and slave fds. The reader thread then gets EOF and exits, and the writer thread exits when its channel closes. On Windows, where the Bun build also uses bun-pty, the drop calls `ClosePseudoConsole`. That's the same thing `kill()` already does there. Today an exited Windows terminal also keeps its ConPTY and reader thread alive, and this patch releases those too. I haven't run it on Windows: the pty session tests skip on win32, and PR CI only runs on Linux.

### How did you verify your code works?

A standalone script on macOS arm64 (Bun 1.4.4) spawns N `sh -c 'exit 3'` terminals, waits for every `onExit`, then counts this process's `/dev/ptmx` fds with `lsof -p`:

| | open `/dev/ptmx` fds after N natural exits | total fds |
|---|---:|---:|
| dev, N = 30 | 60 | 12 → 102 |
| patched, N = 30 | 0 | 12 → 12 |
| patched, N = 200 | 0 | 12 → 12 |

Also checked with the patch:
- Exit codes are still reported (all 3), with exactly one `onExit` per terminal.
- Output printed right before exit still arrives (`printf hello-done; exit 7` gives `hello-done` and exit code 7, 20 of 20 times).
- `kill()` on a running `sleep 30` terminal: one `onExit`, the child is gone, fds go back to 0. A second `kill()` is a no-op.
- Calling `kill()`, `write()` and `resize()` from inside `onExit`: one exit event and 0 leaked fds. On dev, the same listener got a second `onExit` with code 0.
- The patch applies from scratch: I deleted the store entry and ran `bun install` again.

Tests:
- `packages/core`: `bun test test/pty test/persistent-pty-session.test.ts test/persistent-pty-daemon.test.ts`: 36 pass, 2 skip (Windows only)
- `packages/server`: `bun test` on the pty-socket, pty-socket property, pty-transport and persistent-pty tests: 14 pass
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` in `packages/core`, and `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.build.json --noEmit` in `packages/server`, `packages/sdk` and `packages/simulation`: all clean

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

### What does this PR do?

For a new session, the title prompt included the whole first user message. When that message had a pasted file in it, the whole file went to the title model. prs.title: fix(core): poll Console config hourly while signed out
prs.body:
## Observed problem

From Cloudflare Workers Observability on `opencode-console-api-production` (24h ending 2026-11-26 ~20:56 UTC): `GET /console/api/v2/config` receives **10.84M `401` responses/day** (~10.3% of all `/v2/config` traffic).

## Diagnosis

When a client's credentials are revoked or signed out (`SignedOutError` / HTTP `401`), the connection stays in place with `needs_auth` status and the background poller keeps asking `GET /api/v2/config` on the normal interval forever. Only a new sign-in fixes that state.

## Change

- `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/opencode.ts`: while the last load was refused as signed out, poll **hourly** instead of every 5 minutes. The poll loop is one `Schedule` whose delay is the interval plus jitter. A successful load, a non-401 failure or a disconnect returns to the normal interval. Switching or signing in refreshes immediately and restarts the timer.
- `SsoRequired` (`403`) stays on the 5-minute interval so completing SSO in the browser clears promptly.

## Trade-off

A session the Console rejects by mistake now shows "Reconnect" until the next hourly poll, a 401 on a model request (which re-checks at once), or a new sign-in. Previously it cleared on the next 5-minute poll. The existing test for that case now advances 62 minutes.

## Expected impact

Signed-out clients go from one request per ~5.5 minutes to one per ~60.5 minutes: about 11x fewer `401`s from clients on this version.

## Verification

- `bun run script/test.ts test/plugin/provider-opencode.test.ts test/plugin/provider-opencode-artifacts.test.ts test/plugin/provider-opencode-watches.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 109 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun run typecheck` in `packages/core`: passed.

prs.title: fix(core): skip in-flight retries on warm SharedCache refreshes
prs.body:
Follows #66673 (independent; branched off `dev` so it can be reviewed and merged in either order).

## Observed Problem

From Cloudflare Workers Observability on `opencode-console-api-production` (24h ending 2026-11-26 ~20:56 UTC):

- `GET /console/api/v2/config` receives ~105.7M requests/day (~1,223 req/s).
- During PlanetScale stalls (e.g., 2026-11-25 07:40–07:55 UTC: 118 `500`s; 11:35:30–11:36:00 UTC: 260 `500`s; 11:48:00–11:48:30 UTC: 100 `500`s), Worker requests hang up to ~30s (`wallTimeMs` ~30,023–30,137ms) before returning `500`.

## Diagnosis

`packages/core/src/shared-cache.ts:61-63` retries every transient failure (`TimeoutError`, `TransportError`, `408/429/5xx`) **3 times** with unjittered `Schedule.exponential("1 second")` — even when the cache already holds a valid cached value that will be kept on failure. Because `fetchConfig` / `fetchList` time out at 5s (`packages/core/src/plugin/provider/opencode.ts:621,653`), every polling client sends **4 overlapping requests in ~27s** during a database stall while earlier timed-out requests are still held server-side.

## Changes

- **`packages/core/src/shared-cache.ts`**:
  - Skip in-flight retries on warm refreshes (when `entry.last?.exit` is already a success), keeping the cached value until the next interval.
  - On cold loads (no cached value yet), reduce retries from 3 unjittered to **2 jittered** (`Schedule.exponential("1 second").pipe(Schedule.jittered)`).
- **`packages/core/src/plugin/provider/opencode.ts`**: update the timeout comment on `fetchConfig` to reflect cold-load-only retries.
- **Tests**: updated retry-count expectations in `packages/core/test/shared-cache.test.ts` and `packages/core/test/plugin/provider-opencode.test.ts`, and added a test verifying warm-refresh stalls do not amplify requests.

No feature flag is added (per `AGENTS.md`, fixes do not require a flag).

## Expected Impact

- Cuts stall retry amplification on warm refreshes by **4x** (4 overlapping requests/27s -> 1 request per client), combining with #66673 for a ~20x reduction in load during database stalls.

## Verification

- `bun run script/test.ts test/shared-cache.test.ts test/plugin/provider-opencode.test.ts test/plugin/provider-azure.test.ts test/plugin/provider-digitalocean.test.ts test/plugin/provider-github-copilot.test.ts` in `packages/core`: **126 pass, 0 fail**.
- `bun run script/test.ts test/shared-cache.test.ts test/plugin/provider-opencode.test.ts --rerun-each 10 --randomize` in `packages/core`: **620 pass, 0 fail**.
- Verified the new stall test goes red when the warm-refresh guard is removed.
- `bun typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:tsc` in `packages/core`: passed.
- Pre-push `bun run check` across all packages: passed.

prs.title: fix(core): register a new ChatGPT client when adding an account
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/56298

Adding a second ChatGPT account while one was connected failed on OpenAI's page with `3p_login_workspace_scope_denied` (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/56298). Each issued ChatGPT client belongs to one account and workspace, and "Sign in with ChatGPT" always reused the active connection's client, including from Add account.

```text
Sign in with ChatGPT (incl. Add account)
- active connection's client, always
+ active connection expired (refresh got invalid_grant) → reuse its client, with login_hint (its email)
+ otherwise → client_id=dynamic_agent_client (register a new client)
```

```text
                          before        after
add a second account B    error         new client for B
A expired, Add, remove A  reuses A      reuses A
A working, Add as A       reuses A      new client (same as any other add)
```

- When a refresh gets `invalid_grant` (the "Connect again" case), I record that client as expired in plugin storage. A successful sign-in with that client clears it.
- The account's email (from the verified ID token) now lives in the credential's metadata. It's only sent as `login_hint` when reconnecting that connection, and logout deletes it with the credential. I don't store or send the ID token itself.
- Signing in after removing every ChatGPT account still registers a new client, same as today. Choosing the client has to happen before the user picks an account, and with nothing connected there's no way to tell "same account again" from "a different one" without asking.

No UI or public API change. It's only `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/chatgpt.ts` and its test.

## Verification

- `bun test test/plugin/provider-chatgpt.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 27 pass. The reauthorization test now checks that a working connection registers fresh (no hints) and an expired one reuses its client with `login_hint`.
- `bun typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:tsc` in `packages/core`: pass.
- Not covered by a test: recording the expired client from a real refresh, since the token URL isn't injectable through the method. Not tried live with two ChatGPT accounts.

prs.title: fix(core): convert each tool schema to JSON Schema once
prs.body:
Saving the config could freeze a busy server for seconds, long enough for shell commands to time out. Tool input and output schemas are now converted to JSON Schema once per schema object instead of on every tool-list rebuild.

On a config change, each of the 13 built-in tool plugins that watch config reloads the tool list in every Location, and every reload converted all ~186 tool schemas again, without yielding to the event loop. With 43 Locations (a real long-lived `opencode serve` setup), one save ran about 560 rebuilds back to back. When that freeze passes 5 s, the PTY client's 5 s timeout fires: the command either runs untracked, or a large command is cut off mid-send and never runs.

```diff
 definition(tool)
-  inputSchema: toJsonSchema(tool.input)        // every rebuild
+  inputSchema: cached(tool.input, toJsonSchema) // once per schema object (WeakMap)
```

Measured on a dev server with 43 Locations, 16 plugins, and 3 config saves while a session ran shell commands:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Worst event-loop stall | 2.2–2.7 s | 0.44–0.55 s |
| Slowest PTY `create_pipe` reply | 2.0–2.7 s | 0.48–0.57 s |
| Schema conversions | 312,697 | 11,739 |

Callers now share the converted object, like `codecFor` already does for JSON Schema codecs. Nothing writes to `inputSchema` or `outputSchema` after `definition` returns. Plugins with real tools (more than the test ones) will still see some stall from the 13 rebuilds per save. Cutting that to one rebuild is a separate change.

## Verification
- `tool-execute.test.ts`: the shared-runtime test expected a new inventory to convert the same schema again. It now expects one conversion.
- `bun test test/tool` in `packages/core`: the 3 ShellTool failures also fail on `dev`.
- `tsc --noEmit` in core, and `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json --noEmit` in server, sdk and simulation.

prs.title: fix(core): read effort and system update flags from models.dev
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No issue. Found while reworking https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66648.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

models.dev records per API whether a model takes effort changes (`effort_updates`) and system messages (`system_updates`) mid-conversation, but opencode never read either flag. https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61492 gave the AI package matching capabilities (`reasoning.updates`, `systemUpdates`) and left filling them from the catalog for later; that step never landed. So every catalog model fell back to each route's model-ID guess (GPT-6+ on OpenAI Responses, Claude 5.x on Anthropic Messages), and routes without a guess, like the shared Open Responses route Copilot uses, never sent either.

This reads both flags from the model's API in models.dev:

```text
models.dev api.<name>.capabilities
  effort_updates = true  → compatibility.supportsEffortUpdates → capabilities.reasoning.updates
  system_updates = true  → compatibility.supportsSystemUpdates → capabilities.systemUpdates
  unset or false         → nothing set, the route keeps its own detection
```

- **Only a yes on the model's API counts.** An unset or false flag changes nothing, so no model loses support it has today. The model-wide `system_updates` isn't read: models.dev sets it for Chat Completions developer messages on many hosts that also list an Anthropic Messages API (Kimi, DeepSeek, Qwen, OpenRouter, Vercel), where it would turn on native system messages nobody tested.
- **New `compatibility.supportsSystemUpdates`**, next to `supportsEffortUpdates`: models.dev fills it, and a config can override it per model. It is model-only, like `supportsEffortUpdates`. This is an additive public schema field (client, OpenAPI and cli-rs types regenerated or updated, docs updated).
- **`tools.updates` is left out on purpose.** The routes act on it as soon as it's set: OpenAI Responses moves every tool into a leading `additional_tools` item and Anthropic sends tool changes in place. That changes the request shape for many models, so it should land on its own.

What changes with today's catalog (APIs where models.dev says yes and the route's guess says no):

| Flag | Newly on |
| --- | --- |
| `effort_updates` | OpenAI GPT-5.6 on `openai` (Responses); GPT-5.6 and GPT-6 on GitHub Copilot once https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66648 makes the Open Responses route honor it |
| `system_updates` | MiniMax M3 and M3.1 Flash on MiniMax's Anthropic Messages API (4 providers) |

Everything else marked yes is already on through the routes' guesses: GPT-6 on OpenAI, Azure, Cloudflare AI Gateway and Vercel; Claude on Anthropic, Bedrock and Copilot.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `models.test.ts`: `effort_updates` and `system_updates` set to true on the API set both compatibility flags; false leaves them unset.
- `model-resolver.test.ts`: the compatibility flags reach the AI model as `reasoning.updates` and `systemUpdates`, and stay unset when the model has none.
- `bun run check` passes. Full `packages/ai` suite passes. Full `packages/core` suite passes except two shell-scan tests that fail the same way on `dev` locally.

Not a UI change.

prs.title: feat(core): keep MCP tools through dropped connections and reconnect on demand
prs.body:
### Problem

When an MCP server's connection drops, its tools disappear until someone reconnects it from /mcps. In Code Mode the model is then told the tools are "no longer available", and later that they are "new" again, with every signature listed. In 14 days of one local database, 391 of these removal notices showed up across 62 sessions, and most of the tools came back: remote servers after about 13 s, the desktop browser tools after about 3 min. Restarting opencode or moving a session to another directory causes the same churn, because every server starts from nothing.

### Change

Behind the `mcp_resilience` flag (on in local and dev builds), a server keeps its tools until the user disables, removes or reconfigures it, or the server itself drops them:

```text
connection drops        → disconnected, tools kept
next call needs it      → reconnect once (concurrent calls share it)
  ok                    → connected; same list = model told nothing
  fails                 → disconnected, calls fail at once for 1 s,
                          doubling to 30 s, then the next call retries
needs a sign-in         → needs_auth, tools kept, no retries until sign-in
user reconnects/sign-in → restart with the tools kept while it connects
user disables/removes   → tools removed now
```

- **New status `disconnected`** (`{ status: "disconnected", error }`) for a server that dropped or whose reconnect failed. The app, gui-plugins details, TUI, CLI and Rust TUI/CLI show it as a warning with its reason, and a click opens the same error view as `failed`, with retry and disable.
- **No background retries.** Only a request that needs the server reconnects it, so a server that's gone for good never respawns on its own.
- **Saved tools.** Each server's last listed tools and instructions are saved in the `kv` table under `mcp/tools/<sha256>`. The hash covers the connection identity (`McpPool.key`: transport, command or URL, fingerprints of env, headers and OAuth secret, protocol, timeouts, client info), the signed-in credential and the workspace, so secrets only reach it as fingerprints. At startup the saved tools and instructions are offered right away and the first step doesn't wait for that server. The live list replaces them once it connects. If it fails to start, the saved tools stay and the server shows `disconnected`.
- **Moving to another directory.** A local server's tools can depend on the directory it runs in, so its key includes that directory. A second key without it lets a directory the server hasn't run in yet start from the list another directory saw, until the server answers.
- **Cleanup.** Every connect saves again, so an entry's update time is when a server with that connection last connected. At startup, entries not updated in 30 days are deleted (removed servers, old configs, directories not opened in a month).

With the flag off, behavior is unchanged.

### Trade-offs

- A server that's permanently broken keeps its tools listed until it's disabled, and calls to it fail with its last error. Removing tools on every blip is what causes the churn above.
- A remote server that silently loses its network isn't detected: its calls fail while its tools stay listed, as today.
- Desktop-app tools (attached clients) still drop on disconnect; that path is separate and left for a follow-up.
- `Mcp.Status` gains a member. Old clients that decode the status strictly won't know `disconnected`; the Rust client keeps unknown members.
- Regenerating the Rust client types also picked up existing drift on `dev` (`experimental_browser_tunnel`, `experimental_space_set`).

### Tests

"MCP reconnect" in `packages/core/test/mcp.test.ts`, with an in-process stdio server behind a fake spawner and `TestClock`:

- a dropped server keeps its tools and shows `disconnected` with stderr; nothing respawns in the background; the next call reconnects, and two concurrent calls share one attempt
- a failing reconnect returns its error; within the backoff a call fails at once without spawning; the backoff doubles
- a reconnect that needs a sign-in goes to `needs_auth`, keeps its tools and isn't retried
- reconnecting from /mcps keeps the same tool objects while it restarts
- disconnecting clears the tools; with the flag off, behavior is unchanged
- saved tools and instructions are offered while a server starts, a config change uses a different key, no secret appears in a key or value, entries older than 30 days are deleted while recent and unrelated ones stay, a new directory starts from another directory's list, and a server that fails to start keeps its cached tools and reconnects on the next call

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

I exported a session with `/export` and the header of the page shows the cost without its dollar sign:

```
Cost: 0.300
```

It should be `$0.300`. `/share` and `pi --export` produce the same page.

`generateHtml` (`export-html/index.ts:164-176`) inserts the viewer script, the vendor scripts and the CSS with `String.prototype.replace` and a string as the replacement. In a replacement string `$$` becomes `$` and `$&` becomes the matched text. The viewer writes the cost as `$${totalCost.toFixed(3)}` (`template.js:1542`), so the `$` is lost. `highlight.min.js` contains both patterns too, so the exported copy is changed: the R operator regex `[-+*\/?!$&|:<=>@^~]` becomes `[-+*\/?!{{HIGHLIGHT_JS}}|:<=>@^~]`, and the Swift variable rule loses a `$`. The page still loads.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `pi -ne`, send a prompt, run `/export`.
2. Open the HTML file: the header shows `Cost: 0.300` instead of `$0.300`.

I reproduced it on main with `pi --export` on a session with one assistant reply that cost $0.30.

### Expected behavior

The header shows `Cost: $0.300`, and the exported page contains the viewer and vendor scripts unchanged. Fix: #12609.

### Version

1.6.1 (main at cb32f74f9)

issues.title: nativeToolChanges is unreachable on 1.6.1: getInitialSystemMessage requires messages[0] to be a system message

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
# `nativeToolChanges` is unreachable on 1.6.1: `getInitialSystemMessage` requires `messages[0]` to be a system message, but transcripts start with a user message

## Summary

Configuring `supportsMidConvoSystemMessages` + `supportsMidConvoToolChanges` on an Anthropic-compatible model does not enable the native `tool_addition` path. The guard requires `initialTools.length > 0`, but `initialTools` comes from `messages[0].toolsAdded`, and a normal 1.6.1 transcript starts with a `user` message. As a result, any mid-session tool change rewrites the top-level `tools` array and invalidates the entire prompt cache.

## Environment

- pi 1.6.1 (also reproduced on 1.6.1 only; not bisected yet)
- macOS 15 (arm64)
- Provider: custom Anthropic-compatible endpoint via a local gateway (`anthropic-messages`)
- Model: `claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]`
- No custom transport; stock pi + a probe extension

## Steps to reproduce

1. Save this probe as `probe-tools.ts`:

```ts
import { appendFileSync } from "node:fs";

export default function probe(pi: any) {
  let n = 0;
  pi.on("before_provider_request", (event: any) => {
    n += 1;
    const p = event?.payload;
    const tools = Array.isArray(p?.tools) ? p.tools.length : -1;
    const betas = Array.isArray(p?.betas) ? p.betas.join(",") : "(none)";
    const msg0 = p?.messages?.[0]?.role ?? "(none)";
    appendFileSync(
      "/tmp/probe-tools.log",
      `[probe #${n}] model=${p?.model} tools=${tools} msg0=${msg0} inlineBeta=${betas.includes("inline-tools")}\n`,
    );
    return undefined;
  });
}
```

2. Ensure the model has:

```jsonc
"compat": {
  "supportsMidConvoSystemMessages": true,
  "supportsMidConvoToolChanges": true
}
```

3. Run a fresh session and ask the model to load a tool group mid-conversation:

```bash
pi -p --no-session -e ./probe-tools.ts --model "<your anthropic-compatible model>" \
  "Call tool_search to load the playwright tools, then reply DONE"
```

4. Inspect `/tmp/probe-tools.log`.

## Observed

```
[probe #1] model=... tools=39 msg0=user inlineBeta=false
[probe #2] model=... tools=47 msg0=user inlineBeta=false
```

- `tools` grows from 39 to 47.
- `msg0` is `user`, not `system`.
- `betas` never contains `inline-tools-2026-09-15`.
- The next request re-bills the whole prompt: TUI shows `Cache miss: 43k tokens re-billed (~$0.17)`.

Same result in an interactive TUI session (not only `-p`), with the same probe.

## Expected

With both compat flags on, a mid-session tool addition should be sent as a `tool_addition` block in `messages`, keeping the top-level `tools` array stable (`[...initialTools, DEFERRED_TOOL_PLACEHOLDER]`), so the prompt prefix and cache stay intact.

## Root cause

`node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/api/anthropic-messages.js`:

```js
const initialTools = initialSystemMessage?.toolsAdded ?? [];
const nativeToolChanges =
  compat.supportsMidConvoSystemMessages &&
  compat.supportsMidConvoToolChanges &&
  initialTools.length > 0;
```

`initialSystemMessage` comes from `getInitialSystemMessage(messages)`:

```js
export function getInitialSystemMessage(messages) {
    const first = messages[0];
    return first && isSystemMessage(first) ? first : undefined;
}
```

A 1.6.1 transcript starts with a `user` message; the system prompt travels via `context.systemPrompt` and prompt-section patches are appended as mid-conversation system messages. Therefore `getInitialSystemMessage()` returns `undefined`, `initialTools` is always empty, and `nativeToolChanges` is always `false` — regardless of compat settings.

## Version history

- 0.86.0 (2026-09-19): "Added transcript-backed mid-conversation system prompt and tool changes … while preserving cached prefixes on supported models" (#9548). This is the feature that is now unreachable.
- 0.99.0 (2026-09-29): built-in `codemode` / `tool_search` / MCP support (#10040), which made mid-session tool changes common.
- 1.4.0 (2026-10-21): fixed the OpenAI Responses equivalent — "losing the prompt cache on every deferred tool load after a tool was removed" (#10940).
- No corresponding Anthropic fix is listed.

This looks like a regression introduced by the later transcript shape, not a bug that existed since the feature landed.

## Impact

- Every mid-session tool load (MCP `tool_search`, extension tool activation, deferred tools) rewrites the whole prompt prefix.
- Cost: proportional to context size. Observed 43k tokens (~$0.17) on a small session and 338k/345k (~$1.35) on a long one.
- Anthropic also drops historical thinking blocks as `prefix_binding_mismatch` on the same request.

## Suggested fix

Make `initialTools` independent of `messages[0]`:

1. Prefer a snapshot of the initial tool declarations carried by the request context (e.g. the same source `params.tools` would be built from), or
2. Read the first system message anywhere in the transcript that carries `toolsAdded`, or
3. Fall back to `context.tools` (the agent's declared tool set) on the first request.

Also worth covering: when `nativeToolChanges` is false but `compat.supportsMidConvoToolChanges` is true and `tools` changed, emit a diagnostic in `--debug` so users can tell "configured but inactive" from "not configured".

## Workaround

Until fixed:

- Load the tools before the long context grows (start of session), or
- Set the MCP exposure to eager/direct so the tool set is fixed at session start, or
- Accept one full cache rewrite at the load point; it is stable afterwards.

A local extension can also warn when tool count changes without `inline-tools` in `betas` (we added `NATIVE_TOOLCHANGES_INACTIVE` for exactly this).

issues.title: Extension-registered providers: fresh sessions intermittently ignore defaultProvider/defaultModel and start on another provider's default

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

A fresh pi session intermittently does **not** start with the configured
`defaultProvider`/`defaultModel` from settings.json when that provider is
registered by an extension via `pi.registerProvider(name, config)`. Instead, pi
silently falls back to another provider's default model
(`defaultModelPerProvider`) — in our case `google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview`,
which our Google credential (free tier, quota `limit: 0`) cannot serve, so the
first request fails with a 429.

Measured over repeated fresh launches: ~4 of 10 sessions start on the wrong
model; the rest start correctly on the configured default. Instrumenting
`findInitialModel` (step 3) shows the outcome correlates 1:1 with the
availability snapshot state at resolution time:

```text
step3 <default-provider>/<default-model> -> HIT auth=false  → session starts on the fallback
step3 <default-provider>/<default-model> -> HIT auth=true   → session starts on the configured default
```

Root cause: `createAgentSession` resolves the initial model
(`restoreModelFromSession` / `findInitialModel`) before name+config provider
registrations from extensions are applied to the model registry.

- `pi.registerProvider(name, config)` queues into
  `runtime.pendingProviderRegistrations` while extensions are loading
  (loader.js, "Pre-bind: queue registrations…"); the queue is flushed in
  `bindCore`, which runs when the `AgentSession` is constructed — after
  initial model resolution.
- `findInitialModel` step 3 (model-resolver.js) requires
  `getModel(provider, id)` **and** `hasConfiguredAuth(provider)`; the latter
  reads `snapshot.configuredProviders`, which is rebuilt asynchronously by
  `runAvailabilityRefresh` and can lag the registration.
- When step 3 misses, step 4 returns the first `defaultModelPerProvider`
  match from the available snapshot — silently, with no warning.

Note that `pi.registerNativeProvider(provider)` (object form) is flushed in
`createAgentSessionServices` _with_ an awaited
`modelRuntime.refresh({ allowNetwork: false })` before model resolution — the
name+config form has no equivalent before `findInitialModel`.

Possibly a residual of #6948 / #6922 (async provider model refresh vs startup
resolution, addressed for the built-in llama.cpp provider): model lists now
hydrate from the store at startup, but the configured/auth snapshot can still
lag, and the fallback is silent instead of an error. #2291 is an earlier
instance of the same ordering problem from a `session_start` hook.

Suggested direction: after extension loading completes, flush both pending
registration queues (`name+config` and native) and await
`modelRuntime.refresh({ allowNetwork: false })` before initial-model
resolution — mirroring what `createAgentSessionServices` already does after
extension load. Happy to send a PR if the direction looks right.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Register a provider from an extension using the name+config form:

```ts
export default function (pi) {
  pi.registerProvider("acme", {
    name: "acme",
    baseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:9/v1", // never called in this repro
    api: "openai-completions",
    models: [
      {
        id: "acme-model",
        name: "Acme Model",
        contextWindow: 128000,
        maxTokens: 8192,
      },
    ],
    auth: {
      apiKey: {
        name: "acme",
        check: async () => ({ type: "api_key" }),
        resolve: async () => ({ auth: { apiKey: "demo" }, source: "acme" }),
      },
    },
    fetchModels: async () => [],
  });
}
```

2. Add a stored credential for it in auth.json:

```json
"acme": { "type": "api_key", "key": "demo" }
```

3. settings.json:

```json
{ "defaultProvider": "acme", "defaultModel": "acme-model" }
```

4. Launch several fresh sessions back-to-back and inspect each session
   journal's first `model_change` entry:

```bash
for i in $(seq 1 10); do
  d=/tmp/repro-$i; mkdir -p "$d"; (cd "$d" && pi -p "hi" >/dev/null 2>&1)
done
# first model_change per journal: acme-model @ acme on good launches,
# gemini-3.1-pro-preview @ google on fallback launches
```

Measured: 4 of 10 fresh sessions started on the fallback provider; 10 of 10
with the refresh applied before resolution started on the configured default.

### Expected behavior

Every fresh session starts with `defaultProvider`/`defaultModel` from
settings.json — regardless of how long extension loading takes. If the
configured provider cannot be resolved yet, pi should say so explicitly
instead of silently starting on an unrelated provider's default model.

### Version

0.84.4

issues.title: Windows: a pi that dies mid-run leaves Kitty keyboard reporting on — even in regular mode — and the PowerShell prompt becomes unusable
issues.body:
# Windows: a pi that dies mid-run leaves Kitty keyboard reporting on — even in `regular` mode — and the PowerShell prompt becomes unusable

Follow-up to #12133 (closed, but reproducible on **1.6.0**; I added a detailed comment there as well). This report is the case where **no alternate screen and no mouse tracking are involved at all**, which I think matters for the scope of the fix: the Kitty keyboard / modifyOtherKeys / bracketed-paste set is enabled in `regular` mode too, so `regular` is not a workaround.

Drafted with AI assistance (a pi agent, per CONTRIBUTING.md); every measurement below was taken on my machine.

## Environment

- pi **1.6.0** (npm global install, `%APPDATA%\npm\node_modules\@earendil-works\pi-coding-agent`), Node **v24.15.0**
- Windows 11 **10.0.26300**, Windows Terminal **1.25.3131.0**, Windows PowerShell **5.1**
- `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`: `"tuiMode": "regular"` (i.e. `TuiMainScreen`, no alt screen, no mouse tracking)
- Project dir `E:\Translate`; the session that died is 13.8 MB

## What happens

pi was killed/died in the middle of a run (frozen `── ⠧ Working ──` frame), and the tab was left in a state where **every real keypress at the PowerShell prompt is turned into a Kitty keyboard report that gets stuffed into the command line as literal text**. The user cannot see or edit what they type: the input line ends up hundreds of characters long, so the pane looks dead ("I can't type"). Typing does reach the shell — I injected `xy` into the console and it landed at the end of the junk line.

Screen content of the stuck pane (read from the console buffer with `AttachConsole` + `ReadConsoleOutputCharacterW`):

```
── ⠧ Working ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PS E:\Translate> /[uuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuu…
uuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuu…
uuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuu^C
PS E:\Translate>
```

## Measurements

**It is the keyboard-protocol leak, not mouse.** With the pane in that state:

- Sweeping the pointer over the pane appends **nothing** (`ESC[?1000/?1002/?1003/?1004/?1006` are off — expected in `regular` mode), and
- Writing `ESC[?1049l` does **not** swap to another screen (no alt screen was left behind this time; contrast with the alt-screen case in #12133),
- but **one real keystroke** (`a`, sent with `SendInput`/`SendKeys` to the focused pane) appends `[;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;129:3ua[uuuuuuuu…` to the line.

So the terminal still has the Kitty keyboard mode that pi pushes in `ProcessTerminal.queryAndEnableKittyProtocol()` (`\x1B[>7u\x1B[?u`, i.e. flags 7 — disambiguate + report event types + report alternate keys), plus `\x1B[>4;2m` (modifyOtherKeys) and `\x1B[?2004h` (bracketed paste). None of them were turned off, because the process never ran a teardown at all:

- the session jsonl's last entry is a normal tool-call record, nothing after it;
- `~/.pi/agent/crashes.json` has no entry for that time;
- the Windows *Application* log has no `node.exe` WER record for the last two days;
- the console input mode left behind is `0x0200` (`ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT` only, no `ECHO_INPUT`/`LINE_INPUT`/`QUICK_EDIT`), while a healthy pi pane measures `0x0208`.

## Recovery that worked (verified twice, without closing the tab)

`?1049l` is only needed when the alt screen was left behind; the rest is needed in both cases. Because you cannot type in the pane, write it from another console:

```powershell
$e = [char]27
$seq = "$e[?1049l$e[?1006l$e[?1004l$e[?1003l$e[?1002l$e[?1000l$e[?2004l$e[<u$e[>4;0m$e[?25h"
Add-Type -Name C -Namespace W -MemberDefinition @'
[DllImport("kernel32.dll")] public static extern bool FreeConsole();
[DllImport("kernel32.dll")] public static extern bool AttachConsole(uint p);
[DllImport("kernel32.dll", CharSet=CharSet.Unicode)] public static extern IntPtr CreateFileW(string n, uint a, uint s, IntPtr x, uint d, uint f, IntPtr t);
[DllImport("kernel32.dll", CharSet=CharSet.Unicode)] public static extern bool WriteConsoleW(IntPtr h, string s, uint l, out uint w, IntPtr r);
'@
[W.C]::FreeConsole(); [W.C]::Attach([uint32]12345) | Out-Null    # 12345 = any process in the stuck pane
$h = [W.C]::CreateFileW("CONOUT$", 0x40000000, 3, [IntPtr]::Zero, 3, 0, [IntPtr]::Zero)
$w = 0; [W.C]::WriteConsoleW($h, $seq, [uint32]$seq.Length, [ref]$w, [IntPtr]::Zero)
```

Then press **Ctrl+C** in the pane to clear the polluted line. Verification after the reset: the same real `a` keystroke produced a plain `a` in the command line, and the prompt was usable again.

## Why it looks intermittent

On this machine the junk only materialises when the console is owned by a VT-raw reader (`0x0200`); with a cooked console (`ECHO_INPUT|QUICK_EDIT|…`) at a plain prompt, ConHost swallows the reports and nothing appears even with all the modes on — I could not produce a single stray character in that configuration. So "sometimes it happens" ≈ "sometimes the pane ends up with a VT-raw reader at the prompt after the unclean exit".

## Requests / suggestions

1. **Scope of the teardown fix**: the Kitty/modifyOtherKeys/`?2004` resets matter in `regular` mode as much as in fullscreen, so switching to `regular` is not a workaround for this class. Same for any picker or transient alt-screen TUI.
2. **A startup breadcrumb would fix this automatically**: if pi wrote a small marker when it starts and removed it on clean shutdown, then a start could detect "the previous run died uncleanly" and unconditionally write the full terminal-restore sequence *before* enabling anything. A previous hard death (OOM/`taskkill`/window close) can never be caught by `process.on('exit')`, so this is the only path I can see that self-heals the pane on the next launch.
3. **Document the recovery**, including the "attach and write" trick above — it is the only way out when the input line is full of junk and you cannot type. A small documented `pi-reset-terminal.ps1` / shell one-liner would be enough.
4. (Also reported in #12133) `tuiMode` accepts unknown values silently: this project's settings had `"tuiMode": "inline"` and `getTuiMode()` maps everything except `"regular"` to the default `"fullscreen"`, so the attempted workaround silently did nothing. A startup warning would have made this diagnosable immediately.

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Give `@earendil-works/pi-mcp` consumers public hooks for request capabilities and extension-defined results. The concrete case is the [draft MCP Files extension](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/experimental-ext-file-uploads/blob/8a859b8f268926fe4beb84d78565e7cc6f9fa617/specification/draft/file-uploads.md), building on #10416 and #12479.

### Why?

Piclaw uses `pi-mcp` behind Code Mode. We want the host to move files without handing bytes or signed URLs to the model. #12479 adds modern MCP and handles `input_required`; its result decoder still rejects `upload_required`.

### How? (optional)

Let hosts supply extension capabilities on `tools/list` and `tools/call`, inspect completed result `_meta`, and explicitly continue with unchanged arguments, capabilities, and opaque `requestState` after a host-managed upload. Leave approval, HTTP transfers, and storage to the host. Don’t replay a continuation automatically after an uncertain outcome.

We can offer [Memento’s staged asset upload](https://github.com/rcarmo/memento/blob/5db820a93a5023acab7319e4ea9a63bc6720f9b0/examples/upload-with-stage-ticket.sh) as a server-side implementation example for interoperability testing. It already issues a ticket before a separate HTTP upload; it doesn’t implement the draft today.

issues.title: codemode: parse errors report only `codemode.js:line:col`, so models retry blind on shell-heavy scripts
issues.body:
## What happened?

When a codemode script fails to parse, the result is only QuickJS's message and a position, for example `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ')' at codemode.js:16:28`. It contains no source excerpt. The model then has to find column 28 of line 16 in a script it wrote as one JSON string, and it often guesses wrong. Several sessions hit the same error 2-5 times in a row.

The failures concentrate in scripts that embed shell code (bash, python heredocs, markdown with backticks) inside JS. Their text crosses several quoting layers (JSON argument, JS string or template literal, shell). Template literals and `String.raw` interpolate `${...}` and `$(...)` from the shell code, and an inner backtick ends the template.

In `@earendil-works/pi-codemode` 1.6.0, `dist/runtime/vm.js:274` evaluates `(async (tools, console) => {${data.code}\n})` as `codemode.js`. The prefix shares line 1 with the script, so line numbers already match the user's code (column is offset by the prefix on line 1 only). `describeException` (`vm.js:112`) returns just `name`, `message` and the QuickJS `stack`.

## Evidence

From 355 local Pi sessions (2026-11-22 to 2026-11-25; Claude Sonnet/Opus and DeepSeek), about 180 codemode calls failed with `SyntaxError` or `ReferenceError` before any tool ran ("No tool calls were made"). Examples:

- `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ')' at codemode.js:16:28`
- `SyntaxError: unexpected end of string at codemode.js:65:404`
- `SyntaxError: expected '}' after template expression`
- `SyntaxError: Unexpected string template`, from `tools.bash({command` followed by a template containing a nested backtick
- `ReferenceError: PCT is not defined`, from shell `${PCT}` inside a JS template literal
- `ReferenceError: sh is not defined`, from a helper defined in an earlier call (each call is a fresh scope)

## Why it matters

Each failed call costs a full script rewrite (see also #12394) and a turn. Without a visible excerpt the next attempt often repeats the same mistake.

## Proposal

1. On a parse error, append the offending line of the user's script with a caret under the column, plus one line of context before it. Line 1 needs the prefix length subtracted from the column.
2. Optionally, when that line contains a template literal with `${` or `$(`, add a one-line hint: `template literals interpolate ${...}; use a plain string or escape the $`.

Nothing else: no new tools and no change to the execution model.

## Steps to reproduce

Call codemode with a script such as `await tools.bash({command: \`echo \${PCT} \`date\`\`})` (inner backtick) and read the error: it gives a position and no source line.

## Expected behavior

The error shows the offending source line and a caret.

## Version

@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 1.6.0 (pi-codemode 1.6.0)

## Related

- #11226 (top-level `tools` declaration is a SyntaxError)
- PR #11878 (open), #11920 (closed)
- #12150 (malformed codemode call poisons session)
- #12394 (patch and rerun a syntax-failed script; closed, no-action)

issues.title: AgentSession.dispose() / ExtensionRunner.invalidate() retains bound session closures, preventing GC of disposed sessions

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What happened?

In a long-running process hosting multiple sessions via the SDK, disposed `AgentSession` and `SessionManager` instances remain retained in the V8 heap until the process hits OOM. `invalidate()` marks the context stale without breaking strong references back to the disposed session:

1. `packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/runner.ts:898-899`: unlike the other getters that read through `runner.*` dynamically, `createContext()` captures `this.getModel` and `this.getScopedModels` in local constants for the `model` (L927) and `scopedModels` (L931) getters. Even if `runner` properties are cleared during `invalidate()`, any externally retained `ExtensionContext` still holds strong references to `AgentSession` and `SessionManager` through those two closures. This also contradicts the L894 comment (`"Context values are resolved at call time, so changes via bindCore/bindUI are reflected."`).
2. `packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/runner.ts:734-741` and `packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/loader.ts:200-207`: `ExtensionRunner.invalidate()` and `createExtensionRuntime().invalidate()` only set `staleMessage` and clear eventBus subscriptions. Bound session callbacks (`runtime.sendMessage`, `getCommands`, `createContext`, `runner.getModel`, `getScopedModels`, `isIdleFn`, etc.) and internal references (`extensions` handlers, `sessionManager`, `modelRegistry`, `mcpServers` change listener) remain attached. If any extension retains a reference to `pi`, `runtime`, or `ctx` at module scope, the entire disposed session graph stays reachable.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start Node with `--expose-gc` and register a minimal extension that stores `ctx` (or `pi`) in a module-level variable inside `session_start`.
2. Create an `AgentSession` via the SDK and track both the `AgentSession` and `SessionManager` with `WeakRef`.
3. Call `session.dispose()` (which triggers `extensionRunner.invalidate()`), drop external references, and run `global.gc()` multiple times.
4. Check `WeakRef.deref()`: both references still resolve to live objects instead of `undefined`.

### Expected behavior

1. Resolve `model` and `scopedModels` in `createContext()` through `runner.getModel()` and `runner.getScopedModels()` at call time instead of capturing them in local constants.
2. On `runtime.invalidate()` and `ExtensionRunner.invalidate()`, replace bound session callbacks with functions that throw the same `staleMessage` (or no-ops where appropriate), and clear `extensions` handler/tool maps, `sessionManager`, `modelRegistry`, and the `mcpServers` change listener so invalidated objects no longer keep disposed sessions alive.

### Version

@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 1.6.0 (verified still present on main)

issues.title: Make truncated tool output resumable, including inside a long line

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Give built-in tools a consistent way to say what was omitted and how to retrieve it. The first case is `read` on a UTF-8 line longer than 50 KiB. The tool reports the line size, returns none of its text, and suggests a shell command that prints the first 51,200 bytes. `offset` takes a line number, so a second `read` has no way to resume inside that line.

### Why?

Run this in a scratch directory, then call `read` with `{"path":"long.json","offset":1,"limit":1}` in `pi -ne`.

```sh
node -e 'process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({value:"a".repeat(100000)}))' > long.json
```

The 100,012-byte file has one line. Reading at `offset: 1` gives only the size notice, and `offset: 2` is past EOF. The behavior is visible in the [Pi 1.6.1 `read` source](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/db79712854e5154f48f10564c3f235abadfcefdc/packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/read.ts).

### How? (optional)

- Keep `offset`/`limit` for line paging. When a byte cap cuts a line, return a UTF-8-safe chunk and a separate, exact next byte offset. Repeated reads of an unchanged file should cover it without gaps or duplicate bytes.
- Include shown and omitted counts or ranges in the notice and `details` where available. `bash` can point to the omitted prefix in its spill file. `grep`, `find`, and `ls` can distinguish count limits from byte limits and report totals only when known.
- In `codemode`, include the omitted byte range in the spill file and apply a host-side UTF-8 byte ceiling to visible text. `max_output_tokens` currently uses four UTF-16 code units per token and lets the script raise the display budget. Keep the existing programmatic result schemas.

Related: #134 established the current notices, and #11699 covers what nested tools return to scripts.

_(AI-assisted draft: reproduced locally on Pi 1.6.1 and verified by me before submitting.)_

`packages/tui/src/components/editor.ts` (published as `dist/components/editor.js`): `runAutocompleteRequest` awaits `this.autocompleteProvider.getSuggestions(...)` with no `try`/`catch`; `startAutocompleteRequest` assigns `this.autocompleteRequestTask` an async IIFE whose first statement is `await previousTask`; `cancelAutocompleteRequest` never resets `autocompleteRequestTask`. issues.title: sudo pi update leaves a root-owned release and current-version, so pi no longer launches for the user

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
## Summary

Running `sudo pi update` on a managed install leaves the new release owned by root with mode 700 inside the user's home directory, and rewrites `current-version` as root. The user's own account can no longer launch Pi.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have a working managed install at `~/.pi/agent/install/releases/1.6.0` (macOS, installed as a normal user).
2. Run `sudo pi update`. Output: `Updated pi from 1.6.0 to 1.6.1`.
3. Run `pi` as the normal user.

## Actual result

```
Managed Pi executable is missing: ~/.local/bin/../../.pi/agent/install/releases/1.6.1/node_modules/.bin/pi
```

`releases/1.6.1` is `drwx------ root staff`, so the user cannot read `node_modules/.bin/pi`. `install/current-version` is `-rw-r--r-- root staff` and contains `1.6.1`. The older release still works, but Pi now points at the unreadable one.

## Expected result

Either `pi update` refuses to run as root with a clear message, or it creates the release and `current-version` owned by the invoking user (for example from `SUDO_USER`).

## Second effect: root-owned npm cache

The root run also writes about 300 root-owned files into the user's `~/.npm` cache (`_cacache`, `_logs`), because npm runs as root with the user's `HOME`. A later normal `pi update` then fails in `npm ci` with `EACCES` and "Your cache folder contains root-owned files".

## Workaround (verified)

1. Replace `current-version` with the previous version (the install directory is user-owned, so the user can delete and recreate the file).
2. `sudo rm -rf` the root-owned release folder.
3. `sudo chown -R <uid>:<gid> ~/.npm`.
4. Run `pi update` without `sudo`. It then reports `Updated pi from 1.6.0 to 1.6.1` and `pi` launches.

Refusing to run `pi update` as root, or dropping to `SUDO_USER` before writing anything, would avoid both effects.

## Environment

Pi 1.6.0 to 1.6.1, macOS.

| `fullscreenScrollbar` | `"always"` |
| `fullscreenWheelScrollLines` | `"auto"` |

## Actual

In fullscreen mode with a long session, scrolling the transcript with the mouse wheel moves the
transcript correctly, but the scrollbar thumb on the right edge stays where it was. The thumb
does not advance at all while wheeling, even across dozens of wheel events.

Dragging the scrollbar (and clicking the track) works and keeps the thumb in sync.

## Expected

The thumb should track the scroll position while wheeling, the way it does when the transcript is
scrolled by other means (e.g. dragging).

## Steps

1. Start pi with the settings above, in a session with a transcript longer than the viewport.
2. Wheel-scroll up/down through the transcript.
3. Watch the right-hand scrollbar: the content moves, the thumb does not.

## Analysis

Fullscreen scrolling paths share one render mode. `TuiAltScreen.scrollBy()` (used by the
transcript scroll keybindings) and `TuiAltScreen.routeWheel()` both request a *view-only* frame:

```js
// pi-tui/dist/tui-alt-screen.js:301
scrollBy(lines) {
    this.getPrimaryScrollView().scrollBy(lines);
    this.requestViewRender();
}
```

```js
// pi-tui/dist/tui-alt-screen.js:825  (routeWheel)
this.requestViewRender();
```

A view-only frame leaves `contentChanged` false, so the previous frame's component output is
reused (`tui-alt-screen.js:1463`, `renderLayoutFrame(..., reusableOutput)`). This is the
optimization from #11968 that fixed #9549.

The scrollbar is painted during the layout pass, not during component render:

```js
// pi-tui/dist/layout.js:278 (inside paintBox)
paintScrollbar(box, screen, totalWidth);
```

and `paintScrollbar()` reads the live scroll position each time it runs:

```js
// pi-tui/dist/layout.js:195
const thumbOffset = maxScrollTop === 0 ? 0 : Math.round((box.scrollView.scrollTop / maxScrollTop) * maxThumbTop);
```

`paintBox`/`paintScrollbar` do run on view-only frames, so in principle the thumb should be
repainted from the live `scrollTop`.

### Hypothesis 1: thumb position quantizes to nothing at wheel granularity

`thumbOffset` is a rounded integer cell index:

```js
// pi-tui/dist/layout.js:188-195
const minThumbHeight = Math.min(2, trackHeight);
const thumbHeight = Math.max(minThumbHeight, Math.min(trackHeight, Math.round((trackHeight * trackHeight) / contentHeight)));
const maxScrollTop = Math.max(0, contentHeight - trackHeight);
const maxThumbTop = trackHeight - thumbHeight;
const thumbOffset = Math.round((scrollTop / maxScrollTop) * maxThumbTop);
```

With a 40-row track and, say, 8000 lines of transcript: `maxScrollTop = 7960`, `thumbHeight = 2`,
`maxThumbTop = 38`. One thumb cell therefore corresponds to about 209 lines of content. With
`fullscreenWheelScrollLines: "auto"` a wheel event moves a few lines, so the rounded
`thumbOffset` stays constant for a very long stretch of scrolling. The bar looks frozen even
though `scrollTop` is changing.

If this is the cause, it is not a repaint bug: the thumb geometry is simply too coarse for
wheel-sized deltas.

### What I could not determine

I could not measure whether `scrollTop` actually changes during a wheel event in the real TUI,
or whether `thumbOffset` recomputes but is not composited. A small extension that sampled
`getPrimaryScrollView().scrollTop` before/after `routeWheel()` and recomputed
`getScrollbarGeometry()` after an idle repaint was unreliable and I removed it.

An attempt to force a repaint by calling `doRender()` (which reuses
`currentLayout.renderCache` and leaves `contentChanged` false) after 140 ms of wheel idleness did
not make the thumb move, while it did not disturb the scroll position either. That is consistent
with hypothesis 1, but not proof.

## Possible fixes

1. If it is quantization: map the scroll position to the thumb without rounding away small
   deltas, for example keep the unrounded thumb offset and render a half-cell indicator, or scale
   by `maxScrollTop / maxThumbTop` using an accumulated remainder so every
   `ceil(maxScrollTop / maxThumbTop)` lines moves the thumb by one cell. A cheaper variant is to
   make the minimum thumb height larger for very long transcripts so the mapping is finer.
2. If it is compositing: repaint the scrollbar explicitly on view-only frames, or mark the
   scrollbar column dirty when `scrollTop` changed since the last frame.

Happy to test either change on this setup.


### Steps to reproduce

## Steps

1. Start pi with the settings above, in a session with a transcript longer than the viewport.
2. Wheel-scroll up/down through the transcript.
3. Watch the right-hand scrollbar: the content moves, the thumb does not.

### Expected behavior

The thumb should track the scroll position while wheeling, the way it does when the transcript is
scrolled by other means (e.g. dragging).

### Version

1.6.0

issues.title: TUI content reflow / terminal 'shaking' during large streaming tool results (write)

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### Summary

During a large streaming tool result (e.g. `write` of a multi-line file), the TUI "shakes"/jitters: the content above the tool-call block visibly jumps up as the call's preview block grows, which reads as the terminal window vibrating. This happens with the default/stock setup and is **not** related to any plugin (verified: the `write` tool renderer is unaffected by plugin overrides).

### Reproduction

1. In an interactive session, run a `write` tool that streams a large file (e.g. > 10 lines, ideally several hundred).
2. Observe the bottom of the screen while the call is `Working...`: the write call block appears and grows line-by-line, pushing the content above it upward.
3. The repeated upward shifts (one per streamed line, until the preview caps) are perceived as terminal "shaking".

A screen recording at 30fps shows the write call block growing during streaming and a ~1-line (-26px) vertical displacement of the content above, plus a constant repaint of the block region while `Working...` is active.

### Root cause

`packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/renderers/write.ts` — `formatWriteCall`:

- The call preview is capped at `maxLines = options.expanded ? lines.length : 10` (hardcoded 10).
- As content streams in, `lines` grows and the preview renders `lines.slice(0, maxLines)` — so the block **grows from 1 to 10 rows**, one row per streamed line.
- The status row `... (N more lines, M total, ctrl+o to expand)` is appended only when `remaining > 0` — so a row is **added** when content crosses 10 lines.

Because the tool-call block sits at the bottom of the TUI, every height change reflows the content above it (the view autoscrolls up to keep the newest content visible). Repeated height changes during streaming = repeated shifts = perceived shaking.

The TUI re-renders the call on every content delta (`ToolExecutionComponent.updateDisplay`), so the block repaints frequently even when only the status count changes.

### Suggested fix

Keep the **streaming preview block height stable** so it does not grow/shrink while content streams:

- While `isPartial && !expanded`, render the preview at a fixed height of `maxLines` rows (pad short content with empty rows) and always reserve the status row. This keeps the block a constant height during streaming, so the content above no longer reflows.
- On completion, render the actual line count (unchanged behavior for completed calls).

This is exactly the change I have applied locally as a stopgap (patching the installed dist). It eliminates the growth-induced reflow; the only remaining transition is the block appearing (a single shift) and the `Working...` spinner repaint.

A more general fix would also cover other tools whose call/result previews grow during streaming, and/or coalesce `updateDisplay` calls during streaming to reduce repaint frequency.

### Environment

- pi-coding-agent 1.6.0
- Windows 11, Windows Terminal (WT_SESSION), fullscreen TUI
- No plugin involved in the reproduced case (stock `write` renderer)

issues.title: Extension factory cache is keyed by cwd, so every new project re-imports all global extensions

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What happened?

The extension factory cache in `packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/loader.ts` is one slot keyed by cwd, and `useExtensionCacheCwd()` clears it whenever the cwd differs from the last one. A factory depends only on the file it was imported from, and the global extensions under `~/.pi/agent/extensions` are the same files for every project, so a host that serves several projects from one process (pi-web) re-imports every global extension through jiti on the first request of each new project.

That is not a small re-import here. On this machine one `lstat` costs ~0.7 ms (a filesystem filter driver), so each jiti resolution — 4 base URLs × 10 extensions × 2 forms — costs ~80 stat calls. Loading 11 extensions means 1153 resolutions, i.e. tens of thousands of syscalls, and they run inline on a read-only request.

`GET /api/models` for a project the process has not served yet:

| | time |
|---|---|
| first cwd | 1.6 s |
| second cwd | **14.5 s** |
| third cwd | **38.9 s** |

This is not an extension's fault, so `pi -ne` will not show it: the cost is the loader's per-cwd re-import, and it scales with the extension set rather than with any one extension.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install a few extensions globally (any that live in `~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules`, i.e. cwd-independent).
2. In one process, load extensions for cwd A, then for cwd B (`loadExtensionsCached` via `ResourceLoader.reload()`, or `GET /api/models` from pi-web).
3. Time the second cwd. On a fast-metadata host it is smaller in absolute terms but the same shape: the whole module graph is resolved again.

### Expected behavior

The second project costs about what the first one did, because the extension files are identical. Only a project-local `.pi/extensions` should ever need its own import.

### Version

1.6.0 (checked on `main` at 941d420: the single-slot cache is still there)

### Fix I have ready

Key the cache by the extension's resolved absolute path instead of by cwd. `clearExtensionCache()` keeps working as the invalidation for a reload. Same sequence after the change: 2.9 s and 3.9 s instead of 14.5 s and 38.9 s, and 43–57 ms once any project has warmed the process.

Branch: `flying-dragon-ai/pi` → `perf/extension-cache-and-fs-metadata`, one commit, also hoists the jiti instance (so its resolver cache survives), memoizes `canonicalizePath`, TTL-caches `getFileRevision`, and does one `readdirSync` in the skill walk. `tsc --noEmit` and the `paths / auth-storage / package-manager / skills / extensions-discovery / resource-loader` suites are identical to baseline.

I have not opened a PR: CONTRIBUTING asks for `lgtm` first. Happy to open it as soon as that lands.

issues.title: A throwing tool progress subscriber can settle a run while tools are still running

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What happened?

A synchronous throw from a `session.subscribe()` callback handling `tool_execution_update` can make `await session.prompt()` return with `session.isIdle === true` and `agent_settled` already emitted. A tool from that run is still running, its signal has not been aborted, and neither tool result is in the session history.

If a second run starts before the old tool finishes, an `Agent.subscribe()` listener can receive the old tool's `tool_execution_end` with the second run's `AbortSignal`. If the tool that emits progress stays running after the callback throws, Node can instead exit with code 1 due to an unhandled rejection.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use the SDK with a faux model response that calls two tools in parallel. `fast` calls `onUpdate()` once and returns. `slow` waits on a Promise controlled by the test.
2. Register a `session.subscribe()` callback that throws synchronously on `tool_execution_update`. Call `await session.prompt()` without releasing `slow`.
3. Check `session.isIdle`, the `agent_settled` event, and the persisted tool results. To check signal ownership, start another run, then release `slow` and inspect its end event through `session.agent.subscribe()`.

The SDK reproduction was also verified with `noExtensions: true` (the setting used by `pi -ne`) and zero loaded extensions.

### Expected behavior

A run should settle only after all tools it started have settled and their results have been recorded. Tool events should retain their originating run's signal. A subscriber failure should not cause an unhandled rejection.

### Version

Reproduced on `a8ecc194` with Windows and Node.js `24.14.0`. The relevant Agent and Session code is identical to `c11a73bf`.

issues.title: Bash command logging can self-match its own output file and exhaust TMPDIR

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
## Summary
Pi command logging can recursively capture its own active `/tmp/pi-bash-*.log` output when a command searches the same glob. The log grew to 24.4 GiB on a 32 GiB tmpfs and crashed Pi with ENOSPC.

## Location
The exact upstream logger source location is not identified from the published package metadata; the affected behavior is the Pi bash-command capture path in `@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent`.

## Reproduction
1. Configure or run a Pi command whose stdout/stderr is captured to a `/tmp/pi-bash-*.log` file.
2. From that command or a nested helper, search or process the same `/tmp/pi-bash-*.log` glob.
3. Observe that the active output file matches the search and receives the command’s growing output recursively.
4. Repeat until the temporary filesystem is exhausted.

## Result
Observed warning:
```text
Warning: pi crashed on 11/24/2026, 8:06:50 PM (ENOSPC: no space left on device, write).
```
The proven orphaned log reached 24.4 GiB while `/tmp` was a 32 GiB tmpfs at 96%. Root filesystem capacity and inode availability were healthy.

## Cause
```text
pi-bash command output -> active /tmp/pi-bash-*.log
       ^                                  |
       |                                  v
       +---- recursive glob/search -------+
```
The active output file is not excluded from searches that match the logger’s own filename pattern, and output is not bounded before the filesystem fills.

## Impact
Pi can terminate with ENOSPC and lose the active session/workflow. No user data loss was confirmed, but the running session and its temporary evidence become unreliable. This is a resource-exhaustion and availability defect.

## Suggested fix
- Keep active command logs outside any user-searchable glob, or use a unique non-matching active filename.
- Exclude the active output path from recursive searches and child command environments.
- Add bounded output/rotation and a fail-closed disk-headroom check before appending.
- Add a regression test proving a command cannot capture or recursively grow its own output file.

## Environment
- Pi `1.6.0`
- Node `v22.23.4`
- Linux host with `/tmp` on a 32 GiB tmpfs
- Package: `@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent`
- Repository: `badlogic/pi-mono`
- Incident date: 2026-11-24
- Local recovery moved `TMPDIR` to a mode-700 path and added a repository-side 10% headroom guard; the upstream logger defect remains.

**Priority:** P0 availability / temporary-filesystem exhaustion

prs.title: feat(interactive): auto-reload resources on file change (no manual /reload)
prs.body:
## What

Adds an opt-out file watcher so edits to local resources are picked up automatically, without running `/reload`.

Watches the agent + project resource directories:
`~/.pi/agent/{extensions,skills,prompts,themes}` and `<cwd>/.pi/{extensions,skills,prompts,themes}`.

## Why

Iterating on extensions, skills, prompt templates or themes currently requires a manual `/reload` after every edit. This makes that automatic while staying unobtrusive.

## How

- **settings**: new boolean `autoReload` (default `true`) — defaults, TypeBox schema, getter/setter, and a toggle in `/settings` ("Auto reload").
- **ResourceLoader.getWatchDirs()**: exposes the directories worth watching (only existing ones).
- **interactive-mode**:
  - `fs.watch(dir, { recursive: true })` over each watch dir, started after `init()` and re-armed after every reload (picks up new dirs / toggled setting).
  - **1.2s debounce** coalesces bursts of writes (editors often save several files).
  - **Idle guard**: if a turn is streaming/compacting, the reload is deferred and retried until idle — never interrupts a response.
  - `handleReloadCommand({ auto })` runs quietly (no modal box, brief status line) for watcher-triggered reloads.
  - Watcher torn down on shutdown.
  - Ignores transient editor artifacts (`*~`, `*.swp`, `*.tmp`, `.DS_Store`).

## Notes / scope

- Covers the same resources as `/reload` for extensions/skills/prompts/themes/keybindings. Does **not** hot-reload `mcp.json` (already-spawned MCP servers don't reload live by design) or `settings.json`.
- Recursive `fs.watch` is native on Windows/macOS; on platforms without recursive support it degrades gracefully to no watch (per-dir try/catch), leaving manual `/reload` working.
- Can be disabled via `/settings` → Auto reload → false, or `"autoReload": false` in settings.

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.build.json`: clean.
- `npm run build`: clean bundle.
- Verified recursive `fs.watch` fires on Windows against the real prompts dir.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): keep $ in exported HTML
prs.body:
Closes #12608.

**Problem.** `generateHtml` inserts the viewer script, the vendor scripts and the CSS with `String.prototype.replace` and a string as the replacement, which expands `$$` to `$` and `$&` to the matched text. The viewer writes the cost as `$${totalCost.toFixed(3)}`, so the exported header showed `Cost: 0.300`. `highlight.min.js` contains both patterns as well: the exported copy had `{{HIGHLIGHT_JS}}` in the R operator regex in place of `$&`, and the Swift variable rule lost a `$`.

**Fix.** Every value is passed through a function (`.replace("{{JS}}", () => templateJs)`), which inserts it as is. Applied to all ten replacements, the CSS ones included, so a value with a `$` in it can no longer change.

The chained replacements could also replace a placeholder that an earlier inserted file contains. No inserted file contains one today, so this PR does not change that; a single `replace(/\{\{(\w+)\}\}/g, ...)` pass would rule it out if wanted.

**Validation** on main `cb32f74f9`:

- New `test/export-html-embedded-scripts.test.ts` exports a session with `exportFromFile` and checks that the header keeps `$${totalCost.toFixed(3)}` and that `template.js` and the three vendor scripts are embedded unchanged. Three of its five tests (the cost, `template.js`, `highlight.min.js`) fail without the fix.
- Manual: `pi --export` on a session with one $0.30 reply. Before: `Cost: 0.300`, and one `{{HIGHLIGHT_JS}}` left in the page. After: `Cost: $0.300`, none left.
- The existing export tests pass. `npm run check` passes.

prs.title: Let hosts choose where Pi Durable starts runnable tasks
prs.body:
A host that returns a submission receipt can finish its request before Pi starts the next model or tool call. Add optional `HarnessOptions.schedule(run)` so the host can start that work in an invocation it keeps open.

Calling the same `run()` twice returns the same promise. It resolves after Pi reserves and launches available tasks, so the host can inspect `wake()` while those tasks run. Cloudflare Agents uses this boundary to launch the pass inside an awaited same-object RPC. Omitting the hook preserves microtask scheduling. Tests cover execution context, delayed reservation, duplicate delivery, and retrying a retained callback after an asynchronous dispatch failure.

[Interactive walkthrough and trace evidence](https://tracing-pi-on-workers.andreisavu.chatgpt.site/#handoff) · [Companion Agents PR](https://github.com/andreisavu/agents/pull/1)

prs.title: fix(ai): replay GitHub Copilot reasoning_opaque in openai-completions
prs.body:
Fixes #12418.

Problem: on `openai-completions`, Copilot streams `reasoning_text` deltas followed by a single `reasoning_opaque` delta (observed live with `claude-opus-5.5` on `/chat/completions`). Pi kept the text but dropped the opaque value, so later requests replayed `reasoning_text` without it.

Fix, following the existing `reasoning_details` handling:

- While streaming, keep the latest `reasoning_opaque` in memory and, when the thinking block ends, store it with the reasoning field in `thinkingSignature`: `{"field":"reasoning_text","reasoning_opaque":"..."}`.
- On replay, send `reasoning_opaque` next to the reasoning text in its original field. When it arrived without text, send it alone, without `reasoning_text`.
- With interleaved reasoning, the text is concatenated and the latest opaque value is replayed (as the Copilot VS Code client does).
- Thinking from another model is already dropped by `transformMessages`, so the opaque value is never sent to a different model.

Tests: `packages/ai/test/openai-completions-reasoning-opaque.test.ts` (text + opaque, interleaved, opaque without text, other model). Verified live with a two-turn tool call against Copilot `/chat/completions` (`claude-opus-5.5`): the replay carried `reasoning_text` and `reasoning_opaque` and the request succeeded. Gemini was not available on the test account, so the reported missing-`finish_reason` failure was not reproduced directly.

prs.title: feat(coding-agent): repeat restriction and resource flags in the OSC 7577 resume command
prs.body:
Follow-up to #12557 and #12595 (OSC 7577 program resume).

## Problem

pi reports `pi [--agent-dir A] [--session-dir S] --session <id>` as its resume command, whatever flags it was started with. A session started with restrictions or extra resources comes back without them:

```
started:   pi -t read,grep,find,ls --no-extensions
resumed:   pi --session <id>          # bash, edit, write and all extensions are back
```

## Changes

- `parseArgs()` records the restriction and resource flags in `Args.resumeFlags`, as typed and in order, with the values the parser consumed: `--tools`/`-t`, `--exclude-tools`/`-xt`, `--no-tools`, `--no-builtin-tools`, `--extension`/`-e`, `--no-extensions`, `--no-mcp`, `--skill`, `--no-skills`, `--prompt-template`, `--no-prompt-templates`, `--theme`, `--no-themes`, `--no-context-files`, `--system-prompt`, `--append-system-prompt`, `--approve`, `--no-approve`, `--models`. Not repeated: what the session keeps (model, thinking level, name), session pickers, cosmetic flags, and `--api-key` (a terminal stores the command in plain text).
- `getProgramResumeCommand()` appends them after `--session <id>`. The command printed on exit is unchanged.
- When the session's directory differs from the directory pi was started in (after `/resume` into another project), pi clears the command: relative paths in the flags would point elsewhere, and resuming without them would drop the restrictions. pi never changes its working directory, so `process.cwd()` is the directory the flags were typed in.
- Docs (`terminal-setup.md`): which flags are repeated, and that a terminal rule must trust each combination.

## Why "as typed"

A Rex rule matches the reported command word for word, so the command has to repeat what the user types (`-t read` stays `-t read`, `./ext.ts` stays relative), and a rule per combination trusts it:

```lua
rex.set("resume.trust.pi_readonly", {
  command = { "pi", "--session", rex.match.uuid, "-t", "read,grep,find,ls" },
})
```

Rex rules with a `flags` table, which accept any combination, compare the flags with `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`. pi's `process.title = "pi"` overwrites that under Node on Linux (and, per the Node docs, macOS), so such rules reject pi with `flags_differ`. Claude Code is not affected: Bun's `process.title` only changes `comm`. Making flags tables work needs either a change in how pi names its process (on Linux, writing `/proc/self/comm` instead) or Rex reading the command line before the program renames itself; not part of this PR.

## Testing

- `npm run check`
- `test/args.test.ts` (recorded flags, as typed and in order; flags left out), `test/format-resume-command.test.ts` (`getProgramResumeCommand`: flags appended, exit hint unchanged, cleared from another directory, no flags from another directory still resumes)
- Manual with an isolated Rex server, real pi built from this branch, and the rule above:
  - `pi -t read,grep,find,ls`: reported with the flags, trusted by `pi_readonly`; after a Rex restart resumed by that rule, and the resumed pi reported `-t read,grep,find,ls` again.
  - `pi --no-context-files` with no matching rule: `flags_differ`, the pane came back as a plain shell instead of a session without the restriction.
