prs.title: feat(coding-agent): add --agent-dir and carry it in the resume command
prs.body:
Follow-up to #12557 (OSC 7577 program resume). Removes its known limitation "`PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` set for one run only is not carried".

## Problem

A terminal resumes pi's reported command without the environment pi was started in. A session started with `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` (for example from a shell function that picks a separate profile for one directory tree) comes back with the settings and auth of `~/.pi/agent`.

Trace, before this change, with `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=~/.pi/earendil/agent` and `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR=~/.pi/earendil/agent/sessions`:

1. pi reports `pi --session-dir ~/.pi/earendil/agent/sessions --session <id>`.
2. Rex restarts and runs that command through `exec`, so no shell function and no old environment.
3. pi finds the session through `--session-dir`, but loads auth, settings, models and extensions from `~/.pi/agent`.

The spec asks for exactly this case to go into argv: "A program whose target depends on its environment or on other state outside the command, such as a credentials profile ..., SHOULD put the resolved values in its argv using its own flags." pi had no flag for the config directory.

## Changes

- `--agent-dir <dir>`: the flag form of `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`, taking precedence like `--session-dir` over `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`. It is applied by setting `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` to the absolute path, because pi, extensions (through the exported `getAgentDir()`) and child processes all read the agent dir from there.
- When it is set: `main()` applies it first (`applyAgentDirArg`), before anything reads the agent dir and before subcommands are recognized, so `pi --agent-dir D install ...` works. Modules have loaded by then, so a value cached from `getAgentDir()` at module load would ignore the flag. `config.ts` and `cli/agent-dir-arg.ts` warn against such caches. Setting the variable before any module loads (a setup module imported first by the entries) was tried and dropped: esbuild code splitting put the setup's imports into the chunk with `main()`, which needed its own bundle entry and a build guard to keep the order.
- `getResumeArgs()` adds `--agent-dir <absolute dir>` when `usesDefaultAgentDir()` is false. This covers both the command printed on exit and the OSC 7577 report. Default setups keep `pi --session <id>`.
- `tools-manager.ts` cached `getBinDir()` in a module constant at import, before `main()` runs, so `fd`/`rg` downloads ignored the flag. It now reads it per call. No other module-level reads of the agent dir exist in `src/`.
- Docs: `cli.md`, `environment-variables.md`, `terminal-setup.md` (Program resume: longer commands need their own terminal rule).

## Testing

- `npm run check`
- `test/agent-dir-arg.test.ts`: `applyAgentDirArg` (any position, last wins, absolute and `~` paths, `--` stops scanning, missing value); `src/cli.ts --agent-dir D --list-models` lists a model from `D/models.json`
- Bundled `dist/bundle/cli.js --agent-dir D --list-models` lists the same model
- Manual with an isolated Rex server (`rex server run --listen unix:///tmp/... --state-dir ...`) and this rule:
  ```lua
  rex.set("resume.trust.pi_earendil", {
    command = { "pi", "--agent-dir", "/home/houskape/.pi/earendil/agent", "--session-dir", "/home/houskape/.pi/earendil/agent/sessions", "--session", rex.match.uuid },
  })
  ```
  pi started in `~/earendil/...` through the shell function reported the command above (`trusted: true`). After `rex server stop` and start, the log shows `resuming saved program program=pi rule=pi_earendil`; the resumed process had no `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` in its initial environment, `!echo $PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` printed `/home/houskape/.pi/earendil/agent`, and the conversation and profile's model were back.

prs.title: docs(coding-agent): reset the terminal after Pi was killed
prs.body:
Refs #12564.

A killed Pi leaves its terminal modes on. The previous advice, "run pi again and quit", does not reset Kitty keyboard reporting: the terminal keeps those settings on a stack, Pi pushes once and pops once per run, so each killed run leaves one entry behind. It also only resets the alternate screen and mouse reporting when the next run uses fullscreen mode.

This updates "Recover the terminal after Pi was killed" in `docs/terminal-setup.md`:

- States that the real fix is finding what kills Pi.
- Gives a reset command for bash/zsh and PowerShell: pops up to 16 Kitty entries (`\e[<16u`), sets the rest to 0 (`\e[=0;1u`), turns off modifyOtherKeys, bracketed paste, mouse and focus reporting, restores wrap and cursor.
- `\e[?1049l` only when the alternate screen is still active, since on the normal screen it desyncs the shell's line editor (reported in #12564).
- When the pane cannot be typed in: start Pi in another tab and ask it to write the reset to the stuck tab's terminal.

Both PowerShell variants (5.1 and 7) were checked to expand the sequence correctly.

prs.title: fix(tui): append Kitty images without a full redraw in regular mode
prs.body:
Second part of #12548: the scrollback wipe on image append. The image loss in Konsole was fixed in #12596.

## Problem

In regular mode the differential renderer reserves an image's rows before drawing it: it writes blank lines over the rows, moves back up and draws the placement, so WezTerm does not erase the image (#5618). A guard fell back to a full redraw (`\x1b[2J\x1b[H\x1b[3J`) whenever those rows reached past the bottom of the screen. A newly appended image starts near the bottom and is usually taller than the space left, so practically every image append cleared the screen and the scrollback, as in the report's log:

```
fullRender: kitty image pre-clear would scroll (39 + 27 > 45)
```

## Fix

Writing the reserved rows at the bottom scrolls the screen like any appended line, and moving back up to the image's first row works as long as the image fits on the screen. So the differential path now falls back only when the image is taller than the screen, the same condition the full redraw already uses for its own row reservation. Rows are still cleared before the image is drawn, so the WezTerm fix is unchanged.

## Verification

- New regression test: appending an image that scrolls the screen stays differential, writes neither `\x1b[2J` nor `\x1b[3J`, reserves rows before drawing, and keeps later output differential. It fails without the fix.
- The existing full-redraw reservation test now forces the full redraw instead of relying on the old fallback.
- Ghostty and Konsole 26.08.3: three appended images went from 3 full redraws to none (only the first render), with the same output and all images visible.

This PR is AI-generated.

prs.title: fix(tui): keep Kitty image IDs within signed 32-bit range
prs.body:
Part of #12548 (image loss). The scrollback wipe on image append is a separate fix.

## Problem

`allocateImageId()` returned random IDs in `[1, 0xfffffffe]`. Konsole parses Kitty graphics keys with `QStringView::toInt()` (signed 32-bit), so about half of all IDs read as `0`:

- `a=T` displays the image but does not store it (`if (keys['i']) _graphicsImages[...] = pixmap`).
- Fullscreen redraws place already uploaded images with `a=p,i=<id>`; Konsole looks up image 0, finds nothing, and the image disappears.
- Regular mode deletes a changed image with `a=d,d=I,i=<id>`; Konsole reads `i=0` and deletes every placement with an overflowed ID, including images in scrollback that are never redrawn.

## Fix

Allocate IDs in `[1, 0x7fffffff]`. Other terminals accept the full 32-bit range, so nothing changes for them.

## Verification

Konsole 26.08.3 (same as the report), a script that appends three images, changes the status line above the third, then appends text:

| Mode | IDs > 2^31-1 | IDs < 2^31 |
|---|---|---|
| Fullscreen | all 3 images lost | all shown |
| Regular | images 1 and 2 lost | all shown |

With this change and random IDs, all images stay in both modes. Added a unit test for the ID range.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): do not count !! output in context token estimate
prs.body:
A `!!` command is stored as a `bashExecution` message with `excludeFromContext: true`. `convertToLlm()` drops these messages, so the model never sees them. But `estimateTokens()` in `compaction.ts` still counted the command and its output. As a result, large `!!` output inflated the context estimate, which could trigger auto-compaction early, and it used up the `keepRecentTokens` budget during cut-point selection, so compaction kept less real history.

`estimateTokens()` now returns 0 for `bashExecution` messages with `excludeFromContext` set. Plain `!` commands are estimated as before.

The other callers already handle a 0 estimate:
- `findCutPoint` and the projected cut-point search skip zero-token entries.
- Branch summarization and bug-report message selection convert through `convertToLlm()` before sending, so a cost of 0 matches what is actually sent.

`excludeFromContext` exists only in coding-agent, so no copies in other packages needed changing.

**Testing**
- Added a test in `test/compaction.test.ts`. With a usage anchor, an excluded `!!` message adds 0 trailing tokens to `estimateContextTokens()`, and the same message without the flag adds 202. The test fails without the fix.
- `npm run check` passes, and so does `test/compaction.test.ts`.
- The reproduction from the issue (`convertToLlm([msg]).length, estimateTokens(msg)`) printed `0 202` before the fix and `0 0` after.

Fixes #12513

Requested by @davidbrai

prs.title: feat(coding-agent): honor DO_NOT_TRACK for install telemetry and attribution
prs.body:
Draft for discussion. Context: a public telemetry audit of 25 agent harnesses (https://x.com/ZryMiller/status/2125497546772812061) rated pi C. It found no third-party SDKs or IDs, but pi does not honor `DO_NOT_TRACK`.

## Problem

`DO_NOT_TRACK=1` (https://consoledonottrack.com) is a cross-tool opt-out. Today pi ignores it. A user with `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` in their shell profile still sends:

- the `pi.dev/api/report-install?version=...` ping after an install or update
- provider attribution headers (`HTTP-Referer: https://pi.dev`, `X-OpenRouter-Title: pi`, ...)

## Change

`isInstallTelemetryEnabled()` now resolves in this order:

1. `PI_TELEMETRY` set: use it. It names pi explicitly, so it wins.
2. `DO_NOT_TRACK` is `1`/`true`/`yes`: off.
3. Otherwise the `enableInstallTelemetry` setting (default `true`).

Both call sites (install ping, `getClientIdentity` attribution) go through this function, so both honor it.

## Not in this PR (open questions)

- Should `DO_NOT_TRACK` beat `PI_TELEMETRY=1`? Currently no.
- Should `DO_NOT_TRACK` also skip the `pi.dev/api/latest-version` check (same as `PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK`)? That request carries the pi version in `User-Agent`, but it is an update check, not telemetry. The convention does not cover update checks.
- Should `DO_NOT_TRACK` also force `enableAnalytics` off? Nothing reads that setting yet beyond first-run setup.
- `/settings` still shows "Install telemetry: true" when an env var overrides it. Could show it as locked/overridden.
- `DO_NOT_TRACK` should not imply `PI_OFFLINE`: that would also stop model catalog and package update checks, which are not tracking.

prs.title: feat(chord,durable): delete conversations on StoreStorage
prs.body:
Refs #11026. Stacked on #12562; review that first. This PR's diff is only the store part.

Lets `StoreStorage` (Durable on Chord's store) delete conversations, as asked in the review of #12562.

## Chord

- New store write `document.purge` (`purgeDocuments(step, owner, namespace)`). It deletes a namespace's records, live or retired, with every revision whatever their history. Each purge is recorded with the record's revision, and a replica applying it checks that revision; one that does not hold the record at that revision is `Diverged`, as for a retirement.
- `OwnerTable.encodeKey`, `delete`, `deleteWhere`: an adapter deletes its rows in a step, recorded with their counts.
- Outbox format 2 adds the purge, and every commit is now written in format 2. Format 1 commits read unchanged. Archives stay format 1: an archive holds state, and a purged record is simply absent from it.
- Decision entry "Erasure in the store" in `decisions.md`. It supersedes in part slice 6b R1 (`rewindable` kept everything) and point 4 of the outbox decision (archive and outbox had one format number). Sync batches carry no format yet; that is a carry-over for the sync layer.

## Durable

- `StoreStorage` sets `deletesConversations`. It deletes rows with `deleteWhere` on the indexed `conversation_id` and purges the documents of the conversation's scopes and of its tasks.
- Its conversations table moves to version 2, which adds `parent_conversation_id` with an index and a backfill through `evolveTable`.

## What it does not erase

- With the outbox on, the commits stored before the deletion keep their writes, the deleted data included, until `outbox.trim` passes the deletion. The sync layer trims once the remote has acknowledged; without sync, the app has to trim itself.
- Freed pages and the WAL belong to the store's connection: an app that must erase opens it with `PRAGMA secure_delete = ON` and checkpoints the WAL.

## Tests

- Chord: purge in the engine, the applier through `applyBatch` (a missing record and a wrong revision both diverge), the archive write schema, outbox formats, and a new `adapter.test.ts`. New example `test/examples/79-erasure.ts`.
- Durable: the storage conformance suite with `deletesConversations` (also across reopen), the store tests, and `npm run test:store`, which runs the harness deletion tests on the store.

prs.title: feat(durable)!: delete conversations for good
prs.body:
Refs #11026. This was also escalated to us directly, outside the issue.

Adds `Harness.deleteConversations(ids, context)`. It closes conversations against new work, aborts their work (background work included), and then removes them for good, together with their forks and the conversations their tasks own (subagents), recursively. Stacked on top: #12582 adds the same for `StoreStorage` (Chord store), which needs a Chord write and an outbox format change.

## Use case

Long-lived hosts that serve many conversations from one Harness: bots, agent servers, a Durable Object that resets a session. Today they can only delete the whole storage.

## How it works

Deletion runs in two commits, with a durable closing state between them. This avoids the retry loop in the first version: a submit that lands between "abort" and "delete" no longer leaves everything aborted and nothing deleted.

1. **Closing commit.** It computes the set: the given conversations plus, transitively, their forks (whose history reads the parent's entries, found through a new `parentConversationId` index) and the conversations their tasks own. It refuses with a typed `DeletionRefused` (`refusal.kind`) before anything is aborted or written:
   - `unsupported`: the Storage does not set `deletesConversations` (JSONL, `StoreStorage` in this PR);
   - `root`: `root()` would recreate it with the reserved ID;
   - `owner`: a live task outside the set owns it.

   Otherwise the commit records the set in a built-in session document, `pi.deletions`, settles the inboxes `unanswered` with reason `deleted`, and abort-marks every live task of the set.
2. **Closed.** New submissions, tasks and forks are refused with `ConversationDeleting`. The check touches the document's key on the Session line, so it waits for an unpublished closing commit (group commit stays correct). A plain Session never deletes; the Harness implements the check through one `TransactionHost` hook.
3. **Delete commit.** Once the set's tasks have ended, the scheduler, as its own work, makes one commit. It settles leftover submissions, retires the current documents (watches and the cache follow the existing retirement path), writes one `conversation.delete` per conversation after the other writes, and clears the set from `pi.deletions`.
   - The write is a barrier for group commit: every read waits until it is stored.
   - Its publication drops the record cache (in-flight reads included), the newest-entry index and the kept contexts, and ends conversation views `ended`.

Cancelling the call only stops the wait. A crash or close leaves the set closed, and the reopened Harness finishes it at its first `resume()`. A failure while finishing is reported as `deletion_failed` and leaves the set closed rather than failing the Session. `inspect().deleting` lists closed sets. A task elsewhere that waited on a deleted task reads its outcome as `orphaned` with reason `deleted`. IDs stay claimed and are never reused.

## Storage contract

- `StorageWrite` gains `{ type: "conversation.delete", id }`, which `TableCommitChange` (`observeCommits()`) also carries.
- `Storage.deletesConversations?: true` is opt-in. Only a Storage that sets it gets the write and the `parentConversationId` filter, so a custom backend that does not delete needs no change.
- `registerStorageConformance(..., { deletesConversations: true })` runs the deletion cases.

| Backend | Deletion |
|---|---|
| Memory, IndexedDB (DB version 2) | Records removed |
| SQLite (schema version 3), Durable Object SQLite | Rows removed. Opt-in `secureDelete: true` runs the connection with `secure_delete` and truncates the WAL after a deletion, at open and at close. Durable Objects refuse the pragma. |
| JSONL | `unsupported`: `main.jsonl` is append-only |
| Chord store | `unsupported` here; see #12582 |

## Tests

- Conformance cases for memory, SQLite, IndexedDB and Durable Object SQLite, each also across reopen. They cover:
  - the order within the batch and later batches in the same call;
  - forks, owners, the indexes and reads at an earlier seq after a deletion;
  - IDs staying claimed.
- The SQLite randomized agreement test now generates deletions, forks and owned conversations.

prs.title: feat(chord,p3): switch a store's outbox at runtime; drop p3's backup marker
prs.body:
## What
- Chord: `Store.setOutbox(on, ctx)`: switch an open store's outbox at runtime, in the commit queue (a commit is recorded whole or not at all), persisted like `openStore`'s `outbox` option.
- p3: drop the `backup/enabled` marker file. The worker opens the session store with its persisted outbox setting; the backup plugin switches it via `WorkerRuntime.store.setOutbox`.

## Why
Backup on/off belongs to the backup plugin, not the base, and should take effect without restarting the worker. The plugin will serve one object per session (enabled from the global and the session's setting) that its worker side follows, calling `setOutbox` on change.

## Tests
- `packages/chord/test/store/outbox.test.ts`: switching on and off an open store, kept across opens, idempotent; commits queued before and after the switch; refused once closed.
- `apps/p3/test/skeleton.test.ts`: the marker test becomes "a plugin switches its session store's outbox, and the next start keeps the setting" (probe gains `outbox(on)`).

prs.body:
Adds `packages/coding-agent/docs/telemetry.md` under Reference ("Telemetry"), based on a read of the current code.

The page covers:

- Requests to `pi.dev`: install/update ping (the only automatic telemetry), version check, model catalog updates. For each: when, data sent, how to turn it off.
- Metadata Pi adds to model requests: `User-Agent` and its exceptions, attribution headers (OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM, OpenCode), `originator: pi` for Codex, session ID.
- Identifiers (`deviceId`, `trackingId`, session ID) and that extensions can read them.

- What `/bug` sends, and its redaction limits.
- Controls: `PI_TELEMETRY`, `enableInstallTelemetry`, `PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK`, offline mode; Pi does not read `DO_NOT_TRACK`.
- What the controls do not cover: extensions, Pi packages, MCP servers, tool commands.

Functional network traffic (MCP connections, provider model lists, package checks, tool downloads, `/share`) is out of scope.

Also links the page from `settings.md` and `environment-variables.md`.

Findings in the code, not changed here:

- The experimental first-run setup tells users to inspect shared data with `/privacy`, which does not exist.
- `enableAnalytics` and `trackingId` are stored but unused. `pi.getSettings()` exposes both, and the merged value lets a trusted project's `.pi/settings.json` override them.
- `PI_OFFLINE` is parsed inconsistently: some checks test whether it is set, others parse the value, so `PI_OFFLINE=0` disables the `pi.dev` requests but not package checks.

Claims were checked against the source and reviewed independently by GPT-6.2 Astra, GPT-6.2 Sol, and Claude Opus 5.5. Verified with `test/documentation.test.ts`.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): summarize the selected prompt when navigating the tree
prs.body:
Closes #12576.

**Problem.** When `/tree` goes back to a user message with "Summarize", the new leaf is that message's parent, but the entries to summarize were collected up to the selected message. So the prompt left the context and was never summarized. For `hello` / `hi` / `migrate the parser…` / `Done.`, selecting the second prompt sent the summarizer only `[Assistant]: Done.`

**Fix.** Compute the new leaf first and collect up to the common ancestor with it, as `docs/compaction.md` describes. `collectEntriesForBranchSummary` accepts `null` for the root, which covers selecting the first prompt. Selecting an assistant message is unchanged.

**Validation** on main `db79712854`:

- New regression test (faux harness, summarizer request captured): the selected prompt is summarized, also for the first prompt; selecting an assistant message still summarizes only what follows it. The first two fail without the fix.

prs.title: fix(ai): retry Bedrock "Too many tokens" throttling
prs.body:
Closes #12573.

**Problem.** `formatBedrockError` turns a Bedrock `ThrottlingException` into `Throttling error: <message>`. Bedrock sends two throttle messages with HTTP 429:

- `Too many requests, please wait before trying again.` matches `"too many requests"` and is retried.
- `Too many tokens, please wait before trying again.` (the per-minute token quota) matches no retryable pattern, so the run ends with the error.

The AWS SDK's own retries give up after about a second, much shorter than a per-minute window, so a sustained token throttle always reaches pi. #2699 already excluded this message from overflow detection so it would be retried instead of compacted (`overflow.ts:78`), but no retry pattern was added.

**Fix.** Add `"throttling"` to `RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN`, next to `"too many requests"`. It matches the `Throttling error:` prefix from `BEDROCK_ERROR_PREFIXES`, so both throttle variants are classified by the exception type rather than by message wording. The non-retryable quota patterns are still checked first.

The other Bedrock prefixes already classify correctly: `Internal server error` and `Service unavailable` are retried, `Validation error` is not.

**Validation** on main `db79712854`:

- New cases in `test/retry.test.ts` for both throttle messages. The token case fails without the fix.
- The real Bedrock adapter against a local server answering 429 `ThrottlingException` (`AWS_BEDROCK_FORCE_HTTP1=1`): `Too many tokens` produced `Throttling error: Too many tokens, please wait before trying again.` and was not retryable before the fix; `Too many requests` was retryable.
- Faux harness with `retry.enabled`: a token throttle followed by a normal reply made one provider call and no `auto_retry_start` before the fix, and two calls with one retry after.
- `retry.test.ts` and `overflow.test.ts` pass. `npm run check` passes. In `./test.sh` the only failures are unrelated to this change:
  - The find tool tests fail because fd is not installed here and the test config prevents downloading it.
  - The pi-env tests need cargo, which is not installed here.
  - chord's `routines` test failed once under load and passes on its own.

labels.name: priority/P2

labels.name: type/feature-request
labels.description: New feature or enhancement request

labels.name: category/core
labels.description: Core engine and logic

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Allow the operator of a containerized Managed Runtime Worker to select its control listener with `qwen managed-runtime-worker --container-boot <file> --port <port>`. For example, a deployment with an existing ingress on port 4096 should be able to start the Worker on that port and complete native attestation. The ready document should report the actual listener.

### Why is this needed?

The current container entry point binds port 43190 and rejects a port argument. Runtimes that address a sandbox directly by port cannot use an existing ingress rule for a different port. A deployment-level option would let them reuse that rule.

### Acceptance criteria

- A valid explicit port works for each supported container boot document, including file workspaces.
- Omitting the option preserves the current container default. A local process Worker continues to use an ephemeral loopback port.
- Invalid port arguments fail before the Worker starts. Native authorization, attestation and the separate publication listener retain their existing contracts.

issues.title: Desktop AppImage: gray window on current Mesa — bundled libwayland-client lacks wl_fixes_interface, host EGL vendor fails to load

labels.name: priority/P2
labels.description: Medium - Moderately impactful, noticeable problem

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/platform
labels.description: Platform compatibility

labels.name: scope/linux
labels.description: Linux specific issues

labels.name: scope/packaging
labels.description: Package distribution

issues.body:
### What happened?

The Desktop AppImage (v0.28.4, linux x64) opens a window but renders **only a gray rectangle** on Bluefin / Fedora with current Mesa. stderr shows:

```
Could not create default EGL display: EGL_BAD_PARAMETER. Aborting...
```

Root cause: the AppImage bundles an **old `libwayland-client.so.0`** (via `linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk`) that lacks `wl_fixes_interface`. The AppImage's `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` makes it shadow the host's wayland 1.26, so the host Mesa EGL vendor fails to load:

```
OSError: /lib64/libEGL_mesa.so.0: undefined symbol: wl_fixes_interface
```

With no EGL vendor available, `eglGetDisplay(EGL_DEFAULT_DISPLAY)` returns `EGL_NO_DISPLAY` / `EGL_BAD_PARAMETER`, WebKitGTK aborts display initialization, and the WebView never paints.

Verified step by step on the affected machine:

1. Minimal ctypes probe (`eglGetDisplay(None)` + `eglInitialize`) **under the AppImage's `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`** → `EGL_NO_DISPLAY`, error `0x300c` (`EGL_BAD_PARAMETER`). Same probe with a clean environment → Mesa, EGL 1.5, works.
2. `LD_PRELOAD` of the bundled `libwayland-client.so.0` alone reproduces the failure; `libwayland-egl.so.1` alone does not.
3. With the bundled client preloaded, `ctypes.CDLL("libEGL_mesa.so.0")` raises `undefined symbol: wl_fixes_interface`. `nm -D` confirms: bundled client exports 0 `wl_fixes*` symbols, host 1.26 exports them.

### What did you expect to happen?

The Desktop window renders the Web Shell UI on any current Linux distro, instead of a gray window. The AppImage should not let a bundled, outdated `libwayland-client` shadow the host library that host Mesa links against.

### Client information

<details>
<summary>Client Information</summary>

```console
$ qwen /about
Qwen Code v0.28.4
Model: qwen4-max
Fast Model: not set
Agent Loop: headless: shared
Auth: Qwen Subscription
Platform: linux x64 (7.3.4-300.fc45.x86_64)
Node.js: v26.13.1
Session: 0e922834-9321-4684-9810-a8b16070cc89
Git commit: e8424c88dd
LSP: disabled
```

</details>

Platform: Linux — Bluefin `latest-45.20261125.1` (Fedora Silverblue base), GNOME Wayland, AMD Radeon 780M iGPU.
Host packages: `mesa-libEGL-26.2.7-2.fc45`, `libwayland-client-1.26.0-3.fc45`.
Desktop AppImage: `Qwen Code Desktop` v0.28.4 (Tauri v2, bundled `webkit2gtk-4.1`).

### Login information

Qwen Subscription (same account as the CLI). The gray window appears before any login/UI interaction, so auth is not involved.

### Anything else we need to know?

#### Workarounds (both tested and confirmed to render)

**1. Environment variable (most convenient) — make the host wayland library win over the bundled one:**

```bash
LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib64/libwayland-client.so.0 "./Qwen Code Desktop"
```

Host library path per distro:
- Fedora / RHEL / openSUSE: `/usr/lib64/libwayland-client.so.0`
- Debian / Ubuntu: `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libwayland-client.so.0`
- Arch: `/usr/lib/libwayland-client.so.0`

To make it permanent in the launcher, edit the `.desktop` entry:

```ini
Exec=env LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib64/libwayland-client.so.0 "/path/to/Qwen Code Desktop"
```

(Note: AppImage managers such as AppManager/Gear Lever may regenerate the `.desktop` file on app updates, reverting this edit.)

`LD_PRELOAD` is the only env-var lever that works: the conflict is at dynamic-link time (the bundled library shadows the host one before any graphics code runs). The AppImage's ELF wrapper hardcodes the bundle dirs at the front of `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, so an externally set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` cannot win.

**2. No `LD_PRELOAD` — extract the AppImage and drop the bundled wayland libraries** (the dynamic linker then falls back to the host's):

```bash
"./Qwen Code Desktop" --appimage-extract
rm squashfs-root/usr/lib/libwayland-client.so.0 \
   squashfs-root/usr/lib/libwayland-cursor.so.0 \
   squashfs-root/usr/lib/libwayland-egl.so.1 \
   squashfs-root/usr/lib/libwayland-server.so.0
./squashfs-root/AppRun
```

Optionally repack with `appimagetool squashfs-root` for a single-file fixed AppImage.

#### What does NOT help (all tested)

`--disable-gpu`, `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1`, `WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1`, unsetting `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, Mesa env vars (`LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE`, `MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE`, …) — the failure happens when `libEGL_mesa.so.0` is dlopened (undefined symbol), before any of those paths or settings are read. The bundled GTK hook forces `GDK_BACKEND=x11`, but the failure is backend-independent.

#### Suggested fix (build side)

Exclude `libwayland-client/libwayland-cursor/libwayland-egl/libwayland-server` from the AppImage bundle (wayland is backward-compatible; host libs are present on every desktop that can run the app), or bundle wayland ≥ 1.24. This likely affects every distro whose Mesa references `wl_fixes_interface` (Fedora 43+/Bluefin, etc.); Ubuntu-LTS-based CI images have older Mesa and would not catch it.

Related but distinct: #16030 (bundled WebKitGTK missing 9 libraries → image paste fails). Same bundling strategy, different failure: this one is an *outdated bundled library shadowing a host library*, not a missing one.

issues.title: Anthropic: no message cache breakpoint when the user turn ends with an image or PDF

labels.name: priority/P2
labels.description: Medium - Moderately impactful, noticeable problem

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/performance
labels.description: Performance and optimization

labels.name: scope/caching
labels.description: Caching mechanisms

issues.body:
### What happened?

On the Anthropic provider, `addCacheControlToMessages` puts the conversation cache breakpoint on the last block of the last user message, but only when that block is `text` or `tool_result` ([converter.ts#L1485-L1490](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/6b0cd79/packages/core/src/core/anthropicContentGenerator/converter.ts#L1485-L1490)). When the turn ends with an image or a PDF (an Anthropic `image` or `document` block), the function sets no breakpoint and stops searching ([converter.ts#L1447-L1497](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/6b0cd79/packages/core/src/core/anthropicContentGenerator/converter.ts#L1447-L1497)). The request then carries breakpoints only on the system prompt and the last tool, so nothing after them is cached.

The next request (for example, the `tool_result` after a tool call) repeats that prefix, but the furthest breakpoint it can read is on the system prompt, so the whole user turn, media included, is written to the cache again instead of being read.

Anthropic's prompt-caching docs list images and documents in user-turn `messages.content` as cacheable, so the media block itself can carry the breakpoint.

On current main, these entry points produce a user turn that ends with media:

- ACP: an `image` content block is mapped in place to `inlineData` ([Session.ts#L20767-L20781](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/6b0cd79/packages/cli/src/acp-integration/session/Session.ts#L20767-L20781)), and a prompt made only of text and image blocks keeps the client's block order ([Session.ts#L20883-L20889](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/6b0cd79/packages/cli/src/acp-integration/session/Session.ts#L20883-L20889)). A client that sends `[text, image]` therefore produces a turn that ends with the image.
- `qwen serve` hosted input: `parseHostedInput` returns `parts: [text, ...image attachments]` ([hosted-input.ts#L163](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/6b0cd79/packages/cli/src/serve/hosted-input.ts#L163)).

The interactive TUI does not reach this case (pasted images become `@` references, which end the turn with text), and neither does the SDK stream-json path (it turns non-text blocks into JSON text).

**Reproduction.** With the helpers in `converter.test.ts`, on main:

```ts
const { messages } = convert([
  { role: 'user', parts: [{ text: 'what is this?' }, inline('image/png', 'AAAA')] },
]);
// Expected: the image block carries cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' }.
// On main: no block in `messages` has cache_control.
```

### What did you expect to happen?

The last cacheable block of the user turn (here, the image or document) carries the message breakpoint, so the next request reads the turn from cache. If the last block cannot be cached, the breakpoint moves to the nearest earlier cacheable block instead of being dropped.

### Client information

Qwen Code: source checkout at `6b0cd79` (main, 2026-11-26)
Platform: macOS 26.3.1 (arm64)

I found this by reading the converter and replaying captured requests, not through the interactive CLI, so there is no `/about` output.

### Login information

`authType: anthropic` with an API key against `api.anthropic.com`, prompt caching on (the default).

### Anything else we need to know?

**Cost.** I replayed four captured requests against the API, once per arm, on `claude-opus-5-5` (adaptive thinking, medium effort). The four requests form two short conversations: `[prompt text, PNG]` followed by a `read_file` tool result, and `[prompt text, PDF]` followed by a tool result. Costs use Opus 5.5 prices with the 5-minute TTL.

| | Without fix | With fix |
|---|---|---|
| Request 2 (tool result after the image turn) | writes 5,821, reads 14,644 | writes 155, reads 20,311 |
| Request 4 (tool result after the PDF turn) | writes 11,125, reads 14,644 | writes 109, reads 25,659 |
| Input cost, all 4 requests | | −27.1% |
| Total cost, including output | | −26.3% |

The fixed version pays for a cache write on each media turn (requests 1 and 3) and recovers it on the following request. The same four requests on `claude-sonnet-4-5`, with its default 32,000-token thinking budget, gave −26.1% input cost.

Scope: these are fixed-trajectory replays of captured requests, not end-to-end sessions. The captures came from a driver that calls `sendMessageStream` with the part shapes listed above; the driver did not run the ACP session code. The PDF conversation shows the converter's behavior only: on current main I did not find an entry point that ends a turn with a PDF, because ACP now places the prompt text after embedded resources. The saving grows with the size of the media turn relative to the rest of the prompt.

**Related.** #11627 and #11640 (merged 2026-09-12) fixed breakpoint placement around reattached images on the DashScope path; #11651 (closed) was an alternative PR. The skip for the reattach and memory-catalog tail added for #11627 (`volatileTailBlockCount`) is not affected. I found no existing issue or PR for the Anthropic case.

**Fix.** I have a patch with tests ready. It marks the last non-empty `text`, `tool_result`, `image` or `document` block at or before the existing anchor, and falls back to an earlier user message when no block qualifies. Each request still gets one message breakpoint. The four new converter tests (image-terminal turn, PDF-terminal turn, image followed by the request-only memory catalog, one breakpoint after earlier history) fail on `6b0cd79` and pass with the patch; the converter tests pass 138/138 and the anthropicContentGenerator tests 258/258. I can open a PR once this is confirmed, or a maintainer can take it.

prs.title: fix(desktop): fail the AppImage smoke check when a host library is bundled
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The release smoke check for the Linux AppImage now fails when the extracted image ships its own copy of a library that must come from the host. Previously it only rejected a dynamic dependency that was neither bundled nor on the host baseline list, so an image carrying a host library passed silently. The AppImage closure test grows a case for the bundled `libwayland-client.so.0`, and the desktop README explains both directions of the check.

## Why it's needed

The AppImage's bundle directory leads `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, so any host-baseline library inside the image shadows the host's newer copy instead of falling back to it. On Fedora 43+/Bluefin an AppImage-built `libwayland-client.so.0` lacks `wl_fixes_interface`, so the host's `libEGL_mesa.so.0` cannot be dlopened (`undefined symbol: wl_fixes_interface`), no EGL vendor is available, and the Desktop window stays a gray rectangle (#18486). The CI build root is Ubuntu 22.04, whose Mesa does not reference that symbol, so the same shadowing never shows up there and the current gate cannot catch it from runtime behaviour. Rejecting the package state itself turns the failure into a build-time error that describes the fix.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. `cd packages/desktop && node scripts/test-release.js` — passes.
2. Confirm the new assertion is discriminating: restore the pre-PR `packages/desktop/scripts/smoke-linux-installers.js` (only that file) and rerun; the test fails with `expected: /AppImage must not bundle host-baseline libraries: usr\/lib\/libwayland-client\.so\.0/`, then passes again with the PR version.
3. The same fixture technique as before: a fake extracted root plus a fake `readelf` on `PATH`, so no real AppImage or Linux host is needed.

### Evidence (Before & After)

```
# pre-PR verifyAppImageClosure + PR test
control exit=1
  expected: /AppImage must not bundle host-baseline libraries: usr\/lib\/libwayland-client\.so\.0/,

# PR verifyAppImageClosure + PR test
restored exit=0
Desktop release helper checks passed.
```

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Plain `cd packages/desktop && node scripts/test-release.js` on macOS (Node v22.23.4), no install required.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a legitimate application library that happens to share a soname with a host baseline entry would now block the release instead of shipping. The alternative — silently shadowing the host's copy — is the bug being fixed.
- Expected release effect: **the next `Desktop Release` dispatch (and the daily `Desktop Checks` dry run) fails at `Verify Linux installer runtimes` before publishing.** The released `Qwen-Code-Desktop_0.28.4_amd64.AppImage` already carries `usr/lib/libwayland-client.so.0` and the three wayland siblings, and this PR does not change packaging (`src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` sets only `bundle.linux.appimage.bundleMediaFramework`; there is no `--exclude-library`, linuxdeploy hook or `usr/lib` prune), so the rebuilt image trips the new rule. `publish` needs `build`, so that dispatch publishes nothing on any platform. This is deliberate: the image it would publish is the shadowed one from #18486, so failing is better than shipping it. It stays red until a separate PR excludes the wayland family at packaging time.
- Not validated / out of scope: the real EGL/Mesa failure was not reproduced; that needs a Linux host with current Mesa and a built AppImage. Removing the libraries at packaging time is that separate PR, because the bundler exclusion is not reachable from the Tauri config and cannot be validated on macOS — its acceptance is `npm run smoke:linux-installers` green on a real built AppImage, which no unit fixture can show (also worth checking the `wl_fixes_interface` case the reporter hit).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.
- UI verification: N/A — the change is to a build-time verification script and its README; the user-visible behavior it protects (the AppImage rendering instead of a gray window) is not reachable from any local CLI/TUI/Web surface on this host.

## Linked Issues

Refs #18486 — this PR does not resolve it: the image users install today is unchanged until the packaging change lands.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

Linux AppImage 的发布冒烟检查现在会在解包后的镜像自带某个本应由宿主提供的库时失败。此前该检查只拒绝“既不在镜像内、也不在宿主基线名单上”的动态依赖，因此镜像里打包了宿主库反而能静默通过。AppImage closure 测试新增了打包 `libwayland-client.so.0` 的用例，desktop README 也补充了该检查的两个方向。

## 为什么需要

AppImage 的 bundle 目录排在 `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` 最前，因此镜像内任何宿主基线库都会遮蔽宿主更新的副本，而不是回退到宿主库。在 Fedora 43+/Bluefin 上，用 AppImage 构建的 `libwayland-client.so.0` 缺少 `wl_fixes_interface`，导致宿主的 `libEGL_mesa.so.0` 无法被 dlopen（`undefined symbol: wl_fixes_interface`），没有可用的 EGL vendor，Desktop 窗口只剩一块灰矩形（#18486）。CI 构建环境是 Ubuntu 22.04，其 Mesa 不引用该符号，所以同样的遮蔽在 CI 上永远不会暴露，现有门禁也无法从运行时行为发现它。直接拒绝这种打包状态，可以把故障变成一个说明修复方向的构建期错误。

## 审阅验证步骤

1. 执行 `cd packages/desktop && node scripts/test-release.js`，应通过。
2. 确认新断言确实有区分度：仅把 `packages/desktop/scripts/smoke-linux-installers.js` 还原为 PR 之前的版本并重跑，测试会以 `expected: /AppImage must not bundle host-baseline libraries: usr\/lib\/libwayland-client\.so\.0/` 失败；换回 PR 版本后再次通过。
3. 沿用原有夹具手法：伪造的解包根目录加上 `PATH` 里的假 `readelf`，无需真实 AppImage 或 Linux 主机。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险：若某个应用库恰好与宿主基线名单中的 soname 同名，现在会阻止发布而不是继续发货。另一种选择——静默遮蔽宿主副本——正是本 issue 的缺陷。
- 预期的发布影响：**下一次 `Desktop Release` 派发（以及每日 `Desktop Checks` 试跑）将在 `Verify Linux installer runtimes` 处失败，不会发布。** 已发布的 `Qwen-Code-Desktop_0.28.4_amd64.AppImage` 自带 `usr/lib/libwayland-client.so.0` 及三个 wayland 兄弟库，而本 PR 不改打包（`src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` 只设 `bundle.linux.appimage.bundleMediaFramework`，没有 `--exclude-library`、linuxdeploy 钩子或 `usr/lib` 清理），因此重新构建的镜像会触发新规则。`publish` 的 `needs` 含 `build`，所以那次派发在所有平台上都不会发布任何东西。这是有意为之：否则发出去的就是 #18486 里那个被遮蔽的镜像，失败好过发货。在另一个 PR 于打包阶段排除 wayland 家族之前，它会一直保持红色。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：未复现真实的 EGL/Mesa 故障，那需要装有当前 Mesa 的 Linux 主机以及构建好的 AppImage。在打包阶段移除这些库属于那个单独的 PR：打包排除无法通过 Tauri 配置触达，也无法在 macOS 上验证——它的验收标准是在真实构建的 AppImage 上 `npm run smoke:linux-installers` 为绿色，这是单元夹具证明不了的（也可顺带确认报告人遇到的 `wl_fixes_interface` 情况）。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。
- UI 验证：N/A —— 改动对象是构建期校验脚本及其 README；它所保护的可见行为（AppImage 正常渲染而非灰窗口）在本机无法通过任何 CLI/TUI/Web 入口触达。

</details>

prs.title: feat(managed-agent): allow a container worker to select its control port
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Container launchers can pass `--port 4096` together with `--container-boot <path>` to select the Managed Runtime Worker’s control listener. The ready receipt reports the bound port. Omitting the option keeps the container default of 43190. Stdin and SSH workers use an ephemeral loopback port.

## Why it's needed

Some sandbox platforms route ingress directly to a process on an approved port. A hard-coded listener forces operators to change ingress rules or add a forwarding layer just to reach an otherwise healthy Worker.

## Reviewer Test Plan

- Boot a container Worker with and without an explicit port and attest it using the identity that launched it.
- Check that a file workspace uses the same selected port and an external workspace keeps publication on its dedicated listener.
- Confirm that a port supplied without a container boot, an out-of-range value or a duplicate is rejected. An external workspace must reject 43191 before binding its control listener.

### How to verify

Use a synthetic container boot and registration, start the Worker with `managed-runtime-worker --container-boot <path> --port 4096`, and compare the ready URL with the listening socket. Send a native attestation request for that boot and verify the returned binding identity. Repeat without `--port` for the default and use the ordinary stdin launcher for the process case.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before this change, a container rejected `--port 4096` before readiness. The focused CLI, container, CSI, attestation and publication suites cover the new behavior. All 283 distinct tests passed across six files, including a rerun of the process-start cases. In isolated Linux, both session-isolated and registered external workspace boots bound 0.0.0.0:4096 and returned HTTP 200 with matching native v2 and v3 attestation identities.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Focused CLI and Worker tests passed |
| Linux | Six isolated process cases passed with the built CLI, including both native attestations |
| Windows | Not run |

## Risk & Scope

The option selects the control socket at process startup. The launcher and ingress must use the same port. An external workspace reserves 43191 for publication. The existing boot, lease and attestation protocols are preserved.

Kubernetes runtime — [English](https://github.com/rockybot2026/qwen-code/blob/09c26a1473c0f9c14a78e861f8a16034673b870d/docs/design/2026-10-01-managed-kubernetes-runtime.md) · [中文](https://github.com/rockybot2026/qwen-code/blob/09c26a1473c0f9c14a78e861f8a16034673b870d/docs/design/2026-10-01-managed-kubernetes-runtime.zh-CN.md)

External container publication — [English](https://github.com/rockybot2026/qwen-code/blob/09c26a1473c0f9c14a78e861f8a16034673b870d/docs/design/2026-10-25-external-container-publication.md) · [中文](https://github.com/rockybot2026/qwen-code/blob/09c26a1473c0f9c14a78e861f8a16034673b870d/docs/design/2026-10-25-external-container-publication.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Closes #18501

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

容器启动时可同时传入 `--container-boot <path>` 和 `--port 4096`，ready 回执报告实际监听端口。省略端口时容器仍使用 43190，stdin 和 SSH 进程仍在回环地址使用临时端口。直接按端口寻址的沙箱因此可以复用已开放的入口。

评审时可使用合成的 boot 和 registration 启动 Worker，核对实际监听地址与 ready URL，再发送原生 attest 并比对完整绑定身份。另验文件 Workspace、默认启动和独立 publication 监听。缺少容器 boot、重复或越界端口会被拒绝；external Workspace 在绑定前拒绝已保留给 publication 的 43191。

旧版本在传入 `--port 4096` 后直接退出。macOS 上六个测试文件的 283 项用例已通过，包含对进程启停用例的复验。Linux 隔离容器已复现旧行为，新构建通过六项实进程验证，两类 Worker 均实际监听 4096，原生 v2、v3 attest 均返回 HTTP 200，绑定身份匹配。Windows 未执行。部署配置和入口路由需使用相同端口，现有 boot、lease 和 attest 协议沿用。

</details>

prs.title: fix(ci): fail closed on authority-surface PRs and ambient credential probes
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The precheck that decides whether automated triage and review may run on an outside contribution now judges what a pull request can reach, not only whether its wording matches a known-bad phrase. A contribution from someone without write access that modifies the surfaces deciding what CI executes, or what the reviewing agent reads as instructions, is held for maintainer approval instead of being handed to the reviewer. Reads of recognized credentials the runner holds ambiently — cloud instance metadata endpoints, the process environment, well-known credential files — count as a review signal on their own, without having to be paired with a named secret reference or a JavaScript logging call. A diff that had to be truncated to fit the collection cap now fails closed rather than being reported as clean, and a failure to read the PR's title and body does not silently discard that input channel. The recognized forms are deliberately bounded; the additional credential, URL and lifecycle paths documented in the linked design are not certified safe.

The held state is the existing one: a maintainer can still opt in explicitly with a triage or review command. Nothing is auto-closed, and authors with write access are unaffected.

## Why it's needed

Two fork pull requests opened ten minutes apart probed this automation. One modified a script that CI executes after checking out the contribution, adding an environment dump and a walk of the Alibaba Cloud and AWS instance metadata endpoints for role credentials. The other added a documentation page whose text instructed the reviewing agent to run a list of commands with its shell tool and paste their raw output verbatim into a public comment; the list included the process environment and the same metadata endpoints. Neither payload named a GitHub secret, and the precheck admitted both with an empty finding list.

The manual "Approve workflows to run" setting does not cover this path. It gates fork events of one kind, while the triage and review automation runs on the privileged base-branch trigger and started within a second of each pull request being opened; the lane the setting did protect recorded zero jobs. So the human step was guarding the lane that was not attacked, and it still asks a person to recognise a payload phrased as routine read-only diagnostics.

The existing rules could not see either payload for structural reasons: their sinks are JavaScript-only, so a shell `echo` is not a sink; their notion of a secret is a named reference, so an ambient credential source is invisible; their injection rules match known phrases, and both payloads used ordinary operational vocabulary; and they never looked at which paths a contribution changes. A `.github`-only path rule would still miss the second pull request, which changes no CI path at all. The agent's own instruction files remain a stronger channel than a documentation page for any lane that runs in the contributed tree. The present review lane checks out the default branch, so it does not load the contribution's own contextual instruction files; that checkout boundary, rather than a claim about the second payload's documentation path, is what isolates its workspace.

Separately, a capped diff was reportable as clean. A payload the existing rules do catch flips to admitted once padding pushes it past the two-megabyte cap, because the collection step tolerated the resulting broken-pipe status and only failed closed on an empty diff.

This is defence in depth. It does not remove the payoff: a runner that holds a cloud role still hands out credentials to anything that executes on it, and disposable runners and container isolation do not change that. That hardening is listed as out of scope below.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Replay both probe payloads through the precheck, on this branch and on the base, and compare. This is the decisive check and needs nothing beyond `gh` and `node`.

```bash
for n in 18362 18364; do
  gh pr view "$n" --repo QwenLM/qwen-code --json title,body,headRefOid > "/tmp/pr-$n.json"
  gh pr diff "$n" --repo QwenLM/qwen-code --patch > "/tmp/pr-$n.diff"
done

# This branch.
for n in 18362 18364; do
  node .github/scripts/pr-safety-precheck.mjs \
    --pr "/tmp/pr-$n.json" --diff "/tmp/pr-$n.diff" \
    --trusted-author false --diff-truncated false --output /dev/null
done

# The base, for comparison (it takes no truncation flag). Keep this copy inside
# the checkout: the script only enters main() when its own module URL matches
# argv[1], and on macOS /tmp is a symlink, so a copy placed there exits silently
# with no output at all.
mkdir -p .qwen/tmp
git show origin/main:.github/scripts/pr-safety-precheck.mjs > .qwen/tmp/base-precheck.mjs
for n in 18362 18364; do
  node .qwen/tmp/base-precheck.mjs \
    --pr "/tmp/pr-$n.json" --diff "/tmp/pr-$n.diff" \
    --trusted-author false --output /dev/null
done
```

Expected on the base: `allow_triage` with `"reason_codes": []` for both. Expected on this branch, observed locally:

```
18362  manual_required  ["protected_path:authority_surface","ambient_credential:cloud_metadata","ambient_credential:env_dump"]
18364  manual_required  ["ambient_credential:cloud_metadata","ambient_credential:proc_environ"]
```

Note that the second payload is caught without any path finding — that is the case a CI-directory-only rule misses.

Then run the suites:

```bash
node --test .github/scripts/pr-safety-precheck.test.mjs .github/scripts/pr-safety-precheck.workflow.test.mjs # expect 255 pass, 0 fail
node --test .github/scripts/ci/classify-profile.test.mjs     # expect 27 pass, 0 fail
```

Behaviours worth confirming individually, all covered by named cases in the precheck suite:

- A contribution that only deletes a CI guard, only renames a file into a protected directory, or only changes a file mode is still held.
- A path git quotes because it contains a tab or a non-ASCII byte is still held. Before this was handled, adding a file under the CI workflow directory with a tab in its name returned `allow_triage`; that bypass is now closed and pinned.
- An `env VAR=value command` prefix is **not** held — the environment rule targets dumps, not ordinary command prefixes.
- A truncated diff is held even when the visible portion is clean, and a trusted author is never held by any of the new rules.
- The collection step reads one byte past the cap so that a read of exactly the cap is distinguishable from a complete diff of that size. At exactly two megabytes the truncation flag stays false; at one byte more it becomes true.

Three cases in the precheck suite previously asserted that outside changes to CI and script directories are admitted. They were retargeted to the new policy rather than removed. One fixture also lacked a diff header, so it had been passing without exercising path detection at all; it now carries a real header.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no user-visible or TUI surface. The before/after comparison is the base-versus-branch replay above.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit suites only, plus a stubbed `gh` on `PATH` to drive the collection step's shell across the cap boundary. No model calls and no runner time.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: false positives hold legitimate outside contributions for a maintainer opt-in. In a sample of 80 open pull requests, out of 578 open at the time, 67 had authors without write access and 7 of those touched a protected surface; the sample is not a repo-wide rate. The repository's own network-policy and fetch fixtures contain instance-metadata addresses, so an outside edit to them is held as well. The cost per hit is one maintainer decision, not a rejected contributor — which is why this holds rather than closes.
- Not validated / out of scope: attaching no cloud role to CI runners or hardening the instance metadata service; a default-deny egress allowlist for the reviewing agent; redaction of agent-authored comments before publication. Also unmeasured: whether the diff API can itself return a silently shortened patch for a very large contribution — the witness byte only detects truncation by the collection step, so an upstream short read would arrive under the cap and look complete. One further observation is recorded rather than explained: the review run for the second probe aborted at its first check because its bot token was empty, while an in-repo review in the same minute succeeded; the mechanism was not determined, so an empty secret is not counted as a control.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. Existing finding codes are retained. New codes identify protected authority surfaces, recognized ambient credential sources, truncated diffs and unreadable PR metadata. Automated dependency pull requests from outside authors will now need a maintainer opt-in, since dependency manifests are in the protected set — whether they should stay there is an open question in the design.

Design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/pr-precheck-authority-gate/docs/design/pr-safety-precheck-authority-gate.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/pr-precheck-authority-gate/docs/design/pr-safety-precheck-authority-gate.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

References #18362 and #18364 (the two probe pull requests). No closing keyword.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

决定「自动化 triage 与 review 能否在外部贡献上运行」的那道预检，现在依据 PR **能触达什么**来判定，而不只依据其措辞是否命中已知坏词。无 write 权限的作者若改动了「决定 CI 执行什么」或「评审 agent 把什么当指令读」的那些面，改为扣住等维护者批准，而不是直接交给评审器；对 runner **环境自带**中已识别凭据的读取——云实例元数据端点、进程环境、知名凭据文件——本身即算评审信号，不再必须与具名 secret 引用或 JavaScript 日志调用配对。为采集上限而被截断的 diff 现在 fail closed，不再被报成干净；读取 PR 标题和正文失败也不会再静默丢弃这条输入通道。识别范围有意保持有界；链接设计文档所述的其他凭据、URL 和生命周期路径不因此获得安全认证。

扣住用的是既有状态：维护者仍可用 triage 或 review 命令显式放行。不自动关闭任何 PR，有 write 权限的作者不受影响。

## 为什么需要

相隔十分钟开启的两个 fork PR 探测了这套自动化。其中一个修改了 CI 在检出贡献**之后**执行的脚本，加入环境导出以及对阿里云与 AWS 实例元数据端点的遍历以取角色凭据。另一个新增了一个文档页，其正文指示评审 agent 用 shell 工具执行一串命令、并把原始输出**逐字**贴进公开评论；清单里包含进程环境与同样的元数据端点。两个载荷都没有点名任何 GitHub secret，而预检对两者都以「零发现」放行。

人工的「Approve workflows to run」设置**不覆盖这条通路**。它作用于某一类 fork 事件，而 triage 与 review 自动化跑在带权限的基线分支触发器上，在每个 PR 开启后一秒内就起跑；被该设置守住的那条车道记录到零个 job。所以那道人工步骤守的是没被攻击的车道，而且它仍然要求人去识别一段措辞为「例行只读诊断」的载荷。

既有规则看不见这两个载荷是结构性的：它们的 sink 只认 JavaScript，所以 shell 的 `echo` 不是 sink；它们的「secret」概念是具名引用，所以环境凭据源不可见；它们的注入规则匹配已知短语，而两个载荷都用普通运维词汇；而且它们从不看贡献改了哪些路径。**只挡 CI 目录**的路径规则仍会漏掉第二个 PR——它根本没改任何 CI 路径。对任何在贡献树里运行的车道，agent 自身的指令文件都比文档页更强，因为它们承载着指令。当前 review 车道检出的是默认分支，不加载贡献自己的上下文指令；隔离其工作区的是这个检出边界，而不是把第二个探针的文档路径说成一条已验证的指令通道。

另外，被截断的 diff 原本可以被报成干净。一条现有规则**确实能抓**的载荷，一旦用填充把它推过两兆上限就翻成放行——因为采集步骤容忍了由此产生的 broken-pipe 状态码，且只在 diff 为空时 fail closed。

这属于防御纵深，**并未消除收益**：挂着云角色的 runner 仍会把凭据交给任何在其上执行的代码，一次性 runner 与容器隔离都不改变这一点。该加固列在下面的范围之外。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

把两个探针载荷分别在本分支与基线上重放过预检并对比。这是判定性检查，除 `gh` 与 `node` 外不需要任何东西。

```bash
for n in 18362 18364; do
  gh pr view "$n" --repo QwenLM/qwen-code --json title,body,headRefOid > "/tmp/pr-$n.json"
  gh pr diff "$n" --repo QwenLM/qwen-code --patch > "/tmp/pr-$n.diff"
done

# 本分支。
for n in 18362 18364; do
  node .github/scripts/pr-safety-precheck.mjs \
    --pr "/tmp/pr-$n.json" --diff "/tmp/pr-$n.diff" \
    --trusted-author false --diff-truncated false --output /dev/null
done

# 基线，用于对比（它不接受截断旗标）。这份副本要放在检出目录**之内**：
# 该脚本只有在自身模块 URL 与 argv[1] 相同时才进入 main()，而 macOS 上
# /tmp 是符号链接，放在那里的副本会**静默退出、毫无输出**。
mkdir -p .qwen/tmp
git show origin/main:.github/scripts/pr-safety-precheck.mjs > .qwen/tmp/base-precheck.mjs
for n in 18362 18364; do
  node .qwen/tmp/base-precheck.mjs \
    --pr "/tmp/pr-$n.json" --diff "/tmp/pr-$n.diff" \
    --trusted-author false --output /dev/null
done
```

基线上的预期：两者都是 `allow_triage`、`"reason_codes": []`。本分支上的预期（本地实测）：

```
18362  manual_required  ["protected_path:authority_surface","ambient_credential:cloud_metadata","ambient_credential:env_dump"]
18364  manual_required  ["ambient_credential:cloud_metadata","ambient_credential:proc_environ"]
```

注意第二个载荷是在**没有任何路径发现**的情况下被拦下的——这正是「只挡 CI 目录」的规则会漏掉的情形。

然后跑套件：

```bash
node --test .github/scripts/pr-safety-precheck.test.mjs .github/scripts/pr-safety-precheck.workflow.test.mjs # 预期 255 通过、0 失败
node --test .github/scripts/ci/classify-profile.test.mjs     # 预期 27 通过、0 失败
```

值得逐条确认的行为，预检套件里都有对应命名用例：

- 只**删除**一个 CI 守卫、只把文件**重命名**进受保护目录、或只改文件**权限位**的贡献，仍被扣住。
- 因含 tab 或非 ASCII 字节而被 git 加引号的路径，仍被扣住。在处理这一点之前，以带 tab 的名字在 CI workflow 目录下新增文件会返回 `allow_triage`；该绕过现已关闭并被钉住。
- `env VAR=value command` 前缀**不**被扣住——环境规则针对的是导出，不是普通命令前缀。
- 被截断的 diff 即使可见部分干净也被扣住；可信作者不会被任何新规则扣住。
- 采集步骤多读一个字节，使「恰好等于上限的读取」与「一个正好这么大的完整 diff」可区分。恰好两兆时截断旗标保持 false；多一个字节即变 true。

预检套件里原有三条用例断言「外部作者对 CI 与脚本目录的改动应放行」。它们被**改靶**到新策略而非删除。另有一条夹具原本缺 diff 头，因此一直在**没有真正走到路径检测**的情况下通过；现已带上真实头。

### 证据（Before & After）

N/A——无用户可见或 TUI 面。前后对比即上面的基线／分支重放。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### 运行环境（可选）

仅单元套件，外加在 `PATH` 上放一个打桩 `gh` 来驱动采集步骤的 shell 跨上限边界。无模型调用、无 runner 占用。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险／取舍：误报会把合法的外部贡献扣住等维护者放行。取样 80 个开放 PR（当时开放总数 578）：67 个作者无 write 权限，其中 7 个触及受保护面；该取样**不是全仓比率**。仓库自己的 network-policy 与 fetch 夹具含实例元数据地址，因此外部对它们的编辑也会被扣住。每次命中的代价是一次维护者决策，而不是拒绝贡献者——这也是选择「扣住」而非「关闭」的原因。
- 未验证／范围之外：给 CI runner 不挂云角色或加固实例元数据服务；给评审 agent 配默认拒绝的出网白名单；agent 撰写评论在发布前脱敏。同样未实测：diff API 自身是否可能对超大贡献返回被静默截短的 patch——见证字节只能检测**采集步骤**的截断，上游短读会以小于上限的体量到达、看起来完整。另有一条只记录不解释的观测：第二个探针的 review run 在第一道检查就因其 bot token 为空而中止，而同一分钟内一个仓内 PR 的 review 成功；机制未查明，因此「secret 为空」不被算作一道控制。
- 破坏性变更／迁移说明：无。既有发现码保留；新增发现码分别指向权限面、已识别的环境凭据来源、截断的 diff 与无法读取的 PR 元数据。来自外部作者的自动化依赖 PR 从此需要维护者显式放行，因为依赖清单在受保护集合内——它们是否应留在那里，是设计文档里的一个未决问题。

设计文档：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/pr-precheck-authority-gate/docs/design/pr-safety-precheck-authority-gate.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/pr-precheck-authority-gate/docs/design/pr-safety-precheck-authority-gate.zh-CN.md)

## 关联 Issue

引用 #18362 与 #18364（两个探针 PR）。不使用自动关闭关键字。

prs.title: perf(managed-agent): Avoid replay floor full-table scans
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The replay-floor candidate scan now uses a generated pending flag and a composite index, so discovery reads only pending Sessions in `gmt_modified` order and no longer falls back to a full table scan plus filesort. The same index-ordered lookup is used for batched event-tail reads by replacing the wide row-constructor `IN` with OR equality groups. Schema projection and row decoding include the new generated column.

## Why it's needed

At 200k candidate Sessions, candidate discovery used about 118 ms per 64-row batch, so a complete 3,125-batch pass spent roughly 6.1 minutes just finding targets, and it scanned and sorted the whole event-stream table on every pass. The new index reduces that stage to 2.0 seconds for the same 200k rows; the complete database-side advance pass, including every per-target transaction, measures 4.05 minutes versus an estimated 10.1 minutes before.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the focused H2 suite:
```bash
cd packages/managed-agent-server
mvn -q -pl verification -am -Dtest=ManagedEventTailsTest,ReplayFloorAdvancerTest,ReplayFloorAdvancerBacklogTest,ReplayFloorRetractionTest,ManagedSchemaProjectionTest,ManagedSchemaRowsTest,ManagedSchemaTest -DfailIfNoTests=false test
```
Expected: 45 tests, 0 failures and 0 errors. On MySQL, `EXPLAIN` of the candidate query should use `idx_ma_stream_replay_floor` as an index range scan with no `Using filesort`; after advancing a floor, `is_replay_floor_pending` should flip to 0.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: 200k-candidate query did a full table scan plus filesort, about 118 ms per 64 rows, about 6.1 minutes per 3,125-batch pass. Batched event-tail lookup with 500 pairs could fall back to a full scan.

After: index range scan with no filesort; 3,125 batches covering 200k rows complete in 2.008 seconds. A full database-side advance pass completes in 243.0 seconds with 200k targets and 0 remaining candidates. The 500-pair tail lookup returns in about 9.3 ms. Benchmarks used temporary table clones and stored procedures, which were dropped afterward; canonical test tables were not modified.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--: | :--: |
| macOS | Yes: focused Maven/H2 tests |
| Windows | Not tested |
| Linux | Not tested |

### Environment (optional)

Local Maven with Java 21 and H2 MySQL mode; MySQL 8.0.18-compatible test instance for the `EXPLAIN` checks and full-pass benchmark.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Adds one generated `TINYINT` column and one index to `ma_event_stream`, so every event-stream write maintains the extra index. The flag is derived from existing columns, so no application backfill or dual-write is needed.
- Not validated / out of scope: The full-pass number is database-side and excludes WAN RTT, Spring transaction overhead, and Java row mapping. Per-target advance remains the dominant cost at about 241 of 243 seconds and is not changed here.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None for fresh databases. Following the repository policy for the unreleased schema, the V1 baseline is updated in place instead of adding a migration; existing non-production databases need to be recreated or altered manually.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

Replay floor 的候选扫描现在使用一个生成列标记和一个复合索引，只按 `gmt_modified` 顺序读取仍待推进的 Session，不再退化为全表扫描加 filesort。批量事件尾部读取也改用同样的索引有序查找，把过宽的 row-constructor `IN` 替换为 OR 等值组。Schema 投影和行解码同步包含新增的生成列。

## 为什么需要

在 20 万候选 Session 的规模下，候选发现每批 64 行约需 118 ms，完整 3,125 批仅查找目标就要约 6.1 分钟，而且每次都会扫描并排序整张 event-stream 表。新增索引后，同样 20 万行的候选阶段降到 2.0 秒；包含每个目标事务在内的完整数据库端推进耗时实测 4.05 分钟，此前估算约 10.1 分钟。

## Reviewer 验证步骤

### 如何验证

运行聚焦的 H2 测试：
```bash
cd packages/managed-agent-server
mvn -q -pl verification -am -Dtest=ManagedEventTailsTest,ReplayFloorAdvancerTest,ReplayFloorAdvancerBacklogTest,ReplayFloorRetractionTest,ManagedSchemaProjectionTest,ManagedSchemaRowsTest,ManagedSchemaTest -DfailIfNoTests=false test
```
预期 45 个测试全部通过，0 failure、0 error。在 MySQL 上，候选查询的 `EXPLAIN` 应使用 `idx_ma_stream_replay_floor` 索引范围扫描，且不出现 `Using filesort`；推进 floor 后，`is_replay_floor_pending` 应变为 0。

### 证据（前后对比）

优化前：20 万候选查询做全表扫描加 filesort，每 64 行约 118 ms，3,125 批一轮约 6.1 分钟；500 对的批量事件尾部查询可能退化为全表扫描。

优化后：索引范围扫描且无 filesort；3,125 批覆盖 20 万行仅需 2.008 秒。完整数据库端推进一轮耗时 243.0 秒，处理 20 万个目标，剩余候选为 0。500 对的尾部查询约 9.3 ms。压测使用临时克隆表和存储过程，结束后均已删除；正式测试表未修改。

### 测试环境

| 系统 | 状态 |
| :--: | :--: |
| macOS | 已测试：聚焦的 Maven/H2 测试 |
| Windows | 未测试 |
| Linux | 未测试 |

### 环境说明

本地 Maven、Java 21、H2 MySQL 模式；MySQL 8.0.18 兼容测试实例用于 `EXPLAIN` 检查和完整推进压测。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：为 `ma_event_stream` 增加一个生成 `TINYINT` 列和一个索引，因此每次事件流写入都会维护额外索引。标记由现有列派生，不需要应用回填或双写。
- 未验证或不在范围内：完整推进数据是数据库端测量，不包含公网 RTT、Spring 事务开销和 Java 行映射。单目标推进仍占主要成本，243 秒中约 241 秒用于该阶段，本次未修改。
- 破坏性变更或迁移说明：全新数据库无影响。遵循仓库对未发布 schema 的策略，直接原地更新 V1 基线而不新增迁移；已有非生产数据库需要重建或手工变更。

</details>

prs.title: fix(core): accept other harnesses' names for file-tool arguments
prs.body:
## What this PR does

A call to the file-read, file-write or edit tool that names its path `path` instead of `file_path` now runs as if it had said `file_path`, and an edit call that says `old_str` / `new_str` runs as if it had said `old_string` / `new_string`. The names are rewritten once, when the scheduler takes the call in, so permission rules, hooks, approval prompts, checkpoints, telemetry and the tool all see the canonical names, on every surface (terminal UIs, headless, ACP sessions, subagents). The chat history keeps the call the model actually made; the places that read file paths back from the history (the read-cache bookkeeping of microcompaction, the read-residency check, the file list restored after compaction) apply the same names on a copy, so a cleared `path` read is not answered later as "unchanged". When a call sends both names, nothing changes: the canonical one wins, as before.

When a tool call still fails schema validation, the error now also names the arguments the tool did not recognise and lists the ones it accepts, for example `params must have required property 'command'. Unrecognized parameters: cmd. Accepted parameters: command, is_background, timeout, description, directory.` Before, the model only learned which argument was missing. A closed schema gets the same note, since its "must NOT have additional properties" does not name the key either. Schemas that can accept keys their top-level properties do not list (composition, `$ref`, pattern or open additional properties) get no note. A valid call with an extra key stays valid.

## Why it's needed

Some models name file-tool arguments the way another harness does. On the Harness Leaderboard, Qwen Code with the Flint model spent 2518 of 9274 tool calls (27 %) in 142 sampled trials on schema errors. With these aliases, 2375 of them (94 %) pass validation as sent: nearly all are these file tools with `path` instead of `file_path`, a few are edits with `old_str` / `new_str`; most of the other 143 lack a required argument altogether. 2462 of the 2464 `path` values were absolute paths, so the renamed calls run as they are. The model switched to `file_path` after an error in 104 of the 133 trials that had one, and 95 of those went back to `path` later, so a clearer error alone does not help it; accepting the name does.

For other models the existing error is usually enough: seven Bailian models (qwen3.7-plus, qwen3.8-flash, qwen-flash, qwen-plus, qwen3-coder-flash, glm-5, deepseek-v4.1-flash) switched to `file_path` on the next round after one injected `path` error. The unrecognised-argument note costs one line and tells any model which name it got wrong; its benefit over the current text was not measured. Design: [English](docs/design/2026-11-27-tool-arg-name-aliases.md) | [简体中文](docs/design/2026-11-27-tool-arg-name-aliases.zh-CN.md).

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Point Qwen Code at an OpenAI-compatible mock that answers with fixed tool calls and records the requests.

- Headless with `--yolo`: `read_file {"path": <abs path>}` returns the file; `write_file {"path": …, "content": "x"}` creates the file; `edit {"path": …, "old_str": "hello", "new_str": "hi"}` changes it.
- `read_file {"filepath": …}` and `run_shell_command {"cmd": "ls"}` fail with the missing-argument error followed by "Unrecognized parameters: filepath / cmd" and the accepted names.
- `read_file {"file_path": A, "path": B}` reads A.
- A deny rule `Read(./a.txt)` denies `read_file {"path": …/a.txt}` the same way it denies the `file_path` call.
- A PreToolUse hook that logs its input sees `file_path`.
- The next request's history still carries the model's call with `path`.
- ACP session with `tools.approvalMode: "default"`: `write_file {"path": …/b.txt}` asks for permission with the title, location and diff of `b.txt`, the same request as for `file_path`.
- A foreground subagent whose call is `read_file {"path": …}` reads the file.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Built CLI from this branch against the released 0.27.4, headless and ACP against the mock:

| Call | Before (0.27.4) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `read_file {"path"}` | `params must have required property 'file_path'` | file content |
| `write_file {"path", "content"}` | same error, no file | `Successfully created and wrote to new file` |
| `edit {"path", "old_str", "new_str"}` | same error | `The file: … has been updated.` |
| `read_file {"filepath"}` | `params must have required property 'file_path'` | `… 'file_path'. Unrecognized parameters: filepath. Accepted parameters: file_path, offset, limit, pages.` |
| `run_shell_command {"cmd"}` | `params must have required property 'command'` | `… 'command'. Unrecognized parameters: cmd. Accepted parameters: command, is_background, timeout, description, directory.` |
| deny `Read(./a.txt)`, `read_file {"path"}` | schema error | `denied by permission rules. Matching deny rule: "Read(./a.txt)"` |
| PreToolUse hook input | `{"path": …}` (the call then failed) | `{"file_path": …}` |
| ACP `write_file {"path"}`, default approval | schema error, no permission request | permission request "Writing to b.txt" with location and diff `b.txt` |
| subagent `read_file {"path"}` | schema error | file content |

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Built CLI (`npm run build`) against a local mock server; baseline with the released 0.27.4.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the aliases are a fixed list for three tools. A call that sends both names keeps today's behaviour. Arguments replaced after intake (a hook's updated input, an external-editor edit) are not aliased again. Clients or tests that match a schema error's full text see one more sentence when the call carried an undeclared key.
- Not validated / out of scope: macOS and Windows. Aliases for other tools or MCP tools, guessing names, and the hosted workspace file tools, which validate `file_path` themselves and say so. The benefit of the unrecognised-argument note was not measured with a model that needed it.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The schemas the model sees do not change.

## Linked Issues

None.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

读文件、写文件和编辑工具的调用，如果把路径参数写成 `path` 而不是 `file_path`，现在会按写了 `file_path` 的方式执行；编辑调用写成 `old_str` / `new_str` 时，按 `old_string` / `new_string` 执行。参数名在调度器接收调用时改写一次，所以在所有界面（终端 UI、headless、ACP 会话、子代理）中，权限规则、hook、审批提示、checkpoint、遥测和工具本身看到的都是标准参数名。聊天历史保留模型实际发出的调用；从历史中读回文件路径的地方（microcompaction 的读取缓存记录、读取驻留检查、压缩后恢复的文件列表）在副本上套用同样的名字，因此被清除的 `path` 读取不会在之后被当作“未变化”来回答。调用同时带两种名字时不做改动：和以前一样以标准名为准。

工具调用仍然没通过 schema 校验时，报错现在还会点出工具不认识的参数，并列出它接受的参数，例如 `params must have required property 'command'. Unrecognized parameters: cmd. Accepted parameters: command, is_background, timeout, description, directory.`。以前模型只能知道缺了哪个参数。封闭的 schema 也会带上这句说明，因为它的 "must NOT have additional properties" 同样不点名是哪个键。可能接受顶层 properties 之外的键的 schema（组合、`$ref`、pattern 或开放的 additional properties）不加说明。带多余键的合法调用仍然合法。

## 为什么需要

有些模型按别的 harness 的方式给文件工具的参数命名。在 Harness Leaderboard 上，Qwen Code 配 Flint 模型，抽样的 142 个 trial 里 9274 次工具调用有 2518 次（27%）花在 schema 错误上。套用这些别名后，其中 2375 次（94%）按原样就能通过校验：几乎都是这几个文件工具用 `path` 代替 `file_path`，少数是编辑时用 `old_str` / `new_str`；其余 143 次大多是完全缺了某个必填参数。2464 个 `path` 值中有 2462 个是绝对路径，所以改名后的调用可以直接执行。出过错的 133 个 trial 中，有 104 个在报错后改用过 `file_path`，其中 95 个后来又回到了 `path`，所以只靠更清楚的报错帮不了它；接受这个名字才行。

对其他模型来说，现有报错通常就够了：百炼的 7 个模型（qwen3.7-plus、qwen3.8-flash、qwen-flash、qwen-plus、qwen3-coder-flash、glm-5、deepseek-v4.1-flash）在注入一次 `path` 错误后，下一轮都改用了 `file_path`。未知参数的说明只多一行，能告诉任何模型它写错了哪个名字；相比现有文本的收益没有测量过。设计文档：[English](docs/design/2026-11-27-tool-arg-name-aliases.md) | [简体中文](docs/design/2026-11-27-tool-arg-name-aliases.zh-CN.md)。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

让 Qwen Code 连接一个用固定工具调用回复并记录请求的 OpenAI 兼容模拟服务。

- headless 加 `--yolo`：`read_file {"path": <绝对路径>}` 返回文件内容；`write_file {"path": …, "content": "x"}` 创建文件；`edit {"path": …, "old_str": "hello", "new_str": "hi"}` 修改文件。
- `read_file {"filepath": …}` 和 `run_shell_command {"cmd": "ls"}` 失败，报错是缺少参数的那句话，后面跟着 "Unrecognized parameters: filepath / cmd" 和可用的参数名。
- `read_file {"file_path": A, "path": B}` 读取 A。
- deny 规则 `Read(./a.txt)` 拒绝 `read_file {"path": …/a.txt}`，和拒绝 `file_path` 调用的方式相同。
- 记录输入的 PreToolUse hook 看到的是 `file_path`。
- 下一次请求的历史中仍是模型带 `path` 的调用。
- ACP 会话、`tools.approvalMode: "default"`：`write_file {"path": …/b.txt}` 请求权限时带 `b.txt` 的标题、位置和 diff，与 `file_path` 时的请求相同。
- 前台子代理发出 `read_file {"path": …}` 时能读到文件。

### 证据（修改前后）

本分支构建的 CLI 与已发布的 0.27.4 对比，headless 和 ACP 对接模拟服务：

| 调用 | 修改前（0.27.4） | 修改后 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `read_file {"path"}` | `params must have required property 'file_path'` | 文件内容 |
| `write_file {"path", "content"}` | 同样的报错，没有文件 | `Successfully created and wrote to new file` |
| `edit {"path", "old_str", "new_str"}` | 同样的报错 | `The file: … has been updated.` |
| `read_file {"filepath"}` | `params must have required property 'file_path'` | `… 'file_path'. Unrecognized parameters: filepath. Accepted parameters: file_path, offset, limit, pages.` |
| `run_shell_command {"cmd"}` | `params must have required property 'command'` | `… 'command'. Unrecognized parameters: cmd. Accepted parameters: command, is_background, timeout, description, directory.` |
| deny `Read(./a.txt)`，`read_file {"path"}` | schema 错误 | `denied by permission rules. Matching deny rule: "Read(./a.txt)"` |
| PreToolUse hook 输入 | `{"path": …}`（调用随后失败） | `{"file_path": …}` |
| ACP `write_file {"path"}`，默认审批 | schema 错误，没有权限请求 | 权限请求 "Writing to b.txt"，带 `b.txt` 的位置和 diff |
| 子代理 `read_file {"path"}` | schema 错误 | 文件内容 |

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅  |

### 环境（可选）

已构建的 CLI（`npm run build`）对接本地模拟服务；基线为已发布的 0.27.4。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：别名是针对三个工具的固定列表。同时带两种名字的调用保持现在的行为。接收之后被替换的参数（hook 的 updated input、外部编辑器中的修改）不会再次套用别名。按 schema 报错全文匹配的客户端或测试，在调用带有未声明键时会多看到一句话。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：macOS 和 Windows。其他工具或 MCP 工具的别名、猜测参数名，以及托管工作区的文件工具（它们自行校验 `file_path` 并会明确说明）。未知参数说明的收益没有用真正需要它的模型测量过。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。模型看到的 schema 不变。

## 关联 Issue

无。
