prs.title: fix(core): stop worktree snapshot capture from freezing the daemon event loop
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Three defects in the worktree-retention snapshot path introduced by #18009 are fixed. The post-capture checkout check now verifies file membership with a `Set` lookup instead of a per-entry linear scan, so the check is O(N) rather than O(N^2). The snapshot archive no longer includes a checkout's own nested managed-worktree directory or Qwen's regenerable `.qwen/tmp` and `.qwen/logs` caches, through the same exclusion matcher the archive and the post-capture check share, so the two geometries cannot disagree. The retention sweep re-reads `worktree.maxRetained` before each candidate's capture instead of once per sweep.

## Why it's needed

#18489 reports a `qwen serve` daemon on v0.28.7 (23 workspaces, 300k-file snapshots) freezing its whole event loop for 376–467 s, starving `/health` and every other route. A `perf` capture against the frozen process put 99.87% of samples in `Builtins_ArrayIncludesSmiOrObject` inside a microtask, and 55 snapshot archives totalled 7.27 GiB, 93.2% of the largest being nested `.qwen/` content.

Every reported number is the reporter's own measurement on Linux; nothing here reproduces a full daemon.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

The reported acceptance sentence is "a large capture must not freeze the event loop, and one checkout must not produce an unbounded archive". Neither is reachable through a unit fixture alone, so the primary instrument is a mechanism witness that drives the real `captureWorktreeSnapshot` path with a synthetic checkout, plus one timer that records the longest stall:

| instrument | exercises | cannot show |
| --- | --- | --- |
| mechanism witness (scratch harness, not committed) | the real capture path and the reported scan shape at 1k–300k members | a full daemon, multi-workspace scheduling, real `.qwen/` content |
| `worktree-snapshot-service.test.ts` (new + existing) | archive membership, restore, post-capture check | event-loop liveness at production scale |
| `worktree-retention.test.ts` (new) | sweep re-read of `maxRetained` across candidates | capture cost reduction |

Mechanism witness, reported scan shape versus the fixed Set lookup, one synchronous pass over N members:

```text
members=1,000     includes()     6 ms   Set.has()   ~0 ms
members=30,000    includes()   440 ms   Set.has()    2 ms
members=300,000   includes() 41,902 ms  Set.has()   14 ms   (0 timer ticks during the stall)
```

Same witness through the real capture path, with a 300,000-entry nested `.qwen/tmp` tree plus `.qwen/worktrees/` and a stated `.qwen/skills/` subject:

```text
origin/main   captureMs=11,408  archiveMembers=300,013  .qwen/tmp=30,002  checkoutMatchesCapture=true
this branch   captureMs=   112  archiveMembers=      7  .qwen/tmp=     0  .qwen/skills=3 (kept)
```

The mutation control is the `origin/main` column itself: the same harness, pointed at the unpatched tree (`REPRO_ROOT`), reproduces both the stall and the unbounded archive.

Local suites on macOS arm64, Node v22.23.4:

- `packages/core/src/services/worktree-snapshot-service.test.ts`: 86 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is `refuses capture when a deleted path is not valid UTF-8`, which fails identically on unmodified `origin/main` (`EPERM` creating a non-UTF-8 filename under this sandbox). The three new/covering tests pass.
- `packages/cli/src/serve/server/worktree-retention.test.ts`: the new test passes; 47 tests in that file fail identically on unmodified `origin/main` (`snapshot failed: ... an in-progress git operation holds private state`), so they are environmental, not from this change. Mutation control: with the new re-check disabled, the new test fails (`expected 2 to be 1`), i.e. it catches the reported capture-and-discard sweep.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — daemon-internal change, no UI surface. The tables above are the before/after.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅    |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   N/A   |

The reporter's Linux x86_64 / Node v26 numbers were not re-run; the defect is platform-independent string scanning, and the failing boundary is reproduced on macOS.

### Environment (optional)

Local checkout, dependencies linked from the repo's own install; unit tests run with `vitest run` per package, witness harness run under Node's type-stripping loader.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a snapshot no longer contains `.qwen/tmp` or `.qwen/logs`. Both are regenerable scratch/log state, not session work; `.qwen/skills`, `.qwen/commands`, `settings.json`, drafts and any other `.qwen/` path are still archived. A checkout's nested `.qwen/worktrees/` holds *other* checkouts, which retention already manages on their own behalf.
- Not validated / out of scope: the full daemon, multi-workspace scheduling, and the reporter's numbers on Linux. Deliberately not changed: defects 3 (W² 30 s timers and the per-tick `retention scopes=` log) and 4 (retry/backoff on repeated capture failures) from the issue. Both need a design call — one daemon-wide scheduler and a circuit breaker — and are better as a follow-up than smuggled into this fix.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. Existing archives remain readable; older large archives are unaffected and still pruned by the existing quota.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #18489

## 为什么需要

#18489 报告 v0.28.7 上的 `qwen serve` 守护进程（23 个工作区、30 万文件的快照）整体事件循环冻结 376–467 秒，`/health` 与所有其他路由都被饿死。针对冻结进程的 `perf` 采样显示 99.87% 的样本落在微任务内的 `Builtins_ArrayIncludesSmiOrObject`；55 个快照归档合计 7.27 GiB，其中最大归档的 93.2% 是嵌套的 `.qwen/` 内容。

### 测试平台

| :--------: | :--: |

|  🐧 Linux  | N/A  |

未复跑报告者的 Linux x86_64 / Node v26 数据；该缺陷与平台无关，失败边界已在 macOS 上复现。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：快照不再包含 `.qwen/tmp` 与 `.qwen/logs`。二者是可再生的临时与日志状态，不属于会话工作内容；`.qwen/skills`、`.qwen/commands`、`settings.json`、草稿及任何其他 `.qwen/` 路径仍会被归档。检出目录下嵌套的 `.qwen/worktrees/` 存放的是*其他*检出，其保留由各自负责。
- 未验证 / 范围外：完整守护进程、多工作区调度，以及报告者在 Linux 上的数据。有意未改动：issue 中的第 3 项（W² 的 30 秒定时器与每 tick 的 `retention scopes=` 日志）与第 4 项（重复捕获失败的退避/熔断）。二者都需要设计决策——守护进程级单一调度器与熔断器——更适合作为后续工作，而不是塞进本次修复。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。既有归档仍可读取；较旧的大归档不受影响，仍由现有配额清理。

prs.title: perf(core): persist prompt-time sidecar, bound cold scans, and extend transcript index incrementally
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This PR eliminates the repeated full-transcript index rebuild storms triggered by multi-workspace session listings and actively appending transcripts while preserving the existing session summary and transcript pagination contracts.

- Persists a lightweight per-session prompt-time sidecar checkpoint storing the transcript file identity, snapshot size, modification timestamp, active leaf identifier, first-record ownership metadata, and a 64-byte suffix fingerprint. Trusted prompt writes update it, rewinds and message-group deletions remove it, trusted cold reads self-heal it once project ownership is verified, and archive, unarchive, conflict resolution, and session deletion keep it synchronized. Read-only secondary workspace listings and foreign-project transcripts never write the sidecar.
- Accelerates cold prompt-time resolution through an exact-match O(1) sidecar hit, a suffix-verified tail-only linear extension on append-only growth (capped to bounded record counts and falling back automatically on rewinds, branches, duplicate identifiers, or prefix rewrites), and a dedicated lightweight cold scanner that extracts only minimal envelope fields instead of building a full dense transcript index or polluting the dense index cache.
- Introduces a process-wide concurrency gate across cold transcript scans and index builds (defaulting to two concurrent operations) and propagates request cancellation through refcounted shared in-flight tasks, queued semaphore waiters, and line-streaming reads so abandoned requests stop reading promptly without aborting other active sharers.
- Extends cached physical transcript indexes incrementally on append-only growth from the largest valid cached prefix after verifying the 64-byte boundary suffix fingerprint. Incremental extensions use copy-on-write over shared index maps, branch-point records, and turn ordinals (clearing stale ordinals for rewound turns) so frozen cursors and turn snapshots remain immutable, while keeping continuation state sanitized and atomically accounted within each cache entry's existing byte-budget class.

## Why it's needed

Production profiling on multi-workspace daemons (`#17889`) showed that default session-list requests across dozens of workspaces could simultaneously trigger full dense-index builds on the main thread during cold starts, cache evictions, or owner re-registrations, and that active append traffic invalidated the dense index cache key on every write—forcing repeated full-file parses from byte zero and causing multi-minute event-loop stalls that starved health checks. Because external consumers rely on the optional last-human-prompt timestamp remaining present on default session lists, removing the field is not acceptable; instead, both prompt-time enrichment and append-only transcript indexing must avoid redundant full-file rebuilds and bound main-thread concurrency and abandoned work.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- **Cold list & restart behavior**: Open or list a workspace with persisted sessions after a daemon restart. Confirm that the initial cold prompt-time lookup resolves the exact latest human prompt timestamp without constructing a full dense transcript index, persists the prompt-time sidecar for trusted workspace-owned sessions, and serves subsequent post-restart listings directly from the sidecar without re-reading the transcript file.
- **Append, rewind, and rewrite accuracy**: Append assistant output and a new human prompt to a session with an existing sidecar and restart or clear memory caches; confirm only the appended tail is scanned and the returned timestamp updates accurately. Then append a rewind record branching back to an earlier turn, corrupt the sidecar, or rewrite the prefix in place on the same inode; confirm each case safely falls back to a full lightweight scan and returns the authoritative active-branch timestamp.
- **Trust and lifecycle boundaries**: List a read-only secondary workspace and a transcript belonging to a foreign workspace; confirm no sidecar is written to disk. Verify that recording a user prompt creates the sidecar, archiving and unarchiving move it between active and archive storage while keeping archived reads fast, rewinding removes it, and deleting the session cleans it up.
- **Concurrency and cancellation**: Issue many concurrent cold prompt-time reads across multiple workspaces while aborting both a queued request and one of two shared waiters; confirm active cold scans stay bounded by the process-wide concurrency cap, the aborted queued request never opens the transcript, aborting a sole waiter stops streaming early, and aborting one of two shared waiters leaves the surviving caller unaffected.
- **Incremental transcript index extension**: Read a transcript page and retain its frozen cursor, append new turns and branch checkpoints, then append a rewind and a duplicate-identifier fragment; confirm subsequent reads extend from the cached prefix offset, match a fresh cold rebuild field-for-field, clear turn anchors for rewound turns, leave the earlier frozen cursor and turn snapshot unchanged, and fall back to a full build if the prefix is rewritten in place longer on the same inode.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (backend daemon/core performance and indexing change; no TUI or visual layout changes).

Verified locally with clean full repository build, full workspace and integration typecheck, ESLint, Prettier, and 860 passing unit tests covering the new sidecar codec, lightweight scan, tail linear extension, concurrency gate, refcounted cancellation, incremental index parity, recording/archive/removal lifecycle, and read-only session-list isolation.

### Tested on

| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Local Node.js v22.22.2 on macOS (arm64); verified with full workspace build, full typecheck, ESLint, Prettier, and package-level Vitest suites.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Retaining compact continuation hints alongside cached transcript indexes adds a small per-entry byte footprint within existing cache class budgets (sanitized to essential fields and dropped automatically when it would cross a budget class or exceed the class cap), and trusted sessions gain one small derived sidecar file per active/archived transcript.
- Not validated / out of scope: Offloading very large cold index builds onto worker threads remains separate follow-up work under `#17889`. Windows and Linux validation will run in CI.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None. Missing, older, or corrupt prompt-time sidecars degrade transparently to the lightweight transcript scan, and no wire protocol or external API contracts change.

多工作区 daemon 的生产采样（`#17889`）显示，几十个工作区的默认会话列表请求在冷启动、缓存淘汰或 owner 重新注册时会同时在主线程扇出大量全量稠密索引构建，且活跃会话的每次追加都会使稠密索引缓存键失效，触发从字节 0 开始的反复全量解析，造成数分钟级别的事件循环卡顿并饿死健康检查。由于外部消费者依赖默认会话列表中的可选最近用户提问时间字段，不能简单删除该字段；必须同时降低提问时间补齐与追加态索引重建的成本，并收紧主线程并发与取消清理边界。

- **追加、回退与改写准确性**：向已有 sidecar 的会话依次追加助手输出和新用户提问并清空内存缓存，确认仅扫描新增尾部区间且时间戳准确推进。随后分别追加回跳到更早轮次的 rewind 记录、损坏 sidecar 文件以及在同 inode 原地改写前缀，确认均安全回退到轻量全量扫描并返回活动分支的真实时间戳。
- **信任与生命周期边界**：对只读次级工作区与跨项目转录执行列表读取，确认磁盘不生成 sidecar。验证记录用户提问会写入 sidecar，归档与取消归档会同步迁移 sidecar 且归档读取依然零扫描，rewind 会删除 sidecar，删除会话会彻底清理 sidecar。

- **增量转录索引扩展**：读取转录页并保留冻结游标，追加新轮次与分支检查点，再追加 rewind 与重复标识片段。确认后续读取从已缓存前缀偏移增量扩展，结果与清空缓存后的全量重建逐字段一致，被 rewind 移除轮次的锚点被正确清除，旧冻结游标与轮次快照保持不受影响；若同 inode 原地改写前缀得更长，则安全回退到从头全量构建。

prs.title: feat(core,cli): add ledger-backed session census and daemon session-end usage persistence
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This follow-up to #17902 completes the two remaining session-accounting gaps across the daemon status Usage dashboard and cross-session `/stats`:

- **Ledger-backed distinct-session census:** Summary session counts, daily session bars, cross-session statistics session counts, and period-over-period session deltas now count distinct active session identities across the union of per-request ledger entries and ended non-supplement session records in the window. A conversation resumed multiple times within a window now counts once instead of once per run, and ledger-only days (such as processes killed before exit or historical daemon sessions that never persisted a summary record) report their actual active session count instead of zero.
- **Daemon and ACP session-end usage persistence:** Live per-session telemetry is now tracked separately from replayed or restored transcript history. When a daemon or ACP session is explicitly closed, retired while idle, or torn down during graceful shutdown, its own live delta (tokens, tools, changed lines, skills, duration, project, and request execution identities) is persisted at most once as a run-scoped summary record. Resumed sessions closed with no new live activity write nothing.
- **Localized daily chart subtitle:** The daily sessions chart subtitle in the daemon status Usage view is updated across all locales (`en`, `zh-CN`, `zh-TW`, `ru`) from ended runs per day to active sessions per day.

## Why it's needed

After #17902 aligned token, request, latency, and cache-read totals with the per-request ledger, session counts still came solely from persisted summary records. On heavy histories, hundreds of sessions recorded in the per-request ledger were missing from the session tile and daily chart — producing days with positive token consumption but zero sessions — while a single conversation resumed multiple times was overcounted as multiple sessions. At the same time, daemon and Web Shell sessions discarded their in-memory telemetry on close without persisting a summary record, losing durable per-project, tool, changed-line, duration, and skill metadata and forcing repeated transcript replay on dashboard refresh.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. **Deduplicated distinct-session counting:** Run a conversation once and resume the same conversation for a second turn in a separate process so two run-scoped summary records share one session identity. Open the daemon status Usage dashboard (Today and 7D) and `/stats`: the session total and daily session bar for that day should show `1` (while token and request totals sum both runs).
2. **Ledger-only session census:** In an isolated home containing only per-request ledger files (no persisted summary records and no transcripts, simulating killed processes or unpersisted historical daemon sessions), query the daemon Usage dashboard and `/stats`: the session count, daily session bar, and completed-day session delta should reflect the exact distinct session identities present in the ledger rather than `0` or `null`.
3. **Daemon / ACP session-end persistence without replay inflation:** Start an ACP or daemon session, execute one prompt, and close the session cleanly: a single run-scoped summary record should be appended with that run's exact token, project, and execution-identity delta matching the ledger. Then reload (resume) the same session and close it without sending a new prompt: no second summary record should be written.
4. **Localized daily sessions subtitle:** Open the daemon status Usage tab in Web Shell under `en`, `zh-CN`, `zh-TW`, and `ru` and verify the daily sessions subtitle reads `active sessions per day` / `每日活跃会话数` / `每日活躍會話數` / `активные сессии по дням`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Measured against freshly built CLI, daemon, and ACP processes in isolated temporary homes using an ephemeral loopback mock model:

| Scenario | Before | After | Expected / Ledger truth |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Same session resumed once (2 run-scoped records, 4 requests / 600 tokens) | `sessions: 2`, `daily[today].sessions: 2` | `sessions: 1`, `daily[today].sessions: 1` | `1` distinct active session |
| Ledger-only history (summary records and transcripts deleted; 4 requests / 600 tokens) | `sessions: 0`, `daily[today].sessions: 0` | `sessions: 1`, `daily[today].sessions: 1` | `1` distinct active session |
| Real ACP session (`session/new` -> `session/prompt` -> `qwen/control/session/close`) | `0` summary records persisted on close | `1` run-scoped record (`300` tokens, 2 execution IDs, project recorded) | `300` tokens / 2 ledger rows |
| Resumed ACP session closed with zero new activity (`session/load` -> close) | N/A (never persisted) | `0` new records written (total stays `1`, exit code `0`) | `0` replay copies |
| Web Shell daily sessions subtitle (`en` / `zh-CN` / `zh-TW` / `ru`) | `runs ended per day` / `每日结束运行数` / `每日結束執行數` / `завершённые запуски по дням` | `active sessions per day` / `每日活跃会话数` / `每日活躍會話數` / `активные сессии по дням` | Matches active-session semantics |

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Local full workspace build, full typecheck (including integration tests), bundle build, ESLint, Prettier, focused unit test suites (core 458 passed, CLI 76 passed / 1 skipped plus 2 ACP close-wiring tests, Web Shell 13 passed across all 4 locales), and real-process CLI, daemon, and ACP end-to-end runs in isolated temporary homes.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: switching from run-record counts to distinct active session identities changes the displayed session number for histories where one conversation is resumed multiple times in the same window (now counted once instead of once per run), while increasing counts on histories with unpersisted ledger-only runs. The per-request ledger intentionally remains at schema version 1 without storing workspace paths to preserve the existing path-privacy boundary; per-project, tool, file, and skill metadata for daemon sessions now comes from persisting summary records at session close.
- Not validated / out of scope: Windows and Linux native local runs (covered by CI); modifying the per-request ledger schema to store project paths; changing low-level record-only aggregation helpers.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. Existing summary records and per-request ledger files require no migration, and the API payload shape is unchanged.

Design document: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/usage-ledger-session-census/docs/design/2026-11-25-usage-ledger-session-census.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/usage-ledger-session-census/docs/design/2026-11-25-usage-ledger-session-census.zh-CN.md). Both versions are complete and synchronized.

## Linked Issues

## 这个 PR 做了什么

本 PR 是 #17902 的直接后续，补齐了 Daemon 状态用量面板与跨会话 `/stats` 遗留的两项会话统计缺口：

- **台账口径唯一活跃会话普查：** 汇总会话数、每日会话柱状图、跨会话统计会话数以及环比会话变化现在统一统计时间窗口内「逐请求台账记录的会话 ∪ 已结束非补充运行记录的会话」的唯一会话数。同一会话在窗口内被多次恢复现在计为 1 次而非按运行次数重复累加；仅存在于台账中的日期（例如退出前被强杀的进程或历史未落盘的 daemon 会话）也会显示真实活跃会话数，不再出现有 token 消耗但会话数为 0 的情况。
- **Daemon 与 ACP 会话结束用量持久化：** 按会话隔离维护实时遥测与运行起始时钟，与重放或恢复的历史记录严格分离。当 daemon 或 ACP 会话显式关闭、空闲回收或随守护进程优雅停机销毁时，只将本会话自身产生的实时增量（token、工具、变更行数、技能、时长、项目及执行 ID）以按运行记录形式至多持久化一次；恢复后无新实时活动直接关闭则零写入。
- **多语种每日会话图副标题更新：** Web Shell 全部语种（`en`、`zh-CN`、`zh-TW`、`ru`）将每日会话图的副标题由「每日结束运行数」同步更新为「每日活跃会话数」。

## 为什么需要

在 #17902 将 token、请求数、平均延迟与缓存读取率对齐逐请求台账后，会话计数仍仅依赖持久化的摘要记录。在重量级历史上，逐请求台账中记录的大量会话在面板与每日图表中缺失，导致出现有 token 消耗却显示 0 会话的日期，同时同一会话多次恢复又会被重复算成多个会话。另一方面，daemon 与 Web Shell 会话在关闭时直接丢弃内存遥测而从未落盘摘要记录，导致关闭后丢失按项目、工具、代码变更、时长与技能明细，并迫使每次刷新重复重放 transcript。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

1. **唯一活跃会话去重：** 在两个进程中对同一会话运行首次对话与恢复续聊，生成两条共享同一会话 ID 的按运行记录。查看 Daemon 用量面板（今日 / 7 天）与 `/stats`：会话总数与当日每日会话柱应显示 `1`（同时 token 与请求数汇总两次运行）。
2. **纯台账会话普查：** 在仅保留逐请求台账文件（无摘要记录文件、无 transcript，模拟进程被强杀或历史未落盘 daemon 会话）的隔离 home 中查看 Daemon 用量面板与 `/stats`：会话数、每日会话柱以及已完成日环比应准确反映台账中的唯一会话数，而非 `0` 或 `null`。
3. **Daemon / ACP 会话结束落盘且不重放计费：** 启动 ACP 或 daemon 会话，执行一轮对话后正常关闭会话：应恰好追加 1 条按运行摘要记录，其 token、项目与执行 ID 增量与台账精确一致。随后重新加载（恢复）同一会话且不发送新请求直接关闭：不应追加新的重复记录。
4. **多语种副标题核对：** 在 Web Shell 中分别切换 `en`、`zh-CN`、`zh-TW`、`ru` 打开 Daemon 状态用量页，确认每日会话副标题显示为 `active sessions per day` / `每日活跃会话数` / `每日活躍會話數` / `активные сессии по дням`。

### 证据（修前与修后）

基于新鲜构建的 CLI、daemon 与 ACP 进程，在隔离临时 home 中连接一次性本地 mock 模型实测：

| 场景 | 修前 | 修后 | 预期 / 台账真值 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 同一会话恢复一次（2 条按运行记录，4 请求 / 600 token） | `sessions: 2`、`daily[today].sessions: 2` | `sessions: 1`、`daily[today].sessions: 1` | `1` 个唯一活跃会话 |
| 纯台账历史（删除摘要记录与 transcript；4 请求 / 600 token） | `sessions: 0`、`daily[today].sessions: 0` | `sessions: 1`、`daily[today].sessions: 1` | `1` 个唯一活跃会话 |
| 真实 ACP 会话（新建 → 提问 → 关闭） | 关闭时持久化 `0` 条摘要记录 | 落盘 `1` 条按运行记录（`300` token、2 个执行 ID、含项目路径） | `300` token / 2 条台账行 |
| 恢复后的 ACP 会话无新活动直接关闭 | N/A（此前从未落盘） | 新增 `0` 条记录（总数保持 `1`，退出码 `0`） | `0` 条重放副本 |
| Web Shell 每日会话副标题（`en` / `zh-CN` / `zh-TW` / `ru`） | `runs ended per day` / `每日结束运行数` / `每日結束執行數` / `завершённые запуски по дням` | `active sessions per day` / `每日活跃会话数` / `每日活躍會話數` / `активные сессии по дням` | 与活跃会话口径一致 |

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

### 环境（可选）

本地全仓构建、全仓类型检查（含集成测试）、bundle 打包、ESLint、Prettier、核心单元测试（core 458 passed、CLI 76 passed / 1 skipped 及 2 条 ACP 关闭接线测试、Web Shell 4 语种 13 passed），以及隔离临时 home 下的真实 CLI、daemon 与 ACP 进程端到端实测。

prs.title: feat(web-shell): support optional session adapters
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds an optional session adapter for hosts embedding WebShell. The adapter can supply the client and handle standalone session creation, history restoration, and prompt submission. Both paths use the same WebShell UI. Hosts that omit the adapter continue to use the daemon client.

## Why it's needed

An embedding host may use a session service that assigns its own IDs, has no workspace directory, and reports prompt completion through a separate stream. The adapter gives the host a place to handle those differences while reusing WebShell's composer and transcript.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Open WebShell against a daemon with no adapter configured. Create a session, send a prompt, refresh the session URL, and send a follow-up. Verify that the transcript is restored, the session ID is reused, and requests reach the daemon.
2. Mount WebShell with a session adapter. Send the first prompt and verify that creation runs once, the UI adopts the service-assigned ID, and the reply renders in the transcript. Reload that URL and send a follow-up. Verify that history is restored and the follow-up uses the same ID without another create request.
3. For an adapter-backed prompt, interrupt the response stream after admission. Verify that the failure reaches the UI and the prompt is not automatically submitted a second time.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A for visual comparison. Earlier integration smoke tests covered daemon session creation, reply, and refresh, and adapter-backed creation, reply, refresh, and same-session follow-up. Both package builds and typechecks passed on this branch, along with 171 SDK tests and 1,036 Web Shell tests.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ SDK and Web Shell builds, typechecks, and focused tests passed locally. |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ Not tested |

### Environment (optional)

Local browser smoke tests used the same WebShell build for the daemon and adapter-backed routes.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Both routes share session lifecycle code. Review workspace notification scoping and event reconnect behavior in the daemon path.
- A live embedding backend and end-to-end notification scoping remain unverified. The local provider test uses a simulated host stream.
- The SDK constructor accepts standalone metadata without a workspace directory. `DaemonSessionClient.workspaceCwd` remains a string and returns an empty string for these sessions. Adapter hosts supply user messages through live events and restored history. Continuations and side questions use the session client directly.

## Linked Issues

None.

## 为什么需要这项改动

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

prs.title: fix(cli): preserve archive coordinator prefix without sidecars
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Restores a deterministic synchronous archive-coordinator prefix for sessions without a worktree sidecar and keeps unsafe sidecar entries on the strict fail-closed path.

- Only a genuine `ENOENT` from a synchronous `lstat` allows the no-sidecar path to skip sidecar lock inspection.
- Dangling symlinks and non-regular entries still reach the existing strict reader and produce `Could not read worktree sidecar for archive lock: unsafe sidecar file type`; unreadable parents surface their original stat error (`EACCES` / `ENOTDIR`) through the same strict path.
- Archive and unarchive regression tests now pin both the synchronous coordinator entry and the unsafe-sidecar refusal.

The export-budget conflict with main was resolved by adopting #18456 unchanged. This PR now has no net diff in `packages/web-templates/src/export-html/build.mjs`.

## Why it's needed

PR #18009's asynchronous sidecar probes allowed another session in the same batch to acquire its coordinator first. A gate-race fixture could then reject asynchronously and leave an unhandled `SessionArchivingError` even after all test assertions passed on retry.

The first fix used `existsSync`, which review correctly identified as unsafe because it treats dangling symlinks and other stat failures as absent. The final implementation uses the same missing-vs-invalid distinction as the strict reader while preserving the synchronous prefix.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Run `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run --no-coverage src/serve/server/session-archive.test.ts`: **156/156 passed**.
- Confirm the two no-sidecar tests still observe `assertNotTransitioning` throw synchronously when the batch Promise is returned.
- Confirm the new archive/unarchive dangling-symlink cases return one strict-read error and do not move the transcript.
- Confirm the unreadable parent-directory case rejects with `EACCES` and never calls `move()`. It is gated on `arePermissionBitsEnforced()` rather than `getuid()`, so it also runs on root CI lanes where the DAC capabilities are dropped.
- Real daemon HTTP tests in `integration-tests/cli/qwen-serve-routes.test.ts` also passed: no-sidecar batch archive/unarchive restored each transcript byte-identical to its pre-archive bytes (user prompt, assistant reply and `custom_title` system record; titles are unique per attempt so the retitle-on-collision path cannot fire). A dangling sidecar symlink was rejected without moving the transcript. The complete route and hosted-harness integration suites passed **55/55** (`qwen-serve-routes` 44 + `hosted-harness-process` 11) on a bundle rebuilt from the final head.
- Negative witnesses measured locally: restoring the old `existsSync` predicate fails exactly the two new dangling-symlink tests; treating every stat error as missing fails the unreadable-parent case; dropping the synchronous prefix fails the prefix cases; a mutant that appends a stray `system` record on unarchive fails the byte-identical HTTP assertion while the previous `slice(1)` check stayed green. Every mutated file was restored byte-identically, and the real-daemon `existsSync` mutation archived the session that the fixed build rejects.
- CLI build and typecheck passed after the final code change. The web-templates build passed with the #18456 thresholds (`2157683` actual bytes).

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — backend coordination and regression-test change, no UI behavior changed.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested locally; covered by CI |
|  🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested locally; covered by CI |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ Archive suite, CLI build/typecheck, export build and mutation witness run locally |

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: restores the synchronous prefix only when both sidecar entries are genuinely missing; every other case retains the strict read and ownership-lock path.
- Not validated / out of scope: no budget, schema, retention or restore semantics are changed by the final diff. CI is still settling on the new head and is not claimed green here.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Follow-up to [PR #18009](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18009), already merged as `ed5d033e813f90ecb12153ae3307fd035d4b3741`. The separate non-blocking hardening issue #18446 remains open. The pre-existing `existsSync` copies on the session-delete fast path are tracked in #18475 and are not part of this PR.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

对没有 worktree sidecar 的会话恢复确定性的同步归档协调器前缀，同时让不安全 sidecar 继续走严格 fail-closed 路径。

- 只有同步 `lstat` 返回真正的 `ENOENT` 时，才允许跳过 sidecar 锁检查。
- 悬空符号链接和其它非常规条目仍进入已有严格读取器，返回 `Could not read worktree sidecar for archive lock: unsafe sidecar file type`；父目录不可读则通过同一严格路径返回原始 stat 错误（`EACCES` / `ENOTDIR`）。
- archive 与 unarchive 回归测试同时钉住同步协调器入口和不安全 sidecar 的拒绝行为。

导出预算与 main 的冲突通过原样采用 #18456 解决。最终 PR 不再修改 `packages/web-templates/src/export-html/build.mjs`。

## 为什么要这样做

PR #18009 的异步 sidecar 探测会让同批次另一个会话先取得协调器，使 gate-race 用例异步拒绝，并在测试重试通过后仍遗留未处理的 `SessionArchivingError`。

第一版使用 `existsSync`，评审正确指出它会把悬空符号链接和其它 stat 错误误判为不存在。最终实现采用与严格读取器一致的 missing/invalid 区分，同时保留同步前缀。

## 审阅者验证计划

### 如何核验

- 运行 `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run --no-coverage src/serve/server/session-archive.test.ts`：**156/156 通过**。
- 两条无 sidecar 用例仍在批次 Promise 返回时同步观察到 `assertNotTransitioning` 抛错。
- 新增 archive/unarchive 悬空符号链接用例返回一项严格读取错误，且不移动 transcript。
- 非 root POSIX 父目录用例返回 `EACCES`，并且绝不调用 `move()`；该用例按 `arePermissionBitsEnforced()` 而非 `getuid()` 门禁，因此在丢弃 DAC capability 的 root CI 通道上也会执行。
- `integration-tests/cli/qwen-serve-routes.test.ts` 的真实 daemon HTTP 用例同样通过：无 sidecar 批次归档/解档后每份 transcript 与归档前字节完全一致（用户提示、assistant 回复与 `custom_title` system 记录；标题按尝试唯一，不会触发撞标题的 retitle 路径）；悬空 sidecar symlink 被拒绝且 transcript 未移动。在由最终 head 重新打包的 bundle 上，完整路由与 hosted-harness 集成套件 **55/55 通过**（`qwen-serve-routes` 44 + `hosted-harness-process` 11）。
- 本地负向见证：恢复旧 `existsSync` 判定恰好使两条新增悬空链接用例失败；把所有 stat 错误当缺失使不可读父目录用例失败；删除同步前缀使前缀用例失败；在解档时追加杂散 `system` 记录的变异体使逐字节相等的 HTTP 断言失败，而旧的 `slice(1)` 检查仍为绿。每个被变异的文件都按字节还原；真实 daemon 的 `existsSync` 变异确实归档了修复版会拒绝的会话。
- 最终代码修改后 CLI 构建和类型检查通过；web-templates 在 #18456 阈值下构建通过（实测 `2157683` bytes）。

### 证据（改动前后）

不适用——仅后端协调与回归测试改动，无 UI 行为变化。

### 验证平台

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ 本地未测，交由 CI 覆盖 |
|  🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 本地未测，交由 CI 覆盖 |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ 已运行归档套件、CLI 构建/类型检查、导出构建与变异见证 |

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：仅当两侧 sidecar 都真正缺失时恢复同步前缀，其它情况保留严格读取和 ownership 锁路径。
- 未验证/范围外：最终 diff 不改变预算、schema、保留或恢复语义。新 head 的 CI 仍在运行，此处不宣称已全绿。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：无。

## 关联 issue

承接已合入的 [PR #18009](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18009)（squash 提交 `ed5d033e813f90ecb12153ae3307fd035d4b3741`）。独立的非阻塞加固 issue #18446 继续保持打开。会话删除快路径上既有的 `existsSync` 副本跟踪于 #18475，不属于本 PR。

</details>

prs.title: fix(core): skip managed auto-memory extraction when every write tool is denied
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Managed auto-memory extraction now checks whether both write tools are denied before it forks the extractor agent, and records a `writes_denied` skip instead of running a fork that is guaranteed to save nothing. The check treats only bare tool-name rules as a blanket deny; a rule with a path specifier (`edit(src/**)`) constrains one path and is left to the scoped agent, which re-decides each write.

## Why it's needed

In non-interactive runs the CLI adds `write_file` and `edit` to the deny list for `default` and `auto` approval, because there is no UI to answer a prompt. The managed memory agents are forked from a Config that inherits that deny list, and the scoped memory permission manager merges the base verdict in with `mergePermissionDecision`, where `deny` outranks the scoped `allow`. So the extractor is forked, reads the transcript, spends its token budget, and then has every save refused.

Reported in #15597: 19 of 19 memory writes denied over six runs, 143K–234K extractor tokens per run, and an empty project `MEMORY.md`. The run is slow and pure cost with no possible durable result, so the fix is to not start it.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Reproduce on `main`: run `qwen --approval-mode auto --output-format json -p "For this project, always use pnpm instead of npm, and run tests with vitest. Please remember that. Reply with OK."` and inspect `stats.tools.byName.write_file` — every call is denied and `memory/MEMORY.md` stays empty. With this branch the same run reports the extraction as skipped for `writes_denied` and never forks the extractor.

A reviewer can confirm the two halves directly:
- `packages/core/src/memory/write-access.test.ts` pins the rule classifier: aliases (`Write`, `Edit`, `WriteFileTool`, `replace`) count, specifier rules and MCP names do not, and both tools must be denied.
- `packages/core/src/memory/extract.test.ts` pins the effect: with `['run_shell_command', 'write_file', 'edit']` the extractor is never called and the cursor is untouched; with only `write_file` denied extraction still runs.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no user-visible output changes, only whether a background agent is forked.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only, run from `packages/core`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the gate is deliberately conservative — it only fires when a bare rule denies *both* write tools. A deny list that leaves one write tool usable still runs extraction, so the only behavior change is the case that could never have saved anything. The cursor is not advanced on the skip, so turns stay owed and are picked up if the caller later allows writes.
- Not validated / out of scope: the two other memory agents (remember, dream) share the same inherited deny list and have the same failure mode; this PR covers extraction, which is the one that runs on every turn and was the reported cost. Widening to the remaining agents is a follow-up, not a change in this diff.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. `writes_denied` is an additive member of the existing skip-reason union and the matching telemetry enum.

## Linked Issues

Refs #15597

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

托管自动记忆的抽取（extraction）在 fork 出抽取 agent 之前，先检查两个写工具是否都被整体拒绝；如果是，就记录一个 `writes_denied` 的跳过，而不是启动一次注定什么都存不下来的 fork。这个检查只把「裸工具名」规则当作整体拒绝；带路径 specifier 的规则（如 `edit(src/**)`）只约束某一个路径，仍然交由 scoped agent 在每次写入时自行判定。

## 为什么需要

在非交互模式下，`default` 和 `auto` 审批会把 `write_file` 和 `edit` 加入拒绝列表，因为没有 UI 可以回答授权提示。托管记忆 agent 由继承了这份拒绝列表的 Config fork 出来，而 scoped memory 的权限管理器在 `mergePermissionDecision` 里合并基础判定时，`deny` 的优先级高于 scoped 的 `allow`。结果是抽取器被 fork 出来、读了 transcript、花掉了 token，然后每一次写入都被拒绝。

#15597 里记录的现象：六次运行中 19 次记忆写入全部被拒，每次运行抽取器消耗 143K–234K token，项目 `MEMORY.md` 始终为空。这类运行既慢又是纯成本，不可能产生任何可持久化的结果，所以正确的做法是干脆不启动它。

### 如何验证

在 `main` 上复现：运行 `qwen --approval-mode auto --output-format json -p "For this project, always use pnpm instead of npm, and run tests with vitest. Please remember that. Reply with OK."`，然后查看 `stats.tools.byName.write_file`——每次调用都被拒绝，`memory/MEMORY.md` 保持为空。在这个分支上，同样的运行会把抽取记为因 `writes_denied` 跳过，并且不会再 fork 抽取器。

评审可以直接确认两部分：
- `packages/core/src/memory/write-access.test.ts` 钉住规则分类：别名（`Write`、`Edit`、`WriteFileTool`、`replace`）算，带 specifier 的规则和 MCP 名称不算，且必须两个工具都被拒绝。
- `packages/core/src/memory/extract.test.ts` 钉住实际效果：拒绝列表为 `['run_shell_command', 'write_file', 'edit']` 时抽取器完全不会被调用且 cursor 不变；只有 `write_file` 被拒时抽取照常运行。

### 证据（改前 / 改后）

不适用——没有用户可见输出变化，只是后台 agent 是否会启动。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

### 环境（可选）

只跑了单元测试，在 `packages/core` 目录下。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：这个门禁刻意保守——只有一条裸规则同时拒绝两个写工具时才会触发。只要还留下一个可用的写工具，抽取就照常运行，所以唯一的行为变化是那种本来就不可能存下任何东西的情况。跳过时不会推进 cursor，因此这些轮次仍然「欠着」，如果调用方之后允许写入会被重新处理。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：另外两个记忆 agent（remember、dream）共用同一份继承来的拒绝列表，存在同样的失效模式；本 PR 只覆盖 extraction，因为它是每轮都会跑、也是被报告的那部分成本。推广到其余 agent 属于后续工作，不在本 diff 内。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。`writes_denied` 是既有 skip-reason 联合类型和对应 telemetry 枚举的新增成员。

## 关联 issue

Refs #15597

</details>

prs.title: docs(verify-pr): document author-trust classification and its host-held context binding
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds two paragraphs to the verify-pr skill documenting the author-trust classification the verify infrastructure computes host-side: how `prTrust` is derived (fork status overrides everything, the `--local-owner` prepare flag, otherwise the author's collaborator-permission lookup with fail-closed `unknown`), the mandatory escalation rules that force `hardware-isolated` regardless of author trust, how the resulting `executionClass` selects the VM lane's backend (`firecracker`/`vfkit`/`provider-vm` vs `container`), and that the classification reaches the pre-publish checker only through the digest-bound host-held snapshot — a bare checker run skips it entirely.

## Why it's needed

The mechanism ships with #18370, but the skill says nothing about it, so local rounds neither use it nor understand it. In round 13 of #18370 the checker ran without a host-held snapshot, so the classification never participated even though the PR author is a maintainer — and the PR's own CI-workflow changes would have forced `hardware-isolated` anyway. Without this documentation, "untrusted PR code" reads as a judgment about the author rather than a provenance-based classification of the code a round executes, and maintainer identity gets mistaken for a boundary exemption. The new section states the actual rule: author trust selects the isolation class, it never removes the boundary; a host round still needs the explicit maintainer waiver the skill already documents.

This PR is stacked on `fix/pr-precheck-authority-gate` because the scripts it documents arrive with #18370; once that PR merges, this one retargets to main and shows the same docs-only diff.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Read the new section (in the local-invocation area, right after the waiver shapes) against the code it describes: `classifyPrTrust` and `ESCALATION_RULES` in `scripts/verify-pr-prepare.mjs`, the `--context`/`--context-root`/`--context-sha256` handling and `checkTrustClassification` in `scripts/verify-pr-check.mjs`, and the backend selection in `scripts/verify-pr-vm-lifecycle.mjs`. Every claim was cross-checked against those files at head `5363176a` (the five commits after `397d1f24` touch only the precheck script, its tests, and the design docs — not the documented scripts). The classification behavior was also measured by calling the head's real `classifyPrTrust` on five scenarios: fork + `--local-owner` → `external`; `local-owner` + docs-only diff → `trusted-shared-kernel`; `collaborator` (admin) + docs-only → `trusted-shared-kernel`; read permission → `external`/`hardware-isolated`; `local-owner` + #18370's actual diff → `hardware-isolated` with two `ci-workflow` escalation reasons. `prettier --check` passes on the changed file.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — documentation only.

### Tested on

| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  N/A   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

N/A — docs-only change; formatting verified with the repository's Prettier config on aarch64 Linux.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the section describes the scripts #18370 introduces; if those scripts change before merge, the wording needs a re-sync (the escalation list and flag names are the load-bearing parts).
- Not validated / out of scope: the waiver approval flow and the CI container recipe's `--context-out` binding are already documented and are referenced, not restated; no code or workflow change.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Reference #18370 (companion documentation; no closing keyword).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

给 verify-pr skill 增加两段文档，说明验证基础设施在宿主侧计算的作者信任分类：`prTrust` 如何得出（fork 状态压倒一切信号、prepare 的 `--local-owner` 标志、否则查作者的 collaborator 权限且查询失败时 fail-closed 落到 `unknown`），哪些强制升级规则会无视作者信任一律强制 `hardware-isolated`，得出的 `executionClass` 如何选择 VM lane 的 backend（`firecracker`/`vfkit`/`provider-vm` 对 `container`），以及该分类只有经过 digest 绑定的 host-held 快照才能到达发布前 checker——裸跑 checker 会完全跳过它。

prs.title: fix(core): keep the Anthropic message cache breakpoint when a turn ends with an image or PDF
prs.body:
## What this PR does

On the Anthropic provider, the conversation cache breakpoint now lands on the last cacheable block of the last user message, where a cacheable block is non-empty text, a tool result, an image, or a document. Before this change only text and tool results qualified, so a user turn whose last block is an image or a PDF got no message breakpoint at all. If the latest user message has no cacheable block, the breakpoint falls back to an earlier user message instead of being dropped. Each request still carries at most one message breakpoint.

The existing skip for the request-only tail (reattached images and the auto-memory catalog, added for #11627 / #11640) still runs first. The walk-back starts at the block that skip selects, so a breakpoint never lands on a block that stored history does not reproduce.

## Why it's needed

When a user turn ends with an image (ACP clients that send `[text, image]`, or `qwen serve` hosted input with image attachments), the request carries breakpoints only on the system prompt and the last tool. The current turn is still written to the cache, but the next request (for example, the tool result that follows) can read the cache only up to the system prompt and tools, so it writes the whole turn, media included, a second time. Anthropic's prompt-caching docs list image and document blocks in `messages.content` as cacheable, so the media block itself can carry the breakpoint. #18498 has the details and replayed costs (about −27% input cost over a four-request replay on Opus 5.5).

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Four new converter tests cover the cases requested in the #18498 triage, plus one more:

- `marks a user turn that ends with an inline image (no lost breakpoint)`: `[text, image]` puts the breakpoint on the image.
- `marks a user turn that ends with an inline PDF document`: `[text, PDF]` puts the breakpoint on the document.
- `anchors the persisted image, not the request-only catalog, when both trail`: with the auto-memory catalog appended after the image, the breakpoint goes on the image, not on the catalog. This checks that the volatile-tail skip still runs before the walk-back.
- `places exactly one message breakpoint for a media-terminal turn after history`: with earlier history, the request has exactly one message breakpoint, and it is on the image.

Expected: all four fail without the change (no block carries `cache_control`) and pass with it. Existing breakpoint tests (text, tool results, the volatile tail, a catalog-only message) are unchanged and still pass.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (no user-visible UI). The test counts below come from a full `corepack pnpm install` on `6b0cd79`, where the patch was written. This branch is rebased onto `382ee86`, and `git diff 6b0cd79 382ee86 -- packages/core/src/core/anthropicContentGenerator/` is empty, so the converter, the generator and their tests are byte-identical between the two commits and the patch applied without changes. I did not rerun the tests on the rebased commit.

- Before (on `6b0cd79`): the four new tests fail.
- After: `converter.test.ts` 138/138 passed, `anthropicContentGenerator.test.ts` 258/258 passed.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ unit tests (on `6b0cd79`) |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ not tested |

### Environment (optional)

N/A, unit tests only. The cost numbers in #18498 came from replaying captured requests against the Anthropic API, not from this branch.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: two behaviors change. A media-terminal turn now gets a message breakpoint, and a latest user message with no cacheable block now falls back to an earlier user message (before, it got none). In both cases there is still one message breakpoint per request, so the request uses the same number of breakpoints as a turn that ends with text. Turns that end with text or a tool result are marked exactly as before.
- Not validated / out of scope: the PDF arm is converter-level only. As the triage notes, no current entry point ends a turn with a PDF, because ACP places the prompt text after embedded resources. It is included so that image and document blocks are handled the same way, but the measurable saving is on the image arm. I did not run full `npm run preflight`, a build or typecheck, or a live session on this branch.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #18498

Related: #11627 / #11640 (volatile-tail skip on the DashScope reattach path), #11651 (closed alternative).

prs.title: feat(web-shell): surface and control session scheduled tasks in-session
prs.body:
## TLDR

Surface both session-bound durable scheduled tasks and live in-memory session schedules (recurring cron jobs and self-paced loop wakeups) directly inside the Web Shell conversation view, with inline pause, run-now, delete, and stop controls.

Also prevents a confirmed deletion during replay or detached client-id recovery from allowing a queued Run now admission. Accepted manual runs still record at the original owner after a visible-owner change.

## Dive Deeper

Previously, once a conversation had a bound durable scheduled task or created an in-session cron job or self-paced loop wakeup, Web Shell gave no persistent in-conversation indicator that the session would keep waking up, and no direct way to inspect or stop session-scoped schedules without scrolling back to an older creation turn or typing a slash command.

This change closes both the protocol gap and the in-session UI gap in one pass:

- **Live session-scoped schedule status and cancellation**: The daemon's existing session tasks status snapshot now carries active in-memory session-scoped cron jobs and pending loop wakeups (including projected next-fire timestamps, expiry, and optional gate info) without mixing them into the background process list or exposing durable tasks there. The existing session task cancel endpoint now accepts cancelling session-scoped cron/wakeup entries while explicitly refusing durable tasks so persistent schedules stay managed through their dedicated routes.
- **Persistent conversation header entry**: Whenever the active conversation has at least one bound durable task or active session-scoped schedule, a calendar-clock entry appears in the conversation header showing either the next-fire countdown (for a single active schedule) or the count, styled muted when all schedules are paused. Clicking it opens the right-hand environment panel directly to the scheduled tasks section.
- **Inline Environment Panel management**: A dedicated Scheduled Tasks section in the environment panel lists all schedules attached to the conversation, clearly tagged as Persistent, Session, or Loop, with human-readable cadence, live next-run countdowns, and inline actions to enable/disable, run now, delete, stop session-scoped schedules, open the detail panel, or jump to the full Scheduled Tasks page. Durable queries remain strictly scoped to the active workspace without falling back to the primary workspace.
- **Composer activity chip & turn/detail sync**: Active session-scoped schedules surface as a compact chip above the composer (matching the existing background task chips) so users immediately know the session is still armed to wake up. Historical creation cards in the transcript reflect live active or paused status when a live snapshot is available and otherwise keep their creation snapshot without inferring cancellation; the detail panel now lets users stop active session-scoped tasks directly instead of showing a read-only snapshot.

### Dark Theme

![Web Shell session scheduled tasks in dark theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/session-scheduled-tasks/assets/session-scheduled-tasks/session-scheduled-tasks-dark.png)

### Light Theme

![Web Shell session scheduled tasks in light theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/session-scheduled-tasks/assets/session-scheduled-tasks/session-scheduled-tasks-light.png)

### Narrow Chromium Viewport (430 px)

The scheduled entry stays reachable as the environment layout folds; clicking it opens the floating scheduled-tasks section.

![Session scheduled tasks in a narrow Chromium viewport](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/session-scheduled-tasks/assets/session-scheduled-tasks/session-scheduled-tasks-narrow-chromium.png)

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

### 概要

在 Web Shell 对话界面内直接展示并控制当前会话的定时任务，统一覆盖绑定到当前会话的持久化定时任务与会话内存中运行的临时 cron / 自驱循环唤醒任务。

也修复了删除与“立即运行”的时序竞争：在回放或 detached 客户端身份恢复期间已确认删除的任务，不会继续派发 prompt；已被接纳的手动运行在界面 owner 改变后仍保存在原 owner 下。

### 改动说明

此前，当会话绑定了持久化定时任务或通过工具创建了会话级 cron / 循环唤醒后，Web Shell 对话界面没有常驻状态提示，用户既不容易察觉会话还会继续自动唤醒，也无法就地停掉会话级循环。

本次改动同步补齐了协议能力与会话内界面展示：

- **会话级定时任务状态与取消接口**：复用现有会话任务快照接口返回当前会话内存中活跃的会话级 cron 与待触发循环唤醒（含下次触发时间投影、过期时间与可选 Gate），不混入原有后台任务列表，也不掺杂持久化任务；复用现有会话任务取消接口支持按 `cron` 类型取消会话级任务，并明确拒绝通过该接口取消持久化任务。
- **会话顶部栏常驻入口**：当当前会话存在至少一条关联定时任务时，顶部栏显示日历时钟入口；单条活跃任务展示下次触发倒计时，多条展示总数，全部暂停时置灰；点击后打开右侧环境面板并定位到定时任务分区。
- **右侧环境面板「定时任务」分区**：区分标注「持久化」「仅当前会话」「循环唤醒」，展示人类可读频率、实时倒计时与就地操作（启停、立即运行、删除、停止会话任务、打开详情/编辑、跳转管理全部）。持久化任务查询严格限定在当前会话所属工作区，不会回退到主工作区。
- **输入框上方活跃芯片与详情同步**：当存在活跃会话级 cron 或循环唤醒时，在输入框上方任务芯片栏显示活跃定时任务芯片，提醒用户会话仍在等待自动唤醒；对话轮次里的创建卡片在实时快照可用时同步展示运行中/已暂停状态，否则保留创建快照且不把缺席推断为已取消；右侧详情面板也支持直接停止活跃的会话级任务。

#### 暗色主题

![Web Shell 会话定时任务暗色主题截图](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/session-scheduled-tasks/assets/session-scheduled-tasks/session-scheduled-tasks-dark.png)

#### 亮色主题

![Web Shell 会话定时任务亮色主题截图](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/session-scheduled-tasks/assets/session-scheduled-tasks/session-scheduled-tasks-light.png)

#### 窄屏 Chromium 视口（430px）

窄屏下环境面板按响应式布局收起后，顶部定时任务入口仍然可达；点击入口即可打开浮层中的调度任务分区。

![Web Shell 窄屏定时任务浮层截图](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/session-scheduled-tasks/assets/session-scheduled-tasks/session-scheduled-tasks-narrow-chromium.png)

</details>

## Reviewer Test Plan

- **Header entry and Environment Panel listing**: Open a Web Shell conversation that has a bound persistent scheduled task and at least one in-session cron job or loop wakeup. Confirm the calendar-clock entry appears in the conversation header with the total count (or live countdown for a single active task), and clicking it opens the Environment Panel to the Scheduled Tasks section with Persistent, Session, and Loop tags.
- **Inline stop for session-scoped schedules**: Click the stop action on an active session-scoped cron job or loop wakeup from either the Environment Panel or the detail panel opened from a turn card. Confirm the task disappears from the list, the header count decrements, the composer scheduled chip updates or disappears, and the turn card no longer carries a live status badge.
- **Inline controls for persistent tasks**: Click pause/enable, run now, or delete on a session-bound persistent task in the Environment Panel. Confirm paused tasks dim immediately and the header entry switches to a muted paused state when no active schedules remain.
- **Safety boundary**: Attempt to cancel a durable scheduled task through the session-scoped cron cancel endpoint and verify it is refused rather than deleting the persistent schedule.

- **Manual run/delete interleaving**: Open a recurring persistent bound task and its independent Artifact detail. Start Run now while the actual manual replay is held. Complete Delete before daemon replay resumes, then release it. Verify no prompt or `/run` request is admitted, every marker-bearing model request stays zero (including turn-end managed-memory extraction), and the task remains physically deleted rather than paused, cancelled, or restored. In the no-delete control, require exactly one HTTP 202 prompt admission, one successful run, and one durable manual record at the original workspace/owner. Do not use a timeout as proof of either outcome. Retain the auxiliary managed-memory payload and its distinct role separately from the single business execution.
![R21 delete-before-replay verification at commit 51526982a4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/session-scheduled-tasks/session-scheduled-tasks/r21/delete-after-settlement-51526982a4.png)

- **Detached client recovery**: Force the first detached HTTP attempt to return `invalid_client_id` before turn registration, delete while re-attachment is held, and verify no second dispatch or admission occurs. The negative control with no deletion must still recover with the actual new client id and admit once.
- **Accepted admission followed by owner change**: After actual admission resolves, change the visible owner. Recording must still target the original workspace/session exactly once. This does not revoke an already-accepted prompt and does not reconstruct history after a confirmed physical deletion.

## Testing Matrix

|          | 🍏  | 🪟  | 🐧  |
| -------- | --- | --- | --- |
| npm run  | ❓  | ❓  | ✅  |
| npx      | ❓  | ❓  | ❓  |

| Podman   | ❓  | ❓  | ❓  |

prs.title: fix(ci): provision the managed OSS MySQL test database
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Pre-provisions the dedicated MySQL database that #17471's `SessionOssStorageMySqlIT` will read through the O4 settings, and passes that URL to Maven in the SDK Java MySQL lane. This PR also includes two related CI follow-ups: a green Managed Agent gate can retire its own pre-merge failure report once both its PR and exact commit match, and the session archival race test handles its expected competing rejection immediately.

## Why it's needed

Extracted from #17471 so the lane plumbing can be reviewed and land independently of the Session ownership change. On current `main` no `*MySqlIT` reads `qwen.o4.mysql.url`: `SessionOssStorageMySqlIT` still uses the isolated-schema helper and creates its own `schema32_case_<uuid>` database. This change becomes load-bearing only once #17471 moves that test onto the O4 settings, whose URL validator rejects `createDatabaseIfNotExist`.

The `-Po4-mysql-gates` step in the same workflow keeps its own copy of `qwen_o4_ci`; this PR does not touch it.

The issue resolver previously had no trigger for green pre-merge Managed Agent gates, because their runs report the PR head branch rather than `main` and older runs often have an empty `pull_requests` array. The resolver now locates the PR through the exact commit on its green run. It retires only reports whose commit matches, when the commit belongs to one main-bound PR; it does not close failures from another PR or an amended commit. This is cleanup of already-green failures, not a claim that the underlying chronic failures are fixed.

The session archival test's deliberately rejected competing operation otherwise has no rejection handler while its orchestrator awaits another operation in `finally`. Its handler now follows creation of that promise directly.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Confirm the SDK Java MySQL lane creates `qwen_o4_ci` on the first disposable container before Maven connects, and passes `-Dqwen.o4.mysql.url` / `-Dqwen.o4.mysql.user` plus `QWEN_O4_MYSQL_PASSWORD`. The lane is skipped in the fast tier, so a live MySQL run cannot validate this PR on its own.

Confirm a green Managed Agent gate retires its own earlier red report only at the same PR head SHA, including approval-triggered reruns, while a different PR or rebuilt SHA is left alone. The resolver uses a commit-to-PR lookup because its real historical run has no PR association on the run payload.

Confirm the session archival race test no longer reports an unhandled rejection before it asserts its existing session outcome.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A for CI and test changes.

### Tested on

macOS. The workflow resolver and workflow-size contracts pass: 258 tests passed, 1 skipped. - The issue resolver closes reports only after the covered jobs are green at an associated PR's same commit. The eleven existing Managed Agent reports will be retired only when their individually covered gates go green after this resolver change merges; merging this PR does not mark them resolved immediately.

prs.title: fix(cli): give static transcript text an explicit wrap width
prs.body:
## What this PR does

On the static transcript path, a block of text that had no width of its own was measured implicitly by the layout engine, so a line that filled the terminal could run into the reserved right margin and the terminal would then break it hard in the middle of a word. This PR states the width explicitly for the three conversation block types that were affected: ordinary paragraphs, markdown list items, and markdown blockquotes. The width is opt-in per call site, and only the conversational call sites opt in; call sites whose available width already includes their own border and padding are deliberately left alone.

This is a take-over of #15021 by agreement with its author (@PanSHIgg), who asked for the work to move forward here and will close that PR once this one is open. The paragraph half is his change, carried over as-is; the list-item and blockquote halves extend the same mechanism to two call sites that were left as follow-ups in the original PR.

## Why it's needed

The reported symptom is one or two characters landing alone in column zero after a line that reached the right edge, with the following line's indent shifted by a column. It is width-dependent and was reported on Windows at 100 columns. The root cause is that the wrapping text had no declared width, so the layout engine could hand the terminal a line one or a few cells wider than the space actually reserved for it. Giving the block its real width removes that possibility for the three affected block types.

The original PR covered paragraphs only and explicitly deferred list items and the remaining call sites. While verifying the paragraph fix in a real terminal, the same defect was observed on numbered lists and on blockquotes, so all three are fixed here rather than in three separate rounds.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

The regression tests render the real transcript component inside a real static list at a fixed terminal width and assert that no rendered line is wider than the space the transcript reserves (terminal width minus the two-column margins). Each of the three block types has its own test, and each test fails on the build where its own block type is still unfixed:

| build | failing tests |
| --- | --- |
| current `main`, no fixes | paragraphs, flat list, nested list, blockquote — `5 failed` |
| + paragraph fix only | flat list, nested list |
| + list fix only | blockquote |
| + all three | none — `237 passed` across the transcript and markdown suites |

So the three defects are separated by independent signals: fixing one does not hide another. A reviewer can reproduce the first row by reverting the source changes and re-running the transcript test file.

For the live check: run the CLI in a 100-column Windows terminal with the virtualized history disabled, and ask for a long single-paragraph answer, a numbered list of two long items, and a long one-line blockquote. Before the change, words break mid-word at the right edge and the fragment lands in column zero. After the change, wrapping happens at word boundaries and the right margin stays intact.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Both frames below are the same model, the same working directory and a real 100-column Windows ConPTY; only the built bundle differs.

Before — build without the fixes:

![Before: blockquote, paragraph and list all break at the right margin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aleks-0/qwen-code/pr-assets-14075/pr-assets/14075-three-base-100col.png)

After — build with the three fixes:

![After: the same three blocks wrap at word boundaries and the right margin is intact](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aleks-0/qwen-code/pr-assets-14075/pr-assets/14075-three-fixed-100col.png)

The same frames as text, so the break points are greppable. Before — blockquote, paragraph and list all break; worst line is 100 cells against a 98-cell ceiling:

```
  ◆︎  │ История вычислительной техники начинается с механических счётных устройств — абака, счётовой
       доски и арифмометра Лейбница, — продолжается разностной и аналитической машинами Чарлза Бэбби
джа
       с первыми программами Ады Лавлейс, переходит к электромеханическим реле Конрада Цузе и лампов
ым
```

After — same three blocks, no orphan in column zero, worst content line 98:

```
  ◆︎  │ История вычислительной техники начинается с механических счётных устройств — абака, счётовой
       доски и арифмометра Лейбница, — продолжается разностной и аналитической машинами
       Чарлза Бэббиджа с первыми программами Ады Лавлейс, переходит к электромеханическим реле
```

Breaks visible before and gone after: blockquote `Бэбби`/`джа`, `лампов`/`ым`; paragraph `сформулиров`/`ано`, `вме`/`сте`; list `врод`/`е`.

Independent verification of the original paragraph work, carried over from #15021: the paragraph regression test fails on the base commit (`2 failed | 42 passed`) and passes with the fix (`44/44`), and the Windows build, typecheck, lint and bundle are green here. Credit to @holny for the earlier reproduction attempts in the issue thread.

One caveat about the pair above, stated plainly: the "before" frame was captured from the commit this branch was cut from, while the branch itself sits on a later `main` after a merge. The comparison therefore shows the product before and after the three fixes plus unrelated upstream movement. The per-path unit tests, not the screenshots, are what attribute the fix to these changes.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ✅   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests via the package's own vitest runner. Live frames from a real ConPTY session driven through a pseudo-terminal harness with the terminal buffer captured headlessly; the CLI was built and bundled locally on Windows.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: an explicitly declared width clips instead of overflowing if a call site opts in while passing an available width that already accounts for its own border and padding. That is why the opt-in is per call site and is enabled only on the conversational paths, which pass the width the block may actually use.
- Not validated / out of scope: macOS and Linux. Also not validated: terminals that render ambiguous-width characters as two cells. The fix restores the reserved two-column right margin, which absorbs that drift on lines with no ambiguous glyphs, but a boundary line carrying several of them can still exceed the terminal width by more than the margin; that residual is unchanged by this PR and is tracked in the issue.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. No public options or settings are added or changed.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #14075

Take-over of #15021 by agreement with its author; the paragraph change and the verification above are carried over from it. The remaining caveat noted under Risk & Scope is carried over as well, so the closing keyword reflects the reported symptom being addressed on the reported platform, not a claim that ambiguous-width terminal behaviour was measured.

QwenCode QwenLLM

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

在静态会话（static transcript）渲染路径上，没有自身宽度的文本块会被布局引擎隐式测量，因此占满终端宽度的行可能侵占预留的右边距，随后由终端在单词中间强制断行。本 PR 为受影响的三类会话内容块显式声明宽度：普通段落、markdown 有序/无序列表项，以及 markdown 引用块。该宽度按调用点逐个开启，只在会话类调用点启用；那些可用宽度本身已包含自身边框与内边距的调用点有意保持不动。

这是与 #15021 作者（@PanSHIgg）协商后对该 PR 的接手（take-over）。作者已同意在此推进，并在本 PR 开出后关闭原 PR。段落部分原样沿用其改动；列表项与引用块两部分把同一机制扩展到原 PR 中留作后续项的两个调用点。

## 为什么需要

报告的症状是：某行顶到终端右边缘后，有一两个字符单独落在第 0 列，下一行的缩进也随之错位。该问题与宽度相关，报告环境为 Windows、100 列。根因是换行文本未声明宽度，布局引擎可能交给终端比实际可用空间宽一格或数格的行。为这三类内容块声明真实宽度即可消除该可能。

原 PR 只覆盖段落，并明确把列表项及其余调用点留作后续。在真实终端中验证段落修复时，同样的缺陷在有序列表和引用块上也被观察到，因此三者一并在此修复，而不是分三轮。

## 评审验证方案

### 如何验证

回归测试在固定终端宽度下把真实会话组件渲染进真实的 static 列表，并断言任何渲染行的宽度都不超过会话预留的空间（终端宽度减去两列边距）。三类内容块各有自己的测试，并且每个测试都在“该类型尚未修复”的构建上失败：

| 构建 | 失败的测试 |
| --- | --- |
| 当前 `main`，无任何修复 | 段落、扁平列表、嵌套列表、引用块 — `5 failed` |
| 仅段落修复 | 扁平列表、嵌套列表 |
| 仅列表修复 | 引用块 |
| 三项全部 | 无 — 会话与 markdown 两个测试套件共 `237 passed` |

因此三个缺陷由彼此独立的信号区分：修复其中一个不会掩盖另一个。评审者可以回退源码改动后重跑该测试文件来复现第一行。

实机验证：在 100 列 Windows 终端中关闭虚拟化历史运行 CLI，要求模型给出一个长段落、一个含两条长条目的有序列表和一行长引用。修改前，单词在右边缘被截断，碎片落在第 0 列；修改后按词边界换行，右边距保持完整。

### 前后对比证据

以下两帧来自同一模型、同一工作目录、真实 100 列 Windows ConPTY，唯一差别是构建产物。文件：`14075-three-base-100col.png`、`14075-three-fixed-100col.png`。

修改前 — 引用块、段落、列表均断裂；最宽行 100 格，上限为 98 格（见英文正文代码块）。

修改后 — 同样三块内容，第 0 列无孤立碎片，最宽内容行 98 格。

修改前可见、修改后消失的断裂：引用块 `Бэбби`/`джа`、`лампов`/`ым`；段落 `сформулиров`/`ано`、`вме`/`сте`；列表 `врод`/`е`。

来自 #15021 的独立验证结论一并保留：段落回归测试在基线提交上失败（`2 failed | 42 passed`），加上修复后通过（`44/44`）；本分支在 Windows 上的构建、类型检查、lint 与打包均为绿。感谢 @holny 在 issue 讨论中的早期复现尝试。

关于上述对比的一个坦率说明：“修改前”那一帧取自本分支切出时的提交，而分支本身在合并后已位于更新的 `main`。因此该对比展示的是“三项修复加上无关上游变更”前后的产品状态。真正把修复归因于本次改动的是按路径拆分的单元测试，而不是截图。

### 测试平台

|     系统     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ✅   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### 运行环境（可选）

单元测试使用各包自带的 vitest。实机截图由伪终端脚本驱动真实 ConPTY 会话并无头抓取终端缓冲得到；CLI 在 Windows 本地构建并打包。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：若某个调用点在可用宽度已包含自身边框与内边距的情况下开启该开关，显式宽度会造成裁切而不是溢出。因此该开关按调用点启用，且只在会话类路径启用，这些路径传入的正是内容块真正可使用的宽度。
- 未验证／范围之外：macOS 与 Linux。同样未验证：把 ambiguous-width 字符按两格渲染的终端。本修复恢复了预留的两列右边距，在无 ambiguous 字符的行上足以吸收该偏差；但若边界行含有多个此类字符，仍可能超出终端宽度并超过该边距，这一残余问题本 PR 不改变，并在 issue 中继续跟踪。
- 破坏性变更／迁移说明：无。未新增或修改任何公开选项或设置。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #14075

与 #15021 作者协商后的接手 PR；段落改动与上述验证结论均由其继承。Risk & Scope 中提到的残余说明同样保留，因此关闭关键字表示“在报告平台上已处理所报告的症状”，并不声称已测量 ambiguous-width 终端行为。

</details>

prs.title: fix(core): point at the JSON error when a tool arg arrives as broken text
prs.body:
## What this PR does

When a tool argument that must be an array or object arrives as a string whose text starts like JSON but does not parse, the validation error sent back to the model now explains it: it adds the JSON parse error, the text around the failing position with the exact spot marked `<<HERE>>`, and asks for the value as a JSON array/object instead of a string. The quoted text never cuts a character in half. All other validation errors are unchanged. This change is confined to the validator's error text: the hint is part of the ordinary tool error, stored and shown like any other.

Before: `params/docs must be array`

After: `params/docs must be array; params/docs arrived as a string whose text is not valid JSON (Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON at position 2215 (line 1 column 2216)). Text near the error, with <<HERE>> at that position: "…可辨读\"}]}<<HERE>>]}}, \"issues\": [{\"co". Fix the text there and send it as a JSON array, not as a string`

## Why it's needed

A structured-output run on DashScope qwen3.8-max failed after 15 turns: the model called `structured_output` eight times and every call was rejected with `params/docs must be array`. Bailian's server logs confirmed the chain: the model generated a `docs` array with an unbalanced bracket around character 2216 of a 2300-character value; with `tool_stream` off, DashScope buffers array/object arguments and, when the buffered value is not valid JSON, sends it on as a string; qwen-code's existing stringified-JSON coercion cannot parse it, so validation fails with a type error. That message does not say the text is malformed, so the model guessed at newlines and escaping and resent the same broken text each time.

Replaying the first failed call against qwen3.8-max (10 runs per message), the next call produced a complete valid document 1/10 times with the current message and 5/10 with the new one. Giving only the nearby text without the marker reached 3/10, which is why the exact spot is marked.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Point the CLI at an OpenAI-compatible mock whose first `structured_output` call passes an array-typed field as a string with one `]` too many, then inspect the tool result in the next request. Expected: the message names the field path, the parse error and position, shows the nearby text with `<<HERE>>`, and asks for a JSON array. A string that does not start with `[` or `{`, or one that is valid JSON, keeps today's message. Nested paths are reported once even when the field sits under `anyOf`, and a plain object-typed field gets the same hint with "JSON object".

### Evidence (Before & After)

Mock-server E2E (headless, `--json-schema`), tool result in turn 2:
- Before (0.28.7, latest release): `params/docs must be array`
- After: `params/docs must be array; params/docs arrived as a string whose text is not valid JSON (Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON at position 74 (line 1 column 75)). Text near the error, with <<HERE>> at that position: "[{\"pages\": [1], \"category_id\": \"tpl_a\", \"fields\": {\"a\": {\"raw_value\": \"x\"}<<HERE>>]}, \"issues\": []}]". Fix the text there and send it as a JSON array, not as a string`

Unit tests: schema validator and synthetic output tool suites pass (130 tests), including a plain object-typed field and an excerpt whose edges would otherwise split a surrogate pair (that test fails with the boundary handling removed); core type-check, prettier and eslint clean.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Built CLI (`npm run build`) against a local mock server; real-model replays against DashScope Standard (Beijing) qwen3.8-max.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the extra text is appended only to type errors whose value is a JSON-looking string that fails to parse, so other tools and errors see no change. The message quotes up to 100 characters of the model's own argument back to it; that argument is already in the conversation history in full, so the excerpt adds nothing new to what is stored.
- Not validated / out of scope: the provider-side behavior (turning a broken array into a string) is not changed here; the model still has to resend the value. Parse-error wording comes from the runtime's JSON parser; when it has no position, the marker is omitted.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Supersedes #18346 (closed): same change, kept to the validator's error text, plus the two review items raised there (object-typed field test, character-safe excerpt). Related to #18242 and #18256 (other DashScope tool-argument failures seen in the same structured-output workload).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

当一个要求是数组或对象的工具参数以字符串形式到达，并且这个字符串以 JSON 的样子开头却解析失败时，回给模型的校验错误现在会说明原因：附上 JSON 解析错误、出错位置附近的原文（并用 `<<HERE>>` 标出确切位置），并要求以 JSON 数组/对象而不是字符串发送这个值。引用的原文不会把一个字符切成两半。其他校验错误保持不变。改动只限于校验器的错误文本：这段提示就是普通工具错误的一部分，和其他错误一样存储和展示。

改动前：`params/docs must be array`

改动后：`params/docs must be array; params/docs arrived as a string whose text is not valid JSON (Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON at position 2215 (line 1 column 2216)). Text near the error, with <<HERE>> at that position: "…可辨读\"}]}<<HERE>>]}}, \"issues\": [{\"co". Fix the text there and send it as a JSON array, not as a string`

## 为什么需要

一次在 DashScope qwen3.8-max 上的结构化输出运行在 15 轮后失败：模型调用了 8 次 `structured_output`，每次都被 `params/docs must be array` 拒绝。百炼服务端日志确认了因果链：模型生成的 `docs` 数组在 2300 字符长的值中约第 2216 个字符处括号不配对；`tool_stream` 关闭时，DashScope 会缓冲数组/对象参数，缓冲的值不是合法 JSON 时，就把它作为字符串下发；qwen-code 现有的字符串化 JSON 修正无法解析它，于是校验报类型错误。这条信息没有说明文本本身是坏的，模型只能去猜换行和转义的问题，每次都重发同样的坏文本。

把第一次失败的调用对 qwen3.8-max 回放（每种信息 10 次），下一次调用产出完整合法文档的次数：现有信息 1/10，新信息 5/10。只给附近原文、不加标记时为 3/10，所以加上了确切位置的标记。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

让 CLI 连接一个 OpenAI 兼容的模拟服务端，第一次 `structured_output` 调用把一个数组类型字段以多一个 `]` 的字符串传入，然后检查下一次请求中的工具结果。预期：信息给出字段路径、解析错误和位置，展示带 `<<HERE>>` 的附近原文，并要求 JSON 数组。不以 `[` 或 `{` 开头的字符串、或本身是合法 JSON 的字符串，信息保持现状。嵌套路径即使位于 `anyOf` 下也只报告一次；普通的对象类型字段也会得到同样的提示，措辞为 "JSON object"。

### 证据（前后对比）

模拟服务端 E2E（headless，`--json-schema`），第 2 轮的工具结果：
- 改动前（0.28.7，最新发布版）：`params/docs must be array`
- 改动后：`params/docs must be array; params/docs arrived as a string whose text is not valid JSON (Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON at position 74 (line 1 column 75)). Text near the error, with <<HERE>> at that position: "[{\"pages\": [1], \"category_id\": \"tpl_a\", \"fields\": {\"a\": {\"raw_value\": \"x\"}<<HERE>>]}, \"issues\": []}]". Fix the text there and send it as a JSON array, not as a string`

单元测试：schema 校验器和 synthetic output 工具的测试全部通过（130 个），包括普通对象类型字段，以及一个引用窗口边界原本会切开代理对的用例（去掉边界处理后该用例失败）；core 类型检查、prettier 和 eslint 通过。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### 环境（可选）

构建后的 CLI（`npm run build`）连接本地模拟服务端；真实模型回放使用 DashScope 标准版（北京）qwen3.8-max。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：额外文本只附加在"值是形似 JSON 但解析失败的字符串"的类型错误上，其他工具和错误不受影响。信息会把模型自己参数中最多 100 个字符回传给它；这个参数本来就完整地在对话历史里，摘录不会给存储的内容增加任何新东西。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：这里不改变服务端行为（把坏数组转成字符串），模型仍需重发这个值。解析错误的措辞来自运行时的 JSON 解析器；没有位置信息时省略标记。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。

## 关联 Issue

取代 #18346（已关闭）：同样的改动，只限于校验器的错误文本，并加上那里提出的两项评审意见（对象类型字段的测试、按字符边界截取原文）。与 #18242、#18256 相关（同一结构化输出场景中出现的其他 DashScope 工具参数问题）。

</details>
