### Summary

Running `openclaw models status --probe` offline in **OpenClaw `2026.11.10 (6ea542f)`** on **Windows 11 + Node.js `v26.13.1`** deterministically emits:

1. **20+ repeated runtime warnings** during the live provider check:
   `Warning: File descriptor 13 closed but not opened in unmanaged mode`
2. **Self-triggered `[DEP_PLUGIN_SDK]` deprecation warning** in first-party CLI output:
   `DeprecationWarning: Plugin SDK: resolveAuthStorePathForDisplay is deprecated; use provider/profile identifiers for displays...`

While the SQLite clean-close receipt succeeds on Windows, mismatched managed/unmanaged FD closes in the same code family are already implicated in `EXC_GUARD` crashes on macOS (see [openclaw/openclaw#144772](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/144772)).

### Environment

- **OpenClaw version:** `2026.11.10 (6ea542f)`
- **Node.js version:** `v26.13.1` (x64, native Windows)
- **OS:** Windows 11 26H2
- **Gateway state:** Stopped (`openclaw gateway stop` prior to offline `--probe`)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Stop the background Gateway service (`openclaw gateway stop`) to satisfy offline state ownership.
2. Run:
   ```powershell
   openclaw models status --probe --probe-provider synthetic
   ```

### Actual Output (sanitized)

```text
(node:9992) [DEP_PLUGIN_SDK] DeprecationWarning: Plugin SDK: resolveAuthStorePathForDisplay is deprecated; use provider/profile identifiers for displays (there is no public async database-path replacement) instead. The legacy contract remains supported during its deprecation period. Final compatibility day: 2026-12-31.
Checking synthetic (synthetic:setup-<UUID>)..(node:9992) Warning: File descriptor 13 closed but not opened in unmanaged mode
(Use `node --trace-warnings ...` to show where the warning was created)
Checking synthetic (synthetic:setup-<UUID>)..(node:9992) Warning: File descriptor 13 closed but not opened in unmanaged mode
... [repeated ~22 times for FD 13] ...
Checked 1 target in 5.7s
```

### Expected Behavior

1. First-party `openclaw models status` should not call its own deprecated `resolveAuthStorePathForDisplay` helper (`src/agents/auth-profiles/path-resolve.ts` / `src/plugin-sdk/agent-runtime.ts`), avoiding noisy `[DEP_PLUGIN_SDK]` output before the 2026-12-31 removal deadline.
2. File descriptors opened via managed handles / SQLite / lockfile helpers during `--probe` should be closed through their owning handle rather than raw unmanaged `fs.close` / `fs.closeSync(fd)` on Node.js 26.

### Related Issues & PRs

- Guarded FD / `closed but not opened in unmanaged mode` warning class: [openclaw/openclaw#144772](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/144772)
- `resolveAuthStorePathForDisplay` deprecation & auth-store display refactors: [openclaw/openclaw#169714](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169714), [openclaw/openclaw#126955](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/126955), [openclaw/openclaw#126918](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/126918), [openclaw/openclaw#181584](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181584)

issues.body:
### Summary

In **OpenClaw `2026.11.10 (6ea542f)`** on Windows 11, `src/commands/daemon-install.ts` still suffers from two install-time runtime-selection bugs when writing `~\.openclaw\gateway.cmd` for the `OpenClaw Gateway` Scheduled Task:

1. **Ephemeral `fnm_multishells` symlink/junction is recorded verbatim while the installing shell is still alive:**
   PR [openclaw/openclaw#143159](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143159) (`f8066ed`) added reactive replacement when a previously recorded Gateway service Node binary is *already missing* on a subsequent `openclaw gateway install --force` run. However, during initial `onboard` / `gateway install` inside an active `fnm` shell (`fnm env`), `%LOCALAPPDATA%\fnm_multishells\<PID>_<TIMESTAMP>\node.exe` exists at install time, so `process.execPath` is written directly into `gateway.cmd`. Once that shell exits (or `fnm` cleans up / is removed), the Scheduled Task immediately fails on boot/start with `spawn ... ENOENT`, leaving `127.0.0.1:18789` with `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`.
2. **Bun's fake `~/.bun/bin/node.exe` shim on Windows is not rejected:**
   On Windows, Bun can place a `node.exe` shim in `%USERPROFILE%\.bun\bin\node.exe` whose `fs.realpathSync()` resolves to `bun.exe`. Because `gateway.cmd` injects V8-specific flags (`--max-old-space-size=32541`), any service or probe picking up `.bun\bin\node.exe` fails immediately with `error: Invalid Argument` (and even `node -v` fails under that shim).

### Environment

- **OpenClaw version:** `2026.11.10 (6ea542f)`
- **OS:** Windows 11 26H2 (x64)
- **Real Node.js runtime:** `v26.13.1`

### Observed Diagnostic Output (sanitized)

From `openclaw gateway status --deep` after closing the `fnm` shell:

```text
Command: C:\Users\<USER>\AppData\Local\fnm_multishells\38344_1795483895345\node.exe --max-old-space-size=32541 ... gateway --port 18789
Service file: ~\.openclaw\gateway.cmd
Service config issue: Gateway service Node runtime check failed. (Node runtime check failed for C:\Users\<USER>\AppData\Local\fnm_multishells\38344_1795483895345\node.exe: Error: spawn ... ENOENT.)
Runtime: stopped (state Ready, last run 1)
Connectivity check: failed (connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:18789)
```

And when `%USERPROFILE%\.bun\bin\node.exe` precedes the real Node installation on `PATH`:

```text
> node -p "require('node:fs').realpathSync(process.execPath)"
C:\Users\<USER>\.bun\bin\bun.exe
> node -v
error: Invalid Argument '-v'
```

### Root Cause & Proposed Fix (`src/commands/daemon-install.ts`)

1. **Canonicalize the runtime path at install time via `fs.realpathSync()`:**
   On Windows (via `GetFinalPathNameByHandleW`) and Unix, `fs.realpathSync(candidateNodePath)` resolves the per-shell `fnm_multishells/<pid>_<ts>/node(.exe)` junction/symlink straight to the persistent installation directory (`.../fnm/node-versions/vX.Y.Z/installation/node.exe`), preventing post-exit / post-reboot `ENOENT` before it happens (or optionally prefer `%APPDATA%\fnm\aliases\default\node.exe` when configured).
2. **Guard against non-Node shims (`bun.exe`):**
   After `fs.realpathSync(candidate)`, verify `path.basename(realPath).toLowerCase() !== "bun.exe" (and validate `execFileSync(realPath, ["--version"])` starts with `v` and accepts V8 flags) before persisting it into `gateway.cmd` / `systemd` / `launchd`.

### Related Issues & PRs

- Direct predecessor (post-hoc missing Node replacement): [openclaw/openclaw#143159](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143159) (`f8066ed`), `src/commands/daemon-install.ts`, `src/cli/daemon-cli/install.integration.test.ts`
- Related daemon/service runtime work: [openclaw/openclaw#142322](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/142322), [openclaw/openclaw#107930](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/107930)
- Upstream `fnm` per-shell symlink lifecycle context: [Schniz/fnm#1163](https://github.com/Schniz/fnm/issues/1163), [Schniz/fnm#1228](https://github.com/Schniz/fnm/issues/1228), [Schniz/fnm#1555](https://github.com/Schniz/fnm/issues/1555)

issues.body:
## Summary

The Codex native-tool creator capture records native `exec` without execution-placement metadata, while the stream admission predicate requires that metadata. A native Codex surface can therefore expose read/exec and still fail the initial Gateway stream qualification under Gateway/full/off defaults.

This is a source-contract reproduction. It does not establish that an earlier observed automation refusal traversed this branch, and no live automation mutation was retried for this investigation.

## Source baseline

Inspected installed OpenClaw and Codex plugin version 2026.11.10. The same missing plumbing is visible in official commit `0273f4a57a75eff0dff021e8b82ca0fc5769c7ad`:

- [Codex SDK wrapper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0273f4a57a75eff0dff021e8b82ca0fc5769c7ad/src/plugin-sdk/codex-mcp-projection.ts): captureFinalCodexCronCreatorToolAllowlist forwards canonical native read/exec names when nativeToolSurfaceEnabled is true, without a native execution target.
- [Both real capture callers](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0273f4a57a75eff0dff021e8b82ca0fc5769c7ad/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-tool-setup.ts) pass that boolean, without a successful physical-client/current-run execution-placement binding.
- [Shared creator capture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0273f4a57a75eff0dff021e8b82ca0fc5769c7ad/src/agents/tools/cron-tool-creator-cap.ts) distinguishes native exec origin and execution target.
- [Stream policy preparation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0273f4a57a75eff0dff021e8b82ca0fc5769c7ad/src/agents/tools/cron-tool-write.ts) retains the requirement for qualifying Gateway execution authority.

## Isolated reproduction and limits

Nine local source-extraction/VM tests pass against the saved installed wrapper, shared capture/normalization code and initial stream predicate. They replace the wrapper's dynamic import and provide narrow dependencies; they do not import a running Gateway, issue real grants or execute jobs.

The relevant cases are:

1. Call the installed Codex wrapper with nativeToolSurfaceEnabled=true and no dynamic OpenClaw-origin exec tool.
2. Captured native entries are read and `{name:'exec', execOrigin:'native'}`. The exec entry has no execTarget.
3. Feed that result to the unchanged initial stream predicate with effectiveHost=gateway, security=full, ask=off and no sandbox alternative. Qualification fails.
4. The installed wrapper constructs a new options object, so supplying nativeExecTarget to that wrapper does not forward it either.
5. An isolated forwarding candidate passes the initial predicate with an explicit synthetic Gateway target. Missing/disabled/native-node targets, deny security, effective node placement and allowlist/ask=off remain refused.

Case 5 is contract testing only. Synthetic target metadata is not a host placement attestation and is not an acceptable production fix. Approval handling, final persistence, physical execution placement and the actual failed historical turn are outside this reproduction.

## Expected outcome

Please reconcile the native Codex creator capture with stream qualification using host-owned evidence for the actual successful initialized client and exact admitted run. Preserve remote/node/sandbox, currentness, cancellation, revocation, policy and approval restrictions through final mutation. Do not infer Gateway authority from the nativeToolSurfaceEnabled boolean or ordinary shell availability.

A regression should verify valid host-owned local capture and final protected mutation, together with remote, stale, revoked, replaced-client and disabled-native negative cases.

## Duplicate search

Searched issues and PRs for the wrapper symbol, nativeExecTarget, and stream/Codex/creator terms. #137241 concerns canonical native scope disappearing from toolsAllow, rather than native exec already captured without placement. #202499 concerns an undifferentiated expired creator-grant error; this finding concerns the separate initial stream-execution qualification, and is not claimed as that issue's root cause. #196199 and #194403 concern helper completion lifecycle/cleanup and are also separate.

issues.body:
## Summary

The `typesafe` decision provider leaves `prepared-generation-lease` references on its plugin generation after evaluations finish. Some are owned by a run that has long since ended, and several carry `owner: "unknown"`. Because they never release, a targeted plugin replacement can never reach a drain state: `openclaw plugins reload typesafe` fails at `phase: drain` after 60 s every time, and `--wait` sat past 10 minutes with no progress. Only a full Gateway process restart clears them.

## Environment

- OpenClaw `2026.11.10` (6ea542f), official container image, single Gateway.
- `@openclaw/typesafe` `2026.11.10`, custom `baseUrl` (local System One server), no hosted credential.
- Backend answers in ~50–600 ms and is reachable throughout; failures are not transport hangs.

## Actual

```
$ openclaw plugins reload typesafe
Plugin operation failed during drain: plugin typesafe admitted work did not settle within 60s;
the previous plugin generation stays active. ... | plugin host cleanup timed out: retained plugin work
Gateway generation 2: replacement not applied.
```

Gateway log, same moment:

```
Plugin replacement queued behind 11 retained work item(s) for plugin typesafe.
Running turns keep typesafe until they finish because it does not declare reload.turnHandover.
```

Instance snapshot from the same log record:

```json
{"pluginId":"typesafe","generation":2,"acceptingCalls":true,"replacementPending":true,
 "references":[
   {"reason":"prepared-generation-lease","owner":"unknown","cleanupState":"active"},
   {"reason":"prepared-generation-lease","owner":{"agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:main"},"cleanupState":"active"},
   {"reason":"prepared-generation-lease","owner":"unknown","cleanupState":"active"}
 ]}
```

The count grew across the session (4 → 6 → 8 → 11 → 13) and none were released after the owning turns ended; `openclaw plugins reload typesafe --wait` (bounded 10-minute drain) also failed. A process restart resets the count to zero, after which the same sequence re-accumulates.

The same behaviour was observed on a different plugin in the same deployment (`image-ui-autostart`: 4 → 6 retained items), so the leak is probably in the shared prepared-generation lease path, not specific to decision providers.

## Expected

Leases acquired for a single evaluation are released when that evaluation settles (success, error, cancellation, or timeout), so the generation reaches zero retained work and can be replaced without restarting the Gateway.

## Reproduction

1. Select the typesafe decision provider with a custom `baseUrl` and issue several `decision_evaluate` calls (any question type; failures count too).
2. End the turns.
3. `openclaw plugins reload typesafe` → drain timeout after 60 s.
4. Inspect gateway log for `Plugin replacement queued behind N retained work item(s)` and for the `prepared-generation-lease` instance snapshot; `owner` is `unknown` for several entries with `cleanupState: active`.

Note step 1 is the only producer needed — the leak occurs even when the decision call itself fails with `unsupported-input`, i.e. on the error path.

## Demonstrated impact

- Plugin upgrades and hot-fixes are impossible on a long-lived Gateway: every replacement requires a full process restart, which is a service interruption rather than the targeted reload the command exists for.
- Since a version change re-stages the plugin from npm, any local workaround is discarded on restart — operators cannot pin a patched build while waiting for an upstream fix.
- Repeated reload attempts themselves add leases, so retrying makes the condition worse rather than clearing it.

## Remediation advice

- Release `prepared-generation-lease` references in a `finally` on the decision evaluation path (including early `unsupported-input` returns and provider errors), and ensure leases created without an owner are attributed or cleaned.
- As a backstop, treat ownerless leases older than a bounded age as reclaimable during drain, or report them in the drain error (`13 retained items, 9 ownerless older than 10 min`) so the operator is not required to restart the process.

---
Drafted from live gateway logs by an automated agent running on the affected instance; log excerpts above are verbatim, with the plugin/host names kept generic where they are not needed to reproduce.

issues.body:
### Summary

When the agent asks for a credential with the `secrets` tool and the owner saves it, the same run's next `exec` still can't use it, because exec captured its store snapshot on the run's first command. The agent has to tell the owner "send another message so I can try again", right after asking them to do the safe thing.

### Problem to solve

1. Mid-task, the agent hits an API that needs a token and calls `secrets` `action: "request"`.
2. The owner types it into the masked prompt; the tool returns `status: "stored"`.
3. The agent runs the command again in the same run: no sentinel for the new name, the call fails.
4. The documented answer is "from the next reply" (`docs/gateway/secrets/secret-store-and-egress.md`: "Gateway-hosted exec captures the store snapshot on its first execution in a run ... storing a credential does not refresh an already-captured exec snapshot"). The tool result even says "Stored does not prove ... current exec snapshot" (`src/agents/tools/secrets-tool.ts:360`).

For the owner this looks broken: they did what was asked and the task still stops.

Where it happens, at main eb0faf79a5b: `createExecTool` memoizes one `storeEnvPromise` per tool instance (one per run) and reads it on the first exec only (`src/agents/bash-tools.exec-run.ts:101-119`); every later command in the run reuses it (`:420`).

### Proposed solution

Narrow on purpose: refresh only for additions the run itself asked for and got.

- When the run's own `secrets` request returns `stored` for name `N`, the next exec in that run adds `N`'s sentinel and its current allowed hosts to the snapshot (one selected read, like `readSelectedSecretStoreEntries`).
- Nothing else changes: names already in the snapshot keep their captured value and hosts; deletions, replacements and host edits by anyone else still apply from the next run; already-running processes keep their fixed grants (the #152557 contract).
- Because the added entry is a committed answer ("A committed answer is terminal", docs), this avoids the stale-binding and rollback questions that came up for the broader refresh in #155027.

### Alternatives considered

- #155027 (open, stale since October) refreshes the protected layer on any store mutation and re-validates bindings at launch. Its review found a rollback admission problem and a main-thread read; a run-scoped "own answers only" rule sidesteps both and is a smaller contract change.
- Ending the turn and asking the owner to send another message: the current workaround, a poor experience for a step the agent itself started.

### Impact

Every first-time credential setup through the `secrets` tool hits this, which is where the store is most often used.

### Evidence/examples

- #152409 (closed, stale): the review there named the per-run snapshot as a likely cause of a "token inactive" report after saving a credential mid-session.
- #155027: open PR for the broader version, labelled security-boundary and needs proof, no maintainer decision yet.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance. It changes the documented snapshot contract, so we would wait for a maintainer's OK on the direction first.

### Additional information

Seen on 2026.11.10; source references are at main eb0faf79a5b.

labels.name: P3

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With a custom provider using `api: "anthropic-messages"`, assistant text emitted before a tool call is never tagged as `commentary`, so Telegram `progress` drafts with `streaming.progress.commentary: true` never show it; only the tool/status line (e.g. "Exec") appears.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a custom model provider with `api: "anthropic-messages"` (here: a self-hosted OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible gateway in front of Claude) and use a Claude model on the built-in (embedded) runtime.
2. Telegram account streaming config:
   ```json
   { "mode": "progress", "progress": { "commentary": true, "toolProgress": false, "label": false, "maxLines": 3 } }
   ```
3. In a Telegram DM, ask the agent to run a multi-step task where each step writes a short sentence and then calls a tool (e.g. three ~10 s waits, each preceded by "Stage N: ...").
4. Watch the progress draft while the turn runs.

### Expected behavior

Per `docs/concepts/progress-drafts.md` (Commentary lane / Status headline), the pre-tool sentences should appear in the progress draft as commentary rows (or as the status headline).

### Actual behavior

The draft only shows the current-operation line ("Exec"). None of the pre-tool sentences appear at any point during the ~30 s turn. The final answer is delivered normally.

Inspecting the session transcript via `sessions_history`, every affected assistant message has `api: "anthropic-messages"`, `stopReason: "toolUse"`, content `[thinking, text, toolCall]`, no message-level `phase`, and the `text` block has **no `textSignature`**. So `resolveAssistantMessagePhase` / `extractAssistantCommentaryText` return nothing, and `embedded-agent-subscribe` never publishes the `item` event with `kind: "preamble"` (it only does so when `phase === "commentary"`).

From the shipped `dist` of this build: the only stream parsers that tag pre-tool text as commentary are the Responses path (`encodeTextSignatureV1` with a phase) and the Claude CLI stream-json parser (`flushPendingClaudeText("commentary")` on `content_block_start` of a `tool_use` block). The `anthropic-messages` stream parsers that handle `content_block_start` contain no commentary handling at all.

This looks like the same class of gap as #133922 (native Ollama stream left pre-tool narration unphased). A comment there states that the Anthropic transport already tags commentary; that does not seem to hold for custom providers on `api: "anthropic-messages"`.

Suggested fix: in the `anthropic-messages` stream, when a `tool_use` content block starts in the same assistant message, tag the preceding visible text block(s) with `textSignature: {"v":1,"phase":"commentary"}`, mirroring the Claude CLI parser, and keep tool-free answers untagged.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.10 (6ea542f)

### Operating system

Linux arm64 (kernel 7.0.0-1015-oracle)

### Install method

Docker image (Gateway runs in a container)

### Model

claude-opus-5-5

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw (embedded runtime) -> custom provider with `api: "anthropic-messages"` -> self-hosted new-api gateway -> Anthropic

### Additional provider/model setup details

The provider's default `api` is `openai-responses`; the Claude models override it with `api: "anthropic-messages"`. For comparison, a Grok model on the same provider via `openai-responses` (proxied, response ids `chatcmpl-...`) also produced untagged pre-tool text blocks, since the proxy does not return a `phase`, so switching wire API is not a workaround here.

### Logs

Gateway logs for the affected runs contain no `preamble` / `commentary` entries. Turn timing shows `embedded_run`.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Transcript shape of an affected assistant message (from `sessions_history`, text shortened):

```json
{ "api": "anthropic-messages", "stopReason": "toolUse",
  "content": [ {"type":"thinking"}, {"type":"text","text":"Stage 1: ..."}, {"type":"toolCall"} ] }
```

issues.body:
### Summary

Protected (`kind: "secret"`) store entries can't serve unattended helper processes. Durable exec (`durable: true`) launches without sentinels, proxy grant or proxy environment, by design, because grants end with the Gateway. In practice, owners who want a background helper that calls an HTTPS API keep its token in a plaintext file or an agent-readable `env` entry instead.

### Problem to solve

The flow we keep hitting:

1. The agent asks the owner to save a token in Settings → Secrets (or via the `secrets` request tool), with its allowed host.
2. The work that needs it is long-running or must survive Gateway restarts: a watcher, a sync loop, a periodic API poller started with `exec durable=true`.
3. The command starts with the warning `Durable execution starts without N secret-store credentials: secret-egress grants end when the Gateway restarts ...` (`src/agents/bash-tools.exec-run.ts:426-430` at eb0faf79a5b) and the API call fails.
4. The only working options are non-durable background exec (dies on every Gateway restart or update) or moving the token out of the protected store into a file the process reads, which is exactly what the store was meant to replace.

So the store's main promise, "save it once, the agent can use it without seeing it", holds only for work that fits inside one Gateway lifetime.

### Proposed solution

A grant model for durable processes that keeps sentinel-only exposure:

- At launch, a durable command that opts in (e.g. `secrets: ["NAME", ...]`, admin or owner approved, same exact-host bindings) gets sentinels plus proxy and CA variables, like non-durable exec.
- The grant is owned by the durable process record (the same owner that already survives restarts), not by the Gateway process, and is re-registered with the proxy when the Gateway starts and re-adopts the durable process. Stopping, exiting or retiring the durable process revokes it, as today.
- What would need to stay stable across restarts for this to work: the proxy endpoint the child was given (today `listen(0, ...)`, `src/secrets/egress-proxy/proxy-server.ts:680`), the proxy credential, the sentinel keys (process-local, `src/secrets/sentinel.ts:24-32`), and the CA the child trusts (generated per Gateway start, docs "secret egress proxy"). One option: a small per-durable-grant state (fixed loopback port or socket, persisted grant token, a durable-scoped CA and sentinel key) written under the state dir with the same 0700/0600 rules. The existing job-scoped grant owner (`withJobSecretEgress`, `src/secrets/job-egress.ts`) already shows one proxy and grant per job.
- While the Gateway is down, requests just fail (407 or connection refused), and no plaintext is ever handed to the child.

### Alternatives considered

- Non-durable `background: true`: works until the next Gateway restart or update, then the helper is gone.
- `kind: "env"` entries: plaintext to every Gateway exec and to `store list/get`.
- Tool-owned plaintext files: the status quo, outside any OpenClaw policy or audit.
- #199092 (cron `command` payloads) asks for the same thing for a different launcher; a shared answer to "who owns a grant that is not tied to an agent run" would likely cover both.

### Impact

Anyone who runs long-lived helpers next to the Gateway on Linux or macOS. Today it pushes credentials back into plaintext, so the security effect of the store is lost for exactly the tokens that live longest.

### Evidence/examples

- Docs say it directly: "Durable commands launch without these grants, sentinels, or proxy settings because grants end with the Gateway" (`docs/gateway/secrets/secret-store-and-egress.md`, `docs/gateway/background-process.md` "Durable processes").
- Related: #152557 (merged) moved grant ownership to the process supervisor for non-durable background commands; this asks to extend that owner model to durable ones. #199092 (cron command payloads, open, needs product decision).

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance. It changes a security boundary, so we would only start after a maintainer picks the direction.

### Additional information

Seen on 2026.11.10; source references are at main eb0faf79a5b.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With a `claude-cli` agent, the stranded-reply retry prompt (`[System] Your previous reply was not delivered because you did not call message(action=send). Your reply text was: "…"`) comes back from the Claude Code session file as an ordinary user message, so the Control UI shows it as a right-aligned bubble in the operator's own color, as if the operator had typed it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On 2026.11.10, set `messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"` and run an agent whose model goes through the `claude-cli` backend.
2. In a Control UI WebChat (dashboard) session, send a message. In 2026.11.10 the turn guidance for this surface says there is no current conversation and to reply normally, so the agent ends with ordinary final text and no `message(action=send)`.
3. The Gateway logs `source-reply/private-final` (`message_tool_only`) and queues the stranded-reply retry.
4. After the retry run finishes, look at the chat (or `chat.history`) for that session.

### Expected behavior

The retry is a host-generated turn. It should be hidden or rendered as a System notice, and never attributed to the operator. `resolveStrandedReplyRecovery` already sets `suppressNextUserMessagePersistence: true` and `transcriptPrompt: undefined`, so the retry is clearly not meant to appear as a user message. OpenClaw's other host turns in the same Claude Code session files are stored as `isMeta` rows and skipped by the import (see Logs).

### Actual behavior

The chat shows the retry prompt as a user bubble on the operator's side, quoting the agent's whole previous reply. In the session history the row looks like this (IDs and reply text elided):

```json
{
  "role": "user",
  "content": "[System] Your previous reply was not delivered because you did not call message(action=send). Your reply text was: \"…\". If the user should see a reply, send it now with message(action=send). If no reply is needed, answer exactly NO_REPLY.",
  "__openclaw": { "id": "…", "importedFrom": "claude-cli", "cliSessionId": "…", "externalId": "…" }
}
```

It has no `provenance`, no `display: false` and no sender fields. The operator's real messages in the same session carry `provenance: { kind: "external_user" }` and the sender identity.

Code path (traced in the 2026.11.10 dist; the same logic is on `main` @ 01a178c, where `stranded-reply-recovery.ts` is byte-identical to the tag):

1. `resolveStrandedReplyRecovery` builds the retry run from `...params.base.run` and never sets `inputProvenance` ([stranded-reply-recovery.ts L56-L84](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/01a178c900eeb3d107289af541b3987fe01a7a15/src/auto-reply/reply/stranded-reply-recovery.ts#L56-L84)). The retry inherits the provenance of the user turn that produced the stranded final (`external_user`).
2. The CLI runner sends a prompt as host input only when `isHostGeneratedInputProvenance(inputProvenance)` is true ([execute-plugin.ts L481-L483](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/01a178c900eeb3d107289af541b3987fe01a7a15/src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin.ts#L481-L483), [input-provenance.ts L28-L31](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/01a178c900eeb3d107289af541b3987fe01a7a15/src/sessions/input-provenance.ts#L28-L31)). So the retry reaches Claude Code as normal user input, and Claude Code writes it as a plain `type: "user"` row, not `isMeta`.
3. The claude-cli history import assumes this never happens. It skips only `isMeta` rows ([L322-L328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/01a178c900eeb3d107289af541b3987fe01a7a15/src/gateway/cli-session-history.claude.ts#L322-L328)), and its comments say "OpenClaw sends its own turns as synthetic input, which Claude stores as meta rows" ([L295-L310](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/01a178c900eeb3d107289af541b3987fe01a7a15/src/gateway/cli-session-history.claude.ts#L295-L310)) and "Forwarded and host inputs are synthetic meta rows, which never reach this branch" ([L433-L440](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/01a178c900eeb3d107289af541b3987fe01a7a15/src/gateway/cli-session-history.claude.ts#L433-L440)). The `[System]` row matches none of the known internal shapes, so it is imported as `role: "user"` with no provenance.
4. The Control UI renders user-role rows as System notices only when `provenance.kind === "internal_system"` ([chat-system-notice.ts L225](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/01a178c900eeb3d107289af541b3987fe01a7a15/ui/src/pages/chat/chat-system-notice.ts#L225)), so this row is drawn as the viewer's own message.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.10

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (x64), Node 26.13.1

### Install method

npm global install; Gateway runs as a systemd user service

### Model

claude-opus-5-5 (`claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5`)

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw Gateway → claude-cli agent harness → Claude Code CLI 2.1.332 → Anthropic

### Additional provider/model setup details

- `messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"` and `messages.groupChat.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`.
- The dist carries two local patches outside this code path. One in `cli-session-*.mjs` keeps the native session across prompt-tool drift (#186684). One in `source-reply-delivery-mode-*.mjs` keeps internal WebChat on `automatic`; it was applied after the observations below and removes the WebChat trigger, not this bug. I have not re-run the scenario without the first patch.

### Logs

One host, 2026-11-26 (redacted):

```text
12 x [source-reply/private-final] agent produced a private final reply without calling the configured
     delivery tool (message_tool_only); response kept private and not delivered to the source channel
     (all channel=webchat, 5 dashboard sessions, 06:28Z-23:58Z)
```

- Claude Code session files from the same day contain 11 stranded-retry turns. All 11 are plain `type: "user"` rows without `isMeta`.
- In the same files, OpenClaw's other host turns from that day were written with `isMeta: true` and the prefix `[MESSAGE FROM NON-USER SOURCE - NOT USER INPUT]`. Examples are `[System] Your previous turn was interrupted…` and the Gateway-restart interruption note. The import skips those rows.
- The retry row I inspected in session history, the one from the screenshot case, is imported exactly as shown under Actual behavior.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

No screenshot is attached because the bubble quotes a private reply. It is a right-aligned bubble in the same color as the operator's own messages, and its text starts with `[System] Your previous reply was not delivered…`.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: any `claude-cli` agent where the stranded-reply retry fires. In 2026.11.10 that includes WebChat turns that end with a plain final while `messages.visibleReplies` is `message_tool`. That trigger is tracked in #205158 and #159230.
- Severity: misleading rather than blocking. The chat shows a message the operator never wrote, attributed to them, and it repeats the whole previous reply.
- Frequency: every stranded retry on `claude-cli`. All 11 that day were written as plain user rows.
- Anything that reads the imported transcript also sees the turn as user input. #189955 (memory-lancedb stores this turn as a user memory) looks like the same root cause.

### Additional information

Suggested fix: give the retry run host provenance, for example `inputProvenance: { kind: "internal_system", sourceTool: "stranded_reply_retry" }`. `transcript-followup-run.ts` already does this for its own `formatSystemTurnPrompt` turns ([L45-L48](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/01a178c900eeb3d107289af541b3987fe01a7a15/src/auto-reply/reply/transcript-followup-run.ts#L45-L48)), next to the same `suppressNextUserMessagePersistence: true`. The CLI runner would then send the retry with `promptOrigin: "host"`, Claude Code would store it as `isMeta`, and the import would skip it, as #185746 intended.

One caveat: `inputProvenance` also feeds the retry's reply-expectation and reply-threading checks. If changing it there is a problem, setting `promptOrigin: "host"` for `strandedReplyRetry` runs would also work.

Related: #159230, #205158, #189955 / #189956, #133938 / #149322, #185746, #122908 (earlier fix for recovery prompts that appeared as operator-authored messages), #167710.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

For the first minutes after the Gateway starts, Sign in with ChatGPT (token-sharing) requests from isolated cron runs fail and fall back. The refresh path reports `OAUTH_PROVIDER_CONFIGURED_UNAVAILABLE` even though the bundled `openai` plugin is enabled. The fallback is logged with `reason=unknown`. The same job succeeds on GPT a few minutes later without any configuration change.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in with ChatGPT (`--method siwc`) and give the agent `openai/gpt-6.2-sol` as primary, with a fallback on another provider. Keep `plugins.allow` including `openai`, `plugins.deny: ["codex"]` and `models.providers.openai.agentRuntime.id: openclaw`.
2. Create an isolated agent cron job with `--model openai/gpt-6.2-sol --fallbacks <other provider>/<model> --light-context --session isolated`.
3. Restart the Gateway. Within about a minute of `http server listening`, trigger the job with `openclaw cron run <id>`.
4. Wait a few minutes after startup and run the same job again.

The failure is timing-dependent. In our deployment, a run 37 seconds after `http server listening` fell back. Runs at 5 minutes, and an hour later, used GPT. While the stored access token was past expiry, the refresh error repeated for at least 3 minutes after startup, until the pod was replaced.

### Expected behavior

The cron run uses `openai/gpt-6.2-sol`, as the identical job does a few minutes later on the same process with the same credential. Alternatively, it waits for or activates the owning provider plugin before treating the credential as configured-unavailable.

### Actual behavior

The run falls back to the secondary model. Gateway log, with profile ID redacted:

```
[gateway] http server listening (7 plugins: browser, memory-core, openai, ...; 15.3s)
[agents/model-providers] openai: OAuth profile "openai:token-sharing:<redacted>" could not be resolved (OAuth token refresh failed for openai: OAuth provider "openai" is configured but unavailable. Install or enable its owning plugin, then retry; run openclaw doctor for diagnostics.. Please try again or re-authenticate. | OAUTH_PROVIDER_CONFIGURED_UNAVAILABLE); ...
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=openai/gpt-6.2-sol candidate=openai/gpt-6.2-sol reason=unknown next=<fallback>
```

In the 37-second case the access token was fresh, so no refresh error was logged. The only record of the failure is `reason=unknown`. The `openai` plugin is listed as loaded in the startup line in both cases.

`refreshOAuthCredential` (src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-provider-operations.ts) throws `OAuthProviderConfiguredUnavailableError` when `resolveProviderOAuthCredentialWithPlugin` finds no runtime plugin for a provider whose ownership is configured. That suggests the provider runtime plugin is not yet resolvable for the isolated cron lane during startup.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.8 (2d4ab29), image ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.11.8-slim

### Operating system

Linux x86_64 container (Kubernetes)

### Install method

Docker image

### Model

openai/gpt-6.2-sol via Sign in with ChatGPT (token-sharing)

### Provider / routing chain

openai (SIWC, `agentRuntime.id: openclaw`) → fallback to an OpenAI-compatible provider

### Provider setup details

Bundled `openai` plugin enabled, `codex` denied, tools code mode disabled. Credential created with `openclaw models auth login --provider openai --method siwc`. Access tokens have a one-hour lifetime and are refreshed normally once the Gateway has been up for a few minutes: a run just after expiry, on a warm process, refreshed and succeeded.

### Logs, screenshots, and evidence

See Actual behavior. Five isolated cron probes with the same job definition on the same credential:
- 37 s after startup: fell back, `reason=unknown`.
- About 3 min after an earlier startup, with an expired stored token: fell back after `OAUTH_PROVIDER_CONFIGURED_UNAVAILABLE`.
- 5 min after startup with no foreground turns: GPT, 8.4 s.
- Warm process, just after token expiry: refreshed, GPT, 7.4 s.
- Warm process: GPT, 8.3 s.

### Impact and severity

Scheduled jobs that start soon after a Gateway restart (deploys, config changes that roll the process, upgrades) silently run on the fallback model. Severity: degraded output without an actionable error. Frequency: intermittent, tied to restart timing. The `reason=unknown` fallback log makes it hard to diagnose.

### Additional information

Possibly related: #201933 (token-sharing refresh failure classification) and #172563 (SIWC `token_expired` recovery, closed). Neither covers the startup window. Separately, it would help if the fallback decision logged the underlying error instead of `reason=unknown`.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The Secret Egress Proxy fails to connect to HTTPS upstreams that use an internally trusted or self-signed certificate, even when that certificate is trusted by the host OS and available through NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS.

The request reaches the egress proxy successfully, but the proxy then fails its own upstream TLS connection with:

Secret egress proxy could not reach the upstream host.

### Steps to reproduce

IIS Proxy for a local app.
NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
Protected secret stored with the proxy set as allowed host
OpenClaw: 2026.9.x
Node: 24.19.0
Ubuntu host
Internal HTTPS upstream:
https://internal.example.local
resolves to a private RFC1918 address
Self-signed certificate trusted by Ubuntu
NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
secrets.egressProxy.enabled=true
internal.example.local present in allowedHosts
bypassHosts=[]

### Expected behavior

Ability to communicate with service using the stored protected secret.

### Actual behavior

OpenClaw reports The curl command returned a 502 Bad Gateway error. The secret egress proxy could not reach the upstream host. This happens whether it's an authenticated endpoint or not.
Putting the host into the bypass list allows unprotected endpoints to work.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.4

### Operating system

Ubuntu 26.04

### Install method

npm global

### Model

qwen 3.5 122B

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

_No response_

### Additional information

Root cause

The Secret Egress Proxy currently constructs its own upstream TLS agent approximately like this:

const upstreamTlsAgent = new Agent({
  ca: [...rootCertificates, caPem]
});

Because the proxy supplies an explicit ca list, privately trusted/self-signed upstream certificates are not automatically available to that TLS connection.

In testing, adding the required upstream certificate explicitly to this CA list resolves the issue.

Temporary workaround

The following local workaround resolved the issue.

The generated runtime bundle contained:

const upstreamTlsAgent = new Agent({
  ca: [...rootCertificates, caPem]
});

It was changed locally to:

const upstreamTlsAgent = new Agent({
  ca: [
    ...rootCertificates,
    fs.readFileSync(
      "/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/internal-service.crt",
      "utf8"
    ),
    caPem
  ]
});

After restarting the Gateway, Secret Egress requests to the internal HTTPS service succeed, including requests using protected-secret substitution.

This is only a temporary workaround because:

the certificate path is environment-specific;
generated dist files are replaced by OpenClaw upgrades;
it requires modifying compiled output directly.

issues.body:
The last tool result can push a turn over the soft compaction threshold while there is still room for the full answer. In that situation, OpenClaw can save a checkpoint, resume the turn, and immediately reopen a source the agent already read successfully. The user sent the request only once.

I found this while reproducing [#205387](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205387), when the drafting turn reread sources across multiple compactions before the reported stall.

## Reproduction

1. Run Gemini on an isolated gateway with a 40,960-token effective context window, an 8,192-token output allowance, and 2,500 recent tokens retained during compaction.
2. Ask the agent to review five drafts against release documentation, follow six linked evidence pages in order, and return the five texts with a brief editorial note. Require a reference found on the final page so completion of the last read is observable.
3. Size the pages so the final read crosses the soft threshold while the intact input plus the full output allowance still fits. Compare the next model action on main with a candidate that defers soft compaction once.

Of 16 scored pairs, **15 reached a matching closing-page boundary where main saved a checkpoint**. In **5 of those 15**, the first model action after resumption reread an earlier source and received identical content. Main answered after the checkpoint in the other 10.

In **all five corresponding candidate runs**, the deferred call returned the five drafts, the editorial note, and the closing reference. There was no reread or later compaction in those turns.

## Proposed fix

When soft compaction becomes due after a tool batch has settled, allow one ordinary model call with the intact history if the **conservative input estimate plus the full output allowance fits within the effective context window**. Use the larger of the outgoing request estimate and the maintenance estimate for this check.

Allow at most one deferral per user turn, including retries. If the model requests more tool work, reevaluate compaction at the next boundary. Hard overflow, insufficient output headroom, and unfinished tool work remain ineligible.

This result covers one model, Gemini, and one release-review fixture. The observed 5-in-15 rate is specific to that setup.

issues.body:
## Environment
- OpenClaw **2026.11.10 (6ea542f)**, npm global install, macOS (Apple Silicon, launchd `LaunchAgent` gateway)
- 17 configured agents, each with an isolated per-agent SQLite store (largest ~144 MB / ~24k transcript events / 420+ sessions)
- 15 Telegram accounts (isolated polling); several agents run scheduled jobs (hourly + daily cron) and a 30-minute heartbeat

## What happened
One isolated agent went dark with `AgentDatabaseAdmissionError` on every boot:

```
AgentDatabaseAdmissionError: Agent <id> (~/.openclaw/agents/<id>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite):
  plugin load reentry detected for cache key: 91547e5d…183d
Sessions remain unavailable. Stop the Gateway, run "openclaw doctor --fix" to inspect and repair
this agent database, and restart.
```

Observed 19 times on the first day, zero on the two prior days (nothing changed in that agent's config). A normal `openclaw gateway restart` did **not** clear it — the error re-fired on the next boot. Only a **full forced process cycle** cleared it: `openclaw gateway stop --force` → health endpoint down (000) → `openclaw gateway start`. After that, the agent's DB admitted normally, a probe turn succeeded, background integrity verification completed, and the error never recurred.

## Key finding: the fault is in-memory, not in the database
The recommended repair (`doctor --fix`) targets the agent database, but the database is healthy:

- `PRAGMA integrity_check` → `ok`
- No row anywhere in the store contains the reentry cache key
- All ~70 tables intact (transcripts, FTS indexes, session state, cache_entries, …)

So the "reentry" is **plugin-loader state inside the gateway process** that wedges that agent's admission latch, and it survives ordinary restarts but not a full stop→start. That also explains why the repair hint is misleading: there is nothing in the DB for the doctor to fix.

## Impact
- **Every scheduled job of the affected agent starves** (in our case 5 jobs + the heartbeat). Runs either fail closed or appear as 30–60 minute "model timeouts" — the model call never receives a real context because admission never completes.
- The failure is **silent per-agent**: the rest of the fleet stays nominal, so it reads like a provider problem.
- Admission stalls block everything that touches that agent's store (~60 s per attempt, e.g. the usage-cost background refresh fails with the same error).

## `openclaw doctor --fix` cannot complete in this state
Doctor never reaches repair: it dies ~55 s into "Preserve original state" with `Doctor interrupted by SIGTERM; cancelling inspections and settling admitted repairs before exit`, leaving "Doctor could not complete maintenance". The preserve phase appears to block on the same wedged admission. (In a supervised environment the SIGTERM arrives from the supervisor; either way the sanctioned repair path is unusable exactly when it is needed.)

## Workaround we run today
An external watchdog (outside the gateway process) detects fresh `plugin load reentry` log lines and performs the full stop→start cycle, then verifies health — restoring the lane within ~10 minutes without human intervention. This works but is a blunt instrument: **a full gateway cycle drops every other agent lane mid-flight** to fix one agent.

## Proposed fixes
1. **Make the reentry guard self-recover.** A "plugin load reentry" detection should time out and retry the load (or fail that one load) instead of latching the agent's admission as permanently unavailable until a process cycle. The guard exists to catch recursive loads; a wedged latch is worse than the condition it prevents.
2. **Don't block `doctor --fix` on the wedged admission.** The preserve phase should time out / skip the affected store and still complete maintenance for everything else, and the repair hint should distinguish "DB corruption" from "in-memory admission latch" — the DB is provably clean here.
3. **Offer a per-agent admission reset** (e.g. `openclaw agents reset-admission <id>` or a gateway RPC) so one dark lane can be recovered without cycling the whole gateway.

Happy to provide the full gateway log excerpt, the watchdog implementation, or the DB dumps (schema only) if useful.

## Related
- #197708 — released builds lacking admission recovery (sibling admission-refusal class)
- #190307 — agents permanently "degraded" after restart with the same `doctor --fix` repair hint (macOS/launchd, many agents — likely the same wedge viewed from a different error string)

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After `openclaw devices revoke --device <id> --role operator` on a Mac that should stay connected only as a node, the macOS app (2026.11.4 and 2026.11.5) re-opens its operator/control connection every 30–60 s, indefinitely.

- While the revoked token is still stored, the app sends it as `auth.token` and the gateway rejects it with `token_mismatch` (same mechanism as #190145; its fix #191424 is on `main` but not in v2026.11.5, v2026.11.6 or v2026.11.7).
- After I removed the stored operator token by hand, the app keeps re-dialing with no credentials (`auth=none`, `token_missing`) at the same cadence, although `authTokenMissing` is listed in `GatewayConnectAuthError.isNonRecoverable`.

The node connection of the same app is fine (`auth=device-token`). I found no documented way to run the macOS app as a node only.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Gateway 2026.11.5 on macOS with `gateway.auth.mode: token`, the token kept in a `file` SecretRef, and `gateway.nodes.pairing.autoApproveLocal: false`.
2. A macOS app paired with roles `operator` + `node` (remote mode over the app-managed SSH tunnel; a local-mode app on the gateway host shows the same).
3. Run `openclaw devices revoke --device <id> --role operator`.
4. Gateway log: `unauthorized … role=operator scopes=6 auth=token … reason=token_mismatch`, every ~30 s, for days.
5. Quit the app. Delete only the operator row (role key ending in `.b3BlcmF0b3I`) from `device_auth_tokens` in the app's client credential store. Relaunch the app.
6. Gateway log: `unauthorized … role=operator scopes=6 auth=none … reason=token_missing`, every 30–60 s. The node connects normally.

### Expected behavior

A device whose operator role was revoked on purpose can stay connected as a node without an endless operator reconnect loop. Either:
- after a revoked-token or credential-less (`token_missing`) rejection, the control channel stops re-dialing until the user acts, as `isNonRecoverable` suggests; or
- the app has a node-only mode that does not open the operator connection.

### Actual behavior

Operator connect attempts continue for as long as the app runs. Each attempt writes WARN lines on the gateway.

- Two Macs with revoked operator tokens: 1,039 `token_mismatch` log lines between 00:00 and 02:18 on one day.
- After the stale token was cleared on one Mac: 8 `token_missing` attempts in 6 minutes (02:23:55 to 02:29:55), still ongoing.

### OpenClaw version

Gateway 2026.11.5; macOS app 2026.11.4 (remote mode, SSH tunnel) and 2026.11.5 (local mode, same host as the gateway)

### Operating system

macOS 27.2.1 (gateway host and client)

### Install method

Gateway: OpenClaw runtime under ~/.openclaw as a launchd LaunchAgent; clients: OpenClaw.app release builds

### Model

N/A (no model call involved)

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable (gateway auth / macOS app connection)

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
# gateway log, stored (revoked) operator device token sent as auth.token
unauthorized conn=… peer=127.0.0.1:58522->127.0.0.1:18789 remote=127.0.0.1 client=<mac> ui v2026.11.4 role=operator scopes=6 auth=token device=yes platform=macOS 27.2.1 … reason=token_mismatch guidance=unauthorized: gateway token mismatch (provide gateway auth token)
{"cause":"unauthorized","handshake":"failed","phase":"auth_credentials_received","authMode":"token","authProvided":"token","authReason":"token_mismatch","role":"operator","scopeCount":6,"hasDeviceIdentity":true,"client":"openclaw-macos","mode":"ui","version":"2026.11.4"}

# after the stored operator token was removed and the app relaunched (local times)
02:23:55 role=operator auth=none reason=token_missing
02:23:59 client connected mode=node role=node auth=device-token version=2026.11.4
02:24:55 role=operator token_missing
02:25:56 role=operator token_missing
02:26:55 role=operator token_missing
02:27:25 role=operator token_missing
02:28:25 role=operator token_missing
02:29:25 role=operator token_missing
02:29:55 role=operator token_missing
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Code reading on tag v2026.11.5:

- `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/GatewayChannel.swift`, `selectConnectAuth`: with no explicit gateway token, `authToken = storedToken`, so the stored device token goes out as `auth.token`.
- `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/handshake-auth-helpers.ts`, `resolveUnauthorizedHandshakeContext`: `canRetryWithDeviceToken` is `true` for `token_mismatch` + device identity + `authProvided === "token"`, also when that token is the stored device token. The client therefore treats the error as recoverable, but `shouldRetryWithStoredDeviceToken` needs an explicit gateway token, so it reconnects with the same token.
- `rejectedStoredDeviceTokenOnlyAuth` from PR #191424 is on `main` but not in the v2026.11.5, v2026.11.6 or v2026.11.7 tags.
- With the token gone, `.authTokenMissing` is in `isNonRecoverable`, yet the operator connection is re-dialed every 30–60 s. Something above `GatewayChannel` (control channel refresh?) re-dials it. I did not trace which caller.
- `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/GatewayEndpointStore.swift`, `resolveLocalConfigAuthValue`: only `env` SecretRefs are resolved for `gateway.auth.token`. A local-mode app on a gateway that keeps its token in a `file` SecretRef therefore cannot present the shared token and cannot re-pair its operator role, so for that app the loop is permanent.

Related, not duplicates: #190145 (closed by #191424; same `token_mismatch` mechanism, fix not in a release yet), #204511 (iOS Share variant), #166707 (closed as not planned: a valid token not being sent, same `token_missing` cadence), #118035 (closed: status surfacing, the retry loop itself stays), #168743 (Control UI 4008 loop). None covers an intentionally revoked operator role or a node-only mode for the macOS app.

### Impact and severity

Affected: macOS apps whose operator role was revoked to keep them node-only. Severity: low; the node keeps working and every operator attempt is rejected. Frequency: continuous, one to two rejected connects per minute per app. Consequence: steady WARN lines on the gateway that bury real auth failures.

### Additional information

Why the operator role was revoked: exec-approval prompts should not appear on these Macs (the prompter in the app runs for any operator connection with `operator.approvals`). A node-only setting for the macOS app would cover this use case directly.

issues.body:
## Summary

On **2026.10.6 (fe06181)**, every agent turn on the **native Codex harness** appears to load the Codex plugin's module graph from `state/tmp/plugin-captures/<id>/captures/...` again, in the **main isolate**. The old copies are never released. In a controlled test, 3 one-word turns left **+152 MB of retained heap**, roughly **50 MB per turn**. That alone matches the slow main-heap growth reported in #159783 / #184843.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.6 (fe06181), bundled Node runtime, Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 26.04), `systemd --user`, 8 GB RAM
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=2048 --max-semi-space-size=8 --heapsnapshot-signal=SIGWINCH`
- 8 agents; 6 use `openai/gpt-6-sol` through the native Codex app-server harness (ChatGPT OAuth). Plus 7 Telegram accounts and WhatsApp.

## Controlled reproduction

1. Gateway started at 15:35. A heap snapshot (`kill -WINCH`, which forces a full GC first) was taken at 15:38:50: **A**.
2. Exactly 3 sequential turns ran on three different Codex-backed agents, each in a fresh session key: `openclaw agent --agent <id> --session-key agent:<id>:test:leakexp --message "answer with one word"`. Each finished in 7–10 s. No other agent runs were started in that window, and the Codex rollout directories show exactly 3 new threads.
3. A second snapshot was taken at 15:46:13: **B**.

Retained self size by node type (streaming aggregation of both snapshots):

```
total self size: 633.0 MB -> 785.3 MB (+152.3 MB); nodes 6,844,191 -> 8,674,890
  +57.6 MB  string                      244.3 -> 301.8
  +10.5 MB  array                        35.4 ->  45.9
   +9.7 MB  array (object properties)    36.2 ->  45.9
   +8.7 MB  concatenated string          22.7 ->  31.4
   +8.5 MB  object Object                29.5 ->  38.0
   +3.1 MB  object system / Context      10.3 ->  13.4
```

Strings grouped by prefix show **whole module sources duplicated, two copies per turn**:

| string (module source / path prefix) | copies in A | copies in B | per turn |
|---|---|---|---|
| `import { registerCodexCliMetadata } from "./cli-metadata.js"; ...` (Codex plugin entry) | 11 | 17 | +2 |
| `import { i as isJsonObject } from "./protocol-CANUwXJ3.mjs"; import { _ as resolveCodexPolicyMo...` | 128 | 220 | ~+31 |
| zod `core/util.js` locale modules (`const Sizable = ...`) | 684 | 1026 | +114 |
| zod `core.js` / `errors.js` / `$ZodCyclicError` modules | 12 | 18 | +2 |
| `/…/state/tmp/plugin-captures/<id>/captures/…` path strings | 64,062 | 93,005 | ~+9,600 |
| `file:///…/state/tmp/plugin-captures/<id>/captures/…` URL strings | 47,903 | 71,864 | ~+8,000 |

The same pattern shows over a longer window of the previous process: 8 → 17 copies of the Codex plugin entry, and 513 → 1,026 copies of the zod locale module, in 17 minutes with ~5 Codex turns.

## Expected

The Codex plugin modules are imported once per plugin generation and reused across turns. Or, if a fresh evaluation is intentional, it should run in a disposable worker or vm context that can be collected. ESM modules loaded into the main isolate can never be unloaded.

## Impact

About 50 MB of permanent main-heap growth per Codex turn. An active multi-agent gateway with a few hundred turns a day hits the V8 heap limit or the systemd memory cap within hours, and needs scheduled restarts. A tighter heap cap only shortens the time to OOM.

## Notes

- Snapshots were aggregated by node type/constructor and by normalized string prefix with a streaming parser. Happy to run more targeted checks, for example a retainer path for one duplicated module record, if a maintainer suggests what to look for.
- Possibly related: #181687 (catalog worker retention), #156191 (plugin capture memory pressure, closed for 9.5).

issues.body:
## Summary

Add an opt-in, single-owner escalation provider for Active Memory so a plugin can decide whether to start deep recall after the deterministic lane has no strong hit.

## Problem to solve

Active Memory has a sound two-lane architecture: the deterministic lane is cheap, while the deep lane runs a blocking embedded agent only when escalation is warranted. In the default escalate mode, however, the escalation decision is closed inside the bundled plugin and based on a built-in lexical intent matcher.

That leaves operators with only three choices:

- off: never run deep recall;
- always: pay for a blocking recall agent on every eligible turn;
- escalate: depend on the built-in matcher.

The matcher has already required language-specific repairs, including CJK support and the current PT-BR work in #135085 and #136502. A third-party plugin cannot replace only this decision: prompt-build hooks compose rather than claim the decision, and replacing the bundled Active Memory plugin also means taking ownership of its session isolation, privacy rules, timeouts, cleanup, caching, circuit breaker, status and deep-recall orchestration.

The missing capability is not another recall engine. It is a supported extension point for the small decision immediately before deep recall.

## Proposed solution

Expose an optional, lifecycle-aware Active Memory escalation provider through the plugin SDK.

Conceptually:

- a plugin registers one provider by id;
- Active Memory selects it through an optional escalationProvider config field;
- the provider runs only in escalate mode, after the deterministic lane has no strong hit and before the embedded recall agent starts;
- it returns recall, skip, or abstain;
- the provider receives an AbortSignal and a short bounded timeout;
- absent, missing, timed-out, failed or abstaining providers fall back according to an explicit, documented policy;
- off, always and strong deterministic hits retain their current behavior;
- existing configurations and defaults remain unchanged.

A dedicated provider is preferable to a general accumulating hook because exactly one component should own this decision. The SDK contract should not require or bundle any model. Implementations could be deterministic, local learned classifiers, or another policy chosen by the operator.

I plan to open a focused PR containing the SDK contract, registry/lifecycle handling, Active Memory integration, config/schema/UI hints, documentation and tests. It will not add a model, weights, network request or new runtime dependency.

## Alternatives considered

### Keep adding language-specific matcher rules

This preserves zero-dependency behavior but does not provide a scalable customization path. The PT-BR gap demonstrates that operators cannot currently supply a better policy without replacing the whole plugin.

### Run a generic LLM completion before recall

This adds another serial model request, authentication/failure surface, cost and latency to the path whose purpose is deciding whether to pay for deep recall.

### Replace the bundled Active Memory plugin

OpenClaw supports config plugins overriding bundled plugins, but this forces a third party to duplicate and track the full deep-recall implementation merely to change one decision.

### Use an ordinary prompt-build hook

Prompt-build hook results compose and do not offer a single-winner handled/cancel contract for this decision.

## Impact

Affected users and systems:

- multilingual personal-assistant deployments;
- operators with local or domain-specific recall-intent policies;
- latency-sensitive agents that cannot use always mode;
- plugin authors who want to improve escalation without owning memory retrieval.

Severity: medium. The current default works for covered formulations, but uncovered language or semantic forms can silently skip deep recall, while always mode adds a blocking agent run to ordinary turns.

Frequency: every eligible conversational turn reaches this policy after a weak deterministic result.

Consequence: either missed historical context, unnecessary latency, or downstream maintenance of a private Active Memory replacement.

## Evidence/examples

- PT-BR recall-intent gap: #135085
- PT-BR matcher repair: #136502
- Prior CJK matcher repair: #117419
- Blocking Active Memory latency report: #72015
- Active Memory documents that lane 1 makes zero model calls and lane 2 is a real agent turn:
  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/concepts/memory-architecture.md
- Current decision is internal to:
  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/active-memory/escalation.ts

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

## Additional information

The intended PR is additive and opt-in. It preserves the current built-in policy as the default and keeps model selection, datasets and classifier artifacts outside OpenClaw core. I will include focused provider lifecycle, sync/async, timeout, error, missing-provider, mode, strong-hit and embedded-run boundary tests.

issues.body:
## Summary

`exportTrajectoryBundle()` applies secret redaction **twice**: once correctly over structured
values before serialization, and then a second time as **regex raw-text replacement over the
already-serialized JSON/JSONL**. The second pass can rewrite JSON structural characters, so
`sessions export-trajectory` can emit **invalid JSON** that fails `JSON.parse`.

This reproduces deterministically for a given session and affects `events.jsonl` and every `.json`
file in the bundle.

## Affected code

In `src/trajectory/export.ts` (current `main`):

- **Serialization** — `trajectoryJsonlFile()` at L664-671 maps events through
  `safeJsonStringify(event)`; `jsonSupportBundleFile()` produces `JSON.stringify(...)`. `content`
  is now a string.
- **The problem** — `redactTrajectoryBundleFileContent()` at L674-680:
  ```ts
  return {
    ...file,
    content: redactToolPayloadText(file.content),
  };
  ```
  `redactToolPayloadText()` (`src/logging/redact.ts`) is a **string** redactor: it runs
  `redactRegisteredSecretValues()` then regex `redactText()` over the whole input.
- **Applied at** L1227 `const redactedFiles = files.map(redactTrajectoryBundleFileContent);`
  and again at L1234 for `manifest.json`.

When a redaction pattern matches a span of the serialized text, the replacement is written over
that span — including any JSON delimiters (`"`, `:`, `{`, `}`, `,`) inside it. The result is a
structurally broken document. A nested object value is enough to trigger it, e.g.:

```json
{"logo":{"@type":"ImageObject","url":"https://example.invalid/logo.png"}}
```

Consumers then fail with errors such as `Expecting ',' delimiter` at the byte offset where the
replacement landed. Because the source events are well-formed, the corruption is introduced purely
at export time.

## Why the second pass appears to be unnecessary

Every file written by `exportTrajectoryBundle()` already receives **structured** redaction before
serialization (line numbers from current `main`):

| File | Pre-serialization redaction |
|---|---|
| `metadata.json` | `redactTrajectoryExportValue` (L1169) |
| `artifacts.json` | `redactTrajectoryExportValue` (L1178) |
| `prompts.json` | `redactTrajectoryExportValue` (L1187) |
| `events.jsonl` | `redactEventForExport` per event (L1125) |
| `session-branch.json` | `redactTrajectoryExportValue` (L1197) |
| `system-prompt.txt` | `redactTrajectoryExportValue` (L1211) |
| `tools.json` | `redactTrajectoryExportValue` (L1219) |
| `manifest.json` | `redactTrajectoryExportValue` |

Nothing in the bundle — including `system-prompt.txt`, the only unstructured file — relies on the
post-serialization pass as its sole redaction.

The structured leaf path also appears to be a **superset** of the text path.
`redactSensitiveFieldValueWithOptions()` calls `redactRegisteredSecretValues()` and `redactText()`
with the same resolved patterns that `redactToolPayloadText()` uses, and additionally applies
`redactAppSpecificPasswords()`, `STRUCTURED_APP_PASSWORD_FIELD_RE`, and
`shouldRedactStructuredAuthorizationCode()`. Structured redaction further covers non-string
primitives via `shouldRedactStructuredPrimitiveField()`, which a text pass cannot reach.

So the post-serialization pass appears to add no redaction coverage while being the sole source of
the corruption.

## Suggested fix

Remove `redactTrajectoryBundleFileContent()` from the pipeline (both call sites and the helper),
leaving pre-serialization structured redaction as the single redaction boundary.

A JSON-aware variant (parse → redact → re-serialize) would also be correct, but looks redundant
given the structured pass already covers every emitted file.

Happy to open a PR with the change plus a regression test asserting **both** properties together:

1. every `.json` file and every non-empty `.jsonl` line parses, and a nested object value such as
   `"logo":{"@type":...}` round-trips intact; **and**
2. a synthetic secret is still masked and appears in no emitted bundle file.

Both assertions matter — fixing the corruption by weakening redaction, or preserving redaction
while emitting invalid JSON, would each be a regression in the other direction.

## Regression origin

The post-serialization pass appears to have been introduced in #89354 ("fix: redact trajectory
exports consistently", merged 2026-06-02). The structured redaction added there looks correct; it
is specifically the additional text pass over completed output that causes this.

## Environment

- Observed on OpenClaw `2026.7.1`, and the same code path is present on current `main`.
- Reproduces deterministically for an affected session; the stored trajectory itself is well-formed.

### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect state without a crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
OpenClaw for macOS 2026.9.2 repeatedly connects to an independently managed local Gateway without an auth token when `gateway.auth.token` is a protected SecretRef, while the embedded dashboard can authenticate separately.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Run OpenClaw Gateway 2026.9.2 on macOS in local mode at `ws://127.0.0.1:18789` through the existing per-user LaunchAgent.
2. Configure token authentication using a protected store reference:
   ```json
   {
     "gateway": {
       "mode": "local",
       "auth": {
         "mode": "token",
         "token": {
           "source": "store",
           "provider": "default",
           "id": "<redacted>"
         }
       }
     }
   }
   ```
3. Install and launch the signed OpenClaw 2026.9.2 macOS app from the official DMG.
4. Select the existing local Gateway / This Mac flow.
5. Authenticate the embedded dashboard with the same Gateway token.
6. Observe the menu-bar health state and macOS unified logs.

### Expected behavior
The macOS app should attach to the already-running local Gateway and authenticate its native control, health, and Mac-node connections. If it cannot resolve a protected SecretRef, it should request and store a client credential in macOS Keychain rather than repeatedly probing or restarting the existing Gateway.

This expectation is based on the macOS documentation stating that the app attaches when a Gateway already occupies the configured port and that token/password Gateway profiles store credentials in Keychain.

### Actual behavior
- The embedded dashboard can connect after its separate token prompt.
- The menu-bar app remains in a sleeping/needs-attention state.
- Native health, control, presence, and Mac-node WebSocket attempts omit the token and are rejected.
- During connection/configuration attempts, the app's Gateway readiness path restarted the existing Gateway more than once even though CLI health checks succeeded before and after.

### OpenClaw version
macOS app 2026.9.2; Gateway 2026.9.2 (build `3928bad`)

### Operating system
macOS 26.4.1, Apple Silicon (arm64)

### Install method
Official `OpenClaw-2026.9.2.dmg`; independently managed local CLI Gateway running as `ai.openclaw.gateway` LaunchAgent.

### Model
`openai/gpt-5.6-sol` (not involved in the failing connection path)

### Provider / routing chain
OpenClaw macOS app → direct loopback WebSocket → local OpenClaw Gateway

### Additional provider/model setup details
The model provider is not involved. Gateway token authentication succeeds from the CLI and embedded dashboard. The failure is confined to the macOS app's native connection.

### Logs
```shell
[ai.openclaw:gateway] gateway ws connect failed unauthorized: gateway token missing (provide gateway auth token)
[ai.openclaw:health] health refresh failed This gateway requires an auth token.
[ai.openclaw:presence] presence send failed: This gateway requires an auth token.
[ai.openclaw:mac-node] mac node gateway connect failed: unauthorized: gateway token missing (provide gateway auth token)
[ai.openclaw:gateway.process] gateway readiness failed reason=Gateway listener found on port 18789 (...) but health check failed: Gateway health probe timed out
```

At the same time, a direct CLI health check returned:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "eventLoop": { "degraded": false },
  "channels": {
    "telegram": {
      "lifecycle": "ready",
      "connected": true
    }
  }
}
```

All credentials, device identifiers, process identifiers, account details, and home-directory paths have been removed.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
Observed consistently in the menu-bar warning and native Connection settings. Screenshots are omitted because they included local machine details and masked credential fields; the sanitized logs above capture the failure.

### Impact and severity
- **Affected:** macOS app users attaching to a token-protected local Gateway whose token is stored as a SecretRef.
- **Severity:** High for the native-app workflow; the existing Gateway and browser/Telegram clients remain usable.
- **Frequency:** Reproduced on every native reconnect during this setup.
- **Consequence:** Menu-bar health, native Mac-node capabilities, Quick Chat/control connectivity, and reliable app attachment are blocked. Reconnection attempts can also restart an otherwise healthy local Gateway and briefly interrupt channels.

### Additional information
The Gateway was restored to `gateway.mode: "local"`, the experimental remote block was removed, and the protected `gateway.auth.token` SecretRef was preserved. The local Gateway and Telegram channel immediately returned healthy status. No plaintext credentials are retained in the submitted evidence.

### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect update validation / rollback)

### Summary
A managed npm-global update from 2026.11.4 to 2026.11.8 stable passed candidate Doctor, lint, config, plugin, schema and Gateway startup checks, but the activation-stage Doctor failed with `Invalid config`, triggering a successful rollback. The exact rejected field is absent from the retained update report.

### Steps to reproduce
Observed once on an existing production installation, not reproduced on a clean installation:
1. Start with a working 2026.11.4 Gateway managed by a systemd user service.
2. Initiate a stable update from Telegram `/update`.
3. Observe the candidate checks and activation result in `openclaw update status --json`.
4. After rollback, run `openclaw config validate --json`, `openclaw doctor --lint`, and `openclaw update --dry-run`.

### Expected behavior
Either detect the incompatible configuration before stopping the production Gateway, or apply the configuration migration consistently between candidate and activation environments. If activation fails, provide the rejected configuration field and error reason without exposing values or secrets.

### Actual behavior
Candidate admission: admitted with a legacy configuration warning. Database schema, runtime and plugin availability checks passed. Candidate Doctor exited 0 (~105.7 s); candidate lint exited 0 (0 errors, 16 warnings); candidate Gateway startup exited 0. Candidate config, plugin and recovery checks and package swap succeeded. Activation-stage Doctor failed in ~2.47 s. Database and package rollback completed, and 2026.11.4 was verified ready with channels ready and no plugin errors.

Total elapsed time about 20 minutes; reported downtime 397341 ms. After rollback, config validation returned `valid: true`, `warnings: []`. Two lint runs each completed 40 checks with two warnings (browser extension bootstrap not inspected and retained pre-migration database snapshot), no errors. A later dry run planned the same target and indicated package recovery admission could proceed. A dry run is not a full candidate validation or a second reproduction.

### OpenClaw version
Source 2026.11.4 (d843d6a); target 2026.11.8 stable.

### Operating system
Ubuntu Linux x64.

### Install method
npm global, systemd user Gateway; Node 24.22.1 (both CLI and managed Gateway), npm 11.19.1. CLI and service use different Node executable paths but the same version. SQLite state and agent databases.

### Model / provider
Not relevant to the local update failure.

### Logs
```text
status: rolled-back
reason: doctor-failed
candidate admission: config=warn, database-schema=ok, node-runtime=ok, plugin-availability=ok
candidate-doctor: exitCode=0
candidate-doctor-lint: exitCode=0; error=0; warning=16
candidate-gateway-startup: exitCode=0
package-swap: exitCode=0
openclaw doctor: status=failed; exitCode=1
exit; Invalid config at [redacted-path]
rollbackOutcome: succeeded
runningVersion: 2026.11.4
readyz: true
channelsReady: true
```
During startup of the restored release, two shared-state WAL TRUNCATE busy warnings and two `Gateway restart recovery state changed before orphan marking` errors occurred. These are subsequent observations, not established causes of the update failure.

### Additional information
Observed 2026-11-24. Original update report and retained pre-migration snapshots are available locally. No manual database cleanup or config edits performed as part of this diagnosis. The exact invalid field, whether heartbeat migration is involved, and whether the issue is reproducible on a fresh installation remain unknown.

Related but different activation Doctor error: #203442. Possibly relevant config migration discussion: #200224; no evidence yet that it is the same root cause.

### Impact
Stable update fails and causes ~6.6 minutes of production downtime before verified rollback. Request: investigate the mismatch between candidate and activation Doctor/config validation and improve actionable, redacted diagnostics.
