issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a Linux systemd-user Gateway deployment with local embeddings enabled, the kernel recorded 223 OOM kills of `llama-server` processes in `openclaw-gateway.service` within one calendar day, plus three OOM kills of processes named `openclaw`.

This is an incident report with kernel evidence, not a confirmed memory-leak diagnosis or a deterministic reproduction. Please advise whether it belongs to an existing issue and which supported, payload-free diagnostic would identify the memory owner and bound recovery attempts.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Actual behavior

Read-only examination of the retained kernel journal for 2026-10-03 00:00 through 2026-10-04 00:00, timezone UTC+08:00, found:

| Kernel OOM victim process name | Recorded kills |
| --- | ---: |
| `llama-server` | 223 |
| `openclaw` | 3 |
| `MainThread` | 7 |

All 223 `llama-server` victim PIDs were paired with an `oom-kill` record naming `openclaw-gateway.service` as their cgroup. These were `global_oom` / `CONSTRAINT_NONE` records, not proof of a service-specific memory cap being exceeded. The generic process name `MainThread` alone does not identify the executable; those seven events are not attributed to the Gateway main process here.

Distinct PIDs recur through the day. This demonstrates repeated kills of this process family, but does not establish whether each restart was automatic recovery, demand-driven loading, or another lifecycle path.

Three `openclaw` OOM kills occurred at 18:28:43, 19:03:49, and 19:05:59 UTC+08:00. The process name alone does not distinguish CLI invocations from the Gateway.

### OpenClaw version

Installed package inspected at report time (2026-10-04 UTC+08:00): `2026.9.8`. The exact build running at each earlier OOM event was not independently established; this installed version is not asserted to be the version of every historical victim.

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, Linux `6.8.0-142-generic`, x86_64; Node.js `v24.19.0` at report time.

Report-time `/proc/meminfo`: `MemTotal: 8128448 kB`, `SwapTotal: 4092924 kB` (approximately 7.75 GiB RAM and 3.90 GiB swap). Historical RAM size or changes earlier in the incident window were not independently established.

### Install method

Installed Node package; Gateway launched as a systemd user service. Package installation provenance: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Model

Report-time local embedding model configuration: `embeddinggemma-300m-qat-Q8_0.gguf`. The model used by each killed child is not individually verified. No conversational-model dependency is established.

### Provider / routing chain

Report-time memory search provider: `local`, enabled. Kernel victim membership establishes Gateway-service child involvement; exact per-event request routing is NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Report-time service contains `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3969`. This is a context observation, not proof that the worker-limit interaction in #157575 caused these incidents. Non-minimal deployment with additional integrations; no plugin-isolation A/B or clean-install comparison was performed for this report.

### Logs

Minimal redacted kernel extracts; timestamps preserved, hostnames/account details omitted:

```text
2026-10-03T00:01:16+08:00 global_oom CONSTRAINT_NONE victim-cgroup=openclaw-gateway.service task=llama-server pid=138998
2026-10-03T00:01:16+08:00 Out of memory: Killed process 138998 (llama-server) anon-rss:632308kB
2026-10-03T18:26:32+08:00 Out of memory: Killed process 380069 (llama-server) anon-rss:1113332kB
2026-10-03T18:28:43+08:00 Out of memory: Killed process 380902 (openclaw) anon-rss:345556kB
2026-10-03T18:39:27+08:00 Out of memory: Killed process 385053 (llama-server) anon-rss:1157876kB
2026-10-03T20:34:15+08:00 Out of memory: Killed process 405313 (llama-server) anon-rss:985076kB
```

Later retained Gateway memory-diagnostic sample (2026-10-03 23:50:38 UTC+08:00):

```text
level=critical reason=rss_threshold
rssBytes=3573121024 heapUsedBytes=1795562496
externalBytes=536553075 arrayBuffersBytes=214917684
workerHeapUsedBytes=597964432 workerCount=12 workerHeapSampledCount=11
workerMemoryCoverage=partial workerMemoryScope=direct
```

This is a later warning sample, not a measurement at the time of an OOM kill. ArrayBuffers must not be added to external memory as an independent total, and partial worker coverage does not account for every allocation.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

At report time the currently running service's systemd accounting showed:

```text
MemoryPeak=7424712704
MemorySwapPeak=4089634816
```

These are service-cgroup peaks, not Gateway-process RSS; they include children and cgroup-accounted memory. The peaks need not have occurred simultaneously. They are not the total memory of the whole host.

No raw configuration, database, session contents, heap dump, or full log archive is attached. No stress reproduction, restart, configuration change, or forced OOM was performed while preparing this report.

### Impact and severity

Affected: one observed Linux deployment. Repeated process termination is confirmed by the kernel (223 embedding-service-family victims and 3 `openclaw` victims in the retained day). Resource pressure can disrupt availability, but individual missed messages, data loss, or failure of every semantic request have not been established. Normal semantic recall was able to succeed during report preparation; the deployment is not asserted to be continuously unavailable.

### Additional information

Related reports reviewed before filing:

- #159356: managed embedding-child failures and OOM-correlated recall failures; different deployment and historical readiness concerns. Related symptoms, not proven identical cause.
- #125792: oversized context allocation for a different embedding model; this report does not establish the same context-allocation mechanism.
- #125344 (closed): accumulating local embedding workers / app-server processes; this report does not establish unbounded concurrent live children.
- #154812: RSS growth outside V8 heap; no native-leak attribution has been established here.
- #157575: managed Gateway heap policy overrides per-worker old-space limits; presence of a heap option alone does not prove that mechanism explains these kills.

No known-good/first-bad version, isolated regression, or deterministic trigger is established. The question for triage is how to attribute aggregate memory pressure and prevent repeated local-service kills/recovery attempts from compounding it, without exposing private memory or deliberately exhausting production RAM.

issues.body:
## Summary

After upgrading to openclaw 2026.10.7, the sqlite transcript migration moved ~8 months of historical sessions (from sessions.json) into the new sqlite transcript storage, but the reclamation subsystem **cannot drain the migrated backlog**: `commit checkpoint expired` fires repeatedly (194x in one night) and every checkpoint is invalidated. Consequences:

1. `active` transcript table grows to **441k rows / ~1.8 GB** with only 1,433 archived rows.
2. Periodic reclamation burns CPU/memory, pushing the V8 heap into cgroup OOM (gateway killed by memguard), and systemd-oomd kills again on PSI pressure (68% > 50%).
3. After each restart, startup reclamation fails -> agent DB enters degraded -> **all channel messages rejected** with `AgentDatabaseAdmissionError`.

Three incidents with the identical signature (2026-10-30, 2026-11-08, 2026-11-26), **all after the 2026-10-27 upgrade**. In the 8 months before the upgrade: zero incidents of this kind.

## Environment

- openclaw 2026.10.7 (upgraded from pre-10.x on 2026-10-27)
- node v24.22.1, Ubuntu 22.04, 12GB RAM
- ~8 months of history migrated from sessions.json (migration artifact `.pre-startup-migration.bak` present as evidence)

## Repro

1. Upgrade a long-running deployment (months of sessions.json history) to 10.x.
2. Watch reclamation logs: `commit checkpoint expired` repeats, backlog never drains.
3. On any OOM/restart, agent sqlite becomes degraded; channel messages get rejected with AgentDatabaseAdmissionError.

## Evidence

- journal: `checkpoint expired` x194 in one night; `AgentDatabaseAdmissionError` rejections; `dreaming startup cleanup failed`
- sqlite table stats: active = 441,284 rows vs archives = 1,433 rows, DB = 1.8 GB
- OOM timeline: memguard kill at 21:12 (V8 heap at cgroup limit), systemd-oomd kill at 23:05 (PSI 68%)
- 3 recurrence events with identical signature, all post-2026-10-27 upgrade

## Workaround applied locally

Archived 21,825+393 sessions with no activity for 14 days, using the official archive format (`reason=deleted`, zstd). DB shrank 1.8 GB -> 925 MB, reclamation resolved and DB healthy again.

## Suggestion

- After migration, run an **offline archive pass** proactively (or ship a `maintenance` command) so the migrated backlog is drained once, up front.
- Reclamation over a large backlog should **batch and rate-limit** instead of attempting one monolithic checkpoint that always expires.

The iOS app and OpenClawKit maintain separate suites for the same deep-link parser. Four cases overlap, while sixteen unique app cases are absent from the shared suite. Parser changes therefore require maintaining two test owners.

issues.body:
### Summary

I reproduced a Git update from 2026.9.37 to main at `4300f4156313293efcd8b794b6709076370c8bb3` failing with:

```text
State schema inspection failed (exit) after N seconds during shared database discovery
```

The worker’s strace shows PID 8259 refusing access because updater PID 2899, its own parent, holds the offline-maintenance lease.

In my tested matrix, every 9.x Git cell failed, including main alone and combinations with and without #204342/#204344. The 10.x Git and npm cells passed. Failed installations rolled back healthy, with shared schema 19, agent schemas 24, and integrity checks passing.

### Cause traced in source

1. **Git activates the new runtime before capturing the rollback databases.** The 9.37 runner calls `runtimePromotion.activate()` before `opts.onTransaction()`. That callback reaches `captureUpdateDatabases()`, which acquires `acquireGatewayLock({ role: "sqlite-maintenance" })` and retains it until capture finishes.  
   [Activation ordering](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/81da850122080b7187816ab70f145f3bc9e5efff/src/infra/update-runner-git.ts#L471-L505) · [Lease acquisition and release](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/81da850122080b7187816ab70f145f3bc9e5efff/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-database-backup.ts#L39-L89)

2. **The 9.37 inspection launcher selects the replaced runtime.** It resolves the worker’s installed `dist` path directly, without `captureRuntimeWorkerSource()`. Consequently, the old updater launches the new worker rather than its retained old worker. The missing binding was added by #160614 and exists in 10.10, but not in 9.37.  
   [9.37 launcher](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/81da850122080b7187816ab70f145f3bc9e5efff/src/infra/update-candidate-state.inspection.ts#L33-L38) · [Binding change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7a17d8ccbc13844fb74fb875792a62077312ceef)

3. **The old request does not provide the newer discovery inputs.** Its backup worker request omits `additionalPaths` and `preserveSourceArtifacts`. On the target, absent `additionalPaths` triggers supplemental plugin discovery, which reads persisted plugin metadata through the ordinary shared-state reader. This happens during “shared database discovery,” before discovery completes.  
   [Old request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/81da850122080b7187816ab70f145f3bc9e5efff/src/infra/update-database-backup.ts#L280-L298) · [Target discovery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4300f4156313293efcd8b794b6709076370c8bb3/src/infra/update-candidate-state.shared.ts#L184-L201)

4. **Parenthood does not transfer maintenance authority.** The admission check allows an appropriately scoped same-process owner, but rejects a different PID holding maintenance ownership. The parent’s process-local maintenance scope does not cross the subprocess boundary. This exclusion is intentional; the incompatible caller/worker combination is the problem.  
   [Admission check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4300f4156313293efcd8b794b6709076370c8bb3/src/infra/gateway-state-owner-record.ts#L122-L144)

This places the implicated failure in **pre-migration database capture after Git runtime activation**, despite the generic schema-inspection error. It is consistent with rollback retaining schemas 19/24.

The npm difference also fits: its transaction callback runs before package activation. Newer Git updaters retain their inspection worker and supply the newer capture inputs.

### Expected behavior

I expect a supported 9.x Git update to complete database capture and verification without treating its own inspection work as a competing maintenance operation, while retaining foreign-writer protections.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With a pre-commit hook in the backup repository that unstages a declared table file, `openclaw backup git create` exits 0 with no warnings while the commit it returns is missing that table, and `backup git verify` and `backup git restore` on that commit exit 1 with nothing restored. This is a proven mechanism for the failure mode reported in #206081, which was closed after the reporter's `.gitignore` steps did not reproduce.

### Steps to reproduce

Reproduced in a fresh Ubuntu ARM64 VM on OpenClaw 2026.11.10, with a 78-commit backup repository (three Git packs) and a 469,540,750-byte `agents/main/tables/memory_embedding_cache.jsonl`:

1. Set up a git backup that verifies clean: `openclaw backup git create --repository ~/openclaw-backup --all`, then `openclaw backup git verify --repository ~/openclaw-backup --agent main` (43 declared tables, all present).
2. Install a pre-commit hook in the backup repository that unstages the table, for example a `~/openclaw-backup/.git/hooks/pre-commit` containing `git reset -- "agents/main/tables/memory_embedding_cache.jsonl"`, and make it executable.
3. Run `openclaw backup git create --repository ~/openclaw-backup --agent main`.
4. Run `openclaw backup git verify --repository ~/openclaw-backup --ref HEAD --agent main`.
5. Run `openclaw backup git restore --repository ~/openclaw-backup --ref HEAD --agent main --target <fresh path>`.

Control on the same repository without the hook: three consecutive `create` runs re-add the table and verify passes, on both current main and release 2026.11.4.

### Expected behavior

`create` should not report success for a commit that fails its own `verify`: it should either fail, or record the omission as a warning so scheduled-backup status is not `ok`. This is the standard the code already holds restore to: `src/snapshot/git-backup-ownership.test.ts` deliberately commits refs missing declared artifacts and requires restore to reject them without publishing a target.

### Actual behavior

- `create` exits 0; JSON output contains the commit and `"warnings": []`; text mode prints `Git backup committed: <sha>`.
- The returned commit declares 43 tables in `agents/main/manifest.json` but contains 42 files under `agents/main/tables/`: the unstaged `memory_embedding_cache.jsonl` is absent from the tree.
- `verify` and `restore` on that commit both exit 1, and restore writes no file.

### Cause on current main (checked at e11a36d, 2026-11-27)

`commitGitBackup` in `src/snapshot/git-backup.ts` stages artifacts through a private temporary index set via the `GIT_INDEX_FILE` environment variable, then runs a plain `git commit` and returns `rev-parse HEAD`. Two gaps combine:

- The commit is not run with `--no-verify`, so the backup repository's own hooks run during `git commit`. Hooks inherit `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, so a pre-commit hook that resets paths edits the same private index after `update-index` has already staged every declared artifact.
- Nothing after the commit compares the new tree with the manifest's declared paths, so a commit that silently dropped an artifact is returned and recorded as a successful backup.

I could not find any handling of hooks (`--no-verify`, `core.hooksPath`) anywhere under `src/snapshot/` or `src/commands/backup-git.ts`, so this looks unintentional rather than a documented operator contract.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.10 (reproduced above). The same code path is present on current main (e11a36d) and was confirmed on main e6b35a1 and release 2026.11.4.

### Operating system

Ubuntu ARM64 (fresh VM)

### Install method

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Model

N/A, reproduced entirely in the backup CLI.

### Provider / routing chain

N/A, CLI-only.

### Logs

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Impact and severity

- Affected: any backup repository with a pre-commit hook that modifies the index, such as large-file filters or lint hooks, plus any other process that mutates the inherited index during `git commit`.
- Frequency: every `create` while the hook is installed; the reporter of #206081 saw the same symptom on every ref created after the exclusion.
- Severity: data risk. Scheduled backups record `ok` with no warnings while every new ref is unrestorable, and the unstaged tables are silently absent from the backup.
- Consequence: restore is impossible for the affected scope, with no signal at backup time.

### Additional information

Related: #206081. That report was closed as not planned after the `.gitignore` mechanism did not reproduce in clean-room tests, but the reporter's controlled retest still showed `create` exiting 0 with `warnings: []` while the returned commit was missing the declared table, and the path was present in the temporary index immediately after `update-index` yet absent from the commit. A pre-commit hook is a deterministic way to produce exactly that: it runs between `update-index` and the commit, against the same index. Whether the affected repository had such a hook is not established here.

Possible fix directions: pass `--no-verify` to the internal backup commit, since operator hooks were not meant to gate a deterministic snapshot commit, and/or verify the committed tree contains the manifest's declared paths before reporting success.

issues.body:
### Summary

Show `.csv` attachments as a readable table in the Control UI file viewer instead of raw text.

### Problem to solve

When I open a CSV attachment in a Control UI chat, the side panel shows the file as raw comma-separated text in a code block. Quoted fields, embedded commas and long rows wrap together, so a file with more than a few columns is hard to read. I have to download it and open it in another app to see which value belongs to which column.

### Proposed solution

Render CSV attachments (`text/csv` or a `.csv` file name) as a table: the first row as column headers, one table row per record, and quoted fields parsed per RFC 4180 (commas, doubled quotes and line breaks inside quotes). Keep a "View raw text" toggle, the same one Markdown attachments have, plus the existing copy and download actions. No new dependency is needed; the parser is a few dozen lines.

### Alternatives considered

- Adding a CSV library such as Papa Parse: more than this needs, since the viewer only reads files up to the existing 256 KB text preview limit.
- Leaving raw text: works for tiny files only.

### Impact

Affected: anyone who receives or attaches CSV files in Control UI chats (exports, reports, queues).
Severity: annoying; the file is unreadable in place.
Frequency: every CSV attachment.
Consequence: extra steps to download and open the file elsewhere.

### Evidence/examples

Before: a CSV attachment opened in the side panel (made-up data).

issues.body:
### Summary

Mattermost buttons whose value is not plain `[A-Za-z0-9]` open "Page not found." when clicked, and the click never reaches OpenClaw. A button with a Chinese value such as `删掉说明和备注两条帖子，只留表`, or with spaces or punctuation, is enough to break it. On current `main`, every button the agent sends with the `message` tool is affected, because the agent-callback mark (`::`) is part of the value.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure the Mattermost channel with interactions enabled.
2. Have the agent (or `message action=send ... presentation=...`) send a buttons block, for example `{"label":"只留表","value":"删掉说明和备注两条帖子，只留表"}`.
3. Click the button in Mattermost.

### Expected

The click reaches the Gateway, and the agent receives the button's original value.

### Actual

Mattermost shows "Page not found." The Gateway logs no `mattermost interaction:` line.

### Cause

`resolveMattermostPresentation` (`extensions/mattermost/src/normalize.ts`) uses the raw button value as the button `id`. `buildButtonAttachments` (`extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/interactions.ts`) passes it through `sanitizeActionId`, which strips only `-` and `_`. The result becomes both the Mattermost action `id` and `context.action_id`.

Mattermost registers the click route as `/posts/{post_id}/actions/{action_id:[A-Za-z0-9]+}` (`server/channels/api4/integration_action.go`, v11.7.15). Its router answers 404 for any other character before the integration callback runs. `Post.GenerateActionIds` replaces only empty ids, so an invalid id is stored unchanged.

Since #201764, agent-authored callback values are stamped `::<value>`, so even `approve` becomes the id `::approve` and 404s the same way.

Question buttons (`question-<n>`) and model-picker buttons are not affected: once `-` is stripped, their ids are alphanumeric.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.10 and current `main`
- Mattermost Team Edition 11.7.15

Prior attempt: #49920, closed by its author as opened in error, never reviewed.

prs.title: fix: tell users dictation is unconfigured when STT providers have no credentials
prs.body:
Related: #206051

## What Problem This Solves

Starting a dictation session (`talk.session.create` in transcription mode) can
fail with "No realtime transcription provider registered" even when realtime
STT plugins are loaded. That happens when none of those plugins has credentials,
so the error sounds like a missing plugin instead of missing Voice Call
streaming setup, and it does not point users at the right config.

## User Impact

If dictation cannot start because registered STT providers have no credentials,
the session error now says the provider is unconfigured and to check Voice Call
streaming credentials. The old "No realtime transcription provider registered"
message is kept only when the registry is actually empty. No migration or
config change is required. This does not change file-transcription
(`tools.media.models`) behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveConfiguredRealtimeTranscriptionProvider` used one fallback error after
the configured-provider loop. The fix splits that path: keep "registered" for
an empty provider list, and use an unconfigured / Voice Call streaming message
when providers are present but none is configured. That matches the existing
explicit-provider error style and avoids sending people to `tools.media.models`.

A small end-to-end smoke test lives in a sibling file rather than
`handlers/index.test.ts`, which is already over the repo line-cap ratchet.

## Evidence

- Issue #206051 is still open and unassigned; no existing PR claimed it.
- On `main` (HEAD `589a70ac87630a6b13fcf4c5b852ae599e98b2a4`), temporarily
  checking out the unfixed resolver made the new unit test fail: it expected
  "No realtime transcription provider is configured; check Voice Call streaming
  credentials" and received "No realtime transcription provider registered".
  The empty-registry case still passed. After restoring the fix, all three
  unit tests passed.
- An earlier smoke run of `talk.session.create` with
  `mode=transcription`, `transport=gateway-relay`, `brain=none` and two
  unconfigured providers also failed on `main` with

prs.title: refactor(subagents): centralize collector replay decisions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Code Mode and plugin-native collector spawns independently interpret persisted replay fingerprints and pending launch state. Maintaining those decisions in both callers exposes registry rows and duplicates the rule for when a previously accepted collector can be reused.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205482

## User Impact

Collector replays keep the same accepted IDs and refusal messages. The registry now makes the replay decision once; callers receive only the result they need. No public SDK, protocol, configuration, or persisted shape changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `getSwarmRunByLaunchReplayKey` with `resolveSwarmLaunchReplay`, and migrate both production callers in the same change. The query preserves requester scoping and the existing scheduler-owned queued check. It distinguishes the stable launch ID from the current registry run ID used for descriptive metadata.

| Consumer | Required fact | Owner after this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/agents/code-mode-swarm.runtime.ts` | Whether this invocation can reuse a collector, and its accepted IDs/label | Registry replay query |
| `src/agents/plugin-native-subagent.ts` | The same replay decision, plus current run ID for selection metadata | Registry replay query |

The raw lookup and the Code Mode row-to-result helper are removed. This slice covers replay; collection metadata and other consumer migrations remain separate work.

### Mechanical caller updates

- Both spawn adapters use the replacement query and translate its refusal states to their existing messages.
- Code Mode replay and lazy-load test doubles use the query result instead of a registry row.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test-support.ts` supplies the new missing-replay result.

## Evidence

- Format, Node syntax checks for all eight changed files, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent P0–P2 branch review of `af91b89f6524..537b23f7a253`, including unchanged liveness, state, row-type, and native-runtime contracts, found no actionable defects.
- Persisted-read cases cover stable launch/current IDs, mismatched fingerprints, a queued record without a scheduler reservation, and requester isolation. Runtime tests, typechecks, lint, and unused-export proof are pending PR CI.
- The Testbox attempt queued before test execution; its allocation was stopped and reconciled. PR CI supplies the dependency-backed proof under the campaign's standing rule. No local dependency installation was used.
- The final subagent suite must retain attribution of the known baseline `preserves routed native Stop authority ... (consumed-session)` failure if it recurs.

### Before/after

Against the rebased parent `af91b89f6524`:

- Raw replay field decisions in the two consumers: **4 → 0**; the two rules now live in the registry query.
- Consumers importing registry read/type implementation modules: **2 → 0**. Both still import the named registry facade and their existing swarm APIs.
- Subagent-mentioning lines in those consumers: **60 → 54**.
- Production diff: **41 lines removed, 56 added** (net +15 for the explicit result contract). Test diff: net +19.

Complexity scan baseline `df78bb4a3ac` versus the final source: `createRequestNativeSubagentRuntime` **85 → 84**, its `spawn` method **33 → 32**, `runAgentSpawnBridge` **38 → 38**, and the registry API factory **33 → 38**. The owner absorbs the shared decision; this is not an overall complexity-score reduction. Both scans cover all four selected production files without parse gaps.

### Overlap

Rebased after https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206443 merged. Open PRs touching selected owner/caller files were inspected: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188492, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187444, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194732, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/136554, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201774, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201315, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/121309, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155442. This change only replaces collector replay reads; it does not take their lifecycle, retention, or launch-contract work.

prs.title: fix: honor Qwen4-Max thinking levels on Token Plan
prs.body:
Closes #206303

## What Problem This Solves

With Qwen4-Max on Qwen Token Plan, OpenClaw enables thinking but drops the requested `reasoning_effort`. Both `/think low` and `/think xhigh` therefore send the same effort setting.

## User Impact

Qwen4-Max sends the selected `low`, `high`, or `xhigh` effort. `off` disables thinking. The aliases `minimal`, `medium`, and `max` map to the vendor's supported tiers. An explicit thinking budget still takes precedence.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Qwen plugin recognizes the direct Token Plan model reference and applies one model-specific mapping when preparing the payload and after caller payload hooks. The built-in picker profile uses the same supported tiers. See the [Qwen4-Max Chat Completions contract](https://help.aliyun.com/zh/model-studio/qwen4-max).

## Evidence

- Public base `c32abfe2a1a4fb327551723e4af77037db84829e` failed nine newly exercised regression cases across the profile, adapter, and HTTP request. The loopback receiver observed thinking enabled without an effort on both `low` and `xhigh`.
- Candidate `7c5a5563398e286865cbe93261661c586e7825ea` sent `reasoning_effort: "low"` and `"xhigh"` respectively through the OpenAI-compatible HTTP transport to the loopback fixture. The `off` request disabled thinking and omitted effort. All request input and model responses in this check were fictional.
- All seven adapter-level checks for thinking tiers and aliases passed on the candidate with synthetic payloads. The scoped TypeScript check, local formatting, plain lint, and diff checks passed.
- The full repository rerun has yet to complete on the available host. The repository's typed-lint gate stopped during SDK declaration preparation when that step timed out. This PR remains a draft with the scoped proof above.

prs.title: fix(codex): keep local threads across Codex and OpenClaw version upgrades
prs.body:
Related: #200018

## What Problem This Solves

After a routine local Codex CLI or OpenClaw update (for example from `0.172.0` to `0.172.1`), OpenClaw replaces active local Codex threads on the next user turn even when the local `CODEX_HOME` directory, rollout files, endpoint, auth identity, and plugin policy did not change. Users lose native thread continuity, drop pending native subagent recovery metadata, and pay a cold prompt-cache rebuild across active sessions after every patch release.

Three persisted local custody behaviors caused this loss:

1. `buildCodexAppServerRuntimeFingerprint` hashed transient `appServerVersion`, `serverVersion`, and `userAgent` strings into `local-loopback` thread bindings.
2. `buildCodexPluginThreadConfigInputFingerprint` hashed the full versioned `pluginAppCacheKey` (containing `openClawVersion`, `codexPluginVersion`, `appServerVersion`, `serverVersion`, and `userAgent`) into `pluginAppsInputFingerprint`.
3. When a legacy local binding resumed and wrote the updated version-free `appServerRuntimeFingerprint`, `preserveNativePendingAssignments` and `preserveCodexNativeSubagentSubmissions` hashed the raw runtime fingerprint string, saw a connection mismatch, and dropped both pending `nativeSubagentAssignments` and unmatched `nativeSubagentSubmissions` from the committed binding row.

## User Impact

Local Codex sessions (`connectionClass: "local-loopback"`) resume their existing native thread across Codex CLI and OpenClaw version upgrades, including sessions whose bindings were persisted by an earlier release before this fix. Pending native subagent assignments and unmatched submission receipts survive the first legacy upgrade resume and migrate their connection ownership hash atomically in place.

Supervised connection fingerprints introduced by `#104045` (`buildCodexAppServerConnectionFingerprint`, containing top-level `codexHome`, `homeScope`, and `cwd` without `runtimeIdentity`) stay strictly exact and are never normalized by `normalizeCodexAppServerLocalRuntimeFingerprint`. Remote Codex connections still require exact runtime and app-cache fingerprint matches, in-memory app-inventory caches stay versioned across upgrades, and local sessions still rotate threads and clear stale recovery metadata cleanly whenever `codexHome`, endpoint, `authProfileId`, account, desktop generation, supervision scope, or plugin policy changes. No configuration changes or manual migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Local loopback restarts after an in-place Codex or OpenClaw upgrade keep the same `CODEX_HOME` and native rollout store on disk. Separating local runtime fingerprints from transient patch-version strings, keeping supervised connection fingerprints exact, and migrating compatible local recovery ownership atomically inside the binding store preserves active threads and in-flight subagent recovery across routine upgrades without loosening any custody boundary.

## Evidence

### Red-on-base regression verification (`0632420a317`)

- Local `0.172.0` to `0.172.1` thread custody check on baseline `0632420a317` fails as expected: `startOrResumeThread` rotated to a new thread (`lifecycle.action: "started"`) instead of resuming `thread-existing-local`.
- Cold SQLite pending recovery retention test (`native-subagent-submission-store.test.ts`, upgrading a legacy `0.172.0` local binding to `0.172.1`) fails on baseline `0632420a317` with `AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ ... ]` because patching `appServerRuntimeFingerprint` dropped both `nativeSubagentAssignments` and `nativeSubagentSubmissions`.
- Both regressions pass cleanly on candidate `cdd316973ce`.

### Automated test, typecheck, lint, and ratchet checks (`cdd316973ce`)

- All 9 focused Vitest files pass with `--maxWorkers=1` across 2 shards (9 files, 318 tests passed on `cdd316973ce`: 5 files / 102 tests in `extension-codex` and 4 files / 216 tests in `extension-database-workers`):
  - `extensions/codex/src/app-server/plugin-app-cache-key.test.ts`
  - `extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-binding-policy.test.ts`
  - `extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.version-bump.test.ts`
  - `extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-binding.test.ts`
  - `extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-inventory.test.ts`
  - `extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-submission-store.test.ts`
  - `extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.binding.test.ts`
  - `extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-tool-catalog.test.ts`
  - `extensions/codex/src/app-server/plugin-thread-config.test.ts`
- Typechecks pass with zero errors: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`.
- Scoped lint, formatting, ratchets, and merge verification pass with zero issues across all 17 touched files:
  - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json` (0 problems in 17 files)
  - `oxfmt --check` (all 17 files formatted cleanly)
  - `node scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mjs --base 0632420a317` (0 new violations or over-cap growth)
  - `git diff --check 0632420a317..cdd316973ce` (clean, empty `.github/` diff)
  - `git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=0632420a317 origin/main HEAD` (clean 0-conflict merge against `origin/main` `8e2c8f5b57a`)
- Full runtime build (`pnpm build:runtime`) passes on both baseline (`0632420a317`) and candidate (`cdd316973ce`).

### Isolated CLI and native Codex proof

Verified offline on exact head `cdd316973ce` versus baseline `0632420a317` with both built runtimes (`openclaw.mjs agent --local`) driving the real native `codex` binary (`0.172.0`) through a transparent JSON-RPC stdio wrapper and a loopback-only synthetic `127.0.0.1` Responses server, using isolated temporary `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and `CODEX_HOME` directories with zero real credentials and blocked non-loopback proxies. The wrapper logged every `initialize`, `thread/start`, and `thread/resume` call verbatim and rewrote only the `initialize` response version string (`0.172.0` -> `0.172.1` -> `0.172.2`) to simulate local CLI upgrades against the same rollout store.

After Baseline Turn 1 persisted its legacy `0632420a317` SQLite binding row, schema-valid pending `nativeSubagentAssignments` (1 entry) and unmatched `nativeSubagentSubmissions` (1 receipt) keyed to the legacy connection fingerprint were seeded directly into `openclaw.sqlite` (`plugin_state_entries`), and the state and rollout store were snapshotted and restored in place before Candidate Case A to verify real cold SQLite migration.

| Scenario | Built Runtime | Codex Version | `CODEX_HOME` | Observed Native RPC | Observed Thread | Cold SQLite Recovery Metadata | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline Turn 1 | Baseline (`0632420a317`) | `0.172.0` | `CODEX_HOME_A` | `thread/start` (1 start, 0 resume) | `thread-1` | Seeded 1 assignment + 1 submission (legacy hash) | Initial thread created and legacy binding persisted |
| Baseline Turn 2 (control) | Baseline (`0632420a317`) | `0.172.1` | `CODEX_HOME_A` | `thread/start` (1 start, 0 resume) | `thread-2` | 0 assignments, 0 submissions (dropped) | Rotated to fresh thread and dropped recovery metadata |
| Candidate Case A (legacy migration) | Candidate (`cdd316973ce`) | `0.172.1` | `CODEX_HOME_A` | `thread/resume` (0 start, 1 resume) | `thread-1` | 1 assignment + 1 submission (migrated hash verified) | Resumed legacy thread and migrated binding + recovery ownership |

prs.title: improve: reduce repeated receipt copies during plugin catalog refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Preparing a model catalog worker copies published native plugin receipts into the requested plugin inventory. When any receipts exist, the Gateway currently copies the entire receipt map into an array and filters it again for every plugin. An inventory with 40 plugins and 40 receipts visits 1,600 entries during one overlay.

## User Impact

Catalog refreshes that carry native plugin receipts can use less temporary allocation. JavaScript-only inventories with no receipts retain the existing fast path. Operators need no configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Index the resolved roots visible to this inventory, then scan the current receipt map once. Matching uses the first NUL in the producer’s key and preserves the full key and receipt object. Records for the same root keep separate admission dictionaries. Unmatched rows keep their identity. The index is rebuilt for each overlay so mutable inputs and narrower registry views are respected.

## Evidence

Signed `60fb69f7306d` on `7d461e504914`. Focused formatter, whitespace checks and exact-range local review passed. The regression covers receipt order and overrides, mutable roots and receipts, duplicate roots, a filtered inventory, malformed keys, and row identity.

In an isolated Node 24.22.1 comparison of the two overlay functions with a fixed view lookup, serialized outputs matched across all five shapes. Ten alternating batches per shape gave these median microseconds per call.

| Visible plugins | Cached receipts | Before | After | Map entries visited |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 187 | 0 | 0.02 | 0.03 | 0 → 0 |
| 1 | 1 | 0.57 | 0.76 | 1 → 1 |
| 187 | 1 | 50.88 | 49.95 | 187 → 1 |
| 1 | 40 | 3.98 | 3.61 | 40 → 40 |
| 40 | 40 | 106.66 | 19.92 | 1,600 → 40 |

The 187-plugin case uses the number of manifests in this revision. The 40/40 shape matches the repository’s synthetic catalog fingerprint benchmark. These timings describe the isolated join. The one-plugin/one-receipt case took 0.19 µs longer.

The repository's complete worker-input benchmark builds the real catalog worker input and fingerprints it. On macOS arm64, Node 26.7.0, two counterbalanced runs per arm each measured 2,000 calls after 200 warmups. CPU and allocation used separate processes. The allocation pass sampled newly allocated bytes, including collected objects, at a 4 KiB interval.

| Visible plugins / receipts | Stock CPU µs/call | Candidate CPU µs/call | Stock sampled B/call | Candidate sampled B/call |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 / 1 | 15.93–16.80 | 16.06–17.24 | 23,733–23,941 | 23,583–23,990 |
| 40 / 40 | 115.35–123.02 | 39.21–39.39 | 245,883–246,200 | 53,103–53,310 |

All 16 processes produced the same complete fingerprint for each cardinality. The 40/40 test uses synthetic receipts with empty native-artifact inventories. Gateway process RSS was outside this measurement.

Three focused suites passed all five tests, including persisted native companion recovery. With just the new regression on stock, the expected one receipt-map traversal failed with three. The candidate passed the same assertion. Production +28/−11 lines, tests +59/−2.

Related to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192547.

prs.title: test(ios): share demo-chat fixtures and UI test helpers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This is one of a series of pull requests that brings the iOS app's chat in line with the Control UI. The PRs that follow need the same demo-chat launch fixtures and UI test helpers. Without a shared base, each PR would add its own copy to the demo chat transport and the snapshot UI tests. Separately, the voice note UI test can't pass on a Mac with no audio input: the simulator never starts the recording, so "Finish voice note" never appears and the test fails before it reaches what it checks.

## User Impact

None for people using the app. A release build behaves exactly as before:

- The voice note recorder is the same one the app already created by default.
- The new fixture options only read launch arguments, and nothing reads them yet.
- The silent recording fixture exists only in debug builds.

Developers get the voice note UI test passing on simulators without a microphone, plus the shared test support the next PRs build on.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Demo chat fixtures get their own file.** The launch-argument options (`ScreenshotFixtureMode`) and the session-group fixture move unchanged out of `AppleReviewDemoChatTransport.swift` into `AppleReviewDemoChatTransport+LaunchFixtures.swift`. The demo transport file keeps only the transport and its store. The new file also adds the options the following PRs launch with: a reply delay, a turn with failed tool calls, finished turns from two providers, the composer model layout, and model sign-in timing.
- **Voice note fixture.** In debug builds, `VoiceNoteFixtureCapture` keeps the real microphone permission request and writes silence to the m4a a recording would produce. It is used only in screenshot mode with `--openclaw-voice-note-fixture`. `OpenClawApp` hands it to `NodeAppModel` and otherwise passes the default recorder. The voice note UI test resets the microphone permission, allows it the way a person would, and launches with the fixture.
- **UI test helpers:**
  - New helpers for the model picker sheet and the composer's + sheet. Later PRs call them once those screens land.
  - `assertNoHorizontalOverlap` takes an optional allowance (default 0, so current callers behave the same).
  - `agentIdentity` matches the header identity whatever element type it is.
  - `dismissChatKeyboardThroughTranscript` taps only transcript text between the header and the composer, where a tap really reaches the transcript.
  - `openChatGatewaySettings` opens Gateway settings from the sidebar's Gateway control, which already exists.
- **`ChatViewModelTests`:** four tests take SwiftFormat's `hoistAwait` form, with `await` at the start of the expression. Nothing about what they check changes.

## Evidence

Everything ran on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator with iOS 27.2.

- **Build:** the app and a focused unit test bundle build for the simulator, including the SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint build phases. `scripts/lint-swift.sh ios` reports 0 violations in 566 files, and `scripts/format-swift.sh ios` reports 0 of 566 files needing formatting.
- **Unit tests:** every suite in `ChatViewModelTests.swift` passed (390 tests), including the four reformatted tests.
- **Voice note UI test:** `testVoiceNoteDraftKeepsStopAvailableDuringActiveResponse` fails on `main` because "Finish voice note" never appears. It passes with this change.
- **UI tests that call the changed helpers:**
  - These pass with this change: `testChatPresentationInLightAppearance`, `testKeyboardOpenPreservesTranscriptAndFollowsLiveEdgeAfterSend`, `testChatComposerStartsCompactAndGrowsWithDraft` and `testGatewaySettingsOpenedFromChatUsesRootSidebarNavigation`.
  - These fail on `main` and with this change, at the same assertion lines, in code this PR doesn't touch: `testChatComposerAccessibilityControls` (model chip value), `testTextDraftKeepsStopAvailableDuringActiveResponse` (Stop stays after it's tapped) and `testOnboardingPairCommandAndCompletionOpenChat` (copy command value).
- **Not checked:**
  - the rest of the UI suite;
  - the OpenClawKit SwiftPM tests on macOS;
  - the new picker and + sheet helpers, which nothing calls until the PRs that add those screens.

prs.title: fix(ui): say HTTPS or localhost when the mic is unavailable on plain HTTP
prs.body:
Closes #206050

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a dashboard opened over plain HTTP (`http://<lan-ip>:18789` or a Tailscale IP), Talk and dictation fail with "Realtime voice input requires browser microphone access", and the microphone picker says "This browser cannot list microphone inputs". Neither mentions the real cause, which is that the page is not on HTTPS or localhost.

## User Impact

Talk, dictation and the microphone picker now say "Microphone access needs HTTPS or localhost. Open this dashboard over HTTPS, or at localhost on the computer running OpenClaw." Like other microphone problems, it shows as a warning rather than a failure. Secure pages are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browsers remove `navigator.mediaDevices` entirely outside a secure context. `ui/src/pages/chat/talk/input.ts` is the one owner of microphone and camera discovery and capture messages for Talk, dictation and the picker. It treated a missing `mediaDevices` as an unsupported browser. It now reports an `insecure-context` issue when `isSecureContext` is false, the same check `chat-camera-capture.tsx` already makes for `chat.camera.insecure`. Two English strings are added (microphone and camera, since the owner maps each issue to both). `ui:i18n:baseline` reported no baseline changes and `ui:i18n:verify` passes; translations follow through the locale refresh workflow.

## Evidence

**Partial proof: no screenshots of the new message in the running dashboard.**
- What I checked live: I served the Control UI built from `main` by an isolated Gateway bound to a LAN address, and opened it in a Chromium-based browser at `http://192.168.1.3:<port>/chat`. The page reports `isSecureContext: false`, and `navigator.mediaDevices` is undefined, which is the issue's trigger.
- What I couldn't check: plain-HTTP access still needs the Gateway token, and I couldn't complete that sign-in during the run, so the composer messages themselves weren't captured in the browser.
- Before marking this ready, I'll add before/after screenshots of the Talk, dictation and picker messages from a signed-in plain-HTTP dashboard.

Tests:
- New `input.test.ts` case "names HTTPS or localhost when an insecure page hides the microphone": with `isSecureContext` false and no `mediaDevices`, discovery reports `insecure-context` and opening the microphone rejects with the new message.
  - On `main` it fails: `expected { devices: [], … } to match object { issue: 'insecure-context' }`.
  - With the fix it passes.
- The existing "unsupported enumeration" case now stubs `isSecureContext: true`, because real browsers always define it.
- `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/talk` (25 files, 355 tests) and `ui/src/pages/chat/components` (22 files, 171 tests) pass.
- `tsgo:ui`, oxlint, oxfmt, `ui:i18n:verify`, `git diff --check` and `check:test-lines-ratchet` are clean.

Production delta +18/-6 (one owner plus two English strings); test delta +13/-0.

Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the previous messages with no state or config change. Blast radius is microphone and camera messages on non-secure dashboard origins.

prs.title: feat: review dictated local file references in the composer
prs.body:
Related: #205847

## What Problem This Solves

Dictating a filename currently produces text without a way to check which workspace object it names. Similar filenames, extensions and case distinctions can make that text ambiguous.

This PR adds an experimental, explicitly enabled review flow from authorized local file metadata into the unsent Chat draft. **M09 is not fully qualified. This is a draft proposal, the tracking issue remains open, and no merge is requested.**

## User Impact

- Enable **English file-reference commands for this session's local workspace**, then say `reference file src slash auth dot ts end reference`. Ordinary prose, quoted/code text and literal spans remain text. Whole-utterance shorthand has a separate opt-in.
- Inspect the relative path and workspace, select the intended object and confirm. A real CodeMirror transaction binds the visible span and selected identity atomically; undo/redo preserve both. Several commands are reviewed in spoken order.
- The initial provider supports one authorized local session root, including its existing live sandbox backing. Multiple roots, repository/device/exec-node providers and the current-file shortcut remain unsupported.
- Draft restoration, pane handoff and feature disable preserve the recorded identity. Explicit draft replacement clears previous bindings. Entering text-only goal edit is refused while the draft has references; explicit conversion restores normal Edit/Cancel behavior.
- The opaque object identifier belongs to a 60-second resolver lease. A saved draft retains the record validated at insertion, but **this implementation cannot resolve that saved identifier after lease release/expiry**. Durable identity resolution is still required integration work.
- The current chat, queue and suggestion transports cannot carry this namespace. Sending is refused until **Convert file references to plain text** explicitly removes the bindings. Selection neither reads/attaches contents nor sends, executes or grants agent access. Unsupported destinations offer clearly labeled text copying or cancel.
- Identity-bearing session storage uses format 5; the reader accepts 4 and 5. The shared durable browser database advances to version 3 without rewriting records. **Older application versions opening version 2 cannot access that upgraded database, even when recognition is subsequently disabled.** A compatible build is needed to recover those drafts. Native upgrade/downgrade qualification remains pending.

[User-facing behavior and limits](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/blob/9f997d7fe46860713564dad2eca9aaa717ba96bf/docs/web/control-ui/dictated-file-references.md).

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider reuses session-scoped retained reads, the existing file-browser workspace/host-read authorities, live sandbox backing selection and fs-safe canonicalization. Every operation re-enters those authorities. A resolver lease limits retained metadata and unread descriptors; it is not an access grant. Search is bounded to 2 KiB queries, 20 candidates per page, 10,000 examined entries per index chunk, eight connection slots and 64 directory levels. Hidden names, dependency/build directories and symlink escapes are excluded. The grammar permits at most 16 commands and 32 KiB of transcript.

The existing Chat editor owns the reference StateField, one-transaction delivery receipts and synchronous draft metadata publication. Existing persistence/recovery owners carry the field; unsupported consumers refuse it. A metadata-only conversion or undo is admitted through the same composer commit boundary, including equal-text edits. Capture eligibility requires provider final text, completed closure, successful close acknowledgement and no cancellation/disconnect/late partial or error. The existing final-drain subscription remains owned until that acknowledgement; ordinary feature-Off dictation keeps its existing non-reference commit path.

The current MCP resource path supplies generic resource links and materializes them as attachments; the plugin composer API is text-only. Neither currently provides the required atomic object-identity draft contract. This proposed session-local RPC/editor namespace therefore remains a maintainer design decision in #205847, including whether to extend MCP resources instead. The M11 coordinator now exists as **unmerged draft #205973**, with no accepted shared contract. It is not this branch's parent, and this PR does not claim M11 integration or expand the public plugin SDK.

The author simplification pass kept one grammar owner, one existing-authority provider lease and one existing-editor destination. Mechanical identity propagation follows the existing draft lifecycle. It removed an extra finality listener, reused the existing canonical schema-sharing generator, and guarded the borrowed goal editor instead of creating another persisted goal schema. The final repair preserves the original two-argument callback for ordinary drafts and uses the decoder’s canonical identity array for both editor dispatch and receipt comparison. Chooser styles reuse the shared field control and retain scroll limits, long-path wrapping and bidirectional isolation. A provider-only or display-only slice would not establish the requested real provider-to-destination boundary. Remaining growth and the storage/identity-lifetime decisions are explicit review scope.

## Evidence

### Exact-head scripted dictation and comma replay — `5166e8aa8ff61c209dde9a06dd69b4f5678819c9`

Timothy Wayne Gregg ran the [scripted-audio workflow](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45933342189) with the Run 4 scenario and the updated qualification harness (`6187471`, run checkout `0156c86`). The [job log](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45933342189/job/140291196146) records the exact PR head. This uses Chromium’s fake microphone, scripted audio, and live OpenAI transcription through the Gateway; it is not a physical-microphone or live send test.

- **Deterministic chooser replay: 5/5 tests passed** in `composer-file-reference-provider.integration.test.ts`, before the browser proof in the same job. This includes `replays dictation and binds src/auth.ts,`, which replays Run 4’s `src/auth.ts,` transcript and checks both the fallback to `src/auth.ts` and exact-match precedence for a literal comma-suffixed file. The comma transcript did not recur in live STT on this run; the replay is the evidence for the comma fix.

| Scripted case | Result | What qualified or was inconclusive |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contractions | 2/3 PASS; 1/3 `INCONCLUSIVE_STT` | Alloy and Nova bound `@src/auth.ts` in the unsent draft. Sage returned “and reference” instead of “end reference.” |
| Keyboard confirm | 2/3 PASS; 1/3 `INCONCLUSIVE_STT` | Nova and Sage returned `notes.` and bound `@notes`. Alloy returned “and reference.” |
| Keyboard cancel | 2/3 PASS; 1/3 `INCONCLUSIVE_STT` | Alloy and Nova left the draft unchanged. Sage returned “And reference.” |
| Single-quoted command | 0/3 PASS; 3/3 `INCONCLUSIVE_STT` | All three transcripts used double quotes, so none exercised real single-quote protection. |

All six qualifying takes passed; no takes failed, no sends were attempted or blocked by the harness, and no Gateway errors were reported. `INCONCLUSIVE_STT` is neither a product pass nor a failure: those transcripts did not contain the required command terminator or single-quote delimiters. Qualification checks the decoded whole intended path and surrounding words independently of chooser lookup, so a missing candidate after qualification would fail. Separate straight- and curly-single-quote parser regressions passed 2/2 on `d752b31`; that checks parser behavior, not whether live transcription supplies single quotes.

**Still to do:** Timothy will run the physical-microphone checks. Sanitized before/after UI evidence, native IndexedDB upgrade/rollback/recovery, live authorization and restricted-delivery qualification, and fresh paired UI performance measurements remain open. The PR remains a draft.

### ClawSweeper follow-up — `d752b31db27df007f6a84f49d916f0e5d1eda226`

- **Source:** appended the [parser repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d752b31db27df007f6a84f49d916f0e5d1eda226) after a [two-parent merge of upstream `main`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b92136b4e18178281804b91b8ca060db1ade2907) at `20b3afeccc4964fbd8a4a5bbe15fd8069ba4f6a5`. Original fork history and draft state are unchanged.
- **Parser repair:** commands between word apostrophes are recognized without modifying the transcript or its UTF-16 offsets. Real straight and curly single-quoted spans stay protected, including contractions inside those spans. Updated the existing grammar regressions without increasing the test-line allocation.
- **Evidence available:** static syntax and formatting checks on both touched TypeScript files and the merged-tree `git diff --check` passed. The parser regressions were not executed in this session; no fork code or fork CI was run.
- **Independent source review:** bound Auto Review against upstream `20b3afeccc4964fbd8a4a5bbe15fd8069ba4f6a5` and the pre-publish candidate completed all seven passes at P0 coverage with no findings. This was read-only; it did not run tests, confirm merge readiness, or change the ClawSweeper rating.
- **Runtime proof pending:** [OpenClaw CI at this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45897186641) is `action_required` with zero jobs; the other ten PR-triggered runs also reported `action_required`. The sanitized AWS Crabbox preflight could not authenticate to the OpenClaw broker; no lease ran. Prior functional and performance results below are historical, not passes at this head.
- **Qualification requested at this checkpoint:** capture the shipped Control UI/Gateway dictation → chooser → confirmed bound draft journey with sanitized before/after screenshots and runtime output; qualify native IndexedDB upgrade from `v2026.11.10` and rollback/recovery using a disposable browser profile with existing drafts and queued payloads. The stable build opens database version 2; verify preservation and a usable recovery path, not a successful old-binary reopen of version 3.
- **Owner decisions still open:** composer/MCP namespace and M11 interoperability, lease expiration and saved-object resolution, the shared storage format/version fence, draft-only delivery and explicit plain-text conversion, and the always-loaded UI cost. The previous head failed four paired strict UI performance limits; a new paired measurement is still needed.

The sections below preserve the author's historical evidence for `9f997d7fe46860713564dad2eca9aaa717ba96bf`.

### Source and publication

- Base used for final integration: `openclaw/openclaw:main` at `082c211ad2959e25b2aa5366cce4ba099275c162`.
- Head: `CompleteDotTech:feat/dictation-file-references-m09` at `9f997d7fe46860713564dad2eca9aaa717ba96bf`.
- Publication targets the current `main` branch. Preflight observed main at `47027a257c728b267390eaac72147eaea55f0283`, 21 commits beyond the tested integration base. The comparison has no overlapping authored M09 path; its sole overlapping generated predicate adds an unrelated skill-workshop field. A read-only Git merge simulation succeeds. These local results validate the feature tree on the stated integration base, not the simulated merged-current-main tree.
- The original unpublished checkout was lost. This source was reconstructed and reverified; historical lost-checkout test/build claims are not reused.
- Current-main dictation gesture/UTF-16 length limits and attachment-version/newer-caption restoration changes were incorporated before final gates. The fork has its own physical dependency installation.
- Source was published through the authenticated GitHub connection. Exact remote/local tree equality and reachable branch verification are recorded in the accompanying evidence. Commit-signature status: GitHub reports the API-created commit as unsigned; no verified signature is claimed.

### Executed checks

| Check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Physical dependency installation | `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passed in this checkout; no borrowed `node_modules`. Node 24.22.3, pnpm 11.25. |
| Final selected regressions | **116/116 passed** across nine parser, review-owner, finality, baseline-dictation, actual-provider/editor, persistence, schema and send-guard files (16.798 s). |
| Final composer compatibility regressions | **42/42 passed** across five separate real-composer, actual-editor, goal-edit and IME files (12.114 s). These files do not overlap the 116-case run. |

| Other relevant gates | Controller census, i18n verification, script erasability, current plugin boundary checker, documentation links, source-line and test-line ratchets, and normal staged content/format/whitespace guards passed. |
| Production UI build | **PASS**, final production build in 76.644 s, bound to candidate tree `c6ff5da8d6fa47cf025b57d79af40ab2b9fff197` and all 107 source hashes. The build ran before the local Git head was aligned to the published repair commit; emitted version metadata is separately retained. |

| Total CSS gzip | 348,603 B | 348,698 B | 348,683 B | New failure, 15 B over |
| Chat boot JS requests | 21 | 21 | 20 | Inherited failure, unchanged |
| Chat boot JS gzip | 1,337,205 B | 1,346,006 B | 1,336,272 B | Inherited failure, worsened by 8,801 B |
| New Session boot JS gzip | 820,235 B | 822,255 B | 822,243 B | New failure, 12 B over |

The production paired evaluator admits the unchanged inherited request count but still fails four limits: largest CSS is 31 B beyond its paired allowance, chat bytes are 8,737 B beyond their paired allowance, and the two fixed-limit overages remain. These are real release blockers. Startup JS grew 6 B; startup CSS did not change. This is static bundle accounting against the retained measured boot manifest, not a fresh browser capture or startup-latency result.

The feature has an eager code cost while capture is off. The current single owner is retained because saved-reference preservation, unsupported-send refusal and explicit conversion must remain available without capture consent. A deferred presentation or further boot-boundary change needs separate lifecycle review; no reduction of validation or identity protection was made to clear a ceiling.

The 20 Gateway cases remain unrun after two compiled preparations exited 137 before collection. Seven Solid lint warnings and runtime untracked-read diagnostics remain visible and unclassified. The broader documented source and SDK/package extension-boundary commands failed `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` because those scripts are absent; the passing narrower checker is not substituted for them. Full package/release build and native qualification are not claimed.

Earlier failures are retained: UI type/lint defects were repaired; the actual-provider fixture's default polling wait was replaced by the owner's settlement signal without increasing a timeout; goal/callback/receipt regressions were repaired without weakening assertions. One subsequent UI test attempt was killed before Vitest startup; the final serialized 42-case run and separate 116-case run pass. The original six-limit performance result and clean-base comparison remain preserved alongside this final five-limit result.

Every row remains **partial**; implemented/source-tested behavior does not establish the complete issue's live/native acceptance.

The source-bound external probe uses the production fs-safe provider over 10,000 flat nine-byte synthetic files, 20 fresh indexes, 100 warm searches (90 exact, 10 deliberately ambiguous) and 110 candidate revalidations. The 10% ambiguity fraction was designed, not measured from speech. Network, STT, human selection and destination latency were not measured. Separate actual provider/editor cases supply insertion correctness evidence; this benchmark is not an insertion-error-rate estimate.

### Independent review and unresolved qualification

Independent review inspected the actual source and complete AC01–AC12 ledger. It supports a qualified draft, with no remaining actionable application-code finding in the declared scope. Repairs covered live sandbox backing, rollback fences, captured-client cleanup, presenter remount ownership, borrowed goal-editor identity loss, metadata-only composer commits and the final-count announcement. The finality listener and type/lint defects were also repaired. The first review stamped checkpoint `21416612d868d506ed06f7f141ca3fc81b78b5e7`. The final ordered source-manifest SHA-256 is `a545f5e6d38145ecf8d5f68f6bdd265394c6922f3506f94c4f9720faf543b1c7`. The original review remains preserved as a historical checkpoint and the supplement records the later findings. This is not maintainer acceptance or native qualification.

The final test growth is +2,219 net lines, with 1,819 allocated above the ordinary 400-line allowance. The record names distinct filesystem/admission, capture/finality, actual editor/owner, storage/recovery and unsupported-consumer failures. UI helpers and tests share actual owners; no test-only production endpoint or alternate renderer was added.

The native browser installer failed HTTP 403 `SiteUnavailable`, and the system Chromium wrapper has no underlying browser binary. Browser/IndexedDB, screenshots, supported screen-reader/keyboard, clipboard, physical microphone and live provider/authorization/export proof therefore remain pending. The requested package workflow/architecture/stacking/validation/coverage/dependency-summary masters were unavailable; their contents are not claimed as read. Supplied implementation, issue and PR specifications were read completely.

Maintainer decisions remain open for the proposed local namespace versus MCP resources, M11 interoperability, durable identity lifetime and shared-storage compatibility. Multiple roots and identity-capable downstream delivery are not implemented. Broad exact-head CI, release qualification and any required security/design review remain open. No maintainer-only CI dispatch or merge was performed.

prs.title: refactor(subagents): centralize end-of-run decisions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Maintainers currently have to reconcile terminal policy across completion, termination publication, effect dispatch, cleanup bookkeeping, and retry handling. This maintainer-requested cutover gives those adapters one owner for terminal rows and the work owed after publication.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. Completion capture, cancellation reconciliation, collector results, cleanup ordering, and requester delivery retain their existing contracts. No persisted fields, public SDK contracts, or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transition owner prepares result capture, plans terminal row changes, and returns explicit effect, cleanup, and retry decisions. Completion and termination share the outcome writer. Adapters retain persistence, resource dispatch, and live ownership checks rather than deriving terminal policy from row fields.

The decision results add source lines while removing policy from consumers; this is an ownership cutover rather than a line-count-only cleanup. Existing lifecycle tests remain the behavioral contract.

### Mechanical caller updates

The five registry adapters consume the internal transition owner. No announce, requester-custody, or kill implementation files are changed.

### Related work and integration

Depends on the run-manager repair in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206405. That lane released the file for this migration; its final CI and native landing are in progress. Final integration will preserve exact kill claims, claim-bound session assertions, and acquisition-owned session release.

Other open work with overlapping files: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206443, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200231, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199455, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194732, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197335, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/136554, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140956, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201774, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191857, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201613, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198689, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198633, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/121309, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164366, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203303. Most completion-directory overlaps are outside the edited files.

## Evidence

Base: `f769a88c6a4f1b3ef061a8e6d2592fd34d5de3ca`. Reviewed head: `ee97a4bbb0625771a59852d24dbd822fe3b5aa05`.

CI's full production/full-tree export audit has now run: no findings in these owned files; the failures are the pre-existing announce exports fixed by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206429.

The native classifier reports unknown (no matching main job). The failure-owner and test files are unchanged, but that alone is not baseline proof. Focused baseline attribution remains outstanding.

prs.title: fix: keep chat photo previews sharp within their byte limits
prs.body:
Closes #206404

## What Problem This Solves

Photos looked blurry in chat and in the enlarged viewer. The Gateway reduced their dimensions to meet the preview byte limit, and Chromium enlarged those small images to fill the available space.

## User Impact

Photos can use the full requested preview width within the existing download budget. The updated preview URLs let browsers fetch the sharper renditions even if they cached an older version.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway keeps a full-width WebP when it fits. For larger opaque images, it searches JPEG quality levels at the requested width before stepping down in size. Transparent images keep an alpha-capable format. The existing HEIC path still produces JPEG.

## Evidence

I ran the same 1920 × 1920 photograph through separate loopback Gateways built from upstream `66b2e244acf2` and the candidate. A local fixture supplied the model reply with the image. OpenClaw created the attachment and served it to the real Control UI in Chromium 156 on macOS arm64, Node 26.13.1, at 1440 × 960 and device scale 1.

| Requested width | Before, decoded | After, decoded | After, bytes | Limit, bytes |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 480 | 120 | 480 | 89,449 | 98,304 |
| 960 | 240 | 960 | 212,225 | 262,144 |
| 1920 | 480 | 1920 | 500,056 | 524,288 |

Chromium rendered the inline photo at 360 × 360 CSS pixels and the enlarged viewer at 868 × 868 in both runs. The viewer decoded 480 × 480 before and 1920 × 1920 after. The browser requested the new cache version. The full 919,421-byte JPEG matched the input in both runs. A small transparent PNG retained its alpha and dimensions.

The committed photo regression failed on upstream at 480 decoded pixels for a 960-pixel request and passed with this change. The affected Gateway, artifact download, UI, and managed-image end-to-end tests passed, along with core and UI typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and the documentation link check.

| ![Before, 120 pixels displayed at 360](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d9bf0bf-42ea-460f-bc16-ff62f38b66af) | ![After, 480 pixels displayed at 360](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8cadde2a-f5d1-499e-b392-54c3d4640ae7) |

prs.title: fix: let visible children follow their spawning parent
prs.body:
Closes #206460

## What Problem This Solves

I reproduced visible children refusing follow-ups from the same parent that spawned them, asking the operator to repeat the request directly. Resetting a child made this reproducible.

## User Impact

Visible children recognize their own parent's assignments, including after reset. Other sessions retain the existing warning. Agent attribution, tool permissions, and explicit user instructions remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

I use the stored spawning-parent link and existing visible-child policy to mark parent provenance. The model receives an explicit host-verified parent label rather than the generic inter-session warning. Ingress rejects unsupported parent claims, and replay/display preserve the distinction.

## Evidence

I ran real isolated Gateways with live Responses calls and checked effects on disk:

| Reset fixture | Main parent follow-up | This branch, two fresh runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Back up SQLite and remove retired column | Refused | Completed 2/2 |
| Remove obsolete cache | Refused | Completed 2/2 |
| Approve demo change record | Refused | Completed 2/2 |
| Change demo profile theme | Refused | Completed 2/2 |

Identical direct-operator controls completed 4/4 on main. Unrelated-peer controls were refused 2/2 on this branch and changed nothing. I verified parent provenance on both opening tasks and follow-ups, and its absence on peer messages.

- Main baseline: `6d2cb0379cb66e9fc25584f978b71750e29b916a`. Current reset keeps the session ID and rotates its lifecycle revision.
- Published head: `6c727082ecfa656f6a47f9d221f7b6fffa37a9ad`, tree-identical to tested commit `4477f57ed860ef337b8d45500b198514bc176740`. Build, core typecheck, focused lint, formatting, and 99 focused tests passed. Both new regression groups failed without the fix.
- Separate final-head test commands: ingress file 48.70 s wall (9.88 s Vitest, including real store/worker setup); envelope file 1.36 s wall (105 ms Vitest). Hosted CI time is not verified.
- Simplify: shared parent-provenance projection; no permission store or new configuration. Authored production +121/-47 lines; tests +88. The large generated-validator diff is identifier renumbering for one optional field.
- Two AWS model-bridge attempts returned 502 before useful inference. I used the authorized isolated local fallback. Test Gateways and fixtures were removed; both AWS leases report cleanup complete. Production was untouched.

Not verified: hosted CI and independent review. Local autoreview could not start because its Codex installation was inaccessible inside the required read-only sandbox. I did not relax it. The successful build reported non-fatal UI bundle-budget warnings.

Requested by Dan Riccio.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-visible-child-refuses-parent-s69ae811a)

prs.title: fix(macOS): explain protected token failures on local Gateways
prs.body:
Part of #203785
Part of #203737
Part of #141413
Part of #166707

## What Problem This Solves

When a local Gateway requires a token from a protected secret source that the macOS app cannot read, the native connection can fail without explaining why. The Gateway process can still be running.

## User Impact

Connection settings and the menu bar show the credential problem once, alongside any distinct readiness failure, and offer a link to the known issue. When Health reports the same failure, its row offers that link instead of repeating the warning. Connection hides the Dashboard Settings shortcut only for this local failure, when it cannot help. This does not change authentication, pairing, or reconnect behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The diagnostic follows the same local auth selection as the credential resolver, including LaunchAgent inputs when auth mode is implicit. It is a diagnostic improvement, not a fix for the underlying token or device-pairing failures.

## Evidence

- On prior head `bcdc4d4b85770b117139d94308c35d1d5956786b`, Dan reported 44 passing native tests in a disposable macOS VM. He confirmed the credential warning appeared once in Connection and the menu, distinct readiness stayed visible, and the issue link opened from both surfaces. This does not verify the current head.
- On the current integrated tree `19d7810c4d6730d28285405c245b7b73c5b2c426`, native localization and whitespace checks passed, and bound Auto Review found no P0–P2 source findings.

**Draft hold:** On a disposable Mac, build `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --product OpenClaw`, build the native tests, then run `ControlChannelGatewayMessageTests`, `CritterStatusBeatsTests`, `LocalGatewayConnectionPresentationTests`, and `StatusMenuDescriptorTests` through the isolated runner. With a dummy protected credential, verify the Health-row and menu help actions by keyboard, that the warning appears once and distinct readiness and health detail stay visible, and that Dashboard Settings still works with a healthy Gateway. Exact-head native verification is pending.

Contributed by @TheAngryPit.
