prs.title: refactor(codex): centralize native completion delivery
prs.body:
Fixes #206438

## What Problem This Solves

Maintainers currently have to update two completion lifecycles: the shared subagent policy and the Codex plugin's separate ownership, retry, and receipt state. This cutover makes native Codex completions use the existing core completion obligation from [206383](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206383).

## User Impact

Native child results keep their current routing, cancellation, retry delays, and persisted binding format. The plugin keeps Codex-specific receipt correlation; core owns whether a completion is pending, consumed, retrying, or retiring. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

`registerAgentHarnessCompletion` extends the existing completion SDK subpath. The adapter reports completion and consumed receipts, supplies native readiness and persistence effects, and consumes the core handle's recorded facts. The duplicate plugin delivery map, flags, timers, counters, and attempt joining are removed. The existing obligation lifecycle is shared by the ordinary announce flow and the native registration; its policy remains in the owner established by [206383](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206383). Its lifecycle implementation is split into a sibling module to stay inside the existing source-size limit, with all callers migrated and no compatibility re-export.

The operator explicitly approved this narrow SDK extension and core-owner integration in chat. The approval covers the first completion-delivery/receipt cutover; unrelated model, admission, cancellation, and history machinery is deferred.

Native receipts do not identify the child turn. The plugin therefore retains path aliases, predecessor ordering, and result correlation instead of moving Codex wire parsing into core. The inspected upstream source is Codex commit `414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6`: `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs` (`CollabAgentToolCall`, `CollabAgentState`, `RawResponseItemCompletedNotification`), `codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs` (`AgentMessage`), and `codex-rs/core/src/context/{subagent_notification,inter_agent_completion_message}.rs`.

Native detached results retain their six existing retry delays; persisted registry completions retain their existing expiry/backoff policy. These are different persistence mechanisms under the same completion owner. Consumed results never re-enter delivery while bookkeeping retries. Ownership uses the logical agent/requester/assignment across replacement client contexts. If observation discovers unavailable custody, core releases that observation and preserves the durable assignment for fresh recovery.

### Ownership map

All abbreviated filenames below are `extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-<name>.ts`.

| Modules | Fact or decision | Owner and disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `completion-delivery`, `delivery-receipts` | Delivery, consumption, retry, retirement; native receipt correlation | Lifecycle moved to core; native correlation retained. |
| `assignment`, `notification`, `notification-routing`, `turn-observation` | Native identities, lineage, event envelopes, activity/wait facts | Codex adapters; unchanged. |
| `history-recovery`, `recovery-coordinator`, `retry` | Native history, exact-turn recovery, persistence polling | Native observation retained. Broader recovery policy remains a later audit; `retry` still has production consumers. |
| `history-owner`, `pending-assignments`, `assignment-store` | Native binding identity and durable locators | Existing native binding adapter and host storage authority; persisted shapes unchanged. |
| `assignment-inventory` | Locator persistence/recovery and completion acknowledgement | Reads consumed/retiring truth from core; native storage operations retained. |
| `admission-custody`, `model-input`, `model-lookup`, `model-source` | Correlate native input with admitted model/source authority | Existing host authority plus native correlation; broader reference-accounting audit deferred. |
| `parent-owner`, `monitor-types`, `monitor`, `monitor-runtime` | Native registrations, subscriptions, parent observations, pending-child projection | Completion-state readers migrated. Native client/turn orchestration retained. |
| `cancellation-selection`, `cancellation-result`, `cancellation-wait`, `close-owner` | Exact native cancellation/close under host authority | Native execution adapters; unchanged. No unproven deletion. |
| `submission`, `submission-call`, `submission-owner` | Native submission acknowledgements and delayed-turn correlation | Completion-consumption reader migrated; submission correlation and persistence retained. |
| `roster` | Project current native children | Existing `AgentHarness.readNativeSubagents` adapter; unchanged. |

`extensions/codex/test-api.ts` and read-only `extensions/copilot/src/tool-bridge.ts` use the existing SDK session-key predicate for tool context; neither needs a new core-state reader in this slice.

### Mechanical caller updates

- `subagent-announce.ts`: import the shared obligation factory from its lifecycle module.
- `native-subagent-monitor-types.ts`: replace plugin-owned delivery fields with the completion handle type.
- `native-subagent-monitor.test-support.ts`, `native-subagent-monitor.live.test.ts`, and `shared-client-lifetime.test-support.ts`: construct real host-issued scopes through the existing private test SDK. `plugin-test-runtime.ts` provides a test-only factory reexport and remains excluded from production JS/declarations.
- `native-subagent-inventory.test.ts`: remove assertions for the already-ignored `expectedRequester` delivery argument; keep all requester/result and recovery assertions.
- `native-subagent-assignment-inventory.ts`, `native-subagent-parent-owner.ts`, and `native-subagent-submission-owner.ts`: consume the handle's recorded completion facts.
- `native-subagent-monitor.ts`: reset the completion handle when a native assignment resumes.

### Related contributor work

Related and overlapping: [194748](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194748) and [194764](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194764) by @dubr1k; [200947](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200947) by @shannon0430. This PR does not copy their unmerged patches or claim their separate fixes. After landing, each PR will receive the landed link and a specific supersession assessment; unresolved restart and retirement-policy work will remain explicit.

## Evidence

- Implementation base: `277b251bfa80c863e4408607bce9b372eddc24c9`, including [206383](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206383). Campaign baseline: `df78bb4a3ac`.
- Native owned area including `test-api.ts`: 9,957 → 9,796 lines (161 removed). Subagent-mentioning lines: 463 → 460. Direct imports of core subagent internals: 0 → 0.
- Lines referencing the retired plugin lifecycle fields (`nativeCompletionDelivered`, `completionDeliveryAbandoned`, `completionDeliveryAttempt`, `completionDeliveryTimer`, `deliveryOwnerKey`): 40 → 0, measured with `git grep -c`.
- Baseline Testbox: 45 tests passed across the completion SDK, native receipts, monitor completion, and contention suites. Final-head SDK (22 tests), native contention (5 tests), and core typecheck passed on the same Testbox; the owner-read work count changed from one to zero while durable receipt/restart assertions remain.
- Independent P0–P2 full-branch review completed on `3c178af4e45cc286bd5f3e0c6d883dbabb6d4427`, followed by a branch review of the final handoff-order repair at `264c15706de4064a627044df7dd4ab56afa763cf`; both found no actionable findings, with unchanged owner/custody/source context supplied.
- Code-sloppiness: baseline run 44 (four existing files), head run 59 (same files plus the shared lifecycle). Clone SLOC 6 → 0; score 38.84 → 41.19 with expanded coverage, so this is not an aggregate complexity reduction. Native `deliverAttempt` (CC 29) disappears; native `applyReceipts` CC 15 → 12; shared `attempt` is CC 33 and the enclosing lifecycle is CC 63 (the scanner includes nested callbacks). Existing receipt matcher CC 11 and SDK delivery CC 26 are unchanged.
- Across the full TypeScript change: 521 production lines added / 341 removed (net +180); 272 test/support lines added / 13 removed. The growth pays for one shared lifecycle and regressions for receipt/retirement ordering; no new persistence shape or generic task registry.
- Dead-export baseline: the same Testbox reproduces all five flagged exports on the pinned base; none lost a production consumer in this cutover. The findings are the `buildRequesterCompletionDeliveryResult`, `hasMessagingToolDeliveryToSource`, and `isDirectMessageDeliveryTarget` reexports in `subagent-announce-completion-delivery.ts`, plus the first two exports in `subagent-announce-obligation.ts`.
- SDK surface baseline: the same Testbox reproduces `public exports 3931 > 3930` on the pinned base; this branch retains 3,931 public exports and adds one private-local export. The public ratchet failure is pre-existing.
- SDK API acknowledgement: reviewed the new private-local `registerAgentHarnessCompletion` contract on the existing completion subpath. The Testbox API diff reports **No Plugin SDK API changes**, acknowledgement digest `ff7b090f`; no new public barrel export is added.
- Final-head core typecheck and changed-file lint passed. The final full subagent/native suite is running. The one-shot client regression passes on `264c15706de4`; all inventory cases, SDK tests and receipt-contention cases passed before that final adapter-order repair. The API acknowledgement check passed with no public API changes. Broad build and extension checks are owned by PR CI; merge waits for their results.

The known main failure `preserves routed native Stop authority … (consumed-session)` will be reported separately if reproduced by the final full subagents suite; it is not attributed to this change.

prs.title: feat(dictation): propose personal vocabulary groundwork
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related: #205856.

Personal spellings need an explicit lifecycle: authenticated storage, deliberate learning, accessible editing, stable identity, bounded per-turn hints, import/export, conflicts, deletion, and recovery. Existing provider hints in #191109 do not supply that lifecycle.

**This is an incomplete design-review draft. P03 is not implemented in full, every complete AC01–AC12 remains unmet, and #205856 must stay open.** This PR preserves reviewed private groundwork while the required storage and public-contract design decisions remain outstanding.

## User Impact

This candidate does not activate a dictionary editor, durable entries, correction learning, or provider dispatch. Its reusable preparation work preserves exact canonical text, produces immutable bounded personal snapshots, previews explicit imports and existing Deepgram keyterm strings, and prepares canonical hint data for a future admitted caller.

No user-data migration is activated. Reverting these private modules and their benchmark removes the proposal; there is no new stored user data to transform. The eventual feature still needs disabled-mode retention, upgrade/downgrade, scoped recovery/export, and rollback proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current authenticated preferences are owned by `users.prefs` and worker-backed state. Their 4 KiB value, 32-entry mutation, and 128-key profile limits do not directly accommodate the proposed 1,000-entry dictionary. Sharding or silently adding a namespace would still change persistence and lifecycle semantics.

The [storage review checkpoint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1c3de7eb68481e5d7656e21ec96d43855789fbb0/docs/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes.md#review-checkpoint-for-material-changes) requires accepted design before material persistence or public-contract changes. The [automated issue review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205856#issuecomment-7186791734) also requests a coordinated owner, minimum client flow, and vocabulary contract with M06. That review is advisory, not maintainer acceptance. No accepting maintainer decision was found.

The implementation therefore prepares these private boundaries:

- One shared validator preserves canonical Unicode/case/punctuation and uses NFC only for comparisons. The existing M06 locale normalizer and bounded JSON parser are reused.
- Personal snapshots carry copied profile/workspace identity, a pinned revision, deterministic locale-aware selection, a 64-entry bound, and private omission explanations. Supplied scope IDs are isolation metadata, not authorization.
- Import previews attribute invalid rows, duplicates, and ID/canonical conflicts. Every row requires an explicit decision; replacement preserves an existing stable ID and must target a previewed match. Resolution returns a complete proposed term set and expected revision; it performs no CAS or durable write.
- Export projects personal term fields only. The proposed schema and entire envelope are bounded; unknown versions remain errors. Explicit Deepgram strings can be previewed without discovering or rewriting configuration.
- Hint preparation distinguishes term lists, encoded prompts, unavailable capabilities, and unsupported pronunciation. Adapter-owned exact measurement bounds the actual fixture representation. A local-only/remote projection stops preparation before measuring private strings; this is not real egress enforcement.
- Aliases remain candidates. Ambiguous hints are omitted rather than used as unconditional transcript replacements. Numeric summaries exclude term text, scope identifiers, and hashes.

### Reused source and semantic dependencies

The branch now merges `openclaw/openclaw:main` at `47027a257c728b267390eaac72147eaea55f0283`, without rewriting fork history. No sibling transport change is a branch dependency. Current OpenAI transcription prompt and Deepgram batch keyterm transport already exist; this draft does not advertise another endpoint or unverified Google Live fields.

Three foundation files originate from M06 commit `4780aeb034e72a6557f12a54ed506d5e4c690d98`: `vocabulary-types.ts`, `vocabulary-terms.ts`, and `vocabulary-terms.test.ts`. The draft retains the types these helpers use and removes unused shared authority declarations. It exposes the shared comparison/locale helpers, extracts bounded JSON parsing, and fixes canonical precedence before alias conflict indexing. No M06 persistence or lease layer is imported. M06 #205820 was rechecked open/unmerged at `56aef23a43aea74de1f20ed6e1cf81cc3c1756a5`.

P02 remains a sibling, not a dependency. M11 #205845 would consume typed vocabulary; M06 #205633 later owns the authorized shared overlay. None of those proposals establishes an accepted P03 store or provider contract.

The author simplification pass retained one validator/parser/resolver owner and no second store, context collector, or provider constructor. The separable first foundation is the shared validation/resolution source; personal consumers follow it. These helpers have no production caller; this is not a complete feature.

## Evidence

### Published draft at `e3a1b8ddfb649f2ccdb314c00e7ffc736d524eee`

- **Branch refresh.** The conflict-free merge `0263c76c51c94a5e76e89e22c5a306f5955d6f3f` has prior PR head `34eb161f573465301820e44a42d0e1c215a3e79d` as its first parent and upstream `main` at `e13d41d3bd302999c3008f6abc487814331070a1` as its second. The managed publication commit has the same tree (`b29ea0c8cdb7535004ca71c3f1e563dd22a772ed`). The existing branch fast-forwarded without rewriting history and the PR remains draft. `git diff --check` passed against the merged base.
- **PASS — canonical suites and core typecheck.** The contributor’s [fork proof run #45949645324](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45949645324) pinned this exact head. Its [proof job](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45949645324/job/140353419913) ran `personal-vocabulary-import.test.ts`, `personal-vocabulary.test.ts`, and `vocabulary-terms.test.ts`: **3/3 files, 56/56 tests**. `pnpm run tsgo:core` also passed.
- **PASS — scripted dictation compatibility, 6/6 on the same head.** `single-utterance` and `two-utterances` passed **3/3 each** (alloy, nova, sage). Chromium replayed synthetic WAVs as microphone input; the Gateway used live OpenAI transcription; **Stop and keep text** left an editable, unsent Control UI draft. The run contains the per-take artifacts. This exercises the existing dictation path, not the personal-vocabulary helpers in production: the draft has no production caller. It does not establish recognition gains, real-mic behavior, accessibility, or persistence/recovery.
- **Physical microphone — still to do by @CompleteDotTech.** Check real microphone permission, device selection/switching, and real speech through **Stop and keep text** to an editable, unsent draft.
- **Upstream CI — maintainer approval is separate.** The [upstream CI run for this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45947423085) reports `action_required` and has no jobs recorded. The fork proof is not the upstream build or CI gate. Lint/unused-file scan, benchmark, and MDX sanity were not rerun as part of this refresh.
- **Runner handoff.** [Exact commands and artifacts to capture](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/blob/e3a1b8ddfb649f2ccdb314c00e7ffc736d524eee/docs/experiments/personal-dictation-vocabulary.md#local-proof-handoff) for the separate pinned-base comparison and browser/Gateway checks. The three canonical test files are new; their absence on base is not a red assertion.
- **Remaining design and production gates.** Maintainers still need to decide whether to proceed, choose the minimum accessible editor-to-dictation flow, and agree on storage, authenticated scope/revisions, egress, and the shared term contract with #205820. Production vocabulary dispatch, recognition comparison, accessibility, and persistence/recovery proof require that decision and implementation.
- **Prior review.** The [existing ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205880#issuecomment-7188365505) was for `9b8bba978eabe63170081bd5161c3f08b59d62cf`, not this head.

### Earlier evidence (not current-head checks)

- On `34eb161f573465301820e44a42d0e1c215a3e79d`, the [pre-refresh fork job](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45944789015/job/140327144486) also passed all 56 tests, `tsgo:core`, and 6/6 scripted takes. The [earlier audio-only run](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45938967474/job/140308968609) passed 6/6 but did not run the tests or typecheck.
- At the prior refresh, pinned oxfmt, `bash -n` on the handoff block, and the staged test-line ratchet passed. Auto Review reported `scoped-clean` through P2 after the type-only fix; a synthetic probe reproduced `TS2339` with the old discriminant and compiled with the split discriminant. These were scoped checks, not an upstream CI result.
- The benchmark below is from reviewed head `9b8bba978eabe63170081bd5161c3f08b59d62cf`, against implementation base `1c3de7eb68481e5d7656e21ec96d43855789fbb0`. Earlier canonical attempts did not reach test cases. At the subsequent docs-only head `158d1928c28b71608e0a0a7add08bb996fc1daa3`, Crabbox authentication failed before a lease started and [GitHub CI reported `action_required`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45858501294). These attempts establish neither a pass nor an assertion failure.

### Measured preparation only

Reviewed-head run (`9b8bba978eab`): 2026-11-26T09:20:08.504Z; AMD EPYC 9V74 80-Core Processor; Linux 6.18.57 x64; Node 24.22.3 / V8 13.6.233.17-node.63. Nine logical CPUs are visible; affinity provides one available CPU. Load averages before/after were 0.16 / 0.37 / 0.79.

The deterministic fixture has 1,000 entries, 950 enabled, 334 aliases, and 200 entries for each neutral/en/en-US/es-ES/fr-FR locale category. Selection uses en-US. Terms serialize to 106,733 bytes. Quotas are fixture limits: 64 terms, 8,192 JSON bytes, 512 synthetic token units, one unit per term.

One first call, 25 warmups, then 200 serial samples; nearest-rank percentiles. Imports, admission validation, persistence, authentication, microphone, network, and actual provider tokenization are excluded.

| Stage | First call ms | Warm p50 ms | Warm p95 ms | Warm p99 ms | Warm max ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Snapshot | 8.625574 | 1.250781 | 1.635430 | 5.551681 | 7.497758 |
| Snapshot plus hint preparation | 8.975661 | 1.275168 | 1.756432 | 5.574776 | 7.523106 |

Both outputs retained 64 terms. Hints used 1,089 JSON bytes and 64 synthetic units. Omission counts were 50 disabled, 350 locale-ineligible, and 536 beyond the snapshot bound; 22 selected entries had unrepresented aliases. The proposed warm snapshot p95 below 50 ms was observed on this host only. This is not speech-quality, real provider quota, cold-process, or full dictation latency evidence.

The [committed experiment record](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/blob/9b8bba978eabe63170081bd5161c3f08b59d62cf/docs/experiments/personal-dictation-vocabulary.md) retains an earlier measured run at `46c74099c7360a4f8ecbfc556df9ba5cfa936903`; the reviewed-head rerun above is separate.

### Complete P03 acceptance ledger

Every full criterion is **unmet**.

| Criterion | Current preparation and remaining requirement |
| --- | --- |
| AC01 — atomic CRUD and exact identity | Validation and proposed stable-ID replacement only. Canonical unit tests pass; durable add/edit/disable/delete, atomicity and revision checks remain unproven. |
| AC02 — explicit correction learning | Confirmation, locale/scope display, and proof that normal edits create no entry absent. |
| AC03 — bounded scoped snapshots | Pure deterministic snapshot code and measured workload present. Canonical unit tests pass; authenticated account/workspace isolation and capture integration remain unproven. |
| AC04 — supported hints | Pure representation/budget preparation present. Real adapter payloads, unsupported-field handling and endpoint qualification absent. |
| AC05 — ambiguity | Candidate conflict logic present. Canonical unit tests pass; no-dictionary/helpful/misleading recognition comparison remains unproven. |
| AC06 — strings are data | Data-only encoding and schema tests authored. Actual STT/refinement route/tool isolation proof absent. |
| AC07 — concurrent edits/import | Preview, explicit choices and proposed replacement present. Two-window conflict UI, actual CAS and atomic durable import/recovery absent. |
| AC08 — future exclusion | Pure snapshot inputs can omit disabled/deleted entries. Durable changes followed by actual capture proof absent. |
| AC09 — revision-pinned retry | Immutable value reuse modeled. Real capture/edit/retry and disclosed reprocess flow absent. |
| AC10 — selected egress | Pure local-only projection present. Actual destination observation through STT, refinement, retry and diagnostics absent. |
| AC11 — private diagnostics | Numeric summary/error boundary present. Default logs, crashes, telemetry and correction privacy qualification absent. |
| AC12 — migration/recovery | Proposed versioned scoped export/preview present. Accepted storage, upgrade/downgrade, unknown-schema recovery, disablement and rollback absent. |

The supplied archive-level `IMPLEMENTATION_WORKFLOW.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `STACKING_PLAN.md`, `VALIDATION_PLAN.md`, and `references/upstream-snapshot.json` were not supplied or found in bounded searches. The three attached P03 files were read; missing specifications are not treated as accepted contracts.

**Remain draft:** obtain maintainer acceptance of storage, authenticated scope/revisions, minimum accessible client flow, shared vocabulary/provider contract and egress ownership; finish the full lifecycle; then complete production integration, recognition, accessibility, migration, build and required upstream CI proof. No issue closure or upstream merge is requested.

prs.title: feat(android): add smaller architecture-specific APKs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Standalone Android APKs carry native libraries for four architectures, even when a device needs only one.

## User Impact

The archive workflow now produces four smaller, independently installable APKs alongside the existing universal APK. In the earlier archive build, the arm64 APK was 41.5% smaller than its universal APK. All variants share the application ID, version code, and signing key.

The current GitHub publication workflow still selects the universal APK; coordinated release-asset wiring follows separately. This change does not publish a release.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use Android Gradle Plugin ABI outputs with distinct filenames and its public variant-output API. Keep the universal output for existing consumers and archive each APK through the existing signature-verification and checksum flow. Debug installation and Play/Wear bundle delivery keep their current behavior.

## Current integration

Commit `7797bccebd05` brings the archive helper onto current main. The selector dry runs produced five third-party APKs, two store bundles, one Play bundle and one Wear bundle with the respective selectors. The combined plan produced seven distinct artifacts. The pinned AGP 9.5.1 API exposes the variant output controls used here. Its variant validator permits the four ABI filters and a universal APK together.

The measured size and emulator upgrade results below apply to the earlier build. Assembly and inspection of the five APKs at this revision are still pending.

## Evidence

- Focused artifact-contract tests: the old producer fails both new output-name cases; the candidate passes all 12 tests.
- Test-cost evidence from the source-bound 4-vCPU Testbox run: 12/12 tests passed, with 881 ms reported by Vitest and 1.85 s elapsed by the repository test wrapper. The recorded command was `pnpm test test/scripts/android-release-artifacts.test.ts` without an explicit worker override; a whole-command `--maxWorkers=1` wall measurement was not recorded. Per-file CI timing has not been extracted. Exact-head [CI run 35625611502](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35625611502) completed with failures in Android Play, Android third-party, compact-small-37, and the aggregate gate; Wear and Kotlin lint passed. prs.title: feat(ios): add the Control UI's wording for tool calls
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In iPhone chat, most tool calls show only the tool's title, such as "Session Send" or "Read", with a raw argument or path beside it. The Control UI describes what the call is doing or did, such as "Sent message to Release review" or "Couldn't read Header.swift". Anyone who uses both sees different descriptions of the same work, and on iPhone a collapsed row often leaves out the specific action or outcome until you expand it.

## User Impact

The new tool wording is not shown on screen yet. This PR is part of a series that brings the iOS chat in line with the Control UI. It adds the catalog and copy logic, and a later PR wires them into tool rows, the activity group headline, and the step timeline.

One small change is visible right away. When a tool has no display entry in `tool-display.json`, its fallback title now keeps the capital letters from the tool name, matching the Control UI. For example, `listIssues` changes from "Listissues" to "ListIssues", and `get_URL` changes from "Get Url" to "Get URL". Lowercase names such as `knowledge_status` look the same as before. Because `ToolDisplayRegistry` is shared, the same fallback casing applies in the macOS app's work activity.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI owns this wording. Its English catalogs (`en-chat-tool-operations.ts` and `en-chat-tool-labels.ts`) hold about 2,250 strings. Most of them (1,959) are the base, running and completed forms for 206 tools. The rest are shared verbs, launch and delivery states, and activity summaries. The app does not copy them by hand. `scripts/tool-operations.ts --write` generates `tool-operations.json` in `OpenClawKit` from those catalogs, and `--check` flags when the generated file falls behind.

- `ToolOperationCatalog` loads `tool-operations.json` once from the resource bundle and fills in placeholders such as `{name}` and `{count}`.
- `ChatToolOperationCopy` ports the web's `catalogToolOperation` and the named branches of `resolveToolOperationLabel`. It turns a call (name, arguments, outcome, result receipt, exit code, and addressed chat) into row text.
- `ToolDisplayRegistry.operationCall` and `operationSummary` normalize a call the same way the web does before wording it: they strip only OpenClaw's loopback MCP prefixes, parse arguments that arrive as a JSON string, and unwrap dispatcher calls. `displayCall` keeps its existing behavior because icon lookup depends on it.

The wording is English only for now, as in the Control UI.

## Evidence

- The iOS app builds for the simulator from this commit on top of `main`. The build's SwiftFormat lint and strict SwiftLint pass with 0 violations across 566 files.
- `ToolDisplayRegistryTests` passed 7 of 7 on an iOS 27.2 simulator, including the new check that `operationCall` leaves third-party MCP names unchanged. SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint pass on that test file.
- `pnpm tool-display:check` reports the existing tool display snapshot as up to date, and `native-app-i18n verify` reports `changed=false`. The i18n sync adds two entries (`launch.subagent.limitReached` and `launch.subagent.namedLimitReached`) that the extractor picks up from `ChatToolOperationCopy.swift`; both are lookup keys and are never shown to users.
- The wording tests ported from the web's `chat-tool-purpose.test.ts` assert on chat row titles through the row model, so they land with the later PR that wires up those rows. `ChatToolOperationCopy` itself is not exercised by unit tests in this PR.
- Known gap: `scripts/tool-operations.ts --check` reports `tool-operations.json` as stale by two entries. PR #206048 removed `sessionSend.accepted` and `sessionSend.acceptedNamed` from the web catalog and changed an accepted send to read "Sent message to …". Here, `tool-operations.json` and `ChatToolOperationCopy.sessionSend` still use the earlier "Message accepted for …" wording. Nothing renders these strings until the rows PR. Once that lands, its step title will differ from the web for this one receipt until `tool-operations.json` is regenerated and the `accepted` branch maps to `sent`.
- Not checked: a macOS app build and the `OpenClawKit` SwiftPM tests on macOS.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: fix(talk): run realtime voice consults under a fresh root admission
prs.body:
Fixes #202915

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where every FaceTime realtime call refused the `openclaw_agent_consult` tool with "Gateway is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly." while the gateway was healthy, so the caller never got the agent's answer (the voice model hears an error and may invent one instead).
- The same shared helper is used by Voice Call (`extensions/voice-call/src/runtime.ts`) and meeting consults (`src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.ts`); those entry points inherit the same failure shape whenever their consult fires from a callback that outlived its creating request root.
- **Related:** #142692 fixes the same admission mechanism only for meeting consults (caller-side wrap); this PR fixes it once for every realtime voice consult entry point. #202209 documents this exact refusal as "Pre-existing" on main.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` now owns its root admission before any session effect (`beginSessionEffect`). Under a live caller root the consult nests and counts once (the browser Talk contract in `src/gateway/talk/client-agent-consult.ts` is unchanged); under a released or absent root it opens a fresh independent root via `tryBeginGatewayRootWorkAdmission`; during a genuine gateway restart drain or suspension it still refuses with `GatewayDrainingError`.
- **Out of scope:** no change to call authorization, tool policy, consult session preparation, or delivery; the FaceTime controller and Voice Call controller are unchanged.
- **Highest-risk area:** double-counting admission when a caller already holds a live root (Talk). Covered by a regression test that asserts the consult counts once under a live root.
- The reporter's local workaround borrowed the webhook detached-work helper; per the review on the issue this keeps a dedicated consultation admission origin instead, matching the Talk contract.
- Follow-up (clawsweeper review): the new `realtime voice agent consult root admission` suite now initializes the same test fixture (`state` via `createOpenClawTestState`, fork-session mock, voice-session testing reset) as the sibling runtime suite, so selecting it alone with `-t` no longer fails on an undefined fixture.

## User Impact

- FaceTime (and other realtime voice) callers get the configured agent's answer spoken back on `openclaw_agent_consult` instead of a spurious "gateway unavailable" error while the gateway is running normally.
- Genuine gateway shutdown/restart drain and suspension still refuse consults, exactly as before.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** three layers on Linux.
  1. In-process vitest shards running the real consult runtime (real `gateway-work-admission` module, real `beginSessionEffect`, real FaceTime talk driver controller), including the released-root propagation the issue reports.
  2. A real Gateway child process (built from this head's dist) with the shipped Voice Call plugin enabled, mock-auth OpenAI model provider (the repo's own qa-lab e2e pattern), real state persistence, and a realtime media-stream session driven through the shipped voice-call webhook upgrade path. The consult is emitted from a continuation scheduled inside a gateway request root that has already responded (released) — the propagation shape reported in the issue: the scheduling gateway method returns immediately, its request root releases, and the carrier tool call fires 500 ms later, inheriting that released root. On this head the consult admits under a fresh root, the real embedded agent executes (reads the seeded workspace files, produces a structured answer), and the speakable answer comes back through the realtime bridge as the consult tool result. The identical driver run against a Gateway child built from `origin/main` (`3435fb5c94f`) is refused with the exact reported error.
  3. Boundary disclosure: the telephony carrier is the plugin's shipped `mock` carrier; the realtime provider is a debug fixture kept in `/tmp` (never in the repo) modeled on the repo's own qa-lab voice-call runtime fixture, differing only in where the consult tool call is emitted from (a released-root continuation instead of `connect()`). Everything above that boundary — the Gateway child process, admission machinery, session effects, the shipped voice-call plugin, and the embedded agent — is real code from this head.
  - FaceTime's macOS surface itself cannot be driven from this contributor's Linux machine; the FaceTime-level regression drives the real driver's `onToolCall` from an async continuation created inside a since-released root, exactly the propagation the issue reports.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # helper-level regression (released root -> fresh admission), run both isolated and with the full file:
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.test.ts -t 'realtime voice agent consult root admission'
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.test.ts extensions/facetime/tests/talk-driver.consult.test.ts
  skills/fix-pr/scripts/validate.sh src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.ts src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.test.ts extensions/facetime/tests/talk-driver.consult.test.ts
  # typecheck shard covering the changed test file:
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.other.json --builders 1   # exit 0
  # real-gateway voice-call e2e (Gateway child from dist of this head; see "What was not tested"):
  OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime
  node --import tsx <debug driver in /tmp equivalent to test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/voice-call-gateway.ts,
    with the consult emitted from a released-root continuation; run twice against this head's dist,
    and once against a Gateway child built from origin/main (3435fb5c94f)>
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  ✓ |infra| src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.test.ts > realtime voice agent consult root admission > consults under a fresh root after the calling bridge's root released 93ms
  ✓ |infra| src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.test.ts > realtime voice agent consult root admission > counts once under a live caller root 14ms
  ✓ |infra| src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.test.ts > realtime voice agent consult root admission > refuses a consult while the gateway is genuinely draining 10ms
  ✓ |infra| src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.test.ts > realtime voice agent consult root admission > releases the consultation root after a failed run 12ms
  ✓ |infra| src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.test.ts > realtime voice agent consult root admission > releases the consultation root after cancellation 13ms
  ✓ |extensions| extensions/facetime/tests/talk-driver.consult.test.ts > FaceTime talk driver consult root admission > answers a consult issued from a released plugin-service root 3636ms
  Test Files  2 passed (2)   Tests  35 passed (35)
  ```
  ```text
  # real-Gateway run, released-root propagation (head 8fbc75de, dist buildstamp verified; two runs, same result):
  [voice-call] Webhook server listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>/voice/webhook
  [voice-call] Outbound call initiated: callId=<uuid> providerCallId=mock-<uuid> mode=conversation
  [voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call <uuid> (providerCallId=mock-<uuid>, initialGreeting=queued)
  [proof] streamSession: {"token":"<redacted>","streamUrl":"wss://localhost:8443/voice/stream/realtime/<redacted>","providerCallId":"mock-<uuid>"}
  [proof] consult scheduled from request-root continuation: {"scheduled":true,"delayMs":500}   # method responds first -> its request root releases
  {"event":"consult-scheduled-inside-request-root","delayMs":500}
  {"event":"carrier-tool-call-emitted-from-continuation"}                                   # 500ms after the root released
  # tool results delivered to the carrier:
  {"callId":"qa-consult-call","result":{"status":"working","tool":"openclaw_agent_consult","message":"Tell the caller briefly that you are checking, then wait for the final OpenClaw result before answering with the actual result."},"options":{"willContinue":true}}
  {"callId":"qa-consult-call","result":{"text":"Worked:\n- Read all three seeded files: repo/qa/scenarios/index.yaml, repo/extensions/qa-lab/src/suite.ts, and repo/docs/help/testing.md.\n- Extra QA scenario candidates: config restart capability flip and image generation roundtrip.\nFailed:\n- None observed in mock mode.\nBlocked:\n- No live provider evidence in this lane.\nFollow-up:\n- Re-run with a real model for qualitative coverage."}}
  [proof] OUTCOME: consult delivered an agent answer
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** a consult issued from a callback that inherited a released root now runs to completion — the FaceTime driver delivers the agent's answer as the tool result instead of the admission error, `runEmbeddedAgent` is called once, and no consultation root is left active afterwards (success, failure, cancellation, and genuine drain are each asserted). In the real-gateway Voice Call runs, the consult emitted from a released-root continuation through the shipped realtime voice path admits under a fresh root, runs the real embedded agent, and delivers the speakable answer through the realtime bridge (reproduced twice on this head).
- **Before evidence:** on main, the same two in-process regressions fail: the helper-level consult rejects with `GatewayDrainingError: Gateway is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.` from `beginSessionEffect`'s subordinate-admission check, and the FaceTime driver submits `{"error":"Gateway is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly."}` as the tool result — the exact reported symptom. The same released-root real-gateway driver run against a Gateway child built from `origin/main` (`3435fb5c94f`) is refused:
  ```text
  # identical driver, Gateway child from origin/main (3435fb5c94f):
  {"event":"consult-scheduled-inside-request-root","delayMs":500}
  {"event":"carrier-tool-call-emitted-from-continuation"}
  {"callId":"qa-consult-call","result":{"status":"working","tool":"openclaw_agent_consult","message":"Tell the caller briefly that you are checking, ..."},"options":{"willContinue":true}}
  {"callId":"qa-consult-call","result":{"error":"Gateway is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly."}}
  [proof] OUTCOME: consult refused -> {"error":"Gateway is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly."}
  ```
  Before the fixture fix in this follow-up, selecting the admission suite alone (`-t 'realtime voice agent consult root admission'`) failed with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` (state fixture not initialized in the sibling describe).
- **What was not tested:** a live FaceTime call on macOS run by this contributor (no macOS host / Apple Silicon available here); the FaceTime-level regression reproduces the reported released-root propagation against the real driver code instead. **Since then @withlightsg ran one real inbound FaceTime call on macOS against a 2026.11.5 release build carrying only this PR's production change** ([comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202979#issuecomment-7132792875)): the shipped `@openclaw/facetime` plugin called `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` exactly as released, session-effect admission settled without refusal at 0.09 s, the configured agent ran, and the tool result reached the call at 53.77 s with no `Gateway is temporarily unavailable` anywhere in the log — while the same build without this change refused every consult within ~0.1 s. That is a single-call smoke test of the released-root path on real hardware (it does not cover Talk nesting or drain, which this PR's tests assert). The real-gateway runs used the plugin's shipped mock telephony carrier, a `/tmp` realtime-provider fixture (disclosed above), and the repo's mock-auth OpenAI provider — system-boundary mocks per the repo's own qa-lab e2e pattern; the released-root failure shape is now also demonstrated end-to-end in a real Gateway (refused on main, answered on this head). The official qa-lab scenario `qa/scenarios/plugins/voice-call-cli-rpc-agent-tool.yaml` currently fails on main at the realtime step: its fixture issues the stream session with the internal callId while the signed-call boundary (`realtime-handler.ts`, providerName "twilio") compares the start frame's CallSid with the issuance callId, so the stream is always closed with 1008 "Call identity does not match stream session" (verified identical on origin/main); worth a separate test-infra fix.
- **Proof tier:** L2 (real runtime modules in-process, deterministic RED/GREEN on the reported failure mode) + a real-Gateway Voice Call e2e run from this head's dist demonstrating the released-root propagation end-to-end (refused on main, answered on this head).
- **Proof limitations:** this contributor has no macOS / live FaceTime hardware (the real-hardware confirmation above is @withlightsg's, on a release build carrying this PR's production change); in my runs the model provider, telephony carrier, and realtime provider are system-boundary mocks as disclosed above.
- **Review state:** third follow-up. Rebased onto current `main` (`1e6d3f9bd9e`, head `080cb2c7b72`): main has since split the consult into two entry points — `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` (channel bridges) and the gateway-only `consultRealtimeVoiceAgentInSessionRuntime` (browser Talk) — both delegating to `consultRealtimeVoiceAgentInternal`. The root admission now lives on that shared internal owner instead of a single wrapper, so both entry points get it at the narrowest point: a live caller root still nests and counts once, a released or absent root opens a fresh independent root, and a genuine drain still refuses. The two conflicting test files re-merged cleanly; `src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.test.ts` + `extensions/facetime/tests/talk-driver.consult.test.ts` pass on the rebased head (2 vitest shards green), oxfmt/oxlint clean, `pnpm tsgo:core` exit 0. Earlier follow-ups: the second added a real-Gateway released-root run from this head's dist (agent answer delivered, reproduced twice) plus the identical driver refused on origin/main, answering the review of `8fbc75de`; requesting re-review, including of @withlightsg's real-hardware FaceTime confirmation above.

prs.title: fix: name usage limits in automation failure notices instead of "Cause: unknown"
prs.body:
Closes #206434

## What Problem This Solves

When a scheduled automation fails because the Codex harness hit a ChatGPT usage limit, the failure notice often says `Cause: unknown`. That happens for runs that had already called tools when the limit hit, and for runs that start in the next 20–30 minutes while the account is cooling down. Operators can't tell a usage-limit outage from a broken job without digging through run history.

## User Impact

These failures now record `errorReason: "rate_limit"`, and their notice says `Cause: rate_limit`. Nothing to configure or migrate.

Scheduling also changes for these runs. Retries, provider backoff and notice holds now treat them like the usage-limit runs that were already classified as `rate_limit`. A run that had already called tools can now get a quick transient retry (30 s, 1 min, 5 min, then the normal schedule), instead of waiting for its next natural slot. That's the same treatment cron already gives thrown `rate_limit` and `timeout` failures after execution starts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider class was known at both points and dropped before cron's classification owner saw it. This change carries the producer's typed reason, so display text still can't drive retries (per the comment on `resolveCronAgentErrorClassification`):

- **Run-level failure** (`cron isolated run failed: …`): when the attempt isn't replay-safe, the runner finishes with `meta.error` instead of throwing. `completeEmbeddedRun` now classifies the typed prompt error object with `resolveFailoverReasonFromError` and records it as `meta.error.reason`. `runCronIsolatedAgentTurn` passes that reason to `resolveCronAgentErrorClassification`, which used to get none and fell back to `unknown`.
- **Cooldown refusal** (`Prepared auth profiles are temporarily unavailable …`): when the harness-owned auth path can't admit any prepared profile, it now throws a `FailoverError`. The reason comes from `resolveProfilesUnavailableReason`, the same owner `createAuthProfileCooldownError` and the OpenClaw-owned auth path already use. It replaces a plain `Error`. Model fallback already moved on from either error when another candidate exists, so fallback selection is unchanged.

Not changed: the OpenClaw-owned auth path (`throwAuthProfileFailover`) still throws a plain `Error` when no model fallback is configured. It wasn't involved in the reported runs, so I left it for a separate change.

## Evidence

- **Production, 2026.11.10, Codex harness with ChatGPT sign-in, isolated cron jobs during one usage-limit outage** (run history in the issue):
  - The thrown failures already said `rate_limit`.
  - The `cron isolated run failed: Codex reported a usage or quota limit…` failures and the `Prepared auth profiles are temporarily unavailable…` refusals said `unknown`.
- **New regression tests, red on `main`, green with this change:**
  - `run.meta-error-status.test.ts`: a replay-unsafe prompt failure with HTTP 429 goes through the real `resolveEmbeddedRunTerminal` and then `runCronIsolatedAgentTurn`. On `main`, `meta.error` has no `reason` and the assertion fails. With the fix, it's `rate_limit`, and the cron result's `errorClassification` is `{ kind: "reason", reason: "rate_limit" }`.
  - `runtime-preparation.thinking.test.ts`: the only Codex-harness profile is in a `rate_limit` cooldown and the run is allowed to probe a cooldown. On `main`, `prepareEmbeddedRunRuntime` rejects with a plain `Error`. With the fix, it rejects with `FailoverError` and `reason: "rate_limit"`.
- **Related suites pass:** the ClawSweeper acceptance list (`run.meta-error-status`, `run-error-reason`, `terminal-resolution`, `terminal-resolution.auth`, `auth-controller`, `timer-outcomes.regression`, `timer-outcome-finalization.receipts`, `failure-notification-text`), plus `run.watchdog-cause`, `run.invalid-source`, `run-entry`, `result-fallback-classifier`, `prompt-failure` and `retry-limit`. `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxfmt, oxlint and `git diff --check` pass.
- **Not exercised:** a live Gateway run against a real exhausted ChatGPT usage window. I couldn't reproduce one on demand, so the notice text on a live Gateway after this change is unverified. The tests cover the classification that the notice renders.

prs.title: fix: let an updated Mac app move its Gateway to the new version instead of quitting
prs.body:
Closes #203065

## What Problem This Solves

After an in-place update, OpenClaw.app can stop its bundled Gateway and still be unable to replace it. Doctor sees the old service registration, refuses to prepare credentials, and the app quits. In the reported case, reopening the 2026.11.5 app kept bringing back the 2026.11.4 Gateway.

## User Impact

User impact: the old service registration no longer blocks an update when the Mac app has stopped that exact service. If credential preparation fails after changing the database, the app reports the original error and leaves the old Gateway stopped unless that build confirms it can still use the saved state. A separately installed CLI still refuses to migrate state needed by an older Gateway.

This does not fix configs that still contain `agents.defaults.heartbeat`. A config written by 2026.11.4 setup passed the service check but stopped at `Cannot prepare client credentials with invalid config`; its schema stayed at 22. Thanks to @skrubbb and @BObereder for reporting affected installs, and to @Speculorum9 for the update timeline, confirmation of the heartbeat key, and offer to test. There is no verified signed build of this change to recommend for a live installation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The app passes the stopped service’s entrypoint to its bundled Doctor child in `OPENCLAW_REPLACING_GATEWAY_SERVICE_ENTRYPOINT`. Doctor makes the exception only when that path resolves to the installed service’s entrypoint. It still needs the state lease. Normal startup drops any inherited value, and a plain `doctor --fix` keeps the protection from #186971.

Doctor can commit a schema migration before it discovers an invalid client identity. On that error, the app asks the previous build to check the service’s own config and database before restarting it. A refusal or an inconclusive answer leaves the service stopped; the check does not undo a migration.

<details>
<summary>Root cause</summary>

At merge base `08f45d611b7d`, `StaleGatewayServiceReplacement.run` (`apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/StaleGatewayServiceReplacement.swift:15`) stops the old service before preparing credentials. The CLI still reads the installed LaunchAgent (`src/cli/run-main.ts:844`, `src/cli/run-main-service-installation.ts:114`), so Doctor sees the older package and refuses the migration (`src/commands/doctor-update-schema-guard.ts:467`). The same-version check for #187000 did not exercise this case. The in-app Retry setup action still runs a plain `doctor --fix`; it is not reachable when the app quits during credential startup.

</details>

## Evidence

**Rollback regression, not a packaged-app upgrade.** A Swift harness exercised `StaleGatewayServiceReplacement.run` with the credential error `Invalid client identity requires explicit repair; startup preserved it.` The harness recorded service calls rather than starting a Gateway.

| Revision | What happened after the fixture advanced to schema 41 and credential preparation failed |
| --- | --- |
| `78fc7710` | `run` called `restore`, which would restart the old Gateway against state it cannot read. |
| `a5ff3209` | `run` preserved the original credential error and called neither `restore` nor `install`. The published 2026.11.5 CLI refused schema 41 (it supports 36). |

With compatible schema-36 state, the old CLI admitted the state and the harness recorded `restore`. A retry at schema 41 still did not restore; successful credential preparation called `install` instead.

**Packaged proof remains open.** No packaged app was verified completing a schema-changing upgrade, an upgrade from the latest stable release, or a fresh install on `a5ff3209`. The available local Mac has Command Line Tools only; they lack the SwiftUI macro plugins required to package the app. No isolated Mac with full Xcode was available for these checks. Gateway startup, a client connection, and preservation of credentials, settings, and data through a packaged upgrade remain unverified.

Hosted CI has not built or tested this head.

<details>
<summary>Earlier CLI and release-state checks (not an app upgrade)</summary>

On Apple silicon with Node 26.8.1, the CLI ran against homes created by published 2026.11.4 and 2026.11.5 releases. The test supplied a stopped service registration and used `node --import tsx/esm src/entry.ts doctor --client-credentials --fix --non-interactive`. It did not start launchd, a Gateway, or a client connection.

- With the stopped 2026.11.5 service’s entrypoint, the merge base (`08f45d611b7d`) refused the schema migration. The PR’s CLI exited 0. Omitting the variable or passing another copy’s entrypoint still refused. With credentials already prepared, all six databases kept their versions, row counts, and integrity.
- After the fixture replaced the service registration, credential preparation exited 0 without the variable. `doctor --fix --non-interactive` moved the state schema from 36 to 41: all 26 rows remained, integrity checked out, and `agents list --json` still listed both agents. Doctor did not finish plugin maintenance or lease release in that environment; the agent databases stayed at 38.
- The stopped-entrypoint regression failed on the merge base and passed on the PR.
- `src/commands/doctor-update-schema-guard.test.ts` reproduced the same state-lock and backup failures on the merge base and the PR. The full macOS app test suite was not run.

</details>

<details>
<summary>How the release-state runs were set up</summary>

- Releases: `npm install openclaw@2026.11.5` (e13cf15) and `openclaw@2026.11.4` (d843d6a), each in its own prefix. Branch and merge-base trees come from `git archive` with a production dependency install.
- Each 2026.11.5 case gets an empty HOME, and the published CLI creates the state in place:

  ```sh
  openclaw setup --baseline --workspace "$HOME/workspace"
  openclaw agents add proofagent --workspace "$HOME/proofagent-ws" --non-interactive
  openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive   # its Gateway discovery step cannot finish here
  # the 2026.11.5 app's startup credential step
  OPENCLAW_PROFILE=default OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$HOME/.openclaw" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$HOME/.openclaw/openclaw.json" \
    openclaw doctor --client-credentials --fix --non-interactive
  openclaw agents list --json
  ```

  The 2026.11.4 home comes from 2026.11.4 `setup --baseline`. Its later seeding steps could not finish here because they wait on a state lease holder this environment cannot inspect.
- LaunchAgent: written with this branch's `buildLaunchAgentPlist` to `$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/<label>.plist` under a custom `OPENCLAW_LAUNCHD_LABEL`, running `node <release package>/openclaw.mjs gateway --port <port>`.
- App Doctor run, from each source tree:

  ```sh
  OPENCLAW_PROFILE=default OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$HOME/.openclaw" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$HOME/.openclaw/openclaw.json" \
  OPENCLAW_REPLACING_GATEWAY_SERVICE_ENTRYPOINT=<release package>/openclaw.mjs \
    node --import tsx/esm src/entry.ts doctor --client-credentials --fix --non-interactive
  ```

- Install step: the LaunchAgent is rewritten to run the branch's `openclaw.mjs`, then the app Doctor run repeats without the variable, followed by `doctor --fix --non-interactive` and `agents list --json` from the branch and from 2026.11.5.
- Databases are read with `node:sqlite`: `PRAGMA user_version`, `PRAGMA integrity_check` and `count(*)` per table, before and after each step.

</details>

Merge danger: the exception applies to the Mac app replacing its own Gateway. Reverting the code restores the CLI refusal; it does not reverse a database migration that has already happened. The migration exception still needs an owner decision.

prs.title: improve: reduce redundant prompt context across conversation turns (design proposal)
prs.body:
Related: #206424

## What Problem This Solves

Our work focuses on long-running, multi-user Discord conversations in OpenClaw, particularly on consumer hardware with a 32k local-model context window. Discord is our test environment; the underlying context-management principles have wider applicability.

OpenClaw can spend a substantial portion of its context window on its own bookkeeping rather than the conversation. On the tested route, historical runtime-context snapshots accumulate even when the latest snapshot already supplies the relevant information. Each snapshot also contains unnecessary operational metadata.

This creates a compounding problem: **redundant context → faster context growth → earlier context exhaustion → more frequent compaction, history rebuilding or session resets → potential cache loss and increased inference usage.** A warm cache does not eliminate the context-window capacity consumed by redundant tokens. Depending on the harness and provider, rewriting or resetting the cached prefix can make those tokens expensive to process again.

We have working solutions for both the accumulation of redundant snapshots and the size of the context that remains.

## User Impact — the win

| Live observation | Before | After | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Sampled input tokens | 14,805 | 6,381 | **56.9%** |
| Mean input growth per short exchange | 1,080 | 211 | **80.5%** |
| Runtime metadata block, characters (subsequent experiment) | 405 | 57 | **85.9%** |

The first experiment reclaimed 8,424 input tokens in an existing session without deleting genuine conversation history. Recent-room recall passed. At the measured average growth rates, an equivalent remaining context budget could accommodate approximately five times as many short exchanges before reaching its limit, assuming other inputs stay constant.

The second experiment reduces the overhead of the runtime context that remains. Together, they address both prompt size and its rate of growth.

The potential benefit is more meaningful conversation and task context, fewer context-limit interventions, better continuity, and fewer associated cache rebuilds. This is particularly important for smaller local models, but relevant to hosted models too. Actual reset frequency, latency and usage savings across workloads require longer controlled tests.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two complementary working proofs of concept form the basis of this proposal:

1. [Transient Turn Context v0.1 plugin](https://github.com/Animeleague/openclaw/tree/bank/transient-turn-context-v0.1-2026-11-27/live-bank/2026-11-27-transient-turn-context-v0.1): prevents redundant historical runtime-context carriers from accumulating by retaining the current carrier through the existing provider replay-policy hook. No transcript deletion is required.
2. [Prompt optimization V3.1](https://github.com/Animeleague/openclaw/blob/bank/prompt-optimisation-v3.1-2026-11-27/live-bank/2026-11-27-prompt-optimisation-v3.1/README.md): reduces redundant metadata at its source and separates stable policy from changing facts. This is a scoped, version-pinned runtime overlay.

**We recommend installing and evaluating the plugin alongside V3.1 on a compatible test deployment, and ultimately integrating both optimizations into OpenClaw itself.** The plugin is an integral part of this work, not an optional reference. Follow its documented compatibility and installation precautions, including avoiding simultaneous installation with the original provider plugin.

The objective is not to make agents remember less. It is to stop making them repeatedly read information they already have or cannot use, while preserving attribution, chronology, reply semantics, trust boundaries, execution permissions and checkpoint compatibility. Upstream integration should be capability-aware and validated across applicable providers, without indiscriminately removing tool instructions or security policy.

## Evidence and limitations

November testing used OpenClaw 2026.11.10, Windows, local Gemma via openai-completions and tool-free Discord. Historical carriers fell from 6–9 to one. Derived warm-cache reuse decreased from 92.0% to 82.2%, and mean fresh tokens increased slightly from 1,092 to 1,216 in the first experiment. Subsequent metadata-experiment first-token times were approximately 97, 5 and 40 seconds; history changes and cache behavior confound these observations. The table reports distinct measurements, not a combined speedup.

Related cache investigation: #202001. The renamed transient-context package is locally tested but not independently live-installed; the overlay is tied to exact compiled bundles. Current upstream source integration, regression tests, tool-enabled and cross-provider validation, rollback and controlled combined benchmarks remain outstanding.

This is a draft design proposal, not a merge-ready runtime change. The branch is based on upstream main and contains only the proposal document, excluding unrelated fork commits and private recovery fixtures.

## Our track record: working solutions months before upstream

On August 10, 2026, we submitted [upstream PR #121683](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/121683), addressing a related defect: switching between an owner and a non-owner changed the registered dynamic-tool schema, destabilizing Codex native-thread reuse and prompt caching. We separated the stable advertised tool catalog from actual per-turn execution permissions.

Our published live evidence demonstrated the same native thread and registered-tool fingerprint across six turns, including ownership changes. Non-owner turns retained 99.24% and 98.94% cache reuse without gaining privileged execution rights; across all six turns, cache reuse ranged from 98.30% to 99.83%, including an image turn.

On August 14, we also created our public [Transient Tools plugin](https://github.com/Animeleague/openclaw-plugin-transient-tools) to address persistent tool-history accumulation. Our August PR was closed without merging on September 3. Its live evidence came from an equivalent deployed patch, not the exact PR checkout.

### Upstream subsequently adopted the same architectural principle

On October 17, 2026 — **68 days after our submission** — upstream merged [PR #175309: fix prompt cache misses on completion, heartbeat and non-owner turns](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175309). Its production telemetry identified owner/non-owner tool-list changes as the most frequent raw cause of cache drops. Across all measured causes over 14 days, it reported 925 drops involving 101 million cached tokens on one deployment and 247 drops involving 25.8 million on another.

Its solution? Keep advertised tool definitions stable and enforce actual authority at execution time — the same architectural separation we demonstrated in August.

On November 26 — 108 days after our submission — [upstream PR #206126](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206126) was opened to address remaining Codex native-thread rotation from internal-turn tool-catalog drift, again separating the durable catalog from per-turn execution authority. It was not merged as of November 27.

**We had implemented, live-tested and published a solution in August. Upstream merged a fix based on the same principle in October.** The public records establish this chronology and technical convergence, not code copying or identical implementations.

### Why today's work goes further

Our August fix stopped avoidable cache loss when tool permissions changed. Today's work tackles something more fundamental: unnecessary context growth on ordinary turns.

**Even if cached tokens were "free" (they aren't), context space isn't.** The faster we fill the context window, the sooner we force compaction or resets, potentially dropping the cache and driving up fresh-token usage. We've demonstrated an 80.5% reduction in context growth per short exchange. The resulting long-term usage savings remain to be measured.

## In summary: we have solutions, not just suggestions

We were right about separating durable model state from transient per-turn information in August. Today's work goes further: reducing context growth should reduce cache resets and fresh-token consumption, even where cached tokens are free. Long-term fresh-token savings remain to be quantified.

We've been using the general transient-turn approach in our Discord deployments for months, with approximately threefold improvement in usage efficiency reported from our operational experience. This is not a controlled benchmark of the two November changes.

**We were ahead of upstream on this architectural principle in August. We have working solutions to share again today.**

If upstream chooses not to adopt them, that's fine. We will continue benefiting from and developing them ourselves. We're sharing this work because the wider OpenClaw community could benefit too.

prs.title: refactor(subagents): own descendant Stop cancellation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The gateway owns descendant Stop orchestration and reads raw subagent rows to select yielded requester cancellation, even though that state belongs to the subagents runtime. This makes gateway, Talk, and the subagents tests depend on a gateway implementation for the same cancellation operation.

Related: #205482, #205940.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. Chat Stop, session Stop, Talk cancellation, native descendant cancellation, and cancellation error reporting retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing `abortControlledSubagents` operation into `src/agents/subagents/cancel-descendants.ts` and migrate all callers directly. The gateway retains only RPC error presentation. The moved function body is unchanged; both gateway re-exports are removed rather than kept as compatibility aliases.

### Ownership map

| Consumer | Needed operation or fact | Owner after this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chat-abort-handler`, `chat-abort-exact-run`, `chat-abort-runtime`, `sessions-abort` | Cancel the admitted parent's registry, native, and exec descendants; return settled results | `subagents/cancel-descendants` |
| `chat-abort-runtime.types` | Descendant cancellation result contract | Same operation's return type |
| `chat-abort-descendants` | Present an incomplete cancellation as an RPC error | Gateway, consuming the recorded result |
| Talk and the cancellation benchmark | Invoke the same descendant cancellation operation | `subagents/cancel-descendants` |

### Mechanical caller updates

- `src/talk/agent-run-control.runtime.ts`: import path only.
- `test/subagent-progress-telegram-retirement.integration.test.ts`: import path only.
- `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-control.worker.test.ts`: import path only.
- `src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.requester-settle-cancel.test.ts`: import path only, explicitly approved by the coordinator.
- `scripts/perf/agent-deletion-cancellation-measure.ts`: type import and default owner path only. Historical baseline extraction instructions remain valid.
- Gateway cancellation tests and type consumers: direct owner imports; existing assertions remain unchanged.

### Scope and overlap

This is the descendant-cancellation slice of the gateway ownership campaign. Dormant-child cancellation and other gateway projections remain follow-ups; this PR does not change their semantics.

Open overlap: #205641 touches the old gateway owner and three abort callers. #206405 touches `subagent-control.worker.test.ts`; this PR changes only its import. No kill-owner, requester-custody, or announce implementation is changed.

## Evidence

- Base: `04a03bcb5eb42f6fc9af18b2a3f62015421a7291`; candidate: `2737f4df8279`.
- The entire relocated function body compares byte-for-byte equal to the base.
- Formatting and Node syntax checks passed for all 16 changed TypeScript files; `git diff --check` passed. The normal pre-commit hook passed.
- The previously reported `preserves routed native Stop authority … (consumed-session)` case passed in the manual CI run; no fix to that case is claimed.
- Existing cancellation assertions are preserved. No new tests or test-only seams were added for the relocation.
- Focused Testbox attempt queued before tests ran. Its allocation was stopped and cleanup confirmed. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45952829913) supplied the build, typecheck, lint, and dependency checks, which passed. That manual run completed with one failed test job. [Normal ready-PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45954537461) completed successfully on the same unchanged head, including its CI gate. This is current-head qualification; it does not prove the earlier shutdown failure was fixed.
- The `checks-node-changed` job failed in `gateway.compaction-hot-reload.e2e.test.ts` during Gateway shutdown: `PluginRuntimeCloseRetainedError`, caused by `Native worker execution owners have not joined`. The native failure classifier reports **unknown: no matching job on main**. These shutdown sources are unchanged by the PR; baseline attribution is not yet established. A focused baseline/head comparison also queued on Testbox and was stopped before execution; no reproduction result is claimed. [Failure log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45952829913/job/140353020555).
- Local autoreview: P0–P2, base `04a03bcb5eb4`, head `2737f4df8279`, scoped-clean with no actionable findings. Runtime behavior remains deferred to CI.

### Measurements

Counts use the same L6-owned gateway production scope before and after, excluding test/support files and L4’s `session-restart-resume-*` files. Direct registry/announce importers: **37 → 36**. All subagent importers: **62 → 66**, because four callers now import the named owner operation directly rather than through gateway re-exports. Subagent-mentioning lines: **1,194 → 1,176**. Within the original campaign-listed L6 files only, those counts are **36 → 35**, **59 → 59**, and **911 → 893**, respectively.

Within `chat-abort-descendants.ts`, raw requester/execution/wake decision lines: **4 → 0**. Its cancellation function moves to its state owner; cyclomatic complexity is **48 → 48** for that unchanged operation. This is an ownership improvement, not a claim of algorithmic simplification.

prs.title: test(cli): gate agent --local cold-start processes and workers
prs.body:
## Problem

Cold time-to-first-request of the one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turn (the path benchmark boards run) has no regression gate. A measured turn on `b0a6e8cd` took 6.05 s median to the first provider request (warm Gateway: 0.69 s). Most of it is fan-out: every Node process and worker thread boots its own module graph before the first request. Nothing stops a change from adding another one.

## Change

Add `src/cli/agent-local-cold-start.process.test.ts`: one real `agent --local` turn from source against the local fake OpenAI Responses server (`test/helpers/openai-responses-model-fixture.ts`). A preload ledger counts, up to the moment the fake provider receives the first request:

- CLI Node processes (the startup respawn counts here),
- Node child processes spawned by the CLI,
- worker threads.

The test asserts an exact budget `{ nodeProcesses: 1, nodeChildren: 5, workerThreads: 18 }`. Counts, not wall time: they do not move with host load. A PR that removes work lowers the budget in the same change.

The fixture keeps the default startup (`OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN` unset). It marks host CA discovery done (`OPENCLAW_NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS_READY=1`) because that respawn depends on the host's Node install, not on OpenClaw code.

## Evidence

- Red on the merge base before #206448 (`b0a6e8cd`): the warning-only respawn makes `nodeProcesses` 2. Green on main with #206448.
- Stable across 3 local runs on head (1 / 5 / 18 each).
- Cost: one CLI turn from source, 16-23 s test time locally (88 s once under host load; same 120 s timeout as `agent-local-rpc-cleanup.process.test.ts`). No cheaper layer proves the number of processes and workers a real turn starts before its first request.

Budget source: measured on this head, macOS arm64 (Studio). Linux CI counts are checked by this PR's CI run.

prs.title: fix(talk): keep accepted agent work running when Talk sessions close
prs.body:
Related: #188134, #188798, #171377, #203889, #206329, #206333

## What Problem This Solves

Closing, dropping, or reconnecting a realtime Talk session cancels accepted agent work on the Gateway unless the client opts out with `disposition: "detach"`. That affects `talk.session.close` without a disposition, provider disconnects, provider reconnect continuity resets (`session.continuity.reset`), idle/TTL expiry, `gateway-control-v1` teardown, and bundled OpenAI GPT-Live bridge/lease retirement.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ending, losing, or reconnecting a voice call affects the audio transport, not background agent work that the session already accepted. #171377 introduced explicit `disposition: "detach"` while keeping `"abort"` as the omitted default, and #188798 worked around that default on Android. Because every native client and server teardown path otherwise inherits `"abort"`, reversing the Gateway default ensures a closed, dropped, or reconnecting call never cancels accepted agent work on any platform while preserving explicit `disposition: "abort"` and `talk.session.cancelOutput` behavior:

- `src/gateway/talk/relay/operations.ts`: default `finishRelaySessionClose` and `stopTalkRealtimeRelaySession` to `disposition: "detach"`, keeping explicit `disposition: "abort"` in `cancelTalkRealtimeRelayOutput` and caller overrides.
- `src/gateway/talk/relay/state.ts`: detach accepted agent runs on `resetTalkRealtimeRelayContinuity` (provider reconnect continuity reset) while clearing old audio and provider tool-call associations so stale tool results cannot leak into the replacement provider generation.
- `src/gateway/talk/client-gateway-control.ts`: default `owner.close` to `preserveRuns: true` while keeping explicit `preserveRuns: false` abort handling for `closeDisposition: "abort"` consults.
- `src/gateway/talk/voice-selection.ts`: remove now-unused `isTalkVoiceSessionReplacing`.
- `extensions/openai/realtime-quicksilver-gateway-bridge.ts`, `realtime-session-retirement.ts`, and `realtime-quicksilver-session.ts`: default bridge/lease close and provider disconnect/error teardown to `"detach"` instead of `"abort"`.
- `docs/gateway/protocol/rpc-talk-config-and-agents.md`, `docs/plugins/sdk-provider-plugins/voice-and-audio.md`, and `docs/platforms/android.md`: document `"detach"` as the default close disposition and note that older Gateways advertising `talk-session-close-disposition` understand explicit `"detach"` but still abort when `disposition` is omitted.

AI-assisted: drafted, implemented, and verified with AI coding assistance, with every change reviewed and tested locally.

## User Impact

- Accepted agent runs keep running to completion when a Talk session closes, disconnects, reconnects with a continuity reset, or expires on any client, including clients that omit `disposition`.
- Explicit `disposition: "abort"`, explicit `preserveRuns: false`, and `talk.session.cancelOutput` continue to abort active output or consult runs when requested.
- Clients talking to older Gateways continue sending explicit `disposition: "detach"` when `talk-session-close-disposition` is advertised.

## Evidence

- Verified new regression expectations fail before the fix (`server.talk-consult-history.test.ts -t "settles close disposition undefined"`, `relay/index.test.ts`, and `client-gateway-control.close.test.ts`) and pass after the fix.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/talk/relay/index.test.ts src/gateway/talk/relay/cancellation-recovery.test.ts src/gateway/talk/relay/voice.test.ts extensions/openai/realtime-voice-bridge-reconnect.test.ts extensions/google/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: all 5 suites passed (including continuity reset detaching accepted runs while clearing tool-call associations).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/talk/client-gateway-control.close.test.ts src/gateway/talk/client-gateway-control.test.ts src/gateway/talk/client-gateway-control.mailbox.test.ts src/gateway/talk/handlers/index.test.ts src/gateway/talk/handlers/client-consult-authority.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: all passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server.talk-consult-history.test.ts -t "settles close disposition" --maxWorkers=1`: 9 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/openai/realtime-quicksilver-gateway-errors.test.ts extensions/openai/realtime-quicksilver-gateway-direct.test.ts extensions/openai/realtime-quicksilver-session.test.ts test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: all passed.
- `npx oxlint` (0 warnings, 0 errors) and `npx oxfmt --check` (all modified files formatted).
