prs.title: improve: simplify proactive checks and automation delivery controls
prs.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Do not land.** Still in progress and under discussion. Talk to @vyctorbrzezowski.

Co-authored by [Vyctor Brzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bfb77f08-1fd2-461f-ada5-4f3ff81fa044)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/07129d2b-6d52-42e2-bb0c-db750762cf73)

## What Problem This Solves

The Automations editor exposes several options left over from heartbeat, even though the default Proactive check can use the same schedule and routing as other recurring jobs.

## User Impact

The editor, CLI, agent tool, and Gateway no longer offer Wait until idle, Skip empty scratch, Block direct messages, or the primary `last` channel. **Send to me** still resolves the owner’s direct-message destination. The default Proactive check keeps its cadence but may now run while another session is working on the same agent.

Run `openclaw doctor --fix` to repair stored jobs. Doctor backs up the store, removes the retired switches, and reports the changes. It pauses affected jobs when a custom execution policy has no safe replacement or when removing a direct-message block could allow an unintended send. Jobs are not deleted. For primary `last` chat routes, Doctor pins the most recent recorded successful destination, including the account and thread when recorded. Without a recorded destination, it reports the fallback and leaves normal routing to choose the destination. Owner targeting stays dynamic. The separate failure-alert `last` setting is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Routine checks now use normal scheduler admission, and new jobs can either name a specific chat route or let OpenClaw resolve it automatically. This removes heartbeat-only controls without guessing where existing jobs actually sent results. Expect overlap with the sibling automation cleanups in the editor, Gateway schemas, scheduler, Doctor, and documentation; this draft does not implement those changes.

## Evidence

The SQLite Doctor repair suite passed all 17 tests, including backup creation, most-recent *actual* delivery rather than a newer failed attempt, no-trace fallback, and pausing without deleting jobs. The heartbeat cadence suite and three Gateway protocol conformance tests also passed. Touched-file lint and formatting checks passed. The UI editor test could not load a workspace package in the standalone Vitest configuration; broader focused suites and independent local review are not confirmed green. The local reviewer stopped before starting because its input exceeded the selected pass budget. Full CI and live upgrade checks were not run.

The before and after show the actual Control UI with a mock Gateway and synthetic automation data.

prs.title: feat: links to a setting open and highlight its row in Settings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw tells someone to change a setting, for example after a reply fails because no fallback model is set up, it can only name the Settings page. The person lands at the top of the page and has to hunt for the row. Many rows, including browser-only preferences and rows that plugins draw, had no stable name a link could use, so nothing could point at them reliably.

## User Impact

- A link such as `/settings/infrastructure#gateway.publicOrigin` opens the page, unfolds the group that hides the row, scrolls it to the middle of the screen and marks it with an accent edge bar and a short wash. Focus moves to the row, never into its control, and nothing is changed. The bar stays until the person clicks or types; with reduced motion the page jumps and the mark stays still.
- Every row on every Settings page now has one stable setting ID: config rows use their config path (`gateway.publicOrigin`, `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks`), one agent's rows use `agent.<path>`, browser-only preferences use `local.<key>`, native app settings `device.<key>`, profile rows `profile.<field>`, and other rows `<page>.<name>`. Rows that repeat per item use one pattern plus the item, such as `providers.openai`.
- Plugin Settings views declare the IDs they draw in `controlUi.settingsViews[].settings` (`plugin.<id>.*`, `channels.<owned channel>.*` or `plugins.entries.<id>.*`). The host refuses a row ID the view did not declare. A channel detail opens from `/settings/channels?channel=<id>`, so `/settings/channels?channel=whatsapp#plugin.whatsapp.linkedPhone` lands on the WhatsApp plugin's linked phone. Plugins published before this change keep loading; their views simply have no linkable rows until they declare IDs.
- The Channels page row that opens a channel is now `channelsPage.channel.<id>`; `channels.<id>` stays the channel's config path.

## Why This Change Was Made

One list owns the IDs: `src/shared/control-ui-settings/` maps each hand-built page to the settings it shows, with the disclosure that hides a row and the config section that holds it. Generic config rows need no entry; their config path is their ID. One arrival owner in the Settings shell resolves the link (including renamed IDs and the nearest enclosing setting), waits for rows that render after Gateway reads, and keeps the mark on a row the page redraws.

The arrival and the setting list load with Settings, and the mark is drawn inline on the row, so the chat and new-session boot bundles and the shared stylesheets stay at their current size.

`pnpm check:control-ui-setting-ids` keeps it deterministic in lint, `check:changed` and CI: every row on a Settings page must carry a listed ID or be marked as a status/action row, every listed ID must be drawn exactly once, bundled plugins may draw only the IDs their manifests declare, and `config/control-ui-setting-ids.txt` keeps published IDs: removing one needs an alias so old links still land.

Two nearby fixes came out of checking every row: a config setting with several object shapes (such as `channels.twitch` or a secret provider) was drawn in both the common and advanced groups of the Advanced page; it is now drawn once. Rows in a channel detail sit flush with the dialog edge, so their mark reaches past the text there.

Accepted edge cases: a row the page redraws within 10 seconds of arrival gets the mark again, unless the person has clicked or typed. Rows that only exist with live data (native app, push notifications, cloud workers) are checked statically, not opened in the browser suite.

## Evidence

- Captured with the real Control UI against a mocked Gateway in Chromium at 1280×800, dark theme. Before: `main` at 3f4e2bd3a4c6e. After: the pre-rebase implementation with the channel-detail spacing change (368b856b26386).
- All **10 Chromium Settings deep-link tests** passed on the final integrated source against the mocked Gateway. Coverage includes generated and hand-built pages, model and plugin rows, the theme importer, MCP server switches, per-agent tool access and command allowlists, and provider account priority.
- `pnpm ui:check-performance` against a local build of c635b051de14e: chat boot JS 1336655 → 1336663 B gzip with the same 21 requests, new boot JS 820731 → 820739 B, total CSS unchanged (346225 B gzip, 1783458 B raw).
- `pnpm check:control-ui-setting-ids` OK; `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck all, SAFETY, SQLite, plugin boundaries, Plugin SDK surface and the other gates pass. Lint fails only on `max-lines` in `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-session.ts`, `src/gateway/server-startup-finish.ts`, `src/wizard/setup.ts` and `extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-node-enrollment.test.ts`, and the dead-export scan only on `src/state/state-upgrade-tree.ts: skipEntry`; this PR does not touch those files and they fail the same way on `main`.
- Unit and node suites for touched owners pass (UI lib, components, config and search pages: 9901 passed; `memory-page.browser.test.ts` "keeps the header and every tab panel on one column" also fails on `main`, and `talk-device-navigation.test.tsx` timed out only in the full parallel run and passes alone).
- Test-line check passed against 6c1efeaf6b3ec: +1,049 net lines, 400 allowed and 649 allocated for the ID checker, browser flows (including delayed custom editors), arrival lifecycle and plugin manifest checks.
- Final local autoreview compared 6c1efeaf6b3ec to edd447bc9b9ad (the published tree at f0dd6da311552). No actionable P0 or P1 findings. This was static review; browser and typecheck results are separate.

### Generated config page: `/settings/infrastructure#gateway.publicOrigin`

Before (`main` 3f4e2bd3a4c6e): the page opens at the top. After: the row is centered, marked and focused.

prs.title: perf(config): retain one snapshot for unchanged validation results
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a cache miss, plugin and channel settings validation retained two private copies of the same configuration whenever validation returned its input unchanged. These copies could stay live across config revisions, for up to 512 entries per registry.

## User Impact

Configurations with many plugin or channel settings can use less memory between validations. Operators can keep their existing configuration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cache already owns a snapshot taken before validation. A successful result that returns that exact input can reuse the snapshot. A cache hit still gives its caller a fresh copy. Defaulted values and validation errors keep their independent snapshots.

## Evidence

- A native Node.js 26.7 ARM64 comparison used the original and changed cache owners with the same validator and TypeBox 1.4.3. With 64 and 128 synthetic nested plugin and channel settings, reachable objects under cached inputs and result values fell from 1,024 to 512 and from 2,048 to 1,024. In two measurements per revision, average retained heap per populated cache fell from 203–206 kB to 131–132 kB at 64 entries and from 407 kB to 261 kB at 128.
- The bundled OpenAI plugin's empty settings exercised a schema with defaults. Both versions retained two objects under input and result, with the same 455-byte V8 serialization of the complete cache entry array.
- Original and changed implementations preserved the miss result identity, isolated edits to input and returned hits, retained hydrated defaults, and isolated returned error details. The committed regression checks that an unchanged success stores a single private input graph. Device performance was not measured.

prs.title: fix(test): preserve stack coordinates in redacted failure reports
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150983

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing line and column coordinates in Vitest failure reports when a source filename resembles a credential key, such as a filename containing `.session`.

## User Impact

Developers retain actionable source locations in console, JSON, and JUnit failure reports. Real credential values continue through the existing redaction rules. Application and update behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared assignment matcher was treating the colon after a credential-shaped filename as the start of a secret value. The fix recognizes only terminal numeric coordinates on JS/TS source filenames in V8/Vitest stack frames. Quoted values, consumed credential spans, outer credential fields, and other assignments in the same diagnostic retain their existing precedence. Unknown stack formats remain conservatively redacted.

The existing real-child regressions now use a credential-shaped filename and require matching source-derived locations across all three report formats, after checking secret absence and the original failure exit status. No reporter wiring, dependency, configuration, environment-variable, or schema changes.

Test-tooling LOC: +21/-1 (net +20) for the bounded source-location classifier. Regression tests: +127/-9. Application runtime LOC is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Current revision

- Signed merge revision `03705c843ce292377c8bd1dc35ef9d8ee3270199` reconciles the original fix with main `66b2e244acf2666690741d0e04140087b4570100`. Only the same three files differ from that main revision. Normal commit hooks and signature verification passed.
- The repair preserves the newer credential-field matching, registered-secret scrubbing, GitHub annotations and summary checks. All six existing real-child cases now also require matching source-derived coordinates in console, JSON, and JUnit output; their secret-absence and failure-exit assertions remain in place.
- Node 24.22.1 reproduced the coordinate loss in the frozen main source. The repaired source passed 59 direct assertions covering supported frames, malformed and quoted controls, adjacent and nested credentials, outer fields, and registered-secret precedence. These source assertions are not a Vitest or real-child test run.
- Committed-range autoreview covered base `66b2e244acf2666690741d0e04140087b4570100` through head `03705c843ce292377c8bd1dc35ef9d8ee3270199`: Codex, P0–P2, `scoped-clean`, zero findings. It reviewed the complete three-file diff with nine intact source contexts and verified the final source snapshot. Independent source review also found no blocker. This is code review, not a test result.
- [Current-head CI 45955317039](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45955317039) completed successfully, including the required [openclaw/ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45955317039/job/140363613249). The ordinary PR merge checkout `002d71577` contains byte-identical versions of all three repaired files from head `03705c843ce292377c8bd1dc35ef9d8ee3270199`.
- [Policy tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45955317039/job/140360890908): all 48 tests in `test/vitest-credential-redaction.test.ts` passed. [Reporter tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45955317039/job/140360890899): all seven passed, including the six real-child variants and the existing fork-checkpoint test. The six child cases verify the failure exit, secret absence, and matching source-derived coordinates across console, JSON, and JUnit.
- [Targeted format and lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45955317039/job/140361538935) passed for the exact three changed files, including oxfmt/Bun parity and root-test lint with zero warnings or errors. The owning [root-test type graph](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45955317039/job/140361538977), `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.other.json`, emitted a native compiler receipt with exit code 0.
- Local execution is code-only because the designated dependency installation is unqualified. The supported remote source-capsule launcher also stopped before allocation: its installed host-side `@openclaw/fs-safe` is 0.27.1 while this revision requires 0.28.2. prs.title: fix: preserve emphasis in Markdown table row labels
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw converts a Markdown table to bullets, it makes the first column of each row bold. A label written as `pre**fix**` could display as `prefix****` with only `pre` bold. A mix of adjacent italic and bold text could also expose asterisks.

## User Impact

The entire label reads **prefix**. In `x*old***a**_b_`, all of `xoldab` is bold, with italics on `old` and `b`. The following line keeps its own formatting. Teams preserves CJK italics on either side of the repaired span, and Matrix keeps the authored destination of a bare URL such as `https://example.com/a_b`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bullet formatter keeps the authored spelling whenever adding bold preserves its text and formatting. For labels that need repair, the shared Markdown renderer carries italics and strikethrough across the affected text. Code delimiters, reference keys, link destinations, and escaped punctuation keep their authored syntax. For labels with multiple inline constructs, the formatter copies unaffected source slices and repairs the strong delimiters within the affected slice. It uses the shared CJK emphasis rules to locate those boundaries. When the constructs touch, the formatter compares the rendered text, link destinations and ranges, and coverage of each non-bold style. If formatting changes their meaning, it can remove just the redundant strong delimiters from the authored source and check an alternate bold wrapper. This builds on the earlier table-cell source preservation work. [Earlier table-cell repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/139892)

## Evidence

- Replayed the original failing case and its minimized example. The property passed 10,000 distinct cases at seed `46113`.
- Compared the shared formatter and single serialized messages from the normal Discord sender against the authored text and per-character styles. All 2,791 comparisons passed, including 1,350 adjacent-format cases and 504 strike cases. Every previously correct spelling in these samples was retained.
- Verified the whole strike across two italic words and the space around a bold word, and a struck reference link next to italics. Checked code, literal punctuation, the following row value, and single-column, off, and code table modes.
- The first hosted plugin-SDK declaration build flagged a possibly undefined indexed run. The comparison now checks that the run exists before reading its styles. All 2,791 comparisons and 10,000 generated cases passed again after that change.
- Hosted plugin-SDK declarations passed after the undefined guard. Core lint then flagged the unbraced return that keeps an already-correct label. The follow-up adds the two braces. Targeted native lint and formatting passed, as did all 2,791 comparisons and 10,000 generated cases on that change.
- Earlier revisions passed hosted core lint, plugin-SDK declarations, and the table suite. On this update, all 2,791 shared and serialized Discord comparisons and all 10,000 property cases passed. The Discord sender preserved literal Japanese stars, full-label bold, adjacent italics, and contiguous strikethrough split across two authored spans.
- Captured the normal Teams activity and Matrix event for adjacent constructs. For `pre**fix**前*斜体：*后`, Teams kept the full label bold and `斜体：` italic. For `pre**fix**(https://example.com/a_b)`, Matrix kept the exact URL in both the link text and destination. Independent review passed all 40 original and 36 combined Teams/Matrix controls.
- On the November 25 head, core lint identified a mutating sort in the style-span comparison. [The one-line correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/cf6e02df90e8f670d8e3e94618ec07e0e8afa5e0) uses `toSorted`. All 4,096 deterministic baseline/candidate projections matched and retained their input spans. The repository format check, source syntax check and normal commit hook passed. All 26 registered table tests and the previously failing core lint job passed on this revision. The sender checks above used synthetic transports.

### Multiword label compatibility

On [f95af114](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f95af114b7a1513763c757008204f5e282e48a2b), the formatter checks the full label after reconstructing its parts. Adding a trailing word to the two adjacent-markup examples reproduced the [review findings](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205349#issuecomment-7163669299) on the previous revision. Its table suite passed 26 cases and failed exactly the two added regressions. The corrected source passed all 28 cases in Vitest 5.0.5. The Teams formatter kept the CJK text italic. Matrix emitted the authored `https://example.com/a_b` destination with no added backslash. Both single-word controls stayed byte-identical and the following price row remained intact. These results exercise the real formatter and serialization code with synthetic input. Current-head hosted qualification is pending.

prs.title: fix(subagents): finish claimed stops after session rotation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A subagent Stop could return "session changed; retry" after its durable kill claim committed. Reset or rotation could abandon the original cancellation.

## User Impact

Stop finishes the claimed original run across session reset, rotation, or removal. It cancels captured work and leaves successor runs and replacement-session metadata untouched. A target revoked before claiming is superseded; new descendant batches are admitted against their retained parent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the durable claim for in-flight identity, capture cancellation owners before yielding, and preserve exact metadata writes and publication ordering. Native receipts use the existing registry-owner matcher. Terminal settlement releases only session leases acquired by that settlement.

Remove the unreachable ended-run guard and unused admission-drain test observer. No schema, configuration, or public SDK contract changes.

### Mechanical caller updates

- Kill acceptance/scope/runtime/admin callers drop retired incarnation-check flags and callbacks.
- `subagent-registry-run-manager.ts` carries the original kill claim into termination and tracks acquired leases separately from the borrowed session (coordinator-approved supporting change).
- Spawn authority and gateway abort tests use native admission/settlement barriers; `session-lifecycle-admission.test-support.ts` drops the obsolete observer (coordinator-approved test files).
- `subagent-control.retirement.test.ts` lets an already-selected child finish after parent-session replacement and compares the replacement entry exactly. The gateway test documents its receiver-preserving method interception.
- `subagent-control.accounting.test.ts` counts the healthy sibling's completed kill separately from the held child's pending cleanup.
- `config/session-identity-allowlist.txt` shrinks the settlement allowance from 2 to 1 through the native prune command. No allowance increases.

The terminal-completion handoff is coordinated with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206454, which preserves the claim and acquired-session ownership changes.

Related work with file overlap: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194275, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189391, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188492.

## Evidence

Base: `2ab7b31a13d95bbbb62596679b130445c4c9d3d1`.
Head: `f8dfab0c92cb153794aa1088baafd57aa1bb87f9`.

- Red on base: the registered subagents tool's post-claim session-generation regression returns `killed: false`; the caller-retirement sibling passes. [Base probe](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45936219871).
- Final-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45955926415) is running. It supplies broad proof under coordinator rule 06 after the diagnostic Testbox queued and was stopped. The completed preceding run passed build, types, the identity ratchet, accounting, and all other planned test jobs, except the retired parent-session expectation and the test-spy receiver lint diagnostic. This head corrects those two test-only issues; production code is unchanged.
- Exact final-head dependency-free session-identity ratchet passes. The prune diff changes only the settlement allowance, 2 to 1. `git diff --check` passes.
- Prior-head focused Testbox proof: 98 registry tests, core/all-src test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and docs discovery passed at `c3027fa6`. Five gateway cases and all four spawn-authority cases passed at `918f8bb7`; the remaining gateway assertion was updated to require accepted terminal reconciliation after ancestor-owner closure. Final-head execution is pending CI.
- `pnpm deadcode:exports` found no kill-file exports and reported three failures reproduced on verified main-baseline source: `readUpdateDatabaseEngineConfig`, `DoctorContributionPending`, and `formatUpdateSnapshotCapacity`. prs.title: fix: apply voice and voiceId overrides for OpenAI and Google TTS
prs.body:
Closes #206106

## What Problem This Solves

Passing `voiceId` through the message tool or using the documented `voice` / `voiceId` TTS directive aliases is silently ignored when the active speech provider is OpenAI or Google. Users requesting a specific voice (such as `voiceId=nova` on OpenAI or `voice=Aoede` / `voiceId=Aoede` on Google) hear the default configured voice instead with no error.

## User Impact

Per-message `voiceId` overrides from the message tool and documented `voice` / `voiceId` (`voice_id`) TTS directive aliases now select the requested voice for OpenAI and Google TTS instead of being silently ignored. Invalid OpenAI voice names continue to emit the existing validation warning. No configuration changes or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The message tool encodes `voiceId` as the normalized directive key `voiceid`, and `docs/tools/tts/commands.md` documents `voice` and `voiceId` as supported aliases. Extending OpenAI's voice directive parser to accept `voiceid` / `voice_id` and Google's `voiceName` directive parser to accept `voice` / `voiceid` / `voice_id` aligns both providers with the documented contract without changing generic directive routing or affecting other providers.

## Evidence

### Baseline (`main`) vs Head (`b5f17c783`) end-to-end directive + synthesis proof
Ran `parseTtsDirectives` → `buildOpenAISpeechProvider().synthesize()` against a local loopback HTTP server (capturing the outbound `/v1/audio/speech` JSON payload with default voice `"coral"`) and `parseTtsDirectives` for Google (`voice=Aoede` and `voiceId=Aoede`):

**Baseline (`main` — bug reproduced):**
```text
OPENAI_WARNINGS: ["unsupported openai directive key \"voiceid\""]
OPENAI_REQUEST_BODY: {"model":"gpt-4o-mini-tts","input":" Hello OpenAI","voice":"coral","response_format":"mp3"}
GOOGLE_TAG: [[tts:provider=google voice=Aoede]] Hello Google 1
GOOGLE_WARNINGS: ["unsupported google directive key \"voice\""]
GOOGLE_OVERRIDES: {}
GOOGLE_TAG: [[tts:provider=google voiceId=Aoede]] Hello Google 2
GOOGLE_WARNINGS: ["unsupported google directive key \"voiceid\""]
GOOGLE_OVERRIDES: {}
```

**Head (`fix/tts-voiceid-aliases-openai-google` @ `b5f17c783` — fixed):**
```text
OPENAI_WARNINGS: []
OPENAI_REQUEST_BODY: {"model":"gpt-4o-mini-tts","input":" Hello OpenAI","voice":"nova","response_format":"mp3"}
OPENAI_AUDIO_BYTES: 14
GOOGLE_TAG: [[tts:provider=google voice=Aoede]] Hello Google 1
GOOGLE_WARNINGS: []
GOOGLE_OVERRIDES: {"voiceName":"Aoede"}
GOOGLE_TAG: [[tts:provider=google voiceId=Aoede]] Hello Google 2
GOOGLE_WARNINGS: []
GOOGLE_OVERRIDES: {"voiceName":"Aoede"}
```

### Automated tests & checks
- Added regression tests in `extensions/openai/speech-provider.test.ts` (`voiceid`, `voice_id` → `{ voice: "nova" }`) and `extensions/google/speech-provider.test.ts` (`voice`, `voiceid`, `voice_id` → `{ voiceName: "Aoede" }` and verified synthesized `prebuiltVoiceConfig.voiceName: "Aoede"` request body).
- `pnpm test extensions/openai/speech-provider.test.ts src/tts/directives.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: all passed.
- `pnpm test extensions/google/speech-provider.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 28/28 tests passed.
- `pnpm exec oxlint` and `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on all 4 modified files: 0 warnings, 0 errors, formatting clean.

### Remaining gap
- Booting a full live Gateway on this Windows host is blocked by Node 24.13.0's SQLite 3.50.4 WAL-safety guard (requires Node 24.22.1+); Google's production `synthesize` request body with `prebuiltVoiceConfig.voiceName: "Aoede"` is verified in `extensions/google/speech-provider.test.ts` and OpenAI's real HTTP `/v1/audio/speech` synthesis request is verified above.

prs.title: fix(ios): chat text follows the system body size, with one app red and shared colors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iOS, chat text is drawn at a shrunken size: message text is 13.5 points at the default text size, smaller than the system body text people set their phone up for. The app also uses several slightly different reds and gray backgrounds that don't match the Control UI, so the same chat looks different on the phone and on the web.

## User Impact

This is one of a series of pull requests that bring the iOS app's chat in line with the Control UI. With this change alone, a person sees:

- Message text in the chat is larger and easier to read: 15 points at the default text size instead of 13.5. It still follows the system or per-app Dynamic Type setting in both directions, including accessibility sizes. Headings, lists, tables, code blocks and math scale with it.
- The composer's draft uses the system body size (17 points at the default setting).
- Timestamps, captions and other secondary chat text never render under 11 points, even at the smallest setting.
- One app red (`#CD3535`) in light and dark mode, shared with the share extension, instead of several reds.
- Warm neutral backgrounds, surfaces and borders that match the Control UI, in the chat and on the app's own panels. Dark mode moves from near-black to a dark warm gray.
- The sidebar button in the chat header draws a two-line menu glyph in the primary text color instead of a red sidebar symbol.
- Settings-style toggle indicators match the size of a system switch and use the app's green when on.

Nothing changes in how chats work. Later pull requests in the series build on these sizes and colors, and on a shared sheet close button that this change adds but doesn't place on any screen yet.

## Why This Change Was Made

Chat text moves from a fixed shrink ratio to the system text styles, the way Messages does, so Dynamic Type works the way people expect. The transcript reads at one shared size, while the composer and sheets keep the system body size. The colors move into one place (`OpenClawIOSBrand` for the native tokens, `OpenClawBrand` and the chat theme for the roles), so the app, the share extension and the chat UI can't drift apart again. The older color names stay as aliases of the new roles so existing screens keep compiling unchanged.

## Evidence

- Unit tests on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2): `OpenClawTypographyTests` (including the new rendered-size and composer-size checks at every Dynamic Type setting), `OpenClawBrandTests` and `ChatTranscriptTypographyTests`. 19 passed, 0 failed.
- The iOS app builds with its SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint build phases. `scripts/lint-swift.sh ios` and `scripts/format-swift.sh ios` report no violations.
- `native:i18n:verify` reports `changed=false`. The one new catalog entry is the sheet close button's "Close" label.
- Screenshots: the same fixture chat in screenshot mode on the same simulator, before (current `main`) and after, in light and dark, at the default text size and at the third accessibility size (AX3).
- Not checked: the macOS app and the OpenClawKit SwiftPM tests on macOS, the UI test suite, and a physical device.

prs.title: perf(cli): stop respawning the CLI to hide a warning Node no longer emits
prs.body:
## Problem

Every POSIX CLI call (including the one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turn that benchmark boards run) started Node twice. `buildCliRespawnPlan` re-executed the CLI only to add `--disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning`, a flag added for the `node:sqlite` experimental warning (165841ae7969, 2026-01-13). `node:sqlite` stopped emitting that warning in Node 24.15.0 (`lib/sqlite.js` has `emitExperimentalWarning` in v24.14.0 and none in v24.15.0, v24.16.0, v26.1.0), and `engines` requires Node `>=24.16.0 <25 || >=26.1.0`. The second Node boot is pure waste.

## Change

- Delete the warning-only respawn branch from `src/entry.respawn.ts` and its skip policy `shouldSkipRespawnForArgv` from `src/cli/respawn-policy.ts`.
- Respawn stays for the two cases that need a fresh process: auto-discovered `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` (Linux version-manager Node) and the Windows stack size.
- Tests: the respawn tests now assert that common commands run in process unless Node must reload its trust store. Tests that used the warning respawn as a vehicle now use a CA respawn, or run on Windows only (`node-runtime-recovery` startup-respawn cases: POSIX no longer respawns there).

## Evidence

Acceptance rule (written before the run): cold `openclaw agent --local` one-shot turn, built `dist`, fresh scratch state per run, real OpenAI `gpt-5.4-nano`; metric = process start to `provider.request.started` (diagnostics timeline) and the CLI entry stage; ABAB with the base build, 8 samples each, same load band. Win = one fewer Node process per CLI call and a lower entry stage, no metric worse.

| metric (ABAB n=8, load 15-21) | base b0a6e8cd | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Node processes per CLI call | 2 | 1 |
| node boot + entry wrapper, median | 311 ms | 154 ms |
| node boot + entry wrapper, p90 | 352 ms | 174 ms |
| start -> first provider request, median | 8769 ms | 7440 ms |
| start -> first provider request, p90 | 9777 ms | 9640 ms |

The total is noisy at this load (shared host); the entry stage drop (-157 ms median) is the attributable part.

- No warning: an `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1` `agent --local` turn on Node 24.22.1 printed no `ExperimentalWarning`. `node -e "require('module').registerHooks(...); require('node:sqlite')"` prints nothing.
- Code Mode's worker passes its own `execArgv` with `--experimental-vm-modules`; explicit worker `execArgv` replaces the parent flags, so its warning was never suppressed by this respawn (checked with a minimal worker on and off the flag).
- Tests: `ocx test src/entry.respawn.test.ts src/cli/cli-utils.test.ts src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-node.test.ts src/process/respawn-child-runner.test.ts src/cli/gateway-backed-exit.process.test.ts test/scripts/node-runtime-recovery.built-cli.e2e.test.ts` and importers (`github-exec-launch`, `run-main.cleanup`, `entry.respawn-diagnostics`) pass locally.

## Diff

Production: -58 lines, +3. Tests: net -76 lines.

### Pending baseline integration

Resolution inputs are prepared but not applied: preserve bounded packet admission and cancellation, preserve incoming automation rendering, remove duplicate thread types and the obsolete older-page helper, and carry the fixture's source sequence into its extracted owner.

The combined protocol validator was regenerated and its generation check passed on an isolated Testbox. This is generation proof only. The native refreshed candidate still needs focused cancellation/capacity/visibility tests, incoming UI coverage, types/lint/build, independent review, and exact-head CI/assets.

### Evidence for prior candidate N

[The previous integrated CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44570690892) tested merge `1f38271e94c1df6ebb264ac4f3d179796529b646`, whose parents are baseline `a38c7df01e968814be530663f931432e580e3be5` and candidate `97fb87fc939f8773a96f9bc9e6008611959d93e9`. It completed with 77 successful, 9 failed and 21 skipped jobs. Eight failures were substantive; the ninth was the aggregate gate. Build and all three UI unit shards passed.

- The two correction-owned type/lint failures are covered by the scoped O proof above.
- Node preparation and Cron fixture failures were reproduced or traced on that exact baseline. Captured main now contains [the preparation fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202068), [automatic-name fixture fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201942), and [Cron ownership fixture fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201962). Their presence is source evidence; refreshed runtime results remain pending.
- The provider-removal case passed in the earlier baseline reproduction, so the cause of N's CI failure remains unknown. Captured main contains [a post-reload polling fixture change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202009); that does not retrospectively prove N's cause.
- N exceeded the accepted Chat asset cap. Prior same-toolchain measurements follow; they do not measure O or the future refreshed candidate.

| Normalized gzip | Baseline a38c7df | Prior candidate N |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS | 90,540 B | 90,407 B |
| Chat boot JS | 1,332,622 B | 1,340,658 B |
| New Session boot JS | 820,950 B | 804,794 B |

The accepted Chat cap remains **1,339,362 B**. No cap increase is included. N exceeded it by 1,296 B. The earlier 1,341,357 B proposal remains unapproved and must be remeasured against the refreshed source. Existing CSS/request violations appeared on both sides of the prior comparison.

C1 stays open until refreshed integrated proof and the asset decision are resolved. No merge or deployment has been performed.

## What Problem This Solves

Long chat sessions retain more transcript bodies as readers page. This change bounds reloadable resident history, releases evicted bodies from presentation caches, and keeps older/newer navigation reversible.

## User Impact

Ordinary residency targets **400 entries / 3,145,728 serialized JSON code units / eight source segments**. Source atomicity, the current reader packet and live/pending/error custody have explicit exceptions; one bounded staged packet is separately charged. These are retained-body targets, not a whole-pane RAM ceiling.

Readers can move older/newer, return to Latest and restore semantic bookmarks. Search states its loaded-window scope; export loads complete history separately. Capacity/unavailable outcomes are visible. A local command after an authoritative empty-history read stays before the first later turn, including after resident-prefix retirement and older-page admission. Unloaded or unknown history never implies the beginning. Command replies retain transient custody and retire rather than entering persistent raw history.

**Tradeoff: bounded residency makes a full 900→1→900 traversal perform more pagination and rendering work. Historical matched comparisons remain rejected, with substantial wall-time and renderer-CPU regressions disclosed below. The owner accepts that product tradeoff after investigation; this is no numerical benchmark pass or speedup claim.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical source/packet/cursor ownership controls trimming, reopening, continuity and retirement. SQLite and actor-memory reads certify same-snapshot Stop continuation; UI admission revalidates a fresh selected packet. Numeric adaptive budgets cross awaits, prepared bodies do not. One synchronous owner performs final prefix fit and accepted-prefix receipt adoption. Visible fitting reads commit without an unnecessary fallback/staged read, while sparse/raw progress, smaller-envelope retries and cancellation retain their existing contracts.

Accepted raw source facts and one canonical publication owner govern local-output placement; empty views, stale reads, pending inputs and unavailable outbox storage do not confer authority. Local occurrence placement preserves consecutive command order without inventing durable sequence zero. Edge-only history traversal advances navigation while preserving the original held packet bodies, certificate and opaque endpoints; actual cuts or body changes still revoke that custody.

One native offset producer supplies paging/follow facts before callback-induced rendering, preserving input/link ownership and anchor ordering. Its accepted reader-policy baseline is independent of geometric synchronization: measuring the current position before scroll capture cannot consume upward paging intent. Presentation-owned partial retirement releases dormant bodies while preserving safe survivor seeds. One shared weak derivation owner preserves exact digest bytes for fresh immutable stream/snapshot envelopes and per-source reactions. Reply-preview revisions follow final lookup facts; releasing nonempty quote bodies still invalidates their previews.

Integration is fixed at **b59c593cb0b7ad88ba2118768840c010e3253d95**, through signed native successors of earlier 650/21cd/ed40/99 integrations. The latest join preserves 13 reviewed manual resolutions and 20 clean overlapping postimages; this is source-composition evidence, not a current runtime pass. Navigation-only admission lives in the existing lazy packet runtime; ordinary hydration preparation stays eager, and successful navigation commits synchronously through the already-resolved module. The cold owner now preserves incoming boot boundary probing followed by at most one default 80-entry / 256 KiB fill. Canonical input display places queued steerNow input in pending presentation once, preserving hidden-input omission and persisted-steer deduplication. prs.title: fix: keep automation commands approved after upgrades
prs.body:
Closes #206440

## What Problem This Solves

Automations that were approved with Always allow on an older release can ask for approval again after an upgrade, even when the job and command have not changed. Runtime-generated temporary-directory variables were changing the stored operation binding.

## User Impact

Existing pre-scratch grants keep authorizing the same operation after upgrading. Child processes still use workspace-owned scratch, and caller/plugin environment overrides still participate in approval matching. Command changes, revocation, expiry, and host policy remain enforced. No settings change or grant migration is required.

Grants minted with the buggy scratch-dependent binding are not rewritten; they may require one new approval.

## Why This Change Was Made

I separated runtime execution overrides from the requested environment at their existing preparation owner. This fixes both grant creation and lookup without ignoring temp-variable names, weakening exact matching, or adding a compatibility lookup.

I ran the pr-simplify pass: no new owner, migration, cache, or fallback. The production delta is +3 lines and the regression-test delta is +49 lines against main.

## Evidence

- I reproduced the bug with a published 2026.9.37 Gateway and a live OpenAI-backed automation: one initial approval, then a prompt-free reuse; unchanged main at `277b251bfa80c863e4408607bce9b372eddc24c9` prompted again with `TEMP`, `TMP`, and `TMPDIR`. I declined that extra request and the command did not run.
- I built and integrity-checked the self-contained package from tested commit `2e35ebce3dc5a2c0c8133838816e6ca6c50b8516`. prs.title: chore(ios): bundle the Control UI's chat icons and provider marks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The iOS app's chat draws its link, file, tool, provider and pull request icons with SF Symbols and a handful of bundled marks, so the same chat looks different on iPhone than in the Control UI. The app has no copy of the icons the Control UI uses, so it cannot match them.

This is the first PR in a series that brings the iOS chat in line with the Control UI. It only adds the shared images and the view that draws them. Later PRs in the series switch the chat over to them.

## User Impact

Nothing in the chat changes yet, because no screen uses the new images until later PRs in the series. The only visible change is in Settings › Licenses, which now lists three more entries: "GitHub Octicons", "Lucide" and "Octicons". "GitHub Octicons" and "Octicons" open the same MIT License text.

The new images make the app bundle somewhat larger. Nothing needs to be migrated, and there is nothing for users to do.

## Why This Change Was Made

The icons ship as vector template images in asset catalogs, so they scale with Dynamic Type and take their color from the surrounding text, as SF Symbols do:

- **Chat icons** (90 image sets): the Control UI's Lucide icons for tools, attachments, links and inline chips, plus a GitHub mark. They live in a new `ChatIcons.xcassets` in the shared `OpenClawChatUI` module, registered in `Package.swift`, so the chat view code can use them.
- **Provider marks** (83 image sets): the same provider logos the Control UI shows, in the app's asset catalog. Their source is already credited in the bundled "CodexBar Provider Icons" license.
- **Pull request state icons** (4 image sets): the GitHub Octicons for open, draft, merged and closed.
- **`ChatVectorGlyph`**: the single SwiftUI view that draws one of these icons. It scales with a text style and sits on the text baseline. Using one view keeps sizing and alignment the same everywhere the series uses an icon.

The Lucide (ISC) and GitHub Octicons (MIT) license texts are bundled with the app, and the license test checks for them.

## Evidence

- Built the iOS app for the iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2) on top of current main. SwiftFormat lint reported 0 of 565 files needing changes, and strict SwiftLint found 0 violations in 565 files.
- `LicenseDocumentLoaderTests`: 3 of 3 passed, including the check that the GitHub Octicons and Lucide licenses are bundled.
- `swift build --target OpenClawChatUI` on macOS succeeded, and SwiftPM compiled the new asset catalog into the module's resource bundle (`Assets.car`), so the package builds outside Xcode too.
- Nothing in the app draws the new images yet. I did not check them visually here; the later PRs that use them carry their own screenshots.

Screenshots: Settings › Licenses on the iPhone 17 Pro simulator, light appearance, with the app's screenshot fixture (no Gateway or account data). Before is current main and After is this branch. The rows "GitHub Octicons", "Lucide" and "Octicons" are new.

prs.title: fix(sessions): keep independent sessions' reports visible
prs.body:
Fixes #202292

## What Problem This Solves

When an agent starts an independent session with `sessions_create`, reports that session sends back can disappear from the receiving chat. The receiving agent's reply disappears too, because the independent session is mistaken for a supervised subagent.

## User Impact

Reports from newly created independent sessions and the replies they trigger remain visible in chat history. Supervised subagent coordination stays private.

This applies to sessions created after the fix. Existing sessions without the new creation marker retain their current classification; their recorded lineage cannot reliably distinguish independent sessions from supervised children.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record independent creation in trusted, write-once session metadata and carry it through the existing runtime-identity and persistence paths. The shared coordination classifier reads that fact instead of treating every session with spawn lineage as a subagent. Spawn-depth admission and inherited isolation remain unchanged.

The simplification pass retained one classification owner and existing creation metadata, with no new delivery pipeline or migration. Against current `main`: production +25/−2 lines, tests +196/−1, documentation +5/−1.

<details>
<summary>Changed-file walkthrough</summary>

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-depth-policy.ts` | Exclude explicitly independent sessions from coordination classification |
| `src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-visible.ts` | Stamp trusted independent creation |
| `src/agents/tools/in-process-gateway.ts` | Carry marker through runtime identity |
| `src/gateway/agent-runtime-session-spawn-context.ts` | Type trusted creation marker |
| `src/gateway/agent-runtime-identity-token.ts` | Sign and validate the marker |
| `src/gateway/session-creation-provenance.ts` | Restore trusted marker at creation |
| `src/gateway/session-create-service.types.ts` | Carry marker in creation contract |
| `src/config/sessions/session-entry-provenance.ts` | Build and preserve creation stamp |
| `src/config/sessions/types.ts` | Preserve write-once marker across merges |
| `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-entry-cache.types.ts` | Retain marker in cached entry facts |
| `src/plugins/session-entry-slot-keys.ts` | Include marker in session metadata slots |
| `src/gateway/gateway.independent-session-reports.e2e.test.ts` | Exercise reports, replies, reset, and supervised privacy |
| `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-depth-policy.test.ts` | Cover classification and immutable creation intent |
| `src/agents/tools/sessions-create-tool.test.ts` | Assert independent creation stamp |
| `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-session-row.test.ts` | Verify persisted marker preservation |
| `src/gateway/agent-runtime-identity-token.test.ts` | Verify signed marker transport |
| `docs/concepts/session-tool.md` | Document visibility and existing-session limitation |

</details>

## Evidence

- **Interaction with #206058 (merged as `2f665749`).** #206058 uses `isSubagentSessionFromEntry` on the recipient side: a `sessions_send` turn into a spawned child still requires a result, so `NO_REPLY` fails. This PR makes that classifier return `false` for `createdIndependently` sessions. I traced both effects in the code and tested them on this head:
  - **(a) Creator's `sessions_send` to its independent session.** In `resolveCommandReplyExpectation` (`src/agents/reply-completion.ts`), the turn now counts as a peer send. It skips the internal-channel `result-required` branch and reaches the ordinary inter-session silent-reply policy. An exact `NO_REPLY` is accepted, no retry or fallback runs, and the waiting creator gets `status: "no_reply"`. On the sender side, this PR already classifies the target as a peer (`replyMode: "peer"`), so both sides agree. Before this PR, the session's `spawnDepth: 1` made it a child, so `NO_REPLY` gave `status: "error"`. That was the regression, not intended behavior (see below).
  - **(b) The `sessions_create` opening task keeps its result obligation.** The opening runs through `sessions.create` → `dispatchSessionCreateInitialTurn` with `inter_session` provenance whose `sourceTool` is `sessions_spawn` (or `sessions_create` for an agent-created session). The peer-send exemption applies only when `sourceTool` is `sessions_send`. So the opening still takes the internal-channel branch and stays `result-required`, without using the classifier. Nothing regresses, and no product change was needed.
  - **Tests added:** three rows in the shared reply-policy table (`attempt-execution.announce.test-support.ts`). Each row runs on both the embedded runner and the `claude-cli` runtime with a model that answers `NO_REPLY`. An independent session receiving `sessions_send` gets `required`: `NO_REPLY` is accepted as silence on `claude-cli`. Its opening, with source `sessions_spawn` or `sessions_create`, gets `result-required`: `claude-cli` rejects it as an empty response. If the `createdIndependently` check is removed from the classifier, the `sessions_send` row fails with `result-required`. A new real-Gateway test in `gateway.independent-session-reports.e2e.test.ts` makes real `sessions_create` and `sessions_send` calls; only the model's replies are scripted. When the opening answers `NO_REPLY`, the run refuses it and asks again (2 model calls), then ends `ok`. When the creator's waited `sessions_send` gets `NO_REPLY` back, the target makes 1 model call and the send returns `status: "no_reply"`.
  - **Verdict:** this is the intended behavior. An independent session acts as a peer, and its opening task keeps the result obligation that #206058 describes. There is no open product question.
  - **Run:** fresh Studio `local-container` lease `cbx_f4796d457d3e`, run `run_a43db13f17c51264b5119e178aa0de31`, head `005fcff3608c`, image `node:24.22.1-trixie` (`sha256:f1e03497…`), exit 0, with the lease stopped afterwards. Gateway E2E 2/2. `attempt-execution.cli.test.ts` 87/87, including the new rows. Neighbours 89/89: depth policy, `sessions_create` tool, sessions tools, send a2a and admission, creation provenance. The `agents-other`, `gateway-root` and `agents-tools` test typecheck shards, lint and format all passed.
- **Why this isn't intentional:** #164304 says a `sessions_create` session "is not a supervised child". #192037 moved `sessions_create` onto the visible-spawn path "minus supervision". That path writes `spawnedBy` and `spawnDepth: 1`, which made the entry classifier treat these sessions as subagents. #204167 documents `sessions_create` sessions as unsupervised, with ordinary recipient turns. The `isSubagentSessionFromEntry` classifier (#151019, Sep 17) predates `sessions_create`, so it was never designed with independent sessions in mind.
- **Upgrade from the released 2026.11.10 (latest stable):** I upgraded a real state directory from `openclaw@2026.11.10` to head `aa9a8dd71956` in a Studio lease. Both versions ran through the shipped CLI and Gateway on one state directory. Only the model provider was a loopback mock.
  - **Migrations:** the agent database went 42 → 45 and the state database 40 → 42. Upgrading to `main` gives the same versions, so this PR adds no migration.
  - **Stored data:** every session, its lineage, every `chat.history` message and every transcript row count was unchanged. `integrity_check` reported `ok`.
  - **After the upgrade:** existing sessions kept working. A new `sessions_create` session got the marker, and its report and A's reply were visible. Supervised reports stayed hidden.
  - **Restart:** the marker survived `sessions.reset` and a Gateway restart.
  - **Control:** the same flow upgraded to `main` hid the new session's report.
  - Details: [upgrade proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202343#issuecomment-7210077075).
- **Base and fix tests on current `main` (`5b6cc381e1d0`):** each of the five added or changed test files fails on `main` and passes on this head. That includes the Gateway regression, which fails on `main` with no `createdIndependently` after reset.
- **Rebase:** this branch is rebased onto `9e78ddc05cbc`. #206058 had narrowed `isSubagentSessionFromEntry`'s input type, so `cd2c127e81e4` adds `createdIndependently` to it. `fefeac0f5eca` updates two test objects to match.
- **Real model, real Gateway on the Mac Studio (pre-rebase head `09c8e9e830e0`):** the agent in A called `sessions_create`; the agent in B called `sessions_send` back to A; A replied. `chat.history` contained both the attributed inbound update and A's reply, neither marked `display:false`. B retained `spawnDepth:1` and its `spawnedBy` lineage, plus `createdIndependently:true`.
- **Studio comparison:** the same live-model flow on pinned `origin/main` hid both rows (`sourceRole:"subagent"`, `display:false`); the candidate exposed both. Each final probe passed its expected-behavior assertion.
- **Focused tests (pre-rebase):** 38 passing tests across the five touched test files, including a real-Gateway/scripted-provider regression that also verifies supervised reports remain hidden and independent creation survives reset. Another 65 tests passed across send admission/delivery, ingress lineage, creation provenance, and memory transcript consumers.
- **Checks on `aa9a8dd71956`:** in a Studio lease, the core typecheck and four affected test-typecheck shards passed, and lint and formatting passed for all touched files. `pnpm build` passed in the upgrade lease, and `git diff --check` against `main` passed.
- **Independent Astra review:** complete 17-file diff and relevant callers reviewed; no verified P0–P2 findings. This was static review, separate from the executed checks above.

The Studio proof is Linux-in-container execution on the Mac Studio, not native macOS testing. The live fixture is headless, so no Control UI screenshot or browser-click interaction is claimed. The supervised negative control was verified by the committed Gateway regression, not the final live-model probe.

<details>
<summary>Exact revisions, Studio command, and output</summary>

Candidate: `09c8e9e830e0588eb8ad1131f561a5caca56af49`.
Baseline: `3b63f9ea1f552930f8d20215a1cb89a95a261fd0` (`origin/main` at comparison setup).
Provider: `local-container`; lease: `cbx_9aec7da26651`.
Image: `node:24.22.1-trixie`, runtime digest `sha256:f1e034976f948cf212ef1f659c12e5dd58ac7eab947831813e81a62401ca38be`.
Candidate run: `run_fedc08f61838744988c51bb7a6dbb121`, exit 0, command 325.488s, end-to-end 484.676s.
Baseline run: `run_6e0407e06cad8a7468fa29f412cdfe46`, exit 0, command 260.780s, end-to-end 262.100s. The lease was deleted after collecting evidence; no Crabbox containers remained.

The task-owned harness uses the existing live-Gateway fixture with `gpt-6-astra` through ClawRouter's native OpenAI Responses route. Only its provider configuration and test driver differ; product code remains the pinned revision. Credentials are passed through the allowed environment, not written into the harness or repository.

Launched on the Studio from a clone checked out at the pushed candidate:

```sh
crabbox run --provider local-container --keep --ttl 1h --idle-timeout 30m \
  --local-container-image node:24.22.1-trixie \
  --local-container-cpus 8 --local-container-memory 24g \
  --local-container-volume "$HOME/crabbox-proof/report-202292:/proof" \
  --allow-env OPENAI_API_KEY --no-hydrate --timing-json --shell -- \

   node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.live.config.ts \
     src/agents/independent-session-report.proof.live.test.ts'
```

For the baseline, the retained lease's tracked source was explicitly restored to `3b63f9ea1f552930f8d20215a1cb89a95a261fd0`, and `git diff --exit-code HEAD` confirmed a clean tracked tree before building. It then used the same harness with `--id cbx_9aec7da26651 --no-sync`, omitted the creation-only volume flag, verified `git rev-parse HEAD`, rebuilt, and set `REPORT_PROOF_LABEL=base`. A prior sync attempt failed the exact-HEAD preflight and did not run the test; only the verified baseline run is counted here.

Contributor: [Mert Başar (@MertBasar0)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205438#issuecomment-7178756423).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/c499a8eb-55c7-44ea-ba80-15889ca0e9cd)

`decision_evaluate` rejects a selected model ID missing from the prepared catalog before its provider can declare decision capabilities. That breaks documented custom TypeSafe routes such as `typesafe/decision` with a configured `baseUrl` and `models: []`. #205944 covers diagnostic wording; this follow-up fixes dispatch.

OpenClaw sends the configured custom model ID unchanged when the provider supports the requested input. Unsupported inputs are still rejected before dispatch. Existing configurations need no migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the exact catalog row is absent, prepared execution uses the explicit provider configuration for route identity only. The provider still has to supply decision capabilities, and the existing preflight still checks them before auth and dispatch. No other model’s capabilities are borrowed and no picker row is added.

prs.title: fix(discord): log why a dropped voice session ended and rejoin autoJoin
prs.body:
Closes #206113

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a Discord voice connection drops and does not recover within `voice.reconnectGraceMs`, the bot leaves the channel with one log line that gives only a numeric code, and a plain `voice.autoJoin` channel (no `whenOccupied`) stays empty until the next Gateway READY/RESUMED or a manual `/vc join`.

## User Impact

The Gateway log now says which voice session ended and why (`discord voice: session ended guild=… channel=…: voice connection or audio worker stopped`). The bot rejoins its configured autoJoin channel. `/vc leave` still keeps it out.

## Why This Change Was Made

The audio transport already emits `stopped` when the connection is destroyed or the worker stops. `voice-session.ts` turned that into a session stop whose reason went into the guild lifecycle, where nothing reads it. Rejoining only happened through `reconcileAutoJoinGuild`, which returns early for entries without `whenOccupied`. That path also runs when the bot's voice state changes, which happens before the grace period ends and after `/vc leave`, so it is the wrong place to rejoin.

The transport-initiated stop now reaches the voice manager's existing `onSessionStopped` as a self-stop. Requested stops (leave, manager shutdown, realtime failures) stay as they are. The manager logs the stop and, when the stopped channel is the guild's autoJoin target, enqueues one attempt through the existing `enqueueAutoJoin`. That function already applies `whenOccupied`, allowlist and fatal-failure suppression. The log carries only the fixed reason, not error text (#174476).

## Evidence

**Partial reproduction, no live Discord.** I have no Discord QA bot lease (the `discord-e2e` readiness probe fails at Convex lease acquisition), and the QA lane has no voice-channel recipe. The proof runs the real `DiscordVoiceManager`, voice session, audio transport and in-process `DiscordAudioWorker` from the existing voice test harness. Only the `@discordjs/voice` SDK and the Discord client are mocked. The worker's `Disconnected` handler runs and recovery fails, as it does when the grace timer expires.

- **Main:** after the drop, `status()` is `[]`, `joinVoiceChannel` was called once (no rejoin), and the only warning is `discord voice: audio worker failed`. With a real grace timeout its context is `{ code: 23 }` (`TimeoutError`).
- **Fix:** the warning `discord voice: session ended guild=g1 channel=1001: voice connection or audio worker stopped; rejoining autoJoin channel` is logged, `joinVoiceChannel` is called a second time, and the session reports `connected` in channel 1001 again.
- **Control:** an explicit `leave` on the same plain autoJoin channel does not rejoin and logs no "session ended" line, on both main and the fix.

Tests:
- New `voice-auto-join.test.ts` case "logs why a dropped autoJoin session ended and rejoins its channel": fails on main (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called 2 times, but got 1 times`), passes with the fix. The new control "stays out of a plain autoJoin channel after an explicit leave" passes on both.
- `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/voice`: 55 files, 629 tests passed.
- `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check` and `check:test-lines-ratchet` are clean.

Still needed for full proof: a live Discord run (join an autoJoin channel, drop the bot's voice connection, see the log line and the rejoin). That needs a Discord test bot and guild with a voice channel.

Accepted edge cases (no code for them):
- A moderator who disconnects the bot sees it return after about one grace period, the same as `whenOccupied` channels do today.
- An audio worker that dies right after every join would rejoin repeatedly. Open PR #186254 adds autoJoin backoff in the same file; because this rejoin goes through `enqueueAutoJoin`, it would pick up that backoff.

Production delta +24/-10; test delta +35/-0; docs +1 line in `docs/channels/discord/voice-channels.md`.

Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores log-less drops and no rejoin, with no state or config change. Blast radius is Discord voice sessions that end on their own, and plain autoJoin channels in those guilds.

prs.title: fix(exec): report a run with no captured exit code as failed, not completed
prs.body:
Related: #146426

## What Problem This Solves

An exec run can terminate without reporting an exit code. When the supervisor supplies `reason: "exit", exitCode: null, exitSignal: null`, the tool currently reports a successful `completed` result with exit code `0`.

This change reports `failed`, preserves `exitCode: null`, and uses the existing `aborted` reason: "Command aborted before exit code was captured". Agents and automation can then distinguish an unknown outcome from a successful command.

## Why This Change Was Made

Require a captured exit code before taking the normal-exit branch in `buildExecExitOutcome`, now owned by `bash-tools.exec-output.ts`. The two-file patch adds this guard and one regression in the existing foreground suite.

Ordinary numeric exits, including nonzero codes, retain their existing behavior. Signal kills already use `reason: "signal"` and were not the false-success bug; signal and timeout classifications are unchanged.

## Evidence for the submitted code

Candidate: `2866e4414f2cc1bab920b14c85aca39a7161a2ab`, synchronized with main `b546280f5b53b5509b8ed8c2032acc32ed0bf0e0` during the last code repair. This November 11 update reorganizes existing records and verifies hosted CI; it introduces no code changes or new local executions.

| Evidence | Result and scope |
|---|---|
| Current-head hosted CI | [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40117264412) and [aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40117264412/job/120942567160) succeeded; the run's head SHA matches the candidate. Skipped jobs are not execution evidence. |
| Recorded classifier red/green | Exact base classifier plus the ported regression fails (1 failed, 11 skipped); restoring the guard gives 12/12 foreground tests passing. The existing supervisor fixture supplies the nullable tuple; real tool/runtime/output code computes failed/null/aborted. |
| Recorded current-source consumer controls | Runtime suite 18/18 and real-child process/session E2E 8/8 pass on macOS, covering ordinary exits, timeout/finalizer behavior and cancellation. Scoped formatting, type-aware lint and diff checks pass. |
| Historical Linux trigger | Real runtime → supervisor → relay → anchor fault injection observed completed/0 before (3/3) and failed/null/aborted after (3/3). This archive lacks the exact execution SHA and an independent native receipt; it is not a fresh current-head Linux run. |

**Proof limit:** the current-source consumer tests do not reproduce the Linux anchor-loss trigger. No fresh Linux installed-service, Windows, Gateway or channel execution is claimed. The full historical probe, logs, earlier CI attribution and setup failures remain below so the evidence can be inspected without conflating revisions.

The [existing review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/148807#issuecomment-5675382048) already names this exact candidate, reports sufficient proof, and lists no findings or before-merge actions.

<details>
<summary>Detailed validation and historical reproduction records</summary>

## Detailed validation records

The current repair is synchronized with main `b546280f5b53b5509b8ed8c2032acc32ed0bf0e0`, which had moved the classifier into `bash-tools.exec-output.ts` but still classified an unknown exit code as success. The conflict resolution preserves that extraction and moves the original captured-code guard to the existing `buildExecExitOutcome` owner. The submitted change remains two files: the guard and its foreground regression. Current local head is `2866e4414f2cc1bab920b14c85aca39a7161a2ab`.

Current validation on this synchronized source:

- **Red:** with the exact main classifier bytes and the ported regression, the focused test fails because the caller receives `(no output)` instead of `Command aborted before exit code was captured` (1 failed, 11 skipped). Restoring the captured-code guard makes the complete owning foreground suite pass **12/12**. The existing supervisor fixture supplies only the raw nullable exit tuple; the real tool/runtime/output path computes the asserted failed/null/aborted outcome.
- The runtime consumer suite passes **18/18**, covering ordinary captured exit status, timeout/signal handling and outcome delivery through the same owner.
- The current process/session E2E file passes **8/8** with real child processes. Its controls include post-exit finalizer failure, timeout after a clean child exit, quiet successful and nonzero exits, and interactive cancellation. These are local consumer controls, not a fresh Linux null-trigger reproduction.
- Repository `oxfmt` check and type-aware `run-oxlint` pass on both changed files; the complete submitted range also passes `git diff --check`. The ordinary E2E preparation completed before the 8/8 result. No separate repository-wide typecheck or aggregate check result is claimed.

The owning-file cost measurement was one `pnpm test src/agents/bash-tools.exec-foreground-failures.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` run: 31.86 s command wall time, including compiled-worker preparation, and 4.51 s Vitest duration. Publication-time note (superseded): hosted CI was not yet available when this local cost measurement was recorded. The current-head CI links and result are listed above. An earlier process-suite attempt failed during build preparation with ENOSPC before running tests; its logs remain recorded as setup failure, and the later successful 8/8 run supplies the consumer result.

Prior-head CI attribution for the [October 10 review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/148807#issuecomment-5675382048) is retained separately. The five notification cases that failed in the older `checks-node-changed-2` observation later passed in [the immutable Linux/Bun process/session job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39338150948/job/118353210606), whose complete process file passed **12/12**. The cases cover post-exit finalizer failure, clean-exit timeout, quiet successful/nonzero completion wakes, and acknowledging the terminal notify-on-exit poll. The [separate foreground job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39338150948/job/118353210631) passed **10/10**, including the nullable-exit regression.

Those hosted jobs ran CI merge `c5e83abc96e7c65ae93bdb15c6718c9618f37720`, with parents base `2d305eb2061955123f799c97c108ea8718fba392` and prior PR head `34664c114b9b5d18d83568efa7d129299a33f879`. The merge and prior head share exact tree `3252b0ace59ee5e882c77c3168c5947dd6ce8c80`; archived qualification preserves checkout facts, named cases and immutable log hashes. These jobs supersede the old failing-check observation for that prior source. They do not prove individual historical causes, a base/reverted-classifier experiment, or Linux execution of the newly synchronized head.

The original author's Linux relay/anchor null-trigger observations below remain historical. Their archive has no independent Linux native receipt or exact execution commit. The separate historical Darwin supervisor receipt covers ordinary stdout/UTF8 controls; it does not reproduce the null-trigger. This macOS run supplies current classifier and real-process consumer coverage, but no new Linux `/proc`, installed-service, Windows, channel, or Gateway evidence. Gateway proof is not applicable to this local exec classification change.

<details>
<summary>Original historical evidence (original source/platform bindings retained)</summary>

The following original observations and failures are historical, not re-labelled as current execution.


### A real run reaches this record on Linux — no stub anywhere in the chain

The producer is OpenClaw's own service-child relay host. On non-Windows, `createChildAdapter` takes that path whenever the run owns its process tree or `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER` is set (`src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.ts:150-154`), which is the path a non-PTY exec under an installed service is supervised through.

The trigger: an anchor that loses host-side authority while the command is still alive and outlives the graceful-cancel window.

1. exec starts `/bin/bash --noprofile --norc -c 'trap "" TERM; while :; do sleep 1; done'` — a command that ignores SIGTERM.
2. The anchor process receives SIGTERM out of band. The host never calls `kill()`, so its `requestedSignal` stays unset.
3. The anchor's own handler runs `requestCleanup("parent-lost")` and signals its process group; the command ignores it.
4. The 5 s `GRACEFUL_CANCEL_TIMEOUT_MS` grace expires with no root result, so `closeAuthority(reason, hardKill=true)` runs `process.kill(0, "SIGKILL")`. The anchor and the command die together, before any `root-result` is sent.
5. The host sees the closing receipt and observes the group's disappearance (`ESRCH`) with no root result, so `finishAuthorityClose` closes authority as `rootResult = { code: null, signal: requestedSignal ?? null }` → `{ code: null, signal: null }`.
6. The supervisor maps that record to `reason: "exit"`, `exitCode: null` — exactly what `buildExecExitOutcome` receives.

Both rows below are real processes: the real supervisor, the real relay host, a real anchor, and the real `runExecProcess` entry point. Nothing is stubbed, mocked, or injected, and the teardown is a real signal to a real process.

| Step | Observed |
|---|---|
| Real supervisor + relay host + SIGTERM-ignoring command | `RunExit { reason: "exit", exitCode: null, exitSignal: null }` |
| Same teardown at `runExecProcess` **before** this change | `status: "completed", exitCode: 0` — 3/3 runs |
| Same teardown at `runExecProcess` **after** this change | `status: "failed", exitCode: null, failureKind: "aborted", reason: "Command aborted before exit code was captured"` — 3/3 runs |

<details>
<summary>Before the change — a run with no captured status reports exit 0</summary>

```text
=== A: real supervisor, real relay host, real process ===
[A]   pid=2067050 argv=/bin/bash --noprofile --norc -c trap "" TERM; while :; do sleep 1; done
[A] SIGTERM -> anchor 2067029 at +61ms
[A] waited 5089ms after the signal
[A] RunExit {
  "reason": "exit",
  "exitCode": null,
  "exitSignal": null,
  "oomScoreWrapperSelected": true,
  "durationMs": 5797,
  "stdout": "",
  "stderr": "",
  "timedOut": false,
  "noOutputTimedOut": false
}
=== B: real runExecProcess entry point ===
[B] SIGTERM -> anchor 2068103 at +71ms
[B] waited 5103ms after the signal
[B] ExecProcessOutcome {
  "status": "completed",
  "exitCode": 0,
  "exitSignal": null,
  "exitReason": "exit",
  "durationMs": 7027,
  "aggregated": "",

  "noOutputTimedOut": false
}
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>After the change — the same teardown reports failure with the null preserved</summary>

```text
=== A: real supervisor, real relay host, real process ===
[A]   pid=2065282 argv=/bin/bash --noprofile --norc -c trap "" TERM; while :; do sleep 1; done
[A] SIGTERM -> anchor 2065267 at +61ms
[A] waited 5090ms after the signal
[A] RunExit {
  "reason": "exit",
  "exitCode": null,
  "exitSignal": null,
  "oomScoreWrapperSelected": true,
  "durationMs": 5736,
```
