```text
  "noOutputTimedOut": false
}
=== B: real runExecProcess entry point ===
[B] SIGTERM -> anchor 2065793 at +51ms
[B] waited 5081ms after the signal
[B] ExecProcessOutcome {
  "status": "failed",
  "exitCode": null,
  "exitSignal": null,
  "exitReason": "exit",
  "durationMs": 6484,
  "aggregated": "",
  "timedOut": false,
  "noOutputTimedOut": false,
  "failureKind": "aborted",
  "oomScoreWrapperSelected": true,
  "reason": "Command aborted before exit code was captured"
}
```
</details>

Repeated runs of the identical probe are stable in both directions: 3/3 `completed` with `exitCode: 0` before the change, 3/3 `failed` with `exitCode: null` after it.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction (scratch probe, run from the repository root; not part of the change)</summary>

```ts
// tmp-probe.mts — real runExecProcess, real supervisor, real anchor
import { readFileSync, readdirSync } from "node:fs";
import { runExecProcess } from "./src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.js";

const PROGRAM = 'trap "" TERM; while :; do sleep 1; done';

function ppidOf(pid: number): number {
  try {
    const match = /^PPid:\s+(\d+)$/m.exec(readFileSync(`/proc/${pid}/status`, "utf8"));
    return match ? Number(match[1]) : -1;
  } catch {
    return -1;
  }
}

// Our own anchor only: anchor -> relay -> this probe.
function findAnchorPid(): number | undefined {
  for (const entry of readdirSync("/proc")) {
    if (!/^\d+$/.test(entry)) continue;
    const pid = Number(entry);
    if (pid === process.pid) continue;
    try {
      if (!readFileSync(`/proc/${entry}/cmdline`, "utf8").includes("service-child-group-anchor")) {
        continue;
      }
    } catch {
      continue;
    }
    if (ppidOf(ppidOf(pid)) === process.pid) return pid;
  }
  return undefined;
}

const handle = await runExecProcess({
  // exec runs this as the `-c` program of its own shell, so that shell is the
  // root process and it ignores SIGTERM itself.
  command: PROGRAM,
  workdir: "/tmp",
  env: { PATH: process.env.PATH ?? "" },
  usePty: false,
  warnings: [],
  maxOutput: 100_000,
  pendingMaxOutput: 100_000,
  notifyOnExit: false,
  timeoutSec: null,
});

const deadline = Date.now() + 15_000;
let anchorPid: number | undefined;
while (anchorPid === undefined && Date.now() < deadline) {
  anchorPid = findAnchorPid();
  if (anchorPid === undefined) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 25));
}
if (anchorPid === undefined) throw new Error("anchor process never appeared");
process.kill(anchorPid, "SIGTERM");
console.log(JSON.stringify(await handle.promise, null, 2));
```

```bash
OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER=openclaw pnpm tsx tmp-probe.mts
```
</details>

### Sibling paths through the same entry point

Same real entry point, no signal interference, after the change:

| Command | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `true` | `completed`, `exitCode 0` |
| `exit 3` | `completed`, `exitCode 3` |
| unknown command | `failed`, `exitCode 127`, `shell-command-not-found` |
| `kill -9 $$` | `failed`, `exitCode null`, `exitSignal SIGKILL`, `exitReason signal`, `failureKind signal` |

Only the null-code `"exit"` record changed classification; the signal, not-found, and ordinary exit paths are untouched.

### Regression coverage

| Path | Mode | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| New case in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-foreground-failures.test.ts` | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec-foreground-failures.test.ts` | Before fix: FAIL — 1 failed, 21 passed. After fix: PASS — 22 passed |
| 5 exec suites (`exec-runtime`, `exec-foreground-failures`, `exec-runtime-output`, `exec-runtime.cleanup`, `process.activity`) | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <files>` | 80 passed |
| Repo gate | `pnpm check:changed` | pass (`GATE_EXIT=0`; lanes core+coreTests, oxfmt, typecheck, lint, all guards) |

The unit-level case asserts the same record through `runExecProcess` at the seam the existing exec suites use, so the fix stays covered in CI without depending on process signals. Before the fix it failed as `expected { status: 'completed', exitCode: 0 } to match { status: 'failed', exitCode: null }`.

### What was not tested

- No Windows host was available. The relay-host closure above is now reproduced on Linux; the Windows job-object hard-kill path (`useWindowsJobAnchor`) is still unexercised, and it is the likeliest other producer of this record.
- The last settle that can still carry a null code is unreachable by construction, not untested: the PTY adapter's `dispose()` settle is a no-op because the supervisor disposes only after that adapter's `wait()` has already resolved, and `settleWait` ignores a second settlement.
- The reproduction above constructs the trigger deliberately (out-of-band SIGTERM to the anchor plus a command that ignores SIGTERM) rather than waiting for it to happen in the field; it exercises real shipped code, but no production incident was captured.
- No live channel or Gateway proof: the change is local to exec outcome classification.

## Historical prior revision only: merge conflict resolved and validation refreshed

This revision resolves the merge conflict against `main` that ClawSweeper recorded as the only
remaining item, and re-runs the focused exec validation on the resulting head.

The branch was rebased onto current `main`. The only content conflict was in
`src/agents/bash-tools.exec-foreground-failures.test.ts`, where `main` had in the meantime moved the
suite to a `fullExec()` / `tool.execute()` idiom and dropped the direct `runExecProcess` call this
branch's test used. The conflicted region was therefore taken from `main` and the regression test was
re-expressed in the current idiom with the same assertions — `status: "failed"`, `exitCode: null`,
`failureKind: "aborted"`, `exitReason: "exit"`, and the reason text
`Command aborted before exit code was captured`. `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts` auto-merged
with the classifier change intact. The diff is unchanged in scope: 2 files, +29/-1, matching the
surface recorded in review.

Validation on the rebased head:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `bash-tools.exec-foreground-failures.test.ts` (owner regression file) | 12/12 pass, including the new null-code case |
| `bash-tools.exec-runtime.test.ts` (sibling suite) | 20/20 pass |
| `supervisor.output-activity.real.test.ts` (real supervisor, real child processes) | 2/2 pass — ordinary exits still classify as `completed` |
| `pnpm tsgo:test:src` | pass |
| scoped `oxlint` on both changed files | 0 warnings, 0 errors |

Environment limitation: this rebase and validation run happened on `darwin` (macOS), where the
Linux-only service-child relay host path cannot be re-created, so the real-process before/after
traces above were not re-captured here; what was re-run locally is the focused suite plus the real
supervisor test listed above. No Gateway or channel proof applies, because the change is confined to
local exec outcome classification.

Main's dependency check fails on unused subagent completion exports left after [the completion-policy refactor](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206383).

prs.title: feat(gateway): admit sessions_send wake starts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_send` can fan out wake-starting work through the gateway `agent` RPC. Before this change, concurrent senders could bypass sender-local batching and rate limits. This adds an optional gateway-owned admission boundary for typed `sessions_send` wake traffic. It intentionally does not affect `mode:notify`, which does not create recipient work.

## Summary

- add a disabled-by-default `gateway.sessionsSendWakeAdmission` policy (six starts per 15 minutes by default)
- enforce it at the common gateway `agent` admission boundary only for typed `inputProvenance.kind=inter_session` / `sourceTool=sessions_send`
- persist one idempotent per-recipient decision in a separate SQLite database, atomically, and fail closed if state is unavailable

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/sessions-send-wake-admission.test.ts`: 4/4 passed (default-disabled, seven-recipient load, restart/idempotency, fail-closed state error)
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm format:check`, and `git diff --check` passed locally
- implementation is based on released OpenClaw `v2026.10.9` / `8b18b557`, matching the runtime that exposed the issue

## Rollout

Feature remains off by default. This PR contains no config enablement, runtime rollout, or gateway restart. Rollback is retaining the disabled flag or reverting this commit; the receipt database remains as audit evidence.

prs.title: refactor(github): migrate repository integration to a plugin
prs.body:
## Summary

Depends on #192349. Review and merge the SDK foundation first.

GitHub repository integration spans account connections, repository discovery, execution identity, publication, and browser presentation. This PR moves the vendor implementation into the bundled `github-repositories` plugin using [the Plugin SDK foundation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192349).

The plugin supplies the existing GitHub workflows. OpenClaw retains sessions, approvals, local Git custody, durable account/publication records, and recovery. Generic SDK additions belong to the foundation; this consumer supplies GitHub registration, lifecycle, configuration migration, and presentation.

**Upgrade:** run `openclaw doctor --fix` to move legacy native GitHub settings into `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`. Explicit plugin allowlists and deny rules remain authoritative; include `github-repositories` to use this integration.

The independent `github` plugin continues to own `github_read`, `github_search`, public link previews, and reader views. GitHub Copilot, Gateway sign-in, and verified profile identity remain separate owners.

## Ownership

| Capability | `github-repositories` supplies | OpenClaw retains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts and OAuth | Credential selection, GitHub transport, refresh policy, and connection presentation. | Canonical managed/personal account records, profile authority, config writing, and refresh settlement. |
| Repository sources | Discovery, URL admission, authenticated clone/fetch, repository/object identity, and worker adapters. | Picker/session admission, checkout storage and leases, worktree placement, accepted checkpoints, and recovery. |
| Execution identity | Identity facts, credential scrubbing, private child-launch adapters, and supported sandbox preparation. | Command policy, approvals, final launch, and sandbox provisioning/permission. |
| Publication | GitHub targets/content, remote operations, and author/coauthor policy. | Local Git/index custody, verified participant/consent facts, exact receipts, accepted-operation settlement, and live effect authority. |
| Agent tools | `github_identity_status`, `github_publish`, and their policy descriptions. | Caller-bound dispatch, workspace access, tool/child-policy ceilings, handoff, and cleanup. |
| PR/check presentation | Reads, subscriptions, plugin read store, badges, actions, Settings, and session accessories. | Session/audience admission, layout, navigation, captured requests, and retained operations. |
| Board and Doctor | GitHub Actions binding, secret/config metadata, migration, and health checks. | Grant preparation, config persistence/migration orchestration, managed service scheduling, and cleanup. |

The plugin entry registers repository and execution contributions, tools, Board data, Gateway methods, and a V2 managed account service. The manifest declares startup activation, Settings views, secret exclusions, and Doctor participation. Heavy handlers load when invoked. The host keeps its existing stores and lifecycle owners. The released `GatewayRequestContext.githubOAuthService` lookup remains a guarded projection of the canonical plugin-owned service through the documented December 31, 2026 compatibility window; it does not create a second account service.

### Repository and execution

The qualified source `github-repositories/repositories` feeds the repository picker and follows `sessions.create` into session, checkout, and worker preparation. Default worktree preparation uses source-owned `resolveBase()` to observe authenticated remote HEAD, hydrate the selected commit, and follow a renamed default branch. Explicit selectors preserve their Git namespace and literal branch names; missing refs remain actionable. The host verifies the commit locally without ambient-origin fetches, retains safe local branch updates under checkout custody, and pins ref/commit before setup. Retries retain that accepted pin. The isolated Fake Forge plugin uses the same contract with a local transport and an HTTPS canonical origin. GitHub callbacks perform authenticated transport; the host retains destinations, cancellation, pinned commits, and recovery.

Worker preparation returns immutable repository/object identities and a nonsecret cache partition. The host revalidates the lease around Git-pack preparation; the plugin asserts caller and credential authority at effects. Cache identity is not access authority. Admitted credential readers retain the original dispatch actor and request; issued credentials register cleanup with the host.

Execution uses the SDK environment provider. Local wrappers enclose the reviewed command after policy/approval. Sandbox preparation explicitly selects backend and scope rather than copying local identity. Declared exclusions keep bearer credentials out of nonsecret environment facts and prepared repository snapshots.

### Publication and lifecycle

The plugin consumes `native-github-account-host`, `native-github-publication-host`, and `native-github-session-read` to work with the existing native records and receipts.

- `github_publish` uses caller-bound Gateway operations and the existing publication/handoff owner. Session and approval checks remain in force. PR preparation retains the selected requester through the existing host continuation; publication keeps its existing accepted-operation settlement.
- The plugin supplies typed provenance and Git author facts. Core records and compares existing receipt fields for replay and uses the author for source-integration commits. Live request/account assertions authorize effects; verified participant/consent facts stay host-owned.
- PR automation reads the session’s own publication without an import-authorship preflight. A different captured target retains its existing authenticated read workflow. The recipe retains jobs after authentication, inspection, network, and checkout blockers and after successful remediation; cleanup is reserved for a verified merged/closed result.
- Plugin-owned `session-pr:v1` declarations retain their SHA256 identity bytes. Wire/storage DTOs and accepted publication records retain their contracts.
- Refresh, publication-provider installation, and session presentation use managed scheduler, Gateway, and plugin-instance lifetimes. The legacy service projection shares its existing exact-Gateway lookup across native and compiled module graphs. Native source loading and compiled SDK consumers use the same canonical owner and installed publication-host lookup. Accepted publication and checkout transfers remain one-use operations under that owner; cleanup, replacement, and revocation end stale capabilities.

### Browser presentation and reader independence

Control UI V2 contributions provide Profile connections, Agent tools Settings, session PR/check accessories, actions, and retained publication operations. They reuse host controls, responsive layout, serialized config mutations, and captured requests. Plain host-owner subscriptions feed plugin-local reactive state across the separately bundled Solid runtimes. The plugin read store owns PR presentation. Hovercards preserve the compact ten-PR limit and remaining count; branch/diff metadata occupies an adjacent row in the existing accessory layout. Branch and publication controls stay in the native Environment section through the generic `session-environment` slot; published PRs use the separate context section.

Explicit shorthand such as `owner/repo#123` names `reader: { pluginId: "github", id: "github" }`. Both contributions must be admitted and active; the reader owns URL filtering and remote reads. Checkout names, project aliases, and adjacent links never infer a destination, so formatting needs no background project-catalog read.

Public `github.preview` and `github.detail` use the reader's data path directly, so disabling `github-repositories` leaves public reading operational. Enabled managed identity retains its current-selection checks; disabled integration skips that managed selection and uses the existing service/environment/anonymous public path. GitHub App installations verify identity with a temporary installation token and support public reads/search scoped to the requested repository. Temporary tokens are revoked before delivery; App access does not broaden the public-only reader or enable shell execution/publication. Request authority is checked during reads and before delivery. Session/Enterprise readers retain their admitted session-specific path.

Disabling repository integration removes its operations, managed service, tools, and browser contributions. Disabling `github` removes public reading without changing repository ownership. Neither operation broadens allow/deny policy.

Session rows render passive plugin badge facts through the native row renderer. The same bounded, data-only facts join the existing scoped sidebar snapshot, so PR indicators survive a reload before plugin reconnect. Pending results retain facts only for the same complete session target and current registration; ready-empty results and retirement clear them. No plugin code, catalog, new storage manager, or capture timer is persisted.

## Configuration and upgrade

Canonical settings live under `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`:

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `system` | Shared managed GitHub execution identity. |
| `agents.<id>` | Complete per-agent identity override and optional sandbox permission. |
| `host`, `apiBaseUrl` | Matching GitHub or Enterprise endpoint pair. |
| `service.host`, `service.token` | Gateway-side discovery and reader service credential. |
| `repositorySearch.useNativeCredentials` | Explicit opt-in for native-credential repository search. |

`openclaw doctor --fix` invokes the plugin-owned transform for `tools.github`, per-agent `tools.github`, `gateway.github`, `gateway.controlUi.github`, and `gateway.projects.nativeGitHubSearch`. Explicit canonical values win, identities remain atomic, and unknown legacy fields remain available for explicit repair. Normalization is idempotent; conflict warnings omit credential values.

Managed OAuth records, personal connections, and accepted publication state retain their existing storage owners. Runtime reads canonical configuration; migration does not add a legacy runtime reader or rewrite receipts. Explicit allowlists, deny rules, disabled entries, and independent-reader policy are preserved.

See `docs/plugins/github.md` and `extensions/github-repositories/config-migration.test.ts` for configuration and migration details.

## Test scope

Native contracts remain with their host owners. GitHub unit and integration suites live with the plugin; native UI fixtures activate its declared public browser entry and consume protocol events. Coverage includes canonical configuration migration, serialized writes, account selection and retirement, publication handoff, worker credentials, execution approvals, browser freshness and independent reader admission. A standalone fixture allocation covers real provider setup, typed public adapters, lifecycle cleanup and passive-badge reload proof; the shared scalar is unchanged. A separate exact allocation covers App status/read lifetime, automation target/blocker guidance, and App capability presentation regressions.

## Validation

- Full local `pnpm build` passes, including SDK declarations, all 102 bundled plugins, all 167 public SDK subpaths and Control UI. Core, Gateway, agent-execution, extension and UI typechecks pass for the affected scopes. The supported local package passes tarball inventory and import-graph integrity checks.
- The intervening handoff and worker-recovery owners pass 98 targeted cases. Publisher installation rollback passes eight host/loader cases; native-menu error isolation and plugin-owned live/persisted badge parity pass 31 UI cases, with affected production/test typechecks and scoped lint.
- A supported local CLI turn with both GitHub plugins disabled executes successfully with the independent Fake Forge identity and no GitHub token in its child environment.
- Published 2026.10.9 state survives Doctor migration, a second idempotent Doctor run and restart, preserving its project, managed worktree, session and published request. Explicit deny remains authoritative when both GitHub plugins are also allowlisted: two Doctor runs and a restart leave both plugins unloaded and absent from UI/repository catalogs while OpenAI remains active. A separate real Gateway interruption during an accepted publication resumes the same request/account/destination through idempotent replay and produces exactly one PR with the expected commit. A crash after a remote effect with its response lost remains synthetic-fault coverage.
- Focused native checkout/publication, RPC, execution identity/approval, sandbox, App/OAuth/Git transport and browser suites pass. Cached badge reload and cross-tab deletion proof includes actual persisted badge facts; capture cadence is unchanged.
- Real isolated Gateway checks verify App identity, public PR reading/search, and refusal to disclose a private PR despite installation access. Native identity also publishes to disposable public/private repositories, resumes an advanced private head, refreshes the base, and uploads/associates sandbox evidence.
- A real scheduled auto-fix occurrence reads the selected PR's feedback, verifies the requested edit, and publishes to the same PR while retaining its job. The 14 recipe contract cases pass; repeated fresh-observation behavior remains unqualified as described below.
- Focused repair suites pass: 63 App/reader/RPC cases, 15 connections cases, 14 automation cases, and the SDK readiness regression.
- Targeted account lifecycle proof verifies unavailable selection and exact-config recovery with real reads; seven credential/profile retirement and cleanup cases pass. Nineteen publication response-loss, duplicate replay, authority, and restart-recovery cases pass through the real host/plugin adapter with synthetic GitHub faults.
- Fresh isolated Fake Forge proof passes: plugin transport supplies the advanced remote commit, the host owns the managed worktree, and one real successful agent `exec` receives `FAKE_FORGE_IDENTITY=sdk-trial`. The Gateway remains available locally; the model is a synthetic loopback fixture.
- Production and test compiler-boundary guards pass without exemptions. English catalogs load through the declared public artifact and retain Vite dependency watching and fresh reloads; source localization verification passes.
- Startup JavaScript gzip passes its unchanged cap: 90,661 bytes against 90,687 bytes. Startup/auth behavior, native Agents settings, browser subscription cleanup and reconnect have focused passing proof.

Interactive OAuth issuance, distinct-account isolation, native Codex-harness execution, Enterprise endpoints, real cloud provisioning, factory-native proof issuance/redemption, and migration from the newer 2026.11.1 release remain unqualified. Reliable full recurring auto-fix monitoring also remains unqualified: the complete recipe can return quietly without reading fresh feedback, and that failure mode is reproduced on untouched upstream as well. Live feedback-to-publication execution is verified separately.

## Browser evidence

Existing sanitized synthetic captures illustrate shorthand and desktop/mobile Settings presentation; they are not live OAuth or current-head runtime qualification.

- skip agent heartbeat-timeout resolution for command payloads
- keep command jobs runnable while agent database startup admission is pending
- add a regression test proving command execution does not consult agent heartbeat state

## Root cause
The generic timer watchdog resolved an agent heartbeat timeout for every payload. For host command jobs this metadata is irrelevant, but the gateway resolver asserts agent database admission. A command scheduled during gateway startup therefore failed before its argv ran.

## Verification
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.cron.config.ts src/cron/service/command-timeout.test.ts --reporter=default` (4 passed)
- `git diff --check`

prs.title: feat(ios): new app icons for iPhone and Apple Watch, release and debug
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The OpenClaw iOS app still ships the first version of its Home Screen icon: a large mascot that fills the tile edge to edge, with cyan eyes, on a plain white square (or a plain black square in Dark). The development build adds a heavy yellow and black hazard frame with a bug badge in the corner. Neither matches the approved OpenClaw icon artwork, and the Apple Watch app uses the same outdated art.

## User Impact

- **iPhone and iPad, App Store and TestFlight builds:** the Home Screen shows the new OpenClaw icon. A smaller, brighter red mascot sits on a soft off-white tile in Light, and on a near-black tile with a warm red glow in Dark.
- **Development builds:** the same new mascot holds a wrench inside a thin hazard-stripe border, with a light tile and a dark tile. It still reads as a development build at a glance.
- **Apple Watch:** the Watch app gets the new art for both build types, redrawn from the same artwork.
- **Tinted Home Screens:** iOS still derives the Tinted icon on its own, as before.

Nothing else changes. The asset catalogs declare the same sizes and slots, and no setting or text changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The approved artwork arrives as flattened 1024 px PNGs, with one Default image and one Dark image for each icon set. There's no vector source. The icon generator now treats those two PNGs as the source of truth:
- `apps/ios/scripts/app-icon-variants.sh generate` redraws every smaller iPhone, iPad and Watch size from the Default image.
- `check` verifies that every file the catalogs name exists and matches a fresh render. It also checks that both 1024 px images are opaque, 8-bit and sRGB.

Since the Dark development icon is now provided artwork, the Swift renderer that used to cut a Dark version out of the Default image (`app-icon-debug-dark.swift`) is no longer used. This PR removes it.

## Evidence

**Release icon (`AppIcon`).** Before (main) on the left, After on the right. Light on top, Dark below.

![Release icon on the Home Screen. Left: the current icon on main, a large mascot on a white tile and on a black tile. Right: the new icon, a smaller red mascot on an off-white tile and on a near-black tile with a red glow.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/43426760-1f35-4896-9e25-5c1f2d3df890)

**Development icon (`AppIconDebug`).** Before (main) on the left, After on the right. Light on top, Dark below.

![Development icon on the Home Screen. Left: the current icon on main, with a thick yellow and black frame and a bug badge. Right: the new icon, the mascot holding a wrench inside a thin hazard-stripe border, light and dark.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e45b5b15-9a43-4bf2-b06c-f514a22927a6)

Captured on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator running iOS 27.2, from the Home Screen icon row. The Home Screen icon style was set to Dark with Auto, so it follows the system appearance. Before and After use the same simulator, wallpaper and crop. Each build was uninstalled before installing the next, so the Home Screen didn't show a cached icon.

**Builds:**
- `xcodebuild` of the `OpenClaw` scheme (Debug, iOS Simulator) on this branch and on main. It compiles the iOS asset catalog and the embedded Watch app's asset catalog with `AppIconDebug`.
- The same build with `ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME=AppIcon` (the Release setting) compiles both catalogs with `AppIcon`.
- All four builds succeeded. SwiftFormat and SwiftLint ran as part of each build.
- On both main and this branch, `actool` reports the same three notices about legacy 57 px and 76@1x sizes, and no icon warnings or errors.

**Icon files:**
- `apps/ios/scripts/app-icon-variants.sh check` passes. Every size is a byte-exact render of the 1024 px artwork, both 1024 px images are opaque sRGB, and each icon set has one Default image, one Dark image and one automatic Tinted slot.
- Each of the four icon sets (iOS and Watch, release and development) names exactly the files it contains. No unused image is left behind.

**Not checked:**
- The Watch icon on a watch face or Watch Home Screen, because no watchOS simulator runtime was available.
- A signed Release archive, the Tinted and Clear icon styles, Spotlight, and Settings.

prs.title: fix(ci): keep memory completion test within its execution deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The private-memory transcript test can report a successful optional inference as failed on slower CI workers. Its global clock jump advances 100 seconds while the detached inference is still running, crossing that run's execution deadline before the test settles the response.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205687
Observed failure: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45945915837/job/140330702470

## User Impact

CI retains the existing completion, interruption, transcript privacy, cleanup, and parent-watchdog assertions without expiring the separate inference. Production behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Advance the fixture clock by one millisecond: enough to prove semantic-deadline renewal, while keeping the detached execution deadline valid. The patch changes one value and adds an explanatory comment.

## Evidence

- The unchanged file passed in isolation; the original shard ordering was not replayed.
- Controlled reproduction held the response for 1.5 seconds after the watchdog assertions: the 100-second jump reproduced the same expected-completed/received-failed error; changing only the clock advance to one millisecond passed both cases.
- The diagnostic delay was removed from the final patch. No tests or assertions were added or removed.
- Final committed file: both Bun integration cases passed (30.08 seconds in Vitest; 93.03 seconds including worker preparation). Boat run `run_89eb414a1871f09068b36ea09fe5ee0a`, lease `cbx_1a53a858719c`, verified file digest `baf9e264ec44b3696c89ff94c3f6662f2a48a8ed1c4d884c68589561b6142e25`.
- Local ClawSweeper review completed with no findings on `d95d852e054f61cb654c478511537e2562317c33..8b60699c1be926cfdc9818a11292d2f76fdd3235`.
- Focused lint passed with zero warnings or errors on the same source tree (Boat run `run_8e67ff7360b49b3091a0a8b788dbfcb9`). Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Broader PR CI remains to run.

prs.title: feat: review finalized dictation before inserting it
prs.body:
Related: #205845

## What Problem This Solves

Dictation users need a way to stop capture, inspect the completed transcription, and choose when it becomes editable draft text. Optional refinement needs one current-result lifecycle so a delayed transcription or cancelled rewrite cannot replace a newer draft.

This PR implements the private M11 coordinator and a working opt-in review path in the main Chat composer. **M11 is not fully qualified. This PR remains a draft and the tracking issue stays open.**

## User Impact

- Open **Dictation text options** in the main Chat composer and enable **Review dictated text before inserting**. The choice defaults off for each composer instance.
- Provisional captions stay separate from the editable draft. Stop releases capture through its existing owner and shows finishing while waiting for eligible final text.
- Inspect the candidate and original, then choose **Use reviewed text** or **Keep raw transcript**. Acceptance inserts once. Finishing a review-required recording does not send a message.
- Edits/replacement, including immediate edit followed by undo, new captures, owner/account/connection/target/locale changes, capability withdrawal and cancellation retire the old result.
- Incomplete captures remain manual recovery; oversized text is rejected visibly without clipping. New Session and Side chat do not advertise refinement because their insertion/submit contracts differ.

The browser uses conservative local text cleanup (outer whitespace only). Its UI says model-assisted refinement is unavailable in this build and distinguishes local text processing from the separately selected speech-recognition provider. There is no persistent configuration migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The neutral immutable request/plan/result owner is independently usable without M01–M10 feature stores. Optional handlers contribute authorized edits and combined model instructions; absent features are disabled capabilities or explicitly labelled conformance fixtures. Existing capture, provider/authentication, draft and delivery owners retain their responsibilities.

The core validates schema/revisions, half-open UTF-16 ranges at grapheme boundaries, protected bytes and opaque identities. Only outer whitespace changes are eligible for automatic semantic acceptance; uncertain material changes require review. One current operation, bounded snapshots/payload/output, and an absolute deadline constrain the lifecycle. Default ceilings are 32 KiB transcript/output, 8 KiB context and vocabulary each, 64 KiB combined payload, and 2,500 ms.

A real private selected-model adapter and optional measurement route reuse exact provider/model/profile, credential and transport ownership, disable failover, and permit one bounded streaming completion with cancellation and lease disposal. Logical adapter attempts are distinguished from observed HTTP requests.

Public request/RPC exposure, authoritative speech/refinement locality ownership, and admission-versus-revocation semantics still need maintainer acceptance in #205845. The automated issue review is not approval. The browser does not expose an unaccepted model route. Historical #187371 and other dictation drafts are not parents or accepted dependencies.

## Evidence

### Current main integration and CI status — `194fcb3f317e5d256d1c35e9a9a69a230c81a45e`

- `roboclaw-bot` merged upstream `main` through `9239eeb2df3779992fc6c2b8a4501c9ed79e98ae` into the existing fork branch without conflicts or rewriting history. Remote readback verified both that commit and Timothy’s `1377354f965656111db3c370636298a6863df9a2` in the new head’s ancestry, with the exact candidate tree. `git diff --check` passed against that main tip; the static test-line delta is 2,888 (400 ordinary + 2,488 allocated, unchanged by the merge).
- The previously queued [fork PR preflight](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45885527025/job/140135172297) produced no qualifying result. The separate author-run scripted-audio workflow below is not upstream PR CI.
- Upstream PR checks on this draft have not supplied a qualifying exact-head build and functional suite receipt. The deterministic five-second-drain regression, focused suites, and the repository's real-Gateway browser suite still need an exact-head run; the prior-head results below are historical. A maintainer can dispatch upstream [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/workflows/ci.yml) from `main` with this SHA as `target_ref`, or use approved secretless AWS Crabbox.

### Author-run live OpenAI speech proof — `194fcb3`

[Scripted audio proof #205973](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45938967474/job/140308968689) in [fork run 45938967474](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45938967474) completed successfully. The job log identifies checkout `194fcb3f317e5d256d1c35e9a9a69a230c81a45e` and records **9/9 passing takes** (alloy, nova, and sage):

| Scenario | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `file-review-and-keep-raw` | **3/3** — buffered file transcription, review, and explicit raw insertion |
| `realtime-cancel-during-finalization` | **3/3** — cancellation during realtime finalization preserves the draft |
| `realtime-review-and-insert` | **3/3** — realtime final review and explicit insertion without sending |

This is interim live-provider evidence from Timothy Wayne Gregg (@CompleteDotTech): prerecorded OpenAI TTS WAVs fed Chromium's fake mic, through the built Control UI and real Gateway to live OpenAI transcription. All cases were no-send. The job is distinct from the other jobs in the fork matrix. It is not physical-mic proof, a deterministic late-segment timing test, or a substitute for upstream CI. Matched, inspected before/after images embedded in the PR are still pending.

**Physical microphone and device checks: still to do by Timothy Wayne Gregg.** The maintainer scope decision remains open, and the PR stays draft.

### ClawSweeper feedback repair — `1377354f965656111db3c370636298a6863df9a2`

This continuation preserves `291c5b5aede953fdbf78ef00e90119f40d5552ce` and merged main through `2fda93cf03a882cd080e7984392d50b95c4737aa`. It adds the production-relay regression, browser journeys and CI ownership, plus UI corrections exposed by rendered proof. The concurrent finalization timestamp, preference lock, span-limit raw recovery, direct-textarea length handling, and latest preview assertions are retained.

**The repair is published; this PR stays draft and #205845 stays open pending the owner decision and remaining proof. No GitHub comments or re-review command comments were posted.**

#### Changes and behavior

- Capture review uses the existing 10-second total finalization bound, accommodating the production realtime relay’s five-second drain. The separate 2.5-second text deadline starts at actual terminal finalization (`finalizedAt`), so later scheduling delay consumes that budget.
- The actual-relay regression sends nonempty PCM, preserves another final segment at 4,500 ms, stays finishing through 4,999 ms, and waits for the production 5,000 ms close. It verifies immediate microphone release, explicit insertion once, and cancellation that ignores late callbacks. It failed on the originally reviewed timing owners.
- Rendered proof exposed a hidden settings control and narrow footer column. The options button now uses an existing visible control class, and review uses the existing full-width composer lede, including empty/unfocused mobile. This adds no CSS, timers, listeners or state owner.
- The shared options producer normalizes an absent account ID to `undefined`; four textareas use Solid’s typed `readonly` attribute. These resolve six production UI type diagnostics found during the iteration.
- Fresh tests exposed an inherited fixture querying reactive DOM before Solid settled. One `flush()` now follows the synchronous owner assertion; all status, preference-lock, literal, deadline, span-fallback and acceptance assertions remain.
- Realtime and file **real-Gateway** scenarios are added and registered with CI. External speech-provider transport is a loopback fixture. Their runtime preparation remains unqualified below.

#### Verification on the integrated source

| Check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Shared core | **37 passed** |
| Capture/preview/dictation/composer suites | **167 distinct cases passed** across the combined run and focused Solid-fixture repair |
| Actual production-relay regression | **2 passed**; 91.74 s native wrapper |
| Selected-model adapter boundary | **21 passed**; 94.74 s native wrapper; external model transport remains a fixture |
| CI browser-owner planner | **18 passed** |
| Actual Chromium + production-config UI | **5 selected cases passed**: three refinement and two native-background; 56.33 s Vitest; 17 unrelated status cases excluded |
| Native production UI types | **Passed**, 136.93 s, `tsconfig.ui.json` |
| Changed UI, script inventory and Vitest configuration lint | **Passed** through native wrappers |
| Canonical UI build | **Exit 0**, 74.73 s overall / 38.05 s Vite; budget violations recorded below |
| Native pre-commit, diff and test-line checks | **Passed** |

These are **250 distinct passing cases**, without double-counting repeats. The final commit differs from the browser-tested staged tree only in its documentation receipts. The 28 other verified files, including runtime, tests and CI inventories, match the browser snapshot.

[Current AC01–AC13 qualification and historical receipts](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/blob/1377354f965656111db3c370636298a6863df9a2/src/shared/dictation-refinement/README.md). Prior passing results and the unchanged text benchmark stay pinned to their recorded source. The original combined current-source test run failed on the missing DOM flush; the focused repaired suite passed without weakening assertions.

#### Browser and screenshot boundary

The current Chromium run verifies the real production-config Control UI with synthetic Gateway messages and browser microphone transport. The three refinement cases cover default-off behavior, keyboard opt-in, read-only mixed RTL/literal inspection, delayed normal close, explicit insertion with zero `chat.send` calls, cancellation, incomplete recovery, ordinary pointer access, and empty/unfocused mobile layout. The two background cases retain actual Chromium `getUserMedia`/`AudioContext` with generated audio and synthetic blur/visibility events; they do not establish actual OS window switching or physical-device capture.

HEAD, staged tree `a7e24b14706773838b1f00ade4d8469c7eab0f7e`, patch, worktree/index state and 29 source hashes stayed unchanged throughout the run. The production-config Vite bundle took 23.16 s. Inspected 400 × 1,000 captures show a 366-pixel ready preview/status within a 368-pixel composer; empty options occupy the full 350-pixel inner surface. The targeted before reproduction restored the `7dab77e` capture/refinement timing owners into the browser fixture and showed premature manual recovery at 2,501 ms; it was not a whole-tree browser build of that commit.

**Public screenshot delivery remains blocked.** The authenticated GitHub connector has no attachment upload operation, and the local CLI has no usable authenticated upload route. Inspected clean and same-frame annotated before/after captures are delivered in the originating task. Private/local captures do not satisfy the public inline PR screenshot gate. No generated media was committed.

#### Remaining requirements

- Same-build **real-Gateway** realtime/file browser execution remains pending. Native isolated runtime preparation received SIGKILL before Gateway/browser launch, including a 4,352 MB heap and one Rayon worker. No case pass is claimed from setup failure. Physical microphone and live-provider proof remain unqualified.
- The broader `ui/tsconfig.json` editor/test graph and required `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json` leaf remain unqualified after earlier exit-137 resource failures. Production UI types now pass; targeted lint does not replace those broader type checks. The current build reports largest CSS **58,659 vs 58,315 B gzip**, Chat boot **21 vs 20 requests**, and Chat boot JS **1,337,626 vs 1,336,272 B gzip**. It transformed 5,730 modules and verified 1,124 finalized sidecars. These violation classes existed before this iteration, but exact attribution against merged main/original fork point remains unqualified.
- Exact-head broad CI: the [CI run for this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45882051016), and the other newly observed workflows, report `action_required`. No successful broad CI result has been observed. Draft publication is not CI approval; no maintainer-only dispatch or merge is requested.
- The maintainer decision remains open: minimal private main-Chat review versus the broader coordinator/selected-model foundation, including placement and admission-once versus current-authorization semantics. #205788 is unchanged; automated review is not owner acceptance.
- Real provider/attempted-egress observation, human semantic adjudication, screen-reader/200% zoom/device journeys, complete W1/long/cold/network/load measurements, and installed retained-state upgrade/downgrade remain unqualified. The unchanged measurement JSON is historical: core changes in `291c5b5` invalidate any claim that its fingerprint matches this implementation.

The test-line ratchet passes with 2,888 net lines against merged main `2fda93cf03a882cd080e7984392d50b95c4737aa`: the ordinary 400 plus 2,488 allocated. The coverage spans distinct schema/protection, capture, composer, selected-model, actual-relay and realtime/file browser boundaries. No budget or runner assertion was weakened.

Independent source review found no actionable P1/P2 in this repair’s compatibility with the refreshed branch. The latest observed hosted ClawSweeper review still names `7dab77e`; it is not approval of this head.


### Historical main integration and patch-quality follow-up — `291c5b5aede953fdbf78ef00e90119f40d5552ce`

- Merged `openclaw/openclaw:main` through `2fda93cf03a882cd080e7984392d50b95c4737aa` into the existing fork branch without conflicts or a history rewrite. GitHub readback confirmed the exact candidate tree and ancestry from both main and the previous fork head. The PR is still a draft.
- The text-refinement budget now starts when capture actually settles, separate from the Stop-to-close allowance. The review preference cannot interrupt an active capture or pending review. The literal cap counts merged spans, not overlapping matches; if the true cap is exceeded, finalized text remains available for explicit raw acceptance. Empty edits skip redundant grapheme work, and synthesized new protections still get validated. The current Gateway relay assigns one active turn at a time and ends it synchronously, so this follow-up does not add a second turn tracker.
- **Ran:** targeted formatting and lint (no warnings or errors), `git diff --check`, static test-line count (2,064 = 400 ordinary + the unchanged 1,664 allocation), and a source review that identified the fixes above. A separate static review of the [follow-up commit](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/commit/bfe5c8dddb23e5e90fa65b379f169a8dda06ba5e) reported no actionable P0–P2 findings in that commit’s diff. Bash, JavaScript, and Python syntax checks passed for the runbook. These are not behavioral passes, a measured performance gain, or a new ClawSweeper rating.
- **Pending:** red/green drain regression, focused suites, same-build Gateway/Chromium file and realtime proof, inspected screenshots, and exact-base/head UI size and boot-budget attribution. See the [local proof runbook](#local-proof-runbook). Earlier evidence below is historical only.
- **Maintainer decision remains open:** minimal private main-Chat review vs. the broader coordinator/selected-model foundation ([#205845](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205845), [#205788](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205788)). No scope decision, re-review request, or approval to land is implied.

### Historical final-drain follow-up — `28781e05fca4cda4b7b689ec1930c00a42b5844d`

- The fix allows up to 10 seconds for the realtime capture to close after Stop, including the relay's five-second drain. The 2.5-second text-refinement budget starts after capture finalizes. The review still requires terminal closure before it offers insertion.
- **Verified on this change:** targeted formatting and lint, `git diff --check`, and independent static review of the final-drain change. GitHub readback confirmed the managed `roboclaw-bot` push to the existing fork branch, exact candidate tree, and draft state.
- **Not run on this head:** five-second regression (red on the reviewed head, green on the fix), focused runtime suites, or real-Gateway browser proof. The [draft checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205973/checks) show the Proof job skipped. Stop → review → explicit insertion without sending, cancellation, and inspected before/after screenshots remain unverified for file transcription and the realtime relay. [#205892](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205892) is a Vosk file-transcription reference, not proof for this PR or for the realtime relay.

### Earlier qualification — `7dab77ee268617d70ab5f035bb7864cc278aa327`

prs.title: fix(cli): selected TTS providers appear configured without credentials
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`infer tts providers --local` can report a selected speech provider as configured even when its required API key is missing.

## User Impact

Local provider inspection distinguishes selection from credential availability, matching Gateway inventory. It retains the inspected agent's saved API-key visibility and reports unavailable SecretRefs as nonfatal diagnostics. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Local inventory uses the speech provider's existing asynchronous configured check and read-only, agent-scoped credential helpers. Provider selection, inventory metadata, and speech conversion retain their existing owners.

The conflict resolution accepts main's removal of redundant image/video test permutations in #205574 and keeps the dedicated TTS provider regressions. It adds no production behavior, tests, dependency changes, or test-line allocation beyond the existing PR.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `da0ffb2d3e42765b06e7afd27391fb355c722c6c`, merging main `3fa253a2dc68555e405454dd3324a5c604742d69` into previously submitted `218c35364ad6efe40494547d596359dcf11c9521`. The four-file diff from this main has SHA256 `7284892c5e46d28ba8bb3855d3a3ed48110fe22c65f606951b6c8d7dd7178b76`.

For this exact candidate, whitespace checks, esbuild TypeScript transpilation, and oxfmt checks passed. The direct production owner, shared configuration reader, and dedicated TTS regression file are byte-identical to the prior hosted head. This does not establish an unchanged dependency graph or a current runtime pass. Code execution and commit creation used secretless, non-root, no-network containers with read-only source/dependencies and limits of 256 MiB, 0.5 CPU, 64 PIDs, and 32 MiB private temporary storage.

The prior one-worker inventory Vitest attempt exited with SIGKILL/137 after writable task-owned artifact/cache overlays were prepared; it established no test pass. It was not repeated for this test-deletion conflict repair. Full tests, type-aware lint/typecheck, a new built CLI/Gateway run, and heavy builds were not rerun locally. Current-head GitHub CI remains required; earlier CI results below cover only their recorded heads.

An independent coding-agent reviewer examined the complete four-file committed diff, related owners/callers, conflict resolution, and raw validation evidence for the exact base/head above. prs.title: fix(gateway): stop fencing session recall on transcript-only refreshes
prs.body:
Closes #205386

## What Problem This Solves

On a busy Gateway, `sessions_search` called with a query but without `sessionKey` intermittently failed with:

> Session search scope changed while reading; retry the request

The failure was not one-shot: recall captures the disclosure revision before its SQLite worker read and re-validates it afterwards, twice. Any transcript activity happening anywhere on the Gateway reset that revision, so both read attempts were fenced and the call threw. Supplying `sessionKey` skips the recall path, which is why the same search worked when the key was passed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/gateway/session-row-projection.ts` called `revisions.invalidate()` inside `transcriptUpdates.refresh()` on every transcript refresh — both the certified fast path and the materialized slow path. `invalidate()` clears the memoized sharing token that `searchRecallSessionTranscripts` captures as `projection.sharingRevision` and compares after each worker read (`sessions-search-recall.ts:55,187,197`). A transcript write to any unrelated row therefore looked like a disclosure-scope change.

Transcript-only refreshes update presentation facts (activity summary, preview, transcript watermark); they do not change who may read a session. The fix removes that single invalidation and documents the invariant. Every genuine scope change still invalidates the token through its own path:

- `mark()` for structural and visibility publications;
- `revisions.materialized()` for board and membership changes;
- `revisions.replace()` / `remove()` for row replacement and lifecycle;
- the catalog owner refresh.

Fact consumers are unaffected: `publishFacts` still runs on both refresh paths, so summaries and previews keep updating. No change to the recall fence itself, no new dependencies, no guard weakening.

## User Impact

Session recall on a busy Gateway keeps working while other sessions are writing transcripts: `sessions_search` without a `sessionKey` no longer needs retries. Disclosure protection is unchanged — real visibility, sharing, membership, owner, or lifecycle changes during a read still fence the response and produce the same error.

## Evidence

Real runtime: the shipped `startGatewayServer` entry (`node --import tsx` against this worktree's source), a fresh `chmod 700` state dir, a real WebSocket protocol client, and 48 materialized busy sessions receiving continuous transcript writes while each search is in flight. Each scenario runs 4 recall searches without `sessionKeys` plus 2 searches with explicit `sessionKeys`.

Before the fix (bug present in the same harness):

```
[proof] round 3 recall without sessionKeys (1609ms): {"ok":true,"hits":["agent:main:visible-target"]}
[proof] round 4 recall without sessionKeys (1972ms): {"ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"Error: Session search scope changed while reading; retry the request"}}
[proof] round 1 search with explicit sessionKeys (1430ms): {"ok":true,"hits":["agent:main:visible-target"]}
[proof] with explicit sessionKeys: 2/2 succeeded
[proof] RESULT: FAIL (recall reported a scope change)
```

After the fix:

```
[proof] round 1 recall without sessionKeys (8668ms): {"ok":true,"hits":["agent:main:visible-target"]}
[proof] round 2 recall without sessionKeys (1580ms): {"ok":true,"hits":["agent:main:visible-target"]}
[proof] round 3 recall without sessionKeys (1095ms): {"ok":true,"hits":["agent:main:visible-target"]}
[proof] round 4 recall without sessionKeys (1097ms): {"ok":true,"hits":["agent:main:visible-target"]}
[proof] with explicit sessionKeys: 2/2 succeeded
[proof] RESULT: PASS (recall tolerated transcript-only activity)
```

Regression tests (new tests fail with the invalidation restored, pass with the fix):

```
node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/session-row-projection.test.ts \
  src/gateway/session-row-projection.invalidation.test.ts \
  src/gateway/session-row-projection.transcript-regression.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-search-scope.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-search.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-search-invited-policy.test.ts
 Test Files  6 passed (6)
      Tests  64 passed (64)
```

- `session-row-projection.test.ts`: sharing revision stays stable across a transcript-only refresh, and still changes on membership edits.
- `sessions-search-scope.test.ts`: recall succeeds while unrelated rows emit transcript activity during the worker read, and still throws when the disclosure scope genuinely changes during both attempts.

`oxlint` on the three touched files: 0 warnings, 0 errors. `tsgo` cannot run in this environment (system GLIBC is older than 2.32), so type checking is delegated to the exact-head CI run.

prs.title: improve: scan configured models once when enabling provider plugins
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw decides which provider plugins to enable, each provider declared by a plugin can trigger another scan of every configured model. Configurations with many agents pay for the same traversal repeatedly, even when none of those providers are configured.

## User Impact

Provider detection visits the model configuration once and reuses the result for all provider claims. The same plugins receive the same activation reasons in the same order. This change requires no configuration or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The detector already needs the complete model list to resolve model owners. It can also use that list to identify configured providers within the same call. With no provider claims, it still skips inspecting auth profiles and configured provider keys. A single claim that matched an early auth profile previously allowed an early exit, so savings depend on the registry and configuration.

## Evidence

- Through the public detector, the new regression makes one call without provider claims and one with four unique claims. The original code read the selected model field four times in total. The updated code reads it twice, once per call. The test also verifies mixed-case claims, normalized profile and configuration keys, duplicate claim ownership and the order of provider and model reasons.
- The provider and core auto-enable suites passed all 56 tests. Configuration documentation and formatting checks passed.
- On a synthetic 128-agent configuration with 770 model references and 13 unmatched provider IDs from bundled manifests, the detector's owning loop made 14 complete model traversals before this change and one afterward. The zero-claim case took one traversal in both versions. These are work counts. End-to-end startup latency was not measured.
- Independent source review and a complete local branch autoreview reported no actionable findings.

prs.title: fix: preserve trusted certificates through nested secret egress proxies
prs.body:
Closes #135955
Related: #144830

## What Problem This Solves

A protected egress proxy started behind another trusted proxy drops inherited CA trust. HTTPS requests then fail with a 502 and `UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE`, even though the parent connection works.

## User Impact

Nested protected HTTPS requests retain configured extra/system CA trust without losing the proxy's existing bundled roots in OpenSSL-CA mode. Certificate verification, exact-host secret bindings, and the emSign distrusted-root filter remain enabled. No new setting or migration is needed; a restarted process picks up the corrected trust bundle.

## Why This Change Was Made

I kept the existing startup trust owner, combining and deduplicating bundled roots with Node's exported default CA set for upstream TLS and the child bundle. Node omits the OpenSSL store from `getCACertificates("default")`, so replacing bundled roots with that list alone breaks public HTTPS under `--use-openssl-ca`.

The pr-simplify pass kept this additive fix without a new helper, flag parser, configuration, or fallback. Against main, production is +6/-4 lines and tests add 91 lines.

## Evidence

I reproduced the original nested-proxy failure on main `277b251bfa80c`. I also reproduced the review finding on the previous draft `a1e13524c432`: Node 24.22.1 returned zero default CAs under `--use-openssl-ca`, and a real public HTTPS request through the proxy returned **502 / UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY**.

On the final code, AWS Pond/Linux with Node 24.22.1 produced:

| Startup trust | Real proxy result |
| --- | --- |
| `--use-openssl-ca`, no extra CA | Public HTTPS 200 |
| `--use-bundled-ca` | Public HTTPS 200 |
| `--use-system-ca` | Public HTTPS 200 |
| OpenSSL-CA plus an extra private CA | Private HTTPS 200, protected synthetic credential verified |
| Bundled-CA plus an extra private CA | Private HTTPS 200, protected synthetic credential verified |
| System-CA with only the private system trust file, no extra CA | Private HTTPS 200, protected synthetic credential verified |

The two new real-process regressions both failed on the previous draft and passed with the correction. They verify the exported trust bundle with OpenSSL, covering both empty and extra-only default CA sets. The existing nested-proxy regression and emSign-chain rejection also passed.

**9 files, 128 tests passed**, wall time 54.31s. Core and affected-test typechecks, targeted lint, formatter parity, and `git diff --check` passed. Published head `517abe629f9f` has the identical tested tree.

[OpenSSL failure reproduction](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_d985c655f1505cc893f4bf202b0d2322) · [Live CA-mode proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_3d686a1d337b8be386cecfc420d5ab23) · [Final red/green regressions and checks](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_21ec7d2bb54e220fb3ea3ab28c12bfb6)

The live-proof run initially exposed an ambiguous test oracle that verified two same-named CA certificates. I corrected it to verify the inherited CA's issued leaf, then reran red/green proof and the complete selection without weakening the assertions. I released the AWS lease after verification.

**Limits:** This preserves the pre-existing bundled baseline in OpenSSL-CA mode; it does not enumerate OpenSSL-only trust entries that Node does not export. Independent/security-owner review remains outstanding: the earlier local autoreview was refused by its sensitive-path guard, which I did not bypass. Hosted broad CI, Bun runtime tests, non-Linux platforms, and a full Gateway/model run remain unverified. Hosted CI seconds are unavailable. I kept the PR draft as requested.

## Contributor credit

Requested and co-authored by Dan Riccio.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-nested-proxy-drops-ca-trust-s725e3d60)

## Worked on by

- @daniel-lxs

prs.title: fix: refuse root updates of a system service that runs as another account
prs.body:
Related: #204775

## What Problem This Solves

On Linux, a common layout is a root-owned global npm package with a systemd system unit that runs the Gateway as a service account (`User=openclaw`, state in that account's home or the unit's `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`). `sudo openclaw update` then exits 0 and reports success, but every safety step (candidate admission, the database snapshot, Doctor, the report) runs against root's own empty state, and the warning points at `openclaw update repair`, which as root changes nothing. With `sudo env OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<service state> openclaw update`, root writes into the service's state, the package can roll back onto a migrated database, and the unit stays down.

prs.title: fix: recycle MCP sessions rejected as invalid
prs.body:
Closes #200106

## What Problem This Solves

A streamable HTTP MCP server can reject an existing session with `invalid session`. OpenClaw kept sending later tool calls through that stale session, so GitHub-hosted MCP tools stayed unusable until the Gateway restarted.

## User Impact

When a stateful streamable HTTP server returns a 4xx response containing `invalid session`, the next explicit tool call now uses a fresh MCP session instead of remaining stuck on the rejected one.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared MCP session-expiry classifier now recognizes the reported invalid-session response alongside the existing stateful HTTP 404 signal. The failed call is still returned to the user and is never replayed; retirement and replacement use the existing lifecycle path.

## Evidence

The following is a redacted, inspectable trace from the production `createSessionMcpRuntime` against an isolated local streamable HTTP server. It records the MCP method, `mcp-session-id`, HTTP status, and response body.

```text
HTTP response status=400 session=s1 body=invalid session
error three SdkHttpError: Error POSTing to endpoint: invalid session
error four Error: bundle-mcp server "proof" is paused after repeated tool failures
{"initializeCount":1,"calls":[{"attempt":"one","session":"s1"},{"attempt":"two","session":"s1"},{"attempt":"three","session":"s1"}],"activeSession":"s1"}
```

Base keeps the rejected `s1` and eventually pauses; no replacement initialize occurs.

### Fixed `8f38a4530223a4e11c34b7747e53e3ec26e9de25`

```text
HTTP request method=POST mcp=initialize session=<none>
HTTP response status=200 session=s1 body={"...":"initialize"}
HTTP request method=POST mcp=tools/call session=s1 attempt=before
HTTP response status=200 session=s1 body={"...":"ok:s1"}
HTTP request method=POST mcp=tools/call session=s1 attempt=expired
HTTP response status=400 session=s1 body=invalid session
[bundle-mcp] recycling server "proof" after expired HTTP session
expired SdkHttpError: Error POSTing to endpoint: invalid session
HTTP request method=POST mcp=initialize session=<none>
HTTP response status=200 session=s2 body={"...":"initialize"}
HTTP request method=POST mcp=notifications/initialized session=s2
HTTP response status=202 session=s2 body=
HTTP request method=POST mcp=tools/list session=s2
HTTP response status=200 session=s2 body={"...":"probe"}
HTTP request method=POST mcp=tools/call session=s2 attempt=after
HTTP response status=200 session=s2 body={"...":"ok:s2"}
after { content: [ { type: 'text', text: 'ok:s2' } ] }
{"initializeCount":2,"calls":[{"attempt":"before","session":"s1"},{"attempt":"expired","session":"s1"},{"attempt":"after","session":"s2"}],"activeSession":"s2"}
```

Fixed retires `s1` after the 400 rejection, initializes `s2` only for the next explicit call, and does not replay `expired`.

## Verification

- The focused Docker proof passed with non-root, no network, read-only source, 256 MiB memory, 0.5 CPU, 64 PIDs, and 32 MiB tmpfs.
- The trace harnesses above exited 0 and exercised the production runtime over real local HTTP.
- `oxfmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and esbuild syntax checks passed for both changed files.
- The focused Vitest worker was SIGKILLed by the mandated 256 MiB limit before tests started; repository CI should run the committed regression. The local oxlint config could not load its Solid plugin from the offline dependency copy, so lint remains for CI.
- Independent read-only review of the complete `origin/main..HEAD` diff found no actionable P0/P1/P2 findings.

prs.title: fix(process): use glibc-compatible proc-safe bindings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On supported Linux hosts with glibc 2.28 through 2.32, OpenClaw 2026.10.10 and later can refuse every supervised child-process launch because the published `@openclaw/proc-safe@0.4.2` GNU binding requires newer GLIBC symbols than the host provides. The affected user reports in #191841 cover Gateway `exec`, CLI backends, and scheduled scripts on RHEL 8 compatible systems.

## Root cause

OpenClaw selects the native child owner from the runtime entrypoint, then `proc-safe@0.4.2` fails to load when its GNU binding requests `GLIBC_2.33` or newer. The failure happens before the command launches. Falling back to process-group supervision would weaken the native descendant-cleanup guarantee.

`openclaw/proc-safe#37` was merged and released as `proc-safe@0.6.0`. Its GNU bindings are built against glibc 2.28, so the existing native ownership and cleanup semantics remain in place.

## Change

- Update the OpenClaw dependency from `@openclaw/proc-safe` 0.4.2 to 0.6.0.
- Refresh the lockfile for all platform optional bindings.
- Keep the existing native process-owner path unchanged.

This supersedes the fallback approach in #191914 and preserves the cleanup contract called out by the maintainer.

## Evidence

The verification host reports `glibc 2.28`.

- Before, loading the 0.4.2 GNU binding fails with `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED: GLIBC_2.33 not found`.
- After, the 0.6.0 public API reports `loaded: true` for `linux-x64-gnu`.
- After, `readProcessAncestry` succeeds, `becomeChildSubreaper()` reports `isChildSubreaper() === true`, an orphaned child is observed through `inspectChildWaitState()`, and `reapChild()` returns exit code 0.

Targeted process-supervisor verification passed 6 tests across the Linux subreaper, relay startup, and native-owner suites.

## Packaged product behavior proof

The conflict-repaired candidate is `b588b3716733cb2107cdd3654a70546b91b56700`, based on current `main` `72b63a35495e8c030d4229db2696c852b537fb11`. Its `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` trees are identical to the previously reviewed `d2823b2ee5a8931826b2c9373a392d03ab8a532a` candidate. On the candidate worktree, the host reports `ldd (GNU libc) 2.28` and Node `v24.16.0`; a fresh public `@openclaw/proc-safe` probe loads `0.6.0` for `linux-x64-gnu` and reports child-reaper support.

The earlier real `openclaw agent exec --json` capture was run on the tree-identical `d2823b2ee5a8931826b2c9373a392d03ab8a532a` candidate. It launched a supervised command that created a delayed descendant, then the command was cancelled by the product timeout (`awaitResults=true`, `timeoutSeconds=2`, `yieldMs=1000`). A second real `exec` waited four seconds and checked the same marker path. Its captured output was:

```text
CLEAN
NORMAL_OK
```

The product command exited with `RC=0` and returned `ok: true`. The first tool call's timeout is the intentional cancellation step. The conflict repair changes ancestry only. The dependency tree remains identical to that proof. A fresh candidate-specific frozen offline install and native glibc 2.28 probe passed. No full test suite was run.

## References

- Fixes #191841
- Supersedes #191914
- Compatible native build in https://github.com/openclaw/proc-safe/pull/37

prs.title: fix(agents): persona disappears after large inline avatar updates
prs.body:
Related: #127507 (remaining identity/avatar path; the ordinary workspace editor limit was fixed separately).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent loses its persona and custom identity instructions after saving a supported large inline avatar.

## User Impact

A supported 2 MiB avatar stays available for display while the agent continues receiving its name, persona, and instructions before and after the avatar field. Stored identity and avatar bytes remain intact. Ordinary workspace files and projected identity text retain their 2 MiB limits. No configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model receives a text projection with the inline image omitted. Identity publication and raw sandbox copies use the existing bounded 4 MiB identity allowance. Raw files and prepared identity text share the existing cache byte budget.

The implementation follows the canonical bootstrap file reader and preserves parallel read settlement, prompt order, source identities, and live workspace revocation. Extra-file discovery moves unchanged into its own module to keep the existing oversized workspace module from growing, retaining main's complete-file glob matching.

## Evidence

**Review target:** `8c2519786a3812cbd3b7b681164df33c51ce8edd`, comparison base `27f243756a45f02724b70597803571e2f0e1d020`. [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42196349159), including the [test-line ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42196349159/job/127820963084) and [aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42196349159/job/127823558387), passed. GitHub associates those checks with this exact head; the CI execution used the merge commit documented below.

| Revision | Evidence and scope |
| --- | --- |
| Current `8c251978` | 13 focused tests across projection, raw sandbox copy, and bootstrap cache; production-source filesystem probe preserves persona and exact raw copy, rejects an oversized ordinary file, and checks managed glob selection. Current-head hosted CI passed. |
| Previous `3034a560` | 224 tests, one existing skip, core typecheck and typed lint passed. Its CI ratchet failed on inherited debt. The recorded full-index PR patch is byte-identical to the current patch; this does not make its CI green. |
| Historical `4fd20c3` | Built Gateway/agent CLI and real host-model generation preserved four persona facts with a 2 MiB inline avatar. Separate base/candidate probes demonstrated the original loader and copy failures. These executions belong to that historical revision. |

The current candidate's recorded full-range independent review covers all 15 changed files, including the discovery extraction, bounds, cache, and publication owners, with no actionable findings. Its retained full-index diff SHA256 is `c76627e0c35fe7241bf1818f41e63e98807af184814b6ca211de00941b8ade0b`. This description update adds no code or new test execution. The [November 11 hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173124#issuecomment-6192419182) now covers `8c2519786a3812cbd3b7b681164df33c51ce8edd`, with sufficient proof and no findings or before-merge actions. Its 4/6 proof assessment explicitly retains the historical-revision and model-bridge limitations below.

**Proof limits:** No full Gateway/model E2E was rerun on `8c251978`. The historical real-model proof used a manually orchestrated host-model bridge, not a genuine external Responses service compatibility test. Historical builds skipped declaration emission; skipped CI lanes are not build/test proof. The failed historical ratchets and unavailable local autoreview remain recorded below.

<details>
<summary>Retained verification records, commands/observations, and historical limitations</summary>

### Retained CI-repair verification (8c251978)

Candidate `8c2519786a3812cbd3b7b681164df33c51ce8edd`, base `27f243756a45f02724b70597803571e2f0e1d020`.

The previous hosted [run 42179630823](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42179630823) failed its test-line ratchet by 25 inherited lines; its aggregate gate failed for the same reason. The new base has 35 lines of headroom. This rebase applies the identical PR patch to that corrected base: no tests removed, no shared-budget increase, and the PR's existing exact 213-line allocation is unchanged.

Current-head local results in secretless isolation:
- Native test-line ratchet: **6,534,770 lines / 6,534,805 ceiling; 35 lines slack**.
- **13 tests passed across 3 files**: identity avatar projection, raw sandbox copy, and workspace bootstrap cache. The canonical runner retained its completed compiler cache; dependency bundler directive warnings were nonfatal.
- Formatting of all 14 applicable changed files and diff whitespace checks passed.
- Production-source filesystem probe: decoded avatar **2,097,152 bytes**, raw identity **2,796,289 bytes**, model-facing identity **85 bytes**; persona before/after preserved; raw sandbox copy exact; oversized ordinary file rejected; managed glob selected only `packages/core/IDENTITY.md`.
- Hosted [CI run 42196349159](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42196349159) **completed successfully**, including [baseline ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42196349159/job/127820963084) and the final [openclaw/ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42196349159/job/127823558387): 46 successful jobs, 30 skipped jobs. Skips are not counted as executed proof. Its actual merge `fc8aecc0d` combines this head with newer main `f6c70269845ce57772227801514d171d6c7c9642`; the native test-line gate reports **6,536,136 / 6,536,170, 34 lines slack**.

The prior head `3034a5608bb18de6dd60b47c99b1152229d49144` passed 224 tests (1 existing skip) across 11 files, core typecheck, typed lint and formatting. Those are prior-head results. Its hosted CI was not green because of the inherited 25-line deficit. The earlier real Gateway/model evidence below belongs to `4fd20c3`; it is historical evidence, not a new full Gateway/model E2E run on the current head. Selected current-head broad checks passed in the hosted CI run linked above; its skipped lanes, including build-artifacts, are not proof of a build or test run.

Fresh independent host-agent review of the complete 15-file committed range passed with no actionable findings. The review inspected current-base discovery extraction, raw/prompt bounds, cache and publication owners. Canonical full-index diff SHA256: `c76627e0c35fe7241bf1818f41e63e98807af184814b6ca211de00941b8ade0b`, byte-identical to the previous reviewed PR patch. Local autoreview remains unavailable as described in the historical evidence; no successful run of that tool is claimed.

### Historical behavior proof (previous head)

Historical validated candidate (before the CI repair): `4fd20c3236043d4090b7e56bd7fa261a5134954c`, based on `6b9a762375a4044ce7b69a626fa13d36c8f63738`. The exercised source tree is `7b65a7a8d7f77fd857869a90d2a2b9c57a86fb51`; the dirty candidate diff SHA256 is `6fbf623f75c8252beef335d43c1f11b2947fe6c2ec383443d9ce473815901cbc`.

- Historical focused tests: 224 passed and 1 existing/configured skipped across 11 files (124 Gateway + 100 agent tests), including prompt-prefix stability, managed/local reads, and file-publication boundaries. The canonical runner completed both serial shards in 290.94 seconds.
- Production core typecheck and all 29 affected canonical test-consumer typegraphs passed.
- Formatting, typed lint for all 13 changed TypeScript files, file-line-cap, and diff whitespace checks passed. Test-line accounting has the inherited failure described below.

Historical local test-lines result before this repair (superseded by the passing current-head result above): 6,434,192 lines against a 6,433,276 effective ceiling, over by 916. This PR adds 213 net regression-test lines and a separate allocation of exactly 213 for local/managed projection, raw sandbox copying, cache accounting, publication refusal, and alias bounds. The shared scalar is unchanged. Subtracting this PR's test growth and allocation leaves the same 916-line debt on the pinned base; this was an attributed inherited failure, not a passing gate at that old revision.

The supported built-CLI path passed (`node scripts/run-node.mjs --help`, 308.8-second cold build; declaration emission was skipped, so this is not full release-package/DTS proof). Its build input signature matched the exercised candidate. A normal built Gateway and agent CLI then produced:

```text
decodedAvatarBytes=2097152; persistedIdentityBytes=2796357
agents.update=ok; identity+roster avatar/name readback=exact
primaryResponsesRequests=1; personaMarkers=4; inlineAvatarInPrompt=false
providerReplyReturned=true; agent.wait ended=true; activeSessions=0
```
