prs.title: fix(update): stop using foreign recovery records as admission
prs.body:
## Class: foreign updater records must not grant admission

Instances: #203486, #205736, #203917, and the modern release route refusing an old unfinished recovery.

The release preparation owner now takes its existing lock, checks the installation and physical restore guard, then records other unfinished runs as `failed: interrupted` and continues. It preserves its current run and the serving trial's handed-over run. The bounded drain reads current rows, not an enclosing Doctor snapshot.

In modern release preparation, the two recovery refusals remain: a positively live in-place lease holder, and `.openclaw-restore-*` that may contain the original state. Current modern locks/trials and normal preflight still apply.

## What disappears

- The 808-line interrupted plugin-cohort settlement owner, its run/finalize/repair discovery and replay paths, and obsolete killed-driver/death-proof suites.
- Foreign saved-row permission for plugin peer links, snapshot collection, interruption/reconciliation and terminal capture. Foreign cohort rows remain unchanged; another update does not replay their rollback.
- The critical-path retained-runtime census and its timeout branches. Existing owned-release path collection runs after ready; Doctor retains its separate old-runtime cleanup.
- Current mutation and Gateway completion read only their named pair. Main's existing all-row admission reader is retained only by the shipped package-finalization bridge, as the accepted fallback below.

Current source/executor/lifecycle/transaction/finalizer checks remain. Explicit repeated repair uses its existing abandonment and exclusive-ownership checks, not a foreign stored-recovery veto; it does not replay the saved cohort. Snapshot collection defers only inside this operation's existing live publication capture, preserving its rollback bytes without consulting foreign records. The shipped `finishInterruptedUpdate` export keeps its real staged finalization, pinned as a source build entry because the compatibility inventory names it.

No new state, flag, timer, death proof, schema/stored shape, or launcher/Gateway protocol change. Doctor-compatible reads remain for legitimate current cross-build bookkeeping, not foreign admission.

**Accepted legacy edge:** package-only finalization retains main's `recoveryAdmission` worker, coherent facts and assertion on its selected service/history roots. The schema-refusal/copy-cost cleanup is not redesigned here. Ordinary readiness guards keep their original no-recovery early return; modern release admission remains physical-only.

## Size

`tokei` on this PR's 39 runtime source files, excluding tests/support/harnesses and fixtures, against merged main `1e6d3f9bd9ecdbb061908ed30090bcf2fd6d7c2f` (original before-code base: `5c815265d5281c7929ab7483bd4e471e54e5c0ff`):

| | Before | After | Net |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Production code lines | 11,335 | 10,365 | **−970** |
| Test/support lines | | | **−2,465** |

Tooling routing/inventory and the update implementation contract are updated with the cut; their deletions are not counted as runtime savings.

## Verification

- Current head: `63010e7d0af9c6cb5e6b03bcdc4ce5e5b07d390e`, tree `800914ece7b1c639760b7c95dd7d3af89e478a92`. Runtime is identical to `95f7a34700d5`; the latest change only removes this PR's foreign-cohort seed/assertion/imports from the legacy healthy-caller test, matching the accepted fallback. Original persistence/publication/transport checks and all revocation cases remain. Package-finalization selected/history paths retain main's original admission; modern physical-only admission stays cut. Normal commit/merge hooks passed. Exact-head CI and maintainer delta review remain pending; **no head-green claim yet**.
- Corrected AWS Linux base proof: seven selected contracts, **six meaningful failures and one terminal-history control pass**. A pre-repair repeated-repair comparison selected two positive cases; both failed meaningfully. This supersedes the initial host-only baseline, which is not counted as Linux proof.
- AWS `747bd654fa01`: **145 passed, two skipped** across nine files; core/core-test/scripts/tooling types, changed lint/format and dead-export scans passed. AWS `9901b03a6ae4`: **132 passed** across six affected files, including real snapshot rollback and CLI deadline integration; core/core-test types, scoped lint/format and dead-export scans passed. [Final run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_95deb2b3c2b56df85ff53e839750f5c5). These are qualified source snapshots, not exact `2dfc213fbdc6` proof.
- The final local identity ratchet could not resolve the original base object after normal synthetic-source sync; that is a setup gap, not a policy verdict. Current CI owns the ratchet and the later two-root schema repair. Both owned AWS leases were released with exact `stop --wait` receipts; no paid resource remains.

prs.title: fix(models): back off consecutive catalog expiry renewal failures
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** when a provider's model listing expires and its background renewal keeps failing, catalog discovery restarts with no delay. Only the first failure advanced the retry backoff: the failure counter in `createCatalogAttemptReporter` ran from a `beforeProviderFailure` callback that fired only when the failure *notification* was not deduplicated. Background (expiry) acquisitions set no pending scope, so every failure after the first was deduplicated, `discoveryFailures` stayed 1 and `expiresAt` stayed in the past. Each later expiry read started discovery again while the provider kept failing.
- **Fix:** the acquisition records its own failure. `acquireCatalog` records exactly one discovery failure per failed provider acquisition (worker recovery callback and rejection share one flag), then reports it. The reporter only reports; the `beforeProviderFailure` callback is removed. Notification dedupe is unchanged.
- **User impact:** a provider that keeps failing now retries at 30 s → 60 s → 120 s (capped at 30 min) instead of on every expiry read. Less CPU and fewer provider calls; no visible UI change.

Reported by @DonnieFi in #206097 (section 3). Split out of #206122; fix and regressions start from DonnieFi's branch commit 9620e47a48.

## Evidence

Two regressions, red on the merge base `fbba71f65223`, green on this head (vitest-source, `ocx test`):

- `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.pool.integration.test.ts` "backs off expiry reads across consecutive real worker failures" (real catalog worker pool, terminated workers). Base: `expected { discoveryFailures: 2, … }`, received `discoveryFailures: 1`.
- `src/gateway/server-chat-metadata-lifecycle.catalog-renewal.test.ts` "backs off consecutive expiry renewal failures instead of spinning at 0ms" (Gateway metadata lifecycle with fake timers: 1 → 2 → 3 failures at 30 s / 60 s, one broadcast). Base: same mismatch.

Head: those two files plus every test file that imports the changed sources (27 files) pass.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: in-memory retry bookkeeping only; no stored state, config or published contract changes. A revert fully undoes it. Blast radius: catalog discovery retry timing for providers whose listing fails.

prs.title: fix(memory): start default index managers at Gateway boot
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#194164 asks for memory indexing to be fresh right after a Gateway restart:
with the current demand-driven cold start, an agent's index opens on its
first search, flush, or turn, and until then `memory_index_sources`
receives nothing — the reporter observed roughly ten hours of stopped
indexing after an app relaunch.

The original draft of this PR restored eager boot-time indexing for every
configured agent. Review and history showed why that is the wrong default:
#167756 started Memory Core's index service eagerly on every Gateway start,
and #174718 (`6c050f8043`) deliberately reverted it after startup peak RSS
rose from ~1.1 GB to ~1.8 GB (startup catch-up touches every
session-transcript read lane, each spawning its own worker isolate). This
revision keeps that policy intact and adds an explicit operator opt-in
instead:

```jsonc
// memory.search.coldStart
"demand" // default — exactly today's behavior, unchanged
"eager"  // open every configured agent's index at boot and on later service starts
```

Each agent can override the global default with
`agents.entries.<id>.memory.search.coldStart`; the per-agent value wins over
the global setting in both directions, matching how the memory config
resolver treats other `memory.search` fields. Operators who need fresh
indexes immediately (the reporter's local-GGUF fleet) pay a known,
self-inflicted cost; everyone else sees zero change. The demand default, the
`liveIndexing` retention semantics, and the worker/RSS characteristics of
#174718 are untouched.

## The Change

- `memory.search.coldStart` (`"demand"` default | `"eager"`), registered in
  the config schema, field labels/help, and `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`.
- `memory-core-index` service start resolves the opt-in per agent:
  `resolveAgentConfig(cfg, agentId)?.memory?.search?.coldStart ?? global`.
  `"demand"` (effective) keeps `retainMemoryIndexingAgents` exactly as
  before; `"eager"` opens the agent's index through the existing host-aware
  runtime (`memoryRuntime.getMemorySearchManager`, which supplies the host's
  local-service acquisition — resolving the Revision 1 P2 finding). Manager
  construction marks each agent live, so later reloads retain them like any
  watched index.
- Boundary tests on untouched agents (so acquisition cannot be explained by
  prior demand): a per-agent eager override under a global demand default
  opens only that agent; a per-agent demand override under a global eager
  default keeps that agent lazy. Both fail against the previous
  global-only selector.

## Evidence

- **Unit/boundary tests** (worktree, committed source): `extensions/memory-core/index.test.ts` — 35 passed (2 new per-agent cold-start boundary cases; the previous single eager case was rewritten on untouched agents per review), and `src/config` schema regressions (config.schema-regressions, dead-config-keys, schema.hints) — 263 passed after registering the new field.
- **Regression check:** the two new boundary cases fail on the previous
  global-only selector (2 failed | 33 skipped) and pass with the per-agent
  resolution (35 passed).
- **Live redacted output, built from the committed source** (isolated
  state/workspace, local Ollama `nomic-embed-text`, synthetic data; the same
  state is upgraded in place between scenarios):

  ```text
  ===== SCENARIO 1: coldStart demand (default) =====
  gateway ready (demand)
  # memory file written + chat.send delivered, 45s watcher window, no consumer opens an index
  demand: memory_index_sources rows = 0

  ===== SCENARIO 2: upgrade in place -> coldStart eager =====
  gateway ready (eager)
  # same state, settings and sessions intact, 45s after boot, no consumer call
  eager: memory_index_sources rows = 2
      memory|memory/proof-demand-note.md
      sessions|sessions/main/34d590f2-28ad-4c95-91df-bda672a78c92.jsonl
  eager: memory_search -> {"ok":true,"results":[{"path":"memory/proof-demand-note.md",...
  ```

  Scenario 1 confirms the demand default is byte-for-byte unchanged
  (untouched agents stay lazy). Scenario 2 is the reporter's requested
  behavior, available under the explicit opt-in.

- **Latest-stable → candidate upgrade trace (redacted live output):** a
  dedicated run upgrades a state directory created by released
  **v2026.11.3** (npm, `847611d`) to the candidate built from this PR's
  head, covering both the upgrade-compatibility and data-model items:

  ```text
  ## PHASE S — stable v2026.11.3 (847611d), config without any coldStart key
  [stable] consumer memory_search -> {"ok":true,...}   # demand: index opens on first consumer
  [stable-final] memory_index_sources rows: 2          # memory/upgrade-note-a.md
  [stable-final] memory_index_chunks rows: 2           # + sessions/main/ff028686-….jsonl

  ## PHASE C-MIG — candidate refuses unmigrated DB (documented admission guard), then migrates
  "…uses schema version 27; … run openclaw doctor --fix to upgrade it to
   schema version 42 …" | gateway.maintenance_required
  $ openclaw doctor --fix --yes    ->  schema_meta primary = 42
  [post-migration] memory_index_sources: 2  memory_index_chunks: 2   # data survived

  ## PHASE C-A — candidate on migrated stable state, config UNCHANGED (demand default)
  booted healthy; memory_search retrieves the stable-era note
  [candA-final] memory_index_sources: 2                 # demand unchanged: no boot-time growth

  ## PHASE C-B — only delta: memory.search.coldStart = "eager"
  # new file written, then boot with NO consumer call
  [candB] rows BEFORE boot: sources=2 chunks=2
  [candB] rows AFTER eager boot: sources=3 chunks=3     # note B indexed at startup
      memory|memory/upgrade-note-a.md                    # stable-era data intact
      memory|memory/upgrade-note-b.md                    # newly indexed at boot
      sessions|sessions/main/ff028686-….jsonl            # stable-era session intact
  consumer memory_search("Post-upgrade synthetic") -> upgrade-note-b.md
  ```

  Existing settings are preserved (the stable-era config carries no
  `coldStart` key; the candidate boots it unchanged under the demand
  default), the stable-written database migrates via the documented
  `doctor --fix` path and loads/works (schema 27 → 42, index rows,
  session transcript, and provenance intact), demand semantics are
  unchanged after upgrade (no growth without a consumer), and the opt-in
  eager mode works on the upgraded state.

  Data-model note: this change adds an optional config field only — no
  stored index, session, or state format changes; the trace above
  demonstrates the stable-release upgrade end to end.

### November 24 conflict refresh

Integrated upstream main `4708bac52397` into `04af0f2c2c3`. Only the two generated config baselines conflicted. Regenerated both using `pnpm config:docs:gen`.

- `pnpm config:docs:check`, scoped formatting, and `git diff --check` against the integrated main passed.
- Memory Core startup and config schema suites passed, 64 tests across two files.
- The live upgrade traces above are from earlier revisions. This refresh validates the integration with current main. The opt-in startup policy remains open for maintainer review.


### Generated baseline refresh

Integrated upstream main `328a43818a1` in `4114126f480`. The generated hash conflict is resolved by regenerating from the integrated configuration. The generated core hash matches the previous PR head, and the plugin hash matches current upstream. `pnpm config:docs:check` passed and all 64 Memory Core and config schema tests passed.

### November 27 configuration baseline refresh

Integrated upstream main `6089b804582` at `5835496e1f5` and regenerated both configuration baseline artifacts. The combined and core hashes now include the startup option. The channel and plugin hashes match upstream.

- `pnpm config:docs:check`, scoped formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- All 64 tests in the Memory Core startup and config schema suites passed.
- The stable-release upgrade trace above predates this integration. The opt-in startup policy still requires a maintainer product decision.

prs.title: improve: remove the address bar from the link reader
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The link reader that opens pull requests, issues and commits beside the chat puts a browser address bar above every document: Back and Forward, the item's URL in an editable field, a new-tab button, Refresh, a link to the original, and a menu. It takes a full row of a narrow panel, and its main parts go unused. Links in chat already open in their own reader tab, so the URL field and the history buttons serve only a link followed inside a document, and the document header right under the bar already names the item.

Originally stacked on #203982. Now targets `main` after that PR merged.

## User Impact

The document starts one row higher, and the reader has one way to move between items: tabs.

- **Document header:** Refresh and the link to the original (for example **Open on GitHub**) are two icon buttons at the end of the header's first line.
- **Links inside a document:** a link to another supported item opens in its own tab, as a link in chat does. A link to the same item, such as a comment anchor, stays in its tab. Back and Forward are gone.
- **Refresh outcome:** a failed refresh, or a notice that the item changed, shows as text where the date was, in the same line. It used to sit behind a tooltip and a menu.
- **Empty tab:** the tab strip's **+** opens an empty tab with a URL field, as before. This is the only place where a URL is typed.
- **Removed:** the **Copy link** menu item. The link to the original still offers the browser's own copy action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Vyctor's review of the redesigned reader: the bar at the top does not earn its place, since new links open new tabs; only the link to the original needs a new home.

Decisions worth a reviewer's attention:

- **One item per tab.** With no address bar there is no visible way back from a link followed inside a document, so that link opens a tab instead of replacing the document. The per-tab history, its 30-entry bound and the `newTab: false` routing exception are removed; a tab now holds one target.
- **Actions live at the top of the document, not in a fixed row.** Refresh and the external link scroll away with the header. Refresh still keeps the reading position; the browser tests dispatch the click for that reason and say so.
- **A notice outranks the reference.** In a phone-width panel the header's first line cannot fit both, so the reference truncates and the notice keeps its width. The row height never changes, so the title below does not move.
- **Two strings changed** to fit their new place: the "item changed" notice is shorter, and the screen-reader text for a refresh in flight reads as a sentence.

Known limits: opening the reader from the Chat side panel's **+** menu for the first time does not focus the URL field (unchanged). Typing the URL of an item that is already open in another tab loads it in the empty tab instead of selecting the existing one (unchanged; only links deduplicate).

Size against #203982: production TypeScript +80 −247, styles +37 −109, tests +85 −145, docs +18 −16.

## Evidence

Same reader panel and document in the preview bench (simulated Gateway, dark theme), at 820 px and 400 px. Before is #203982 at `f8e3071c4803`; After is this branch.

**Before**

![Before: an address bar with Back, Forward, a URL field, new tab, Refresh, a GitHub link and a menu sits above the document](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c93c578d-fe6e-4a1d-9592-7e3a12bd4f8f)

**After**

![After: the document starts under the tab strip, with Refresh and Open on GitHub as two icons at the end of the header's first line](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f5196781-ac6b-4b31-bdf6-8a91d02a06ff)

At 400 px:

**Before**

![Before, 400 px: the address bar takes a row and truncates the URL](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/35d690e2-64c1-4b77-9be0-97b5cc0408d8)

**After**

![After, 400 px: the header's first line holds the state, the reference, the date and the two actions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4888188c-31af-4042-9b87-dbbb5b947da3)

Checked on the final commit: reader panel, content and routing tests; the GitHub panel, checks, loading, refresh and Activity browser tests. The refresh browser test now uses a realistic reference and asserts, at 1400, 820 and 390 px, that the failure notice is fully visible and that the title keeps its position. Lint for the touched files, the style lint, UI typecheck, format and the i18n check are clean. Local autoreview of the commit before the copy pass found no P0–P2 issues; the later changes were wording, two strings, the notice's width rule and its test.

Gap: layout shift was not re-measured against a real isolated Gateway for this change; the header row's height is unchanged, and the mocked-Gateway browser tests cover the title's position.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```
pnpm test ui/src/components/link-reader-panel.test.ts ui/src/components/link-reader-content.test.ts ui/src/app/link-reader-routing.test.ts
pnpm test ui/src/e2e/github-panel.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/link-reader-checks.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/link-reader-loading.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/link-reader-refresh.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/activity-session-git.e2e.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:ui && pnpm ui:i18n:verify && pnpm check:control-ui-controllers
pnpm exec stylelint --config config/stylelint.config.mjs "ui/src/components/link-reader-*.css"
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep live replies responsive after directive-bearing output
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI live replies re-parse the full accumulated response after a settled `[[audio_as_voice]]` directive, managed `MEDIA:` line, or runtime-context block. The repeated parser work grows quadratically with reply length and runs on the Gateway event loop.

A shipped-projection probe at 16 KiB measured about 24.4 s for the settled audio path, 28.8 s for managed media, and 195 ms for runtime context. The same work scales with each later delta until the live buffer cap is reached.

This links the cumulative media transform to #185298 and keeps the shared cases for the broader streaming-pipeline audit.

## User Impact

Long Control UI and webchat replies that contain audio directives, managed media, or copied runtime context no longer progressively stall live updates. The repaired media and runtime paths complete at 64 KiB in roughly 250-400 ms instead of continuing to grow with every delta. Final visible text remains the same across CRLF, protected blocks, Markdown code spans and links, coalesced deltas, replacements, and prepared-source recovery.

No configuration or public contract changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime-context filter now uses one shared linear streaming adapter in both Gateway projection and user-facing filtering. It recognizes complete delimiters and carrier preambles, withholds partial delimiter tails consistently with the canonical preview, and delegates to the canonical scrubber only when syntax can still alter ownership.

Managed `MEDIA:` lines are detected when they complete. After removal, ordinary prose is appended directly when Markdown ownership cannot change. A new `MEDIA:` line or a syntax checkpoint re-enters the canonical parser. The audio path similarly extends a settled visible result while preserving code ownership and replacements.

The follow-up repairs the ClawSweeper boundary findings:

- Partial-delimiter withholding now derives the visible prefix from the canonical sanitized result, so a previously removed runtime block cannot be restored.
- A provisional protected opener is rechecked when later bytes prove that the line is ordinary text.
- Audio ownership is invalidated when an unfinished code span closes around a raw directive marker.
- Terminal projections use the non-streaming runtime filter, so a valid final `<` is released.

## Evidence

- Running Gateway proof used a 46,222-byte reply containing runtime context, a current runtime carrier, an audio directive, and managed media: 176 `agent` events and 170 `chat` events, 221,244 bytes of `chat` payload, 46,931 ms send duration, 19 ms event-loop-delay p95, and 7,057 ms max delay.
- The same proof found no runtime context, current runtime carrier, audio directive, or private managed-media path in `chat` events.
- 165 focused Gateway, agent, runtime-context, directive, and sanitization tests pass, including every-prefix parity and one-character deltas.
- `git diff --check`, targeted formatting, targeted Oxlint, and `pnpm tsgo:core` pass.
- Full core lint remains blocked by inherited `max-lines` errors in unrelated files. The independent autoreview helper ran for more than 40 minutes without producing a report, so it provides no clean verdict.

Closes #185298.
Related: #184473.

## What Problem This Solves

The Swedish Control UI translation memory still contained 115 user-facing English or unnecessarily anglicized strings. This updates shared labels for support, skills, automatic mode, online presence and the popular plugin category, improves wording for patches and heartbeat monitoring, distinguishes reading in UI resources from downloading files, normalizes Git terminology to the established Swedish words *incheckning* and *pull-begäran*, and standardizes visible plugin terminology as *tillägg*. The latest batches replace visible uses of “Skills” with *färdigheter* in the library, agent overview, search, navigation, filter, catalog, learning and configuration views; use *tillägg* in visible labels, help and messages without changing technical paths or commands; replace remaining visible Git uses of “commit” with *incheckning*; and use Swedish macOS names for System Settings, Screen Sharing and Remote Management. Technical paths such as `skills.*` remain unchanged. The shared labels are used by multiple views, so the change also keeps terminology consistent with the native-app catalogue.

## Evidence

- Updated JSONL records parse successfully.
- Hunspell-sv recognizes the ordinary new Swedish words; the latest batch reports only the product name `OpenClaw`. svlang finds no anglicisms; its combined-input V2 warnings are false positives caused by concatenated UI fragments.
- A focused Gitleaks scan of the introduced values found no secrets. The full generated catalog contains opaque record hashes that make a raw standalone Gitleaks scan unsuitable.
- `l10n-lint` does not currently support this translation-memory JSONL schema, so it was not presented as a passing check.
- Existing catalog wording supports `Färdigheter`, `Stöd`, `automatiskt`, `Anslutna`, `Frånkopplad`, `incheckning` and `pull-begäran`.

Built-app runtime screenshots are attached in the PR conversation. The paired English/source and Swedish/current-head images show the real Plugins and Skills routes served by an isolated loopback Gateway.

The latest follow-up translates five visible Control UI status and support labels: Get support, offline duration, device-offline status, and the active/idle presence states. It uses the established terms Stöd, Ansluten and Frånkopplad. JSONL parsing, Hunspell-sv, svlang and a focused Gitleaks scan of the delta pass. l10n-lint does not support this translation-memory JSONL format.

Four more visible offline messages now use Frånkopplad or the natural phrase utan anslutning. Session interpolation and count placeholders are unchanged. JSONL parsing, Hunspell-sv, svlang and focused Gitleaks pass for this delta.

One additional visible configuration-help entry now uses Tilläggs-ID and ägartillägg. Configuration keys and commands remain literal. JSONL parsing, Hunspell-sv, svlang and focused Gitleaks pass.

Update: normalized the remaining short, user-facing plugin labels to Swedish “Tillägg” across the tab, tool source, plugin panel, and plugin-app catalog. This adds five shared records (eight visible placements) without changing configuration keys, command names, or identifiers. Focused JSONL parsing, Hunspell-sv, svlang, and Gitleaks checks pass. The archive is updated: https://github.com/yeager/translations/blob/main/openclaw/2026-11-15/ui.md . Additional runtime screenshots are attached in the PR conversation; they show English/source labels alongside Swedish translations from the current PR head.

Follow-up: standardized ten user-visible plugin-installation status and error messages to use “tillägg”, including download, file preparation, dependencies, retry, and availability. Focused JSONL parsing, Hunspell-sv, svlang, and Gitleaks checks pass. Archive: https://github.com/yeager/translations/blob/main/openclaw/2026-11-15/ui.md .

Follow-up: completed the remaining short visible plugin-page wording in this review pass: catalog loading, compatibility notices, ClawHub search, and UI capability descriptions now use “tillägg” consistently. prs.title: fix(gateway): hold remote model catalog publication during plugin drain
prs.body:
Closes #178396

**AI-assisted: yes.** Authored by an AI coding agent; every check below executed in this checkout.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a plugin reload can start after remote model-catalog adoption has passed its initial replacement wait but before pricing/discovery finishes. The serialized publication commit validated owner identity, generation, refresh state, and candidate plugin availability, but not the plugin replacement drain — so it could publish catalog owners for a generation that was already retiring.

## User Impact

Model catalog publication no longer adopts remote catalog data into a plugin generation whose replacement already started. The prior catalog and dispatch stay visible; the replacement generation (or the next catalog update check) publishes after the drain releases. No duplicate publication, no blocked queue.

## Why This Change Was Made

The commit effect boundary in `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.configured-refresh.ts` now revalidates `host.getPendingReplacement()` immediately before staging/publishing and throws the existing `PreparedModelRuntimePublicationSupersededError` instead of committing. It never awaits the drain, so the publication queue stays live; staged candidates are retired in `finally`, and existing owner-identity/generation/auth checks are untouched. This restores the effect-boundary check that `PR #162301` had and `PR #170626` deliberately simplified away.

## Evidence

```text
# red on base (-t "revalidates the plugin replacement boundary")
1 failed | 2 passed | 9 skipped — expected 'published' to be 'superseded'
# green with fix (full file)
12/12 passed
# related suites
plugin-drain 7/7; hot-reload-dispatch/catalog-owner/owner-supersession/reload-auth 75/75
```

Regression cases: no drain → published; drain released before commit → published; drain pending at commit → superseded with the prior catalog held, then retried after release. Checks: oxfmt, oxlint (0/0), `git diff --check`, mock-factory ratchet — pass.

**Real-process evidence (shipped entry point, both arms).** The guarded span is `publishPreparedModelRuntimeOwnerBatch` → `prepareModelPricingContext` → `loadFullModelCatalog`; the last step runs live provider discovery. Using the bundled ollama catalog hook (real HTTP `/api/tags` + `/api/show`) pointed at a deliberately slow local stub widens that window to ~24 s, past the ~2.9 s plugin-reload preflight:

```text
19:11:07.204 [gateway] Plugin replacement queued behind 2 retained work item(s) for plugin ollama
19:11:26.268 [gateway] remote model catalog check superseded; deferred to the next check
19:11:26.346 [gateway] Plugin replacement applied: ollama
```

Reproduced twice at this head. Control with the same slow discovery and no reload publishes normally (`remote model catalog applied`), which isolates the drain as the cause. The post-release retry is covered by the test in this PR rather than the live run (after release the revision was already current, so the retry returned `unchanged`).

**Retained rows / final recovery (product surface).** After the drain released, `openclaw models list --json --all` still showed the previous generation's overlay (`proof479c-alpha`/`beta`) while the DB held v2 — the supersede discarded the publication, not the download. Recovery through the same surface (`models list --refresh` with no drain pending) then produced 14 rows with a kimi overlay of 5 = 4 manifest rows + exactly 1 remote row (`kimi/proof479c-gamma`) matching the served inventory, and zero old-generation rows. Control with identical slow discovery and no reload gives the same shape via `proof479c-epsilon`. Timeline: served `21:36:52` → drain queued `21:37:04` → superseded `21:37:18` → applied `21:37:51`.

**Known local gap.** `tsgo` cannot run in this worktree (symlinked `node_modules` guard); CI runs `check-prod-types`.

prs.title: fix(gateway): recover session previews past long hidden transcript tails
prs.body:
Part of #127630

**AI-assisted: yes.** Authored by an AI coding agent; every check below executed against this checkout.

## What Problem This Solves

`session.preview`/Talk show an empty preview when a short visible history sits behind a long tool-only (non-projectable) transcript tail. On current main the readers already read bounded tail pages (64 events / 1 MiB, then 1024 / 8 MiB) instead of materializing the whole transcript — but the recovery page stopped at 1,024 events, so a visible history behind a longer `toolResult` tail exhausted the window, the projection produced no items, and `sessions-read` published `status: "empty"`. The same widening loop was duplicated in three places.

This PR adds the final ceiling-sized window and stops widening when the previous page was limited by bytes rather than events, so a byte-capped recovery page no longer re-reads the same 8 MiB tail.

## User Impact

Session previews and Talk model context recover the newest visible messages instead of showing an empty preview (or reading unbounded history) for sessions with long tool-only tails. Short histories and small limits behave exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

- New `src/gateway/session-transcript-preview-bounds.ts` owns one bounded widening policy with explicit `SESSION_PREVIEW_SCAN_MAX_EVENTS = 2048` and `SESSION_PREVIEW_SCAN_MAX_BYTES = 8 MiB` ceilings: a small page, a recovery page, and a final ceiling-sized page, stopped early when the requested count is reached or no older events remain.
- The shared policy also stops before a window that cannot make progress: if the previous page selected fewer events than its event cap, the byte budget stopped it, and a next window with the same byte budget would repeat the same tail.
- The exact selected-row count comes from the bounded active-context hydration result (`selectedEventCount`, excluding the session header and injected boundary events) and is carried to Talk through an internal bounded-selection record. Every bounded hydration producer reports it: SQLite, actor-backed incognito history, and the empty-memory snapshot. `SessionManager.onTruncated` stays `() => void`, so this adds no public SDK callback surface. Display and incognito readers report their selected-event counts directly.
- The display preview reader, Talk model-context reader, and incognito in-memory history path all use the shared policy instead of three copies of the old 1,024-event loop.
- Projection stays on the bounded page (`buildSessionPreviewItems`); output shape and ordering are unchanged; the sync reader handles display/incognito, the async reader handles Talk.
- The new module is listed in `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt`, so the trusted-anchor PR wrapper inventory stays closed over runtime imports.

## Evidence

Regression tests prove the base/fixed split (64 visible rows + 1,500 `toolResult` rows, limit 12):

```text
base reader (1,024-event recovery): status "empty", items []
fixed: newest 12 visible rows (visible 52-63)
Talk model context, limit 16: base [] / fixed newest 16
incognito memory preview: base [] / fixed newest 12
incognito model context (actor-backed hydration), limit 16: base [] / fixed newest 16
byte-capped recovery: stops after [64, 1024] windows instead of repeating 8 MiB
byte-capped Talk page (header + 1,023 selected rows): windows [64, 1024];
  a header-inclusive count regresses to [64, 1024, 2048]
hidden tail beyond the ceiling: [64, 1024, 2048] windows, no unbounded scan
```

Local checks on head `f80d0b291`:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/config/sessions/session-actor-transcript-replica.test.ts
  -> 1 file, 16 tests passed (typed Bounded fixture now reports selectedEventCount: 2)

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json --noEmit --incremental false
  -> passed

git diff --check -> clean
```

The removed helper-only `session-transcript-preview-bounds.test.ts` window-count cases are covered by the production reader regressions in `server.sessions.preview-resolve.test.ts` (explicit tail scan ceiling, and Talk byte-cap stopping) and `session-transcript-readers.memory.test.ts` / `session-actor-memory-history.test.ts` (incognito recovery).

### Real behavior proof

#### 1. Display preview (`sessions.preview` RPC)
Isolated state dir, 64 visible assistant rows + 1,500 `toolResult` rows seeded through the session accessor, local Gateway started from the repo CLI entry with `gateway.mode=local` and auth `none`, then the public RPC:

```text
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway call sessions.preview \
    --params '{"keys":["main"],"limit":12,"maxChars":120}' --port 39481 --json
{
  "previews": [{
    "key": "main",
    "status": "ok",
    "items": [
      { "role": "assistant", "text": "visible 52" },
      ...
      { "role": "assistant", "text": "visible 63" }
    ]
  }]
}
```

#### 2. Shipped Talk entry point (`talk.client.create` RPC)
Tested through an isolated Gateway on an ephemeral port with an isolated voice provider registered (`createBrowserSession`). Both scenarios executed end-to-end through `openclaw gateway call talk.client.create`:

**Scenario 1: Byte-capped stopping (durable session)**
64 visible assistant rows behind a 5 MiB row and 1,023 ~4 KiB rows (exceeding the 8 MiB page budget before event limit). The 8 MiB recovery page is byte-limited below its 1,024-event cap, so the policy stops early instead of repeatedly re-reading the 8 MiB tail; 0 items produced for Talk context:

```text
$ openclaw gateway call talk.client.create --port 39485 --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:byte-capped"}' --json
[gateway] [talk.client.create -> createBrowserSession] initialItems count: 0
[gateway] [talk.client.create -> createBrowserSession] initialItems sample: []
[gateway] [ws] ⇄ res ✓ talk.client.create bytes=259
{
  "provider": "test-talk",
  "transport": "webrtc",
  "clientSecret": "proof-ephemeral-secret",
  "model": "test-model",
  "voice": "alloy",
  "voiceSessionId": "<uuid>"
}
```

**Scenario 2: Hidden-tail visible history recovery (durable session)**
64 visible assistant rows behind 1,500 `toolResult` rows (exceeding the old 1,024-event cap). The recovery policy widens through the 2,048-event ceiling window and recovers the newest 16 visible items into Talk context:

```text
$ openclaw gateway call talk.client.create --port 39485 --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:hidden-tail"}' --json
[gateway] [talk.client.create -> createBrowserSession] initialItems count: 16
[gateway] [talk.client.create -> createBrowserSession] initialItems sample: [
  {"role":"assistant","text":"visible 48"},
  {"role":"assistant","text":"visible 49"},
  {"role":"assistant","text":"visible 50"}
]
[gateway] [ws] ⇄ res ✓ talk.client.create bytes=259
{
  "provider": "test-talk",
  "transport": "webrtc",
  "clientSecret": "proof-ephemeral-secret",
  "model": "test-model",
  "voice": "alloy",
  "voiceSessionId": "<uuid>"
}
```

In-memory incognito recovery through `readTalkRealtimeInitialItems` on the shipped session-actor storage binding (64 visible assistant rows + 1,500 `toolResult` rows):
```text
caller: readTalkRealtimeInitialItems (invoked by talk.client.create)
scenario: 64 visible + 1500 toolResults; limit=16 items / 8,000 bytes
count=16
items=[{"role":"assistant","text":"visible 48"}, ...,
       {"role":"assistant","text":"visible 63"}]
```

**CI note.** `check-test-types` passes on this head (the typed `Bounded` fixture fix). `checks-node-changed` is red on `test/gateway-openai-compaction-replay.e2e.test.ts:102` (`"Continue from the compacted transcript"` split length 2 vs 3). The identical failure is present at every head that ran that job (`301269dec`, `6005d42a9`, `89de4013f`, `f80d0b291`), the failing test is not modified by this PR, and its retry path (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/terminal-resolution.ts`) is untouched by this diff; the last behavior change there is #178192, merged before this branch's base. Main pushes skip the node CI jobs (verified: node checks are `skipped` on recent `main` check runs), so a same-job main comparison is not available; the repo's own `test:ci-failed` classifier reports `[unknown] No matching job on main` for this job. The failure is deterministic across heads, so a retrigger is not expected to change it. Treat this check as inherited/unattributed, not caused by this change.

**Residual risk / boundary.** A tail longer than the 2,048-event / 8 MiB scan still yields `empty` with no truthful truncation field — surfacing truncation needs a preview result-shape change and is deliberately out of scope here. Byte-heavy tails can stop at the 8 MiB page budget below 2,048 events, and the policy now stops there rather than re-reading the same tail. Oversized single rows remain omitted by the existing SQLite reader; filters needing history older than the ceiling cannot recover. The linked issue's remaining truthful-truncation contract is why this PR is `Part of` rather than closing it.

prs.title: feat: choose where automations run
prs.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Do not land.** Still in progress and under discussion. Talk to @vyctorbrzezowski.

Co-authored by [Vyctor Brzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bfb77f08-1fd2-461f-ada5-4f3ff81fa044)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/2fa4bdf2-6cf6-4471-9df7-8c95bf40f48e)
- [Conflict repair and focused local verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-automations-cleanup-prs-s0ac320b6)

## What Problem This Solves

The automation editor offers Main and Isolated, but it can’t create an automation that continues a selected conversation. The team-server audit found 221 of 312 automations already use that kind of target.

## User Impact

- **New session each time** starts a fresh run. Enable **Include recent chat** to give it recent context without continuing the source transcript.
- **Continue a conversation** lets you pick a conversation, including the agent’s main conversation.
- Doctor backs up cron state, then converts `current` jobs to new sessions with recent chat while preserving their linked workspace and sandbox. It converts `main` jobs to the owning agent’s main conversation. If a target can’t be mapped faithfully, Doctor retains the job, pauses it, and reports why. Existing isolated and explicit conversation targets keep their placement. After a direct upgrade, run `openclaw doctor --fix` before relying on old jobs.

## Why This Change Was Made

A fresh run and a continuation are the two execution choices. Recent chat is a setting on a fresh run, not a third place to run. The editor, CLI, Gateway, and automation tool use the same two targets.

This draft overlaps the sibling cleanup that retires `main`/`systemEvent`, especially in the Doctor migration, payload validation, scheduler routing, editor, and tests. This change keeps the system-event payload working with an explicit conversation until that sibling removes it. Other automation editor and delivery cleanups may touch the same files.

## Evidence

I merged main at `fc25865d99bd0166efbe6f70d93df979e68e19ac` without rebasing or rewriting history, resolved the conflicts, and fixed the nine ClawSweeper findings. I also completed the affected consumer-test conversions after main's refactors and retained CLI system-event defaulting to an explicit main target.

I reproduced both migration defects before fixing them. The persisted Doctor regression uses execution hashes captured with main's real storage serializer. It checks valid authority rebinding, unchanged stale captures, preserved placement, and idempotence. The effective-agent regression fails before the repair and passes afterward.

I ran 42 focused test files locally, without a VM: 964 cases across the selected suites. After correcting the failures, I reran every failing file and the affected migration/notification suites on the final code; all passed. Core and UI typechecks, scheduler/Doctor/Gateway test typechecks, targeted production lint, UI copy validation, formatting, and the PR diff whitespace check passed. The broad selected run took 571 seconds; the final two-file rerun passed 39 tests in 133 seconds. CI duration is not measured.

I ran pr-simplify on this repair: I reused the existing agent resolver and Doctor repair path, retained runtime admission checks, and replaced duplicate binding coverage with an explicit-conversation case. No new runtime compatibility reader or execution-policy bypass was added.

Local autoreview was unavailable: the configured Codex installation could not execute inside its read-only reviewer sandbox. I did not broaden reviewer permissions or request a hosted re-review. This PR remains draft under the existing do-not-land hold.

prs.title: fix(failover): classify Claude Code org-disabled subscription notice as auth_permanent
prs.body:
Closes #206216

## What Problem This Solves

When an organization disables Claude subscription access for Claude Code, the CLI fails every turn with the message "Your organization has disabled Claude subscription access for Claude Code." OpenClaw classifies this as `reason=unknown` because the message does not match any existing auth-permanent pattern. Chat then shows a generic failure notice instead of telling the user their login is not accepted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `HIGH_CONFIDENCE_AUTH_PERMANENT_PATTERNS` array in `message-patterns.ts` already matches "not allowed for this organization" as a permanent auth failure (403). The Claude Code organization-disabled notice is an equivalent permanent access denial — the same login cannot succeed until an admin re-enables access or the user switches to an API key — but the exact wording was not in the pattern list. Adding it ensures `isAuthPermanentErrorMessage` returns true, so `coerceToFailoverError` classifies the failure as `auth_permanent` and the existing 403 failure contract applies.

## User Impact

Scripts and users that encounter an organization-disabled Claude Code login will see the existing "isn't accepting your saved login" guidance instead of a generic "couldn't finish this reply" error. Model fallback decisions will record `reason=auth_permanent` rather than `reason=unknown`, making logs and diagnostics actionable.

## Evidence

### 1. Shipped CLI run via Gateway

A stand-in `claude` executable emits the exact org-disabled notice to stderr and exits 1. The shipped OpenClaw CLI (`node scripts/run-node.mjs agent --agent main --message "test" --json`) was run with the Gateway on port 19001 (build `c3e38eb`, `~/.openclaw-dev` state, `auth=none`). The stand-in was on PATH ahead of the real claude.

Terminal output (head-green, fix `c3e38eb`):
```
$ openclaw agent --agent main --message "test" --json
Claude Code process exited with code 1
{
  "ok": false,
  "runId": "935b7145-d44e-4ba1-a128-1e979ef4b417",
  "origin": "gateway",
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Claude Code process exited with code 1"
  }
}
```

Gateway log captured the stderr and the terminal failure:
```
[agent/cli-backend] cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-4 durationMs=2283 runId=935b7145... error=Claude Code process exited with code 1
stderr (process-wide; may include earlier turns): Your organization has disabled Claude subscription access for Claude Code · Use an Anthropic API key instead, or ask your admin to enable access
```

The shipped CLI's JSON output does not expose `reason`/`status` fields — the failover classification is consumed internally by the embedded agent runner for fallback decisions and `recordTargetUnavailable` (see `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-entry.ts:587-596`). The terminal output is identical between base-red and head-green because the classification only affects internal routing, not the CLI's external error response.

### 2. Failover classification via shipped function

To demonstrate the classification change, the stand-in's stderr was captured via `execSync` and fed through `createCliExitFailoverError` — the same shipped function `execute-process.ts` (line 631) calls with `candidates: [stderr, ...]`.

**Stand-in stderr:** `Your organization has disabled Claude subscription access for Claude Code · Use an Anthropic API key instead, or ask your admin to enable access`

| Field | Before (origin/main) | After (fix `c3e38eb`) |
|---|---|---|
| `reason` | `unknown` | `auth_permanent` |
| `status` | `undefined` | `403` |
| User-facing copy | `Couldn't reach claude-cli with any of your saved logins right now.` | `claude-cli isn't accepting your saved login.` |

The base-red run used `origin/main`'s `message-patterns.ts` in the same worktree; the head-green run used the patched file. No other files changed between runs.

### 3. Unit tests

`npx vitest run src/agents/failover/classify.test.ts` — 43 tests passed including the new `auth_permanent` classification case.

prs.title: fix(vydra): require distinct Kling motion references
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The native Vydra Kling adapter rejected video references and sent its image URL as both `image_url` and `video_url`. Motion control requires a character image and a distinct motion video.

## User Impact

Use the existing typed `inputImages` and `inputVideos`: exactly one remote HTTPS image and one distinct remote HTTPS motion video. Missing, buffered, duplicate, extra, credential-bearing and unsupported audio references fail before upstream I/O. The existing Models create and original-job GET flow stay intact. Veo3 remains text-only.

Kling advertises motion support with model-specific image/video limits, while image-only generation is disabled. The shared video runtime already supports mixed references through its typed video-to-video capabilities; no SDK input type or model family is invented.

## Why This Change Was Made

This corrects the frozen and current native client against the [primary Kling schema](https://www.vydra.ai/docs/models/kling) and the published contract in https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/586 (landed3b75c3a9eaabaf927314ec9cf35c3164e4528de6). No Worker, manifest, pricing, credentials or controller changes are included. ClawRouter `vydra.model_video_create` activation still requires qualified schema/runtime support on the existing `vydra.jobs` lifecycle, preserving the original model/create route and GET-only controls.

Release-note context: Vydra Kling motion control uses the supplied motion video instead of reusing its image reference, with truthful per-model capabilities and early unsupported-input errors. CHANGELOG.md is release-owned; user docs and the plugin README are updated here.

## November 25 live-test repair

Signed head `2793bd85574e142c34571ea177530e0a42bbb05d` updates the existing live test and both live-testing guides. Kling now gets separate, overridable character-image and motion-video URLs. Selecting Kling explicitly runs that motion test once. Veo3 retains its text-only input.

A credential-free replay of the actual live-test callbacks and registered adapter reproduced the previous rejection before submission. The updated callbacks passed with the default media and with both URL overrides. The replay captured the request at the generation boundary. The public defaults responded with a 2752×1536 PNG and a 10.04-second H.264 video. Native pre-commit and targeted formatting passed. Hosted CI passed all 15 Vydra video-provider tests, the documentation check, production and test typechecks, and the test-line ratchet. [Provider test results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45572080138/job/139061988443) · [Test-line results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45572080138/job/139061988538) The follow-up adds three net test lines and three lines of budget in the existing allocation. Live Vydra submission and billing remain untested on this head. [Kling request contract](https://www.vydra.ai/docs/models/kling) · [Public fixture source](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/kling-video/v3/standard/motion-control/api) · [Current checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192028/checks)

## Earlier adapter qualification

- Earlier signed candidate `7c25de1886304bceda3dd6ab1cfa3ea3001ddbe3`, tree `52d408e88d0711188fcf2ba3ade16b994412e7f6`, used frozen product base `21d44cf768fe94ec1d502bf4a88aadd1ae054a4f`.
- The retained native workflow now qualified a private physical frozen installation and ran the registered provider fixture: all 15 tests passed. They cover distinct Kling POST references, original-job GET, Veo3, download bounds and eleven pre-I/O rejection cases.
- Extension TypeScript checks, focused typed lint, and `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` passed on that exact source. The package/SDK build completed in 214.7 seconds. Previously qualified formatting, syntax, whitespace and privacy checks remain unchanged-source evidence.
- [Historical manual CI 41665867852](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41665867852) is failed: 229 successes, 21 failures, 2 cancellations and 11 skips. Its workflow head is `a4d32afaaa320f0efb3616ee67174908b952a44a`. It is not current-head passing evidence; no failure is waived or reclassified.
- Historical native line-budget proof remains visible: base 6,436,159 / 6,436,092 is 67 over; candidate 6,436,224 / 6,436,157 is the same 67 over. The separate 65-line allocation exactly covers this regression coverage and remains unchanged. Fresh native qualification must resolve the actual required gate; no allocation padding or unrelated deletion.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45572080138) passed on `2793bd85`. The [changed-extension job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45572080138/job/139061988443) ran all 15 registered video provider cases, including submission of separate Kling image and motion references, rejection of buffered inputs before transport, and retrieval of the original job. Both required CI contexts passed. Normal native landing admission remains. No paid generation was performed for this verification.

prs.title: fix: notify parents when child runs die in a Gateway crash
prs.body:
Closes #206422

## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway crash can leave a timer subagent marked running with delivery pending after restart. Its yielded parent never receives the interruption, even though the child process is gone.

## User Impact

Restart settles the original child as failed and tells its parent. Saved work remains available; child execution is not replayed. No configuration, schema, or permission changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

I reactivated the existing registry sweeper after restoration and scheduled it when fresh requester custody resumes a dead child. Crash settlement also records an empty terminal reply, preserving any previously recorded terminal reply, instead of waiting for output from a dead executor. The existing completion and authorization owners remain responsible for delivery.

## Evidence

- I reproduced main `fbba71f65223e` on AWS CrabBox: the original run remained `running` / `pending` after SIGKILL and same-state restart. [Failing run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_9abfbd63c399a4d9d80130f8e3e34b48).
- The regression now passes for SIGKILL and graceful SIGTERM: original run becomes `terminal` / error, delivery becomes `delivered`, parent receives exactly one interruption, and child inference is not restarted. Two cases took 46.6 seconds, 87 seconds including the test harness. [Final checks](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_60f9dd49cdd2c446dee01321213987cf).
- 37 focused recovery, refusal, collector, and settlement tests passed. Production and test typechecks, targeted lint, and formatting passed.
- I ran pr-simplify: no new recovery owner, state, or API; the production change is 10 additions and 2 deletions.
- I also ran the real OpenAI model through spawn, a live timer, parent yield, SIGKILL, and same-state restart on AWS CrabBox. The timer process was gone, the original child became `terminal` / error with delivery `delivered`, and the parent replied `CRASH_NOTICE_RECEIVED` 16.9 seconds after restart began. [Live proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_a591dc4c43bffb752fdb060cace4ef5b).
- An earlier live setup timed out before the timer started. The diagnostic rerun passed without a product-code change; that earlier setup failure remains unexplained.
- Local autoreview could not execute in its required read-only sandbox. I did not broaden permissions. Hosted review, full CI, and non-Linux platforms are not yet verified.

Worked on by:
- Dan Riccio

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-child-stuck-running-after-crash-s3e668b52)

## Worked on by

prs.title: feat: let doctor --fix tell when its config writers have nothing to save
prs.body:
Related: #204775

## What Problem This Solves

Every `openclaw doctor --fix` stops a healthy Gateway before it knows whether any step has work. The plan in #204775 makes that stop conditional once every step can say "nothing to do" and mean it. The two config writers (`doctor:write-config-migrations`, which saves what the config flow prepared, and `doctor:write-config`, which saves later edits and runs the post-write repairs) had no check, so they always traced the default `work`.

This PR also records what the config flow itself really touches on a healthy install, measured rather than read from source, because the earlier source count (about 50 conditional sites and 9 always-firing ones) was the reason it was left at the default.

## User Impact

None yet. Every `--fix` still stops the Gateway and runs every step and repair as before. With `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE=1`, the two writers now report their real decision:

| Contribution | Healthy install | With real work |
|---|---|---|
| `write-config-migrations` | `pending=none check=owner` | `pending=work` when the config flow prepared a write (seeded: the agent roster removed from `openclaw.json`); the write still happens |
| `write-config` | `pending=none check=owner` | `pending=work` for an edited config, a recorded model retirement, a queued auth-profile or Phone Control cleanup, or cron rows the post-write repair would rewrite |
| `config-flow` | unchanged, `pending=work check=default` | unchanged |
| `skills`, `final-config-validation` | unchanged, `check=default` (see below) | unchanged |

## Why This Change Was Made

Each check is built from the plan its runner writes, so the trace and the write cannot disagree.

- `planConfigWrite` (the pending config write, provider renames, and the "config edited since the last save" comparison) and the initial-write gate moved into `doctor-health-contribution-runners.config-plan.ts`; `runWriteConfigHealth` and `runInitialConfigWriteHealth` now call them instead of computing the same values inline.
- The cron post-write repair ran its planning inside `applyLegacyCronStoreRepair`. That planning moved into `cron/legacy-repair-plan.ts` (`planLegacyCronStoreRepair`), together with the repair state types so the plan stays a leaf module; the repair consumes the plan and writes only when it says `changed`. The one moved type assertion (`cfg.cron` read as a record) became `asOptionalRecord`, so the assertion baseline for `legacy-repair.ts` shrinks by one. The check runs the same plan on a read-only load (`loadLegacyCronRepairState({ readOnly: true })`), the same load the cron health finding already uses. Both moves also keep the two files under the 700-line cap.
- A refused write (`configWriteRefusal`) has nothing to do (`none`); a committed-write failure, which the runner rethrows, is `undecidable`. Read-only config and the legacy update handoff still answer `work` when a write is planned, although the runner then skips it; that over-reports and never under-reports.

**Not converted here:**

- `skills`: building the skill status (`buildWorkspaceSkillStatus`) publishes plugin skills into `~/.openclaw/plugin-skills`, so a check that builds it is not read-only. A check needs that publication split out first.
- `final-config-validation`: its config read records config health observations (`observeConfigSnapshot`) when the file changed. The "would this observation change anything" plan lives inside that function.
- `config-flow`: see the measured list below. What it still touches on a healthy install sits in the legacy state migration graph, which the `legacy-state` contribution also drives, so its plan split belongs with that owner rather than a second copy here.

No schema, stored field, config option, protocol, dependency, retention or permission change.

## Update behavior

No update-path change. A published updater that runs Doctor on this build runs the same writes and repairs in the same order; only the trace lines differ.

## Evidence

### What the config flow touches on a healthy install (measured on base)

Linux cell, systemd user Gateway, npm install, config with a Telegram channel and the bundled `memory-core`, `browser`, `active-memory` and `llm-task` plugins, two settling runs first. Two healthy `doctor --fix` runs ran under `strace -f` plus a harness-only preload that records every write-intent `fs` call and every `node:sqlite` open, write and `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` with its calling frames, windowed to the `doctor.config-flow` span. Stores were snapshotted (bytes, inode, mtime, SQLite rows) and compared against a plain Gateway restart.

- **(a) Bytes changed:** nothing that a plain Gateway restart does not also change. The one row the flow writes is `agent_databases.last_seen_at`, which every Gateway boot rewrites too. `openclaw.json`, the agent database rows and the credentials store are unchanged.
- **(b) Opened or locked a shared store, changed nothing.** All but one sit inside `autoMigrateLegacyState` (`cli.bootstrap.legacy-state-migrations`, 1.7 to 3.7 s):
  - `prepareOpenClawStateDatabaseSchema` → `repairStateSchemaAsync` opens the state database read-write, takes the schema lease (4 inserts, renewals and deletes in `state_leases`) and 13 to 14 `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transactions, runs `DROP ... IF EXISTS` no-ops, and opens the quarantine store and `client/credentials.sqlite` read-write under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`.
  - `migrateAgentDatabase` opens the agent database read-write (3 `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`) and invalidates its clean-close seal.
  - `detectLegacyDeviceIdentity` → `readStoredDeviceIdentityReadOnly` opens `client/credentials.sqlite` read-write; a read path that takes the writable custody handle.
  - Outside that graph: the preflight's `state-write-admission` opens `openclaw.sqlite` with `r+` on every run to prove the file is writable.
- **(c) Scratch private to Doctor:** read-only snapshot copies under `~/.cache/openclaw/sqlite-*` (create, copy, remove).

The source audit was wrong about several sites. The Tailscale step opens nothing. The plugin capture directories under `~/.openclaw/tmp/plugin-captures` are made by the Gateway at boot, not the flow. No media persistence or cold navigation lease was taken on a healthy run; the leases seen are the schema leases above. None of the roughly 50 conditional sites wrote. The state-schema claim was right in effect, but the writable open comes from the migration graph's own schema preparation, not from the preflight's `state-schema` step (that one reuses the startup receipt).

A first cell had `discord` and `diffs` configured, which cannot install under an unpublished version. In that state every run also ran `npm view` six times and rewrote `migration_runs` row `deferred-plugin-migration:discord`: it is reopened as pending in `converged()` and settled again in `complete()`, under the plugin lifecycle lease and the `openclaw.json` source lock. That is real work each run while a configured plugin cannot be installed, and it is the only kind (a) site found.

Plugin-defined migrations: the contract already has a read-only answer. `detectLegacyState` returns a preview, and core migrates only plugins whose preview is non-empty (`collectPluginDoctorStateMigrationPlans`); a detector that throws is dropped with a warning, which a check would count as undecidable. No SDK addition is needed.


### Cells

Base is `main` at `c32abfe2a1a` (the fresh `origin/main` when this work started); head is `6ae2042addb` (this PR's first commit). Both are npm installs of a pack under an unpublished version. `measure-*` cells: the two healthy runs under the traces above, then a plain restart and one untraced run. `guard-*` cells (Telegram configured but disabled, so `/readyz` measures the Gateway rather than a channel that cannot log in with a fixture token): two healthy runs, then the agent roster is removed from `openclaw.json` while the Gateway serves, then `doctor --fix` twice.

| | base `c32abfe2a1a` | head `6ae2042addb` |
|---|---|---|
| `write-config-migrations`, healthy | `work check=default` | `none check=owner` (under 0.1 ms) |
| `write-config`, healthy | `work check=default` | `none check=owner` (227 to 267 ms untraced) |
| Guard: roster removed | config rewritten (1176 → 1270 bytes) | `write-config-migrations` `work check=owner`, same rewrite |
| Guard: next run | `openclaw.json` byte-identical | `none check=owner`, byte-identical |
| `config-flow` write-intent list | (above) | identical to base |
| Outage, healthy / work / clean (250 ms `/readyz`) | 22.7, 22.7 / 23.2 / 22.7 s | 27.5, 25.9 / 26.5 / 28.7 s |

The `write-config` check costs about 250 ms because the cron read goes through the read-only worker; the runner itself takes 33 to 45 ms. The check opens `openclaw.sqlite` read-only and nothing else (io trace). The 3 to 5 s outage difference is not from the checks: phases this PR does not touch grew by the same proportion on head (`doctor.maintenance.begin` +0.9 to 2.5 s, `doctor.maintenance.finish` +1.1 to 2.7 s), and the head pack was built from a newer `main`. Nothing is skipped yet, so the checks cannot shorten the stop in this PR.

Recordings replay the raw cell logs.

RED/BASE, `c32abfe2a1a`:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ade4564d-aba2-4892-b35b-f3e13c4f4967

GREEN/HEAD, `6ae2042addb`:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8358a804-f52d-4216-b001-625640cd7555

<details><summary>Raw evidence, base (home paths shortened)</summary>

```

cell measure-base: Linux, systemd user Gateway, npm install of pack 2026.11.26 c32abfe2a1a; config: telegram channel, memory-core, browser, active-memory, llm-task

---- doctor1: OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE=1 openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes (healthy install, strace + io trace)
  trace: doctor.pending.config-flow pending=work check=default (0.0ms)
```

prs.title: fix: let agents use short Workboard card IDs
prs.body:
Related: #206133

## What Problem This Solves

Workboard's CLI and `/workboard` display short card IDs, but agent tools reject those same IDs and force the agent to look up the full ID before retrying.

## User Impact

An agent can use the displayed ID to read, claim, comment on, or move a card. If the prefix identifies more than one card, the tool rejects it rather than choosing one. Full IDs, existing claim checks, and stored IDs are unchanged. No migration or configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse Workboard's existing exact-or-unique-prefix lookup for agent tools that target an existing card. Full IDs use the exact lookup first. Mutations use the resolved full ID and keep their existing permission and claim checks.

## Evidence

- On clean upstream source plus the two new regressions, both failed: a valid short ID returned `card not found`, and an ambiguous prefix returned that same generic failure instead of an ambiguity error.
- With the fix, **45 tests passed** across the Workboard tools, CLI, and slash command using the real SQLite test harness. The new tests exercise read, claim, comment and move with the short ID, a subsequent full-ID read, and rejection of an ambiguous prefix without mutation. Existing tests cover full-ID reads and claim enforcement.
- Targeted TypeScript checking, file-level Oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The repository's broader lint wrapper stopped while preparing SDK declarations in the cloud; file-level results are reported separately.
- The cloud Gateway runtime build completed on the tested source. The isolated Gateway then failed during startup with `listen EPERM` on a local Unix socket. No Gateway tool request or live model turn was exercised. This remains a draft; full upstream CI has not run.

### Shipped-entry-point proof (macOS, 2026-11-27)

Built the exact PR head and started the shipped CLI’s Gateway with a fresh temporary config, state, workspaces and Workboard SQLite. A real `deepseek/deepseek-flash` model ran seven agent turns through `openclaw agent` via the Gateway (no `--local`). The assertions checked the model identity, actual tool arguments and tool results from the SQLite transcript, and persisted state using the Workboard CLI. Only synthetic cards were used. The UI shows eight characters; a shorter real collision was used for the ambiguity case, while the regression test covers an eight-character collision.

```text
Exact PR head: 1953c848ded707edc6a0b3469f1f1621ae25f486; macOS; temporary state; only synthetic data; deepseek/deepseek-flash.
PASS: shipped CLI Gateway loopback /healthz
PASS: Workboard CLI displayed 852e62de for the synthetic card
PASS unique read: actual owner model called workboard_read({"id": "852e62de"}), exact matching card, status=todo
PASS unique mutation: actual owner model called workboard_comment({"id": "852e62de", "body": "Unique ID persisted marker"}), exact matching card, status=todo
PASS: full-ID CLI read confirms mutation persisted
PASS ambiguous read: actual owner model called workboard_read({"id": "8"}), result: Ambiguous card id prefix
PASS ambiguous mutation: actual owner model called workboard_move({"id": "8", "status": "ready"}), result: Ambiguous card id prefix
PASS: both ambiguous matches unchanged
PASS authorized claim: actual owner model called workboard_claim({"id": "852e62de"}), exact matching card, status=running
PASS claim protection: actual other model called workboard_comment({"id": "852e62de", "body": "Rejected synthetic marker"}), result: card is claimed by owner
PASS: non-owner write rejected; claimed card unchanged
PASS claim owner move: actual owner model called workboard_move({"id": "852e62de", "status": "review"}), exact matching card, status=review
PASS: authorized owner's short-ID move persisted; end-to-end validation complete
```

The macOS run closes the cloud startup proof gap above. The full upstream CI matrix has not run. No code or head change; leaving this PR in draft for the re-review.

prs.title: fix: stop forked subagents from seeing accepted spawns as aborted
prs.body:
Closes #206430

## What Problem This Solves

A child started with `sessions_spawn(context: "fork")` can receive `aborted` for the same spawn call its parent sees as accepted. The fork captures the call before its result exists, and ordinary history repair mistakes that missing result for an interrupted operation.

## User Impact

Forked children retain the parent's context and completed tool results. Unfinished calls are described as unavailable at fork time rather than failed. Actual tool errors are preserved. No configuration, schema, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fork snapshot now supplies neutral results for its unfinished tool batch, before the child continues. This fixes the producer without changing generic Responses repair, fabricating a successful spawn receipt, or modifying the parent's transcript. Selected-branch ancestry and subsequent child messages remain intact.

## Evidence

I used the repository CrabBox wrapper on AWS (`cbx_cec7a766059b`, Linux, 4 vCPUs, 8 GB), a real Gateway, and a live OpenAI Responses model on the embedded runtime.

- Main `288e52aab044f`: 2/2 captured forks contained `aborted` for an accepted parent spawn call.
- Fixed tree `9579c3364cb33a08d7a9177b513ae53a9a2f74dc`, published at `283f414e6fbac` (identical tested tree): 0/2 contained `aborted`; both children read the file and returned the inherited context marker and file marker. Each comparison captured 14 actual Responses requests.
- Both new regression cases failed on main with `isError: true` instead of `false`, then passed with the fix. They cover the ordinary branch and an explicit leaf with an opaque append parent, completed errors, parallel unfinished calls, unchanged parent history, and child continuation.
- All 59 tests in the five focused fork/prefix-stability files passed. The final committed tree's parent-fork file passed again: 11 tests, 52.55 seconds wall time, about 7.4 seconds test time. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Targeted oxlint passed with no warnings or errors; `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.config-cli.json` typecheck passed; format and `git diff --check` passed.

The live fixture exits nonzero during Gateway shutdown with `Native worker execution owners have not joined` on both unchanged main and the fix. I independently validated the retained before/after wire evidence; I am not calling the entire live suite green. Waiting for parent and child run-owner settlement did not clear that pre-existing cleanup failure.

Local autoreview could not start because the installed Codex executable failed its read-only sandbox preflight. I did not broaden permissions or substitute a self-review for an independent result. Hosted review remains unverified; the draft PR's substantive CI checks were skipped. Task abandonment did not occur in these captured samples; release and Codex-native runtime were not tested.

The pr-simplify pass retained the two-file owner-level fix: production +72/-4 lines, regression tests +77. No new state owner, configuration, or generic replay policy was added.

The AWS lease was released and inspected: `state=released`, `cleanupStatus=complete`, `provisioningResourceMayExist=false`.

## Contributor credit

Co-authored with Dan Riccio.
