prs.title: fix: keep models.json loading when one configured provider has no api
prs.body:
Related: #206097 (section 2)

## What Problem This Solves

One configured provider whose models have no `api` (for example a legacy `models.providers["google-antigravity"]` entry with only `baseUrl` and `models`) was still written into the agent's `models.json`. The model registry then rejected the **whole** file with `Provider google-antigravity, model …: no "api" specified. Set at provider or model level.` Every other provider in `models.json` stopped loading from it, and each catalog load logged the same warning again (about 118k lines a day in the report).

## User Impact

- Valid providers in `models.json` load again when one configured or discovered provider has no `api`.
- The provider that cannot load is left out of `models.json`, and its stale row from an older version is removed. OpenClaw logs one warning when `models.json` or a provider-plugin catalog changes, for example: `Model catalog omits a provider the model registry cannot load: Provider google-antigravity, model gemini-4-neon-high: no "api" specified. Set at provider or model level.` Catalog loads do not repeat this warning.
- Config stays valid. Users do not need a migration. Set `models.providers.<id>.api` to load that provider again.
- A provider that a user added only to `models.json` is never deleted. As on base, it stays in the file, and the registry reports it if it cannot load.

## Why This Change Was Made

The models.json planner (`isWritableProviderConfig`) and the registry (`validateProviderModels`) each had their own rule for a valid provider. The planner checked only `baseUrl` and `apiKey`. The rule now lives in one function, `findProviderModelsError` in `models-config.merge.ts`. The registry calls it through `validateProviderModels`, which throws. The planner calls it through `findUnwritableProviderReason` for every provider it builds (config, discovery, generated plugin catalogs) while it routes them to root or plugin catalogs. A skipped root provider also removes its stale row from the existing file, as a valid entry would replace it.

Decisions:
- **Entries that exist only in `models.json` keep base behavior.** `mergeWithExistingProviderSecrets` and its retention check (`isWritableProviderConfig`, now private) do not change. Deleting a user-authored file entry would lose data that exists nowhere else, and setting `api` later could not restore it. The issue's case is a config provider, which config rebuilds on every write.
- **Warning owner: the `models.json` writer, not Doctor.** Only the planner knows whether a provider plugin filled in `api` during normalization. A Doctor check on raw config would give false positives for plugin-owned providers (for example `models.providers.openai` with no `api`). The warning shows only when `ensureOpenClawModelsJson` changes `models.json` or a plugin catalog, so it appears once per change and not on each catalog worker run.
- **No `openai-completions` default in `models.json`.** The embedded runner still defaults a config provider with a `baseUrl` and no `api` to `openai-completions` (`resolveConfiguredProviderDefaultApi`). That runtime path does not change. To write this default into `models.json`, the planner would need a second copy of that rule.
- Accepted: the warning repeats whenever `models.json` or a plugin catalog actually changes, even for an unrelated change (a live `models list --refresh` on a host with live discovery logs it once per refresh). It does not repeat on catalog loads or unchanged rewrites.
- Accepted edge case: an `apiKey` that existed only in the old file row of a skipped config provider is removed with that row. The provider cannot load until `api` is set, and the key belongs in config or an auth profile.

## Evidence

- Base e9f9556bca5f, scratch profile, `openclaw models list --refresh` with the reporter's config shape (one provider without `api` plus one valid `openai-completions` provider): `models.json` contained `google-antigravity` with no `api`, and the log had `model catalog load issue: Failed to load models.json: Provider google-antigravity, model gemini-4-neon-high: no "api" specified. Set at provider or model level.`
- Head, same profile, starting from the base-written `models.json` (the upgrade case): `models.json` keeps only the valid provider. The log has one `… omits a provider the model registry cannot load …` line and no `model catalog load issue`. A second run added no new warning.
- Regression test `models-config.applies-config-env-vars.test.ts` › "omits configured providers the registry rejects and keeps the rest loadable": it plans `models.json` from a config provider with no `api`, with an old file row for it and a stale malformed row under a valid key. It then loads the planned contents in `ModelRegistry`. It fails on base (`expected [ 'valid', 'legacy' ] to deeply equal [ 'valid' ]`) and passes on head. "keeps a provider that exists only in models.json" checks that a rewrite does not delete user data.
- `models-config.model-input-presence.test.ts` and `test/openai-model-discovery-auth-order.test.ts`: their fixture providers had no `api`, so the registry would have rejected the `models.json` they produce. The fixtures now set `api`, as the real chutes catalog does.
- `ocx test` on the touched tests plus every test file that imports a changed module (15 files): all pass on the final head. `tsgo:core`, the core test-type shards, `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.other.json`, oxfmt and oxlint: clean. Earlier `check:changed`: the dead-export scan fails on `readUpdateDatabaseEngineConfig`, `DoctorContributionPending` and `formatUpdateSnapshotCapacity`. This PR does not touch those files.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the old behavior completely. The change writes no stored state beyond the regenerated `models.json` and makes no config, schema or protocol change. Blast radius: models.json planning and the registry's provider validation messages. The messages stay the same.

prs.title: improve: resolve the agent directory once for local model requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Preparing one local model request resolves and registers the same agent directory three times. Acquisition already owns the directory when it asks for tentative and metadata-backed model selections. Both selections repeat the directory lookup, and acquisition overwrites both results.

## User Impact

Local model preparation resolves the directory once. Model and profile selection, directory overrides, and standalone callers keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The internal selection request returns the routing fields it owns. Standalone selection still attaches its agent directory after it selects a model. Acquisition already attaches the directory it captured. The existing plugin scope key and post-callback workspace lookup remain in place for custom selection callbacks.

## Evidence

- The Node 24.22.1 source probe followed the public acquisition entry to the prepared-runtime lease with deterministic dependencies. Directory lookups fell from three to one, preserving the selected model and profile. Standalone implicit and explicit directory cases performed one and zero lookups respectively. Both acquisition variants computed two plugin scope hashes.
- In the native PR checkout on macOS ARM64 and Node 26.7.0, a synthetic fixture called the real directory resolver after initial registration. Median time for three versus one warmed lookups was 4.04 versus 1.34 microseconds for one agent (20,000 iterations per batch) and 24.71 versus 8.27 microseconds for 128 keyed agents with the selected one last (3,000 per batch).
- The repository’s native review test runner passed all 20 selection tests at the signed head. With the new test held fixed, the original selector failed its one-call assertion and Vitest recorded three calls to `resolveAgentDir`. The candidate passed normal acquisition, standalone override, missing selection, and implicit standalone resolution. The original source was restored to the signed head after the baseline run.
- Local ClawSweeper 0.3.5 reviewed the complete committed range `e13d41d3bd30..b3c4543f8d49` with medium reasoning. It reported no actionable findings, risks, or rank-up moves. Independent source review approved the same change.
- Pinned formatting, whitespace checks, and the repository’s type-aware lint wrapper passed on all three changed files. The local probe covers lookup cost. Device end-to-end latency was not measured for this patch.

prs.title: fix(streaming): stop rescanning settled reply state
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Issue #205935 shows that once `createInboundMetadataProbe()` activates, `createConditionalTextProjector()` calls `stripInboundMetadata(input.text)` for every later delta. The work therefore grows with the full accumulated reply on every update, including repeated JSON fence parsing, line scanning, active-memory handling, delivery-hint scanning, and trailing-context checks.

This change adds a bounded inbound-metadata stream projector that consumes completed metadata blocks once, retains only the current line or unfinished block that can still change, and appends settled ordinary text without canonicalizing the completed reply prefix again.

The same projector now handles the directly related streaming edge cases needed for safe append-only output. MiniMax scanning reports unclosed encoded envelopes and invocations so private tool arguments are withheld. Relevant-memory scanning reports an open memory block so private content does not pass through before the closing tag arrives.

Running the shipped Gateway path exposed a broader visibility defect. Gateway `chat` events previously bypassed inbound metadata, MiniMax, relevant-memory, and active-memory filtering, while raw `agent` events retained provider text. The live-chat projection now applies the user-facing sanitizer chain before publishing `chat` events. Raw `agent` events remain unchanged for diagnostics.

## User Impact

Long streamed replies that contain copied inbound metadata no longer perform cumulative whole-reply parsing after the metadata becomes settled. Visible output remains canonically equivalent at every streamed prefix, including split CRLF, U+2028, U+2029, unfinished MiniMax envelopes, and unfinished relevant-memory blocks.

Control UI and webchat `chat` streams no longer publish copied inbound metadata, MiniMax tool-call payloads, relevant-memory content, or active-memory content. An unfinished active-memory block stays hidden until its closing line is settled.

The inbound-metadata issue is #205935. MiniMax and relevant-memory handling are included because they share the bounded streaming projector and otherwise still require cumulative or unsafe provisional output when their markers activate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous probe correctly detected when canonical processing was still needed, but its active state never deactivated after metadata settled. Removing the probe without an output-equivalent incremental owner would leak or delay visible text at provisional boundaries.

The stream projector therefore keeps canonical output and event-loop work as separate requirements. It tracks the narrow mutable suffix, emits atomic replacements when that suffix settles, and appends marker-free suffixes directly. MiniMax and relevant-memory scans expose only the additional state needed to suppress unfinished private suffixes.

The ClawSweeper follow-up keeps an EOF active-memory closer provisional until its line is terminated and invalidates tag projections whenever Markdown ownership changes. The Gateway now shares the inbound metadata owner and applies the `live-chat` visibility profile while preserving its existing trailing-whitespace and partial-invisible-text behavior.

## Evidence

- Running Gateway proof emitted 157 `chat` events and 247,016 bytes of `chat` payload with a 57,798 ms send duration, 17 ms event-loop-delay p95, and 9,143 ms max delay.
- The `chat` events contained none of the injected inbound metadata, `MINIMAX_PRIVATE`, `MEMORY_PRIVATE`, or `ACTIVE_MEMORY_PRIVATE` markers. The underlying raw `agent` events correctly retain provider text for diagnostics.
- 325 focused inbound-metadata, shared streaming, MiniMax, Gateway chat-state, and marker-absence tests pass, including every-prefix parity, reversible active-memory closers, and GFM ownership changes.
- `git diff --check`, targeted formatting, and `pnpm tsgo:core` pass.
- Targeted Oxlint could not start in this sparse worktree because `tools/solid-lint/index.mjs` is absent, although `git ls-tree` records it in `HEAD`. Full core lint is also blocked by inherited `max-lines` errors in unrelated files.
- The independent autoreview helper ran for more than 40 minutes without producing a report, so it provides no clean verdict.

Closes #205935

prs.title: fix: allow CLI inference with an explicit auth profile
prs.body:
Closes #206121

## What Problem This Solves

CLI inference rejects an explicitly allowed model when `--model` includes an `@profile` suffix. This prevents selecting a particular account through the running Gateway without broadening the model allowlist.

## User Impact

The existing `provider/model@profile` syntax keeps its model identity for policy checks and selects the named credential for that run. Disallowed models remain blocked, and the stored session selection stays unchanged. No configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

I reused the existing profile-suffix parser and per-attempt credential selection rather than changing allowlist semantics or adding a new API field. The fix covers both separate provider/model fields and full model references.

## Evidence

- I reproduced the rejection through the real CLI and isolated Gateway on main `c32abfe2a1a4`. Both added regression cases failed without the fix.
- I rebuilt published head `c24c1d8b3d6c` on a fresh AWS CrabBox and verified its exact source. `pnpm test src/agents/command/model-selection.configured.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **39 passed**. Earlier focused tests, formatting, lint and typechecks passed on the same source.
- **The shipped-CLI multi-profile check passes.** I used the package's `openclaw.mjs` executable with two configured profiles: a deliberately invalid stored default and a working explicitly selected profile. The `@selected-proof` run exited **0** and replied `ok` through the Gateway. The selected profile's successful-use receipt advanced while the observed default-profile success/failure fields stayed untouched.
- I separately requested the invalid default. Its recorded error count changed from 0 to 1, then OpenClaw rotated to the working profile and returned `ok`, matching the [documented same-provider auth rotation](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/model-failover#session-stickiness-cache-friendly). I did not disable fallback or treat this intended behavior as a bug. The configured default, explicit profile order, stored user pin and complete config bytes stayed unchanged across both runs.
- The previous 502s were OpenClaw's standalone secret-egress controller dropping inherited CA trust, not CrabBox or the model route. A no-key probe reproduced `UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE` and HTTP 502 without CrabBox. The separate task-only repair preserves effective CA trust, TLS verification, destination restrictions and the distrusted-root filter; **138 security tests passed**. It is signed local commit `772cfc216c1b`, not included in this PR or deployed to the shared Gateway.
- [ClawSweeper's source review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206399#issuecomment-7210646376) passed on this head with no findings. prs.title: fix(runway): use valid model-specific Veo video durations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Runway's generic five-second default produced invalid Veo requests. Veo 3.1 and 3.1 Fast now default to four seconds and accept 4, 6 or 8. The legacy `veo3` model defaults to eight seconds and accepts only 8. Text and image requests use the same model-specific rules. Both the normal runtime and direct provider calls round fractional seconds before validation. Unsupported values fail before submission.

## Verification on the corrected head

- The [signed candidate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/94b89e44e24cb8f4d62b15b1f271ac93f6444af2) passed all 45 registered Runway tests and all 23 shared duration and runtime tests. Before each correction, four legacy-model cases and three direct fractional-duration cases failed respectively. Formatting, the changed-doc MDX check and the test-line ratchet passed. A fresh independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issues.
- Runway's published SDK specifies exactly eight seconds for legacy [text](https://github.com/runwayml/sdk-python/blob/3ae44e965e8a82d5044deb89e9747b392e47bbe2/src/runwayml/types/text_to_video_create_params.py#L307) and [image](https://github.com/runwayml/sdk-python/blob/3ae44e965e8a82d5044deb89e9747b392e47bbe2/src/runwayml/types/image_to_video_create_params.py#L413) requests. The [current catalog](https://docs.dev.runwayml.com/guides/models/) lists Veo 3.1 and 3.1 Fast. The legacy setting remains recognized. No paid generation was performed.
- `pnpm build` on the signed candidate exited 1 at the public SDK declaration budget, 5,396,987 bytes against 5,385,536 allowed. The unchanged baseline measured exactly the same size. The UI build phase completed on this candidate. The six UI overages below were measured on earlier builds. Native review retained the investigated local failure and published the candidate through ordinary GitHub-gated preparation.

## Scope

The native baseline refresh preserves the original provider fix, duration regressions and 31-line allocation while incorporating frozen `1ed570fb2b288299e2e2a99036d2b9b1e1953a3e`, including its polling/error handling and validation-input repairs. No provider activation, routing, credential or public SDK API change is included.

The code and build evidence below was collected at `15996e353ff22d9d9b8c01206ea469799e5a6e10`, tree `5b2267a14cf349c8347169e4c200267a226f9929`, ordered parents [`b01d76f2480c8d6c5c6b918a6fb71acdf3cfe17a`, `1ed570fb2b288299e2e2a99036d2b9b1e1953a3e`].

The subsequent [documentation correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3c08d2500021566e03599f7900e7ee6d62dcc47f) changes only the Runway provider guide. Its formatter and whitespace checks passed. On this corrected head, [all 38 Runway provider cases passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45944803567/job/140327462242), along with [the docs check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45944803567/job/140327462260) and both required CI checks.

## Earlier evidence on `15996e35`

- Own physical frozen install on Node 26.13.0/pnpm 12.15.0/macOS arm64; all five dependency inputs unchanged.
- Registered provider tests: 38/38 passed, including the 15 original default/explicit-duration/pre-egress regressions plus current polling, errors, auth and deadlines. Wall time 82.995s; Vitest 75.79s, 94% cold transformation. The cases need the registered provider and request/deadline orchestration; direct duration-helper assertions would not prove submission and denial behavior. HTTP is mocked; this is not live-provider or Worker proof. Current hosted file timing is pending.
- Production extension and owning test type graphs passed in 18.150s/24.363s. Focused lint passed in 121.547s including first declaration preparation; format and whitespace passed.
- Test-line ratchet passed: net +31, 400-line allowance, existing 31-line allocation unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes valid delayed uploads failing when a tunnel request reuses an idle upstream HTTP connection.

## User Impact

A fragmented first body frame no longer leaves the upstream socket idle until its previous keepalive deadline closes it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Flush request headers after response/error handlers are installed and before waiting for DATA. Keep authentication, framing limits, and timeout policy unchanged. The regression observes the request head on the same warmed socket before releasing the body.

## Evidence

- The retained exact-source regression failed on the original code and passed with this patch; 51 focused tests and a real seven-second reused-socket upload passed at that earlier pin.
- The patch applies cleanly to current base 232ba9a63de6912b613aa7aa00ec0e0bbf9e7f99; formatting hook and `git diff --check` pass.
- Local autoreview (GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2) found no actionable issues in the two-file patch. Simplification review retained the two-line production fix and one behavior regression.
- Exact-head hosted regression passed: the request headers arrived on the same warmed socket before releasing the first DATA payload; the upload then completed with its expected body and HTTP 200. The peer-isolation and GET/HEAD/DELETE/OPTIONS/TRACE framing cases also passed. [Boundary regression results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44048071123/job/133919506075). Production types, test types and lint passed in the completed CI run below.

prs.title: feat: review spoken self-corrections before adding dictation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related: #205645

Dictation can leave an original phrase and its spoken correction in the unsent draft, such as “Meet on Tuesday sorry Wednesday.” This draft now tests a narrower behavior: retain and optionally review the words the recognizer actually provided, without guessing which words to change. It also keeps received dictation when the browser–Gateway connection drops in the same conversation.

**This is still a draft for design acceptance and client qualification.** Whether original-only review should ship with a saved preference, and whether eventual correction support should be built in or plugin-owned, remains open.

## User Impact

**Spoken corrections** defaults to **Off**. The optional **Review original (corrections unavailable)** mode offers **Keep original** or **Cancel** after recording, with no production candidate or rewrite. **Literal for this recording** skips that review for one uninterrupted recording when its draft is still current. Neither review action sends anything. Choosing Off leaves existing draft text intact and restores ordinary raw dictation for future recordings.

The capture cannot change a sent message, run a tool, enter Talk, or replace a selection that predates the recording in review mode. A real destination, permission, or draft change still prevents stale insertion. The saved preference is scoped to the browser and Gateway; pending review text and Literal are not saved as preferences. There is no new public refinement contract or native-client integration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing capture and composer owners retain transcript text and check live pane, physical session, compose authority, capture identity, and both component and authoritative draft revisions before keeping an original. A review choice is consumed before handing text to the insertion owner. A temporary transport outage no longer masquerades as a destination change.

The unused edit-plan validator, preparer, and per-event recognition metadata are deferred. Only raw interim and final text, capture/draft ownership, and the original-only review are needed here. The [issue proposal review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205645#issuecomment-7178569403) was advisory, not product acceptance.

## Evidence

### Merged draft head: `8d399bf4575d40a12146b68616974b99defbcfa0`

The recognizer returned “go forward and mirrors.” The review showed that exact output; Keep original inserted it once into the previously empty draft, with zero send requests. The accuracy assertion did not pass; preserving the actual recognizer output did. This is recorded speech replay—not a physical microphone or a hosted provider qualification.

prs.title: fix(dictation): honor realtime transcription authority
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related: #205855.

Realtime transcription already requires a session to stop when its existing `assertCurrent` callback rejects. Deferred setup and inbound messages did not consistently honor that contract: a retired URL resolver could continue into credential preparation, and a provider message could reach capture, parsing, or transcript callbacks after authority was revoked. OpenAI client-secret creation also sends configured transcription hints before the WebSocket exists, so the HTTP dispatch needs the same assertion.

This PR repairs those existing transport boundaries. The broader P02 context-aware transcription feature remains unimplemented, and #205855 stays open.

## User Impact

Revoked or retired transcription work stops at the affected setup, HTTP-dispatch, and message-processing boundaries. Authorized sessions retain startup, queued audio, reconnect behavior, and delivery of their final transcript after Stop.

The patch adds no context source, setting, permission, RPC schema, migration, or audio-retention behavior. Configured OpenAI prompts are inherited behavior. Reverting this PR restores the previous transport behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair stays with the existing owners:

- The shared WebSocket session checks attempt settlement, generation ownership, closure, and current authority before URL work and again before deferred headers. A retired attempt cannot abort its replacement.
- Inbound messages check socket ownership and authority before capture, parsing, or provider callbacks, while preserving the authorized graceful-finalization window.
- The OpenAI transcription factory forwards its existing assertion to the private client-secret helper. That helper checks before preparation and at the guarded-fetch `beforeRequest` boundary after asynchronous DNS/transport preparation. The existing voice caller can continue omitting the optional private argument.
- The Gateway relay retains its existing publication checks.

The OpenAI authority regression replaces the earlier mocked fixture with a four-case test using the real OpenAI factory, shared session, guarded fetch, response parser, native HTTP, native hostname lookup, and a real local WebSocket server. It counts HTTP request arrivals before body completion and covers credential-await revocation, DNS-await revocation, revoked late-final delivery, and authorized startup/Stop/final delivery. Cleanup uses the existing test-port and fixture-cleanup owners; all imports cross the public extension SDK boundary.

The [issue review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205855#issuecomment-7186786824) still requests a maintainer decision on a composer-only per-turn contract, consent ownership, collection limits, and revocation semantics for already-admitted context-derived requests. This transport repair does not establish those new semantics. M11 (#205845), M10 (#205846), and P04 (#205852) remain semantic design dependencies for the feature; #191109 is an adjacent hints request, not a physical parent branch.

## Evidence

### Current head: `45971d0305bf`

- **Scripted audio through Chromium, the Gateway, and live OpenAI transcription: 6/6 passed** on `45971d0305bfaf4a7096d14ba7dbfe3e28b18b3a`. [Timothy Gregg’s #205876 job](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45942073519/job/140318633794) verified the source SHA, built the PR with `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` before secrets were exposed, and logged six passing takes. The [active-pane runner change](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/commit/6ee7fd5570d4232778fbd01464b7844d1595bc1a) is included unchanged in the workflow checkout `522c845a52a4`.
  - `live-start-and-vad`: **3/3** (`alloy`, `nova`, `sage`); the final transcript arrived before Stop.
  - `stop-keeps-final-transcript`: **3/3** (same voices); the final transcript arrived after Stop. Both cases verified the final text stayed in the composer without sending.
  - This job passed even though the multi-PR workflow was red for a different matrix job. It did not run the listed test/check lanes, full declaration emission, or physical-mic testing. The environment-key path does not exercise the client-secret POST; the matched loopback tests below are the evidence for credential/DNS revocation and revoked late-final suppression.
- **Upstream CI is still open:** [the upstream CI run for this SHA](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45875137110) reports `action_required`. The fork job proves the runnable browser/Gateway build and authorized live flow, not the full build or required upstream checks.
- `roboclaw-bot` merged upstream `main` at `2fda93cf03a8` into the existing PR branch without conflicts or rewriting history, then published [`45971d0305bf`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/45971d0305bfaf4a7096d14ba7dbfe3e28b18b3a). Read-back verified both parents of merge commit `d09be9092d9d` and the full published tree. The merge changed no PR files; the only incoming changes were two upstream Activity files.
- `git diff --check` passed. The PR remains at +16 net production lines and +383 net test lines. Bound static Auto Review found no P0 issue; no fork code or live-provider smoke ran in this session.
- **Timothy’s fork CI (secretless, not upstream CI):** [CompleteDotTech/openclaw#17](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/pull/17) shares PR head `45971d0305bfaf4a7096d14ba7dbfe3e28b18b3a`. [Run 45875138236, attempt 1](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875138236) was **queued** as of 2026-11-26 19:19 UTC. [`preflight`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875138236/job/140100207904) **passed** and logged checkout of `refs/pull/17/merge` at `6c3b8ce6361c5a0626a8c97e50d78670d714b151`; both commits have Git tree `f2e8a672381dc6347931a0959cea7e215cc002dd`. This verifies source identity for preflight, not execution of the queued tests.
- **Fork job status:** [`build-artifacts`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875138236/job/140102135906) and [`checks-node-agentic-gateway-core-1`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875138236/job/140102146791) were **queued**. The [run graph](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875138236) showed **0/173** Node matrix jobs and **0/12** `checks-ui-e2e` jobs completed; `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway` was **skipped**. Its [GitHub App token setup](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45874425999/job/140101324760#step:7:24) failed because the required `private-key` input was empty. This is a workflow setup failure, not a product test result.

### Previous main integration: `ac30e5d72f6f8`

- `roboclaw-bot` published [`ac30e5d72f6f8`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ac30e5d72f6f8ae57b518c5b4e3cf6ebe34ad756) to the existing fork branch. Verified the fork and PR refs, the merge parents, and the published tree against the staged tree.

All five PR blobs match `40cef00eabcc`. `git diff --check` passed; the static simplification pass kept the existing authority and transport owners, with no new public API, flags, or configuration. prs.title: fix(ui): skip account listing without operator.read in chat picker
prs.body:
## Problem

Team Gateway logs `[ws] ⇄ res ✗ users.listModelAccounts … FORBIDDEN missing scope: operator.read` (8 refusals, 8 connections, 5 users, all `client=openclaw-control-ui mode=webchat`, still after the latest update). Those users have session scopes (they call `sessions.patch` successfully) but no `operator.read`.

Caller: the chat composer model picker. `onModelPickerOpen` in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-session-controls.ts` prefetched model accounts when `sessions.patch` was allowed, and the account section (with its own prefetch and toggle) rendered whenever `models.list` returned an `accountSelection`. `models.list` is readable with session scopes, `users.listModelAccounts` is not. In one sample the refusal is 23 s before the same connection's `sessions.patch` (model switch), matching "open picker → prefetch → pick model". The new-session picker already gates the same prefetch on `selfUser` + write access.

## Fix

Gate the account section and the picker-open prefetch on `hasOperatorReadAccess`. The method's scope is unchanged (no permission decision).

## User impact

- Session-only operators: the model picker still works; the account list section is no longer shown (before, it showed a list that could only fail). The current account label in the composer is unchanged.
- Operators with `operator.read`: no change.

## Proof

- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-session-controls.permissions.node.test.ts` "lists model accounts on picker open only when the connection can read them": red on base (`listModelAccounts` called with `operator.sessions.write` only), green on head. The old assertion in "persists an explicit Standard choice" pinned the refused call and is removed.
- 11 importer test files of the changed source: 137 tests pass. oxfmt/oxlint clean.
- Production diff: +9/−2 in one file. Net positive because the cause is a missing check; no new state or flag.

prs.title: fix: send BytePlus Seed Speech speed and emotion in the v3 audio parameters
prs.body:
Closes #197294

Thanks @Jo2234 for the vendor-contract reference and the synthetic transport capture.

## What Problem This Solves

The BytePlus Seed Speech v3 API-key route put speed and emotion beside `audio_params` as `speed_ratio` and `emotion`. The v3 HTTP TTS contract reads them from `req_params.audio_params.speech_rate` and `req_params.audio_params.emotion`, so configured speed and emotion never reached the vendor in the documented shape. The legacy AppID/token v1 route has a separate `audio.speed_ratio` contract and is not affected.

## User Impact

Speed settings and per-request overrides now arrive in the fields BytePlus documents. Values outside v3's 0.5x–2x range saturate at the nearest endpoint, while the shared `speedRatio` setting keeps its existing 0.2–3 range for other providers and for v1. Unset speed and emotion stay omitted. No configuration, migration, or new setting is involved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The translation belongs in the plugin's v3 request builder, next to the payload it shapes. `speech_rate` maps linearly to the existing ratio (`(ratio - 1) * 100`), so 0.5x is -50, 1x is 0, and 2x is 100. The shared ratio is resolved separately from its neutral default so the v3 builder can tell "unset" from "explicitly 1"; v1 still receives its previous default. A comment records the boundary clamp so the wider shared setting is not silently narrowed elsewhere.

## Evidence

Request construction is the affected boundary, and the tests assert the full payload. Before, with `speedRatio: 1.5` and `emotion: "happy"`:

```json
{"req_params":{"text":"...","speaker":"...","audio_params":{"format":"mp3","sample_rate":24000},"speed_ratio":1.5,"emotion":"happy"}}
```

After:

```json
{"req_params":{"text":"...","speaker":"...","audio_params":{"format":"mp3","sample_rate":24000,"speech_rate":50,"emotion":"happy"}}}
```

`extensions/volcengine/tts.test.ts` covers the documented payload, the 0.2/1.5/3 range mapping, the unset case, and the unchanged v1 payload:

```
CI=1 ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/volcengine/tts.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests       24 passed (24)

CI=1 ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/volcengine/tts.test.ts extensions/volcengine/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  Test Files  2 passed (2)
  Tests       29 passed (29)
```

Formatting and `git diff --check` are clean. Not exercised: an authenticated BytePlus synthesis. The report established the request-construction defect, and this change stays at that boundary.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the old payload. Only the BytePlus v3 request body changes; v1, the shared setting, and stored state are untouched.

prs.title: fix: keep recently edited Workshop skills out of unused-skill cleanup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workshop could archive a skill as unused just after you edited it. After a nested support-file removal, 500 later changes to other skills could push the only record the curator consulted out of the agent’s feed. A foreground edit could also commit after the curator selected a skill for cleanup and before it archived that skill.

## User Impact

A recently edited skill stays available when cleanup runs. Unrelated edits to other skills can fill the visible feed without making the edited skill eligible for archival. Skills that meet the existing inactivity cutoff can still be archived.

## Why This Change Was Made

Workshop records the latest committed change time for each live skill in the same database transaction as the public change. The curator rereads that time while holding the target skill’s mutation lock, immediately before archival. Older stores can use a recent removal snapshot together with the current file list to identify a completed removal. The public feed keeps its existing 500-entry limit.

The schema generator also keeps the exact SQL hashes used by readers installed before the activity table was added. Those readers can still load their original tables and views when an update replaces the catalog assets. This preserves the existing [build-swap contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196800).

## Evidence

- On the parent, removing a nested support file and making 499 unrelated changes kept the skill live. The 500th displaced its change from the feed, and cleanup archived it. Independent cold reads confirmed the archive and that Restore recovered the exact post-removal bundle.
- A separate seven-row reproduction captured the curator archiving skill A, a foreground write committing to skill B, and the curator then archiving B with the new contents. The regression covers an edit during cleanup as well as an edit before the sweep.
- The Workshop repair passed 47 focused cases across maintenance (8), registered CLI contracts (10), and Workshop library/change recording (29). These include the 499/500 boundary, the edit during cleanup, and a refused removal that had already saved a snapshot. Three storage-kernel cases passed separately before the final module extraction. The CLI tests exercised the registered handler in process.
- The first signed version failed 11 of 215 catalog-equivalence cases. The correction passed all 225 cases, including the historical schema and runtime variants.
- A reader loaded from the pre-activity parent resolved all 127 original schema hashes against the replacement catalog. Each returned the same tables and views. The published catalog retains those 127 entries and adds six. The swap test covered the loaded reader and replacement asset.

- **Populated upgrade from v2026.11.10.** The released CLI created three archive/restore history entries and two saved versions. The compiled Gateway at `4bc5c4fd` reopened the same state with mode `auto`, watch disabled, the same live skills, all three history entries and the original archive bytes. Restoring a version saved by the released CLI recovered both `SKILL.md` and its nested support file byte-for-byte.
- **Cleanup on the upgraded state.** A separate process called the production curator with a controlled 30-day cutoff. It archived only the idle skill. A fresh compiled Gateway listed the recently edited and restored skills, returned five history entries, and preserved the settings and all four original archived file digests.
- **Automatic cleanup through the registered service.** In the passing Gateway maintenance contract test, an agent-end event triggered the service. The test waited for it to settle, read the registered change feed, and found the curator’s stale-skill archive. The used, recently changed, scheduled and fresh-file controls all stayed live. [Gateway maintenance contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4bc5c4fd1401d234053eb668fa1b8232ac153dd0/src/gateway/server-maintenance.workshop-contract.test.ts#L228-L250)
- The PostgreSQL conformance shard that caught the inventory mismatch passed on `4bc5c4fd`. [Hosted PostgreSQL conformance (3/6)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45916735758/job/140238336251)

prs.title: fix: warn when Discord voice has no transcription model configured
prs.body:
Closes #206033

Thanks @anmol0b for the source analysis that pinpointed the silent branch.

## What Problem This Solves

In Discord voice `stt-tts` mode, when no audio transcription model can be resolved, the bot still joins the channel and accepts every utterance, then retires each one as `unavailable`. Nothing is written to the log. The operator sees a bot that joined successfully and never answers, with no hint that `tools.media.audio` is missing a model.

## User Impact

A voice session without a usable transcription model now logs one actionable warning per session, naming the configuration that fixes it. Sessions with a working model behave exactly as before, and the recording path keeps its existing unavailable-batch warning. No new configuration or join-time preflight is involved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The no-model branch already distinguishes the two owners of the utterance: a recording capture receives `onBatchUnavailable`, while a plain conversation had no callback and returned silently. The warning is emitted at that existing boundary and recorded on the session entry, so a channel that keeps receiving speech does not repeat it on every utterance. Keeping the check beside the `unavailable` return means the result handling stays unchanged.

## Evidence

Regression tests in `extensions/discord/src/voice/segment.test.ts` drive the real voice segment path with the media-understanding runtime mocked:

- A no-model result on a plain conversation warns once, with the configuration remedy, and a second utterance in the same session does not warn again.
- A recording capture still routes the same result through its own unavailable handling and does not emit the new warning.

Focused runs:

```
CI=1 ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/discord/src/voice/segment.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests       21 passed (21)

CI=1 ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/discord/src/voice/segment.test.ts extensions/discord/src/voice/transcripts-conversation.test.ts extensions/discord/src/voice/transcripts-realtime-recording.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  Test Files  3 passed (3)
  Tests       63 passed (63)
```

`oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` are clean on the changed files. Not exercised: a live Discord voice channel without STT credentials; the report and the change both target the source-proven no-model branch.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the previous silent behavior. No config, schema, stored state, or public contract changes; the added entry field is optional.

Related: #205853 (P01), #205846 (M10). Semantic reference: #205851 (P06).

## What Problem This Solves

The proposed desktop dictation workflow still lacks an accepted native owner, first insertion control, and delivery guarantee. Existing Quick Chat dictation edits its own composer, while reply paste-back selects an application when invoked. Neither establishes original-control dictation insertion.

## User Impact

This draft changes no runtime behavior. It provides one concrete proposal for the joint P01/M10 decision: the existing macOS app and Apple Speech, a separate opt-in shortcut, review before insertion, and explicit Copy recovery.

TextEdit's plain-text editing control is a research candidate, not a supported target. External insertion remains unavailable until its contract can satisfy the original-target/selection guarantee or maintainers explicitly accept a revised guarantee. P01 and M10 remain open, with every acceptance criterion still unqualified.

## Why This Change Was Made

[ClawSweeper's P01 review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205853#issuecomment-7186720252) and [M10 review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205846#issuecomment-7186467107) request this bounded native decision before implementation.

The proposal reuses Quick Chat capture and existing voice coordination. It limits state to the current request, retained target, reviewed text, and one pending edit/result. It defers cross-platform APIs, persistent delivery queues, clipboard restoration, and a new provider hierarchy. Target freshness is a destination check, not repeated authorization.

The document explains the unresolved Accessibility comparison/write race and preserves truthful inserted/unknown outcomes after cancellation or disable. It also distinguishes process restart from same-process re-enable so a pending effect cannot disappear.

Browser parent #204107 has merged. This branch targets main and is based on inspected commit `cab8e5aca1c26f0a7b2fec0270ae5aa4153d48a2`, which includes merge `762aa006f9482f44d7975efe9cef2679d498c885`. prs.title: fix: report one exec-policy scope for a mixed-case agent key
prs.body:
Closes #204994

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw exec-policy show` (and `openclaw approvals get`, which renders the same table) reports the wrong policy for an agent whose `agents.entries` key is written in mixed case. Config entry keys stay verbatim, while runtime and stored approvals use the normalized agent id, so one agent appears twice.

With `agents.entries.Ops.tools.exec = { security: "allowlist", ask: "always" }` and a stored approval for `ops`:

```text
tools.exec: auto · allowlist · ask on miss · fallback deny
agent:Ops: auto · allowlist · always ask · fallback deny
agent:ops: auto · deny · ask on miss · fallback deny
```

Neither row is the policy the runtime applies: `agent:Ops` carries the requested policy without the host approvals, and `agent:ops` carries the approvals but reports `ask on miss` for an agent configured to always ask.

## User Impact

User impact: the effective-policy table shows one row per agent again, matching what the runtime enforces. The displayed `agents.entries.<key>` path keeps the literal key the operator wrote, so it still points at their config. Runtime enforcement is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`collectExecPolicyScopeSnapshots` merged configured entry ids and stored approval ids as written. Group configured entries by the normalized runtime id instead, and use that id for the scope label and the approval lookup, while the recorded config path keeps the literal key. Stored approval keys are left untouched: they are already written under the normalized id, and re-normalizing them would change labels for ids the approvals file is allowed to hold verbatim.

## Evidence

**Behavior checked:** the same isolated state directory and config before and after the change, through the shipped CLI (`node scripts/run-node.mjs exec-policy show`, state dir and config path set through `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`).

base, `96adcab5508` (`upstream/main`), with `agents.entries.Ops` configured and approvals stored for `ops`:

```text
TERMINAL ACCESS — SELECT AGENT
Configured agents: main, ops

── COMMAND APPROVALS (LOCAL) ──────────────────

tools.exec: auto · allowlist · ask on miss · fallback deny
agent:Ops: auto · allowlist · always ask · fallback deny
agent:ops: auto · deny · ask on miss · fallback deny
```

head, `85b49835735`, same state and config:

```text
TERMINAL ACCESS — SELECT AGENT
Configured agents: main, ops

── COMMAND APPROVALS (LOCAL) ──────────────────

tools.exec: auto · allowlist · ask on miss · fallback deny
agent:ops: auto · deny · always ask · fallback deny
```

Regression test: `src/cli/exec-policy-cli.test.ts` → `reports one scope for an agent whose config key is mixed case`, which asserts a single `agent:ops` scope, `security` requested `allowlist` / effective `deny`, `ask` requested `always` / effective `always`, and `configPath` `agents.entries.Ops.tools.exec`.

The same test on the base commit, with only `src/infra/exec-approvals-effective.ts` reverted:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/exec-policy-cli.test.ts -t "reports one scope for an agent whose config key is mixed case"
 × |cli| src/cli/exec-policy-cli.test.ts > exec-policy CLI > reports one scope for an agent whose config key is mixed case
   → expected [ 'tools.exec', 'agent:Ops', …(1) ] to deeply equal [ 'tools.exec', 'agent:ops' ]
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 35 skipped (36)
```

On the head, the whole file:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/exec-policy-cli.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  36 passed (36)
```

`pnpm tsgo:core` passes; `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` reports `All matched files use the correct format.`; `git diff --check` is clean.

**Not run / gaps:**

- Local ClawSweeper's input scan refuses this checkout on this host (`scanner_failed` while bootstrapping its scanner), so the only local review evidence here is autoreview, which reported `scoped-clean` for this head.
- Fork PR CI needs a maintainer to approve the run, so it has not run.

prs.title: fix: send the next turn to a provider that takes over an existing cooldown
prs.body:
Related to #205985 and #205998.

## What Problem This Solves

A gateway can recover while OpenClaw still remembers its earlier 429. Even after its provider plugin takes over availability, the next turn can go straight to a fallback without contacting the recovered gateway. The documented policy also applies to rate-limit windows saved before the declaration took effect.

## User Impact

A provider that manages its own availability can answer the next turn before its old retry deadline. Other providers continue to honor their retry times.

## Why This Change Was Made

Request admission and fallback ordering both read the same model/account limit. Both now consult the current provider declaration when they find a saved limit. An ordinary request with no saved limit needs no metadata lookup.

This complements #205998, which prevents recording new limits for providers that already manage availability. A window recorded before the declaration takes effect requires the read-side check here.

## Evidence

The committed regression uses the completion transport on the same route and credential. After a 429 with a 3,120-second retry time, an undeclared provider receives one request total. On the base revision, enabling the declaration still produced a local 429. With this change, the second provider call returns its normal response and the fallback health query sees the route as available.

I also ran a built Gateway with real OpenClaw agents and a local HTTP Responses provider. Three primaries each returned HTTP 429 with a 3,120-second retry time, and all three accepted a direct probe after recovery. On each build I enabled one provider's declaration by hot reload in the same Gateway process before sending the next turns.

The second turns produced the following HTTP request log, condensed to the route that actually received each request. Times are seconds since each Gateway run started. Each line represents one upstream request.

```text
base 1ecc37e1e48f
  41.806s   managed at startup   fallback  200
  42.533s   undeclared           fallback  200
  43.598s   managed at reload    fallback  200

with this change
  42.647s   managed at startup   primary   200
  43.524s   undeclared           fallback  200
  44.824s   managed at reload    primary   200
```

The managed primaries received these requests about 21 and 9 seconds after their respective 429s. The undeclared primary received no second request on either build.

Across seven focused suites, all 93 tests passed, including shared limits, fallback ordering, plugin availability, auth-profile cooldowns and prompt-prefix stability. One cold metadata test needed a rerun with the macOS boot identity available. The same SQLite lock error reproduced on an unmodified checkout under the restricted environment.

The core typecheck, all 29 core test typecheck shards, changed-file lint and formatting passed. The changed-file check suite passed 34 of its 35 checks. Rerunning its unused-export scan on the base and on this branch found exactly the same existing export, `toSimpleContextMessages` in `src/agents/btw-runtime.ts`, in both the production and full-tree scans.

prs.title: fix(gateway): clean up transient isolated hook base sessions after run (#202621)
prs.body:
Closes #202621

## What Problem This Solves

Every isolated webhook run (`POST /hooks/agent`) creates an ephemeral agent execution session that was never cleaned up after completion. Over time, gateways running automated webhooks accumulate hundreds of orphaned base session records (`agent:<id>:cron:<jobId>`) that cannot be purged by standard cron retention sweeps.

## User Impact

User impact: Prevents unbounded session record leaks and database bloat on gateways handling webhook triggers, ensuring transient isolated hook sessions are immediately purged after execution while preserving history for persistent hooks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Isolated hook runs create ephemeral jobs with `sessionTarget: "isolated"` but previously omitted `deleteAfterRun`. Setting `deleteAfterRun: value.sessionMode !== "persistent"` marks transient hook runs for post-run base session cleanup in `cleanupCronRunSessionAfterRun` once finished, while keeping conversation history intact when `sessionMode === "persistent"`.

## Evidence

Verified that the new unit test fails red on base (`expected undefined to be true` for `call.job.deleteAfterRun`) and passes green with the fix.

Targeted test suites:
- `src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts` (21 passed)
- `src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts` and `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.session-lifecycle.test.ts` (33 passed)
- Linters and formatting: `oxlint` (0 errors, 0 warnings) and `run-format.mts` clean.

prs.title: fix: show sender phone number for quoted WhatsApp messages (#202554)
prs.body:
Closes #202554

## What Problem This Solves

When replying to a quoted message in a WhatsApp group where the quoted sender is identified by an internal `@lid` (such as `1234567890@lid`), the agent's inbound reply context displays the opaque `@lid` JID rather than the contact's phone number or display name, even though the receiving account already has the contact's reverse mapping stored in its local credentials folder (`authDir`).

## User Impact

User impact: When someone quotes another user in a WhatsApp group, the AI agent correctly sees the sender's phone number (e.g. `+15555550123`) in the quote context instead of an unreadable `@lid` identifier.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inbound quote extraction (`describeReplyContext`) was not provided with the receiving account's `authDir`, so the participant lookup fell back to the unmapped identifier. Additionally, `resolveComparableIdentity` retained the raw identifier in the `label` property even after resolving the phone number, causing the downstream reply envelope formatter to render the stale raw `@lid`.

This patch:
1. Passes `authDir` from delivery intake and message enrichment into `describeReplyContext`.
2. Updates `resolveComparableIdentity` to update `label` to the resolved `e164` when the existing label is a raw identifier (`@lid` / `@s.whatsapp.net`).
3. Explicitly normalizes and asserts `sender.lid` (and `sender.label = e164`) in expectations, preserving the existing identity normalization contract.

## Evidence

### Behavior comparison

- **Before:**
  Quoted group message with sender `1234567890@lid` mapped to `+15555550123`:
  Agent sees: `[Replying to 1234567890@lid]\noriginal message\n[/Replying]`
- **After:**
  Agent sees: `[Replying to +15555550123]\noriginal message\n[/Replying]`
  Identity data cleanly retains `lid: "1234567890@lid"`, `e164: "+15555550123"`, and `label: "+15555550123"`.

### Automated Tests Verified

All tests pass cleanly across unit, visibility, and monitor integration suites:
1. `extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/extract.test.ts`: Added unit test `resolves quoted LID sender to phone number via authDir mapping` asserting `sender.lid`, `sender.e164`, and `sender.label`.
2. `extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/inbound-helpers.test.ts`: Added visibility context test `resolves quoted LID sender to mapped phone label via authDir` asserting `resolveVisibleWhatsAppReplyContext` yields mapped phone label.
3. `extensions/whatsapp/src/monitor-inbox.reply-context.test.ts`: Added monitor inbox test `resolves quoted LID sender to phone number using account authDir` verifying full delivery through Baileys event emission.

prs.title: fix(google): keep Vertex tool declarations append-only, exclude legacy Vertex from AI Studio caching, and report Vertex prefix telemetry
prs.body:
Related: #203726, #191159, #198100, #204805

## What Problem This Solves

Vertex AI sessions lose implicit prompt-cache prefix stability on two client-side paths and emit opaque cache-drop diagnostics when prefix shifts occur:

1. Legacy Vertex configurations that still specify `api: "google-generative-ai"` with `provider: "google-vertex"` or a Vertex `aiplatform.googleapis.com` base URL are treated as direct Google AI Studio routes. OpenClaw attempts unsupported AI Studio `POST /cachedContents` calls and marks those sessions eligible for `cache-ttl` pruning.
2. When an `on-demand` tool (such as `computer` or `github_publish`) is loaded during a run or promoted across turns, alphabetical re-sorting in `prepareSessionToolSurface`, `sessionToolAllowlist`, and `convertGoogleTools` inserts the new tool ahead of existing `functionDeclarations` instead of appending it at the end, shifting earlier declaration slots on both the immediate follow-up round in the same run and subsequent turns. In addition, `prepareFinalModelRequestJson` skipped host request encoding whenever no `transformPayload` policy was active, leaving Vertex `providerPrefix` telemetry as `unavailable`, and `provider-prompt-serialization` did not recognize native Google/Vertex `systemInstruction`, `contents`, `parts`, `generationConfig`, `toolConfig`, or `cachedContent` fields.

Scope boundaries preserved intentionally:
- Preserves `#204805` immediate same-run `loadTool` behavior untouched (`attempt-deferred-tool-resolver.ts` and `packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop-run-tools.ts` are unmodified). Looking up an `on-demand` tool on Vertex loads it immediately for the next round of the same run, now appended at the end of `functionDeclarations` instead of shifting earlier slots.
- Preserves `#198100` `/compact` operator prompt-refresh and promoted-tool reclamation semantics untouched across all embedded providers.
- Zero file overlap and zero symbol dependency on `#203726` (runtime-context replay across Vertex tool rounds), and excludes `promptMode` / `exec`-wake changes covered by `#191159`.

## User Impact

- Legacy Vertex routes (`api: "google-generative-ai"` with `provider: "google-vertex"` or Vertex `aiplatform.googleapis.com` endpoints) skip AI Studio `/cachedContents` calls and `cache-ttl` pruning cleanly while direct Google AI Studio keeps its existing explicit caching behavior unchanged.
- On-demand tools loaded mid-run (`#204805`) or admitted within an active series append at the end of Vertex `functionDeclarations` so earlier declarations remain 100% byte-identical on both Round 2 of the same run and subsequent turns. Direct Google AI Studio continues sorting declarations alphabetically, and `/compact` continues refreshing prompts and reclaiming promoted tools per `#198100`.
- Prompt-cache diagnostics now fingerprint real Vertex wire payloads and report structured `providerPrefix` classifications (`prefix-match`, `system`, `tools`, `message:N.parts`, `parameters:generationConfig`, `parameters:toolConfig`, `parameters:cachedContent`) with wire byte/prefix metadata while ignoring `generationConfig.maxOutputTokens`-only cap changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Vertex AI implicit prompt caching keys on exact byte identity of the leading `systemInstruction`, `tools`, and `contents` prefix. Keeping previously pinned tools in append-only order through `mergePinnedToolDefinitions`, `attempt-client-tools`, and `convertGoogleTools(..., { preserveOrder: true })`, excluding legacy Vertex routes from AI Studio explicit-cache paths, and routing wrapped Google/Vertex payloads through `prepareFinalModelRequestJson` eliminates avoidable client-side declaration reordering while keeping immediate same-run `on-demand` execution (`#204805`), `/compact` refresh semantics (`#198100`), and all security/execution-gating boundaries intact.

## Evidence

### Red-on-base regression verification (`8e2c8f5b57a`)

Running the compacted regression suites against unmodified `8e2c8f5b57a` reproduces all failures cleanly:

- Legacy Vertex AI Studio cache guard (`google-prompt-cache.test.ts` > `skips AI Studio cachedContents for legacy google-generative-ai Vertex routes`): fails on baseline (1 failed / 24 passed) because baseline wraps legacy Vertex routes in AI Studio `/cachedContents` creation.
- Vertex append-only wire tool order, allowlist and surface order, `prepareFinalModelRequestJson` host encoder, and same-run `loadTool` append order (`vertex-tool-append-order.test.ts`): 4/4 tests fail on baseline, including `expected finalJson to be defined` and both `google-vertex` and legacy `google-generative-ai` Vertex same-run `loadTool` append checks (`expected [ 'alpha_pub', 'dispatch_action', 'tool_describe', 'tool_search' ] to deeply equal [ 'dispatch_action', 'tool_describe', 'tool_search', 'alpha_pub' ]`).
- Vertex prefix telemetry and wire serialization (`prompt-cache-provider-prefix.test.ts` and `provider-prompt-serialization.test.ts`): 2/2 tests fail on baseline (`expected 'parameters:other' to be 'prefix-match'` and missing `contents` / `parameters.fields` extraction).

All regressions pass cleanly on exact head `9b06deb97e5`.

### Automated test, typecheck, lint, and ratchet checks (`9b06deb97e5`)

- Focused Vitest suite passes across all 17 test files and 5 shards (347 tests passed, 0 failed on exact head `9b06deb97e5`: `unit-fast` 4 files / 21 tests, `unit` 2 files / 52 tests, `agents-embedded-agent` 5 files / 118 tests, `agents-embedded-agent-run` 5 files / 34 tests, `extension-database-workers` 1 file / 122 tests):
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/cache-ttl.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/google-prompt-cache.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/prompt-cache-retention.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/google-api-base-url.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/session-prompt-state.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-runtime-prepare.history-boundary.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-runtime-prepare.on-demand.test.ts`
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/google-messages.test.ts`
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/google-interactions.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/prompt-cache-provider-prefix.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/provider-prompt-serialization.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model-request-body.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/provider-prompt-state.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-client-tools.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-deferred-tool-resolver.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/vertex-tool-append-order.test.ts`
  - `extensions/google/transport-stream.test.ts`
- Full TypeScript typechecks pass with zero errors on exact head `9b06deb97e5`: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm tsgo:test:packages`, and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` (all 22 shards).
- Scoped lint, formatting, ratchets, and merge verification pass with zero issues across all 23 touched files:
  - `oxfmt --check` (all 23 files formatted cleanly)
  - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` (0 problems in 21 `src/` and `packages/` files)
  - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json` (0 problems in 2 `extensions/` files)
  - `node scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mjs --base 8e2c8f5b57a` (0 new violations or over-cap growth)
  - `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base 8e2c8f5b57acc8dfd553e2d7ef0029f79529e286 --no-merge-base` (PASS: +369 net test lines, allowance 400, allocation credit 0)
  - `git diff --check 8e2c8f5b57a..9b06deb97e5` (clean, empty `.github/` diff)
  - `git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=8e2c8f5b57a origin/main HEAD` (clean 0-conflict merge)
  - `git merge-tree --write-tree remotes/origin/pr-203726 HEAD` (clean 0-conflict merge, 0 overlapping files with `#203726`)
- Full runtime build (`pnpm build:runtime`) passes on both baseline (`8e2c8f5b57a`) and exact-head candidate (`9b06deb97e5`).

### Isolated built-CLI and built-Gateway offline loopback Vertex proof

Verified offline on exact head `9b06deb97e5` versus baseline `8e2c8f5b57a` with both built runtimes (`openclaw.mjs agent --local` for Case 1 and `openclaw.mjs gateway run` driven by `openclaw.mjs gateway call` for Case 2) talking exclusively to a synthetic `127.0.0.1` loopback HTTP Vertex server, using isolated temporary state and workspace directories, synthetic credentials, and blocked non-loopback proxies.

| Case | Built Runtime | Key Wire and Lifecycle Observations | Telemetry (`systemPromptSeries` / `providerPrefix`) | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Case 1: Legacy Vertex route (`api: "google-generative-ai"`, `provider: "google-vertex"`, `cacheRetention: "long"`) | Baseline (`8e2c8f5b57a`) | Sent `POST /v1beta/cachedContents` (1 call) before `:streamGenerateContent` (1 call) | N/A (single turn) | Attempted unsupported AI Studio `/cachedContents` on Vertex route |
| Case 1: Legacy Vertex route (`api: "google-generative-ai"`, `provider: "google-vertex"`, `cacheRetention: "long"`) | Candidate (`9b06deb97e5`) | 0 `/cachedContents` calls, direct `:streamGenerateContent` (1 call) | N/A (single turn) | Skipped AI Studio `/cachedContents` cleanly |
| Case 2: Same-run `tool_describe("computer")` -> immediate Round 2 `computer` call + Turn 2 follow-up | Baseline (`8e2c8f5b57a`) | Round 1: 16 tools (`7dc1d409bfe021f1`). Round 2 (same run): 17 tools (`43427e5e388f1d82`) with `computer` sorted into index 1 (`earlierDeclarationsByteIdentical: false`, shifting slots 1..15). Turn 2: `computer` at index 1 (`earlierDeclarationsByteIdentical: false`) | Round 2 `restarted:new` / `unavailable` (`requests=undefined`), Turn 2 `pinned` / `unavailable` (`requests=undefined`) | Shifted earlier declaration slots alphabetically in Round 2 and Turn 2, and lacked Vertex wire prefix telemetry |
| Case 2: Same-run `tool_describe("computer")` -> immediate Round 2 `computer` call + Turn 2 follow-up | Candidate (`9b06deb97e5`) | Round 1: 16 tools (`7dc1d409bfe021f1`). Round 2 (same run): 17 tools (`39ce388aecf53f80`) with `computer` loaded immediately (`#204805` intact) and appended at index 16 (`earlierDeclarationsByteIdentical: true`, slots 0..15 byte-identical), and `computer` executed cleanly in Round 2. Round 3 and Turn 2 keep `computer` appended at index 16 (`39ce388aecf53f80`, `earlierDeclarationsByteIdentical: true`) | Round 2 `restarted:new` / `tools` (`requestBytes: 71999 -> 84318`, `prefixBytes: 4096`), Turn 2 `pinned` / `message:5.role+parts` (`requestBytes: 84777 -> 98896`, `prefixBytes: 4096`, identical `prefixHash`, runtimeContextCarrier rewrite tracked in `#203726`) | Immediate same-run `loadTool` preserved, append-only `functionDeclarations` on both Round 2 and Turn 2, and structured Vertex wire prefix telemetry |

prs.title: fix: explain chat update errors when a session changes
prs.body:
<!-- PR title: fix: explain chat update errors when a session changes -->
## What Problem This Solves

When a session changes while OpenClaw is setting up chat updates, the chat page can show an internal request name instead of explaining what happened. When connecting to chat history, OpenClaw retries this error automatically for up to a minute. If the message connection already works but adding approval updates fails, the same notice appears right away.

## User Impact

The notice now names the session change without implying that messages stopped arriving. **Retry** still starts a fresh check for updates to the same session.

- **Before:** “session changed before sessions.messages.subscribe; retry the request”
- **After:** “This session changed before OpenClaw could finish checking for updates. Try again.”

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already identifies this specific change. The chat page now uses the same typed cause for its explanation and its existing retry decision. A denial, timeout, or an error with similar wording does not get the new message. No permissions, retry timing, history storage, or wire responses change.

**Skill in practice:** The reader is opening a chat or returning to one. The copy names what changed and points to the action already on screen. It doesn’t claim messages were deleted, saved, or missed. The internal request name offers no additional recovery step, so there’s no disclosure to open.

## Evidence

When opening or reconnecting the chat on the base, repeated session-change responses appeared verbatim after automatic retries ended. On the patch, the same responses produced the new sentence. In both cases below, clicking **Retry** made one fresh subscription request and no send request. The initial view then showed the message. The refresh view kept its visible message and cleared the notice.

Real Control UI with synthetic session and Gateway responses, light theme, Chromium. The browser clock advanced the retry window. Before: `7857d5ae3a5a`. After: staged tree `c64b52143b82`. This proves the UI and its read action, not a production session race.

**Initial load, 390 × 844**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Internal request name on initial load](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a9a4570-f0d1-4f4e-ac01-9d80db3d3722) | ![Session-change explanation and Retry on initial load](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c6353e7b-ab63-419b-8514-c66c9425b18e) |
| ![Internal request name outlined](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/51f2cd1e-8fc8-468e-a1a2-328f1175a999) | ![Session-change explanation outlined](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0225fcb-5826-40ea-ad08-7019bc7e4b9a) |

**Refresh with messages already visible, 1000 × 760**

Before

![Internal request name above the retained message](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b74a2be6-90b8-4ce1-8b01-9332c17c5151)

After

![Session-change explanation above the same retained message](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/97487075-fbed-4d89-8360-f031f58db347)

Annotated before

![Original inline notice outlined](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d8df799b-e905-4561-8b24-dee316ca7422)

Annotated after

![Revised inline notice outlined](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b15b4ab0-07d5-461e-b9a0-e623935f1a88)

Two regressions failed on the base: opening a chat hit the retry deadline, and adding approval updates to a working message subscription failed immediately. Both showed the old request name. All three focused suites passed on the patch (69 tests). The approval case kept the message subscription and recovered approval updates on Retry in the pane lifecycle test. It uses the same history notice, not a separate approval screen. The browser fixtures did not reproduce that upgrade separately. Denials, timeouts, and similar text without the typed cause retained their existing messages. Control UI typecheck, scoped lint and formatting, English catalog verification, copy-check, and the staged diff check passed. No full CI, live Gateway, or provider run was used.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: fix(a2a): keep outbound delivery working after peer token rotation
prs.body:
Closes #198978

## What Problem This Solves

Rotating an existing A2A peer's inbound token with `openclaw channels add` clears the peer's URL and outbound credential. The next outbound send fails.

## User Impact

Operators can rotate the inbound credential and keep sending messages to the same peer without reconfiguring it.

## Why This Change Was Made

I changed A2A setup to update the inbound token on the saved peer record so its outbound settings survive the write.

## Evidence

- On upstream main `f25b6ed`, I rotated a token while two live Gateways were exchanging A2A messages. The saved peer lost its URL and outbound credential. The next send failed with `has no url configured for outbound A2A`. Adding a new peer in the control run preserved delivery.
- With the A2A patch applied to `f25b6ed`, the same rotation kept both outbound fields and the second Gateway completed the next outbound task. The Gateway where I rotated the token accepted the new credential and rejected the old one.
- The rotation regression failed on unpatched `f25b6ed`. I ran `pnpm test extensions/a2a --maxWorkers=1` on `38cbec0b3051` and all 112 tests passed across 10 files.
- My local ClawSweeper review of `1e6d3f9bd9ec..38cbec0b3051` completed with no findings.

prs.title: fix(decisions): explain undeclared decisionModel ids instead of input-size guidance
prs.body:
Closes #205438

## What Problem This Solves

When `agents.defaults.decisionModel` selects a model ID that is not declared in the provider's decision catalog (for example `typesafe/decision` when the provider declares `jev-latest`, `jev-preview`, `jev-1.13.0`, and `kev-latest`), `decision_evaluate` rejects every call pre-dispatch with `status: "unavailable", reason: "unsupported-input"` and returns only the generic host-bound input-size guidance ("Shorten the state or rubric, reduce question counts..."). Callers and operators cannot tell whether the payload was rejected or the configured model ID is missing from the provider catalog.

## User Impact

When a call is rejected as `unsupported-input` with no resolved decision capabilities and the selected provider declares decision models in the catalog, `decision_evaluate` now reports the undeclared `provider/modelId` along with the provider's declared decision model IDs (bounded to 12 entries). Host-bound input rejections and declared-model capability rejections keep their existing guidance, and the `DecisionEvaluateOutput` schema and `reason` enum are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`decision-tool.ts` already inspects the active prepared catalog or plugin metadata snapshot to resolve decision capabilities for `guidance`. Reusing the same bounded catalog lookup to build an `UndeclaredDecisionModelDiagnostic` when capabilities are absent avoids changing the shared `ProviderFailureReason` contract or adding extra runtime I/O, while surfacing the actual configuration mismatch directly in the tool result.

## Evidence

- Reproduced before the fix: adding an undeclared model ID (`decision-tool-fixture/undeclared-custom`) assertion in `src/agents/tools/decision-tool.integration.test.ts` failed with the generic `"Shorten the state or rubric..."` guidance.
- Verified after the fix:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --maxWorkers=1 -t "keeps capability guidance|reports undeclared decisionModel diagnostics" src/agents/tools/decision-tool.integration.test.ts` -> 2 passed, 0 failed (covers catalog precedence, undeclared model guidance, >12-model truncation suffix, and host-bound fallback).
  - Full `src/agents/tools/decision-tool.integration.test.ts` passed every runtime assertion (including the new end-to-end undeclared-model assertion and `trace.calls` remaining unchanged with zero provider dispatches).
  - `oxlint src/agents/tools/decision-tool.ts src/agents/tools/decision-tool-contract.ts src/agents/tools/decision-tool.integration.test.ts` -> 0 warnings, 0 errors.
  - `oxfmt --check src/agents/tools/decision-tool.ts src/agents/tools/decision-tool-contract.ts src/agents/tools/decision-tool.integration.test.ts` -> pass.
- Known local gap: on Windows, `afterEach` temp-dir cleanup in the full SQLite-backed integration test hits `EPERM` on `rmSync` after all test assertions complete; PR CI on Linux/macOS will verify the full integration teardown cleanly.

prs.title: fix: clarify when OpenClaw can’t find a linked session
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When you open a session link and OpenClaw finds no match, the Control UI suggests the session was removed or the link is wrong. The lookup doesn’t establish either cause or tell you whether you can read the session another way.

## User Impact

**Before:** “The session may have been removed, or the link may be incorrect.”

**After:** “OpenClaw couldn’t find a session for this link.”

The page stays on the link and offers the same two choices: **Go to main session** or **View sessions**. Only the wording changes. The lookup, access rules, and saved work are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

A session can be readable by its exact key even when the link lookup finds nothing. The English notice now describes the lookup result without guessing what happened to the session or what you can access. The two existing buttons already offer a way onward, so the notice doesn’t repeat their instructions or suggest a retry.

**Skill in practice:** The writing guide separates what OpenClaw knows from what the reader can do. That distinction took one sentence in the existing English catalog. One assertion in the existing browser test protects the sentence where readers see it.

## Evidence

In Chromium, the bundled Control UI opened `/chat/main/deadbeef` against a controlled Gateway fixture containing a main session and no matching link. The revised assertion failed on the earlier “session you can view” wording and passed with the lookup-only sentence. The composer stayed hidden, and the page did not request chat startup or message subscriptions. **Go to main session** opened the main chat with its composer. **View sessions** opened the Sessions page.

The fixture verifies the panel and both destinations, not real session permissions. Independent source review identified the distinction between [link resolution](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7857d5ae3a5a4b432b405ef43bb5ed7d2d2bd911/src/gateway/server.sessions.preview-resolve.test.ts#L144-L151) and [direct reads](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7857d5ae3a5a4b432b405ef43bb5ed7d2d2bd911/src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-read-visibility.test.ts#L575-L584). Those existing tests were inspected, not rerun.

Control UI types, the English catalog and raw-copy baseline, focused lint and formatting, and the writing guide’s copy check passed. English and light theme only. No live Gateway permissions, translated locale, or full CI suite were exercised locally.

Mobile, 390 × 844, light theme. The bundled Control UI opened the same missing link on base `7857d5ae3a5a` and corrected head `6f7372b2c63c` with the same controlled Gateway data. The outlines on the annotated copies use the measured subtitle bounds.
