prs.title: fix(linux): reduce desktop release package size
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Linux desktop downloads and installations include static symbol tables that are unnecessary for running the app.

## User Impact

The measured x86_64 executable is 31.3% smaller, and its Debian package is 12.0% smaller. Release backtraces and profilers lose names that depend on the removed static symbol tables.

## Why This Change Was Made

Enable Cargo's release-profile symbol stripping at the binary producer. This preserves the AppImage bundler's existing `NO_STRIP` workaround and leaves optimization, LTO, and panic settings unchanged. The shared Tauri release profile also applies to its macOS and Windows builds.

## Evidence

Built the unchanged baseline and candidate with Rust 1.97.1 and Tauri CLI 2.11.4 on Ubuntu 22.04 x86_64, using the same locked dependencies. The baseline used its actual Cargo defaults, including automatic debug-info stripping.

| Artifact | Before | After | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Executable | 39,580,872 bytes | 27,200,224 bytes | 31.3% |
| Debian package | 11,888,048 bytes | 10,467,250 bytes | 12.0% |

- Both extracted Debian executables passed the existing native first-run flow and retryable local-start-failure scenario with the WebKit sandbox enabled.
- All 685 dynamic symbol contracts, library dependencies, loader flags, version requirements, and the existing ABI scan matched. Static tables disappeared; unwind metadata remained.
- The packaged executables differ from their corresponding build outputs only by Tauri's documented bundle-type marker. All six other package members and their permissions matched.
- All 190 native build inputs remain byte-identical after the main-branch integration. Focused ABI scanner tests passed (15 tests), along with Cargo formatting and `git diff --check`.

Size and runtime measurements cover Debian x86_64. AppImage sizes and native macOS/Windows release builds were not measured.


### Landing review, 2026-11-27

The unchanged head `14dbc418fa1f737e354760ce72d213716b4ce7f7` still adds a profile absent from inspected main `b0503c0644be4a1d677866934e847dbf19ef9452`. The retained exact-head native review records a clean P2 autoreview and independent final review. [Exact-head Linux app CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35601033098) passed its Linux, macOS and Windows jobs; the logs confirm these use development/test profiles. The release measurements above are reused historical Linux proof, with their original platform limits. Both required `openclaw/ci-gate` contexts pass.

prs.title: fix: explain when a new session can’t use the selected project
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When you select a project in New Session, OpenClaw checks whether the session can use it. If the check finishes and neither workspace option is available, OpenClaw says the check failed and asks you to select the same project again. The disabled workspace options give the same retry instruction to people who can’t start sessions.

## User Impact

- **Before:** “Couldn’t check the checkout. Select the project again to retry.”
- **After:** “This session can’t use this project.”

A check that actually fails still offers a retry. If you can start sessions and another project is available, you can select it and start with the prompt you already wrote. If you don’t have access to create sessions, Start still explains that permission is missing.

## Why This Change Was Made

New Session already distinguishes a failed check from a completed result. It now uses that distinction in the composer and checkout picker. A result with no options doesn’t say why the project is unavailable or whether another one will work.

**Skill in practice:** Name the fact the reader can rely on. Keep the retry instruction for a failed check, but don’t tell a read-only caller to choose another project. No permissions, checkout choices, retry behavior or draft handling changed.

## Evidence

Two focused Chromium scenarios exercised the production-built New Session page with controlled Gateway replies:

- **Caller with create access:** The first check for **Garden plans** failed. Selecting it again retried the check. It returned no usable workspace and stayed blocked after another selection. No create request was sent. **Field notes** offered both workspace options. Selecting it preserved “Review the planting schedule.” Pressing **Start session** sent exactly one create request, with that prompt and the Field notes project ID.
- **Read-only caller:** Both disabled checkout options exposed the factual sentence in their titles and accessible descriptions. Trying to start showed the unchanged “You don’t have permission to create a session.” No create request was sent.

Both browser scenarios failed on the original wording and passed with the change (2.87 s and 1.38 s test time). The permanent regression failed on the base only for a completed check. All 54 cases in that test file passed on the patch (3.89 s wall time). Scoped types, lint, formatting, English copy and i18n checks passed. This verifies the UI and its requests, not live permissions or filesystem provisioning. Full CI was not run locally.

**Screenshot comparison:** Garden plans after the completed check, in the same light-theme desktop composer. Before: `7857d5ae3a5a`. After: `6ff0807f3978`. See the [400 px composer and read-only picker](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206414#issuecomment-7210756718) for the other views. The picker annotations quote the verified option titles; the clean screenshot does not paint a native tooltip.

**After**

## Why this fix?

prs.title: fix: preserve non-GitHub credential helpers in worker turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workers using a non-GitHub HTTPS remote can lose its configured credential helper when a turn prepares the managed GitHub identity.

Fixes #198461

## Why This Change Was Made

Worker turns now reset and install the credential helper only for `https://github.com`, preserving helpers for other HTTPS hosts. This follows the existing `managedGitHubIdentityEnvironment` and `GITHUB_PUBLIC_HOST` contract.

## User Impact

Managed GitHub operations keep using the turn identity, while other HTTPS remotes can authenticate through their configured helpers.

## Evidence

- The committed test launches the production worker CLI (`src/entry.ts worker`) with a fake Gateway, then runs real `git ls-remote` requests through a loopback TLS/CONNECT proxy. The checkout fetch and both HTTPS requests use that proxy; only GitHub and Forgejo are allowed. Credentials are random per run and no external network is used.
- Before: the validation-base binding runtime authenticated GitHub but Forgejo authentication failed.
- After: exact head `e4cd40e3070bfd5485c8cdca145243354f79a8f3` authenticated both hosts. The assigned GitHub identity and profile permissions were checked inside the active turn; the token was not printed or recorded in transcripts.

```text
$ pnpm test src/worker/worker.runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --testNamePattern='runs the worker CLI with the turn GitHub identity'
base 4cffd43ee043275f6a4c693aaacee8d8e5a61288: worker CLI authenticated GitHub; Forgejo authentication failed.
head e4cd40e3070bfd5485c8cdca145243354f79a8f3: worker CLI authenticated HTTPS: forgejo-authenticated, github-authenticated; loopback CONNECT: github.com=4, forgejo.example=2; profile active and assigned identity matched.
negative-control: GitHub helper remained !gh auth git-credential; credentials were absent from output and transcripts.
```

<details>
<summary>Repro: committed worker CLI proof</summary>

```ts
// src/worker/worker.runtime.test.ts
it.skipIf(process.platform === "win32")(
  "runs the worker CLI with the turn GitHub identity and authenticates managed Git access without publishing its token",
  async () =>
    await runManagedWorkerGitIdentityProof({ setup }),
);
```

The committed `worker-runtime-github-identity-proof.test-support.ts` starts the CLI process, holds the temporary profile checks inside the turn, and routes checkout and shell Git traffic through the constrained local proxy.
</details>

prs.title: fix: stop /reasoning on making Claude refuse every later turn until /new
prs.body:
Closes #205486 ## What Problem This Solves When someone turns reasoning visibility on with `/reasoning on` or `/reasoning stream`, the next Claude turn (for example `claude-opus-5-5` on the `claude-cli` runtime) fails with Anthropic's `[reasoning_extraction]` refusal. Every later turn in that session fails the same way until `/new`, and the error says nothing about the cause. ## User Impact `/reasoning on`, `stream` and `off` change only what OpenClaw shows, as the reasoning visibility docs describe ("whether thinking blocks are shown in replies"). Claude-backed sessions keep answering after the toggle. The command's reply and the saved level are unchanged, and `/elevated` still tells the model about its change. No action is needed after upgrading. Queued system events are held in memory only, so nothing stored carries the old line. ## Why This Change Was Made A reasoning level change queued a system event (`Reasoning ON - include .`, `Reasoning STREAM - emit live .`, `Reasoning OFF - hide .`), and the next turn carried it as a `System:` line, for every provider. Almost every provider plugin reports native reasoning output (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, MiniMax), and the prompt builder gives those models no `` tag hint. For them the event was the only instruction to write their reasoning out as visible text, which Anthropic refuses as reasoning extraction. Tagged-output models already get the `` rule in the system prompt on every turn, along with `Reasoning=`, so the event added nothing for them either. The fix removes the event where it is made, in the directive handler, rather than filtering it later. ## Evidence **Result in plain words.** On the current stable release, `/reasoning on` followed by a plain question puts the line into the next Claude Code prompt, and Anthropic refuses the turn. On this branch, the same steps on the same state and config give a normal answer for both `on` and `stream`. The prompt holds no reasoning line, and the Gateway logs no refusal. **Real Gateway runs.** Each run used a throwaway state directory with a stub Telegram Bot API (`channels.telegram.apiRoot`), with the turns sent as owner DMs through Telegram updates. The agent was `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` on `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"` with `reasoningDefault: "on"` and no fallbacks, on Node 24.22.3 with Claude Code 2.1.332. A logging wrapper recorded each Claude Code launch's stdin. Steps: `/new`, `/reasoning off`, one plain turn, `/reasoning `, then "a bus leaves at 9:50 and the trip takes 1 h 25 min. When does it arrive? Answer briefly."
Before: OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f) from npm, level on ```text level=on reasoning_line_in_prompt=1 reasoning_extraction_log_lines_added=3 replies_after_question=["⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply. For details, open Settings → Logs in the OpenClaw app or run openclaw logs"] ``` The question's Claude Code stdin held: ```text System: [2026-11-25 18:52:10 UTC] Reasoning OFF - hide . System: [2026-11-25 18:52:39 UTC] Reasoning ON - include . ``` Gateway log: `lane task error: lane=cli:claude-cli:... error="API Error: Opus 5.5's safeguards flagged this ...` `Details: [reasoning_extraction]`
After: this branch (3edf959 on main 04cd806fe), built with pnpm build and started with node dist/index.js gateway run on a copy of the same state ```text level=on reasoning_line_in_prompt=0 reasoning_extraction_log_lines_added=0 replies_after_question=['11:15. 9:50 plus 1 h is 10:50, and 25 more minutes makes 11:15.'] level=stream reasoning_line_in_prompt=0 reasoning_extraction_log_lines_added=0 replies_after_question=['It gets in at 11:15. Adding 1 hour to 9:50 gives 10:50, and 25 more minutes makes it 11:15. ...'] ```
**Regression test.** A new case in `reply.directive.directive-behavior.shows-current-verbose-level-verbose-has-no.test.ts` changes the level to `on`, `stream` and `off`. It then drains the real system-event queue with `drainFormattedSystemEvents`, the function that builds the next turn's `System:` block, and checks that the block holds no reasoning or `` text. A second case checks that `/elevated on` still reaches that block. The two existing tests that expected the reasoning event now expect none.
Regression test on the base (main 04cd806fe without the fix): 3 failed ```text FAIL keeps /reasoning on out of the next turn's model context FAIL keeps /reasoning stream out of the next turn's model context FAIL keeps /reasoning off out of the next turn's model context AssertionError: expected 'System: [2026-11-25 18:59:11 UTC] Rea…' not to match /reasoning|/i + Received: "System: [2026-11-25 18:59:11 UTC] Reasoning OFF - hide ." Test Files 1 failed (1) Tests 3 failed | 13 passed (16) ```
**Checks on the head**, Node 24.22.3: - `pnpm test --maxWorkers=1` on the directive-behavior file (16/16), `directive-handling.model.test.ts` and `directive-handling.mixed-inline.test.ts` (64/64), and `get-reply-directives-apply.test.ts` (14/14) all pass. - `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass. - `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files pass. - `pnpm build` passes. **Local review.** A manual review of `upstream/main..HEAD` (one commit) found no findings. Nothing else reads `formatReasoningEvent` or the `mode:reasoning` context key, and the system-event queue is not persisted, so an upgrade leaves no stale line behind. **Gaps.** - I ran no real Telegram client; the transport was the stub Bot API. - I did not run the `anthropic-api` runtime or non-Anthropic providers live. For those, the regression test is the proof, since the change is provider-independent. - I did not check here whether the "Thinking" message shows in the chat. This change does not touch display, but on `claude-cli` Opus 5.5 returns empty thinking unless Claude Code's thinking summaries are on, which is a separate issue.

prs.title: fix: stop suggesting a send when removing a queued message fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When you choose **Remove** on a queued message or **Discard** on a pending chat message, the browser can fail to confirm the removal. Chat then tells you to reconnect and send the message you were trying to remove.

## User Impact

Chat now suggests trying **Remove** or **Discard** again only if the control is still available. A message can remain in the transcript after those controls disappear. Removing the local copy does not cancel a message the Gateway already received.

**Before:** “Couldn’t save this message. Free browser storage or reconnect to send it.”

**After:** “Couldn’t confirm that your browser removed this message. If Remove or Discard is still available, try it again.”

## Why This Change Was Made

The single-message removal action knows it didn’t confirm a change. It doesn’t know whether storage refused the write or another pane changed the item. The alert names the action without guessing what happened to the message. Saving a message, clearing several paused messages, and canceling queued work on the Gateway are separate actions and stay unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Remove:** In the real Control UI, we queued two messages offline and entered a separate draft. With browser-storage writes temporarily refused, Remove showed the old alert on main and the new one on the patch. Once writes worked again, Remove cleared just the chosen row and the alert. The other row and the draft remained. The fixture received no send requests in either version.
- **Discard:** We withheld the Gateway’s acknowledgement of a send, disconnected, and made the browser refuse a storage write. Discard showed the new alert. Once writes worked again, we dismissed the alert, which covered the inline control in this one-message view, and selected Discard. The local row disappeared without another send or any cancellation request. In a separate run, reconnecting instead left the message visible but neither Remove nor Discard available. The fixture observed the existing reconnect request using the original message key.
- The focused bundled-browser regression failed on main at the new alert and passed on the patch, including the removal, ordering, and reconnect assertions. UI typecheck, changed-file lint and formatting, localization checks, and the focused copy check passed. Screenshots were inspected at 400 and 960 pixels wide. The alert has no expandable details; **Report a bug** is unchanged. The Gateway was a controlled fixture: this isn’t proof of live delivery or permanent storage exhaustion.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Chat suggests sending after Remove fails](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/506a0eb6-5e35-4369-84ba-e1dce35580fa) | ![Chat suggests retrying only while Remove or Discard is available](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1140f6f3-6120-4b20-83ac-e60c6c6e0f97) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![The old alert recommends a send after a removal attempt](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46056797-16af-4025-a141-fcd65ebf0ea0) | ![The new alert makes retrying conditional on a removal control](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/340e6acf-4689-40df-b9ab-195b03acaefc) |

Offline queue in the Control UI, 400 × 760. Before: main `7857d5ae3a5a`. After: reviewed tree `44314d58ab3c`. The fixture temporarily refused a write to browser storage.

### Skill in practice

“Couldn’t save this message” fits a save attempt, not a removal. Following both controls to the same result let us give one conditional next step without adding another error renderer or changing what happens on retry.

Independent review found that seeing a message in the transcript does not mean it can still be discarded. The correction was verified with the inline Discard and reconnect cases above.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e346c5e4-f828-45b2-be8f-1aad6754fbad)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/0842fdc7-1006-45f7-b80b-2af6432a02d2)
- [Review correction and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/5e3133b6-5e05-4045-b36b-f265fe899fc1)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix: keep answering your first message after the agent replies to a second one mid-task
prs.body:
Root cause: src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/message-tool-terminal.ts:184 returns `terminate: true` for any delivered final message-tool send, without checking whether an earlier input of the same run is still waiting for its answer.

Fixes #202669

Thanks @Davidnovarro for the detailed report and trajectory.

## What Problem This Solves

In a chat with the default `steer` queue, you send message A, the agent starts working on it with tools, and you send message B while it works. If the agent answers B with the message tool (no `final`, which means final), OpenClaw ends the whole run. A never gets an answer and you get no notice, so you have to ask again.

## User Impact

- The answer to B is delivered and the run continues, so A still gets its answer.
- When the agent then sends A's final answer, the run ends there with no extra model request.
- A single message with a final send behaves as before (same number of model requests). Progress sends (`final: false`), a new message after A is fully answered, and follow-up queueing are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hook that decides "a final send ends the run" already keeps per-input reply state. It now also tracks inputs that ran a tool and have no final reply yet. A final send completes its own input first (else the oldest open one), and ends the run only when no input stays open. The Code Mode nested-send completion uses the same rule. The model still decides whether one message answered both requests: if it did, its next turn simply ends.

`docs/concepts/agent-loop.md` now says that a final reply completes only one input, which matches the existing sentence in `docs/concepts/messages.md`.

Other runtimes:
- Codex app-server runtime: not affected. After a steer, a delivered final reply loses its terminal authority (`run-attempt-lifecycle-controller.ts`, `hasSubmittedMessages()`), so the turn runs to the model's own end.
- CLI runner (Claude CLI live sessions with steering): same pattern. `execute-tool-tracking.ts` interrupts the turn after the latest delivered final send and does not track earlier inputs. Not changed here; it needs its own per-input bookkeeping and live CLI proof.

## Evidence

Base is `d877e8007fba` (merge base); candidate is this branch head. Full captures: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206412#issuecomment-7210719550

- **Unit regression** (`message-tool-terminal.test.ts`, "ends the run only once the input before a steer has its own final reply"): fails on base (`expected { terminate: true } to be undefined`), passes here. The four test files that import the hook pass.
- **Agent loop, real `Agent` + real message tool + scripted model** (A runs `exec`, B is steered in, send for B with no `final`, then send for A):
  - base: 2 model requests, 1 delivery (`4`), run ends at `toolUse`.
  - fix: 3 model requests, 2 deliveries (`4`, then A's answer), no extra request.
  - Controls, same on both: single input with a final send (2 requests); `final: false` progress (3 requests); B after A was fully answered (new run, 3 requests); B queued as a follow-up (3 requests).
- **Telegram Test Server DM, real Gateway, deterministic provider** that replays the reported trajectory (Code Mode off, default steer queue):
  - base: the user sees only `2+2 = 4`; the provider gets no further request and A is never answered.
  - fix: the user sees `2+2 = 4`, then `notes.txt contains PELICAN-…`; 3 tool requests, no failure notice, no duplicate.
- **Telegram Test Server DM, real Claude (Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5)**: 21 completed runs (13 base, 8 fix), including 6 per side where B asks for the message tool directly. The reported model choice (a send for B with no `final`) did not occur: in 20 runs the model sent B's answer with `final: false`, and in one it wrote B's answer as text beside a tool call. So the live gap is the model's choice, not the product path; the deterministic Telegram run above covers the reported path. The live runs show the unchanged progress path: A's answer arrives on base and on the fix, with no duplicate.

## Merge danger

Two-way door. No stored state, config, or contract change; a revert restores the old behavior. Blast radius: embedded (`openclaw` runtime) runs where a message-tool final send happens while an earlier input of the same run ran tools and has no final reply yet. Cost in the rare case where one send answered both inputs: one extra, normally empty, model request.

prs.title: fix: explain why Delete all archived stopped before deleting sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On the Sessions page, **Delete all archived** first loads the complete list of archived sessions. If that read stops early, the alert talks about “enumeration” but doesn't say whether anything was deleted or how to bring up the confirmation again.

## User Impact

The alert now says which part of the read failed and that OpenClaw didn't delete any sessions. After the alert, OpenClaw waits for you to try again. Choose **Delete all archived** in **Filters** to start a fresh read. If that read succeeds, OpenClaw still asks for confirmation. This changes the wording, not where the alert appears: on a short phone, close Filters to see it.

| Read failure | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No list returned | archived session enumeration returned no result | OpenClaw couldn’t load the list of archived sessions, so it didn’t delete any. To try again, choose Delete all archived in Filters. |
| Cannot advance to the next page | archived session enumeration did not advance | OpenClaw couldn’t load the next page of archived sessions, so it didn’t delete any. To try again, choose Delete all archived in Filters. |
| Not every archived session was returned | archived session enumeration was incomplete | OpenClaw couldn’t list every archived session, so it didn’t delete any. To try again, choose Delete all archived in Filters. |

## Why This Change Was Made

The Sessions page already refuses to confirm a partial list. Only this read happens before confirmation, so its alert can say what happened without making a promise about a failed delete request. The same pagination checks still select the three messages. Actual request errors retain their original details.

**Skill in practice:** Following [Writing for OpenClaw](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/.agents/skills/openclaw-writing/references/error-messages.md), the alert uses the task's words, names the known outcome, and points to one control on the current page. No new dialog, error category, or retry mechanism was needed.

## Evidence

- On the real Control UI Sessions page, a controlled Gateway supplied a missing page, a non-advancing page, and a short list. Each produced its own alert without confirmation. After restoring the complete list and choosing the same action again, the confirmation named two archived sessions. Cancelling sent no delete request. These results held on base and patch at 1050 × 680 and 390 × 844.
- Filters stayed open after the alert. At 390 × 844 the alert was on the page behind the dim backdrop, not in the sheet. At 320 × 568 the opaque sheet covered all three alerts; they became readable after closing Filters. At 1050 × 680 the popover left the alert unobscured. This copy change does not fix the separate phone visibility issue.
- Three alert assertions failed on the unmodified production source and passed on the patch. All seven focused archived-deletion tests passed, including the thrown-request error case. UI types, targeted lint and formatting, English catalog verification, extracted-copy checks and diff checks passed.
- The captures used synthetic sessions, not a live Gateway or a physical phone. They prove the page and its requests, not what a live backend does after confirmation. No new details disclosure, translations, or full local CI run.

**Clean comparison after closing Filters:** incomplete archived list at 390 × 844. Base `7857d5ae3a5a`; patch `2f77962e19cc`. Both use the same fixture, viewport, and light theme.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Incomplete archive list alert before the change](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d4b3d6f3-e15a-452a-92e7-741a3e6c3c68) | ![Incomplete archive list alert with deletion status and Filters recovery](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9cb9d24a-1c3a-4763-bbc7-e77d69cbe303) |

**Annotated comparison after closing Filters:** the highlighted alert now explains what happened to the sessions and how to try the read again.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![The highlighted alert describes only the list diagnosis](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c67c8ac7-9e75-4a18-ba8f-b6ced7c4e817) | ![The highlighted alert explains what happened and where to try again](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c73b3a95-0dee-4700-b5dd-c8ee303ddd79) |

[See each failed read with Filters still open and after closing it, the compact-phone visibility problem, and the successful retry confirmation.](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206411#issuecomment-7210658603)

Contributor: @vyctorbrzezowski

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e346c5e4-f828-45b2-be8f-1aad6754fbad)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/5a9c63a3-ed48-46ad-9015-4eb0a3dedc94)

prs.title: fix: open publisher-qualified Template links in the Control UI
prs.body:
Closes #198770. Follows #198831.

## What Problem This Solves

Opening a creator's Template link in the Control UI can show a catalog error even though the Gateway found the requested release. This happens when the link uses the publisher-qualified name and ClawHub stores the Template under its bare name.

## User Impact

Both names open the same Template. File preview and Add use the package and version from the returned release. A different publisher, package, or pinned version still produces an error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already returns the stored name and its verified publisher. The UI can match either the stored name or the qualified reference built from those two fields. The Gateway and UI use the same name check, including when the UI returns to the link to show an Add error or ask for ClawHub risk confirmation. The CLI keeps its existing exact-name preference and uses the shared formatter.

## Evidence

The Templates page regression failed on the base revision and passed with the change. It covers a publisher-qualified link, the file preview and Add requests, and rejection of a response for another publisher, package, or pinned version. Two further regressions reproduced lost Add errors and confirmation prompts when returning to the link. Both pass with the shared name check.

In Chrome against an isolated Gateway, the same encoded link requested `@atlas/research-briefing` at `1.2.0` on both builds. The Gateway returned `research-briefing` on both. The base UI displayed a catalog error. The candidate opened Research Briefing and successfully fetched the contents of `SOUL.md` using the stored package name at `1.2.0`. The bare-name link opened on both builds. For a flagged release, Add returned to the qualified link and showed the security review prompt. After cancelling and pressing Add again, the prompt reappeared and neither request contained an acknowledgement. The local ClawHub fixture served a synthetic community Template; both runs used the same Gateway build.

Local checks passed for all 52 Templates page and Add tests, 60 ClawHub catalog tests, and the CLI Gateway Add test. The CLI integration test needed host process visibility to identify its isolated Gateway. The UI production build, UI typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, and formatting checks passed.

prs.title: fix: files sent in a Teams 1:1 chat from the iPhone app reach the agent
prs.body:
Closes #206021

## What Problem This Solves

When someone sends a file to an OpenClaw Teams bot in a 1:1 chat from the Teams iOS app, the agent never gets the file. It sees only the typed text and answers that nothing was attached. Bot Framework posts that message with no `attachments` entry at all, although the file is on the chat message in Graph. Channels and group chats already recover such files through `graphMediaFallback`; personal chats cannot, because a Bot Framework DM ID is not a Graph chat ID.

## User Impact

With `channels.msteams.graphMediaFallback: true`, a file sent in a personal chat reaches the agent even when the activity leaves it out, as it already does in channels and group chats. Nothing changes with the setting off (the default), for messages whose file the activity already carries, or for personal-chat messages with attachment markers (those keep the Bot Framework v3 route).

**Compatibility: this widens what an existing setting does.** A deployment that already has `graphMediaFallback: true` starts making one Graph message read for each personal-chat message that downloads nothing and has no attachment markers, ordinary text DMs included, because Teams gives no other sign that a file is missing. That read needs `Chat.Read.All` (application), plus the file permissions the channel path already uses.

- Without `Chat.Read.All`, Graph refuses the read. `downloadMSTeamsGraphMedia` logs `graph media message fetch not ok` with the status at debug level and returns no media. The message then reaches the agent as text only, exactly as it does today.
- The read runs under the same media deadline, size cap, host allowlist and SSRF guard as the channel path.
- The setting's UI help (`config-schema.ts`) and the configuration reference now say this, so an operator who turns it on sees the per-message lookup and the permission.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every personal-chat activity names its Graph chat in `channelData.chat.id` (`19:…`), and the activity ID is the Graph message ID. That is exactly what the existing Graph recovery needs, so the change reuses `buildMSTeamsGraphMessageUrl` and `downloadMSTeamsGraphMedia` instead of adding a new download path. The personal-chat exclusion came from #90738, where a Bot Framework DM ID could not address Graph. This keeps that exclusion for the DM ID and addresses Graph by the chat ID instead. Only a `19:` chat ID is accepted.

Docs reviewed and updated:

- `docs/channels/msteams/manifest-and-permissions.md`, "Channel/group file recovery (`graphMediaFallback`)": the setting also covers personal chats, how the lookup is addressed, its cost, and that `Chat.Read.All` covers personal-chat file recovery. The heading is unchanged, so existing anchors still resolve.
- `docs/channels/msteams/configuration.md` and the setting's help in `extensions/msteams/src/config-schema.ts` (ClawSweeper's P3). The generated channel metadata and the config docs baseline hash are regenerated with `pnpm config:channels:gen` and `pnpm config:docs:gen`.

## Evidence

Gates on the exact PR tree (head `ab18061a6c7`, base `96adcab5508`), run on my fork with Node 24.22.3 on `ubuntu-latest`, following `docs/ci/local-proof.md`. The workflow commit is dropped before anything runs.

- **Full run:** https://github.com/colton-octaria/openclaw/actions/runs/45881398581
  - The new focused tests fail on the base source and pass on this head: with only `inbound-content.ts` and `sdk-types.ts` reset to the base, 2 of 20 fail (the two recovery cases); on this head, 20 of 20 pass.
  - `pnpm test:extension msteams`: passed.
  - `pnpm config:channels:check`, `pnpm config:docs:check`, `pnpm plugins:inventory:check`: passed.
  - `pnpm check:docs`: passed.
  - `node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main --no-merge-base`: passed.
  - `pnpm test:changed`: the regenerated core metadata file selects the broad suite, which was still running when this was written. An earlier run on the same source finished 1,895 test files with no failure before its time limit: https://github.com/colton-octaria/openclaw/actions/runs/45857592263
- **`pnpm check:changed`:** https://github.com/colton-octaria/openclaw/actions/runs/45885854950
  - It passes with only its dead-export scan skipped (`OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1`).
  - The dead-export scan fails with one entry, `src/agents/btw-runtime.ts: toSimpleContextMessages`. It fails identically on the base `96adcab5508` in the same run, so it isn't from this diff.
- **Focused tests** in `extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/inbound-content.test.ts` cover:
  - recovery by `channelData.chat.id` (the Graph URL is asserted);
  - a file-only message isn't dropped as empty;
  - no Graph read with the setting off, without a chat ID, or with a non-Graph chat ID;
  - attachment markers stay on the Bot Framework route.

  The existing gate test (a personal chat without a chat ID gets no recovery) is unchanged.

## Real Behavior Proof

Behavior addressed: a PDF sent in a Teams 1:1 chat from the iOS app reaches the agent.

Real environment tested: a production OpenClaw 2026.11.8 gateway on Amazon Linux 2023 (Node 24.22.3), `@openclaw/msteams@2026.11.8`, a real Teams tenant, the bot behind a plain reverse proxy, and the iPhone Teams app as the sender. The same change was applied to the installed plugin's `prepareMSTeamsInboundContent` (identical logic to this PR), followed by a gateway restart.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: from the Teams iOS app, sent a 3 KB PDF with the text "what's this one" in the 1:1 chat with the bot; read the gateway runtime logs (debug level) and the agent's session transcript.

Evidence after fix: gateway runtime logs and transcript (IDs redacted):

```text
15:26:36 DEBUG {"name":"msteams"} {'count': 1} | downloaded attachments
15:26:48 DEBUG [context-diag] pre-prompt: sessionKey=agent:main:msteams:direct:<uuid> ... promptChars=1432 promptImages=0
15:26:58 DEBUG message processed: channel=msteams ... outcome=completed duration=22079ms
transcript user turn: "what's this one\n\n<file name=\"<uuid>.pdf\" mime=\"application/pdf\"> ..."
```

Before the change, the same DM from the same phone produced `promptChars=55`, no `downloaded attachments` line, and a transcript with only the text (four attempts). The raw HTTP body Bot Framework posted had no `attachments` key (`clientInfo.platform: "iOS"`), while Graph showed the message with a `reference` attachment.

Observed result after fix: the agent read the PDF and summarized it ("A Simple PDF File", two pages of filler text) in its reply. A later PDF sent the same way was also read, and the agent sent a PDF of its own back into the chat, which opened in Teams.

What was not tested: other Teams clients (desktop or web) sending to a personal chat, where the activity may already carry the file (unchanged path), and personal chats with `graphMediaFallback` off (unchanged).

prs.title: docs: serve a holding page during Gateway downtime
prs.body:
Related: #191925

## What Problem This Solves
A first-time Control UI visitor sees a failed connection when the Gateway is stopped, even if the deployment already has a reverse proxy that can respond.

## User Impact
Operators can configure their existing Caddy ingress to show a small holding page for browser navigation and return retryable JSON to other callers. The guide distinguishes a Gateway process restart from a host outage and preserves authentication and Gateway responses.

## Why This Change Was Made
The loaded Control UI already supports cached navigation. This recipe covers first visits and cache misses at the existing ingress boundary, without adding a Gateway daemon or claiming that every outage is an upgrade.

Work from Vincent Koc.

## Evidence
- Isolated Caddy v2.11.7 validation and 34 HTTP assertions passed: normal responses, 401/403/503 passthrough, auth failures, HTML/JSON negotiation, HEAD, retry/cache headers, and a prefixed Control UI path.
- Native pinned formatter and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent source/contract review found no actionable issues.
- Exact-head [docs CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41644820554/job/125947957427) and [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41644820554/job/125949981256) passed at `916dc8eff6d8b6182434c7a4bf92ead67db89052`.
- No production proxy or Gateway was changed.

prs.title: fix: let setup-code device pairing finish when another process updates the state schema
prs.body:
Closes #202258

## What Problem This Solves

Operators pairing a node or mobile device with a setup code (`openclaw qr`) can have the handshake rejected with `UNAVAILABLE: duplicate column name: setup_id` when the running gateway opened the SQLite state database before another process (such as `openclaw qr` or `openclaw doctor`) added `setup_id` to `device_bootstrap_tokens`. Because the running gateway's cached schema facts still believe the column is missing, post-connect bookkeeping tries to run `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN setup_id` again, failing the connect handshake and leaving setup completion unrecorded.

## User Impact

Setup-code bootstrap pairing now completes cleanly even when another OpenClaw process adds additive columns to the shared SQLite state database while the gateway is already running. The connecting device receives its `hello-ok` response and device token, the one-time bootstrap token is consumed, and setup completion is recorded with `setup_id` preserved. No config changes, schema migrations, or manual recovery steps are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cached admitted SQLite schema facts avoid catalog lookups on hot paths, but an out-of-band process can legally add an additive column after a long-lived gateway handle has already admitted its schema snapshot. Fixing this at the shared schema-fact and column-helper owners keeps the fast path free of extra `PRAGMA` queries while recovering cleanly when SQLite reports a duplicate-column error:

- `ensureColumn` parses the target column identifier (including quoted SQLite identifiers), and on a SQLite duplicate-column error (`SQLITE_ERROR` + `duplicate column name`), verifies via live `PRAGMA table_info` that the column actually exists before calling `refreshAdmittedSqliteSchemaFacts` and returning `false`. Non-duplicate errors and unconfirmed failures still throw.
- `readDeviceBootstrapTokenRecordsFromDatabase` selects live columns directly (`selectAll()`) instead of branching on cached `tableHasColumn(..., "setup_id")`, so `verifyDeviceBootstrapToken` does not strip an out-of-band `setup_id` before post-connect completion runs, while `optional()` treats missing/nullish values as absent for pre-`setup_id` tables.

## Evidence

- **End-to-end Gateway + CLI + WebSocket proof** (same command on base `ea27b2143ecd` and exact candidate head `058a95ca8370`: `node proof-202258.mjs --checkout <dir>`):
  - Real entry exercised: built `openclaw.mjs gateway` started against a pre-`setup_id` SQLite state DB, primed via `openclaw devices list`, followed by a separate `openclaw qr --json` CLI process adding `setup_id` out-of-band and minting a setup code, then an Ed25519 `openclaw-android` WebSocket node connect with `auth.bootstrapToken`.
  - **Before (`ea27b2143ecd`, exit 1 — RED):** `beforeGatewayHasSetupIdCol=false`, `afterPrimeHasSetupIdCol=false`, `afterQrHasSetupIdCol=true`, `qrSetupIdPresent=true`. WebSocket connect returned `ok=false`, `error={ code: "UNAVAILABLE", message: "Error: duplicate column name: setup_id: code=ERR_SQLITE_ERROR" }` (`failurePhase=hello failureCause=handler-error`). Read-only SQLite readback: `tokenConsumed=false`, `completionRecorded=false`, `completionDeliveryState=null`.
  - **After (`058a95ca8370`, exit 0 — GREEN):** Identical sequence returned `ok=true`, `payloadType="hello-ok"`, `authMethod="bootstrap-token"`, `role="node"`, `hasDeviceToken=true`, `error=null`. Read-only SQLite readback: `tokenConsumed=true` (`device_bootstrap_tokens` row removed), `completionRecorded=true` (`device_pair_setup_completions` matched `setup_id` and `device_id`), `completionDeliveryState="confirmed"`, `pairedDeviceRecorded=true`.
  - **Replay / negative controls:** A second Ed25519 WebSocket connect reusing the same consumed `bootstrapToken` failed with `ok=false`, `code="INVALID_REQUEST"`, `details.code="AUTH_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_INVALID"` (0 replay redemptions vs 1 initial redemption). Focused tests verify healthy admitted handles execute 0 `PRAGMA table_info` reads in `ensureColumn`, and non-duplicate SQLite errors or duplicate errors where the column is absent still rethrow.
- **Focused tests & measured costs (`--maxWorkers=1`):**
  - `src/state/openclaw-state-db-schema-helpers.test.ts`: 8/8 passed — 23.99s Vitest (35.37s wall, 570ms tests).
  - `src/infra/device-bootstrap.test.ts`: 39/39 passed — 128.90s Vitest (159.44s wall, new regression test 3.70s).
  - `src/state/openclaw-state-db-schema-additive.test.ts`: 6/6 passed (27.85s Vitest).
  - `src/infra/device-pairing-store.test.ts`, `src/infra/sqlite-schema-facts.test.ts`, `src/infra/sqlite-schema-facts.physical-cache.test.ts`: 69/69 passed (25.46s Vitest).
- **Typecheck, lint, build & review:**
  - `pnpm tsgo`, test tsconfigs (`state-logging`, `infra`), `scripts/check-tsgo-core-boundary.mts`, `oxfmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and `pnpm build:runtime` all passed (exit 0).
  - `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base ea27b2143ecd`: 31/35 checks `ok` (including SQLite worker/dialect ratchets, changed-file lint/format, pairing guards, and import cycles); the 3 `tsrs` checks could not run due to host `GLIBC_2.32` absence and were covered by `tsgo`, plus 1 unrelated pre-existing dead-export warning in `src/config/sessions/transcript-shell-receipt.ts`.
  - Independent adversarial source review (P0–P3) completed with no remaining findings.
- **Not tested:** PostgreSQL connections (reconciliation is SQLite-only and skips Postgres handles), non-Linux OS platforms, and native Android/iOS mobile app UI shells (protocol handshake exercised directly with an Ed25519 `openclaw-android` WebSocket client against the built gateway).

prs.title: fix(sessions): stop tool-usage retention from recreating a missing store
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway maintenance runs `pruneRegisteredAgentToolUsage` over every row in the agent database registry. Its `write` helper captured the execution with inherited creation authority and then called `execution.prepare()`, which materializes the SQLite file when it is missing.

Following Doctor's orphan-directory guidance — remove stale agent directories that are absent from `agents.entries` — leaves the registry row whose store is now gone. The next retention sweep then recreated an empty database at that path, and within minutes the removed directory was back with a fresh SQLite store. Doctor only swapped one warning for another; the cleanup never stuck.

## Solution

- `pruneRegisteredAgentToolUsage` now writes **existing-only**: the `write` helper captures without the inherited creation authority, skips `prepare()`, and treats an `undefined` `runExisting` result as "nothing to prune". Flush, reset and import keep their creating behavior.
- Doctor's orphan-directory warning now points operators at `openclaw agents delete <id> --force` after restoring the roster entry, and states that deleting the directory alone leaves the agent-database registration behind.

A retired agent whose directory the operator removed on purpose stays removed: retention no longer recreates its store, and its registry row is preserved for the owner to retire (an absent database is not deletion authority). Live stores keep pruning normally.

## Evidence

### Shipped Gateway + Doctor CLI proof (redacted terminal output)

A real `openclaw gateway` process (built `dist` CLI) and a real `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` run against an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (`chmod 700`, `{ gateway: { mode: "local" } }`). The driver registers a hand-removed agent `stale` in the `agent_databases` registry **without creating its file**, seeds live agent `main` with a fresh row plus a directly-inserted expired row (`now - 91d`), starts the Gateway with `OPENCLAW_TEST_MINIMAL_GATEWAY=0` so the shipped side runtimes run, and waits 160s for the Gateway's own **startup+130s tool-usage retention timer** to fire. It then runs the real Doctor CLI against the same state dir.

Driver + full redacted output: [`proof/retention-existing-only`](https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/tree/proof/retention-existing-only/.artifacts/proof/retention-existing-only) ([HEAD](https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/blob/proof/retention-existing-only/.artifacts/proof/retention-existing-only/head-gateway-doctor.txt) · [BASE](https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/blob/proof/retention-existing-only/.artifacts/proof/retention-existing-only/base-gateway-doctor.txt) · [EVIDENCE.md](https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/blob/proof/retention-existing-only/.artifacts/proof/retention-existing-only/EVIDENCE.md)).

**HEAD (with fix) — PASS.** The running Gateway's retention timer pruned the live store and left the removed store absent; Doctor also left it absent and reported the skip:

```
[proof:head] after gateway retention cycle:
[proof:head]   expired row pruned=true
[proof:head]   fresh row preserved=true
[proof:head]   removed store recreated=false (false = stays absent)
[proof:head]   registry row survives=true
[proof:head] running real doctor CLI (openclaw doctor --non-interactive)...
[proof:head] doctor exit=0
[proof:head] after doctor:
[proof:head]   removed store recreated=false (false = stays absent)
[proof:head]   registry row survives=true
  doctor| │  - Skipped missing registered agent database
  doctor| │    <state>/agents/stale/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite.  │
[proof:head] gatewayOk=true doctorOk=true
[proof:head] PASS
```

**BASE (before fix, `6356ddabdd3`) — FAIL (bug reproduced).** The same shipped retention timer recreated the hand-removed store:

```
[proof:base] after gateway retention cycle:
[proof:base]   expired row pruned=true
[proof:base]   fresh row preserved=true
[proof:base]   removed store recreated=true (false = stays absent)
[proof:base]   registry row survives=true
[proof:base] after doctor:
[proof:base]   removed store recreated=true (false = stays absent)
[proof:base] gatewayOk=false doctorOk=false
[proof:base] FAIL
```

Both runs prune the expired row and keep the fresh row (live-store pruning continues); only HEAD stops the removed store from being recreated, and only HEAD's Doctor reports `Skipped missing registered agent database`. Paths and tokens are redacted (`<state>/`, `token<redacted>`); no IPs, API keys, phone numbers, or non-public endpoints appear.

### Regression tests

`src/gateway/server.tool-usage-retention-existing-only-product-proof.test.ts` drives the shipped maintenance scheduler on a **controlled `createGatewaySchedulerClock`** (no wall-clock sleep): advancing past the startup+130s tick prunes the expired row, keeps the fresh row, and leaves the removed store absent with its registry row intact; a Doctor state-integrity pass on the same state dir does not recreate it either.

`src/config/sessions/tool-usage.test.ts` registers a missing store and seeds an aged live store, then runs retention: the missing store is not created and its registry row is still present; the live store's expired usage is still pruned. Red on base (`expected true to be false`), green with the fix.

```
pnpm vitest run src/config/sessions/tool-usage.test.ts src/gateway/server.tool-usage-retention-existing-only-product-proof.test.ts src/commands/doctor-state-integrity.test.ts
# all passed
```

`src/commands/doctor-state-integrity.test.ts` asserts the new guidance text for both `agents.list` and `agents.entries` rosters. `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet` — OK (no new violations or over-cap growth).

Closes #205927

prs.title: fix: let a self-managed provider answer again before an old 429 retry time passes
prs.body:
Closes #205985

## What Problem This Solves

Some users route models through their own local gateway, which balances several accounts and handles its own cooldowns. They mark that provider with a plugin that declares `managesOwnAvailability: true`, so OpenClaw leaves capacity recovery to the gateway. When the gateway briefly answered 429 with a long retry time (52 minutes in the report), OpenClaw kept failing every later turn for that provider locally until that time passed. It did this even after the gateway had recovered and was answering requests again. The gateway received no requests from OpenClaw during that window, and every turn fell back to another model.

## User Impact

A provider that manages its own availability gets the next request again, so turns use it as soon as it has recovered instead of waiting out an old retry deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

`managesOwnAvailability` already stops the auth-profile rate-limit cooldown. A second, in-memory hold for long provider retry times lives in the shared request limiter, and that hold never checked the declaration. The limiter now skips creating that hold for a provider that declares it, using the same policy reader as the auth-profile cooldown. The check runs only when a long 429 arrives, so ordinary requests do no extra work. Providers that don't declare it keep the existing behavior.

## Evidence

**Regression test:** `lets a provider that manages its own availability answer before a timed 429 resets` in `src/agents/model-fallback.sticky-rate-limit.test.ts`. A declared provider observes a 429 with `retry-after: 3120` (the reporter's 52 minutes), and the next request is admitted.
- On base, the next request is refused locally with `FailoverError: 429 Shared model rate limit. Retry-After: 3120 seconds exceeds maxRetryDelayMs=60000.` and `code: 'rate_limit_exceeded'`. That is the same `status: 429`, `code: rate_limit_exceeded` the reporter logged without any request reaching their gateway.
- With the fix, the request is admitted.
- The existing `blocks later turns on a generic timed 429` test still passes. It covers the same input for a provider without the declaration.

**Real product run, before and after:** this uses the built CLI's local embedded chat (`openclaw chat`, the TUI in local mode), one long-lived process with no Gateway and isolated state.
- **Provider:** a local OpenAI-compatible stand-in for the reporter's gateway. Its first `gw/primary` request gets HTTP 429 with `retry-after: 3120`, and every later request gets 200, meaning the gateway has recovered. `gw/backup` is the configured fallback.
- **Plugin:** a manifest-only plugin like the reporter's (`managesOwnAvailability: true`, `providers: ["gw"]`), installed by path. `plugins inspect` shows `Status: enabled`.
- **Turns:** turn one runs in `agent:main:main`. Then `/session second` switches to `agent:main:second` in the same process, and turn two runs there. A second session keeps the per-session sticky fallback out of the result; the limiter's hold is process-wide.

Requests the provider actually received:

| Run | Turn one (`main`) | Turn two (`second`), 9 s later |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base `c9cc022~1`, plugin declared | `primary` 429 (retry-after 3120), then `backup` 200 | **no request to `primary`**; `backup` 200 |
| This branch, plugin declared | `primary` 429 (retry-after 3120), then `backup` 200 | **`primary` 200**: the recovered provider answers |
| This branch, no plugin (control) | `primary` 429 (retry-after 3120), then `backup` 200 | no request to `primary`; `backup` 200 |

On base, turn two logged `model_fallback_decision` `candidate_failed` for `gw/primary` with `reason: rate_limit`, `status: 429`, and `rate-limit retry floor 3111121ms exceeds retry.provider.maxRetryDelayMs=60000 for gw/primary; failing over`. That is the remaining 52-minute hold enforced locally while the provider received nothing, the reporter's symptom. In the control, the undeclared primary is still skipped (`reason: rate_limit`, `code: MODEL_FALLBACK_SKIPPED`), so providers without the declaration keep the existing protection.

**Also run:**
- Every test that covers the shared limiter or `managesOwnAvailability`: auth-profile failure marking, usage state, session override, auth labels, `models auth list`, the prepared and sticky rate-limit fallback tests, the availability policy, the stream host and the DashScope throttle integration (141 tests).
- All of `src/llm/` and the non-end-to-end `model-fallback*` tests (383 tests).
- `oxfmt`, `oxlint` and `git diff --check` are clean, and the core test typecheck reports nothing in the changed files.

**Gap:** the provider here is a local stand-in for the reporter's gateway, not a real multi-account gateway, and the run used the local embedded runtime rather than a Gateway service. Both use the same limiter and fallback runner, in one process. The two `model-fallback.*.e2e` tests need a full local build that this machine could not produce; CI runs them.

prs.title: fix: let protected secrets reach HTTPS services using configured CAs
prs.body:
Closes #135955
Related: #144830

## What Problem This Solves

Protected-secret requests to an HTTPS service signed by a private CA fail with an upstream TLS error even when the Gateway already trusts that CA through `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` or another Node default trust configuration. The secret egress proxy builds an explicit CA list from bundled roots and its own interception CA, dropping the configured trust.

## User Impact

Protected secrets can reach services signed by the operator's configured CA. Restart the Gateway after changing CA configuration. The upstream verifier and exported subprocess CA bundle both inherit that trust; clients using independent trust stores are unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing shared certificate list rather than introducing a separate trust path or configuration option:

```diff
- bundled roots + local proxy CA
+ deduplicated (bundled roots + Node default CAs) + local proxy CA
```

Keep bundled roots as the existing fallback when an OpenSSL trust store cannot enumerate its roots, and apply the existing emSign ECC G3 distrust filter to the combined set. Issuer and hostname verification, proxy authentication, exact-host secret bindings, and revocation remain enforced.

The simplification pass left two production-line replacements, a documentation update, and one focused runtime test. The test reuses the existing CA, sentinel, port-claim, and authentication helpers; it generates independent private issuers at runtime and sends only a synthetic credential.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the runtime regression reached the real proxy but failed at the configured-private-CA request: expected HTTP 200, received HTTP 502. With the fix, the request succeeds and the private HTTPS origin receives the substituted synthetic credential.
- The final regression also checks rejection before CA configuration, acceptance through the exported bundle by a verified TLS client, and refusal of an unknown issuer and a certificate hostname mismatch without another credential reaching the origin.
- Six targeted files pass: proxy server, configured CA regression, Worker, lifecycle, WebSocket, and environment — **112 tests**. Existing Worker tests retain the emSign distrust check.
- Core typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Targeted test typecheck passes (`agents-tools` graph via `--changed-paths-json`).
- `pnpm build` completes successfully (exit 0; 3m 57s). It emits advisory Control UI size/request-budget warnings; these are not represented as passing budgets.
- Independent local autoreview could not start: its evidence-path filter refused the unchanged `src/secrets/egress-proxy/proxy-forward.ts` context as sensitive. No independent-review verdict is claimed. Full PR CI and maintainer security review remain pending.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way; reverting restores the previous CA selection without a state migration.

**Blast Radius:** TLS trust. Operator-configured CAs become trusted issuers for protected-secret destinations and the exported subprocess bundle. Existing host bindings and the explicit distrust filter still apply.

Closes #205979

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: A background refresh fails with a missing-history warning when a temporary internal session is removed before it runs.

## User Impact

User impact: After an internal run ends, the background refresh no longer fails with a missing-history warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

Temporary internal sessions no longer queue transcript refreshes, since they are removed when the run ends. The durable and memory refresh paths also stop failing the whole batch when a requested transcript is gone: they refresh the transcripts that still exist and report the missing ones, and the queue then runs one full rescan so the removed session's old rollup is pruned. prs.title: fix: explain when a saved project can’t load before a session starts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw can’t load the project you last selected, starting a new session shows “Restoring your last session setup…” even after the lookup has failed. Waiting there doesn’t start the session. The same message appears when you start a session from the command palette.

## User Impact

**Before:** “Restoring your last session setup…”  
**After:** “Your saved project didn’t load. Choose a workspace.”

In New Session, open the project picker and choose your workspace. In the command palette, open session settings and select the workspace there. If you want to keep using the saved project, New Session also offers **Retry** in the project picker. No session starts until you submit again.

## Why This Change Was Made

The project list already records whether a read failed or is still running. The start control now uses that distinction only when a saved project is waiting for the list. Pending reads and retries keep their loading message. The saved selection, permission checks, retry behavior and underlying picker diagnostic stay unchanged.

**Skill in practice:** The suggested action works in both places. The command palette doesn’t have the project picker’s **Retry** button, so the shared message doesn’t tell people to look for one there. The final wording fits without clipping on the 390-pixel-wide New Session page.

## Evidence

In the actual Control UI, a controlled Gateway rejected the saved project lookup. On both surfaces, pressing the start shortcut sent no create request. Choosing a workspace and submitting again sent one create request with the original prompt and without the saved project. On New Session, retrying the list and then submitting instead sent one request for the saved project. A remembered GitHub repository in the palette recovered through the same workspace choice.

The focused saved-project regression failed on the base with the old message. All 39 tests in the submit-gates and project-catalog files passed on the patch, as did the UI type check, deterministic i18n validation, copy check, targeted lint and formatting. No live Gateway, GitHub search, full CI, non-English locale or native client was exercised.

### Clean comparison

prs.title: fix: enable Perplexity Search through ClawRouter
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter catalogs can offer Perplexity Search, but OpenClaw rejects its declared search format. This prevents `web_search` from using an otherwise eligible native or manifest offer.

## User Impact

Users selecting ClawRouter can search through eligible Perplexity Search offers with their selected Router credential. Results keep the existing untrusted-content and unsafe-URL handling. This does not change the default search provider or enable the Perplexity Agent API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing search codec registry now encodes the model-less `{query,max_results}` request and reads ordered Perplexity results. Queries must fit both the existing string limit and 8192 UTF-8 bytes. Malformed or unsafe rows consume their original result slots; later rows do not refill the requested window.

## Evidence

- Both actual registered-tool native/manifest cases failed on the unchanged base and pass with the codec.
- All 17 new registered-tool HTTP controls pass: selected credential/path/body, query/count bounds, rotation, denial, stale offers, cancellation, 30-second deadline, malformed/oversized responses and response closure.
- Timing for the new 17-case file: 63.05 seconds wall time (59.24 seconds reported by Vitest), including 30.006 seconds for the unfinished-body deadline case. The >30-second case keeps a real HTTP body open and proves the production deadline aborts it and releases the connection; a fake clock or isolated codec test cannot establish that timer/transport/closure interaction. Hosted run 44738834457: 17/17 passed; deadline case 30.009 seconds, Vitest 95.89 seconds, test shard 97.20 seconds (exit 0), tested merge `b26fd77846970350656dd4c8caa7f58a5fd925a3`. The hosted build-artifacts job was skipped; the local 160.874-second build remains separate proof.
- All 14 existing ClawRouter search-provider controls pass.
- Core, extension and agents-tools test typechecks; focused typed lint/format; extension SDK boundary guard; and `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` pass.
- Scoped source review found no actionable regression. The subsequent braces-only lint correction was reversed in memory to verify the reviewed test source exactly.

The client tests above are registered-plugin and loopback HTTP proof. Merged [ClawRouter #443](https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/443) separately qualified this exact OpenClaw head `addccb3274d885d3e06fb4662e0a620e8829523a`: 23 registered Search SDK cases and 15 outer tests through the Worker and SQLite, including post-progress cancellation retirement. Its [original consumer workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/actions/runs/44750179479) passed; all 71 products across the original CI, consumer and CodeQL workflows succeeded without skips. Registered Search uses standard pricing and cannot select Fast. Synthetic proof does not establish live vendor access, entitlement or invoices. No deployment or release is included.

prs.title: fix(daemon): resolve shell-scoped Node runtime links to their installation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related: #206272. On Windows, running openclaw gateway install (or onboard) inside a version-manager shell records that shell's own Node link into gateway.cmd. fnm exposes the running interpreter as LOCALAPPDATA/fnm_multishells/pid_stamp/node.exe, a junction that only exists while the installing shell lives. The install probe sees a supported Node and persists the junction verbatim. When the shell exits, the Scheduled Task fails with spawn ENOENT, 127.0.0.1:18789 answers ECONNREFUSED, and gateway status --deep reports a service Node runtime check failure for the vanished path.

## User Impact

A Gateway installed from an fnm shell keeps starting after that shell exits, after a reboot, and after fnm removes its per-shell junctions, because the recorded interpreter is the installation the link points at instead of the link. Operators no longer have to re-run gateway install --force from a shell that happens to still be open, and an install no longer persists a runtime path that is already doomed.

## Why This Change Was Made

resolveStableNodePath is the owner that turns a recorded interpreter path into one that survives what removes it; it handled Homebrew Cellar paths after #166222. It now resolves the selected path through fs.realpath before looking for a Homebrew replacement, so a shell-scoped junction collapses to its target with no new option, config, or policy. Existing behavior is preserved: an unresolvable path falls through untouched, and Homebrew opt/bin stabilization still runs on the resolved path. The issue's second half needs no change here: the runtime probe already labels a Node-labelled executable that answers with a Bun version as unsupported, so a Bun shim is never selected.

## Evidence


### Base vs fix

New regression test (`resolves shell-scoped runtime links to the persistent installation path`) on the
branch base `7857d5ae3a5`, before any source change:

```text
 RUN  v5.0.5 <workspace>/openclaw-main

 [skip] |boundary| src/infra/stable-node-path.test.ts > resolveStableNodePath > returns non-cellar paths unchanged
 [skip] |boundary| src/infra/stable-node-path.test.ts > resolveStableNodePath > prefers the Homebrew opt symlink for default and versioned formulas
 [FAIL] |boundary| src/infra/stable-node-path.test.ts > resolveStableNodePath > resolves shell-scoped runtime links to the persistent installation path 19ms
   expected '...\\fnm_multishells\\38344_1795483895345\\node.exe' to be '...\\fnm\\node-versions\\v26.13.1\\installation\\node.exe' // Object.is equality
Expected: "C:\\Users\\...\\dir-0\\fnm\\node-versions\\v26.13.1\\installation\\node.exe"
Received: "C:\\Users\\...\\dir-0\\fnm_multishells\\38344_1795483895345\\node.exe"
 at src/infra/stable-node-path.test.ts:45:53

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 4 skipped (5)
```

The same test file on the fix head:

```text
 [pass] |boundary| src/infra/stable-node-path.test.ts > resolveStableNodePath > returns non-cellar paths unchanged 2ms
 [pass] |boundary| src/infra/stable-node-path.test.ts > resolveStableNodePath > prefers the Homebrew opt symlink for default and versioned formulas 10ms
 [pass] |boundary| src/infra/stable-node-path.test.ts > resolveStableNodePath > resolves shell-scoped runtime links to the persistent installation path 8ms
 [pass] |boundary| src/infra/stable-node-path.test.ts > resolveStableNodePath > falls back to the bin symlink for the default formula, otherwise original path 4ms
 [pass] |boundary| src/infra/stable-node-path.test.ts > resolveLaunchableNodePath > keeps the running Cellar executable until an upgrade removes it 9ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

Consumer of the changed helper (`resolveStableNodePath` is also used by the CLI shim and the daemon
restore path):

```text
 [pass] |infra| src/infra/openclaw-cli-shim.test.ts > renders a Windows PATH launcher for the running CLI 29ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed | 7 skipped (10)
```

### Intent audit

`git log --oneline -3 -- src/infra/stable-node-path.ts` is dominated by
`f0c9bcfbe30 fix(process): exec and MCP servers fail with ENOENT after a Homebrew Node upgrade (#166222)`.
That commit introduced this owner for exactly one reason: an upgrade removed the recorded interpreter
path. This change keeps that contract and extends the same normalization to shell-scoped links, so a
recorded path is the installation rather than a link the installer shell owns. No existing behavior is
overturned: paths that cannot be resolved still fall through unchanged, and Homebrew Cellar stabilization
now runs on the resolved path.

### Not run / boundaries

- `src/daemon/runtime-paths.test.ts` fails 19 cases on this Windows host **on the unmodified base as well**
  (`ERR_INVALID_FILE_URL_PATH` while probing fake POSIX and drive paths; e.g.
  `selects a supported current versioned Node executable on Windows` fails with
  `Node runtime check failed for D:\Tools\node24.exe ... ERR_INVALID_FILE_URL_PATH`). Re-ran that single
  case with `src/infra/stable-node-path.ts` restored to base: same failure, so it is pre-existing and
  unrelated to this change.
- The issue's second half (a Bun-provided `node.exe` shim written into `gateway.cmd`) is already handled by
  the existing runtime probe: `resolveRuntimeInfo` reports `capabilityError = "The executable is Bun, not Node."`
  for a Node-labelled executable that answers with a Bun version, so the candidate is `unsupported` and is
  not selected. No Bun shim exists on this Windows host, so that half was verified by reading the probe
  contract and the existing `rejects a Bun node shim ...` case in `src/daemon/runtime-paths.test.ts`, not by
  a local run.
- No end-to-end `openclaw gateway install` run: on Windows that writes `gateway.cmd` and registers the
  `OpenClaw Gateway` Scheduled Task in this machine's real profile. The recorded-path claim is proven at the
  owner boundary (`resolveStableNodePath`) with a real junction on disk instead.
- Local ClawSweeper: WARN, engine did not complete (raw output kept in the proof directory as
  `local-clawsweeper.log`).
- Fork PR CI stays `action_required` until a maintainer approves the run.

prs.title: improve: copy less session data when restoring warm prompt caches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the Gateway first checks which prompt caches to keep warm, it requests every saved session’s summary. A store with hundreds of inactive sessions sends their metadata back to the Gateway even if only a few sessions qualify.

## User Impact

The Gateway can resume an existing keep-warm series or find a recently active chat by receiving only the matching session keys. This reduces the amount of data copied into the Gateway after startup. Existing installations pick up the change automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session worker already owns database selection and canonical validation. It now checks the original activity and last-ping timestamps before returning keys. A single read snapshot and ordered 64-row pages bound the candidate scan, including on PostgreSQL, which buffers each query. The worker still checks cold rows for invalid delivery aliases. Memory-only sessions use their existing actor and permissions.

## Evidence

- On Linux x64 with Node 24.22.1, both readers selected the same two keys from 133 synthetic sessions. The original worker returned 133 summaries. The new response contained those two keys and zero summaries. Serializing the complete returned objects with Node V8 measured **189,142 bytes versus 330 bytes**. This measures response size. Peak process RSS was outside this test.
- The original full list, the key-only read, a repeat key-only read and a repeat full list took 40.90, 3.46, 1.62 and 1.36 ms in one retained worker. These ordered timings include a first read and cached repeats.
- The focused Node suites passed all 11 cases, including the exact cutoff, a recent preserved ping with old activity, stale side-column values, a dirty alias elsewhere in the store, memory-only actor ownership, and deferral under host memory pressure.

prs.title: fix(exec): charge shared pages once in the host memory budget
prs.body:
Root cause: src/process/child-memory.ts:165 `readMemory()` charged each process its full `VmRSS`/`VmSwap`, and `totalUsage()` adds every distinct PID, so a page shared by N processes in an exec tree was charged N times.

Fixes #206082

## What users see

- Before: headless Chromium (about 425 MiB real) and forked worker pools were killed in about 1.5 s with "Command killed because the shared host exec memory budget was exceeded".
- After: each process is charged its proportional share (`Pss`/`SwapPss` from `/proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup`), so a shared page counts once. Real private growth is still killed.
- A process whose `smaps_rollup` is unreadable or has no `Pss` line (non-dumpable, old kernel) keeps the full `VmRSS` charge. A parse miss never charges 0.

## Change

- `src/process/child-memory.ts`: read `smaps_rollup` first, fall back to `status`. Comment on the remaining overcount updated.
- `docs/tools/exec.md`: describe PSS charging and when shared pages can still count more than once.
- Test: one new case (PSS under budget with RSS over budget: no kill; PSS grows over: cancelled once, swap from `SwapPss`). The degraded-read case now rejects both reads.
- No config, flag or state.

## Evidence

Observed lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206396#issuecomment-7210339681

Real agent `exec` turns through an isolated Gateway built from base and this head (secretless Linux container, scripted model), two passes each. Budget 593-624 MiB.

| Workload | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Python 200 MiB + 5 idle forks (RSS 1234, PSS 207) | killed, RAM 1294/601 | exits 0 |
| `chromium --headless=new about:blank` 60 s (RSS 1023, PSS 425) | killed in 1.5 s | alive at 60 s |
| 900 MiB private hog | killed | killed |
| 900 MiB hog with `PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0` | killed | killed (RSS fallback) |
| 2 fork trees + 400 MiB hog | both trees killed | only the hog cancelled |
| 700 MiB + 9 `setsid` copies, `background: true` | killed, RAM 7114 | killed, RAM 729 (copies stay charged) |

Poll cost: `smaps_rollup` takes about 6-7 ms per GiB resident per process on a libuv pool thread (8 GiB touched + 7 forks: 442 ms per poll; base `status`: 1 ms). An 8 GiB shared tree ran 45 s through a real Gateway exec with `/readyz` p50 1.0 ms, p95 2.3 ms.

Thanks @jzmudzinski for the report, the measurements and the proposed fix.

prs.title: fix: hide internal session delivery failure notices from chat queue and history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a delayed peer `sessions_send` delivery fails (for example, when the target session is stopped or its run fails while the requesting session is busy), OpenClaw wakes the requesting agent with an internal model instruction (`sessions_send delivery to ... failed. The target may not have received the message; retry or report the failure instead of assuming delivery succeeded.`). Because that notice was persisted like a normal peer message without `display: false`, it leaked into the Control UI composer queue as a queued row (with a `"Forwarded from ..."` avatar and remove button) and stayed visible in chat history alongside the assistant's actual response.

## User Impact

Internal `sessions_send` delivery failure instructions stay in the model transcript for the requesting agent to handle, and no longer appear in the chat composer queue, live updates, or chat history. Genuine peer `sessions_send` messages, replies, and human quotes remain visible, and the requesting assistant's own response stays visible. Already-persisted failure notices are also hidden from history on reload. No configuration changes or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Mark host-authored `sessions_send` delivery failure wakes as hidden (`hideInput: true`) at the producer (`runSessionsSendA2AFlow`) and carry that fact through the existing in-process `SessionSendDelivery.returnedResult` admission boundary so `prepareAgentRunUserTurn` persists them with `display: false`.
- Share the notice text contract in `src/sessions/sessions-send-failure-notice.ts` so display projection also hides already-persisted legacy failure notices without matching human messages or genuine peer replies.
- Exclude hidden queued inputs from `readChatPendingInputs`'s `queuedCount` and from the Control UI composer queue projection so hidden internal wakes do not surface as queued items or trigger spurious queue-discovery pagination.

## Evidence

- [Before and after: the composer queue](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205104#issuecomment-7209747580) (Chromium, simulated Gateway, synthetic inputs). The rebased head passed 74 focused server tests and 2 queue-display tests.

- Regression tests failed on base (`8fd2185d49da`) and passed after the fix across all touched boundaries:
  - `pnpm test src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.a2a.test.ts src/agents/tools/agent-step.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-send-reply-flow.requester.test.ts src/gateway/chat-display-projection.visibility.test.ts src/gateway/chat-display-projection.automation-repair.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/chat-pending-inputs.test.ts src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-settle-continuation.native.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pending-input-display.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pending-inputs.pagination.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pending-inputs.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (10 test files, 145 tests passed).
- Static checks passed on the final tree:
  - `pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:ui && pnpm tsgo:test:src && pnpm tsgo:test:ui`
  - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on all 17 modified/added files (0 problems)
  - `pnpm format:check && git diff --check`
- Local review: `autoreview` (`codex` / `gpt-6.1-sol`, `--mode local --max-priority P2`) completed on the full local diff with 0 actionable P0–P2 findings (`scoped-clean`). Local `clawsweeper` is not installed on this host.
