prs.title: fix: explain why chat won’t attach an empty file
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a chat attachment is empty, OpenClaw says to try again. The same empty file will fail every time, whether you chose it or an embedded app supplied it.

## User Impact

**Before:** “Could not attach file. Try again.”

**After:** “OpenClaw can’t attach empty files.”

If you chose the file, you can attach a nonempty replacement without rebuilding your draft. If an app supplied it, the notice explains what failed without telling you to use a file picker. The app still receives a rejection; its message isn’t sent.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw already checks for empty files before trying to read them. Only that notice changes. A genuine read failure keeps its existing message, and an oversized file still takes priority when a selection contains both oversized and empty files.

**Skill in practice:** Name the cause the system knows. Offer a next step only if the reader can take it: here the composer knows the file is empty, but not who chose it.

## Evidence

In the real Control UI, a draft already contained text and an attached `agenda.txt`. Selecting a zero-byte `meeting-notes.txt` in the file picker showed the notice and left the text and original attachment intact. A nonempty replacement with the same name attached successfully. The synthetic Gateway received no send request until **Send message**, then received the draft and both files. Verified in Chromium at 390 × 800 and 1060 × 720. This proves the outgoing browser request, not delivery by a live Gateway or model.

The empty pasted-file regression failed on the base. Both the paste and embedded-app regressions failed on the earlier two-sentence wording. With the correction, the app test observed the same notice, a negative receipt, and no call to the send handler. All 45 tests in the two focused suites passed. The UI typecheck, touched-file lint and formatting, copy check, i18n baseline and verification, and diff check passed. The production Control UI build completed; its size report flagged largest CSS gzip (57.2 vs. 56.9 KiB), chat boot requests (21 vs. 20), and chat boot JS gzip (1306.2 vs. 1305.0 KiB).

Independent source review identified the embedded-app caller as a case where a file-picker instruction would be misleading. After the correction, the campaign coordinator checked the shared notice, the app regression, and the revised screenshots.

The four screenshots below show the same draft at 390 × 800 in the light theme. Before: `7857d5ae3a5a`. After: reviewed source tree `1a80245aa523`.

prs.title: improve(memory): release matched rows before indexing workspace files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

During a workspace-memory rescan, the index manager keeps the entire stored source snapshot and a second set of eligible paths until stale deletion finishes. A deferred batch can hold those collections across a foreground yield.

## Proposed Change

Compare every eligible entry against the same stored snapshot, including duplicate host paths. Then discard matched keys and retain only stale rows in database order. Apply their captured hashes through the existing locked deletion operation after successful indexing. Session cleanup, watcher policy and file discovery keep their existing owners. This draft tracks a candidate for [the large-directory Gateway investigation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/200227).

## Preregistered Acceptance

- Use the frozen [baseline](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/269fb089edfbf3bd910383f9b65968a475610541) and the same Linux x64 AWS host, Node version, pnpm install, 101,963-file tree and 7,778 observed directories. Restore a byte-identical indexed database to the same path for each process. The five-append workload comes from the [historical driver](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/200227#issuecomment-7182141581), SHA-256 `89fc4509ec104495e72fe3b93dae4af165017a96f1d29d8e06af0774e3ee9b53`.
- Run five interleaved pairs, alternating which build runs first. Each process warms the resident Gateway search tool, receives five appends six seconds apart, indexes all five before the next search RPC, returns all five hits and settles for 20 seconds. Require zero observer overflows. Separately verify, on both builds, an equal-size sibling edit with its mtime restored.
- The primary metric is sampled **whole-Gateway peak RSS from the first append through settled search**. Require a lower candidate median and lower candidate peaks in at least four of five matched pairs. Report median, nearest-rank p95 and range. Also report warm-up separately, main and total CPU, time to five search hits and filesystem access counts. Investigate material slowdown or higher tail cost.
- Inspect retained state across indexing and a foreground yield separately. Exercise duplicate paths, eligibility, failed indexing, retry order and captured-hash cleanup. A phase-local improvement alone will close this draft without a production landing.

### Measurement driver revision

The [corrected Linux driver](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/074cfad15678c42eb6084a6de2f40fe246f895c9/scripts/perf/memory-gateway-append-measure.py) has SHA-256 `78f8e3f804cdd5dfa6f0831d5564ab24bf00165a0eab7d22133d0773efb5ad9b`. The historical driver above skipped samples while the search RPC blocked. Use the corrected driver for every formal arm. An independent 100 ms sampler checks the listener's process group and start ticks, reports sample counts and maximum gaps both during the RPC and across the primary interval, and rejects gaps over one second. Only fixture initialization creates an owned private directory. Each run locks it, restores its checkpoint and creates its five files exclusively. The three-directory smoke fixture and 7,778-directory full fixture both check registration coverage. The runtime requirements and invocation are in the driver. The workload, pair order and acceptance thresholds above are unchanged.

## Full Gateway comparison

The candidate met the preregistered threshold on the frozen baseline and signed head. Median peak fell **154,292 KiB (7.01%)**. Four of five paired peaks fell. Nearest-rank p95 fell from 2,328,164 to 2,271,336 KiB. Stock ranged from 2,116,620 to 2,328,164 KiB and the candidate from 1,934,460 to 2,271,336 KiB. [All ten arms and output](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_608202059330e8b154d2e1284929b93a)

| Pair | Stock peak KiB | Candidate peak KiB |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 2,200,084 | 2,045,792 |
| 2 | 2,209,596 | 2,271,336 |
| 3 | 2,155,824 | 1,982,340 |
| 4 | 2,116,620 | 1,934,460 |
| 5 | 2,328,164 | 2,194,564 |

Median main-thread CPU was 20.57 → 20.24 s and total CPU was 90.58 → 90.21 s. Time to the five search hits was 36.459 → 36.952 s (nearest-rank p95 37.453 → 37.957 s). Time through settlement was 69.484 → 69.473 s. Median sampled RSS peak **after the resident tool search returned, through warm-up settlement**, was 1,505,884 → 1,450,416 KiB. All ten processes registered 7,781 watches, indexed all five files before the next RPC, returned all five paths, and recorded 101,968 distinct Markdown paths, 305,912 access events and zero observer overflows. The independent sampler collected 679–715 interior samples across each primary interval (largest gap 100.3 ms), and 9–10 during every search RPC (largest gap 100.2 ms). prs.title: fix: keep sessions going when a model writes its tool call as text instead of calling the tool
prs.body:
Closes #205006

## What Problem This Solves

Local models on OpenAI-compatible providers sometimes write their next tool call as plain text instead of calling the tool, in two shapes the issue reports:

- OpenClaw's own history notation, `[tool call id=... name=...] {args}`, which the model sees for past calls and copies.
- An XML-style call, `<tool_call><function=read>...`, written after some prose or cut off mid-sentence where the model starts it.

In both cases OpenClaw treats the turn as a finished answer: no tool runs, nothing is logged, and the interactive session or scheduled job stops mid-task. For the bracket shape the raw pseudo-call is the last message; for the XML shape the call is stripped and the user is left with a half sentence such as "Let me check the notes file first".

## User Impact

A reply that is only bracket-notation calls, or that ends in an XML text call for an offered tool (complete or cut off, on its own lines or after prose on the same line), now goes through the existing text-tool-call recovery: the model gets one request to call the tool natively when replay is safe, and a repeated text call ends with the existing visible "wrote a tool call as text" failure instead of a silent success. Nothing is executed from text, transcripts are not rewritten, and no configuration changes.

Accepted edges, on purpose:

- A call followed by more prose stays a literal example, as do calls inside code spans or fences and calls naming a tool that is not offered.
- An answer that merely ends by naming a tag ("To read a file the model writes `<function=read>`", written without code formatting) stays an ordinary answer: a bare opening tag with no parameter, no closing tag and no `<tool_call>` wrapper is not treated as a call.
- A fragment cut off before the tool name is complete (a bare `<tool_call>` or `<function=re`) is not recognized, since it names no tool.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recovery path already exists and is documented in `docs/concepts/agent-loop.md`; two things kept these replies away from it.

- The non-executing detector did not know the one notation OpenClaw itself renders (`convertMessages` in `packages/ai/src/openai-completions-messages.ts`). It now accepts a reply made only of `[tool call id=<id> name=<tool>] {json object}` entries, at least one naming an offered tool.
- For XML calls, the stream wrapper that scrubs text calls out of a reply with other visible text runs before the terminal check, so the check only saw the leftover prose. The scrub now reports when the removed text ended the reply (a complete call followed at most by an orphaned wrapper closer, or an unfinished call), and the terminal check also recognizes a `<function=tool>` call that ends the reply in the middle of a line, which the line-start scrub grammar does not cover. Both feed the existing `textToolCallAttempt` fact; there is no new recovery path.

## Evidence

Live, isolated Gateway from source (`pnpm openclaw gateway`) with a stub OpenAI-compatible model that answers the first request with text only, `finish_reason: "stop"` and no `tool_calls`; one `pnpm openclaw agent` turn asking what `notes.txt` says. Before runs are on the previous head `36ef4b5` (bracket: on main); after runs are on this branch.

Reply cut off at an inline XML call (`Let me check the notes file first <tool_call><function=read><parameter=path>notes`):

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shu-chen-dot-ca/shu-chen-dot-ca/1b7b56716a206eb6d7c8cef8b89e93bfbd0c4dd3/draft_aa11dc/ev_c7f7d2.jpg) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shu-chen-dot-ca/shu-chen-dot-ca/1b7b56716a206eb6d7c8cef8b89e93bfbd0c4dd3/draft_aa11dc/ev_b76e36.jpg) |

Complete XML call on its own lines after prose:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shu-chen-dot-ca/shu-chen-dot-ca/1b7b56716a206eb6d7c8cef8b89e93bfbd0c4dd3/draft_aa11dc/ev_2f662d.jpg) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shu-chen-dot-ca/shu-chen-dot-ca/1b7b56716a206eb6d7c8cef8b89e93bfbd0c4dd3/draft_aa11dc/ev_c1f8ab.jpg) |

Bracket notation as the whole reply:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shu-chen-dot-ca/shu-chen-dot-ca/1b7b56716a206eb6d7c8cef8b89e93bfbd0c4dd3/draft_aa11dc/ev_da5a06.jpg) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shu-chen-dot-ca/shu-chen-dot-ca/1b7b56716a206eb6d7c8cef8b89e93bfbd0c4dd3/draft_aa11dc/ev_b88514.jpg) |

- The two inline runs (cut off, and a complete call on the same line as prose, where the user previously got only the prose) were repeated on the final commit and recover with a real `read` call. The screenshots and the other live runs were taken on earlier commits of this change, before the bare-opening-tag rule above was added; that rule does not touch the shapes they show.
- Also run live: a reply cut off inside a multi-line call (before: prose plus a stray `<tool_call>`) recovers; a call followed by "That is all." is unchanged, one model request and a literal reply; with a stub that repeats the cut-off XML text on every request there are two model requests, then the visible failure "The model wrote a tool call as text instead of calling the tool. No tool ran for that call."
- Red on base, green with the fix: with the production files from `36ef4b5`, the new cases in `run/attempt-result.test.ts` and `run/attempt-tool-call-text-promotion.test.ts` fail; with the fix both files pass. For the first commit, the new cases in `packages/tool-call-repair/src/attempt.test.ts` fail with `attempt.ts` from main.
- `pnpm test` with `--maxWorkers=1` on the four `run/attempt-tool-call-text-promotion*.test.ts` files, `run/attempt-result.test.ts`, `run/run-attempt-result.test.ts`, `run/terminal-resolution.text-tool-call.test.ts`, `run/attempt.test.ts`, `run/attempt-execution-phase.test.ts`, `run/attempt-stream-prepare.test.ts`, `run/attempt-stream-finalize.test.ts`, `run/attempt-stream-settle.test.ts`, the `stream-normalizer`, `stream-normalizer.scrub-cache`, `attempt` and `grammar` tests in `packages/tool-call-repair`, `src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` and `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.lifecycle.test.ts`: all pass.
- `pnpm check:changed` (lint, format, core and core-test typechecks, guards) passes with `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1`. The dead export scan did not complete locally: Knip's full-tree scan hits its 600 s limit on my machine, on unchanged main as well. The change adds no exports.
- Not run: local autoreview or ClawSweeper, and a real Qwen/vLLM setup; the stub model reproduces the reported turn shapes only.

prs.title: fix(agents): Code Mode secret requests are cancelled when the turn ends
prs.body:
Root cause: `src/agents/code-mode-bridge.ts:202` `requiresCodeModeCompletion` made a cell required only for native `ask_user` (since #197108) and for `exec`/`agents_wait` with `awaitResults: true`. A native `secrets({action: "request"})` call, which also waits for the human, was left out. So the cell parked as `waiting` after the 10 s cell budget, turn teardown closed it, and the pending secret card was cancelled and shown as "API key: Skipped".

Follow-up to #197108 / #197024 (same root cause, same harm, different human-waiting tool). Thanks @migelizaga-rgb for the original `ask_user` report and @harjothkhara for the #197108 fix this extends.

Real occurrence: I found no user report of this one. GitHub issue searches and the Discord archive (keyword and semantic) turned up nothing. The bug was found while proving #197108. It has the same root cause as #197024 and the same user harm, reproduced below on current main.

Evidence (Control UI, before/after screenshots and controls): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206403#issuecomment-7210517388

## What Problem This Solves

In Code Mode, if an agent asks for an API key with `secrets({action: "request", ...})` in an ordinary cell, the secret card disappears about 10 s after it appears. The transcript then says "API key: Skipped" although nobody skipped it, and the agent never gets the key.

## User Impact

The secret card stays open until the owner enters the value, skips it, the request's `timeoutSeconds` runs out, or the run is stopped. Entering the key through the card stores it and returns `status: "stored"` to the agent. The agent no longer has to remember `wait` or `awaitResults` to keep the card alive.

## Why This Change Was Made

#197108 made native `ask_user` required Code Mode work so a pending question is never cancelled at turn end. A secrets `request` is the same kind of call: it opens a question card and waits for the human. This change treats only the native core binding `openclaw:core:secrets` with `action: "request"` as required. `list` and `delete` return immediately and stay as they were. A client tool named `secrets` resolves to a different binding id, so it doesn't match.

## Evidence

Built in secretless `node:24.22.1` Docker (base `2bacc4a6e9`, current main including #197108; candidate `04c20a9ba4`). The Gateway runs in the container, real Chromium drives the built Control UI, and a scripted model runs one ordinary cell that calls `secrets({action: "request"})`. On `waiting` the model ends its turn and never calls `wait`.

| Case | Build | Card | Question | Agent got |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| request, run 1 | main | gone at t+10 s, "API key: Skipped" | `cancelled` after 11 s | `waiting` (handed back) |
| request, run 2 | main | gone at t+10 s, "API key: Skipped" | `cancelled` after 9 s | `waiting` (handed back) |
| request, run 1 | fix | visible at t+5/20/64 s, key entered via the card at t+66 s | `answered` | `completed`, `status: "stored"` |
| request, run 2 | fix | visible at t+5/20/64 s, key entered via the card at t+66 s | `answered` | `completed`, `status: "stored"` |
| Stop at t+20 s | fix | gone after Stop | `cancelled` | run stopped |
| `timeoutSeconds: 30` | fix | visible at t+20 s | `expired` at 30 s | `completed`, `no_answer` |
| `timeoutSeconds: 30` | main | gone at t+10 s | `cancelled` | `waiting` |
| `action: "list"` | main / fix | no card | n/a | `completed` in 1-2 s (unchanged) |

The secret was a fresh random fake per run, typed into the masked field. It does not appear in the page after the reply, `chat.history`, the Gateway log, the model requests, or any other run output. The only place it is stored is the secret store row (`secret_store_entries.value`), where it belongs.

Unit: the #197108 regression in `src/agents/code-mode.wait.test.ts` now runs for both `ask_user` and `secrets` `request`. On base the `secrets` case fails (`status: "failed"`) and on this branch it passes. `code-mode.wait` plus the tests that import `code-mode-bridge.ts` pass. oxfmt and oxlint are clean.

Merge danger: two-way door. One predicate branch and one doc line; a revert fully undoes it. No state, config or contract change. Blast radius: Code Mode cells that call native `secrets` with `action: "request"`. Such a cell now stays open until the request is answered, skipped, times out or the run is stopped. Like `ask_user` since #197108, `secrets` request followed by `yield_control` now fails as unfinished required work, where before the card was silently cancelled.

prs.title: feat: review conservative English dictation cleanup before sending
prs.body:
Related: #205635

**Draft. Conservative mode currently preserves recognized text for review; semantic cleanup is unavailable.**

## What Problem This Solves

Control UI dictation normally adds the recognizer’s text straight to the unsent draft. This proposal lets people review that text before insertion, without guessing whether a hesitation, correction, or repetition was intentional.

## User Impact

- **Off** remains the default and keeps existing dictation behavior. The browser/Gateway-scoped **Conservative — English (unavailable)** option preserves recognized text for review in Chat, New Session, and the session sidebar; it makes no semantic edits.
- **Use original** stays disabled while recognition is finalizing and inserts only into the unsent draft. Escape closes the dialog without dismissing the review. An intervening edit revokes insertion but leaves **Copy original text** available while the review remains authorized.
- There is no cleaned candidate, cleaned acceptance, or **Restore original** action. Source text over 32 KiB is not retained for copying. Setting Off removes the override. Native clients, recognition-provider selection, and sent messages are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing composer owns capture and ordered finalization; the review reuses its draft and connection scope. Deterministic source-range validation stays in place but does not decide intent. There is no regex intent classification, new model route, or public Gateway contract.

**Decision needed:** choose browser-local scope or a shared preparation and preference contract, and approve a semantic decision owner and preservation criteria before shipping cleanup. See [the original review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205789#issuecomment-7184803694), [the shared-settings proposal](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205638), and companion drafts #205788, #205794, #205791, and #205792. This is not maintainer approval of those contracts.

This work was implemented with Codex and peer-agent review. It does not claim human maintainer design acceptance. Contributor: [@CompleteDotTech](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech). Allow edits by maintainers is enabled; this update changes no workflows or secrets.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/11774947-fc71-4ad4-9414-25c958e5c810)

## Evidence

**Current candidate:** `fff944112b3b5bf65301c5c2cce3ad450ec87ac0`. This fast-forward addresses the [revision 2 P2 finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205789#issuecomment-7184803694): original-text review no longer constructs or validates a synthetic deletion plan or computes an unused candidate/source map. The 32 KiB UTF-8 limit, source checks, draft ownership, and original-text insertion are unchanged. Targeted formatting, whitespace, and source-only Auto Review (no P0–P2 findings) passed. The candidate’s focused tests, paired visual capture, and stable-upgrade/data compatibility lane are pending contributor execution. The WAV results below apply to the earlier head only.

**Previous candidate:** `8b9b1489296846a05300227a2670a14df8cd67a8`. This is a fast-forward of `79b16ed99b15a2cfcbb03ebbd6a9afd78fd46eda` and preserves the merged upstream `2fda93cf03a882cd080e7984392d50b95c4737aa`. Both PRs point to the same source head. The repair separates cleanup labels from the select’s option text, records direct composer edits after the owning input handler, fixes removal metadata type narrowing without relaxing validation, and uses the shared modal layout instead of a separate stylesheet. All 36 preservation scenarios remain.

- **Static checks on the published tree:** isolated TypeScript check of `dictation-cleanup.ts`, targeted formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The trusted test-line ratchet passed against the merged upstream base (+1,095) and the fork CI comparison base `47027a257c728b267390eaac72147eaea55f0283` (+1,129): 400 ordinary lines plus 729 allocation. The extra 34 on the fork base comes from the upstream Activity-chart regression merged into the feature branch, not from dictation tests. Source-only Auto Review of the repair delta against `79b16ed` reported no findings at P0–P2; it did not run browser tests or compile the application.
- **Product CI:** ordinary fork PR CI was retired; [fork run 45882652922](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45882652922) is no longer a proof route. Upstream product CI skips drafts; the PR context/evidence check is not product CI. The contributor workflow below is separate interim evidence, not an upstream production typecheck/build, deployment-fixture, Chromium regression suite, or paired boot-budget result.

### Prerecorded-WAV proof and follow-up

- On `8b9b148`, the contributor’s [separate scripted-audio workflow](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45921015603/job/140251899230) used Chromium fake-media capture with a prerecorded WAV and live OpenAI buffered transcription. Reported results: Chat Off 3/3 passed; Chat Conservative retained the exact final text but reported failed preparation 3/3; New Session and Side chat did not render a composer 3/3 each. No send was observed. The public job recorded the failure; the per-take artifact is not publicly downloadable, and the old harness did not retain marker metadata or visible alert text.
- **Previous WAV candidate:** `7ea1297feb705b5ac8350bb45c93823837d659a3`. This fast-forward fixes finality by excluding the relay’s empty audio-commit/turn-end lifecycle markers from transcript processing, and restores the shared direct-composer listener import. A deterministic regression replays the source-defined buffered-relay sequence. The +16 allocation covers this test only. Targeted formatting, whitespace, and trusted test-line checks passed on the repair (+1,111 versus merged upstream; +1,145 versus the previous fork comparison base). Source-only Auto Review found no P0–P2 issues in the three code/test files.

- **Exact-head rerun for `7ea1297` — [Actions run 45936334236](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45936334236):** the contributor’s [public job log](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45936334236/job/140300587449) records checkout of `7ea1297feb705b5ac8350bb45c93823837d659a3`, a successful build for the harness, and **13/13 passed** in `composer-dictation-source.test.ts` before the browser run, including the buffered-relay finality regression. Chromium fake-media capture with a prerecorded WAV used live OpenAI buffered transcription (`gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`). **12/12 takes passed** across Alloy, Nova, and Sage:

  | Case | Passed |
  | --- | ---: |
  | `chat-off` | 3/3 |
  | `chat-review-and-send` | 3/3 |
  | `new-session-edit-and-copy` | 3/3 |
  | `sidebar-use-original` | 3/3 |

prs.title: fix: preserve Qwen4-Max thinking effort selections
prs.body:
Closes #206303
Related: #206346 (parallel draft)

## What Problem This Solves

Qwen4-Max requests enable thinking but omit the selected effort, so `low` and `xhigh` send identical thinking settings. The [vendor contract](https://help.aliyun.com/zh/model-studio/qwen4-max) supports distinct `low`, `high`, and `xhigh` values.

## User Impact

Qwen4-Max sends the requested effort on Standard and Token Plan routes. `minimal`, `medium`, and `max` remain accepted and map to `low`, `high`, and `xhigh`. Thinking off, explicit token budgets, and Qwen3.8's different middle-tier mapping are preserved. No configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

I extended the existing Qwen-owned effort mapper and thinking-profile fallback instead of adding another payload adapter or a core setting. Both payload passes use the same mapping, including caller replacement hooks.

## Evidence

I exercised the production Qwen wrapper, `streamSimple`, and serialized HTTP requests in an AWS Crabbox VM against a loopback recorder. The response was synthetic; this is request-boundary proof, not live Qwen inference.

Before, on main `eb138870ef39b80cf34a58aabbd052871c4eff41`:

```text
qwen4-max low:   enable_thinking=true reasoning_effort=(absent) FAIL
qwen4-max xhigh: enable_thinking=true reasoning_effort=(absent) FAIL
RESULT: 3/7 contracts passed
```

After, on candidate `21ba09aac376b663ba59c8977fdc229dec7b72c2`, repeating the same seven-case HTTP check:

```text
qwen4-max off: enable_thinking=false reasoning_effort=(absent) expected=(absent) PASS
qwen4-max low: enable_thinking=true reasoning_effort=low expected=low PASS
qwen4-max medium: enable_thinking=true reasoning_effort=high expected=high PASS
qwen4-max high: enable_thinking=true reasoning_effort=high expected=high PASS
qwen4-max xhigh: enable_thinking=true reasoning_effort=xhigh expected=xhigh PASS
qwen3.8-max low: enable_thinking=true reasoning_effort=low expected=low PASS
qwen3.8-max high: enable_thinking=true reasoning_effort=xhigh expected=xhigh PASS
RESULT: 7/7 contracts passed
```

I also ran the actual thinking-selection owner before the same HTTP transport. This caught an alias-admission regression in the unpublished draft, which I fixed before committing:

```text
qwen4-max minimal: admission=ACCEPTED enable_thinking=true reasoning_effort=low expected=low PASS
qwen4-max medium: admission=ACCEPTED enable_thinking=true reasoning_effort=high expected=high PASS
qwen4-max max: admission=ACCEPTED enable_thinking=true reasoning_effort=xhigh expected=xhigh PASS
RESULT: 3/3 contracts passed
```

- 68 focused tests passed: Qwen stream, registration, catalog, discovery, and agent-tool prefix stability. The original new regressions failed without the mapping fix. Wrapper wall time: 113.79 seconds; hosted CI seconds not yet available.
- Qwen production package typecheck, targeted lint, formatting parity, and `git diff --check` passed. The first typecheck lacked SDK declarations; lint generated them through the supported owner, and the unchanged typecheck then passed.
- `pr-simplify`: one shared mapper, existing hook/budget regressions extended rather than duplicated. Against the base: production +46/-15 lines, tests +62/-33, documentation +6.
- Remaining limitations: live Qwen acceptance and isolated Gateway/real-model execution remain unverified. The prior protected live attempt reported an unconfigured provider. The prior local autoreview attempt failed its required read-only Codex sandbox preflight; no independent review of the final candidate is claimed. 

### Review follow-up

I addressed the [ClawSweeper P2 finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206385#issuecomment-7210351454) by renaming all six model-discriminator uses from `generation` to `modelGeneration` in `extensions/qwen/stream.ts`. The detector's hit was a false positive for session identity, but the resulting CI failure was real. Mapping behavior, tests, the checker, and its allowlist are unchanged.

I reproduced the ratchet failure on `4f02fc2cf0f949e7f7722aa31a2c96ce3a422174` and reran the same command after the rename:

```text
Before: extensions/qwen/stream.ts: 1 > 0
QWEN_RATCHET_BEFORE_EXIT=1
After: Session identity ratchet OK: 1555 files, 6192 grandfathered pins.
```

On repair commit `6e9de65488717637130eb1e53a7de2e2350bac78`, I reran the Qwen stream and registration tests plus agent-tool prefix stability: 62 tests passed in 83.88 seconds. Qwen package typecheck, targeted lint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Published head `abd85167431e7090cf4e10153e1d233be91f3150` has the identical tested tree (`3ac30d1069b181aff793e92774228f623c7afe6c`). The repair only renames the discriminator; simplification review removed nothing.

The review's live-model proof request is a valid remaining evidence gap, not a reason to change the mapper. The configured provider was unavailable, so I do not claim isolated-Gateway/live-Qwen success on either Standard or Token Plan. [Recorded, redacted HTTP proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206385#issuecomment-7210472133) is posted with the explicit limitation that live Qwen inference was not run.

Hosted CI is green on `abd85167431e7090cf4e10153e1d233be91f3150`, including [checks-fast-baseline-ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45944428355/job/140326362124) and [openclaw/ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45944428355/job/140328043025). Out-of-scope skipped lanes are not claimed as passed.

## Contributor

Co-authored with @daniel-lxs.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-qwen-effort-mapping-fix-sd80760ea)

## Worked on by

- @daniel-lxs

prs.title: fix: let a per-call timeoutMs reach closed-schema Codex tools instead of failing after the gate passes
prs.body:
Root cause: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.ts:337` (main 2237f16b7e27). The Codex bridge forwards `call.arguments` unchanged after the dynamic-tool watchdog has already used the per-call `timeoutMs`/`timeoutSeconds` (`dynamic-tool-execution.ts:506-518`). Hooks run before validation (`src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts:382` then `:429`). So a tool whose schema allows no extra properties rejects the call only after its `before_tool_call` gate has finished.

Fixes #206056

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex harness docs say a per-call `timeoutMs` gives a slow dynamic tool more time than the 90 s default. For tools with a closed schema, such as `workboard_complete`, the override does extend the timer. But the call then fails with `Invalid arguments for tool "workboard_complete": <root>: must not have additional properties: "timeoutMs"`, and only after a `before_tool_call` gate (for example a 2–10 minute test run) has passed. The card is not completed and the passing test run is lost. A hook cannot remove the field, because returned `params` are merged into the original arguments.

## User Impact

`workboard_complete({ ..., timeoutMs: 600000 })` behind a slow gate now completes the card, both as a direct call and from a Code Mode `exec` cell. These calls are unchanged:

- A tool that declares `timeoutMs` or `timeoutSeconds` (for example `image_generate`, `tts`, browser) still receives it.
- Open-schema tools and external MCP tools get the same arguments as before.
- Any other undeclared key is still rejected.
- Without `timeoutMs`, the 90 s default still applies.
- Stop and a failing gate still keep the card open.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bridge already reads these two fields as its own control arguments. It is also the one place that knows the tool's schema before hooks and validation run. `handleToolCall` now removes the two fields once, through `omitUndeclaredTimeoutArguments` in `dynamic-tool-catalog.ts` (next to the schema validator). It removes them only when the schema sets `additionalProperties: false` and does not declare the field, and never for external MCP tools (the same exemption `validateArguments` uses). Hooks, validation and `executedArguments` therefore see the arguments the tool accepts. The watchdog and abort path are not touched.

Rejected: adding `timeoutMs` to Workboard schemas (one tool at a time, and it changes the model-facing schema), and letting hooks delete keys (that reverses #142700).

`dedupeQuarantinedDynamicTools` moves from `dynamic-tools.ts` to `dynamic-tool-catalog.ts`. The body is byte-identical and it has the same single caller. This is only to stay under the file line-cap ratchet; behavior does not change.

Docs: `docs/plugins/codex-harness-reference/timeouts.md` now says a closed-schema tool that does not declare the timeout argument does not receive it.

Not in this PR: a gate longer than 90 s without `timeoutMs` still times out. That belongs with #154733 (the watchdog counts approval and hook time).

## Evidence

Gateway proof: main 2237f16b7e27 and this branch e8c9082b7748 were each built in a secretless `node:24.22.1` container and run as an isolated Gateway with the Codex harness, Workboard, and a plugin `before_tool_call` gate on `workboard_complete` (registered with `timeoutMs: 1830000`). The gate runs `sleep 120` with `ctx.abortSignal` and blocks the call if the sleep fails. A stand-in Codex app-server sent the `item/tool/call` requests that Codex sends: `workboard_create`, then `workboard_claim`, then `workboard_complete({ id, summary, timeoutMs: 600000 })`. These ran as top-level calls and nested inside an `exec` Code Mode cell item. Full observed lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206400#issuecomment-7210456853

| Case | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| direct call, `timeoutMs: 600000`, 120 s gate passes (×2) | gate passes at ~120 s, then `Invalid arguments ... "timeoutMs"`; card not done | card `done` |
| same call inside a Code Mode `exec` cell (×2) | same error; card not done | card `done` |
| `timeout_echo` (closed schema that declares `timeoutMs`) | receives `timeoutMs: 600000` | receives `timeoutMs: 600000` |
| `timeoutMs` + undeclared `foo` | rejected (`"timeoutMs", "foo"`) | rejected (`"foo"`) |
| no `timeoutMs`, 120 s gate | times out at 90 s, gate abort signal fires, card open | same |
| Stop 20 s into the gate | gate's sleep killed, card open | same |
| gate exits 1 | blocked, card open | same |

Tests: one new case in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts` (closed schema, passing hook, `timeoutMs: 600000` and `timeoutSeconds`; declared and undeclared variants). It fails on main with `must not have additional properties` and passes here. The touched test file and the 17 Codex test files that import the changed modules pass (437 tests).

Not covered here: the same calls through the real `codex` 0.172.0 binary against a scripted local Responses endpoint fail at ~10 s on both main and this branch, with `Tool call blocked by PreToolUse hook: Native hook relay timed out`. The reason is that Codex also sends `PreToolUse` for dynamic tools, so the native hook relay runs the same gate under its fixed 10 s hook timeout before the call reaches the bridge. This PR does not change that. It is tracked separately.

Merge risk: low, two-way door. A revert fully undoes it. No stored state, config or schema changes. Only arguments to closed-schema, non-MCP tools change, and only the two timeout keys those tools would have rejected.

prs.title: feat: add opt-in Agent Profiles for small local models
prs.body:
Part of #204354. Related: openclaw/rfcs#18 (Agent Profiles RFC)

## Decision for @vincentkoc (about five minutes)

**The question.** Should OpenClaw ship named, opt-in Agent Profiles and retire `experimental.localModelLean` through Doctor, as RFC openclaw/rfcs#18 describes?

**Our recommendation: yes, as this slice implements it.** This slice follows the RFC as written, including your 2026-11-25 change (`bbac942`): `openclaw/small` is the exact Lean migration, and the smaller-context behavior is a separate profile, `openclaw/compact`.

| RFC #18 point | Where it is met |
|---|---|
| `openclaw/small` is an exact Lean migration (same `lean` tool filtering, no new behavior) | `src/agents/agent-profiles/builtins.ts`; `small-lean-parity.test.ts` compares it with Lean on `main` |
| Broader tuning is a separate profile that must not change `openclaw/small` | `openclaw/compact`: the bounded workspace context, opt-in only, with `automations` kept |
| Doctor: `true` becomes `openclaw/small`; an explicit `false` becomes an explicit non-Lean profile at the same scope; an absent flag is left alone | `legacy-config-migrations.agent-profiles.ts` and its test |
| The registry rejects duplicate ids, unknown parents and cycles | `resolve.ts`, `builtins.ts`, `builtins.test.ts` |
| Unknown profile ids fail validation | `src/config/agent-profile-ids.ts` |
| Runtime reads only the canonical selector | the legacy field is read only by Doctor |

**Where we differ from the RFC, on purpose.** The RFC makes `"auto"` the default. In this slice an unset selector means `openclaw/base`, so nobody's prompt changes on upgrade, and `auto` is an explicit opt-in (#204132). Making `auto` the default later takes one schema default change, once size bindings have evidence behind them.

**Why `compact` keeps `automations`.** A small model without the scheduler fakes a reminder through a shell command and then reports it as scheduled. `openclaw/small` stays an exact Lean copy, so it still drops `automations` as Lean does today. `openclaw/compact` is the choice for an operator who wants the smaller context and the scheduler.

**Evidence.** Everything below ran on a real Qwen3-8B Q8_0 in llama.cpp (Mac Studio, 32K context), through the shipped CLI. A turn on `main` starts at 13,144 prompt tokens, about 40% of the window (#204354). On this slice, with identical inputs (a 12,000-character `AGENTS.md` and a 3,000-character `IDENTITY.md`) and the default Tool Search mode, llama.cpp reports 13,014 prompt tokens for `base` (15 tools, 39.7% of the window), 11,957 for `small` (14 tools, -8.1%) and 10,648 for `compact` (14 tools, -18.2%, `AGENTS.md` cut from 12,000 to about 4,660 characters). With every tool schema sent directly, no profile fits in 32K: the server refused `base` at 42,969 tokens, `compact` at 38,583 and `small` at 33,929. A Doctor upgrade from the latest stable release, 2026.11.10, keeps every explicit choice, passes `config validate`, changes nothing on a second run, and a stored session from the old release is listed and continued by this head.

**Cost to reverse.** Low. Profiles are opt-in, so reverting the slice leaves unconfigured users untouched. Doctor's rewrite is the only one-way step, and `openclaw/small` reproduces Lean exactly, so a revert only needs the selector mapped back to the boolean.

**The three lasting contracts and why each is needed:**
1. `agentProfileId` at defaults and per agent: the one selector the RFC asks for. It survives restarts and replaces `experimental.localModelLean`, so there is one setting, not two.
2. `openclaw agent exec --agent-profile`: picks a profile for one isolated run. `--local-model-lean` stays as its alias.
3. The `agentProfileApplied` harness option (Plugin SDK): tells external harnesses which profile shaped the tool list. `localModelLeanApplied` stays as a deprecated alias.

**What else is outside the code:** the security-sensitive path needs a maintainer.

## What Problem This Solves

A local model with a small context window gets the same system prompt as a hosted model. On a 32K window that prompt fills about 40% of the window before the user says anything. Lean mode (`experimental.localModelLean`) trims only some of it and cannot be set per model size. Agent Profiles (RFC 18) give each agent a named profile that sets the tool surface and, for `compact`, the workspace budget.

This is slice 1 of 3 of the Agent Profiles work, split from one 90-commit branch so each part can be reviewed on its own. Base of the stack. Slices 2 and 3 are stacked on this branch.

Dependencies: none. This PR does not depend on slice 2 or slice 3. It adds no package: the Agent Profile spec types are vendored in `spec-types.ts` (types only, from RFC openclaw/rfcs#18 and agentprofiles 0.1.0), and the `agentprofiles` package can return once the RFC ships it as a published contract.

## This slice

Original reviewed range: `1601f86def0..f6a84ab8cb4`. Since the previous body (`ee3f53e01f45`) this head adds, as signed commits and merges with no rebase and no force:

- `2075fb3c2425`, `7f7416864f9e`, `fef700594ae7`, `e6f53c08abdb`: make `openclaw/small` the exact Lean migration, add `openclaw/compact`, update the docs and tests, and raise the test-line record for the Lean parity fixtures.
- `44f407ebe8f8`: move `indexBuiltInAgentProfiles` from `resolve.ts` into `builtins.ts`, so it is no longer an export that only a test uses (`pnpm deadcode:exports` flagged it).
- `e76271a9efae`: merge main `387d6d61a4b8`; the generated config baseline was regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`.
- `dac87601f31b`: the scoped test run found one test that still expected the 11,500-character cap from `openclaw/small`; it now uses `openclaw/compact`.
- `b5ed34c3cd2d`: merge main `9239eeb2df37`. Main added a per-agent `sharedUserDir` (a shared USER.md directory) next to our per-agent `agentProfileId`; both agent entry fields are kept, in the config types, the schema, the help text and the labels (the merge also carried back the per-agent localModelLean entry that this slice retires; see c35d5717a514). The generated config baseline was regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`.
- `092232f02ac2`: one test that a shared USER.md is bounded by the `openclaw/compact` workspace budget like a workspace USER.md (see Evidence).
- `a6f94b447536`: the test-lines allocation record is raised from 1733 to 1752 for that test and for the base moving to `9239eeb2df37`.
- `c35d5717a514`: removes the per-agent `experimental.localModelLean` entry (type, schema, help and label) that the merge had brought back from main's side of the conflict. This slice retires that field, and Doctor owns the legacy key. Found by local ClawSweeper r3; the config baseline was regenerated again.
- `6f65e015fa24`: vendors the Agent Profile spec types and drops the `agentprofiles` dev dependency (no package is added; `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` match main). Tests that called its validator now assert the structure directly.
- `52025d0a2ba2`: merge main `df32bed58501`; the generated config baseline was regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`.
- `efe9e0886ae6`: types the built-in id set in one test as strings and keeps three spec types unexported (found by `check:test-types` and `deadcode:exports`).
- `f69ffdd114ad`: hosted CI failed `compact.hooks.test.ts` (`expected 12000 to be less than 12000`). The compaction budget test still selected `openclaw/small`, which carries no workspace limits. It now selects `openclaw/compact`. A search of `src`, `extensions` and `test` for every test that names `openclaw/small` found no other test that asserts a workspace cap, a truncation, 11,500 or 7,500 with it (see Decisions).
- `e00ac504d2a0`: `docs/concepts/agent-profiles.md` no longer describes the removed `agentprofiles` validator. It says OpenClaw keeps the spec types in its own tree, tests check the built-ins' structure, and full portable validation can return when the RFC publishes the package as a contract.
- `19031d818f37`: removes one sentinel assertion in `workspace-context.test.ts` that the exact-content assertion on the line before already implies.

This slice adds the profile object and everything that applies it. It does not select a profile by model size.

- Agent Profiles: the vendored spec types, the OpenClaw profile extension, the built-ins `openclaw/base`, `openclaw/small` and `openclaw/compact`, the resolver, and `agents.defaults.agentProfileId` with the per-agent override.
- `openclaw/small` is the exact migration of `experimental.localModelLean`: the Lean tool filter (it drops `automations`, `browser`, the image, music and video generation tools, `pdf` and `tts`, and `message` unless it is forced), the forced-message preservation, and the Tool Search default only when unset. It carries no workspace limits.
- `openclaw/compact` is the opt-in profile that keeps the previous small behavior. It caps the content OpenClaw prepares from `AGENTS.md` (7,500), `SOUL.md` (2,000), `IDENTITY.md` (1,024) and `USER.md` (2,000) at 11,500 characters together, and keeps `automations`. Project-local instructions that Codex loads natively follow Codex's own settings and are outside these caps. Compaction uses the shared `resolveBootstrapContextForRun` owner.
- Diagnostics: `/context` and the system prompt report show the selected profile and budget; `openclaw agent exec --agent-profile` picks one for a run.
- Lean retirement: `openclaw doctor --fix` turns `experimental.localModelLean: true` into `agentProfileId: "openclaw/small"` and an explicit `false` into `agentProfileId: "openclaw/base"`, at the same scope (defaults and agent), as the Agent Profiles RFC specifies. An absent flag is left alone. `--local-model-lean` stays as an alias for `--agent-profile openclaw/small`.

## User Impact

- With no `agentProfileId` set, every agent uses `openclaw/base`: the prompt and tool list are the same as on `main`.
- An operator who set `experimental.localModelLean: true` gets exactly the Lean behavior after `openclaw doctor --fix`, now as `openclaw/small`. Nothing about their prompt changes: no workspace caps are added.
- An operator who wants the smaller workspace context picks `openclaw/compact` by hand, per agent or in defaults. It keeps `automations`.
- `auto` and size classes are not in this slice (slice 2). Compact context serialization is not in this slice (slice 3).

## Why This Change Was Made

The workspace budget, the tool surface and the Doctor migration all read one resolved profile, so they land together: split apart, a profile would select nothing. Selection by model size (slice 2) and compact serialization (slice 3) build on this resolver. `small` and `compact` are separate so the migration stays exact and the extra tuning stays a choice (RFC 18, `bbac942`).

Config and API surface: this slice adds `agents.defaults.agentProfileId` and the per-agent `agentProfileId`, the `openclaw agent exec --agent-profile` flag, and the `agentProfileApplied` harness option (`localModelLeanApplied` stays as a deprecated alias). A persisted selector is needed because the profile has to survive restarts and be set per agent; Doctor retires `experimental.localModelLean` into it, so there is one setting, not two.

## Evidence

### Runtime output

Shipped entry points, run from a clean environment with a throwaway `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`. Nothing under a real home was touched. Paths and ports are redacted. Part (a) ran on `c35d5717a514`, built with the runtime-only build (`pnpm build:runtime`, exit 0). The later commits add the type vendoring, merges of main, and test and docs fixes, listed above; none changes the prompt or tool code, and part (a) was not re-run on them. Part (b), the Doctor upgrade, and the session check ran on the final head `19031d818f37`, built with `pnpm build:runtime` on a macOS runner.

#### (a) Real-model prompt tokens for `base`, `small` and `compact`

A temporary llama.cpp server ran Qwen3-8B Q8_0 (`--jinja`, 32K context, all layers on the GPU). A recording proxy sat between OpenClaw and the server. It forwards each request unchanged, except that it asks for token usage in the stream. Token counts are the server's own (`usage.prompt_tokens`, or its error message). The temporary server was stopped by process id afterwards.

Each run is one shipped CLI turn, `openclaw agent --local --agent main --message "Say ok." --json`, with `agents.defaults.agentProfileId` set to the profile, a 12,000-character `AGENTS.md` and a 3,000-character `IDENTITY.md`, and throwaway state. Default setup (Tool Search on), same workspace files for every row.

| Profile | What it is for | Prompt tokens (real) | Share of 32K | Tools offered |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `openclaw/base` | Today's behavior, nothing trimmed | 13,014 | 39.7% | 15 |
| `openclaw/small` | Exact Lean migration: fewer tools, no `message`, no scheduler | 11,957 (-8.1%) | 36.5% | 14 |
| `openclaw/compact` | Smaller workspace context, keeps the scheduler | 10,648 (-18.2%) | 32.5% | 14 |

- `base` offers `apply_patch, dispatch_action, edit, exec, ls, message, openclaw, process, progress_card, read, session_project, sessions_yield, tool_describe, tool_search, write`. `small` and `compact` offer the same list without `message`.
- `compact` cuts `AGENTS.md` and `IDENTITY.md` because the four workspace files share the 11,500-character total, and marks the cut in the prompt with `Some workspace bootstrap files were truncated before Project Context injection.`

Direct tool schemas (`tools.toolSearch: false`): no profile fits in a 32K window. The server refused `base` at 42,969 tokens, `compact` at 38,583 and `small` at 33,929 (`400 exceeds the available context size (32768 tokens)`). `small` drops `automations`, `browser` and `tts` from the tool list and `compact` drops `browser` and `tts`.

#### (b) Doctor upgrade from the latest stable release

`openclaw@2026.11.10`, the latest stable release (`npm view openclaw version`), was installed with `npm --prefix ... --ignore-scripts` in a scratch directory. Three configs were written, and all three passed `config validate` with 2026.11.10. Before each upgrade, 2026.11.10 ran one real stored session turn (`openclaw agent --local`, session key `agent:main:upgradeproof`) against the same temporary Qwen3-8B server as part (a), so a stored session existed. The temporary server was stopped by process id afterwards. Then this head ran `openclaw doctor --fix` and `config validate`, and Doctor ran a second time.

Home A (explicit `true` at defaults, one agent set to `false`, and an unrelated setting), sanitized:

```json
before: {"agents":{"ownership":"explicit","defaults":{"experimental":{"localModelLean":true}},"entries":{"main":{},"full":{"experimental":{"localModelLean":false}}}},"logging":{"level":"debug"}}
after:  {"agents":{"ownership":"explicit","defaults":{"agentProfileId":"openclaw/small"},"entries":{"main":{},"full":{"agentProfileId":"openclaw/base"}}},"logging":{"level":"debug"}}
```

Home B (defaults set to `false`):

```json
before: {"agents":{"defaults":{"experimental":{"localModelLean":false}},"entries":{"main":{}}},"logging":{"level":"debug"}}
after:  {"agents":{"defaults":{"agentProfileId":"openclaw/base"},"entries":{"main":{}}},"logging":{"level":"debug"}}
```

Home C (only an unrelated setting, no Lean flag):

```json
before: {"agents":{"defaults":{},"entries":{"main":{}}},"logging":{"level":"debug"}}
after:  {"agents":{"defaults":{},"entries":{"main":{}}},"logging":{"level":"debug"}}
```

```text
2026.11.10 config validate (A, B, C): Config valid
2026.11.10 stored session turn (A, B, C): exit 0, reply "stable turn ok", stopReason stop
candidate doctor --fix (A, B, C): completed
candidate config validate (A, B, C): Config valid
second doctor --fix (A, B, C): SECOND RUN: no change (the config file is byte for byte the same)
```

Key-sorted diff of home A, before and after Doctor, with Doctor's unrelated stamps left out:

```diff
-      "experimental": { "localModelLean": true },
+      "agentProfileId": "openclaw/small",
-        "experimental": { "localModelLean": false }
+        "agentProfileId": "openclaw/base"
```

- `true` became `openclaw/small`, the explicit `false` agent became `openclaw/base`, the defaults `false` home became `openclaw/base`, home C was left alone (an absent flag stays absent), and `logging.level` is unchanged in all three.
- Doctor also made its usual unrelated writes (a system agent owner, a per-agent workspace path, `meta` and `wizard` version stamps, default skill entries). Those migrations already exist on main and are left out above.

#### Data-model compatibility

The session stored by 2026.11.10 before the upgrade is listed by the candidate CLI after Doctor ran, with the same key, session id and counters, and one more turn with the candidate CLI continued it (same session id, `updatedAt` moved forward, reply "candidate turn ok", stopReason stop). `openclaw sessions --agent main --json`, redacted to the fields that show continuity:

| home | step | count | key | session id | startedAt | updatedAt | totalTokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 2026.11.10, before upgrade | 1 | `agent:main:upgradeproof` | `2d714f4a` | 1795746804341 | 1795746835551 | 13843 |
| A | candidate, after Doctor | 1 | `agent:main:upgradeproof` | `2d714f4a` | 1795746804341 | 1795746835551 | 13843 |
| A | candidate, after one more turn | 1 | `agent:main:upgradeproof` | `2d714f4a` | 1795746804341 | 1795746914886 | 13113 |
| B | 2026.11.10, before upgrade | 1 | `agent:main:upgradeproof` | `d61dad0e` | 1795746924136 | 1795746961855 | 15339 |
| B | candidate, after Doctor | 1 | `agent:main:upgradeproof` | `d61dad0e` | 1795746924136 | 1795746961855 | 15339 |
| B | candidate, after one more turn | 1 | `agent:main:upgradeproof` | `d61dad0e` | 1795746924136 | 1795747046531 | 14194 |
| C | 2026.11.10, before upgrade | 1 | `agent:main:upgradeproof` | `543c577c` | 1795747055813 | 1795747088123 | 15301 |
| C | candidate, after Doctor | 1 | `agent:main:upgradeproof` | `543c577c` | 1795747055813 | 1795747088123 | 15301 |
| C | candidate, after one more turn | 1 | `agent:main:upgradeproof` | `543c577c` | 1795747055813 | 1795747178413 | 14265 |

All rows use model `qwen3-8b` on the local `llamacpp` provider. Not checked: the transcript text itself was not diffed, and the second turn did not ask the model to recall the first.

### Red and green

- `small-lean-parity.test.ts` copied onto `ee3f53e01f45` (the previous head, where `small` still carried the caps): `2 failed | 8 passed` (the Lean deny set including `automations`, and the profile for an ad-hoc agent and a session key). On this head: `10 passed`.
- `pnpm deadcode:exports` before the dead-export fix flagged `src/agents/agent-profiles/resolve.ts: indexBuiltInAgentProfiles`. After it, the scan no longer lists any file this change touches; the one remaining entry, `src/agents/btw-runtime.ts: toSimpleContextMessages`, is identical on main `387d6d61a4b8`.

### Shared USER.md and the profile budget

Main's `sharedUserDir` loads USER.md from a directory outside the workspace. `resolveBootstrapContextForRun` hands that file to the profile budget in the same list as the workspace files, and the budget keys on the file name, so the shared USER.md is capped like a workspace one. `bootstrap-files.agent-profile.test.ts` now covers it: with `openclaw/compact`, a 12,000-character `AGENTS.md` and a 12,000-character shared USER.md, the shared file is loaded (`bootstrapFiles` holds all 12,000 characters) and the prepared context stays at or under 11,500 characters. The test is 5 of 5 passing.

### Gates on the final head `19031d818f37`

Focused tests and the build ran on a macOS runner through crabbox with `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1` (plain `pnpm test` worked, no vitest fallback). `check:changed` and the test-lines ratchet ran in a local checkout, because the runner copy has no git history. Changed-file gates ran against freshly fetched main `103f40f50782`.

| gate on `19031d818f37` | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm test` on 8 files: `compact.hooks.test.ts`, the four agent-profiles tests, `agent-profiles.test.ts`, and the Doctor agent-profiles and Lean migration tests, `--maxWorkers=1` (macOS runner) | exit 0: 8 files passed, 156 tests passed (`compact.hooks.test.ts` alone: 90 of 90, including "bounds the compaction workspace context with the selected profile budget") |
| `pnpm tsgo:core` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:test-types` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base 103f40f50782` | exit 0 (net +2141, allowance 400, credit 1752) |
| `pnpm check:changed` | exit 1: 2 lanes, both reproduced on main (below); format, lint, typecheck, config docs baseline and every ratchet passed |
| `git diff --check` against `df32bed58501` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm build:runtime` (for the Doctor proof) | exit 0 |
| `pnpm test`, full suite | deferred to hosted CI |

`pnpm check:changed` fails two lanes on this head:

- Plugin SDK surface budget: `public exports 3931 > 3930`. The number is unchanged by this change; it is the same line main prints.
- Dead export scan: the production scan lists `toSimpleContextMessages` and `SubagentCancellationControl` (also in the full-tree scan) plus three exports in files this change does not touch (`openSettingsDialog`, `checkDoctorLegacyStateDirPending`, `startBrokerExeca`).

Not re-run on this head, because the three commits after `efe9e0886ae6` touch one test support file, one test file and one docs page and no package file: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm deps:npm-lock:check:changed`, `pnpm config:docs:check` (it passes inside `check:changed`) and `pnpm deadcode:unused-files` (also inside `check:changed`). The results on `efe9e0886ae6` were: frozen install exit 0 with the lockfile unchanged, npm-lock check exit 0, and `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` have no diff against main.

The earlier gates, for the record (on `e76271a9efae`, with the one scoped test row on `dac87601f31b`; changed-file gates ran against main `387d6d61a4b8`):

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm build` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm tsgo:core` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm tsgo:core:test` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm config:docs:check` | exit 0 |
| every `check:*-ratchet` script (baseline, database dialect, database worker, line cap, max lines, session identity, test timeout race) | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base 387d6d61a4b8` | exit 0 |
| `git diff --check` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:changed` | exit 1: 3 lanes, all reproduced on main (listed here) |
| `pnpm exec vitest run` on the 71 test files this change adds or changes, plus every test of the agent-profiles, doctor migration, tool-surface and workspace-context code (macOS runner) | exit 0: 70 files passed, 1 skipped; 1,080 tests passed, 4 skipped (the first run found one failing test, fixed in `dac87601f31b`) |
| `pnpm test`, full suite | not run here: deferred to hosted CI |

On that earlier head, `pnpm check:changed` failed three lanes that failed the same way on main `387d6d61a4b8`:

- Plugin SDK surface budget: `public exports 3931 > 3930` (main `9239eeb2df37` prints the same line).
- Dead export scan: `src/agents/btw-runtime.ts: toSimpleContextMessages` and `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-control.types.ts: SubagentCancellationControl`. Main `9239eeb2df37` lists the same two.
- Lint: `max-lines` and UI lint errors in 32 files this change does not touch, such as `src/wizard/setup.ts`, `src/node-host/runtime.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-mutations.ts` and the `ui/` components; none of them is in this change's diff, so they are byte-identical to main.

Local ClawSweeper (native, clean checkout of the committed range, committed-range mode, a body passed with `--body-file`), one row per round:

| round | head | P0 to P2 | P3 | tiers overall / proof / patch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| r1, an earlier draft of this body | `e76271a9efae` | none (patch is correct, security cleared, proof sufficient) | 1 P3 (profile-merge machinery that no built-in profile exercises yet; kept, see Decisions) | C / B / B |
| r2, an earlier draft of this body | `dac87601f31b` | none (patch is correct, security cleared, proof sufficient) | 1 P3 (the model-presence gate on the workspace budget in `bootstrap-files.ts`; kept, see Decisions) | C / B / B |
| r3, after the merge of main | `a6f94b447536` | none (patch is correct, security cleared, proof sufficient) | 1 P3 (the per-agent `experimental.localModelLean` entry that the merge brought back; fixed in `c35d5717a514`) | C / B / B |
| r4, after that fix | `c35d5717a514` | none | none | C / B / B |
| r5, after vendoring the spec types and merging main | `efe9e0886ae6` | none (patch is correct, security cleared, proof sufficient) | none | C / B / B |
| r6, after the hosted CI and review fixes | `19031d818f37` | none (patch is correct, security cleared, proof sufficient, data-model compatibility sufficient) | none | C / B / B |

The overall tier C is held by the maintainer product-direction question at the top of this body, not by a code finding.

### Hosted review and CI follow-up (earlier rounds, still true)

Findings of the hosted review of `d1587b2b80b` and of the first CI run were fixed in this slice as their own signed commits: the worker profile forwarding wrapper was inlined (`e02aef016b4`), two low-value tests were removed (`d9ce2699571`), compaction budgeting moved to the shared bootstrap owner (`5e290475574`), the message-tool fixtures were fixed (`dc5e7c84411`), oxlint findings were fixed (`41afefa34f3`), two files were added to the wrapper component list (`da17569700e`), and one test was listed in the codex attempt-light vitest config (`5e38527fa4d`).

Why the test lines are needed: each profile effect has its own regression test on each runtime that consumes it, because each runtime builds its prompt and tools through its own seam: embedded runner, CLI runner, Codex app-server attempt, ACP harness, agentsapi prompt, isolated completion, worker turn, compaction and the coding-tool surface. The record in `config/test-lines-allocations/202517-agent-profiles-core.txt` was raised again for the Lean parity fixtures and the `compact` cap tests (`e6f53c08abdb`).

### Decisions

| decision | choice | evidence | how to reverse |
|---|---|---|---|
| `small` versus `compact` | Split: `small` is the exact Lean migration, `compact` carries the old small behavior and is opt-in | RFC 18 at `bbac942`; `small-lean-parity.test.ts` red on the old head, green here; request capture above | revert `2075fb3c2425` and `fef700594ae7`, which restores the combined profile |
| `compact` keeps `automations` | Keep the scheduler | a small model without it fakes reminders through a shell command and reports them scheduled | change the `compact` tool profile |
| Dead export `indexBuiltInAgentProfiles` | Move it into `builtins.ts` (a production consumer in `resolve.ts`) instead of a `testing` export | the `testing` export in `resolve.ts` was itself flagged by the production dead-export scan; after the move the scan no longer lists it | revert `44f407ebe8f8` |
| Merge main into the branch | Plain signed merge commit `b5ed34c3cd2d` of main `9239eeb2df37`, no rebase. Where main's `sharedUserDir` and our `agentProfileId` both add an agent entry field, keep both fields, and keep the per-agent localModelLean entry retired (fixed in `c35d5717a514` after r3 found it); regenerate the config baseline | conflicts were in `agent-scope-config.ts`, `schema.help.core.ts`, `schema.labels.ts`, `zod-schema.agent-entry-base.ts` and `docs/.generated/config-baseline.*`; `config:docs:check`, both tsgo graphs, the scoped tests and the test-lines ratchet pass on `c35d5717a514`; a new test shows the shared USER.md is capped by the profile budget; the latest merge of main `df32bed58501` conflicted only in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.*`, regenerated | revert the merge commit |
| Model-presence gate on the workspace budget (ClawSweeper r2 P3) | Keep | the budget applies only when the caller names a model, because the profile is chosen for the model the turn runs; a caller that names no model gets the operator's own limits, and every production caller passes one; `bootstrap-files.agent-profile.test.ts` covers both paths | follow-up: apply the budget whenever a profile declares one |
| Profile-merge machinery (ClawSweeper P3) | Keep | RFC 18 defines inheritance (`extends`, unknown parents and cycles rejected); `small` and `compact` both extend `base`, and user-defined profiles are the RFC's next step | trim to a direct read in a follow-up |
| Full test suite | Scoped tests here, full suite in hosted CI | the scoped run covers every test file this change touches. A search of `src`, `extensions` and `test` for every test that names `openclaw/small` found one that asserted a workspace cap, the compaction budget test, which hosted CI failed and which now selects `openclaw/compact` (`f69ffdd114ad`); the earlier one was fixed in `dac87601f31b`. Every other test that names `openclaw/small` checks the tool surface, config or Doctor, which `small` does change | n/a |
| Test-line overage | Allocation record raised for the parity fixtures, and to 1752 for the shared USER.md test and the new base | `check:test-lines-ratchet --base 9239eeb2df37` exit 0 | delete tests and lower the record |
| Upgrade proof | Latest stable release 2026.11.10 with its own `agents.entries` schema, plus a stored session from that release | the stable release validated all three configs; a second Doctor run changes nothing; the stored session is listed and continued by this head | n/a, evidence only |
| `localModelLean: false` migration | Write `openclaw/base` at that scope, at defaults and on agents | RFC 18 migration rule; `openclaw/base` keeps the full tool surface | revert the migration commit |
| `agentprofiles` dependency | Drop it and vendor only the types OpenClaw reads (`spec-types.ts`, header names RFC openclaw/rfcs#18 and agentprofiles 0.1.0); the validator is not vendored, and the tests assert the built-ins' structure directly | the package was used for types in production code and for validation in three tests; `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` now match main; `check:test-types` and the focused tests pass | add the package back as a dev dependency once the RFC ships it as a published contract, and restore the validator calls in the tests |
| Duplicate built-in profile ids | Reject in the profile index | `builtins.test.ts` fails without the check | revert the duplicate-id commit |

### Credit

Onur Solmaz and Mitchell Etzel authored the original signed commits. Mitchell Etzel authored the split.

### Needs a maintainer

- The security-review approval on the current head.
- vincentkoc's go-ahead.

prs.title: refactor(ui): simplify Settings layout reporting
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory, Meeting Capture, and Session Storage register extra shell-layout reporters for a Settings trait already owned by their retained page component. This duplicates presentation lifecycle work during Settings rendering and maintenance.

Requested by @vincentkoc as part of the continuing Control UI simplification work.

## User Impact

No user-visible change or required action. Page markup, classes, controls, tabs, advanced editors, and connection/agent retirement policies remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove five redundant `settingsPage` reporters while retaining Memory’s unconditional trait superset and the unconditional `SettingsPage` siblings in Meeting Capture and Storage. Shared layout components keep their reporters for independent consumers. The Settings tab uses a fragment, which saves no lines by itself.

Production code decreases from 2,346 to 2,335 lines across the four touched files: **−11 lines total**, including imports, fragments, and formatting. Tests, docs, and generated files are unchanged. No new helper, state, flags, or framework.

## Evidence

- Existing focused suites pass before and after: 79 tests in the six-file lane (5.29 s / 4.45 s), plus 38 Memory-page tests in its isolated registry lane (3.25 s / 2.42 s). All baseline assertions retained; no implementation-count test padding added.
- UI typecheck, focused lint, formatting, diff check, and controller ownership guard pass. Focused lint retains the same existing `liveValue` reactivity warning in Session Storage.
- Stock `build:ci-artifacts` passes on the base and stock `ui:build` passes on the candidate. An isolated stock base build uses the identical frozen lock, Node 26.12.1, and toolchain; all 41 consumed packaged-plugin inputs are byte-identical.
- The supported performance checker passes against that base: startup JS 91,389 → 91,389 B gzip; Chat 1,338,117 → 1,338,117 B; New 821,227 → 821,227 B; measured CSS unchanged. Existing absolute debt remains: largest CSS 58,603 > 58,315 B; Chat 21 > 20 JS requests and 1,338,117 > 1,336,272 B. No budgets were changed.
- Actual production-bundle browser flows against a real isolated Gateway pass before and after at 400, 820, and 1280 px: every Memory tab, both advanced editors, Refresh, and navigation away. Trait classes and editor-control counts match. Built relay/anchor ownership and explicit built Gateway entrypoint were used; cleanup completed. No capture, maintenance job, model turn, or live-account write was performed.
- Layout observers recorded one 0.0134 cold-arrival shift on the 400 px base Meeting Capture page and none in the sampled candidate flows; this is not a general performance claim. This transparent-reporter cleanup changes no DOM or visual design.
- Independent precommit source review: no findings. Full local ClawSweeper review of `15c0afe34e3eed3d49d6831851ab676fd6be80dc..36e9db2e9124ae2ecf43e2b26dd14a0f3e0eccf8`: complete coverage of all four paths, no comments, security cleared, no low-value tests.
- Retained setup failures: the first browser attempt had a nested-summary selector collision, corrected before the passing comparison; the first performance comparison overlapped atomic output replacement and failed with a missing asset, then passed after both builds settled. Neither failure was treated as product proof or hidden by a rebuild.
- Full exact-head PR CI [run 45943381303](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45943381303) passed: all 67 jobs terminal (41 successful, 26 intentionally skipped), including `security-fast` and `openclaw/ci-gate`. Decoded UI selection manifests match all 3,527 observed test files across 3 UI, 10 UI E2E, and 2 real-Gateway shards; case receipts report 31,158 passed, 0 failed, 9 skipped, 0 pending. `ci:full` was set and read back while draft, before ready. The published commit has the identical locally reviewed source tree.
- Hosted ClawSweeper also passed on exact published head `86a8d516f279c5b10bf3066a99ccd4c6c080aeb8` with no findings or before-merge requests. Protected native landing completed as `288e52aab044fc885aa8b4ed47d59a46f08e3da7`; the retained native outcome is complete and the landed commit is verified on `main`.

## Worked on by

- @vincentkoc

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/e8c29f83-c1ff-4bf2-99dd-89f7b614e71e)

prs.title: docs(workshop): clarify when skill edits reach running sessions
prs.body:
## What changed

The Workshop guide said an existing session kept its starting skill snapshot until a new session began. The guide now explains when a saved edit to a local, file-backed skill becomes visible.

The current turn keeps the catalog from its prompt. A later `skills_read` sees the saved `SKILL.md` when the run reads the local file directly. A worker that received a copy keeps using that copy for the rest of the turn. Once OpenClaw publishes the refreshed catalog, the next turn sees it in either the same session or a new one.

## Verification

A registered Workshop save changed a synthetic skill from “amber” to “birch”. The held prompt still described “amber”, and a subsequent file read in that turn returned the complete “birch” instructions. The next turn in the same session and the first turn in a fresh session both received “birch”. A no-edit control kept “amber”. The comparison included prompt rendering, actual skill reads and independent cold reads of the saved files.

The original documentation revision passed the one-page MDX check, markdownlint, formatter and whitespace checks. The worker qualification follows the [existing transfer regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3819eedeca19c1294e50ecbbf470546e610c1da3/src/gateway/worker-environments/skill-resource-transfer.test.ts#L279), which changes the host file after transfer and checks the instructions returned inside the worker. The page retains its existing headings, anchors and links. This is an English documentation correction for the behavior documented in [the skills guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/skills).

prs.title: fix: keep channel status checks working when update status uses --timeout 30s or longer
prs.body:
Closes #206141

## What Problem This Solves

Running `openclaw update status --timeout 30` (or any `--timeout` of 30 seconds or longer) fails to read channel status. Because the remaining budget is computed from `performance.now()` without rounding, `channels.status` receives a fractional `timeoutMs` that the Gateway rejects with `INVALID_REQUEST: at /timeoutMs: must be integer`, leaving `Channel inspection unavailable` in the output and `INVALID_REQUEST` errors in the gateway log.

## User Impact

Scripts and operators passing `--timeout 30` or higher to `openclaw update status` now get normal channel inspection results instead of spurious `Channel inspection unavailable` errors and gateway `INVALID_REQUEST` log noise. No configuration changes or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rounding the shared remaining budget upward with `Math.max(1, Math.ceil(deadline - performance.now()))` guarantees positive integer milliseconds at the budget producer while preserving deadline and abort behavior, matching the existing convention in `src/commands/gateway-diagnostic-readiness.ts`.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test in `src/cli/update-cli/status.deadline.test.ts` that runs `updateStatusCommand({ json: true, timeout: "40" })` with fractional `performance.now()` values and verifies `channels.status` receives an integer `timeoutMs` accepted by `validateChannelsStatusParams`.
- `pnpm test src/cli/update-cli/status.deadline.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 9/9 tests passed.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/cli/update-cli/status.ts src/cli/update-cli/status.deadline.test.ts`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/cli/update-cli/status.ts src/cli/update-cli/status.deadline.test.ts`: clean.
- Live Gateway execution was not run locally; RPC parameter compliance is verified against the production `validateChannelsStatusParams` validator.
