prs.title: refactor(subagents): centralize requester turn custody
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Subagent completion, cleanup, recovery, and status paths repeat the same recorded pause, pending-result, and requester-yield decisions.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. Existing pause, delivery, cancellation, and requester-turn semantics are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds one runtime-free owner for three predicates: `isSubagentPausedByYield`, `hasPendingRequesterTurnResult`, and `hasRequesterTurnYielded`. Migrates matching decisions in the allowed callers while preserving the separate live-requester and frozen-cohort owners.

Exact requester-turn ID comparisons remain at their existing sites. The original extraction moved one existing equality into the new module, which failed the session-identity per-file ratchet (`2 > 0`). The follow-up restores those expressions and removes both binding helpers; it changes neither the ratchet nor its allowlist and adds no alternate comparison syntax.

The kill files and `announce/subagent-announce*.ts` flows are unchanged. No state, schema, public API, configuration, or dependency changes.

## Evidence

- Base: `2ab7b31a13d95bbbb62596679b130445c4c9d3d1`; current head: `cc429cf90829a20753598a1004ff3863bd3e10bd`.
- Current [Blacksmith Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45941785279), lease `tbx_01m8dn540ww4hbw6xjkskwr4x8`: wrapper verified the current source and frozen dependencies; observed 4 CPUs and 15 GB RAM. **316 focused tests and all 2,260 subagent tests passed**, with zero failures and one existing opt-in benchmark skipped. `pnpm tsgo:core`, all `pnpm tsgo:test:src` shards, and changed-file oxlint passed (zero warnings/errors).
- Current independent local review at P0–P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. A separate read-only review verified exact restoration of the baseline comparisons and complete removal of both helper symbols.
- Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. [Current-head GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45942268302) is green, including the session-identity ratchet and required CI gate. The standalone ratchet probe rejected an unsupported `--base=` argument before inspecting source; this accounts for the Testbox command's combined exit 1. Its test, typecheck, and lint checks all exited 0. Ratchet proof is the successful exact-head CI job, not the rejected probe.
- Earlier [base/head Testbox comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45924543844) at `1078eff569cc190788a30693e30ed3a5c54f5c82`: 316 focused tests passed on base and head; full subagent suite had 2,260 passed, zero failed, one opt-in benchmark skipped; core and source-test typechecks and changed-file lint passed. This is historical proof, not a current-head CI claim.

The campaign's known baseline failure was reproduced by running `preserves routed native Stop authority and existing receipts (consumed-session)` alone on base: expected `aborted: false`, received `aborted: true`. It passed in both head runs' full suites. This refactor does not claim to repair that failure; no behavior-fix red/green claim is made.

<details>
<summary>Measurements and retained semantics</summary>

Counts use `git grep -c` over `src/agents/subagents`, `src/agents/tools/subagents-tool.ts`, and `src/gateway/session-restart-*.ts`, excluding `*.test*`. Counts are matching lines, not AST reads; field access includes writes, projections, and parameters.

| Measurement | Base | Head including owner | Head callers only |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Raw `requesterTurnRunId` / `requesterTurnYielded` property-access lines | 71 | 66 | 64 |
| Raw `pauseReason ===/!== "sessions_yield"` decision lines | 77 | 7 | 6 |

The six remaining caller pause comparisons are in excluded kill and announce-flow files. The new owner has three functions with CC 1, 2, 1.

Code-sloppiness scans 15 → 32 cover the same 36 caller files; scan 33 covers the new owner. No parse failures. Largest-function CC remains unchanged: `startSubagentAnnounceCleanupFlow` 98, `scheduleRequesterSettleWake` 94, `planTerminalCompletion` 94, `settleRequesterTurnAfterSessionSpawns` 86. Caller score 39.0223 → 39.0307; clone SLOC 47 → 47. This centralizes decisions without claiming a complexity-score improvement. Production diff: +141 / -85 across 36 files; test diff: 0.

Retained raw fields serve normalization, writes, forwarding, projections, exact frozen identities, or different presence rules. Memory retirement distinguishes explicit false from an absent completion flag; recovery can require no binding regardless of completion; registry retirement also recognizes frozen membership. Inline acknowledgement keeps its existing truthy yield check; the shared predicate serves strict-true sites.

`subagent-requester-turn-liveness.ts` remains the physical live-requester owner. `subagent-requester-settle-identity.ts` remains the frozen-cohort owner. Follow-up through the owning lanes: migrate the excluded kill/announce pause checks. No unrelated behavior repairs are included.

prs.title: fix: show the Gateway URL when the browser blocks sign-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When someone opens OpenClaw over HTTPS and enters a remote `ws://` Gateway URL, the browser can block the connection before the Gateway receives a sign-in request. OpenClaw tells them to open a secure page even though they are already on one, and hides the URL they can correct under **Change**.

## User Impact

| | Sign-in heading and message |
| --- | --- |
| Before | **Secure browser context required** — “Couldn’t connect over HTTP because this browser needs a secure page to identify itself.” |
| After | **Browser blocked the Gateway connection** — “Check the Gateway URL. If the Gateway uses HTTPS, use its wss:// address. If the address is already correct, open Show details.” |

**Gateway URL** and **Connect** are directly below the message. If the address is wrong, enter the secure address the Gateway actually serves, then choose **Connect**. If it is already correct, open **Show details** for the browser-policy diagnostic instead of changing the address or credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser client already distinguishes a blocked connection from a missing device identity. The sign-in screen now uses that distinction to show its existing URL form for a blocked connection. Review caught an important distinction: the browser can also refuse an already-correct secure address. The field stays editable, but OpenClaw does not mark it invalid from that refusal alone. Missing-device-identity and credential errors keep their existing guidance. No transport code, URL validation, credential handling, retry behavior, storage or permissions change.

**Skill in practice.** Name the cause the browser actually detected. Offer an address correction only when it fits, and an existing diagnostic when it does not. The original, redacted technical explanation remains under **Show details** rather than becoming the heading.

## Evidence

- Exercised the production Control UI in Chromium at 1280 × 900 and 390 × 844. On an HTTPS page, the native browser refused the remote plaintext connection before it sent a Gateway request. Before the change the URL was collapsed; after the change it was editable immediately. The expanded diagnostic was identical.
- At each viewport, entering a working local `wss://` address and selecting **Connect** sent one new sign-in request. The isolated Gateway fixture asked for its token. No authenticated session or access grant was simulated.
- For the secure-address case, a test fixture threw a synthetic `SecurityError` from the WebSocket constructor only for `wss://gateway.example.test`. The production sign-in screen kept that address editable without `aria-invalid`. Opening **Show details** revealed the browser-policy diagnostic; no connection request was sent. This tests how OpenClaw handles that browser error, not any particular browser policy.
- The mixed-content regression failed on main. The secure-address regression failed on the reviewed candidate because it marked the URL invalid. Both passed in the revised candidate: 62 tests in two focused suites (3.07 s runner wall time; CI time not measured). Both production builds completed. Their advisory bundle reports flagged CSS, chat boot request count and chat boot JavaScript size on both revisions (chat boot JavaScript: 1306.2 → 1307.1 KiB against a 1305.0 KiB target).
- The [first hosted performance check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45940101859/job/140312850685) found that importing the socket transport at runtime added 925 gzip bytes to chat startup. The sign-in screen now checks the browser error code at compile time without importing the transport. The local CI gate passed against pinned main `2237f16b7e27`: 1,336,893 → 1,336,777 bytes (116 fewer), with 21 requests on both revisions. All 62 focused tests passed again. Hosted CI was pending when this repair was published.
- UI typecheck, lint and formatting of all five changed files, the writing checker, localization verification and `git diff --check` passed. The localization baseline did not change.
- These are emulated viewports with a synthetic, loopback-only TLS Gateway fixture, not a physical phone or production Gateway. Other browser engines and full CI were not run locally.

**Clean comparison**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![An HTTPS sign-in page asks for a secure page and collapses its Gateway URL](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/78aff5e4-b268-4b8c-a4e4-c262bcae7387) | ![The same sign-in page explains the blocked connection and shows the editable Gateway URL](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6b3a292-1901-4cee-b944-23be886c0fd8) |

**Annotated comparison**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![The device-identity explanation is outlined on a page already using HTTPS](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/63bf5daa-fdf2-4c40-a3f5-35d7eba24e2f) | ![The field containing the blocked address is outlined](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a015e900-19e8-4d7e-8dae-487ad0e94ce2) |

Same HTTPS sign-in failure and synthetic address, Chromium at 390 × 844. Before: main `2237f16b7e27`. After: captured on `64f2ce58747b` (tree `a611f3bda910`). The phone, desktop and expanded secure-address screenshots were byte-identical after the performance repair.

**An already-secure address.** The screenshot below shows the synthetic constructor refusal at 1280 × 900 with **Show details** open. Unlike the plaintext case, the browser diagnostic points to its connection policy.

![Secure Gateway URL remains editable and expanded details identify browser security policy](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84713036-dd30-4d9c-8727-c2e4f8aa9dda)

Contributor: @vyctorbrzezowski

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e346c5e4-f828-45b2-be8f-1aad6754fbad)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/8782855f-de99-4cb2-be3a-e969d817611a)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix(update): send integer channels.status timeoutMs from update status
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update status --json --timeout 30` (or any `--timeout` of 30 or more) cannot read channel status. It sends `channels.status` a fractional `timeoutMs`, the Gateway rejects it (`at /timeoutMs: must be integer`), and the output carries `Channel inspection unavailable` instead of the channel check. Each call also logs an `INVALID_REQUEST` error.

Root cause: `src/cli/update-cli/status.ts` computed `remainingMs = () => Math.max(1, deadline - performance.now())`, which is fractional. For `--timeout >= 30` the per-check budget (`Math.min(checkTimeoutMs ?? 5_000, remainingMs())`) is bounded by this fractional remainder, and `ChannelsStatusParamsSchema.timeoutMs` is `Type.Integer`, so the RPC is rejected.

## Fix

`src/commands/gateway-diagnostic-readiness.ts` already rounds the same kind of RPC deadline with `Math.ceil`. Apply the same at `status.ts:133`:

```ts
const remainingMs = () => Math.max(1, Math.ceil(deadline - performance.now()));
```

This also keeps the integer contract for the other `remainingMs()` consumers (git target probe, service command/audit, run-report health).

## Impact

- Scripts and `--json` consumers get the real channel check instead of `Channel inspection unavailable` for `--timeout >= 30`.
- No more `INVALID_REQUEST` noise in the Gateway log per status call.

## Evidence

Unit regression (`src/cli/update-cli/status.test.ts`): "sends an integer channels.status timeoutMs when the overall budget bounds it" — red on base (`expected false to be true` on `Number.isInteger`), green on HEAD.

Real product proof, built dist (OpenClaw 2026.11.10 @ 40d5336) + a real `openclaw gateway run --port 18833 --bind loopback` (token auth) + real `openclaw update status --json --timeout 40`:

- BASE: `inspectionErrors: [{"section":"channels","message":"Channel inspection unavailable: invalid channels.status params: at /timeoutMs: must be integer | INVALID_REQUEST"}]`; Gateway log `⇄ res ✗ channels.status 42ms errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=invalid channels.status params: at /timeoutMs: must be integer`.
- HEAD: `inspectionErrors: null`; Gateway log `client connected ... name=gateway:channels.status ... auth=token` with no `INVALID_REQUEST`.

Fixes #206141

prs.title: fix: let a Workboard card start again after its worker run fails
prs.body:
Related: #205625 (fixes the retained claim; the issue's second expectation, reporting skipped cards in `startFailures`, is not changed here)

## What Problem This Solves

When a Workboard worker run fails after it was accepted (for example the model keeps returning errors, or the run times out or is killed), the card moves to `blocked` but stays claimed by the dead worker for 30 minutes. If you move the card back to `ready` and dispatch, nothing starts and the result lists no failure. Other `ready` cards of the same owner wait as well, because the leftover claim still fills the owner's one active slot.

## User Impact

A card whose worker failed can be moved to `ready` and dispatched again right away, and the owner's next card is no longer held back for the rest of the claim. No config or schema change.

Not changed:

- A run that ends successfully and lands in `review` keeps its claim until it expires. Worker selection documents that a card waiting for review counts while its claim has not expired, so I left it.
- A card that was manually moved out of `running` (for example to `backlog`) while its worker was still running keeps the claim when that worker later fails. Lifecycle sync does not change the status of such a card, and this change only acts where the card is moved to `blocked`.
- Scheduled dispatch still skips claimed cards without a `startFailures` entry (the second expectation in the issue). ClawSweeper's review on the issue notes that this would change the selection contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

`WorkboardStore.syncLifecycle` (`extensions/workboard/src/store.ts`) writes the `blocked` status with a fresh lifecycle source. `updateCard` skips `settleManualStatusTransition` for those writes, which is where a plain status move to `blocked` drops the claim. Attempts and `failureCount` are already settled on this path by `syncExecutionAttemptMetadata`; of what `finishRun` does for a blocked run, only the claim release was missing. `workboardCardConsumesOwnerSlot` and the dispatcher's `cardHasActiveClaim` then keep honoring the claim until `expiresAt`.

The fix releases the claim in the same lifecycle write that moves the card to `blocked`. It is tied to the status write, not to every terminal observation, so a claim taken later on an already settled card is not touched by the once-a-minute sweep.

## Evidence

Source Gateway from this checkout, isolated dev profile, default agent on a local OpenAI-compatible stub that answers every request with HTTP 500, so the worker run is accepted and then fails. Same steps on `main` (4d2d537) and on this fix applied to that commit. The branch was rebased onto cdadcea afterwards; no Workboard file changed in between, and the tests and checks below ran on the rebased commit:

```
openclaw workboard create "Retry after a failed worker" --status ready --json
openclaw workboard dispatch --max-starts 1 --admin --json
# wait until the run has failed
openclaw workboard show <id> --json
openclaw workboard move <id> --status ready --json
openclaw workboard dispatch --max-starts 1 --admin --json
```

Output condensed to status, claim, and dispatch result.

`main`:

```
show      {"status": "blocked", "execution": "blocked", "attempts": ["blocked"], "failureCount": 1, "claim": {"ownerId": "workboard-dispatcher", "expiresInMin": 29}}
move      {"status": "ready", ..., "claim": {"ownerId": "workboard-dispatcher", "expiresInMin": 29}}
dispatch  {"started": [], "startFailures": []}
```

With the fix:

```
show      {"status": "blocked", "execution": "blocked", "attempts": ["blocked"], "failureCount": 1, "claim": null}
move      {"status": "ready", ..., "claim": null}
dispatch  {"started": [{"cardId": "0cf38620", "runId": "workboard:0cf38620-…:1795661798594"}], "startFailures": []}
```

Store-level script with the real dispatcher and SQLite store, before and after:

- `subagent_ended` with `error`, `timeout`, `killed`: before, the claim stays for 30 minutes and neither the same card (after a move to `ready`) nor the owner's next `ready` card starts; after, both start.
- Recovery sweep that reads a `failed` session: stuck before and starts after, like the hook path.
- `subagent_ended` with `ok`, and a card parked in `backlog` while its worker fails: claim kept before and after (see "Not changed").
- A card that failed, was then claimed by another owner while `blocked`, and is swept again with the failed session reporting a newer timestamp: the new claim is still there after the sweep.

Tests and checks:

- `pnpm test extensions/workboard/src/lifecycle-sync.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 40 passed. The new test `dispatches a card again after its failed worker ended` fails on `main` with `expected [] to deeply equal [ ObjectContaining{…} ]` and takes about 0.7 s.
- The ten Workboard test files that use the lifecycle write path (`lifecycle-sync*.test.ts`, `store-lifecycle`, `store.attempts`, `store`, `store-verification`, `tools`, `dispatcher-compensation`, `index.lifecycle`): 174 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint on the two touched TypeScript files, and `pnpm format:check` on the three touched files: clean.
- Tests ran with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` on Node 26.10.0; the pinned Bun fork was not used.

Not done: the full suite, `pnpm check:changed` as a whole (I ran its format, lint, typecheck and line/assertion ratchet steps one by one; `check:test-timeout-race-ratchet` did not finish in my shallow clone), the Control UI dispatch action, the PostgreSQL store, and local autoreview or ClawSweeper.

Related: #204775

## What Problem This Solves

A dev-channel Git install kept a full day of builds after nothing needed them. One operator reported 21 non-serving builds using 105 GB. The disk filled, updates failed, and the Gateway could no longer write to its databases. A failed preparation could also leak its build after renaming its staging directory.

## User Impact

The resident updater collects unused releases before allocating another build. It protects the serving release, active trial and fallback, running Gateway and updater, leased builds and open-run references. Failed preparation disposes of its own build. If custody cannot be verified, it keeps the files. Status, Doctor and the cleanup preview report the last cleanup warning and observed logical bytes, not a promise of physically reclaimable space. The fix takes effect when the corrected updater drives an update, not when the previous updater installs it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The 24-hour minimum from #198835 protected processes starting before lease acquisition. The resident updater can protect them without retaining a day of builds. For historical directories whose UUID is not their run ID, the restore receipt identifies the run; both the successful target build and verified running build must match the release on disk. Legacy npm retains its conservative grace. There is no parallel cleanup job or new configuration.

Dev discovery checks hourly and only campaigns when behind upstream; preparation skips a known matching serving commit. pnpm deliberately uses clone-or-copy imports rather than hard links. Neither the schedule nor dependency import settings change.

## Evidence

Four real unpatched updates grew the isolated `releases/` directory from 4.45 to 8.90 to 13.35 to 17.80 GB apparent. An initial fix bounded new builds but left five historical releases behind. We tested the correction on that same populated install, without manual cleanup:

| Driver → verified serving revision | Release trees | Apparent size |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `580960bca025` → `04109c40415f` (installed the correction) | 8 | 35.60 GB |
| `04109c40415f` → `577687d24f8b` | 3 | 13.35 GB |
| `577687d24f8b` → `b161788986a6` | 3 | 13.35 GB |
| `b161788986a6` → `35bd3f199106` | 3 | 13.35 GB |

The first update driven by the correction removed all five stranded historical directories. Btrfs-exclusive usage fell from 8.84 to 3.32 GB. Each live Gateway build matched the selected commit, trial receipt and terminal update record. Serving and rollback trees stayed readable; these hops did not induce rollback. Outside `releases/`, 11 prunable Git worktree registrations occupied 84.97 MB; this test does not establish a bound on that metadata.

Regression tests failed before the fix for excess young builds, leaked failed publication, and the historical release/run ID mismatch. The historical correction passed 34 focused tests. Earlier checks included 129 passing custody tests (four platform skips), 42 diagnostics tests, and 64 CLI and census tests. Four journaled npm crash tests failed identically on clean base and patch because the checkout lacked the built sealed helper; those runs do not verify npm journal crash recovery. Native Windows updates were not exercised. The reporting installation was untouched.

Reported by @jesse-merhi.

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @jesse-merhi](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/13ac8e78-b532-411b-be97-79ef7a79a2c7)

prs.title: fix(test): isolate PostgreSQL upgrade schema ownership checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The PostgreSQL upgrade conformance test counted every schema in its shared test database. A concurrent Talk test created two schemas between snapshots, making a correct missing-permission refusal fail. [Failed conformance shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45941142127/job/140316013093)

## User Impact

Contributors can run upgrade and Talk coverage together and still detect leaked upgrade schemas. The change only affects the test.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each run creates a unique restricted role that owns the original schema. PostgreSQL also assigns any backup created through that connection to that role. Assert that its complete inventory after rejection consists of the original schema. This catches additional schemas regardless of their names and preserves the exact database and role in the expected grant hint.

## Evidence

- On PostgreSQL 16.15, a second connection committed an unrelated schema while the observing transaction remained open. The old whole-database query gained one row. The new owner-scoped query still returned the original schema.
- A positive control created a second schema owned by the fixture role. The same query returned both, then returned only the original after removal. The restricted role lacked database CREATE throughout.
- The signed change passed the pinned formatter and local ClawSweeper found no source issue. PR conformance CI exercises the existing real upgrade preflight and its exact error.

prs.title: fix: keep Codex turns running while another session is deleted
prs.body:
Related to #183790. This fixes one cause of that error: authority reads denied while another session's deletion settles. The original incident there and the unknown-outcome recovery questions remain open.

## What Problem This Solves

When a native-harness session (Codex, for example) is deleted, pruned by session maintenance or cut, its binding row is settled in one transaction. While that transaction is in flight, every other Codex turn that starts fails with `Plugin state authority is unavailable` and ends without a reply. On a busy Gateway this means accepted channel messages and cron runs fail whenever any other session is being cleaned up.

## User Impact

Turns in other sessions keep running while one session is deleted or pruned. Reads of the session being deleted are still refused until its outcome is known, so no turn can act on a binding that's about to disappear. Nothing to configure or migrate.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runSessionNativeBindingWorkerOperation` opened its pending publication with no scope, and `publicationScopesOverlap` treats no scope as "the whole database". The settlement only ever deletes, or on compensation restores, each participant's own binding row, so the hold now lists those rows. `beginPluginStatePublication` accepts a list of scopes, and the participant scopes use the same rule `publicationScope` already applies to keyed registrations (exact key unless the namespace can evict), now shared as `registrationPublicationScope`.

Kept as before: compound operations (no scope) still deny the whole source, the deleted session's own key is still denied while pending, and an unknown outcome still latches the whole source until `reconcilePluginStatePublication` confirms committed state.

Alternatives considered: reading the last committed snapshot would let the guard act on a binding whose deletion is about to commit, which this guard exists to prevent. Waiting for the hold to clear would still serialize unrelated sessions behind slow deletions (we saw 12-second ones).

## Evidence

- New test in `session-native-binding.test.ts`: while a Codex session's deletion is held at `native-binding-ready`, an authority read (`preparePluginStateRead`) of a sibling session's binding returns its value, and a read of the deleted key is still refused. On current `main` without the fix, the sibling read throws:
  ```
  Error: Plugin state authority is unavailable
   ❯ assertPluginStatePublicationSettled src/plugin-state/plugin-state-publication.ts:368:11
   ❯ assertPublicationCurrent src/plugin-state/plugin-state-native-binding-facts.ts
   ❯ capturePluginStateNativeBindingFacts src/plugin-state/plugin-state-native-binding-facts.ts
   ❯ preparePluginStateEntry src/plugin-sdk/plugin-state-runtime.ts
   ❯ preparePluginStateRead src/plugin-sdk/plugin-state-runtime.ts
  ```
- With the fix: `src/plugin-state/` (10 files, 139 tests), `session-native-binding.test.ts` and `session-native-binding.settlement.test.ts` pass, and oxfmt, oxlint, `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:test` pass.
- Production timing on one Gateway (2026.11.10) is in [this comment on #183790](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/183790#issuecomment-7193724002). Failures fell inside in-flight `sessions.delete` calls or right after session maintenance.
- Real Gateway proof (2026.11.10 Linux Gateway, native Codex harness, synthetic prompts only, delivery off). An eval script ran N copies in parallel. Each turn runs one Codex `agent` call in a fresh session, then `sessions.delete` on it, so deletions constantly overlap turns starting in other sessions. Same host, same load, before and after installing this change:

  | Build | Load | Turns | Turns failed with `Plugin state authority is unavailable` | Failed `sessions.delete` in the Gateway log |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | without this change | 8 parallel × 2 repeats | 256 | 13 | 0 |
  | with this change | 8 parallel × 2 repeats | 256 | 0 | 0 |
  | with this change | 12 parallel × 2 repeats | 384 | 0 | 0 |

  After the change, every turn returned a reply from the Codex harness (no fallback). The Gateway log had no `authority is unavailable` lines and no failed `agent` responses in either window. The deleted session's own key isn't read by later turns in this workload, so the Gateway runs don't exercise its denial. The regression test covers that.
- Not reproduced: the original Telegram incident in #183790. It may be this branch or the unknown-outcome latch, which this PR doesn't change.

prs.title: feat: use Nodecode's Cyber v1 as a model provider
prs.body:
Closes #205653

## What Problem This Solves

People who run security-research agents on Cyber v1, Nodecode's abliterated DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, have to add api.nodecode.ai as a custom OpenAI-compatible provider by hand: no onboarding, no context, output or price metadata, no reasoning-effort mapping, and no per-session cache key.

## User Impact

Users can install `@openclaw/nodecode-provider`, run `openclaw onboard --auth-choice nodecode-api-key` (or set `NODECODE_API_KEY`) and get `nodecode/nodecode-cyber-v1` as the default model, with its 1,048,576-token context, 131,072-token output limit and prices. The model list is read live from the account's `/v1/models`; Nodecode's non-chat models in that list (Decide v1, Image v1) stay out of the default model picker. The Control UI shows the Nodecode mark next to the provider and the model. Signing in again, or adding Nodecode beside another provider, keeps the primary model, aliases and hand-written `models.providers.nodecode` settings the user already has. Nothing changes for anyone who does not install the plugin.

## Why This Change Was Made

It follows the Abliteration plugin (#182248), the closest existing provider: an official external package, a manifest catalog, and the OpenAI-compatible replay and tool-schema hooks. Unlike Abliteration it lists models live (`discovery: refreshable`), with `unknownModelChatEvidence: "unlikely"` because Nodecode's model list carries no capability fields. The API accepts all seven `reasoning_effort` values, so every OpenClaw level passes through unchanged and `off` sends `none`. `prompt_cache_key` is on because Nodecode routes a key's requests to the same machine. Onboarding sets `preserveExistingPrimary`, as Cerebras does: without it, signing in replaced a primary model the user had already chosen (caught by the new upgrade test, fixed in the second commit).

Disclosure: I run Foresight Labs, which operates Nodecode. The icon is our own mark, used with permission (see `ui/public/provider-icons/ATTRIBUTION.md`). We are glad to maintain this plugin, either as an official package here or published by Nodecode on ClawHub if maintainers prefer.

## Evidence

### Gateway run from a fresh `OPENCLAW_HOME` (this branch, f4b6932d6)

- `openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --skip-health --mode local --auth-choice nodecode-api-key --nodecode-api-key "$NODECODE_API_KEY" --gateway-port 18805 --gateway-bind loopback --gateway-auth token` set `nodecode/nodecode-cyber-v1` as the primary model with the alias `Cyber v1`.
- With `openclaw gateway run --port 18805 --bind loopback` running (`openclaw gateway status`: connectivity check ok), `openclaw models list --provider nodecode --refresh` listed the account's models live: `nodecode-cyber-v1` (1049k, `default,configured,alias:Cyber v1`), `nodecode-decide-v1`, `nodecode-image-v1`, and one staff-only model.
- A Gateway-backed turn, `openclaw agent --agent main --session-id gateway-proof --message "Create ports.txt with the lines 22/tcp ssh and 8080/tcp http-alt, run wc -l ports.txt, and reply with its output only."`, created the file and answered `2 ports.txt`.

### Upgrade from latest stable (OpenClaw 2026.11.10, 6ea542f), then signing in with the plugin

On stable: Nodecode added by hand as a custom provider (`openclaw onboard --auth-choice custom-api-key --custom-provider-id nodecode ...`, key stored in `models.providers.nodecode.apiKey`, then `openclaw config set models.providers.nodecode.timeoutSeconds 300`), DeepSeek signed in and made the primary model (`openclaw models set deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`), and Nodecode added as a fallback with an alias (`openclaw models fallbacks add nodecode/nodecode-cyber-v1`, `openclaw models aliases add cyber nodecode/nodecode-cyber-v1`). A Gateway turn on stable created `notes.txt` in session `signin-proof`. Then the same `OPENCLAW_HOME` on this branch:

- The branch Gateway started on the stable state and was stopped again: non-interactive sign-in needs the state directory to itself, and with a Gateway still running OpenClaw refuses the state migration. That refusal is where the previous transcript stopped.
- The config stayed byte-identical to stable's.
- `openclaw onboard --non-interactive ... --auth-choice nodecode-api-key` ran to its end. Because a Nodecode key already existed, OpenClaw saved the new key as a separate, inactive profile and changed nothing else: "Replacement credential saved but inactive. Your connection is unchanged." It exits 1 there, which is how core non-interactive onboarding reports a staged replacement for any provider (`src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local/auth-choice.plugin-providers.ts`).
- Before and after the sign-in, the primary model (`deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`), the fallback (`nodecode/nodecode-cyber-v1`), the aliases, the hand-written provider entry (128k context, `timeoutSeconds: 300`) and the stored key (same SHA-256 prefix) are identical.
- `openclaw models auth list --agent main` lists the new inactive profile `nodecode:setup-...` next to `deepseek:default`.
- Through the restarted branch Gateway, the stable session resumed on the DeepSeek primary (`notes.txt: axolotl`), and a turn with `--model cyber` ran a tool on Nodecode (`8 notes.txt`).

### Provider mark in the Control UI

The chat model picker with the same hand-configured `nodecode` provider on both sides (from `openclaw onboard --auth-choice custom-api-key`), each on its own Gateway with a real key, light theme, 1280x800 at 2x. Before: main dcba477b0. After: this branch f4b6932d6. No fixtures or DOM edits.

#### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: a letter N fallback in the provider row and no mark on the model chip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c458ed08-f72e-4376-b226-90e775da2258) | ![After: the Nodecode axolotl mark in the provider row and on the model chip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7e96b6f1-7977-407a-b1b3-e04c27e085c1) |

#### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Letter fallback and bare model chip highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c76dc1fb-072c-4518-97e5-ef20f295896f) | ![Nodecode mark highlighted in the provider row and on the model chip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3149131d-b06e-49f0-962b-dda75e281158) |

### Tests

- `pnpm test:extension nodecode`: 4 passed. The new test signs in over a config with another primary model, a fallback, an alias and a hand-written provider entry, and checks all four are kept; without `preserveExistingPrimary` it fails (`Expected: "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5"`, `Received: "nodecode/nodecode-cyber-v1"`).
- Live against api.nodecode.ai, `NODECODE_LIVE_TEST=1 pnpm test:live extensions/nodecode/nodecode.live.test.ts`: a text request and a full tool-call round trip, 2 passed.
- `src/plugins/contracts/provider-live-listing.contract.test.ts`: 40 passed, including `nodecode requests the account's model list`. `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts`: 9 passed. The three `bundled-provider-auth-literal-parity` shards: 44 passed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck, format, config docs baseline and the other lanes pass. Three lanes fail only on files this PR does not touch: changelog attributions (`CHANGELOG/2026.11.10.md:8130`), the dead export scan (`scripts/publish-model-catalog.mts`) and lint max-lines (crabbox, agents, gateway, wizard and ui files). `oxlint` on the changed files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Docs: MDX check, markdownlint, docs format and the link audit pass; the spellcheck findings are all in other pages.

Not verified: the hosted release live lane, and publishing to npm or ClawHub.

prs.title: improve(discord): guide Goal actions with native subcommands
prs.body:
Related: #205931

## What Problem This Solves

Discord's native `/goal` command presents separate `action` and `text` options rather than guiding people through each action's inputs. Starting or editing a goal should offer an objective field, while status and clear should not ask for unnecessary text.

## User Impact

The Discord command picker offers eight Goal subcommands. Start and Edit require an **objective**; Pause, Resume, Complete, and Block offer an optional **note**; Status and Clear need no extra fields. The new form appears after Discord command registration refreshes. Ordinary text `/goal` commands, other channels, and Goal execution are unchanged.

This remains a draft: exhaustive lifecycle coverage and inspected before/after menu screenshots are not provided. No production bot registration was changed for this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the change in the Discord adapter: reuse its existing subcommand serializer and leaf dispatch handler, translating action-specific fields into the existing shared Goal arguments. Shared parsing, authorization, session routing, and lifecycle remain authoritative. The diff contains the adapter change, focused boundary regressions, and a short documentation update; no dependency, config, or state-schema changes.

Rollback is to revert the adapter change and refresh Discord command registration.

## Evidence

Validation reused from commit `8908bcd808cc8b9c2e86e07b03c2d9e8a7c0378b`:

- 79 focused tests passed across five files, including serialized registration, nested raw Discord interaction dispatch for all eight actions, plugin dispatch, and authorization siblings. The registration regression failed on the original flat form and passed with this change.
- Discord production and touched-test typechecks, focused lint, formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed. The exact source was built for the isolated Canary.
- Independent scoped autoreview completed clean at P0–P2 with no actionable findings; unchanged surrounding implementation and live client rendering were outside that review's coverage.
- Isolated Canary API readback confirmed all eight subcommands and required/optional fields. Both global and target-guild registrations were inspected; a pre-existing guild override was corrected only in the Canary fixture.
- Human native Discord start/status and client-visible outputs were observed. Correlated live Goal state confirmed three automatic continuation turns followed by completion, with no active run.
- [Public sanitized correlated runtime readback and evidence scope](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205976#issuecomment-7195090994): the existing multi-turn snapshot records `status: complete`, `continuationTurns: 3`, `hasActiveRun: false`, and `tokensUsed: 1687`. Internal session/goal/message identifiers were removed. These values belong to the multi-turn goal; the earlier counting goal's status output is a different observation.
- Screenshot delivery remains blocked: the existing native start/status and checkpoint screenshot was inspected and its human name/avatar redacted, but upstream attachment upload requires repository write access. Uploads in the author's existing public fork returned asset URLs whose public reads returned HTTP 404; no working public screenshot is claimed.
- ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head with no actionable code findings; its proof and maintainer-layout gates remain unresolved. A fresh review is being requested after publishing this bounded evidence.
- Not claimed: exhaustive Goal lifecycle testing, before/after menu screenshots, publicly rendered interaction screenshot, production activation, broad build/test CI, or a cleared hosted-review verdict. The public runtime snapshot is not a substitute for command-picker comparison proof.

Publication recovery preserves the reviewed implementation without rebasing or changing its source.

prs.title: fix: use the full width of chat side panels
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When you open an HTML attachment in the chat side panel, the filename bar, toolbar and preview stop 16 px short of both edges. Some other viewers waste even more space: a catalog app can stay 300 px wide in a 480 px panel, and expanding the Knowledge tab can leave large empty margins.

## User Impact

File and Canvas previews, MCP Apps, tool output and the Knowledge activity tab now use the available panel width. Text and controls keep their own spacing. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The enclosing panel owns the available width; the viewer owns the spacing inside it. This removes a per-view list that left catalog apps at their intrinsic width. The full-page Knowledge reader keeps its existing width limit.

## Evidence

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![The filename bar and preview are inset from both panel edges](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28019c1e-a29f-406a-8594-7449b89eecf6) | ![The filename bar, toolbar and preview meet the panel edges](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/08581b8d-cba3-4bae-936a-f5ad22f24c91) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![The preview starts 16 pixels to the right of the tab bar](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06f96d20-e085-480b-9a44-3c6e1db8a9a7) | ![The preview and tab bar now share the same left edge](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c1190ff5-c495-4021-a62e-1fd28030a3c2) |

Same 480 px panel at a 1,440 px viewport in Chromium, with a synthetic HTML attachment and an isolated preview frame. Base: `1da4ec2b1537`; candidate: `d296a0cfcf05`. The filename bar, toolbar and iframe each measured 448 px before and 480 px after.

All 18 focused browser cases passed on the candidate: HTML Preview/Source, long Markdown and plain text at desktop and phone widths, PDF preview and download, Canvas resizing, MCP Apps in Chromium and WebKit, and short and long tool output. The layout audit also measured all 14 built-in panel types, the two bundled plugin tabs and the new-tab surface in split and expanded modes. The expanded Knowledge surface used all 1,610 px; its full-page reader was unchanged. The file source meets the toolbar with no gap and keeps a 16 px text inset. Markdown cards keep a 16 px margin on either side.

Independent design review caught a second frame around Source and missing space around attachment cards; both were corrected and rechecked. Local autoreview covered `1da4ec2b1537..d296a0cfcf05` with attachment source context and reported no actionable P0–P2 findings. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; hosted review is due when the draft is marked ready.


### Rebase verification

The rebase to 2704fd360767 preserves both the current main branch's CSV styling and this PR's panel insets. On head 97b732819172, the combined Chromium run passed eight cases and failed two HTML-preview cases: HiDPI clicks after navigation and in-page navigation with scripts. The isolated rerun of the three relevant preview cases passed on both the base and the rebased head. The combined-run failures were not reproduced in isolation; their cause remains unconfirmed.


🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)



### Updated panel proof

[Clean and annotated Canvas and MCP comparisons for `d46786bd1db6`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205595#issuecomment-7210288757). The focused bundled browser replay passed 17 tests, including the retained MCP iframe in Chromium and WebKit. The measured CSS total was 348,678 B gzip against the unchanged 348,683 B ceiling. The consolidated flush flag preserves the existing 16 px reading inset for other content.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A session with a display name but no manual label could change names at the point of deletion. Sessions listed “Backup maintenance”, but its confirmation and linked-automation warning called it “agent:main:backup”.

## User Impact

The person can check the conversation’s name in the confirmation dialog. The actions menu’s accessible name, the confirmation from that menu and the confirmation for a single-item selection use the same displayed name; selecting several sessions still shows the count. Cancel, deletion, transcript retention and linked automations behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The display name identifies the conversation to its reader; the key and session ID identify it to the Gateway. Reuse the existing UI name resolver rather than replacing mutation identifiers or adding another confirmation.

## Evidence

Chromium, synthetic Gateway data: same session and linked automation, same dialog crop. Base `8d98397fcc5c` shows the routing key; candidate `ffc0734c73ad` shows the display name. The browser scenario also cancels once, confirms once, and checks that no automation is modified. The sidebar case remains unchanged. On an isolated real Gateway, selecting one session in the table showed its displayed name in the confirmation; cancelling kept the row.

The production build reports three existing asset-budget overages (largest CSS, chat startup JS request count, and compressed chat startup JS). A clean build of the same base revision reports all three; no budget was raised.

prs.title: refactor(subagents): centralize completion delivery decisions
prs.body:
Closes #206373
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204178

## What Problem This Solves

Maintainers currently have to follow subagent completion decisions through direct response classification, announce-flow reporting, and lifecycle cleanup. The same delivery obligation is interpreted in several places, making receipt precedence and fallback changes difficult to review.

This is the maintainer-requested cutover to one completion-decision owner.

## User Impact

No intentional user-visible behavior change. Direct delivery, queue custody, requester handoff, and requester-history settlement retain their existing behavior. The legacy `suspended`, `failed`, and `discarded` readers and active admission expiry remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The obligation module owns reply policy, response/fallback decisions, once-only receipt reporting, and cleanup outcomes. Transport adapters execute those decisions and return receipts; the existing lifecycle owners still persist state. Child-result preparation is separated from dispatch. Existing import surfaces used by `sessions_send` continue to expose the same implementations.

The explicit decision and fact contracts add 286 production SLOC in the measured scope while reducing the large functions below. No stored-state format or configuration is added.

## Evidence

Pinned base: `2ab7b31a13d95bbbb62596679b130445c4c9d3d1`  
Current head: `41a93922a7d9133306268d767bb7d1894f3f9d14`  
Runtime-proof head: `5639d82df867f6078604bec1df5611609770b839`

Validation ran on **Blacksmith Testbox** `tbx_01m8dj32n7ns87rv8wnj2zynme` (4 CPUs, about 16 GB RAM, Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0), using the repository source-capsule wrapper. [Allocation workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45936610991); the command receipts verified the runtime-proof head above independently of the allocation workflow.

- Focused announce, `sessions_send`, and prompt-prefix coverage: **434 tests passed in 37 files**, five shards.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:test:src`: passed.
- Targeted oxlint on all seven changed files: **0 warnings, 0 errors**.
- `pnpm test src/agents/subagents --maxWorkers=2`: **all six shards passed**; existing skips were retained.
- The campaign-listed `preserves routed native Stop authority and existing receipts (consumed-session)` case **passed** in this run. The previously reported failure did not reproduce here; this PR does not claim to fix it.
- Local branch review at **P0–P2**: **no actionable findings**. Unchanged delivery-state, lifecycle, transport, history-admission, and regression-test neighbors were supplied as source context.
- Formatting and `git diff --check`: passed. Live-provider tests were not run.
- CI assertion-ratchet repair: document the existing typed receipt assertion and remove its obsolete allowance from the old file. The local assertion SAFETY ratchet passed at the current head. The source delta since the runtime-proof head is one comment, so the runtime and type/lint proof above is reused; current-head PR CI remains required.

`code-sloppiness` 0.2.0+vk.4, identical scope/engine, complete coverage with no parse failures:

| Function | Base CC | Head CC |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `runSubagentAnnounceFlowBound` | 143 | 101 |
| `sendSubagentAnnounceDirectlyBound` | 109 | 90 |
| `createDirectAnnounceResponseClassifier` | 101 | 1 |
| `startSubagentAnnounceCleanupFlow` | 98 | 92 |

The new response-decision functions have CC **45** and **35**; classification complexity was split along evidence and outcome boundaries, not discarded. Measured production SLOC: **5,178 → 5,464**.

`git grep -c` over production announce files and the two cleanup files, using `\.delivered|delivery\??\.status|announceOutcome ===`: **45 → 43** matching lines. Legacy-state predicates in `subagent-delivery-state.ts`: **5 → 5**.

Open overlap: [#198204 — completion review no longer repeats a result the user already saw](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198204) also changes the announce flow. This branch remains pinned to its reviewed base; integration belongs to the coordinator.

prs.title: fix(ui): hide blank Not sent rows in Home
prs.body:
Closes #205960

## What Problem This Solves

Home could show an empty **Not sent** row above the composer. The row looked like a failed message the user could recover, but it was an internal receipt with no message content.

## User Impact

Home no longer shows retired receipts in either the dock or the full page. The user can still copy or remove a genuinely recoverable unsent message. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared queue projection now honors the Gateway's explicit non-visible marker. This is a one-line presentation change; it doesn't change pending-input storage, receipt custody, or delivery. The existing composer test covers recovery actions, and the Chromium test covers the two Home entry points and checks that opening them doesn't call chat.send.

## Evidence

- Independent local review of the three-file change (base 0f73e04b3f9, submitted head 306e86843eb): no blocking findings.
- Focused checks: 29 passed (16 composer, 8 queue/lifecycle siblings, 4 Gateway custody, 1 Chromium regression). The Chromium scenario built the Control UI and verified the dock and full page against a simulated Gateway; it also asserted no chat.send. Ten unrelated browser cases were filtered out.
- Targeted lint, format, UI and touched-test typechecks, and git diff --check passed. Broad CI and full-package builds were not run locally.
- The corrected Control UI bundle was verified on a live local Gateway after deployment. The empty rows were absent in the operator's browser and in the macOS app's Home dock. The synthetic two-record regression itself was not replayed against an isolated real Gateway with a model.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Empty Not sent row above a recoverable message](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a24c64f1-cdf2-4ced-a5a3-ee3c7d76c7aa) | ![Only the recoverable message remains](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2528bf16-c14b-4fa3-af43-631baf3411ff) |

prs.title: fix: let Gemini voice-note transcription run at a lower thinking level
prs.body:
Root cause: `extensions/google/media-understanding-provider.ts:59` (origin/main `a48488cc6`) builds the `generateContent` body from the prompt and inline audio only and never reads `params.query`, although `src/media-understanding/runner.entries.ts:336` already passes `providerOptions.google` to it as `query`. So no config reaches Gemini's `generationConfig`, and audio transcription always runs at the model's default thinking level.

Related: #181086 (audio part; video is not wired in the runner, see Scope below)

## What Problem This Solves

People who transcribe voice notes with Gemini through `tools.media` cannot choose the thinking level. The Google media provider ignores the `providerOptions.google` values the media runner already passes, so every note runs at the model's default (high) thinking. For chat voice notes that means long waits and several times the cost, with no config switch to turn it down.

## User Impact

Google audio transcription now honours two documented options on a `tools.media.models[]` entry (or `tools.media.audio`):

```json5
{
  provider: "google",
  model: "gemini-3-flash-preview",
  providerOptions: { google: { thinkingLevel: "low" } }, // or thinkingBudget: 0
}
```

They are sent as `generationConfig.thinkingConfig`. With neither set, the request body is unchanged, so existing setups behave exactly as before. No migration.

Scope: audio only. The runner passes `query` only to audio providers (`VideoDescriptionRequest` has no `query`), so video description is not changed here; wiring it would mean touching the shared runner and request type.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveProviderQuery` already flattens `providerOptions.<provider>` into `params.query`, and other audio providers (Deepgram, OpenRouter) read it. The Google provider was the gap. This maps only the two thinking keys, ignores anything else, and adds no new config surface.

## Evidence

Upstream CI on this head is waiting for workflow approval (fork PR).

- **Runtime proof through the shipped CLI entry point** ([report](https://github.com/khensthoth/openclaw/blob/5da9af64fe5f796a783a2d12d24f61f10aa01dc9/evidence/google-audio-thinking-level/2026-11-26/README.md)). A source-built `pnpm openclaw infer audio transcribe --file <wav> --json` with an isolated config whose only `tools.media.models[]` entry is `google/gemini-4-neon` with `providerOptions.google.thinkingLevel: "low"` (no `--model`, so it takes the configured-entry path). Audio is a synthetic text-to-speech clip.
  - [Stub run](https://github.com/khensthoth/openclaw/blob/5da9af64fe5f796a783a2d12d24f61f10aa01dc9/evidence/google-audio-thinking-level/2026-11-26/stub-run.json): the request OpenClaw sends contains `"generationConfig":{"thinkingConfig":{"thinkingLevel":"low"}}`.
  - [Live run](https://github.com/khensthoth/openclaw/blob/5da9af64fe5f796a783a2d12d24f61f10aa01dc9/evidence/google-audio-thinking-level/2026-11-26/live-run.json), one real Gemini call: HTTP 200, `modelVersion: gemini-4-neon`, exact transcript, `usageMetadata.thoughtsTokenCount: 175`. Gemini accepts the option for inline audio on `generateContent`.
  - The request capture wrapper is [included](https://github.com/khensthoth/openclaw/blob/5da9af64fe5f796a783a2d12d24f61f10aa01dc9/evidence/google-audio-thinking-level/2026-11-26/capture-gemini.mjs). It records the body without headers or audio bytes, and forwards through the checkout's own undici fetch and dispatcher.
- Focused tests in `extensions/google/media-understanding-provider.video.test.ts`: body has `generationConfig.thinkingConfig` when `thinkingLevel` / `thinkingBudget` is set (including `thinkingBudget: 0`), and no `generationConfig` when the options are unset or unrelated.
  - With the fix: 11/11 pass (`vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts`). On `main` without the fix the two option-set cases fail (2 failed, 9 passed), so they cover the bug.
  - `tsgo -p tsconfig.extensions.json`: 0 errors. `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on touched files: clean. `git diff --check`: clean.
  - Run on Windows; `pnpm test <file>` stalled there with no output before Vitest started, so Vitest was called directly with the same config.
- Real-world measurement that motivated this (run outside OpenClaw against the Gemini API, same request shape): 77 real WhatsApp voice notes from Malaysian customers (36 Mandarin, 34 Hokkien, the rest Teochew, Cantonese, English/Malay or unclear), transcribed with `gemini-4-neon`. Outputs were blind-ranked by `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` listening to the audio. Aggregate numbers only; no transcripts are shared.
  - `thinkingLevel: "low"`: median 8.9 s, about $0.011 per note.
  - Default (high) thinking: median 47 s, max 283 s, about $0.05–0.12 per note.
  - Accuracy: low got items wrong on 9/77 notes and invented words on 6/77. Default was somewhat more accurate (judged better on 39, worse on 15, 23 ties).
  - So low is the practical setting for chat voice notes, but it cannot be selected today.
- Not covered: a Gateway run with a channel attachment (the CLI uses the same `tools.media` runner), video (not wired, see above), and `thinkingBudget` against the live API (unit tests only).

prs.title: fix(workboard): preserve peer column edits on a Sessions board rename
prs.body:
## What problem does this solve?

Two people can edit a Sessions board at the same time. If one person renames the board and types ` A` into a column already labeled `A`, the normalized label is unchanged. Saving used to submit the entire list of columns from the open editor. That could undo a peer’s saved change to a different column. Choosing a different fallback column and then switching back could trigger the same overwrite.

## What changed?

The editor compares the normalized opening and outgoing columns before saving board metadata. For this comparison, an omitted fallback flag and an explicit `false` mean the same thing. A genuine column edit still sends the validated column values. This extends @steipete’s earlier rename fix to edits that normalize back to the opening values. [Original rename fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167348) · [Solid UI port](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168606)

## Evidence

- The original registered-handler reproduction changed a peer column from `B` to `C` before the appearance save. After the save, SQLite and a fresh editor both showed `B`. Independent replays with a leading space and a trailing space reproduced the same loss.
- On the current parent, both mounted editor regressions received `B` instead of `C`; three controls passed. All five passed with the repair.
- With the production handler and SQLite, clicking Save after moving the fallback from **Done** to **Working** committed one fallback change. A fresh editor showed **Working**. After moving away and back, renaming the board sent only the metadata update and preserved the peer’s column.
- On the final formatted tree, the reduced `Desk` → `Desk review` case was replayed against the registered Workboard handlers. After the peer committed `C`, Save emitted one metadata update and zero column writes. Independent SQLite and a fresh editor both retained `C`.
- The declared Workboard UI package build succeeded. The generated manifest resolved to a 19,746-byte JavaScript entry and a 94,200-byte stylesheet in the same asset generation.
- **Matched-base UI performance.** The first release run compared the original branch with a main revision 23 commits beyond its parent and reported +111 B of chat-boot gzip. After merging main into this branch, the hosted job compared the reviewed PR tree against that exact main parent. Chat boot measured 1,336,732 B and 21 requests on both sides (+0 B). [Original comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45925662729/job/140266776623) · [Matched comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45926986424/job/140271002589)

The editor proofs used mounted jsdom components, registered handlers and SQLite. The build verified the packaged browser assets. An interactive capture from an installed dashboard remains unmeasured. [Redacted replay records](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206292#issuecomment-7207847427)

A plugin reload can complete successfully and return an informational warning such as “Plugin replacement waited for retained work to finish.” The update owner treated any warning as a failed activation and told the operator to reload plugins that had already reloaded. The existing successful lifecycle-test row now returns a warning and requires a completed plugins step, the warning text and no false retry action. Existing RPC rejection coverage remains. The restart-required branch is unchanged.

prs.title: fix: stop an idle Control UI tab from relisting models in a loop
prs.body:
Fixes #206097

## What Problem This Solves

With a Control UI chat tab open and idle, the Gateway can list models thousands of times per minute. Each `models.list` reply says the catalog is still pending, the Gateway broadcasts `chat.metadata.changed`, and the tab asks for `models.list` again, forever. The trigger in the report: two agents share one OAuth sign-in, and the catalog worker uses newer credentials than the ones the agent's runtime started with (OAuth refresh or adoption from the main agent, or an external CLI credential).

## Root cause

`acquireProviderCatalog` (`src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.catalog-access.ts:314` on main) records each completed provider's credential key from the auth the worker discovered. `listChangedPreparedCatalogProviders` (`prepared-model-runtime.catalog-source.ts`) compares that key with the generation's startup `params.agentFacts`. When the two differ, every `changedOnly` read marks the provider pending (`modelCatalogStatusChanged: true`), and the tab reads again.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. Completed discovery now records the generation input it satisfied, `preparedProviderCatalogCredentials(params.agentFacts, …)`: the same input the comparison reads. The worker-discovered auth still owns the published catalog auth and account retention. A real credential change starts a new generation with different facts, so it is still rediscovered once.
2. The credential key and `hasSamePreparedModelCatalogAuth` now use one identity function, `preparedModelCatalogAuthIdentity` (extracted, not new logic). For an OAuth profile with an account identity, the volatile `access`/`refresh`/`expires`/`idToken` fields are left out, so a hot reload after a token rotation of the same account keeps the learned catalog instead of rediscovering.

Removed from this PR: the expiry-failure backoff change (`failProvider`, the moved `recordFailedDiscovery`, the `beforeProviderFailure` parameter removal) and its two tests. That path has no observed occurrence in #206097. Both backoff tests are red on the merge base `36395007cf` (second consecutive failure stays at `discoveryFailures: 1`, `expiresAt` unchanged), so the defect is real; it moves to its own fix. The `models.json` missing-`api` warning in the report is handled in a separate PR.

## User Impact

An idle Control UI tab no longer drives a `models.list` / `chat.metadata.changed` loop and the CPU and provider `/v1/models` traffic it caused. A real credential change still refreshes the model list once. No config, schema or protocol change.

## Evidence

Regressions (vitest-source, merge base `36395007cf` vs head):

- `prepared-model-catalog-worker.integration.test.ts` "settles models.list follow-up reads after real worker external-auth discovery" (real catalog worker, through the `models.list` handler and the metadata lifecycle): fails on the base, passes on head.
- `prepared-model-runtime.scoped-refresh.test.ts` "retains discovery across a hot reload with rotated identified OAuth": fails on the base, passes on head.
- Head: touched tests plus every test importing a changed source, 46 files, all pass. `pnpm check:changed`: all lanes pass except the dead-export scan, which reports two untouched files (`src/agents/btw-runtime.ts`, `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-control.types.ts`) also reported on the base.

End to end: built Gateway (`pnpm build:docker && pnpm ui:build`) in a secretless `node:24.22.1` container, a real Chromium Control UI tab, and a local stand-in OAuth provider (plugin loaded from `plugins.load.paths`; sign-in, refresh and `/v1/models` go to a local server; no real credentials). Setup from the report: agents `main` and `helper`; `helper` holds an older copy of the same sign-in, `main` signs in later; the first token is inside the refresh window when discovery runs; tab on `/chat/helper`. Counts over 60 s idle after the tab loads.

| Build | Scenario | `models.list` | `chat.metadata.changed` | stand-in `/v1/models` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base `36395007cf` run 1 | reporter topology | 2467 | 2467 | 2466 |
| base `36395007cf` run 2 | reporter topology | 3060 | 3060 | 3061 |
| head `081b1405b1` run 1 | reporter topology (OAuth adoption logged 1×) | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| head `081b1405b1` run 2 | reporter topology (OAuth adoption logged 2×) | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| head `081b1405b1` | real key change after startup (`openclaw models auth paste-api-key --provider standin`) | 4 in the action window, then 0 over 60 s idle | 7, then 0 | 2 at the action (OAuth + new key), then 0 |

The base also relists once on a real key change and then stays at 0 (base-side comment below).

Base-side runs: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206122#issuecomment-7203236168

Thanks @DonnieFi for the report, the root-cause analysis and the original fix.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert fully undoes it; nothing is written to state or config. Blast radius: model catalog rediscovery decisions for `changedOnly` reads and hot reloads of identified OAuth accounts.

prs.title: feat: let four more doctor --fix repairs tell when they have nothing to do
prs.body:
Related: #204775

## What Problem This Solves

Every `openclaw doctor --fix` stops a healthy Gateway before it knows whether any step has work. To make that stop conditional, each step must answer "is there work?" from a read. After #206247, 29 decisions on a healthy install still answered "work" only because they had no check. Several of them also opened a write transaction on every run just to find nothing to do: the agent database path repair, the generated exec-approval cleanup, and the retired usage-cost cleanup (a `DELETE` on every agent database).

## User Impact

Doctor repairs nothing differently. On a healthy install with the trace on (`OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE=1`), 68 of 94 decisions now trace `pending=none check=owner` (64 before). Three repairs no longer take a SQLite write lock when their store is clean, so `config-audit-scrub` drops from about 167 ms to about 18 ms on four agent databases, and a clean store no longer fails or waits 5 s when another connection holds its write lock.

## Why This Change Was Made

Same mechanism as #206247: each check calls the repair's own predicate, split out at its owner where it sat inside the write.

| Contribution | Check (`work` when) | Read path |
|---|---|---|
| `config-audit-scrub` | the config-audit scrub dry run would rewrite an entry; a legacy usage-cost sidecar exists; a registered agent database holds a retired usage-cost row (same `WHERE` as the `DELETE`, now one shared expression); skill-upload staging or the old Control UI cache exists | read-only agent database open, file stats |
| `legacy-state` | its two core repairs have work (derived as in #206247); preflight did not already migrate this exact config (the existing in-memory gate); the stored exec-approval policy holds generated grants the cleanup removes (`countObsoleteGeneratedExecApprovals`) | direct read-only state database read (no copy) |
| `release-configured-plugin-installs` | configured ids exist and either the config has not crossed the release gate (a completed step stamps its touched version) or the repair's pre-lease no-op plan says there is package or record work | the repair's existing read-only plan, now one exported function shared by the repair |
| `legacy-plugin-source-captures` | a legacy capture root exists, or a native capture root the cleanup would reclaim (the cleanup's own walk in its existing `collect` mode); an incomplete inspection is `undecidable`. A managed root counts as work even if its payload is retained, because reclaiming it takes the root's SQLite custody lock | directory walks only |

Read first, then write (each still rereads inside its transaction before writing):
- `noteDoctorAgentDatabasePathHealth` opens its write transaction only when the read-only plan finds a registration to repair. The plan is a pure function over the rows; the repair and the check share it.
- `repairObsoleteGeneratedExecApprovals` opens its write transaction only when the store holds such a grant.
- The usage-cost cleanup calls the retire path only for agent databases that hold a retired row. An unreadable database or one without the agent schema still goes through the retire path, as before.

Also: the new read-only SQLite reads sit in `src/commands/` so the main-thread SQLite worker ratchet does not grow; `release-configured-plugin-installs`' run moved unchanged into `doctor-health-contribution-runners.state.ts` to keep `doctor-health-contributions-initial.ts` under its line cap; the unused export `DoctorContributionPending` from #206247 is now module-private (the unused-export scan flagged it). No schema, stored field, config option, protocol or retention change.

### Left on the default, with the reason

| Contribution | Why it still answers `work` |
|---|---|
| `state-integrity` | its path repair now reads first, but `noteStateIntegrity` decides its plugin session-route repairs by loading plugin doctor-contract modules and, for explicit runtime selections, a plugin registry inspection; it reads deferred plugin migrations through an artifact-preserving read that can copy the state database; and backup scratch liveness is only provable by taking the scratch lock. A check needs a probe of `noteStateIntegrity` with a declining prompter, an injectable note sink and a non-copy migration read |
| `legacy-cron` | `maybeRepairLegacyCronStore` loads the mutable cron store, which commits retired-job deletions and runtime-authority repairs before any prompt; the read-only loader hides both and stages a snapshot copy under artifact-preserving reads. Its health detect also disagrees with the repair (misses invalid config rows, flags advisory-only items). Needs read-only counts of retired rows and authority repairs at the cron store owner, and an inference-binding plan that keeps the authorization-restore path |
| `auth-profile-migration` | the archive resume step decides each receipt after taking the auth store file lock, the plugin model catalog repair runs for every agent under `--yes` even with nothing detected, and the OAuth id repair loads provider plugins; it also writes config inside the contribution |
| preview-only owners (`session-transcripts`, `-headers`, `-labels`, `codex-session-routes`), `heartbeat-*`, `memory-search`, `sandbox`, `gateway-auth`, `auth-profiles`, `structured-health-repairs` | not started in this PR; reasons as listed in #206247 |
| config writers, service definition | not this lane (config-flow result and a daemon-side plan) |

## Update behavior

No update-path change. A published updater that runs this release's Doctor runs the same repairs in the same order. The visible differences are trace lines and that three clean stores are no longer opened for writing.

prs.title: improve: load less code in the shared database writer
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every shared-state SQLite writer loaded the code for claiming and inspecting agent database leases. The writer needs one operation from that code to retire a lease after its worker exits. Loading the whole module also initialized its ordinary close-receipt cache and pulled in the agent deletion journal.

## User Impact

A cold Gateway shared database writer loads less JavaScript. Existing operators need no configuration or migration. These measurements cover one SQLite worker. Gateway RSS and low-memory startup remain separate questions.

## Why This Change Was Made

[The shutdown fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203241) keeps exited-worker cleanup available after an in-place update replaces files on disk. The writer still imports its cleanup handler synchronously. The handler and ordinary lease owner now share only their lease-row queries, physical-file alias invalidation and receipt-checked deletion. A confirmed refused open still preserves a surviving borrower’s validation. An unconfirmed exit still invalidates it.

## Evidence

- On Linux x64 with Node 24.22.1, a fresh physical `dist/infra/sqlite-store.worker.js` opened the packaged shared-state backend against an existing SQLite file. V8 reported 446 evaluated package modules on the base and 432 on the change. Their emitted files totaled 3,827,265 and 3,686,033 bytes respectively. Only the base initialized the ordinary agent lease cache and evaluated the deletion journal and ordinary SQLite worker-store chunks.
- Six separate unprofiled workers were measured in alternating order. The median physical V8 heap at actor open was 100,282,368 bytes on the base and 99,540,992 bytes on the change. Median used heap was 65,105,504 and 64,655,800 bytes. These are three single-point samples per version and do not measure process RSS.
- The import regression failed on the base and passed with the change. The shared-writer imports, agent execution cleanup and lease owner suites passed. All three selected real lifecycle cases passed, including the refused-open survivor, killed-worker cleanup and stale admission. The packaged comparison exited 0 in the [private test environment allocated by this run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45936739212). The final source correction moves the five lease identity fields into a shared TypeScript type. All three affected files emit identical JavaScript before and after that correction under the pinned esbuild transform.
- The SQLite inventory moves three existing lease-row queries into the new file. Total calls and policy classification for those queries stay the same. The full generator already disagrees with the untouched base document (825 files and 2,816 actual calls versus 2,813 recorded). Running it on both source trees verified the only new owner is the lease-row file. This PR applies only that between-version change to the snapshot. The [required SQLite worker ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45939778435/job/140311980086) passed on the final head with 166 live T1 and 15 deprecated-only T1-compat calls in each tree.
