prs.title: fix: distinguish creating a setup code from checking a device connection
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In **Devices → Connect a device**, two different failures offer the same **Reload** button. If the dialog couldn’t get a setup code, that button requests a code. If it couldn’t find out whether the device connected, the button checks the original setup instead. Neither action reloads the page.

## User Impact

| When | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A setup code request fails | “Couldn’t create a setup code. Try again.” · **Reload** | “Couldn’t get a setup code.” · **Create setup code** |
| The code reaches its expiry and the connection status check fails | “Couldn’t check whether the device connected. Try again.” · **Reload** | “Couldn’t check whether the device connected.” · **Check connection status** |

The first button makes another code request using the selected access level. The second checks the same setup without requesting another code. No migration or permission change is required. The Gateway’s explanation stays visible, and the separate secure-access instructions for a loopback-only Gateway are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dialog already knows which request failed. It now uses that information to name the existing action without changing pairing, approval, expiry, or retry behavior.

**Skill in practice:** The writing guide says to name what happened to the reader’s work and what they can do next. A timeout tells the dialog it didn’t get a code, not that the Gateway never created one. “Couldn’t get a setup code” preserves that distinction, and the button names the next request rather than promising that trying again will fix it.

## Evidence

- Reproduced both failures in the actual English Control UI before and after the change, then followed each button. A synthetic Gateway returned “The Gateway is busy.” for both. Code recovery sent a second code request; status recovery checked the original setup ID, reported **Setup code expired** when no completed pairing was recorded, and sent no additional code request.
- The affected dialog and lifecycle tests passed (42 tests, 2.41 s). The updated accessible-action assertions failed on the base because only **Reload** was offered. The focused Chromium test against the production UI bundle also passed (23.89 s including setup): after a rejected or timed-out code request, **Create setup code** returned the dialog to its QR state.
- UI typecheck, touched-file lint and formatting, writing checks, and the English catalog checks passed. The Gateway was synthetic. Live phone pairing and full CI were not run.

- Simplification pass: removed the generic **Reload** and **Try again** wording from these two states. The existing error source chooses the label; the request and permission checks are unchanged. Relative to the base: production +11/−3 lines; tests +11/−9. The status test checks that the button reads the original setup ID.
- Independent native source review of `2237f16b7e2753ded72412795aa614c298dd8c4e..ca0be9501acbb6e171ec41fdf9af9023dbe3390e`: no actionable findings through P2. The reviewer did not rerun tests. This was not autoreview or ClawSweeper.

English Control UI in Chromium, light theme, 840 × 760 emulated viewport. Before: `2237f16b7e27`; after: `ca0be9501acb`.

### Clean comparison

**Setup code request — before**

![After a code request fails, the button says Reload.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bdce4b86-0574-4430-af5a-eb1a8c19d407)

**Setup code request — after**

![After a code request fails, the button says Create setup code.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0f717aaf-ec8a-485e-b277-cf1e826469fb)

**Connection status check — before**

![A failed status check also offers Reload.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d36a997b-1b25-42a2-a35c-69076c231560)

**Connection status check — after**

![The status error offers Check connection status.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1f70b636-2255-4521-aa94-a240fa8e0011)

### Annotated comparison

prs.title: feat: let Learn from Memory imports continue where they stopped
prs.body:
Closes #205796

## What Problem This Solves

When **Knowledge → Scribes → Learn from Memory** stops partway through a large archive, the import has no saved position. Starting again goes through the selected files from the beginning, and the operator has no reliable count of which files finished.

## User Impact

- I added an optional **Save progress** checkbox to the import dialog. It is off by default.
- A saved import that stops with files pending shows **Needs attention**, the number of files imported, and **Continue**. Continue resumes in the same conversation with the pending files. **Start again…** stays available.
- Saved progress stays linked to the import when its start or Continue message is older than the latest 100 messages.
- The page shows **Done** only after it reads the complete checkpoint and verifies that every listed file is done. If it cannot read saved progress, **Retry** reads it again without starting an import.

## Why This Change Was Made

I used a Knowledge note to keep the file list. The import lists its selected files before reading them and marks each one done after saving its items. Continue uses that list, and the existing duplicate check covers items saved from a file that stopped partway through. The Scribes page looks for the opt-in message in older conversation history when necessary and reads every page of the checkpoint before deciding whether the import finished.

## Evidence

The existing live-flow screenshots show **Save progress** selected, an interrupted import at 3 of 8 files, and the completed import at 8 of 8 files.

![Import from Memory dialog with Save progress selected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/17eb60ba84c83f9be7f89e1dba1f2c604703846a/images/2026/11/8722f98f-826e-4ddd-b5d2-373ee04ba472.png)

![Interrupted import at 3 of 8 files with Continue available](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/17eb60ba84c83f9be7f89e1dba1f2c604703846a/images/2026/11/57b26d24-2ff8-4812-bfcd-13fae5b80c85.png)

![Completed import at 8 of 8 files](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/17eb60ba84c83f9be7f89e1dba1f2c604703846a/images/2026/11/f2fe4776-98db-4b96-b3d0-3630b5bee2b5.png)

I ran 76 focused tests on `75950d29f20`. They passed, including recovery after grouped Claude CLI tool results, long histories, multi-page checkpoints, and failed reads. These regressions fail with their fixes removed. Extension type checks, lint, formatting, and [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45939157580) passed on the same commit. I did not rerun the live model flow on that commit or test the 122-file archive from the issue.

prs.title: improve: make pull requests easier to read in the link reader
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves The link reader that opens pull requests, issues and commits beside the chat does not read like a finished surface. On a pull request with one failed check it opens the whole check list (85 rows on a typical OpenClaw PR) in its own scroll box, so the description starts about 450 px lower, below the first screen on a laptop-height window. The header spreads its facts across a grid, the section bar gives no sign of where you are, each changed file and each comment sits in its own bordered box, diffs have no line numbers, and authored images shrink to thumbnails. When checks arrive a second after the page, everything under them jumps. ## User Impact Opening a pull request shows what it is, whether CI is green, and what it says on the first screen, and nothing moves while the rest loads. - **Header:** state badge, repository reference and time on one line, then the title, the author with their picture, the branch, and the signed totals. It follows the hover preview's order, so the reader looks like that card opened up. - **Section bar:** Overview, Checks, Files and Discussion mark the section you are reading. The Checks tab carries a state dot from the first paint. - **Checks:** one summary with a fixed height. A ring and a legend count failed, in-progress, passed and skipped runs, and the failed runs are named beside the title. Expanding it, or selecting Checks, lists the runs grouped by state. A partial list says "Checks incomplete", leaves the ring open and counts the runs it could not show, instead of reading "Checks unavailable" above known results. - **Description and comments:** one reading scale for authored Markdown, framed full-width images with their description as caption, restyled tables, code, quotes, task lists and disclosures. - **Changed files:** one list with the file name first and its directory after it, signed totals, a status word for added, removed or renamed files, and a header that stays in view while its diff scrolls. Diffs have line numbers from their hunk headers; copying a diff still yields the patch text. - **Discussion:** a thread with authors, relative times, review location and collapsible diff context, not a stack of boxes. - **Loading:** the first-load skeleton has the document's geometry, the checks placeholder has the height of the loaded summary, and changed files reserve one row per expected file. ## Why This Change Was Made The first revision of this pull request kept the description on the first screen. Vyctor's review was that the reader still did not look like part of the product, so this revision rebuilds the document. Decisions worth a reviewer's attention: - **Nothing moves when late content arrives.** The first revision listed failed runs under the summary, which pushed the description down when checks loaded. The summary now has one height from loading to loaded: failed runs are named on its title line, long lines fade and never wrap, and the Checks tab shows a state dot, not a late count that would move the tabs after it. - **Counts come from the passive check items.** The host already grouped items by state for the open list; the legend is that grouping, collapsed. The source's own summary stays as the legend's tooltip and still speaks when there are no items. The GitHub summary now says "in progress" where it said "pending", matching the reader. - **The section bar is still one scrolling page.** Find-in-page, comment anchors and the lazy file load keep working; the bar reads the scroll position and reuses the product's tab look. - **GitHub plugin:** the overview now carries the author's picture, the same cached public avatar bytes the hover preview already sends. It loads beside the content reads with a 500 ms budget, so a slow avatar host cannot hold the document, and section requests never read it. It ships here because only the new header shows it. - **Authored emphasis tags:** bare ``, ``, ``, ``, ``, ``, `` and `
` in reader Markdown now render, without attributes and through the existing sanitizer. Review bots write `…`, which showed as literal tags. - **No contract change.** The reader document, the plugin SDK types and the Gateway protocol are untouched. Known limits: the relative date does not tick while the reader stays open. The GitHub plugin reads at most 100 check runs, so a pull request with more reports "Checks incomplete"; raising that bound is a separate change. Diff syntax highlighting is not part of this pull request. Size against the merge base: production TypeScript +995 −529, styles +1023 −340, tests +221 −34. The growth is the redesign's styles and the checks, files and thread components. Reader chunks are lazy: the paired performance comparison against `origin/main` reports chat boot JS −3 B, new-session boot JS −3 B, and no CSS asset change. ## Evidence Same reader panel in the Control UI shell, same document (openclaw/openclaw#203950 as returned by the GitHub plugin, with the check states from the original report: 1 failed, 9 in progress, 30 passed, 45 skipped; one synthetic review comment), dark theme, 795 px panel, mocked Gateway. Before is `origin/main` at `862c71e4cda9`; After is this branch. **Before** ![Before: a plain header with a facts grid, and one failed check opening all 85 checks above the description](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c296a9d-cd18-46bc-8f24-97ab138c7ce7) **After** ![After: a compact header with the author's picture and branch, a section bar, and a one-line checks summary above the description](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f9f8b2ef-5c42-4815-8ed1-37881c18f1c5) Changed files with one diff open: **Before** ![Before: each file in its own box with a native disclosure triangle and an unnumbered diff](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e609dc37-6c84-4f36-a8f4-2a020b93547a) **After** ![After: one file list with names first, signed totals and a numbered diff](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c440eae-ace4-4afe-8341-fecd0d7df7e9) Discussion: **Before** ![Before: comments as bordered boxes with link-colored timestamps and literal strong tags](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd546d33-8e0c-4b36-980d-c3daede2ca79) **After** ![After: comments as a thread with authors, relative times and a review location](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/69d8bb37-9d82-4e88-a63b-fd3a3618448a) Annotated: ![Before, annotated: the facts grid repeats the tabs and the open check list pushes the description down](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5bbc3057-4d76-49e6-a94b-77cfc426debe) ![After, annotated: one header, a section bar that follows the reading position, and a fixed-height checks summary](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f5a2218-f646-41dc-9c75-fc25bab05cbb) Layout stability: a `layout-shift` PerformanceObserver on the reader with a simulated Gateway, at 400, 820 and 1280 px, while the overview, checks (about 1.4 s later) and discussion arrive, recorded no shift inside the document for three documents (1 failure, 5 failures, 14 files with incomplete checks). The only entry is the panel's tab title, 0.0001 to 0.0002. The loading browser test now asserts that the description and the tabs keep their position through a failed check load, a retry, and the arrival of 85 checks with five failures. Real Gateway: the same observer against an isolated Gateway built from this branch, with the real GitHub plugin, opening openclaw/openclaw#203950 from a link in a chat reply at 1280, 820 and 400 px. No layout shift was recorded after the document's title rendered, in two runs; checks arrived 0.8 to 1.3 s after the title. The observer recorded 15 to 16 earlier entries per width (app boot and the panel opening), so it was recording. Limits: this used a local, uncommitted test and GitHub's live response, in which that pull request has only passed and skipped checks (48 and 52, one not shown). The failed and in-progress states were measured with the simulated Gateway only. ## What Problem This Solves

The real-Gateway browser-pairing CI fixture rebuilds the production UI after the job has already prepared and validated it. Two successful Blacksmith samples spent 23.08s and 24.29s on that extra build.

## User Impact

Less repeated work in the existing CI proof. No product behavior or test assertions change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consume the prebuilt-assets context already owned by the real-Gateway configuration. Ordinary local runs without that context retain the fixture's production build. The fixture still starts its own isolated Gateway and verifies withdrawal, offline cancellation, approval, reconnect, and approval-wins cancellation.

## Evidence

- Source inspection: the sampled fixture blob matches the inspected source before this change.
- Historical jobs: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45604476107/job/139172768023 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45360647583/job/138330652978.
- Local dependency-free syntax and whitespace checks passed.
- Isolated Boat / Node 24.22.1 syntax, oxfmt and focused oxlint checks passed. The first typecheck command used an unavailable direct binary; the corrected scoped repository typecheck passed.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed 52c50a016213a70b56a8c37c3fffa1c4b6a5897f..83e5baa0c0678c65b2d57d8441bcbe50a51b67ed: complete, no actionable findings, security cleared.
- Native real-browser proof passed on the unchanged head: the prebuilt configuration ran the existing pairing scenario with zero private UI builds; the ordinary standalone configuration ran it with one. Chromium and worker-generation cleanup passed.
- Both comparative warmups passed with the same one-to-zero build count. No accepted performance result: the initial comparison stopped at a harness cache-storage cap before measured pairs, and the resumed run was stopped because the remaining nonextendable lease could not fit all five pairs.
- Boat allocation: requested large tier; observed 8 CPUs, affinity 8, 16,375,780 KiB RAM. Qualified production preparation completed in 87.6s, excluded from comparison.
- The initial prebuilt setup correctly rejected wrapper-owned transport metadata as untracked source. After confirming every untracked entry belonged to the exact temporary transport directory, only that directory was excluded in the disposable checkout's local Git metadata; source status was clean and the unchanged native prebuilt gate passed.
- Performance acceptance remains open. No job-wide, billing, or measured invocation savings claimed. PR remains draft.

### Acceptance rule (recorded before comparative execution)

Run the existing browser-pairing real-Gateway scenario on one prepared, isolated Linux lease, serially, with the same production artifacts, runtime, worker cap, and fixture. Use one unmeasured warmup per variant, then compare the exact base fixture against the candidate in five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs with separate warm transform caches. Keep cold preparation separate from warm invocation timing.

Accept only if every invocation passes all existing assertions and cleanup, the redundant fixture UI build count falls from one to zero, median invocation wall time improves by at least 10%, and median CPU, p95 wall time, and peak RSS do not regress. Record hardware, all samples, medians/p95, and limitations. Separately run the unmodified native prebuilt configuration and the ordinary standalone fallback. Job-wide and billing savings remain unmeasured.

prs.title: improve: reduce Git metadata checks when opening a workspace
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening a managed workspace can make OpenClaw check four missing Git operation files for every linked worktree while it considers advancing the local default branch. In repositories with hundreds of linked worktrees, that work adds filesystem traffic and Gateway allocation, including when a dirty checkout will prevent the advance.

## User Impact

An eligible clean default checkout can advance with fewer metadata reads. A linked rebase or bisect that reserves the default branch still leaves the local tip in place and reports “Local default retained” while the new workspace can use the remote commit. A checkout already ineligible for advancement exits before examining reservations.

## Why This Change Was Made

Git checks whether another worktree owns a branch when switching to it. A fast-forward merge from the primary checkout updates its already-attached HEAD and does not check linked reservations. OpenClaw still needs to protect rebase, bisect, and rebase `--update-refs` reservations. After checking checkout eligibility, it lists each linked Git metadata directory once and reads reservation files only when the corresponding operation marker is present. The final symbolic HEAD check still runs before the merge.

## Evidence

The production Gateway on `2ab7b31a` served about 276 RPC/min during a 30-second allocation sample. The path join inside the reservation-file reader accounted for 11.16 MB of 1,997 MB sampled, the fourth-largest individual site. The reservation guard at the production SHA matches the benchmark parent. The profile does not contain the scan count or the managed-create denominator. Local evidence uses Git 2.56.0; the deployed Git version was requested from the lead.

Real Git rejected an ordinary switch and a rebase that explicitly selected `main` in a linked worktree. Git's supported duplicate-checkout override let the already-attached linked checkout start an interactive rebase or bisect of `main`. The exact fast-forward merge advanced the primary ref during each linked operation. It also advanced during a paused `--update-refs` rebase with an attached topic HEAD. The owner tests verify retention and warning for the linked operations and advancement during unrelated operations. [Git branch checks](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.56.0/branch.c#L881-L897) · [Rebase entry](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.56.0/builtin/rebase.c#L1696-L1740) · [Bisect state](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.56.0/builtin/bisect.c#L912-L967) · [Merge path](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.56.0/builtin/merge.c#L1656-L1692) · [HEAD update](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.56.0/builtin/merge.c#L480-L504)

The new dirty-checkout regression fails on baseline because the owner still starts the reservation scan. The candidate skips it and keeps the local tip. The worktree cohort test also covers 20 concurrent dirty creates sharing a single local-default decision.

<details>
<summary>500-worktree synthetic benchmark</summary>

Measured the real `baseFastForward` phase with 500 actual linked worktree registrations and a 62,000-file, 1.116 GB primary checkout on APFS. The remote is local. Five serial, interleaved A1/A2/B samples per scenario with a warmed base selection and a fresh Node process for each. A1 and A2 are identical source at `93ce03aada9fb8`. The wall and CPU columns show median and nearest-rank p95. One-minute host load ranged from 14.6 to 29.5 across the unprofiled runs.

| Per attempt | A1 | A2 | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Clean Node reservation filesystem requests | 2,002 | 2,002 | 502 |
| Clean V8 allocation, median MB | 39.97 | 37.64 | 31.60 |
| Clean Node CPU, median / p95 ms | 118.51 / 134.88 | 109.79 / 115.06 | 68.57 / 118.28 |
| Clean wall, median / p95 ms | 495.43 / 505.85 | 532.77 / 565.73 | 486.69 / 602.60 |
| Dirty Node reservation filesystem requests | 2,002 | 2,002 | 0 |
| Dirty V8 allocation, median MB | 37.61 | 40.13 | 12.90 |
| Dirty Node CPU, median / p95 ms | 111.39 / 228.27 | 93.15 / 106.74 | 26.15 / 31.93 |
| Dirty wall, median / p95 ms | 522.38 / 1,311.62 | 331.49 / 802.50 | 340.51 / 426.50 |

Acceptance required fewer calls and allocations for clean attempts, zero dirty scans, identical ref outcomes, and no median or p95 wall or Node CPU regression greater than 20%. Clean median allocation fell 16.0–20.9%, while clean p95 wall rose by 6.5–19.1%. Dirty median wall was within the large A/A spread. Node CPU includes libuv workers. Git child CPU and syscalls are outside the counters, and this is an APFS owner measurement rather than a production Gateway or Btrfs latency result. Separate CPU profiles are emitted by the harness.

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/worktree-fast-forward-measure.ts \
  --base 93ce03aada9fb82d3759316d75feb934c38d181c --output <new-scratch-directory>
```

</details>

Runtime code shrinks by 3 lines. Tests add 29 net lines. Rerunnable benchmark tooling adds 287 net lines, including its Knip entry.


Both focused suites passed, with 101 tests and one Windows-only test skipped on macOS. The full changed-file check found type and lint errors in the benchmark harness. Those passed on targeted recheck after correcting the instrumentation types and names. The runtime source hash matches the benchmark. The full check also found three unused exports reproduced on the exact parent. The update reports were introduced by [#205987](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205987), and the Doctor report by [#206247](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206247).

Codex autoreview was scoped-clean through P2 on the local diff against 93ce03aada9fb8, committed as `c0e689580ec1a315d1e5a05b100786252d30693d`.

prs.title: fix(ui): stop showing background processes as sidebar activity
prs.body:
## Problem

A session whose turn had ended but still had a background process running (a dev server, a watcher, a long build) kept a quieter spinning ring in the sidebar, stayed pinned past the quiet-row cap like an active run, and lit its catalog group's running dot. A leftover process is not the session working, so the sidebar read as busy when nothing was happening.

## Change

Background processes no longer count as sidebar activity:

- The leading ring on sidebar rows, rail shortcuts and catalog rows only shows for an active turn or running subagents. The quiet `--background` ring variant, its CSS and the `Background work running` label are removed.
- `rowDemandsVisibility` and `catalogSessionActivity` no longer treat `backgroundProcessCount` as activity, so background-only rows follow the normal quiet-row cap and no longer light running dots.
- The `unread` state description no longer depends on background processes.

Kept on purpose: a paused (yielded) subagent waiting on its own command still shows its parent as working (`childShowsParentWorking`), since that turn will resume. Processes stay visible where they belong: **Details → Processes** and the **Processes** panel. The Gateway's `backgroundProcessCount` row field is unchanged.

Docs: `docs/web/control-ui/sessions-and-sidebar.md` now describes the ring without the background variant.

## Evidence

Mocked Gateway Control UI E2E, dark theme, same fixture on both revisions: one running session, one session with `backgroundProcessCount: 1`, one idle session. Before = `af9c697714fb` (main), after = this branch.

prs.title: improve: reduce Codex shutdown overhead on busy Linux hosts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a Linux Gateway with thousands of processes, shutting down a Codex app-server that ran native commands can read all of procfs several times. Team's 30-second allocation profile sampled 26.3 MB across 11 Codex stdio transport stacks, including 10.9 MB in asynchronous reads and 3.9 MB in the bounded procfs reader.

## User Impact

Linux Codex cleanup spends less Gateway CPU and allocates less memory on busy hosts. The change applies automatically to existing deployments and preserves the cleanup and deadline contracts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the discovery scan before stopping the root, and discover any children forked before the stop took effect. A quiescence retry can inspect the known root alone while it is still running. Retry signals use the same PID, boot ID, start ticks, parent and group checks.

Use one deadline timer per snapshot and one 4 KiB scratch buffer for the kernel records. The reader keeps EOF detection, the byte cap, and descriptor cleanup even when a syscall returns after timeout. It still reads boot ID from procfs per observation.

Production +18 LOC, test +59 LOC, benchmark +74 LOC. The Linux root preflight adds 14 production lines to preserve the separate identity and topology checks. The reader adds four lines to grow the buffer only when a record exceeds its current capacity.

## Evidence

- Parent `93ce03aada9fb8`; Node 24.22.1 on Linux with 2,304 synthetic processes (at least 2,308 visible rows). Five A/A and five interleaved A/B pairs, 20 warm snapshots plus one cold snapshot per arm, with independent collected-object V8 heap sampling.
- The fixture had over 2,000 live rows per snapshot. The final-head repeat confirmed lower V8 allocation and warm CPU. Wall time stayed within the A/A variation.
- The native stdio client and Codex 0.172.0 completed two turns against a synthetic loopback provider. Procfs enumerations were 0 → 0 during registration, cold and reused-client turns, and graceful retirement. Retirement with a live native command took 3 → 3. Holding the first SIGSTOP for one retry took 4 → 3 scans and 9,272 → 6,958 stat opens. Both arms observed the child exit. The fixture uses synthetic workspace files and session metadata, with a sparse placeholder for the reported database size.
- The pending-stop regression failed on the parent and passed with the change. Tests also cover a process disappearing with ENOENT after enumeration, PID reuse with a different start tick, boot ID changes, and deadline/descriptor cleanup. The focused run passed 92 tests with 16 platform skips across eight files in 66.44 seconds. Codex autoreview was scoped-clean through P2.

| Warm metric per scan | A/A first | A/A second | Parent | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Wall median / p95, ms | 173.4 / 243.2 | 161.0 / 232.7 | 177.8 / 246.7 | 160.2 / 238.6 |
| Main CPU median / p95, ms | 85.7 / 118.7 | 82.4 / 110.3 | 89.5 / 115.0 | 77.2 / 108.4 |
| Total CPU median / p95, ms | 140.0 / 192.9 | 130.7 / 175.0 | 144.4 / 186.2 | 130.5 / 178.2 |
| Sampled V8 allocation median, bytes | 37,051,828 | 37,086,408 | 37,402,382 | 28,110,733 |

Sampled V8 bytes exclude Buffer backing stores. The final-head confirmation used five more interleaved rounds on a fresh fixture with the same process and measurement shape.

| Warm metric per scan | Baseline | A/A repeat | Final candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Wall median / p95, ms | 168.0 / 211.3 | 162.1 / 198.1 | 166.0 / 217.1 |
| Main CPU median / p95, ms | 85.0 / 100.5 | 82.9 / 98.1 | 79.5 / 99.1 |
| Total CPU median / p95, ms | 137.3 / 171.7 | 131.1 / 155.1 | 128.3 / 160.5 |
| Sampled V8 allocation median, bytes | 37,122,353 | 37,111,898 | 28,213,721 |

Allocation fell 24.0% on the final head. Warm median main CPU fell 6.4%. The 1.2% warm wall change was smaller than the 3.5% A/A change. Cold timings also varied widely. The evidence supports lower allocation and CPU per scan. The benchmark entrypoint is `scripts/perf/codex-procfs-snapshot-measure.ts`.

`pnpm check:changed` surfaced three unused exports reproduced in both Knip modes on the exact parent. Two Update exports lost their last outside consumers in #205987, and the Doctor type was exported without a consumer in #206247. The first patch also flagged parameter reassignment. The final patch passed the same targeted extension lint and the snapshot suite (39 passed, one platform skip).

prs.title: fix: make Knowledge annotations and file errors easier to use
prs.body:
Closes #205802

## What Problem This Solves

Knowledge calls that only link a claim or add evidence need an otherwise unused `annotations: {}`. A nested-field mistake gets an unhelpful rejection, while the compact hint hides the correct fields. File uploads also collapse missing-file and workspace-boundary failures into one error.

## User Impact

Entity-only and evidence-only annotations work without the empty wrapper. `entities` and `addEvidence` remain top-level siblings beside `annotations`; nested calls are rejected with guidance showing the correct shape. Both fields now appear in the 220-character compact input hint, within the unchanged 300-character budget.

File errors identify the authorized workspace and distinguish missing/unreadable files from alias failures. Existing and missing paths outside the workspace receive the same error. No migration or configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

I keep one accepted argument layout rather than silently normalizing nested payloads. The annotation owner uses an empty default without changing the request payload used for replay checks. Empty mutations still fail; revision/hash fences, unlinking, and existing explicit-wrapper calls are preserved.

The shared hint renderer keeps required arguments and their detail first. It adds shallow top-level optional fields only when all of them fit in the remaining budget. Nested optional fields and oversized root field sets retain the existing fallback. Feature-tool schema errors reuse that bounded hint, so rejection before the storage handler also explains the shape.

I export the existing `describeRootFileOpenFailure` helper through `file-access-runtime`. The attachment owner checks lexical containment before opening a file, then uses the helper only for in-workspace failures. Symbolic-link, hardlink, sandbox, and hash protections remain intact. Broader API naming is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Initial regressions: 3 failures on main `ce0e1b0ebd375`, covering wrapper-free annotations and attachment diagnostics.
- Follow-up regressions: 5 failures on `fb50a81`, covering compact hints and both the registered-tool and storage rejection paths.
- Final code: 87 local tests passed across 8 focused files (104 seconds), including tool-search metadata/validation and prompt-prefix stability. The registered production annotation tool rejects the nested call, then accepts the corrected call using the same request ID; vault readback confirms exactly one new revision.
- The real Knowledge schema renders both fields in 220/300 characters. The storage-path error is: `Invalid annotation input. Pass entities and addEvidence as top-level fields beside annotations, not inside it.` The registered tool rejects earlier with the schema error plus the bounded top-level input shape.
- Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, and `pnpm build` passed on the final source. Build time: 185 seconds. It emitted the same UI asset-budget warnings seen before this follow-up but exited successfully.
- I ran `pr-simplify` before pushing: the existing shallow-type renderer is reused, with no schema aliases, new state, or larger hint budget. Whole-PR net change: +42 production, +113 test, +20 documentation lines.
- Hosted review of `fb50a81` had no actionable findings. Local autoreview remains unavailable because its configured Codex installation cannot execute inside the read-only sandbox; the new head needs hosted re-review.
- Not checked: macOS/Windows runtime behavior or completed new-head CI/review. CI timings are pending.

## Verification

Real run on `ab2188c`, reported by the requester: isolated Gateway on a VM with a real model, OpenRouter Nemotron (free).

- Nested `entities` are refused with an error naming `entities` and a hint showing `entities`/`addEvidence` at the top level.
- Wrapper-free entity and evidence annotations are stored at revisions 2 and 3, confirmed by an independent readback.
- Missing-in-workspace, alias, and outside-workspace errors are correct; existing and missing outside paths give identical errors.
- All 49 focused tests pass.

Co-authored with @daniel-lxs.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-issue-205802-investigation-s06057aec)

## Worked on by

- @daniel-lxs

prs.title: fix: show the whole reply when you reopen a TUI session
prs.body:
Closes #200408 ## What Problem This Solves In `openclaw tui`, a reply longer than 8,000 characters is complete while it streams, but after you close and reopen the session it stops mid-sentence with `...(truncated)...`. The full reply is stored, yet the TUI gives no way to see the rest, so it looks as if the model stopped early or text was lost. ## User Impact User impact: reopening a TUI session (Gateway or `--local`) shows long replies in full again. If the full text cannot be shown, the preview stays and says why, instead of ending silently. ## Why This Change Was Made The Gateway caps text in `chat.history` to keep history pages small. The Control UI already loads capped rows in full through `chat.message.get` (#122207); the TUI took the capped text as it came. The TUI now does the same as the Control UI: after loading history, each assistant row marked `truncated: true` / `reason: "display-cap"` is replaced by the stored message, newest first, four reads at a time. History pages stay bounded, and there are no protocol or schema changes. When the full text cannot be shown, the preview is kept and its marker says why: - read failed, not found, or a Gateway without `chat.message.get`: `...(truncated; couldn't load the full reply. Reopen the session to try again)...` (same advice as the Control UI's "Couldn't load the full message. Try again.") - `chat.message.get` reports the stored reply as oversized (over its ~25 MB payload limit): `...(truncated; the full reply is too large to show here)...` Local mode (`openclaw tui --local`) had the same cap. Its history read moves from `embedded-backend.ts` into `src/tui/embedded-history-messages.ts`, unchanged, and full text is loaded after the existing budgets pick the rows (the 128 KiB per-message limit and the page limit), so loading full text never drops an older row from the page. The stored message is then read in-process with the same limits as the Gateway's `chat.message.get` handler, so both modes show the same reply. A reply over 128 KiB shows in full in both. As with Gateway clients, a page with loaded replies can end up over its byte budget. The first revision of this PR loaded local full text before those budgets. A reply over 128 KiB then became `[chat.history omitted: message too large]` instead of its preview, and expanded rows could push older rows off the page. This revision fixes both. Known limit, left as is: `chat.message.get` caps text at 1,000,000 characters, so in both modes a longer reply loads its first million characters, ending in the plain `...(truncated)...` marker. Command-line runs (`openclaw agent`) are not affected by any of this: they print the run result, not history. ## Evidence Live check, Windows 11, against a running 2026.11.5-beta.4 Gateway: the session from #200408 holds an 11,532-character reply that `chat.history` returns as 8,018 characters ending `...(truncated)...`. - Before (installed 2026.11.5-beta.4 TUI, session reopened): the reply stops mid-sentence at "forest ecology", followed by `...(truncated)...`. - After (this branch built from source, same session reopened): the whole reply is shown, ending with `THE END`. Before: After (Gateway): After (`--local`): live run of this branch, `openclaw tui --local --session agent:main:proof`, Windows 11. The run used throwaway `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, config and `OPENCLAW_WINDOWS_TASK_NAME`. The session holds two stored assistant replies, written with the repo's own transcript writer (`upsertSessionEntryCore` + `replaceTranscriptEvents`). An 8,000-character preview of either stops partway through paragraph 72. - 11,539 characters, ending `THE END`: after reopening, it shows in full (paragraphs 1–103 and `THE END`). - 150,078 characters, over the 128 KiB per-message limit: after reopening, it also shows in full (paragraphs 1–1,326 and its last line, `HUGE_REPLY_LAST_LINE`), as it does over the Gateway. The `src/tui/tui-pty-local.e2e.test.ts` harness times out on this Windows machine (its own existing cases too), so this was a manual run in a terminal. The retrieval-failure case can't be triggered live without corrupting storage; the unit tests below cover it.
Reopened TUI screen text (repeated middle paragraphs elided) ```text openclaw tui - local embedded - agent main - session proof session agent:main:proof Write the huge reply. Huge paragraph 1: the tide pool keeps its water between waves, and every stone holds a small world of its own. Huge paragraph 2: the tide pool keeps its water between waves, and every stone holds a small world of its own. [... paragraphs 3-1,324 elided ...] Huge paragraph 1325: the tide pool keeps its water between waves, and every stone holds a small world of its own. Huge paragraph 1326: the tide pool keeps its water between waves, and every stone holds a small world of its own. HUGE_REPLY_LAST_LINE Write the long reply. Long paragraph 1: the tide pool keeps its water between waves, and every stone holds a small world of its own. Long paragraph 2: the tide pool keeps its water between waves, and every stone holds a small world of its own. [... paragraphs 3-100 elided ...] Long paragraph 101: the tide pool keeps its water between waves, and every stone holds a small world of its own. Long paragraph 102: the tide pool keeps its water between waves, and every stone holds a small world of its own. Long paragraph 103: the tide pool keeps its water between waves, and every stone holds a small world of its own. THE END local ready | idle agent main | session proof | gpt-5.5 | deliver:off | tokens ?/200k ```
Focused tests: - `src/tui/gateway-chat.test.ts`: a capped row is replaced by the `chat.message.get` result; when the read reports unavailable, reports oversized, or is rejected, the preview is kept with the matching marker. - `src/tui/embedded-history-messages.test.ts` (new) runs the real history budgets with synthetic transcript rows: a capped reply shows its stored text; a 150,000-character stored reply shows in full; a reply the reader reports oversized, and a missing reply, keep their marked previews; loading a 30,000-character reply under a 40,000-byte page budget keeps the older 15,000-character row. The 150,000-character and page-budget cases fail when full text is loaded before the budgets (the order in the first revision) and pass here. - `gateway-chat.test.ts`, `embedded-backend.test.ts` and `embedded-history-messages.test.ts`: 172 passed. `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck, lint, format, line-cap and mock-export ratchets pass. The dead-export scan reports three exports in untouched files that are already on `main` (`approval-shared.ts`, `spawn-broker/host.ts`, `system-agent/operation-types.ts`).

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The roster lifecycle suite repeats the stale-client response scenario already exercised through the transport suite's correlated requests. Keeping both duplicates fixture setup and assertions for the same preview, pagination, and notification behavior.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. The transport suite remains the owner of stale-response coverage.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the duplicate lifecycle case and preserve its explicit refresh-completion wait in the existing replacement-client transport case. The keeper still checks that an old response cannot replace the current preview, request another page, or notify subscribers.

Production +0/-0; tests +3/-32 lines. One duplicate case is removed; the two affected suites retain 35 cases.

## Evidence

- Before the edit, all 36 cases passed on matching test, owner, and dependency inputs.
- Disabling the session-window current-scope check caused all three retained reconnect cases to fail for an unexpected third page request. Original production source was restored byte-for-byte.
- Independent preservation review caught the need to retain refresh settlement; the final diff includes it. Final local-range review reported no findings against base `d877e8007fbae09f1d4c94fe402df17d2b7c82a1` and head `20490c7a1aadba6ec65697e12c5af63d638c36b7`.
- Formatting, commit hooks, and whitespace checks passed.
- All 35 retained cases passed at the reviewed head. The repeated mutation failed all three reconnect rows for the intended extra-page request; production source was restored exactly.
- Targeted core lint and the selected UI typecheck graph passed.
- All removal-specific dead-code phases ran. Both unused-file scans and the script-export scan passed. Dependency and production/full-tree export scans report three inherited diagnostics: `readUpdateDatabaseEngineConfig`, `formatUpdateSnapshotCapacity`, and `DoctorContributionPending`. The same three reproduced with the full tracked working tree restored to exact base `d877e8007fbae09f1d4c94fe402df17d2b7c82a1`; they remain unresolved outside this test-only change.
- Normal PR CI is pending.

prs.title: test(ui): isolate agent deletion guards
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two agent-deletion tests could pass without reaching the guard they named. Replacing the client emptied its roster, so roster eligibility masked the client-identity check. System and missing-agent assertions used only one normal agent, so the last-agent check masked target eligibility.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. The tests now reject these deliberately introduced regressions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep a valid roster after replacing the client and verify the target is still eligible before resolving confirmation. Check system and missing targets with two normal agents, then retain the separate last-normal-agent assertion.

One test file changes: +8/-3 lines; production +0/-0. All 10 cases remain, with no new fixtures or cases.

## Evidence

- All 10 original cases passed. Three deliberate regressions also passed the original tests: omitting the post-confirmation client check, using an unfiltered roster for target membership, and omitting target membership.
- All 10 repaired cases passed on matching production and dependency inputs. The same three regressions now fail the repaired tests. Both test and production source were restored exactly after the controls.
- Independent source review is clear. Formatting, whitespace checks, normal commit hooks, and signing passed.
- Final pinned local-range review found no correctness or security findings.
- Native exact-head validation passed all 33 cases across deletion and agent-capability suites. Targeted core lint and the selected UI typecheck graph passed.
- Normal PR CI is pending.

prs.title: feat(apple): add Talk status chimes
prs.body: Related: #204311 ## What Problem This Solves In Talk on iPhone or Mac, people may have to look at the screen to know when a call is listening, ready for another reply, or ended. ## Why This Change Was Made Key points: - Three cues mark the moments a hands-free user cannot see: Talk first becomes ready (**Listening**), a call ends cleanly (**Call end**), and native speech recognition resumes after a completed reply (**Ready for reply**). - **Decision needed (ClawSweeper), quoted:** "Should the three Apple Talk chimes default on independently of an existing macOS Phase sounds opt-out?" **Author’s design (pending Apple Talk owner approval):** the three cues default on (voice use means not watching the screen), and an explicit Phase-sounds opt-out carries over to the chimes. When the `talk.chimes.*` keys are unset, a user who explicitly turned macOS **Phase sounds** off reads all three chimes off; a user who never set **Phase sounds** reads them on. A stored chime setting always wins, and reading never writes. The chimes replace Submarine and Bottle, Pop is removed because speech announces itself, and Tink stays under **Phase sounds**. - Owner decision, macOS phase sounds consolidated: the **Listening** and **Ready for reply** chimes replace the built-in Submarine (listening) and Bottle (listening after speaking) sounds. Pop (speaking) is removed because speech announces itself. Tink (thinking) stays under the existing **Phase sounds** setting (`talkPhaseSoundsEnabled`), which now covers only the thinking sound. The setting key and label are unchanged. No overlap workaround is needed. - Unchanged: realtime stays always-listening and plays no reply cue. Switching routes does not overwrite the saved preference. The microphone is gated around cue playback where it could feed the cue back into Talk. - Decision rules: the end cue plays on a clean user stop, including while thinking or speaking (push-to-talk is excluded). The reply cue follows the active route and plays only after the assistant's speech played to its end, including the incremental speech path, where a failed or interrupted segment now blocks the cue. Starting push-to-talk cancels the end cue's delayed audio-session cleanup so it cannot deactivate the new capture. The iOS realtime-to-native fallback now plays the "Ready for reply" chime. - Upgrade safety: the three new keys read as on when unset, except that an explicit macOS Phase-sounds opt-out is inherited as off; reading never writes. The rule lives in one shared function (`TalkChimePlayer.isEnabled`). iOS has no Phase-sounds setting, so it reads on when unset. ## User Impact Three independent, device-local **Status chimes** default on when unset (a macOS user who explicitly turned **Phase sounds** off keeps all three off): **Listening**, **Call end**, and **Ready for reply**. Each can be turned off separately. On macOS, Submarine, Bottle and Pop no longer play; Tink still plays under **Phase sounds**. ## Evidence ### Installed upgrade (physical iPhone) **Result:** All 16 existing app-written preferences survived the install-over unchanged. Both injected test preferences also survived. - **A:** Plain main `c44c610d32627fc2a5d3de483a52d51c3d771e43`, build 5, installed over build 4 in the separate debug test slot. - **B:** The same main plus #204362 at `c7ff2afe3ac9cd4f4ee18b2b1c3d205967dd528b` (merge `48f86e74be7`), build 6, installed over A in the same slot. There was no uninstall, and neither A nor B was launched. The raw diff between the build 4 readback and the after-A readback was empty (16 keys). After A, two test keys were injected. The full raw diff between that seeded readback and the after-B readback was also empty (18 keys), before redaction. | Preference | Origin | Before B (A after injection) | After B | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `gateway.autoconnect` | App-written | `true` | `true` | | `gateway.backgroundAlive.lastSuccessAtMs` | App-written | `` | `` | | `gateway.backgroundAlive.lastTrigger` | App-written | `` | `` | | `gateway.focusedChatSessionKey.v2.` | App-written | `` | `` | | `gateway.hasConnectedOnce` | App-written | `true` | `true` | | `gateway.lastDiscoveredStableID` | App-written | `` | `` | | `gateway.onboardingComplete` | App-written | `true` | `true` | | `node.displayName` | App-written | `'iPhone'` | `'iPhone'` | | `node.instanceId` | App-written | `` | `` | | `onboarding.completed` | App-written | `true` | `true` | | `onboarding.first_run_intro_seen` | App-written | `true` | `true` | | `onboarding.last_mode` | App-written | `` | `` | | `onboarding.last_success_time` | App-written | `` | `` | | `talk.enabled` | App-written | `false` | `false` | | `voiceWake.triggerWords` | App-written | `["openclaw", "claude", "computer"]` | `["openclaw", "claude", "computer"]` | | `watch.execApproval.bridge.state.v1` | App-written | `` | `` | | `talk.background.enabled` | Injected | `true` | `true` | | `talk.preferredInputDeviceID` | Injected | `` | `` | After B, `talk.chimes.start`, `talk.chimes.end`, and `talk.chimes.reply` were all absent. On iOS, [`TalkChimePlayer.isEnabled`](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/c7ff2afe3ac9cd4f4ee18b2b1c3d205967dd528b/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/TalkChimePlayer.swift#L7-L23) resolves absent keys to on without writing them. The defaults are inferred from the readback and source, not observed in a launch of build 6. **macOS opt-out:** No installed upgrade was run on macOS. The Kit unit test [`TalkChimeLifecycleTests.swift:95–111`](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/c7ff2afe3ac9cd4f4ee18b2b1c3d205967dd528b/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Tests/OpenClawKitTests/TalkChimeLifecycleTests.swift#L95-L111) checks that legacy `openclaw.talkPhaseSoundsEnabled=false` makes unset start and end cues read off, an explicit reply setting wins, and reading leaves the unset keys absent. ### Settings persistence (physical iPhone) On a physical iPhone running OC build 102515 (`c7ff2afe3ac`), all three `talk.chimes.*` preferences were absent at baseline. After turning **Call end** off in **This iPhone → Status chimes**, a device preference readback showed `talk.chimes.end = false`. The `talk.chimes.start` and `talk.chimes.reply` keys remained absent (default on). After force-quitting and relaunching, the native settings still showed **Listening on**, **Call end off**, and **Ready for reply on**. This checks persistence for the Call end switch on iOS, not audio playback with the switch off. Code at this head: [write preference](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/c7ff2afe3ac9cd4f4ee18b2b1c3d205967dd528b/apps/ios/Sources/Settings/DeviceSettings/IOSDeviceSettingsActions.swift#L70), [read for display](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/c7ff2afe3ac9cd4f4ee18b2b1c3d205967dd528b/apps/ios/Sources/Settings/DeviceSettings/IOSDeviceSettingsSnapshot.swift#L61), and [gate call-end playback](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/c7ff2afe3ac9cd4f4ee18b2b1c3d205967dd528b/apps/ios/Sources/Voice/TalkModeManager.swift#L900-L904) using the [shared preference reader](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/c7ff2afe3ac9cd4f4ee18b2b1c3d205967dd528b/apps/ios/Sources/Voice/TalkModeManager.swift#L161-L163). ### macOS (physical Mac) One Talk session on a physical Mac running build 102515 with this PR at `c7ff2afe3ac`. The recording contains the listening cue, two ready-for-reply cues, and the call-end cue. [Screen recording with audio](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/e8f2c26c1c9287454555a70e4542b41cb7e1a4bb/apple-chimes-204362/macos-102515/retake.mp4) (63 s). | Recorded cue | Time | Bundled asset | Normalized cross-correlation | |---|---:|---|---:| | Listening | 4.334 s | `chime_wake.caf` | 0.999590 | | Ready for reply | 23.384 s | `chime_follow.caf` | 0.999446 | | Ready for reply (second turn) | 44.270 s | `chime_follow.caf` | 0.999515 | | Call end | 46.317 s | `chime_bye.caf` | 0.999263 | ### Real iPhone: split STT/TTS turns with the follow-up (reply) chime (26 Nov 2026) > Review: *native turn-based reply playback*. The same physical iPhone and device build (OC 102513), with Talk in **STT/TTS** mode, did three consecutive spoken turns: "nine squared", "10 squared" and "11 squared". The screen recording was made on the phone with audio. Video: [ios-device-split-turn.mp4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/pr-evidence-apple-chimes-204362/apple-chimes-204362/ios-device-split-turn.mp4) (48 s). | Recorded sound | Time | Normalized cross-correlation | |---|---|---| | follow-up chime after the spoken reply "100" | 28.9 s | `chime_follow.caf` **0.91** (wake 0.64, bye 0.59) | | spoken replies "100" and "121" | 25.6 s, 41.9 s | none (TTS speech, not a cue) | | end chime after the call ends | 44.6 s | `chime_bye.caf` **0.77** (follow 0.63, wake 0.52) | The next question, "What's 11 squared", was spoken after the follow-up chime and was recognized correctly (). ### Physical iPhone retest: microphone readiness on `c7ff2afe3ac` (26 Nov 2026) On build OC 102514 (`a8a260ed0c8`), Talk failed to start with “No microphone audio.” The readiness check waited for the recognizer to report running, which on this device happened only after speech started. The current head waits for the first microphone buffer, not that recognizer state. A readiness timeout no longer fails Talk startup. On a physical iPhone running OC 102515 (`c7ff2afe3ac`) in STT/TTS mode, Talk started normally. The tester spoke immediately after the wake and follow-up cues. Both transcripts retained the opening “12345,” and Talk answered 10 and 12, respectively. The recording contains playback, not microphone speech. The speech markers show approximate post-cue positions, not measured microphone onsets. [Cropped screen recording with playback audio](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/d5836391357a3d8c00651f3514d7f7ecd288bb68/apple-chimes-204362/ios-102515/retest-small.mp4) (54 s). The wake (23.17 s), follow-up (38.66 s), and end (52.63 s) cue segments each matched their corresponding reference extracted from the earlier recording at 1.00 normalized cross-correlation (rounded). | After wake | After follow-up | |---|---| | | | On this head, 8/8 Kit chime tests and 56/56 iOS simulator TalkModeManager tests passed (proof job `talk-204362-c7ff-1126-r2`); lint was stubbed. The earlier delayed-capture regression failed on baseline `8acd5b4de2f` (wake and follow played without readiness events) and passed with the initial fix `542873c917d`. No independent local automated review was performed for that follow-up. Limits: one follow-up turn on the patched iPhone. ### Real iPhone: one Live Talk turn with audible chimes (26 Nov 2026) > Review: *audible native cue playback* and *real-device evidence*. This is a physical iPhone running a device build of this PR's code (OC 102513: main `b48d578d023` plus this PR at `8acd5b4de2f`). It shows one **Live (Realtime)** Talk turn against a real Gateway. The screen recording was made on the phone, with audio. Video: [ios-device-talk-turn.mp4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/pr-evidence-apple-chimes-204362/apple-chimes-204362/ios-device-talk-turn.mp4) (24 s). | Listening started | Reply received | |---|---| | | | Audio track of the recording: | Recorded sound | Time | Normalized cross-correlation with the bundled asset | |---|---|---| | when Listening (Realtime) appears | 2.6 s | `chime_wake.caf` **0.97** (follow 0.66, bye 0.26) | | after the call ends | 23.4 s, cut off when the recording stops | `chime_bye.caf` **0.71** (follow 0.61, wake 0.48) | There is no ready-for-reply chime in this recording, and none is expected. `TalkChimeLifecycle.resumedListening(isRealtime:)` plays the reply cue only for STT/TTS turns, never for Live. The model's spoken reply is also absent from the recording, because iOS screen recording didn't capture the Realtime voice stream. Only the app's own cue playback appears. Limits: this covers a Live turn only. A split STT/TTS turn, which is where the reply chime plays, wasn't recorded here. Proof job on head `8acd5b4de2f` (iOS 27.2 simulator and macOS test run), all steps passed: macOS app build, 8 OpenClawKit tests in 3 suites, macOS `TalkModeControllerPublishingTests` and `AppStateRemoteConfigTests`, and 80 iOS simulator tests. **Audio.** Waveform of the shipped chime assets laid out on the call timeline decided by the real `TalkChimeLifecycle` (markers: Listening 0.5 s, Ready for reply 4.0 s, Call end 7.5 s). Generated by `TalkChimeAudioProofTests`, which decodes `chime_wake.caf`, `chime_follow.caf` and `chime_bye.caf` and checks they carry audible samples (peaks 0.60, 0.34, 0.38): Audio file: [talk-chimes-call.wav](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35390557/talk-chimes-call.wav) (48 kHz mono, 9.4 s, the three chimes at those markers). Cue events, with asset SHA-256 hashes: ``` wake Listening 0.5 s 0.45 s peak 0.600 chime_wake.caf 808e0d89bd71... follow Ready for reply 4.0 s 0.45 s peak 0.339 chime_follow.caf 5b6f24fa22d9... bye Call end 7.5 s 0.92 s peak 0.380 chime_bye.caf dc0e69bf94cb... ``` **Cue lifecycle in the iOS app logic** (simulator test with the player stubbed; the microphone recovers after the reply): ``` TALK_CUE_TRACE cue wake | listening=true | cue follow | listening=true (microphone recovered after reply) | cue bye ``` **Settings** (the Control UI device section `talk-device-controls.tsx` rendered in headless Chromium with a mocked macOS native-device-settings snapshot; Status chimes shown with all three on): **Upgrade** (settings stored before the chimes existed; no `talk.chimes.*` keys). All passed: ``` ✔ settings stored by the previous stable release carry an explicit Phase sounds opt-out to the chimes (Phase sounds off -> start, end, reply all off; nothing written) ✔ settings stored by the previous stable release with Phase sounds unset keep the chimes on ✔ an explicit legacy opt-out carries over only to cue keys that were never stored (a stored cue choice wins; reading never writes) ✔ defaults saved before chimes existed read all three cues on ✔ an explicit stored choice survives and a mixed snapshot reads per key ``` iOS tests also cover: the fallback-route and end-chime behavior, push-to-talk taking over during the end cue keeping its audio session, and a single-line reply whose whole-reply playback fails not requesting the reply cue. Lint: the repo's pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1 in lint mode reports 0 files needing formatting on the touched Swift sources. Build lint phases were bypassed in the proof job. **Proof limits, stated plainly.** - The WAV and waveform are the shipped chime assets placed on the lifecycle timeline, not a tap of the app's live output: the player uses `AVAudioPlayer`, which cannot be tapped without changing production playback. - The cue trace uses a stubbed player: it shows cue order and microphone recovery, not audible output. - The Kit upgrade tests seed the old preference shape. The installed iPhone check above used a debug-to-debug update, not an App Store–signed build. - The settings screenshots are the Control UI component with a mocked snapshot, not the shipped native iOS or macOS settings screens. - The earlier hands-on iPhone check (main004 build 4, earphones) predates this head. AI-assisted. Reviews: Codex found macOS native fallback still reported the reply cue as unavailable (fixed). A separate cross-family review of the shared lifecycle, player, defaults and capture gate reported no blocking findings. Second review: Marvin (claude-opus-5-5), no blocking findings. **CI notes.** Run 45768644324 (head c7ff2afe3ac) had two red checks, neither in code this PR touches: - `ios-screenshots`: only `OpenClawSnapshotUITests.testReleaseChatScreenshot()` failed. The control and settings screenshot tests passed in the same job. prs.title: fix: finish healthy Git updates after an older verifier exits
prs.body:
Closes #204145

## What Problem This Solves

A Git install with the format-1 launcher can start a healthy new Gateway and migrate its database, then have the older updater fail because its verifier cannot read the newer schema. That verifier can remove the trial before its history write fails, leaving the original update abandoned and status recommending repair.

## User Impact

The serving Gateway retains the matching publication before listening, rechecks the selected running build at core readiness, and recovers the original run after the old updater exits, even if the trial file is already gone. Temporary canary boots leave the real trial armed. History errors do not block an authorized install or restart, or keep a healthy release eligible for rollback.

## Why This Change Was Made

I keep trial removal independent of history recovery and use the existing installation observer and history worker. A retained publication fingerprint links recovery to one original run. Captured evidence alone grants no authority: selected-root/build checks and the worker's driver, active-run, recovery and acknowledgment checks still apply. Replaced or invalid trials are rejected.

Recovery retries while this Gateway serves. If it restarts before recovery completes, the original history can remain unchanged even though the healthy release stays selected.

## Evidence

- Candidate: `26388beb83edd70e0e25aad01a46baba33514af8`, with main `407f889190cff3b147bb7ebc922e5817e47edf34` merged. This includes the landed 9.37 Git-update lease fix `3909540`; its eight files match that main revision.
- The regression in `src/gateway/server-startup-legacy-completion.test.ts` exercises a healthy schema-40 verifier removing the trial before refusing history. The original run succeeds with the matching build, the trial stays absent, status does not recommend repair, and no repair run is created. Its pre-fix run on `740c3ab` recorded `failed / abandoned` with empty outcome fields.
- The test uses real Gateway startup and HTTP readiness, real trial removal, migrated SQLite state, native child-process exit and the byte-identical d44 schema-admission function. It is not a full installed legacy-updater run.
- After `pr-simplify`, 89 unique focused tests passed across nine files, with one existing case-insensitive-volume test skipped. The initial run exposed the status-summary API removed by main; after migrating the test to the current summary API, the full startup regression passed. The other eight files' production inputs were unchanged.
- Format, lint and six type graphs passed. Unchanged-input import-cycle, Kysely, identity, database-worker and test-budget checks passed. AutoReview returned P0-only scoped-clean, not a broader-priority or hosted ClawSweeper verdict.
- The conflict resolution preserves main's required-plugin completion ordering and this change's independent legacy recovery. Shared Doctor inspection code replaces duplication.
- [CI run 45922581201](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45922581201) started on this exact head.
- Not independently rechecked for this body update: hosted CI outcome.

## Verification

I received real-update proof from @daniel-lxs on a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 arm64 VM (16 GiB): Git updates from v2026.9.37 and v2026.10.34 to `26388be` using `openclaw update --channel dev --yes --json` both exited 0 with status `ok` and `lastRun` succeeded. After each update, the Gateway served `26388be` (2026.11.10), was ready, and returned RPC health true. The workspace hash, session, verified transcript and disabled 12-hour cron job were identical before and after. Doctor inspection exit 1 was advisory, matching main. The VM was deleted afterward.

Contributor: @daniel-lxs

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @daniel-lxs](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-t_scdvyj)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/e33ad202-0f23-40fa-beb2-7329f01ee7e0)

prs.title: fix: show each temporary model switch once in chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When several commands or turns use the same temporary model, the Control UI transcript repeats the model switch between them. Five identical notices can make four commands look like five separate model changes.

## User Impact

Chat now shows one quiet line naming the temporary model. If a reason was recorded, expand the line to read it. The commands and replies stay visible, and chat shows another line if it switches to a different model or returns to the selected one.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcript already records each fallback. Its display now follows model transitions rather than printing every receipt, and keeps the activity boundaries that separate command rows. Loading an earlier page moves the notice to the first occurrence in the loaded history. The existing model-name lookup is shared with manual selections; there is no new store or change to model selection, routing, provider retries or stored events.

## Evidence

In an isolated Chromium test of the Control UI with synthetic Gateway history, five repeated notices became one. All four commands and the final reply remained visible. The reason opened with Enter and the single notice survived reload. Focused tests also covered restoration, a different fallback, older-page loading and independent sessions. This exercises presentation, not a live provider outage. The focused UI type, lint and translation checks passed. Local autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issues in the diff.

prs.title: fix(update): bound release CLI Gateway waits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A short `openclaw update --timeout` can enter a fixed 30-second Gateway request, a fixed 10-second status request, or a full two-second polling sleep. Replacement-Gateway capability consent can also reuse an earlier allowance.

## User Impact

Gateway dispatch, observation, restart requests and consent retries share one client deadline. Expiry prevents further requests and polling while the RPC owner joins cleanup. Accepted server work, captured authentication and published trials retain their existing owners. Unconfirmed consent/restart outcomes include status guidance.

No config, schema or protocol changes. This repairs client Gateway waiting; it does not establish universal preparation wall-clock enforcement.

## Why This Change Was Made

The release CLI owns this budget. One private wrapper reuses the existing absolute-deadline scheduler and Gateway cancellation contract, checks synchronously before dispatch, and caps waits. It replaces the independent fixed wait allowances and clamps polling sleeps. Successful responses captured before cleanup remain valid. Omitted server timeouts stay omitted, and the canonical summary renderer from [PR #205987](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205987) is preserved.

Production: +117/-55 (**+62**), implementing the existing cancellation and synchronous-dispatch contract. Tests: +491/-97 (**+394**), retaining all 47 cases with no test-budget allocation. Docs: +7.

## Evidence

- Final head `a7ec7947c0a08becaf0f576f7fc7a2b29c76e3c2`: [47/47 CLI tests passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45934424111/job/140294871008), including seven actual-client/WebSocket cases covering acknowledgement, status, polling, consent and captured-auth reuse. [Ratchets passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45934424111/job/140294870808): **+394 / allowance 400 / credit 0**. [The repaired lint shard passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45934424111/job/140295892219). [Full current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45934424111) passed: **38 jobs succeeded, 26 skipped, zero failures**. Security Review also passed.
- The clock-sensitive fixture passed all 47 tests locally on Node 26.7 and pinned OpenClaw Bun 1.4.4 at prior test head `2fd1cb3`. Removing only the production polling clamp fails the exact-deadline promise-state assertion on both runtime routes. The final commit only renames a shadowed argument and gives the Promise executor a block body; targeted syntax lint and the polling regression passed again before push. Formatting, signed commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed.
- [Unfixed acknowledgement execution](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45919178457/job/140246041582) supplies the qualified deadline comparison. Earlier status/poll fixture failures are not claimed as product RED.
- [Full build and Docker survivor proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45926867740/job/140270695359) passed at prior head `b4a3642`: declarations, package integrity, healthy committed activation, intentional-crash rollback, migration proof and joined cleanup. Production/build inputs are unchanged since that head; subsequent commits change tests only. The fixture asserts the packed commit matches its selected Git HEAD. This is Linux container proof with a disposable migration.
- [Exact-head source review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206252#issuecomment-7206839732) passed with no findings or before-merge requests.

The installed-CLI short-timeout run against a delayed Gateway was not performed: this proof route had no qualified disposable installed fixture for that scenario. Native-service/latest-stable upgrade matrices were not run. The wire cases cover the changed RPC boundary; container lifecycle proof does not replace those omitted scenarios.

Separate follow-ups: preserve acknowledged run IDs when observation expires; preparation/delegation execution budgets; investigate intermittent native-copy fixtures (runtime cause unproven); native PR cache-collection cost.

prs.title: fix: show the first message when session naming fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When automatic naming fails, a session can end up with a random nickname or show its checkout instead of the conversation. If the first message is already available, it can also briefly replace the loading state before the generated name arrives.

## User Impact

During initial naming the header keeps its loading bar and the sidebar reserves the title line. A generated name appears directly; if naming fails, a short excerpt of the first message appears instead. Later attempts keep the excerpt visible until a generated title is available. Naming does not change activity order. A textless session keeps its checkout or “New session”; neither the excerpt nor an eventual rename changes its branch.

## Why This Change Was Made

For dashboard sessions, the naming owner records that a fallback is available, not the message or a made-up name. The roster reads the excerpt from the transcript for failed sessions; the existing branch-naming path still uses a real title or its own two-word fallback. The header menu first appears next to the settled title rather than moving from a provisional position. Existing explicit and saved names are unchanged. Native iOS and Android session keys retain their saved two-word fallback because the shipped apps do not display derived titles.

## Evidence

Same open conversation, 1280 px Chromium, cropped to the title and adjacent sidebar rows. Synthetic Gateway responses hold the title request until each state can be observed.

**Before — excerpt and menu visible during naming:**

![Excerpt appears before the generated title](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6cf31eb4-2cb5-45d4-8875-33433895122a)

**After — naming in progress:**

![Header loading bar, hidden menu, sidebar title space reserved](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22a0a6b6-d031-42e3-9e57-4bdc2a49e841)

**Annotated comparison — the sidebar row and header during initial naming:**

![Before: premature excerpt and menu outlined](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6577c74b-e9ca-4957-a7e5-3ad41fd758c2)

![After: reserved title space outlined](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1024dad7-e3d5-40f8-99ee-c6a532216014)

**After — naming failed:**

![Excerpt and menu appear; the neighboring row stays in place](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4df82b50-cb67-4b40-a97c-450a03249ba6)

The browser regression exercises initial success and failure, followed by recovery, and measures unchanged sidebar row and link bounds. The desktop menu waits for the settled title. A later genuine rename keeps the menu beside its text.

Chromium against the built Control UI and an isolated real Gateway (`d5c987d2a96c`), with a controlled title provider: sampled every animation frame from Start session through navigation. No frame showed “New session” or the message excerpt while initial naming was held. After the provider failed, both the header and sidebar showed the first message; they kept it during retry and then displayed “Release checklist”. This exercised the real transport and session store, not a failure at an external model service.

The native transport regression failed with no saved name before the compatibility fix and passes for both iOS and Android session keys. Local autoreview covered `1da4ec2b1537..885f79747e34` at P0/P1 and reported no actionable findings at those priorities.

prs.title: fix: report Chromium versions in external browser benchmarks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The lightweight browser benchmark left `engineVersion` blank whenever it attached to an externally managed Chromium instance. That made it harder to tell which browser produced a result or compare it with a native run.

## User Impact

External Chromium runs over HTTP or WebSocket now report the version advertised by the browser when available. The JSON shape, timing and memory definitions, native runs, and other engines are unchanged. The reported version is not binary provenance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the guarded CDP diagnostic and the profile’s existing control policy after the measured work. This adds no discovery logic or extra connection before the first measured attachment. If the diagnostic cannot identify the version, the field remains `null`.

## Evidence

- Ran the documented benchmark CLI against a dedicated sandboxed Chromium headless shell. Both HTTP discovery and direct WebSocket runs completed the local form and PNG checks. On base `93ce03aada9f`, both reported `null`; on `679804ea54a4`, both reported `HeadlessChrome/159.0.8154.6`, matching Chromium’s `/json/version`. External startup remained `null` and memory sample count remained zero.
- The new opt-in live regression runs the actual benchmark and checks its saved JSON against the endpoint’s advertised version. It failed at the version assertion before the fix and passed for both transports after it.
- Focused typecheck, extension lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Simplification kept discovery and policy logic in the existing owners: +17 production lines, +55 test and fixture lines.
- Local autoreview could not start because the isolated temporary directory was inside the checkout. No local independent review is claimed.
