Related: #205848. Shared-contract proposal: #205845.

## What Problem This Solves

Code/configuration dictation needs exact symbols, case, and whitespace. Prose insertion can trim meaningful whitespace or reinterpret command-looking drafts, while symbol words need explicit scope before becoming punctuation.

**Remain draft; keep #205848 open.** The merged head passed the paired UI startup budgets and exercised exact review and native undo in a built UI. The [placement and ownership decision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205845) is still open.

## User Impact

Users can opt into English (en-US) Prose, Literal, or Developer modes with plain-code, JSON, TypeScript, or Python fragment profiles. Literal/Developer captures stop for exact preview, diagnostics, alternatives, character inspection, original recovery, preview undo, copying, or unsent insertion. Bytes already altered by recognition cannot be recovered.

The disabled, closed disclosure does not request the optional engine/profile/refinement/owner/target/panel implementation or review stylesheet. Opening it or restoring settings that require review loads them. Capture before readiness is declined before microphone/provider preparation; retry after loading. Load failure never falls through to raw insertion. Closing settings retains unfinished profile JSON and exports.

Insertion remains unsent, rejects stale destinations, and supports real native textarea undo. Unavailable editing APIs, CR/CRLF, and replacements leaving a nonempty wholly whitespace-only draft remain copy-only because existing owners cannot preserve those bytes. 

Browser/Gateway-scoped profiles are bounded data, excluded from server appearance sync. Authored JSON survives disable/re-enable and failed imports; retained future settings can be exported. This feature persists no dictated original/preview. The tested upgrade preserves existing preferences/navigation/exact drafts. **Old v2026.11.10 UI startup drops the new profile envelope**, even without manual preference changes. Disable/re-enable is the supported profile-preserving rollback; export profiles before binary downgrade. No second store or downgrade shim was added.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explicit deterministic scopes distinguish commands from prose. A versioned profile supplies symbol/spelling/casing/spacing rules; the planner emits bounded exact edits, diagnostics, and protected ranges. Composition validates capture/generation/transcript/profile identity and UTF-16 ranges, with explicit offset conversion and grapheme checks.

Existing capture/session/FIFO owners retain microphone settlement and ordered delivery. Profile/destination admission stays synchronous before microphone work. The existing chat loading boundary defers optional code without another capture queue or authority. Exact insertion retains current input/history ownership and stale, permission, cancellation, and representability checks. Optional prose refinement sees only unprotected text; no M01–M05 model/context/vocabulary stage is enabled.

### Shared ownership and scope decisions

[M11 now has an actual draft implementation, #205973](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205973), observed at `7dab77ee268617d70ab5f035bb7864cc278aa327`. It remains open, draft, unmerged, and unaccepted as a shared contract. Its finality, target/context, policy/result states, and 32 KiB/256-edit bounds differ from M08's private 128 KiB/64-edit boundary. Its [unresolved final-drain P2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205973#issuecomment-7193928672) concerns a 2,500 ms review deadline versus the relay's 5,000 ms drain; this repair does not adopt that policy or coordinator.

[M07 draft](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/pull/2) is a design reference only. M11 `authorizedEdits` integration remains a proposal; #205845 still needs human core/plugin, scope, profile/refinement ownership, and lifecycle decisions.

The full PR has **2,229 net test lines**: 400 normal + [1,829 allocated][test-allocation]; follow-up +532. All seven prior mounted capture cases retain their assertions in the focused review file. No dependency, second capture owner, public SDK, performance-baseline increase, or budget suppression. Final source/diff inventory: 25 follow-up files, +1,118/−406; full PR 49 files, +6,184/−289.

GitHub reports the draft mergeable, not ready to land. The resolution retains main’s background recording and explicit mouse/keyboard Stop, and keeps syntax capture admission synchronous before media setup.

- **Local checks on the published source tree:** 175 focused tests across eight files, three bundled Chromium scenarios with a mocked Gateway, UI typecheck, i18n verification, and focused lint/format passed. The scoped static review found no P0/P1 issue in the merge resolution.

The [upstream checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205892/checks) include PR metadata/governance and security reporting, not a completed candidate build/test run. No OpenClaw-hosted exact-head build, test, or real-Gateway proof is claimed.

The [placement and ownership decision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205845) stays open.

### Verified on `adcf312b6`

The syntax owner, grammar, review copy, and panel load only when needed. Chat reuses existing form styles rather than shipping a syntax stylesheet. Stopped-review bookkeeping stays in the lazy FIFO owner, and the microphone canvas code loads with voice activity. Capture admission still makes its decision synchronously, before opening the microphone or asking the Gateway for a session.

- **Paired upstream budget check:** Regenerated `ui/config/control-ui-boot-modules.json` with `pnpm ui:boot-manifest:gen`. `pnpm ui:check-performance:base 5ef69f167d2f500b4030dc581c06f1266accf38e` built both revisions with the same toolchain and exited 0. No thresholds changed.

The inherited 21st JS request did not increase; the paired check accepts that unchanged count. The independently tested UI file contents match this published tree.

- **Focused checks:** 170 tests passed across eight UI Vitest files. The three bundled Chromium scenarios passed: disabled startup excludes the optional code and review copy; reviewed Stop/Insert restores the prior draft with native undo; capture is refused without microphone or Gateway session setup while the required runtime is held, and succeeds on retry. UI typecheck, focused lint, formatting, and i18n verification passed. Independent local Auto Review found no P0 in the follow-up delta from `922c63de`.
- **Released data → built UI:** OpenClaw `2026.11.10` (`6ea542f`) saved an unsent draft and Light appearance in an isolated Gateway and Chromium profile. The new built UI on the current Gateway loaded the same draft and preference at the same origin; an additional draft edit survived reload.
- **Gateway and provider:** Chromium 158 fake-media capture with a prerecorded, synthesized WAV went through `getUserMedia`, the real Gateway and its file-transcription path, and local Vosk with a bounded English fixture vocabulary. Stop opened the exact `hello_world` preview without touching the draft. Preview Undo restored the original. A second capture inserted only `hello_world`; native Ctrl+Z restored the previous textarea, and no message was sent. The cold visit and warm reload with review disabled requested none of the syntax-owner, grammar, review-copy, or panel code; opening the disclosure loaded it. No separate syntax stylesheet was requested.
- **Not run for this follow-up:** physical microphone, cloud transcription provider, non-Chromium browser, assistive-technology pass, installer/downgrade, and the full repository test suite. The maintainer placement decision in #205845 remains open, and this PR remains draft.

### Response to ClawSweeper

The [hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205892#issuecomment-7189577635) covers **e554**, not this follow-up. No review-request comment was posted under the author's no-comments instruction. A push or body update is not represented as a new hosted review or approval.

- **Lazy-loading P2:** [pane state][capture-state], [capture admission][capture-options], and [lazy slot][slot] now defer runtime/panel/styles. Final browser requests exclude all optional implementation groups and review CSS until use. Holding required runtime yields zero microphone acquisitions and transcription sessions; retry reaches review. The canonical manifest was regenerated. Four absolute asset overages still fail independently.
- **Stop → exact review → insert → undo:** [maintained browser regressions][browser-tests] pass **3/3 on final assets in 17.55 s**. Real Chromium exercises the built UI with synthetic Gateway/media fixtures. Baseline e554 fails the intended disabled-load and native-undo assertions. Real configured Gateway/provider/physical microphone qualification and inline PR visuals remain open.
- **Latest-stable data compatibility:** actual published v2026.11.10 authors preferences and an IndexedDB draft, then the same origin/context loads final assets. Upgrade/disable/re-enable/downgrade observation passes **1/1 in 18.36 s** (15.434 s test), without page/programming errors. [Maintained regressions][compat-tests] cover the stable-produced shape. This is released-UI/storage proof, not a full installer/Gateway upgrade; old startup's profile loss remains explicit.

### Regressions demonstrated before and after repair

- **Disabled boot:** baseline requests contain optional implementation and review CSS; final requests exclude them until disclosure. The manifest supports, but does not substitute for, actual requests.
- **Native undo:** baseline keyboard undo leaves `prefix: customer_account_id`; final unsent insertion undoes to `prefix: `. The target uses native `execCommand("insertText")` within the exact-insertion scope after focus and cancelable `beforeinput` rechecks. The jsdom helper models editing only; Chromium supplies real history proof.
- **Retained owner/remount:** the mounted test first fails on missing visible review. Requesting the slot when the retained owner returns a review receipt fixes it without reopening settings.
- **Disclosure retention:** the mounted test first fails on empty unfinished JSON after reopening. Retaining the settings subtree preserves import/export text while native `details` controls visibility.

Independent AI source review found the disclosure regression, re-reviewed its correction, and found no outstanding actionable source defect in its snapshot. Both mounted regressions pass in the final 102-test run. This does not supply hosted ClawSweeper approval, human design acceptance, or passing performance budgets.

### Actual released-UI compatibility and visual evidence

The unchanged official [v2026.11.10 UI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.11.10), published 2026-11-25T05:42:47Z at source `6ea542fd97e2876aa4c871ccc494ed5419a03c5c`, comes from an integrity-verified package; UI index SHA-256 `35c5b6a47a488e8cd109dabe8115a3da0246609678a5eb3c698fe8bb178bbc74`.

Visible stable controls author Dark mode, 125% text, modifier+Enter, and a draft containing boundary spaces, a tab, Arabic, a decomposed accent, and an emoji. Its real writers persist preferences/navigation and IndexedDB draft, and stable reload restores them before upgrading. Final assets preserve them, then a UI-imported `ticket → CASE_007` profile retains its authored JSON string through disable/reload/re-enable; export normalizes formatting but preserves validated data. Synthetic Gateway/account/session responses are explicit. The fixture blocks service workers and retains one open browser context: full installer/Gateway upgrade, service-worker migration, persistent-profile restart, real provider, and physical microphone remain unqualified.

The canonical screenshot helper retained sanitized baseline/final UI frames for disabled startup, settings, review, unsent insertion, native undo, pending runtime, retry review, and released-UI compatibility stages. ### Deterministic component benchmark — historical, unchanged engine

The November 26 e554-era [benchmark][benchmark] used a shared AMD EPYC 9V74/nine-logical-CPU Linux host, Node 24.22.3/V8 13.6/ICU 78.3: 1,000 tokens, 256 mappings/9,713-byte profile, 4,999-byte input, 995-byte independent output, 20 warmups, 200 warm samples, and 20 fresh processes.

| Component | Samples | Median | p95 | Maximum |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Warm grammar + composition | 200 | 3.69 ms | 7.48 ms | 62.13 ms |
| Fresh-process first grammar + composition | 20 | 31.68 ms | 84.14 ms | 188.32 ms |

The 50 ms p95 target passed warm and failed cold. Canonical browser source is linked above; scoped configs, released-UI proof, red/green logs, and resource limits remain in the handoff.

The browser smoke test used prerecorded audio with real Gateway/local Vosk; physical-microphone, cloud-provider, and broader client/assistive behavior were not qualified. Feature placement, browser-profile ownership, and rollback expectations remain undecided in #205845. No merge or issue closure is requested.

prs.title: fix: hide desktop Details when there is nothing to show
prs.body:
**Wide desktop — the first detail opens beside the conversation.**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8de3706d-b1aa-4e8d-8d99-880e82ac4acd

**Narrow desktop — the button appears without moving the conversation. Select it to open the overlay.**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1f1a7a1a-13cf-4ecb-b5dd-87b4612a07f0

## What Problem This Solves

Desktop conversations show a Details button even when there is nothing to inspect. On a wide screen, the empty column takes space from the conversation just to say that it has no details.

## User Impact

The button and column stay out of the way until there is something to show. When the last detail goes away, both disappear. The mobile Details sheet is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Desktop now uses the sections that actually have content, including actionable errors, to decide whether to show Details. Existing docking and dismissal rules still apply. On wide screens, the chat recenters when the column opens; this is expected layout behavior.

## Evidence

Both videos show the real Control UI in Chromium with synthetic Gateway data. They show the same progress item arriving, updating in place, and being removed; the narrow recording also shows the click that opens the overlay.

Empty conversation, same viewport, theme and fixture. Before: main at `864efbb52a9e`. After: `83fe96efdb77`.

### Clean comparison

**Before**

![Before: the empty Details column beside the chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e91726ab-2e09-4ac9-8ee9-65f6872e5a41)

**After**

![After: the same chat without the Details button or column](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f43c77e-62e3-4957-b511-e8a2f183d91d)

### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![Before: Details button highlighted above the empty column](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed74c9e7-c009-473a-b068-0f54a96934b0)

**After**

![After: the same header position with no Details control](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d269f4b-1f60-46fb-a8cc-9c121044a3bf)

On this commit, Chromium and WebKit sampled 7,623 frames across 216 arrival, update and removal transitions. No unexpected layout reversal, flashing control, lost composer focus, or lost draft text was observed. Keyboard focus also returns to the composer if the Details control disappears while focused. These are browser-side checks, not a live Gateway test.

One related scroll check is intermittent: while a long run grows with a PR in Details, the measured gap below its last row was 29 px in both a grouped run and a standalone run on this commit (expected at most 1 px). The same scenario passed in the earlier integration run. This draft does not claim that scroll issue is fixed.

## What Problem This Solves

People who already use the OpenCode Browse extension can connect it to OpenClaw, but the browser docs don't show how. It is easy to look for a browser profile when Browse belongs in the MCP registry.

## User Impact

The docs show how to set up Browse under the Gateway's OS account, pair a dedicated Chrome profile, register it with MCP, verify it in an agent chat, and disconnect it. Browse can act with the paired profile's site logins; OpenClaw browser profile settings do not apply. There is no runtime or default change.

## Why This Change Was Made

A registry recipe and a browser-docs link use the existing MCP tool controls and the extension's existing pairing flow. No new driver, plugin, dependency, or configuration field is needed.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` and both changed files' formatting checks passed. The anchor audit checked 20,268 links and matched the same 11 unrelated failures on the unchanged base. The published tree matches the reviewed docs change.
- In loopback-only Linux containers, OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (`2ab7b31`) discovered all three tools from Browse 0.1.5, and applying the registry include filter removed `execute` from probe output. Browse paired with a disposable Chrome for Testing 156.0.8078.4 profile.
- Across four guided turns in one embedded OpenClaw agent session, local Qwen3 called Browse MCP to check pairing, open the synthetic page, snapshot and submit its form, and close the tab. Gateway history showed the rendered `Saved: fixture-name` result and successful close; the fixture counted exactly one POST. The initial one-turn attempt did not submit because the model added a `tab` key to the new-tab call. No signed-in profile, remote setup, or other platform was tested.

Requested by @vincentkoc.

prs.title: fix: recover a completed Codex reply after a brief disconnect
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

After a Codex WebSocket disconnect, chat can report a failure even though the native parent saved its answer. A worker result can also wake the parent twice, or disappear when the same worker finishes another task. If the parent is idle, the Gateway can declare shutdown safe before it has delivered the result.

## User impact

The Codex plugin recovers completed replies after brief connection loss. It leaves a paused goal paused, respects Stop, and never resubmits work or executes tools from history. If an acknowledged follow-up on the same worker is still running, the plugin watches for its result. Failed or ambiguous work can still require explicit recovery.

## How it works

- On abnormal socket closure, recheck the current session, binding, runtime and turn. Read the latest parent turn at most twice within ten seconds. A proven foreground wait can acknowledge an already completed first child without a second wake.
- When reusing a worker, distinguish the previous assignment from the accepted successor. Release an unused input reference once that exact task succeeds. Keep the separate reference for result delivery.
- When the parent has already detached, keep the accepted worker receipt through cleanup and attempt a bounded history read on the original endpoint. Require the latest completed successor of that child, current delivery authority and an unconsumed receipt. Use the existing per-turn delivery claim. Other workers keep their receipts.
- If the latest turn is the exact accepted successor and is in progress, observe it on the read-only connection. An idle or unloaded notification for that worker triggers a fresh read. A system error clears the running status without triggering an immediate read. After five quiet minutes, check the thread’s status without loading its turns. Each read has a ten-second deadline. A live parent that takes back the same active assignment takes precedence.

Use verified TLS or a trusted isolated endpoint. A bearer token alone cannot authenticate the server. The changes stay inside the Codex plugin.

## Evidence

### Repeated worker tasks at `e56ce1d9`

OpenClaw `3ae62ae0` recovered one follow-up but missed a later one after parent registration was pruned. Codex’s latest-turn summary included a cursor to older history. The fix retains IDs for up to 256 settled direct worker assignments in the same monitor and requires an exact match with the newest validated successful turn before inferring a predecessor from paged history.

I ran a real Gateway and Codex 0.164.0 with scripted answers on Linux. Both builds included the two proposals and upstream pin listed below. Only the worker input preparation code differed. I paused the parent on the fourth reuse and cut its loopback connection. The test held every new connection until a separate history read confirmed the worker’s fifth task had finished.

| Check | `3ae62ae0` | `e56ce1d9` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parent received the fifth answer while paused | No receipt within 45 s of releasing the answer | One receipt naming the exact turn |
| After one explicit goal Resume | Skipped because the receipt was missing | Two more tasks on the same worker, one goal completion |

The successful run recorded seven worker turns, six distinct follow-up receipts and zero pending inputs. The earlier build’s later outcome is unknown.

The test-only change failed three cases before the fix. The three affected suites passed 88/88 in 172.75 seconds with the fix and cached compiler output. A different latest turn still failed to qualify. Lint and formatting passed. A fresh monitor or an evicted record cannot infer a predecessor from multiple turns.

### Worker acknowledgment after reconnect

Both builds used upstream main `398c8db2` with #193024 at `a4e8d899` and #206231 at `b917e9cb`. Only one included the changes from this PR at `3ae62ae0`. The test used a real Gateway and Codex 0.164.0 over loopback WSS, cached older dependencies, and scripted inference.

The same worker handled two successive tasks, with its second answer held until the foreground turn settled.

- Both builds completed active goals exactly once, with and without a socket drop.
- When the parent was deliberately paused before disconnect, the worker completed both tasks in each run. Both builds reconnected. The PR delivered exactly one acknowledgment identifying the second answer's exact turn, 1.532 seconds after the scripted answer. The parent remained paused.
- The control failed the acknowledgment check after 40.256 seconds from confirmed worker completion. Its later outcome is unknown.

On the first conflict resolution, 225 of 226 tests passed. The existing regression from #206114 caught a generic error when a resumed worker belonged to another parent. I corrected the refusal and kept the test unchanged. All 68 tests in the three affected suites passed in 248 seconds, including compilation. Type-aware lint and formatting passed.

### Earlier packaged comparisons

I ran a real Gateway and Codex CLI with synthetic inference. One goal used the same worker twice. I dropped the socket during the first wait, paused the parent after the second submission, and dropped the socket again after the worker finished but before the Gateway received the notification.

- At `96b29225`, after 60.536 s the parent had no result and the Gateway reported ready to stop. A separate read found the exact completed turn and answer.
- At `42682e51`, shutdown stayed blocked while the worker ran, after it finished, and during a deliberately held history read. One announcement arrived 1.393 s after the second disconnect. Explicit Resume read the original goal and completed it. After returning to the original Gateway, the same session and threads retained both answers.

The packaged comparisons used CLI 0.164.0 and the production changes on OpenClaw `82b682c6` alongside #193024. Earlier trials on CLI 0.164.0 and 0.169.0 exercised the original foreground recovery. The remote configuration change in #201621 was omitted from this trial.

Earlier tests covered changed certificates, wrong turns, Stop, concurrent registration, queued siblings and stale authority. Removing the cleanup fixes left an extra receipt for the completed task and produced an unhandled abort.

### Disconnect before the worker finishes

I paused the parent, disconnected while the worker was still running and held the response for over eleven seconds. At `42682e51`, the Gateway reported ready to stop and the parent missed the result.

At `3e0756c7`, the worker was the only shutdown blocker after 11.406 s. The Gateway still refused to stop during the result read. The parent received one announcement 2.313 s after the worker replied and stayed paused until Resume. With an active goal, the next automatic turn waited on the same worker. It finished without another input or announcement. An intermediate build without the handoff attempted a redundant announcement. In both cases the worker ran exactly two tasks.

Lint, formatting and the commit hook passed. The updated `native-subagent-submission-store.test.ts` suite passed 39/39 in 230.89 s with one worker, including compilation. Six additional cases took 10.459 s total. They cover both orders of a status change during the read, an inconclusive reread, authority revoked while waiting, an unrelated parent releasing its guards and re-registration on a live connection.

### Stored worker records across an upgrade and return

Three separate Vitest processes using local dependencies ran the old, proposed and old binding-store code against the same SQLite database. The PR merge base (`81d69df5`) wrote two synthetic V1 child receipts and an assignment with a recorded result. Candidate `3e0756c7` reopened the database and recovered both receipts and the assignment exactly. It rejected an incorrect submission ID without modifying the row, then consumed only the matching receipt and assignment. On return, the original code reopened the same parent binding with only the sibling receipt remaining. No schema migration was needed.

The probe reused the fixture in `native-subagent-submission-store.test.ts`. Each process passed one assertion-based test and reported its final state.

```jsonl
{"phase":"seed","assignments":1,"submissions":2,"binding":true}
{"phase":"candidate","assignments":0,"submissions":1,"binding":true}
{"phase":"return","assignments":0,"submissions":1,"binding":true}
```

### Worker visibility during recovery

At `3e0756c7`, `sessions.describe` with `includeNativeSubagents` lost the running worker after a disconnect, even as the plugin watched for its result. The session now shows the worker from that same watcher while its pending assignment, session and delivery authority remain valid. A live parent takes priority. This adds no Codex RPC or permission.

With the plugin changes from `afd551cc`, the same worker was visible 11.421 s after the disconnect. Shutdown still reported busy. The parent received one result and the running row disappeared. One explicit Resume completed the paused goal. Switching back preserved both results.

The binding-store suite now registers the recovery scenarios in a separate file. Three cases failed on the prior implementation. All 43 cases passed with the fix, including status changes during a read, an unrelated turn and five simulated minutes without a notification. The final suite took 244.58 s on one worker including compilation, with zero skips. The split keeps the same cases and order.

## Limits

Detached observation requires a saved, acknowledged follow-up under the same authority. A lost recovery connection, changed binding, read timeout or inconclusive history can still leave the result pending. These trials used local maintenance restarts. They do not establish zero downtime or recovery across a cluster outage.

The worker view relies on status changes from the recovery connection between reads. An empty worker list can mean observation was lost. If observation fails, a ready-to-stop status alone cannot prove that the worker finished. Reconcile the original task before shutdown or resubmission. If the goal is paused and you intend to resume it, the following command worked in the same conversation on the original Gateway.

```text
/goal resume Read the current goal. Wait for the existing worker and verify its result. Do not resend the task or spawn a replacement.
```

Resume starts a parent turn. Check for activity, unresolved effects and the reason for the pause first. In the unmodified Gateway trial, the scripted parent used `wait_agent` on the existing worker. The native server stayed up.

The available registry lacked the locked `@openclaw/fs-safe` version. Local typechecking with the existing dependencies reported the same 48 diagnostics before and after the change. Exact-lockfile CI and maintainer review remain outstanding. Independent source reviews were completed. The standalone review helper could not start on this host.

prs.title: fix: keep shell results when Tokenjuice fails
prs.body:
Contributor: @vincentkoc

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e4d1d244-6f2b-44f3-877a-b689b11af05a)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/377f98ba-cea3-40e2-8e6f-6f9876df455e)

## What Problem This Solves

A malformed local Tokenjuice rule can replace the output of a successful shell command with a generic post-processing error. In Code Mode it can also hide the original exit status, leaving the assistant unable to tell what the command did.

## User Impact

If optional compaction fails, the assistant gets the original shell result without rerunning the command. Timeout and spilled-output results stay intact so the assistant can see retry guidance or recover the full output. No configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Tokenjuice adapter declines to replace a result when its own processing fails and logs one warning per plugin registration without command data. Unrelated tool results no longer count toward rule-cache eviction. The generic middleware failure policy and the Tokenjuice 0.11.2 pin are unchanged.

## Evidence

- With the pre-fix plugin on the current host build, a malformed rule replaced a successful `git status` result with an error in Direct and Code Mode. The patched compiled plugin preserved the original text and, in Code Mode, the typed exit code `0` and status. The isolated CLI and scripted loopback provider checked plugin off/on in both modes, linked every result by exact call ID in its immediate next request, and verified all 50 history copies. Healthy results still compacted; literal CRLF, exit `7`, and typed JSON controls passed. This was deterministic fixture proof, not a live-model test or benchmark.
- 25 focused tests passed, including timeout guidance, spill links, cache churn, and the unchanged generic middleware behavior. `pnpm build:ci-artifacts`, scoped typecheck, lint, format, and both profiling-script smoke runs passed. Native Codex and live remote-node execution were not exercised.
- Independent source review found two profiling callers that needed the logger argument; both are updated and covered by the smoke runs. Managed autoreview was unavailable.

## Worked on by

- @vincentkoc

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The packaged browser eval verifies launch, emulation, and cleanup, but not whether a saved tab handle and snapshot refs still point at the right page after opening and focusing another tab. A wrong-tab submission could pass a single-tab smoke test.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior or configuration changes. The existing packaged browser eval now detects wrong-tab writes and verifies that closing one tab leaves the other usable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the packaged browser scenario and its authenticated CLI/Gateway boundary. Two synthetic loopback pages have identical controls but record distinct server-side submissions. The fixture checks the exact path, payload, and submission count rather than trusting a successful CLI response alone.

## Evidence

- Ran the new helper through OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (`2ab7b31`) and Chrome for Testing 156.0.8078.4 on Ubuntu x86-64 in a disposable offline container with Chromium sandboxing enabled. The background-tab form reached `/first` with `alpha` exactly once; after that tab closed, the remaining tab reached `/second` with `beta` exactly once. Gateway and browser teardown completed.
- Negative control: a scratch copy deliberately sent the first action to the second tab. The browser accepted the action, but the fixture rejected the actual `/second` POST when `/first` was expected.
- Shell and Node syntax, targeted formatting, commit hooks, and diff whitespace checks passed. The complete Docker scenario against the exact PR head was not run locally.
- Local autoreview could not launch in its read-only sandbox; no independent local verdict is claimed.

Contributor: [Vincent Koc (@vincentkoc)](https://github.com/vincentkoc)

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/f67a9873-4c20-4d15-ab33-b4acb646ba28)

prs.title: fix(release): explain prepared receipt recovery requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a receipt recovery command stopped during its final admission check, reconciling its request file produced an unconfirmed run with unknown status. The same output also covered a request that might already have reached GitHub. An operator who saw an HTTP 503 during admission had no way to tell which next step the retained file supported.

## User Impact

`pnpm frv recover --reconcile-request` now explains when it read the prepared phase and found no matching run. An operator can wait for the original command to exit, reconcile the same file again, and, if it is still prepared, resolve the original error before starting a fresh recovery with a new private request file. Text and JSON both carry the guidance and the read-only reconciliation command.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dispatcher durably records its attempt before sending. A second observer can read the prepared phase while the original command is still checking admission. Reconciliation labels that snapshot only when it finds no matching run. An observed run continues through the existing identity and receipt checks. Reopening a retained request stays read-only.

## Evidence

- The focused regression observes the request while the original admission check is running, returns an HTTP 503, then reopens the file. It also checks the identity-matched run before its witness arrives and counts zero dispatches.
- A local synthetic probe of the reconciliation implementation reproduced the previous ambiguous result and passed for prepared, attempted and observed states after the change. Both changed scripts passed Node syntax checks. The staged-content guard and `git diff --check` passed.
- The [hosted compact test shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45624869546/job/139243327358) passed the focused receipt-recovery suite, including the new pre-dispatch 503 regression and the existing uncertain-POST test. A separate local synthetic check confirmed the matching witness and completed-receipt paths take precedence over a stale prepared observation, and checked the text and JSON renderers.

prs.title: fix(tts): explain why a reply is too long to read aloud
prs.body:
Closes #206096

## What Problem This Solves

When a reply exceeds the configured text-to-speech limit, `/tts latest` sends users to the logs with a generic audio error. Retrying the same reply always fails.

## User Impact

Chat now shows the input length and the effective limit, with a suggestion to read a shorter excerpt using `/tts audio`. Direct `/tts audio` input gets the same guidance when it exceeds the limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

The synthesis validator already knows the effective limit for each request. It passes that limit to the shared slash command reply handler, which formats the length message. Provider failures still use the existing log guidance.

## Evidence

### Real Control UI captures

Before is upstream `9d39d4d8f535`. After is this PR at `491eae6308a4`. Both runs use Chrome 158 on macOS arm64 with separate loopback Gateways. I sent each slash command from the chat composer and verified the matching Gateway request and rendered reply. The assistant replies and direct input use synthetic text.

| Command and case | Input / effective limit | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `/tts latest`, default | 4097 / 4096 | Generic audio error and log guidance | Shows 4097 characters, limit 4096 |
| `/tts latest`, agent override | 101 / 100 | Generic audio error and log guidance | Shows 101 characters, limit 100 |
| `/tts audio`, same agent | 101 / 100 | Generic audio error and log guidance | Shows 101 characters, limit 100 |

#### Clean comparison · default `/tts latest`

**Before**

![Generic audio error in chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7ced54df-4d48-4657-9227-6c97c74726d9)

**After**

![Chat reports 4097 characters and a limit of 4096](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b21a0084-b078-432e-a95f-89608963b8b7)

#### Annotated comparison · default `/tts latest`

**Before**

![Highlighted generic audio error in chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e6c83395-8c95-4152-9ea7-adfea94a9b27)

**After**

![Highlighted length and limit in chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bdec6d52-0635-417f-9940-5727a4ff2bc4)

#### Agent limit · `/tts latest`

**Before**

![Generic audio error under the agent limit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/278987e7-e886-4710-bd0b-89aa9acc33e6)

**After**

![Chat reports 101 characters and a limit of 100](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/80a59bba-84f7-4bc5-81e1-027ee21ee28c)

#### Agent limit · `/tts audio`

**Before**

![Generic audio error for direct input](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/70f74f66-6bae-43e5-a194-fdf0b43256ae)

**After**

![Direct input error reports 101 characters and a limit of 100](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a8223f04-7a53-4484-81ee-5dbba400e39d)

### Other validation

- On an isolated Gateway on macOS arm64 with Node 26.13.1, `/tts latest` displayed “4097 characters, limit 4096” for the default and “101 characters, limit 100” for an agent override. Direct `/tts audio` also reported the scoped limit.
- A short reply produced a playable WAV with local macOS `say`. Repeating the command returned the existing already-sent message. The transcript input was synthetic and the Gateway, validation, and speech synthesis were real.
- Both new regression cases failed before the fix with the generic chat error and passed afterward. `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/commands-tts.test.ts src/tts/tts-runtime-routing.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 25 tests.
- `pnpm build:runtime`, core and messaging-test typechecks, targeted lint and formatting, and Markdown lint passed.
- Local Codex autoreview covered the full six-file diff against `27a9a1c537a4` through P3 and reported no findings in one pass. The reviewed diff matches commit `491eae6308a4`.

prs.title: feat(ui): render LaTeX in Control UI markdown
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI Markdown displayed supported LaTeX literally. This renders bounded math while preserving code, escaped input, currency, URLs and sanitized output.

## User Impact

Math is lazy-loaded; ordinary messages request no KaTeX engine, styles or fonts. Equations stay readable as source until ready, and failures keep that fallback. Wide equations scroll inside the message and now show a fade where content continues. Math stays findable in transcript search and readable in paste excerpts and web source previews.

Original contribution by @jjjhenriksen; repair work requested by @RomneyDa. Contributor authorship and coauthor credit are preserved; Allow edits from maintainers remains enabled.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @RomneyDa](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/clawtributor-review-pr-144324)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/41d889a9-23c8-4603-889b-a35ad86acfb6)

- [Rebase discussion and verification with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/ac39fc44-8e46-4656-ba81-f57ba2533d4c)

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the existing parser, generation-fenced leaf, shared lazy runtime, MathML and separate sanitizer. One 200-expression allowance covers stable streamed additions and the mutable tail. KaTeX is pinned to `0.19.1` with `trust: false`. Inline math uses `\(...\)`, and display math uses `\[...\]` or `$$...$$`. Single-dollar text stays literal. Plain-text consumers of the shared parser (search, paste excerpts, source previews) read math tokens as their TeX source, so math stays searchable and readable outside the rendered view. Wide equations reuse the table fade convention rather than adding a new affordance.

This remains built-in math, not a plugin. Product decision (2026-11-08, @vyctorbrzezowski): use built-in math rendering with KaTeX and prepare this selected PR for merge; merging remains a separate decision. #175507 contains the earlier equivalent implementation, not this latest rebase. KaTeX is the one new dependency (MIT, pinned 0.19.1, loaded only when a message contains math); dense math retains real CPU cost, bounded by the 200-expression message budget.

## Evidence

- **Rebased November 22, 2026:** signed head `d9d99865410de426d0827e34e7e0f935b79b8b46` on main `f066f9cba3135d28a6ff7df1e1e1ba95684dda74`; tree `3b29185c5bcf51f74f56cf2a4104a62903c792ff`. Existing absolute-baseline debt remains; no budget was raised. No new visual behavior was introduced, so the earlier screenshots below are reused, not recaptured.

prs.title: feat(codex): delegate selected host tools to native children
prs.body:
Closes #197376

## What Problem This Solves

A native Codex child can inherit a tool declaration without inheriting a handler. For example, the parent can use `memory_get`, yet a child that asks for the same tool gets "OpenClaw did not register a handler for this app-server tool call."

## User Impact

This adds an opt-in grant for directly spawned native children on a host-owned stdio app-server. Set `plugins.entries.codex.config.nativeChildTools`, for example:

```json
{
  "allow": ["memory_get", "catalog__get_*"],
  "deny": ["catalog__get_private_*"]
}
```

- Omitted policy or empty `allow`: no child host tools. Match whole canonical tool names, not plugin IDs or Codex's discovery prefixes. Deny wins. A wildcard also admits *future* eligible tools matching that pattern; a name starting with `get_` is not a promise of read-only access.
- **Host tools use the owning requester's OpenClaw authority, not the child's native Codex sandbox.** A host file tool can write even if the child's native filesystem access is read-only. The grant does not restore denied tools, create credentials, or waive host-side approvals, workspace restrictions or revocation.
- The parent keeps its existing tool surface. Native shell, delegation and native Codex MCP are unchanged. OpenClaw-projected MCP is in scope; reply delivery and parent-session controls do not run on the parent's behalf. Remove the allowlist and apply the normal Gateway restart/replacement procedure to disable it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The foreground turn selects from host-executable tools and records their declarations and owner identities. The native-child monitor admits calls from a direct child on the same physical connection and active child turn. Requests with the same thread, turn and call ID share an execution. Cancellation, retirement and revocation retain their own checks; inheritance of a declaration is not evidence of permission.

Instead of relaxing the parent's exact-thread guard, the host admits a distinct child run and rebuilds the selected tool under that run. The bridge checks the retained requester, configuration, tool identity and declaration; normal argument validation, hooks, approvals and timeouts still apply. MCP tools use the requester's existing OpenClaw projection. Child guidance reports selected names. The `codex native child tool catalog` debug record lists selection decisions, known owners and unmatched patterns without invoking any tool.

**Foreground lifetime:** ordinary projected MCP calls capture form-request context before contacting the server. A child inherited the foreground question/answer context via async-local storage, so capturing it asserted the **finished parent's** reply authority and rejected an otherwise admitted child call. The child host runs its operation inside `withAgentQuestionAnswerAuthority(undefined, ...)`, so it no longer borrows the parent's question/answer scope. The child receives a noninteractive MCP view: ordinary projected calls return their results, decline server requests for input, and do not install the automatic sign-in presenter or build a parent-session App preview. This applies to the delegated view, not the shared server connection or the parent's own view. The child's admitted caller, operator restrictions, revocation checks and normal host-side tool approvals still apply.

Shared WebSocket/Unix transports, scheduled runs, workspace-only placement and one-shot CLI paths are outside this grant. This does not change detached *reply delivery* or grant cross-restart durability.

## Evidence

- **Parent finished; native child calls MCP:** The [committed Gateway regression](https://github.com/lastguru-net/openclaw/blob/2ec0e1df599c184aaa30e2bc6758f2b1fbd4f00e/test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/codex-native-child-mcp-lifetime.e2e.test.ts) withholds both child tool requests until `agent.wait` reports the parent run finished successfully and `sessions.describe` reports no active parent run. Neither the child nor the backend had made a tool call at that point. When this test and fixture were first run against `8301e826c0a`, the denied call was rejected but the allowed call failed before server I/O. On [`12a5345e2f9`](https://github.com/lastguru-net/openclaw/commit/12a5345e2f9b7786f395a5009b813c01e5760522), the denied sibling was still rejected, the allowed call returned the fresh fixture value to the child, and the backend log was exactly `["get_nonce"]`. The [submission commit](https://github.com/lastguru-net/openclaw/commit/2ec0e1df599c184aaa30e2bc6758f2b1fbd4f00e) makes one test-only change: its missing-tool lookup explicitly returns `undefined`. The ordered E2E passed again on this test revision using the identical packaged production runtime; the allowed result matched a new fixture value and only `get_nonce` reached the server.
- **Earlier controls on [8301e826c0a](https://github.com/lastguru-net/openclaw/commit/8301e826c0a397d5dd1175a44117dda8ad539352), not new-head reruns:** the parent read its own file in all three memory scenarios. The child got the missing-handler error with no policy, its different file value with an allowance, and an explicit denial with wildcard allow plus exact deny. With the foreground held active, a child returned the wildcard-allowed MCP value, while the denied sibling never reached the stdio backend. When the parent was free to finish, two runs received **zero backend calls**; on repeat the child was told its run had ended. A passing direct executor test after teardown did not establish native end-to-end success.
- **Other verification on `12a5345e2f9`:** the fresh scoped QA runtime build and both committed Gateway E2Es passed (ordered MCP lifetime and allowed memory-plugin access). Nine focused tests also passed: seven for MCP materialization and UI isolation, and two for child-host authority and post-teardown execution. Formatting, targeted lint and code review completed. On submission `2ec0e1df599`, the targeted no-emit TypeScript check exited 0 with no diagnostics. The full upstream suite and hosted CI were not run; no end-to-end claim about a third-party OAuth flow.

**Stable upgrade and stored-session compatibility:** Tested the published v2026.11.10 host (`6ea542f`) and matching Codex plugin against the reviewed PR head (`2ec0e1df599`) in one disposable profile. The stable Gateway wrote a real Codex conversation. On upgrade, the PR migrated the existing global and agent databases in place, read the original user and assistant messages, and completed a new turn under the same session ID. The config file was byte-identical and the effective Codex settings were unchanged.

With `nativeChildTools` omitted, both child calls returned the missing-handler response and neither reached the MCP server. After adding only the opt-in policy and restarting, the same session retained its history. The child received the fresh nonce from `fixture__get_nonce`; `fixture__get_denied` was explicitly denied. The entire backend log was one `get_nonce` call.

The attached evidence package:[openclaw-206241-evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35489104/openclaw-206241-evidence.zip). See `evidence/upgrade/` for the redacted three-stage capture, migration excerpt, release provenance and reproducible Gateway test. Only inference is scripted. This tests compatibility of the upgraded runtime with existing state, not an interactive installer or upgrade of an in-flight child.

prs.title: fix: keep queued WebChat turns on their Codex subscription route
prs.body:
Related: #202519. This PR verifies the WebChat queue trigger, not the Goal or exec-completion triggers in that issue.

## What Problem This Solves

A WebChat follow-up can be accepted into the queue and then fail before inference when it drains on a Codex session configured for subscription sign-in only. The error asks the user to sign in again even though the turn was admitted with a compatible subscription route.

## User Impact

A queued WebChat turn can use the same configured Codex subscription as a direct turn. It still runs in the original session and replies once. No configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native model capability rows do not carry all transport facts. Resolve the route from the published picker catalog captured on the turn's prepared runtime snapshot, not from an ambient borrowed snapshot that the queue does not necessarily have. The same catalog fallback remains for snapshots without a capture. Runtime selection, authentication policy, account selection, permissions, and queue delivery are unchanged.

## Evidence

On upstream `3ff1109b0a666e1163fea47abc5d24afb80cda1e`, the synthetic queued case fails before inference: `openai-responses` requires an API key, but the configured profile supports subscription auth. With this change the queued turn reaches the synthetic Codex harness once with `openai-chatgpt-responses` and its configured OAuth profile, retains its session/thread, and delivers one reply.

117 tests passed across 8 files; typed lint and formatting passed. Focused suites cover native/host route ownership, authentication planning, catalog capture, queued custody and settlement, WebChat admission, and queued cancellation/revocation. The regression uses real queue drain and route planning with an invented catalog and a synthetic harness; it does not use a real account or launch the native Codex app server.

The fork branch is based on its existing main; its clean merge with the upstream SHA above produces the exact tree tested locally.

prs.title: fix: keep compaction working regardless of whose turn triggered it
prs.body:
Related: #204847, #202552

## What Problem This Solves

Since the Participate split P2 (#204847, part of #202552), compaction of a Claude CLI (native-compaction) session uses the operator authority of whichever turn triggered it. That breaks compaction in two ways:

- If the triggering turn has already ended, its authority is released. Native compaction then fails with "Operator execution ended. Reconnect to the Gateway, then resend your message." (`closure-released`) because admission tries to `retain()` the dead authority.
- If an invited participant (send access) triggered it, compaction fails with "Participating inputs require the OpenClaw runtime", even though compaction is session upkeep and not that participant's turn.

Before P2, native CLI compaction ran as System work with no operator authority, so neither failure was possible.

Josh's requirement (2026-11-25): "Compaction should never fail due to whose turn it was. Anyone invited into a session with send should trigger compaction if compaction needs to happen."

## User Impact

Native CLI compaction now works regardless of who triggered it, whether that is the owner, a same-credential device, or an invited participant with send access. It also works after the triggering turn has finished. Triggering compaction gives the triggering person no extra authority. Single-user compaction is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native CLI compaction goes back to the same System admission it used before P2 (`prepareSystemAgentRunAdmission(..., "agents.native-compaction")`), with no operator authority, no turn source assertion and no participant runtime check. Both callers stop passing the turn's authority (`compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirect` and the queued `/compact` path). This is safe for participants because native compaction is a control operation (`controlOperation: "compact"`): OpenClaw refuses its tool calls (`toolCallsRefused` in `cli-runner/mcp-grant-context.ts`, enforced in `gateway/mcp-http.ts`). It lists the session's tools only so that its request prefix matches the session's normal turns.

The following stay as they are, by design:

- **Embedded (non-CLI) compaction.** It still carries the participant ceiling, but only as data for the permission root and tool surface. It never calls `retain()`, so it already works after the turn ends. A new test case covers this.
- **Plugin and agent-harness compaction** (`harness/compaction.ts`). It keeps its guards: the participant runtime check and the source retain. Its hosts (queued `/compact`, `sessions.compact`, CLI post-turn compaction, preflight compaction) retain the source when the work starts and hold it until the compaction settles. So an earlier turn ending does not affect them, and P2 did not change that behavior.

Possible follow-up, not changed here: P2's durable context-engine turn maintenance (`harness/context-engine-turn-authority.ts`) re-admits a participant's saved source before running maintenance. If that participant was removed after their turn, or the replay runs without a Gateway request scope, re-admission fails and the maintenance (and any compaction it would do) is skipped with a warning. Changing that would relax P2's participant ceiling for plugin maintenance, so it needs a separate decision.

## Evidence

- **Failing first, on `main` (`compact.native-cli.test.ts`, through `compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirect`):**
  - Manual compaction of a Claude CLI session whose triggering turn's authority was already released failed with `Operator execution ended…` from `retain()` (`admitted-run-context.ts:531`).
  - The same compaction triggered by an invited send participant failed with `Participating inputs require the OpenClaw runtime`.
  - Both pass with the fix. The compaction child's admission also carries no operator authority, so the participant lends and gains nothing.
- **Ordinary single-user compaction is unchanged:** the existing native CLI tests pass.
- **Embedded path:** the P2 participant clamp test now also runs with an ended-turn authority (`compact.hooks.test.ts`). It passes, and the tools stay at the participant's permission root and mode.
- **Focused suites:** 204 test files covering compaction, context engine, maintenance, operator run authority and participation (agents, context-engine, auto-reply, commands, gateway, sessions, plugins) all passed.
  - Two earlier failures came from the host environment, not this change: a group-writable `TMPDIR` and an inherited exec marker. Both suites passed once those were removed from the environment.
- **Checks:** `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` pass. oxlint and format are clean on the changed files. The madge import-cycle check reports 0 cycles.
- **Independent review:** a read-only review found no P0–P2 issues. It confirmed that the native compaction child gets no participant authority. It also confirmed that no other caller relied on the removed refusal, and that participant runtime checks elsewhere are unchanged. It raised two non-blocking notes:
  - An invited participant's `/compact <text>` on a CLI-backed session now reaches the owner's native `/compact` as summary instructions. That text can only shape the summary, with no tool path, which matches the behavior before #204847.
  - The queued path's entry retain would still reject an already-ended authority. No current caller passes one: `/compact` and `sessions.compact` pass live authority, and preflight compaction never takes the native path.
- **Mac Studio proof on head `bc2bd231`:** Crabbox `local-container` lease `cbx_a429f23894cc` (run `run_8bc17a525f667e289ba967fbba641bb6`) ran `compact.native-cli.test.ts` against both commits. On `main` `5b6cc381` the 2 new tests fail (2 failed, 5 passed). On the PR head all 7 pass. The neighboring `compaction-runtime-context.test.ts` (35 tests) passes on both.
- **Not exercised:** a live Gateway end-to-end run with a real Claude CLI session and an invited participant.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: Control UI: keep reply headers off subagent completion notices
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In shared chat, a subagent's completion notice can acquire a “Replying to” header when it appears between a participant's message and the assistant's answer. The actual answer then shows a second header.

## User Impact

The completion stays in chronological order on its own line. The reply header appears on the answer, where it links to the original message. A leading completion notice is centered with the assistant avatar when the avatar is visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

A completion receipt records an event. It is not a reply to the most recent participant. Skip automatic reply attribution for groups that contain only completion receipts.

## Risk and coverage

The change is limited to shared chat presentation and the alignment of a leading completion row. The browser regression reproduces two reply headers on the base and expects one header on the actual reply with the fix. The reply attribution suite, UI type check, focused lint, formatting, and CSS lint passed.

## Evidence

After rebasing on `c32abfe2a1a4`, the production comparison passed without changing any budget: total CSS gzip fell from 348,656 to 348,646 bytes, and chat startup JS fell by 22 bytes with the same request count. The grid now names the avatar and message columns, including in compact activity. The Chromium reply-attribution suite passed all 10 tests, including the check that the completion and avatar centers differ by at most one pixel. All 25 spacing and avatar-layout tests passed. Formatting and stylelint passed. Local Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issue in the final patch; it reviewed source rather than executing tests. Updated head: `a5ae3081d81e`.

The bundled Control UI was run against an isolated mock Gateway. In both captures, a subagent finishes between Jordan's message and the assistant's reply. The screenshots use synthetic messages.

prs.title: fix: compare Logbook activity times on one bar scale
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Logbook’s **Day at a glance** could draw a longer bar for a shorter activity. For example, 60 minutes of design looked longer than 61 minutes of writing, even though both duration labels were correct.

## User Impact

The category bars now use the same scale, so you can compare how you spent your time without having to double-check the labels. The recorded totals do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each row used to reserve only as much space as its own duration label needed. “1h” left more space for the bar than “1h 1m.” Sharing the duration column gives every bar the same available width.

## Evidence

The existing phone screenshots show the same 121 minutes of activity before and after. The 60-minute bar used to be 238 px long, compared with 225 px for 61 minutes. It now measures 220 px, correctly shorter than the 225 px bar. The earlier comparisons found the same ranking error and correction on both tablets and desktop.

The mounted regression on the publication base reproduced the reversed ranking on a landscape tablet and passed after the chart change. It used synthetic activity; no capture or stored durations were changed. Screenshot baseline: `5a3e6b1cb09bb`. Isolated repair: `71bbd2be0b00c`.

prs.title: fix(android): detach accepted work on TalkModeManager and Wear OS closes
prs.body:
Related: #206321, #206329, #188134, #188798

## What Problem This Solves

After #188798 moved phone End Talk (`NodeRuntime.setTalkModeEnabled(false)` -> `stopAllCapture()`) to `disposition: "detach"`, two Android-side Talk close paths still sent aborting closes on Gateways that advertise `talk-session-close-disposition`:

1. `TalkModeManager.setEnabled(false)` passed `TalkSessionCloseDisposition.Abort` instead of `Detach`.
2. `WearRealtimeTalkController.closeGatewaySession` omitted `disposition`, inheriting the pre-#206321 abort default on Gateways that advertise `talk-session-close-disposition`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Paired with Gateway PR #206321 (which makes Gateway Talk close default to `"detach"`) and Apple PR #206329, this aligns every Android phone and Wear OS Talk close path so ending or dropping a call preserves accepted agent work consistently, including against existing Gateways advertising `talk-session-close-disposition`:

- `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/TalkModeManager.kt`: change `setEnabled(false)` from `TalkSessionCloseDisposition.Abort` to `TalkSessionCloseDisposition.Detach` and update the `stopAllCapture` KDoc comment.
- `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/wear/WearRealtimeTalkController.kt` & `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/NodeRuntime.kt`: pass a `supportsCloseDisposition` check (backed by `operatorSession.captureRequestLease(gatewayId)?.supportsCapability("talk-session-close-disposition")`) and include `disposition: "detach"` on `talk.session.close` when advertised, omitting it on older Gateways.
- `apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/TalkModeManagerTest.kt` & `WearRealtimeTalkControllerTest.kt`: update the `setEnabled(false)` close-disposition test to expect `"detach"` (and `null` when unadvertised) and add a Wear test covering both advertised and unadvertised `talk-session-close-disposition`.
- `docs/nodes/talk/client-ui.md`: document that both phone and Wear OS realtime Talk closes send `disposition: "detach"` when advertised.

AI-assisted: drafted and reviewed with AI coding assistance. Opened as a draft for Android CI / handoff verification because no JDK or Android SDK is installed on the authoring host.

## User Impact

- Ending Talk through `TalkModeManager.setEnabled(false)` or on Wear OS keeps accepted agent runs alive when the Gateway advertises `talk-session-close-disposition` (older Gateways without that capability continue to receive no `disposition` field).
- Stopping an active agent run remains an explicit action via the chat Stop control or saying "cancel" before ending Talk.

## Evidence

- Static review and ktlint/editorconfig check against `apps/android/.editorconfig`: Kotlin types, nullability, visibility, import ordering, and callers (`NodeRuntime`, `TalkModeManager`, `WearRealtimeTalkController`, `WearRealtimeChannelRegistryTest`, `GatewaySessionReconnectTest`) verified clean.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/native-app-i18n.ts verify`: passed (`entries=4984 changed=false`).
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- Local Gradle compilation, `ktlintCheck`, and Android/Wear unit tests were not executed on this macOS host (no JDK/Android SDK installed); ready for CI or Android environment verification.

prs.title: fix(doctor): restore cold session archives before session reimport
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #204834

On `2026.11.8`, upgrading from `2026.11.7` rolled back after `Doctor blocked invalid session-history migration` / `sqlite_transcript_count_mismatch`: 608 transcripts had already been moved to cold storage by session maintenance, while Doctor's legacy reimport and active-original settlement still read them as hot SQLite history. Each read raised `SessionTranscriptColdError`, the migration batch rolled back, and the update reverted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cold-storage maintenance archives transcript events but keeps the session window and entry metadata. Two Doctor-owned paths still assumed hot history:

- `importPendingLegacySessionStoreSourcesInBatches` verifies/imports retained legacy transcripts (including recovery-inventory `*.imported-<ts>` originals) without restoring cold archives first.
- `settleImportedActiveOriginals` reads the canonical transcript to reconcile an active original, with the same assumption.

Both now call the existing cold-storage owner's restore for exactly the pending batch's session ids before verification/reading, mirroring the Gateway's `sessions --repair-imported` path. Hot batches are untouched. Review then noted the restore ran for every batch session before the skip decision, so one missing archive failed the whole batch. The restore loop now tolerates a per-session missing/unreadable archive: that session stays cold and the per-record import skips it when its legacy original is already gone. Custody rebounds (session turned active, source changed, writer claim changed) still rethrow and abort the batch, and the recovery-inventory identity is re-checked via the existing `assertCurrent` in the catch. No schema, config, or protocol changes.

## User Impact

Users whose sessions were cold-archived between releases can upgrade again: Doctor restores the cold archives it needs, completes verification/import/settlement, and the update no longer rolls back with `sqlite_transcript_count_mismatch`. A single missing archive no longer blocks the other sessions in the batch; that session is left cold and skipped when its legacy original is already gone. Session content and ordering are preserved.

## Evidence

**Shipped CLI upgrade, intact archives (current head `66c3a896de6`).** Published stable `openclaw@2026.11.10` (`OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f)`) seeded an isolated state with 3 legacy June-2026 sessions (3 events each) via the real import path; the stable cold sweep archived all 3 to file-backed `.jsonl.zst` (agent DB `user_version=42`), legacy originals retained. BEFORE (stable): `doctor --fix` exits 1 — each session reports `Transcript is in cold storage. Restore its archive before reading or changing the transcript.` AFTER (reviewed branch build = main + this patch), from a byte-identical snapshot:

```console
$ openclaw.mjs doctor --fix
Upgraded agent database schema in …/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: v42 -> v44.
…
- Legacy entries: 3; SQLite entries: 3.
- Transcript events: imported=0; validated=0.
- Archived 3 legacy transcript artifact(s).
exit=0
```

Data-model compatibility on the upgraded state: all 9 `transcript_events` rows read back with original ids, timestamps (`2026-06-01T00:00:0{0,1,2}.000Z`) and roles (baseline: 6 of 9 payloads cold-archived); `session_windows` keys unchanged; `session_transcript_cold_archives` rows cleared by the restore; pre-migration SQLite backup saved. Follow-up `doctor --session-sqlite import --yes` on the same state: `0 target(s), 0 legacy entries, 0 sqlite entries, 0 issue(s)`, exit 0.

**Shipped CLI, dangling archive (review repro).** Same published `openclaw@2026.11.10` driver; two loaders mirror the patch onto its dist differing only in the per-session catch (base = prior-head bare loop, head = this head). State: 3 cold-archived June sessions, legacy originals retained; `june-proof-0`'s archive payload and legacy JSONL deleted, cold row kept.

```console
# base arm: whole batch fails on the one dangling archive
$ node --experimental-loader proof-loader-1110-base.mjs openclaw.mjs doctor --session-sqlite import --yes
Cold transcript archive ac3958d7817798dc73013328e9652e83212313646e4a31ddaaed1bf30f5f38df.jsonl.zst is missing or unreadable. Restore it from a backup; its transcript has not been replaced with empty history.
exit=1
# head arm: dangling session skipped, the other two restored and settled
$ node --experimental-loader proof-loader-1110-head.mjs openclaw.mjs doctor --session-sqlite import --yes
session-sqlite import: 1 target(s), 3 legacy entries, 3 sqlite entries, 0 issue(s)
- main: imported=2/0 events, validated=1/3 events, archived-unreferenced-jsonl=0, unreferenced-jsonl=0
exit=0
# cold rows after: base keeps all 3 (batch aborted); head keeps only june-proof-0
# transcript_events: 3 rows per session in both arms (no history replaced with empty data)
```

**Regression.** The settlement case is now `it.each(["retained","skipped","rebound"])`. RED on the original merge base `032a2b3367c` (sources reverted, test at head): retained case fails with `sqlite_transcript_count_mismatch` — `Transcript is in cold storage. Restore its archive before reading or changing the transcript.` RED on the prior head (no per-session tolerance): `FAIL ... skipped legacy original — expected Error: Cold transcript archive a0ac7e68....jsonl.zst to be undefined` (batch aborted). RED with only the rethrow clause removed: `FAIL ... rebound legacy original — expected undefined to be an instance of SessionColdTurnReboundError` (custody abort swallowed). GREEN on this head (blob-verified restore): `doctor-session-sqlite.active-settlement.test.ts` 9 passed; siblings `session-accessor.sqlite-import.test.ts` 14 and `doctor-session-sqlite.failure-reports.test.ts` 15 passed (2 Vitest shards, exit 0). `oxfmt --check` and type-aware `oxlint` clean on all changed files.

Limits: the issue's 608-archive scale is reproduced with a 3-session fixture on the same path; recovery-inventory originals feed the same batch loop. Blob-backed payloads share the unchanged restore owner (existing cold-storage suite, 21 passed).
