prs.title: improve(ui): highlight skill references in the composer
prs.body:
Related: #152599 (inline `$skill` references; standalone slash commands are unchanged). Builds on #192242.

## What Problem This Solves

Selected skills remain raw `$command_name` text in the composer, making them harder to distinguish from surrounding prose and person mentions.

## User Impact

Chat and New Session show known skill references as highlighted, atomic names with the existing skill icon and no visible `$`. Copying and sending preserve the canonical reference. No configuration or migration is required.

**Studio benchmark:** Chat matched the first person mention. New Session still falls short of p95 parity (77.28 vs 71.63 ms across 50 matched observations per variant). The current CI and existing asset budgets passed; the performance gap is open.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the generic native-first editor and extension contract from the final merged #192242, rather than introduce another editor, overlay or dependency. Skills use the existing command catalog and share atomic boundary editing with people. Display labels no longer grant reference identity: only canonical commands and normalized command identifiers are recognized. Unknown references, shell variables, escaped dollars and code remain literal.

Ordinary edits map existing skill decorations instead of rescanning the draft. Token/Markdown-sensitive edits still use the canonical parser; image-bearing drafts deliberately retain full parsing. Atomic editing checks only affected chip boundaries and does not serialize large pastes for single-character separator checks. Literal dollars may load the small parser, but cannot fetch CodeMirror until a reference is admitted. Catalog replacement explicitly refreshes labels/removals and admits unchanged restored drafts; subscriptions end with their native/editor owners. Native undo snapshots, asynchronous handoff, IME boundaries and retired-frame guards are preserved. Skill integration still composes through the mention adapter, not a new feature framework.

## Performance acceptance for this landing

Use production builds and alternate samples on the same host. The known-good reference is `491c2944` (merged person mentions); keep an identical-reference control and the previous skill head `0283e5b6`. Collect at least 10 paired Chromium samples per route, cold and warm separately, and record renderer CPU median/p95, structural work counts and request/asset sizes.

Chat and New Session must stay native for a long unrelated draft containing `$HOME`, with zero whole-draft skill scans on subsequent unrelated typing. In rich mode one ordinary key after a 64 or 128 KiB word must not require work proportional to the word. Confirm exact `$command_name` output, late catalog changes, Markdown/escaped text, cursor, undo and chip selection.

Person-only typing, selection, undo, mixed typing and large paste must stay within the identical-reference sample spread, with no repeatable regression in median or p95. Time cold first skill from the first `$` through selection and an interactive editor; compare with the analogous first person mention and the old skill head. Validate the real Gateway flow as well as the repeatable benchmark. Enforce the startup asset gate without raising the limits.

## Evidence

### Rebased composer and Chromium regression

Rebased onto 93ce03aada9f. The rebased product tree matches the expected integration; the follow-up changes only the browser test. The controlled rewrite leaves the caret at the end of a long draft. Chromium reproduced the previous assertion with the skill correctly present as an atomic range but outside the rendered viewport. The test now checks admission before moving the caret, reveals the token, and still asserts the actual rendered label.

On this candidate, all 43 focused Chromium cases and both end-to-end skill-reference cases passed, as did the UI typecheck, targeted lint, and formatting. This does not assert that the historic New Session p95 gap below has disappeared. The earlier live Gateway proof was not rerun for this test-only repair.

### Studio qualification of the final product tree

Paired production Chromium, renderer CPU in ms, synthetic Gateway for timings, with identical baseline as a control. Kept the original tails. Repeated five scenarios whose original runs overlapped other validation.

| First use | Known-good person mention | Candidate skill |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Chat, 10 pairs | 84.50 / 88.26 | 84.25 / 86.96 |
| New Session, all 50 pairs | 68.95 / 71.63 | 67.63 / 77.28 |
| New Session, 20 pairs | 69.25 / 71.63 | 67.83 / 104.45 |
| New Session confirmation alone, 10 pairs | 69.62 / 72.99 | 68.53 / 72.21 |

Values are median / p95. New Session originally had two higher samples (104.45 and 117.36 ms); neither recurred in the ten untraced confirmation pairs or the separate trace. The cause is unconfirmed, so this does not claim full p95 parity. The following 30 untraced pairs retained the earlier observations and produced no candidate samples above 77.28 ms. The 50-pair identical person-mention control was 68.43 / 73.93 ms. A local matcher experiment removed 400 name normalizations on the first dollar with 200 skills, but the measured paired median improved only 0.91 ms, within control variation; that experiment is not part of this PR. For ordinary typing, undo and mixed paste, differences were within the matched run's variation.

- An unrelated 69,014-character draft stayed native. Skill scans over 12 unrelated keystrokes fell from 38 to zero in Chat and 27 to zero in New Session. The rich editor reads four old document positions after an ordinary key, down from 65,540 in the long-word case.
- An isolated real Gateway and production Chromium accepted exact skill references in both routes. Chat also demonstrated downstream expansion. The bundled Chat E2E checks handoff and the raw payload for two skills; the 390 px New Session E2E and 12 focused Chromium tests passed after consolidating duplicate coverage.
- The paired build against main passed the existing asset limits: Chat −10 B gzip, New Session +372 B gzip, no new startup requests. The test-only follow-up removed 97 counted lines and passes the exact CI ratchet with 34 lines to spare.


### Current candidate

- Signed head \`86339fea5f6d65f5b3eb4c5e61eeee3fee5fb027\` matches the production build verified in Chromium against an isolated real Gateway on Chat and New Session. Raw \`$HOME\` stays native; person avatar selection and undo still work; the installed skill was copied and accepted by the Gateway as the exact raw reference. The test model endpoint was local; explicit expansion was verified in Chat only.
- On the 69,014-character literal-dollar draft, twelve unrelated keys caused 38 → 0 full lexical scans in Chat and 27 → 0 in New Session. One rich edit after a 65,536-character word went from 65,540 → 4 document reads; the revised count stayed 4 at 32,768 and 131,072 characters.
- The current-main merge build passes all asset budgets without changing limits. JavaScript request counts stayed 21 for Chat and 17 for New Session. Gzip change: Chat −10 B, New Session +372 B, largest JavaScript asset +430 B. The older budget evidence below refers to its pinned historical base.
- Late catalog, token boundary and Markdown coverage passed in Chromium. A trusted browser case also proves the fast path invalidates correctly when a controlled writer changes earlier text to a known skill without changing the draft length. Typechecks, focused lint and independent P2 review passed.

### Current repair and review — November 16

Published head `0283e5b68266ebb706dab8a9d74623406693488e` has exactly the tested product tree of implementation `ec4b449ebd8e2e0e468f10da9fec32b8ec9b789b` (`37b3739503d08c1fbe431ff51ae1ba6af24bcb99`); the publisher's final commit is attribution-only.

- **218 browser tests passed in 13 files**, including person/skill editor consumers, native handoff, undo, paste/drop, composition simulation, ref disposal, catalog/command consumers, overflow, height and mobile fixtures. UI and script typechecks, scoped lint/format, controller guard and whitespace checks passed.
- **Both source-server real-UI Chat/New Session flows passed** with a synthetic Gateway. The new network assertion first failed on both routes: `$HOME`/`$unknown` fetched the rich editor. It now passes while actual skill selection and canonical submission still work.
- Both hosted P2 findings on `6d45233` were reproduced red and repaired: display-name aliases could look selected without resolving on submission; unchanged drafts did not react to catalog arrival/rename/removal. The catalog regression verifies stable editor identity, raw text and selection.
- Independent local **autoreview through P2 was scoped-clean** for the final staged repair against `6d45233`, subsequently committed as `ec4b449`. It included the generic editor, mention adapter, import lifecycle, catalog owner, Gateway reference-resolution contract and Markdown parser as context. Static review is not runtime proof. Earlier reviewer findings for indentation, adjacent backticks, native history and literal-dollar loading were repaired; the staged-only loading finding disappeared when the reviewed working-tree fix was committed.
- **900 valid repair timing observations** were collected across explicit source stages: 390 at `08ec3b39`, 270 at `452d63a5`, then **240 on the final product tree**. Completed interrupted work was retained rather than replayed; one restart interruption in the first stage is excluded from valid observations. Earlier-stage measurements are not relabeled as final-head proof.
- Final separate diagnostics found **zero full-draft skill scans for twelve unrelated keys** in both Chat and New Session, down from twelve on the original feature. Ten people/eight skill chips and exact raw text survived; one editor remained mounted and stylesheet rules did not grow during typing. A final bounded 21-round-trip session lifecycle replay also passed on baseline and candidate; this is not a universal no-leak claim.

### Acceptance rule — unchanged

Baseline `491c2944f56ad7d6d9a561a17dfffcd42cab49e3` already contains the final merged mention foundation. Compare same-toolchain production builds with at least ten serial rotating baseline/candidate/identical-baseline rounds. Report median, p95, ranges and host load; keep traced diagnostics separate. Require no correctness loss, unexpected RPCs, per-key remounts/owner-echo transactions or unbounded resource growth. Median regression must be at most 5% with no worse p95; unresolved tails need confirmation. A confirmed move above 20% blocks blanket performance acceptance. Existing asset limits remain unchanged. Mock-renderer, live-Gateway and native-device evidence remain separate.

### Final production-build timings

Chromium `156.0.8078.4`, Linux x64, real production UI with a synthetic Gateway. These are **renderer main-thread CPU milliseconds per action**, not per-key latency, INP, total process CPU or live-provider latency. Long typing is twelve trusted characters in a 64 KiB draft; mixed drafts contain ten people/eight skills. Paste is 256 KiB synthetic clipboard input. Catalog size is 200. Each row has ten observations per variant; each cell is **median / p95**. A/A is an identical baseline.

| Flow | Baseline | Final candidate | A/A control |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Chat person-only long | 55.567 / 60.265 | 55.551 / 60.269 | 56.480 / 59.302 |
| Chat mixed long | 52.028 / 58.309 | 54.160 / 57.572 | 54.125 / 56.980 |
| Chat literal dollars | 38.862 / 43.498 | 39.343 / 42.133 | 38.111 / 45.286 |
| New Session person-only long | 52.058 / 54.542 | 53.371 / 58.238 | 53.519 / 57.152 |
| New Session mixed long | 45.783 / 50.206 | 46.555 / 55.102 | 46.154 / 49.780 |
| New Session mixed paste | 23.195 / 25.057 | 23.746 / 26.502 | 22.933 / 25.102 |
| Chat first skill, including first dollar | 47.118 / 52.273 | 87.230 / 91.677 | 48.570 / 52.067 |
| New Session first skill, including first dollar | 45.679 / 49.449 | 74.020 / 81.182 | 44.615 / 48.706 |

The original mixed-typing median regressions were +8.39% Chat and +8.97% New Session. Final mixed medians are +4.10% and +1.69% versus baseline, and +0.06% and +0.87% versus A/A. This supports removal of the measured hot-path waste, not universal parity: New Session person/mixed/paste p95 are still +6.78%, +9.75% and +5.77% versus baseline. The complete acceptance rule therefore remains unmet.

**First-use work is not hidden in preparation.** New `first-skill` workloads start from an untouched native draft and include the first dollar, catalog readiness, typing the query, selecting the skill and settling imports. Older `activate-skill` rows measured selection after typing the query; they are selection-only evidence, not cold first-use parity. Native-to-rich first-use cost remains approximately +40.1 ms in Chat and +28.3 ms in New Session. At the earlier `08ec3b39` stage, short skill-only typing was 20.170 → 36.529 ms and 200 occurrences were 64.712 → 127.286 ms. Those are native-versus-rich feature costs, not all attributable to parsing, and are not waived or claimed as final-head measurements.

Final CPU ranges: Chat mixed baseline 49.655–58.309 / candidate 51.451–57.572 ms; New Session mixed baseline 45.098–50.206 / candidate 44.695–55.102 ms; Chat first-skill baseline 46.277–52.273 / candidate 85.950–91.677 ms; New Session first-skill baseline 43.821–49.449 / candidate 70.785–81.182 ms. Final host load ranged 1.95–6.04 on 128 logical CPUs. Complete distributions and per-run manifests remain in the linked task under `catalog-final-summary.txt`, `catalog-final.log.summary.json`, and raw observations. No outliers were removed.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction, prior evidence and scope</summary>

The committed workload extends `scripts/lib/control-ui-chat-composer-scenarios.ts`, using the existing engine runner. With matched baseline and candidate builds:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts \
  --bundle-dir .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base/dist/control-ui \
  --compare-bundle-dir dist/control-ui \
  --control-bundle-dir .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base/dist/control-ui \
  --source-root .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base \
  --compare-source-root . \
  --control-source-root .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base \
  --engines chromium --viewport desktop --pairs 10 \
  --steps composer-qualification-chat-first-skill,composer-qualification-new-first-skill,composer-qualification-chat-literal-dollar,composer-qualification-chat-person-long,composer-qualification-chat-mixed-long,composer-qualification-new-person-long,composer-qualification-new-mixed-long,composer-qualification-new-mixed-paste \
  --output .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/rerun
```

Earlier qualification of `6d45233` retained 510 editing/activation and 62 startup observations, 157 browser cases, eight emulated narrow/dark observations, four scan diagnostics, profiles and bounded retention. Its boot CPU and heap results are historical evidence, not a fresh final-head certification. Earlier repairs retained their own exact-source summaries; only the final table above qualifies the current product tree.

The simplify pass preserves the existing foreign-DOM owner and CodeMirror extension contract. No dependency, editor, overlay, global cache, custom Markdown parser or permission change was added. Necessary growth covers the skill feature, selective invalidation, native history and catalog notification/disposal. Versus `491c2944`, production UI is +714/−263 lines, tests +488/−19, and benchmark code +359/−1. Net test growth is 469 lines; the documented per-change allocation is 69 beyond the standard 400 for reproduced handoff, Markdown, lazy-loading and catalog/identity failures. Startup/performance limits were not raised.

</details>

### Startup asset gate — still failed

Final normalized largest-JS gzip is **569,985 → 570,497 bytes (+512)**. The inherited-over-cap differential permits only 64 bytes: **448 bytes remain over the allowed increase**. Original feature growth was +676 bytes; this repair does not claim the remaining failure is harmless. Chat/New boot gzip grows 539/486 bytes; request counts remain 21/17. CSS bytes and request counts are unchanged. The boot manifest was regenerated without a source diff. No unrelated byte-offset changes or budget increases were used.

Reproduction: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-control-ui-performance.mts --dist dist/control-ui --base-dist .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base/dist/control-ui --json`. The strict comparison exits 1. Inherited absolute CSS/request overages are distinguished from this new differential failure.

### Remaining limits

This is a verified repair update to a draft, not a shipping or zero-regression claim. Startup size, native-to-rich feature cost and remaining p95 regressions are unresolved. WebKit/Firefox could not load the app under the environment's proxy policy on either build; no bypass was attempted. Native OS IME, mobile Safari, real-device/network and live Gateway/provider performance remain unqualified. Composition browser tests simulate events, not a physical input method. No merge or deployment occurred.

prs.title: fix(apple): keep accepted work running after End Talk
prs.body:
Related: #206321, #188134, #188798, #203889

## What Problem This Solves

On iOS and macOS, ending Talk or losing the Talk transport cancels accepted agent work:

1. `RealtimeTalkRelaySession.stop()` omitted `disposition: "detach"`, and `TalkRealtimeWebRTCSession.stop()` defaulted `preserveRuns` to `false` across End Talk, session-switch, background, disconnect, and push-to-talk teardown paths.
2. In the shared `.clean` composer chrome, an active run or draft replaced the Talk button with Stop/Send, leaving no way to end Talk without stopping the agent response or clearing the draft.
3. On iOS and macOS, tapping End Talk ran the focus-update callback (`focusChatSession` / `recordActiveSessionKey`) before disabling Talk, which could retarget Talk when the active call belonged to a different session than the displayed chat.
4. The iOS Talk footer showed a camera-flip button with no visual feedback (no live video preview) that crowded the compact composer footer.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ending or losing a voice call stops audio capture and playback, not accepted agent work. Paired with Gateway PR #206321 (which makes Gateway Talk close default to `"detach"`), this updates the Apple Talk stack so every normal teardown path detaches cleanly and works with both existing Gateways advertising `talk-session-close-disposition` and Gateways with #206321:

- `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/RealtimeTalkRelaySession.swift` & `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/TalkModeRuntime+Realtime.swift`: `stop()` and `stopAndWait()` always send `disposition: "detach"` when `supportsCloseDisposition()` is true, wait for any in-flight `talk.session.cancelOutput` before detaching so Stop Speaking followed immediately by End Talk still cancels the turn, and remove now-unused `stopAfterFailure()`.
- `apps/ios/Sources/Voice/TalkRealtimeWebRTCSession.swift` & `TalkModeManager.swift`: default `stop(preserveRuns:)` and `stopRealtimeSession(preserveRuns:)` to `true` across all teardown paths while keeping explicit `preserveRuns: false` available and locking the first stop's choice against subsequent cleanup calls.
- `apps/ios/Sources/Design/ChatProTab.swift` & `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/WebChatSwiftUI.swift`: skip `focusChatSession(sessionKey)` / `recordActiveSessionKey(sessionKey)` when ending Talk (only focus when starting Talk), and use session-independent help text (`"Stop realtime chat"`) when Talk is enabled.
- `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawChatUI/ChatComposer.swift`, `ChatComposer+CleanControls.swift`, `ChatCameraFlipButton.swift`, `OpenClawChatTalkControl.swift`: keep the active Talk button reachable beside Stop/Send in `.clean` chrome via `showsSeparateActiveTalkControl` across iOS and macOS, add a narrow-width `ViewThatFits` fallback so End Talk, Stop, and Send stay reachable on compact widths, and remove the dead camera-flip control (`ChatCameraFlipButton`, `OpenClawCameraFacingSelection`, `cameraFacing`/`flipCamera`) along with its iOS mutation helpers (`flipPreferredCameraFacing`, `setPreferredCameraFacing` in `NodeAppModel.swift`), keeping the stored `camera.preferredFacing` fallback read intact (matching Android).
- `apps/.i18n/native-source.json` & `docs/nodes/talk/client-ui.md`: drop the three removed camera-flip strings from the native i18n baseline and document iOS/macOS End Talk detach behavior.

AI-assisted: drafted, implemented, reviewed, and verified with AI coding assistance, with every change tested locally.

## User Impact

- Ending Talk on iOS or macOS stops listening and playback while keeping accepted agent runs alive when the Gateway advertises `talk-session-close-disposition` (older Gateways keep their legacy aborting close) and across direct WebRTC calls.
- Users can tap End Talk directly beside Stop or Send during an active response or while drafting a message.
- Ending Talk while viewing a different chat session ends the active call without switching focus or aborting its run.
- The non-visual camera-flip button is intentionally removed from the iOS composer (matching Android, which does not show one). Existing saved `camera.preferredFacing` defaults are still read by camera capture commands when no explicit camera is specified.

## Evidence

- `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter "RealtimeTalkRelaySession|ChatTalk|VoiceNoteRecorder"`: 71 tests in 10 suites passed (including default detach close, Stop Speaking followed by End Talk preserving `talk.session.cancelOutput`, and `showsSeparateActiveTalkControl` coverage).
- `xcodebuild test -project apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClaw -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=..."` on `TalkRealtimeConsultCancellationTests`, `TalkRealtimeVoiceSessionCleanupTests`, `TalkModeManagerTests`, `CameraControllerClampTests`, `ChatVoiceObservationTests`, and `ChatTypingFocusTests`: all 6 suites passed (75 tests, including `testEndTalkDoesNotSwitchFocusOrAbortMismatchedSessionRun`).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/ios-lifecycle-workflow.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 73 passed.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/native-app-i18n.ts verify`: passed (`entries=4981 changed=false`).
- `swiftformat --lint --config config/swiftformat` on all 16 modified Swift files: 0 files require formatting.
- `swiftlint lint --strict` with `apps/ios/.swiftlint.yml` (9 files) and `config/swiftlint.yml` (2 macOS files): 0 violations.

prs.title: fix(access): label invite-only roles in the role picker
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On the Access page, choosing a role for a member shows a short description of what that role can do. Roles configured with `sessions.others: "invited"` (a valid config value) showed the raw key `sessions.invited` instead of a readable description. This was seen on a live claw with a custom `collaborator` role.

## User Impact

Owners now see "Only sessions they're invited to" for invite-only roles in the role picker. The other session-access descriptions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway passes each role's `sessions.others` value through to the Access page unchanged, and the config schema allows `none | invited | view | suggest | write`. The Access page's English catalog and its `Role` type only covered four of those values. This change adds the missing English label and a shared `RoleSessionAccess` type that lists all five values. The English `sessions` catalog is now checked with `satisfies Record<RoleSessionAccess, string>`, so a missing label fails typecheck instead of showing a raw key. No other session-access consumer in the extension or the owner link projection branches on this value.

Foreign locales are not edited by hand. They follow the repository's i18n rules (generated after merge). Until then, `translateControlUiMessage` falls back to English for the new key.

## Evidence

- New `people-roles.test.ts` case renders every access level and checks the invite-only description. It fails on `main` (raw key) and passes with this change.
- Removing the `invited` label makes `pnpm tsgo:extensions` fail with `Property 'invited' is missing in type ... Record<RoleSessionAccess, string>`.
- Gap: no screenshot. The only visible change is one description string in the role picker.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openclaw-id-access/browser` — 6 files, 21 tests passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — pass
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/openclaw-id-access` — no problems
- `oxfmt --check extensions/openclaw-id-access/browser` — clean
- `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` (no diff), `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` — pass

</details>

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: docs: separate bug reproduction from CI regression tests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Contributors fixing a user-visible bug were told both to rerun the real product and to commit proof of the fix, without a clear distinction between the two. In #205573, the plugin reload fix initially grew a 109-line Gateway-boot test even though a 52-line test could catch the same quarantine regression without starting a Gateway.

## User Impact

Contributors still verify the real user flow and report what happened. CI keeps the smallest test that catches the defect, preferably in the existing owner suite. No runtime behavior, existing test, or CI configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

#168083 favored focused contracts; #176308 required end-to-end verification; #197557 removed rules that encouraged speculative work. The new guidance keeps the useful parts: a disposable reproduction is PR evidence, not a permanent test harness. A new Gateway-boot or `.e2e.test.ts` file needs a transport, process lifecycle, or startup wiring defect that a narrower test cannot detect. Future testing-rule changes must weigh defect detection against net test lines and CI seconds.

## Evidence

`pnpm check:agents-md-size` passed; root `AGENTS.md` shrank from 19,694 to 19,426 characters. `pnpm format:docs:check` passed for 1,445 files. `pnpm docs:check-links` found no broken links among 16,883 checked. All four changed files passed formatting and `git diff --check`. Net production and test LOC: zero. Future CI savings were not measured.

Reported and scoped by @hannesrudolph.

prs.title: feat: let users expand the Code Mode tool index
prs.body:
Related: #196858

## What Problem This Solves

Code Mode's tool-signature index has a fixed 8,000-character budget. With a large catalog, operators cannot trade a larger prompt for more upfront tool visibility. Omitted tools remain callable, but their names and signatures are absent from the index.

## User Impact

Operators can set `tools.codeMode.catalogIndexMaxChars` globally or override it through `agents.entries.<agentId>.tools.codeMode.catalogIndexMaxChars`:

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "codeMode": {
      "catalogIndexMaxChars": 32000
    }
  }
}
```

- Unconfigured deployments retain the 8,000-character default.
- Positive integer settings resolve to an effective budget clamped to 1,000–128,000 characters.
- Existing selection and ranking, including upstream scheduling-tool priority, are preserved.
- Larger budgets consume more prompt/context space. They do not guarantee inclusion of a particular tool or improved model behavior. Prompt refresh follows the documented session-prefix lifecycle.

This does not pin memory/wiki tools or change Memory Recall guidance, so it does not claim to fully fix the linked issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change reuses the existing Code Mode schema, configuration resolver and index formatters instead of adding another renderer or a tool-priority mechanism. The effective budget participates in prompt-cache identity and is carried in configured worker presentations. Unconfigured presentations omit the field, preserving their shape; this is not a claim of cross-version worker admission compatibility.

The core configuration inventory increases from **2,677 to 2,679** because the shared option creates exactly two documented paths: global and per-agent. Channel/plugin budgets are unchanged. This is the configuration-surface tradeoff for an explicit operator-controlled prompt-size limit.

Canonical predicate regeneration also synchronizes the already-existing upstream `revoke: true` schema. That schema was not changed by this contribution; generated content was not hand-edited.

## Evidence

Qualified source: **7fe1a779cd017e271b26f2e2c4f11255216d322c**, based on **b7bd237d00508e0999c7a3fc6e36bc32bf421098**. After rebase completion, all source/lock manifest hashes and the complete binary diff were matched to the executed and independently reviewed snapshot.

All following checks exited **0** on that integrated source, using Node 26.13.1 and pnpm 12.15.0 with frozen dependencies, secretless isolation and offline validation:

- **119 passing tests across 9 complete files**, **148.048 seconds** wall time, `--maxWorkers=1`. Includes upstream's native-scheduler crowding regression, default/configured budgets, schema acceptance, cache isolation, both ranked/unranked clamp endpoints, compiled admission, serialized per-agent presentation and Gateway prompt projection.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: **12.405 seconds**.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: **all 29 shards**, **320.465 seconds**.
- Changed TypeScript lint through the canonical oxlint wrapper: **21.731 seconds**; changed-file `pnpm format:check`: **0.436 seconds**.
- `pnpm config:docs:check`, `pnpm config:schema:check`, `pnpm docs:check-config-examples`.
- `pnpm gateway:validators:check`, `pnpm protocol-registry:check`.
- `pnpm --filter @openclaw/gateway-protocol build`, including emitted public-type contract checks: **7.479 seconds**. This is not a full application/release build.
- `pnpm check:test-mock-exports --staged --base HEAD`, `pnpm check:bundled-channel-config-metadata`, and diff whitespace checks before rebase completion.

<details>
<summary>Focused test command</summary>

```sh
pnpm test \
  src/agents/code-mode.catalog-index.test.ts \
  src/agents/code-mode.config.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts \
  src/agents/code-mode.skill-read.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/session-prompt-state.tool-usage.worker.test.ts \
  src/agents/harness/tool-surface-bridge.test.ts \
  packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/worker-gateway-tool.test.ts \
  packages/gateway-protocol/src/worker-session-tools-compat.test.ts \
  src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-gateway-tool-runtime.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

</details>

Test cost: **288 added / 1 deleted test lines** across three files. Transport checks extend existing fixtures/cases rather than introducing a new boot matrix. Timings above include isolated-runner overhead, not hosted CI measurements.

Local review: an independent Claude audit reran the pre-integration candidate and identified two low-severity test-fidelity/coverage improvements, both addressed. A separate final read-only review inspected the complete integrated diff and relevant owners, including those improvements and upstream conflict resolution, and found no concrete correctness, security/privacy or integration defects. prs.title: fix: let Claude CLI agents check on and collect a Deep Research job they started
prs.body:
Closes #205799

## What Problem This Solves

An agent running on the Claude CLI can start a Deep Research job but can never check its progress, fetch the report, resume it or cancel it: the `deep_research` tool it is given only offers the `start` and `capabilities` actions, so the job's result is out of reach.

## User Impact

Claude CLI agents see all six `deep_research` actions (`start`, `status`, `result`, `resume`, `cancel`, `capabilities`) and can follow a research job through to its report. Other tools' schemas are unchanged unless they nest a list of allowed values the same way. No setup or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the Gateway flattens a tool's top-level `anyOf` for the Claude CLI tool list, it pools the allowed values of each variant's `action`. `deep_research` writes one variant's values as a union of literals (TypeBox emits `anyOf` of `const`), which the pooling did not recognize, so it kept the first variant only and logged "conflicting schema definitions". The fix treats such an `anyOf` of literals like a single literal list before pooling, in the shared helper `mergeLiteralSchemas`, so its other caller (provider tool schemas) gets the same behavior. Anything else in that `anyOf` (non-literal variants, extra keywords) is left as before.

## Evidence

**Live, before and after:** a Claude CLI agent on a test Gateway was asked to print the `deep_research` `action` schema it was given.

| Build | Actions the agent sees | Gateway log |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Released 2026.11.10 | `start`, `capabilities` | `conflicting schema definitions for "deep_research.action", keeping the first variant` |
| 2026.11.10 + this fix | `start`, `status`, `result`, `resume`, `cancel`, `capabilities` | no such line |

![Before and after: deep_research actions a Claude CLI agent can call](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stealthybear/openclaw/205cce9d00bce8362ac570bbc0bf6b7516b804e1/before-after.png)

Tested on e8ee1744da (base 8fea10c4543; no later main commit touches the changed files).

- Review: autoreview, 8fea10c4543..e8ee1744da, P0–P2: clean, "patch is correct (0.8)".
- Tests: `src/gateway/mcp-http.test.ts` gains a variant written as a union of literals; it fails without the fix and passes with it (62 tests, 63.5 s with `--maxWorkers=1`).
- **No request proof:** the change is in the tool list the Claude CLI loads from the Gateway; the live run above shows that list as the model received it. Not run: a full Deep Research job through `status`/`result`; this checks only that the actions now reach the agent.

prs.title: fix(feishu): route p2p chat ids to the sender session
prs.body:
Closes #205708

## What Problem This Solves 📌

Replying to a Feishu one-to-one chat started a different conversation than the one the message came from, so the assistant "forgot" the thread it was answering. The reply now lands in the same conversation.

- Problem: Feishu chat ids (`oc_...`) address both groups and one-to-one chats, but outbound routing assumed every `oc_` target was a group. A reply to a DM's chat id produced a group-scoped session key (`...:feishu:group:oc_...`) while the inbound DM had been recorded under the sender (`...:feishu:direct:ou_...`), so the two never joined up.
- Solution: Resolve the chat kind before choosing the session peer. For `chat_mode = p2p`, read the chat member list (`im.chatMembers.get`): that endpoint excludes bot members, so a single human member names the direct peer — the same identity inbound DM routing uses — while `chat:<chat_id>` stays the delivery address.
- Rework note: the previous revision read a `p2p_chatter_id` field from `im.chat.get`. That field does not exist in the Feishu API/SDK (review finding P1), so this revision replaces it with the member-list lookup above. It also revalidates `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` before any route-discovery read, so a retired sender cannot trigger new provider requests (review finding P2).
- What changed: `extensions/feishu/src/session-route.ts` and its route regression tests. Nothing else.
- What did NOT change: group routing, `ou_`/legacy `user:` receive-id handling, and the delivery address for any existing target. Ambiguous member pages and failed lookups keep today's group behaviour.

## Why This Change Was Made

The receive-id type alone is not enough information — `chat_id` only says "this is a chat address", not "this is a group". The chat directory knows the kind (`chat_mode` via `resolveFeishuChatType`) and the p2p member list knows the counterpart, so routing consults both instead of guessing.

- Best fix: yes. It reuses existing helpers (`getChatInfo`, `getChatMembers`, `resolveFeishuChatType`) and converges on the same direct-peer identity inbound routing already derives; no SDK or wire-protocol changes.
- Alternatives rejected: `p2p_chatter_id` on `im.chat.get` (field does not exist — the earlier revision's mistake); matching on `oc_` prefix or `chat_type` presence (neither distinguishes p2p from group reliably).
- Risk / non-goals: up to two extra API calls per `oc_` target route, only after the transport-authority revalidation. Lookup failures fall back to the previous group behaviour instead of erroring, so no existing send breaks. A retired sender's handoff assertion throws before any lookup, keeping the send-authority baseline byte-identical (no chat lookup after retirement).

## User Impact

Feishu DM replies now continue the originating conversation, so context, routing, and per-session state stay intact. Group behaviour is unchanged and operators need to do nothing.

## Evidence 📌

Routing matrix for an `oc_` target, asserted in `extensions/feishu/src/session-route.test.ts`:

| Scenario | Peer | Deliver to | Session key |
|---|---|---|---|
| p2p, single human member | `ou_sender` (direct) | `chat:oc_...` | `...:feishu:direct:ou_sender` — matches inbound |
| genuine group | `oc_...` (group) | `chat:oc_...` | unchanged |
| p2p, member page empty/ambiguous | `oc_...` (group) | `chat:oc_...` | unchanged (fallback) |
| p2p member lookup throws | `oc_...` (group) | `chat:oc_...` | unchanged (fallback) |
| chat metadata lookup throws | `oc_...` (group) | `chat:oc_...` | unchanged (fallback) |
| sender retired (handoff assert throws) | error propagates before any provider read | — | no chat lookup after retirement |

The new p2p/handoff regression tests fail on the unpatched baseline (3 failed) and pass with this change:

```
$ npx vitest run extensions/feishu/src/session-route.test.ts \
    extensions/feishu/src/outbound.send-authority.test.ts \
    extensions/feishu/src/chat.test.ts
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  50 passed (50)   # session-route 9 + send-authority 30 + chat 11
```

`oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the touched files: 0 errors.

Live Feishu proof at head f245db51 (org-tenant self-built app; Gateway websocket long connection; `session.dmScope=per-channel-peer`; user/bot ids redacted):

```
[feishu] feishu[default]: bot open_id resolved: ou_63d5…
[feishu] starting feishu[default] (mode: websocket)
[feishu] feishu[default]: WebSocket client started
[ws] ws client ready
```

Inbound DM "hello p2p" → direct-peer session (gateway.log verbatim):

```
sessionKey=agent:main:feishu:direct:ou_2c04…
message processed: channel=feishu chatId=user:ou_2c04… messageId=om_x100b7fb66197c440b087bf506ba1189
```

Real p2p member discovery `GET /im/v1/chats/oc_fcb0…/members?member_id_type=open_id&page_size=2`: `{"code":0,"msg":"success","member_count":1,"members":["ou_2c04…"],"has_more":false}` — one human member (bot excluded), exactly what `resolveP2pChatterId` consumes.

Outbound CLI to that p2p chat id: `openclaw message send --channel feishu --target oc_fcb0…` → `✅ Sent via feishu. Message ID: om_x100b7fb674e2e8b0c1b85a81a44f8a9`, delivered in the same DM.

Continuity (agent store): exactly one feishu session node `agent:main:feishu:direct:ou_2c04…` (`created_via=channel`, no `group:oc_` node); transcript seq1 user 12:16:16Z "hello p2p" + seq9 assistant 12:19:07Z "proof: outbound p2p route continuity check" share session 79256dc8…. Agent auto-reply not exercised (sandbox model endpoint 400); outbound used the real message-send path.

prs.title: fix(clawrouter): preserve provider paths for Messages models
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter Messages models can advertise a provider-specific URL prefix, such as Cloudflare AI Gateway's `/anthropic/v1/messages`. OpenClaw discarded that prefix and sent requests to a different endpoint. Rejected or ambiguous catalog entries could also regain a configured model fallback.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/468

## User Impact

Eligible native Messages models use the catalog-selected route and Router credential. Rejected, withdrawn or ambiguous Messages offers fail before inference. Genuinely absent legacy offer metadata remains supported, and existing Vercel, Chat and Responses selection precedence is preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The client validates the provider, model, upstream identity, POST method and both Messages formats, then removes only the terminal `/v1/messages` suffix before handing the base URL to the Anthropic transport. Provider/model uniqueness uses the same normalized identity as catalog projection, so whitespace-equivalent duplicates cannot select another row's route or metadata.

prs.title: fix(cron): use the service's free memory for extra automation runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Linux, a Gateway with a delegated cgroup mount can read a sibling’s free memory when deciding whether to start a ninth automation. A busy service can start one extra run, and a service with enough room can leave a job waiting.

## User Impact

The scheduler uses the service’s free memory for runs beyond the eight default slots. It still needs at least 1 GiB free and admits at most one extra run per drain, up to sixteen. If it cannot read the delegated service’s remaining allowance, queued jobs keep their place. Running jobs and provider backoff keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both scheduler ticks and explicit queue drains use one memory reader selected for the scheduler. Ordinary layouts continue to use the native runtime reading. On a delegated Node/Linux mount the reader follows the service’s current cgroup membership and reads its charged bytes. This reuses the validated mount mapping from [the pressure fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206308). Cron makes an absolute free-byte decision and does not need to read process rlimits.

## Evidence

- On a real Linux/arm64 delegated mount with Node 24.20.0 and libuv 1.52.1, the same process saw 1,073,741,824 free bytes in an empty sibling and 1,007,828,992 in the service. The previous cron decision admitted an extra run. The new decision declined it. This control called the production decision without starting a job.
- A synthetic stock/candidate control exercised the production cron predicate with one byte below the 1 GiB floor, exactly at the floor, and a service outside the visible mount. With the native reading pointed in the opposite direction the candidate returned false, true and false. Ordinary Linux, unverified mounts, macOS and Bun retained their native results. Three decisions on an ordinary Linux scheduler performed one mount lookup in total. None of these cron cases read process rlimits.
- A Linux Node test drove ten due jobs through the real scheduler. Committed running-job counts were eight below the floor, nine at the floor and nine after the process moved outside the visible mount. The test passed in 865 ms and all 32 host-memory tests passed. Those product and test blobs are unchanged on the final head. [Focused hosted test results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45932900504/job/140290697703).
- Existing capacity fixtures now control the scheduler’s own reading, including the manual-ack child process. This isolates the eight-to-sixteen capacity and provider-backoff tests from the runner’s actual memory. The Linux regression keeps the real delegated mapper and a contrary native reading.
- The pinned formatter, repository signing hook and `git diff --check` passed. Production changes add 22 net lines. Test and test-selection changes add 115 net lines.
- Draft CI also identified three unused updater/doctor exports already reported on main, plus a Bun Gateway teardown failure with a retained native-worker handle. On the final head the same Gateway recovery test passed, including shutdown, in 22.675 seconds. The Linux scheduler gate and all 14 cross-tick admission cases also passed on that head. [Final scheduler and capacity cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45934012716/job/140293475253) · [Final Gateway shutdown case](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45934012716/job/140293475327). [Main’s matching unused-export report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45928608789/job/140276138304) · [Draft Bun shutdown result](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45932900504/job/140290697811).

prs.title: fix(build): reuse stamps after identical pnpm installs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeating an identical pnpm 12 installation changes its cache-pruning timestamp. The source runtime fingerprints that timestamp, so an otherwise reusable build is rejected and build/runtime preparation asks to run again.

## User Impact

Identical installs can retain their build and runtime stamps. Dependency graph, layout, install policy, compiler, source, platform and environment changes still invalidate them. Unsupported metadata formats keep their existing byte-sensitive behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Normalize only the top-level string `prunedAt` in recognized pnpm 12/layout-5 JSON metadata at the existing fingerprint owner. Every other field remains part of the fingerprint; no parser dependency, stamp rewrite or workflow bypass is added.

## Evidence

- The real stamp-reader regression fails on the base: changing only the timestamp requests both build and runtime work. With the fix, both stamp readers permit reuse. This is a preparation decision, not a measured count of executed builds.
- Dependency/layout/policy and unknown-field changes still reject reuse; unsupported JSON/YAML retains raw-byte sensitivity. Existing source, lockfile, missing-output and strict-head checks are retained.
- Two separately installed exact-revision checkouts produced different fingerprints before the fix and identical build/runtime fingerprints afterward, without replacing either metadata file.
- Focused typecheck, lint and formatting pass. All 9 stamp-reader cases, 6 existing build-stamp cases and 7 artifact-transfer cases pass, including the sparse native-Node harness. The new regression was red on the base. Last artifact/build-stamp run: 78.73s wrapper wall; final stamp file: 113.72s wrapper wall / 11.332s tests on a loaded host. These are validation costs, not speedup measurements. Local ClawSweeper reviewed the complete committed range `e3dd914318e748a03cbc0a7e1d6c0865bc1ca2d5..19aac8e2605ee7a4e5490d499045ca8a7a4c8bd2` at high reasoning effort: no actionable findings. The separate independent source review was also clear; neither review reran tests.

This removes a demonstrated false invalidation. Cross-job runtime artifacts are not enabled here, and no whole-CI runtime or billing saving is claimed.

prs.body:
Related: #204432

## What Problem This Solves

A failed image inspection still split surrounding chat activity into two command groups and added a separate “View image failed” line.

## User Impact

User impact: Routine image inspections stay inside the activity group, including failures and lone inspections. Expand the group to see the original result. Inspections that need approval still get their own visible row.

## Why This Change Was Made

Image inspection is ordinary tool activity. The conversation can keep it in one disclosure without losing the preview, error, or approval request.

## Risk and coverage

Control UI presentation only. The existing browser scenario now checks a failed inspection between commands, during a run and after reloading history. It opens the error inside the group and checks that the delivered image stays visible. Component coverage checks lone inspections and approval requests.

## Evidence

75 focused component tests and both Chromium scenarios passed on the Studio, along with typecheck, lint, and formatting. The baseline showed two command groups around the failed inspection. The changed UI shows one activity group and the error remains accessible.

Native Codex review found no actionable issues. The screenshots show the same fixture in the built Control UI against an isolated mock Gateway: `7642a7fa6975` before, `377f6ad25c7d` after.

prs.title: fix: clarify sent-message labels and chat activity icons
prs.body:
Related: #204399

## What Problem This Solves

The chat activity row said “Message accepted for [chat]” for an ordinary cross-chat send. It showed the receipt's internal wording where a simple confirmation would do. The generic activity group used a tree icon even though it opens to show a list of actions.

## User Impact

User impact: Once the destination chat accepts the send, the activity row reads “Sent message to [chat]”. Queued, deferred, timed-out and unconfirmed sends keep their distinct labels. Chat activity disclosures such as “Ran commands” and “Used tools” share a collapsible-list icon.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing translated success label for the accepted receipt. The underlying send, reply behavior and raw tool result are unchanged. Use the list icon at the existing shared activity-group fallback, preserving disclosure behavior and specialized icons.

## Risk and coverage

The changes are limited to one confirmed-outcome label and the generic chat activity icon. The existing component coverage checks direct and tool-dispatched sends, along with the failure and pending states.

## Evidence

118 focused Control UI tests passed, along with the locale catalog check, typecheck, lint and formatting. Both accepted-receipt cases showed the old wording before the change and the expected wording afterward. Native Codex review found no actionable issues.

The same accepted receipt rendered in the built Control UI with an isolated mock Gateway: `c09a73a3a142` before and `d8b7f3444610` after.

prs.title: feat(llm-task): process bounded batches with per-item outcomes
prs.body:
Closes #177325

## What Problem This Solves

Workflows extracting or classifying several independent inputs need bounded fan-out and per-item outcomes without rebuilding that orchestration around every `llm-task` call.

## User Impact

Callers can submit 1–20 inputs, inspect ordered results, keep successful siblings, and explicitly resubmit selected unsuccessful inputs. Existing single-input behavior is unchanged. The optional plugin remains opt-in; this adds no core tool or persistent job service.

New feature proposal: maintainer acceptance of this optional-plugin API is requested, not assumed. `maxTokens` is per item, not a batch spending limit. Cancellation may occur after usage is incurred, and outer agent cancellation may suppress the response. This is not durable recovery or a provider's offline Batch API.

## Why This Change Was Made

`batch.items` shares the existing prompt, schema, routing, and host-authorized isolated-completion path. The existing public concurrency runner limits fan-out to 1–4 (default 2). A single deadline includes queue time, and invalid batch admission fails before inference. Each started input invokes the existing completion API once; the batch scheduler adds no retries and does not change underlying runtime/provider retry policy.

Failures return stable categories rather than raw provider exceptions or rejected model output. Results distinguish successful, failed, interrupted, and never-started items. No model credentials, file access, message delivery, new config settings, dependency changes, or storage migrations are added. Documentation explains manual retry and the non-persistent response boundary.

Related, not duplicated: #137450 adds native Codex output constraints; #161344 connects embedded Lobster stages. All-state PR searches for `llm-task` batch/parallel/concurrency found no matching batch implementation.

## Evidence

### Main integration — 2026-11-14 (`e7b0db2b1202d8ac867d7840e62ea03cb80eaedd`)

Merged main `db8cab9d3ea38f2f6583ab9350bc568f19d47839` into the original PR branch. GitHub now reports the PR can merge without conflicts. The sole content conflict was in the tool result path: default model selection stays with the completion runtime when no override is provided, and both single and batch calls return compact JSON text with the existing structured details intact.

- Main's existing compact-result assertion failed against the intermediate resolution because single-call text was still pretty printed. After restoring compact serialization, **all 38 tests across the three llm-task plugin test files passed** (Vitest 14.96s, wrapper wall time 19.04s). These tests cover default routing, schema forwarding, ordered results, partial failures, cancellation, and the shared deadline with fictional inputs.
- Extension production and test typechecks, typed lint for the three changed TypeScript files, formatting, plugin import boundaries, the test-line budget, and documentation link checks passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview completed for the five changed public files against `db8cab9d3ea38f2f6583ab9350bc568f19d47839`, with no accepted P0–P2 findings. It reviewed the supplied public runtime contracts and fictional tests; it did not run the tests or independently verify provider internals. Reviewed tree: `79a5648d43b221607ba281edd47096de78e4d5a6`.
- [GitHub CI for this commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43553709576) reports `action_required` with zero jobs started. Could a maintainer approve the pending fork workflow runs for this commit? The October CI and real-model Gateway evidence below belong to earlier commits. This follow-up did not exercise a live provider.

Maintainer acceptance of the optional batching API remains open. Only public source and fictional fixtures were used for the repair and review. Maintainer branch edits remain disabled.

### Previous main integration — 2026-10-27

Current integration head: `c83390ef3308588e834eb909d4abac13ec02a036`. This merge preserves original PR head `3b00bdbefd677053831294b62bbe4c978643bfda` and actual main `4d8806c8c2e297af9bc06f5cc73d4b0a3a8f949b` as its two parents.

Resolved four conflicts while retaining main's inlined model selection, simplified fixtures, native `outputSchema` forwarding, and documented same-route native-schema fallback. Every batch item keeps the shared isolated completion owner. The batch scheduler adds no retries; the runtime's existing fallback is not disabled or presented as a one-provider-request guarantee.

- All **36 tests across the three llm-task plugin files pass** on the integrated candidate (Vitest 60.40s; wrapper wall time 65.90s, including 35.21s initial worker compilation).
- The existing repeated-`$id` schema-forwarding test was run unchanged with the original PR production owner: **one failed / 25 skipped**, because `outputSchema` was undefined (76.66s wall time). Restoring the integrated owner byte-for-byte made the same test **one passed / 25 skipped** (30.19s). No new test, full-suite replay, or model call was added for this comparison.
- Targeted production and test typechecks passed (11.88s / 21.76s), along with typed lint, formatting, assertion/line-count ratchets and documentation links (16,044 checked; zero broken). An initial temporary typecheck configuration selected the wrong root; correcting that ignored verification configuration resolved its TS6059 setup error without a product/configuration change.
- Fresh canonical independent **P0–P2 review completed scoped-clean**, 1/1 pass with complete usage reporting. Static review and executed tests are separate evidence.
- Frozen contribution diff SHA-256 against that main: `705dc6845c8c5df2f1054b4170215b7ebf09605c50565e6344070c6565c17725`. Only the original five contribution files differ from main.

For the October 27 head, checks completed: 39 successful, 65 skipped, zero failed or pending checks were reported. [ClawSweeper's completed review of this exact integration head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177326#issuecomment-6267939700) reports no actionable findings and accepts the original live proof together with the integration comparison; the remaining blocker is maintainer API acceptance. The separate hosted Codex attempt failed with an unknown service error, not a new code verdict. Earlier real-model/Gateway evidence below remains attributed to its original head and was **not rerun** for this integration. This work used only public source and fictional fixtures; no real account authorization, private material, raw logs, secrets or permission expansion. Maintainer acceptance of the optional batching API remains outstanding.

### Historical implementation and runtime proof

- Node 24, isolated source checkout, synthetic inputs only. The plugin lane passed **34 tests across 3 files**, including existing registration and Doctor contracts. Measured run: **30.71s wall time** including worker compilation.
- Production extension typecheck, extension test-type check, targeted typed lint, assertion-safety and line-cap ratchets, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. After the final test-fixture type repair, the changed owner suite passed **24 tests in 12.85s wall time** (the other 10 plugin tests retain their unchanged-input passing evidence). Documentation audit: 15,720 internal links checked, zero broken.
- Regression scenarios: out-of-order completion with bounded concurrency; independent JSON/schema/provider failures without scheduler retry; no raw error leakage; admission rejected before any completion; completed/active/queued outcomes on cancellation and whole-batch timeout; strict-schema null placeholders preserve single-input behavior.
- Independent Codex autoreview completed for P0–P2 with **no actionable findings**. The review included the unchanged public concurrency owner; it did not execute project code or prove provider cancellation behavior.
- Previous-head (`fbd1b630`) [CI run 39254802659](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39254802659) passed, including production/test types, lint, changed boundary/extension tests, source contracts, guards, docs, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. The applicable dependency/security gates also passed. This is not presented as CI for the follow-up commit below; new-head CI is pending. Skipped unrelated lanes are not counted as executed.
- Additional generic prompt-prefix stability check did **not** complete: the unchanged agents-core test lane stalled after worker preparation and was terminated by its no-output watchdog (exit 143). It is not counted as passing. No timeout or assertion was weakened. PR CI remains the broader verification gate.

Implementation is intentionally limited to the existing optional plugin and two documentation files. The shared model prompt and completion-selection rules remain unchanged; the optional tool schema gains the batch argument. Maintainer edits are disabled at the author's request to avoid granting fork Actions/Secrets access; requested changes can be applied by the author.

### Deadline settlement follow-up (2026-10-21)

Follow-up head: `3b00bdbefd677053831294b62bbe4c978643bfda`. The initial live runs retained successful results and stopped queued work, but one timed run returned `completion_failed` for the slow item instead of `cancelled`. Its underlying provider/runtime failure cause was not established and is not inferred from the unit fixtures.

Investigation independently reproduced a missing batch-owner check: if completion resolves or rejects after `expiresAt` but before the timer callback executes, the old code can publish `ok` or `completion_failed` for that expired item. The fix checks the existing deadline at admission and both settlement paths, without changing the deadline, routing, credentials, provider runtime, or error-redaction policy. It keeps earlier successes and prevents queued dispatch.

- The two synthetic regressions both failed on `fbd1b630` for the intended late-result statuses (24 existing tests passed), then all **26 owner tests passed** after the repair: **15.72s wall time**, including cached worker preparation; test execution itself stayed below 5s. Existing registration/Doctor proof remains unchanged.
- Production and extension-test typechecks, targeted typed lint, formatting, assertion-safety and line-cap ratchets, and `git diff --check` passed. Checks were serialized after a build-lock conflict; the rejected concurrent attempts were infrastructure failures, not counted as passing.
- Fresh canonical Codex autoreview completed **P0–P2 scoped-clean** for this two-file follow-up, with no actionable findings. It did not independently run the tests or establish the cause of the earlier live runtime error.
- The follow-up removes duplicate admission-only deadline logic in favor of one shared check; only the existing tool and its test file changed (production +10/-8 lines, tests +35).

### Live behavior proof (2026-10-21)

Head: `3b00bdbefd677053831294b62bbe4c978643bfda`. Built with the repository's `qaRuntime` build profile and launched through `pnpm openclaw gateway run`. A fresh local-only Gateway used separate config, state, and workspace, with only the optional `llm-task` tool exposed. Requests used the production authenticated `POST /tools/invoke` entry point and the existing host-authorized isolated runtime with a real model, not mocked completions. Native session discovery and additional tool capabilities were disabled. No personal notes, conversations, private source, configuration, credentials, or raw authentication logs are included in this evidence.

Ordered partial outcomes: concurrency 2, shared schema requiring `category` to be `billing` or `technical`, and three synthetic inputs. The task classified an invoice and a startup problem; an explicit negative-control input requested `{"category":7}` to exercise schema rejection. The two successful results survived their sibling's failure and all IDs remained in submission order.

```json
{"http":200,"status":"completed","results":[{"id":"request-a","status":"ok","category":"billing"},{"id":"request-b","status":"error","error":"schema_mismatch"},{"id":"request-c","status":"ok","category":"technical"}]}
{"scenario":"ordered_partial_results","passed":true}
```

Whole-batch deadline: six inputs, concurrency 1, a 10,000ms whole-batch budget. The task requested a tiny JSON object for the fast/queued inputs and a deliberately long numeric-array response for the slow input. The unchanged diagnostic assertion requires retained completed results, an interrupted active item, and at least one never-started queued item in the same run. Only categories/statuses are exported, not the generated array. The clean final-head run passed both scenarios without temporary diagnostic instrumentation:

```json
{"gatewayReady":true,"head":"3b00bdbefd677053831294b62bbe4c978643bfda","cleanSource":true,"syntheticOnly":true}
{"http":200,"status":"timed_out","results":[{"id":"fast","status":"ok","category":"billing"},{"id":"slow","status":"cancelled"},{"id":"queued-1","status":"not_started"},{"id":"queued-2","status":"not_started"},{"id":"queued-3","status":"not_started"},{"id":"queued-4","status":"not_started"}]}
{"scenario":"whole_batch_deadline","elapsedMs":10019,"passed":true}
{"cleanup":"gateway_exited"}
```

The runtime proof is deliberately limited to this tool entry point and these synthetic scenarios, not model quality, a surrounding Lobster workflow, or a provider-side billing cutoff. A response reporting cancellation does not prove that the provider incurred no usage. Failures before the deadline/caller cancellation retain the existing `completion_failed` category; expired settlements are cancelled even when the deadline timer callback has not yet run.

The separate human owner decision is still outstanding: should `batch.items`/`batch.concurrency` and these per-item outcomes be accepted in the bundled optional plugin? No bot recommendation or passing check is presented as maintainer approval.

prs.title: refactor(android): reuse the shared TLS test fixture
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/202818

## What Problem This Solves

Android notification and favicon tests each build their own certificate and TLS socket factory even though the Gateway tests already provide a shared fixture. Maintaining three versions of this setup adds duplicate cryptography and key-store code to the tests.

## User Impact

Test-only cleanup; no intended app behavior, data, permission, protocol or dependency change. The same notification trust, connection replacement and authenticated favicon scenarios remain covered.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `gatewayTlsTestFixture()` directly and remove both local certificate generators and their imports. The shared fixture itself is unchanged. The complete diff removes 106 test lines; production code is unchanged.

The shared certificate has a localhost DNS SAN. Both affected paths connect to `127.0.0.1`, so the hostname mismatch remains. Original and replacement certificates still come from separate calls, and the existing unequal-fingerprint assertion remains. No scenario assertions were removed.

## Evidence

- Reviewed source head `94aeae8e166d29d7f5a8df703212ae2b665ba323`, based on `7f3bd14b7f7ec681b58076addfc14024223b08d4`.
- Passed 28 tests in each phone flavor: four notification trust/replacement cases, all 21 custom-header/favicon tests and all three Gateway TLS tests. Zero failures, errors or skips.
- Both phone Kotlin compiles, Kotlin lint and the staged-content guard passed. The retained proof checkout used the exact candidate Android sources, shared fixture and matching build inputs over frozen root tooling.
- The original test files and build inputs match the previously passing [baseline CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45911100427).
- Independent review and full committed-range local ClawSweeper review found no actionable correctness or security issues (confidence 0.94). [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45923020797) passed.
- No physical-device run was performed for this unit-test fixture consolidation.

## Delivery

Merged the unchanged reviewed head as `52c50a016213a70b56a8c37c3fffa1c4b6a5897f`. [Native completion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206280#issuecomment-7209123700) is verified; the generated PR checkout is removed and the authored source/proof checkouts are retained. Transient shared-cache contention and GitHub read failures were resolved without changing source, dependencies or credentials.

prs.title: feat: let doctor --fix tell when its startup repairs have nothing to do
prs.body:
Related: #204775

## What Problem This Solves

Every `openclaw doctor --fix` stops a healthy Gateway before it knows whether any step has work. The plan in #204775 makes that stop conditional, but only once every step can say "nothing to do" and mean it. This is step 4: the startup steps inside the stop (state database repair, database migrations, runtime checks) still reported the default `work`, so a later conditional stop could never skip them.

## User Impact

None yet. Every `--fix` still stops the Gateway and runs every step. With `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE=1`, these steps now report their real decision:

| Step | Healthy install (4 GiB agent database) | With real work |
|---|---|---|
| `state-database-repair` | `pending=none check=owner`, 7 to 10 ms | `pending=work` (mode 0644, orphan delivery row), and the repair still runs |
| `runtime-checks` | `pending=none check=owner`, 17 to 50 ms | `pending=work` (unusable deletion journal row), and the quarantine still runs |
| `database-migrations` | `pending=undecidable check=owner`, under 1 ms (see below) | `pending=work` (pending agent schema migration), and the migration still runs |
| `config-flow` | unchanged, `pending=work check=default` | unchanged |

## Why This Change Was Made

Each check lives with its step's owner and calls the predicates the step acts on, so the trace and the write cannot disagree. Contract for every check: no writable open, no file creation, no database copy, no lock. A check that throws counts as undecidable, which counts as work.

- **State database repair** (`state/openclaw-state-db-repair-pending.ts`). The existing `needsOpenClawStateDatabaseSchemaRepair` answers a different question (schema version and legacy shapes, for the backup and `state-schema` steps) and copies the database under an updater's capture. The new check opens the live file read-only and decides from what the index and readability scopes act on: broadened file modes (the same mode comparison `ensureOpenClawStatePermissions` skips on), a quarantine or recorded open failure, the integrity check the repair runs (quick check, or the full scan's damaged-index plan under `--full-integrity-check`), the dangling Skill Workshop review index, orphan task delivery rows, and the registry key the repair asserts first. The repair now calls the shared `hasRecordedStateDatabaseDamage` and `classifyStateDatabaseIntegrity`, and `hasOpenClawStatePermissionDrift` shares the target list with `ensureOpenClawStatePermissions`.
  - It cannot decide, and reports undecidable: PostgreSQL, an updater's migration capture or an artifact-preserving read (both would need a copy), and a WAL store no connection holds open, because a read-only open creates the `-wal` and `-shm` files (`readOnlyOpenWouldCreateSqliteSidecars`). Ownership refusals are not checked; they are preconditions, not work.
  - What the quick check cannot see, neither can the quick repair: a damaged index key needs `--full-integrity-check` in both (test "decides damaged index keys").
- **Database migrations** (`doctor-heartbeat-migration-backup.ts`). `checkDoctorMigrationBackupsPending` uses the step's own gates: a pending, refused or indeterminate store in the prepared preflight, `needsSharedStateMigrationBackup` (now the backup's gate too), an automatic heartbeat repair, and `needsHeartbeatMigrationBackup` (now the heartbeat backup's gate). It reads live stores (`withLiveStateReads`), never copies.
  - **Why it is undecidable inside the stop.** The heartbeat predicate reads each agent database. Once the Gateway stops, nothing holds the agent store open and its sidecars are gone, so the read would create them. Beside a serving Gateway (where step 6 will run the checks) the sidecars exist and the check decides; the unit test holds the store open as the Gateway does and gets `none`. Making it decidable under the stop needs an immutable read path through the agent read owner; I left that for step 6 rather than widen this PR.
- **Runtime checks** (`doctor-health-startup.ts` composes owners): the deletion journal (`checkDoctorAgentDeletionJournalPending`, the repair's gates plus the rows quarantine reads via the now-exported `readAgentDeletionJournalRecoverySource`), Control UI assets (`checkUiProtocolFreshnessPending`, the same detector and the prompter's auto-approve rule), the Bun launcher (planning split from the repair) and the pnpm launcher (`hasPublishedPnpmLauncherRepairWork`, the read-only half of the repair). Source install notes, plugin runtime links, NOCOW inspection and startup hints only print notes. The pnpm launcher repair was written by us (#201735, #203447), not by the updater owner, so it got a check too. A stale launcher owned by another account still reports work although the repair refuses it; that over-reports, never under-reports.
- **Config flow stays at the default.** I enumerated its write sites from source (preflight, flow body and `runDoctorRepairSequence`). About 50 sites write conditionally. These have no read-only detector:
  - Sites that open or lease on every run: the state schema step in doctor mode, which bypasses `needsOpenClawStateDatabaseSchemaRepair`; the media persistence lease and registry `last_seen_at`; the cold navigation lease; the post-core plugin convergence lease; plugin source capture directories; and the Tailscale profile migration's writable open.
  - Repairs whose plan exists only inside the function: legacy auth profile stores, the auth profile import, configured plugin installs, skill workshop retirement and ACP metadata.
  - Plugin-defined doctor migrations.

  Step 3 measured that these write no store bytes on a clean run. A `none` answer still needs a detector per site, and several of those depend on network or plugin code. Composing only the existing detectors (`detectLegacyStateMigrations`, `collectCronCodexRuntimePolicyTargetsReadOnly`, `detectLegacyExecApprovals` and about 20 others) would be wrong in the "none" direction, so the flow keeps `check=default`. The site-by-site inventory goes in the step 4 note on #204775.

The first CI run also flagged one uncommented type assertion in the permission drift helper; it is gone.

No schema, stored field, config option, protocol, dependency, retention or permission change.

## Update behavior

No update-path change. A published updater that runs Doctor on this build runs the same repairs in the same order. Under an updater's migration capture every new check reports undecidable, so nothing could be skipped there later either.

## Evidence

**Cells: Linux, systemd user Gateway, npm install of a pack under an unpublished version, 4.4 GB agent database (3.3 MB state database) under 1 MiB/s of writes, `/readyz` probed every 250 ms.** Base is `main` at `fcc9a0648c2`; head is `f720994f8f1` (this PR's first commit). Each doctor cell runs `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes` three times on a healthy install. Each guard cell then seeds real work while the Gateway serves (state database mode 0644, an orphan `task_delivery_state` row, an unusable deletion journal row for the reserved `openclaw` agent) and runs `doctor --fix` twice.

| | base `fcc9a0648c2` | head `f720994f8f1` |
|---|---|---|
| `state-database-repair`, healthy | `work check=default` | `none check=owner` (6.9 to 9.7 ms) |
| `runtime-checks`, healthy | `work check=default` | `none check=owner` (17 to 50 ms) |
| `database-migrations`, healthy | `work check=default` | `undecidable check=owner` (under 1 ms) |
| Outage, three healthy runs | 41.6 / 41.9 / 38.4 s | 44.9 / 41.9 / 41.9 s |
| Guard: seeded work | repaired (mode 600, orphan recovered, journal quarantined) | same repairs, traced `work check=owner` |
| Guard: next clean run | `work check=default` | `none check=owner` |
| Guard outage, settle / work / clean | 38.8 / 39.4 / 36.1 s | 40.6 / 41.6 / 40.3 s |

The outage difference (about 1 to 3 s) is larger than the checks' own cost (under 60 ms in total). Host load was 13 at the start of the head doctor cell and about 5 at the start of the base one, so I read it as host noise. Nothing is skipped yet. The checks' cost depends on the state database (quick check) and on the agent database's `heartbeat_outcomes` rows, not on the agent database file size, so at 10 GiB I expect the same tens of milliseconds. That is an estimate; I did not run a 10 GiB cell.

Recordings replay the raw cell logs.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An initial New Session render error can leave the panel stuck on Retry when the Gateway connects while automatic recovery is checking whether the page is reachable. The connection succeeds and the document returns HTTP 200, but the pending reload loses its connection authority.

## User Impact

The existing automatic recovery can finish during normal startup. Persistent errors still get only one automatic reload per tab, Retry can restore the composer, and an already usable draft remains protected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the connection handle across the first fresh hello when no bootstrap credentials need retirement. The existing credential owner tracks that one-time transition. Later hellos, reauthentication, bootstrap retirement, and stale builds still replace the handle and invalidate pending work; the reload guards remain intact.

The browser regression holds the real document probe across the normal deferred Gateway handshake, then verifies reload, Retry, and session creation. Owner tests cover the distinct authority transitions.

## Evidence

- Before the fix: the held-probe browser case observed the same client and credentials but a different connection handle; HTTP 200 succeeded and the reload wait timed out. The owner regression failed the first-hello case while all five cancellation controls passed.
- After the fix: 74 Gateway observer/authentication tests and all six New Session browser scenarios passed. The bundled production UI build passed.
- Final native staged checks passed typechecks, lint, formatting, size limits, and other guards. The aggregate remains red only for three existing unused exports: `readUpdateDatabaseEngineConfig`, `DoctorContributionPending`, and `formatUpdateSnapshotCapacity`. The exact same export scan reproduced all three on unchanged base `56ac8695558f16520dc00a53d60dd45ec09456d2` with the same installed dependencies.
- Autoreview of base `56ac8695558f16520dc00a53d60dd45ec09456d2` to final head `d9ca01f2b3ec9e7c847580d1b8186f2a3e5ed635` reported no actionable P0–P2 findings. No checks, timeouts, or assertions were relaxed.
