prs.title: fix(gateway): parent prompt cache misses when a subagent settles
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/195328

## What Problem This Solves

A subagent completion must retain the parent conversation’s skill-library presentation while losing the human requester’s execution authority. Reconstructing that presentation only from a live grant or process memory leaves the Gateway without a durable record after restart.

## User Impact

Conversations retain their skill-library tool shape across human and completion turns, including a listing recorded by the first chat. Personal-library calls still require a current human requester. Ordinary unsandboxed Workshop access remains available; sandbox and expired-authority restrictions remain enforced.

This changes security-sensitive authority handling. **Fresh maintainer security approval is required on the final head before merge.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing session entry owns two bounded presentation facts (`multipleProfiles` and `defaultTarget`). The Gateway reads them through the session worker and commits them through the canonical session writer. First-chat creation records them atomically with the new session row; an earlier patch-only write had no row to update.

The conflict port uses current main’s shared `src/agents/stable-skill-authoring.ts` for CLI and embedded runs. It preserves main’s `expired: true` semantics, transcript-followup expiry, and abort/cron/native-app lifecycle behavior. It does not restore the removed CLI-only helper. Current main’s turn-local deferred directory remains separate from the cached system directory.

Original contributor work and ancestry by @AmoghAtreya are preserved. The maintainer updates port that work to the current owners and cover first-chat persistence. Release-note context: keep skill-library presentation stable without granting background personal-library access. There is no new config/default or SQLite schema version; the optional field uses the existing session `entry_json` store.

## Evidence

Reviewed and tested head: `a4d57cb71504a4d19b0070e29c398763b9e24017`.
Frozen main baseline: `cf9a9839e03ba76b526d9f61fe453e3ccc8a93a9`.
All execution used sanitized AWS machines with no instance profile, Tailscale, credential hydration, or forwarded secrets. Contributor code was not executed locally.

- **54 focused tests passed:** Gateway first-chat persistence and storage reopen, human→settle→human presentation, requester/profile/scope/role revocation, shared CLI/embedded expired-grant behavior, plugin-tool selection, Workshop sandbox denial and ordinary unsandboxed access, and prefix siblings.
- **Formatting, targeted lint, core typecheck, full build, and whitespace checks passed** on that head.
- **Real Gateway + fixture provider behavior assertions passed:** seven parent provider requests retained the same prefix and cache identity through first human chat, actual spawned-child completion, and Gateway restart. The completion’s personal-library call was refused; the subsequent human call returned the library listing.
- **Published stable upgrade passed:** `openclaw@2026.11.2` created a real session; candidate `doctor --fix --non-interactive` exited 0; the stored entry remained byte-identical and retained its session ID and label; the candidate Gateway listed it after restart. The new optional field was absent in the stable row. This proof covers that session row, not an old transcript fixture.
- Fresh scoped autoreview found no P0–P2 source issue.

### Retained failure and follow-up

The Gateway behavior assertions passed, but its suite **failed during teardown** with `shutdown step failed (gateway close): Plugin openai is retiring`. A separate fresh machine at frozen main reproduced the same failure and stack (`src/plugins/plugin-instance.ts:793` → `src/gateway/server-shutdown.ts:210`). No checkout, HOME, or compiler cache was shared between the two heads. This is a named follow-up for Gateway/OpenAI plugin retirement after restart; it is not reported as a green suite or used to waive security/review gates.

Main also refused the internal call using its existing expired-grant message. The baseline’s different refusal text is not evidence of a cache regression. The port preserves that existing boundary while adding durable Gateway presentation.

<details>
<summary>Exact proof receipts and review scope</summary>

- Candidate scoped gates and Gateway trace: https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_e1de1ec3b641f00fdac491cfb9632b51
- Successful corrected stable-upgrade fixture: https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_e3d4e148d5929eb47859d5f2c00e64e0
- Isolated main teardown comparison: https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_1d9d30976efeb8cef7052aaefac30597

```json
{"head":"a4d57cb71504a4d19b0070e29c398763b9e24017","gateway":{"parentRequests":7,"stablePrefixAssertions":"passed","firstHumanListing":true,"internalPersonalRefused":true,"restartHumanPersonalAllowed":true,"suiteTeardown":"failed; matching isolated-main signature"},"stableUpgrade":{"baseline":"2026.11.2","doctorExit":0,"sessionIdPreserved":true,"entryBytesPreserved":true,"candidateGatewayListsSession":true,"entrySha256":"107d5cb655e5cce9fd2bb1428338b99ddcfccd6c00842193a7ce96e542bc6829"}}
```

The first upgrade attempt stopped before session creation because the disposable fixture used a noncanonical device-identity path. It was corrected to the existing `client/credentials.sqlite` contract; only the upgrade proof was rerun on the unchanged candidate and its already completed build.

Scope reviewed: Gateway dispatch/session creation → prepared authoring → worker-owned session facts → tool construction/invocation; shared CLI/embedded helper; transcript followup; plugin-tool and Workshop siblings; session parser/reserved slots; relevant history and current main. Direct Codex dependency inspection covered `codex-rs/protocol/src/dynamic_tools.rs:13`, `codex-rs/app-server/src/dynamic_tools.rs:16`, `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs:1100`, and `codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:810` in the sibling source checkout. This is source-contract evidence, not a Codex runtime test claim.

Production: +229/-20 (net +209). Tests: +383/-7 (net +376). The production growth provides durable presentation ownership, guarded persistence, and first-chat atomic creation; it does not add another runtime store or restore the obsolete helper.

### Terminal hosted CI and native preparation

- Exact-head CI run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44479122294, **attempt 2**, completed with **69 successful, 2 failed, and 26 skipped jobs**. `security-fast` and all seven secondary workflows passed. CI is not green.

Its reconstructed tree matches; its introduced patch is byte-identical to the frozen-main candidate patch. The failed aggregate is accounted for by that Visitor shard.
- Named follow-up for the owner of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201334: align Visitor assertions with admitted-run lifetime while retaining caller-current, renewal-denial, before/after-commit, and eventual-cleanup coverage. This PR preserves main's product semantics and carries no unrelated Visitor test changes.
- Native preparation completed on the exact head with `github_pending` evidence; no new push was needed. Fresh Claw review reports no actionable findings or remaining code rank-up move: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195378#issuecomment-6726374867.

**Fresh human maintainer security approval on `a4d57cb71504a4d19b0070e29c398763b9e24017` remains mandatory.** The inherited-CI evidence does not supply that approval. No merge has been requested.

prs.title: fix(talk): retain chat-backed consult prompts in model history
prs.body:
Root cause: src/gateway/talk/handlers/client.ts:475 (origin/main b402f04fac, unchanged since merge base 2c4413a6ab) records the generated consult prompt of talk.client.toolCall with transcript { display: false, excludeFromContext: true }. The prompt is sent to the model in its own turn, then dropped from every later request, so each later consult/typed turn rewrites history at that prompt and the provider cache misses from there. #199538 (81ca4f4d71) already removed the same flag for native consults (client-agent-runtime.ts); the PR drops it on the chat-backed route and keeps display:false.

Closes #179236

## What Problem This Solves

#199538 made native Talk consultations retain their hidden generated consult input in model history, so later requests keep the already-dispatched prefix. The chat-backed consult route (`talk.client.toolCall` in `src/gateway/talk/handlers/client.ts`, used by browser providers such as Google Live and by app relay sessions) still records the same hidden prompt with `excludeFromContext: true`. Every later consult in that session therefore rewrites history at the earlier prompt and misses the prompt cache from that point on.

## User Impact

Later voice questions on browser/relay Talk keep the cached conversation prefix, the same as native Talk after #199538. The generated prompt stays hidden from chat, exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

This applies the contract #199538 already adopted for native consults to the remaining route: hide from chat, retain in model history.

- `client.ts`: drop `excludeFromContext` from the chat-backed consult transcript options.
- `index.test.ts`: expect the new transcript options.
- `server.talk-consult-history.test.ts` (the #133855 regression test): the generated input stays out of chat history and Markdown, carries no exclusion flag, and appears exactly once in reopened model context, mirroring the assertion #199538 added for the direct-call case.
- Docs: one sentence now covers both native and chat-backed consults.

Existing stored records are not rewritten.

## History

This PR was originally a larger change (retention plus speech ordering and preview filtering) waiting on the retention decision. #199538 settled that decision for native consults, so the branch is now rebuilt on current `main` with only the remaining route. The earlier version is kept on `khensthoth:fix/talk-consult-prompt-cache-v1-backup`. Live observations from the original version (22 Oct) showed 96–98% cached input on follow-up Gemini Talk consults with this route fixed.

## Evidence

Upstream CI on this head is waiting for workflow approval. Run on `d7bb6636` in a clean `node:24-bookworm` container (Linux, Node 24.22, `CI=true`, prompt-cache assertion on):

- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the changed files: clean.
- `index.test.ts`, `client-native-actions.test.ts`, `client-native-control.test.ts`: 113/113 passed.
- `relay-consult-adoption.regression.test.ts`: 9/9 passed.
- `server.talk-consult-history.test.ts`: 20/22. The two failures (`keeps host-authenticated node approval cancellation`, public callback false/true) fail identically on unmodified `main` at `2c4413a6` in the same container (`SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: approval cannot safely bind this interpreter/runtime command`), so they come from that environment, not this change. In one earlier full-file run `isolates registered Talk replay across authenticated callers` hit its 10 s `agent.wait` timeout; it passed on rerun, alone and in the full file, with the assertion on and off.

prs.title: fix: move ended one-time automations to run history
prs.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Do not land.** Still in progress and under discussion. Talk to @vyctorbrzezowski.

## What Problem This Solves

A one-time automation that failed or had unconfirmed delivery stayed in the Paused list, even though nothing was scheduled. Over time those entries accumulated, and Run history did not offer a way to try the task again.

## User Impact

- After its final attempt, a one-time automation leaves the list whether it succeeds, fails, or has unconfirmed delivery. Failure notices point to Run history rather than telling people to re-enable an ended job. Transient retries and explicitly scheduled next checks still work.
- Administrators with unrestricted run-history access can select **Retry** on eligible failures in **Automations → Run history**. Retry starts a fresh attempt, not a delivery replay; check uncertain delivery before retrying. Jobs with authority tied to their original identity aren't automatically recreated.
- Doctor reports the old entries it finds. On repair it backs up cron state, moves recognized ended failures to Run history, and preserves the existing run or reconstructs the last recorded outcome if older history has expired. When an explicit keep-after-run or cleanup policy has no faithful conversion, Doctor keeps the definition paused and explains why. It does not rerun anything. The retired option is removed from the CLI, tool, protocol, and editors.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scheduler records history and retains the definition privately in the same transaction that removes the ended job from the list. This lets Retry look up the original run without putting the job back in Paused or returning its definition in the history response. The implementation reuses the existing history retention, scheduler admission, and Doctor backup, rather than introducing a separate archive service.

Related automation cleanup PRs may overlap in schedule settlement, Doctor cron repair, Gateway/agent tool schemas, and the Control UI automation editor. Those cleanups are not folded into this change.

## Evidence

I merged main `2ab7b31a13d95` without rebasing and fast-forwarded the verified repairs to `52aac6873c4668462d3f313575bc1eca30c603b6`. Both new commits include the daniel-lxs co-author trailer.

I preserved running background commands and held legacy cleanup policies for backed-up Doctor conversion. Local checks also exposed and reproduced three additional defects: the reader worker discarded the private Retry view, no-prompt Doctor skipped SQLite-only legacy policies, and alert delivery receipts could not settle after a definition was retired. I fixed those at their existing owners.

I ran the final focused checks locally with Node 26.12.1:

| Check | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Cron lifecycle, recovery, settlement and persistence | 466 | 0 | 0 |
| Gateway Retry, delivery and invitation boundaries | 134 | 0 | 0 |
| CLI | 64 | 0 | 0 |
| Doctor migration and ownership | 34 | 0 | 0 |
| UI unit tests | 48 | 0 | 0 |
| Control UI browser flows with a mock Gateway | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| Plugin contracts, state migration, ownership and scenario fixtures | 67 | 0 | 0 |
| **Total across 50 test files** | **815** | **0** | **0** |

All 10 targeted production/test typecheck graphs passed. Production lint, changed-file formatting, the normal pre-commit line-cap gate, and `git diff --check` passed. The complete cron selection passed after the cross-store fixture assertion was corrected; the unchanged 36-case authority matrix passed again after its fixture-only extraction.

The simplify pass kept the scheduler, history and Doctor owners. I updated terminal assertions to read retained outcomes, changed terminal-write fault injection to exercise deletion, and preserved the delivery, authority, restart and no-replay checks. Existing Doctor ownership projection and authority scenario data moved to their existing helper modules to satisfy file-size gates. Against merged main: production +758/-242 lines; tests/fixtures +736/-683; other files +25/-35.

**Still draft and under the existing landing hold.** I posted no PR comments and requested no re-review. No clean independent review is claimed; the earlier local review failed its read-only sandbox preflight. Full CI, PostgreSQL/Windows/native lanes, and the separate runtime/update proof were not run here.

The separate VM work must cover **v2026.11.5**, **9.x extended-stable**, and **10.x** updates to this head, preserving settings/history, legacy keep policies before Doctor and queued/running cases, plus the old updater round trip. Full original-review base-red/head-green runtime evidence remains pending.

prs.title: fix(macos): treat failed port inspection as unknown, not free
prs.body:
Closes #190152

## What Problem This Solves

macOS `PortGuardian` asks `lsof` which process listens on a port, and `lsof` can fail in ways that say nothing about the port: missing from `PATH`, exceeding the 5 s deadline (a wedged SMB/NFS mount), or exiting non-zero for another reason. The old code folded all of those into "no listener", so every caller read the port as free: `gateway install --force` / launchd repair overwrote a hand-started Gateway, `ManagedNodeGatewayMigration` took custody, and child start skipped attach and spawned a second Gateway ("Gateway stopped after five failed starts").

## Why This Change Was Made

A missing answer is not a negative answer, so `PortGuardian.inspect(port:)` returns `PortInspection`: `.free` (lsof ran, exited 1, no diagnostic), `.owned(Descriptor)`, or `.unknown` (timeout, pre-flight failure, unexpected exit, unparsable output). `lsof` runs with `-b` so a stalled mount cannot block the probe, and the call goes through `ShellExecutor.runDetailed` because the old `run` discarded the exit code.

`lsof -b` writes its own `avoiding readlink(...)` / `WARNING: can't stat()` notes to stderr even on a clean no-match, so "stderr is empty" cannot identify a clean probe; any other `lsof:` diagnostic is a failed probe. Every consumer handles `.unknown` conservatively: persistence ensure returns `.skipped`, repair withholds evidence, migration preserves the existing owner, attach never spawns a child on an uninspected port, and Onboarding says the port could not be checked. Everything lives under `apps/macos/`: no shared package, CLI or protocol surface, and no `Codable` type changed.

## User Impact

* Failing probes no longer replace, migrate, or double-start a Gateway; the app waits for the next probe.
* Healthy machines are unchanged: a successful `lsof` with no match is still `.free`.
* Diagnostics and Onboarding report that the port could not be inspected instead of "nothing is listening".
* Accepted trade-off: an inconclusive probe during migration records one failed attempt and retries next launch instead of stealing a running service.

## Evidence

Throwaway workflow on hosted `macos-26` (Xcode 26.6, Swift 6.3.3), proof head `7f95387`, base `main` `f91f580b7f`. One unrelated pre-existing build break is patched in the jobs only (`ChatMediaVideoAttachment.swift` uses `VideoPlayer` without an availability guard); it is not in this diff.

```
Build complete! (692.57s)                                          # swift build --build-tests
✔ Test run with 8 tests in 1 suite passed after 5.845 seconds.     PortGuardianDiagnosticsTests
✔ Test run with 92 tests in 1 suite passed after 26.338 seconds.   GatewayProcessManagerTests
0/440 files require formatting, 6 files skipped                    swiftformat (0 errors)
```

### The shipped app-hosted start, with a real broken `lsof`

`app 1` calls `startAppHostedGateway` (the function this PR changes) on a real `GatewayProcessManager`; only the supervisor launcher is replaced, so the launch count is observed rather than inferred. It reaches the port decision and publishes the new unknown-port failure with **zero** child launches:

```
[proof-app] app 1 installation=managed hosting=service
[proof-app] app 1 shipped startup status: failed("Could not inspect port 18789 to identify its owner; health check failed: ...")
[proof-app] app 1 supervisor launches: 0 (active=false pid=nil)
```

`Could not inspect port ...` is the text this PR adds (`GatewayProcessManager.swift:962`); the pre-change probe collapsed the same fault into an empty listener list, which is why startup spawned.

### The real packaged app, Onboarding connection page

Every run below is a packaged `OpenClaw.app` started with `--attach-only`, a clean state dir and no `openclaw.json`, so Onboarding opens by itself. `lsof` resolves through `/usr/bin/env`, so putting a stub first on the app's `PATH` decides which `lsof` the shipped probe runs; the stub logs every invocation (`-b -nP -iTCP:18789 -sTCP:LISTEN -Fpcn`).

Rows below are OCR of the app window, lowercased.

Base (`main` `f91f580b7f`), scan fails — the page still promises the install:

```
on this mac recommended
private to this computer. installs and starts automatically.
```

Candidate, same binary (`sha256 1eb00eba931a…`), driven down both probe answers:

```
# lsof exits 1 with a diagnostic on stderr: the scan could not be trusted
on this mac recommended
could not check whether port 18789 is free. startup walts until it can.

# lsof exits 1 with no diagnostic: this is what an idle port returns
on this mac recommended
private to this computer, installs and starts automatically.
```

### A real latest-stable → candidate upgrade

`v2026.11.10`'s own CLI installs the Gateway service on one home; the candidate build then reads that state back.

```
v2026.11.10 gateway install --runtime bun --runtime-path <old>/bin/bun
Installed LaunchAgent: /Users/runner/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist

# the candidate reads that state back
"runtimeIntent": { "status": "known", "stored": true,
  "revision": "1bc195fdd5574fdc428cbdf21d22d26ab48967b02544cf82e62cff7801a4bad7",
  "pin": { "runtime": "bun", "path": "<old>/bin/bun" } }

PASS: LaunchAgent is byte-identical after the candidate ran
PASS: the pin store is byte-identical after the candidate ran
PASS: the candidate reports the same service intent   # 12/12 PASS
UPGRADE_FAIL=0
```

The old Gateway is up throughout (`Port 18789 is already in use. - pid 41167 runner: openclaw-gateway`), and the candidate reports the revision and pinned runtime the old build wrote.

### Not covered

The resume command is written by the app's own service install, so a CLI-driven upgrade cannot seed or check it; `app 3` covers it instead (`gatewayNodeResumeCommand` read back through a fresh `UserDefaults` instance). Upstream's `xcode-27` runner is unavailable to a fork, and every changed file is macOS-only.

prs.title: fix(mcp): bound unavailable server notices in each turn
prs.body:
Refs #192268 (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192268)

## What Problem This Solves

When several MCP servers are unavailable, their per-turn diagnostics can grow without a total limit in the model's prompt. An OAuth failure also receives a generic reachability or later-turn retry hint even though it waits for a credential change.

## User Impact

The assistant receives a deterministic, bounded summary of unavailable servers on the affected turn. It retains sign-in guidance from the diagnostic and gets accurate operator next steps. Additional failures are counted when they do not fit. No configuration or transcript migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prompt assembly boundary already owns the turn-scoped diagnostic projection. It now sorts the server notices and limits the **MCP diagnostic group** to 2,000 UTF-16 characters in both legacy and escaped model renderings, counting wrappers and the omission count. This is a group limit, not a byte limit or a cap on the entire runtime context. Server names are shortened before escaping so a long name cannot crowd out early sign-in guidance.

The shared next-step text stays outside truncated server data. `openclaw mcp status --verbose` describes configuration; `openclaw mcp probe <name>` performs a live check; `openclaw mcp doctor <name>` helps with shared OAuth credentials. Per-requester sign-in guidance remains in the producer diagnostic. The existing log-once/backoff and recovery owners are unchanged. Production delta: +58 lines (67 added, 9 removed); tests are counted separately. The positive delta establishes the aggregate prompt-budget boundary and preserves actionable guidance.

## Evidence

- Signed source commits `360181751843a66db9830104ef070fc6fd5b7f38` and `e9547981dacf9fee0ae771ef5d4a674c0e30d1be`; independent exact-commit and lint-fix diff reviews found no remaining actionable source issue. `git show --check` passes.
- Added focused coverage for deterministic order, both rendered size limits, omission count, a single long diagnostic, a long escaped server name with OAuth sign-in text, healthy catalog, and turn-scoped version 3/4 recovery without transcript or system-prompt rewrite.
- Focused tests have not been separately confirmed; local type/lint checks have **not run**. This managed checkout has no qualified `node_modules` link. Remote proof stopped before allocation: the configured tooling root has `@openclaw/fs-safe` 0.27.1 while this source requires 0.28.2. No shared install was changed.
- The prior draft CI run at `3601817` found two owned array lint errors, corrected by `e954798`; other failed jobs showed gateway cleanup and Knip unused export failures outside this diff, with attribution still pending. The new head still needs CI proof.
- This draft needs exact-head hosted CI, including focused tests and the build/check jobs, before it can be marked ready or merged. Issue #192268 remains open for the separate operator-visible policy question.

## What Problem This Solves

Test suites repeat fixture labels, counts, callback wiring and optimization details alongside functional coverage. This maintainer-requested batch retires selected ordinary assertions to reduce test maintenance, with an explicit record of the coverage being given up.

## User Impact

Internal test maintenance only; production behavior is unchanged by this diff. The tradeoff is deliberate loss of unique ordinary presentation, shape, permutation and implementation-detail oracles. The functional keepers below cover the same module or area; they are not claimed to replace every deleted case or assertion.

The selection uses assertion value rather than uniqueness alone. prs.title: feat: review dictated paragraphs and lists before applying them
prs.body:
Related: #205634

## What Problem This Solves

People dictating paragraphs or shopping lists into the Control UI currently receive a text transcript and must manually recreate its structure. Treating every occurrence of “bullet” or “new paragraph” as a command would also corrupt ordinary discussion, quotes, and code. This contribution adds an explicit, reviewable formatting path while retaining the current recognized-text behavior by default.

## User Impact

Users can opt into **Interpret explicit structure (English)** in the existing microphone controls. After Stop, they can compare semantic, plain, and original-text previews, confirm ambiguous paragraph commands, and apply an eligible result or copy it for recovery. Formatting never continues into Send. The draft remains editable in Explicit mode; editing it invalidates the captured insertion target instead of allowing an older result to overwrite it.

The initial grammar supports paragraphs, line breaks, ordered and unordered lists, and nesting up to the proposed depth of three. Explicit item numbers, order, quantities, negation, names, protected strings, and literal marker discussion stay source-backed. Headings, tables, inferred Suggest structure, attachments, spreadsheet operations, and document automation are outside this initial scope.

| Representation | Supported boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Plain text | An unchanged direct-dictation field whose actual capabilities support safe multiline text and an existing undoable adapter; otherwise review/copy. |
| Markdown (`commonmark-0.31.2-lists`) | The built-in Markdown composer with an empty draft or the entire captured draft selected. Partial insertion is refused because surrounding Markdown could reinterpret the result. |
| Rich preparation (`safe-blocks-v1`) | Allowlisted paragraph/list HTML and semantic preview only. **No native/external rich insertion adapter is qualified by this PR.** |
| Unknown, stale, or revoked capability | Readable review/copy recovery; no guessed target and no automatic fallback write. |

**This PR must remain a draft.** See Evidence for the checks that ran and the remaining qualification and maintainer decisions.

Rollback is the existing mode control: choose **Preserve recognized text**. Absence, malformed policies, unsupported versions, and Preserve normalize to the previous behavior. The version-1 Explicit opt-in is stored in the existing Gateway-scoped browser preference record; it is not synchronized through server `ui.prefs`. Disabling it preserves drafts, speech-provider selection, unrelated preferences, and message history.

## Why This Change Was Made

One bounded semantic document drives plain text, Markdown, and allowlisted HTML. Its validator checks source coverage and order, consumed-marker reasons, source/grapheme ranges, protected content, cycles, node kinds, and resource bounds before any representation is used. Markdown is checked with independent `markdown-it` parsing; rich output is checked with `parse5`. No generated HTML or remote resource is trusted, and spoken URLs are never fetched by formatting.

Live triage did not establish an accepted physical M11 parent to stack on. This PR therefore implements the minimal private lifecycle prerequisite in the **existing** dictation owner/session: immutable capture policy and source revision, generation and deadline eligibility, current target/selection/capability, cancellation, and truthful delivery receipts. It does not claim the wider M11 proposal is complete. Optional M01/M02/M03/M05/M08 integrations are not implemented as new renderer-local rewrites. The formatter adds no speech/model request, durable transcript store, clipboard manager, automation owner, or public RPC.

Related parallel proposals now published are [M01 punctuation #205788](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205788) and [M02 cleanup #205789](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205789). Both remain drafts; neither establishes an accepted M11 parent. Their shared owner/policy boundaries require consolidation and enabled-together proof before joint acceptance. This contribution does not claim that integration.

Preparation and insertion are separate. Main, Side chat, and New Session reuse their existing draft owners and editor history boundary. An attempted indivisible edit produces `not-committed`, `committed`, or `outcome-unknown`; uncertainty cannot trigger a plain-text retry. Rich preview success does not qualify an external rich editor. A proposed 2,500 ms Explicit finalization deadline cannot turn partial recognition into a complete formatted result.

The implementation is cohesive across recognition finalization, validation, preview, settings, and reviewed placement. A renderer-only slice would leave the required lifecycle and user recovery behavior unimplemented. The stateless helper extraction keeps lifecycle authority with the existing owner. Test growth is +2,842 LF lines against the integrated `main` base, with a 2,442-line allocation request above the 400-line default. Separate suites cover independent parser/source invariants, owner races, settings retention, real owner/adapter/component boundaries, submission guards, and the canonical browser fixture; the test file cap remains unchanged.

## Evidence

### Current draft head `b682e77091c8be85cee269051ad6b828e4b2b2a0`

**Local product checks passed; OpenClaw-hosted execution is still pending.** Published by @roboclaw-bot without rewriting the existing branch. GitHub’s commit metadata matches tested/staged tree `8239079bbd317f4b2bba732d528407a5b00e7bc6`. Its parent `97fb1ba1ed400fbc3a7c2b11a62b6c654a6b18ee` is the separately measured product tree `2200bf6975c983f5c1dca728e77a8cf6b202b67a`. The only change in the current head is sharing an identical Playwright context fixture across five browser cases; no product input changed. The bundled browser suite was rerun after that edit.

- **Unchanged paired production budget against `b7b81558906bd47c7c774d1d082169fced9c3922`: passed locally.** Chat boot JS gzip 1,337,214 → 1,337,278 B (+64 B, exactly the build-variance allowance; 21 requests on both); New Session 820,235 → 820,594 B (+359 B, below its 822,243 B cap; 17 requests on both); total CSS gzip 348,603 → 348,567 B (−36 B, below its 348,683 B cap). The paired checker exited 0 without a threshold or baseline change. It still prints its largest-CSS advisory; that inherited warning does not fail the paired check.
- **Bundled Chromium: 20/20 passed** across dictation and preferences reconnect (mock Gateway and synthetic STT). Cases cover keyboard opt-in with native menu radio rows, Finish when the visual status chunk fails to load, Preserve raw insertion, Side chat and New Session submission guards, stale/uncertain receipts, Apply and native Undo, and narrow/RTL controls.
- **Isolated real Gateway + local Vosk: passed** on the same product inputs. Chromium fake media supplied a recorded synthetic WAV; Vosk decoded 73,727 PCM samples. While the final transcript was held, Enter did not submit and Start stayed disabled. Markdown Apply replaced the captured range, native Undo restored the draft, and there were zero send RPCs. This was neither a physical microphone test nor cloud STT.
- **Focused local validation:** 193/193 tests across nine files, UI typecheck, controller guards, English i18n, targeted oxlint, stylelint and formatting. The final test-line check against `b7b81558906b` passed (+2,841 vs a 400-line allowance and the unchanged 2,442-line allocation).
- **Known limitation:** Finish is synchronous and usable if the visual status asset fails; listening/finalizing announcements are part of that asset and are unavailable in that failure case. A real screen reader was not exercised.
- **Runner handoff:** The author’s fork CI is disabled. No terminal approved OpenClaw-hosted run or usable Crabbox lease was obtained for this head. An OpenClaw maintainer can dispatch `gh workflow run ci.yml --repo openclaw/openclaw --ref main -f target_ref=b682e77091c8be85cee269051ad6b828e4b2b2a0` and confirm the job actually checked out this SHA. The custom Gateway/Vosk journey above is a separate replay, not claimed as standard workflow coverage.

![Final product tree: formatted list inserted into the captured draft without sending](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/096972d0-1f47-4a92-824e-c2b2e1a3872c)

### Historical draft head `c0a3a98a414d25cbe5dee873f9b39b511585d57a`

- **Exact-head real Gateway and Vosk: passed.** Production Chromium and an isolated OpenClaw Gateway ran from the published tree `9aa2f30514eeacdf7e5bbacf6b21f191238f4b76`. The browser trace observed audio append and close; it asserted zero `chat.send`, `sessions.dispatch`, and `sessions.companion.ask` requests. Source audio was a prerecorded synthesized WAV through Chromium fake media, not physical microphone input or cloud STT. Captured stdout matched the SHA-256 below:

  ```text
  Ready: isolated built Gateway
  Vosk decoded 73727 PCM samples; recognized: shopping list bullet milk next item eggs next item rice
  PASS New Session, real Gateway + Vosk: Stop, Enter blocked and Start disabled before transcript, semantic review, Apply, native Undo, no Send; browser fake media from prerecorded synthesized WAV.
  ```

- **Exact-head paired production bundle budget against upstream `b7b81558906b`: failed.** Both builds completed; Chat boot JS gzip 1,337,214 → 1,340,806 B (+3,592; 21 requests on both), New Session boot JS gzip 820,235 → 823,951 B (+3,716; 17 requests on both), total CSS gzip 348,603 → 349,111 B (+508; 348,683 B cap). Largest JS gzip also exceeded its cap. Upstream Chat was already over cap, but the branch adds bytes beyond the allowed 64 B build variance. Thresholds were unchanged.

**Published via @roboclaw-bot.** The previous branch head and the integrated upstream base are both ancestors. The published Git tree matches the final staged tree.

Integrated upstream `b7b81558906bd47c7c774d1d082169fced9c3922` without resolving any conflicts or rewriting the branch. The published repair uses the mounted preference snapshot instead of reading browser storage during render, does not emit a composer change for an idle cancellation, keeps the dictation browser fixture on the shared production bundle, and fixes the test-query types, lint errors and docs formatting.

- **Hosted CI is not qualified on this head.** The author disabled CI on the personal fork and asked to use OpenClaw’s approved upstream/secretless runners or an approved Crabbox lease. The earlier fork snapshot below is historical only; no terminal exact-head fork result is claimed.
- **Final-tree bundled browser: 19/19 passed** across the dictation and preferences-reconnect suites, 52.87 s. These use the production UI bundle and mock Gateway/synthetic STT; the real Vosk replay below is a different lane.
- **Focused local checks on prepared tree `9aa2f30514eeacdf7e5bbacf6b21f191238f4b76`:** 180/180 tests across eight files (formatter, dictation owners, New Session and composer siblings); scoped oxlint finished with no errors, and the upstream-relative test-line ratchet passed (2,833 net lines, 400 default + 2,442 allocated). UI app and hosted UI test typechecks, the CI private-server ownership guard, the Control UI controller guard, English i18n verification and docs lint passed in this repair series.
- **Real replay on prepared tree `227ff6f5f87541c40df696224a5610366d07eb54`:** an independently rerun production Chromium + isolated real Gateway + local Vosk journey produced the same captured output printed below, including 73,727 decoded PCM samples, blocked Enter and disabled Start during held finalization, confirmed list commands, Markdown Apply, native Undo and zero sends. That is the tree actually exercised; it precedes the final lint-only and fixture edits. The microphone was Chromium fake media from a synthesized WAV, not a physical device.

prs.title: feat: review dictation with optional punctuation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related: #205630.

Dictation users need an explicit choice between recognizer output and conservative punctuation, with a chance to review the result before inserting it. Technical strings, negation, numbers, existing draft text, and selected recipients must survive that process.

**This remains an incomplete implementation draft.** It integrates the proposed Control UI flow and repairs the reported submission bug, but does not claim full M01 acceptance, human design approval, real microphone/browser/accessibility qualification, or passing required CI. Keep the issue open.

## User Impact

The existing default is Off. Opting in adds original/refined review, explicit insertion, reprocessing of an unsent original, and target-scoped Undo.

| Setting | Implemented behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Off | Preserves the established capture and submission path. |
| Verbatim | Preserves recognizer-provided words, punctuation, and casing. It cannot restore acoustic words or marks already changed by the recognizer. |
| Automatic | With explicitly resolved `en-US`, changes only an eligible unprotected opening letter at the beginning of a field and an eligible missing final period. It does not infer internal sentences or rewrite grammar. |
| Explicit punctuation | Requires a separate enablement and a bounded spoken-mark grammar. Introduced `insert …` phrases are supported; the only bare shorthand is `hello comma <one plain word> period`. Ambiguous punctuation words remain text. |

Locale and policy are frozen before asynchronous capture work. Session locale takes precedence over an enabled profile and then the saved preference. Missing or unsupported locale/context, non-Latin input, and explicitly identified mixed-language input retain the original. Arbitrary Latin-script code switching is not detected or qualified. Only synthetic `en-US` fixtures have been qualified; no physical client or speech-provider combination is claimed as tested.

Finishing an opted-in capture stops for review. Side chat keyboard/form submission retains that decision even if cancellation retires the capture. Main chat keeps provisional captions out of menu/history/deferred-send actions while recording. Recording phase changes no longer invalidate their own frozen draft revision.

Approved insertion replaces the captured selection, including the insertion owner's spacing joins, as one isolated rich-editor edit. Untouched recipient identities survive. The native textarea fallback uses the existing mention binding for exact edit metadata and restoration during the existing Undo transaction. Identical-result insertion makes no edit. Unknown write outcomes are disclosed and not retried; Undo is retired when the field, editor, binding, or owning revision changes.

**Rollback:** choose Off or remove the preference. Subsequent captures use the established path, unrelated voice settings and committed draft text remain, and an already admitted utterance retains its frozen policy unless explicitly reprocessed. No automatic reversal of a committed edit is promised.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing capture, provider session, finalization, and commit queue remain authoritative. A private helper freezes the capture’s selected policy and bounded draft context, prepares a validated review, and ties the eventual insertion and Undo to the captured draft target. It does not add a plugin API.

The deterministic engine returns bounded edits at half-open UTF-16 offsets and validates ICU grapheme boundaries, original revision/schema identity, replayed output, protected strings, permitted edits, lexical coverage, and idempotence. Model confidence cannot bypass validation. It adds no provider/model call, punctuation request queue, transcript store, or cloud fallback. Translation, paraphrasing, spelling correction, number-word normalization, ordinary Talk response rewriting, and external-application insertion are outside this change.

Only a strict versioned browser preference is stored. Invalid/future values disable refinement visibly; unvalidated fields are dropped by the existing settings writer. The setting is excluded from Gateway preference synchronization. The new native metadata capability is owned by the existing textarea binding; it does not add a history manager or persistent transcript/recipient store. Existing whole-draft composer-task replacements retain their previous transaction path.

[The issue's automated review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205630#issuecomment-7178173319) and [formatting draft #205791](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205791) require a shared preparation/preference decision. Neither draft is an accepted M11 parent, and enabled-together compatibility has not been demonstrated. Maintainers still need to decide private versus plugin placement, preference ownership, initial client/locale qualification, and reference hardware. No public SDK/RPC/schema or retention approval is assumed.

## Evidence

- **Current branch:** [`a58e59097da0`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/commit/a58e59097da0089adf1a59ba6c86002a2f407bc5) (tree `46986ece5b94cfcfad805a8648ebc4ae96fc13e6`), still draft on the existing `feat/dictation-automatic-punctuation` branch. The bot pushed only fast-forwards: [`ab49be8eadbb`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/commit/ab49be8eadbb25ce11a962846c9f65e3bbb7daa1) removed unused plumbing, [`475b752c71c1`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/commit/475b752c71c1cacaf890710fe9ba9e8337fa1e18) repaired the Talk fixture, and [`a58e59097da0`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/commit/a58e59097da0089adf1a59ba6c86002a2f407bc5) removed the obsolete span-limit claim and a duplicate broad Talk assertion. The earlier [non-rewriting merge](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/commit/86523500deffce8402f1538c314b2aa5cbe83145) preserved `5d165f9` and integrated upstream `main` at `2fda93cf`.
- **Side chat P1 — source checked:** The [finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205788#issuecomment-7184969924) was reviewed at `1f701cf`. Source inspection confirms that keyboard/form submission retains the capture’s review decision through finalization and that a pending review blocks later submits. The branch includes focused regression cases; RoboClaw did not run them on the published head.
- **Released baseline — observed:** published OpenClaw `2026.11.10` (`6ea542f`), Chromium `158.0.8127.88`, real isolated Gateway and local Vosk. Chromium’s fake microphone played a prerecorded synthesized WAV; Vosk used a bounded English fixture vocabulary. Light mode and the exact Main chat and New Session drafts survived reload. Stable inserted “the spoken part” directly into an unsent Main chat draft with no review and no submit. This is stable-only evidence, not physical microphone proof.

**Before — OpenClaw 2026.11.10.** The dictated phrase is appended to an unsent draft; the model label is redacted.

![Stable Control UI: the words “the spoken part” appear in the unsent Main chat draft without a dictation review panel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/097b1473-d5c5-4cde-afbf-9fed8b8d6052)

- **Prior-head fork CI — verified for `47326763be2e`:** [CompleteDotTech/openclaw#11](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/pull/11) checked out GitHub merge `446c64b8`; Git readback confirms its source tree exactly matches this commit (the [fork comparator](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875230294/job/140100519309) is `47027a2`, not newer upstream `main`). [Build artifacts](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875230294/job/140101766454) and UI shards [1](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875230294/job/140101765302) and [3](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875230294/job/140101765334) passed; [UI shard 2](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875230294/job/140101765487) failed with 51 unhandled errors in the Talk test fixture because dictation settings could not read the theme settings. [Control UI performance](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875230294/job/140101766167) failed: Chat boot JS gzip **1,308.4 KiB** vs **1,305.2 KiB** cap (the comparison base was already at 1,336,500 B vs its 1,336,272 B cap; only 64 B growth is allowed); New Session **803.7 KiB** vs **803.0 KiB** cap. The check also reported total CSS gzip at 349,008 B vs a 348,683 B fixed ceiling. Values in KiB are rounded GitHub annotations. [Production types](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875230294/job/140101767991) passed (`pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, and `pnpm tsgo:extensions`); the [test-types shard](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875230294/job/140101768091) passed `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` and `pnpm tsgo:scripts`. Ordinary PR CI does not schedule the unused-file scan; it did not run here. These results are specific to the stated tree and are not real dictation or upgrade proof.
- **Current-head upstream CI — not run:** [OpenClaw PR checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205788/checks) at `a58e59097da0` contain metadata checks only; the [upstream CI workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bf298a53334aa01379f52e6fb4f87106f2743a4b/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L122-L129) skips build/test preflight for drafts. No further runs will be sourced from the fork. To keep the PR draft, an OpenClaw maintainer can use [upstream Actions → CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/workflows/ci.yml) from `main` with exact `target_ref=a58e59097da0089adf1a59ba6c86002a2f407bc5`, using ordinary manual validation (not `release_gate`). Verify the runner's checkout SHA and diff base before crediting build, UI tests, type checks, boot gzip/budgets, or dependency/unused-file outcomes. A scoped sanitized AWS Crabbox run is the alternative. Neither has been dispatched from this session; no current-head result is claimed.
- **Candidate browser/upgrade proof — pending:** Timothy's [local proof runbook](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/14d6e4b6-d83a-4d22-8d7d-7cc8b302ce0d) (`205788-local-proof-final.md`) covers the Side chat P1 red/green, same-profile upgrade, real browser/Gateway/transcription with keyboard and button flows in Main chat, Side chat, and New Session, accessibility, and redacted After screenshots. Those candidate receipts have not been supplied.
- **Cleanup and Talk fixture — source checked:** Removed the unused provenance callback, caller-injected spans, and context override with their dead UI, labels, tests, and documentation. Actual draft-derived context, intrinsic lexical protection, validated edits, stale-draft recovery, and Undo remain. The Talk tests now supply the existing theme-settings fixture and scope voice queries to the realtime voice picker, instead of including the new punctuation controls. Scoped source review and `git diff --check` passed; the Talk shard has not been verified on this head.
- **Readiness remains open:** Maintainers still need to decide private Control UI plus shared browser preference vs. a plugin contract (see #205630 and #205791) and the initial locale/client/reference hardware scope. The prior fork run measured both boot JS gzip overages and a CSS overage. The current head needs fresh measurement and, if still over, a verified fix or explicit maintainer acceptance. Thresholds were not changed. Keep the PR draft; request re-review after the requested current-head proof is attached.

<details>
<summary>Historical author-run component, build, and budget evidence (not current-head results)</summary>

### Historical receipt source and review

- Implementation base: `b48d578d023765ac86fe44d38d65cfac991ad03c`.
- Pushed head: [`4aafc9e62cc95cbc58e805c6ed6bae7ef15ae391`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/commit/4aafc9e62cc95cbc58e805c6ed6bae7ef15ae391).
- Tree: `dc3d533dc65207dd429a3af744e05f5182da8504`; parent `1f701cf7f53ddeed8d22ebc44d1e472f0b65e8e6`.
- Target: `openclaw/openclaw:main`, observed at `92d40cbd98217c6ccdef583ded341eab691d206f`. GitHub reports mergeable, still draft, with maintainer edits enabled.
- Fork branch: [CompleteDotTech/openclaw:feat/dictation-automatic-punctuation](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/tree/feat/dictation-automatic-punctuation).
- The authenticated Git Data tree matched the staged tree exactly; the non-forced, expected-head update was read back, fetched, and adopted into a clean local worktree. Final local checks recorded the parent HEAD plus staged-source hashes; `continuation/review-fixes/publication.json` binds every selected receipt to the identical pushed tree. Historical receipts retain their original heads.
- The open-PR author count, including drafts, was refreshed at 6 against the contribution limit of 20. This updates the existing PR; no other branch, issue, or PR was modified and no merge was performed.

The [hosted review at `1f701cf`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205788#issuecomment-7184969924) identified the Side chat P1. Its initiating-capture fix has a genuine failing/passing six-case component test, including cancellation and Off/false-finish behavior.

Expanded real-component proof then found and repaired Main chat's capture self-retirement and separate Enter/history preview promotion. prs.title: fix(android): pause idle gateway discovery without blocking consumers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android keeps scanning for local Gateways without an active consumer. Pausing discovery must not break background recovery, connected discovery browsing, or secondary Gateway connections.

## User Impact

Android can pause idle local scans. If the first connection to a saved Gateway is interrupted before an address is accepted, returning to the app can retry when the Gateway reappears. Stop cancels that pending retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stop idle NSD scans and retire their callbacks. Resume for a visible Discovered list or onboarding, foreground enabled secondary Gateways, and the initial saved discovered-route recovery. Rebuild local results on resume; accepted sessions retain their own reconnect address. When no address has been accepted yet, the foreground path waits for the saved Gateway's fresh address and retries once without overriding a newer Gateway action.

This preserves #104226's cold sticky-service recovery with foreground-only capabilities disabled, and #111932's foreground-only secondary operator sessions with device capabilities owned only by the focused Gateway. The refresh onto `main` keeps discovery eligibility tied to the existing Gateway connection state instead of restoring the duplicate flag removed in #202898.

## Evidence

- On the refreshed head `f4c26cfe`, all three `GatewayDiscoveryLifecycleTest` cases passed in an isolated Android Play JVM run, including reconnect on rediscovery and Stop canceling the pending retry. Kotlin lint on the conflict resolution and `git diff --check` passed. [Fresh hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45892044886) is separate from those local results.
- The reconnect regression timed out on `ccd5afac` and passed with the fix on `e618cb5d`. [Hosted CI on `e618cb5d`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45704308651) passed Play, third-party, and Wear unit suites, Kotlin lint, both Android Access jobs, and the required gate. That result predates the conflict resolution.
- No physical-device run on the refreshed head. The original device proof applies only to `dfcb5f99`.

prs.body:
Related: [original PR #192940](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192940). This is the bot-published replacement of that message-only change; the original PR remains open separately.

## What Problem This Solves

A worktree publication that reused an existing pull request told the user “Published,” even though that request did not push a commit or trigger CI.

## User Impact

When the Gateway confirms reuse, the conversation links to the existing PR and explicitly says this request pushed no new commit and triggered no CI run. Other successful results still link to the PR. There are no public receipt or protocol changes, migrations, or required user actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conversation notice uses the recorded source head, published head, and GitHub effect evidence from the worktree receipt. A recovered publication that pushed a commit still receives the ordinary PR notice. Publication execution and storage are unchanged.

## Evidence

This replacement reuses the patch-identical operator proof recorded in [#192940](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192940); the tests and independent review below were not rerun in this publication session.

- Three real-Git transcript regressions fail on the pinned base at the old “Published” notice and pass with the fix. Reuse keeps the existing commit and write count; both lost-response cases show the ordinary PR link.
- 156 focused tests passed across worktree, repository, personal publication, transcript reporting, readiness, and source/compiled protocol validation. The three regressions passed again after the final test-helper cleanup.

prs.title: fix: end voice calls when transcription cannot recover
prs.body:
Closes #206115. Thanks to @anmol0b for reporting the classic streaming failure.

## What Problem This Solves

A classic streaming Voice Call can stay connected after its transcription session permanently stops recognizing speech. The caller can keep talking without being heard.

## User Impact

When transcription cannot recover, Voice Call closes the affected media stream and lets the existing disconnect and hangup flow finish the call. Calls with recoverable transcription errors can keep listening after reconnecting.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcription owner reports an optional terminal disposition when it exhausts retries or deliberately shuts down after a permanent error. Voice Call uses that signal only while it still owns the media socket. The existing disconnect grace period continues to protect replacement streams.

## Evidence

- Two failing fixture checks reproduced the missing terminal signal and the missing media disconnect on the original source.
- 78 tests passed across the shared transcription socket, Voice Call media stream, and webhook suites. The loopback media fixture delivers a transcript after a recoverable error, then observes close code 1011 and one disconnect after terminal failure.
- 105 tests passed across the Talk relay and the five bundled transcription provider suites, including the terminal provider and transport controls.
- Core and extension-test type checks, targeted lint and formatting, the test-line budget, and independent read-only review passed.

prs.title: fix: find Chinese and Japanese words inside sentences in Knowledge search
prs.body:
Closes #205667

## What Problem This Solves

When Knowledge is the memory provider, `knowledge_grep` and the Knowledge page's search cannot find a Chinese or Japanese word that sits inside a sentence. Chinese and Japanese text has no spaces, so the whole sentence is indexed as a single word. Searching for `新加坡` returns nothing for a page that says `客户希望地理位置在新加坡`. Latin words written next to CJK text, like `NAS` in `按NAS方式`, are not found either. Agents then tell the user that nothing relevant is stored, even though the record exists.

## User Impact

- People who keep notes in Chinese or Japanese can find a word wherever it appears in a record. No spaces are needed, and the user does not have to do anything.
- In `all` and `phrase` modes, the CJK part of a query matches as an exact substring. This includes single characters. The same characters in a different order do not match: `坡新` does not find `新加坡`.
- Stored Markdown, hashes, citations and snippets stay byte-for-byte unchanged. Snippets show the original text, not the index form.
- Existing stores upgrade on their own. The keyword index is a rebuildable projection. Its tables move from `v1` to `v2`. The first search in each scope builds the `v2` tables and drops that scope's `v1` tables. No migration step or user action is needed.
- Cost applies only to CJK text. The CJK part of the index grows about 2.3×, and building the index for CJK text is about 5.6× slower than before the fix. Non-CJK text is indexed exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`node:sqlite` cannot register a custom FTS5 tokenizer (see #193815). The fix therefore keeps FTS5 `unicode61` and changes the text it indexes. Before a record is indexed, each Han, Hiragana or Katakana run is expanded into overlapping character bigrams, plus the run's last character as a unigram. Queries are expanded the same way:

- In `all` and `phrase` modes, a CJK term becomes a phrase of adjacent bigrams. This is exact-substring matching.
- In `any` mode, it becomes an OR of its bigrams.
- A single character uses an internal prefix. Every character starts some token, so single-character recall is complete. Users still cannot use prefix search: a `*` they type is treated as punctuation.

Highlight offsets are mapped from the index text back to the stored text, so snippets stay exact. The issue's evaluation on 348 real meeting passages compared unicode61, trigram, CJK unigram, CJK bigram and `Intl.Segmenter`. Bigram had complete exact-substring recall and zero false hits. Dictionary segmentation lost about 30% of exact substrings, and trigram cannot match two-character words. The change adds no dependencies.

### Differences from the issue's proposal

- **The last character of each CJK run is kept as a unigram.** The first proposal kept a unigram only for runs of one character. Keeping it for every run means every character starts some token, so single-character queries always find their match. It also lets a term that ends in CJK followed by Latin, such as `先按NAS`, require that the run ends there. The cost is one extra token per run.
- **Index-only folding.** Inside CJK runs, the index text is NFC-composed and combining marks are removed. This covers three cases:
  - **Decomposed kana:** unicode61 splits a token at U+3099/U+309A. Without folding, NFD `が` was indexed as `か`. A search for `か` then matched it by mistake, and NFC and NFD `が` did not find each other.
  - **Ideographic variation selectors:** `葛\u{E0100}城` matches `葛城`.
  - **CJK compatibility ideographs:** U+F900 `豈` matches the unified U+8C48, as the existing rule says canonically equivalent spellings must.

  Folding applies only to the index text. Stored bytes and snippets do not change.
- **The highlight bound counts stored bytes.** The 64 KiB bound that decides between a located snippet and an opening excerpt used to count the indexed text. CJK index text is about 2.3× longer than the stored text, so located snippets would have stopped at about 28 KB of Chinese. The FTS tables now have a `body_bytes UNINDEXED` column, and the bound compares the stored body's UTF-8 size.

  This does not loosen the cost bound. For any text, the number of tokens is at most (stored bytes + 1) / 2, the same as the worst Latin case (`a a a …`). The 64 KiB CJK worst case measured about 500 ms of highlight work, against about 1,150 ms for the existing Latin worst case.

### Not in this PR

- `extensions/knowledge/src/recall-keyword.ts`, which matches automatic-recall triggers, tokenizes the same way and has the same CJK problem. It is a separate code path with its own contract. I will send it as a follow-up.

### Known limitations

These are accepted edge cases, so the code does not handle them:

- **Spaces and punctuation at a CJK/Latin boundary count as word breaks**, as they do for Latin text today. `坡NAS` also matches stored `坡 NAS` and `坡，NAS`. "Exact substring" applies to the CJK part of a term.
- **In `phrase` mode, a space between two CJK words is a word break.** `新加坡 补贴` does not match stored `新加坡补贴`, but `all` mode does. Matching both forms would need an OR over every boundary combination, which grows exponentially. The docs describe this behavior.
- **`v1` cleanup is lazy and per scope.** After the upgrade, a scope's `v1` tables stay until that scope is first searched or verified. The isolated Gateway run below shows this.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

**Base fails, head passes (regression tests only).** In a `git worktree` at the PR base `a143512578c`, I checked out only `retrieval.test.ts` and `lifecycle.test.ts` from this PR (implementation left at base) and ran them:

- Base: `Tests 3 failed | 44 passed (47)`. The failures are `CJK words match inside sentences…` (first failure: `expected [ '新加坡', [] ] to strictly equal [ '新加坡', [ 'chinese_note' ] ]`), `a v1 keyword projection is dropped and rebuilt as v2…` (`流量` total 0, expected 1), and one existing test whose fixture now drops `keyword_history_fts_v2_*`, which is a setup failure, not a behavior assertion.
- With `expect.soft`, 23 assertions fail on base: every in-sentence Han and kana query, mixed `B300配额` / `NAS方式` / `先按NAS`, the single-character prefix `坡`, NFD / IVS / U+F900 folding, any-mode, the snippet offsets, and the v1→v2 rebuild. The controls pass on base as expected: a whole-alias `星洲`, `english`, the spaced phrase `Spot 计费`, and all must-not-match cases.
- Head: `Tests 47 passed (47)`.

**Isolated upgrade 2026.11.10 → this PR, through the real Gateway path.** The setup used a fresh `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `HOME` and a scrubbed environment, with a loopback Gateway on a spare port and a scripted, credential-free OpenAI-compatible model. Every write and read was an agent turn started with `chat.send`, calling the Knowledge tools.

1. On the published `openclaw@2026.11.10` I created a `company` page (alias `星洲`, body containing `…地理位置在新加坡，出网流量按100G计价。共享存储先按NAS方式配置。B300配额审批中，按 Spot 计费。`) and six claims via `knowledge_remember`, each with excerpt evidence. I then superseded one claim (`札幌` → `福冈`) and withdrew one (`曼谷…合同`). Before the writes, all 14 probe queries returned 0 hits. After the writes, every in-sentence CJK query still returned 0 hits on 2026.11.10; only `星洲`, `Spot` and `Spot 计费` matched.
2. I stopped that Gateway and started this PR's build on the same state dir:
   - Config: all 21 original leaves are unchanged. The host migration only added `meta.*`, `wizard.*` and default `skills.entries.*`.
   - `knowledge_status` is identical: same vault id, records 5, same ontology fingerprint.
   - `knowledge_records lifecycle=all` lists the same 7 ids, revisions, hashes and lifecycle states.
   - `knowledge_verify` returns 5/5 passed.
   - The sha256 of all 19 vault files and the vault git log are byte-identical before and after, so no record was rewritten.
   - `knowledge_record includeEvidence` and `knowledge_evidence_read` return the same citation locator and passage text. The withdrawn record's evidence stays unavailable, exactly as on 2026.11.10.
3. Keyword projection: before the upgrade the store had `keyword_fts_v1_<scope>` (`tokenize='unicode61 remove_diacritics 2'`). After the first read on the PR build it has `keyword_fts_v2_<scope>` with `body_bytes UNINDEXED`, plus the history and row tables. All `*_v1_<scope>` tables were dropped. The v2 table holds the page and the 4 active claims, and the history table holds the superseded claim; the withdrawn claim is in neither. A separate run where `knowledge_grep` was the first call after the upgrade rebuilt v1 → v2 the same way, with identical results.
4. Search on the PR build:
   - `新加坡`, `出网流量`, `配额`, `NAS方式`, `B300配额`, `大阪`, `东京`, `告警阈值`, `福冈` and `坡` all hit, as does `新加坡 补贴` in any mode.
   - `札幌` (present only in superseded wording) returns the current replacement with `via` pointing at the superseded revision.
   - `曼谷` and `合同` (present only in the withdrawn claim) return 0 hits for both `lifecycle=active` and `lifecycle=all`.
   - All 47 returned snippets are verbatim substrings of the stored record text.

**Downgrade.**

- Starting 2026.11.10 on the upgraded state dir is refused cleanly by the host schema guard (`state database … uses schema 42; this build supports 40`). This comes from the PR base, not from this PR.
- With only the host databases restored from the pre-upgrade copy, 2026.11.10 loads the Knowledge store that this PR had touched. Records, evidence and verify are unchanged. It recreates its v1 tables and leaves the v2 tables in place.

**Upgrade → rollback with writes → re-upgrade: found by this run, fixed in `cf0fa8e02c4`.**

- Scenario: after a rollback to 2026.11.10, a claim is written or withdrawn there, then this PR's build is started again.
- Before the fix (observed on the isolated Gateway): the PR build reused its stale v2 tables. A claim written during the rollback was not found, and a query whose only stale v2 match was a claim withdrawn during the rollback returned `index.state: "unavailable"` (fail-closed; nothing withdrawn was returned). It persisted until a later reconcile rebuilt the index.
- Cause: `keyword_state_v1` is shared by both projection versions, so 2026.11.10's refreshed snapshot made the stale v2 tables look current.
- Fix: a surviving `keyword_*_v1_<scope>` table means a pre-v2 build ran after v2, so v2 treats both of its tables as untracked, rebuilds them from scratch and drops the v1 projection (this also removes the orphaned v1 tables).
- Regression test `a v1 projection rebuilt by an older build after v2 forces a full v2 rebuild`: fails on `0d4a79c8d9b` (`expected [] to strictly equal [ 'added_cjk' ]`), passes on `cf0fa8e02c4`. The unit test reproduces the persisted state (matching state row, stale v2 rows, v1 table present); the Gateway replay below repeats the full sequence on `cf0fa8e02c4`.
- A one-way upgrade was unaffected before and after the fix.

**Rollback-with-writes → re-upgrade, replayed through the Gateway on cf0fa8e02c4.**

Same isolated setup as before: fresh state dir and HOME, scrubbed environment, loopback Gateway on a spare port, a scripted credential-free model, and every read/write issued as an agent turn via `chat.send` calling the Knowledge tools. The build under test reports commit `cf0fa8e02c468fd70545d0cf72cc18349e82bf33`; the rollback side is the published `openclaw@2026.11.10`. Rollback is emulated as before: the host databases are swapped back to the pre-upgrade copy and the Knowledge store is left untouched.

1. **Upgrade.** On 2026.11.10 I wrote one page and three claims and withdrew one of them. After the first turn on this build the store has only `keyword_*_v2_<scope>` tables; all `*_v1_<scope>` tables are dropped, and `新加坡` / `大阪` / `福冈` hit while the withdrawn `曼谷` claim does not.
2. **Roll back and write.** On 2026.11.10 I added the claim 「复盘会议定在名古屋举行。」 (`名古屋` still has 0 hits there). A read-only look at the store shows the v1 rows are current while the leftover v2 rows lack the new claim, and `keyword_state_v1` has been refreshed by 2026.11.10.
3. **Re-upgrade.** On this build, the very first turn runs `knowledge_grep 名古屋`, with no `knowledge_verify` before it. It returns the new claim, and `复盘会议` and `新加坡` hit as well.
4. **Roll back, withdraw and write.** On 2026.11.10 I withdrew the 名古屋 claim and added 「年会安排在仙台。」. A read-only look shows v1 rows `{大阪, 福冈, 仙台, page}` and stale v2 rows `{大阪, 福冈, 名古屋, page}`, with both table generations present. This is the state that previously made the query return `index.state: "unavailable"`.
5. **Re-upgrade again.** The first turn runs, in order:
   - `knowledge_grep 名古屋` returns 0 hits and no `index` error.
   - `knowledge_grep 名古屋 lifecycle=all` returns 0 hits.
   - `knowledge_grep 复盘会议` returns 0 hits and no `index` error.
   - `knowledge_grep 仙台` returns the new claim, with an exact snippet.
   - `knowledge_grep 新加坡` returns the old page.
   - `knowledge_grep 曼谷 lifecycle=all` returns 0 hits.

   No `knowledge_verify` call was needed. A read-only check afterwards shows the v2 rows are `{大阪, 福冈, 仙台, page}`, `keyword_state_v1.indexed_at` advanced, and every `*_v1_<scope>` table is gone.

Result: claims added during a rollback are searchable immediately after re-upgrade, claims withdrawn during a rollback are excluded from both the default and `lifecycle=all` searches, none of the queries reports an unavailable index, and the orphaned v1 tables are cleaned up. Tokens, endpoints and local paths are omitted; record ids are a throwaway store's.

### End-to-end reproduction on an isolated Gateway (real agent and model)

**Setup**

- Two source builds from this checkout: base `a143512578c` and this PR's commit `0f389e08044`. `0d4a79c8d9b` differs from `0f389e08044` only by an oxfmt line wrap in `retrieval.test.ts`; `cf0fa8e02c4` adds the rollback fix described above.
- Each build ran with `pnpm openclaw gateway run --port 19891 --bind loopback` under a clean `env -i`, using a temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`/`OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1` and `plugins.slots.memory: "knowledge"`.
- The model was `amazon-bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5`, using an assumed AWS IAM role.
- No service was installed, and no existing Gateway or state was touched.

**Flow**

1. On base, a Control-UI-style `chat.send` turn asked the agent to call `knowledge_save_page`. The page had title `客户资源需求记录`, type `note` and body `客户希望地理位置在新加坡，出网流量单价按100G计价。共享存储先按NAS方式配置10TB。`. The receipt was `81d6d6b4-…`, revision 1.
2. In the same session, the agent called `knowledge_grep` once per query.
3. I stopped the base Gateway and started the fix build on the **same state directory**. This is the upgrade path existing users take. The same grep turn then ran in the same session.
4. The counts and snippets below are copied from the verbatim tool results in `chat.history`, not from the model's summary.

| Query (default `all` mode) | Base `a143512578c` | This PR `0f389e08044` | Snippet on this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `新加坡` | 0 | **1** | `客户希望地理位置在新加坡，出网流量单价按100G计价。共享存储先按NAS方式配置10TB。` |
| `出网流量` | 0 | **1** | same as above |
| `NAS` | 0 | **1** | same as above |
| `坡新` (reversed, must not match) | 0 | 0 | — |
| `客户资源需求记录` (whole title, control) | 1 | 1 | `客户资源需求记录` |

- On base, only the control query that equals an entire unbroken CJK run matched. This shows that the record was indexed and that the misses come from segmentation.
- After the upgrade, the searched scope had `keyword_{fts,rows,history_fts,history_rows}_v2_*` tables and no `v1` tables. Two other scopes that were never searched on the fix build still had their `v1` tables. This is the documented lazy cleanup.
- Gateway logs had no knowledge errors on the fix build.
- The `knowledge_grep` result returned to agents only has a compact snippet, so this run does not show where the highlight landed. Exact highlight offsets are covered by the focused test below.

### Focused tests (on `0d4a79c8d9b`; on `cf0fa8e02c4` the knowledge retrieval, lifecycle, ingestion and storage-schema suites pass 73/73)

```
pnpm test extensions/knowledge/src/retrieval.test.ts extensions/knowledge/src/lifecycle.test.ts extensions/knowledge/src/record-capacity.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  52 passed (52)
   Duration  191.62s (tests 83%, transform 11%, import 5%)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 198.66s

pnpm tsgo:extensions
EXIT=0
```

The same command on `0f389e08044` also passed (52/52, 283.50 s, of which 40% was transform on a cold compile cache).

**Why this run takes more than 30 seconds**

- Each test in these files builds a real vault, with a SQLite state database, the storage worker thread and local Git checkpoints. Nothing is mocked.
- Summed test time was about 159 s: `lifecycle.test.ts` about 85 s over 23 tests, `retrieval.test.ts` about 41 s over 24 tests, and `record-capacity.test.ts` about 34 s over 5 tests. The single `near-limit records …` capacity test took 30.9 s.
- The rest of the wall time was Vitest transforming and importing the plugin and core import graph with one worker. That share was 11% with a warm cache and 40% with a cold one.
- The two tests this PR adds take about 2.1 s (`CJK words match inside sentences as exact substrings with exact snippets`) and 1.6 s (`a v1 keyword projection is dropped and rebuilt as v2 on the next search`). Both are in `retrieval.test.ts`, which was already over 30 s before this change.
- `record-capacity.test.ts` is included because it consumes the highlight bound. It checks that bodies over 64 KiB and NUL-containing bodies still fall back to an opening excerpt.
- CI timings are not available yet.

The new CJK test covers:

- Chinese, Japanese and mixed Latin/CJK terms inside sentences, plus single characters in `all` and `any` modes.
- Queries that must not match: reversed order, a simplified-only form, and decomposed kana.
- `phrase` mode in order and reversed.
- Aliases and titles.
- Folding of NFD kana, IVS and compatibility ideographs.
- Exact snippet offsets more than 100 characters into the body.
- A filtered query, which uses the temporary corpus.
- A superseded-history match, with `via`.
- A Chinese body of about 46 KB whose snippet is still located.

The long-body case failed on the intermediate commit that still bounded highlights by the indexed text. I did not separately rerun the new unit tests against base. The base side is shown by the end-to-end table above.

### Other checks

Run on the current head:

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: pass.
- oxlint on the three touched `.ts` files (including `max-lines`): pass. `retrieval.ts` is about 657 of 700 non-blank, non-comment lines.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` on the three `.ts` files and `retrieval.md`: pass. This check found one unformatted test line, which the final commit fixes.
- `pnpm check:assertion-safety`: pass (checked on `0f389e08044`).
- `git diff --check`: pass.

Run on the pre-squash branch, with `docs/plugins/knowledge/retrieval.md` unchanged since:

- `node scripts/format-docs.mts --check`: pass.
- markdownlint on `retrieval.md`: pass.

**Pre-commit hook:** it did not run locally, so the commit was made with `--no-verify`. The hook's `check:line-cap-ratchet` step calls `git cat-file --batch -z`, which needs git 2.36 or later, and this machine has git 2.34.1 (`error: unknown switch 'z'`). The checks the hook covers for these files were run directly and are listed above. CI runs the full gates.

### Performance (`keywordSearch` with real SQLite, not through the Gateway, medians)

| Scenario | Before the fix | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Filtered search: 200 of 2,000 records selected, about 6 KB of Chinese each | 0 hits (the bug) | about 160 ms |
| Building the persistent index: 200 records, about 16 KB mixed text each | 75–77 ms | 416–433 ms |
| Expanding 27 KB of Chinese for the index | — | about 1.6 ms (about 17 MB/s) |

The compatibility-ideograph check added after these measurements cost about 1% in the expansion microbenchmark.

Scheduled Android security scans fail on Boat before compilation because the runner has no Android SDK. The November 22 run failed with `SDK location not found`, so it did not produce a successful Android analysis.
