prs.title: Fix Gateway pressure checks on delegated Linux cgroups
prs.body:
## Problem or Why

On Linux with a delegated cgroup v2 mount, Node can read memory counters from a different cgroup. The Gateway can retire idle workers while its service has headroom, or continue optional work while its own service is under pressure.

## User Impact

The Gateway's pressure tick and optional-work check now follow the visible service cgroup. The existing warning and critical thresholds remain 80% and 90%. This applies to Node on a verified delegated cgroup v2 mount.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw already maps a process's cgroup membership through the visible mount. The heartbeat selects this reader on startup and rechecks live membership, masks, limits and charge on delegated ticks. On an ordinary mount it keeps Node’s native tick. The leaf still counts raw charged memory. Optional work still checks the working set of visible ancestors separately.

The two native inputs have different contracts. Available memory comes from the cgroup ceiling and its current charge. Starting with libuv 1.52.1, the constrained limit also includes finite soft address-space and data limits. [libuv change](https://github.com/libuv/libuv/pull/4899)

## Evidence

A private Linux/arm64 mount exposed a real 256 MiB service and an equally capped decoy at the path used by libuv. On Node 24.20.0 with libuv 1.52.1, stock issued no retirement at 251,133,952 B of real charge and issued a critical retirement at 249,585,664 B of decoy charge. The candidate issued a critical retirement and deferred optional work at 249,909,248 B of real charge. With 249,765,888 B charged only to the decoy it admitted optional work and emitted no retirement. These measurements exercise the real pressure callback, channel and optional-work predicate with unrelated logging and metrics stubbed. The test used disposable cgroups and synthetic pages.

A finite-limit control applied a 512 MiB soft data limit to the Node process under a 1 GiB cgroup high limit. At 82% service charge, both the identity-mounted stock and delegated candidate admitted optional work and emitted no retirement. At 93.5%, both emitted a warning and deferred work. The candidate read 69,427,200 B of service headroom while the native probe still returned 1 GiB.

One quiet process per case ran 128 pressure ticks. On the ordinary mount, stock and candidate median/p95 times were 14.8/53.5 and 14.4/37.0 µs. On the delegated mount they were 19.6/70.2 and 70.1/208.1 µs. The extra reads apply to delegated ticks. These samples measure a single callback in a fixture.

The regression tests cover membership moves, masked controllers, missing mount information and both sides of the libuv soft-limit change. Local review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45929088924)

The absolute free-memory threshold in cron's extra-run decision is a separate follow-up. This change corrects the pressure signal. The Gateway's 768 MiB first-turn memory investigation remains open. [Related report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192547)

prs.title: improve(config): reuse plugin metadata during auto-enable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When configuration processing decides which plugins to enable, an apply call without a supplied registry resolves the same plugin metadata during both detection and materialization. Even a matching current snapshot is selected twice; the cold fallback can invoke the metadata loader twice.

## User Impact

Configuration processing avoids the second metadata selection within each synchronous apply. Plugin enablement policy, explicit registries, standalone Doctor helpers, and metadata replacement between calls keep their existing behavior. No configuration changes or migration are required. Startup latency has not been measured.

## Why This Change Was Made

Detection already owns the resolved registry, so it now carries that fact into materialization. The public detection helper still returns only candidates. This adds no cache and leaves async setup's post-await resolution and the existing bounded result caches unchanged.

## Evidence

- Acceptance: the existing apply flow invokes the cold metadata loader once, or selects the current snapshot once, while preserving the enabled plugin and observing a replacement on the next call.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45925065480) checked out `55510e4`. All 77 auto-enable tests passed on Bun/Vitest: core 41, materialize 4, providers 14, channels 12, capture 6. This includes the cold-loader regression and current-snapshot replacement/count regression. Production/test types, source contracts and guards also pass. The subsequent [normal ready-PR CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45925925267) completed successfully at the same head.
- Baseline/staged owner-body replay: all 11 synthetic cases emitted identical results. Cold loader calls fell 2→1 and current-snapshot getter calls 2→1; separate-call replacement, standalone helpers, disabled/no-need cases, and explicit-registry cache behavior were preserved. This executes the real apply/detect/shared/materialize bodies with synthetic external readers; it is not a native Vitest baseline, filesystem scan count, or latency benchmark.
- Native formatter check and `git diff --check` pass. Independent source review and autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings for the complete staged change against `2ab7b31` (snapshot `e6fd0ad6`). Autoreview used the configured Codex route; local ClawSweeper was unavailable because its runner checkout was not clean. Hosted intake acknowledged an existing cross-route review request after readiness; no hosted review result is claimed.
- [Config-doc validation passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45925065480/job/140264866584), including both generated baseline files, on the CI merge tree containing this head. This closes the earlier local dependency-mismatch gap for the documented scoped commit exception; no schema/help/generator inputs changed.
- Production delta: +13 lines for the prepared result and unchanged public helper shape; tests: +25 lines. No import edges, dependencies, provider requests, or async lifecycle behavior changed.

The earlier draft CI dependency check reported three pre-existing Knip symbols: `readUpdateDatabaseEngineConfig`, `formatUpdateSnapshotCapacity`, and `DoctorContributionPending`. [The candidate job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45925065480/job/140264866908) and [the frozen main baseline job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45922594758/job/140256915435) report the same names and classifications; the baseline checkout is `2ab7b31`. Their source and dependency inputs are unchanged by this PR. That draft-run failure remains recorded; the subsequent normal ready-PR run is green.

The loader and snapshot counts above measure one synchronous `applyPluginAutoEnable` call. The complete CLI entry point was not instrumented. The change therefore establishes the work removed per apply while whole-command counts and latency remain open.

prs.title: fix: restore Discord voice-note transcript echoes
prs.body:
Closes #206087

## What Problem This Solves

When Discord users send a captionless voice note in a DM or address the bot by voice in a mention-gated channel, they can get an assistant reply without the transcript receipt they enabled. The preflight step has the transcript but has not resolved where to send it.

## User Impact

When transcript echo is enabled, admitted voice notes receive one transcript receipt in the originating conversation before the assistant replies. The same setting and format continue to apply. Messages rejected by mention gating produce no echo, and users can still turn the receipt off. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord now uses the shared deferred-echo sender after the inbound session is recorded, when Discord's account and reply route are available. Preflight carries the selected attachment's original position through media preparation so the main pass can recognize the same attachment, including native voice notes without an audio MIME. This leaves audio scope policy to the separate work in #204121.

## Evidence

On base `2ab7b31a13d9` and the tree committed as `fefc2272ea62`, the same command drove captionless voice-note events through Discord admission, session recording, and the production outbound adapter. An isolated HTTP server captured the ordered `POST /api/v10/channels/<id>/messages` request bodies. Transcription, media fetch, and the assistant reply used fixtures.

| Scenario | Base HTTP readback | Candidate HTTP readback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Allowed DM, echo enabled | 0 echoes, 1 reply | 1 `Heard: voice $&` echo, then 1 reply in the DM |
| Spoken mention in a public thread | 0 echoes, 1 reply | 1 `Heard: hey openclaw $&` echo, then 1 reply in the same thread |
| Thread voice note without a mention | 0 POSTs | 0 POSTs |
| Allowed DM, echo disabled | 0 echoes, 1 reply | 0 echoes, 1 reply |

The disabled-echo case also checked that the MIME-less voice note reached dispatch as already transcribed. That assertion failed on the base (`false`) and passed with the repair (`true`).

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight-echo.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
```

With Node 24.22.1 and one worker, the base exited 1 in 214.44 seconds with the two missing echoes and the attachment assertion. The candidate exited 0 with 4/4 cases in 214.64 seconds, including compiled worker preparation. The unchanged production tree and existing Discord preflight, reaction, and audio tests passed 81/81 in the prior focused run. The source runtime build passed on the same production inputs. Formatting, the test-line budget, and typed lint passed on the committed tree.

Local Codex autoreview did not return a completed report. Hosted Discord, a live transcription provider, and a live assistant model were not tested. AI assistance was used for implementation and verification.

prs.title: improve: copy only the selected model for agent completions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An agent-scoped simple completion selects a provider and model, then deep-copies every model in the prepared catalog before resolving that one selection. Local model commands and other callers of the same helper pay this cost on each acquisition.

## User Impact

The built-in resolver can start with the selected catalog row. A provider that needs a sibling model or enumerates the catalog still receives its captured inventory. Custom resolvers keep the full, mutable request-local registry and credential store they receive today.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepared simple completions already let the built-in resolver open its model stores after normalizing the selection. The agent acquisition path now uses the same option. Credential selection, route materialization and the lifetime of the acquired model still have their existing owners.

## Evidence

- A source-level probe exercised the acquisition context, the built-in store-selection block and the production registry fork with synthetic catalogs. With 1,024 rows, the initial copy went from 1,024 rows to one. With a one-row catalog, both copied one. Later enumeration preserved the selected object and exposed sibling rows. Both versions kept the same full mutable stores on repeated custom resolver calls.
- The regression assertions cover normalized rows through the public agent acquisition path and store identity across custom route rematerialization.
- A physical ARM64 device returned all 13 expected replies from a synthetic loopback endpoint, including one seed. With two cold sessions per version in ABBA order, mean launch to visible reply fell from 70.539 s to 67.818 s (3.86%). Both candidate cold sessions were faster than both baseline sessions. The four warm replies per version averaged 5.621 s and 5.544 s. After 45 s idle, the means were 5.399 s and 5.520 s. A warm improvement remains unresolved. The runs excluded real OpenAI network time, recorded no OOMs and left the daily installation in place.
- The device comparison exercised the foreground local `infer model run` action and recorded its loopback replies and timing. The registry copy counts above came from the separate instrumented catalog probe. The device run kept the same timing observer in both versions, so it produced no per-row copy log.
- The exact-head Bun jobs passed 36 tests across the public agent, worker, isolated completion, custom resolver and generation paths. Pinned formatting, the native commit hook and scoped P0–P2 review passed. [Selected-model tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45925228887/job/140265473028) · [Runtime and generation tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45925228887/job/140265473008)
- Both Linux Node 24 jobs built the runtime and Control UI with private QA enabled and declaration emission skipped. The planner skipped the standalone package build. This change uses an existing internal option and preserves the public type and package exports. [First runtime build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45925228887/job/140265472481) · [Second runtime build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45925228887/job/140265472464)
- Ready-for-review CI passed on this head. The earlier draft run reported three unused exports also present on scheduled main and a Bun Gateway compaction hot-reload failure during plugin teardown. [Ready CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45926167485) · [Draft CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45925228887) · [Scheduled main dependency check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45922594758/job/140256915435)

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A reviewed incoming PR cannot reach preparation when its frozen tooling is broken: workflow succession previously required preparation records that do not exist yet. This blocks the Android CodeQL repair in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203843.

## User Impact

`prepare-workflow-successor --incoming-review` advances authenticated current-main tooling while preserving the exact reviewed source and evidence. Ordinary preparation and all existing review, CI, and merge gates still apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change extends the existing V3 binding, evidence inventory, authentication, and atomic transition owners. It rejects pending transitions and incompatible lifecycle state before any recovering guard can change the checkout. Prepared READY, correction, and proof paths retain their contracts. Production growth is 49 net lines for the missing incoming-review lifecycle stage; tests add 193 net lines.

## Evidence

Final head: `75da2142c384d65f2b4aab702f8e3e623cdc25d8`, based on `eb8e41d8847be846cf260bb15ef0e832bd34a757`.

- Independent final-source review and local ClawSweeper review completed with no actionable correctness or security findings. The hosted comment reviewed the intentional tests-only baseline; the final committed range supplies its missing implementation. The local review's remaining runtime-proof request is satisfied below.
- [Normal PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45925784922) passed. Its [Bun successor job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45925784922/job/140268854441) passed all 118 cases. [Exact-head Node successor proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45927096364/job/140271484859) also passed all 118 cases. Both execute incoming succession followed by ordinary preparation using the extracted selected materializer and sibling cache helper, all three CAS/lock interruption cases, and correction/proof/prepared-READY siblings.
- Changed-test lint, targeted formatting, whitespace, shell syntax, and four embedded JavaScript syntax checks passed. [CodeQL](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45925784735) passed. The actual required `openclaw/ci-gate` rollup is successful; no exemption is requested.
- [Tests-first baseline](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45913090241/job/140226340781) at `bdde034781f5b8b6be700e74efdde57b56cd9ee4` executed 118 Bun cases: 114 passed and four failed at the missing incoming-transition capability. This is historical failure evidence. Historical V3 reader refusal is verified from its strict discriminator check, not a separate historical-reader runtime execution.
- The separate Node workflow was needed because normal PR CI selects Bun and the focused remote wrapper could not bootstrap against the available mismatched dependency installation. Its target suite passed, but the supplementary whole workflow remains failed on three inherited unused exports (`openSettingsDialog`, `checkDoctorLegacyStateDirPending`, `startBrokerExeca`), independently fixed by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206238. This does not claim whole-workflow success. Normal automatic CI and the actual required rollup subsequently passed on this same head.
- Earlier CI found two missing test braces, now fixed, and an inherited unused export already fixed by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206165. The branch incorporates that exact landed base; all three signed task commits retain their authors and messages.

prs.title: fix(update): keep recovery sets when a capture or its root is unreadable
prs.body:
Related to #191855. This head owns the status half of the report: an unreadable capture directory, an unreadable capture root, or an ancestor that denies search permission to the capture root no longer erases the recovery-set list; the unreadable entry is reported beside the captures that can still be verified. `openclaw backup create` keeps its documented refusal of unreadable sources (`docs/cli/backup.md`); the backup-walker symptom is deliberately not changed here.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update status --json` returned `recoverySetsError` and dropped every recovery set when one retained capture directory, the `.update-captures` root, or an ancestor of that root could not be read by the current user (#191855: a root-owned `.fseventsd` inside the state tree).

- `collectCaptureRootInventory` in `update-capture-cleanup.ts` ran a bare `readdirSync`/`lstatSync`, so permission failures became a global `recoverySetsError` hiding every readable set. The root `readdir` and per-capture marker `lstat` were guarded first; review then reproduced that an ancestor denying search permission fails the root `lstat` itself, before the `readdir` guard can run.
- Fix: the root `lstat` now uses the same EACCES/EPERM classification as the existing `readdir` guard — the root is recorded as a `protected` artifact with `reason: "unreadable-capture-root"` and status lists it as `unreadable` ("Update capture root at ... is unreadable") next to the readable sets. Other errnos still throw; an absent root still returns an empty inventory.
- Not changed: malformed/FIFO/oversized/present-but-unreadable markers still refuse; aliased or non-directory roots still fail globally; `backup create`, the tar walker, SQLite discovery and header probe keep their permission-failure contract. Per-path omission reporting for foreign directories belongs to draft #194166.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each reader already had a tolerant "entry is not here" path; the permission case landed in the fatal branch because the errno set was written for missing paths only. Classifying EACCES/EPERM where absence is already classified keeps the two-tier model (private capture stays protected and loud; a directory this process cannot inspect degrades to one `unreadable` entry) without a new shared policy module. A shared per-path warning/omission policy was rejected because #194166 owns it; making `backup create` skip unreadable directories was rejected because its documentation promises refusal.

## User Impact

`openclaw update status` (text and `--json`) keeps listing every recovery set it can verify when a capture directory, the capture root, or an ancestor of the root is unreadable: the locked entry appears as `unreadable` with the OS error and the existing next action, instead of one `Update recovery sets unavailable` line hiding the healthy sets. `openclaw backup create` behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

Shipped CLI matrix (`node openclaw.mjs update status --json`, isolated `env -i` state, real sealed manifests). Before arm = prior head `b39f8c4` dist; after arm = this head `be1a6792f03` rebuilt with only the root-`lstat` guard added:

| Case | Before (`b39f8c4`) | After (`be1a6792f03`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| control: two readable captures | no `recoverySetsError`, 2 sets | identical |
| capture dir mode 000 | no error; 1 `unreadable` + 1 readable | identical |
| capture root mode 000 | no error; root `unreadable` | identical |
| capture root mode 111 | no error; root `unreadable` | identical |
| **parent of root mode 000** (review repro) | `recoverySetsError: EACCES ... lstat '<state>.update-captures'`, sets missing | no error; root `unreadable` |

```console
# before, parent-000 (verbatim)
recoverySetsError: EACCES: permission denied, lstat '<evidence>/repro/parent-000/state.update-captures'
recoverySets: <missing>
# after, parent-000 (verbatim)
recoverySetsError: <absent>
recoverySets: unreadable state.update-captures
```

Earlier base→head matrix (base `ca33faf`, shipped arms self-reporting `OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (ca33faf)` / `(b39f8c4)`): capture-dir-000 went from `recoverySetsError: EACCES ... lstat '<captures>/<run>/.openclaw-private-update-capture'` to one `unreadable` set beside the readable one; root-000 went from `EACCES ... scandir` to `Update capture root at ... is unreadable`. `backup create` cells were byte-identical across arms: unreadable workspace dir → exit 1 `Private update capture marker is unreadable; export refused.`; malformed marker → exit 1 `... invalid or unreadable; export refused.`; control → exit 0, same archive entries.

Regression (folded into the existing root-unreadable case as `it.each(["root","parent"])`, platform-guarded). RED with only the production guard reverted:

```console
FAIL  keeps the recovery set when the capture parent is unreadable
AssertionError: expected { update: { …(4) }, …(6) } to not have property "recoverySetsError"
+ Received: "EACCES: permission denied, lstat '/tmp/update-status-recovery-uQGUmt/state.update-captures'"
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed | 29 passed (30)
```

GREEN on this head: `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 30 passed (30)` (`vitest.cli.config.ts`, `status.recovery.test.ts`). `oxfmt --check` and type-aware `oxlint` clean on both changed files.

Limits: EPERM shares the EACCES branch but is exercised on Linux only through EACCES; the backup surface is unchanged this round (documented refusal path shown above). Collision check: #204709 (kitiyeung) touches the same status files for a complementary question (label foreign/unverified captures); no other open PR touches `update-capture-cleanup.ts`.

prs.title: fix: run QuickJS Code Mode on portable cloud workers
prs.body:
Closes #205716

## What Problem This Solves

A portable cloud worker can start with QuickJS selected, then return `runtime_unavailable` on every Code Mode call. The reporter confirmed that selecting Node for the cloud agent restores execution.

## User Impact

Workers installed from the updated bundle can use QuickJS and call the Gateway tools allowed for their session. When the selected model is known to use tools, dispatch and Move reject a known unsupported executor before allocation. Turn admission checks the actual tool policy before issuing turn credentials. The existing worker upgrade path delivers the new archive using the current config and wire formats.

## Why This Change Was Made

Portable workers run from a sealed archive. The archive now includes the bundled QuickJS executor, worker entry, and WASM assets, so it can load the configured executor after relocation. Gateway admission checks the selected executor and existing plugin policy before preparing execution. The worker still requires the selected executor to load before any call can dispatch.

## Evidence

Product commit `d008b49d426fdeff7d9bd762ba12daedf033fc1b` with reviewed tree `a8c9c0f5b65c253cdad0a85eb790e5b0f432c738`, upstream baseline `ea27b2143ecd3c773a20f9a12cf91abdbc80ee89`, Linux x64, Node 26.13.1.

The final worker build took 52.70 s using the runtime entries in `tsdown.config.ts`. The proof uses `node <relocated-archive>/worker.mjs` with a synthetic launch descriptor on stdin. It extracts an archive from the normal bundle producer, admits a turn over loopback WebSocket, and reads the worker start and committed transcript. The base and candidate use identical turn input.

| Run | Worker start | Transcript readback | Gateway tool calls | Wall time |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Before, QuickJS | 0 executor starts | `status=failed`, `code=runtime_unavailable` | 0 | 34.07 s |
| After, same QuickJS turn | `code-mode-quickjs.worker.mjs` | `status=completed`, `{"text":"quickjs-cell-ok","answer":42}` | 0 | 32 s |
| After, QuickJS with a permitted tool | `code-mode-quickjs.worker.mjs` | `status=completed`, `{"hostReply":{"status":"ok","people":[{"name":"Ada"}]}}` | 1 `presence` | 31 s |
| After, explicit Node selection | `code-mode-node.worker.mjs` | `status=completed`, `{"answer":42}` | 0 | 32 s |
| After, QuickJS entry removed from the test archive | 1 QuickJS attempt, 0 Node starts | `status=failed`, `code=runtime_unavailable` | 0 | 37 s |

Run the fixture from the source checkout with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs ../proof-205716.mts . quickjs-cell <red-or-green> <worker-build-root>`. The expectation argument only changes the assertions. The other scenarios are `quickjs-host-tool`, `node-control`, and `quickjs-refusal`. The checked-in `test/scripts/worker-deploy-build-plugin.test.ts` also exercises the relocated packaged executor. Dispatch tests cover explicitly denied or disabled QuickJS and admit a model with tools disabled.

The baseline archive hash was `55321931442b26bb54b9f610644c17bd8ac62a012d95e75db181211c109986fc`. All four candidate runs started from archive `266da6b3cdc71330db14dfae54d1ed8d97ce4ab71af823f3ba8fba3acb299024`.

The final tree passed the relocated-archive regression in 295.76 s wall, including 152.68 s of cold worker-cache preparation and 6.230 s for the test case.

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/worker-deploy-build-plugin.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'executes QuickJS cells'
```

The final core and scripts type checks passed with `OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo`, along with changed-file type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks. On `a46f34208d699a9adc33dbf45201c7b53df5941d`, before the dispatch and transport extractions, five focused suites passed 89 tests for executor selection, registered dispatch, Move, and tool authority. The independent reviewer found no issues in the initial diff or the final extraction.

The patch includes 14 production files (+482/−103) and 10 test or fixture files (+292/−5). The production count includes moving the existing dispatch and tool transport code into their owning modules to keep both files within the repository's limits.

The loopback Gateway supplies synthetic inference and records requests. All worker processes exited cleanly. The harness removed the extracted archives and used isolated state. Cloud allocation, hosted inference, reconnect, non-Linux targets, and a deployed Gateway's admission decision were not tested. The policy probe was source-level. The full bundle, build-config, compaction, and exec-approval fixture suites were not rerun on the final tree.

prs.title: test: trim low-value read and benchmark coverage
prs.body:
Refs https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/198737

## What Problem This Solves

The test-maintenance campaign is reducing optional profiling workloads, implementation counters, repeated wiring and presentation inventories. This packet removes a selected maintenance surface while keeping named functional guards; it deliberately retires the listed noncritical coverage rather than claiming every removed assertion is duplicated.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. Developers maintain 3,984 fewer tracked lines. The tradeoff includes less optional stress/performance and large-input parity coverage, selected placement forwarding/progression checks, and native cosmetic/default-positive payload permutations. Those losses are explicit below; retained tests do not claim identical performance measurements.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prefer existing functional keeper suites and a few small guard folds over replacement harnesses. Preserve auth/privacy, stale-result, session placement, retirement and data-preservation checks. The added folds retain created-session INITIAL assistant-final visibility and a literal-derived Codex fingerprint digest; Android's new bare-CR math and stronger CRLF UTF-8-limit fixtures remain.

| Category | Paths | Added | Deleted | Net removed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Tests/support | 44 | 31 | 4,000 | 3,969 |
| Owned test routing/mock/timing metadata | 5 | 0 | 15 | 15 |
| Total | 49 | 31 | 4,015 | **3,984** |
| Runtime production / new tracked files | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The five metadata paths are `scripts/lib/ci-policy-test-watch.mts`, `scripts/lib/ci-proof-test-inventory.mts`, `test/vitest/vitest.gateway-server-paths.mjs`, `config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt`, and `config/ci-test-timings.json`. They remove only references belonging to the retired suites. Six normal-formatter blank-line deletions account for the difference from the 3,978-line preformat proposal.

## Evidence

**Draft / validation incomplete.** Source head `b70aafe40aec7bcbf6cad6303f5a69e54fd9f905`, frozen parent `973e0ba78f7b970dafdd9166c6598a572a5d0d46`, tree `1afbe9204fdb0f86f50a2785b79c05d79bbdfc4a`. Patch SHA-256: `28572c40cb4678c75529c517ed00acdae27bf77591a714e276d56a61646bb972`.

- Complete: signed commit and normal hooks; admitted native oxfmt 0.74; native i18n freshness; exact 49-file pre/post bindings and 59 keeper bindings; `git diff --check`; deleted-path reference closure; timing JSON parse and three metadata syntax probes; added-line privacy check.
- **UNRUN:** application execution, Vitest/scoped runtime, test types, oxlint, Android and broad/required CI. Existing app dependencies are unqualified; no install or provider fallback was used.
- **Source review BLOCKED / no verdict.** Native full-context preflight exited 1 before any model ran: `refusing sensitive --source-context: src/secrets/runtime-degraded-state.ts`. The mandatory keeper `src/secrets/runtime-state.test.ts` also needs an installed reviewed pin absent from native policy. This review attempt is stopped; the PR remains **OPEN / DRAFT / on hold**. Resumption requires supported policy-owner admission for the required source and keeper contexts. This is an admission blocker, not a coverage objection or a passed review; no helper/policy change or bypass is proposed.
- No current-head CI or review proof is borrowed from the preceding campaign PR. No ClawSweeper re-review has been requested by this agent.
- Dependency/source inspection only: Codex `414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6`, `codex-rs/protocol/src/dynamic_tools.rs:1–173`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs:106–139,1054–1180,1254–1265`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs:210–318,1210–1217`, `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs:1891–1978,2153–2255`, and `codex-rs/state/src/runtime/threads.rs:399–448,1180–1250`. These establish protocol/list/read boundaries, not performance equivalence or execution proof.
- AI-assisted, maintainer-requested cleanup. This public 49-row table is the durable keeper/value manifest. The ignored local replay manifest is maintainer-only bookkeeping, not a publicly available artifact or a substitute for this table.

### File-level keeper and retirement manifest

Net is deleted minus added; negative values are guard additions. Keeper line ranges refer to the frozen base, unless the row explicitly describes a new fold. Same-file keepers mean retained cases in the named file. Resource/work-count and stress budgets below are intentionally lost where listed, not implicitly covered by output-only tests.

prs.title: fix: say which agent's session store blocked an update and why
prs.body:
Related: #205202

## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw update` (or `openclaw doctor --fix`) stops because Doctor cannot read a session store during the legacy-main session migration, the report ends at the redacted path and says nothing else:

```
Failing check plugin-doctor-post-session-state (blocked-by-session-repair-failure): Post-session plugin repair was blocked because prerequisite session repair failed: Error: cannot read legacy session store [redacted-path]
```

The operator cannot tell which store failed or why, so there is nothing to act on before retrying the update.

## User Impact

The same refusal now names the agent whose store failed and the cause, and the store path stays redacted:

```
Failing check plugin-doctor-post-session-state (blocked-by-session-repair-failure): Prerequisite session repair failed: Error: cannot read legacy session store for agent ops: StartupMaintenanceRequiredError: OpenClaw agent database [redacted-path] uses schema version 21; stop active
```

No behavior change besides the message: Doctor still refuses on an unreadable active store, and the update still rolls back. The unredacted error keeps the full store path at its end for local logs.

Not covered here, which is why this is `Related` and not `Closes`: the cause of the reporter's own read failure is still unknown (this change is what would show it), unreadable stores are not skipped, and `doctor --lint` does not gain a finding for them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both doctor-fix throw sites in the legacy-main migration wrote the store path before the cause. Support redaction replaces a path together with everything after it, so the cause never reached the update report. They now follow the cause-before-location order that `formatSchemaMigrationFailure` already uses: agent and cause first, store path last.

The fact is also capped at 200 characters, and the receipt's wrapper sentence used 83 of them before the error started, which cut a longer cause such as the schema-version message above. The refusal code and check id already say that the post-session plugin repair was blocked, so the receipt message now leads with the failure.

Detect-mode warnings and outcomes are unchanged. The helper lives in the scan module because the migration module is at its line cap.

## Evidence

### Packaged upgrade from the latest stable release

Linux, Node 24.22.1, isolated `HOME`, npm prefix, state directory and config. `npm install -g openclaw@latest` installed `2026.11.10 (6ea542f)`. The config has one agent `ops` whose `session.store` points at a SQLite file left at schema version 21. The candidate is the PR head `8e7ca920757` packed with `node scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs --allow-unreleased-changelog` (tarball integrity check passed; a plain `pnpm pack` is refused by the repository's prepack guard).

Before, the released CLI's own Doctor on that install (`openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes`, exit 1):

```
Failing check plugin-doctor-post-session-state (blocked-by-session-repair-failure): Post-session plugin repair was blocked because prerequisite session repair failed: Error: cannot read legacy session store [redacted-path]
```

After, the same install updating to the candidate with the released updater (`openclaw update --yes --json --no-restart --tag <candidate.tgz>`, exit 1, `status: error`, `reason: doctor-failed`), which runs the candidate's Doctor before it would activate:

```
Failing check plugin-doctor-post-session-state (blocked-by-session-repair-failure): Prerequisite session repair failed: Error: cannot read legacy session store for agent ops: StartupMaintenanceRequiredError: OpenClaw agent database [redacted-path] uses schema version 21; stop active
```

After the refused update, `openclaw --version` still reports `2026.11.10 (6ea542f)` and the config file's sha256 is unchanged. The session store is still at schema version 21 with its table. The update's session import reopened the file (its journal mode is now WAL) and left a byte-identical copy of the original next to it as `sessions.sqlite.migrated-<id>` (sha256 matches the original).

| Before: released 2026.11.10 | After: update to this PR |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shu-chen-dot-ca/shu-chen-dot-ca/b540a0486a12def1b8e8c1675a8833c9c2998a58/draft_0c9840/ev_f92c89.jpg) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shu-chen-dot-ca/shu-chen-dot-ca/b540a0486a12def1b8e8c1675a8833c9c2998a58/draft_0c9840/ev_c41b76.jpg) |

### Doctor CLI from source

Reproduced through the real Doctor CLI (`pnpm openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes`) on Linux, Node 24.22.1, with an isolated `HOME`, state directory and config, one agent `ops`, and three unreadable-store shapes. Before is `main` at `69b81b5a063`; after is this branch. Exit code is 1 in every run.

| Store problem | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Configured store file is not a database | `cannot read legacy session store [redacted-path]` | `cannot read legacy session store for agent ops: Error [ERR_SQLITE_ERROR]: file is not a database; store [redacted-path]` |
| Configured store is at schema version 21 | `cannot read legacy session store [redacted-path]` | `cannot read legacy session store for agent ops: StartupMaintenanceRequiredError: OpenClaw agent database [redacted-path] uses schema version 21; stop active` |
| Retired `main` store path is a directory | `cannot inspect legacy session store [redacted-path]` | `cannot inspect legacy session store for agent main: Error: session store is not a regular file: [redacted-path]` |

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shu-chen-dot-ca/shu-chen-dot-ca/3d7f8fd33a2cf0d7a72a7a3d75406f1b498f8a99/draft_daffcc/ev_939713.jpg) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shu-chen-dot-ca/shu-chen-dot-ca/3d7f8fd33a2cf0d7a72a7a3d75406f1b498f8a99/draft_daffcc/ev_266d9e.jpg) |

### Tests and gates

- New regression in `src/commands/doctor-session-transcripts.sqlite.test.ts` runs the real migration against an unreadable store (not a database, and a dangling link) through the Doctor refusal receipt and `DoctorStateMigrationRefusalError`'s update facts. It asserts the agent and cause are in the public fact and that the store directory is not. Red on `69b81b5a063` (2 failed), green on this branch.
- `pnpm test src/config/sessions/legacy-main-session-migration.test.ts src/config/sessions/legacy-main-session-migration.retained.test.ts src/commands/doctor-session-transcripts.sqlite.test.ts src/commands/doctor-session-transcripts.test.ts src/infra/state-migrations.schema-diagnostics.test.ts src/logging/diagnostic-support-redaction.test.ts src/flows/doctor-health.update.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1 pnpm check:changed`: core typecheck, all core test typecheck shards, lint and format of the changed files, the line-cap ratchet and the other gates passed. One gate failed, `changelog attributions`, on `CHANGELOG/2026.11.10.md:8130`, which this branch does not touch. The Knip dead-code scan was skipped because it exceeds its time limit on this host. `git diff --check` is clean.

Gaps: the packaged upgrade ran with `--no-restart` and no Gateway service in the isolated install, so a serving Gateway staying up through the refused update was not observed; what is shown is that the installed release, config and store contents are unchanged. Through the packaged updater only the schema-version store reaches the candidate Doctor: with a store file that is not a database, the same update to this package stops earlier, in the updater's own state schema inspection (`reason: update-failed`, `State schema inspection failed (exit): ERR_SQLITE_ERROR`), with the release and the file left as they were, so that shape is covered by the source Doctor runs above. prs.title: fix: keep cancelled requests out of agent history previews
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

If you stop a queued request, an agent that later reads the session history can still see the original request as a user message, along with its attachments. The agent can mistake that cancelled request for work you still want done.

## User Impact

The agent can see which pending input was cancelled, when it was accepted, and why it ended if the cause is known. It can no longer recover its text, file paths, or attachment references from that entry. You can still inspect visible cancelled messages in the Control UI. Queued and interrupted previews are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway serves human chat history as well as agent tools. Only the agent's `sessions_history` projection clears the cancelled message, before previewing content or media. The row and its pagination cursor stay in place. Nothing changes how Stop works, how long inputs are kept, or when queued work runs.

## Evidence

- Called the real `sessions_history` tool with a synthetic Gateway response and an anchored, paginated read. On `9ad935f281e0` it returned the cancelled instruction, a file path, and a media reference as a user message. With the fix the same row has `message: null` and `endCause: "user-stop"`. The anchor, cursor, queued media, and interrupted text are preserved without truncation.
- The human-facing `chat.history` RPC test still returned the original visible cancelled text before dismissal. All 51 focused tests passed (history tool, anchor and byte budgets, Gateway handler, and prompt-prefix stability). Targeted typecheck, lint, and formatting passed.
- Local autoreview covered the complete `9ad935f281e0` → `4bc4e2355f0c` patch at P0–P2 and found no actionable issues. The proof checks what the tool returns, not a live model's next action; no live model or browser E2E was run.

prs.title: fix: keep Gateway ready while plugins drain after updates
prs.body:
Related: #205435, #195478

## What Problem This Solves

A plugin reload after an update could make the whole Gateway fail `/readyz` for its 60-second drain, even though the previous plugin generation was still serving. A cancelled cron run could also abandon its selected plugin-generation lease before execution started, leaving future reloads waiting on work that had ended.

## User Impact

Ordinary plugin reload drains no longer make the Gateway not-ready. Failed activation or recovery still fails readiness. Cancelling a prepared cron run releases its selected generation. No settings, stored formats, drain budgets, retries, or active-turn pinning rules change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The readiness owner treated every reload status as a core outage. It now distinguishes an ordinary reload from failed or recovering activation.

Cron preparation acquired its selected execution lease before two awaits, but execution only registered disposal inside the later callback. The preparation owner now owns the lease across resource cleanup, session admission, and execution; the later duplicate ownership is removed. Its existing cleanup stack releases the session preparation hold, joins the session owner's settlement receipt, deletes the continuation after admission unwinds, then releases the lease. This preserves #180877 without a timer or retry.

This fixes a concrete leak on the cron preparation path used by the fleet run. The decision-only path reported in #205435 is **not yet proven** to have this cause, so that issue remains open. This does not solve #195478: active turns still retain their admitted plugins; only abandoned cron holds are removed.

## Evidence

- Base `caf2a4d4f7dc`: the new cron owner regression fails because one real retained plugin work reference remains after cancelled session admission; execution never starts (45 ms test time).
- Readiness owner regression fails on the base with `plugin-reload` and passes on the candidate. Recovery/failed-health cases remain covered.
- Real isolated source Gateway, with `plugins.reload` unresolved behind an admitted held request: base HTTP **200 → 503 → 200**; candidate HTTP **200 → 200 → 200**. Base run 23.11 s, candidate run 50.34 s. Both Gateways and state were cleaned.
- Gateway consumer batch: 8 files / 179 tests passed, including real HTTP readiness during a held drain and after its forced drain failure.
- Production delta measured with `tokei`: **+8 code lines** (971 → 979 across the three changed production modules).
- Initial focused batch: **15 files / 271 tests passed** in 376.50 s wall time. After the cleanup-order repair, the final three cron owner files passed **21/21 tests**, including #180877's external ordering assertion and the cancelled-continuation regression (12 ms; 45 ms on the failing base).
- `check:changed` passed core production/test typechecks, formatting, and guards. Its dead-export scan reported three untouched exports (`readUpdateDatabaseEngineConfig`, `DoctorContributionPending`, `formatUpdateSnapshotCapacity`); no suppression or unrelated code repair is included.
- Final scoped checks passed: formatting, oxlint (zero warnings/errors), core production types, and the services-cron test type graph. Final checks plus the three-file test run took 69.40 s; Vitest itself took 43.60 s.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed `caf2a4d4f7dc` → `25e3fdb6b90c` at default service tier: complete, **patch is correct**, zero findings, security cleared. The offline review did not receive execution receipts; the observed runs are summarized above.

### Readiness decision

Serving-health readiness is the requested contract for this repair: an ordinary reload does not report the whole serving Gateway as unavailable. New agent runs still wait on the existing replacement gate, visible in status. Recovery and failed activation remain unhealthy. This resolves the local review's advisory product-direction question without changing admission policy.

prs.title: fix: retry eligible accounts for automatic chat titles and summaries
prs.body:
Closes #204811

## What Problem This Solves

Automatic chat titles and activity summaries can switch providers as soon as the first account returns a rate limit, even when another configured account can serve the selected model.

## User Impact

OpenClaw can finish these background requests on the operator's selected model using another eligible account. The configured fallback takes over after eligible accounts are exhausted. Operators can inspect which accounts were tried through a bounded diagnostic with profile IDs and outcomes.

Existing configuration works without migration. This change uses the existing profile eligibility and authority rules and adds no config or protocol fields.

## Why This Change Was Made

Built-in utility requests now use the simple-completion account order for automatic profile selection. An eligible account can be retried on a rate-limit or billing failure before the request produces output. The cursor keeps the prepared provider route and checks authority again before dispatch. An explicit profile pin continues to select a single account for that model.

## Evidence

Product commit `129a5b717679ee80a15dc20f5dcd547b774958d7` with reviewed tree `26cd3d5c131aeb0e97e853d6d610be99b64591a0`, upstream baseline `ea27b2143ecd3c773a20f9a12cf91abdbc80ee89`, Linux x64 and Node 26.13.1.

Using `pnpm build:runtime`, the harness launched the packaged Gateway with `openclaw.mjs gateway run --bind loopback --port <fixture-port>`. It called the real `sessions.title.prepare` handler over WebSocket and independently recorded HTTP request order at local provider-compatible endpoints. A chat turn also verified the committed activity summary through `sessions.describe`.

| Run | HTTP recorder | Gateway readback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before, automatic title | A 429 → fallback 200 | `Cross provider fallback` |
| After, same title request | A 429 → B 429 → C 200 | `Haiku used third profile` |
| After, every primary account limited | A 429 → B 429 → C 429 → fallback 200 | `Cross provider fallback` |
| Before and after, explicit pin A | A 429 → fallback 200, zero requests to B or C | `Cross provider fallback` |
| Before, completed chat | Primary chat 200, then A 429 → fallback 200 | Session `done`, activity summary `Cross provider fallback` |
| After, same completed chat | Primary chat 200, then A 429 → B 429 → C 200 | Session `done`, activity summary `Haiku used third profile` |

`node proof-204811.mjs <built-checkout> <new-output-dir> rotation` ran the same title scenario on both revisions. The paired chat readback uses `summary`. The `exhaustion` and `pin` controls use the same runtime harness. The harness SHA-256 is `a7177ae364cb738fbfbeebc66fa3bf0d9de76efb2a2719c7b2a7b5463c56a993`.

The exhaustion run recorded `isolated_completion_auth_exhausted` with `reason=eligible_profiles_exhausted`, `failedProfileCount=3`, and three `rate_limit` attempts with status `429`. The event contained no credential values or provider response bodies. A subsequent `models.probe` got HTTP 200 from profile A on Opus, confirming that the Haiku failures did not block another model on that account.

Four focused Vitest suites passed 81/81 on `cbe6e378ae78cfae82847b280f0eee4a56afda20` before the local diagnostic-buffer correction. The routed provider test file ran 3 cases in 19.03 s and reported 59.82 s with import and transform. The simple-completion runtime file reported 78.77 s for all 8 cases. The buffer-cap correction passed its selected regression in 192.85 s wall, including 135.06 s preparing the cold DB-worker cache and 2.507 s for the test case. The final delta changes only a local binding name and was independently re-reviewed. Repo `tsgo`, changed-file type-aware lint, format, and whitespace passed on the final tree.

The patch includes six production files (+449/−149, including moves of existing dispatch and auth preparation) and three test or routing files (+356/−1). The final runtime build took 431.70 s. The four packaged runs passed in 110–128 s each, exited cleanly, and left the isolated config unchanged. Coverage uses synthetic credentials and provider-compatible endpoints on loopback. The runs have not tested hosted quota, commercial billing, or non-Linux platforms.

prs.title: fix(crabbox): reuse source mirrors after canceled preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Canceling a Crabbox run after source preparation finishes but before provider admission can strand its reusable source mirror. Cleanup records preserved artifacts and changes the lifecycle phase to `preserved`, even though the mirror has never had a consumer. The next run then rejects the mirror's otherwise complete idle handoff and must prepare another copy.

## User Impact

Interrupted remote-check preparation can leave a completed, unused mirror available for the next run. Active or incomplete staging remains protected. This changes developer tooling only; no configuration, migration, or historical-receipt rewrite is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Artifact preservation now changes the phase only after admitted consumers have settled. Earlier phases retain their existing state while recording the same artifact manifest and durability result. The idle-admission rules remain unchanged.

The regression coverage extends existing fixtures for prepared and settled mirror reuse, incomplete/admitted preservation, and cancellation queued during synchronous preparation before the first admission checkpoint. Production delta is +2 comment lines; test delta is +42 lines. The simplification pass retained the single producer-side condition and reused the existing fixtures.

## Evidence

- Original-order failure observed during validation for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201971: cancellation was queued during source copying, preparation completed, and no provider was admitted. Cleanup retained a receipt with `users=none` and `state=preserved`; the native idle-mirror check rejected that combination. This PR does not alter that retained receipt.
- Independent source and test reviews found no actionable issue. The normal commit hook formatted the three changed files and completed successfully; its only change to the reviewed patch was a multiline test-call closing delimiter. `git diff --check` and signature verification passed.
- Exact-head hosted runtime proof passed the four focused families: staging 42, staging-fsync 5, staging-location 4, and wrapper 324 passed / 1 skipped. Matching scripts/test types, formatting, and lint passed. The original [direct-head run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45919798115) still records five unrelated inherited unused-export failures; this is not relabeled a green run.
- The normal [pull-request CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45921588495) is now successful, with no failed jobs. Preflight actually checked out merge `1ceb6f948591b53322c0aba713376646d8324459` (tree `d9a9257d0fad0f5e3d36f26d524b9dcc81f6340d`), whose ordered parents are base `7642a7fa697517f612e8d9de2a975ddb1c16b459` and reviewed head `0f4427a025562b735280cde14fa6722a59109cdb`.
- Committed-range autoreview reported zero findings for that head. Its automated sandbox review was limited to the supplied diff; separate direct reviews covered the complete staging/wrapper owners, callers, dependency contracts, and regression fixtures.

## Review follow-up: receipt compatibility and cancellation

This addresses the [same-head review's compatibility and behavior-proof requests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206267#issuecomment-7207061858).

- **Released contract:** the current stable [v2026.11.10](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.11.10) resolves to `6ea542fd97e2876aa4c871ccc494ed5419a03c5c`. Its complete staging owner and wrapper are byte-identical to this PR's base and the source used for the observed cancellation failure. The release's staging artifact, claim, directory-identity, location, process-provenance, user, and witness owners also match the PR base. Relevant dependency pins remain Zod 4.6.7, TSX 4.23.15, and Vitest 5.0.5, with the same supported Node range. The existing source-capsule optimization differs from the release, so this is not a claim that the entire checkout equals the release.
- **Stored data:** receipt version remains 2. The strict schema, bounded reader, directory/owner identity checks, durability/artifact verification, and idle-admission predicate are unchanged. New unused completed mirrors retain the already-supported `users=none,state=prepared` combination; settled consumers still produce `users=settled,state=preserved`. Existing receipts remain readable under the same rules. Previously stranded `none/preserved` receipts are not promoted, migrated, or automatically removed by this fix.
- **Original-order runtime proof:** the wrapper regression uses the actual source-local shim and compiled wrapper, queues SIGTERM while synchronous preparation completes, then checks exit 143, joined owners, no provider run/claim, preserved source, and a durable idle `none/prepared` receipt. The staging handoff regression then exercises preservation and subsequent acquisition, verifies reuse of the same source inode, verifies preserved output bytes, and checks final native disposal. Prepared and settled variants both pass; incomplete/admitted/unknown-writer guards remain covered.
- **Proof limits:** the original failure was observed with the real wrapper and Crabbox 0.83.2 before provider admission. The repaired cancellation and reuse paths above are hosted runtime regression fixtures, including a controlled Crabbox 0.83.2 protocol fixture; they are not a claimed live provider run or a replay of an installed release. This producer-only change requires neither a provider allocation nor alteration of retained historical staging to verify the lifecycle transition.

prs.title: fix: report an unanswered plugin approval as a timeout, not a missing route
prs.body:
Closes #205267

## What Problem This Solves

When a plugin asks for approval before a tool call and the agent runs inside the Gateway, an approval prompt that was shown and then expired is reported to the agent as `Plugin approval unavailable (no approval route)`. The plugin's `timeoutReason` is dropped and its `onResolution` callback gets `cancelled`. The agent then tells the people who could have approved that their conversation cannot approve things, when they only missed the prompt.

## User Impact

An unanswered prompt now blocks the tool call with the plugin's `timeoutReason` (or `Approval timed out` when none is set), and `onResolution` receives `timeout`, the same as the two-phase path. A request that really had no approval route still reports `no approval route` with `cancelled`. The tool call stays blocked in every case; no config, schema or protocol change.

## Why This Change Was Made

A single-phase request answers with `decision: null` both when the prompt expired and when no route existed, and the agent read every immediate null as no-route. The approval owner already records which one happened, so the single-phase response now carries the record's `terminalReason` (as `waitDecision` already does) and the resolved `deliveryRoute` (as the two-phase accepted response already does). The agent only treats an immediate null as no-route when the recorded reason is not `timeout`; a recorded timeout falls through to the existing shared timeout outcome, so there is no second copy of that logic. A response without `terminalReason` keeps the previous no-route behavior.

Production delta is +10/-2 in two files. #177713 carries a similar single-phase change inside a larger resolver-attribution feature; this PR is only the bug fix.

## Evidence

Live, through the real product: an isolated Gateway (own state dir, loopback, token auth), a scripted OpenAI-compatible model that calls `read` and then repeats the tool result it is given, and a one-file plugin whose `before_tool_call` returns `requireApproval` with `timeoutMs: 15_000`, a `timeoutReason` and an `onResolution` logger. I sent one message from the Control UI chat, let the approval card post in that chat, and did not answer it.

- Before (`main` at `54dc56391a7`): tool result `Plugin approval unavailable (no approval route)`; Gateway log `approval-demo onResolution: cancelled`.
- After: tool result is the plugin's `timeoutReason`; Gateway log `approval-demo onResolution: timeout`.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shu-chen-dot-ca/shu-chen-dot-ca/6e57971504b94ef7ece7ab0ee327b8370502ec2f/draft_8d3be8/ev_a02a83.jpg) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shu-chen-dot-ca/shu-chen-dot-ca/6e57971504b94ef7ece7ab0ee327b8370502ec2f/draft_8d3be8/ev_d5e5a8.jpg) |

The live run used the same two production edits on the older base `54dc56391a7`. The checks below ran on this branch's commit on `387d6d61a4b`; the live run was not repeated on that base. Discord and the Codex harness from the report were not exercised; the Control UI chat reaches the same in-process single-phase request.

Regression tests, red on the base and green on the head. Both runs use this branch's test files; the base run has the two production files checked out from `main` at `387d6d61a4b`, the head run is this branch's tree. Each file was run on its own with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`.

| Test | Base (production files from `387d6d61a4b`) | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plugin-approval.test.ts` > reports a delivered single-phase request that expired as a timeout | fails | passes |
| `plugin-approval.test.ts` > expires immediately when no approval route (now also asserts `terminalReason: "no-route"`, `deliveryRoute: "none"`) | fails | passes |
| `agent-tools.before-tool-call.approval-policy.test.ts` > reports an in-process approval that expired with the plugin timeout reason | fails | passes |
| `agent-tools.before-tool-call.approval-policy.test.ts` > reports an in-process approval that expired without a plugin timeout reason | fails | passes |
| `agent-tools.before-tool-call.approval-policy.test.ts` > reports an in-process approval that had no approval route | passes | passes |
| File totals | 2 failed, 24 passed (26); 2 failed, 8 passed (10) | 26 passed (26); 10 passed (10) |

The no-route row passes on both sides on purpose: it pins that a real no-route keeps its text and `cancelled`.

Other checks, all run with `--maxWorkers=1`:

- `approval-request-delivery.test.ts` pinned the exact single-phase response, so its expectation now includes `deliveryRoute: "none"`.
- Consumers: 15 approval test files under `src/gateway/server-methods` and `src/agents` pass, including the exec approval suites that share the handler.
- `run-format --check` on the changed files, `git diff --check`, and `pnpm check:changed` pass. `check:changed` ran with `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1`, so the Knip dead-code scan was not run locally.
- No local autoreview or ClawSweeper run.

prs.title: perf(secrets): skip plugin metadata for entries without config values
prs.body:
## Problem

Preparing SecretRefs loads plugin manifests for entries that only set activation policy. The CLI can do this during command preflight and local resolution even though those entries have no configuration fields for a plugin contract to match.

## User Impact

Local commands and secret preparation can skip this discovery when no plugin config contains a value. Plugins with config values keep their existing activation, stale-entry and warning behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The collector and snapshot preparation use the same check for plugin config fields before requesting metadata. Channel, web-tool and exec-provider requests keep their own discovery conditions. Refresh records whether an origin inventory was observed, so a later config change can discover a newly configured plugin and resolve its credentials.

## Evidence

On the frozen base with only the new tests applied, three cases failed. Policy-only entries, an empty config and the initial snapshot each triggered one metadata lookup. On the candidate all three triggered zero lookups. A later refresh that added a plugin credential discovered its owner and resolved the SecretRef.

Five focused suites passed all 20 tests, including bundled plugin manifests, disabled and stale entries, external-channel discovery, and snapshot cleanup. The production diff spans five files (+22/−17). There are no config or defaults changes. Device latency remains unmeasured.

An isolated run against the built JavaScript and normal CLI offline state owner prepared two snapshots with a core env SecretRef. An enable-only entry and an empty plugin config both produced zero manifest-helper imports and no recorded plugin inventory. Refresh added Tavily's `webSearch.apiKey`, loaded the real bundled manifest, and resolved the synthetic credential. The [normal package build and integrity check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45925643671) passed.

The draft Bun Gateway config-patch job failed during native-worker teardown. The exact test passed on [the frozen Linux base](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45922594758/job/140256917305) and in a focused Bun replay on the signed head. The [draft dependency check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45924417944/job/140262856301) matched [the base’s three Knip findings](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45922594758/job/140256915435). A separate npm install budget measured 47,950 entries against 47,500. An [earlier source build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45754810101/job/139696150497) also exceeded that budget. The exact base-to-head entry-count change is unmeasured.

prs.title: fix: keep additive state columns idempotent when the schema snapshot lags
prs.body:
Closes #202258

## What Problem This Solves

A node client connecting with a bootstrap token can be rejected in the hello phase with `duplicate column name: setup_id`. `ensureColumn` decides whether to add an additive state column from the **admitted schema snapshot**, and that snapshot can predate a column another connection just added. The `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` then races into SQLite's duplicate-column error, which fails the connect bookkeeping instead of completing it. The operator sees a rejected pairing and a Gateway error, while the column they need is already there.

## User Impact

User impact: a node pairing no longer fails when a first-use state column was added by another writer moments earlier — the additive step is treated as already done. A column that exists with a different definition still fails closed, so an incompatible shape is never silently accepted.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ensureColumn` now keeps its snapshot check and wraps the `ALTER` only for the documented race. On a duplicate-column error it reads the live catalog (`sqlite_master` plus the existing canonical table parser) and returns `false` — already present — only when the live column definition equals the requested column SQL after whitespace normalization. Anything else, including a generated column, a different type, or extra `NOT NULL` / `DEFAULT` / `CHECK` / `COLLATE` clauses, keeps the original error so the shape problem stays visible. The earlier fallback of comparing only `PRAGMA table_info` type and nullability could not see check, collation or reference constraints; this revision compares the full definition instead.

## Evidence

**Behavior checked:** an admitted connection whose schema snapshot predates a peer write. The peer adds the column, then the owner's `ensureColumn` runs.

base, `6ac896f4cbb` (fix reverted, new test kept), `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/state/openclaw-state-db-lazy-column-race.test.ts`:

```text
 × treats a column added by another connection as already present
   → duplicate column name: synthetic_lazy_column
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 1 passed
```

head, `4417d1cce5d`, same command:

```text
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

The three cases are: the identical racing column is treated as present; a different type still throws; a constrained duplicate (`TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'x'` requested as `TEXT`) still throws.

Neighbouring schema suites on the head:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/startup-migration-checkpoint.inspection.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  16 passed (16)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-recovery-database.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-standing-intents-schema.admission.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)   Tests  12 passed (12)
```

`pnpm tsgo:core` passes; `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` reports `All matched files use the correct format.`; `git diff --check` is clean. Local autoreview reports `scoped-clean` (0.8) on this head after its two earlier findings — comparing only type and nullability, then check/collation constraints — were addressed in the shipped comparison.

**Not run / gaps:**

- `src/state/openclaw-state-db-first-use-column-strict-migration.test.ts` has one red case on this head (`migrates legacy device_bootstrap_tokens (doctor: false)`, "expected function to throw"). It fails identically on the base commit, so this change does not cause it; I did not fix it here.
- No live bootstrap-token handshake was run: the failing owner is the schema helper, and the regression works through the same admitted-connection boundary the Gateway uses.
- Local ClawSweeper's engine cannot complete on this host, so autoreview is the only local review evidence.
- Fork PR CI needs a maintainer to approve the run, so it has not run.

## What Problem This Solves

On macOS, Doctor tells you to run `--fix` for stray launchd jobs even when that invocation will refuse the repair. A relocated state directory can put you in that loop.

## User Impact

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The release-note verifier can look up the same issues and pull requests three times in one audit. With snapshots disabled, each collector pass sends another GitHub request even when it already has every reference it needs.

## User Impact

A release operator gets the same contribution record with fewer GitHub requests. Newly discovered closing pull requests still get fetched. Missing references still get checked again, including cases where live evidence can invalidate a historical attribution.

## Why This Change Was Made

The collector already owns the ordered list of references and each pass's recovery evidence. It retains the most recent complete live lookup for this invocation. Each pass still applies recovery to its own map. The persisted snapshot keeps its existing repository, base and target identity.

## Evidence

Ran the verifier CLI before and after the change against a Git fixture with snapshots disabled and a recording GitHub API stub. An already-known closing PR went from three metadata requests to one. Discovering the closing PR from a legacy issue went from three requests to two. Both cases produced the same PR and the same writer and reporter credits before and after. Targeted formatting and diff checks passed.

prs.title: fix: let agents answer before soft compaction repeats source reads
prs.body:
Closes #205954

## What Problem This Solves

A final source read can cross the soft compaction threshold even when the intact request and full answer still fit. Compacting there can make the resumed agent reread completed sources instead of answering.

## User Impact

The agent gets one ordinary call with intact history after a settled tool batch if the full output allowance fits. Trailing trusted runtime-context carriers do not hide that boundary. They remain in the request and its token estimate; ordinary user messages are not skipped.

The limit survives attempt retries. Hard overflow, insufficient headroom and unfinished tools retain their existing handling. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

I reused the request-boundary pressure owner and the canonical runtime-context metadata predicate. The check uses the larger input estimate, the effective context window and the full completion reservation.

I added the three supplied regression cases and a production-projection case using the real carrier builder, tail relocation, prompt submission, tool, serializer and checkpoint path. Only the provider HTTP reply is scripted in that integration case.

I ran pr-simplify. The PR adds no new configuration or compaction owner; the net diff against its main base is +47 production, +103 test and +8 documentation lines.

## Evidence

- **Red:** on the rebased, unfixed head `f30679b32741`, [VM job 139969078400](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45836913703/job/139969078400) failed both carrier cases. The real projection produced a trusted user-role tail and sent `[ordinary, summary]` instead of `[ordinary, ordinary]`; the rebuilt-boundary case raised `MidTurnPrecheckSignal` instead of deferring.
- **Green:** on `165d58e53b2264ab7852b8b84714b2e1ccb6836b`, the identical test file passed **11/11** in [VM job 139972835943](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45837973820/job/139972835943). The integration case retained the tool evidence and runtime context and saved no checkpoint. The retry case allowed exactly one deferral.
- The selected embedded-run project passed 104 files and 1,618 tests, with one existing skip. Its CI duration was 119.90 seconds; the 11 boundary cases reported 183 ms combined. Standalone file wall time was not separately measured.

prs.title: feat: dismiss browser completion notifications after viewing replies
prs.body:
Related: #202178

## What Problem This Solves

Browser/PWA completion notifications can remain after the corresponding reply has been read, leaving stale alerts to dismiss manually.

## User Impact and Read Boundaries

Dismiss only the notification for an exact final reply visibly viewed in the foreground. Preserve unrelated sessions, newer/unseen replies and legacy alerts without reliable identity. Cleanup is local to the same browser/service-worker registration, not cross-device recall.

Payload and transcript identity match on agent/session/run/message/recipient. Message identity prefers the persisted idempotency key and otherwise uses the row ID. Session opening, history loading and notification tags alone do not acknowledge a completion.

The layout review finding is corrected: read presentation requires an active row, settled initial position and release of the transcript's hidden state. Resource preparation remains independently enabled. Layout/foreground/connection/profile ownership fences queued callbacks synchronously.

At most 512 page-memory visibility receipts are retained for six minutes (five-minute push TTL plus margin). The worker's after-display hint reconciles late pushes while a page is visible. Closing all pages forgets receipts; there is no durable cross-restart acknowledgement guarantee. Support is limited to the serving Gateway's origin and registration scope.

## Evidence

Current head: `77c4b9c37366360e09a1137064d6ad0ed9afc750`.

### Import-cycle repair — validation NOT RUN

Moved the unchanged read-presentation context into `chat-transcript-read-presentation.ts`, a dependency leaf importing only Solid, and updated the hook, renderer and hook test to import it directly. The old layout export is removed. This addresses the reported static dependency edge without changing visibility or receipt policy (five files, +7/−6).

Static diff review and `git diff --check` passed. **The canonical import-cycle gate, affected tests, formatting, lint, UI types and UI build have NOT RUN for this repair.** The two bounded fork proof pushes produced no Actions runs; the cause remains unresolved. No checks, hooks or baselines were bypassed. This is a transparent review submission, **not merge-ready**. Repository proof guidance prefers draft publication when builds are unavailable; the existing non-draft status is preserved, not a claim that its ready-proof standard is met.

### Historical proof — predates the import-cycle repair

All evidence and input-equivalence inventories below apply to their stated prior revisions, not to the changed import graph at the current head. They do not validate this repair.


- [Prior-head formatting, allocation and input-equivalence proof at 45b07b2](https://github.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/actions/runs/44847422160): **passed**. The runner verified the exact formatter-only transformation from the preceding tested head plus allocation 704 → 706, with every other tracked entry unchanged. No browser/test rerun is claimed at this formatting-only head.
- [Behavioral proof at 81b1d5daa9e6853930dd70637261d89998ecda84](https://github.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/actions/runs/44846626872): Chromium upgrade/notification test, 2 identity tests, 8 runtime tests and the required scoped canonical lint wrapper **passed**. That run's sole failure was the formatter line-wrap now corrected and verified above.
- Chromium installs the pinned released v2026.11.5 worker, retains its identity-less notification, updates the same registration without clearing storage, verifies the running candidate's embedded build identity, and preserves exact legacy notification data. It then verifies unread/newer/other-session preservation, exact foreground-read dismissal, emulated foreground return and delayed-delivery reconciliation. Listener installation is acknowledged before injection. The redundant key-inequality test was removed; observable identity-separation coverage remains.
- Reuse inventory SHA-256 versus the behavioral head, excluding only the exactly verified formatter/allocation files: `ce5102240c16f636e511e8c8dca8085292eeede95f053412ec2497073a982668`. Final browser-test bytes SHA-256: `18202c2d781d9021027d5964ed34384d218bb82a836d343eb5403646085ed1e4`.
- At prior head `45b07b2be25bbbeddafde2ba4511c3a15f88bd12`, production/dependency/configuration inputs independently matched the previously tested layout repair at `e0b0cb680c18b19585d52f72d65cb00e5f9dab89`; only two tests, the historical worker fixture and allocation differ. Inventory SHA-256: `8de953c2417347cb9d5fd655abe535e218627ef3b20b9b79feaa5675f36cc227`. The [full production build and real-renderer regression](https://github.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/actions/runs/44801786340), [affected layout suites, UI production types and UI build](https://github.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/actions/runs/44800188759), and independently unchanged [core-type proof](https://github.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/actions/runs/44797497267) retain their original scopes. Historical format/lint failures in the core-type run were separately repaired; its entire run is not described as passing.

## Tested Scope and Remaining Decisions

This is desktop Chromium behavior using real ServiceWorker/Notification APIs, CDP-injected push, mocked Gateway transport and emulated visibility transitions. It does not establish real encrypted Web Push transport, native OS notification shade/suspension, Safari/mobile behavior, or a complete old UI/Gateway upgrade. No device access or mobile acceptance is claimed. Android-specific validation is not automatically a prerequisite for this browser feature; the stated tested scope remains for reviewer acceptance.

[Current-head upstream CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45926700776) is `action_required` as last checked; maintainer admission and required upstream results are separate from the fork evidence.
