prs.title: fix: honor conversation voice settings in agent prompts
prs.body:
Closes #206103

## What Problem This Solves

An agent can receive the global TTS instructions while the conversation uses a different voice setting. For example, a Feishu channel in `tagged` mode receives no guidance for adding a TTS tag, and an account with voice set to `off` can still receive guidance to prepare a voice reply.

## User Impact

The agent sees voice guidance for the channel and account saved on that conversation. A `tagged` channel gets guidance on tagging speech, and an account set to `off` gets no voice guidance. The saved conversation scope also holds when another account wakes the turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prompt preparation already has the saved session delivery route. Pass its channel and account into the existing TTS settings resolver, which applies the same configuration precedence used by delivery. The embedded prompt, CLI preparation, compaction, and `/system-prompt` use this shared builder.

## Evidence

The regression passes prepared conversation delivery metadata into the embedded agent's prompt builder. The Anthropic adapter serializes the prompt and an in-process fetch recorder captures the request's `system` blocks. The fixture uses a global `inbound` policy, a Feishu `tagged` override, and a Feishu account set to `off`. Each turn uses the opposite account from the conversation metadata.

| Saved conversation setting | Base `2ab7b31a13d9` | Candidate `02714b6e3f17` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Channel `tagged`, `voice` account | Global inbound guidance | 1 voice guidance section with tagging instructions |
| Account `off`, `quiet` account | Global inbound guidance | 0 voice guidance sections |

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-system-prompt.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'uses saved .* voice settings'
```

Both cases failed on the base and passed with the candidate tree. The candidate took 446.55 seconds with one worker, including worker compilation and the transport fixture setup. Formatting, typed lint, and the test-line budget check passed. AI assistance was used for implementation and verification.

An independent source and evidence pass on `2ab7b31a13d9..02714b6e3f17` found no blocking implementation issue and clarified the recorder's scope. No structured autoreview result is available for this commit.

- Not tested: Session storage and reload, hosted Feishu calls, speech synthesis, prompt-prefix stability, live CLI backends, compaction, and `/system-prompt` execution.

prs.title: feat: use one check script for model-free automations
prs.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Do not land.** Still in progress and under discussion. Talk to @vyctorbrzezowski.

## What Problem This Solves

Today, writing an automation that checks something without a model starts with a choice between a condition script and a script payload. They share the same saved state, but have different result formats and cannot be combined.

## User Impact

- Use one JavaScript check to stay quiet, post a message through the automation’s delivery, or append a message to a configured agent prompt and run it. Configure it in the Control UI, use `--check-script` in the CLI, or send `check` through the automations tool or Gateway. Shell command jobs keep their separate operator policy.
- Run `openclaw doctor --fix` after upgrading. Doctor backs up cron storage, reports each conversion, and carries over saved state, once behavior, execution limits and tool restrictions for jobs it can convert. If it cannot preserve what a job does—such as a script waking an existing conversation, a condition starting a shell command or system event, or a result it cannot safely translate—it pauses the job and reports why. Recover the original definition from the backup, edit the check, then re-enable it.

## Why This Change Was Made

One executor and one check result replace the two JavaScript execution paths. Shell commands do not become agent-callable checks. The draft touches shared automation schema, run finalization, Doctor, CLI flags, and the Control UI editor; those are likely conflict points with the sibling automation cleanup PRs.

## Evidence

I merged main at `fc25865d99bd0166efbe6f70d93df979e68e19ac` without rebasing or force-pushing. The draft head is `ca0e135843943c7c02f5b9e63994452335dabd1c`.

I reproduced the dropped flat/dotted check fields, incorrect validation classification, failed quiet check-only completion, and state loss on check-budget edits before fixing them. Focused local CLI, Gateway, scheduler, runtime, storage, Doctor, and UI suites passed after migrating the affected fixtures. The last backend rerun passed 104 tests; the final UI run passed 72 tests. Core/UI production and affected cron, Gateway, Doctor, and UI-test typechecks passed, along with changed-file lint/format, the UI copy baseline, and generated Gateway validator verification. The SQLite tests cover backup, conversion, state/tool-cap preservation, unsupported-job pausing, idempotency, and legacy finalized-script state recovery. These are local boundary tests, not released-install upgrade proof.

The simplification pass removed the retired script executor path and the opt-in screenshot-only regression test while preserving timeout, authority, cancellation, delivery, state, and recovery coverage. The generated Gateway validator change is required for the new public check contract; it is generator output, not a hand-written workaround.

Runtime proof still needed: a real Gateway quiet/post/wake flow with an actual agent/model and delivery, state/once/pacing and restart behavior; fresh-install and real upgrades from supported older releases, including 9.x extended-stable and 10.x, with the old updater round trip and in-flight legacy recovery; accessible annotated before/after captures from the real editor. A final production build and final-head CI are also not verified. Local independent review could not start because Codex failed its read-only sandbox preflight. prs.title: refactor: use task prompts for scheduled reminders
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scheduling a reminder in an existing conversation shouldn’t require a special action just for the agent’s main conversation. The editor, CLI, and agent tool offered two ways to schedule that work, with different delivery and execution rules.

## User Impact

Use an agent task with `session:<key>` to continue an existing conversation, including the main conversation. Control UI no longer offers **Post to main session** or **Runs in: Main session**. CLI scripts should replace `--system-event` and `--session main` with `--message` and the actual conversation key, for example `--session session:agent:main:main` or `--session session:global` on a global-scope install.

After upgrading, run `openclaw doctor --fix`. Doctor backs up cron state and reports each conversion. It rewrites eligible jobs in place, retaining their ID, schedule, enabled state, run history, scratch, and valid delivery settings. The target is the owning agent’s main conversation, with `session:global` for global scope. If Doctor cannot faithfully continue a job (for example, a headless script that used the old main-session notification behavior, a missing prompt, or an unresolved owner), it pauses the job and explains what to review before enabling it. The model now sees the reminder as a **task prompt**, not as a system notice.

## Why This Change Was Made

An explicit conversation key uses the same queue and execution path regardless of which conversation it names. Immediate hook wakes, channel join and lifecycle notices, and post-run notices from scheduled plugin commands still use the internal notice path where applicable: they report an event to the conversation, rather than being user-authored automation prompts. Backup schedules already run an isolated command and do not need the removed mode.

Expected overlap with the sibling automation cleanups: the shared cron schema and generated validators, Doctor’s cron repair, scheduler routing, CLI and agent tool descriptions, and the Control UI editor and docs. This change does not redesign the remaining modes or wake policy.

## Evidence

- Doctor’s SQLite repair tests passed for a named agent with a custom main key and for global scope (2 tests). They cover backup creation, preserved job ID, disabled state, schedule, last-run state, delivery, prompt, and a no-op second repair.
- Cron protocol validation passed (93 tests); generated-validator parity, core and UI typechecks, formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed. The focused CLI run was interrupted by a source change while the subprocess compiler was building; the full CLI, scheduler, native client, and upgrade suites were not verified here.
- Local Codex autoreview (P1, three passes) found that same-kind payload edits had lost their field updates. The update logic was restored; the follow-up core typecheck passed. The final delta was not independently re-reviewed.
- The real Control UI was exercised in Chromium with a mocked Gateway and a fictional weekly garden-inventory reminder. Both capture checks passed. The before capture used the original worktree UI source, which matched `origin/main` outside translation artifacts. The captures show the Action picker; no live model or channel delivery is demonstrated.

prs.title: fix: keep Gateway responsive while scanning large model catalogs
prs.body:
Closes #145675
Alternative to #145676
Related: #156054

## What Problem This Solves

When an operator configures a large model catalog (500-1,000+ entries), `projectCatalog` and Gateway `models.list` evaluate routes, credentials, and public model projections in uninterrupted synchronous loops. Across a persistent `openclaw gateway` daemon and controlled 500-1,000 model scans, this blocks the Node.js event loop for roughly 0.9s to 22.9s at a time, stalling concurrent health checks, control-plane RPCs, and channel traffic until the scan finishes.

## User Impact

- Concurrent loopback HTTP requests stay responsive both on a running `openclaw gateway` daemon serving live CLI/WebSocket `models.list` calls (`GET /healthz` median `2,467.4 ms -> 16.0 ms`, max `5,186.7 ms -> 159.4 ms` across 1,011 models) and in controlled in-process benchmarks, and repeated `prepared.read()` calls on a prepared catalog avoid multi-second synchronous projection stalls (see Verification gaps below for live external cloud-provider network discovery).
- No configuration, schema, migration, or caller API changes are required; public synchronous reader contracts remain unchanged and the change can be reverted cleanly.
- Operational boundaries:
  - The `8 ms` budget (`CATALOG_SCAN_YIELD_BUDGET_MS`) is a cooperative checkpoint between model entries during asynchronous preparation. It cannot preempt synchronous work inside a single model evaluation, non-per-entry setup/sorting, WebSocket JSON serialization, or the final single-frame live readiness publication pass, so it is not a hard real-time latency bound; in standalone `projectCatalog` benchmarks, median scan wall time stayed within `-0.3%` to `+2.9%` while `models.list` end-to-end wall time in direct in-process benchmarks dropped by removing redundant read-time work.
  - Callers that pass a `withCurrent` authority wrapper without a synchronous `assertCurrent` callback disable inter-entry slice yields inside that wrapper (after pre-wrapper selected-account settlement when applicable) so wrapper-scoped invariants hold.

## Why This Change Was Made

Catalog preparation and `models.list` now split static preparation from live synchronous publication:

1. **Cooperative sliced preparation and static warming:** `projectCatalog` and `prepareModelsListResult` (`provider-config`, `default`, `all`, and `configured` views) yield via `node:timers/promises` `setImmediate` after `8 ms` slices while warming host route evaluations, static native policy and non-`openclaw`/`auto` host configuration, memoized harness policies/support contexts/provider ownership, shared configured route overrides, and static public display/thinking fields.
2. **Reasserted authority and single-frame live publication:** Slice resumptions and publication boundaries recheck the path's active guards (caller `CurrentReadAuthority`, independent draft and publication scopes, and entry-to-stale transitions on owner currency and `authValidUntil`), while `notePendingAccountCatalogPreparation` and `accountCatalogEpoch` coordinate `projectCatalog` rescanning when concurrent selected-account outcomes publish. New static warmers stop before revocable native readiness (`evaluateNative` / `readModelCatalogReadiness`) and live `harness.supports` probes so final `projectCatalog` projection and synchronous `prepared.read()` re-evaluate live readiness, `harness.supports`, and alternative-runtime exclusion in one synchronous frame (while preserving existing preparation-time checks for picker-alternative base selection, heterogeneous default previews, and initial `provider-config` projection), and `src/agents/model-auth-*.ts` stays untouched to preserve the provider-config fast path landed in #156054.

Thanks to #145676 and its author for earlier investigation on #145675; with the provider-config comparison fast path landed separately in #156054, this PR implements cooperative slicing and static warming against current `main`'s catalog preparation and multi-view Gateway projection paths.

<details>
<summary>Implementation details</summary>

- `src/agents/model-catalog-decision-runtime.ts` & `src/agents/model-catalog-decisions.ts`:
  - `createCatalogProjectionReader` warms per-entry host evaluations, static native policy, and static route projections in `8 ms` slices (`CATALOG_SCAN_YIELD_BUDGET_MS = 8`), rechecking active `authority?.assertCurrent?.()` and entry-valid-to-stale transitions across credential expiry, secret-snapshot revisions, personal-catalog currency, owner currency, and selected-account observations on slice resumptions and before publication.
  - `notePendingAccountCatalogPreparation` and `accountCatalogEpoch` synchronize concurrent session-metadata `projectCatalog` and `prepareModelsListResult` callers across `0..M` selected-account discovery publications, retiring per-provider and auth-alias `evaluations` entries and resetting `projectedCatalog` whenever account outcomes update, and caching `projectedCatalog` only for unretired, authority-free callers.
  - `createCatalogDecisionRuntimeResolver` preserves no-registry policy selection and `openclaw` fast-path semantics, memoizing `resolveProviderRefOwnership` per normalized provider, `resolveAgentHarnessPolicy`, and `buildAgentHarnessSupportContext` while keeping CLI-binding short-circuits, `auto` selection hints/priorities, `fallbackRuntime`, and live `harness.supports` checks intact, and skipping `withPluginRuntimeRegistryScope` when no plugin registry or only `"openclaw"` policy applies.
- `src/agents/model-catalog-view.ts`:
  - `createCatalogNativePolicyPreparer` exposes `prepareNativePolicy` to warm static harness policy and per-provider merged host configuration while preserving the `openclaw` / `auto` short-circuit (no extra `resolveMergedModelProviderConfig` or `apiKey` getter reads on ordinary rows) and stopping before revocable `readModelCatalogReadiness` checks.
  - `createModelCatalogView` accepts an optional shared `resolveOverrides` resolver and reuses cached donor projections when route variants match while keeping narrowed runtime donor sets isolated.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/models-list-result.ts` & `src/gateway/server-methods/models-list-runtime-choices.ts`:
  - `createScanAuthority` combines active `preparationAuthority`, `draftAccountSelection`, `publicationScope`, and entry-valid-to-stale transitions on personal-catalog and target-projector currency across `provider-config` inventory warming and logical-visible catalog preparation while keeping `withCurrent` wrapper entry counts bounded.
  - `createModelsListPublicProjector` and `prepareModelPickerRuntimeChoices` cache static display/fast-mode fields by `(provider, id)`, worker-placement `agentRuntime` by `(id, source)`, and main-row thinking profiles, keying per-entry projections by `(runtimeChoice, selectedRuntime.id, selectedRuntime.source)` and filtering picker alternatives against the live selected runtime on each read so live harness fallback transitions update the main row, `runtimeChoices`, and `defaultModelRuntimes` consistently while keeping alternative runtime donors' `thinkingLevels` isolated.

</details>

## Evidence

In separate segmented `prepareModelsListResult` measurements on `e4517b0ef2f4`, the 1st synchronous `prepared.read()` took `35.3-36.6 ms` at `N = 500` and `72.4-81.1 ms` at `N = 1,000` across the three picker views, and `15.0 ms` / `36.6 ms` on `provider-config` (down from `3,899.1 ms` and `14,179.8 ms` before the fix on `default` view).

prs.title: fix(memory): keep note frontmatter out of durable memory
prs.body:
Closes #148186

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes note bookkeeping such as `status: active` entering memory recall and durable-memory promotion when it appears inside complete leading YAML frontmatter.

## User Impact

Recall returns note bodies with their original citation lines, and promotion rejects stale frontmatter hits. Unchanged notes are reindexed after upgrade; YAML-looking session content and incomplete frontmatter remain eligible.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse Markdown Core's delimiter and newline grammar through one dependency-free extractor, preserve source-line offsets, and advance the chunking revision from 6 to 7. Indexing, `memory_get`, and promotion rehydration agree on LF, CRLF, and bare CR.

Thanks to @gisk0 for #148186 and the earlier #148190, closed **unmerged** for inactivity. This change addresses that PR's index-invalidation and CR-line findings, with committed regressions and an upgrade from genuinely contaminated pre-fix index rows. Its complete discussion and related PR discussions were checked again; open #151299 covers separate promotion-anchor ambiguity rules.

## Evidence


Current integration `5e0b26c810c55c16e59d7d002a5fdd25a764d0dc` merges pinned main `11eaf275705bb106275ce9071061464b016d8291` into the original branch to include the accepted monotonic-clock fixture repair [#187454](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187454), merged as `933304ebaa40c3bcc6503567cbce7a480df808db`. This addresses the exact `tools.index-upgrade.test.ts:197` warning assertion that failed on prior head `3adeaba9`; the detailed prior-head CI diagnosis is retained below. The correction advances the same `performance.now()` clock used by the cooldown owner and includes performance in the three sibling suites' fake clocks. It changes no production clock, assertion, timeout, check rule, dependency, or test budget.

On this exact merged tree (`c9042b04801ae2fe9ceef5a2cf5983b4b89e6443`), **182 tests passed across eight complete files**, using Node 24.22.1 and the repository runner in 272.86 seconds wall. This covers all four upstream clock-fixture files, the original three frontmatter indexing/promotion/readback suites, and Markdown Core's parser suite. The previously failing detached-maintenance/provider-cost case passed in 3.65 seconds. Scoped typechecking, lint and format for the ten PR-owned TypeScript files plus four clock fixtures, and `git diff --check`, passed. Command:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/tools.index-upgrade.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-session-delta.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-reindex-resume.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-startup-close.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-index-preparation.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/read-file-shared.test.ts packages/markdown-core/src/frontmatter.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The merge uses both true parents (`3adeaba9` and pinned main), with historical merge base `50c3ff63`. All eleven PR-owned file blobs, including all product changes and original regressions, remain byte-identical to `3adeaba9`; the diff against main remains exactly those eleven files. Earlier feature/Gateway/stable-upgrade and canonical P0–P3 autoreview evidence below is retained for those unchanged product bytes and its recorded inputs; it is not relabeled as an execution or full-range review of this new head. This synchronization adds no product code or tests. An independent read-only integration review confirmed both parents, all retained upstream paths, unchanged PR-owned blobs, identical dependency manifests/lockfiles, and unweakened clock-fixture assertions; no actionable finding. Its scope is this mechanical integration, not a replacement canonical review of the full feature. Current-head hosted CI now passes, including test types, changed-extension/Bun, baseline ratchets, and all three PostgreSQL conformance checks. No additional Gateway build or release run was performed for this mechanical merge.

- **Original feature proof: 158 tests passed**: the three affected indexing, promotion, and readback owners (122 tests, 179.07s wall time), plus Markdown Core's existing parser suite (36 tests). Against the unfixed production owners, six regression cases fail; fixed owners pass. Coverage includes LF/CRLF/CR, metadata-only notes, incomplete blocks, session preservation, relocated promotion candidates, and citation readback at line 4.
- **Actual built CLI/Gateway upgrade passed** (547.28s including packaged bootstrap and rebuilding the fixed runtime). The old CLI indexed and recalled two YAML-contaminated notes at revision 6. Without editing those files or manually changing persisted revision metadata, the fixed CLI's ordinary `memory index --agent qa` rebuilt revision 7 with only the body chunk at line 4. Through real plugin registration and QA-channel ingress, `memory_search` then `memory_get` used `from: 4` and returned the body without YAML. The final channel reply contained the recalled fact.
- **Actual `memory promote --apply` passed**: one valid body was appended to `MEMORY.md`; both pre-fix metadata-only and mixed metadata/body recalls were rejected during source rehydration. The resulting durable memory contained the body and no `status: active` metadata.

prs.title: feat: set up Llama and llama.cpp without installing a plugin first
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

To use the Llama app or a llama.cpp server, people first have to run `openclaw plugins install @openclaw/llama-cpp-provider` -- until then, neither shows up in `openclaw onboard`. LM Studio and Ollama are there out of the box.

## User Impact

Llama and llama.cpp show up in `openclaw onboard` on a fresh install, like LM Studio and Ollama. Local GGUF memory embeddings no longer need the install step either. The plugin stays published to npm and ClawHub, for standalone builds that leave it out.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin moved out of core when it depended on `node-llama-cpp`. Since [the managed-server change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/123105) it manages a `llama-server` instead, and its only runtime dependency is `@openclaw/fs-safe`, which core already ships.

It follows the Cloudflare pattern from [the Cloudflare packaging fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174287): dropped from the root package's exclusion list, and its official catalog entry marked `bundledDist: true`. Publication is unchanged.

The docs drop the install step (llama.cpp, Llama, memory and custom-provider pages), and the plugin inventory is regenerated.

## Evidence

- `pnpm plugins:inventory:check` passes.

Approved the lightweight bundled-provider direction using the existing packaging/catalog owners. No runtime dependency or provider-specific core path is added. Runtime and test code: unchanged; packaging metadata: +3/-1; docs: +11/-28.

Verified unchanged head `6545a24e47f7efe0bdae9de34795dfd96ddfe948` on Darwin arm64 with Node 26.7.0 and pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`:

Model selection, endpoint/provider configuration, credential use, and explicit disablement survived. Doctor retired the old install record. Inspection selected exactly one bundled plugin from the candidate package; after re-enabling, keyed inference passed.

The archive was reused after standalone native validation; the original packer exceeded its outer five-minute limit during cleanup. This addresses the installed-package/upgrade evidence and owner-decision requests in the existing ClawSweeper review. The reviewed source head is unchanged, so no redundant re-review was requested.

prs.title: feat: preview saved snippets during browser dictation
prs.body:
Related: #205639

**Draft — existing fork experiment for design and source review. Product/composer/SDK/storage decisions and runtime qualification remain open. This is not an accepted small first slice or a ready-to-merge implementation.**

## What Problem This Solves

People dictating repeated replies or signatures need to deliberately select saved wording, inspect the expansion, and keep the result editable and unsent. Literal spelling, Unicode, line breaks and leading zeroes should survive insertion.

This draft exposes the existing M07 implementation for upstream review. The unresolved first decision is whether automatic expansion should use a narrow finalized-dictation extension contract or whether the first milestone should be a manually invoked draft plugin. The [durable issue review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205639#issuecomment-7178316740) also requires a bounded storage decision and reconciliation with request-start admission. No human acceptance of those contracts is claimed.

## User Impact

The source adds disabled-by-default browser snippet management and review surfaces, exact phrase resolution, and dictation capture integration. It shows source and expansion before application and treats snippet bodies as inert text.

The experiment is broader than the proposed small consumer: it includes multiple triggers/locales, sensitivity, import/export and a large reserved catalogue. Actual capture-order review survival, untouched mention metadata, one Undo, destination fidelity and absence of implicit Send still need production-path qualification. There is no accepted migration or retention promise for experimental authored data.

## Why This Change Was Made

This publishes the unchanged source branch from [CompleteDotTech/openclaw#2](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/pull/2):

- Source: `CompleteDotTech:feat/dictation-voice-snippets`
- Head: `1ebef5438b9c1b46b345c64fb9adeb01538c597c`
- Tree: `4f719b24510f81c87d01d7b424bc4aaf3c4d0646`
- Original fork PR base: `b7bd237d00508e0999c7a3fc6e36bc32bf421098`
- Upstream target: `main`; pre-filing comparison pin `9ced54f92982564d9504bc1c5d08196c37dea914`
- Common merge base: `b48d578d023765ac86fe44d38d65cfac991ad03c`

No new product implementation, rebase or source-branch rewrite was performed for this publication. At the stated comparison pin, the branch is four commits ahead and 391 behind; the merge-base-to-head diff is 60 files, +6,605/−128 lines. These are not residual-change statistics from an equivalent current-main tree, and no current-main mergeability is claimed.

The diff includes 13 prior [design and evidence documents](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/tree/1ebef5438b9c1b46b345c64fb9adeb01538c597c/clawsweeperv2/M07-voice-snippets). They record an earlier design-only iteration. Their proposed tiny catalogue and host contract are not implemented or accepted merely because they appear beside the existing experiment. The size and inherited differences need reconciliation before this becomes a ready candidate. M07-related tooling changes include the benchmark's Knip registration, a 1,631-line test allocation and one database-worker test-routing entry; no workflow files change.

### Decisions and source findings still open

| Boundary | Existing source and required reconciliation |
| --- | --- |
| Storage | The fork retains a 9-MiB reserved value, 500 total records and 16-KiB bodies, with a key-quota exemption and special comparison, access, deletion and merge rules. These material changes are unaccepted. The proposed eight-entry, 64-byte-trigger, 256-byte-body alternative within a complete 4,096-byte value is documentation, not this implementation. Generic 4,096-byte/128-key/32-entry limits remain the design baseline unless an expanded owner contract is accepted. |
| Admission | Review preparation, acceptance and export reload catalogue state and reject revision changes. The proposed one-admitted-snapshot behavior is not implemented. Actual transport/input/target authority must remain distinct from feature-content revalidation. |
| Capture lifetime | Starting a later capture cancels the preceding snippet-capture instance. Existing transcript commit ordering does not establish survival of an earlier stopped snippet review. |
| Input transaction | The private review path assigns text and calls the draft commit helper. Untouched mention identity and one Undo require the accepted editor/proposal integration and actual proof. |
| Feature-Off work | Catalogue loading starts before the enabled state is known. Disabled output behavior does not establish a zero-catalogue-work path. |
| Current-main integration | The owner files predate newer background-recording and normal-prose capacity handling. Selective adaptation must preserve those current behaviors rather than transplant the older files. |

These are source observations, not reproduced live failures or accepted standalone prerequisite fixes. M11 #205973 and developer-literal #205892 remain distinct drafts, not accepted shared APIs or automatic dependency approval. Existing Talk/Gateway transport authority, explicit Stop/Cancel and input/target checks must remain intact.

## Evidence

- Refreshed the canonical issue, durable review, existing fork PR and its separate discussion/formal-review/inline inventories. No human M07 acceptance was found.
- Checked upstream duplicates, author filing capacity, exact source identity, current repository guidance and the comparison stated above.
- Read the named snippet/shared owners, capture/direct/session owners, actual review/catalogue components, immediate caller/input contracts and preference owners to the bounded coverage recorded in the source audit. This does not constitute exhaustive transitive-caller or framework qualification.
- Manually inspected added, deleted and context lines in all 60 returned file patches at the unchanged source head. No missing patches or apparent credential/private-data publication blocker was found; this bounded inspection is not a security certification or runtime test.
- The fork PR's historical test/build/benchmark reports remain attributed to their original source and body. They were not rerun for this publication. Previously committed synthetic byte arithmetic establishes only serialization sizes.
- **NOT COLLECTED for this publication:** repository tests; affected type/lint/build checks; actual built Control UI served by a real Gateway; physical microphone and provider flow; keyboard/screen-reader proof; exact Apply/Undo/mention behavior; and stable-to-candidate binary upgrade/rollback.
- The inspected browser E2E harness uses a mock Gateway and fake-media flags. It cannot establish the requested physical-microphone/real-provider journey.
- No build-capacity exception, runtime pass, maintainer acceptance or successful ClawSweeper re-review is claimed. Source inspection and document checks are not runtime qualification.

### Follow-up source reconciliation (not runtime proof)

- Read the [full ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206273#issuecomment-7207321545) and the [tracking issue’s owner decision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205639#issuecomment-7178316740). A local reconciliation of this PR head with main at `d7c76283f28c` found two conflicts: dictation placement/settlement and the browser dictation E2E suite. The workspace resolution keeps main’s background recording coverage and UTF-16-safe normal-prose capacity handling. **No source changes from this follow-up are on the PR head.**
- [Stopped-recording delivery (`340610b`)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/340610b09eece489c19555bbf80c5474262fe7d7) establishes the ordering invariant: Stop releases the microphone but retains each recording until the provider settles; later provider results must not overtake earlier stopped captures. Coverage still needs the snippet-enabled case with two captures, a newer final observed first, and review outcomes delivered in capture order.
- **Pending proof:** Built Control UI + isolated Gateway + live provider for review, exact Apply, mention identity, one Undo, zero implicit Send, ordered stops, and the disabled path. Scripted Chromium audio is useful interim proof if the provider is live; physical microphone/permissions and device behavior are separate. Also pending: shipped v2026.11.10 → exact candidate with two durable profiles, exact preference readback, and the accepted reserved-key and profile-merge behavior.
- No fork runtime code was run for this follow-up. No test pass, upgrade pass, maintainer decision, or rating improvement is claimed.


This draft remains pending the product/composer/SDK/storage decision, reconciliation of the source findings, applicable exact-candidate validation and required owner/security review. It does not close the umbrella issue.

prs.title: fix(update): read SQLite lock bytes as zeros through fs-safe
prs.body:
> **Draft, blocked on an fs-safe release.** This needs `@openclaw/fs-safe` with `zeroRanges` (openclaw/fs-safe#1111). After that PR is released, this branch will add the `package.json` and lockfile bump to the new version. Until then, typecheck in CI fails against 0.28.2. The branch is rebased on `main` after #205668 merged.

## Problem

#205668 fixed the post-migration hash, the step that fails in the Windows `EBUSY` reports in #197083. On Windows, SQLite's lock bytes at 1 GiB are mandatory locks. Another path still reads them: when the database has retained WAL frames, `prepareSqliteReadOnlyLocation` makes a private copy with `copyRootFileSync` and verifies it with `sameFileContentsSync`. Both read every byte. Under another connection's `EXCLUSIVE` lock, that copy fails on any database larger than 1 GiB. #205668 also added a hand-written hash loop to OpenClaw.

## Solution

Use the new fs-safe `zeroRanges` option: byte ranges treated as zeros without being read.

- `SQLITE_LOCK_BYTE_RANGES` (`sqlite-snapshot-file.ts`) is the single definition of SQLite's 512 lock bytes.
- The main-database generation hash calls `hashFileDescriptorSync(fd, { zeroRanges })`. The hash loop from #205668 is removed. Digests are unchanged, because SQLite leaves those bytes zero.
- The main-database private copy (`copySourceFile`) and its verification (`sourceMatchesCopy`) pass the same ranges. WAL and journal copies pass none and still read every byte, since a WAL can hold frames at that offset.
- `hashFileDescriptorSync` now takes an options object (`maxBytes`, `zeroRanges`); its three `maxBytes` callers are updated.

## Evidence

Real Windows proof on Windows 11 ARM64 (Node 24.22.3) with a 1.15 GB WAL database:
- **Setup:** a second process held the migration owner's native exclusion (`PRAGMA schema_version`, then `locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE; BEGIN EXCLUSIVE; ROLLBACK`). In one case it kept committed WAL frames, which forces the private copy.
- **Build:** the real `readUpdateDatabaseGeneration`, bundled from #205668 and from this branch. This branch used a locally built fs-safe#1111 together with the published 0.28.2 binaries and win32-arm64 native binding.

| Owner state | #205668 | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| unlocked | ok | ok |
| exclusive, drained | ok | ok; digest matches the unlocked empty-reader alternate |
| exclusive, retained WAL frames (copy path) | `guarded synchronous file copy failed` | **ok**; same content digest as unlocked |

Local checks:
- New test `sqlite-readonly-location.lock-bytes.test.ts`: a read of the lock bytes throws `EBUSY`, and a sidecar copy fails. The main-database copy succeeds and writes zeros there. Test time is about 0.7 s.
- Consumer tests pass: `update-database-generations`, `sqlite-readonly-location` (base and copy), `update-doctor-migration-wal-rebuild`, `sqlite-snapshot`, `file-descriptor`, `plugin-runtime-artifact-identity`. That is 184 passed and 2 skipped.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint, format check and `git diff --check` pass against the patched fs-safe.

Not covered: the async `copySqliteFile` (`root.copyIn`) path. It isn't used under the migration owner's exclusion, and fs-safe#1111 doesn't add `zeroRanges` there.

Refs #197083

- @RomneyDa

prs.title: fix: make automation billing accounts explicit
prs.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Draft for code-owner review. Not ready to land.

Co-authored by [Vyctor Brzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with Vyctor Brzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bfb77f08-1fd2-461f-ada5-4f3ff81fa044)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/c14a2bf3-3d4e-4c7c-b7db-9c4c9f1b616b)
- [Merge repair and local verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-automations-cleanup-prs-s98cd1ab4)

## What Problem This Solves

Creating an automation can quietly lock in the billing account from the moment it was created. The editor doesn’t show that choice, and jobs without a saved account can be refused even when the agent has a working sign-in.

## User Impact

User impact: Automations use the agent’s normal account selection unless their model ends in `@profile`. Edit the model to choose a specific billing account. If that account is removed or revoked, the job won’t silently charge another account on the same provider; configured fallbacks on other providers can still run.

For upgrades, Doctor backs up cron state, turns each compatible saved account into an explicit model and account choice, preserves the recorded runtime where present, and reports each conversion. If Doctor can’t verify the same route, it pauses the job and tells you why. No jobs are deleted. Jobs without saved accounts are left untouched unless an earlier owner transfer left the job awaiting a new account choice. Run `openclaw doctor --fix` before starting a manually upgraded Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model field already accepts an account suffix, so the billing choice can live alongside the model instead of in a second hidden record. This also removes the old account-adoption flow. Parallel automation cleanup PRs may touch the automation editor, scheduling API, or Doctor’s cron repair flow; this draft does not redesign them.

## Evidence

I merged main at `fc25865d99bd0166efbe6f70d93df979e68e19ac` without rebasing or force-pushing. The repair head is `115d6e9553f1e0c7c63926aed6ffa6816e2853a3`; its merge commit includes the requested daniel-lxs co-author trailer. This remains a draft, with no hosted re-review requested.

I reproduced both ClawSweeper findings locally. Before the fix, the Doctor cron flow kept only one of four jobs, and startup deleted both migration-pending rows during sibling quarantine. After the fix, Doctor converts compatible accounts before generic repair, pauses mismatches, and preserves pending rows through startup and sibling saves. The three continuity cases now assert the explicitly pinned model rather than changed defaults. The Template test preserves rejection of an explicitly selected foreign personal account while allowing an unpinned job.

I verified 393 distinct focused tests across 21 files locally, without a VM, including SQLite migration, Gateway validation, CLI/session routing, and isolated/session cross-provider fallback. The final eight-file run passed 56 tests in 262.94 seconds; the other 337 cases passed on unchanged inputs. Core TypeScript, targeted lint, formatting and the PR diff whitespace check passed. Provider HTTP was intercepted by the integration fixtures, not live. CI timing is not available.

The pr-simplify pass retained the existing model/account owners and the required migration, with no new state owner. The current main-to-head change removes the hidden binding/adoption path; production-oriented files are +570/-1924 lines and tests are +436/-4075 lines. Local autoreview did not run: its selected Codex installation failed the read-only sandbox preflight. I did not broaden permissions or request a hosted review.

Runtime proof still needed: shipped-entry-point runs for fresh unpinned and pinned jobs, native CLI selection, and real cross-provider fallback; real upgrades from supported 9.x extended-stable, 10.x, and v2026.11.5 through the old updater round trip and full Doctor, preserving settings, jobs, history and approvals. Full CI, packaged builds, broader test/UI type lanes and final-head independent review remain unverified. No Control UI source or layout changes.

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: improve: show restored and extended guest access in the Inbox
prs.body:
Related: #182352, #182528

## What Problem This Solves

When a visitor is invited back after access ends, OpenClaw starts another Welcome chat. Extending a current invitation changes the expiry without telling the visitor in the app.

## User Impact

User impact: returning visitors see “Welcome back” in their private **Inbox → System**, and a visitor whose current access is extended sees the new expiry there. Neither action opens, creates, or restores a chat. First-time visitors still get a Welcome chat.

## Why This Change Was Made

Visitor Access decides which notice applies from the signed-in guest’s admitted invitation. The Inbox displays that notice without browser push permissions. Visitor Access keeps a bounded record of which verified profiles have already received a Welcome chat so it can recognize them after a grant ends. Active welcomes are recognized when guests next sign in; already-ended grants from older builds are not backfilled. Existing chats and access permissions are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Visitor Access and Gateway welcome tests passed (six files). These cover one first-time conversation, no new chat on re-invite, and the committed expiry after an extension.
- All seven guest Control UI browser tests passed. The new test exercises Inbox → System for both notices without navigating away or creating a session. Browser data is synthetic; no live identity provider or production Gateway was changed.
- Targeted UI and extension type checks, lint, formatting, and Auto Review passed.

### Review follow-up

- Fixed the Outbox test's typed Inbox fixture and kept the Welcome callback bound to its store. The UI test typecheck and targeted type-aware lint passed.
- Added a Chromium regression against an isolated real Gateway and the real Visitor Access plugin. The only external fixture is the Cloudflare policy transport. It checks first-time Welcome creation, the original chat staying archived on re-invite, and the new expiry appearing in **Inbox → System** while the guest stays connected.
- Ran the same flow after upgrading an isolated source installation from latest stable `v2026.11.10` (`6ea542fd9`). The stable Gateway wrote the original grant, transcript, and archive. Doctor migrated a copy in its final state directory (shared schema 40 → 41; agent schema 42 → 43). The revised Gateway loaded the same archived chat and transcript, and Chromium verified restored and extended notices without creating another chat.

- The same regression failed on the original base `3091ba81d`: two Welcome chats (one active and one archived) instead of one archived chat. It passed with the PR applied. The separate Dashboard Gallery case that failed in the original CI run passed on the base replay; no gallery code was changed.

### Stable upgrade: real Gateway and Control UI

Chromium connected to an isolated Gateway using a copy of state created on `v2026.11.10`, after Doctor migrated the copy in place. The Visitor Access plugin, Gateway, browser UI, and database were real; only the external Cloudflare policy API was simulated. All profiles and invitation text shown are synthetic.

1. **After upgrade:** the original Welcome transcript and archived state are intact.

   ![Archived Welcome chat with its original invitation note and the archive banner](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2ef6bd25-a962-47a7-8f11-3c6783ccb93d)

2. **After re-inviting:** the guest sees the new note and expiry in System, without reopening or creating a chat.

   ![System Inbox showing Welcome back, the expiry, and the inviter note](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0c96e068-06ed-4bd8-9ccd-ea9f27ff3daf)

3. **After extending access while still signed in:** System shows the new expiry.

   ![System Inbox showing Guest access extended and the new expiry](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/efdec370-0561-4606-918f-e2c3b0ad08e0)

The revised regression fits within the CI test-line limit (399/400; no allocation). Type-aware lint, the fresh real-Gateway regression, and the stable upgrade browser run passed. The two Dashboard Gallery and Meetings cases that failed in the prior CI run passed in focused local replays; neither feature was changed.


Captured in the real Control UI with a synthetic guest and a mocked Gateway, in dark mode at 1280 × 800 and cropped to the Inbox. Before: base `3091ba81d`. After: the new notice row; the final extraction of the row and loader was rechecked in Chromium.

### Clean comparison

![Before: no access extension notice in the System Inbox](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c000e3a3-3330-4764-bdda-72a21584f939)

![After: guest access extension and the full expiry in the System Inbox](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aaa66df9-d8b3-4a91-ac17-993c2ae14217)

prs.title: fix(update): check finalizer requester once and verify interrupted recovery by RPC
prs.body:
## Problem
The adopted update finalizer can reload full requester policy inside the callback that guards each filesystem mutation. Recursive cleanup invokes the callback for each entry. This matches part of the reported stack in #205547 but does not establish the cause of the prolonged stall. Interrupted managed recovery could also settle on HTTP readiness without proving the health RPC.

## Change
- Check requester policy at first admission in an adopted finalizer. Keep native executor and local ownership checks live on every mutation. Explicit admission still reads fresh policy; other callers retain their existing checks.
- Require a successful authenticated health RPC and matching version/build identity before existing interrupted managed-service recovery records success. Preserve rollback, ownership, and data-risk guards. No schema, config, or dependency changes.

## Route and target line
Per the [bridge rules](src/cli/update-cli/AGENTS.md), this is legacy in-place update code. On `main`, `update.run` for an owned install goes through `src/update/` (release directories plus a launcher trial). An isolated cell updating a `main` candidate to a newer fixture served the new version from `~/.openclaw/git-install/releases/…` and never started a migrated finalizer. On `main`, the changes reach:
- **Candidate side of a shipped updater's first update:** requester policy checked once in the migrated-finalize worker. This is candidate code, so it also runs on the hop from stock 2026.11.8/2026.11.10.
- **Helper:** RPC-verified interrupted recovery. On `main` it runs only on legacy routes that have not moved, none of which is `update.run`. Users get it only through the 2026.11.11 line, where the release branch still uses this updater (no `src/update/` at `v2026.11.10` or on `release/2026.11.11`). **Target stable line: 2026.11.11.** No backport was made.
- **Hop from stock 2026.11.8/2026.11.10:** stock code bounds the worker only when an explicit timeout is given (`v2026.11.10:src/cli/update-cli/update-command-migrated.ts:286,340`), and stock writes the helper source. The candidate worker and Doctor run during this hop, but a worker-side timer cannot bound a stopped process. A self-abort after candidate start would also end in the same pending state shown below. This PR does not add a candidate-side guard for that hop.

## Evidence
- Requester-policy patch: the new recursive package-settlement test failed on the base. On the fix, settlement of a 32-file backup checks requester policy once, keeps more than 32 native owner checks, removes the backup, and preserves the new install. Explicit re-admission detects revocation.
- Interrupted managed-service fixtures: HTTP-only settlement failed on the base and passes with the fix. The daemon probe rejects matching HTTP identity when an authenticated health RPC is required.
- A default worker deadline was tried and has been removed (`b9adfb02781c`), following ClawSweeper's P1. Without an operator deadline, finalization stays unbounded, as on the base (d79393ea). A joined timeout ends in a pending recovery that leaves the Gateway stopped (see the cells below), so killing a slow but still-progressing finalizer would make things worse. CI on `6688230ca9da` was green; CI on the new head is pending.
- The earlier local `update-command-doctor-authority-callers` failure was not caused by this PR. That run reported `Source changed during compiled subprocess invocation` because files were edited mid-run. The file passes 22/22 at `d7ff04f51065` in a network-none container and passes in CI.
- Service cells ran in private rootless Podman with systemd PID 1, a systemd user unit, synthetic state (12 agents), and an authenticated `update.run` over a loopback registry. The backport cells used the build from before the revert. That build still had the default deadline, which is not involved in the SIGKILL cells. A cell counts as verified only with authenticated `health` RPC ok **and** a `gateway status --require-rpc` build ID matching the expected package.
  - **(a) Normal, `2026.11.8 → exact candidate`** (`d7ff04f51065`, labeled 2026.11.10, package sha256 `6be033c5…`): reached terminal `succeeded`/`finished` in 4m30s. Health RPC ok. Serving build `2026.11.10-d7ff04f51065-2026-11-26T02-14-52.032Z` matches the package. Verification: `settled: true`, `readyz: true`.
  - **Stock first hop with a stalled worker, `2026.11.8 → candidate`** (explicit `timeoutMs: 420000`, worker sent SIGSTOP): the stock deadline fired after about 322s and cancellation settled. The updater reported `update-activation-timeout` with `serviceRestartSafe: false`. The helper logged `recovery not attempted: updater explicitly rejected activation`. **The Gateway unit was left `inactive (dead)`**, and `health` returned ECONNREFUSED ten minutes later. The explicit `timeoutMs` workaround bounds the wait but does not bring a Gateway back.
  - **(c) Owner killed during a stalled finalization, on a `release/2026.11.11` + this PR build → newer fixture:** the worker was sent SIGSTOP and its waiting updater was sent SIGKILL 20s later. The helper logged `handoff failed: managed update command lease binding was lost`, then `failed to finalize update run`, and exited 1. It never reached interrupted recovery because the still-living worker held the delegated lease. **The Gateway was left stopped.**
  - **Operator workaround after both processes were killed:** the Gateway stayed `inactive` and the ledger stayed at `running`/`activating` for 15 minutes. Then `openclaw update repair --yes` exited with status `warning`, `coreUpdate: completed`, and started the service. The Gateway then served `2026.11.12-d7ff04f51065-main-next-fixture`, which matches the fixture package, with health RPC ok.

## Open proof and scope
This PR does **not** meet the requirement that a timed-out or interrupted finalizer ends with a verified successor or a verified restored predecessor. It does not close #205547.
- **Timeout:** any worker timeout, explicit or inherited, surfaces as `UpdateCommandPendingRecoveryFailure` (`update-command-unwind.ts`: owned handoff not completed) with `serviceRestartSafe: false`. The helper then leaves the Gateway stopped, as the stock explicit-timeout cell shows.
- **Killed owner:** once the updater has delegated the executor to the worker, killing the waiting updater makes the helper fail with `lease binding was lost` **before** it reaches `recoverInterruptedUpdater`. A second cell killed both the worker and the waiting updater (`release/2026.11.11` + this PR → newer fixture) and got the same result: the Gateway stayed `inactive`. So the RPC check added here is correct at fixture level but is not reached in either installed SIGKILL cell. The fixtures do not model the delegated lease. Until that is fixed, recovery takes a manual `openclaw update repair`.
- **What closing this needs:** a joined worker timeout and a dead delegated executor must both route into the existing verified interrupted-recovery owner. That changes the stopped-Gateway recovery policy and lease custody, so it needs maintainer agreement first.

## Reconciliation (2026-11-26)

- **Where this matters.** The helper-side and updater-side commits (`e193237d270d`, `8e47da50fb55` RPC-verified interrupted recovery; `b9adfb02781c` unbounded finalization) take effect only on a line whose own updater is this legacy code, which today is **2026.11.11**. They are carried and completed there by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205758 (`fix(update)[2026.11.11]`). That PR routes an operator-timeout finalizer stop and a lost updater or worker into the verified interrupted recovery. Like `b9adfb02781c`, it keeps finalization bounded only by an explicit timeout (its head `e978dfa8e13e`). A hang inside the Doctor phase still ends in the existing data-at-risk stop; that is left open there for a maintainer decision.
- **main.** `update.run` goes through `src/update/`. Isolated cells on `origin/main` `1140fc54a32d` show that path already meets the #205547 bar without changes. A launcher trial SIGSTOPped before ready rolled back after its 20-min budget, and the previous build served, verified by authenticated health RPC and build ID. A launcher plus candidate SIGKILL during the trial ended with the new build verified serving. A Gateway SIGKILL during release preparation left the previous build serving within 18 s.
- **Recommendation.** Land on `main` only if maintainers want the candidate-side piece: the requester policy check once in the migrated-finalize worker, plus the `healthRpcVerified` probe field. That code runs when a shipped 2026.11.10/11.11 updater updates *to* a `main` release. Otherwise close this PR in favor of #205758. `b9adfb02781c` (no implicit deadline) is consistent with #205758 and can stay.

## Worked on by

- @RomneyDa

prs.title: perf(update): avoid reading full runs twice during reconciliation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup and update repair check whether any running update needs reconciliation. When the ledger contains matching runs, the preliminary query returns and sorts entire update records, including their recorded step output. Reconciliation then reads those records again inside its authoritative snapshot.

## User Impact

Populated update ledgers transfer at most one seven-byte status value across the database boundary during the preliminary check. Operators see the same reconciliation results. Empty selections still skip the snapshot.

## Why This Change Was Made

The same Kysely selection supplies both queries. The probe projects `status` with a SQL-level `LIMIT 1`. Broad probes can stop at the first entry of SQLite’s active index. An explicit list of run IDs retains its ordering so SQLite can seek by primary key before it has planner statistics. Inside the snapshot the reader checks that the table exists and loads current records in run-ID order. A caller already holding a transaction goes directly to that read. The SQL limit also bounds what the PostgreSQL bridge receives before it takes the first result.

## Evidence

- Node 24.22.1, SQLite 3.53.4, Linux x64. A new regression failed on `ce0e1b0ebd37`. On `a01d067f02c3`, all 39 checked-in reader and reconciliation worker tests passed, plus the synthetic measurement. The regression observes bound SQL outside and inside the transaction, a phase change before `BEGIN`, and removal of the table before `BEGIN`. [Focused Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45923700526)
- With 128 valid running records containing synthetic step output, the preliminary result went from 128 rows and 1,074,560 UTF-8 bytes of string values to one row and 7 bytes. The snapshot still returned all 128 records and the same 1,074,560 text bytes. The limit reduced the one-match case from 8,395 to 7 bytes, and a late pair from 16,790 to 7. Missing-table, no-match, and explicit-ID misses returned zero rows before and after. All seven output hashes matched.
- Native query plans showed an active covering-index lookup without the broad temporary sort, and primary-key seeks for two-ID hits and misses. In 21 warm calls per case, p50/p95 for all 128 records was 3.580/8.177 ms before and 3.475/7.070 ms after. Two-ID misses were 0.008/0.010 ms before and 0.011/0.014 ms after. Late pairs were 0.056/0.060 ms before and 0.061/0.075 ms after. These small samples describe this fixture. Process RSS and Gateway memory-limit acceptance were unmeasured.
- Final committed range reviewed locally with autoreview at P0–P2. It reported no actionable findings. The pinned formatter and scoped lint both passed. The Kysely 0.29.7 builders clone the query when adding ordering or a limit. Product delta +26/−16 lines, test delta +59/−1.

prs.title: fix: show persistent webhook replies once
prs.body:
Closes #206084

## What Problem This Solves

Persistent `/hooks/agent` calls with `deliver: false` show the final answer twice when you open that conversation. The reporter reproduced this with three webhook calls, each of which returned a single successful completion.

## User Impact

Each webhook turn leaves one visible reply in the persistent conversation. The existing test covers delivery-disabled scheduled runs that target a named conversation as a control. This repair needs no configuration change or data migration. It applies to future runs. Existing transcript rows and the Discord outbound recovery report in the issue are outside this fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cron settlement already knows when a successful run used the settlement conversation as its execution session and the execution's own reply is visible. Use that fact when deciding whether the result needs a display copy. Scheduled outputs that are hidden during execution still need the settlement row. A child handoff can supply its own result and retains that path.

## Evidence

The regression starts the Gateway with isolated state and a loopback Anthropic-compatible model fixture. It submits three persistent HTTP hook calls with delivery disabled, checks all completion receipts, then reads `chat.history` and the next model request. The verified tree is commit `938c80e14569`.

| Observation | Base `2ab7b31a13d9` | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Visible assistant rows for the three replies | 6 | 3 |
| Copies in the next model request | 3 | 3 |
| Named-session scheduled run, visible rows / model copies | 1 / 1 | 1 / 1 |

The focused candidate run passed both the webhook regression and the named-session control. With one test worker it took 329 seconds including worker artifact compilation and Gateway startup. The base run exercised the same Anthropic cases inside the whole file. Its OpenAI path timed out on the cold start and is separate from this comparison.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/session-cron-result-single-copy.gateway.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'anthropic-messages.*(session-target cron reply|keeps one visible reply)'
```

The full Gateway test file and `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.double-announce.test.ts` passed all 76 tests with one worker. This includes both the OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages fixtures, as well as the existing child handoff and scheduled notification cases.

This proof uses the real Gateway and history RPC with a synthetic local provider. Formatting, typed lint, and the test-line budget check passed. AI assistance was used for implementation and verification.

- Not tested: Hosted provider calls and external notification delivery.

prs.title: fix: keep the full Doctor timing line in update reports
prs.body:
Related: #204775

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update` records a "Doctor sections" diagnostic for each Doctor it runs: where the Doctor's time went, section by section, plus its five slowest contributions. Update reports and outage investigations rely on that line. Since #206152, each Doctor step also writes a `doctor.pending.<step>` decision to the startup trace (about 94 per run). The update's collector counted each decision as a 0.0 s section, so on a first update the line hit its 1024-character limit after about 17 decisions. Everything after `config-flow` was cut: `contributions`, `external-config`, `maintenance-ready`, `sqlite-reclamation`, `maintenance.finish`, `maintenance.release`, and the whole "slowest contributions" list.

## User Impact

The update run record and `update --json` output carry the full Doctor timing line again, with the same content they had before #206152. No user-visible behavior changes otherwise. The startup trace still has every `doctor.pending.<step>` line when `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE=1` is set by the operator, and later Doctor work depends on that.

**Update behavior.** The collector runs in the release that owns the Doctor child: `createUpdateDoctorSectionTiming` is called by this release's package/fresh Doctor runners and by its finalization. A published driver (for example 2026.11.10) hands its Doctor run to the new release, so the first update onto a release with this fix already gets the full line. Nothing in the installed updater changes; no stored field, run-record shape, limit or config changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

A pending decision is not a timing; its 0.0 ms duration is the cost of a read-only check. The section-timing owner (`src/infra/update-doctor-section-timing.ts`) now skips trace names that start with `pending.` when it collects phases, so they use neither the line's length budget nor its 256 phase slots. I did not raise the length limit, and I did not add a summary of decisions (no consumer for it exists). The Doctor's trace emitter (`traceDoctorMaintenancePending`) is untouched.

Competing explanation ruled out: the line was not already near its limit before #206152. The same captured trace with the pending lines removed (what the parent of `d0f76989509` emits; the owner file has no commits in between) produces a 690-character line with every section.

## Evidence

Tested commits: red on `origin/main` `2ab7b31a13d`, green on this PR's head `a93cc2d4bdc`.

**Real capture.** One `doctor --fix` trace from a real first update on Linux (npm global, systemd user Gateway): published 2026.11.10 as the driver, a candidate packed from `main` at `fcc9a0648c2` (after #206152). 153 Doctor trace lines, 73 of them `doctor.pending.*`. The recordings replay that stderr through `createUpdateDoctorSectionTiming().wrap(...)` and `annotate(...)`, the same calls the update's Doctor runners make, then run the owner's tests. I did not run a new update cell for this change: the fix is inside the line collector, and the capture already contains the exact Doctor output an update feeds it.

- Red, base `2ab7b31a13d`: line length 1024, truncated, 17 pending entries, 6 sections and the slowest contributions missing. The new regression test fails.
- Green, head `a93cc2d4bdc`: line length 690, not truncated, no pending entries, every section present. Byte-identical to the line the same owner produces from the pre-#206152 shape of the trace.
- Negative control (test): 80 genuinely timed sections still produce a line of exactly 1024 characters ending in `…`.
- Trace kept (test): with `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE=1` set by the operator, the wrapped Doctor stderr is returned unchanged, with every `doctor.pending.` line.

prs.title: fix: stop announcing before_model_resolve routing as a model fallback
prs.body:
Closes #206118

## What Problem This Solves

When a plugin's `before_model_resolve` hook deliberately routes a turn to another provider/model via `providerOverride`/`modelOverride`, the user receives a misleading `↪️ Model Fallback: <override> (selected <primary>; selected model unavailable)` notice even though the configured primary model was never attempted or failed. Because that false fallback state is also persisted on the session entry, the next normal turn on the primary model emits a second spurious `↪️ Model Fallback cleared: ...` notice.

## User Impact

- Turns intentionally routed by a `before_model_resolve` hook stay silent instead of emitting false `"Model Fallback … selected model unavailable"` and follow-up `"Model Fallback cleared"` notices.
- The session's persisted primary model remains unchanged across single-turn hook overrides.
- If a hook-selected model actually fails and falls back to another candidate, fallback accounting still reports the real fallback with the hook-selected model as the turn's selected origin and the real attempt failure reason.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. **`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/result.types.ts` & `run-entry.ts` / `run-entry-terminal.ts`**: Carry `hookModelSelection` on `EmbeddedAgentMeta` when `before_model_resolve` overrides the nominal provider/model (and model selection is not locked), preserving exact turn-selection provenance at the execution/accounting boundary without clobbering `runtimeModelSelection` or `terminalReceipt.requested`.
2. **`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-core.ts` & `agent-runner-result-accounting.ts`**: Treat `hookModelSelection` as the turn's fallback origin in `resolveFallbackOriginModel` and include it in `preserveRuntimeModel` so a deliberate single-turn hook override neither triggers a fake fallback transition nor overwrites the session's persisted model.
3. **Tests (`run-entry.model-hook.test.ts`, `agent-runner-result-accounting.fallback.test.ts`)**: Added Red → Green tests verifying `hookModelSelection` provenance (with and without `fallbacksOverride`), two-turn hook-routed + primary accounting with no fallback/cleared notices, and real fallback reporting when a hook-routed model fails over.

## Evidence

- Reproduced Red state before implementation edits (`pnpm vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-entry.model-hook.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-result-accounting.fallback.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` failed 4/4 new assertions: `fallbackActive` was `true` with `selectedModelRef: "google/gemini-4-hydrogen"` and `hookModelSelection` was `undefined`).
- Verified Green state after final edits:
  - `pnpm exec oxlint` on all 7 modified files: `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors`
  - `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on all 7 modified files: `All matched files use the correct format`
  - `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed
  - `pnpm tsgo:test:src`: all 22 shards passed
  - `pnpm vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-entry.model-hook.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-result-accounting.fallback.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-core.test.ts src/auto-reply/fallback-state.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **4 passed (4) files, 41 passed (41) tests**

prs.title: fix: remove the unused automation wake setting
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

“Now / Next heartbeat” looked like it controlled when an automation would run. In practice, both choices ran the job when its schedule came due. The setting gave people a choice that did nothing.

## User Impact

**User impact:** Set an automation’s timing with its schedule. The Android editor no longer offers Wake mode, and automation create/edit commands and API requests no longer accept `--wake` or `wakeMode`. The current web editor already didn’t render the picker; this removes its leftover data handling and fixtures.

Full job responses keep deprecated, derived `wakeMode: "now"` metadata for released protocol-v4 clients, including Android v2026.11.10. This is response-only compatibility, not a stored setting or a scheduling control; it remains until protocol v4 retires.

On upgrade, or with `openclaw doctor --fix`, Doctor backs up stored cron state and silently removes the old job field. It does not delete, pause, or reschedule jobs, change what they do, or reset their run state. Current approval references are carried forward; stale ones stay stale.

## Why This Change Was Made

A separate agent `automations` wake action can still send an immediate notice to a session. It has no timing selector: the previous default already sent immediately for a targeted session. Use a one-off automation for a later follow-up. The `next-heartbeat` **script result** is different: it can attach a notice to a real upcoming scheduled run, so it still works and is documented separately. The inbound `/hooks/wake` endpoint, hook mapping wake modes, and `openclaw system` are unchanged and can be reviewed separately.

This shares automation form data, Gateway job contracts, Doctor cron repair files, and generated validators or tool snapshots with the parallel automation cleanup PRs. The changes here are limited to Wake mode. The migration scans existing cron definitions and rewrites only affected jobs after one backup; it does not rewrite run history. Largest-deployment upgrade cost was not measured.

## Evidence

- On `b75aede9e48ae92eaa41a1804ad25af76e60f7c0`, I merged main at `3ffd7660334a88629e3c3c0d546a770fb9b78e7e` without rebase or force-push. The already-pushed Android compatibility fix is unchanged. All 270 focused tests passed across the protocol validators (93), Gateway validation (146), read projection (4), agent inputs (7), CLI edit (1), and Doctor migration (19). Core and cron-test typechecks, full protocol checks (including Swift/Kotlin determinism), focused lint/format, and `git diff --check` passed. The six test shards took 188.03s.
- I applied pr-simplify to the merge delta: no new machinery, compatibility layer, or tests were added, and no existing assertions were weakened. The PR remains draft; I did not request another review. Runtime proof still needed on the final head: actual Android before/after screenshots and released-client new/migrated-job detail reads; shipped CLI/Gateway create/edit and immediate-wake behavior; real upgrades from latest stable and supported 9.x extended-stable/10.x, including the old updater round trip, preserving jobs, runtime state, and approvals. Final-head CI and fresh independent review remain unverified.

- On `c44441e467372699cf3345efda4582f111e06327`, I checked the unmodified Android v2026.11.10 `CronJobDetail.kt` parser against real isolated protocol-v4 Gateway add/get/update/list replies: all four pre-fix replies were rejected, and all four fixed replies were accepted. Create/update requests containing `wakeMode` still failed validation. I removed the test job and isolated Gateway state.
- I verified the regression assertions fail before the fix and pass after it. Final focused runs passed 93 protocol-schema tests and 4 projection tests, plus 27 tool/template consumer tests on the same production code. Core and cron-test typechecks, focused lint/format, and Swift protocol generation/determinism checks passed. Final schema/projection suite wall times were 34.97s (mostly compilation) and 1.27s; exact-head CI time is pending.
- I ran pr-simplify on this follow-up: compatibility stays in the existing read projection, is stripped from recovered writable definitions, and duplicate schema coverage was folded into an existing test. The follow-up changes five files (+17/-1 non-test lines, +14/-1 test lines). Against the PR merge base, the whole PR is +3751/-3863 non-test lines and +201/-525 test lines, including generated artifacts.
- I did not run Android UI/device proof or 9.x/10.x upgrades in this follow-up. No fresh independent local review completed: the existing Codex route failed its read-only sandbox preflight, and I did not broaden its permissions.
- I reproduced the remaining `wakeMode` schema/type failures locally and removed eight obsolete fields in two fixture files, without changing assertions, timeouts, or test cases. On `30994c4ee843bea44176462dcd1f1326f6ba8c6b`, PostgreSQL 17 passed 4/4 cron lifecycle tests, template automations passed 21/21, and the templates typecheck, focused lint, and format checks passed.
- PostgreSQL 16 initially passed 3/4. The graceful-stop test timed out waiting for `restart.close.http-server` after the cron finalizer exceeded its cleanup grace period. One bounded, unchanged rerun passed (1 passed, 3 deselected); that does not establish a fix for the timing failure. The containers were removed. Upgrade testing from 9.x/10.x remains separate.
- Focused Gateway, agent tool, scheduler, Doctor, and editor assertions passed. The SQLite Doctor test verified backup and idempotency, existing standing-grant continuity, and removal from a disabled job. Agent input and prompt-prefix tests passed again on the committed source after an earlier runner rejected files changing during compilation.
- Core, Control UI, and scripts typechecks passed; focused core lint passed on 30 files. Gateway validators, native string inventory, and prompt snapshots were regenerated. Baseline and patched Android debug APKs built, and 43 focused Android tests passed. Full CI and live upgrade E2E were not run locally.
- Visual proof gap: the web form had no rendered Wake mode on main. The Android view did change. The isolated Android emulator never completed boot in the capture window, so neither Android screenshot was captured or uploaded.

prs.title: fix: check recorded automation owners before running
prs.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Draft for code-owner review. Not ready to land.

## What Problem This Solves

An older automation can look like it has a human owner even though the owner was never saved. A scheduled trigger or command can also start after its recorded owner's profile is gone. This draft addresses those two cases; it is the first slice of the single-owner cutover.

## User Impact

- A scheduled occurrence with a recorded human owner checks for that profile before running its trigger or payload. If the profile is gone, the run stops before doing that work and tells an administrator how to select a new owner.
- `openclaw doctor --fix` backs up the cron store and saves a directly recorded creator profile as the owner when no owner was saved. It leaves an existing owner (including a transferred one), the tool list, and the enabled state intact for those jobs.
- If the record says the creator was a profile but provides no usable profile ID, Doctor pauses the job and reports how an administrator can claim it on the Automations page. No job is deleted by this repair. Other unattributed jobs retain existing behavior in this slice.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor now writes the owner once instead of having each store read infer it. The scheduler checks the saved owner at the start of the occurrence, before either the trigger or payload can act.

## Risks and Remaining Work

This slice does not loosen existing tool, channel, approval, sandbox, session, or provider checks. It adds a refusal when the profile catalog is unavailable, the saved owner is gone, or a direct-profile record still needs Doctor. Migration trusts only the same direct creator stamp previously used by the runtime reader; it does not infer a person from delivery or channel settings. Profile presence is not a substitute for permission to use a tool or target.

The full owner-based permission snapshot is not implemented. Other stored authority fields, per-effect rechecks, account-bound scheduled Discord `channel-edit`, and pauses for jobs with no direct creator profile remain out of this slice. Gateway wire types, CLI, agent tool schema, and Control UI are unchanged. Expect overlap with sibling changes in scheduler admission, Doctor cron repair, and automation docs.

## Evidence

- I merged main at `fc25865d99bd0166efbe6f70d93df979e68e19ac` without rebasing or force-pushing. The tested head is `5d25582c9142efe043d1c8e09ddd242668096b06`.
- I reproduced both ClawSweeper test findings locally: one stale owner-decoding assertion and all three transfer-recovery cases failed. The repaired store test keeps the separate-authority and older-writer assertions; transfer recovery now creates real isolated profiles and retains its successful-run assertions.
- I ran 173 focused tests successfully across `store.definition-integrity.test.ts`, `service.session-payload.test.ts`, `timer-execution.occurrence.test.ts`, Doctor `cron/index.test.ts`, and `cron/store-migration.test.ts`, using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ... --maxWorkers=1` locally, without a VM. Doctor coverage verifies persisted owners, transferred-owner preservation, unchanged tool lists, both enabled states, separate runtime authority, backup reporting, incomplete-attribution pausing, and repeat repair.
- I ran the owner-admission and Doctor regressions against main's production files: the scheduler case and both Doctor cases failed as expected. I restored the candidate bytes and reran the full focused selection successfully. These are in-process regression controls, not shipped-Gateway or upgrade proof.
- I passed core, cron-test and Doctor-test typechecks, focused lint, touched-file formatting, and the PR-to-main whitespace check. Whitespace warnings across the merge's first-parent range are confined to unchanged main changelog/vendor-patch files.
- I completed pr-simplify without removing behavior or assertions: shared fixture setup and the existing note assertion helper avoid duplication, and two adjacent warning appends are combined. The main-to-head delta is +61/-10 production TypeScript lines, +87/-4 test lines, and +8 documentation lines.
- I attempted local Codex autoreview at P0-P2 against the merged main base. No review was produced: sandbox preflight rejected the installed Codex executable. I did not broaden permissions or request a hosted re-review.

Not verified: live shipped-Gateway missing-owner rejection before trigger/payload work, valid-owner execution and administrator recovery; real upgrades from supported older releases, including v2026.11.5, 9.x extended-stable and 10.x, preserving transferred owners, tool permissions, enabled state and runtime authority; the old updater's round-trip regression; final-head CI and rendered error-state proof. The PR remains draft.
