prs.title: fix: show how to enter an automation recipient when suggestions fail
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In Control UI Automations, the recipient-suggestion error asks you to check the Gateway connection and try again. There is no Retry button in this state, and the failure does not prevent you from entering a recipient.

## User Impact

The alert now points to **Advanced → Results** in the editor. Enter the chat ID, phone number, or user ID in **Recipient**, then select **Save changes**. If you see the alert on an automation’s details page, select **Edit** to reach that field. Suggestions, diagnostics, account selection, access, and scheduling are unchanged.

| Surface | Exact before | Exact after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Automation details and editor after recipient suggestions fail | Couldn’t load recipient suggestions. Check the Gateway connection and try again. Details: The Telegram directory is unavailable | Couldn’t load recipient suggestions. You can enter the recipient in the editor under Advanced → Results. Details: The Telegram directory is unavailable |

## Why This Change Was Made

The alert reuses the translated names of the existing **Advanced** and **Results** controls. The same wording works on the details page and in the editor, where **Advanced** starts closed.

**Skill in practice:** Use the labels people see on screen and give them a next step that works. A failed suggestion lookup doesn’t tell us the Gateway disconnected, but manual entry remains available.

## Evidence

- Exercised the bundled Control UI in Chromium at 1280 × 900 in light theme. A deterministic Gateway fixture rejected the Telegram recipient lookup without disconnecting. On both revisions, the browser opened the automation from the sidebar, found the alert on the details page and in the editor, entered a new **Recipient**, and sent it only on **Save changes**. Reopening the automation after a reload showed the value returned by the fixture. No live Gateway, scheduler, or Telegram delivery was exercised.
- The browser regression failed on main (`09c738a859bdd`) at the new-copy assertion after the manual save, and passed on the patch (`3f16472a115b1`). All 15 directory tests, the UI production typecheck, scoped formatting and lint, and localization verification passed. Broad CI was not run locally.

prs.title: fix: show native notification settings in the iOS app
prs.body:
Closes #164557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings → Notifications shows Safari Home Screen installation instructions when opened inside the native iOS app.

## User Impact

User impact: iPhone and iPad app users can see their native notification delivery and permission settings and open the existing device settings pages. Browser/PWA and macOS notification flows remain separate and unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page already observes the native device-settings capability but did not pass its snapshot into the notification view. This repair uses that existing owner, shows a loading state while its snapshot is pending, and keeps missing status values unknown. Device links use application navigation so the native Back history is retained; modified clicks keep normal link behavior.

Upstream migrated the settings UI from Lit to Solid. This update keeps the current Solid renderer and ports the native-notification regression with it. Native notification presentation and capability-to-view props live in focused siblings to respect the existing file-size guards. No notification transport, native permission operation, configuration key, dependency, or generated translation memory changes.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(markdown-core): keep block metadata when annotating a transcript-role boundary
prs.body:
Refs: #204999, #206243

## What Problem This Solves

#206243 moved Signal's `> ` quote marker from parse time to render time. The render-time scan reads the parser's `blocks` metadata, which lives on the IR as non-enumerable properties.

`annotateAssistantTranscriptRoleMessageBoundary` in `packages/markdown-core/src/ir-annotations.ts` rebuilds the IR with `{ ...ir }`. A spread copies only enumerable own properties, so the rebuilt IR silently loses `blocks`. When the chunker promotes a transcript-role header to a message boundary inside a quoted block, the renderer then has no quote span to scan and the new chunk starts with bare text:

```
markdownToSignalTextChunks("> > padding padding user[2026-07-02] question", 25)
-> [{"> > padding padding"}, {"user[2026-07-02] question"}]
```

The second chunk should read `> > user[2026-07-02]`, as it does for every other chunk of the same quote. This is the open review finding from #190478, which #206243 did not cover.

## User Impact

On Signal, a quoted message whose transcript-role header lands on a later chunk keeps its quote marker on that chunk, so a long quote split across messages stays readable as a quote from the first line to the last. Nothing changes for unquoted messages, for quoted messages that fit in one chunk, or for any other channel.

## Why This Change Was Made

The annotation pass does not move text: it adds an annotation span and removes overlapping links. So the parser's block offsets are still valid on the rebuilt IR and can simply be re-attached with the existing `attachBlockMetadata` owner, the same way `ir-slice.ts` and `construct-fallbacks.ts` already do.

No new mechanism, no second source of truth for quote spans, and no change to the renderer.

## Evidence

Regression test in `extensions/signal/src/format.test.ts` drives the production entry point and asserts the promoted chunk's text and style offset:

```
without the metadata re-attach (current main):
× keeps the quote prefix when a transcript-role header starts a chunk
  -> expected 'user[2026-07-02] question' to be '> > user[2026-07-02]'

with this change:
✓ keeps the quote prefix when a transcript-role header starts a chunk
```

Rendered chunks with the fix:

```
["> > padding padding", "> > user[2026-07-02]", "> > question"]
MONOSPACE at 4:16 on the middle chunk (the post-prefix offset)
```

Consumers of the changed owner still pass: the full `packages/markdown-core` suite plus the Signal, Slack, WhatsApp, Telegram, iMessage, and Zalo User format suites — 17 files, 349 tests. `oxfmt --check` passes on both changed files.

## Merge Danger

Low. The change only re-attaches metadata that the spread already dropped; annotation spans, links, styles, and text are untouched, so every non-Signal consumer of `annotateAssistantTranscriptRoleMessageBoundary` renders exactly as before. The only behavior change is Signal quoted output, where a chunk that previously lost its `> ` prefix now keeps it.

prs.title: improve(memory): skip the helper used only for recall cleanup at startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Starting the bundled memory plugin launches a separate Node process to prepare a cleanup routine. That routine only deletes matching recall and phase-signal keys when Doctor or nightly repair runs.

## User Impact

Memory starts without that preparation worker or capture broker. Doctor and nightly recovery still remove both copies of a stale entry together, including when dreaming is disabled. Existing installations need no configuration change or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The keyed-store SDK gains one optional method, `deleteKeys(keys, { alsoFrom: peer })`. The existing shared-state writer validates both store grants and their physical database identity, then deletes up to 50,000 exact keys in one transaction. Plugin operations that execute custom code keep their existing module-generation lifecycle. Memory-core can now remove its private prune module.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192547

## Evidence

- Packaged Linux x64, Node 24.22.1, one memory-core-only registration per arm. Stock started one preparation worker and one native broker with three capture claims. The candidate started zero throughout registration, idle, a real Doctor archive and a later nightly repair. Both arms pruned the two seeded namespaces on both repair paths.
- At the idle sample, the stock broker used 84,804 KiB PSS. Main-process PSS rose from 305,653 to 316,547 KiB. Registration took 832 ms on stock and 461 ms on the candidate in this pair. The full Gateway has other potential claimants. This isolated run establishes the memory-core lifecycle change.
- One full ARM64 Gateway pair on the same base, one CPU, 768 MiB service limit and 1 GiB outer limit. Stock and candidate both reached readiness (34.484 s and 31.848 s) and acknowledged chat (by 39.129 s and 36.843 s). Neither reached the mock OpenAI endpoint or completed a reply. The first SQLite session process was killed at 33.756 s on stock and 28.657 s on the candidate. Service kills totaled three and five, respectively. Both services peaked at 768 MiB; outer peaks were 819.76 and 819.33 MiB. The candidate had a separate native broker listening on `resource.sock` by 30.259 s, at about 64.7 MiB PSS near acknowledgement. Its claimant was unidentified. One pair cannot establish why the kill counts differed. [Matched ARM64 run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45904706316)
- A populated SQLite fixture deleted 50,000 distinct keys from each of two namespaces in 3.45 s, including 10,000 expired rows. An existing reader retained its pre-commit view, an unrelated row survived, and the WAL contained one commit frame.
- All 115 focused state-owner, SDK, Doctor and promotion tests passed. Scoped typecheck and typed lint passed. The SDK audit reported zero unauthorized removals and counted 3,931 public exports on both the pristine parent and the candidate, one over the existing 3,930 budget.

The packaged proof used signed production commit `16724e2676e74a1228f1e55ff5d218659de8eff1` on `e11a36d08b9a9fc81d2c6634fd6e252f8f954dad`. The final commit adds SDK documentation. [Linux x64 validation runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45902277626)

prs.title: fix: stop doctor --fix rewriting the plugin registry on a healthy install
prs.body:
Related: #204775

## What Problem This Solves

Every `openclaw doctor --fix` on a healthy install rewrote the persisted plugin registry, even when no plugin had changed. Each run stored a new revision of the whole index, so a second clean run never left the state database as it found it. This is step 3 of the plan in #204775: a clean run should write nothing. A conditional Gateway stop (step 6) can only skip the stop when every step can say "nothing to do" and mean it.

## User Impact

On a healthy install, `doctor --fix` no longer rewrites the plugin registry. The step took 0.09 to 0.24 s instead of 0.36 to 1.19 s in the measured cells (the higher figures are runs under strace). When the registry really is stale (a plugin added or removed, a damaged record), Doctor still rebuilds it as before. With `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE=1` the plugin registry step now reports its real answer (`pending=none check=owner` or `pending=work check=owner`) instead of the default.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Doctor already had a no-op guard here. It rediscovers the plugin inventory and skips the write when it equals the stored index. The guard compared raw discovery with what the store returns. The store keeps only `bundledDist` of a plugin's build metadata, so every bundled plugin that declares worker entries, static assets or a host version always looked different. In the cell, 21 of 79 bundled plugins differed in `packageBuild` alone.
- The plugin index writer now exports `projectInstalledPluginIndexForStore`: the index as the writer would store it and the reader would return it. Doctor compares through it, so "unchanged" means "the write would store the same index". Serialization moved out of the row writer into a helper both paths use, so the two cannot drift apart.
- The guard is now `checkPluginRegistryRepairPending`. The repair uses it to decide whether to write, and the plugin registry contribution uses it as its step 1 `pending` check, so the trace and the write share one predicate. It runs twice per Doctor run under maintenance (trace, then repair), 0.04 to 0.13 s each in the cells. Its state reads reuse Doctor's maintenance connection: run 2 made the same number of read-only database copies on base and head. Contribution `pending` checks now receive the flow context. No other contribution declares one yet.
- Invalid persisted records still go to the repair path, which reports them under its lease as before. The check returns `undecidable` for them, which counts as work.
- No schema, stored field, config option or retention change. The stored index has the same shape. It is just not rewritten when nothing changed.

### Every always-firing write site from the step 1 table, checked

Two cells on unmodified `main` traced every SQL statement that changed rows in the Doctor process tree, plus every write-intent file syscall (`strace -f`). They also snapshotted every store before and after each run, compared against a plain `systemctl --user restart` of the Gateway with no Doctor.

| Site (owner) | On a healthy second run | This PR | Pending check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plugin registry refresh (`commands/doctor-plugin-registry.ts`, `plugins/installed-plugin-index-store-write.ts`) | rewrote `config_machine_state[plugins.installedIndex]` (new `revision`, new `index`) | conditional | owner: `checkPluginRegistryRepairPending` |
| State database repair: writable open and file modes (`state/openclaw-state-db-permissions.ts`, `doctor-config-preflight.ts`) | no change to bytes or mtime. `applyPrivateModeSync` already skips a same-mode chmod. The `r+` open writes nothing. | unchanged | step 4: the composed predicate needs `needsOpenClawStateDatabaseSchemaRepair` (copy plus integrity check) |
| Additive agent schemas and migration backups (`doctor-heartbeat-migration-backup.ts`) | no agent database write and no backup file. It already runs only for pending migrations. | unchanged | step 4 (preflight `pendingMigrations`) |
| Config preflight (`doctor-config-preflight.ts`, `doctor-config-flow.ts`) | no write to `openclaw.json`, its backups or any state row. Every repair there is gated by its own detector. | unchanged | step 4 (compose the detectors) |
| Boot lifecycle (`infra/gateway-boot-lifecycle.ts`) | a write transaction that matches zero rows. No row changes and no bytes change. | unchanged | step 5 |
| Codex session routes (`doctor/shared/codex-route-warnings.ts`) | no write. The forced auth-profile rewrite needs an OpenAI Codex auth-profile id map, which a healthy install does not have. | unchanged | step 5 |
| Shell completion (`doctor-completion.ts`) | no write. It returns early when the profile is installed and the cache exists, and under `--non-interactive`. | unchanged | step 5 |
| Daemon runtime pin (`daemon/runtime-pin-state.ts`) | no write. It runs only while the migration receipt is incomplete. | unchanged | step 5 |
| pnpm launcher (`infra/update-launcher-repair.ts`) | no write. It rewrites only a launcher that names a removed stage. | unchanged | n/a on npm |

### Fields that change on a clean run by design (the run's own record)

These change between the end of run 1 and the end of run 2 on this head. Each is also changed by a plain Gateway restart without Doctor, or belongs to the stop itself:

- `~/.openclaw.update-captures/doctor-<id>`: Doctor's pre-repair capture, one per stopped run, newest kept. It is part of the stop (step 6).
- state database `gateway_boot_lifecycle` (the stopped boot gets `completed_at_ms`, `outcome`, `reason`, and a row for the new boot), `config_machine_state[gateway.crashes]` and `[operator.channelPolicy]` (`updated_at_ms`, the new boot's identity), `config_health_entries` and `diagnostic_events[config-snapshot]` (observation times), `official_external_plugin_catalog_snapshots` (`saved_at`, `updated_at_ms`): written by the restarted Gateway.
- `agent_databases.last_seen_at`: set on every open of an agent database, by the Gateway and by Doctor. `schema_version` and `size_bytes` stay the same.
- `state_leases` and `agent_database_leases`: custody leases. Doctor inserts and deletes its own within the run, and the remaining rows belong to the new Gateway process.
- `~/.openclaw/logs/openclaw-<date>.log` (appended), lock files under `~/.openclaw/tmp/openclaw-<uid>/`, `~/.openclaw/tmp/plugin-captures/<id>` (Gateway plugin-load scratch), `openclaw.json.last-good` (inode and mtime), and SQLite `-wal` and `-shm` sidecars.

Unchanged on both runs: `openclaw.json`, the systemd unit file, the agent database file, and every other row.

## Update behavior

There is no update-path change. A published updater that runs Doctor on this build runs the same repairs in the same order. A plugin registry that is stale after an update (new bundled plugins or new build metadata) still differs from discovery in the stored fields and is rebuilt as before. The cells show the guard does not overreach: with a plugin record removed, the step reports `pending=work` and rebuilds the index.

## Evidence

**Real cells: Linux, systemd user Gateway, npm install of a packed build under an unpublished version, 64 MiB agent database, `/readyz` probed every 250 ms.** Base is `main` at `d0f76989509`. Head is this PR's first commit, `94aa43b7f32`. Each snapshot cell runs `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes` three times. Runs 1 and 2 are under `strace -f` and a harness-only `node:sqlite` statement trace (`NODE_OPTIONS=--import`, Doctor process tree only). A plain Gateway restart runs between runs 2 and 3. Every store is hashed and its rows are dumped before and after each step.

| | base `d0f76989509` | head `94aa43b7f32` |
|---|---|---|
| Doctor-only row changes, end of run 1 to end of run 2 (beyond a plain restart) | `config_machine_state[plugins.installedIndex]`: `index`, `revision` | none |
| `plugins.installedIndex` revision across runs 2 and 3 | changes on every run | unchanged |
| Row-changing SQL in the run 2 Doctor tree, apart from leases and `agent_databases` | 1 `config_machine_state` upsert | none |
| Plugin registry step on a clean run (pending check plus repair) | 0.36 to 1.19 s, "Plugin registry refreshed" | 0.09 to 0.24 s, no write |
| `doctor.pending.contribution.doctor:plugin-registry` | `pending=work check=default` | `pending=none check=owner` |
| Read-only database copies made by run 2 (strace) | 78 to 80 | 78 |

**Guard cells (same setup, no strace).** After one settling run, a script seeded real work while the Gateway served: state database mode 0644, a `startup_failed` boot row with a maintenance startup reason, and the persisted plugin index with one plugin record removed. Then `doctor --fix` ran twice:

| | base | head |
|---|---|---|
| work run: state database mode | 644 → 600 | 644 → 600 |
| work run: seeded boot row | `startup_failure_repaired` | `startup_failure_repaired` |
| work run: plugin index | 78 → 79 plugins, rewritten | 78 → 79 plugins, rewritten, `pending=work check=owner` |
| next clean run: plugin index | rewritten again | untouched, `pending=none check=owner` |
| `/readyz` outage, settle / work / clean | 26.9 / 23.4 / 24.5 s | 29.5 / 27.0 / 26.0 s |

The guard outages differ by about 2.5 s while the plugin registry step itself is 0.3 s faster on head. Host load was higher during the head guard cell (1-minute load 6.4 vs 4.1 at start), and the clean third runs of the snapshot cells went the other way (Doctor reported 28.7 s of stop on base and 23.3 s on head). I read this as host noise.

Recordings replay the raw cell logs: the trace line, Doctor's own output, the row-changing SQL, the per-store diff against a plain restart, the index revision at every snapshot, and the guard cell.

RED/BASE, `d0f76989509`:

prs.title: fix(agent-core): opt-in completed-effect budget for side-effecting tools (#204076)
prs.body:
## Problem

Closes #204076.

The existing loop detectors (`tool-repeat-guard.ts`) compare a tool call against the **immediately preceding** call by name+args hash. A cron agent that alternates signatures — e.g. `lobster run` → `dispatch_action` → `lobster resume` — never trips them, even though every repeat delivers a fresh side effect (a new Telegram card each time). Each call is "successful" and each is "different", so the loop looks like progress.

## What this adds

An opt-in **completed-effect budget** keyed on tool identity:

- `AgentTool.sideEffect?: true | number` declares the tool's budget (default 1; a number sets a per-user-input cap). Plain data, so it crosses the worker wire.
- Successful completions spend one unit in `finalizeToolCallOutcome`, reading structured result details (`ok`, `status`) so self-reported failures do not spend the budget and legitimate retries remain allowed.
- Once spent, further calls to that tool are refused **before execution** with a model-facing redirect; the turn ends with errorCode `side_effect_budget`.
- Interim checkpoint statuses (`needs_input` / `needs_approval`) neither spend nor clear the budget; `cancelled` is a definitive non-success.
- Budget state resets when new user input is committed, matching the repeat guard's lifecycle (per schedule slot for cron).
- Wired through the worker tool surface schema (`sideEffect` on tool definitions) and `projectAgentToolDefinition`.
- Declares `lobster` as `sideEffecting` in its manifest so runaway cron pipelines are capped after one completed run per input.

## Tests

14 unit tests in `tool-repeat-guard.test.ts` (4 new for the budget: alternation block, failed-retry tolerance, numeric cap, no-declaration unaffected). Full `packages/agent-core` suite passes (306 tests); `tsc -p tsconfig.packages.json` clean; oxlint clean on touched files.

## Notes

- Off by default: tools that do not declare `sideEffect` are completely unaffected.
- Counting happens at outcome finalisation, so a completed side effect is never lost to steering/ordering paths.

prs.title: fix(test): clean up fixtures and repair readiness checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The test audit found duplicate assertions and unused fixture data. Validation also exposed mock lint regressions and two existing fixture readiness bugs.

## User Impact

Test maintenance and validation reliability only; no product behavior change is intended. Stronger owner-level tests retain the removed assertions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove unused fixture outputs, consolidate identical setup and cases, and retain the process-exit deadline assertion. Keep mock constructors valid, make the catalog helper receiver-independent, arm compiler cancellation before publishing readiness, let the browser RPC observer capture the startup response its Incognito scenario already awaits, and keep the now-internal OTLP request reader private.

## Evidence

- The final independent review covered all 92 files at `a3a998814f4f66ba0b4465ad76502ed163a2fe0d` without actionable correctness or security findings. Targeted formatting/lint and normal signed commit hooks passed for the repairs.
- Local proof: 47 affected MCP/catalog tests, one real compiler-cancellation test, 15 OTEL tests, one real-Gateway Incognito browser test and five iOS attachment-summary tests passed. The compiler receipt retains process-join and generation-removal assertions; the browser completes startup and two sends.
- [Exact-head manual CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45911615031) completed with 104 successful jobs, seven failed jobs and the failed aggregate gate. Build, both real-Gateway browser lanes, PostgreSQL, Windows and Docker seed checks passed. The main macOS Swift test process passed 2,785 tests; its separate named-profile process failed as listed below.
- The OTLP unused-export finding introduced by cleanup is fixed and absent from the current dependency scan.

Remaining failures are recorded, not counted as passing proof:

- Seven unused exports have unchanged defining modules, references and scanner inputs on the frozen base.
- The UI model-picker readiness case never reaches its provider-ambiguity assertions. Its test, owners and runner are unchanged; the modified browser observer is outside that unit project's execution path.
- Two Gateway shards fail native-worker close/metadata shutdown checks in unchanged tests and executable fixtures. The local Gateway attempt instead timed out during cold startup, so it does not reproduce or clear the CI failure.
- The iPad chat screenshot waits unsuccessfully for the Mermaid button; its screenshot test, app, renderer and build inputs are unchanged. The iPhone capture passed.
- The separate macOS named-profile test times out opening its preferences menu. Its app, test, helpers and process runner are unchanged; it runs separately from the modified test suites.
- The published-driver installed tree exceeds the package budget (47,713 entries; 607,348,004 bytes). [Scheduled main also exceeds that budget](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45904733009).

The UI and native failures have source-based attribution; identical frozen-base runtime reproductions are not claimed. A baseline checkout could not qualify its dependency donor, so no test ran there. The manual run tested the branch head. [Merge-checkout CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45915151397) is now running against `d86afcfa522f198db709846de351f0da50e0a76b`. Independent preservation review accepted all seven files changed on both branches. Parallel upstream work leaves one harmless duplicate `chat.startup` string in a Set initializer; cosmetic deduplication is deferred.

prs.title: perf(ci): skip declaration path translation in canonical checkouts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Declaration checks translate already-canonical checkout paths to relative paths and back to the same absolute paths. The preceding profile showed substantial time in path normalization.

## User Impact

This candidate aims to reduce declaration-check preparation time. **Rejected after measurement; do not merge.** Warm preparation improved, but the full SDK worker failed the preset no-regression gates.

## Why This Change Was Made

When every known checkout spelling equals its physical root, retain the normalized absolute path directly. Aliased checkouts retain the existing translation. Every physical admission, existence check, current-symlink revalidation, and receipt check remains unchanged.

The existing measurement harness selects the shared boundary implementation before TSX loader bootstrap and counts path operations separately from filesystem operations.

## Evidence

Frozen baseline: `6fe8c51914d88331068a102b3976a8c5d097318d`.

Acceptance rule recorded before measurement:
- Measure the actual `prepare-extension-package-boundary-artifacts.mts --mode=package-boundary` entry point with current full SDK receipts.
- Five serial alternating baseline/candidate pairs in fresh Node processes on the same isolated Linux host. Record actual Node version, CPU/RAM, and load.
- Require identical receipt digests, bytes, and modification times; fewer path.resolve and path.relative calls, unchanged existence and native-realpath counts; at least 10% lower median entry-point time; no worse p95 time or median CPU; median peak RSS at most 10% higher.
- Count runs are separate from timing runs. Capture a baseline CPU profile. Report all samples, median, p95, spread, CPU, and RSS.
- Only if warm qualification passes, run five alternating full SDK compiler-worker pairs using `packages/plugin-sdk/tsconfig.json`; require identical lookup/input digests and no worse median/p95 time or median CPU, with the same RSS bound.
- Reject if any gate fails. No whole-CI or billing claim.

A dependency-free base/candidate comparison passed for canonical and symlinked checkout paths, relative/absolute inputs, missing inputs, outside paths, and rejection after a parent retargeted outside the checkout. Remote focused tests passed (55 passed, five platform-specific skips), as did script typecheck, targeted lint, and formatter parity. Final local ClawSweeper review completed on `6fe8c51914d88331068a102b3976a8c5d097318d..afbcda00d663fba479c891aaeaa5e025b002de39`: no actionable correctness findings, security cleared. prs.title: fix: preserve the first reply across gateway restart races
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A follow-up sent while the Gateway is recovering from a restart can reach the model and lose its reply if the recovered turn retries after overflow compaction.

## Cause and Fix

The retry added in #204313 resends the persisted user turn in place. Its one-shot write suppression had no replay write to consume it, so it suppressed the follow-up in the running transcript. SQLite rejected the eventual reply because its parent did not include that follow-up.

I leave write suppression disarmed for an in-place replay, including after saving a keyed copy of a turn that compaction summarized away. The regression checks that the follow-up is stored once and the reply is stored as its child. It also observes failures from steering and persistence without changing when the held responses release.

## Evidence

- **Regression.** With the runtime fix removed, the steering test fails with `SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite`. On `c9c16af1f31`, both steering tests pass.
- **Fixture error handling.** Injecting a rejected persistence promise fails the revised test with that error and produces zero unhandled rejections.
- **Static checks.** Agent-test typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.

### Gateway restart trace

Sanitized trace from the built Gateway at `c9c16af1f310a4565228d6555a6a048bac7aa4f0` in one Ubuntu arm64 VM, with a local deterministic model endpoint.

| UTC | Observed event |
| --- | --- |
| 23:48:07 | SIGTERM while a model turn was in flight |
| 23:48:13 | Fresh Gateway process started |
| 23:48:14.412 | Recovered turn hit a context overflow |
| 23:48:14.824 | Auto-compaction succeeded and the prompt retried |
| 23:48:15.335 | Model began responding to the recovered retry |
| 23:48:15.895 | WebSocket `chat.send` accepted “Reply with EDGE-ALIVE-PINE” while the recovered response was still streaming |
| 23:48:51.801 | WebSocket `chat.history` returned the user message “Reply with EDGE-ALIVE-PINE” |
| 23:48:51.802 | WebSocket `chat.history` returned the visible assistant answer “EDGE-ALIVE-PINE” |
| Read after reply | SQLite assistant row 31 points to user row 30 (`assistant.parentId == user.id`) |

Worked on by:
- @daniel-lxs

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-restart-resume-drops-next-message-sc55fafdb)

The final replay repair and VM trace were supplied by @daniel-lxs outside this Team session; the linked session contains the original investigation and landing verification.

prs.title: fix(codex): keep remote workers when only the OpenClaw version changes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After an OpenClaw update, `resume_agent` can find a saved remote worker but `send_input` refuses its next task. Codex echoes the OpenClaw version in its user agent. That change alone can replace the native parent.

## User Impact

An ordinary chat on the same authenticated remote WSS connection can reuse its worker. Pending assignments survive a later tool change that replaces the parent. Submission receipts stay with their original parent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rebuild the connection fingerprint from the live runtime with only the saved OpenClaw version substituted. Reuse the saved bytes only on a complete match. Supervision, restricted bindings and local connections keep their existing rules. See #206089 for local connections.

## Evidence

The lifecycle regression reproduced the unwanted replacement on the parent commit. All 65 focused tests passed on the first commit (259.31 s). After correcting two indexed reads in the test for strict typechecking, the 22-case file passed again with one worker (163.24 s, 609 ms for the new case). Production code is unchanged. Formatting and type-aware lint passed. Local checks reused older dependencies.

Real Codex 0.164.0 with synthetic inference and a TLS-verified test hostname routed to loopback. Both builds included #193024 and identical packaging patches. Simulated the earlier client by changing only the version in its initialize request. Each forward comparison began with two completed worker turns.

| Case | Parent | Next task | Completed worker turns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unchanged | Same | Completed | 3 |
| Client version changed, no repair | Replaced | Refused | 2 |
| Client version changed, repaired | Same | Completed | 3 |
| Return to previous client version | Same | Completed | 4 |
| New version and endpoint | Replaced | Refused | 2 |
| New version and credential | Replaced | Refused | 2 |

After one Resume, the parent used the third answer and completed the goal in 9.14 s. The return started from that saved state.

### Data-model compatibility with v2026.11.10

Built the [release tag](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.11.10) (`6ea542fd`) and this PR (`b917e9cb`) from unmodified source with cached dependencies. Both report 2026.11.10. These runs check previous-release data separately from the version change above. No runtime patches or edits to the handshake.

- **Gateway upgrade.** Real Codex 0.164.0, remote WSS and synthetic inference. The release saved two completed turns on one worker and a paused goal. Both runs used `tools.gatewayPolicy.allow` set to `get_goal`, `create_goal` and `update_goal`. The candidate opened the copied settings, chat and worker history. One Resume kept the original native parent, verified both answers, used the same worker's third answer and completed the original goal in 8.24 s.
- **SQLite upgrade.** A separate release process wrote two pending assignments, an unmatched submission receipt and a remote binding through the production stores. After the candidate's offline Agent database migration (schema 42 to 45 under the maintenance lease), the second process read the same owner, model, sandbox, approval settings and records. A wrong turn left the receipt intact. Exact consumption succeeded once, replay failed and both assignments remained.
- **Limits.** With the broader tool policy, the release and PR advertised eight different declarations. The parent changed and the old worker refused new input. In a separate trial the parent completed the same saved goal using a fresh child. After that write, the release Gateway exited 78 on shared schema 42 (supports 40). Use a compatible recovery build. This PR changes neither tool-catalog checks nor database schemas.

## Risks

An identical address and credential cannot prove physical server continuity. This trial did not qualify a deployment or a pair of release images. No new privileges, configuration options or migrations.

prs.title: improve(ci): narrow scheduled test inventory scans
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled test coverage asks Git for every tracked path before checking which files still exist, then discards non-test files. The frozen checkout has 67,186 tracked paths but only 23,315 possible test paths, so every lookup probes 43,871 unrelated paths.

## User Impact

Coverage inventory does less filesystem work. Test selection, scheduled coverage, runtime isolation, and CI gates remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use Git’s explicit recursive test-file glob before the existing existence and suffix filters. The existing Git owner still handles missing files and failures. The coverage test retains its independent whole-repository oracle. No new cache or discovery implementation is introduced.

## Evidence

- Frozen base: `2b402e123500158ae1ead5c3b5370ff71b2d9807`.
- Per lookup: 67,186 → 23,315 filesystem existence checks, a 65.3% reduction. Both return the same 23,270 tracked tests before coverage classification.
- Five interleaved warm local samples: median lookup 578.956 → 310.481 ms; p95 2841.679 → 530.948 ms. Host timings are noisy; this measures the inventory helper, not whole CI runtime or billing.
- The recorded full census remains exactly 23,198 scheduled files, four unscheduled files, and one decoded daily matrix row, with identical memberships and execution descriptors.
- A real-Git fixture retained root/nested/hidden paths, spaces and brackets, all supported test suffixes, and near-miss suffix filtering. Tracked-but-deleted tests were excluded, including deletion after a cached lookup.
- All 11 existing census/changed-plan checks passed during the candidate investigation; the final explicit-glob census checks passed 3/3 with the original all-tree oracle.
- Whole-suite timing did not establish an improvement: the earlier 11-case pair was 36.22 → 40.74 seconds. No overall runtime or dollar savings are claimed.
- Final tooling typecheck, scoped lint, formatting and diff checks passed. Independent source review found no issues. Final committed-range local ClawSweeper review completed at `16553b5c1044b7b4c7494f968645699f0747ba12` against the frozen base, high reasoning: no actionable correctness or security findings.

prs.title: fix: reject incomplete Git backup commits
prs.body:
Closes #206186

## What Problem This Solves

A Git backup repository's pre-commit hook can unstage a declared table. Backup creation currently reports success even though that commit cannot be verified or restored.

## User Impact

Creation now fails before reporting success or pushing when the committed tree differs from the prepared snapshot. Hooks still run. The failed commit remains locally for inspection; correct the hook and create a new backup. No backup format or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

I capture the private index's tree before committing and compare it with the returned commit's tree. This checks paths, modes, and blob identities without reading large tables again. Index reconciliation uses that same verified commit.

The pr-simplify pass retained one check in the existing commit owner, with no new abstraction or option: +14/-2 production lines, +32 test lines, and six documentation lines.

## Evidence

I ran the following on an isolated Linux x86_64 AWS Crabbox with Node 24.22.1. The final committed tree is `2da60a7178fec9b23dfd2e1d02e329dbe24d2860`.

- On main `e11a36d08b9a9fc81d2c6634fd6e252f8f954dad`, both new real-Git regression cases failed because creation resolved successfully; the nine existing ownership cases passed.
- With the fix, 45 tests passed across five Git backup suites; one Windows-only case was skipped. This includes a real 256 MiB create/verify/restore with a 256 MiB heap.
- Targeted lint, format (including formatter parity), production types, and the owning test typecheck passed.
- The real CLI, using synthetic agent data and a local bare Git remote, produced:

```text
Before: create=0, warnings=[], recorded status=ok, pushed=true
        verify=1, restore=1, no restored file
After:  create=1, JSON ok=false, recorded status=failed
        remote unchanged, verify=1, restore=1, no restored file
After removing the hook: create, verify, restore passed; table data preserved
```

The proof script initially expected empty stdout on failure. I corrected it to assert the CLI's existing JSON error envelope and reran the full CLI flow successfully.

Not checked: live PostgreSQL or Windows/macOS. Local autoreview could not start because the installed Codex binary was unavailable inside its required read-only sandbox; I did not relax that isolation.

Contributor: Dan Riccio.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-backup-commit-missing-tables-s14355d4b)

prs.title: feat: show CSV attachments as a table in the chat file viewer
prs.body:
Closes #206147

## What Problem This Solves

When someone opens a CSV attachment in a Control UI chat, the side panel shows it as raw comma-separated text. Quoted fields, embedded commas and long rows run together, so any file with more than a few columns is hard to read without downloading it and opening it elsewhere.

## User Impact

CSV attachments (`text/csv` or a `.csv` file name) open as a table: the first row is the header, each record is a row, and wide files scroll sideways. A "View raw text" button switches to the original text view, the same toggle Markdown attachments have. Copy and download work as before. Pasted text and other file types are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The file viewer already renders Markdown and HTML attachments in place, so CSV joins that same component. Parsing follows RFC 4180 (quoted fields may hold commas, doubled quotes and line breaks; CRLF and a leading BOM are handled) in about 40 lines, so no new dependency is needed. The table reuses the existing sidebar Markdown table styles; two CSS rules keep header labels on one line and keep line breaks inside a cell. Files stay under the existing 256 KB text preview limit.

## Evidence

I uploaded a made-up CSV through the chat composer in an isolated Gateway (stand-in model) and opened it in the side panel, once with the `main` UI build and once with this branch.

Before:

![Before: the CSV attachment opens as raw text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/83b09dd783e1e109ab04df031c4e37e1af89aa3d/images/2026/11/f8ebcb3c-4d13-49ea-a0d3-d6cc5132f9a4.png)

After:

![After: the CSV attachment opens as a table with a View raw text button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/83b09dd783e1e109ab04df031c4e37e1af89aa3d/images/2026/11/c6114c32-dc05-4210-b3cf-5dbfa6befc95.png)

In the same run on this branch, "View raw text" showed the original text and "Preview" brought the table back, and at a 390 px phone viewport the table opened in the bottom sheet and scrolled sideways.

Tests: `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-text-attachment.test.ts` gains one case (quoted comma, escaped quotes, a line break inside a field, CRLF, BOM, an empty cell, and the raw text toggle). It fails on `main` (no table rendered) and passes here; the file passes 40 of 40. `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint and the formatter are clean on the changed files. The Control UI bundle budget reports the same numbers as `main`, since the code loads with the lazily loaded detail panel.

prs.title: feat: answer agent questions with Feishu card buttons
prs.body:
Related: #111470

## What Problem This Solves

On Feishu, an agent that needs a decision from the user has to fall back to a plain-text question because the Feishu channel never told the Gateway it can render choice controls. Users of the same session on WebChat get tappable options; Feishu users get a paragraph and must type the answer, and the waiting `ask_user` tool cannot be resolved by a button at all. The channel already receives card callbacks for approval cards, so the missing piece was the question mapping, not the transport.

## User Impact

Feishu DMs and allowlisted groups now render `ask_user` prompts as card buttons. Tapping an option (or the free-text "Other" control) resolves the waiting agent turn in place, and a click on an already-answered or expired card reports that outcome instead of silently doing nothing. Existing plain-text fallback and approval cards are unchanged. No config changes are required; the behavior is on for accounts that already run the bundled Feishu channel.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three small connections in `extensions/feishu`:

- `agentPrompt.questionInputMode = "buttons"` so the Gateway injects `ask_user` for Feishu sessions (the same declaration Telegram uses).
- Question buttons are captured while the card is built: the presentation carries `action.type === "question"` with a Gateway-owned option value, so the envelope stores `questionId` plus the resolved option index (or the custom-input intent) instead of dropping the button to text.
- Card callbacks for that envelope call `questionGatewayRuntime.resolveOption` with the operator''s `open_id`; malformed ids are rejected before any Gateway call.

The envelopes use the existing `ocf1` card-interaction helpers and the existing MFA-free callback route, so no new endpoint or credential handling is introduced.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: `extensions/feishu/src/question-callback.test.ts` (6) and `extensions/feishu/src/presentation-card.test.ts` (7) → **13 passed** with `vitest run`.
- `oxfmt --write` applied to all touched files.
- Repo-wide typecheck/lint were not run in this environment (the contributor checkout is sparse and the workspace package build is absent); PR CI covers those.
- Not exercised end-to-end against a live Feishu tenant: the click path needs a real card tap. A follow-up screenshot from a test bot can be attached if maintainers want it before merge.

prs.title: fix(process): charge shared host exec memory once via proportional set size
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Linux the host exec memory guard charged `VmRSS` for every process in a command's tree. RSS counts shared pages once per process, so a forked tree (headless Chrome, zygote children) charged the same libraries for every member and was killed far below its real footprint.

`readMemory()` now reads `Pss`/`SwapPss` from `/proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup` (Linux 4.14+), which attributes shared pages proportionally, and keeps the `VmRSS`/`VmSwap` status reader as the fallback for older kernels and ptrace-restricted processes. The budget formula is unchanged.

Fixes #206082.

## User Impact

Commands that fork worker processes stop being cancelled while they use a fraction of the shared budget. Single heavy processes are still cancelled — a process with 900 MiB of private memory exceeds a 640 MiB budget under either metric.

## Why This Change Was Made

The guard must charge a tree's real memory use, not the sum of per-process mappings. `smaps_rollup` is the kernel's own proportional accounting and needs one read per process, the same count as the `status` read it replaces. The fallback keeps hosts < 4.14 and processes we cannot read working exactly as before.

## Evidence

Unit tests, `src/process/child-memory.test.ts`:

- base (production file reverted): `Tests 2 failed | 15 passed (17)` — `expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times` (Pss test) and the retry test's read count.
- fixed: `Tests 17 passed (17)`.

Real process tree on this machine (python: 200 MiB touched, 5 idle forked children), watched through the shipped `watchHostExecMemory` with a 512 MiB budget:

- base: `{"pid":364666,"budgetMiB":512,"overLimit":true,"limited":1,"diagnostic":"\nCommand killed because the shared host exec memory budget was exceeded (RAM 1231/512 MiB; swap 0/0 MiB). ..."}`
- fixed: `{"pid":356437,"budgetMiB":512,"overLimit":false,"limited":0,"diagnostic":""}`

Raw `/proc` accounting for the same tree shape: `procs=6 rssSumMiB=1259 pssSumMiB=215`.

`oxlint src/process/child-memory.ts src/process/child-memory.test.ts` → 0 warnings, 0 errors.

## Gate checklist

```
机制对位: 症状在 src/process/child-memory.ts readMemory()（逐进程累加 VmRSS），我改同一函数（优先 smaps_rollup 的 Pss/SwapPss，读不到时回退 status），因为 RSS 让共享页按进程重复计费
复现: 6 进程 fork 树（200 MiB 私有 + 5 个 idle 子进程）在 512 MiB 预算下，base 触发 "RAM 1231/512 MiB" 取消，修复后不触发；单测 base 2 failed → 修复 17 passed
证据类别: 本机 Linux /proc 实测 + 单测，可得
契约核对: readMemory 归 src/process/child-memory.ts 所有；watchHostExecMemory/totalUsage/nearBudget 的预算语义未改
风险: 2 文件、单层（进程内存采样），无状态机、无跨层契约
```

## AI Assistance

Written with AI assistance (DeepSeek Harness agent). I verified every command output quoted above on this machine.

## Proof limits on this machine

ClawSweeper asked for a shipped Gateway exec trace. Driving the `exec` tool here needs an agent turn, and triggering the guard's cancellation needs a cgroup whose limit is below the workload:

- `docker` socket is permission denied for this user, so a `--memory=1g` container cannot run.
- `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=1G` starts, but `process.constrainedMemory()` inside the scope still reports `2^64-1`, so the guard keeps the host budget.
- On this host `getHostExecMemoryBudget()` resolves to `{ memoryBytes: 18763218944, swapBytes: 6254449664 }` (~17.9 GiB). Exercising the supervisor's `memory-limit` cancellation would need an ~18 GiB allocation on a 23.8 GiB shared machine, which is not safe to run here.

To reproduce the shipped cancellation on a constrained host (for example a 1 GiB systemd unit):

```bash
# inside the unit, after building:
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-206082/state node dist/index.js gateway run --port 34931
# then let an agent call exec to run: python3 fork_tree.py  (200 MiB touched, 5 idle children)
# expected after this change: the command completes; before: "Command killed because the shared host exec memory budget was exceeded"
```

prs.title: fix(update): settle after plugins and share one completion summary
prs.body:
## Class: completion is published before required maintenance finishes

Fleet run `4de610c8-e63d-4336-8e85-a76379cfd934` committed and served the new core, but its completion notice preceded the failed plugin result. The bug is ordering, not the core's status.

The modern Gateway-ready owner now settles once **after** required plugin work and sends one final notice afterward. A failed plugin remains a failed step, not a failed core update or a rollback trigger. Existing CLI following and capability-consent behavior remain; the failed-status/early-exit/backoff experiment is removed.

CLI completion, status, Doctor history and the Control UI reuse the existing `renderUpdateRunSummary` over recorded facts. Running results keep their phase; succeeded results name the installed after-version; skipped results keep their existing reason headline, never a guessed serving state. Failed work names its step and exact recovery command. Startup refusal diagnostics, structured failure facts, rollback compensation reasons, recorded signal output and profile-specific recovery commands remain visible. Existing discriminators distinguish repair and reconciled-history records from core updates. Background completion never rewrites the shared trial, preserving a newer pending trial and restart resumption.

## What this deletes

- `renderUpdateRunReport`, its private recovery hints and cause module.
- Routine Markdown completion publication/refresh, automatic `reportPath` output, and artifact-only admission/options plumbing.
- Obsolete completion-export tests and renderer-only assertions. Ledger, recovery, authority, privacy and step-detail assertions remain on their retained data owners.
- The abandoned failed-status classifier, campaign/retry exceptions, early-return CLI path and associated UI/test allocation.

**Kept deliberately:** explicit consent-gated **Report update failure** GitHub preview/submission, its reservation/receipt authority and sanitized issue artifacts. The remaining `update-failure-report*` code serves that user feature and triage, not routine completion. Identity/recovery and legacy result/sentinel projections remain because those manual-report and sentinel consumers still use them.

prs.title: feat: let each Doctor repair say whether it has work before the Gateway stops
prs.body:
Related: #204775

## What Problem This Solves

Every `openclaw doctor --fix` stops a healthy Gateway before it knows whether any step has work. To make that stop conditional (step 6 of the plan in #204775), each step must answer "is there work?" truthfully and without writing. On `main`, 90 of the 94 decisions on a healthy install still answer "work" only because they have no check.

This is step 5: real read-only checks for the Doctor contributions and the late steps.

## User Impact

None visible. `doctor --fix` still stops the Gateway and runs every step exactly as before. With `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE=1`, a healthy install now traces 64 decisions as `pending=none check=owner` instead of 3. The 29 decisions that still say `work check=default` are listed below with the reason each one has no check yet; that list is the input for step 6.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **One small mechanism, no blanket answers.** A contribution's `pending` is either the declared constant `"diagnostic-only"` or a function at its owner.
  - `"diagnostic-only"` (36 contributions) means `run` never writes under `--fix`. A new test runs every declared contribution in repair mode under maintenance on an install with a state database, an agent database, a config and a workspace, and fails when any file changes. A contribution that later starts writing fails that test (shown below).
  - Contributions that only declare health checks get their check derived from them: `runDoctorHealthRepairs` repairs a check only after its detect reports a finding, so there is work exactly when a check with a real repair has one. A check without a repair, a `legacyOwnedRepair` that only describes another owner's work, or a dry run cannot write. A throwing detect counts as undecidable. Core-check contributions (`stale-runtime-build`, `telegram-general-topic-conversations`) use the same rule.
  - Every other check reuses the contribution's own gate. Where the gate sat inside the write function, it is split out at that owner and both the check and the repair call it: TOOLS.md migration, legacy plugin manifests, agent memory schema, project clones, shell completion, Screen Sharing, the model allowlist offer, channel startup maintenance hooks, stray launchd jobs, systemd linger, and the two contributions Doctor defers under maintenance (`gateway-daemon`, `retained-update-runtimes`).
- **Late steps.** `boot-lifecycle` counts the rows its repair would change through a new read operation that shares the repair's `where` clause. `external-config` reads the persisted snapshot with observation off, the same read its validation uses. `maintenance-ready` checks the migration-backup manifests its completion would record (the readiness assertions only read). `retained-runtimes` turns its report-only pass into a decision through an `onRecognized` callback; it counts what the cleanup would try to remove.
- **Contract for each check:** no writable open, no file creation, no database copy, no lock. The agent-memory check runs the repair's existing no-op test without the Doctor SQLite maintenance lock; its databases open read-only. A read-only open of a WAL database can leave an empty `-wal` file; the tests treat that as unchanged because any write leaves frames in it or changes the database.
- **Left on the default.** Service-definition repair decides inside `maybeRepairGatewayServiceConfig` and the daemon runtime pin migration writes during it; that needs a read-only plan from the daemon side. The startup steps belong to the step 4 PR.
- `doctor-health-contributions.ts` was over its line cap after the change, so the systemd linger helpers moved unchanged into `doctor-systemd-linger.ts` and the final contributions import them directly instead of taking them as parameters.
- Ratchets: the new boot-lifecycle count runs only through `gatewayBootReadOperations` in the state read worker, so it is added to that kernel's existing W-tier entry in `scripts/database-worker-inventory.mjs` beside its sibling readers. The tests exceed the 400-line test budget by 303 lines; `config/test-lines-allocations/206247-doctor-contribution-pending-checks.txt` records that, because each new check needs a case with real work and the diagnostic-only declarations need their store test.
- No schema, stored field, config option, protocol or retention change.

### Classification of all 81 contributions

| Class | Contributions | Check |
|---|---|---|
| (a) diagnostic only (36) | node-runtime, runtime-capabilities, gateway-config, database-engine, claude-cli, command-owner, legacy-plugin-dependencies, stale-plugin-runtime-symlinks, ui-protocol-freshness, disk-space, db-bloat, channel-ingress-dead-letters, session-snapshots, codex-bwrap, security, web-fetch-proxy, bundle-lsp-env, github-projects, browser, oauth-tls, hooks-model, legacy-output-cap, model-references, acp-agent-model, provider-catalog-projection, local-audio-acceleration, runtime-tool-schemas, skill-workshop-tool-policy, workspace-status, workspace-alias, bootstrap-size, memory-provenance, gateway-health, whatsapp-responsiveness, device-pairing, workspace-suggestions | declared `"diagnostic-only"`; enforced by the store test |
| (a) health checks without a repair (6) | agent-database-admission, native-status, node-hosting-preconditions, update-snapshots, default-account-routing, channel-package-state-capabilities | derived: no repair means no work |
| (a) at their gate under maintenance (2) | gateway-daemon (daemon repair happens at service restoration), retained-update-runtimes (cleaned before the stop) | the contribution's own gate |
| (b) outside the protected stores (9) | gmail-gog (Homebrew upgrade), legacy-plugin-manifests (manifest files), tools-md-migration (workspace files), shell-completion (cache, shell profile), project-clone-shape (git history), gateway-services (stray launchd jobs on macOS), host-desktop (macOS Screen Sharing), systemd-linger (loginctl), stale-runtime-build (no repair; derived) | owner predicate shared with the repair |
| (c) protected stores, with a check (5) | plugin-registry (step 3), telegram-general-topic-conversations (agent database), agent-memory-schema (agent database), model-allowlist-wildcards (config), startup-channel-maintenance (plugin hooks) | owner predicate shared with the repair |
| (c) protected stores, still default (23) | see the table below | none yet |

### What still says `work` or `undecidable` on a healthy install, and why

| Contribution or step | Writes | Why it still defaults to work |
|---|---|---|
| write-config-migrations, write-config | `openclaw.json`, `config.lastTouchedAt`, cron rows, Codex routes | the write decision compares in-memory candidates (`ctx.cfg` against `cfgForPersistence`, order-sensitive JSON), not the file; a check needs the config-flow result, which is step 4's lane |
| final-config-validation | state database config-health rows | reads the snapshot with observation on; passing `observe: false` is a behavior change for its own PR |
| auth-profile-migration, auth-profiles | auth stores, agent databases, config | the resume step decides under a file lock while writing; OAuth refresh hits the network |
| gateway-auth | secret store, state database snapshot | decision is inline in `runGatewayAuthHealth`; needs a split that also covers `--generate-gateway-token` |
| structured-health-repairs | plugin-driven config and package changes | runs every plugin health check; a check would run every plugin detect a second time |
| legacy-state | state and agent databases, exec approvals | `repairObsoleteGeneratedExecApprovals` decides inside a write transaction on every run |
| session-transcripts, session-transcript-headers, session-transcript-labels | agent databases, backups | owners only offer a preview mode that also prints notes; no pure detect |
| codex-session-routes | agent databases | preview path prints notes and uses a tolerant scan unlike the repair's strict one |
| release-configured-plugin-installs | plugin packages, plugin index, config | its no-op plan is inline and not exported; it also rewrites `lastTouchedVersion` |
| legacy-plugin-source-captures | capture folders | native capture cleanup decides inline while removing |
| state-integrity | state database (opens a write transaction on every run), file modes, agent stores | the agent-path repair checks for pending rows inside its write transaction |
| config-audit-scrub | agent databases (a DELETE on every run), audit log | the usage-cost cache cleanup has no predicate |
| legacy-cron | cron store | loading the mutable store can commit repairs before any prompt |
| sandbox | config, sandbox registry, images | mixes three owners; image check spawns docker |
| skills | config | its kept-skills rule differs from the core detect; needs a shared predicate |
| heartbeat-cadence-migration, heartbeat-scratch-migration, heartbeat-task-cron-migration | state and agent databases, workspace files | their detects use artifact-preserving reads that may copy the database |
| memory-search | plugin state store, workspace files | memory plugin runtime decides inline |
| client-credentials, state-database-repair, database-migrations, runtime-checks, config-flow | state database, config | step 4 lane |
| service-definition | systemd unit / launchd plist | decision is inline in `maybeRepairGatewayServiceConfig` (about 450 lines) and `withDaemonRuntimePinMigration` writes; needs a read-only plan from the daemon side |
| sqlite-nocow | store rewrite | `undecidable` on btrfs without `lsattr` (existing check) |

## Update behavior

There is no update-path change. A published updater that runs Doctor on this build runs the same repairs in the same order; the only difference is the trace lines when the trace variable is set. Nothing here changes what any step does or when the Gateway stops.

## Evidence

**Cells: Linux, systemd user Gateway, npm install of a packed build under an unpublished version, 64 MiB agent database, `/readyz` probed every 250 ms.** Base is `main` at `fcc9a0648c2` (packed as 2026.11.23). Head is this PR's first commit, `241d268c280` (packed as 2026.11.24). One count cell per build runs `doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes` three times on a healthy install. One guard cell per build seeds real work while the Gateway serves (state database mode 0644, a maintenance `startup_failed` boot row, a plugin record removed, a `TOOLS.md`, an abandoned updater runtime and a look-alike folder as a negative control), then runs Doctor twice.

| | base `fcc9a0648c2` | head `241d268c280` |
|---|---|---|
| decisions per healthy run | 94 | 94 |
| `pending=none check=owner` | 3 | 64 |
| `pending=work check=default` | 90 | 29 |
| `pending=undecidable check=owner` | 1 (`sqlite-nocow`, no `lsattr` on btrfs) | 1 (same) |
| any owner check answering `work` on a healthy run | 0 | 0 |
| slowest owner check | 55 ms (plugin registry) | 65 ms (`retained-runtimes`, before the stop), then 46 ms (plugin registry) |
| `/readyz` outage, runs 1 / 2 / 3 | 29.2 / 25.7 / 26.2 s | 25.7 / 22.7 / 22.9 s |

Guard cells, the seeded sites:

| Site | base, work run → clean run | head, work run → clean run | Repaired on both builds |
|---|---|---|---|
| boot lifecycle | `work default` → `work default` | `work owner` → `none owner` | row marked `startup_failure_repaired` |
| TOOLS.md migration | `work default` → `work default` | `work owner` → `none owner` | merged into AGENTS.md |
| plugin registry (step 3) | `work owner` → `none owner` | `work owner` → `none owner` | 78 → 79 plugins |
| retained runtimes | `work default` → `work default` | `work owner` → `work owner` | kept on both: inside a container the process census refuses removal by design, so the folder is still there and the check still reports it |
| look-alike runtime (negative control) | kept | kept, not counted | |
| `/readyz` outage, settle / work / clean | 29.4 / 23.4 / 23.2 s | 26.0 / 22.9 / 23.0 s | |

Head's outage is within noise of base; the checks cost milliseconds and the stop is unchanged.

Recordings replay the raw cell logs: the decision counts, the remaining `work` list, the outages and the guard cell.

prs.title: fix(mattermost): let buttons with Chinese, spaced or agent-callback values be clicked
prs.body:
Root cause: extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/interactions.ts:205 (on main) `sanitizeActionId` stripped only `-` and `_` from the button value it used as the Mattermost action id. Mattermost routes clicks only through `/posts/{post_id}/actions/{action_id:[A-Za-z0-9]+}`, so any other character returned 404 before OpenClaw saw the click.

Fixes #206226

Thanks @hannnnn-l for the report and the fix.

## What Problem This Solves

Clicking a Mattermost button opens "Page not found." when the button's value contains anything other than `[A-Za-z0-9]`, for example a Chinese value like `删掉说明和备注两条帖子，只留表` or one with spaces or punctuation. The click never reaches OpenClaw. Since #201764, every button the agent sends with the `message` tool breaks this way, even `approve`, because agent callback values carry the `::` mark and that mark ended up in the action id. The mark first shipped in v2026.11.10-beta.3 and v2026.11.10 (current `latest`). v2026.10.34 (`extended-stable`) and v2026.11.9 and earlier don't have it, so there only non-alphanumeric values break.

Mattermost keeps the action id the post was created with (`server/channels/api4/integration_action.go`, v11.7.15).

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildButtonAttachments` is the one place that turns a button id into the Mattermost action `id` and the signed `context.action_id`.

- An id that is already `[A-Za-z0-9]+` is used unchanged, so the model picker and raw callers produce byte-identical posts.
- Any other id becomes `<its alphanumerics, max 16>x<button index>`. The index after the last `x` makes derived ids unique within a post by construction, including two values that clean to the same text (`yes?` / `yes!`).
- Accepted edge case, not observed: a raw alphanumeric id that equals a derived id in the same post would clash (Mattermost sends the click to the first action with that id). Agent, question and picker ids can't produce it.
- The value itself still travels unchanged in the HMAC-signed `context.callback_data`, which is what the click delivers to the agent. Signing, the post-action match and the click authorization check are unchanged.

The docs no longer say the value is used as the action id, and the 404 troubleshooting entry names the real cause.

## User Impact

Buttons with any value work again, and the agent receives the exact original value. Posts already sent with broken ids stay broken and have to be re-sent. No config or migration is needed.

## Evidence

- Regression test (`interactions.test.ts`): red on main (`expected '::删掉说明和备注两条帖子，只留表' to match /^[A-Za-z0-9]+$/`), green with the fix.
- Live run against Mattermost 11.7.15 with an isolated Gateway built from main and from this head. A scripted model sends a buttons block through the real `message` tool, and user alice clicks through Mattermost's action route, twice per side: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206228#issuecomment-7206552500
- Chromium screenshots: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206228#issuecomment-7206553442

| Case | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chinese value | 404 "Page not found", no Gateway log, no agent turn | 200, agent gets `删掉说明和备注两条帖子，只留表` |
| Spaces/punctuation `yes, do it! (now)` | 404 | 200, agent gets the exact value |
| Agent value `approve` (`::approve`) | 404 | 200, agent gets `approve` |
| Model picker (`/oc_models`) | 200, id `mdllistb735d7f3f8da` | same id, 200 |
| Tampered `callback_data` or `action_id` | 403 Invalid token | 403 Invalid token |

Merge danger: two-way door. A revert restores the old ids. Nothing is stored and no config changes. Blast radius is Mattermost button posts.

prs.title: fix: keep lean Gateway reads on the shared worker
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On lean Gateways, two overlapping SQLite reads can finish preparing in a different order from their admission. The pool can then retire the reader on the shared worker after 30 seconds and keep a dedicated worker warm. An otherwise idle Gateway keeps an extra physical worker after the burst.

## User Impact

When the pool already has a reader on the shared worker, subsequent reads prefer it. A busy shared reader can still use a dedicated worker for a concurrent request. Operators use the existing lean profile.

## Why This Change Was Made

The host knows whether the worker it constructed is a shared endpoint. The pool uses that fact for idle reuse and for the primary reader’s deadline. A former primary’s burst deadline includes the time it has already spent idle. Pools with an explicitly retained newest reader keep their existing policy.

## Evidence

### Final results on 2f2cc1f6

All 12 fresh Linux/Node 24.22.1 processes exited successfully on the same AWS c7a.8xlarge. The exact corrected benchmark bytes, source-runtime identity and built output checksums were verified for every arm. The ordered controls and all five reversed pairs met the expected physical-worker and endpoint counts. Stock kept five tracked physical workers on every reversed run. The candidate kept four, the same count that both ordered controls retained. The shared sibling stayed live. All 2,400 warm reads returned the seeded value and its timestamp with no replacement worker. Process-wide fixture descriptors were 3 with both readers, 2 at the checkpoint and 1 after all tracked workers and endpoints joined. The final descriptor’s owner remains unverified. [Final comparison and all raw rows](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_1c01bb98a27454466efdac099c3a9ce6) · [Fixed hosted ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45916465736/job/140237413467)

**Reversed-preparation median RSS fell 3.79 MiB (0.46%).** Three of five pairs had lower RSS. The paired changes were −13.48, −12.81, +11.49, −54.44 and +5.20 MiB. The five-pair result measures this source-mode fixture at 32.001–32.005 seconds. The field frequency and whole-Gateway RSS effect are unknown.

All five pairs had faster median and p95 warm reads, lower warm CPU, and lower final reader cleanup CPU. The additional dedicated worker retired during the idle window on the candidate. Idle main-thread CPU rose by 1.912 ms by cohort medians and idle process CPU rose by 14.272 ms. Summed main-thread and process CPU across the measured phases fell 6.44% and 0.24%, respectively. Per-pair summed process CPU differences were −49.542, −207.654, +215.161, +10.839 and −14.085 ms. Reader setup accounts for most of this variation.

Each cell shows the median and minimum–maximum across the five processes. “Higher” counts pairs where the candidate used more memory or time.

On Linux/Node 24.22.1 with one persistent sibling on the shared host, the stock pool closed a SQLite descriptor in both preparation orders. At burst expiry the ordered run had two tracked physical workers and retained the shared reader. The reversed run had three and retained the dedicated reader. The next read reused the survivor, and both runs joined physical shutdown. The separate control on a seeded database showed that a reader created before lean initialization can remain dedicated while the Gateway lock is held. This change addresses pools that actually acquire a shared endpoint. [Native Linux reproduction](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_56efe209d1c613a6c7367f322526b447) · [Gateway lock controls](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_2647ef6bddbf645391aca7cb1239cb65)

The production package build and targeted lint on all seven files passed. [Final build and lint](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_610273817e96f91f4369e27714d60e1c) [Focused test run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_92553a47df9ced2063dc2e1dc1bd2863)

The three new regression cases failed on the frozen base. They cover reversed preparation with timed and untimed primary readers, and a dedicated reader that was already idle when demoted. [Baseline regression cases](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_d8aee0f311a0ae1295c16dbdb8c31cef)

The first ordered stock control exposed two additional source-mode workers after reader teardown. Constructor tracing identified the file logger and the TypeScript loader’s esbuild worker. The benchmark now joins both after timing reader cleanup and still requires zero tracked workers at process shutdown. The corrected smoke reached zero physical workers and endpoints. The process-wide descriptor census still showed one fixture database descriptor at that checkpoint. Its owner is unverified. The isolated Node process subsequently exited. No reversed pair had started. [Cleanup and lint](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_ed147963977859364413e85f9ccf7ef9) · [Worker ownership trace](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_f20b7fab2faf40e68a9e264998c7d4f8)

### Paired benchmark acceptance, recorded before measurement

Run the committed workload on Linux/Node 24.22.1, using the same AWS machine, fixture, driver bytes and runtime settings. Each sample is a fresh Node process. The same committed benchmark bytes run against each arm. A is `9fc8273647739775a2fe91b5745d613311d89083` and B is `810f361e9ec8df39c45221e09ce917229f0a9d35`. Run five reversed pairs in AB, BA, AB, BA, AB order, serially. Use the ordered preparation as a control.

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/state-read-hosted-survivor.ts reversed
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/state-read-hosted-survivor.ts ordered
```

The fixture keeps one SQLite sibling endpoint live, admits two state reads and waits 32 seconds from the completion of **both** reads. A win requires the shared reader to survive in both candidate orders, one fewer tracked physical worker on the reversed workload, and a lower median process RSS at that fixed checkpoint. Every next read must return the expected row, with no replacement worker starts, and final cleanup must join all tracked workers.

After the checkpoint, measure 200 checked warm reads per process. Report per-process median and p95 latency, main-thread and process CPU, and the spread across the five pairs. Report reader setup after sibling initialization, idle-window CPU and physical reader cleanup separately. Sum the four disjoint measured CPU phases within each process. Import time, sibling startup, census, and the final logger/tool shutdown are outside that sum. Census and RSS sampling stay outside read timing. Compare latency and CPU guardrails before landing and disclose adverse movements. These are source-mode worker-pool measurements with an idle sibling. Whole-Gateway RSS and the frequency of this preparation order in field traffic are unmeasured.

### Follow-up benchmark on the state-writer fixture

The baseline ratchet identified a raw write in the synthetic fixture. The corrected driver uses the reviewed in-database state writer, checks its returned timestamp and JSON row on each read, and clears the fixture connection’s query cache before close. This runs before Gateway profiling and the measurement windows. Loading the writer can change the benchmark process’s memory. The historical comparison below records the earlier `810f361e` cohort. [Original failed gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45915032974/job/140234221408) · [Writer fixture validation](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_ff7bc1d4a48a53d7dbf084755dcbb6e6)

Repeat the previously declared acceptance on the same lease with stock `9fc8273647739775a2fe91b5745d613311d89083` and corrected head `2f2cc1f604f531776c9061643f4a8dd1c379ea33`. Both arms use driver SHA-256 `feced4bd1fc588538f9c921fe1cb76316fc2591de1360091553f03c4f5fb242a`. Use two ordered controls and five reversed pairs, AB/BA/AB/BA/AB. All operations, timers, census points, expected physical retirement and warm-read count remain as declared above. Report this cohort separately.

### Historical comparison

Before the synthetic fixture adopted the state writer, the earlier signed head `810f361e` also retained one fewer physical worker and passed all 2,400 reads. Its median RSS was 716.81→677.55 MiB (−39.25 MiB, four of five pairs lower). Four-phase main/process CPU was 32.871→29.425 ms (−10.48%) and 4677.184→4696.218 ms (+0.41%). That driver loaded a different module graph. Its SHA-256 was `917abb03b23688f1eab4ffa2827268a6861d5dad10fd73ef880fae7bc87d5e5e`. The corrected cohort above supplies the current result.
