prs.title: fix(signal): keep quote markers on continuation lines, nested quotes, and later chunks
prs.body:
Refs: #204999

## What Problem This Solves

Signal outbound messages keep the `> ` quote marker only on the first line of a blockquote. Sending `> line one\n> line two\n>\n> second para` delivers `> line one\nline two\n\nsecond para`, so continuation lines and later quoted paragraphs arrive as plain text. Nested quotes collapse to a single `> ` on their first line and lose it on the next, and when a long quote is split across messages, every chunk after the first starts with bare text. #190066 fixed this for Slack and WhatsApp by moving the marker to render time; Signal still baked the prefix into the IR text at parse time, so chunking sliced it away.

The defect is unchanged on current main: `extensions/signal/src/format.ts` still passes `blockquotePrefix: "> "` to `markdownToIR`, and `renderMarkdownWithAttributedRanges` has no equivalent option.

## User Impact

Signal recipients see quoted assistant replies as quotes: every nonempty quoted line carries its full `> ` (or `> > ` for nested) marker, including soft-wrapped continuation lines, later paragraphs inside the same quote, and the first line of each later chunk of a split quote. Style ranges (for example BOLD) still cover the same words after the prefixes are added. This matches the documented Slack/WhatsApp behavior in `docs/concepts/markdown-formatting.md`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal inserted `> ` at IR parse time (`markdownToIR(..., { blockquotePrefix: "> " })`), which puts the marker only where the parser emits it and lets chunk slicing separate it from later lines. The render-time mechanism from #190066 existed only in the marker renderer (`renderMarkdownWithMarkers`); Signal uses the attributed-range renderer, which had no equivalent.

The change reuses the same owner instead of adding a Signal-local post-processor:

- `render.ts`: the inline quote-line scan moves into an exported `collectBlockquoteLineStarts` (no behavior change for marker targets).
- `render-attributed.ts`: `AttributedRenderOptions` gains the same `blockquotePrefix` option, applied through the existing insertion/shift machinery so style ranges stay aligned.
- `ir-annotations.ts`: `annotateAssistantTranscriptRoleMessageBoundary` rebuilt the IR with a spread, which silently dropped the non-enumerable `blocks` metadata; range targets project `blockquote` to fallback text, so a promoted transcript-role header inside a quote lost its prefix. Block metadata is now re-attached (text coordinates are unchanged). This was the open review finding on the previous attempt at this fix.
- `extensions/signal/src/format.ts`: parse-time prefix removed; render passes `blockquotePrefix: "> "`. The link de-dup filter now assigns in place because a spread would drop the same block metadata (the filter is idempotent per render).

## Evidence

The branch was rebased onto current main (`4afe35da99f`) to clear the merge conflict; the change set is unchanged from the reviewed version. No commit between the previous base and the new one touches the files in this PR, so base behavior is identical.

**Real outbound trace** through the production path — channel `sendFormattedText` adapter → `markdownToSignalTextChunks` → `sendMessageSignal` → real HTTP client → loopback signal-cli JSON-RPC recorder. Scenario from the earlier review: a nested quote whose transcript-role header begins a later chunk (`> > padding padding user[2026-07-02] question`, `textChunkLimit: 25`).

Base (parse-time prefix) — the promoted-header chunk loses its quote prefix:

```
chunk 1: message="> > padding padding" text-style=[]
chunk 2: message="user[2026-07-02] question" text-style=["0:16:MONOSPACE"]
loopback signal-cli recorder received 2 send request(s)
```

With this patch — every chunk keeps `> > `, MONOSPACE shifts to the post-prefix offset, each message stays within the 25-char limit:

```
chunk 1: message="> > padding padding" text-style=[]
chunk 2: message="> > user[2026-07-02]" text-style=["4:16:MONOSPACE"]
chunk 3: message="> > question" text-style=[]
loopback signal-cli recorder received 3 send request(s)
```

New regression tests in `extensions/signal/src/format.test.ts`, red on current main and green with the fix:

```
× keeps the quote marker on continuation lines, nested quotes, and later paragraphs
  → expected '> line one\nline two\n\nsecond para\n…' to be '> line one\n> line two\n\n> second pa…'
× keeps the quote marker on the first line of every chunk of a split quote
  → expected false to be true
× keeps the nested quote marker when a transcript-role header starts a later chunk
  → expected 'user[2026-07-02] question' to be '> > user[2026-07-02]'

with the fix: 27 passed
```

The issue's repro now renders:

```
input:  > line one\n> **line two**\n>\n> second para\n> > nested one\n> > nested two
text:   > line one\n> line two\n\n> second para\n\n> > nested one\n> > nested two
styles: BOLD over "line two" (offset shifted by the prefixes)
```

The promoted-header regression is load-bearing on the `ir-annotations.ts` metadata repair: reverting only that file turns the third test red (the chunk degrades to bare `user[2026-07-02] question`).

Consumers of the changed renderers still pass: the full `packages/markdown-core` suite plus the Signal, Slack, WhatsApp, Google Chat, iMessage, Matrix, MS Teams, Telegram, and Zalo User format suites — 21 files, 456 tests. `oxfmt --check` passes on all changed files.

## Merge Danger

Low for non-Signal channels: `renderMarkdownWithMarkers` behavior is unchanged (same scan, now shared), and the attributed renderer's new option defaults to off, so Google Chat, iMessage, Matrix, MS Teams, Telegram, and Zalo User render exactly as before. The annotation metadata repair only adds back metadata the spread already dropped; annotation output is otherwise identical.

Signal output changes intentionally: quoted messages now carry `> ` on every quoted line instead of only the first. That is the documented behavior for the sibling channels and the point of the fix; the marker text counts toward the chunk limit at render time, so splits stay within `textChunkLimit`.

prs.title: fix: let Macs and iPhones join claws that use custom member roles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signing in to a claw with OpenClaw ID from the Mac app (and the upcoming iOS app) fails right after another device approves it, with "Setup did not finish". It happens whenever the claw has a member with a role other than `operator` or `viewer`, for example a custom participant role. Member roles became opaque names in #197697, but the Swift client still rejected any other role and treated the claw's whole membership snapshot as malformed.

## User Impact

On claws with custom member roles, owners and members can approve a new Mac or iPhone again, and members can join them. Claws that only use `operator` and `viewer` are unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Swift snapshot check now accepts any role name matching the protocol's `isMemberRole` rule (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`), so the client agrees with the Gateway and Discovery. The role still grants nothing on the client, and the rest of the strict snapshot validation is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on the iOS simulator (iOS 27.2) against a live staging claw that has a custom member role: after a web approval, the client logged `OpenClawIDNodeEnrollmentError.malformed` from snapshot validation. The macOS app built from main failed the same way.
- `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter 'OpenClawIDMemberJoinTests|OpenClawIDOwnerEnrollmentTests|OpenClawIDNode'`: 56 tests passed on macOS 27.2 / Xcode 27.2. The member-join test now approves a `participant` role.
- With this fix on the iOS simulator, the same web approval completed: the device was admitted as an owner device of the claw ("You're all set").
- Not yet shown: the updated test failing on the base.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: improve: skip unused context engine lookups during model selection
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Local model runs walk every installed plugin’s context engine declarations even when no context engine is selected. Gateway startup performs the same conversion while planning which plugins to activate.

## User Impact

An installation using the default context engine skips this inventory walk, including rows for disabled plugins. Configured engines still use their declared IDs, approved owners and existing ambiguity rules. No configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installed index already contains the plugin ID and its engine declarations. The resolver can read installed rows directly after it checks whether an engine was selected. Manifest callers continue passing their existing rows. This removes four conversions that copied the inventory solely to rename the ID field.

## Evidence

Two isolated Node processes ran the production selected-model metadata scope from the parent and the PR head against the same 190-plugin fixture. With the context engine omitted, two successive resolutions on the parent read 190 declarations each. On the PR head both read zero. Both revisions selected only the requested provider. When configured with an alternate engine ID, both revisions selected the differently named engine owner and requested provider, with 190 reads per resolution.

Separate controls retained the same outcomes for an ambiguous engine, canonical denial, a legacy equal-ID owner and the built-in default. All 107 focused tests passed across model runtime metadata, plugin owner policy, loader context and Gateway startup. The full `pnpm build` passed on the signed head, including declaration emission and plugin SDK export checks. The Control UI build printed asset budget warnings. End-to-end device latency has not been measured.

[Branch CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45912795684) reported the same five production and two full-tree unused exports as the [base dependency check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45910909346/job/140219264465). Branch CI also reported a [Gateway resource-close error](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45912795684/job/140225405805) and a [browser timeout in the cloud profile retry test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45912795684/job/140225405270). Those two failures have separate causes still to verify.

prs.title: feat(litellm): declare managesOwnAvailability in plugin manifest
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

LiteLLM is an upstream proxy and routing gateway that balances requests across multiple models, API keys, and backends, owning its own rate limit backoffs and transient retry handling. When LiteLLM returns a transient 429 (`rate_limit`) or 503 (`overloaded`), OpenClaw recorded and persisted a local auth-profile cooldown for that profile, locking out subsequent requests locally even though the proxy may have alternative healthy backends available.

## User Impact

Users utilizing LiteLLM as their model provider will no longer experience local auth-profile lockouts upon encountering transient 429 (`rate_limit`) or 503 (`overloaded`) responses. The local transient cooldown is bypassed, while authentication failures (401), billing limits (402), and subscription restrictions remain strictly enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Declaring `"managesOwnAvailability": true` in `extensions/litellm/openclaw.plugin.json` opts the LiteLLM provider plugin into OpenClaw's provider-managed transient capacity recovery mechanism (established in #141825 alongside OpenRouter and Kilo Gateway). The core availability policy reads this declaration from metadata before loading the provider runtime.

## Evidence

### 1. Behavior Proof: Production Transport & Failure Handling

Tested against an isolated mock upstream using OpenClaw's real OpenAI completions transport (`streamOpenAICompletions`) and failure recovery pipeline (`handleEmbeddedAssistantFailure` via `failoverRetryController`) with the plugin manifest loaded directly from `extensions/litellm/openclaw.plugin.json`.

```
================================================================
PROOF OF BEHAVIOR: LiteLLM managesOwnAvailability
Production transport: streamOpenAICompletions + handleEmbeddedAssistantFailure
Real plugin manifest loaded: extensions/litellm/openclaw.plugin.json
================================================================

SCENARIO 1: BEFORE PATCH (managesOwnAvailability = false)
- Upstream response: HTTP 429 Rate limit exceeded (retry-after: 60)
- Stream result: stopReason=error errorCode=429
- Persisted state on disk:
    cooldownUntil: 1795643742156
    cooldownReason: rate_limit
- Subsequent request check:
    isProfileInCooldown("litellm:manual", "proof-model"): true
    -> RESULT: Subsequent request WOULD BE SKIPPED locally (profile locked out)

SCENARIO 2: AFTER PATCH (managesOwnAvailability = true)
- Upstream response: HTTP 429 Rate limit exceeded (retry-after: 60)
- Stream result: stopReason=error errorCode=429
- Persisted state on disk:
    cooldownUntil: undefined (NOT PERSISTED)
    cooldownReason: undefined (NOT PERSISTED)
- Subsequent request check:
    isProfileInCooldown("litellm:manual", "proof-model"): false
    -> RESULT: Subsequent request CAN PROCEED (gateway manages recovery)

SCENARIO 3: AFTER PATCH - 503 Overloaded (transient failure)
- Upstream response: HTTP 503 Service overloaded
- Persisted state on disk: cooldownUntil: undefined, cooldownReason: undefined
- Subsequent request check: isProfileInCooldown: false (CAN PROCEED)

SCENARIO 4: AFTER PATCH - 401 Auth Failure (credential failure)
- Upstream response: HTTP 401 Invalid API key
- Persisted state on disk: cooldownUntil: <timestamp>, cooldownReason: auth
- Subsequent request check: isProfileInCooldown: true (ENFORCED & LOCKED OUT)

SCENARIO 5: AFTER PATCH - 402 Billing Failure (balance failure)
- Upstream response: HTTP 402 Insufficient balance
- Persisted state on disk: disabledReason: billing
- Subsequent request check: isProfileInCooldown: true (ENFORCED & LOCKED OUT)
```

### 2. Unit & Integration Tests

- `src/plugins/provider-availability-policy.test.ts`: Verifies bundled `litellm` manifest declares `managesOwnAvailability: true`.
- `src/agents/auth-profiles.markauthprofilefailure.test.ts`: Verifies end-to-end failure marking on disk/SQLite: 429/503 skips cooldown persistence for LiteLLM, while 401 (`auth`) and 402 (`billing`) remain strictly enforced.
- `extensions/litellm/index.test.ts`: All 13 existing LiteLLM extension tests pass.
- Verified test suite passes: 3 Vitest shards passed cleanly.
- Code hygiene: `run-format` and `oxlint` pass with zero errors.

prs.title: fix(discord): repair name-keyed server rules in Doctor
prs.body:
## Summary

Discord Doctor can now move an existing server rule from a name to an operator-confirmed numeric ID. On a writable configuration, unattended Doctor records the IDs of servers that match an ambiguous rule and pauses their incoming activity until the operator resolves it. On a read-only deployment, Doctor reports the matching IDs so the operator can fix the deployment source. This covers existing configurations. [#205554](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205554) covers server selection during setup.

## What Problem This Solves

1. Doctor previously left name-keyed rules in place without identifying the rule or offering a way to move its attached restrictions. The Discord adapter now reports the authored path and repairs each rule in its original scope. See `extensions/discord/src/doctor.ts` and `extensions/discord/src/doctor-guilds.ts`.
2. An unattended run had no durable record of which servers were affected by an ambiguous name. Discord Gateway dispatch, queued-message delivery and voice admission now consult the account's recorded server IDs. See `extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.ts`, `extensions/discord/src/monitor/ingress.ts` and `extensions/discord/src/voice/access.ts`.

## Why this design

- Keep the account-specific pause on the unresolved rule. An interactive repair removes the bookkeeping. A manual rekey to a numeric ID also releases the pause.
- Move the entire rule so user, role, channel, and tool restrictions stay together. Retain both entries and report the conflict when the proposed ID already exists in the same scope.
- Keep the directory lookup inside the Discord plugin. Use the existing config writer for unattended persistence, and preserve regular delivery for other servers and DMs.

## Relation to the setup change

The two PRs are based independently on main. Both touch the server directory reader in `extensions/discord/src/guilds.ts`. When integrating the second PR, retain setup's single-page reader and Doctor's paginated lookup through the same owner. [Setup PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205554)

## Evidence of Fix

| Path and command | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline, `pnpm openclaw doctor --non-interactive` | Doctor completed without identifying the name-keyed rule. |
| `pnpm openclaw doctor --non-interactive`, `pnpm openclaw doctor </dev/null`, and `pnpm openclaw doctor --yes` | Each saved the two matching IDs. The third server's rule and the original restrictions survived. |
| Update child, `pnpm openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` | The candidate persisted the same pause with update mode enabled, including on a config saved by stable 2026.11.10 Doctor. |
| Interactive terminal, `pnpm openclaw doctor --fix` | Entering the intended ID moved the rule with its user and tool restrictions and cleared its pause. The adapter test also verifies that an occupied destination preserves both entries. |
| Three starts of `pnpm openclaw gateway run` against a local Discord simulator | Only the unaffected server reached the durable ingress queue on the first two starts. After manually rekeying the rule, messages from all three reached ingress on the third start. |
| Externally managed diagnosis, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_READONLY=1` and `OPENCLAW_NIX_MODE=1`, each with `pnpm openclaw doctor --non-interactive` | Before the follow-up, a read-only config stopped diagnosis at the write refusal. Both managed modes now finish, name the rule and matching IDs, and leave existing server policy in effect. Correct the key in the deployment source and redeploy. |
| Manual downgrade, 2026.11.10 `openclaw config validate` | The older schema rejected the unresolved pause field and accepted the interactively repaired config. |

The restart check inspected persisted message receipts. Live Discord validation stopped before login because the test bot lease was unavailable.

<details>
<summary>Terminal and persisted-state excerpts (synthetic IDs redacted)</summary>

Stable Doctor completed with the name-keyed rule in place. After switching the isolated install to the candidate, the update-mode Doctor saved the following server rules. The second line is the result from a separate interactive repair of that paused config.

```text
after update Doctor: {"ops": {"users": ["123"], "tools": {"deny": ["exec"]}, "doctorPausedGuildIds": {"default": ["server-A", "server-B"]}}, "server-C": {"requireMention": true}}
after interactive repair: {"server-C": {"requireMention": true}, "server-A": {"users": ["123"], "tools": {"deny": ["exec"]}}}
```

The Gateway fixture sent one message per server on each independent start. These are the actual ingress receipt rows, keyed by message ID. The first two starts used the persisted pause. The third followed a manual rekey.

```text
gateway cycle 0 received ['message-1C'] expected ['message-1C']
gateway cycle 1 received ['message-2C'] expected ['message-2C']
gateway cycle 2 received ['message-3A', 'message-3B', 'message-3C'] expected ['message-3A', 'message-3B', 'message-3C']
```

</details>

The review follow-up exercised an operator edit during the server-directory request on both revisions. These terminal lines come from checking the saved config after Doctor exited:

```text
before: exit 1 operator edit True pause field present False
after:  exit 0 operator edit True pause field present False
```

The local voice admission test rejected an otherwise-allowed speaker from the paused guild and admitted the same speaker from another guild. The durable-queue test admitted both messages before starting the monitor, then observed only the unaffected message at dispatch and a completed receipt for the paused message.

On the read-only fixture, Doctor printed the report below. Both read-only and Nix runs reached `Doctor complete`. Inspection of the read-only fixture showed the original restrictions and no newly saved pause.

```text
Discord account default: could not confirm a saved pause for servers
[server A], [server B] at channels.discord.guilds["ops"].
Check the current config and rerun Doctor, or resolve the name in the deployment source.
```

## SDK and caller upgrade contract

The generated channel config baseline gains six paths: the pause field, account key and ID array element under each of the root and account guild schemas. These represent one optional saved field. The channel Doctor hooks receive optional input for interactive text and a config revision for unattended writes. Existing callers of the guild directory reader keep their single-page behavior. For a manual downgrade, resolve paused rules in the current version first. When rekeying by hand, remove the `doctorPausedGuildIds` field from the rekeyed rule so the older version can load it.

## Boundary decisions for Discord and Doctor maintainers

1. Review the scope of the pause at incoming Gateway dispatch, queued delivery, and voice speaker admission. Scheduled or operator-initiated outbound work remains available.
2. Review the config write during unattended diagnosis. It uses the observed source revision and persists the IDs on the unresolved rule.

## Testing

- `pnpm test src/commands/doctor-prompter.test.ts src/commands/doctor-config-flow.test.ts extensions/discord/src/doctor.test.ts extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/ingress.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/provider.startup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 97 tests on the original revision. ## What Problem This Solves

When a CLI command checks for an older Gateway service, it looks up the CLI package and resolves its filesystem path even if service discovery found nothing to compare. This also happens when a service definition exists but its launcher cannot be traced to a package.

## User Impact

CLI commands skip those filesystem operations on hosts without an identifiable Gateway installation. Service discovery still runs on every inspection, so a service installed between calls is considered. An identified older service still protects its database from incompatible migrations.

## Why This Change Was Made

The service layout already identifies the Gateway package when it can. The CLI now uses that information before looking up its own package, matching the order used by Gateway status.

## Evidence

Linux CI on the final revision passed all 53 relevant tests. The CLI inspection suite (9 tests) checks the missing LaunchAgent, observes the newly created unidentifiable launcher, and verifies that neither inspection resolves the CLI package or its filesystem path. The systemd account suite (19 tests) and worker-policy suite (25 tests) preserve older-service migration restrictions and fresh service selection. prs.title: fix(apple): Gateway connections fail behind hostname-routed HTTPS proxies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where iOS users adding a Gateway through a QR setup code would fail to connect when an HTTPS reverse proxy routes requests using an exact hostname match. The same endpoint worked through a dedicated proxy port.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway WebSocket URLs now omit port 443 for WSS, preventing URLSession from adding an explicit default port to the HTTP Host header. Stored endpoint ports, Gateway identity, cleartext WS ports (including explicit port 80), non-default TLS ports, encoded context paths, and TLS pinning are unchanged. Cleartext ports remain explicit because existing macOS URL canonicalization treats an omitted WS port as 18789.

This replaces the original SNI diagnosis and custom Network.framework WebSocket transport. Live investigation established that HTTP Host matching, not missing SNI, caused this deployment's routing failure. The original URLSession transport and fingerprint probe are restored, retaining their existing authority checks, authentication, cookie, redirect, and WebSocket behavior; the reviewed transport regressions are removed rather than reimplemented.

## User Impact

Users can onboard and reconnect to Gateway endpoints behind hostname-matched HTTPS proxies without requiring a separate frontend port or another TLS setting.

## Evidence

- Physical iPhone on iOS 26.6.1: the author tested the revised local app and confirmed QR onboarding and reconnect after relaunch, against the existing proxy configuration.
- Native before/after proof on macOS and an iOS 26.5 simulator, using the original URLSession pinning session against the same live endpoint (hostname redacted):

  | Input | Result |
  | --- | --- |
  | Explicit `wss://gateway.example:443/` | HTTP 404; no TLS validation failure |
  | Synthetic setup code decoded through the revised URL builder | Stored port remains 443; URL omits the port; HTTP 101 and first WebSocket message received |
  | Reconnect through the same session using the revised URL | HTTP 101 and first WebSocket message received |

  The diagnostic sent no Gateway authentication payload and did not log server message contents.
- Independent IPv4 curl matrix: `Host: gateway.example` returned HTTP 200 with or without DNS-name SNI; `Host: gateway.example:443` returned HTTP 404 with or without DNS-name SNI. Certificate verification was disabled only for the unauthenticated IP-URL/no-SNI diagnostic cases.
- Regression tests demonstrated default-port failures against the original URL builder. After the fix, 73 tests across `DeepLinksSecurityTests`, `GatewayTLSPinningTests`, and `GatewayCustomHeadersTests` passed, including default/non-default ports, IPv6, retained endpoint ports, and encoded paths.
- `pnpm native:i18n:verify`: passed, with no inventory changes needed after removing the custom transport.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Repository `check:changed` for the two-file candidate passed, including app SwiftLint, macOS tooling/process suites, and native schema guards; focused Swift suites and production SwiftLint were rerun after retaining explicit cleartext port 80.
- Follow-up macOS CI repair updates the primary Gateway replacement test to distinguish a default-port setup link from a profile's supplied explicit port, retaining all credential retirement assertions. Changed-file checks and fresh isolated autoreview, including secret scanning, passed with no P0/P1 findings.
- Required `openclaw/ci-gate` passed on 7dec4a7aa5b6c44e17af7bd8b1f0c7fa73b8930d, including successful `macos-swift (tests)`, `ios-build (smoke)`, and `android-test-third-party` checks ([CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34441657776)). The earlier macOS URL assertions are repaired. The earlier Android failure did not reproduce: its exact test and all eight tests in `SettingsScreensContrastTest` passed locally, and fresh CI passed without Android changes.

The native diagnostic proves handshake and reconnect, not a full authenticated app session; physical-device onboarding and relaunch reconnect were separately confirmed by the author. Earlier custom-transport test counts and build evidence have been superseded by this narrower implementation.


## Maintainer review — November 27

Reviewed the unchanged published head `e3cee63d635abb4fd804d4a7ba6c2b762f4f6921` before the follow-up test consolidation. The production change only omits the serialized WSS default port; endpoint storage, identity, explicit WS ports, TLS pins, credentials, and encoded path bytes retain their existing owners. The current mainline DeepLinks source and shared test suite match the PR fork base byte-for-byte. Current iOS and macOS consumers were also inspected.

The [exact-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41007997952) succeeded on October 30, including iOS screenshots, Android lanes, native i18n, and the required CI gate. This is retained evidence, not a new runtime test. The device/proxy and 73-test results above remain attributed to their original author and revisions.

Local ClawSweeper completed the three-file, five-commit range from `3cd0dd6380a1a1586c6db4574b6fc231eb3367df` to the published head with no findings. An independent source review likewise found no change to the security boundaries. No fork code or tests were executed on the operator host.

Closes #192268

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Embedded agent turns omit configured MCP tools without a turn warning when an OAuth server has no saved tokens.

## User Impact

User impact: Operators receive a warning with the server name and authorization guidance on each affected embedded turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

Embedded turn preparation discards the catalog diagnostics the MCP runtime keeps, so a turn whose OAuth server has no saved token runs without that server's tools and says nothing. Log those diagnostics as warnings during turn preparation, once per affected server on every turn. Turns keep their other MCP tools and still complete. prs.title: fix: show how to reload automation events
prs.body:
Related: #202273 changes the trigger setup layout; this PR addresses the catalog error itself.

## What Problem This Solves

When the Control UI can’t load events for the selected MCP server, the alert shows the Gateway’s explanation but doesn’t name the button that retries the load.

## User Impact

- Before (simulated Gateway failure): “Event catalog is temporarily unavailable”
- After: “Couldn’t load events. Try Refresh events and status. Details: Event catalog is temporarily unavailable”

**Refresh events and status** asks for events from the same server again. It doesn’t save or change the automation. If refreshing doesn’t help, the original diagnostic is still visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

The event picker already owns the read and its refresh action. Add guidance only to the alert shown for a catalog response marked `UNAVAILABLE`; preserve other error text, Gateway responses, permissions, retries, and scheduling. No new control or retry logic.

**Skill in practice:** Name the failed action in the reader’s words, use the exact label of the recovery control they can already see, and keep the original reason when they may need it next.

## Evidence

- In connected Chromium on `9d39d4d8f535e`, the user could recover with the existing button, but the alert failed the new copy assertion. On the patch, the same control made a new request for `deployments`, cleared the alert, and let the user select `deployment.changed` without any create or update request. The Gateway responses were simulated; this does not test a live MCP outage.
- All three event source readiness browser tests and six focused event source tests passed. UI test type shards, i18n, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The managed session did not expose a bound local reviewer; independent exact-head review remains a landing gate.

prs.title: fix: keep overlapping meeting speech in conversation order
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When two people overlap in a meeting, a short reply can finish transcription before the question that prompted it. The saved notes, transcript reader, and Markdown download could all show the reply first.

## User Impact

Meeting notes and the Meetings transcript tab show speech in the order it began when the source supplies timestamps with a time zone. New Markdown downloads use that order for the full transcript. Previously saved notes can be regenerated from the stored utterances. Raw JSONL and incremental API reads keep their append sequence.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each audio stream already supplies its speech start time. The shared presentation code now orders turns after resolving speaker identities. Equal starts keep their recorded order. A turn without a usable absolute time stays between the same groups of speech.

## Evidence

The original two-speaker call exposed six backward jumps in the stored transcript. All examples below use synthetic speech.

- The new SQLite summary and Meetings UI cases both failed on the parent commit. The summary showed the reply before the question, and the UI placed a late transcription after all six earlier pages.
- All 104 tests passed on `85d5d5eb5d4d` across five backend/Gateway files and two Meetings UI files. The speech-order check also passed in UTC and Asia/Singapore.
- Calling the registered Gateway handlers against an isolated SQLite archive produced this Markdown order: `Sam (2): Question`, `Sam: Reply`, `Sam: Overlapping reply`. The unpaged reader returned sequences `[1, 0, 2]`. Cursor pages and JSONL returned `0, 1, 2`.
- After a late append, the mounted Meetings page placed the transcription between utterances 1 and 2 across page boundaries. This exercised the real UI component in jsdom with synthetic RPC pages.
- Local ClawSweeper and independent code review found no actionable code defects. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45913631625).

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI still uses uirouter 0.1.2 and misses the published fixes for overlapping navigation loads, cache revalidation, and router restarts.

## User Impact

Control UI builds include uirouter 0.1.3's navigation and cache lifecycle fixes, including preserving the latest joined location and avoiding stale component state after a restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pin the [reviewed 0.1.3 release](https://github.com/openclaw/uirouter/releases/tag/v0.1.3) and regenerate the pnpm lockfile. Add a release-age exception for exactly `@openclaw/uirouter@0.1.3`, with removal due after `2026-12-02T06:20:29.322Z`, seven days after npm publication. The strict seven-day policy continues to apply to other versions.

## Evidence

- On the original candidate, `pnpm install --lockfile-only` and normal `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passed with pnpm 12.15.0 and Node 26.12.1, including strict supply-chain policy verification. The generated lockfile changes only uirouter.
- The UI resolves version 0.1.3; its `dist/index.js` SHA256 is `e8cf4c26d1ea8e5d996c3323e646c7de8449879104402ec7a10978f0f24292fe`, matching the verified published package and the earlier consumer qualification.

prs.title: improve: use less memory when measuring session disk usage
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The first time OpenClaw measures a session store against its disk budget, the packaged background worker loads two broad filesystem library entry points. This consumes extra memory before the scan can return. The worker was visible in low-memory Gateway profiles. [Original report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/181432)

## User Impact

On Linux x64 with one pinned CPU, a fresh packaged process used 22.6 MiB less proportional memory after its first scan of one store, and 31.8 MiB less when it had to identify which sibling databases belonged to the store. Median first-scan time fell from 141 to 53 ms and from 281 to 169 ms respectively. These figures cover the scan process and its worker together. The full ARM64 Gateway memory limit remains a separate investigation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The disk-budget worker now uses the build's existing per-worker rule to bundle the filesystem functions it imports. This removes the eager external imports of `@openclaw/fs-safe/advanced` and `@openclaw/fs-safe/path` and preserves the installed package as the owner of native assets. The change adds one production line. Its private build output grew the compressed release archive by 148,582 bytes (0.12%).

## Evidence

[Linux x64 Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45911635605) compared signed `9c73897c1eb1` with its parent `993d0b77df4f`. Both release tarballs were built and verified, then extracted and exercised through their actual worker pools. Cold and initial warm results used four counterbalanced fresh processes per arm and fixture on Node 24.22.1.

| Median per fresh process | One store, before → after | Sibling stores, before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| PSS after first scan, MiB | 184.39 → 161.74 | 216.28 → 184.52 |
| RSS after first scan, MiB | 189.61 → 166.94 | 221.47 → 189.72 |
| First scan, ms | 141.03 → 53.22 | 281.03 → 169.13 |
| Initial warm CPU per scan, µs | 709.9 → 740.5 | 1805.6 → 1829.4 |
| Initial warm p95, ms | 1.165 → 1.155 | 2.828 → 3.107 |

All archive changes outside the disk-budget worker's private chunks were build identity, build-input fingerprints or their derived UI and file inventories.

The initial sibling-store p95 rose 0.279 ms across all four pairs (+8.3% to +14.8%). A second crossover used 768 warmup scans followed by 720 measured scans per process, in the same counterbalanced order. With 24 transcripts, p95 rose 0.128 ms (3.208 → 3.336; three of four pairs rose), CPU fell 3.2%, and p99 fell from 7.227 to 6.621 ms. With 240 transcripts, every pair improved on p95 (7.871 → 6.488 ms median), CPU fell 6.1%, and p99 fell from 26.296 to 10.837 ms. End-of-run PSS fell 53.38 MiB on the smaller sibling fixture and rose 0.93 MiB on the larger one.

Both arms counted the same physical artifacts and WAL bytes, excluded a foreign sibling and retired their worker. A relocated Bun 1.4.4 process in required-native mode deduplicated symlinked database and WAL paths, excluded SHM and returned the exact same 30,165 total and 24,752 WAL bytes on both arms. All 50 targeted configuration, physical usage and disk-budget tests passed. The new bundle-selection assertion failed on the stock rule.

prs.title: fix: use less memory for installed plugins with native files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After an installed plugin has used a native file, its saved receipt includes facts about the file and its companions. The Gateway copied that entire member list a second time whenever it created a plugin metadata view, even if the operator had disabled the plugin. @jaxonparrott observed repeated members from a disabled plugin in a long-running Gateway heap. Refs https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/198802.

## User Impact

Metadata views use less heap when installed plugins have persisted native-file receipts. Disabling a plugin continues to preserve its installation record. Re-enabling it can reuse the existing native bytes and fill in any missing companion digests.

## Why This Change Was Made

An immutable installed index already owns the complete member list. The native admission cache now shares it until a file identity or digest changes. Overlapping captures retain their namespace identities, worker transfers preserve the distinction between shared index members and live receipts, and mutable input keeps an independent copy.

## Evidence

On Linux x64 with Node 24.22.1, a synthetic managed plugin with 768 companion files produced a genuine SQLite receipt with 774 member records. A fresh Gateway metadata view after disablement created 774 additional member objects on stock and zero with the change. The never-enabled control had no receipt. Across 12 fresh cache owners sharing the same installed index, forced-GC heap growth averaged 411,910 → 3,072 bytes per disabled view and 409,499 → 1,024 bytes per enabled view before inspection. The same allocation pattern reproduced under Bun 1.4.4.

The fixture exercised an unrelated worker, a warm native symlink capture, an enabled worker filling a missing companion digest, and native namespace recapture. The original receipt stayed intact. All 48 focused tests passed under Node 24.22.1, along with formatting, lint, the plugin test typecheck, and production typechecking. Local autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings on the signed change. Whether this reduces the reporter’s 80–110 MB/hour production growth still needs a field retest.

prs.title: fix(agents): honor explicit agentId when compacting global sessions
prs.body:
Closes #145217

## What Problem This Solves

In a multi-agent setup with `agents.ownership: "explicit"`, compacting a session stored under the literal `"global"` key into a summary fails with `"Multiple agents are configured, but session agent resolution has no explicit owner"` even when the request supplies or routes to the owning agent (`openclaw sessions compact "global" --agent <id>`, Gateway `sessions.compact` with `{ key: "global", agentId }`, or `/compact` on an agent-selected `"global"` session). Operators whose `"global"` session fills its context window cannot reclaim context budget by summarizing the existing conversation (leaving line-count truncation via `--max-lines`, which permanently drops older transcript lines without a summary, or `/reset`, which discards the conversation history).

## User Impact

Passing an explicit `agentId` (`--agent <id>` or `sessions.compact` `{ key: "global", agentId }`) now compacts literal `"global"` sessions in explicit multi-agent setups, resolves that agent's configured model fallback chain, and persists the compaction summary to the agent's SQLite transcript.

No user action, config change, or database migration is required, and this one-line fix in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.ts` is cleanly reversible. Strict shared ownership checks in `src/agents/agent-scope.ts`, `src/agents/agent-scope-config.ts`, and `src/gateway/session-request-agent.ts` remain unchanged (requests for a literal `"global"` key without an `agentId` in an explicit multi-agent setup still fail closed with `"no explicit owner"` when no configured compatibility or fixed-store ownership source identifies the session's agent), existing `"global"` session rows stay in place as valid per-agent entries under `session.scope: "global"`, and `docs/cli/sessions.md` / `docs/concepts/session.md` already document that `global` keys require the owning `agentId` (`Docs: none`).

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway `sessions.compact` admission, store resolution, queueing, and `compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirect` already validate and carry `params.agentId`, but `resolveCompactionFallbacksOverride(params)` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.ts` called `resolveRunModelFallbacksOverride` with only `{ cfg: params.config, sessionKey: params.sessionKey }`, omitting `params.agentId`. When `sessionKey` is the unprefixed literal `"global"` in an `agents.ownership: "explicit"` multi-agent fleet, `resolveRunModelFallbacksOverride` falls back to key-only strict ownership resolution and throws `"no explicit owner"` during runtime candidate preparation before summarization runs.

Forwarding `{ cfg: params.config, agentId: params.agentId, sessionKey: params.sessionKey }` matches normal turn fallback resolution in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/runtime-resolution.ts`. `modelSelectionLocked`, explicit `modelFallbacksOverride`, and `agents.defaults.compaction.model` retain their existing precedence, and `sandboxSessionKey` / `sandboxAgentId` handling is intentionally left unchanged so unprefixed or differently prefixed sandbox keys cannot drop or override session ownership.

Context on prior PRs: open PR #145357 (last author commit on `2026-10-05` UTC; review comments through `2026-11-17` UTC reported merge conflicts with `main`) and closed unmerged PR #146918 also targeted #145217. This PR applies the one-line `agentId: params.agentId` forward in place in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.ts` on current `main` with paired before-fix and after-fix runner and Gateway `sessions.compact` persistence regressions, leaving merge selection to maintainers.

## Evidence

Validated against base `1ea3d5f4941d` (`1ea3d5f4941d5dcfe4ec34cba20c4696f6c05d5b`) and candidate `e1d6d6b05856`:

- **Standalone isolated Gateway & shipped CLI proof (`openclaw gateway run` + `openclaw sessions compact`, two separate explicit `pnpm build:runtime` builds in the same isolated build environment):**
  - **Before-fix (`1ea3d5f4941d`, `build_fp=6ca8b586afd52155aa41c8f66e6763584dc597871505e04185a66db5e7a6649a`):** Against an isolated `openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --tailscale off --port "<gateway-port>"` instance configured with `agents.ownership: "explicit"` (`main` and `work` agents, `session.scope: "global"`) and a pre-seeded literal `"global"` session in `main`'s isolated SQLite store, running shipped CLI `openclaw sessions compact "global" --agent main --timeout 30000 --json` exited `1` with `{"ok":false,"key":"global","compacted":false,"reason":"Multiple agents are configured, but session agent resolution has no explicit owner. Pass an agentId, an agent-scoped session key, or a prepared fallbackAgentId."}` (SQLite `MAIN_COMPACTION_COUNT=0`, `COMPACTION_EVENT_COUNT=0`, `WORK_DB_CLEAN=true`, `MOCK_MODELS=none`).
  - **After-fix (`e1d6d6b05856`, `build_fp=afd2e717ecb320c0f68d69a60cc6cdefe4e373172f31b86b4cfbfdb93a7acabd`, patch SHA-256 `75055e7e4224...`):** Against a fresh isolated state directory running standalone `openclaw gateway run` and a local loopback HTTP `/v1/responses` SSE responder (primary `mock-openai/gpt-primary` returning HTTP `429 rate_limit_exceeded` and `main`'s fallback `mock-openai/gpt-fallback` returning `GLOBAL_EXPLICIT_AGENT_LIVE_COMPACTION_SUMMARY`):
    1. **Negative control (omitting `--agent`):** `openclaw sessions compact "global" --timeout 30000 --json` still exited `1` fail-closed (`"Multiple agents are configured, but session key \"global\" has no explicit owner. Pass agentId or use an agent-prefixed session key."`, `NEG_NO_AGENT_REJECTED=true`).
    2. **Positive verification (explicit `--agent main`):** `openclaw sessions compact "global" --agent main --timeout 30000 --json` succeeded (`{"ok": true, "key": "global", "compacted": true, ...}`), switched from `gpt-primary` (`429`) to `main`'s `gpt-fallback` (`MOCK_MODELS=gpt-primary,gpt-fallback`; `0` requests to `gpt-default-fallback`), and after clean Gateway shutdown, read-only SQLite inspection confirmed `main`'s store had `MAIN_COMPACTION_COUNT=1`, `COMPACTION_EVENT_COUNT=1`, and `PERSISTED_SUMMARY_MATCH=GLOBAL_EXPLICIT_AGENT_LIVE_COMPACTION_SUMMARY`, while `work`'s store had no session or transcript rows (`WORK_DB_CLEAN=true`).

Pass an agentId, an agent-scoped session key, or a prepared fallbackAgentId."}`.
  - **After-fix (`e1d6d6b05856`):** `19 passed (19)` (`Duration 63.63s` across the existing 19-case runner suite, command wall time `99275ms` including `30539ms` initial worker compiler cache preparation; new case `2456ms`), confirming `main`'s per-agent `fixture/fallback-model` route, exclusion of `fixture/default-fallback`, persisted `"Fallback route summary."`, and unchanged `/no explicit owner/` rejection when `resolveRunModelFallbacksOverride` is called without `agentId`. Exercising the full embedded compaction runner composition here is necessary because unit-testing the shared fallback resolver directly cannot catch `compact.ts` omitting `params.agentId`, while the Gateway e2e test's single-model summary response does not isolate primary-refusal fallback selection across per-agent vs. default fallback chains.
- **Gateway WebSocket RPC regression (`src/gateway/gateway.compaction-hot-reload.e2e.test.ts`):**

Pass an agentId, an agent-scoped session key, or a prepared fallbackAgentId."}`.
  - **After-fix (`e1d6d6b05856`):** `2 passed (2)` (`Duration 31.44s`, new case `5577ms`; command wall time `246442ms` including `3m 26.7s` `[build-all]` E2E runtime preparation), exercising a live in-process Gateway WebSocket server (`startGatewayWithClient`) + loopback `/v1/responses` SSE responder in an explicit `main`/`work` fleet: `{ key: "global" }` without `agentId` is rejected with `no explicit owner` (`compactionCount === 0`), while `{ key: "global", agentId: "main" }` returns `{ ok: true, key: "global", compacted: true }`, increments `compactionCount` to `1`, and persists the `compaction` event (`GLOBAL_EXPLICIT_AGENT_COMPACTION_SUMMARY`) in SQLite.
- **Adjacent regressions & targeted gates (`e1d6d6b05856`):** `src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts` (`43 passed`, `Duration 8.80s`, wall `13459ms`), `src/gateway/server.sessions.list-changed.test.ts` (`11 passed`, `Duration 55.07s`, wall `59750ms`), `pnpm format:check` (3 files, `18ms`), `oxlint` (3 files, `0` warnings / `0` errors, `20.3s`), `pnpm lint:tmp:tsgo-core-boundary`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test` (`29/29` shards), `check:no-conflict-markers`, `check:coercion-helpers`, `check:line-cap-ratchet`, `check:max-lines-ratchet`, `check:test-lines-ratchet` (`Net test lines: +221; allowance: 400; allocation credit: 0`), `check:assertion-safety`, `check:test-timeout-race-ratchet`, `check:test-mock-exports`, and `git diff --check` all exited `0`. Aggregate `pnpm check:changed --base 1ea3d5f4941d5dcfe4ec34cba20c4696f6c05d5b` exited `1` with `3` step failures unrelated to our diff: `changelog attributions` on `CHANGELOG/2026.11.10.md:8130` (offending attribution line already present in clean base `1ea3d5f4941d`, file untouched by this PR) plus `format changed files` and `lint core changed files` failing at tool resolution because `OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH=/dev/null` is non-executable in this isolated runner (the 3 touched files pass Node `pnpm format:check` and `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` directly above).
- CI: runs after maintainer approval

Local review: local ClawSweeper x3 on 1ea3d5f4941d..e1d6d6b05856: no actionable findings.

**Not covered:**
- Direct calls to an external billed cloud LLM API endpoint were not run: the standalone running `openclaw gateway run` + shipped `openclaw sessions compact` CLI proof used a local loopback HTTP `/v1/responses` SSE responder for primary `429` rejection and fallback summary streaming (and the Vitest suites likewise used local in-process/loopback model fixtures); by source inspection, `compact.ts` resolves the `agentId` fallback chain before issuing outbound model HTTP requests, so equivalence with external cloud endpoints beyond loopback transport is inferred rather than live-tested.

prs.title: fix(discord): keep the selected servers and channels during setup
prs.body:
## Summary

The Discord setup wizard now saves new server and channel selections by numeric ID and shows which Discord server and channel each entry matched.

## What Problem This Solves

When more than one server matched a name, setup could pick the first server. A failed lookup could also discard other successful lookups, switch an existing access policy, or leave a new allowlist empty without telling the operator. Re-selecting a configured channel could also replace its settings.

## User Impact

Enter a server name, `Server/#channel`, or `#channel` during guided setup. If the server cannot be identified uniquely, enter `guild:<id>` to choose it. The wizard retains the requested channel while selecting the server. A bare number still identifies a channel. Each unsuccessful entry can be retried or explicitly skipped, and the summary counts actual additions. If an entry would override an existing name, wildcard, or inherited channel rule, setup explains how to keep or edit that rule. The empty-allowlist warning also applies when the operator skips access configuration. Declining to finish cancels fresh setup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Discord setup hook in `extensions/discord/src/setup-guild-access.ts`, registered by `setup-core.ts`, owns the interactive decision and writes the policy and selected entries together. It keeps existing guild and channel records when adding entries. The wizard reuses the Discord allowlist input parser and REST operations, and treats a full server-list page as inconclusive for name matching. The wizard checks existing rules before writing a more specific ID. Repairing previously saved configurations belongs to the separate Doctor change in #205558.

## Evidence of Fix

| Wizard input or condition | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Duplicate server name, server/channel pair, or channel across servers | On the base revision, declining the edit changed a disabled policy to allowlist. The change preserves the policy and existing restrictions, or writes only the ID selected on retry. |
| Mixed existing, new and skipped entries | The base revision overwrote settings on the selected channel. The new flow retained its disabled flag and mention rule and counted only the new selection. |
| Full guild page, failed lookup, unavailable token reference | The wizard requests a server ID when uniqueness is uncertain, keeps successes from the same edit, and can retry with a lookup credential while preserving the configured reference. |
| Existing name, wildcard or thread-parent rule | Six regression cases failed on the first PR commit. The corrected wizard preserves the prior policy and rule and counts the selection as skipped. |
| Fresh empty allowlist | Two regression cases failed on the first PR commit. Skipping access configuration now shows the warning, and declining to finish cancels fresh setup. |
| Interactive CLI, isolated config and local Discord REST fixture | `pnpm openclaw channels add discord` reported two additions and one skip. The saved file contained the two selected numeric guild/channel pairs. A follow-up CLI run skipped an entry covered by a disabled, name-keyed channel rule and kept the original rule and its guild user restriction. |
| Upgrade from the npm release 2026.11.10 to head `9f17c4a3f4d` | The release wrote and validated the profile. The new CLI read the same file, added the two chosen numeric pairs, and preserved the existing guild sender restriction and disabled name-keyed channel exactly. The final file passed validation. |

[Redacted terminal captures and before/after configuration evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205554#issuecomment-7174672427). Discord responses in this run came from a local fixture.

## Testing

Ran `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/{setup-surface,resolve-channels,resolve-users,setup-adapter,setup-account-state}.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. All 49 tests passed. The eight new review cases failed on the previous PR commit and passed with the correction. The targeted TypeScript, lint and format checks and the CLI build passed. Independent review identified the rule-precedence and empty-setup cases above and verified their corrections. Discord responses in the regression tests came from fixtures. Live Discord validation was unavailable because the shared QA bot lease could not be acquired.

prs.title: fix: preserve Doctor failures during container shutdown
prs.body:
Closes #205095

## What Problem This Solves

When Doctor refuses to repair a configuration, it prints the reason and exits 1. If SIGTERM arrives while it finishes writing that output, both the standalone command and the image entrypoint can instead exit 143. That hides the configuration failure from the service supervisor.

## User Impact

A diagnosed repair failure now exits 1 even when shutdown overlaps it. A SIGTERM that interrupts activation before Doctor diagnoses the configuration still exits 143.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor records its refusal in the one-shot exit handler, which owns signal cleanup as well as output draining. The activation entrypoint preserves an independent failure from its Doctor child and still translates a forwarded signal back to the original signal status when appropriate.

## Evidence

I ran the built CLI and the shipped image entrypoint as separate processes in isolated Linux PID and network namespaces with a read-only configuration containing the retired `agents.list` key. These runs exercised the entrypoint script directly, without a Docker daemon.

| Invocation and signal timing | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`, SIGTERM after the final validation diagnostic | 143 | 1 |
| Entrypoint starting the gateway, same diagnostic and signal | 143 | 1 |
| Entrypoint starting the gateway, no signal | 1 | 1 |

The fixed entrypoint also exited 143 when interrupted during archive preparation, before final validation. The new regressions failed on the original implementation. The entrypoint and CLI tests cover a failure reported on either side of signal cleanup, plus ordinary interruption and forwarded signals.

All 87 focused tests passed, along with the runtime build, core and test type checks, formatting, scoped lint, and local review.

### Captured process output

The following excerpts are from the terminal runs above. The harness watches the child’s output, sends SIGTERM on the diagnostic line shown, and prints the child’s actual exit status after waiting for it. Only matching lines are shown. The test configuration is synthetic.

`node /app/openclaw.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive`

```text
base 15ff7847
Doctor: Final config validation
- agents.list moved to keyed agents.entries. Run "openclaw doctor --fix".
fixture direct term saw validation True sent True exit 143
PR 30eab4f4
Doctor: Final config validation
- agents.list moved to keyed agents.entries. Run "openclaw doctor --fix".
fixture direct term saw validation True sent True exit 1
```

`node /app/docker-entrypoint.mjs node /app/openclaw.mjs gateway`

```text
base 15ff7847
Doctor: Final config validation
- agents.list moved to keyed agents.entries. Run "openclaw doctor --fix".
fixture activation term saw validation True sent True exit 143
PR 30eab4f4
Doctor: Final config validation
- agents.list moved to keyed agents.entries. Run "openclaw doctor --fix".
fixture activation term saw validation True sent True exit 1
```

Control runs on the PR head, using the same entrypoint command:

```text
fixture activation early saw validation False sent True exit 143
fixture activation control saw validation True sent False exit 1
```

prs.title: fix: keep package updates going when backup or indexing tools touch file attributes
prs.body:
Related: #200756

## What Problem This Solves

An `openclaw update` that goes through the in-place package updater refuses to replace the package with `Baseline package scan failed | Package rollback tree changed during verification` when another program changes only file metadata under the installed package while the update scans it. Backup, sync, indexing and antivirus tools do this: on Windows, clearing the archive bit or setting the not-indexed flag; on Linux, a `chmod` to the same mode or an added hard link; on macOS, extended attributes. Not one byte changes, but the update stops and the user stays on the old version.

## User Impact

The update continues when the scan's final re-check finds an entry whose type, mode, owner, size, mtime and contents are unchanged and only the change time or link count moved. It reports a warning naming the first entries and the fields that changed. Every other change is still refused as before: different bytes (even with times restored), a changed mode, a file replaced by a symlink or directory, an entry added or removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The final sweep of a package scan (added in #136329) compares each entry's full stat with what it saw at the start, including `ctimeNs` and `nlink`. Its job is to make sure the digest describes the tree that becomes the rollback copy: a writer that restores mtime after writing still moves the change time, which userspace cannot set. Comparing the change time detects that a change might have happened; it does not show that bytes changed. The scan's digest itself never includes `ctimeNs` or `nlink` (see the existing comment on npm's hidden-hardlink and chmod churn), so the decision belongs to the bytes the digest records.

So when only `ctimeNs`/`nlink` differ, the sweep re-reads that entry, after all strict refusals and in traversal order: a file is re-hashed and compared with the recorded SHA-256, a symlink's target is re-read, a directory's entry names are re-listed. A torn read (a write during hashing) fails this comparison. Only drifted entries are re-read; if an indexer touched every entry, the cost is one more pass over the tree's bytes under the same deadline, and a timeout keeps the existing resource-error fallback (directory identity plus version, with its warning). Legacy-encoded digests seal change times, so they stay strict.

Two checks that follow the sweep needed the same rule, found by the first green cell (below): the hasher's within-read stat checks (the sweep always re-checks against the scan's first stat, so they defer to it) and the swap's permission repair, which `fchmod`s the verified inode and refused on the same metadata drift, failing the update and its rollback.

The sweep and stat policy moved into `src/infra/package-update-integrity-drift.ts` because `package-update-integrity.ts` is at its line cap. The swap passes its warnings list to the baseline reader. No config, schema, protocol or dependency change.

## Update behavior

The installed version runs this check: the package swap belongs to the updater that is already installed, and a newer target cannot change it.

- On `main`, owned installs update through `src/update/`, which never runs this scan. The in-place updater still serves the routes listed in `src/cli/update-cli/AGENTS.md`: node-only package installs, `--tag main`, channel switches, immutable installs and `update repair`. The cells below use the node-only route.
- Every published release up to 2026.11.10 runs the old check on its next update; so does `release/2026.11.11`, which has no `src/update/` at all, so every package update it drives reaches this scan. An installation is protected from the first release that contains this fix, on the update after it is installed.
- `release/2026.12.1` carries code identical to `main` here. Backport notes are with the coordinator; no release-branch PR.

## Evidence

Linux cells: Debian 13 container with systemd, npm global install under a user prefix, node service installed with no Gateway (the route on `main` that still reaches the in-place updater). Each cell installs the driver pack, stops the node service as the updater requires, runs `openclaw update --tag <target pack> --yes --json`, then starts the node service. Packs are local builds under unpublished versions. Metadata injection runs once a second over 228 `dist/*.js` files from the start of the update until it exits.

Cells ran on `a6c67ac5294`. Later commits on this branch are test-only (two refusal assertions made independent of Bun's read order and inode reuse) plus merges of `main` whose update-path changes are limited to Git runtime, run admission and status reads (#205994, #206189), not the package scan or swap, so the cells were not repeated.

Driver is the installed version that performs the scan; target is what it installs. Time not serving: the node service is stopped by the operator for every cell (the updater refuses while it holds the database), so the cells report update wall time and disk instead. **Tests** (red on the base production code, green on head):

- `src/infra/package-update-integrity.test.ts`: accepts same-mode `chmod`, an extra hard link and a directory `chmod` at the final sweep with an identical digest and one warning; accepts drift that lands while the worker hashes the file; refuses same-size content with mtime restored (`contents changed`), the executable bit, symlink and directory substitution, a removed entry, and an added entry with the directory's times restored. On base, the 4 accept cases fail and the content case refuses without naming the content.
- `src/infra/package-update-swap.integrity.test.ts`: the swap commits over baseline drift and reports the warning; a rollback restores 1.0.0; a same-size change to the retained bytes after the scan, times restored, is refused at rollback (`retained package tree changed`). This is how the window between the re-read and the swap is closed: the retained copy is verified against the recorded digest before it is restored.
- `src/infra/package-update-activation-permissions.test.ts`: permission repair tightens the mode after a same-mode `chmod` or an added hard link, and still refuses appended bytes. On base the two accept cases fail.

**Files audited:** the three test files above in full; `package-update-integrity-hasher.test.ts` (unchanged; its "file changed since its admitted stat" case appends bytes, still refused). Nothing removed.

prs.title: fix(gateway): exclude browser UI pairings from silent-prune clustering
prs.body:
Related to #203145

## What Problem This Solves

Pairing a second Control UI browser profile silently deletes the first profile's device pairing. The silent-pairing prune worker clusters records by `clientId + clientMode + displayName`, but browser UI clients keep a durable per-profile device identity (a localStorage keypair), so two profiles are two distinct devices that merely share client metadata. Once the older pairing ages past the 60s grace window and its socket is closed, the next profile's silent pairing prunes it; the old profile then fails closed and its device-bound automations stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

`silentPairingClusterKey` in `src/infra/device-pairing-core.kernel.ts` assumed every silent pairing came from an ephemeral state dir that mints a fresh keypair per run. That holds for CLI/node clients, not for browser UI clients whose device ids are stable per profile. The fix excludes `openclaw-control-ui`, `webchat-ui`, and `openclaw-browser-copilot` (canonicalized with the existing `normalizeGatewayClientName`) from clustering as both anchor and victim, matching the pairing docs' "remembered until revoked or explicitly removed" contract for durable browser identities. CLI/node temp-dir dedup, manual/trusted-cidr exclusions, the recent-approval grace, and connected-device protection are unchanged.

Scope note: this issue also carries `needs-product-decision` / `needs-security-review` labels for the broader account-scoped pairing model. This PR deliberately does not redesign authorization or scope ownership; it only stops the cleanup worker from deleting distinct durable browser identities — the data-loss symptom reported here. Flagging for maintainer and security review accordingly.

## User Impact

Multiple browser profiles (or Control UI + WebChat) on one gateway keep their pairings and device-bound automations across reconnects. No config change. Existing CLI/node ephemeral-state cleanup behavior is preserved.

## Evidence

Real before/after against a live gateway run from this branch's TS source (isolated dev state dir, token auth, loopback). Two WS clients with distinct ed25519 device identities and identical `clientId=openclaw-control-ui` / `mode=ui` / displayName: A pairs (silent-approved), disconnects, 65s elapse (> 60s grace), then B pairs:

| Run | Code | A present after B pairs | prune log |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | origin/main | **false** (A deleted) | `device pairing pruned superseded silent pairing ... prunedCount=1` |
| after | this branch | **true** (A and B both kept) | none |

Commands (cwd = checkout):

```
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway --force
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs pair-prune-proof.mts --token <token> --port 19001 --label before
```

Before output: `after B pairing: A present=false B present=true`, and the gateway log shows `pruned deviceId=3a05371b... approvedVia=silent` at the second B connected. After output: `after B pairing: A present=true B present=true`, zero prune log lines.

Committed regressions in `src/infra/device-pairing-prune.test.ts`: distinct profiles sharing client metadata survive for all three browser client ids (parameterized), plus a case variant where the anchor carries the mixed-case id — the exclusion must normalize the stored clientId before its early return, so on base the anchor clusters with its canonical-id sibling and prunes it. Red/green on the same file, swapping only `device-pairing-core.kernel.ts`:

```
git checkout origin/main -- src/infra/device-pairing-core.kernel.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/device-pairing-prune.test.ts
# 4 failed | 11 passed — all 4 new browser-identity cases fail on base
git checkout HEAD -- src/infra/device-pairing-core.kernel.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/device-pairing-prune.test.ts
# 15 passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/device-pairing-prune.test.ts
# 3 passed — existing gateway prune guards unchanged
node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/infra/device-pairing-core.kernel.ts src/infra/device-pairing-prune.test.ts
# 0 warnings, 0 errors; oxfmt --check clean
```


### Upgrade & data-model compatibility proof (stable v2026.11.10 → candidate)

The run above exercised isolated fresh state only. This run proves that a browser pairing + token created on released stable carries forward and keeps working on the candidate, and that the fix holds on upgraded state. Same isolated state dir across the stable→candidate boundary; distinct ports; throwaway proof token; loopback bind; production `~/.openclaw` untouched.

Binaries — both self-report version `2026.11.10`, distinguished by commit:
- **stable** (bug present): `OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f)`, installed via `npm install openclaw@2026.11.10`
- **candidate** (this branch, fix present): `OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (363ed24)`, built via `pnpm build cliStartup` → `node openclaw.mjs`

Driver: `contributions/pr-203145-evidence/upgrade-proof.mts` (not committed). Profile A's ed25519 keypair is persisted across the boundary to model a browser profile's durable localStorage identity; B gets a fresh keypair. Both share `clientId=openclaw-control-ui`, `mode=ui`, and displayName — the metadata cluster condition.

| Phase | Binary | State dir | Action | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| stable baseline | stable `6ea542f` | fresh BASE | A pairs → disconnect → 65s → B pairs | **A pruned**: `aCountAfterB=0`; gateway log `device pairing pruned superseded silent pairing device=562bc690…` — bug reproduced on released stable |
| stable seed | stable `6ea542f` | fresh UPG | A pairs (keypair persisted) | A silent-approved, listed `count=1` — pre-upgrade state carried into the candidate |
| **upgrade** | **candidate `363ed24`** | **same UPG, not wiped** | load state → reconnect A → disconnect → 65s → B pairs → reconnect A | **A retained end-to-end** (see below) |

Upgrade-phase data points (`proof-upgrade.txt`, A deviceId `f1ed957d…`):
- `aCountAtCandidateStartup: 1` — the pairing written by stable loads on the candidate (data-model compatibility: existing stored data still loads)
- `aAuthenticatedAtStartup: true` — A's retained pairing + token authenticates immediately after the upgrade
- `aCountAfterB: 1`, `bCountAfterB: 1` — after the 60s grace window, pairing B does **not** prune A on upgraded state (the fix)
- `aAuthenticatedAfterB: true`, `aCountAfterBReconnect: 1` — the original profile still authenticates after the second profile paired

Contrast: stable prunes A (1 `pruned superseded silent pairing` log line, baseline `aPruned=true`); candidate retains A (0 prune log lines, `aSurvivedUpgradeAndSecondPairing=true`). Same store, same A identity across the boundary — only the binary changed.
