prs.title: fix: keep a Codex chat on one thread when automation permissions differ between its turns
prs.body:
Related: #148329, #165278, #178498. Applies the session-owned declaration pattern from #184206.

Overlaps #206126, which covers the Automations declaration together with the task-suggestion tools and several other tools in one change. This PR is a narrower alternative for the Automations declaration only. If #206126 lands, this one can be closed.

## What Problem This Solves

The Automations tool is described to the model differently depending on which turn is running. An administrator's or channel owner's turn gets the full management description and schema; for example, `job.agentId`, command payloads and `on-exit` schedules are included. A subagent completion or `sessions_send` turn of the same conversation gets the narrower ordinary schema. The `sessions_yield` requester continuation gets the management-only variant. On the Codex harness, any change in the tool list replaces the native thread. An administrator conversation that delegates work therefore keeps switching threads, and each new thread starts from a bounded projection without earlier tool outputs.

## User Impact

After an authorized administrator or owner turn, the conversation keeps that Automations declaration on its later internal turns and its management-only continuations, so the native Codex thread is no longer replaced by these permission differences. What each turn may do is unchanged:
- an internal turn still cannot use management-only arguments, such as editing a command job;
- a management-only continuation still can only list, get, update, run, remove or bind automations.

Both are refused before any Gateway call, as before. Conversations that never had an authorized turn keep the ordinary declaration. Deployments with `tools.gatewayPolicy.automations.scope: "caller"` and self-remove-only cron sessions are unchanged. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

#184206 established that tool declarations belong to the session, not to the turn. It remembers the session's last human shape for `skill_workshop` and lets the execution grant refuse what the current turn may not do. This applies the same rule to Automations:

- `createCronTool` resolves its declaration through `declareCronTool`. An authorized turn with the full grant (`also`) records that its session holds the full declaration. Later turns of that session declare it too:
  - ungranted internal turns;
  - management-only (`only`) continuations.
- Only the full declaration is remembered. It contains every action that an ungranted or management-only turn declares, so the remembered surface is never narrower than what a turn may do.
- A management-only turn in a session without a remembered full declaration still declares its own shape and is not recorded. Ungranted turns there keep the ordinary declaration.
- The memory is per process and bounded at 512 sessions, like #184206. After a Gateway restart, a session publishes its own shape again until its next authorized turn.
- Execution reads only the current turn's live grant (`bindCronManagementGrant`) and the existing `managementOnly` and caller-scope guards. The declaration never grants authority.

The one policy choice: a management-only continuation now *sees* the full declaration it saw on the administrator turn that started it, while still being limited to management actions at call time. The alternative was to keep the narrower `only` shape, which replaces the thread twice per delegation. #178498 makes a related trade-off for ordinary versus admin turns; this change is narrower and keeps ordinary sessions unchanged.

## Evidence

**Live proof on this head `0a04ef33e0` (2026-11-26).**

Setup:
- Isolated Gateways on WSL Ubuntu, with fresh state per run.
- Packages were built from the exact commits, with bundled Codex 0.172.0.
- The model is the real `openai/gpt-6-luna` through a Codex OAuth login made for the proof.
- Operator turns use `openclaw agent --session-key agent:main:main` on loopback with the Gateway admin token, which gives the full (`also`) grant.

Turns on `agent:main:main`:
1. admin turn;
2. admin turn that calls `sessions_spawn` once and then `sessions_yield`. The requester continuation runs as `announce:requester-settle:…:yield-1`, with a management-only grant;
3. an internal `sessions_send` turn from another session;
4. admin turn.

Thread counts come from the Codex rollouts of `agent:main:main`; the child's own thread is excluded. The digest is a SHA-256 prefix of the declared `automations` spec.

| Tree | Main-session threads | `automations` declaration per turn |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `main` `1108290d41` | 4 (each change rotated with `dynamic tool catalog changed`) | `7ef7f00cdb97` "Schedule saved reminders…" → `fad9ba34f3a4` "Manage any existing automation…" (continuation) → `ff385917336b` without `job.agentId` (internal) → `7ef7f00cdb97` |
| this PR `0a04ef33e0` | 2 | `7ef7f00cdb97` on every turn, including the continuation and the internal turn |

The admin turn, the yield and the continuation shared one thread on this head. The single remaining rotation, before the internal turn, came from a different tool: `message` is added on the inter-session turn of a session created from the CLI, because it has no delivery route. That is another caller-dependent catalog difference of the #148329 class and is outside this PR.

With #206179 merged locally (`0cb501ead9`), a Control UI-style TUI conversation (TUI → `sessions_send` → TUI → `sessions_send`) stayed on 1 thread for 6 turns with 0 catalog rotations; `main` used 4.

Limits: one run per tree, one model; no cache or billing claim. Evidence archive: [proof-automations-0a04ef3.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35488481/proof-automations-0a04ef3.zip), SHA-256 `579a8f0820e25f1c52b8da22a8ba54714108f2e06281cd9e7eca4f41facf6bfe`. It contains the per-run thread and session probes, rollout declaration digests, `openclaw agent` results, requester-continuation markers, filtered Gateway debug lines and the driver scripts, with a README manifest. Home paths, account ids and tokens are redacted.

- **Discriminating tests.** `cron-tool.ts` is restored to `main` `1108290d41` and the new tests kept: 2 of 15 in `cron-tool.management.test.ts` fail. These are "keeps a session's granted Automations declaration on its ungranted turns" and "keeps a session's wider declaration on management-only continuations". With the fix, all 10 non-e2e `cron-tool*` suites pass 131/131 (`--maxWorkers=1`). The new tests also assert:
  - the refused calls never reach `callGatewayTool`;
  - a management-only declaration is never carried to ungranted turns (they keep the ordinary declaration);
  - the process-wide memory is cleared before and after each case.
- **Independent review** (a separate model pass over the diff, before publication) found one defect in an earlier revision: a remembered management-only declaration could narrow later ungranted turns. It is fixed in `0a04ef33e0`. The review confirmed that the declaration never reaches execution authority.
- **Static checks:** `tsgo:core`, the line-cap ratchet, and oxfmt/oxlint on the 4 changed TypeScript files pass. The full `check:changed` gate was not run locally.
- **Live, before.** On the author's Gateway (2026.11.5 and 2026.11.7, Codex 0.169.0), one Control UI administrator conversation logged `codex app-server dynamic tool catalog changed; starting a new thread` three times within a day for this declaration alone. Rollout `session_meta` diffs show:
  - 23:13: "Schedule saved reminders…" → "Manage any existing automation…" (a management-only continuation);
  - 07:32: back again on the next administrator turn;
  - 08:00: a schema without `job.agentId` → with it.
- **Live, after.** The first version of this change, which covers ungranted internal turns, has run on that Gateway since 2026-11-17. The management-only part has run since 2026-11-26 on 2026.11.10, in the earlier revision that also remembered management-only shapes. The current head ran in the isolated live proof above.
- **Known remaining case, separate and not changed here.** After a Control UI reconnect, the first send of each open pane carries `__controlUiReconnectResume`, and `cron-creator-authority-admission.ts` admits no cron authority for it. After a Gateway restart, that one turn still publishes the ordinary shape (the 08:00 case above), and the next administrator turn widens it again.
- **Not covered:** hosted CI for this head (workflows await maintainer approval).

prs.title: fix: keep a Control UI chat on one Codex thread when subagent and background updates arrive
prs.body:
Related: #167277, #148329. Follows the session-recorded client facts from #182191.

Overlaps #206126, which covers this tool pair together with `automations` and several other tools in one change. This PR is a narrower alternative for the task-suggestion pair only. If #206126 lands, this one can be closed.

## What Problem This Solves

In a Control UI conversation on the Codex harness, the native thread is replaced every time an operator message and an internal turn alternate. Internal turns include a subagent or background-task completion and a `sessions_send` message. The operator's turn lists `suggest_task` and `dismiss_task`; the internal turn has no live Control UI client and lists neither. Codex treats the changed tool list as a different thread. Each switch starts a fresh native thread from a bounded projection of the conversation: tool outputs are dropped and the prompt cache starts cold.

## User Impact

A Control UI conversation keeps one native Codex thread across operator turns and the internal turns that report back into it. Task suggestions behave as before: only a turn from the open Control UI can create or dismiss a suggestion. Other turns of that conversation still see the two tools, but a call is refused before any side effect, with "needs a turn from the open Control UI". Sessions that never had a Control UI turn list neither tool, as today. This covers channels, spawned children and Talk/CLI callers. No configuration or migration is needed; existing session entries load unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

This applies the direction recorded on #167277 (option A, 2026-10-08) to the last tool pair it names that still depends on the live caller. Interactive turns record the client fact that shapes the catalog on the session entry. Internal turns reuse it, and each turn's restriction is enforced when the tool is called. #182191 already does this for `clientCapabilities` (`filterToolsByClientCaps`). Task suggestions bypassed it, because `taskSuggestionDeliveryMode` was computed only from the live connection.

- `chat.send` passes its existing predicate into the inbound context: operator UI client, `operator.admin`, and the task-suggestions capability. The session metadata writer sets `taskSuggestionDeliveryMode: "gateway"` or clears it, on the same external user turns that record `clientCapabilities`. Internal turns never write it.
- Tool assembly lists the two tools from the live mode or the session field, with identical specs. It wraps them with `gateAgentToolExecution` unless the current turn has the live gateway mode.
- The intent of #102743 is kept: a surface that cannot present a card never gains the tools, because the fact is recorded per session from a capable turn, not inferred from the deployment.

The listing logic lives in `openclaw-tools.client-caps.ts` next to the client-caps equivalent, which keeps `openclaw-tools.ts` within its line cap.

## Evidence

**Live proof on this head (2026-11-26).**

Setup:
- Isolated Gateways on WSL Ubuntu, with fresh state per run and loopback ports.
- Packages were built from the exact commits, with bundled Codex 0.172.0.
- The model is the real `openai/gpt-6-luna` through a Codex OAuth login made for the proof.
- Operator turns use the shipped `openclaw tui --message`, which is an operator UI client with `operator.admin` and the `task-suggestions` cap, sending through `chat.send`.
- Internal turns come from `openclaw agent` on another session, asking the model to call `sessions_send` into `agent:main:main`.
- Thread counts are taken from the Codex rollouts of `agent:main:main` only. The suggestion-spec digest is a SHA-256 prefix of the declared `suggest_task` + `dismiss_task` specs.

Turns: TUI → `sessions_send` → TUI → `sessions_send`.

| Tree | Main-session threads for the 4 turns | `suggest_task`/`dismiss_task` on internal turns | Remaining catalog delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `main` `1108290d41` | 4 (a new thread at every switch) | absent | the two tools, plus the `automations` schema |
| this PR `c73ba08fd2` | 4 | present, identical spec digest `ead9482ceef5` on all 4 threads | `automations` schema only (fixed by #206180) |
| this PR + #206180 (local merge `0cb501ead9`) | **1** (6 turns, 0 catalog rotations) | present, `ead9482ceef5` | none |

**Refusal on an internal turn (this head).** The model declined to act on an instruction routed through `sessions_send` ("I can't execute the routed inter-session request"). The refusal was therefore driven by a one-shot automation on the same main session, which is an internal turn without a live client. The model called `suggest_task` and received:

```
suggest_task needs a turn from the open Control UI; this turn cannot present task suggestions.
```

`taskSuggestions.list` then returned `{"suggestions": []}`, so no card was created. The session entry recorded `taskSuggestionDeliveryMode: "gateway"` after the first TUI turn.

**Upgrade from the latest stable, v2026.11.10.**
1. Published `openclaw@2026.11.10` (`6ea542f`) with `@openclaw/codex@2026.11.10` ran on fresh state: a TUI turn, then a `sessions_send` turn. On stable, the internal turn lost both tools.
2. The same state was switched to this head with `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`. It exited 0 and upgraded the agent database schema v42 → v45.
3. Settings were preserved. The redacted config diff before and after doctor has additions only: doctor's own defaults (`agents.entries.main`, a provider entry, two bundled skill entries) and `wizard` metadata. No user setting was removed or changed.
4. The existing session (same session id, same model) loaded without the new field.
5. History was preserved: the stable-phase markers are present in the head-phase native threads.
6. The first TUI turn recorded `taskSuggestionDeliveryMode: "gateway"`.
7. The following `sessions_send` turn kept both tools with the same spec digest `ead9482ceef5`.

On this tree, the remaining thread replacement after the upgrade came from the `automations` schema (#206180).

An earlier run from `openclaw@2026.11.8` (agent schema v38 → v45) gave the same result.

Limits:
- one run per tree, one model;
- the remaining `automations` delta is shown, not hidden;
- no cache or billing claim.

Evidence archive: [proof-task-suggestion-c73ba08.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35488487/proof-task-suggestion-c73ba08.zip), SHA-256 `4ca4395c8e15cccb48fc3b0b35368fcbbd97946ae501b951aca50d5ceb57bcdc`. It contains the per-run thread and session probes, rollout declaration digests, TUI screens, `openclaw agent` results, the refusal automation run, the upgrade config diff and doctor log, filtered Gateway debug lines and the driver scripts, with a README manifest. Home paths, account ids and tokens are redacted.

- **Discriminating tests.** The production files are restored to `main` `1108290d41` and the new tests kept: 4 of 92 fail.
  - `dynamic-tool-build.task-suggestions.test.ts`: "keeps one Codex catalog across Control UI and internal turns of a capable session".
  - The registration refusal case.
  - The session-entry round trip.
  - The `chat.send` inbound fact.
  - With this patch, all four changed test files pass 92/92 (`--maxWorkers=1`).
- **Static checks:** `tsgo:core`, the line-cap ratchet, and oxfmt/oxlint on the 21 changed TypeScript files pass. The full `check:changed` gate was not run locally.
- **Live, before.** On the author's Gateway, the Producer main session (`agent:producer:main`) replaced its native thread with `codex app-server dynamic tool catalog changed; starting a new thread` whenever operator turns and `sessions_send`/completion turns alternated. That was 13 flips on 2026-11-02, 11 on 11-03, and about 3 a day on 11-04 to 11-07. In a debug window on 11-07/08, four main-session replacements had this reason. Diffing consecutive rollouts' `session_meta.dynamic_tools` showed that the only difference was `suggest_task`/`dismiss_task`, once the other caller-dependent differences listed on #167277 were out of the way.
- **Live, after.** This change has run on the author's Gateway since 2026-11-17, on builds 2026.11.4, 2026.11.5, 2026.11.7 and 2026.11.10. A check of the Producer main threads from 11-19 to 11-22 attributed every replacement to another identified cause (a version change, a WSL reboot, and a separate Automations declaration flip); none came from the suggestion tools. This is an operator installation with other carried patches, not a pristine-stock reproduction.
- **Independent review** (a separate model pass over the diff, before publication) returned ready. It confirmed:
  - only capable `chat.send` turns write the field;
  - internal turns never write it;
  - the execution gate refuses before any Gateway call;
  - the sync and async assembly paths agree.

  Its one note is now documented: runs started through the `agent` RPC compute the live surface but do not record it on the session.
- **Not covered:** hosted CI for this head (workflows await maintainer approval). The Control UI card flow itself is unchanged and was not re-recorded.

prs.title: improve: avoid an extra worker during transcript archival
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cold transcript maintenance qualifies its database readers on the session-store lane, then starts a foreground-history worker just to enumerate the same targets. A cold process can pay for a second transcript worker before archival begins.

## User Impact

Reuse the already-qualified store lane for cold target inventory. This is intended to avoid an unnecessary worker startup when history is cold. A process whose history reader is already active may see no memory reduction. The completed serial owner-workload comparison reduced cold-history median end RSS by 117.563 MiB (7.028%) and removed one transcript-worker startup in every cold pair. This is not Gateway RSS or concurrent-load proof. This PR remains on performance HOLD.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the existing session-store lane to the cold-inventory read owner, matching ordinary store inventory. Registry checks, qualification before FIFO admission, replacement detection, final validation, and reader cleanup stay in place. No pool merge, new cache, configuration, dependency, or schema change. Store-lane contention remains an unresolved merge gate. Foreground-history latency during active cold inventory must be qualified before lifting HOLD; the prewarmed control does not test concurrent load.

Existing inventory tests cover replacement and rejection for status and maintenance on this route. They are safety coverage, not a claimed failing baseline for the startup count. The committed archive-worker workload now reports worker starts and separates cold-history from a real prewarmed-history reader.

## Evidence

Source review and final committed-range local review found no actionable findings. Linux Node 24.22.1 and pinned Bun each passed the corrected nine-case inventory suite; the unchanged four sibling files contribute 44 previously passed cases per runtime, qualified by a complete physical-source comparison. Scoped format, lint, types, and the full candidate-tree build passed. The required isolated Gateway cold-storage flow subsequently PASSED: automatic archival, hot reload, missing-payload/backup refusals, restart/recovery, and archive/restore byte checks; all three task-owned Gateway process groups were absent afterward. Earlier budget/preflight attempts did not execute this proof. Exact-head required CI/native acceptance remains incomplete.

The build succeeded with five advisory UI budget violations: largest CSS gzip 57.2 > 56.9 KiB; total CSS gzip 331.1 > 329.4 KiB; total CSS raw 1707.5 > 1699.4 KiB; chat boot JS requests 21 > 20; chat boot JS gzip 1302.6 > 1301.4 KiB. ### Acceptance rule declared before measurement

- Workload: committed `scripts/perf/archive-worker-churn-measure.ts`, 64 finished sessions across two stores, 40 sweeps per fresh process, no built-entry override. Its real archive/restore byte oracle must pass in every process. This is a representative small-device fixture, not proof for the benchmark default of 10,000 sessions or large installations.
- Two separately reported modes: cold-empty-history and `--warm-history` (two real reads through one retained reader, with a foreground-worker assertion). Prewarming is not concurrent user load.
- Five serial counterbalanced baseline/candidate pairs per mode: 20 fresh processes, independent n=5 per arm per mode. Identical committed workload, Node 24.22.1, dependencies, full source graph and fixture; only the reviewed cold-target owner differs between arms. The baseline is a counterfactual using the frozen pre-change cold-target module on the same candidate graph, not a separate historical build.
- Counts first: every cold pair must remove exactly one history worker startup, with no added worker in another lane. The prewarmed mode must add no worker startup. Report all-worker and per-lane counts, not just archive workers.
- Report iteration 0 separately. For iterations 1–39, summarize each child's median and p95 before comparing arms; 195 sweeps are not 195 independent samples. Include spread, paired deltas, process CPU, main-thread CPU, event-loop p99/max over each whole 40-sweep child, and host load.
- Report process-wide RSS before/end and the 25 ms sampled peak separately from worker counts. Never add isolate heaps or call this Gateway RSS. Both arms use the same source loader and owner-overlay mechanism; this is an owner workload, not a pristine no-preload process. No RSS saving is assumed.
- Acceptance cells are fixed before the run: for each mode and each declared latency, CPU, RSS, or event-loop metric, compare the baseline and candidate arm median and p95 across the five independent child summaries. Use the usual midpoint median and nearest-rank p95 (`ceil(0.95 × n)`, so the maximum for n=5); adverse percentage is `100 × (candidate / baseline − 1)`. Cold iteration 0, each child’s warm median, and each child’s warm p95 stay separate. Report every matched-pair delta and range as well; do not select a different estimator after seeing results. A zero baseline gets an absolute delta, not an invented percentage, and any increase remains a regression under the rule below.
- Win requires the count reduction and no regression in the declared latency/CPU/memory/tail metrics. Disclose every adverse cell; a >=20% adverse cell stops acceptance. Any worse metric needs explicit owner acceptance recorded here, not an appeal to noise. Otherwise remove the change if no measurable gain.

The rule above was published before measurement in body SHA-256 `49c5ceb46724af1bf87e465aac43363a48b76cb4972309570f3c0771abc19cb3`. The historical instrumented diagnostic motivated this experiment and does not qualify this candidate or waive another PR's HOLD.


## Completed measurement — acceptance HOLD

All 20 fresh serial children completed with exit 0, no signal/error, 40 observations each (800 total), matching archive/restore byte oracles, and zero active/pending lane tasks. Full source and installed-dependency seals matched before/after. Execution is valid; acceptance is still HOLD: **14 of 56 aggregate cells worsened; none reached 20%**. No adverse cell has been waived. There are also 46 adverse matched-pair deltas, including 16 at least 20%; correlated metrics/checkpoints are not separate independent experiments.

Cold-history first-operation median wall time fell 22,098.191 → 14,531.898 ms (−34.239%). Median end RSS fell 1,672.773 → 1,555.211 MiB; sampled peak fell 1,672.648 → 1,555.086 MiB. All five paired cold end-RSS deltas improved (−70.719 to −148.395 MiB). Prewarmed-history median end/peak RSS fell 1,727.367 → 1,709.641 MiB (−1.026%), but first-operation median wall/process CPU/main-thread CPU increased 3.551% / 5.390% / 11.774%. Their causes remain unproven; instrumented diagnosis is separate from acceptance.

The 40 measured sweeps have no eligible archive work; each process then exercises one eligible archive and verifies restored event bytes. These numbers describe the committed owner workload, not 40 real archival jobs, total OS threads, a pristine no-loader process, or Gateway memory. The 25 ms RSS sampler stops before the separate endpoint read: three sampled peaks are 128 KiB below end RSS. The two measurements remain separate.

### Remaining contention gate

The exact-head hosted review requires resolving simultaneous cold inventory versus ordinary store reads before merge. A source-backed bounded risk remains: with two SQLite history workers busy, cold inventory occupying one store worker can overlap another status request’s pre-FIFO qualification and create a second store worker (four retained workers versus three in the baseline scenario). Existing pool caps and retirement remain; this is not evidence of an unbounded leak. Serial/prewarmed measurements do not resolve that overlap or prove load savings. No readiness, auto-merge, or threshold change is implied by this update.

A separate candidate-only run used the compiled Gateway and the existing sequential cold-storage scenario (3 sessions, 9 transcript events; UI, plugins and channels disabled). The archive/backup/restart/recovery/append flow passed. All three serving processes were authenticated by PID, birth identity, executable and compiled-entry arguments; the observer captured 1,026 process rows over 1,202 sample ticks. All three process groups were absent after completion. The scenario and native wrapper exited 0.

Approximate per-process kernel VmRSS, MiB (listener-only rows):

| Lifecycle | Minimum | Median | Maximum | Last listening sample |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Initial exercise | 911.043 | 1,186.590 | 1,515.516 | 1,149.395 |
| Restart | 850.750 | 1,178.377 | 1,380.570 | 1,295.336 |
| Recovery | 828.656 | 1,362.850 | 1,465.355 | 1,465.355 |

The authenticated serving process's full-lifecycle maximum, including pre-listen samples, was the same maximum in each row. These are individual process measurements, not sums of process RSS. Sampling can miss peaks, and VmRSS/VmHWM use approximate kernel accounting.

Existing startup logs reported RSS at HTTP bind of 892.3 / 849.1 / 827.7 MiB. The first two `ready` records reported 1,280.8 / 1,360.1 MiB; the third log had no `ready` record. Post-ready maintenance records reported 1,375.3 / 1,179.5 / 1,340.2 MiB, main-isolate used heap 238.4 / 210.2 / 218.9 MiB, and 17 / 16 / 17 tracked workers. Cached worker heap samples are partial/stale observations; neither those values nor the RSS remainder identify an allocation owner.

prs.title: fix: keep Signal quote markers on every quoted line and message
prs.body:
Root cause: `extensions/signal/src/format.ts:117` (on main 993d0b77df4f) passes `blockquotePrefix: "> "` to the Markdown parser, and the parser writes that prefix only once, where a quote opens (`packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts:1036`). Continuation lines, later paragraphs in the quote, nested levels and later chunks of a split quote never get it.

Fixes #204999

## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw sends a quote to Signal, only the first line keeps its `> ` marker. The next line, later paragraphs in the same quote, nested quotes and every later message of a long quote that gets split arrive as plain text, so a reader can't tell what was quoted. This happens for agent replies and for messages sent through the Gateway.

## User Impact

On Signal, every nonempty quoted line now starts with `> ` (or `> > ` for a nested quote), and so does the first line of each later chunk. Bold and other Signal styles still cover the same words. Text without quotes is sent exactly as before. Nothing to configure.

## Why This Change Was Made

#190066 fixed the same bug for Slack and WhatsApp by adding the prefix while rendering instead of while parsing. This PR reuses that code for Signal instead of adding a second one:

- The per-line quote scan from `renderMarkdownWithMarkers` moves into `collectBlockquoteLineStarts` in `packages/markdown-core/src/render.ts`. Slack and WhatsApp call it as before.
- `renderMarkdownWithAttributedRanges` gets the same opt-in `blockquotePrefix` option. Each prefix is inserted the same way as a link suffix, so Signal's style ranges move past it. iMessage and Zalo Personal don't set the option, so their output doesn't change.
- Signal sets the prefix at render time and no longer passes it to the parser. It now takes a fresh `sliceMarkdownIR` copy before filtering links. The old `{ ...ir }` spread dropped the parser's quote depth, which nested `> > ` needs.
- The scan reads the parser's quote blocks even when a profile drops the quote style. Signal's profile turns blockquotes into a text fallback, so the style is gone by render time. Slack and WhatsApp keep the native quote style, so nothing changes for them.

Because the chunker measures rendered text, the prefixes count toward Signal's `textChunkLimit`.

Thanks @yetval for the report and for #190478, which found the cause and proposed this approach.

## Evidence

Gateway proof: main 993d0b77df4f and this branch 498513ba16f8 were each built in a secretless `node:24.22.1` container. Signal was set to `transport.kind: external-native`, pointed at a local stand-in for signal-cli that records every JSON-RPC `send` request. Each input went through two paths: `openclaw gateway call send`, and an agent reply to an inbound Signal DM (scripted local model). We ran main twice and this branch twice. The long quote ran with `channels.signal.textChunkLimit: 40`. Proof comment with all recorded requests: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206243#issuecomment-7205982479

| Input | main (both runs, both paths) | this branch (both runs, both paths) |
|---|---|---|
| issue quote with bold and nested quote | lines: `> line one` / `line two` / (blank) / `second para` / (blank) / `> nested one` / `nested two`; `11:8:BOLD` = `line two` | lines: `> line one` / `> line two` / (blank) / `> second para` / (blank) / `> > nested one` / `> > nested two`; `13:8:BOLD` = `line two` |
| 18-word quote, limit 40 | `"> word ×7"`, `"word ×8"`, `"word ×3"` | `"> word ×7"`, `"> word ×7"`, `"> word ×4"` |
| plain text control | identical | identical |
| `a **bold** line` control | `2:4:BOLD` = `bold` | identical |

The control requests are byte-identical across all four runs, apart from the inbound quote timestamp.

Tests: a new case in `extensions/signal/src/format.test.ts` fails on main and passes here. Also passing: Signal format and send tests, Slack and WhatsApp format tests, iMessage, Zalo Personal, and markdown-core `ir` and render-aware chunking tests. `pnpm check:changed` passed typecheck and lint. Its dead-export scan fails only on exports in files this PR doesn't touch, which are already unused on main.

Not tested: a real signal-cli daemon or Signal account, and how Signal clients display the quotes.

Merge risk: low. A revert fully undoes it. No stored state, config or schema changes. `AttributedRenderOptions` gains an optional field, so existing callers are unaffected. Only Signal outbound text changes.

prs.title: fix: stop promising unavailable command wakes in local agent runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `agent --local` starts a background command in an ordinary session, its running result tells the model to end the turn and wait for an automatic completion wake. The CLI is one-shot, so that wake cannot start another turn; observed runs instead log failed completion delivery during cleanup.

## User Impact

Local agents receive manual collection guidance and can collect the command result before their turn ends. Gateway, cron, and subagent completion behavior retains its existing policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `oneShotCliRun` fact when assembling exec defaults to disable unavailable exit notifications. The regression extends the existing real CLI process fixture, preserving its session-RPC cleanup check without adding another CLI startup.

## Evidence

- The same CLI regression fails on base `40d533668293d77148f8a94b5da1c697caf9b72a` because the running result promises an automatic wake. It passes with the fix, collects exit code 0 and the command output, and reports no completion-delivery or CLI cleanup failure. The model transport is an isolated loopback Responses fixture.
- All 45 focused tests pass, including background completion and prompt-prefix stability. Core and CLI test type graphs, targeted lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass.
- Linux x86_64, Node 24.19.0, pnpm 12.15.0, 4 CPUs, approximately 16 GiB RAM. The extended CLI test takes 28.7 seconds; its file takes 73.1 seconds including compiler preparation. Hosted CI timing is pending.

Local ClawSweeper reviewed `40d533668293d77148f8a94b5da1c697caf9b72a..bc2b6aec3b7747c7ba9158169fc9096df8eee0fd` and found no actionable code or security defects. The final review accepted the live capture below as sufficient behavioral proof.

A real OpenAI-backed agent also passed on this exact head (macOS arm64, Node 26.13.0, medium reasoning, priority service requested). It received a running handle with manual collection guidance, polled that same process to exit code 0 with `LIVE_EXEC_WAKE_MARKER`, and then returned exactly `LOCAL_EXEC_WAKE_PROOF_OK`. The capture contains zero tool failures and no completion-delivery or CLI cleanup warnings.

## What Problem This Solves

The published `@openclaw/codex@2026.11.10` plugin imports `AgentHarnessRuntimeUpdateRequiredError` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-attempt-runtime`. The current host no longer exposes that named JavaScript export. Node rejects the module before the plugin can start a turn. Two scheduled Dreaming narratives reproduced this failure on a packed host.

## User Impact

Operators can keep the released plugin installed when upgrading the host. The plugin and host can still recognize the same runtime-update failure with `instanceof`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restore the named export of the constructor already imported by the attempt runtime. The tagged host shipped this binding for official plugins. Both entry points now resolve to the same class. This change adds one export and its regression test. [Release source](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.10/src/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-attempt-runtime.ts#L31) · [Release maintenance commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/38174c247574d62360ac24e4bd54e93e505316ff)

## Evidence

The two compiled plugin modules are `run-attempt-DbKhDrWT.mjs` and `usage-limit-error-BMGxvkxS.mjs`. On the packed baseline, Node resolved 124 of 124 imports on the typed harness entry and 18 of 19 on the JavaScript attempt entry. The missing constructor was the sole mismatch. The new regression constructs the error through the attempt runtime and checks its exact host constructor. [Stock package replay](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45907994921)

On the same Linux worker, the independently packed parent accepted the chat, then failed on the missing named export with zero stdio turns. Both official npm imports reproduced that error directly. On the signed candidate, all 46 SDK facade tests and both formatter checks passed. Node imported both compiled npm consumers and verified exact constructor identity through their installed host paths. The packaged Gateway accepted a chat, completed the turn and persisted the expected assistant reply. The official plugin issued one `thread/start` and one `turn/start` to a synthetic stdio app-server in a loopback-only namespace. This exercises the host/plugin boundary without a live model. ## What Problem This Solves

A plugin that deletes keys across a changing set of keyed stores can leave one tracking entry per namespace in a long-running process. Each deletion has completed and its caller received no guard that could use those entries.

## User Impact

Once an exact-key deletion settles, the host can release tracking for both participating namespaces. The deleted rows and neighboring rows retain the same transaction and durability guarantees.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing command lifetime for the built-in `deleteKeys` handler. The native writer still supplies its matching commit receipt. Plugin-defined operations continue to take the receipt lifetime because their callers can retain and validate the returned guard.

## Evidence

On Node 24.22.1 with real SQLite on Linux x64, the parent commit retained two namespace entries after both deletions were durable and their pending sets were empty. The same test on `14deddc9535a` observed both entries at commit admission and neither after settlement. It also checked that an older receipt was invalidated at admission and that both deleted keys were absent and both neighboring rows survived via fresh synchronous read handles. All 45 tests across the operation and store runtime suites passed. [Focused proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45908777948)


Related to [command epoch cleanup](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206196) and [atomic exact-key deletion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206198).

prs.title: fix: retain Codex context after first-turn startup failures
prs.body:
Related: #169431, #168347, #171707.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes earlier context disappearing when a fresh Codex thread fails before its first input is accepted and the user retries the request.

## User Impact

For context engines using `thread_bootstrap`, the retry receives the history that never reached native Codex. Successful follow-ups continue using the accepted native history without resending the bootstrap. This applies to fresh startup; previously persisted false receipts are not migrated.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fresh thread creation saves the bootstrap projection before `turn/start` accepts its input. A later startup or dispatch failure can leave a matching epoch that incorrectly suppresses history on retry.

Keep the engine/policy binding at thread creation and record the projection after validated native turn acceptance, only when the complete bootstrap block survived final input fitting. Guard the receipt update by the exact thread/client owner. If the receipt write fails or loses ownership, preserve the already-accepted turn and its result. Existing resume markers, transient ownership and warm/cancellation cleanup remain unchanged.

This is a narrow acceptance-ordering fix. It adds no retry machinery or context-retention policy. It does not provide crash-atomic delivery: an interruption or storage failure after acceptance can still leave conservative replay uncertainty.

Related PR #171707 proposes `thread/inject_items` for authored-cap history, with an earlier seed acknowledgment. This candidate fixes main's rendered `turn/start` carrier. The changes have not been composed or tested together; if that carrier lands first, reconcile the receipt boundary with its acknowledged seeding path.

## Evidence

**Current head:** `18654634e2a3c8470447fe0a942d17785d60f311`.

**Hosted CI:** [successful run 38632947933](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38632947933), 52 successful jobs and 29 skipped. All four previously failing leaf lanes and the required gate passed. Observed again on October 14 at 21:23 UTC.

**New compatibility evidence:** a supported native-session route now completes the stable 10.3 → current candidate upgrade, preserves the same stored session/native thread, and completes two real local-model continuations with the original facts. The additional archive below contains actual seed/import, migration, native/provider/terminal captures and durable-history checks. This is a bounded native-session result; the earlier legacy-provider-route comparison remains blocked and is disclosed separately.

### Inspectable sanitized artifacts

1. [Original Gateway/native/provider comparison and reproduction archive](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33455012/codex-bootstrap-acceptance-ce5296cf-evidence.zip)

   File: `codex-bootstrap-acceptance-ce5296cf-evidence.zip`.
   SHA-256: `caaed5e4d49d2e1f9211cd28252304f4fca9b4f12096eeead44faef9ffe23ba6`.

2. [Earlier stable-state preservation, route-barrier comparison and CI follow-up](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33459171/codex-bootstrap-18654634-upgrade-followup.zip)

   SHA-256: `758480e533c1342d166e732baddf035491911e7fcc7a84f24a1791506ce2c989`.

3. [codex-bootstrap-18654634-native-upgrade-proof.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33463900/codex-bootstrap-18654634-native-upgrade-proof.zip)

   SHA-256: `a21af0ab8f7fb655b2ec21e772e4c85123b40e0b0297893077443b9e508a716f`.

The original archive includes actual rejection/acceptance inputs, actual provider user input and output, Gateway terminal receipts, the complete comparison matrix, check logs, runnable helpers and an offline correlation verifier. The earlier supplement adds retained stable-state reopening captures, Doctor receipts, pristine-main comparison and CI repair evidence. The new supplement adds successful native-session upgrade continuations. Each has source/artifact hashes, a reproduction recipe, offline verifier and redaction disclosure. Raw operator configuration, credentials, private endpoint/model inventory and real user sessions are excluded.

### Fresh startup: main versus candidate

Built and exercised main `24567afc232dfbcd8da3f1eb4e1b1466925d1352` and original candidate `06daa04093a9eab782ac72893b7c45c95318cbcd` with Node 24.19.0 and pnpm 12.9.0. The shipped Gateway used real native Codex 0.160.0 and an already-loaded local LM Studio model. Four isolated synthetic cases, three successful turns each: **12/12 inference requests completed with HTTP 200 and `response.completed`.**

| Case | Bootstrap blocks in actual provider user input: first success / continuation 1 / continuation 2 | Actual model response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main, ordinary control | 1 / 1 / 1 | Saved goal and checksum on all three turns |
| Candidate, ordinary control | 1 / 1 / 1 | Saved goal and checksum on all three turns |
| Main, first dispatch rejected before acceptance | 0 / 0 / 0 | `MISSING` on retry and both continuations |
| Candidate, same preaccept rejection | 1 / 1 / 1 | Saved goal and checksum on retry and both continuations |

The fault cases reject exactly one first `turn/start` with JSON-RPC `-32602` before forwarding it to native; those two rejected dispatches make zero provider calls. This is controlled fault injection. Other native messages and provider payloads pass through byte-for-byte, with no response substitution or provider adapter.

The rejected request contains 634 characters including the synthetic history. Main's retry sends only the new 234-character request; the candidate retry sends 877 characters including the history and failed request. The accepted turn ID matches the Gateway terminal receipt. Both later turns retain the same native thread/client and send only their new 245-character request. At the provider boundary, successful history appears once in user messages; assistant echoes are excluded. Nonces are generated independently for each case.

The external fixture uses public context-engine registration, current-turn fencing and a real atomic idempotent SQLite worker commit. No legacy fallback occurs in the qualified matrix; every case commits three accepted turns. The engine supplies controlled history, while native binding/projection, Gateway dispatch and inference are real. It is not a benchmark of an external production context engine.

### Existing native-session upgrade: completed on the current head

Fresh isolated case `upgrade-i-native` ran the built stable `v2026.10.3` and exact current candidate with native Codex 0.160.0 and an already-loaded local LM Studio model. **Exit 0, 48.370 seconds, four HTTP 200 / `response.completed` results:** one native CLI seed, one stable Gateway follow-up, then two candidate Gateway continuations.

The real native CLI created a synthetic conversation. Stable adopted it using the public `sessions.catalog.list` / `sessions.catalog.continue` flow, saved settings, and performed an ordinary `agent` RPC. After all owned processes stopped, candidate Doctor migrated that same state with `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_READONLY=1` and external service ownership. Candidate reopened the existing session and performed two ordinary `agent` RPCs. This uses native-owned model/provider configuration without a `models.providers` overlay, fabricated credential/model, direct database seed, admission bypass or payload translation.

| Check | Before upgrade | After upgrade and both continuations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent / global SQLite schema | 24 / 20 | 26 / 22; integrity checks pass |
| OpenClaw session ID and native thread | Saved by stable | Same IDs; genuine `thread/resume`, no replacement |
| Label, pin, verbosity, usage setting | Saved through public session API | Identical on reopening and after continuation |
| Historical messages | Four user/assistant messages | Exactly equal on reopening; content, IDs, sequence and other metadata retained after both continuations |
| Stored transcript events | 5 | 9; original five equal on all seven common stored fields |
| Original native rollout files | Two retained snapshots | Both preserved byte-for-byte as prefixes |
| Authored configuration | Retained bytes | Byte-identical; Doctor made zero model requests |
| Original goal, checksum and history fact | Present in native seed and stable reply | Present in actual provider history and both actual candidate replies |

Follow-up prompts do not repeat the original nonces. Imported user/assistant seed history is checked before the stable follow-up. Each of the three Gateway turns matches a genuine native acceptance, exact provider last-user input and Gateway terminal turn ID. Both candidate turns reuse the same candidate client and the native thread stored by stable. The binding is exact across Doctor; after continuation, runtime fields such as the client ID and covered-history watermark may advance. Whole final binding byte equality is not claimed.

Post-continuation display comparison excludes only `__openclaw.transcriptPosition.source`, a reader-generation coordinate; `rawSeq` and all other message fields remain exact. Separately, stopped SQLite snapshots prove byte equality of all seven original stored event fields. The source-generation change is not presented as ordinary append behavior; its exact runtime caller was not established. A prior attempt failed its overly broad display comparison and remains excluded. Only the fresh corrected case qualifies.

Inspect the new archive's `native-seed/`, `stable/`, `migration/`, `candidate/`, actual native/provider input-output files, `stored-transcript-preservation.json`, and `upgrade-summary.json`. The result was independently checked against raw synthetic SQLite/rollout snapshots and captured responses. No production Gateway participated.

**Scope:** both builds use default legacy mode with native context ownership. This establishes the tested existing native-session migration/continuation boundary. It does not establish custom-engine activation during upgrade or repair the legacy configured-provider route below. The original fresh-startup matrix independently proves the PR's custom-engine acceptance fix; the earlier supplement independently covers preservation of old custom projection/ledger data up to its route barrier.

### Earlier legacy-provider upgrade comparison: candidate versus pristine main

The latest stable release observed for this test was `v2026.10.3`, commit `59cb44796b0f1f0daa0e37af8b1495abb45d9bc1` (tag object `3a8c04b0832eabc4410ba7c7a30c9c27e4b5fc81`). Each case first created settings, a real user/assistant exchange and one committed fixture-ledger row through a stable Gateway. After stopping that Gateway, it retained the same synthetic state and native home, ran the supported Doctor migration, and reopened using the target build.

| Observation | Candidate `18654634e2a3` | Pristine main `24567afc232d` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent / global schema | 24 to 26 / 20 to 22 | Same |
| Stable real provider completions | 1 | 1 |
| Exact old history reopened | Preserved | Preserved |
| Session ID, label, pin, verbosity and usage setting | Preserved | Preserved |
| Active native binding/projection, native history prefix and one-row accepted ledger | Preserved | Preserved |
| Post-upgrade native turn starts / provider calls | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Successful post-upgrade continuations | 0 | 0 |
| Full compatibility | NOT PROVEN | NOT PROVEN |

Both failed with:

```text
Requested agent harness "codex" does not support openai/lmstudio/<local-model> (Codex cannot reproduce the prepared provider route).
```

Doctor canonicalized the explicit local `codex` provider to `openai`. The canonical custom-endpoint route does not declare Codex compatibility, so admission stops before dispatch. The five inspected Doctor/routing owners are byte-identical between pristine main and this candidate; their hashes are included. The repeated main failure separates this barrier from the PR's acceptance-ordering change, without proving that every old stored binding works.

Doctor ran only in the new synthetic cases, with explicit operator approval and `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external`. It exited zero, made no model request, and retained valid pre-migration snapshots/database backups. It also emitted an original-state JSON inspection warning; these were not warning-free runs. Configuration normalization was reviewed, not undone. No admission bypass, fabricated credential, configuration restoration or seeded database row was used.

The supplement's `candidate/` and `pristine-main/` directories contain the actual observations, not only integrity claims. Its verifier reports consistent exported evidence while retaining `fullCompatibility: NOT PROVEN`. The two stable setup completions are separate from the original 12-call matrix and must not be counted as upgraded continuations. All owned test processes stopped; the operator Gateway was untouched.

### Tests and CI follow-up

```text
Original baseline publication-failure regression: 1 control passed, 1 expected failure
Original candidate affected selection:             134/134 passed, 7 complete files
Original final formatted regression suite:          12/12 passed
Published-head provider-review shard:                8 failed / 25 passed
Same shard after two-line CI follow-up:              33/33 passed
Bootstrap regression follow-up:                      12/12 passed
Assertion ratchet, targeted lint/types/format:       passed
Stable and repaired-candidate QA builds:             passed
git diff --check:                                    passed
Hosted CI at current head:                           passed
```

The original 134-test selection covers the new bootstrap boundary plus neighboring active-engine, overflow, binding, warm cleanup and cancellation behavior. It took 143.892 seconds. Three test-only lint repairs and formatting followed it with unchanged runtime implementation; the final 12-test rerun took 50.322 seconds. Coverage includes post-start preparation and dispatch rejection, accepted provider failure/cancellation, indeterminate cancelled dispatch, replacement-owner preservation, receipt-write throw/conflict, fitted-away bootstrap and empty history. Existing expectations were not weakened.

Follow-up commit `18654634e2a3c8470447fe0a942d17785d60f311` adds only the missing `promptState` slot to the provider-review fixture and the required rationale for a mutable bootstrap prompt type assertion. There is no runtime behavior change. The exact previously failing shard now passes; no assertion-ratchet baseline was expanded. Two inherited CI failures came from a wrapper inventory omission fixed upstream by `51afdbea12bb4bd733e5e3594828140194048195`. The successful CI merge includes that repair through its main parent; this branch does not copy it.

Independent Sol 6.1 High source reviews of the original patch and the scoped follow-up found no actionable P0-P2 findings. A separate evidence review checked artifact/source hashes, actual native/provider/Gateway correlations, retained raw synthetic database/prefix preservation and redaction. Source review alone is not counted as execution evidence. Local check receipts retain their actual precommit identities and source hashes rather than relabeling old runs as current-head runs.

### Reproduction and limits

Use each archive's `repro/README.md`: the original for the four-case fresh-startup matrix, the earlier supplement for the expected legacy-route failure, and the new supplement for successful existing native-session upgrade/continuation. Build pinned checkouts with `qaRuntime`; the live entry point is `node openclaw.mjs gateway run`, driven by ordinary `agent` RPCs through public `GatewayClient`. Runners create isolated state and require an explicitly selected already-loaded local model. The new archive's `repro/verify-upgrade-evidence.py` checks its complete file inventory, hashes and exported correlations without service access.

One original preliminary control used an incomplete fixture contract and fell back to legacy; it is excluded from the 12-call matrix. Upgrade setup attempts with missing session permissions, a response-field assumption and an unavailable stable SQLite SDK helper were retained and excluded; the supplement's attempt audit explains each. The earlier custom-engine preservation cases e/f use the common public transaction API and require a committed stable fixture-ledger row before migration. The new native-only case i has no synthetic engine ledger. No failed attempt was discarded or reclassified as success.

Original candidate patch SHA-256: `ce5296cf50997171390a897b9cfddc8311d4e9e3706f1dc46a1b203c35690812`. The immutable original archive remains tied to head `06daa04093a9eab782ac72893b7c45c95318cbcd`; the supplement records head `18654634e2a3c8470447fe0a942d17785d60f311` separately.

The new setup audit also retains an invalid stable config attempt and the display-generation comparison failure; neither counts as a passing case. The corrected test does not ignore stored history changes: it checks all original raw event fields after shutdown. Test processes are stopped; retained fixtures are separate from the production Gateway.

The combined proof establishes local fresh-startup recovery under controlled preaccept failure and successful existing native-session upgrade with preserved history/settings/native thread. It does not establish every provider/engine upgrade combination, repair the separately reproduced legacy route barrier, migrate historical false bootstrap receipts, test remote OpenAI behavior, or prove production incidence, model-quality improvement, latency/cache/billing gains, live store-error/cancellation behavior or crash-atomic delivery. The new supplement has not yet been assessed by the upstream reviewer; acceptance of this bounded compatibility proof remains their decision.

prs.title: fix(sqlite): release retired pooled reader launch owners
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

A pooled SQLite reader can exit cleanly while its slot still owns the retired launch. The launch carries a child environment and, on brokered reads or retained-runtime updates, a broker or runtime generation. Up to four slots can keep those objects alive until another read replaces them.

## What changed

A slot releases its launch once its reader has closed, all queued requests have settled, and its stateful lease has ended. The slot and queue remain available to callers already selecting them. Failed native cleanup continues to occupy capacity. The physical session already owns the compatibility check for reuse.

## Evidence

- Signed candidate `008c2cfaa3231685182a7af7db67827e5cb69d16` against `df32bed585016356e6f280abab43b52d5497b8ae`. Final signed head `bb63d57d4dc7e6c15b6f81731eb2fe0f881d4196` simplifies only the expected values in the queue test after lint flagged `Array.fill`. The pool, GC fixture and timing source are byte-identical. Formatter and `git diff --check` passed. Local autoreview of the initial signed change at `008c2cfaa323` covered P0–P3 and reported no actionable findings.
- On a shared Linux x64 runner, the original pool plus the new fixture left one retired broker reachable after eight GC turns, while an unowned control collected. The candidate collected the retired broker and six completed caller objects while the surviving physical reader continued serving reads. All 14 retention, operation and runtime-generation tests passed, including queued replacement reads, stateful ownership and quarantine. The isolated command exited 0 and restored its source tree. [Runner allocation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45908777948).
- Three fresh processes per arm, 24 warm reads each. Cold read times in ms were `145.574 / 143.196 / 147.966` on stock and `145.824 / 188.751 / 134.344` on the candidate. Warm medians per process were `1.514 / 1.660 / 1.559` and `1.726 / 2.170 / 1.494`, respectively. The sample measures latency only and both ranges overlap.
- [Final CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45910795819) passed on `bb63d57d4dc7`, including [the corrected lint shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45910795819/job/140220375033). The dependency check on the first signed head reports the same four unused production exports and one unused exported type as the prior scheduled main run. Both full-tree checks report the same export and type. [PR job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45909703136/job/140215499117) · [main job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45904733009/job/140199027978).

This change addresses parent-process object reachability after retirement. Whole-Gateway RSS and the constrained-host incident remain unmeasured by this comparison.

prs.title: perf(ci): avoid duplicate probes for declaration inputs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Warm CI declaration checks probe whether each input exists immediately before resolving its physical path.

## User Impact

This candidate aims to reduce declaration-check preparation time. **Rejected after measurement; do not merge.** The candidate did not meet the acceptance rule.

## Why This Change Was Made

Try native realpath first for existing inputs. On any resolution failure, keep the existing nearest-existing-ancestor walk and its final physical confinement check. No filesystem results are cached and no lookup or receipt validation is removed.

The existing declaration measurement harness now selects the shared boundary implementation before loading the TSX bootstrap, so baseline and candidate actually use different implementations.

## Evidence

Frozen baseline: `993d0b77df4f2b9f886b4382f3ce6bbc81699749`.

Acceptance rule recorded before the first performance run:
- Flow: the real `prepare-extension-package-boundary-artifacts.mts --mode=package-boundary` entry point, with current SDK receipts and a warm filesystem.
- Run five serial alternating baseline/candidate pairs in fresh Node processes on the same isolated Linux host. Record runtime, available CPU/RAM, and load.
- Require identical receipt digests and unchanged receipt bytes/mtime on every run; fewer existence probes; at least 10% lower median entry-point time; no worse p95 entry-point time or median CPU; and no more than 10% higher median peak RSS.
- If the warm gate passes, also run five alternating full SDK compiler-worker pairs with `packages/plugin-sdk/tsconfig.json`; require identical lookup/input digests and no worse median/p95 runtime or median CPU, with the same RSS bound. Stop after a failed warm gate.
- Count instrumentation runs separately from timings; capture a baseline CPU profile.
- Report all samples, median, p95, spread, CPU, and RSS. Reject the candidate if any gate fails. No whole-CI or billing claim.

Final local ClawSweeper review completed on `993d0b77df4f2b9f886b4382f3ce6bbc81699749..77713aaa833e52addec843b4e14c2ce7944c5f2a`: no actionable findings; security cleared. Focused correctness checks passed: 55 tests passed, 5 platform-specific cases skipped; script typecheck, targeted lint, and formatter parity passed. An initial single-CPU test failure came from an explicit GOMAXPROCS=2 test invocation; the file passed all 25 tests after removing that invocation override.


## Outcome: rejected

Five serial alternating A/B pairs on Node 24.22.1, 8 CPUs, 16,767,758,336 bytes RAM. Reported one-minute load ranged from 0.8 to 1.09. Same source, frozen dependencies, full SDK receipts, fresh Node process per sample.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate | Result |

| p95 warm entry point (sample maximum, n=5) | 5876.788 ms | 5603.821 ms | Pass |
| Median process CPU | 6.98 s | 7.01 s | 0.43% higher; fails no-regression rule |
| Median peak RSS | 537184 KiB | 537696 KiB | +0.10%; within bound |
| Existence probes (separate count run) | 102103 | 18293 | Reduced |
| Native realpath calls (separate count run) | 97609 | 106646 | Increased |

prs.title: fix: size Linux Gateways from their delegated memory limit
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Linux, a service can see only part of the cgroup hierarchy. The Gateway used its full process membership as a path below the visible mount. That could point at a sibling with a different limit, or leave the Gateway using host RAM for sizing.

## User Impact

Gateway automatic profile selection, worker admission and child-command budgets now use the service’s visible memory limits. A 768 MiB service can select the lean profile even when an unrelated cgroup has a 12 GiB limit. Operators can continue using their existing configuration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The memory reader now maps process membership to the visible cgroup2 mount once per lookup. It uses the same directory and file visibility rules for hard limits, reclaim thresholds, swap limits and ancestor pressure. Worker admission keeps sampling the cgroup that supplied its hard limit. The existing sizing fallback remains available when Linux permits controller reads but hides mount information.

## Evidence

- All 86 focused tests passed across host memory, Gateway profiles, worker budgets and child memory. On a simulated 16 GiB host, the real service and decoy limits were exchanged to verify both automatic profile choices.
- On Linux 6.6.141, the same read-only delegated mount exposed a 768 MiB service and a 3 GiB sibling. Stock reported the sibling’s 3 GiB hard limit, 2,816 MiB reclaim threshold and 128 MiB swap limit. The fix reported the service’s 768 MiB, 512 MiB and 32 MiB limits.
- Stock sampled the sibling at 8 KiB throughout. The fixed worker budget matched the service’s kernel working-set readings of 178,503,680 and 186,933,248 bytes. The child RAM allowance fell from 2,112 MiB to 128 MiB. Both revisions selected lean on the physical 7.65 GiB test host.
- A real nonrecursive bind hid a preexisting file mount. The earlier candidate lost the hard limit in this layout. The final revision read the visible 768 MiB cap. [Linux test run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45909755287)

- Local ClawSweeper reviewed the final committed range and reported zero findings.

prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/202818

## What Problem This Solves

The Android settings assistant records skipped question IDs separately even though the same admitted request already retires every current question. Both the UI and controller check the two sets together, so the extra state and private argument have no separate behavior to own.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. Skipped and answered questions still disappear immediately, cannot be submitted again, and stay retired after a failed reply. Restarting the conversation shows its fresh questions normally. Access checks, captured routes, request payloads and secret handling are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing retired-question set as the single owner. Remove the duplicate dismissal set, its private request argument/update, and redundant checks in the controller and screen. Neither set is persisted, so no data migration is needed.

Production code shrinks by five lines and loses one state collection. Tests grow by 72 lines to replace the old dismissal-field assertion with held-reply and post-reply RPC checks plus one real settings UI flow. The tests reuse existing fixtures; no production test hook is added.

## Evidence

- Reviewed head `0c40d580f83233e0da2e71ea10be7860eda6dcf0`, based on `7f3bd14b7f7ec681b58076addfc14024223b08d4`.
- Original production passed the strengthened 13 controller tests and new UI flow in both phone flavors. The UI flow skips, answers a fresh question, observes a failed reply, then restarts and sees another fresh question.
- Candidate proof passed 18 tests per flavor: all 13 controller tests plus five UI cases covering the new flow, three question-retirement viewport cases and restart. There were no failures/errors/skips. Play proof preceded a formatter-only line-wrapping correction; that diff was inspected and its behavior proof reused. Final third-party proof and Kotlin lint passed after formatting.
- Both phone Kotlin compiles, the staged-content guard and unchanged native-string inventory passed. Local proof used the exact candidate Android source with matching build inputs over retained frozen root tooling; current-head PR CI supplies the broader gate.
- Independent source review and local ClawSweeper review of the complete committed range found no actionable correctness or security issues.
- No physical-device, live Gateway or performance run was performed for this redundant in-memory state removal.

## Delivery

Current-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45911100427) passed. The reviewed head `0c40d580f83233e0da2e71ea10be7860eda6dcf0` merged as `9fc8273647739775a2fe91b5745d613311d89083`. [Native completion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206229#issuecomment-7205900090) is verified. The generated PR checkout is removed; the authored source and shared proof checkout are retained.

prs.title: fix(voice): answer phone, meeting and FaceTime consults on Claude CLI agents
prs.body:
Closes #202208

Related: #188440, #161885, #164229, #199379, #199378; supersedes closed #191683.

## What Problem This Solves

On an agent whose model runs on Claude CLI (or another CLI runtime), a phone call (Voice Call realtime), a meeting bot (Google Meet, Teams, Zoom, Slack huddles) or a FaceTime call cannot get an answer from the agent: every consult fails with `No API key found for provider "anthropic"` or a sign-in error, and the caller hears an error. Typed messages and Discord voice to the same agent work.

## User Impact

User impact: phone, meeting and FaceTime voice consults run on the agent's own runtime, including Claude CLI and its configured fallbacks, like a typed message. Embedded-runtime agents keep working. Tool policy is unchanged: callers and meeting participants are guests, FaceTime owners stay owners, and a phone consult's `voice_call` can still only end the current call.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared helper `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` always ended in `runEmbeddedAgent` with an explicit provider/model, which calls the provider API directly and never selects the agent's runtime. Discord voice works because it runs a normal agent turn through `runCommandFromIngress`.

- `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` gains `runner: "agent-turn"`: after the helper prepares the consult session (fork from the requester, lineage, delivery fields, lifecycle admission), the consult runs as a turn of that session through `runCommandFromIngress` with `deliver: false`. Prompt building, timeout, cancellation, `onRunStarted`, speakable-text extraction and yield acknowledgements are unchanged. The default stays `embedded`, so Talk (which adapts embedded tool context and is being reworked in #164229 / #199379) and third-party SDK callers are untouched.
- Voice Call, meeting-bot and FaceTime opt in. Voice Call passes a model override only when `responseModel` is configured and a thinking override only when `realtime.consultThinkingLevel` is set; otherwise the session's own selection applies. Meeting consults no longer force thinking `high`; they use the session default. A level a bridge does pass (FaceTime always asks for `off`, Voice Call passes `realtime.consultThinkingLevel`) is a one-run choice: a model without that level runs at its closest one, as on the embedded runner (`8711c7b5a`, below).
- Plugin ingress (`runCommandFromIngress` wrapper): a plugin may omit `messageChannel` for a turn on its own surface. Owner authority still needs a bundled or trusted official plugin, and a named channel must still be the plugin's own. `toolBindings` are accepted only for tools the plugin declares in `contracts.tools`. **This widens the plugin ingress capability** (previously only channel plugins could admit turns); it stays narrower than `runEmbeddedAgent`, which any plugin can already call with an owner bit. Flagging for SDK/security owner review.
- The Claude CLI path carries `toolBindings` from the command attempt into the MCP loopback grant, as the embedded runner already does, so `voice_call` stays bound to the live call.
- Voice Call runs the consult in its service context so Gateway-dispatched tools such as `sessions_send` work from webhook handlers.

Not changed: the Voice Call classic (non-realtime) responder (#188440), Talk's Gateway consult path (#164229 / #199379), Discord voice.

## Follow-up fix found by the meeting/FaceTime e2e (`8711c7b5a`)

The first FaceTime e2e (a stand-in plugin with FaceTime's consult parameters, `evidence-e2e-surfaces-red-503beb2ae.log`) failed on `503beb2ae`: FaceTime passes `thinkLevel: "off"`, and on the agent-turn route the command's model selection rejects an explicit level the model lacks, so every FaceTime consult on `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` failed with `Thinking level "off" is not supported for anthropic/claude-opus-5-5. A persistent `/think` override and other callers still get the error. ## Follow-up fix found while tracing a Google Meet e2e failure (`7f72cb5c7`)

Plugin `runEmbeddedAgent` runs its turn as a detached work continuation ("plugin turns can outlive both the triggering request root and its async work scope"); plugin `runCommandFromIngress`, which this PR's agent-turn route uses, did not. A meeting's realtime bridge is opened inside the `googlemeet.join` request, so a consult that reaches the command queue after the request that started it has ended lost its admission with `Gateway is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.`, where the embedded route kept going. `runCommandFromIngress` now runs its turn as a detached continuation, the same way (`src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent.ts`, one wrap). Test: `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent.ingress-continuation.test.ts` (an ingress turn that starts after its parent root and async scope ended), red on `8711c7b5a` with `GatewayDrainingError` at `enqueueCommandInLane` ← `runtime-agent.ts`, green after (`evidence-unit-ingress-continuation-7f72cb5c7.md`); the PR's test-lines allocation goes from 13 to 69 for it. A consult whose tool call itself arrives after that request ended still fails one step earlier, at `beginSessionEffect`, on `main` too; see "Pre-existing" under Evidence.

### Proof status: meeting callback path is blocked by a known bug on `main`

On this PR alone, as on `main`, a meeting consult that arrives through the normal provider callback cannot complete, because of a known bug on `main` that this PR does not touch: a realtime voice consult issued from a callback runs under the already-released root of the request that opened the call (`googlemeet.join` / `googlemeet.create`), and `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` → `beginSessionEffect` refuses it with `GatewayDrainingError` ("Gateway is temporarily unavailable" / "Gateway is draining") before any runner is chosen. It fails the same way on the embedded route on `main`.

- Reported in #142610 (meeting, Google Meet) and #202915 (FaceTime).
- Fixed by #202979 (fresh root admission inside `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent`, covers every voice bridge) and, for meetings only, #142692. Both are open and waiting on maintainers.
- This PR only changes what happens after admission (which runner executes the consult), so it neither causes nor fixes that refusal. Once #202979 (or #142692) lands, the normal meeting callback reaches this PR's agent-turn route unchanged. This is shown below: with #202979 applied **temporarily** on top of `7f72cb5c7` (throwaway local branch, never pushed, not part of this PR), a meeting consult delivered through the normal provider callback after `googlemeet.join` returned was answered by the real Claude CLI; the same run on `7f72cb5c7` alone is refused at `beginSessionEffect` ("Meeting through the normal provider callback").

The meeting callback entry is shown too, with the separate fix applied temporarily; without that fix it stays blocked by the bug above, not by this change.

The Beam test, handler, state lifecycle, and test runner files are unchanged between scheduled `main` revision `e80be914` and the PR CI tested base `79e42e0`. This is a test module lifecycle failure exposed by file order; the production lifecycle guard remains in place.
- MCP archive final effect: [PR job 139002954288](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45554107749/job/139002954288) failed the `profile-revoked` assertion at line 144 because the archive completed. The test passes alone on local `main`, so the failure is sensitive to its run context.

The PR CI report calls both jobs `unknown` because the latest scheduled `main` run had no matching job names, so it did not compare test signatures. The evidence above identifies the matching failures without claiming the PR CI passed. The required maintainer security approval for this revision is still pending.
