prs.title: fix(update): settle plugin version warnings after convergence
prs.body:
Closes #205312

## What Problem This Solves

On the shipped in-place update path, post-install Doctor can see the older official npm plugins before the same update converges them. Its earlier version-drift findings then remain in the completed update's attention summary, asking users to perform an upgrade that already happened.

## User Impact

Users no longer receive stale plugin-version repair instructions for upgrades completed by the same run. Plugins that still need an update, unavailable targets, migration advisories, and unrelated Doctor findings remain visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

The candidate uses the existing shipped-parent plugin-convergence promise to describe pending npm cohort upgrades as provisional information during the package swap. The legacy finalization and resume paths also settle individual earlier version findings against the final confirmed version, including warning rows recorded before resume.

A later Doctor repair is credited only when the committed install record and the installed package version agree. Package-version settlement is independent of pending data migrations. Final mismatch advisories are a fallback when a more specific finding already exists. The owned-install release path already performs plugin maintenance before its advisory checks; this change addresses the compatibility bridge used by published in-place updaters.

## Evidence

- Red on base `8aace0e00`: two package-swap Doctor receipt regressions and the shipped-parent resume regression failed before the fix.
- Focused Vitest: 64 passed across version-drift, workspace status, post-core convergence, deferred warnings, post-plugin readiness and resume completion at `cb643dd4b`. The full resume suite (12 tests) also passed at the final head after removing the fixture-only assertion requested in review.
- Core/scoped TypeScript, lint, formatting, line-cap and assertion-safety checks passed at `cb643dd4b`; final-head scoped test TypeScript, lint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed. `pnpm build:runtime` and candidate tarball integrity checks passed at the final head.

### Real managed Gateway and persisted-state proof

Built and packed exact head [32636db2e](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205491/commits/32636db2ef587cd1eb95ff03b659b1cb33200d38) (candidate version `2026.11.10`; SHA-256: `6c28d7d9a5d2fb59afeb73c630d128a56b5dd8e8bf743130f3ee1088f0709188`). All three runs used Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (arm64), Node 24.22.3, and an actual registered `openclaw-gateway.service` managed by `systemd --user`. The updater performed the service transition; no service shim or `--no-restart` was used. Before the first upgrade, an actual Gateway session, a synthetic chat-history marker, a workspace file, and the three official npm plugins were present. Control and patched runs started from the same consistent pre-upgrade snapshot.

| Real upgrade | Updater / persisted run | Gateway service state (PID before → after) | Matching actionable version warnings in post-swap Doctor | Completed stale warning rows | Stale warnings in saved report |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Published 2026.10.10 → published 2026.11.10 (control) | ok / succeeded | active (819) → active (5046) | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| Published 2026.10.10 → candidate | ok / succeeded | active (10132) → active (14033) | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Published 2026.11.10 → candidate (existing-state compatibility) | ok / succeeded | active (5046) → active (8574) | 0 | 0 | 0 |

In both older-release upgrades, `codex`, `groq` and `tokenjuice` were loaded at 2026.10.10 before the run, all converged to 2026.11.10, and all were loaded afterward. The published control recorded all three actionable version-drift messages in its post-swap Doctor warning receipt; the patched run recorded none, even though the same three plugins still required and completed convergence. The provisional-information classification is covered by the Doctor receipt regression tests. The patched completed run and saved report contained zero of the three obsolete repair instructions. Both older-release runs completed their post-plugin Doctor and readiness checks with exit 0. Subsequent standalone Doctor lint checks contained zero matching diagnostics; this counts only the reported version warnings.

**Stored-data compatibility:** The latest-stable run used the real state from the successful published control upgrade, including its persisted update history. The Gateway switched from the published build ID to the exact candidate build ID. Calls to `update.runs.get` before and after returned the same prior successful run (same status, before/after versions and step array), and the new completed run was readable. The original session ID and chat-history marker were still returned by `chat.history`. Gateway mode, bind, port, auth mode and auth credential, workspace setting and file content were preserved. The existing disabled automation remained disabled and retained its ID.

<details>

Commands: the published control used `openclaw update --tag 2026.11.10 --yes --json --timeout 600`; both candidate runs used the same command with `--tag [candidate tarball]`. prs.title: fix(logging): keep completed turn timings out of warn
prs.body:
Part of #200438

## What Problem This Solves

With reply profiling enabled, every slow agent turn logs `agent turn timings ... outcome=completed` at WARN. Healthy completed turns dominate the warning stream and make real failures harder to spot.

A completed turn with one genuinely slow preparation stage still deserves a warning. A completed turn that only crosses the total-duration threshold, or only spends time in model and tool execution, does not.

## Why This Change Was Made

The agent timing tracker now sends completed turns to INFO unless one preparation stage crosses the same profiling threshold the shared timing tracker already uses. Spans that enclose model or tool execution (`model_fallback`, `embedded_run`, `cli_run`) are recorded with an explicit execution kind, so inference and tool time stays timing detail and cannot make a healthy turn a warning. Completed turns carrying an error and failed turns still log at WARN.

The 500 ms profiling threshold is exported from `reply-timing-tracker.ts` and reused here so the two paths cannot drift.

## User Impact

Operators who enable reply profiling keep the same timing detail at INFO. WARN stays meaningful for failed turns, completed turns with an error, and genuinely slow preparation.

No timing data or failure diagnostics are removed.

## Evidence

- Added table-driven coverage in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-timing-tracker.test.ts` for a healthy turn with real enclosing execution spans (INFO), slow preparation inside execution (WARN), completed with an error (WARN), and failed (WARN); the slow-stage case is retained.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/reply-timing-tracker.test.ts` — 15 passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental` passed.
- `oxfmt --check`, `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, and `git diff --check` pass on the changed files.

This covers the completed-turn timing part of #200438. The idle heartbeat and empty worktree cleanup summaries are separate changes.

## Real behavior proof

Setup: an isolated Gateway on loopback with a dedicated profile under a fresh temp `HOME`, token auth, no channels or real credentials, and a local deterministic OpenAI-compatible stub model. Reply profiling was enabled with `diagnostics.flags: ["reply.profiler"]`. The stub streams `OK` after a real 2000 ms delay, so `model_fallback` and `embedded_run` carry production execution durations. Turns were sent through `chat.send`, which reaches the reply runner (`runAgentFallbackCandidates`), not the separate `agent` RPC path. The base run used a detached worktree at `bd8ef06d^` with its own cloned `node_modules` and port 19648.

Commands:

```bash
# isolated Gateway on the fix working tree (run-node rebuilds dist from source)
HOME=<temp-home> node scripts/run-node.mjs --profile <profile> gateway run --port 19647 --bind loopback

# one reply-path turn
HOME=<temp-home> node scripts/run-node.mjs --profile <profile> gateway call chat.send \
  --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:proof-chat-healthy","message":"Reply with the single word OK.","idempotencyKey":"proof-healthy-fix-1","timeoutMs":120000}' \
  --json --timeout 30000

# base commit, same config and stub, separate worktree and port
HOME=<base-temp-home> node scripts/run-node.mjs --profile <base-profile> gateway run --port 19648 --bind loopback
```

Gateway logs below are projected from the raw JSON lines to `time`, `_meta.logLevelName`, and `message`; the raw lines carry the same level. Synthetic run/session IDs only; IPs, keys, phone numbers, and private endpoints are not present.

```text
# healthy profiled turn on the fix - INFO
2026-11-27T01:34:36.545+08:00 INFO agent turn timings runId=proof-healthy-fix-1 sessionId=bb59bed0-b618-43d3-aa4d-40dc03c247d9 sessionKey=agent:main:proof-chat-healthy outcome=completed totalMs=2185 stages=fallback_prepare_harness:0ms@6ms,fallback_resolve_runtime:0ms@7ms,embedded_run:2175ms@2184ms,model_fallback:2180ms@2185ms

# span details from the same raw line: execution spans are marked, preparation is not
spans=[{"name":"fallback_prepare_harness","durationMs":0,"elapsedMs":6},{"name":"fallback_resolve_runtime","durationMs":0,"elapsedMs":7},{"name":"embedded_run","durationMs":2175,"elapsedMs":2184,"kind":"execution"},{"name":"model_fallback","durationMs":2180,"elapsedMs":2185,"kind":"execution"}]

# same healthy turn on base bd8ef06d^ - WARN
2026-11-27T01:42:26.407+08:00 WARN agent turn timings runId=proof-healthy-base-1 sessionId=2ffff55b-ca97-4ed0-a79c-edf2233f22af sessionKey=agent:main:proof-chat-healthy-base outcome=completed totalMs=2959 stages=fallback_prepare_harness:0ms@10ms,fallback_resolve_runtime:0ms@119ms,embedded_run:2836ms@2957ms,model_fallback:2953ms@2959ms

# provider error (stub returns HTTP 500) on the fix - WARN
2026-11-27T01:37:15.982+08:00 WARN agent turn timings runId=proof-error-fix-1 sessionId=39b33da6-b16a-4086-a41e-5432b0b41629 sessionKey=agent:main:proof-chat-error outcome=error totalMs=82554 stages=fallback_prepare_harness:0ms@2ms,fallback_resolve_runtime:0ms@2ms,embedded_run:82547ms@82550ms,model_fallback:82552ms@82553ms error="⚠️ The AI service is having trouble. Please try again in a moment."
```

One-line results:

| Case | Level | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Healthy profiled turn (fix) | INFO | `model_fallback` 2180 ms and `embedded_run` 2175 ms with 0 ms preparation |
| Healthy profiled turn (base `bd8ef06d^`) | WARN | same 2 s stub and span composition, red before the fix |
| Slow preparation | WARN | focused production-composition test; no real Gateway configuration reaches it (see note) |
| Error turn | WARN | `outcome=error` from the stub provider 500 |

Slow-preparation note: in this Gateway path the only preparation spans that execute are `fallback_prepare_harness` (registered-harness check, 0 ms), `fallback_resolve_runtime` (in-memory config resolution, 0 ms), and `reply_media_context` (sync closure construction); `current_turn_images` is skipped because queue admission sets `currentTurnImagesPrepared`. None can be made to cross 500 ms through configuration or a local mechanism without editing product code, so a real Gateway capture of that case is not reachable. Instead, `reply-timing-tracker.test.ts` records the production composition (`model_fallback` enclosing `embedded_run`) with a preparation span over 500 ms and asserts WARN. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/reply-timing-tracker.test.ts` passes all 15 cases.

prs.title: fix: plugin reload points to a registry refresh when a load path overrides the installed plugin
prs.body:
Related: #205033

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a plugin is selected from `plugins.load.paths` and an installed package with the same ID exists, a plugin reload or other package maintenance fails with "has no authoritative package-owner metadata" and tells you to refresh the plugin registry and run Doctor. Neither step helps: the explicit load path keeps overriding the installed package, so the refusal repeats.

## User Impact

User impact: the refusal now says where the selected plugin is, that it comes from `plugins.load.paths`, which installed package it overrides, and the step that works: remove the `plugins.load.paths` entry that selects it, then retry. The refusal itself and load-path precedence are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ownership resolver already detects a config-selected plugin that shadows an install record for the same ID (the update path reports it as operator-managed). Package maintenance and reload still returned the generic missing-owner error, which points at the registry and Doctor. The resolver now returns a specific message for that case; every other ownership error is unchanged.

Not included, so this PR is linked as related rather than closing the issue: the issue also asks for the installed package version in the message and for an owner-reviewed, automatic config reconciliation. The message shows the plugin root rather than the exact configured entry, because a standalone-file entry selects its parent folder as the root.

## Evidence

- New test in `src/plugins/manifest-registry-installed.ownership.test.ts` runs the ownership check that plugin reload uses for a plugin selected from `plugins.load.paths` that shadows a same-ID install. On the base commit it returns the generic "has no authoritative package-owner metadata ... Refresh the plugin registry and run openclaw plugins doctor" message from the issue. With the fix it says where the plugin is, that it comes from `plugins.load.paths`, and which installed package it overrides. It is still a refusal.
- `pnpm test src/plugins/manifest-registry-installed.ownership.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 3/3 pass. The file takes about 24 seconds wall time locally with a warm transform cache (about 4.5 minutes cold); CI seconds to follow.
- The consumer tests that pin the existing ownership messages, `src/plugins/update-cohort.test.ts` and `src/plugins/management-service.uninstall-ownership.test.ts`, pass 23/23. Global-origin and ambiguous plugins keep their current messages.
- oxlint and the format check pass on the two changed files.
- Live reload on an isolated Gateway built from this branch (fdf55a13d, Node 26.10.0, own state dir and port). Fixture: a plugin `shadow-demo` 1.2.1 installed with `openclaw plugins install <path>`, and a 1.2.0 copy of the same ID selected through `plugins.load.paths`. Paths are throwaway `/tmp` folders.

```text
$ openclaw plugins list | grep shadow
│ Shadow Demo │ shadow-demo │ openclaw │ enabled │ /tmp/oc-proof-205467/dev/shadow-demo/index.js │ 1.2.0 │ record-missing │

$ openclaw plugins reload shadow-demo
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] Reason: Plugin "shadow-demo" at /tmp/oc-proof-205467/dev/shadow-demo comes from plugins.load.paths and overrides its installed package "shadow-demo". Refreshing the plugin registry keeps that override. To maintain the installed package, remove the plugins.load.paths entry that selects this plugin, then retry.

$ openclaw config unset plugins.load.paths
Removed plugins.load.paths. Change will apply without restarting the gateway.

$ openclaw plugins reload shadow-demo
shadow-demo: Selected entry: /tmp/oc-proof-205467/state/extensions/shadow-demo/index.js. Rebuild compiled output after source edits.
Reloaded plugin "shadow-demo" (generation 4).

$ openclaw plugins list | grep shadow
│ Shadow Demo │ shadow-demo │ openclaw │ enabled │ global:shadow-demo/index.js │ 1.2.1 │ origin-path │
```

  The table rows are trimmed to one line each. The same reload on a base build was not run live; the base message comes from the unit test above and the issue report.
- Not run: targeted typecheck (`tsgo` is not installed in this checkout) and local autoreview (not available here). Broad checks are left to PR CI.

prs.title: fix(doctor): source-checkout Gateway advice no longer demands replacement
prs.body:
Closes #205413

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor` detected a Gateway service running from a source checkout, but the same panel unconditionally told every operator to replace the service definition. A source-checkout service is a supported setup, so that advice pushed intentional installs toward an unnecessary repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

The source-checkout warning now keeps the resolved path visible and makes the replacement command conditional:

- No action is needed when the checkout is intentional.
- The force-install command is only suggested for operators who expected the service to use a different installation.

Entrypoint mismatch detection, audit findings, and repair behavior are unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators running a deliberate source checkout see an informational explanation instead of a repair instruction. Operators who actually need to switch installations still get the exact command and destination guidance.

## Evidence

- Updated the Gateway service config regression in `src/commands/doctor-gateway-services.test.ts`. It asserts the conditional wording and that no repair runs; the obsolete negative wording assertion was removed as requested.
- Focused Vitest after rebasing on `main`:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-gateway-services.test.ts` — 48 passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental` passed.
- `oxfmt --check`, `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, and `git diff --check` pass on the changed files.
- Real macOS launchd service proof below covers the shipped CLI path; the fixture remains the unit-level boundary.

## Real behavior proof

Scenario: a user-level macOS LaunchAgent intentionally runs `<checkout>/dist/index.js gateway --port 50935` from this source checkout. launchd loaded the job, `/health` returned 200, and Doctor read the real plist through launchd. The plist checksum was recorded before and after Doctor.

Setup: isolated canonical profile `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=proof205453`, state/config under `~/.openclaw-proof205453`, loopback port 50935, minimal config `{"gateway":{"mode":"local","port":50935,"bind":"loopback"}}`. The default `~/.openclaw` state was not used.

After-fix (PR head `7f7d4a962`):

```console
$ OPENCLAW_PROFILE=proof205453 pnpm openclaw gateway install --port 50935
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway install --port 50935
No gateway token found. Auto-generated one and saving to config.
Installed LaunchAgent: /Users/<user>/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.openclaw.proof205453.plist
...
$ OPENCLAW_PROFILE=proof205453 curl -s http://127.0.0.1:50935/health
{"ok":true,"status":"live"}

$ OPENCLAW_PROFILE=proof205453 pnpm openclaw doctor --non-interactive
...
◇  Gateway service config ───────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                                    │
│  Gateway service entrypoint resolves to a source checkout:         │
│  /Users/<user>/githubProject/openclaw/openclaw-pr/openclaw.        │
│  No action is needed if this is intentional. If you expected the   │
│  service to use a different installation, run `openclaw --profile  │
│  proof205453 gateway install --force` from that installation.      │
│                                                                    │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

Confirmed:
- Retained path: `/Users/<user>/githubProject/openclaw/openclaw-pr/openclaw` remains in the panel.
- Conditional advice: "No action is needed if this is intentional..." with the force-install command only for a different expected installation. The isolated profile adds `--profile proof205453` to the suggested command.

prs.title: fix(imessage): deliver persistent background-task announcements
prs.body:
Related: #196962.

## What Problem This Solves

Persistent background tasks can finish successfully yet fail to deliver their iMessage announcements with “iMessage message reference does not belong to the selected conversation.” An internal session-event ID can be inherited as a reply target despite not identifying a native message.

## User Impact

Tasks can retain their own history and deliver separate, top-level announcements when the account’s exclusive local Messages database proves the automatically inherited reply target does not exist. Native replies and explicit reply validation remain intact.

Remote or unavailable lookup evidence retains existing validation; this is not a blanket fallback on lookup failure. No core contract, configuration, or database schema change.

## Why This Change Was Made

This follows the channel-owned approach in these related adapter PRs:
- Discord: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196963
- Feishu: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177297
- Telegram: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200877

Unlike Discord snowflakes or Feishu message prefixes, native iMessage GUIDs can look exactly like synthetic UUIDs. Format rejection would break legitimate threading. Instead, the adapter carries existing implicit/explicit metadata through automatic-final and message-tool sends and uses its existing worker-backed lookup to distinguish absent messages from wrong-chat or unbound messages. Cross-account/chat references and explicit invalid anchors still reject.

No new cache or core policy is introduced. LEFT JOIN preserves existing messages without valid chat associations as mismatches, not missing messages. The existing send-result parser moves to the sibling message-ID module without behavior changes to respect the send-module growth ratchet.

Simplification pass: retained one authorization owner and existing lookup/cache machinery; no further reduction identified. Original adapter-change delta: 147 additions / 28 deletions across ten files, including 85 regression-test lines. The later routed-reply follow-up adds 9/removes 1 test lines in one additional file.

## Evidence

- Before: on 2026.11.5, a persistent scheduled execution succeeded but iMessage delivery failed with the conversation-binding error. The exact original failed reference was not recovered.
- Offline execution of extracted installed functions reproduced synthetic event-ID propagation with zero history. This is mechanism evidence, not a complete live baseline trace.
- A native-send regression failed before the fix at the observed rejection. Candidate tests exercise both registered adapter send paths with worker-backed SQLite and a mocked native send boundary, including native UUIDs, explicit invalid anchors, wrong-account/chat references, orphan/dangling bindings, unavailable lookup, and receipts.
- Release-based candidate: 65 focused tests passed; after parser extraction, all 38 send tests re-passed. Focused typecheck/lint/format, standalone plugin build and installed imports passed.
- Live release-based candidate after installation and restart: two successive runs in one task-private persistent session delivered through separate DM delivery—automatic final and message-tool send. Native Messages readback found exactly one labeled outgoing message each, both sent/delivered, error 0, and null thread-originator fields. Temporary automation was removed after successful delivery.
- Exact main-based head `dcbf14b14eb08649d726f4d7f8b875a89639acbb`: 64 focused tests across four files passed; formatting and diff checks passed. No 1Password changes.
- Prior independent agent review found a dangling-chat association edge; selecting the joined chat ROWID and a negative control addressed it. This was not ClawSweeper/autoreview, and is not claimed as a fresh review of this main-based range.

**Main-based qualification completed (2026-11-19):** an isolated detached checkout of exact head `dcbf14b14eb08649d726f4d7f8b875a89639acbb` received its own frozen-lockfile dependency install (`@openclaw/fs-safe@0.27.1`). Fresh SDK and package-boundary declarations, targeted iMessage production typecheck, targeted lint of all seven changed production TypeScript files, and standalone iMessage npm-runtime build passed. All 64 focused tests across four files re-passed in two shards (89.46s). Existing exact-head format/diff proof retained. The original checkout and installed runtime were not modified. This resolves the prior dependency/SDK qualification gap; broad PR CI and maintainer review remain outstanding.

**Earlier release-based live-proof limits (superseded for exact-head transition coverage by the capture below):** the live candidate was release-based, not this main-based head; tests used a DM rather than the original group/weather fixture, and recipient UI was not independently inspected. Native `reply_to_guid` values were populated and are not claimed null. There was no same-fixture live baseline/candidate A/B or wire-anchor trace. Ordinary human replies and explicit valid anchors have local coverage, not additional live sends. Raw household logs and private destinations are not published.


## Exact-head Gateway/native runtime transition capture — 2026-11-19

Captured on reviewed head `dcbf14b14eb08649d726f4d7f8b875a89639acbb`, built locally in an isolated checkout. Both runs used the same task-private persistent session and explicit, separate iMessage DM delivery.

**Real boundaries:** Gateway scheduler and session-event dispatch, registered automatic-final/message-tool paths, adapter authorization, worker-backed local Messages database lookup, native imsg RPC, and native database delivery readback. **Stand-in:** a deterministic loopback OpenAI-compatible model selected a final response or one message tool call. It did not provide a reply ID; the runtime inherited it. This is transport/runtime proof, not model-quality evidence.

The observation-only Node loader adds metadata logging to compiled modules in memory; files on disk and production source remain unchanged. No authorization result, arguments, return values, or native send are mocked/changed. Original and instrumented module hashes are below. Internal IDs and native GUIDs are SHA-256 hashes so the chain can be correlated without disclosing identifiers or destinations.

For each lane, the SAME event-ID hash appears at session-event creation, implicit adapter input, and `missing-implicit-anchor-dropped`. Native RPC then has no `reply_to`; its receipt GUID hash matches the exactly-one native message row marked sent/delivered with error=0. Both scheduler runs are delivered, without fallback; the tool lane records matching message-tool delivery. Native thread-originator fields are null.

Setup attempts are excluded from the successful trace: the initial run-scoped session was expired and generated one diagnostic failure-alert DM; a subsequent model fixture mismatch produced intentional silence. These were inspected before the corrected runs. No uncertain send was retried. The temporary automation was removed after delivery evidence; the isolated Gateway exited cleanly and the local model server stopped. Production Gateway remained running unchanged.

**Remaining limits:** recipient UI was not inspected; this uses a DM, not the original group/weather fixture. No identical-fixture baseline run is claimed. Prior release-based live observations remain separate historical evidence. The routed-reply consumer-test finding was subsequently addressed in `c2d22e2ac68` (test-only; production code is unchanged from this live capture).

prs.title: fix: retain Responses request JSON in debug captures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Debug capture could record a successful Responses request without its outgoing JSON. The Responses transport sends UTF-8 bytes, but the recorder accepted only strings and Buffers, so the request row had neither a preview nor a body blob.

## User Impact

When debug capture is enabled, the outgoing JSON is available for inspection, with registered secrets redacted. Capture remains opt-in. Network routing and SSRF checks are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Normalize only `Uint8Array` request bodies at the recorder boundary. The Buffer view uses the original byte offset and length, then follows the existing redaction, binary handling, preview limit, and blob persistence path. No new parser, setting, or storage path.

## Evidence

- The isolated guarded `POST /responses` regression returned HTTP 200 on the base but had a null preview and blob ID. With the fix, the exact JSON survives in both the preview and blob, including a multibyte character and excluding the surrounding backing-buffer bytes; the registered credential value becomes `[REDACTED]`.
- Guarded-fetch suite: 6 passed (7.25s Vitest duration, 42.23s including worker artifact preparation). Runtime and SQLite suites: 39 passed; async store: 2 passed. Core typecheck, focused lint and format, and the CLI runtime build passed.
- Isolated `agent --local` against a synthetic Responses server: `POST /v1/responses` returned 200 through guarded fetch. `proxy blob` returned 53,236 bytes of parseable outgoing JSON; the synthetic input marker was present and the saved authorization header was `[REDACTED]`.
- Local autoreview was attempted on the exact candidate (base `c818ae7ea0004`, candidate `689e155d94b2`, through P2). The installed Codex executable failed the read-only sandbox preflight; no independent local verdict was produced. Hosted review and exact-head checks are pending.

Credit: Hannes Rudolph (@hannesrudolph) provided the Studio reproduction.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/998d0b66-3535-4a5c-9d30-99cc1cdf7134)

## Worked on by

- @hannesrudolph

prs.title: refactor(update): remove unreachable Git database capture cleanup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Git runtime transaction still contains database-capture retirement code from the deleted in-place Git updater. Its sole current caller owns runtime directories and never attaches database captures.

## User Impact

Behavior-preserving cleanup of the maintainer source-update path.

## Why This Change Was Made

[The release cutover](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200578) removed the in-place Git runner and its `onTransaction` handoff. The remaining caller, `scripts/update-gateway-build.mts`, keeps the returned transaction local and only invokes rollback/completion.

Remove the unreachable database snapshot/PostgreSQL cleanup arm, its temporary result and self-reference. Return the existing guarded runtime-promotion cleanup directly. Runtime verification, rollback/completion memoization, ownership guards and filesystem-failure advisories stay with their current owner. Package updates retain their live capture lifecycle and shared transaction fields.

Production: +2/-34, net **−32 lines** in one file. Tests: unchanged. Pure internal refactor; changelog not required.

## Evidence

- Read the complete transaction owner, sole caller, promotion and script tests, shared contract and live package capture writers. Refreshed caller/field-write searches and the deletion history.
- Final local autoreview against `46ecbbe7dfcba93ba47856a7e2944133f7b6f254`: complete scoped-clean through P2, no findings (GPT-6.1 Sol). It executed no project code.
- Signed head `b26d1515f85f5321340802dc51b676a801dc8ab0` has the exact reviewed source blob. Native pre-commit formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Focused proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-runner-git-runtime.test.ts test/scripts-update-gateway-build.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **45 passed** (28 promotion tests, 17 script tests). No failing-baseline claim for an unreachable-code deletion.
- Targeted formatting, type-aware lint (`node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.json src/infra/update-runner-git-runtime.ts`) and `git diff --check` passed.
- Full `pnpm build` passed, including SDK declarations and UI artifacts, in the qualified native checkout. Final HEAD stayed `b26d1515f85f5321340802dc51b676a801dc8ab0`; tracked and untracked source stayed clean. The managed source checkout remains code-only.
- Configured remote proof refused missing organization selection before allocation; this trusted-source build used the documented qualified local fallback.
- [Exact-head ClawSweeper review passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205994#issuecomment-7195714696), with no actionable findings. Its optional focused-test/static-check/build rank-up move is now fulfilled; source has not changed since review.

Follow-up outside this transaction cleanup: the successful build emitted a nonfatal UI budget report (CSS 57.3 versus 56.9 KiB, chat boot requests 21 versus 20, boot JS 1306.4 versus 1305.0 KiB). No UI code changes or performance claim are included here.

Ready-PR [CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45848536869) on verified merge `9cc0cf744388a442ceca6159a8cbb854adcb103d` (main `115f229fee2396102820bcb6e92b693dc2ac3807` plus the unchanged signed head).

Landed by squash as [`27a9a1c537a4e926da4d646dc02d829ebd504873`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/27a9a1c537a4e926da4d646dc02d829ebd504873).

The cold-load capture CLI loads the session-row presentation graph before validating its arguments. The existing CI subprocess checks therefore load session and database code just to reject invalid capture flags.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Defer the existing literal session-row import until argument validation finishes, before creating artifacts or starting servers. The synchronous capture binding keeps using the same implementation. This is the cold-load follow-up to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206209 in the maintainer-requested CI cost audit.

## Evidence

- Base `fcc9a0648c288eb5c4d581af1aa83d907d82029c`; candidate `753bd3d615a1c2e23c730f90387ce0952f83a9e0`.

One comparison: the two cold-load cases fell from 19,107/18,258 ms to 2,439/2,258 ms. The unchanged warm-reload control was 6,654 → 6,222 ms. Whole command wall time was 48.09 → 14.74 s.

prs.title: fix(agents): release deleted agents’ catalog contexts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Deleting an agent releases its SQLite readers, but the gateway's shared catalog worker could keep that agent's unused workspace and plugin registrations. Creating and deleting agents with distinct workspaces accumulated catalog contexts in the same worker.

## User Impact

Deleting the last agent using a workspace releases that catalog context. Agents sharing a workspace keep their warm catalog and can still authenticate on the same worker. If a plugin still holds a native resource, deletion reports the cleanup failure and a retry keeps reporting it until the resource-owning worker exits.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog worker owns the registrations and knows which agents use each workspace. It now receives the deleted agent and directory identities through its existing resource-close transport. The worker fences that agent's active discovery, drains detached generations, and keeps each affected owner's cleanup receipt. Withdrawing a publication after degraded startup leaves a still-configured agent's catalog available.

## Evidence

Signed head `6635d815289917575d511b02660ab4fa41313bd1` (tree `dec63311`) preserves physical retirement, database fences and warm survivor payloads. It skips invalid SQLite JSON parses for unrelated resource keys. On POSIX it also skips full filesystem containment checks when an absolute module-cache key cannot contain the capture directory name. Positive native matches still require filesystem containment. File URL, Windows and failed-load handling keep their existing behavior. [Signed cache change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6635d815289917575d511b02660ab4fa41313bd1) · [Signed decoder change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/bdcaf22dedcb36c387ee0e027fc364652fe19e6d)

### Final snapshot-free timing

Five pairs used fresh Node 24.22.1 processes on one 32-vCPU AWS c7a.8xlarge, baseline `762aa006` first in each pair. Each process ran eight windows creating an agent, loading its catalog, retiring it, closing its SQLite readers and authenticating a surviving agent on the same worker. Each database revive ran outside the timed window. The driver removed heap snapshots, heap/RSS reads and telemetry polling. Both arms kept the same fixture marker writes, transfer counters and assertions. All ten processes and all 80 window rows passed. [Five-pair timing and transfer counts](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_287b1789e3ee646b85e7e2877b8b5296)

| Across eight windows | Baseline median | Final median | Median paired change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Total elapsed | 1,166.65 ms | 1,181.44 ms | +14.80 ms |
| Total process CPU | 2,848.36 ms | 2,889.82 ms | +39.99 ms |
| Retire phase elapsed | 5.55 ms | 22.78 ms | +17.56 ms |
| Retire phase process CPU | 10.59 ms | 38.40 ms | +32.02 ms |

Group medians rose **1.27% elapsed** and **1.46% process CPU**. Elapsed was higher in four of five pairs (differences −9.12 to +72.36 ms), CPU in three (−16.39 to +97.85 ms). All five paid more for retirement. Both arms sent eight compact survivor payloads and zero full survivor payloads per process. The candidate sent eight catalog-retirement requests and the baseline sent zero. Process CPU includes worker threads. Owner acceptance of the measured cost is pending. [Per-process results](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_287b1789e3ee646b85e7e2877b8b5296)

### Retained heap and physical cleanup

- In **one separate final-head process**, one worker retained one catalog context at all nine observations. V8 worker heap growth from cycle 0 to 8 was **4.620 MiB** after heap snapshots at 0, 4 and 8. The five earlier frozen baseline processes using that protocol retained nine contexts and grew a median **7.819 MiB**. The final process grew 2.765 MiB over cycles 0–4 and 1.856 MiB over cycles 4–8. The final sample's whole-process RSS grew 589.3 MiB with snapshots present. Field RSS and OOM incidence remain unmeasured. [Final retention process](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_6b63f2bb7b7c733efabfa3d687874153) · [Five frozen baseline measurements](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_d17b87d29ba0597dbf0e7c134247e1c3)
- A separate diagnostic observed the real CJS teardown. Every deletion had 176 cache keys and evicted two. The final version made two full containment calls per deletion. Earlier code considered all 176. Across eight deletions the cache scan took 7.97 ms before and 1.05 ms after. All eight capture directories were removed in both traces (6.19 and 6.49 ms). Each diagnostic used one process. Parent/worker, generation, instance and callback spans nest and cannot be added. [Before](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_1f12192267afefda952445b19f004822) · [After](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_b41838d8c8578d977268a0bc88418f73)
- Formatting and 66 tests passed in five affected files, including native module loading, retained-generation and captured-artifact cleanup, database dispatch and real catalog/SQLite deletion. The separate decoder regression failed on the preceding implementation, then its five-file suite passed 47 tests. The final signed cache delta and prior signed decoder delta each passed scoped P0–P2 review. [Final focused tests](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_9acd1a099ae08e9f3cf374e04f2b2d7d) · [Decoder regression](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_fac73f41d8a39e97e8a82f4ad4cf9b7e)
- **Residual heap comparison.** Two fresh Node 24.22.1 processes at `6635d815` declared the same 33-agent roster. One deleted eight agents and the other deleted 32. Each took one worker heap snapshot after its final SQLite revive, then read V8 heap statistics and a fresh catalog count. Both retained one context on the original worker. Worker heap measured **93.342 MiB** after eight and **94.552 MiB** after 32, a **1.210 MiB** difference. Both recorded exactly 7,647,761 external bytes. Each deletion completed its catalog and SQLite close and revive, and the survivor authenticated with a compact payload every time. One observation at each length cannot establish a slope, a plateau or the owner of the remaining difference. In the earlier five pairs with intermediate probes, baseline medians were +4.255 MiB over cycles 0–4 and +3.565 MiB over cycles 4–8. The decoder-only head measured +2.768 and +1.850 MiB over the same intervals. [Final endpoints](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_1dc3c8a405d91feac560e4c875f6bb2f) · [Earlier intermediate probes](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_d17b87d29ba0597dbf0e7c134247e1c3)

- **Cost of eight retirements.** A separate instrumented process spent 16.123 ms in worker retirement, including 15.734 ms awaiting generation release. The 32 module cleanup callbacks consumed 9.230 ms in total. Eight physical directory removals took 6.591 ms, and clearing the module cache took 0.970 ms. Those times overlap. Classifying the eight idle close messages took 0.225 ms. Eight already-settled numeric waits took 0.274 ms and their deadline callbacks never fired. The eight idle heap samples took 0.181 ms with `process.memoryUsage()` and 0.052 ms with the Node V8 API. Canonicalizing the eight newly created agents' directory paths took 0.222 ms. These results leave the published five-pair elapsed and CPU comparison unchanged. [Instrumented worker run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_79861b5976722620fbb36379e8517174)

### Final CI and review

All 85 jobs finished on signed head `6635d815`. The aggregate failed on one lint error in `prepared-model-runtime.configured-catalog.ts:120:53`. The checkout was merge `59fcd9ca`, with main parent `cab8e5ac` and PR parent `6635d815`. The scheduled-main classifier returned `unknown` because its selected scope differed. Main PR #206003 had already failed on the same line and `oxc(no-map-spread)` diagnostic. The source, lint configuration, wrapper, package manifest, lockfile and CI workflow were identical on the tested merge and its main parent. The security job passed. [Final CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45856226454/job/140047209182) · [Final lint job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45856226454/job/140037999501) · [Introducing main PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206003) · [Earlier identical lint failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45848357487/job/140010916889)

The superseded decoder-only CI run had a Bun failure in `joins managed reload acquisition during Gateway close`; its cause remains unknown. On this final head the Bun job ran that exact case and passed in 10.879 seconds. [Prior Bun job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45853448745/job/140026519194) · [Final Bun job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45856226454/job/140036290703)

Exact-head review found zero code defects. Its before-merge checklist calls for the catalog performance owner's decision on the measured increases. We deferred the optional full Gateway `agents.delete` RPC and surviving model turn. The current tests exercise physical worker and SQLite cleanup, retry behavior and survivor authentication. The full Gateway scenario remains a follow-up. [Exact-head review and rank-up list](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203841#issuecomment-7088681681)

<summary>Prior revisions, conflict repair and benchmarks with intermediate probes</summary>

Signed conflict repair `224cc157cbf422f211228018d129358a08c2ecc7` (tree `839f270545bb4bc75d88cb864ff8621fd0a40534`) incorporates main `762aa006`. The manual resolution joins the catalog-worker and runtime-auth imports. It preserves the deletion-retirement test and main’s full-catalog auth retention and closed borrowed snapshot tests. The combined production worker is byte-for-byte the measured implementation plus main’s two auth-refresh changes. prs.title: fix(ci): retain parent samples in timing refit reports
prs.body:
Related: #198212

## What Problem This Solves

A timing refit can fail planner admission while its report shows only final timing medians. Operators cannot see which complete generations supplied each parent estimate, or distinguish them from incomplete generations.

## User Impact

The existing refit report now includes per-run generation counts, summed child durations, and the resulting run-level parent sample for changed parent timings. Scheduling weights, test coverage, job limits, and publication admission remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The aggregation owner already computes these values. Retaining its observations avoids a second interpretation of the timing logs. Rows are sorted and limited to changed parent keys; incomplete generations have no parent contribution. Samples are explicitly labeled as preceding cross-run filtering.

## Evidence

- The new sampler regression failed on the base because the report omitted provenance, then passed with the fix. It verifies duplicate-log collapse, complete/incomplete generations, direct-parent precedence, and the unchanged 410-second fixture estimate.
- Seven focused sampler/aggregation cases passed, covering selected PR inputs, provider separation, duplicate run fragments, and deterministic output.
- Scoped formatting, lint, tooling-test typecheck, and whitespace checks passed.
- Full committed-range ClawSweeper review: base `ec97b6c07631669a7a7677f27ab2dca9e511378b`, head `3086b927ec9d6e27992e53134ac2c0d8c0a3b9a3`; no actionable findings, security cleared. The reviewer inspected source; execution evidence is separate above.

This is a diagnostic change. It does not make #198212's timing dataset admissible, and no CI runtime or cost savings are claimed. Natural refit output will be observed after landing.

prs.title: fix(secrets): route auth-profile SecretRefs to the store they were discovered in, not always the agent DB
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #143262 (P1, `impact:security`). `secrets apply` — and the configure planner that feeds it — resolved every auth-profile SecretRef target to the
per-agent auth-profile database and ignored `auth.sharedStore`. With a shared store configured, writing a credential for a shared auth profile silently
landed the SecretRef in the agent-scoped DB: the command reported success while the shared store the rest of the runtime reads from stayed empty, which
surfaces later as auth-provider failures that look like a missing credential.

The planner now carries an explicit store owner for every auth-profile candidate — `authProfileStore: "shared"` for shared-store targets, absent for the
legacy agent database — candidate ordering and labels derive from that owner, and apply routes each SecretRef to the store the target was discovered from
instead of defaulting to the agent DB.

## Evidence

- `src/secrets/plan.ts`, `src/secrets/configure-plan.ts` — candidates carry the discovered store owner; ordering and labels include it.
- `src/secrets/apply.ts` — apply routes by that owner; a shared-store target is written to the shared DB and an agent target still goes to the agent DB.
- Suites (`--maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism`, at head `33fff93ea86` rebased on `main` `3943149f8ac`):
  - `src/secrets/apply.test.ts src/secrets/configure-plan.test.ts src/secrets/configure.test.ts src/secrets/plan.test.ts src/secrets/configure.output.test.ts`
    → `Tests 63 passed | 3 failed (66)`
  - `src/secrets/apply.test.ts` alone on a second run → `Tests 38 passed | 2 failed (40)`
  - Every failure is a Windows temp-directory teardown lock (`EBUSY: resource busy or locked, unlink …openclaw.sqlite` / `ENOTEMPTY: rmdir`), with zero
    assertion failures, and the failing set differs between runs. Both affected tests exist on `main` and are not part of this change.
- Surface: 9 files, +501/−75; no new dependencies.

Closes #143262

---

# PR #144065 — real CLI evidence: `configure → apply → audit` cleans the selected shared row and leaves agent-local credentials alone

- Repo: `openclaw/openclaw`, worktree `D:/code/wt-oc-143262`, branch `fix/oc-143262-descr`.
- HEAD under test: `249dd45e2692` (PR change itself = `33fff93ea86` "fix(secrets): route explicit shared auth-profile targets to the shared state database").
- Isolation: `OPENCLAW_HOME` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` point at `%LOCALAPPDATA%/Temp/ocproof-144065/{home,state}`. The real user profile is never touched.
- Discipline: no `git push`, no PR edit, no repo file added. Worktree restored and left clean:
  `git status --porcelain` → *empty* (verified after both legs).

Claim under test (ClawSweeper): *"does not show this branch's real configure → apply → audit flow cleaning the selected shared row while preserving agent-local credentials."*

## 1. What is real, what is synthetic

**Real:**
- The CLI is the repo's own entrypoint, not a test harness:
  `node --import file:///D:/code/wt-oc-143262/scripts/tsx.mjs D:/code/wt-oc-143262/src/entry.ts secrets …`
  (same entry as `dist/entry.js`; banner `OpenClaw 2026.9.3 (249dd45)`).
- `secrets configure` runs **interactively under a real PTY** (winpty), so the real `@clack/prompts` option list, the real `Secret source` / `Provider alias` / `Secret id` / `Configure another credential?` prompts and the real preflight all execute. Keystrokes sent: `j` (down), `Enter`, `n`.
- `secrets apply --from` and `secrets audit` are plain non-interactive CLI runs.
- Both auth stores are **real SQLite databases** with **real rows**; the row-level dumps are read straight out of the DB files with `node:sqlite`.
- The plan JSON is produced by the CLI's own `configure` (`--plan-out`) and consumed by `apply`.

**Synthetic (fixture only):**
- The initial state is seeded by `%LOCALAPPDATA%/Temp/ocproof-144065/seed-fixture.ts` (scratch, not in the repo) using the repo's own writers: `writePersistedAuthProfileStoreRaw` (shared row + agent row) and `writeConfigMachineState("auth.sharedStore", {location:"state-db"})` — the exact key/value the shipped `shared-auth-store-state-db` doctor migration commits (`src/infra/state-migrations.shared-auth-store.ts`).
- Credential values are marker strings (`…-PLAINTEXT-144065`), not real secrets. No provider, gateway or network call is exercised; the SecretRef target is the built-in `env` provider.
- Flags used, and why: `--skip-provider-setup` (env/store providers are built in, so no provider config is needed) and `--json` (suppresses the interactive "apply this plan now?" confirm so that `apply` is a separate, observable CLI step). `CODEX_API_KEY` as the suggested env id is the CLI's own suggestion for this `openai` profile.

## 2. Fixture (re-seeded fresh for each leg)

| store | row | value before |
|---|---|---|
| shared (canonical state DB `state/state/openclaw.sqlite`, `authProfiles.store`) | `openai:shared` | plaintext `OPENAI-SHARED-SELECTED-PLAINTEXT-144065` ← **selected for migration** |
| shared (same row) | `google:untouched` | plaintext `GOOGLE-SHARED-UNTOUCHED-PLAINTEXT-144065` ← **not selected** |
| agent-local (`state/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`, `auth_profile_store`) | `anthropic:local` | plaintext `ANTHROPIC-AGENT-LOCAL-PLAINTEXT-144065` ← **must survive** |

## 3. Rerunnable steps

```
%LOCALAPPDATA%/Temp/ocproof-144065/
  seed-fixture.ts      # writes the fixture above (repo writers, real SQLite)
  dump-dbs.ts          # row-level dump of both databases (node:sqlite, read-only)
  run-configure.py     # PTY driver: real `openclaw secrets configure` prompt flow
  flow.sh after        # reset+seed → audit → configure → apply → audit → dump
  flow.sh before       # same, with configure limited to the candidate list
  flow-before.sh       # git checkout 33fff93ea86~1 -- <4 PR files>; flow.sh before; restore
  logs/{after,before}/ # full transcripts and outputs (see §6)
```

The three CLI commands under test (after leg):

```
node --import "file:///D:/code/wt-oc-143262/scripts/tsx.mjs" D:/code/wt-oc-143262/src/entry.ts \
  secrets configure --skip-provider-setup --json --plan-out <scratch>/plan-after.json
node --import … src/entry.ts secrets apply --from <scratch>/plan-after.json --json
node --import … src/entry.ts secrets audit
```

## 4. AFTER (branch HEAD `249dd45e2692`)

Interactive `configure` — real rendered option list (raw transcript excerpt):

```
!  Shared auth-profile store has 2 plaintext credential(s). Select a shared-store candidate below
   to migrate it with an explicit shared owner. Run `openclaw secrets audit` to review them.
*  Select credential field
|  > profiles.anthropic:local.key (auth profile, agent main) (auth profile store)
|    profiles.anthropic:local.token (auth profile, agent main)
|    profiles.google:untouched.key (auth profile, shared store)
|    profiles.google:untouched.token (auth profile, shared store)
|    profiles.openai:shared.key (auth profile, shared store)
|    profiles.openai:shared.token (auth profile, shared store)
|    Create auth profile mapping
*  Secret source / * Provider alias (default) / * Secret id (CODEX_API_KEY)
*  Configure another credential?   →  No
```

Plan written by the CLI (`plan-after.json`, target only), preflight included in the same output:

```json
{ "type": "auth-profiles.api_key.key", "path": "profiles.openai:shared.key",
  "pathSegments": ["profiles","openai:shared","key"],
  "ref": { "source": "env", "provider": "default", "id": "CODEX_API_KEY" },
  "agentId": "main", "authProfileStore": "shared", "authProfileProvider": "openai" }
…
"preflight": { "mode": "dry-run", "changed": true,
  "changedFiles": ["…\\ocproof-144065\\state\\state\\openclaw.sqlite"],
  "checks": { "resolvability": true, "resolvabilityComplete": true } }
```

`secrets apply --from plan-after.json --json`:

```json
{ "mode": "write", "changed": true,
  "changedFiles": ["C:\\Users\\Administrator\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\ocproof-144065\\state\\state\\openclaw.sqlite"],
  "checks": { "resolvability": true, "resolvabilityComplete": true }, "refsChecked": 1 }
```

→ writes the **canonical shared state DB**, not the agent DB. (Human-mode run renders `Secrets applied. Updated 1 file(s).`; see `logs/run1-human-after/4-apply.txt`.)

`secrets audit` before → after:

```
before: plaintext=3 … state\state\openclaw.sqlite:profiles.openai:shared.key   PLAINTEXT_FOUND
        plaintext=3 … state\state\openclaw.sqlite:profiles.google:untouched.key PLAINTEXT_FOUND
        plaintext=3 … state\agents\main\agent\openclaw-agent.sqlite:profiles.anthropic:local.key PLAINTEXT_FOUND
after : plaintext=2 … (the openai:shared finding is gone; the other two remain by design)
```

Row-level dump after (verbatim from `logs/after/6-after-dump.txt`):

```
canonical state DB  openai:shared     = {type: api_key, provider: openai,
                                         keyRef: {source: env, provider: default, id: CODEX_API_KEY}}   ← plaintext `key` cleaned
                    google:untouched  = {type: api_key, provider: google, key: GOOGLE-SHARED-UNTOUCHED-PLAINTEXT-144065}  ← untouched
agent-local DB      anthropic:local   = {type: api_key, provider: anthropic, key: ANTHROPIC-AGENT-LOCAL-PLAINTEXT-144065} ← byte-identical
```

## 5. BEFORE (same four PR source files at `33fff93ea86~1`)

`git checkout 33fff93ea86~1 -- src/secrets/{apply,configure,configure-plan,plan}.ts`, same fixture, same CLI:

`configure` candidate list — the shared rows are **not offered at all**:

```
!  Shared auth-profile store has 2 plaintext credential(s). `secrets configure` edits the selected
   agent's local store only and cannot migrate shared credentials. Run `openclaw secrets audit` …;
   a shared-store SecretRef migration path is tracked separately.
*  Select credential field
|  > profiles.anthropic:local.key (auth profile, agent main) (auth profile store)
|    profiles.anthropic:local.token (auth profile, agent main)
|    Create auth profile mapping
```

No plan can be generated for the shared row, so the pre-fix leg is applied **the plan the branch's own configure produced** (same operator intent):

`secrets apply --from plan-after.json --json`:

```json
{ "mode": "write", "changed": true,
  "changedFiles": ["C:\\Users\\Administrator\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\ocproof-144065\\state\\agents\\main\\agent\\openclaw-agent.sqlite"],
  "checks": { "resolvability": true, "resolvabilityComplete": true }, "refsChecked": 1 }
```

→ the SecretRef is written to the **agent-scoped** database while the command reports success.

`secrets audit` after apply: `plaintext=3` — unchanged; the shared `openai:shared` plaintext is still reported.

Row-level dump after (verbatim from `logs/before/6-after-dump.txt`):

```
canonical state DB  openai:shared     = {type: api_key, provider: openai, key: OPENAI-SHARED-SELECTED-PLAINTEXT-144065} ← NOT cleaned
agent-local DB      anthropic:local   = {…key: ANTHROPIC-AGENT-LOCAL-PLAINTEXT-144065}                                ← preserved, but…
                    openai:shared     = {type: api_key, provider: openai, keyRef: {env/default/CODEX_API_KEY}}       ← new agent-scoped row written
```

## 6. Two-sided difference

| observation | BEFORE (`33fff93ea86~1`) | AFTER (HEAD `249dd45e2692`) |
|---|---|---|
| shared-store rows offered by `configure` | none | `google:untouched`, `openai:shared` (label `… (auth profile, shared store)`) |
| plan for the shared row | impossible to select | `profiles.openai:shared.key`, `authProfileStore: "shared"` |
| `apply --json` changedFiles | `state\agents\main\agent\openclaw-agent.sqlite` | `state\state\openclaw.sqlite` |
| selected shared row after flow | still plaintext `key` | `keyRef {env/default/CODEX_API_KEY}`, no `key` |
| agent-local DB after flow | 2 rows (original + wrongly added shared ref) | 1 row, byte-identical to the fixture |
| `secrets audit` plaintext count | 3 → 3 | 3 → 2 |

Raw evidence (both legs, unedited): `%LOCALAPPDATA%/Temp/ocproof-144065/logs/after/` and `…/logs/before/`
(`0-seed`, `1-before-dump`, `2-before-audit`, `3-configure.txt` + `3-configure-transcript.txt`, `3b-plan.json`,
`4-apply.txt`, `5-after-audit.txt`/`.json`, `6-after-dump.txt`). Human-mode apply/audit runs from the first
pass are kept in `logs/run1-human-{after,before}/`.

## 7. Conclusion

The branch's own `configure → apply → audit` flow routes the selected shared auth-profile SecretRef into the canonical shared state DB (shared row cleaned, audit finding disappears), leaves the unselected shared row and the agent-local credential row byte-identical, whereas the pre-fix sources cannot select the shared row at all and instead write the ref into the agent-scoped DB while leaving the shared row plaintext.

### Re-ran by the author

Both legs re-run by hand on this branch (`249dd45e2692`), isolated scratch home, real CLI PTY:

```
$ bash flow.sh after
plan:   profiles.openai:shared.key (auth profile, shared store)   -> apply: changedFiles = state/state/openclaw.sqlite
shared DB   : openai:shared -> keyRef{source:env,id:CODEX_API_KEY}   (plaintext cleared)   google:untouched unchanged
agent-local : anthropic:local unchanged (byte-identical)
audit plaintext 3 -> 2

$ bash flow-before.sh          # four PR source files at 33fff93ea86~1, restored on exit
configure: no shared candidate ("cannot migrate shared credentials")
apply    : plan written into state/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite -> an extra openai:shared row pollutes the
           agent-local store; the shared row keeps its plaintext key; audit stays 3
git status --porcelain after restore: (clean)
```

---

### Revision `372c72240ef` - findings addressed + rebased onto current main

- **P1 shared plans are now rejectable by older readers.** Shared targets emit `protocolVersion: 2`; agent-local plans stay at revision 1. The validator accepts `1|2` and enforces *shared target <=> revision 2*, so a released v2026.9.4 reader (revision 1 only, ignores `authProfileStore`) **rejects** a copied shared plan instead of silently applying it to the agent database. New tests emulate the released validator (accepts agent-local, rejects shared).
- **P2 owner discriminator.** Candidate keys are now `auth-profiles:agent:<agentId>:<path>` vs `auth-profiles:shared:<path>`, built by a single exported key builder used for picker values, the selection map and sort order. New tests: an agent named `shared` with the same profile id in both stores keeps 2 distinct keys/targets, and selecting the shared row resolves to the shared store.
- **P2 raw residue cleanup.** `readPersistedAuthStoreRaw()` inspects the persisted row before change detection, so selecting a profile and keeping its unchanged ref still cleans the raw plaintext (`key` next to identical `keyRef` -> `changed=true`). Same-reference regression added.
- **Merge conflicts resolved.** Branch rebased onto current main `03c70bad04e` (pre-rebase tip preserved as `backup-oc-143262-descr`); conflicts were fixture-level in `configure.test.ts` / `configure.output.test.ts` (main moved fixtures to `createAuthProfileStoreFixture`).

**Red -> green (owner re-run):** per-finding source reverts each reproduced red (residue: `changed=false`; picker: duplicate keys resolving to the agent candidate; revision: shared rejected); after -> scoped suites **70 passed / 2 failed**, the 2 being Windows temp-dir `EBUSY` teardown flakes with no assertion involved (identical at the rebase tip). Full secrets shard delta vs rebase tip: +2 flaky teardown failures, **zero new assertion failures**. `tsgo` clean (core + services/config-cli/other shards), `oxfmt --check` clean, `oxlint` clean.

prs.title: fix: ask for a new login when a Claude Code login reaches its time limit
prs.body:
Closes #206215

## What Problem This Solves

People who run OpenClaw on a Claude subscription through Claude Code (`claude-cli`) eventually see their Claude login expire for good. Claude Code then fails every turn with `Failed to authenticate: this login reached its time limit and cannot be renewed. Run \`claude auth login\` to sign in again ...`. OpenClaw does not recognize this wording, so the chat only says that the reply could not be finished and points at the logs. The person has to dig through logs to learn that all they need is a new login.

## User Impact

Chat replies for this failure now say "Your model provider needs a new login. Send /login from a private chat or the OpenClaw app." and carry the Sign in button, the same as for the older "OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed" wording. Fallback decisions and logs record the reason as `auth` (status 401) instead of `unknown`. No action or migration is needed.

Not changed by this PR:

- When Claude Code exits with code 1 and prints the notice only on stderr, the failure keeps no reason, because OpenClaw shows stderr but deliberately does not classify it.
- `openclaw agent --local` without a fallback model prints Claude Code's own text in both cases; that text already names `claude auth login`.
- The separate notice `Your organization has disabled Claude subscription access for Claude Code ...` stays unclassified. A new login does not fix it, so it needs its own decision.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Claude CLI auth rule already recognizes the earlier wording of an expired login. Claude Code changed the sentence, so the rule now accepts both. The match requires the full new phrase after `Failed to authenticate:` and stays limited to the `claude-cli` provider, like the existing phrases. Everything downstream (status 401, sign-in guidance) already keys on that classification, so no other code changes.

## Evidence

Observed in an isolated run (published `openclaw@2026.11.10` package from npm, integrity checked against the registry; fresh HOME, state and config; `openclaw agent --local`; a stand-in `claude` executable that fails the turn with the notice; a loopback fallback model; no real credentials; `after` is the same package with only this PR's pattern change applied to its bundled `classification-rules` chunk):

- Notice as the failed result record, fallback configured. Before: `decision=candidate_failed ... reason=unknown next=synthetic/fallback-model`. After: `decision=candidate_failed ... reason=auth next=synthetic/fallback-model`, structured failure `reason: "auth"`, `status: 401`. The fallback model answered in both runs.
- Same, no fallback configured. Before: `reason=unknown next=none`. After: `reason=auth next=none`. The CLI printed Claude Code's notice in both runs.
- Notice only on stderr with exit code 1: `Claude Code process exited with code 1`, `reason=unknown`, identical before and after.

Observed in tests on this branch (main at 2d46fdabfc6):

- Two new cases (`classify.test.ts` table row, `exit-error.test.ts` through `createCliExitFailoverError`): `2 failed | 48 passed (50)` without the pattern change, `50 passed` with it.
- Chat reply through the reply runner (temporary local probe, not committed; the error was produced by `createCliExitFailoverError` from the notice): without the change `⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply. For details, open Settings → Logs in the OpenClaw app or run \`openclaw logs --follow\` in your terminal.`; with it `⚠️ Your model provider needs a new login. Send /login from a private chat or the OpenClaw app.` plus the `Sign in` button.
- Consumers: failover classification corpus, `oauth-refresh-failure.test.ts`, `agent-runner-execution-auth-failures.test.ts`, `user-copy.test.ts`: 131 passed.
- `oxlint --type-aware` on the three changed files 0 warnings and 0 errors, `oxfmt --check` clean, `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` clean, line-cap and max-lines ratchets OK.

Observed in the field: one host on 2026.11.5 logged 39 `candidate_failed` decisions with `reason=unknown` and this notice as detail on 19 Nov.

Not observed:

- No run against a real expired Claude login after the change; the notice came from a stand-in executable.
- The chat reply was observed in the reply-runner test harness, not in a live channel.
- The `after` run used the released package with the pattern change applied to its bundle, not a full source build of this branch.

prs.title: fix: tell the sender they were approved when the channel token is a SecretRef
prs.body:
Closes #206138

## What Problem This Solves

When a channel's bot token is kept in a secret (a SecretRef) instead of plain text, `openclaw pairing approve <channel> <code> --notify` lets the sender in but never tells them: the CLI prints `Failed to notify requester: UnresolvedSecretInputError ...` and the person who asked for access is left waiting with no reply.

## User Impact

`--notify` sends the approval notice for channels whose tokens are SecretRefs, as it already does for plain-text tokens. Approval itself, plain-text tokens and approvals without `--notify` are unchanged. No setup or migration. If the secrets can't be resolved, the CLI still prints the same `Failed to notify requester` warning after a successful approval.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI sends the notice from its own process, but it passed the raw config, so the Telegram adapter read the token from an unresolved SecretRef. The fix resolves only that channel's secrets first, through the same path `openclaw message send` and `openclaw directory` use (`getScopedChannelsCommandSecretTargets` plus `resolveCommandConfigWithSecrets`), and keeps it inside the existing warning-on-failure block. The Gateway protocol is untouched (its `code` approval branch never notifies; changing that would be a protocol change).

## Evidence

**Live, before and after:** a test Gateway with Telegram pointed at a local Bot API stub and the dummy token in the secret store. The stub's user DMs the bot, gets a pairing code, and the code is approved with `--notify`.

| Build | Token | CLI output after "Approved" | Notice sent to the requester |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Released 2026.11.10 | SecretRef | `Failed to notify requester: UnresolvedSecretInputError ...` | none |
| This fix | SecretRef | none (only the approval lines) | "✅ OpenClaw access approved. Send a message to start chatting." |
| This fix (control) | plain text | none (only the approval lines) | "✅ OpenClaw access approved. Send a message to start chatting." (unchanged) |

![Before and after: pairing approve --notify with a SecretRef bot token](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stealthybear/openclaw/90fb8dc6adf5fc9e21dbb889adb8a82b1cfe1ea4/before-after.png)

**Real Telegram:** the same fix build with a real bot whose token is a store SecretRef (`{"source":"store","provider":"default",...}`) and DMs on `pairing`. A real Telegram account DMed the bot from a phone, got a pairing code, and the CLI approved it with `--notify`: the CLI printed only the approval lines, and the phone received the notice (user id redacted).

![Real Telegram: pairing code, then the approval notice after pairing approve --notify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stealthybear/openclaw/90fb8dc6adf5fc9e21dbb889adb8a82b1cfe1ea4/real-telegram.png)

Tested on 43f00ec94b4 (base ae2d953b68f).

- Review: autoreview (claude), ae2d953b68f..43f00ec94b4: no findings at P2 or above, clean
- Tests: `src/cli/pairing-cli.test.ts` gains one test that the notice gets the resolved config; it fails without the fix and passes with it (13 tests, 92 s wall time with `--maxWorkers=1`, almost all of it transform; the tests themselves take about a second).
- **No request proof:** the change touches no model request.

prs.title: fix: point the Gateway diagnosis skill at the current log folder
prs.body:
Closes #206217
Related: #198032

## What Problem This Solves

When someone asks their agent to find out why the Gateway is failing, the agent follows the bundled `diagnose-gateway` skill. That skill still says Gateway logs default to `/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-<date>.log`. Since #197978 the Gateway writes to the `logs/` folder of its state directory instead. On an upgraded host the old folder can still hold same-named files from other OpenClaw processes, so the agent can read unrelated or stale records and miss the log of the Gateway it is diagnosing.

## User Impact

The skill now names the current default, `~/.openclaw/logs/openclaw-<date>.log`. Agents that follow it look at the running Gateway's log. Nothing changes for people who set `logging.file`; the skill still tells the agent to use the path printed at Gateway startup.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the one remaining place in the bundled custodian skills that names the retired default (the Codex troubleshooting page is handled in #198033). The sentence keeps its shape; only the default path changes to the one documented in "Where logs live".

## Evidence

Observed on a host running 2026.11.10:

- The Gateway prints `log file: ~/.openclaw/logs/openclaw-2026-11-26.log` at startup; that file was about 14 MB and still growing on 26 Nov.
- `/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-2026-11-26.log` existed as well, about 0.3 MB, last written hours earlier and not by the running Gateway.

Checked on this branch: `oxfmt --check` on the skill file is clean, `git diff --check` is clean. A repository search on main at 2d46fdabfc6 found no test that pins this sentence (`workspace-skill-snapshot.test.ts` and `bun-standalone-snapshot.test.ts` reference the skill by name; both passed, 13 tests, on a branch state that included this change).

Not observed: an agent run that follows the changed skill end to end. The change is one sentence of skill text.

prs.title: fix: make /activation work in Discord server channels
prs.body:
Closes #206213

## What Problem This Solves

On Discord, an owner who runs `/activation always` in a server channel gets "Group activation set to always." and the bot still only answers when mentioned. The command is offered as a native Discord slash command and confirms success, but nothing changes; the only way to stop requiring a mention is to edit `requireMention` in config.

## User Impact

After this change `/activation always` makes the bot answer every admitted message in that Discord channel, and `/activation mention` turns mention gating back on, as on Telegram and WhatsApp. Channels where nobody has run the command behave exactly as before (config decides).

One behavior change for existing installs: a Discord channel whose session already holds a stored mode from an earlier `/activation` (which had no effect until now) starts following it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord's preflight took the mention requirement from config only. It now reads the session's stored `groupActivation` first, the same precedence Telegram's `resolveGroupActivation` uses; no stored mode or a failed read falls back to the config rule. The read is skipped for DMs and bound-thread sessions, which were never mention-gated by this value. `docs/channels/groups.md` lists Discord among the channels that consult the stored mode.

## Evidence

- New unit tests for the resolver (stored `always`, stored `mention`, nothing stored, failed read).
- Ran the Discord extension suite (`pnpm test:extension discord`) with this change on the `v2026.11.6` tag: 3,027 tests passed. Not run on current `main`; relying on CI here.
- Not yet exercised against a live Discord server; I will add the result here once our gateway restarts onto the build.

prs.title: fix: find phrases across emphasis in native Mac chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In the native Mac conversation window, Find could report “No matches” for a phrase visible in a loaded message. For example, when **red** was bold in “red fox,” searching for “red” worked, but entering “red fox” cleared the selection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Find still checks the original message text first. When that misses, Find searches the displayed text within each Markdown paragraph. A phrase can cross emphasis, inline code or a link label. The search continues to use the existing user and assistant text filter and keeps separate paragraphs apart.

## User Impact

A search such as “ripe pears” can select a message when “pears” is bold, italic, inline code or a link label. Existing literal searches still work, including searches for asterisks in code. Moving between matches and retaining a selected message after an update use the existing behavior.

## Evidence

- Entered the phrase through the mounted native Find field in a hidden macOS window. The original cleared the selection. The fix retained the correct message without a redundant reveal. A plain matching phrase selected the neighboring message and a missing phrase cleared the selection.
- Ran the new Swift Testing regression and the existing traversal test in an isolated package. The regression failed on the original source and both tests passed on the fix.
- Both deterministic replays passed across user and assistant text. All 68 navigation and row-update scenarios passed. SwiftLint reported zero violations for the two changed files under both checked configurations.
- The full OpenClawKit package, Xcode application, system Cmd-F shortcut and physical scrolling were not exercised locally.

On the preceding signed head `fb3c9a9b`, hosted OpenClawKit passed the Find regression for visible phrases across emphasis and literal code, with 2,706 tests passing in 246 suites. The macOS build passed. The separate iOS screenshot job timed out waiting for the Mermaid diagram button, a failure recorded before this change. The iOS Access restart check stopped before executing its assertion when SwiftPM could not download WebRTC. The AppKit replay exercised the Find and selection logic. A built-app recording of the system Find shortcut and scrolling remains unavailable. [Package test run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45653913293/job/139346335971), [earlier screenshot failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41917592723/job/126882233381), [iOS smoke run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45653913293/job/139346337456)

### Inline code and link labels on `65dbc42a`

The stable macOS window displayed “ripe pears” in six messages. The previous matcher found four of those message IDs and omitted the plain inline-code and link-label cases. Adding italic text elsewhere in the same paragraph made those IDs appear. The amended matcher found all six without the extra italics.

Across 18 cases and 53 searches, the previous matcher returned 13 incorrect result lists with 17 missing IDs. The amendment returned the expected ordered IDs for all 53. Literal Markdown searches, separate paragraphs, message boundaries and navigation controls passed. The new regression failed on the previous head for the two intended IDs. All three focused Swift tests and both SwiftLint configurations passed on the amendment.

The mounted window evidence used v2026.9.8. The exact source comparisons compiled the matcher and its pinned Markdown preprocessor. The full revised app window remains untested locally.

### Hosted integration on `801a701e`

The protected workflow tested merge `90f9351f` with the reviewed Find matcher and tests and the updated Android session-browser fixture. Play passed all 3,771 tests and third-party passed all 3,893, with zero errors, failures or skips. The archived-query case that failed in the older integration passed in 0.125 s and 0.126 s respectively. [Play report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45813797656/artifacts/15115012106) · [Third-party report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45813797656/artifacts/15114707359)

The workflow remains red on the iOS release screenshot. On the iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator, `testReleaseChatScreenshot()` timed out at line 243 waiting eight seconds for the “Mermaid diagram” button. The earlier screenshot failure linked above also reached that assertion. [Screenshot diagnostics](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45813797656/artifacts/15115665830)

The targeted second attempt reached the same assertion. Both traces started loading `index.html` and reached the watchdog before the first document commit or request for `native.js` (21.365 s and 20.793 s). A passing run with identical renderer, resource, view, model and XCTest sources also cancelled the first subscriber. That run committed the document at 3.343 s and completed rendering at 3.789 s. The traces leave the cause of the timeout open. [Second screenshot diagnostics](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45813797656/artifacts/15116584100) · [Passing comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45790331281/artifacts/15104135392)

The Find matcher and its view modifier compile only on macOS. The earlier iOS Mermaid change documented this intermittent timeout and linked an independent November 5 store run. [Earlier renderer investigation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193227) · [Store run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41958326550)
