prs.title: fix: keep inline Canvas cards usable after their sandbox reloads
prs.body:
Closes #205427

## What Problem This Solves

An inline Canvas card in an open chat can go blank if its sandbox iframe reloads. The message stays visible, but the card's controls disappear.

## User Impact

The card renders again and accepts input without a chat refresh or a new message. This restores the authorized document, not unsaved text in its previous browser document. No new permissions, Dashboard changes, or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the message subscription tied to the retained frame's current window. After validating a new readiness notification, the inline host retires the previous render and private port, cancels any inspection using that port, and replays the document already authorized for the card. Inspection waits for the new port to become ready.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on official main at 645643d0fa458b3201e6345aebd57c0c722303bf: the authenticated Chromium session could fill the persisted card's textbox before reloading the outer frame. After reload, the textbox was absent for the 10-second assertion window.
- On the candidate, the same isolated Gateway and Chromium test passed: the outer element was retained, the restored textbox accepted new input, the inner document still could not read the top document, and the browser issued only one Canvas document read. Three unrelated scenarios were filtered out.
- 56 focused tests passed across routing, mounting, layout, inspection, and widget ownership. The UI build, production UI and focused test typechecks, lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. The build's advisory report flagged the same CSS and chat boot thresholds on the equivalent QA baseline and candidate.
- Local autoreview of the staged candidate against the base above: no P0 findings. See [current GitHub checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205428/checks) and the hosted ClawSweeper review on this PR; the local review is not a Diamond rating.
- Pit manually tested Gabriel's earlier candidate in the Mac app. This is not automated WebKit evidence for the upstream port.

### Chromium / isolated Gateway: terminal evidence

The local regression run used an authenticated chat with a persisted synthetic card. These are excerpts of the captured Vitest output, not GitHub Actions output. [Read the exact assertions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/205d3d95208cf2da0727c6f49b927c895dbf1170/ui/src/e2e/chat-widget-sandbox.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts#L265-L297): they type before reload, reload only the outer frame, check its identity and type again, then check document isolation and the single Canvas read.

**Before — upstream `645643d0`**, with the regression test applied but no production fix:

```text
TimeoutError: inputValue: Timeout 10000ms exceeded.
  - waiting for locator('openclaw-canvas-widget-view .chat-tool-card__preview-frame').first().contentFrame().locator('iframe').contentFrame().getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Local note' })
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed | 3 skipped (4)
```

**After — same base, with the six-file patch published in `205d3d95`:**

```text
✓ reads persisted Canvas bytes through an authenticated browser connection 4662ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  1 passed | 3 skipped (4)
```

The other three cases were excluded by the test-name filter. This records Chromium on Linux, not WebKit on macOS.

Credit: Gabriel validated the original fix; Vítor Cepeda Lopes supplied the handoff and tested it in the Mac app.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/770f19d8-b23c-4317-9f5b-d8b9030fa3d9)

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: fix(feishu): honor explicit filename override for media uploads
prs.body:
Fixes #205246

## Problem

Sending a local file through the `message` tool with an explicit `filename` override could deliver the attachment under the basename of the `media` path instead of the requested name:

```json
{ "action": "send", "media": "/tmp/repro/report_en.pdf", "filename": "季度报告.pdf", "forceDocument": true }
```

Expected: the recipient sees `季度报告.pdf`. Reported actual behaviour: the recipient sees `report_en.pdf`, and server-side evidence in #205246 (reading `file_name` back via `GET /open-apis/im/v1/messages`) showed the override never reached `im.file.create` on the paths below. A control send whose file is actually named in Chinese, with no `filename`, was delivered correctly — so this is specific to the override, not to non-ASCII names.

## What has changed since the report

Current `main` has since landed the direct-path plumbing: `FeishuOutboundSendMedia` now lives in `extensions/feishu/src/outbound-types.ts` with a `filename` field, `channel.ts` puts `filename: normalizeOptionalString(ctx.params.filename)` into the outbound context, and `sendMedia` forwards `fileName: ctx.filename` to `sendMediaFeishu`. That covers a top-level `filename` on the direct send path only. This PR is rebased on current `main` and closes the remaining gaps, aligning with that new `filename` contract instead of duplicating it.

## Remaining gaps this PR closes

1. **Attachment-carried names were still dropped.** Core places the message tool's `filename` into `payload.attachments[].name`, but the Feishu outbound paths only forwarded media URL strings (`resolvePayloadMediaUrls` returns plain strings), discarding `attachments[].name`. This affected `sendMedia`, the `sendPayload` card path, the fallback payload path, and the TTS-supplement path.
2. **The reply-dispatcher path dropped it too.** Media sent as an agent reply never resolved a name from `payload.attachments`.
3. **The `fileName` alias and attachment `name`/`filename` on the direct action were not read.** `channel.ts` only read the top-level `filename` param; an attachment's own name never reached `sendMedia`, and the presentation-fallback payload carried no named attachment.

`sendMediaFeishu` in `extensions/feishu/src/media.ts` already accepts `fileName` and uploads it as `file_name` to `client.im.file.create` (`fileName ?? media.fileName ?? "file"`); the fix is plumbing inside the Feishu plugin, with no core changes.

## Changes

- **Attachment names are resolved through the SDK's owner.** All Feishu payload paths now pair media with attachment names via `collectReplyMediaEntries` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-outbound` — the same pairing the SDK itself uses — instead of resolving names from flattened URL lists. The earlier revision of this PR carried a plugin-local resolver (`media-attachment-name.ts`); it has been removed entirely, along with its `media.ts` re-export, because positional/reference pairing is the SDK helper's job.
- `extensions/feishu/src/outbound.ts`: the `sendPayload` card path, the fallback payload path (`sendFeishuFallbackPayload`), and the TTS-supplement path resolve each media entry's name through `collectReplyMediaEntries` and pass it to `sendMediaFeishu`; `sendMedia` keeps the explicit context `filename` first, then the paired attachment name.
- `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts`: the agent-reply media path pairs entries through `collectReplyMediaEntries` **before** any flattening to URL strings, so positional names (attachments that carry only a `name`, no path) survive to the upload.
- `extensions/feishu/src/channel.ts`: the direct `send` / `thread-reply` action reads `filename` / `fileName` (or the first attachment's `name` / `filename`) and passes it to `sendMedia` as `filename`, and into the presentation-fallback payload as `attachments: [{ path, name }]`.
- Tests: regression coverage in `outbound.test.ts` and `reply-dispatcher.test.ts` for the review's two counterexamples — a referenced name that belongs only to the second file, and positional names with no path references — across the card, fallback, and reply paths. Low-value uploader cases flagged in review were removed.

## Real behavior proof (live Feishu tenant)

Verified against a real Feishu tenant with a dedicated self-built app, a Gateway built from this branch, and two test PDFs (`a.pdf`, `b.pdf`). Every delivered file was read back from Feishu's servers with `GET /open-apis/im/v1/messages/{message_id}`; the `file_name` values below are the server-side records.

| Case | Expected `file_name` | Server-recorded `file_name` | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline (a.pdf, no override) | `a.pdf` | `a.pdf` (`om_x100b7f4f0e9f28a4cfbd0aafa9547ff`) | PASS |
| Referenced name (b.pdf + `attachments: [{path: b.pdf, name: "B-report.pdf"}]`) | `B-report.pdf` | `B-report.pdf` (`om_x100b7f4f0fd7bca8df78c0124450259`) | PASS |
| Positional name, first file (a.pdf + `attachments: [{name: "A-report.pdf"}, {name: "B-report.pdf"}]`) | `A-report.pdf` | `A-report.pdf` (`om_x100b7f4f09c050a0df837813bfb9ccd`) | PASS |

Scope of the live proof, stated plainly:

- Feishu's direct-send surfaces are single-media by design (the send action rejects more than one distinct media source, and the Gateway `send` RPC schema has no `attachments`), so multi-media payloads can only be produced by channel-session reply delivery. The live sends above therefore went through the shipped agent `message` tool, one call per file, with each scenario's `attachments` array passed verbatim.
- Through that entry, the mismatch counterexample (media `a.pdf`, attachment pointing at `b.pdf`) is rejected before sending by the single-media validation — the misassignment cannot be produced there.
- The second positional send through the single-media action took the first named attachment (`A-report.pdf` for `b.pdf`): the send action resolves the upload name as the first named attachment in the call and a per-file call carries no position. That is the direct send-action path, not the payload pairing changed here; in `sendPayload` / fallback / reply delivery the whole payload is paired by `collectReplyMediaEntries` before flattening, which the new unit regressions assert (see Tests).
- A live reply-turn trace could not be captured in the sandbox used for this proof: the host's egress could not sustain Feishu's inbound long-connection (WSS), so no genuine inbound reply turn was available. The pairing paths are covered by the unit regressions below, including red/green verification.

## Tests

- Feishu extension suite: **315 tests passed** (7 files), including the new pairing regressions. Red/green verified: reverting the production changes makes exactly the 5 new regression tests fail with the review's counterexamples; restoring them returns the suite to green.
- Typecheck (`tsgo` for extensions and tests) — clean. `oxfmt` and `git diff --check` — clean. (oxlint could not run in the sandbox; CI will cover it.)

## Notes / out of scope

- This PR supersedes #205407, which was opened against an older `main` and conflicted after upstream's partial fix landed; it was closed in favour of this rebased version.
- Known remaining gap, deliberately **not** in this PR to keep it Feishu-scoped: the Gateway RPC send path (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`) builds outbound payloads without `attachments` / `filename`, so a Gateway-relayed send can still lose the override. Happy to open a follow-up issue/PR for that core path if maintainers prefer.
- `forceDocument` is intentionally untouched: it is not read anywhere in the Feishu plugin, and a `.pdf` already routes to `msgType: "file"` via `detectFileType`.

## What Problem This Solves

The MXC sandbox plugin still uses the preview SDK 0.8 request and process APIs, which are incompatible with the released MXC SDK 1.0 runtime.

## User Impact

MXC sandboxed agents keep the same workspace, network, environment, timeout, and cleanup behavior on SDK 1.0.

Operators need to account for three compatibility changes:

- Windows requires Node.js `>=24.21.0 <25` or `>=26.8.0`. The plugin fails activation with a remediation message on older releases.
- `mxcBinaryPath` must select an SDK 1.0 architecture directory containing both `wxc-exec.exe` and `mxc_ffi.dll`. Invalid or incomplete overrides fail closed instead of falling back to bundled native components.
- SDK 1.0 cannot request LPAC. The `appcontainer-dacl` and `appcontainer-bfs` tiers use a regular AppContainer and can reach resources granted to `ALL APPLICATION PACKAGES`. `base-container` is unchanged. The selected tier and boundary are logged and documented. Chaz accepted this boundary and the upgrade requirements for this migration.

Ordinary sandboxed exec remains non-PTY. The retained SDK PTY path owns its deadline, kills the sandbox on timeout, returns `124`, and writes the timeout notice.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin now builds an SDK 1.0 `ContainerRequest`, uses `spawn` or `spawnWithPty`, and pins `wxc-exec.exe` plus `mxc_ffi.dll` from one validated release directory. Launcher stream errors, backpressure, cancellation, timeout, and cleanup are explicitly owned so a failed stream cannot be reported as exit `0`.

The dependency closure also pins `node-gyp@11.4.2` for `node-pty@1.1.0` source builds on platforms without a prebuild. The packed dependency scanner records the reviewed `node-pty` maintainer-script findings; they are not install-time or runtime paths.

## Evidence

Current branch head `0cbf9b5481de42e1ea4207c1b27fd50441e51c0b` includes a test-only restoration of sandbox-policy admission coverage. Its parent merge `0722b5d9cf4b5c7612bc142b6e68ee90f3333aa7` integrates upstream `061f22646cf6eb3c199f7f776ea6bdb1b92d971a`.

The current-main merge only reconciles upstream owner/localization refactors and tests; it does not intentionally change the validated SDK 1.0 behavior. No candidate source changes arose from the runtime harness work.

prs.title: fix(doctor): pass synthetic agentSessionKey to include session-gated tools in schema inspection
prs.body:
Closes #205370

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor's **Runtime tool schemas** check falsely warns that `ask_user` is an unknown `tools.allow` entry, even when a Discord session correctly offers it (`questionInputMode: "buttons"` in `extensions/discord/src/channel.ts`).

**Reproduction:**
1. Configure a finite `tools.allow` that includes `"ask_user"` and a Discord channel.
2. Run `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`.
3. Observe: `[tools] tools.allow allowlist contains unknown entries (ask_user). These entries are shipped core tools but unavailable in the current runtime/provider/model/config.`

This happens on every doctor run (every Docker boot), which may cause operators to drop a working tool from their allowlist.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Root cause:** `collectAgentRuntimeToolSchemaFindings` in `src/flows/doctor-tool-schema-projection.ts` calls `createOpenClawCodingTools` **without a `sessionKey`**. The session-gating predicate `shouldIncludePrimarySessionToolForOpenClawTools` in `src/agents/openclaw-tools.registration.ts:184` requires a non-empty `sessionKey` to include `ask_user`. Without it, `ask_user` is never added to the doctor's projected tool inventory, so the unknown-entry check fires.

**Fix:** Pass a synthetic `sessionKey` (`doctor-tool-schema-inspection-<agentId>`) when doctor builds the tool inventory. This makes the inspection session look like a real primary session, so session-gated tools are included in the projection and the false warning disappears.

**Why this is safe:**
- The synthetic key is only used for schema projection (read-only inventory), never for execution.
- `isPrimaryBootstrapRun` returns `true` for non-subagent/non-ACP keys, which is the intended classification for doctor's inspection context.
- No behavior change for real agent runs; this only affects doctor's diagnostic inventory.

**Note:** `assembleOpenClawCodingTools` reads `sessionKey`, not `agentSessionKey`. The first version of this fix used `agentSessionKey` and did not eliminate the warning; the correct parameter is `sessionKey`.

## User Impact

- **Before:** Every doctor run falsely warns that `ask_user` is unknown, eroding trust in the warning and tempting users to remove a valid tool from `tools.allow`.
- **After:** Doctor correctly recognizes `ask_user` as a valid entry when the channel supports it (e.g., Discord with `questionInputMode: "buttons"`).

## Evidence

### Shipped CLI Proof (BASE vs HEAD)

**Setup:** Isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` with:
- `agents.entries.main.tools.allow: ["ask_user", "exec", "read"]`
- `channels.discord.enabled: true` (provides `questionInputMode: "buttons"`)
- Fixture model provider (`openai-completions` API)

**Command (both runs):**
```sh
openclaw doctor --lint --only core/doctor/runtime-tool-schemas --json
```

**BASE (524a56ed00d, before fix):**
```
[tools] agents.main.tools.allow allowlist contains unknown entries (ask_user). These entries are shipped core tools but unavailable in the current runtime/provider/model/config.
```
→ **RED**: warning present (1 occurrence in stderr)

**HEAD (bcf44ed8e96, after fix):**
```
(no unknown entries warning)
```
→ **GREEN**: warning eliminated (0 occurrences in stderr)

Both runs produce identical JSON stdout (`"ok": true`, `"checksRun": 1`, `"findings": []`), confirming the warning is emitted to stderr only and does not affect the health-check verdict.

### Latest-Stable Upgrade Proof (v2026.11.10 → HEAD)

This is the exact upgrade scenario reported in #205370 (Docker / npm on official `2026.11.10`).

**Setup:** One shared `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (`/tmp/doctor-upgrade/stable/state` → copied to `head/state`) and one shared `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` with the same allowlist + Discord channel as above. The state dir is populated by the **stable** binary first, then reused unchanged by the candidate binary — settings and data are preserved across the upgrade.

**Step 1 — v2026.11.10 stable (tag `v2026.11.10` = commit `6ea542fd97e`, version `2026.11.10` in `package.json`):**

```sh
$ node dist/cli/run-main.js doctor --lint --only core/doctor/runtime-tool-schemas --json
# stderr:
[tools] agents.main.tools.allow allowlist contains unknown entries (ask_user). These entries are shipped core tools but unavailable in the current runtime/provider/model/config.
# stdout:
{"schemaVersion":1,"ok":true,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":76,"findings":[],"recoveryCopies":{...}}
```
→ **RED**: warning present on the official stable release.

**Step 2 — upgrade to this PR's HEAD (dist built from `b1ff5558330`, same blob as `bcf44ed8e96` for the two touched files), same state dir, same config:**

```sh
$ node dist/cli/run-main.js doctor --lint --only core/doctor/runtime-tool-schemas --json
# stderr: (no `unknown entries` warning; only unrelated DEP_PLUGIN_SDK deprecation notices)
# stdout:
{"schemaVersion":1,"ok":true,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":75,"findings":[],"recoveryCopies":{...}}
```
→ **GREEN**: warning eliminated, settings/data carried over, no config edits required.

**Delta `checksSkipped: 76 → 75`:** HEAD runs one additional internal sub-check now that the projected inventory matches the allowlist; the verdict (`ok`, `findings`) is unchanged.

### Code Path

1. `src/flows/doctor-tool-schema-projection.ts:126` — `createOpenClawCodingTools` called without `sessionKey` (before fix).
2. `src/agents/openclaw-tools.registration.ts:184-186` — `shouldIncludePrimarySessionToolForOpenClawTools` returns `false` when `sessionKey` is empty.
3. `src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts:619-634` — `ask_user` is only created when the predicate passes.
4. `src/agents/agent-tools.assembly.ts:363` — `assembleOpenClawCodingTools` maps `agentSessionKey: e?.sessionKey` (reads `sessionKey`, not `agentSessionKey`).

### Unit Test

`src/flows/doctor-tool-schema-projection.test.ts` verifies that `collectAgentRuntimeToolSchemaFindings` passes the synthetic `sessionKey` and that `ask_user` is not flagged as unknown when present in `tools.allow`.

## Impact Surface

| File | Change | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| `src/flows/doctor-tool-schema-projection.ts` | +4 lines (add `sessionKey` param + comment) | Low: read-only diagnostic path |
| `src/flows/doctor-tool-schema-projection.test.ts` | +95 lines (new test) | None: test-only |

## Cleanup

No production state, credentials, or user data touched. The synthetic session key is ephemeral and never persisted. Test state directories (`/tmp/doctor-proof/{base,head}`) are isolated and removed after proof.

---

**Precedent:** N/A — first fix for this specific false-positive pattern in doctor tool schema inspection.

prs.title: fix: preserve failed Apple chat messages across partial history pages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an Apple chat reopened or refreshed, a nonempty newest history page could move a failed message from the outbox into the composer. The matching user message could still be on an older page. Scrolling back then showed the delivered message, and reopening the chat also showed it as a saved draft.

## User Impact

A paginated history response leaves the failed message available for manual editing. When a complete history read establishes that the message is absent, automatic restore puts it back in the composer once. A canonical match confirms delivery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The history reconciler now tracks whether the live snapshot covered the start of the session before using a tail delta as evidence of absence. An empty unanchored refresh preserves valid evidence from a previous complete read.

## Evidence

Both frozen Swift/SQLite replays reproduced the premature restore. Both passed with this change. Thirteen focused controls covered one-row and 200-row pages, the older canonical echo, presentation changes, tail deltas, exhausted history, and the draft after reopening the database. All 168 existing controls passed.

The new SwiftPM regression drives the view model through a newest-page refresh, an older-page read, a tail delta, and a real SQLite close and reopen. Both changed Swift files passed compiler parsing. prs.title: improve: reduce memory used by SQLite update checks
prs.body:
Related to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192547.

## What Problem This Solves

When a Gateway checks for unfinished updates, a fresh SQLite reader loads plugin-cohort recovery decoders and evaluates a schema lookup used by the recovery writer. Doctor recovery reads load update-reconciliation policy they do not use. That costs memory while other Gateway processes may be starting.

## User Impact

Update checks and Doctor use less memory for these SQLite reads. The existing selection, recovery decisions and database format stay the same. The effect on whole-Gateway peak memory and the constrained ARM64 startup failure remains unknown.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both native read paths now prepare the synchronous reader for the selected command before SQLite admission. Reconciliation uses its existing read module, and Doctor loads the existing recovery implementation. Physical source validation still runs after module preparation. The empty selection keeps its no-transaction fast path, and the populated reads retain their snapshot and validation behavior. The four production files grow by four lines in total.

A one-sided prototype reduced reconciliation memory but increased Doctor's first-reply RSS by 3,158 KiB in all four pairs. Selecting in both directions removes that tradeoff.

## Evidence

Built the normal standalone SQLite package entry for each revision on Linux x64 with Node 24.22.1. Each sample started a fresh packaged OS child with the same file identity, real Gateway owner, and real schema. The ordinary IPC transfer completed and the parent checked the typed reply. The parent read `smaps_rollup` after the reply. Module tracing ran separately. These are child measurements on synthetic state.

| First read | Pairs | Paired median RSS change | Paired median anonymous PSS change | Pairs with lower RSS |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Reconciliation, no matching row | 8 | −4,770 KiB | −2,918 KiB | 8/8 |
| Reconciliation, matching row | 8 | −4,778 KiB | −2,930 KiB | 8/8 |
| One named update | 4 | −4,498 KiB | −2,676 KiB | 4/4 |
| Recovery admission | 8 | −2,542 KiB | −2,498 KiB | 8/8 |

The separate module trace saw 154,032 fewer bytes of packaged JavaScript loaded for reconciliation and 76,792 fewer for recovery. Both loaded 82 files versus 79 before. The complete standalone output grew by 6,025 bytes and six files. The build splits one shared schema module on the config/plugin paths, increasing their loaded bytes by 391. Their four-pair pilot showed about 5–6 ms more time to reply. In 20 further interleaved pairs per command, median paired latency was −9.36 ms for config and +1.90 ms for plugins. Median paired RSS was −96 and +86 KiB, respectively.

All 54 tests in the update-run reader, recovery admission, state read worker and live startup-metadata suites passed on the measured production change. The final test-only adjustment binds spies to the same Vitest module generation as the worker. The measured production bytes are unchanged. Exact-head CI passed both the recovery-policy selection and source-replacement tests, as well as the update-run reader suite. [Startup metadata tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45902483096/job/140191912871) · [Update-run reader tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45902483096/job/140191912838)

prs.title: fix: stop doctor asking for skill_workshop in tools.allow when the plugin is disabled
prs.body:
Closes #205371

## What Problem This Solves

When `plugins.entries.skill-workshop.enabled` is `false` and `tools.allow` is a finite list without `skill_workshop`, `openclaw doctor` still lists a "Fix now" item telling the user to add `skill_workshop` to `tools.allow`. Following it would widen the tool allowlist for a plugin the user turned off on purpose.

## User Impact

Doctor no longer reports Skill Workshop tool-policy findings for a disabled plugin entry, and a minimal `{ enabled: false }` entry stays warning-free. No config change or migration is needed. Findings for an enabled plugin are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Skill Workshop doctor check only read `autonomous.mode`, which defaults to `auto`, so an absent setting counted as "Workshop on". The check now also treats an explicitly disabled plugin entry as off, using the same gate that already suppresses the other findings when `autonomous.mode` is `off`.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test with `plugins.entries["skill-workshop"].enabled: false` and `tools.allow: ["read"]`. On the base commit it failed with the `tools.allow does not include "skill_workshop"` finding; with the fix it passes.
- Allowlist case from the issue thread: Workshop is now judged by the shared plugin activation helper (`resolveEffectiveEnableState`), so `plugins: { allow: ["discord"] }` with no Workshop entry (also `plugins.deny` and `plugins.enabled: false`) produces no Workshop findings. Regression tests cover these; the first three fail on the previous commit, and an allowlist that includes `skill-workshop` still reports.
- `pnpm test extensions/skill-workshop/doctor-health-api.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 8 passed after this update (6 before).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` passed; `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the two changed files are clean.
- I ran `openclaw doctor` end to end from source; see "Shipped CLI proof" below. `pnpm check:changed` did not complete in my environment (the SQLite worker ratchet and the doctor guard tests were interrupted, unrelated to this change), so I am relying on PR CI for the broader checks.

### Shipped CLI proof

Ran the real CLI entry point (`scripts/run-node.mjs`, the source wrapper behind the `openclaw` binary) on Node 26.12.0, Linux, from a throwaway home so no real state was touched. Before = base commit `7d2b9c37c` (only `extensions/skill-workshop/doctor-health-api.ts` reverted to base), after = this PR head `3b4552d58`. Host paths are shortened to `~`.

Config (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`, with the `skillWorkshopPlugin` migration marker a post-upgrade config has, so Doctor does not treat the entry as pre-restoration policy):

```json
{
  "meta": { "migrations": { "skillWorkshopPlugin": true } },
  "plugins": { "entries": { "skill-workshop": { "enabled": false } } },
  "tools": { "allow": ["read"] }
}
```

Command (same for all three runs; `enabled` is the only value that changes):

```sh
export HOME=~/oc-home OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=~/oc-home/.openclaw \
  OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=~/oc-home/.openclaw/openclaw.json CI=1
node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --non-interactive
```

**Before (base, `enabled: false`)**: the finding is present.

```text
Fix now:
- gateway.mode is unset; gateway start will be blocked.
  ...
- tools.allow does not include "skill_workshop".
  Location: tools.allow
  Next step: Add "skill_workshop" to tools.allow.
  Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/skill-workshop
- Gateway health check failed: ...
```

**After (PR head, `enabled: false`)**: no Skill Workshop finding (`grep -c skill_workshop` on the full output is 0). The `Doctor: Skill Workshop tool policy` check still runs.

```text
Doctor: Skill Workshop tool policy
...
Fix now:
- gateway.mode is unset; gateway start will be blocked.
  ...
- Gateway health check failed: ...
Doctor: maintenance release

└  Doctor complete.
```

**After (PR head, `enabled: true`, same `tools.allow`)**: the finding still appears for an enabled plugin.

```text
Fix now:
- gateway.mode is unset; gateway start will be blocked.
  ...
- tools.allow does not include "skill_workshop".
  Location: tools.allow
  Next step: Add "skill_workshop" to tools.allow.
  Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/skill-workshop
- Gateway health check failed: ...
```

The remaining `gateway.mode`, Node patch-level, and gateway-credential lines come from the empty throwaway profile and are unrelated to this change. I did not run a v2026.11.10 to head upgrade.

prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/202818

## What Problem This Solves

Android turn recaps maintain a second transcript-anchor record with the same four fields as the controller's existing contract. The chat screen copies those fields on every recap evaluation, leaving two shapes to keep synchronized.

## User Impact

No intended visual or behavioral change. A missing or wrong-session anchor still cannot settle a recap; an already-settled recap remains visible until matching newer transcript content supersedes it. No migration or configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `ChatTranscriptAnchorState` directly and remove the duplicate DTO and copying adapter. The resolver requires an explicit nullable anchor; it does not restore the old optional transcript-check bypass. The controller remains the sole producer of transcript facts.

Production code shrinks by 12 lines. Existing tests gain 23 net lines to independently check missing and wrong-session anchors before and after settlement, using distinct item IDs so session isolation cannot pass through item equality.

## Evidence

- Reviewed commit `f5bda8805eb0e24ebd1431d7da6cc123b7ede9c2`, based on `7f3bd14b7f7ec681b58076addfc14024223b08d4`.
- The strengthened resolver suite passed on the original implementation using the equivalent all-null record: 22 tests per phone flavor, zero failures/errors/skips.
- Both phone Kotlin compiles, Kotlin lint and the staged-content guard passed with the refactor. Resolver (22), recap layout (2), and ChatScreen (13) tests passed in each flavor: 37 tests per flavor, zero failures/errors/skips. Gradle completed in 41 seconds.
- Local proof used the exact candidate Android subtree with matching Android build inputs over retained frozen root tooling. This is Android-source proof; current-head PR CI supplies the broader gate.
- Independent source review and local ClawSweeper review of the complete committed range found no actionable correctness or security findings. The review-driven test refinement was included in the passing proof.
- No physical-device, live Gateway, or performance run was needed for this internal contract consolidation.

## Current CI and landing

[Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45907008179) passed. The unchanged reviewed head merged as `40d533668293d77148f8a94b5da1c697caf9b72a`. Native completion and generated-checkout removal are verified; the authored checkout is retained.

prs.title: fix: show Waiting and Resumed for Claude CLI subagent handoffs
prs.body:
Root cause: ui/src/pages/chat/chat-sessions-yield.ts:44 compares raw tool names with `sessions_yield`, which misses the `mcp__openclaw__sessions_yield` name that Claude CLI history keeps. src/gateway/cli-session-history-index-policy.ts `mergeCliHistoryRow` sends native Claude rows to chat.history with no run identity, even though the merge already links each local user turn (`<runId>:user`) to its native prompt.

Fixes #206107

Thanks @fubarfu for the report and the clear Codex comparison.

## What changes for users

In Claude CLI sessions, Control UI now shows "Waiting for subagents" after `sessions_yield` while the child runs, and "Resumed · … later" after the child wakes the parent, the same as embedded and Codex sessions. The private Yield call no longer shows as a tool row.

The "Outcome unknown" rows in the report are already fixed on main by #203877. This PR doesn't touch them. On both main and this branch, tool rows show their real outcome, and a failed tool call shows as failed.

## Why

- Claude CLI calls OpenClaw tools over MCP, and its history keeps the bridged name on purpose (`unwrapToolCallForDisplay`). The yield handoff scanner was the one reader that compared raw names, so it never confirmed the yield. It now uses the existing `stripOpenClawMcpToolPrefix`. The paired, completed, non-error and `yielded` receipt checks are unchanged.
- The waiting line and the Resumed rule both need the run that handed off. Embedded and Codex rows carry `__openclaw.runId`. Imported Claude rows carried none. The history merge now gives an unmatched native row the run of the local user turn whose native prompt it answers. The only link it uses is the one the merge already has: the prompt's external id matched to the local user row with `<runId>:user`. Synthetic (meta) wake prompts end a turn but stay hidden, so rows of a wake run never inherit the earlier run. The transient prompt anchor is removed at merge, and nothing is stored: the index is the in-memory display projection. There are no schema or transcript changes.

## Evidence

Docker (secretless node:24.22.1) Gateway + Control UI built from each SHA. Agent on `claude-cli` with a stand-in `claude` that emits the Claude Code stream-json and project JSONL contract and calls the real OpenClaw MCP server as `mcp__openclaw__session_status`, `mcp__openclaw__sessions_spawn` and `mcp__openclaw__sessions_yield`. Real Chromium. Main and this branch were each run twice, with controls on an embedded-runtime session and a failed claude-cli tool call. Results and screenshots: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206158#issuecomment-7203023862

Regressions (each red on main, green here):
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-sessions-yield.test.ts`: an imported Claude CLI call with its result is confirmed as a pending handoff.
- `src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts`: native JSONL through the merge gives the turn's run to its tool rows, no run to rows after a meta wake, and no anchor in the output.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep chat responsive while tool renderers load
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat startup can repeat initial-history work, wait for optional tool presentation, and reproject unchanged sidebar rows when only readiness changes. An ordinary Gateway hello can invalidate pending initial-render recovery by replacing an already-cleared connection. Archived-session notices can also collapse below the normal composer surface and move the footer.

The first-row scheduling budget has a separate ordering defect: a cheap loading or empty projection consumes its one decision before populated history arrives. The first expensive transcript projection can then run without the existing cold-start yield.

## User Impact

Live tool output and previews remain available while optional row rendering loads. Early boot editing retains its editor, draft, selection and scroll through pane adoption; authoritative archived/incognito/view-only state still replaces input through the existing banner owner. Ordinary replacement notices share the composer's responsive minimum height.

The first populated transcript projection now owns the existing 15 ms cold-start decision. Cheap projections, restored panes and accepted submissions remain immediate; loading and empty states stay visible. No configuration, migration, protocol change, deployment or restart is included. Final performance qualification failed below; the PR remains unmerged.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Transfer a matching early history/live-output lease into the pane. Preference changes replace the lease, and failed replacement retires the connection.
- Keep optional rendering and retry inside the row boundary, with eager previews outside it. Remove the obsolete presentation facade; disclosure policy remains with the thread expansion owner.
- Carry prepared snapshot/Details facts forward. Readiness-only updates leave unchanged sidebar rows stable while preserving status, approval, history/search, pagination and pin-wake consumers.
- Preserve connection identity when hello has no bootstrap credentials to retire. Token/profile retirement still replaces the connection; stale-client, navigation, global and storage guards remain authoritative.
- Preserve normal first-commit boot-editor adoption. The discarded metadata/chrome gate is absent: intentional early local editing must not wait for session metadata.
- Share existing responsive composer minimum-height rules with ordinary replacement notices. Preserve narrow-container, landscape, native-resting and short-pane precedence, compact/hidden exceptions and natural growth. No Details animation change or arbitrary maximum height.
- Keep the one-shot cold-row budget until the first projection that would render rows. Measure that projection alone, retain the existing threshold and task-yield owner, never re-hide admitted rows, and prevent a disposed pending task from publishing. The viewport, composer, header and Details remain mounted.

The scheduling defect predates this PR: the construction-time decision is present in [PR #196482](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196482). Earlier pane admission exposes the loading-first order. The 15 ms measurement covers transcript projection preparation, **not** subsequent Markdown rendering, row mounting or geometry. The profile does not establish that the measured workload crossed that threshold; the fresh unprofiled comparison must establish the effect.

The existing real-Gateway benchmark also gains a default-off cold CPU diagnostic mode: `--cold-cpu-profile --route chat --reloads 0 --prime-reloads 0`. It retains full raw/mapped samples, native long-frame attribution and clock/counter snapshots, with explicit coverage limits and cleanup. The ordinary and existing warm-profile paths remain separate; diagnostic captures cannot become ordinary timing acceptance.

Candidate: `fbb33335d3c6c2a08ccac813306d26359ce92ff3`, tree `2ea06ed47877870945099c6a3d6759063198b072`. Frozen integrated baseline: `e11a36d08b9a9fc81d2c6634fd6e252f8f954dad`. The native final-patch refresh preserved the signed correction history and integrated current-main tests; it did not replay abandoned readiness designs. Prior receipts retain their original source and baseline identities.

The Latest test correction now awaits the actual destination after clicking, then retains the existing idle wait and final distance ≤1 assertion. Its owner test demonstrates that stable geometry can coexist with a queued manual command; releasing the existing commit and animation-frame owners reaches the exact tail. Product scrolling is unchanged. This fixes the test's premature observation boundary without claiming that retained CI facts establish the exact cause of the earlier 846 px result.

Versus the frozen baseline: UI/runtime +216/−308 (**net −92**); diagnostic tooling production +383/−30 (**net +353**); combined production **net +261**. Tests +1955/−446 (**net +1509**), diagnostic docs +36, other workflow/manifest/allocation metadata +39/−11. Positive production growth supplies the missing cold CPU attribution capability and the first-populated-projection lifecycle boundary. The test ratchet passes with unchanged shared allowance 400 plus allocation 1109. No checker or performance threshold was relaxed.

## Evidence

**Publication status: NEEDS WORK; final performance failed, CI disposition pending.** Exact-source native95166 passed UI types, scoped formatting/lint and all22 scroll-owner cases; its wrapper then failed an incorrect21-case expectation. That failed receipt remains unchanged. [Remaining native proof86448](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45904919483) authenticated the six original evidence members byte-for-byte and passed lifecycle8 plus reply-attribution9, including both motion modes, zero skips/todos. The verified aggregate is **39 cases:22 carried+17 newly executed**. Complete logs/reports, restored source, joined children, native completion and separate automatic cleanup were independently verified. Archive SHA256: `aa3c2af824b0fe8a2ef7cde0d0f3802b1322a0130798bd1eb91bc04d3e151d33`. The [full unprofiled comparison85014](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45904508017) against frozen e11 completed all48 observations and failed as detailed below. Current [merge CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45906761470) has an external WebKit dependency-install failure and a separate Cron delivery-error visibility assertion under investigation. The exact-head ClawSweeper review is PASS, but it preceded the final performance result and does not accept that result. No current-source performance pass, merge or deployment is claimed.

**Latest completion contract.** [3492 merge CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45897473527/job/140175632528) observed 846 px from the bottom after the first Latest click and geometry-idle helper in the no-preference case; 464 sibling tests passed. The retained failure artifact had no scroll timeline. Source and existing sibling E2Es establish that geometry-idle does not certify queued `afterCommit`/animation-frame command completion. Both corrected sites poll the same exact ≤1 destination, wait for geometry idle and check ≤1 again. A missed command still fails; a transient arrival followed by drift still fails. The new owner test documents the pending-command contract and is not presented as a product RED or reconstruction of that CI capture. Later [b8bd actual-merge CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45900330670) passed, including the formerly failing shard; that does not causally attribute the difference to the Show correction.

**Show callback contract.** [3492 merge CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45897473527/job/140176064462) found TS2745/TS2769 for a zero-argument `Show` child. The canonical `_deferred` parameter satisfies Solid rc.18's API. Solid checks `function.length`, so evaluation intentionally moves into its conditional memo; this is not a type-only or emitted-runtime-equivalence claim. The threshold, yield and content policy stay unchanged. [Exact b8bd native proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45899284660) passed `tsgo:ui` and all eight lifecycle cases, zero skips/todos; full logs/report and separate native completion/automatic cleanup were verified. Archive SHA256: `2d950a2cdba313c62d039d25e5d6fabd36e3b534f7cbce34f44e6c6aba5f007b`. Those owner bytes are unchanged in the integrated candidate; exact final-source UI types passed in95166, and lifecycle8 passed in86448.

**Scheduling-owner regression.** The original-order 3492 regression failed against its parent because populated rows appeared before the held yield, then passed with the correction. Disposal checks actual row rendering after unmount. The existing threshold measures projection preparation only; no claim is made that this explains all measured CPU work. Earlier scoped review passed. Final narrow autoreviews are complete with no findings: the b8bd Show invocation correction with full component/dependency/lifecycle context, and final fbb Latest tests/allocation with owner/caller/sibling context. Relevant runtime owner bytes are unchanged through integration; earlier unchanged scopes retain their prior reviews. Review did not execute tests.

**Historical browser correctness, explicitly carried.** The [3492 native proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45895287144) passed nine full reports: lifecycle8, New Session6, inline7, menu1, guest2, Incognito1, auth5, boot9 and composer-height20 — **59 passed, zero skips/todos**. All 11 complete logs and original reports were verified; paired assets passed. Native completion and automatic cleanup were separate verified outcomes. Archive SHA256: `cb766a3eb6f3a1a118945809b309759e83f65158b68729a42b1e4b01609181eb`. This is exact3492 proof, not a claim that all59 were rerun on the integrated candidate.

The [earlier c5 browser proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45876546173) passed all51 original browser cases. Six responsive-height cases failed under the original CSS with computed `auto` instead of 88/92/112/0/52/92 px, with no mixed setup/global error; restored final CSS passed all20 height cases. prs.title: fix: keep earlier Workboard proof and attempts when a card grows
prs.body:
Related: #113309. Prior work: #113311.

## What Problem This Solves

A later proof entry can erase earlier evidence from a Workboard card. A person reviewing the resulting card sees an incomplete history even though the update succeeded.

## User Impact

Past proof and attempts remain readable after other metadata grows. If all available room is occupied by protected history, the write returns an error and preserves the previous card. A full proof list therefore requires an explicit retention decision before more entries can be accepted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing store already enforces count and byte limits. Protect evidence during trimming, retain the limits, and reject an update that cannot fit. Remove the earlier list slices which discarded records before validation could see them. This approach needs no database migration. The earlier proposal made separate proof rows canonical and addressed pagination. This PR proposes rejecting an update when the protected history alone fills the bound.

## Evidence

At main revision `65a8bc8`, create a temporary SQLite-backed card with one proof and one completed attempt, add other metadata near the byte limit, then append a second proof. The baseline returned one proof. The proposed branch returned both and preserved the attempt. In a separate full card, a 41st proof succeeded on main. The branch rejected it and re-reading the card returned the original object. The existing correlated-proof test also passed. [Prior issue](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/113309) · [Closed implementation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/113311)

Run `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/workboard/src/store.test.ts -t 'keeps earlier proof|refuses a proof past|retains the correlated proof'`. For the baseline, run those same test additions against the unmodified implementation.

On the rebased commit (base `fcc9a0648c`), the full affected test file passed all 84 tests with one worker. The pinned formatter and linter passed on the changed files. TypeScript reported zero errors in the changed files. The wider import graph produced the same 102 diagnostics on the base and candidate using the available dependency cache.

prs.title: fix: release the caller's plugin registry when a session reply continues in the background
prs.body:
Related: #198423.

## What Problem This Solves

A two-session reply can outlive its initiating plugin call. The background wait still sees the registry from the earlier call. That registry can refer to a generation which has already stopped.

## User Impact

A background reply can continue after the original invocation closes. The existing requester selection and separate-turn reply checks still decide where the result goes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The detached reply already exits the prepared model-runtime scope. It can also use the existing plugin-runtime scope exit at this same boundary. The change applies to the background session reply and preserves the original admission and delivery sequence.

## Evidence

In the existing requester regression, give the real reply entry point a distinct caller registry. Compare it with the registry visible when the background wait begins. Close the initiating invocation, finish the wait and check the ordinary destination assertions. On main the old registry remained visible in all three requester cases. With the change all three passed, including the case where the requester changed. [Related lifecycle issue](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/198423) · [Earlier hook dispatch fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198732)

Run `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/sessions-send-reply-flow.requester.test.ts` first with the new assertion on the baseline, then on the fix branch. No external model or channel is required.

prs.title: fix: restore Copy code for carriage-return fences in Full Reader
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening a full chat message could hide the **Copy code** button when the message used carriage returns between lines. Full Reader loaded the entire message, but displayed an ordinary backtick-fenced snippet as prose.

## User Impact

A reader can copy the code body from these messages, including indentation and multiple lines. **Copy Message** still copies the original message with its original line endings.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Markdown parser recognizes LF, CRLF and standalone CR as line endings. The segmenter used to leave standalone CR in its source buffer, so it looked for both fence markers on the same line. Normalizing CRLF first and then standalone CR gives the segmenter the same line boundaries as the parser.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, both reproductions loaded the original message but registered zero code-copy actions for a CR-delimited fence containing `a`. On the reviewed tree, both registered one action and copied exactly `a`. The same Swift caller fixture passed 500 generated cases per seed.
- All 14 direct Full Reader cases passed, including LF, CRLF, standalone CR, tilde fences, mixed endings, indentation and Unicode. The native fixture also passed 26 steps, including full-message and preview-row Copy controls.
- The segmenter regression checks for the same prose and completed code block under each of the three line endings. The hosted OpenClawKit suite and its parameterized regression are pending. The local fixture invoked the Copy callback with an in-memory pasteboard. A mounted app and the system pasteboard remain unverified.

Hosted OpenClawKit passed 2,705 tests in 246 suites, including all three line-ending cases in “fenced code after prose recognizes CommonMark line endings.” The iOS smoke job also passed. The scoped reader tests cover Copy output for CR, CRLF and LF. The installed app and system pasteboard remain unverified. [Package test run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45653122536/job/139343555614)

prs.title: fix: release memory used to track finished plugin writes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A long-running Gateway kept a write-tracking entry for every plugin state namespace it touched. Deep Research uses separate namespaces for the jobs, steps, and cancellations of each conversation generation, so the table grew even after every write finished.

## User Impact

Finished Deep Research writes release their tracking entries. The stored jobs and steps remain readable. This takes effect automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

An ordinary store command invalidates earlier receipts as soon as it is admitted. Once its last overlapping write settles, its tracking entry can be removed. Receipt-producing operations keep their existing revision and pending-write state. Scalar reads and synchronous invalidation now avoid creating entries for untouched namespaces.

## Evidence

- On Node 24.22.1, eight synthetic conversation generations wrote and reread 24 namespaces using the normal V2 store and SQLite worker. Stock retained 24 tracking entries. The change retained zero and released the source table. A lookup in a never-written namespace also left the table empty.
- Two SQLite-worker suites passed 38 tests. Their optional PostgreSQL test skipped. The same run also verified that receipts held by old and updated SDK callers in one process were both revoked by later writes. [Focused Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45903738662)
- The measured unit was a retained tracking entry. Whole-Gateway RSS was outside this comparison.

prs.body:

Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Write for someone who uses OpenClaw but has not read the code. The title and

For internal-only work, name the actual developer or operator workflow affected.

For fork branch edits, follow CONTRIBUTING.md.

Related: #205372

## What Problem This Solves

When an OpenClaw command or reply fails, the error can leave you unsure what to do next. Ask OpenClaw normally needs a working model to explain it, which is particularly unhelpful when model setup is what failed.

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
In 1–3 plain sentences, say who is affected, what happens today, and why it
matters to them. For a bug, name the trigger if known. For a feature or internal
work, describe the need in the actual workflow without inventing harm.
Could a reader understand the problem without knowing your proposed fix?

Good: "Background checks can use up a new user's model allowance before they've
asked the assistant to monitor anything."
Bad: "Turn off periodic checks on fresh installs."
-->

## User Impact

In a ready Ask OpenClaw chat or the setup TUI, type `explain error:` followed by a redacted error line. The reply gives a likely cause and one safe next step, or asks for more context instead of guessing. If chat cannot start, the same request works with `openclaw setup --message` without a configured model.

<!--
What can the affected person do or expect after this change? Name any required
action and material risk, including breaking changes or migrations. For internal
work, describe the workflow outcome and say when there is no user-visible change.
-->

An explicit prefix treats the paste as data before it can reach the model, tools, or approval handling. One shared catalog covers invalid config, missing provider credentials, a Gateway token mismatch, and a prompt that exceeds the model’s context window. It suggests checks without running them. The server saves a placeholder rather than the pasted text, but the client may still display the original; remove private values before sending.

<!--

matters; leave file lists in the diff rather than restating the problem or outcome.

  > Next step: Run `openclaw config validate` on the machine running OpenClaw to identify the invalid settings without saving changes.

  A bare `401 Unauthorized` returned “There isn’t enough information to identify the cause” rather than diagnosing credentials.
- On an isolated Gateway, a synthetic paste containing a private marker and command text returned an explanation. Chat history stored `Explain error: [error text omitted]`; the marker was absent from the response, saved history, and Gateway log, and the configuration checksum stayed unchanged. The browser rendering was not exercised; this uses the existing chat composer and reply layout.

prs.title: improve(ci): build Docker package declarations once
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Docker seed CI builds the SDK declaration subset and then compiles the full public declaration set, which includes the same SDK roots. A [completed CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45831302021/job/139949225912) spent 534 seconds preparing its package and 176 seconds running the seed tests; these durations identify the preparation cost, not a measured saving from this change.

## User Impact

Docker seed jobs prepare the same complete package with one shared declaration pass. All selected Docker lanes, package validation, public types, worker bundles and failure gates remain required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing full build profile with declaration emission explicitly enabled. This removes the SDK-only pass before full emission without adding another build profile or cache. Packaging remains after successful compilation.

## Evidence

- Existing Docker workflow guard fails on the base and passes with the change. The complete workflow guard file passes: 222 passed, 8 skipped (147.13s).
- Seven focused workflow/build orchestration checks pass (46.93s wrapper, mostly initial worker compilation); two canonical public/SDK declaration inventory checks pass (17.91s wrapper).
- Resolved build phases: SDK-only plus full declaration writers → full writer only; every other phase is retained.

prs.title: fix(agents): stabilize system-prompt suffix across normal and announce/yield turns
prs.body:
Fixes the system-prompt suffix digest changing between normal turns and announce/yield turns, causing unnecessary prompt cache invalidation.

## Problem
The `completionEventGuidance` string in `system-prompt-messaging.ts` varied based on `suppressSilentTokenGuidance` — one wording for suppressed mode, another for non-suppressed. This meant the suffix digest changed when a turn switched between modes, causing the prompt cache to be invalidated even though the actual prompt content sent to the LLM was functionally identical.

## Fix
Always use the same `completionEventGuidance` wording regardless of `suppressSilentTokenGuidance`. The guidance text is now a single stable string that does not vary by mode, keeping the suffix digest byte-identical across normal and announce/yield turns.

## Files changed
- `src/agents/system-prompt-messaging.ts` — uncondition the completion-event guidance string
- `src/agents/system-prompt.ts` — remove the conditional branch that selected between two guidance strings
- `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run-execute.ts` — remove the now-unused suppress-silent-token parameter path
- `src/agents/system-prompt-cache-stability.test.ts` — new test verifying suffix stability across modes

Refs: #150081

prs.title: fix: stabilize prompt-cache fingerprint across transcript reloads
prs.body:
Fixes false-positive cache drops when messages are reloaded from the transcript database with different object references or timestamps.

## Problem
Two issues caused the prompt-cache fingerprint to change across transcript reloads, forcing full recomputation (~90k tokens dropped to ~3k):

1. **Timestamp in envelope digest**: The `MESSAGE_ENVELOPE_OMITTED_FIELDS` set did not exclude `timestamp`. Timestamps differ between original message creation and persistence reload, causing the envelope digest to change despite identical content.

2. **Reference identity comparison**: The `divergence` detection in `prompt-cache-observability.ts` used `message !== history[index]` (reference inequality). When messages are reloaded from the transcript database, fresh objects are created with different references even for content-identical messages, triggering false-positive history rewrite detection.

## Fix
1. Add `timestamp` to `MESSAGE_ENVELOPE_OMITTED_FIELDS` — it is persistence metadata that does not appear in the prompt sent to the LLM.
2. Replace the reference comparison with a fingerprint identity comparison (packed string prefix), which is byte-stable across reloads for content-identical messages.

## Files changed
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/prompt-cache-history.ts` — add `timestamp` to omitted fields
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/prompt-cache-observability.ts` — use fingerprint identity instead of reference comparison

Refs: #150081

prs.title: fix: let plugin helpers keep exec after a subagent reports back
prs.body:
Closes #206173

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin helpers that fork a chat with `exec` stop working right after a subagent finishes in that chat. Better (obviyus/openclaw-better-prompt) is one of them: the owner clicks Better in a chat where a subagent just reported back, and gets "This chat's tool policy does not allow read, ls and exec, so the helper cannot read your files." The click only works again after the owner sends a throwaway message. Chats that use subagents, such as Goal chats, hit this most.

## User Impact

- The owner can use fork-based helpers right after a subagent finishes, with no extra message.
- Nothing changes for non-owners. A session writer, or anyone whose turn was not the owner's, is still refused `exec`. A signed-in caller still needs to be the person who sent the turn, as #204411 set.
- Known limit: a completion report stored before this change has no marker, so it behaves as today. If the latest row in a chat is such a report, the owner still needs to send one message, once. The next report the Gateway delivers is marked. There is no backfill. Existing transcripts, sessions and settings load unchanged after an upgrade (proof below).
- No config, schema, protocol or SDK change. The new field is internal transcript metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

A plugin fork checks tool policy as the requester of the turn it reads through, and takes that requester from the latest user-role row. A subagent's completion report is a user-role row, but it records no owner: it delivers the result of work an earlier turn started. So the fork judged the owner's click by the report instead of by the owner's turn.

The fork already skips steering rows for the same reason (a steer joins the running turn). It now also skips completion reports, but only the ones the Gateway delivered itself:

- When the host's own completion delivery writes a report (`subagent_settle`, `subagent_announce`, or an agent-mediated completion), the Gateway records `__openclaw.hostCompletion: true` on the row. It sets this only on its own write path, for backend callers (the same `canUseInternalRuntimeHandoff` check that already guards other internal handoff controls).
- A client can still send completion provenance through `agent`; upstream accepts that on purpose. Its row carries no marker, so it stays that client's own input. `agent` params cannot carry the marker (the agent and provenance schemas are closed), and a `before_message_write` hook can neither add the marker nor keep a forged one.
- A marked report that names a sender other than the earlier input's sender is not skipped.
- If no earlier input is in the read window, the report's own facts are used, as before, so a read-only fork never starts failing.

### Decisions

| Choice | Evidence | How to reverse |
|---|---|---|
| Skip completion reports when finding the turn's requester | Same model as steering rows. One requester for the whole fork, so `read`/`ls` policy and the run's requester stay consistent. | Drop the completion branch in `readSessionForkTurn`. |
| Skip only reports the host marked | The `agent` method accepts completion provenance from any `operator.write` client, and a client without a signed-in identity records no sender. Without the marker, such a row would borrow the owner's earlier turn. | Drop the `hostCompletion` check in the reader. |
| Mark on the write path, not reserve provenance in preflight | Rejecting completion provenance from public callers would change maintained behavior: `agent.events-and-subagents` asserts a public caller may send `subagent_announce` provenance and is recorded as non-owner. The marker leaves that behavior alone. | Reserve the provenance in `agent-request-preflight.ts` instead. |
| Do not admit `exec` on the signed-in caller's own authority | #204411 tests on purpose that a signed-in admin is refused `exec` on another owner's turn through a `sessionAccess` method. #205483 removed a second owner producer so one turn gives one owner answer. | Not built. |
| No backfill of old rows | A stored row cannot prove after the fact that the host wrote it. Old rows keep today's behavior, which is safe and costs at most one message. | Not built. |

## Evidence

**Real-model proof, before and after.** A throwaway Gateway on a Mac with its own `HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, Better 0.1.1 installed from its published package, and a real model: `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` on the `claude-cli` runtime with a Claude Code setup token, the routing a Claude subscription install uses. Tool profile `coding`. The owner asks the agent to call `sessions_spawn`; the model does, the child runs on the same model and finishes, and the Gateway delivers its completion report into the chat. Then the owner clicks Better with no new message, asking the helper to run `sh probe.sh`, which writes a marker file when `exec` runs. Rows are read from the stored transcript.

Base `36395007cf0b`:

```text
user row: senderIsOwner=1 hostCompletion=- provenance=external_user/- text=Call the sessions_spawn tool exactly onc
user row: senderIsOwner=0 hostCompletion=- provenance=inter_session/subagent_settle text=[Subagent Context] Every subagent in thi
== owner clicks Better, no new message
TAKE {"ok":true,"result":{"error":"This chat's tool policy does not allow read, ls and exec, so the helper cannot read your files."}}
== exec marker: absent (exec did not run)
```

Head (this PR):

```text
user row: senderIsOwner=1 hostCompletion=- provenance=external_user/- text=Call the sessions_spawn tool exactly onc
user row: senderIsOwner=0 hostCompletion=1 provenance=inter_session/subagent_announce text=Continue the OpenClaw runtime event.
== owner clicks Better, no new message
TAKE {"ok":true,"result":{"improved":"Run probe.sh to confirm the release status, then investigate what the fork divergence and pending fix actually are (inspect git history, the fork point, and what changed), ..."}}
== exec marker: PROBE_EXEC_RAN 21:53:13
```

Both report kinds (`subagent_settle` from a yield wake, `subagent_announce` from a direct completion) are completion reports, and the real in-process delivery wrote the marker on head. The setup token was passed on stdin only; a scan of each run directory found it in 0 files.

**Upgrade from the latest stable release (2026.11.10, npm).** One state directory, first run on the published 2026.11.10 build, then on this PR's build:

```text
== phase=stable gateway=OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f)
user row: senderIsOwner=1 hostCompletion=- provenance=external_user/- text=Call the sessions_spawn tool exactly onc
user row: senderIsOwner=- hostCompletion=- provenance=inter_session/subagent_announce text=Continue the OpenClaw runtime event.
TAKE {"ok":true,"result":{"error":"plugin \"better-prompt\" may not add core tool \"read\" to subagent runs."}}

== phase=upgrade (this PR's build, same state directory)
[state/upgrade] Migrated .../state/openclaw.sqlite in place from schema 40.
[state/upgrade] Migrated .../agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite in place from schema 42.
== sessions.list after upgrade:
    agent:main:dashboard:<id> label=Goal chat model=claude-haiku-4-5
    agent:main:subagent:<id> label=- model=claude-haiku-4-5
== settings after upgrade: model=anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 toolProfile=coding better=true
== owner clicks Better on the old chat, no new message
TAKE {"ok":true,"result":{"improved":"Deeper release notes from upgrade test evidence. ..."}}
== a new subagent finishes on this PR's build
user row: senderIsOwner=0 hostCompletion=1 provenance=inter_session/subagent_announce text=Continue the OpenClaw runtime event.
== owner clicks Better, no new message
TAKE {"ok":true,"result":{"improved":"Write release notes for OpenClaw Gateway 2026.11.10 upgrade, ..."}}
== exec marker: PROBE_EXEC_RAN 22:04:16
```

The transcript, sessions and settings load after the migration. The published 2026.11.10 build refuses Better's core tools entirely (it predates core tools in plugin forks), so the stable side has no "before" for this bug. Its completion report was stored as a steer into the owner's running turn (`steerTargetRunId` on the row), which the fork already skipped before this change, so that old row behaves as before.

**Old unmarked report as its own turn (the known limit).** The base build's state from the first run, upgraded to this PR's build:

```text
user row: senderIsOwner=1 hostCompletion=- provenance=external_user/- text=Call the sessions_spawn tool exactly onc
user row: senderIsOwner=0 hostCompletion=- provenance=inter_session/subagent_settle text=[Subagent Context] Every subagent in thi
== owner clicks Better on the old chat, no new message
TAKE {"ok":true,"result":{"error":"This chat's tool policy does not allow read, ls and exec, so the helper cannot read your files."}}
== a new subagent finishes on this PR's build
user row: senderIsOwner=0 hostCompletion=1 provenance=inter_session/subagent_announce text=Continue the OpenClaw runtime event.
== owner clicks Better, no new message
TAKE {"ok":true,"result":{"improved":"Run `sh probe.sh` to verify the release is ready, then write comprehensive release notes ..."}}
```

The old unmarked report is refused exactly as before; the next report the Gateway delivers is marked, and the fork is admitted with `read`, `ls` and `exec`. Here the model rewrote the request instead of running `probe.sh`, so no marker file; the admission itself is the change (base and the old row return the refusal above before any model call).

**Regression tests.**

- `gateway-plugin-forked-turn-session-tools.e2e.test.ts` (real Gateway, scripted model): a report written through `agent` by a local backend Gateway client (the host's delivery path) is skipped, and the owner's fork runs `exec`. An ordinary client's `agent` call with `hostCompletion` in its params, or inside `inputProvenance`, is rejected as invalid params. The same client's report without the marker stays its own input, and `exec` is refused before any model call. A host report after a non-owner channel turn is still refused. A signed-in caller's own report through a `sessionAccess` method is refused.
- `session-manager-model-context-limits.test.ts`: the reader skips a marked report, keeps an unmarked report (subagent or media) as its own input, keeps a marked report that names another sender, and falls back to a lone report's own facts.
- `user-turn-transcript.persistence.test.ts`: the marker survives a write hook that clears metadata, a hook cannot add it to an unmarked report, and it is never written on an input that is not a completion report.
- `gateway-plugin-forked-turn.e2e.test.ts`: a chat whose only input is a completion report still forks.

- Red (the source fix reverted with `git apply -R`, new tests kept): the host-report e2e case, the reader unit test and the write-hook test fail.
- Mutations, each removing one guard:
  - the reader ignores the marker: the forged-report cases fail in both e2e tests (the fork settles with `exec`), and the reader unit test fails;
  - the Gateway never writes the marker: the host-report e2e case fails (refused);
  - the write path keeps a hook's marker: the write-hook test fails.
- Green on head: e2e 10 of 10, unit and consumer tests all pass.

- Consumers of the changed reader and user-turn writer: `session-fork-run.test.ts`, `prompt-cache-keep-warm.test.ts`, `input-provenance.test.ts`, `user-turn-transcript.test.ts`, `agent-run-user-turn.test.ts` and the `agent` handler tests pass.

**Not covered.** The Control UI button itself was not clicked in a browser; the click goes through the same `plugins.sessionAction` method the button calls. The e2e host path is a local backend Gateway client, not the in-process announce dispatch; the real-model runs cover the in-process path with a real child. An earlier run of the same flow with a loopback mock model gave the same before and after.

prs.title: improve(exec): avoid copying small buffered command results
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Short Git commands and other buffered subprocesses can return an entire stream in a single pipe chunk. The raw command runner allocates and copies that chunk again at settlement, even when the retained bytes already own their backing storage. It also runs concat for empty streams.

## User Impact

Small command outputs use one fewer capture allocation when their chunk already has the exact backing size. The regression exercises exact binary output, stdout and stderr separation, and output-limit status for a clipped multibyte sequence.

## Why This Change Was Made

The raw buffered runner owns this result. It returns an empty Buffer for an empty stream and reuses a complete single-chunk backing allocation. Multi-chunk results still require one contiguous Buffer, and partial backing views still go through the existing concat fallback. The output-limit admission, process settlement and text runner stay outside the change.

Production **+9 LOC** (+10/−1), tests **+11 LOC** (+24/−13), and **130 benchmark lines**. The extra production lines check byte ownership so the result cannot acquire an unrelated backing range.

The updater history change touches the neighboring runner, and two open changes touch broker pipe retirement and process cleanup. This patch stays in the raw result owner. [#154035](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154035) · [#192999](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192999) · [#189415](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189415)

## Evidence

A Team profile covering 139 seconds sampled 690 ms in concat and 260 ms in its backing allocation under the raw capture owner. The raw path already concatenates once per stream at settlement. The caller chains give no output-size distribution, so the fraction of that production cost eligible for this optimization is unknown.

Run `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/git-buffer-command-measure.ts [gitDir]` on each head. Five serial, counterbalanced A/A/B rounds used real brokered subprocesses, writes up to 64 KiB, and a synthetic Git tree of 62,000 entries. Acceptance required equal bytes and status, removal of the singleton copy, and no added copy or reproducible material timing regression in the controls. A1 and A2 used `f57a32938b7b4b99e25f9d2343c6890978ba9f7d`. The measured capture allocation bytes exclude pipe reads and Node pool slab overhead.

| Workload | Capture bytes copied/allocated A1 / A2 / B | Median parent thread CPU ms A1 / A2 / B |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 KiB | 1,024 / 1,024 / 0 | 0.877 / 0.871 / 0.960 |
| 1 MiB | 1,048,576 / 1,048,576 / 1,048,576 | 1.644 / 1.663 / 1.714 |
| 20 MiB | 20,971,520 / 20,971,520 / 20,971,520 | 9.255 / 9.087 / 9.077 |
| 20 MiB producer, 16 MiB cap | 16,777,216 / 16,777,216 / 16,777,216 | 11.018 / 9.684 / 11.079 |
| 20 MiB producer, 1 KiB cap | 2,048 / 2,048 / 1,024 | 1.411 / 1.217 / 1.177 |
| 6,076,000-byte Git tree listing | 6,076,000 / 6,076,000 / 6,076,000 | 10.269 / 9.675 / 9.511 |

The 1 KiB result and capped prefix each went from one positive-length concat to zero, saving about 4–6 µs of concat wall time per command. The 1 MiB and 20 MiB results still use one payload concat across 16 and 320 chunks respectively. A 1 MiB owner-timing outlier in the first run motivated 30 in-process A/A/B triplets. Concat medians were 34.06 / 28.90 / 34.29 µs, and p95 was 100.46 / 90.29 / 92.42 µs. The work-count saving is clear for a singleton. End-to-end speedup and Team-wide allocation savings are unmeasured.

The regression failed on the pinned base at the extra copy and passed with this patch. The focused command/Git run passed 134 tests in 45 seconds, with 36 platform or runtime skips. Eight Node tests passed, including the real broker path. Nine Chromium browser tests and one isolated real-Gateway UI E2E passed. The desktop-resize E2E skipped because its real-carrier fixture requires the Linux release lane.

Codex autoreview found zero actionable P0–P2 findings on the repaired staged patch against `f57a32938b7b4b99e25f9d2343c6890978ba9f7d`. `pnpm check:changed --staged` passed formatting, lint, typechecks, and all guards except Knip. The exact clean parent reproduces all four Knip findings. `toSimpleContextMessages` and `SubagentCancellationControl` appear in the production and full-tree scans. `checkDoctorLegacyStateDirPending` and `startBrokerExeca` appear in the production scan. The introducing changes are [#205963](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205963), [#205940](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205940), [#206152](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206152), and [#206104](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206104), respectively.

[Initial CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45899710090) caught two benchmark lint suppressions outside the permitted list. The probe now saves the original static factories from their property descriptors. All 14 suppression-audit tests pass, and a real-broker replay reproduces the same copy and allocation counts in all six benchmark cases. The runtime patch and output regression are byte-for-byte identical to the first reviewed head.
