prs.title: improve: use less memory when reading workspace files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reading the first workspace instructions starts two guarded filesystem workers. Each loads fs-safe’s JavaScript dependency graph from the installed package. Those cold loads consume memory and CPU before the instructions are available to the agent.

## User Impact

On Linux x64 with two workspaces each containing four 512 KiB files, median first-read process PSS fell from 290,520 to 224,639 KiB (64.34 MiB less). The first read wave took 242 ms on stock and 123 ms with the change. Both workers still run in parallel. This measures workspace reads after the workers start. The Gateway’s startup memory limit remains tracked in [#192547](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192547).

## Why This Change Was Made

The private filesystem worker now uses the same fs-safe bundling rule as the SQLite location and plugin preparation workers. The installed fs-safe package continues to own its native bindings and helper paths. The normal release tarball grows by 187,222 compressed bytes (123,724,921 to 123,912,143), with 35 additional private JavaScript files. No configuration or migration is required.

## Evidence

Built the normal release package for `e11a36d08b9a` and `706c8403d99c` using Node 24.22.1 on Linux x64. Each process read the default workspace files through `loadWorkspaceBootstrapFiles` and verified every returned byte, filename, and position. Both workers joined on shutdown. The dual-workspace cold wave used 421 ms of process CPU on stock and 225 ms on the candidate. Physical V8 heap across both workers fell from 112.28 to 49.93 MiB. Process PSS includes those workers.

| Repeated large reads | One workspace | Two workspaces |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First comparison, 250 waves, CPU time in ms (stock → candidate) | 869 → 1,011 | 1,747 → 1,852 |
| First comparison, caller p99 in ms | 5.251 → 6.119 | 8.583 → 8.489 |
| Longer comparison, CPU in µs per completed file | 859 → 774 | 806 → 753 |
| Longer comparison, caller p95 / p99 in ms | 4.221 / 5.903 → 3.875 / 5.516 | 7.042 / 8.675 → 6.701 / 7.946 |
| Longer comparison, event-loop p99 in ms | 3.050 → 2.992 | 3.135 → 3.202 |

The longer comparison ran four fresh processes per arm and workload, pinned to CPUs 0 and 1 in ABBA BAAB order. Each process warmed up for 125 waves and measured four 250-wave slices. The table summarizes slice percentiles by process, then across processes. Paired CPU changes ranged from −20.6% to +3.5% for one workspace and −22.2% to +7.2% for two. The warm results changed direction between comparisons, so they don’t establish a throughput improvement. Dual-workspace event-loop p99 was 0.067 ms higher in the longer comparison.

Separate backend observation counted 24 guarded Node file opens and closes and 12 MiB read in each package, with zero fs-safe native addon loads on that read path. Relocated packages passed actual native-required and JavaScript-mode writes, exclusive publication, and late authority revocation. Removing the fixture’s installed native binding produced the expected typed refusal under required mode while JavaScript-mode writes still succeeded. The tsdown configuration suite passed all 16 tests, and both changed files passed formatting. [Testbox allocation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45900743323)

Local autoreview covered the complete `e11a36d08b9a` → `706c8403d99c` range at P0–P2 and returned `scoped-clean` with no actionable findings.

prs.title: fix(test): preserve scoped native selector contracts
prs.body:
## Summary

prs.title: fix: keep voice notes in their spoken language with local whisper.cpp
prs.body:
Related: #176661

## What Problem This Solves

People who rely on a local whisper.cpp install for voice notes, with no audio language set, get English translations instead of transcripts. A Spanish voice note comes back as English text, so the agent and any transcript echo see words the speaker never said. whisper.cpp assumes English when it is given no language, while Python Whisper (the other local fallback) autodetects.

## User Impact

User impact: voice notes transcribed by auto-detected local whisper.cpp stay in the language they were spoken in. An explicitly configured audio language still wins, exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

#176661 made a configured language reach auto-detected whisper.cpp, but with no language configured OpenClaw still passed no `--language` flag, so whisper.cpp's English default applied. The fix passes `--language auto` in that case, which makes whisper.cpp detect the spoken language the way Python Whisper already does. Python Whisper and the other local backends are unchanged.

The audio docs said leaving the language unset means autodetection, which was not true for whisper.cpp before this fix and is still not true for Deepgram batch models (they default to English). The docs now say whisper.cpp uses `--language auto` and that Deepgram needs `providerOptions.deepgram.detect_language: true`. Deepgram's request default is unchanged.

## Evidence

Checked the shipped CLI end to end: `openclaw infer audio transcribe` in an isolated state directory with no provider keys and no audio models, so it auto-detected Homebrew `whisper-cli` (whisper.cpp 1.9.5, multilingual `ggml-base.bin` via `WHISPER_CPP_MODEL`). Input: a short Spanish voice note as Ogg Opus.

| Run | Transcript |
| --- | --- |
| Before (`main`), no language set | "tomorrow afternoon I'm going to the library with my friends. Then we are going to eat together near the station." |
| After, no language set | "mañana por la tarde voy a la biblioteca con mis amigos. Después vamos a comer juntos cerca de la estación." |
| After, `language: "en"` | English, same as before the fix |

Running `whisper-cli` directly matches: no `--language` gives the English translation, `--language auto` gives the Spanish transcript.

Focused test: `src/media-understanding/runner.cli-audio.test.ts` now expects `--language auto` for auto-detected whisper-cli with no language, and for a cleared per-request language, and passes with the change.

A second end-to-end run through `pnpm openclaw infer audio transcribe` with French and Spanish clips (macOS `say`, Ogg Opus) and an English control gave the same result: on `main` both came back in English, and with the fix they stay French and Spanish while English is unchanged. Short English clips ("Yes.", "Call mom.") are still detected as English with `auto`. The test now also covers plain unset language (no conversion), next to the converted and cleared-language cases.

Not covered: English-only `.en` models were not run live. whisper.cpp switches those to English itself, so `auto` should leave them unchanged.

prs.body:
## What this fixes

Workshop's `archive` command printed an Undo command with the agent and skill name. If someone recreated that skill and saved another change before using Undo, the command could report success while restoring the recreated skill. Support files from the original archive could be missing.

## Change

The printed command now includes the version ID returned by that archive, alongside the agent ID. If the archive response contains no version ID, the CLI reports that outcome without offering an Undo command. The documented `restore` command still selects the newest saved version when entered without `--version`.

## Verification

- Ran the actual CLI against isolated local state. After archiving a three-file skill, the registered Workshop tool recreated the same name and wrote a support file. On the parent, executing the printed Undo exited 0 and restored only the recreated `SKILL.md`. With the fix, executing the printed Undo exited 0 and restored the original instructions and both support files byte for byte. The peer agent’s bundle was unchanged.
- Made eleven further registered writes to expire the original snapshot. The same printed command exited 1 and named the missing version. Independent reads confirmed that the live bundle, all ten retained versions, the change feed, and the peer agent were unchanged. A separately entered restore without `--version` recovered the newest retained bundle.
- All 13 focused CLI and plugin tests passed. The persisted CLI contract covers offline and registered Gateway routing, text and JSON output, and the response case where the Gateway supplies no saved version.

prs.title: fix: hide project moves when a run works outside its default workspace
prs.body:
Closes #206146

## What Problem This Solves

Subagents started in another folder and cron children borrowing a parent's project checkout can receive `session_project` even though they are not working in the agent's default workspace. Their session rows do not carry the binding that the old gate expects.

## User Impact

I restrict the tool to runs whose working directory matches their agent's default workspace. Existing project-binding and tool-policy restrictions remain in place. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

I pass the run's cwd, falling back to its workspace, into the shared eligibility check across embedded and CLI execution, compaction, prompt guidance and tool previews. I kept the existing decision owner instead of adding session state or another gate.

## Evidence

- I checked the supplied real-Gateway VM evidence for main `c818ae7ea000` and head `ce810b4b8a85`: `session_project` changes from present to absent for both the alternate-cwd subagent and the cron child borrowing a project checkout. The default-workspace control stays present; the project-bound parent stays absent. Outgoing tool arrays were cross-checked against Gateway logs, with relative reads confirming the working folders.
- The exact PR regression file matches the supplied SHA-256. Against unmodified main production code: **4 failed, 4 passed**; on the PR head: **8 passed**, with 43 unrelated tests filtered out.
- I also verified [8/8 cases in final-head VM CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45891942601/job/140157165957), [production types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45891942601/job/140157798253), [affected test types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45891942601/job/140157798425), and core lint. [Dependency CI still flags two unused exports in untouched files](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45891942601/job/140157165497); I left them outside this fix.
- The VM report confirms gateway/VM/scratch cleanup and an untouched shared checkout. It used scripted loopback replies, not hosted inference, and did not invoke the move action. Local autoreview remained unavailable because its read-only sandbox could not start.
- The pr-simplify pass retained one eligibility owner: +27/-6 production lines and +99 test lines. `git diff --check` passed.

Additional real-model verification supplied by @daniel-lxs, reproduced verbatim:

### End-to-end Gateway verification

I built and installed the npm candidate from `ce810b4b8a851edb031703250d9bd52138857095` on an Ubuntu ARM64 VM and ran the production Gateway with Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 Q4_K_M through llama.cpp. I captured the `tools` arrays from the actual inference requests and forwarded the requests unchanged. In each case, Qwen called `read` with the same relative path and returned the marker it received from the Gateway. [Model weights](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-GGUF/blob/76dc22206b646ece7c569161a42fdd4ae1bdbfcc/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-Q4_K_M.gguf)

The child runs completed after I reduced the VM to 8 GiB. The repeat control exceeded the smaller context window, so the capture uses the completed control from the earlier launch of the same installed package and model. I limited unrelated tools in both launches and left `session_project` eligible under the configured tool policies. Code Mode and Tool Search were off throughout.

```text
Default-workspace control
  Working directory [default-workspace]
  Tools on both requests ["automations", "read", "session_project", "sessions_spawn", "skills_read"]
  Model call read({"path":"workspace-proof.txt"})
  Gateway result DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_MARKER

Alternate-cwd subagent
  Working directory [alternate-cwd]
  Tools on both requests ["read", "skills_read"]
  Model call read({"path":"workspace-proof.txt"})
  Gateway result ALTERNATE_CWD_MARKER

Cron child borrowing its parent’s project checkout
  Working directory [parent-project-worktree]
  Tools on both requests ["read", "sessions_spawn", "skills_read"]
  Model call read({"path":"workspace-proof.txt"})
  Gateway result PROJECT_CHECKOUT_MARKER
```

The cron marker existed only in the parent’s managed worktree. `session_project` appeared in both control requests and was absent from all four child requests. IPs, credentials, phone numbers, and private endpoints are omitted. Absolute paths are replaced with aliases.

Contributed by @daniel-lxs, who supplied the VM reproduction.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-session-project-leak-check-s26ed6c08)

## Worked on by

- @daniel-lxs

Closes #206120

## What Problem This Solves

An approval raised by the backend runtime can appear in shared chat while an authorized non-admin reviewer misses its Inbox event and pending entry. Chat and Inbox can also reject Deny while the standalone approval page works for that same reviewer.

## User Impact

Authorized reviewers can discover backend approvals without matching the backend connection. Direct device requests retain their requester-device restrictions. Session access, explicit reviewer bindings and consent remain enforced. No new configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

I reuse canonical reviewer authorization for unbound approval discovery **after** the existing requester-device checks. Chat and Inbox use the existing `approval.resolve` operation, matching the standalone page.

I ran pr-simplify. The fix removes the UI's resolver-selection branch and adds no state or parallel permission policy. Against main, production changes are +15/-10 and tests +118/-20. The real-Gateway regression now requests approval through the actual plugin runtime, rather than a device-bound client.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix: shorten doctor --fix Gateway downtime by removing old updater folders before the stop
prs.body:
Related: #204775

## What Problem This Solves

Every `openclaw doctor --fix` stops a running Gateway, and the stop covered steps that never needed it. One of them is the cleanup of abandoned updater folders (`openclaw-update-runtime-*`, about 600 MB each). Removing one took 0.8 to 1.1 s inside the stop in our test cell. This is step 2 of the plan in the #204775 design comment: run the steps that do not need the stop while the Gateway serves.

## User Impact

`doctor --fix` removes abandoned updater folders before it stops the Gateway, so the Gateway is down for that much less time. The folders it removes, the ones it keeps and its messages are unchanged. A cleanup failure is reported and no longer blocks the repairs that need the stop. Every `--fix` still stops the Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

I checked each step named in the plan against what the stopped window protects (state and agent databases, config the Gateway holds or rewrites, files it writes concurrently):

| Step | Decision | Reason from source |
|---|---|---|
| Updater runtime cleanup | Moved before the stop | Reads and writes no database. Each runtime's `owner.json` and the process census decide custody. The release updater (`reclaimRetainedUpdateRuntimes` in `src/update/cli.ts`) already runs the same pass beside a serving Gateway. |
| Client credentials | Stays | On SQLite installs it returns at once. On PostgreSQL it migrates the state schema and recreates client identities under an exclusive lock on the local credential store, which the Gateway uses. |
| External config check | Stays | Read-only (0.1 ms), but it decides whether the Gateway may start; moving it after the restart would replace its message with a failed restart. |
| Maintenance readiness | Stays | Verifies the repaired databases before the Gateway starts, and records migration-backup completion, which needs maintenance custody. Its result also gates SQLite reclamation. |
| Workspace and shell completion | Stays in this PR | They are contributions inside the shared contribution run. Moving them needs a placement field on the contribution contract; in the cell they took about 5 ms (plus about 0.3 s of read-only workspace diagnostics). |

Why before the stop and not after the restart: a first version ran the cleanup right after the restart. In two of three runs the census found a process it could not classify (a child the new Gateway starts during startup, such as its SQLite integrity worker) and conservatively kept the folder. The serving Gateway before the stop is in steady state, like the release updater's case.

What the Gateway can do meanwhile: it never runs code from an updater runtime; the census classifies it as a non-updater and treats any process that references the folder as a holder. An update it starts creates a new folder with an owner record naming a live PID, so that folder is kept. Doctor still retires its own idle readers and spawn broker first and keeps any folder one of its own workers loaded code from. A signal lets an in-progress removal finish.

Not changed: the readiness steps that stay in the stop moved unchanged into `doctor-health-maintenance-steps.ts` so `doctor-health.ts` stays under its line cap. The cleanup no longer checks the update requester's write authority, which only governs Doctor's state writes; the release updater runs this pass without it too.

## Update behavior

No update-path change. A published updater that runs Doctor on this build gets the cleanup before Doctor's maintenance begins. The updater's own runtime has an owner record with its live PID, so it is kept, as before.

## Evidence

**Linux cell, systemd user Gateway, npm install, 4 GiB agent database with 1 MiB/s of writes, `/readyz` probed every 250 ms.** Base pack is `main` at `d0f76989509`, head pack is `fe42d651b7d` (this PR), both under unpublished version numbers. Each cell runs `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes` three times. Before each run the harness plants an abandoned updater folder (owner record of an exited PID, hard-linked copy of the installed package: 47,883 entries, 596 MB) and a look-alike folder without an updater's marks (negative control). Run 3 also plants a second folder whose inner directory is read-only, so its removal fails.

Fixture note: the census refuses inside any container it detects, by design. These cells run with a private cgroup namespace and without `/.dockerenv`, so the real census runs. No other container shares the cell's volume. A first base cell without that change kept every folder with "Host process visibility cannot be established from this container".

| Run | Cleanup position (s after "Stopped the managed Gateway") base / head | Cleanup time base / head | Outage base / head |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | +35.2 (inside) / -14.6 (before) | 0.87 s / 0.54 s | 47.9 s / 45.4 s |
| 2 | +34.3 (inside) / -16.1 (before) | 1.11 s / 0.67 s | 47.4 s / 42.8 s |
| 3, failing folder | +31.2 (inside) / -17.1 (before) | 0.78 s / 0.86 s | 43.2 s / 43.9 s |

- Effects are the same in both cells: the planted folder is removed every run, the look-alike folder is kept, the installed package keeps all its files, and in run 3 the read-only folder is kept with `cleanup failed: EACCES` reported. Every run exits 0 with a new Gateway PID, `NRestarts=0`, and the Gateway ready.
- About 0.8 to 1.1 s left the stop per run with work. The host load was high (5 to 11) during both cells, and outage differences between runs are larger than that, so the outage numbers here are within noise. I don't claim an outage win from these cells beyond the cleanup time that moved out.

- The cells ran on `fe42d651b7d`. The branch then merged `main` (unrelated changes, including plugin preparation worker release in #206172). The settlement, retained-runtime, migration-refusal and requester-authority suites were rerun on the merged head `877ca888d77` (59 passed); the cells were not.
- Config publication and service definition repair were not moved; they need agreement from their owners on #204775.

prs.title: feat: send compact chat context to models on the small profile
prs.body:
Closes #204354. Related: openclaw/rfcs#18 (Agent Profiles RFC)

## What Problem This Solves

A local model with a small context window gets the same system prompt as a hosted model. On a 32K window that prompt fills about 40% of the window before the user says anything. Lean mode (`experimental.localModelLean`) trims only some of it and cannot be set per model size. Agent Profiles (RFC 18) give each agent a named profile that sets the workspace budget, context serialization and tool surface.

This is slice 3 of 3 of the Agent Profiles work, split from one 90-commit branch so each part can be reviewed on its own. Stacked on slice 2. Retarget to `main` after slices 1 and 2 merge.

Dependencies: depends on #202517 (slice 1: `contextSerialization` and `toolProfile`) and on #204132 (slice 2: `auto` selection).

## This slice

Head `0ef63c3d6999d11de7334e1f60a085e74437e47b`: the signed merge of main `f57a32938b7b` into `ef5af6bf513a`, a signed fix on top of `4d26753da267` (the signed merge of main `2fda93cf03a8` into `8cdb03c8f44d`). `8cdb03c8f44d` is a signed fix on top of `2cefd2704313`, the signed merge of the current #204132 head `be1e09c662f8` into the previous head `286a1b86900a`. The slice's own work is 21 commits (`ffbd7500b337..a0fafb43ed31`, `8cdb03c8f44d` and `ef5af6bf513a`: 1 by Onur Solmaz, the rest by Mitchell Etzel); no signed commit was rewritten. To inspect only this slice, use `git diff be1e09c662f8 0ef63c3d6999d11de7334e1f60a085e74437e47b`.

This slice lets `openclaw/small` send a compact inbound context. It needs slices 1 and 2.

- Compact context serialization: one marked `Context facts:` block replaces the verbose inbound metadata, with bounded strings like the default path.
- Worker turns use the serialization the profile selects: `prepareWorkerTurnPrompt` resolves it from the selected profile and passes it to the prompt context, as the embedded prompt phase does.
- The Telegram current-message carrier stays outside the marked block, so stripping the block never removes user text.
- A session transcript row is removed from compact history only when a native row of the same window or history has the same timestamp and trimmed raw body. Distinct bodies that display identically are kept. A delivered cron close-out, a message-tool source reply, or an assistant row that happens to share its body with another speaker's message is kept.
- The compact Reply target falls back to the nearest `ReplyChain` entry that has a body, so channels that quote only through `ReplyChain` (Nextcloud Talk) keep the quoted sender and body on `openclaw/small`.
- A Telegram reply sends its quote once: when the Telegram current-message block already quotes the reply (`formatTelegramCurrentMessageContext`), the compact builder skips its Reply target, the same rule the default builder applies (`inbound-meta.ts`, from #151099).
- A chat window that already carries the inbound history or the quoted message is not repeated in compact mode. Both builders use one helper (`resolveChatWindowCoverage`), so `openclaw/small` never sends a row twice where `openclaw/base` sends it once.
- `/context detail` reports the selected context serialization on embedded, worker and CLI turns.
- The benchmark script `scripts/benchmark-context-serialization.ts` and the prompt build entry point tests.

## User Impact

- Only a turn on a profile that selects compact serialization (`openclaw/small`) is affected, on embedded, CLI and worker routes. `openclaw/base` and no profile keep the default context byte for byte.
- A home on the latest stable release (2026.11.9) with `experimental.localModelLean: true` moves to `openclaw/small` through `openclaw doctor --fix`, and an agent that set it to `false` moves to `openclaw/base`. The stored session continues after the upgrade.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compact context is the part of the small profile that shrinks per-turn inbound metadata. It belongs to the profile, so worker, embedded and CLI routes read the same selection instead of a separate switch.

Config and API surface: no new user-facing config option. `contextSerialization` is a field of the profile spec, not a key operators set (`agent-profile-config.test.ts` and the schema do not expose it standalone).

## Evidence

Run on a Mac Studio (macOS arm64, Node 24.22.2). The history-row capture below is from `ef5af6bf513a`. The Gateway and upgrade receipts are from `8cdb03c8f44d`. Since then the head adds the merges of main `2fda93cf03a8` and `f57a32938b7b` and the chat-window coverage fix; none of them touches the Gateway reply route or the Doctor migration. Main's new per-agent `sharedUserDir` field sits next to `agentProfileId`; the per-agent `experimental` block this stack retires stays retired.

### Real behavior proof: a real Gateway turn

`openclaw gateway run` on a loopback port, with its own home, state dir and config, built from this head (`pnpm build`), and a loopback OpenAI-compatible provider that records each request body. The turns go through `openclaw gateway call chat.send`, the webchat send route. Turn 1 is a plain send. Turn 2 replies to turn 1's assistant message (`replyToId`), so the Gateway hydrates the quoted body from session history. Only `agents.defaults.agentProfileId` differs between the runs. Redacted excerpt of the turn 2 provider request:

```text
openclaw/small  bytes=43813  sha256=0639dadd51f74ecb8d6188991fcb886d95d706ebe56f79ebdc3465b883e06a4a
  Context facts: ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧
  Context: {"message_id":"<uuid>","reply_to_id":"<transcript id>"}
  Reply target: {"sender":"Assistant","body":"proof-ack-88dce45cef050ab2"}
openclaw/base   bytes=49052  sha256=8367dc11415860c2936c99e4707cf60a03cfc18807956336efbd46f3b2248912
  Reply target of current user message: ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧
  (fenced JSON) {"message_id":"<transcript id>","sender_label":"Assistant","body":"proof-ack-fee06ce0bfe54137"}
```

This route cannot carry chat-window rows: `chat.send` has no structured-context parameter, and the Gateway sets no inbound history. `openclaw agent` runs the agent command directly and builds no inbound context at all. The shipped producer of same-timestamp native and transcript rows is the Telegram channel, which needs a Telegram Bot API. So the row check below enters one level lower.

### Real behavior proof: what reaches the model, with history rows

The turn enters through `getReplyFromConfig` (the entry every channel plugin reaches) with a fresh state dir and a loopback OpenAI-compatible endpoint that records the exact request bytes. The inbound window has three rows: a native row, a transcript row with a distinct body (`status\nready`), and a transcript row whose trimmed body and timestamp duplicate the native row. The same input runs once per profile; only `agents.defaults.agentProfileId` differs. The verifier decodes the `Conversation data` fragments of the provider user message and checks the rows inside the marked block.

```text
openclaw/base   exit 0  rows=3  bytes=40831  sha256=5981cef6ec3d48d61f9d4b76b252bf7244e646b024049e55d37e3f75b3be663e
  #native-204133 <ts> Alice: status ready
  #session:distinct-204133 <ts> Assistant: status ready
  #session:duplicate-204133 <ts> Duplicate: status ready
openclaw/small  exit 0  rows=2  bytes=37381  sha256=bdc4b583b8ae6a05a59abccd0e0bcef44817c57ed4f00ce44c6b7db9a697e687
  Context facts: ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧ ... History:
  #native-204133 Alice: status ready
  #session:distinct-204133 Assistant: status ready
```

- `openclaw/small` sends exactly one `Context facts:` block, never the verbose header as well, keeps the distinct transcript row and drops only the duplicate. The duplicate id appears nowhere in the provider user text.
- `openclaw/base` sends the verbose block with all three rows.
- Negative control: the same verifier on the #204132 head `be1e09c662f8` (no compact slice) passes `openclaw/base` and fails `openclaw/small` with `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: wrong/missing marked block`. The verifier logs what it saw: `{"matched":0,"seen":[{"header":"Conversation info: ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧","rows":0},{"header":"Conversation context (chronological, selected for current message): ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧","rows":3}]}`. Without this slice the small profile gets the verbose block with all three rows, the duplicate included. So the check fails without the change and passes with it.

### Upgrade from the latest stable release

`openclaw@2026.11.9` from npm (lockfile integrity pinned) seeds a home with `agents.defaults.experimental.localModelLean: true`, an agent `optout` with `localModelLean: false`, an unrelated UI setting and one real session turn against a loopback model. The candidate CLI (`OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (8cdb03c)`, `pnpm build` of this head) then runs `doctor --fix --non-interactive`, `config validate`, and continues the same stored session.

```json
{"version":"OpenClaw 2026.11.9 (0032b1d)","candidateVersion":"OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (8cdb03c)",
 "candidateHead":"8cdb03c8f44d0d30b82b2dad3bbfc3cb5ebcea91","candidateUpgrade":"pass",
 "migratedDefault":"openclaw/small","migratedOptOut":"openclaw/base",
 "samePersistedSession":true,"continuedProviderRequestSawStoredMarker":true}
```

Both `localModelLean` keys are gone after the migration; the model, timeout, ownership, provider URL and UI setting are unchanged.

### CI on the previous head and how this head answers it

`pnpm test:ci-failed 204133` on run [45751719384](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45751719384) (head `286a1b86900a`):

| job | class | cause | on this head |
|---|---|---|---|
| `check-test-types-core-2` | new | `attempt-system-prompt.worker-placement.test.ts` came from main still using `localModelLean` and no `agentProfile` | fixed by slice 1 `b3b155ed`, carried in through #204132; `pnpm check:test-types` passes |
| `checks-node-changed-compact-large-40` | unknown | same file: `params.agentProfile.profile` TypeError | the selected test (`carries worker placement into the prepared sessions_spawn guidance`) passes |
| `android-test-third-party` | new | `SessionBrowserRefreshTest > archivedQueryRetainsOnlyItsOwnAcceptedPageAndReadsOncePerChange`, `ComposeTimeoutException` after 5000 ms | not touched: this PR changes no `apps/android` file. The same test fails with the same exception on scheduled main runs [45755476684](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45755476684) (`1140fc54a`) and [45730770934](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45730770934) (`f57a179eb`); the classifier compared only run 45742688583, where it passed |

### CI on this head: inherited failures

PR CI run [45897447430](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45897447430) on `0ef63c3d6999` has three red test jobs. `pnpm test:ci-failed 204133` classes each as unknown (no matching main job). Each failing file is outside this PR's diff and fails the same way on main `f57a32938b7b`, run locally with the selected command:

| job | failing file | on main `f57a32938b7b` |
|---|---|---|
| `checks-node-changed-11` | `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/telegram-recovered-artifact.e2e.test.ts` | same failure: `AssertionError: expected { …(7) } to match object { status: 'ok' }` |
| `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-11` | `extensions/openai/realtime-live-api.test.ts` | same failure: 1 failed, 8 passed, `expected { session: <redacted len=8>, …(1) } to deeply equal ...` |
| `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-15` | `extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-history-control.test.ts` | same failure: two `ArrayContaining` assertions |

### Gates

Against main `2fda93cf03a8`, then `f57a32938b7b` for this head.

| gate | head | result |
|---|---|---|
| merged-tree gate: `config:docs:gen` then `config:docs:check`, `tsgo:core`, `check:test-types`, and `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` for the 62 stack test files plus main's `bootstrap-files.memory-core.test.ts` and the config schema tests | this head | pass: 62 files, 1098 tests, 0 failed |
| `pnpm test:ci-failed 204133 --run` (selected test) | `02dd4000a793` | pass |
| `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, the 60 test files this PR adds or changes against main | `02dd4000a793` | 59 files, 1051 tests passed, 0 failed |
| red/green: `inbound-meta.compact-window-coverage.test.ts` and `cli-runner/prepare.agent-profile.test.ts` | `ef5af6bf513a` | before the fix 3 fail (`expected 2 to be 1`, `not to contain 'Reply target:'`, `expected undefined to deeply equal { mode: 'compact', ... }`); with it 15 pass |
| `inbound-meta`, compact, current-message, delivery-context, worker and prompt-context suites | `ef5af6bf513a` | 159 passed |
| `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm check:test-types` | `ef5af6bf513a` and this head | pass |
| `pnpm config:docs:check` | `4d26753da267` | pass |
| `check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base <main> --no-merge-base` | this head | pass: net +3886, allowance 400, allocation credit 3486 |
| `pnpm deadcode:unused-files` | `4d26753da267` | pass: production and full-tree scans report 0 entries |
| type-aware oxlint on the changed core files (`run-oxlint-shards.mts --only=core --files-json`) and `run-format.mts --check` | `ef5af6bf513a` | pass |
| `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main` | `4d26753da267` | all lanes pass except three, each identical on main `2fda93cf03a8`: the Plugin SDK surface budget (`public exports 3931 > 3930`, the same count on main), the dead export scan (`btw-runtime.ts: toSimpleContextMessages` and `subagent-control.types.ts: SubagentCancellationControl`, neither touched here, both reported on main), and lint (`max-lines` in `extensions/copilot/src/attempt-execution.ts` and `crabbox-worker-node-enrollment.test.ts`, both byte-identical to main). The full core lint shard timed out on the shared host, so type-aware oxlint ran on the 130 core files this PR adds or changes (`run-oxlint-shards.mts --only=core --files-json`): pass. |

PR CI runs the full suite.

### Earlier measurement (not rerun on this head)

On an earlier head (`745a2db4a37`), a real Qwen3-8B Q8_0 turn on llama.cpp with five history rows, a transcript-only close-out row and a `ReplyChain` quote shrank the inbound block from 915 to 515 characters (server prompt tokens 12585 to 11421; the profile also bounds workspace files and tools, so that difference does not measure the block alone). The close-out row and the quote were kept. A Gateway with a local paired worker on `a6e30e0ad36` showed the worker route sends the compact block on `openclaw/small`; for a short quote it was 7 characters longer, so compact context is a selection, not a guaranteed saving on every turn. Neither measures cloud workers or model quality.

### Decisions

| decision | choice | evidence | how to reverse |
|---|---|---|---|
| Worker serialization | Resolve it from the selected profile and pass it to `prepareEmbeddedAttemptPromptContext` | red/green worker prompt test | revert `a6e30e0ad36` |
| `builtins.test.ts` assertion and `context-serialization/resolve.test.ts` | Kept | `resolve.test.ts` is the original unit test of the resolver (Onur Solmaz); the `builtins.test.ts` assertion pins the documented serialization of `openclaw/small` | delete them and lower the record |
| Telegram reply quote in compact context | Skip the compact Reply target when the Telegram current-message block quotes the reply, the default builder's rule | red/green test in `inbound-meta.compact-reply-chain.test.ts` (Telegram reply sends the quote once; a Nextcloud Talk `ReplyChain` quote keeps its Reply target) | revert `8cdb03c8f44d` |

Only a plugin-executed CLI backend with a group message that has history is affected | follow-up commit in `prompt-context.ts` with a test on that transport |
| Chat-window coverage in compact mode | One helper, `resolveChatWindowCoverage`, used by both builders | red/green test; the default builder's output is unchanged (`inbound-meta.test.ts` passes) | revert `ef5af6bf513a` |

Onur Solmaz and Mitchell Etzel authored the original signed commits. Mitchell Etzel is credited on the follow-up.

### Needs a maintainer

- Sign-off on the new `agentprofiles` 0.1.0 dependency (MIT, exact pin, published by the RFC author). Production code imports only its types. This is part of slice 1.
- A direction call on widening lean mode into the small profile (compact serialization plus the workspace budget).

prs.title: refactor: remove automation reasoning and reminder context options
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

I am narrowing automation setup by removing reasoning delivery and the option to copy recent chat into new reminders. The current run style already provides conversation context.

## User Impact

I removed **Include reasoning**, its CLI switches and API field, and the automations tool's `contextMessages` option. Model thinking settings and existing reminder text are unchanged.

Combined chat + webhook delivery (`delivery.completionDestination`), primary webhooks, failure alerts, tool restrictions, and their documentation remain supported.

Existing jobs retain any inert `includeReasoning` metadata in storage, so retiring the option does not change their approval-bound definitions. The flag no longer affects execution and is hidden from public API reads. New requests cannot set it; recreating a job drops the legacy metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

I removed reminder-history fetching and reasoning forwarding, not existing delivery features. I also removed the unnecessary Doctor data rewrite instead of adding approval-rebinding machinery or relaxing authority checks. Doctor's migration and eligibility code now matches main.

## Evidence

- I rebased onto main at `bf298a53334aa01379f52e6fb4f87106f2743a4b` and folded the repair into the same commit. The final diff has 59 files: production/docs/generated +36/-299; tests/fixtures +70/-82.
- I reproduced the approval regression on `4555f42836c9`: [update Doctor removed the flag and left the execution revision inconsistent](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45893290620/job/140161780776). On final head `97803ada894e`, [the same test passes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45895960734/job/140170774379), including valid standing-grant use after Doctor, stale-source preservation, revocation, and a second no-op repair.
- I proved both legacy-flag API cases fail before the fix and [pass afterward without mutating the stored job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45895960734/job/140170774185).
- Unsupported delivery rows retain main's early eligibility check and filtered legacy-notify migration. I verified those production files match main. The existing mode-42 preservation test passed on the regression baseline; I did not verify a final-head rerun of that unchanged test. No secondary-webhook deletion remains.
- I corrected the obsolete trailing argument without weakening recipient/thread assertions. [All four queued-delivery cases pass on the final head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45895960734/job/140170774207). CI exposed the same stale expectation in cron failure delivery; I corrected it too, and [those cases pass](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45895960734/job/140170774185).
- I pruned only the stale assertion-baseline counts for removed reminder code. [Final-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45895960734), including production/test types, lint, docs, and baseline ratchets. The required `openclaw/ci-gate` is successful.
- I regenerated Gateway validators, prompt snapshots, and the English UI baseline, and checked the final diff for whitespace errors. I did not run a live model E2E flow or the full supported-version upgrade matrix. Independent local autoreview could not start because its Codex installation failed the read-only sandbox preflight.

### Upgrade proof required before landing

I verified that this diff does not change the database layout/writer, Doctor production migrations, or updater code. It does change saved-job validation, normalization, public payload reads, and payload edits. I am treating that compatibility surface as upgrade-sensitive; real 9.x and 10.x updates remain unverified.

Before landing, the real update runs should:

- Start from each supported 9.x baseline, including extended-stable, and 10.x, using each old version's own updater to reach this head. Exercise the old updater's complete request/result/restart round trip, not just installing the new build over a copied database.
- Seed supported legacy jobs and approval state on each baseline. After upgrade, restart and run Doctor twice; verify job retention, correctly bound execution revisions, valid standing approvals on the next run, and continued refusal of revoked or stale authority. Where the baseline supports it, cover both reasoning-flag values and an unsupported delivery row beside repairable jobs.
- Verify combined chat + webhook delivery, legacy notify migration, tool restrictions, and edit/clone round trips. Existing reminder text must survive; retired reasoning metadata must remain inert and hidden from public reads, while final output still delivers normally.

### Historical UI evidence

I retained the original real-Control-UI screenshots below, captured with synthetic data and a mocked Gateway: before `2b58c8e5224ee0d2d9826467b5e1370e4091b1e9`, after `652f5503bde9193c87cc49fad8126c528974f105`. They illustrate the retained reasoning-toggle removal, not a fresh run of this rebased head.

### Clean comparison

**Before**

![The automation Results settings show Include reasoning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6498c8be-02e0-47f9-9f89-c14f19cda81a)

**After**

![The automation Results settings no longer show Include reasoning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cc495f16-f87d-48c7-b970-102c58fb489f)

### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![The Include reasoning row is highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d9282345-dedc-46a9-8959-90d41fb31cb7)

**After**

![The next remaining Results setting is highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5296351-8e19-4b53-84d3-05ca531cc887)

Co-authored with [Vyctor Brzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bfb77f08-1fd2-461f-ada5-4f3ff81fa044)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/3030a105-2a21-460e-baf1-7f72cab4188a)

prs.title: feat: pick an Agent Profile automatically from a model's size
prs.body:
Part of #204354. Related: openclaw/rfcs#18 (Agent Profiles RFC)

## What Problem This Solves

A local model with a small context window gets the same system prompt as a hosted model. On a 32K window that prompt fills about 40% of the window before the user says anything. Lean mode (`experimental.localModelLean`) trims only some of it and cannot follow the model size. Agent Profiles (RFC 18) give each agent a named profile that sets the workspace budget, context serialization and tool surface, but an operator still has to name the profile for each agent and change it when the model changes.

This is slice 2 of 3 of the Agent Profiles work, split from one branch so each part can be reviewed on its own. It builds on slice 1 (#202517: the resolver, `agentProfileId` and the Lean migration), which this branch contains. The PR targets `main`, so until #202517 merges its diff also shows slice 1; the command at the end of the next section shows only this slice.

## User Impact

- Nothing changes until an operator sets `agentProfileId: "auto"`.
- With `auto`, a model that reports 20B or fewer total parameters selects `openclaw/small`. Larger models use `openclaw/base`.
- A model that reports no count stays on `openclaw/base` until the operator sets `modelSizeClass` on its model row.
- Upgrading from a release with Lean settings needs `openclaw doctor --fix` (from slice 1). Doctor turns Lean on into `openclaw/small` and Lean off into `openclaw/base`, keeps every other setting, and existing sessions keep working. This slice adds no new migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Operators of small local models should not have to name a profile per agent. `auto` reads the total parameter count the provider or the config reports, never a model name, and an unknown size keeps `openclaw/base`.

The design comes from the Agent Profiles RFC, [RFC 0067](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/blob/bbac9427439b46b818f8fcfea1621caf28ea530f/rfcs/0067-agent-profiles.md) (openclaw/rfcs#18, authors osolmaz and vincentkoc, status draft). This slice builds three of its phase one parts as written:

- The `"auto"` selector at defaults and agent scope, next to registered profile ids, with agent scope over defaults (RFC section "Initial profiles").
- The four size classes from total parameters with the RFC's limits: `tiny` up to 1B, `small` over 1B up to 20B, `medium` over 20B up to 50B, `large` over 50B; mixture-of-experts models by total parameters (section "Model identity and model size classes").
- `modelSizeClass` as model metadata, which the RFC's profile bindings select on.

Two choices differ from the RFC text, both on the safe side. The RFC makes `"auto"` the default; here it is opt-in, so nothing changes for an operator who does not set it, and making it the default is a later owner decision. The RFC binds `tiny` and `small` to `openclaw/small`, which this slice does; `medium` and `large` stay on `openclaw/base` because their child profiles are not in this stack.

What this slice adds on top of slice 1:

- Size classes (tiny, small, medium, large) from total parameters, as the RFC defines them. Mixture-of-experts models count total parameters.
- Sources of the count: provider discovery for Ollama and LM Studio, `models[].modelSizeClass` in config, the model catalog, and llama-server's `/v1/models` `meta.n_params`.
- Size metadata on the workspace, harness, worker, Codex and catalog routes, so `auto` selects the same profile on each of them, including `/context` and prompt export.
- `--agent-profile auto` on `openclaw agent exec`.

Config and API surface: the value `auto` for `agentProfileId`, `models[].modelSizeClass` (and `parameterCount` from llama-server discovery), and `--agent-profile auto`. A provider that reports no count needs a place to state the class, so the field is required for the feature.

To inspect only this slice against slice 1 on the same main: `git diff $(git merge-tree --write-tree ee3f53e01f45 4934b24699c0) HEAD` (73 files, +1,374 / -185).

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

#### Upgrade from the published releases to this head

Each run starts from an empty, isolated state dir on the Studio: the published npm package (`openclaw@2026.11.9`, and `openclaw@2026.11.10`, which is npm `latest`) writes the config with the older Lean settings and stores a session with one turn against a loopback model fixture. Then this head (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build`, tree verified, no tracked file changed by the build) runs `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`, `openclaw config validate`, reads the stored session and continues it with one more turn. The seed sets `agents.defaults.experimental.localModelLean: true`, an agent `optout` with `localModelLean: false`, and the unrelated `ui.seamColor`. Session ids are shown only as a sha256 prefix and the state paths as `<scratch>`.

#### `auto` selection on a real llama.cpp model

Since that build, the selection code of this slice changed only by moving the built-in profile index next to the built-ins; the newer slice 1 and main merges came in on top. Run against a real Qwen3-8B Q8_0 on llama.cpp, one request at a time, through a capture proxy that records every request body and server `usage` block. Throwaway `OPENCLAW_HOME`, no Gateway, no `modelSizeClass` and no `parameterCount` in user config: the size comes only from llama-server discovery. Hostnames, IPs, ports, paths and session ids are redacted.

prs.title: fix(telegram): report reply targets accurately for split messages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Telegram splits a batched reply into several messages, it can send every page without a native reply reference. The delivery receipt still identified each page as a direct reply. In chats without a topic, progress callbacks could report the same incorrect target before the final receipt arrived.

## User Impact

Callbacks and final receipts report which Telegram messages actually carried a reply reference. If delivery stops partway through, the receipt preserves the reply and topic for each accepted page. The overall receipt keeps the original logical reply target.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Telegram sender now records the accepted reply target, or its observed absence, when it builds each provider result. Progress reporting, partial errors, and final aggregation all consume that result. Adapters that lack physical reply information keep their existing route fallback.

## Evidence

- On the registered Telegram path, 4,000 characters produced one direct reply. At 4,001 characters, neither batched page carried the target, and both pages carried it in all mode. Text, message IDs, ordering, and topic placement stayed intact.
- All 18 callback, returned-receipt, and partial-delivery cases passed across the Telegram sender and registered bridge. Cases included a second page landing in a different topic and an observer failing after two accepted messages. Discord mixed references and unannotated ZaloUser receipts retained their behavior.
- Both original Ephyra replay points and 400 generated cases passed on the revised code. A separate 60-turn matrix covered 120 synthetic text and media sends. The eight shared receipt tests passed with pinned Vitest on the same shared source blobs.
- The full project Telegram HTTP suite, project lint, and compiled storage-worker integration were not run locally.

On commit `8580510a`, [the Telegram HTTP suite](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45657037448/job/139357485322) passed all 61 cases, including reply placement at 4,000 and 4,001 characters with and without a topic and the accepted prefix after a partial send. [The shared receipt suite](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45657037448/job/139357485452) passed all eight cases, including JSON persistence and legacy inheritance. Both changed core lint checks passed, and both Gateway shards built the runtime and Control UI. The diagnostic run retained the background-work timeout also seen in [main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45645122717/job/139314901133) and the two existing Parallels export diagnostics. The Telegram boundary was exercised against the HTTP fixture. Live Telegram delivery remains unverified.

prs.title: improve: simplify the automation editor
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When creating an automation, Advanced settings exposes a raw routing field and lets you save a job that never starts or keep a one-time job around after it has succeeded. The editor also shows a second copy of the prompt you just typed.

## User Impact

New automations start active, and new one-time automations use the Gateway’s existing cleanup default after a successful run. The create and edit forms no longer show **Session key**, **Turn on after creating**, **Delete after it runs**, or the duplicate **Prompt preview**. You can still choose **Runs in**, read the saved prompt, and pause or resume an automation after creating it.

Existing automations are not migrated, rewritten, or deleted by this change. Saving an unrelated edit leaves the job’s existing routing, pause state, and cleanup policy alone. The Gateway API and CLI are unchanged. A duplicate retains its source’s routing, paused or active state, and keep-after-run setting.

## Why This Change Was Made

The editor now relies on the Gateway’s defaults instead of maintaining its own. The revamp had kept the editor’s Markdown **Prompt preview** under Advanced → Task; this removes that duplicate, not the saved prompt shown outside the editor.

The rebase retains main’s current schedule controls and model pickers. Model-agent resolution now reads the saved job’s routing instead of the removed form field. This PR does not change the backend or job migrations.

## Evidence

- I verified [CI attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45893648192/attempts/2) succeeded on `6c79ecde79453c5c6118e08a364b207478762b67`, including the typechecks, UI shards, bundled UI E2E, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. The original UI failure was the unchanged model-setup wizard timing assertion; [checks-ui (3/3) passed on rerun](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45893648192/job/140172498438).
- I inspected the final-head logs: [38 cron controller tests passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45893648192/job/140172499534), including preservation of a paused one-time duplicate with `deleteAfterRun=false`; [27 save/reopen tests passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45893648192/job/140172499774), exercising the real normalization, patch, and public read-projection owners in process. The [built-editor create flow passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45893648192/job/140172499864) against a mocked Gateway.
- **Stored data and updates:** I inspected the complete diff: only `ui/` files change. The removed fields belong to transient `CronFormState`, not the persisted job schema. [Edits omit hidden fields and duplicates copy their saved values](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6c79ecde79453c5c6118e08a364b207478762b67/ui/src/lib/cron/index.ts#L249-L305); the [unchanged Gateway patch owner preserves omitted values](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6c79ecde79453c5c6118e08a364b207478762b67/src/cron/service/jobs.ts#L295-L348). There is no storage-format change, migration, install-time rewrite, or updater change. New jobs use the Gateway's existing activation and one-time cleanup defaults. I found no source basis for the older review's stored-data incompatibility warning, so this diff does not trigger the 9.x/10.x update-proof requirement.
- **Other proof limits:** The real-Gateway CI lane was skipped; the separate run is recorded below. No real 9.x/10.x updates or relevant before/after editor screenshots are supplied here. Local Codex autoreview previously stopped at its read-only sandbox preflight without a result.

### Real Gateway proof

Supplied results cover clean builds of main `65a8bc8` and head `6c79ecd`, each served by its own loopback Gateway in a disposable Ubuntu 24.04 VM (4 GiB). Chromium 156 was paired through the normal dashboard handoff. No mocks or model credentials.

- Both revisions passed browser creation of a one-time automation, with a separate CLI connection confirming `enabled=true` and `deleteAfterRun=true`; duplication of a paused automation with keep-after-run and a saved session key, confirming a new ID and all three settings retained; prompt editing, reload and reopen, confirming persistence and the original intact; and pause/resume from the editor header.
- Regression replay applied the PR's four test files to main without changing production source. Main had **70 unit tests pass, 2 fail, and the browser test fail**: edits still sent `sessionKey`, schedule-kind changes still sent `deleteAfterRun`, and **Turn on after creating** remained visible. Head had **72 unit tests pass and the browser test pass**.

Not covered: scheduled firing, model output, or delivery.

Co-authored with [Vyctor Brzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bfb77f08-1fd2-461f-ada5-4f3ff81fa044)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/17960aa9-0186-4afe-89c2-8640dc88f0c6)
- [Finishing implementation and CI verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-automations-cleanup-prs-s1844eb19)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix: Matrix progress previews missing when the message tool sends the final reply
prs.body:
Root cause: extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/handler-draft-controller.ts:116 builds Matrix's progress-draft reply options without `allowProgressCallbacksWhenSourceDeliverySuppressed`, so with `messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"` core's progress gate (src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.prepare-execution.ts:180) drops every tool/plan/commentary progress callback before it reaches the Matrix draft.

Fixes #203006

Thanks @imshirka for the clear report and @ericcurtin for the fix.

## What Problem This Solves

With Matrix `streaming.mode: "progress"` and `messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`, the progress preview never shows. The final reply still arrives through the message tool, so nothing looks broken except that the progress is missing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core already has an opt-in for channels whose progress draft should keep working while the message tool owns the final reply. Matrix never set it. The other channels with progress drafts do:

- Mattermost `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-turn.ts:445` (when draft progress is on)
- Slack `extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/dispatch.ts:428`
- Discord `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts:661` (draft stream in progress mode)
- Telegram `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch-turn.ts:350` (answer-lane draft stream)
- Signal, iMessage and ClickClack also set it.

Matrix now sets it in `buildPreviewToolProgressReplyOptions`, which only returns options while a Matrix draft stream exists with progress/tool-progress previews on. With streaming off nothing changes.

Safety:
- Reasoning cannot leak: Matrix registers no `onReasoningStream`/`onReasoningProgress`; the option only lets the callbacks Matrix already registers (tool start, item, plan, approval) reach its draft. Core still refuses ambient room events (`InboundEventKind === "room_event"`) and send-policy denials.
- No duplicate final: the option does not touch partial text (`onPartialReply` is not forwarded under suppression, and progress mode ignores partials), and source delivery stays suppressed, so the final is only the message tool's send.
- The draft is removed after the final: the existing preview lifecycle (`cleanupUndelivered: true`) redacts the undelivered draft when the turn ends.

## User Impact

Matrix users with progress streaming see the progress draft while the agent works, then the draft is removed and the message-tool reply arrives once.

## Tests

The new 95-line test file and its worker-list entry are replaced by one regression in the existing `handler.active-turn-steering.test.ts`, which already runs the real Matrix handler through core dispatch. It shares the existing run-with-resolver wrapper with the steering test. Red on main (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 0 times`), green here.

## Evidence

Isolated Gateway built in secretless Docker from main and this head, local Synapse, real matrix-nio client DM, scripted model (read tool, then message tool send). Main (two runs): no progress draft, one final. This head (two runs): progress draft shown, final sent once, then the draft is redacted. Controls with streaming off and with automatic final delivery are identical on both builds. Event lists: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203025#issuecomment-7204007323

## Merge danger

Two-way door: one boolean in Matrix reply options, no stored state or config change; a revert fully restores the old behavior. Blast radius: Matrix rooms with draft streaming on and message-tool final delivery.

prs.title: improve: reduce OpenAI Responses request preparation overhead
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Managed OpenAI Responses requests rebuild a private copy of every tool schema whenever a payload hook is present. Read-only payload observers can run on every request, so they repeatedly pay for copies of schemas that OpenClaw has already normalized and frozen.

## User Impact

Managed Responses spends less time and allocates less memory preparing requests when the payload hook only observes them. Request bytes stay identical for observers. Hooks that can edit payloads still get independent, writable schemas. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Responses builder already decides whether its hook can mutate the message input. Tool preparation now uses the same decision. Published schemas are deeply frozen, so the builder can share those schemas with observers while retaining request ownership of the tool list and descriptors.

Production LOC is unchanged (+1/−1). The regression adds 33 test lines, and the reproducible benchmark adds 125 tooling lines.

## Evidence

Team measured 70 ms in `structuredClone → prepareOpenAIFunctionTool → convertPreparedResponsesTools → prepareResponsesTools`. The profile identifies the clone site. The production mix of read-only and writable hooks is unknown.

The benchmark exercises the managed Responses builder with 109 published tools and 144 synthetic history rows. It ran five interleaved A1/B/A2 processes per timing and allocation mode, each with 300 warmup requests and 1,200 measured requests. A1 and A2 use the same exact main source at `20b3afeccc4964fbd8a4a5bbe15fd8069ba4f6a5`. The acceptance rule is fewer clones and lower allocation with identical request bytes, unchanged writable-hook copies, and no material CPU or p95 regression outside A/A variation.

| Per observer-only request | A1 | A2 | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Structured clones | 109 | 109 | 0 |
| Builder CPU, µs | 727.86 | 724.89 | 66.84 |
| Builder p95, µs | 798.50 | 794.08 | 81.42 |
| Sampled JavaScript allocation, bytes | 750,140 | 751,919 | 260,848 |
| Serialized request, bytes | 213,270 | 213,270 | 213,270 |

All request digests matched. Writable hooks retained 109 clones per request in every arm. These timings cover request construction and exclude provider I/O.

The regression failed on the base at the shared schema identity assertion. On the fix it verifies equal tool JSON, schema reuse through the observer path, and isolation when that same hook becomes writable. prs.title: fix: stop background exec completion wakes from landing mid-line
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

A background exec's completion wake lands mid-line when the output is long. The wake embeds a fixed 2,000-char slice of the command output, and on a long run that slice starts where the bytes happened to be, so the woken turn cannot tell whether the last line is the command's result or just where the cut landed.

This PR makes the wake carry the last non-empty line of the output instead, but only when the retained tail was actually truncated. Output that fit in the tail keeps the full tail exactly as before.

How it works: when the session's total output exceeded the retained 2,000-char tail, the wake producer selects the last non-empty line of the tail, strips a leading `OK: ` or `ERR: ` marker when one is present, trims it through the same 2,000-char cap when it is longer, and falls back to the previous slice when there is no usable last line (empty output, structured tails). When the output fits, the content is the trimmed tail, byte-identical to the pre-change behavior. Header, duration, output-file pointer, routing and delivery are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Update 2026-11-26: real Gateway run (head `197f535527a`)

Built and ran an isolated Gateway from this head (loopback, its own state dir and port, Node 26.12.1, Qwen3.8-27B through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint). A background `exec` that wrote 300 rows (7,819 bytes) woke the session with:

```
Exec completed (swift-me, code 0, 7s), last line of 7819 output chars:
wrote 300 rows
Full output: <tmp>/openclaw-exec-4c73f763275911ae.log (7819 bytes)
```

A follow-up `read` of that path (`limit: 3`) returned rows 001 to 003 exactly. Steps and the redacted transcript: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200854#issuecomment-7203987078.

### Update 2026-11-25 (head `197f535527a`)

Merged main `9fb2059f340` (`e5b7090ff22`, clean; 2,456 commits behind) and pushed two commits on it:

- `b037b26d50c` is oxfmt output only. The previous head `f92d202c20c` was not formatted, and hosted CI never ran on it (`action_required`), so nothing caught it.
- `197f535527a` answers the open half of the P2 "Preserve complete short output and disclose every omission". When a truncated tail is reduced to its last line, the wake no longer says `last 2000 of N output chars` above that one line; it says `last line of N output chars`. A structured tail shown whole keeps `last <n> of N`. On the previous head the updated test fails with the old header: `... last 2000 of 2022 output chars (process log keeps the last 2000; earlier output was discarded):\nall done, 3 files`.

Main `9fb2059f340` has not fixed it, and no main commit has touched the PR's files since (checked through `0f73e04b3f9`). `prepareExecExitWake` still sends `tail.trim()`, and on the merge `e5b7090ff22` with main's `bash-tools.exec-notify.ts` and `bash-tools.exec-output.ts`, the PR's test fails 10 of 11, including "surfaces the stripped marker summary of a truncated oversized tail" (`not to contain 'OK:'`), the original defect.

- Each twice: `bash-tools.exec-output.completion-content` 12/12 (9 `selectExecCompletionContent` cases, 3 wake cases), `exec-background-followup` 28/28, `exec-notify.queue-full` 1/1, `.requester` 2/2, `.store-failure` 1/1. The follow-up suite's output-file assertion `last 2000 of 3008` still holds, because a one-line tail is shown whole.
- `tsgo:core` and the agents-tools test shard pass, each with a TS2322 control; oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- Test cost: the completion-content file 5.1 s warm (26.6 s cold); each case 1 to 7 ms. +102 net test lines, inside the 400 allowance.

On the other P2, "Resolve the whitespace-only test's contradictory expectation": the test asserts `selectExecCompletionContent(raw)` returns `raw` and `selectExecCompletionContent(raw.trim())` returns `""`, and a comment says the caller trims first. Gap: the new header is tested on the process-log branch only. The output-file branch uses the same value, but no test covers it with a truncated multi-line tail.


**On main `eee7a1bd526`** (head `f92d202c20c` applied with no conflicts; main is 2,105 commits past this branch's base; macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1, `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`). These run the repo's own test runner; the loader-based proof below predates them.

- `bash-tools.exec-output.completion-content.test.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-background-followup.test.ts` and the three `bash-tools.exec-notify.*.test.ts` files: 5 files, 43 tests, 0 failed.
- With main's `bash-tools.exec-notify.ts` and `bash-tools.exec-output.ts` and this PR's test file, "surfaces the stripped marker summary of a truncated oversized tail" fails (`expected 'Exec completed (wake-mar, code 0, 1ms…' not to contain 'OK:'`) and "keeps the full tail when the output fits the retained window" passes; the 9 `selectExecCompletionContent` cases fail with `selectExecCompletionContent is not a function`, since main has none.
- `tsgo:core` 0 errors; the PR wrapper inventory test (`eager-import-closure.test.ts`) passes. On `a84c030947a` both failed against its own main base, which `7199e72e732` (`noUncheckedIndexedAccess` on `lines[i]`) and `f92d202c20c` (`sliceUtf16Safe` in place of `bash-process-registry.ts`'s `tail`) fix.
- v2026.11.7 (`e31bbf056de`) carries #199122 as the backport `66364847341` without this change; its wake output is still `tail.trim()`.

- 10 unit cases in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-output.completion-content.test.ts`: last line, trailing blank lines, `OK: ` / `ERR: ` markers, empty marker line, empty and whitespace fallback, JSON object/array tails.
- 2 wake-owner cases in the same file drive the real path (`appendOutput` + `maybeNotifyOnExit` -> `prepareExecExitWake`): a truncated oversized tail surfaces the stripped `OK: ` summary with the truncation header, and output that fits keeps every line of the tail.
- The existing wake tests in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-background-followup.test.ts` pin the header, the `with no output.` case, the bounded tail and the file pointer. Their fixtures end in a single line, so the selected line equals the old tail and those assertions hold unchanged.

Behavior proof (review host): `pnpm install`/build/test are not available on this host, so the proof runs the patched sources directly under Node 26 type-stripping through an ESM hooks loader (`node --import ./loader.mjs proof.ts`). The loader resolves the repo's `.js` specifiers to `.ts` sources and maps workspace packages to their `src`; the only shims are delivery plumbing the wake path does not exercise (logger, system-event queue, terminal-core pass-throughs, published `@openclaw/fs-safe`/`@openclaw/proc-safe` bindings, `chalk`/`tslog`/`semver`/`string-width`, and the parameter-property-only leaves `retry`, `runtime`, `env-substitution`, `plugin-instance-error`). Wakes are rendered through the real entry point (`maybeNotifyOnExit` -> `prepareExecExitWake`) with three synthetic fixtures:

```
=== (a) short multi-line output that fits the retained window (input 27 chars) ===
Exec completed (proof-0, code 0, 0s):
line one
line two
last line

=== (b) oversized multi-line output truncated mid-line, last line is an OK: marker (input 2009 chars) ===
Exec completed (proof-1, code 0, 0s), last 2000 of 2009 output chars (process log has the rest):
done

=== (c) structured multi-line JSON tail (input 2008 chars) ===
Exec completed (proof-2, code 0, 0s), last 2000 of 2008 output chars (process log has the rest):
yyyy...yyy            (1,994 y's, abbreviated)
{
  "a": 1
}
```

(a) fits, so the full tail is kept, the pre-change content, unchanged. (b) is truncated mid-line and ends in an `OK: ` marker, so the wake carries just `done`. (c) is a structured tail whose last line is a JSON closing bracket, so the whole tail is kept.

Cut from upstream main `375daf6d3` (rebased after review). Verified against the main tip that no open PR or recent commit covers this.

One ask: the fork CI run needs a maintainer to approve it before hosted CI executes. Could a maintainer approve https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44837225822 ? It is the CI run for the current head `f92d202c20c`.
