prs.title: fix(test): preserve native test selection across scoped runs
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205106

## What Problem This Solves

Focused test runs can lose escaped filename selections, treat a path outside an owner as contained, or apply exclusions relative to a different directory from their includes. Native Vitest overrides can also be mistaken for defaults, including an explicit empty include list, and a selected browser test can fall out of its isolated partition when discovery moves.

## User Impact

Internal developer tooling only; application runtime is unchanged. The change keeps test selection, exclusions, and isolation consistent from the installed runner through native discovery. This is the third dependent part of the approved test-pattern repair split and remains a draft pending current-head validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve owner constraints after Vitest establishes the effective root, directory, and native overrides. Keep relative fallback includes and exclusions together, preserve physical absolute constraints, and escape physical path prefixes without rewriting native glob syntax. Browser partitions share the same physical isolation inventory and final parent selection while retaining explicit instance overrides.

Installed selector, chunking, and include-file writing paths use Picomatch's native grammar. Picomatch 4.0.7 was already locked transitively and is now an explicit development dependency; lazy loading preserves dependency-free Node planning before installation. No dependency version, patch, override, runtime, or package-manager change is included. The current parent fixtures and lifecycle guards remain intact.

The diff against parent `9cb13a833296ff392a1e5529408f2ed3cc3d7c1e` is 42 files, +2,443/-549 (2,992 changed lines): tests +1,060/-37, validation/configuration tooling +1,375/-512, and manifest/lock/allocation metadata +8/-0. The +863 tooling lines implement the native dependency contract across coordinate projection, override precedence, installed selector handoffs, and resolved-config discovery. Application runtime delta is zero. The separate 1,023-line test allocation accounts for the current dependent comparison, without reusing the original aggregate allocation.

## CI Follow-up

The completed [original exact-ref CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45604820557) executed `2fa1c4ed4af5ff92c19a1b0e4baad25e9fe70a19`. Its 163 jobs ended with 113 successful, 16 failed, 10 skipped, and 24 cancelled after the original work cutoff. The run is nonpassing. Its controller and sole cancellation completed with closed local custody; cancelled coverage supplies no runtime proof. These results do not validate the corrected head below.

The first two owning-check failures were repaired in `4e24f50`: optional native browser instance arrays are now accessed safely without weakening the matching assertions; the full-tree Knip graph explicitly declares the existing opt-in proof entry because Knip does not run Vite config hooks. Its support file remains transitive. No ignore or proof-body change was added.

Further runtime evidence exposed five failing cases, each on Node and Bun. The current correction addresses their owners and fixture assumptions:

- The escaped multi-chunk Gateway case failed in the inherited-selection prefilter before chunking. Installed one-shot runs now intersect physical file identities with both native constraint sets, then encode the result. Explicit owned targets and both negative sets remain effective; dependency-free planning and live watch selectors keep their symbolic path. The original two-mode, multi-chunk, 18-file assertion is unchanged.
- Both prerelease manifest fixtures observed empty file shards because the manifest inspected raw config fields. File-split discovery now invokes the target's native Vitest resolver, handles the evidenced Vitest 4/5 result shapes, and uses its resolved discovery directory. Existing partition, coverage, and runner assertions remain; a hook-only configuration with distinct root/directory and an excluded sentinel supplements the plain-config fixture. No prerelease or release workflow was dispatched.
- The moved-directory glob fixture placed default-policy sentinels outside that directory. Its three vendor/node_modules sentinels now lie inside both tested discovery directories; the separate absolute outside-directory exclusions remain unchanged.
- The POSIX escape fixture used a literal backslash in its crawl root, which tinyglobby normalizes as a separator. The root retains bracket metacharacters, while both bracket and literal-backslash filenames and every matching/discovery assertion remain. No dependency patch was changed.

These latest corrections are +42/-13 across six files, including allocation accounting. Current-head runtime proof remains pending.

## Evidence

Signed commit: `f4a2445e3bf95fb4ae31dfd43c5907e7d6508aa6`.

- Independent source reviews covered containment/native grammar, coordinates/browser inheritance, installed callers/transport, existing-fixture preservation, and the concrete CI follow-ups. Reported findings in those scoped reviews are resolved; this is not a runtime verdict.
- Targeted pinned formatting, the support module's syntax check, normal signed commit hooks, and `git diff --check` passed. Hooks preserved the reviewed postimages.
- The native staged test-line check passed against actual CI comparison base `e59991ed278550583e55d861edc8211dc4537cbc`: +2,249 test lines, allowance 400, allocation credit 1,849 (826 retained parent + 1,023 current change).
- At exact `2fa1c4ed`, Windows Server 2025 / Node 24.22.1 executed the whole native-glob fixture: 3 passed, 0 failed, 4 explicitly skipped. The passes cover CJS/ESM coordinates and Windows drive/filename case. The four POSIX/live-watch rows were skipped. Its owning invocation completed with 3 files passed, 37 cases passed and 9 skipped, no unhandled errors; the job completed all eight shards. Native output retains non-group descendant-completion uncertainty, so this is not a Windows teardown proof or corrected-head runtime proof.
- [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205296#issuecomment-7161752756) covers exact current head `f4a2445e3bf95fb4ae31dfd43c5907e7d6508aa6`: zero findings and no before-merge actions. Its optional request for current validation remains distinct from that source verdict.
- Current `f4a2445e` runtime/static/build proof is not claimed. The corrected follow-up [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45613556024) executes `4108051e899acdbcb0b3787781f61fd54ca8121e` in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205324; the dependent Watch [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45615043934) executes `785e929f87a3a6d83c33a8fb310dae212224bd85`. Both remain pending and retain their own head attribution. The task checkout has no qualified dependency install. Draft publication does not waive build or validation.

Required focused coverage includes the whole pattern-file, native-glob-coordinate, test-projects, UI-TSX-discovery, scoped-config, specialized-config, UI-package-config, unit-fast-config, and both prerelease manifest fixtures on Node and Bun, plus owning checks. The original run passed the whole scoped-config (32 cases per runtime) and specialized-config (11 per runtime) fixtures with their owning invocations, but its UI-TSX owner was cancelled. The corrected follow-up retains that missing UI-TSX obligation alongside its repaired whole-file checks; no cancelled or historical result is promoted to current-head proof.

Additional original-run follow-ups remain unwaived: the session-history benchmark child timed out before JSON parsing; a session-catalog response carried an unexpected export-policy field; and parked exec-completion settlement returned an undefined state where failure was expected. These are observed signatures, not causal conclusions or new repairs in this PR.

## Remaining Landing Limits

The old-head lint jobs also reported 11 max-line violations outside this change. Every listed file has identical Git bytes at comparison base `e59991ed`, parent `9cb13a8`, executed `2fa1c4ed`, and current `f4a2445e`; that does not waive the failures:

- `extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-node-enrollment.test.ts`: 1,062/1,000.
- `ui/src/components/browser/browser-panel-owner.ts`: 710/700; `ui/src/pages/cloud-workers/cloud-workers-page.tsx`: 731/700; `ui/src/components/board/board-widget-frame.tsx`: 710/700; `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-model-picker-panel.tsx`: 714/700; `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page.test.ts`: 1,031/1,000.
- `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-session.ts`: 701/700; `src/gateway/server-startup-finish.ts`: 703/700; `src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-execution.test.ts`: 1,021/1,000; `src/gateway/server.chat-goal-workers.test-support.ts`: 716/700; `src/gateway/server-plugin-reload.recovery.test.ts`: 1,036/1,000.

Parent component evidence remains attributed to its own commit. This draft does not claim a full native aggregate review, current-head runtime success, readiness, or landing qualification. Parent integration and the existing protected identity, setup/profile, key-save, import-boundary, retention, outbox, and deletion holds remain unchanged; no inherited CI failure is waived.

prs.title: fix: detect capability aliases when scanning skills
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The skill scanner can miss process execution and dynamic code execution when code calls an alias instead of the original capability. Skill authoring can therefore accept content that the existing critical rules intend to refuse.

## User Impact

Supported aliases now receive the existing critical finding and `unsafe_content` refusal before a skill file is written. Benign aliases, unrelated receivers with the same property name, shadowed bindings, and sequential reassignment have passing controls. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both rules share bounded syntax analysis using existing runtime dependencies. Lexical bindings and object identity preserve provenance through imports, namespace/method aliases, destructuring, and property storage, including properties named `exec`. Static ESM bindings are seeded before module evaluation; function bodies are inspected after enclosing initialization, without executing their writes in that scope. Sequential runtime writes replace earlier alias values; bare `var` redeclarations preserve them. Markdown file labels select Markdown decoding even when a fence-only document is also valid JavaScript template syntax. The existing Markdown parser supplies decoded fenced and indented examples plus inline code spans, including quoted/listed containers, mapped back to original call locations. TypeScript and TSX syntax alternatives retain angle-assertion coverage. Known object spreads copy current properties in order, so benign overwrites do not retain stale capability values. Destructuring defaults activate only for known JavaScript undefined; supplied benign callbacks and unknown values do not inherit a default capability.

This replaces the child-process-specific alias collector and the custom fence matcher. Literal call rules, finding caps, evidence redaction, and cache ownership remain in place. This is heuristic static analysis, not JavaScript execution or runtime authorization. It does not interpret runtime branch/loop behavior, function invocation order, arguments/returns, arbitrary computed values, call/apply/bind, prototypes, or cross-file flows. Alias analysis requires parseable source or an independently parseable Markdown code block/span; unparseable fragments retain literal rules.

## Evidence

Validated head: `e98325df19809414ccb7836700ee72f1f4455c01` on Linux. Scanned payloads were never executed.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/skills/security/scanner.test.ts src/skills/lifecycle/skill-authoring.test.ts src/skills/security/repository-skill-content.test.ts src/skills/security/workspace-audit.test.ts src/security/audit-extra.async.test.ts` — **5 files, 62 tests passed** (25.43s). Original alias regressions failed on the base; receiver identity, import order, closure initialization, Markdown containers and inline examples, TypeScript/TSX, and spread overwrite regressions each failed before their repairs and passed afterward.
- Process-call coverage includes computed destructuring, second-order method/namespace aliases, literal-array require arguments, TypeScript import assignment/assertions, ESM/CJS/node: forms, hoisted imports, closures, direct controls, and methods retrieved from object properties named `exec`.
- Dynamic-code coverage includes eval/Function aliases, global-derived bindings, destructuring, object-property storage, multiline calls, and nested closures. Harmless eval arithmetic retains the existing critical policy.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --openclaw-focused-config src/skills/security/capability-references.ts src/skills/security/scanner.ts src/skills/security/scanner.test.ts src/skills/lifecycle/skill-authoring.test.ts` — passed.
- `OPENCLAW_FORMAT_TOOL=oxfmt pnpm format src/skills/security/capability-references.ts src/skills/security/scanner.ts src/skills/security/scanner.test.ts src/skills/lifecycle/skill-authoring.test.ts` — clean.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services.json`, and `git diff --check` — passed.

### Real Gateway and plugin write boundary

Started `pnpm openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --allow-unconfigured` with isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, private token authentication, temporary workspace/state, and Workshop background learning off. The supported CLI built the source checkout successfully. The exact-head probe used `POST /tools/invoke` with the registered `skill_workshop` plugin tool for agent `main`; it exercised the real plugin invocation, SDK authoring, scanner, and filesystem.

`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs /tmp/skill-capability-gateway-proof-205275.mts "$GATEWAY_INFO"` — passed, with `GATEWAY_INFO` pointing to the isolated config/state/port metadata. Observed output:

Ten unsafe create operations and four unsafe support-file writes returned HTTP 400 with matching rules. ### Additional local owner proof

`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs /tmp/skill-capability-boundary-proof-205275.mts` — passed outside Vitest with no mocks. The shipped SDK `validateSkillFile` facade and production `writeSkillRootFile` owner each refused six unsafe samples before directories existed; a benign receiver/shadow/reassignment sample saved and read back byte-identically. Direct eval arithmetic remained critical. Focused authoring tests also exercise the combined `scanSkillFile` path.

Compatibility impact: newly recognized capability aliases can trigger the existing critical refusal. The bounded static-analysis limits above remain; this change does not claim complete JavaScript analysis.

prs.title: fix: repair orphaned Workboard card rows with Doctor
prs.body:
Related: #205245

## What Problem This Solves

Workboard card-child rows that reference a missing card can block an update at the candidate state snapshot. The snapshot correctly refuses those broken foreign keys, but affected operators don't have a supported repair.

## User Impact

With the Gateway stopped and Workboard enabled on a build containing this repair, run `openclaw doctor --fix`, then retry the update. Doctor preserves a private WAL-aware SQLite backup, deletes only supported orphan rows in one transaction, and refuses unrelated foreign-key violations. A clean rerun changes nothing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Workboard owns the repair in its existing Doctor contract. The updater and its integrity gate are unchanged; the recovery instructions live in the docs. The existing Doctor SQLite backup helper is exposed through the existing repair SDK subpath because the generic capture rejects FK-invalid databases. The backup retains the removed rows, so no separate export is needed. The writer that created the orphans remains unknown.

## Evidence

**Stable v2026.11.10 → branch-built Doctor, synthetic state.** Stable created the Workboard database and healthy card. After inserting one synthetic orphan, both CLIs ran `doctor --fix` against that same isolated state. Redacted log and SQLite verification excerpts:

```text
v2026.11.10 doctor --fix: Doctor complete; foreign_key_check still reports 1 Workboard label orphan.
Branch doctor --fix: Repaired orphaned Workboard card rows; backup: <private-state>/plugins/workboard/openclaw-workboard-card-orphans-recovery-<id>/database.sqlite
foreign_key_check: []; integrity_check: ok
Preserved: card="Keep stable card", label="keep-label", Workboard enabled, Gateway mode and configured port unchanged.
Backup contains the original orphan: card_id="orphan-fixture", label="remove-label".
Clean doctor --fix rerun: Doctor complete; no Workboard repair reported; recovery backups: 1 (no second backup).
```

**Regression red on main, green on PR head.** Ran `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/workboard/doctor-contract-api.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on both. On main, transplanted only the test diff; production sources were unchanged.

```text

FAIL  repairs card orphans only when no unrelated FK violations exist
Error: expected Workboard orphan repair to be defined
Tests  1 failed | 10 passed (11) — exit 1

PR head c77e357c3110
✓ repairs card orphans only when no unrelated FK violations exist
Tests  11 passed (11) — exit 0
```

The 10 Doctor declaration/import-closure tests, targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, SDK export synchronization/check, docs links, and diff whitespace checks also passed. The smoke was a manual CLI handoff, not an end-to-end run of the native updater. The full runtime build timed out at startup metadata after emitting the CLI exercised here; the full SDK API diff timed out during rendering. Neither is claimed as a pass.

prs.title: fix(irc): let status probes recover from shorter nickname limits
prs.body:
Closes #206163.

Related: #196619 and #40080.

## What Problem This Solves

IRC status probes can report `IRC login failed (432): Nickname too long` even while the bot is connected. The probe's separate connection collides with the bot's nickname, and its generated fallback can exceed a server's nine-character limit.

## User Impact

Probes can finish registration on servers with shorter nickname limits. Normal nickname selection and collision suffixes stay unchanged unless the server rejects a generated fallback. No configuration changes or migration are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`NICKLEN` can arrive after registration, too late to prevent this rejection. On 432, the existing client now shortens only the generated nickname's base, preserving its collision suffix. Each retry removes one character and stops before the base becomes empty; the existing connection timeout also remains in force. Initial configured-nickname errors still fail normally.

The pr-simplify pass kept recovery in the existing client, with no new cache, configuration, or probe-only connection path. The complete delta is +17 production lines and +55 test lines.

## Evidence

I added a real TCP loopback regression through `probeIrc`. The test server holds the original nickname, rejects overlong alternatives, and advertises `NICKLEN=9` only after 001. The regression also verifies the probe disconnects while the original client remains connected.

On main's unchanged client at `494fc885b05a6`, the new regression fails:

```text
pnpm test extensions/irc/src/client.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'probes a connected account when NICKLEN=9'
Received: "IRC login failed (432): Nickname too long"
Test Files  1 failed (1)
Tests       1 failed | 42 skipped (43)
```

With this fix at `047fb814a4278` (published head `bd734a56ce4002` has an identical source tree):

```text
pnpm test extensions/irc/src/client.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       43 passed (43)
Duration    40.03s

pnpm test:extension irc --maxWorkers=1
Test Files  15 passed (15)
Tests       151 passed (151)
Duration    65.96s
IRC_SUITE_EXIT=0
```

I also passed the repository typecheck scoped to both changed files, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check`. The full client file spends under one second in test bodies; the reported wall time includes compilation/imports. Hosted CI seconds are not yet available.

Local Codex autoreview could not execute inside its read-only review sandbox; I did not relax its permissions. The [supplied real-server E2E output](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206162#issuecomment-7203171187) now covers local Ergo with `NICKLEN=9`: main `b0f5ace37cff` fails with 432, while this exact head registers a shortened nine-character fallback, reports `works`, and leaves the bot connected. I reviewed the supplied output rather than running that E2E myself. The supplied report confirms the test VM was deleted; public IRC networks were not checked.

Reported by Dan Riccio.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-irc-probe-nick-length-s622478ec)

prs.title: fix(android): keep your place in code when a chat reply finishes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In Android chat, scroll to the end of a long code block while an assistant is replying. When the reply finishes and moves into history, the reader jumps back to the first line.

## User Impact

The code stays on the line you were reading when the reply finishes and when chat history refreshes. A different reply or another code block starts with its own reading position, even if the code is identical.

## Why This Change Was Made

The streaming reply and the history entry are separate Compose rows. Carry the reading position across that transition only when a unique new entry from the same run starts with the streamed text and the fenced block matches. Keeping the controller’s text and run identity together also preserves the reader when the server acknowledges a locally started run. If history arrives before the stream ends, each mounted fence keeps its own reading position once scrolled. A matching fence still at its start adopts the stream’s position once.

## Evidence

- In mounted Android chat with a 257-line block, **End of code** reached `FAR Ω` at offset 4484. The frozen build jumped to `FIRST` at 0 after the reply finished. The fix held 4484 through final delivery and a separate history refresh. Copy returned the full source.
- A same-run commentary message with identical fences opened at 0/0. The genuine final restored 160/420, and its newly appended third fence opened at 0. An independent mounted replay with offsets 128/364 also retained both through refresh.
- Two concurrent runs showing identical text kept independent offsets of 4484 and 280 across a server acknowledgment. Expanding a truncated history entry retained offset 9101.
- All six `ChatCodeBlockLayoutTest` cases passed on Robolectric SDK 36 with native graphics. The controller and Room replay used a mounted SDK 34 fixture and synthetic Gateway events. Physical-device behavior remains unverified.
- The fenced-reader regression passed in both hosted Android variants on `efb35c5c4821`. Both jobs failed the delivery geometry test at the `OpenClaw · Live` assertion. [Play result](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45703078554/job/139518729869) · [Third-party result](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45703078554/job/139518729928)
- The geometry fixture now uses a Gateway chat delta and a lifecycle end for the same pending run. In a focused SDK 34 replay, the original fixture passed on the parent and missed the Live label on the signed revision. The corrected events passed on both revisions. Both hosted variants passed the geometry and reader regressions on `b3261a980f6f`. [Play](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45706928842/job/139531862760) · [Third-party](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45706928842/job/139531862761)
- **Terminal first.** In the mounted controller replay, the terminal event cleared the stream before the history viewport took over. The reader held 4484 through settlement and a separate refresh. An identical sibling started at 0.
- **History first.** A synthetic `sessions.changed` event loaded the delivered entry while both rows were mounted. The signed parent lost 4484 at terminal. The repair held 4484 through terminal and refresh when the history fence was untouched. When the reader scrolled the history fence to 96 before terminal, it held 96 through both events.
- In the mounted two-fence test, live offsets were 160/420 and history offsets were 96/0. At terminal the history fences showed 96/420. After the reader scrolled the second fence to 500, refresh kept 96/500. All six SDK 36 reader tests passed locally on the tree signed as `2c6b3156f22a`.

**Installed-app proof remains open.** These are mounted Robolectric checks. No task-isolated device was connected, and the existing screenshot scenes do not exercise this event order. The screenshots below show the earlier mounted fixture.

Both screenshots show the settled reply after the same **End of code** action on frozen `b6e7fcfb` and signed `efb35c5c4821`, respectively. The fixture uses synthetic text.

### Clean comparison

The corrected head `2c6b3156` passed both Android flavors. prs.title: fix: keep CLI subagent role instructions on follow-up
prs.body:
Related: #143017. Follow-up to #185887.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Claude CLI subagents lose their standing role instructions when a follow-up arrives without the original launch prompt. A persistent child also lost its persistent-mode instructions once its completed run record was swept, in both CLI and embedded preparation.

## User Impact

Child sessions retain their role and delegation-depth instructions on follow-up. Unchanged role inputs preserve the prepared system prompt and the native-session reuse decision. A persistent (`mode: "session"`) child keeps its persistent standing instructions and prompt fingerprint after the five-minute run-record sweep. Current depth policy and caller-provided additions still take effect. No configuration or migration is required. Children spawned before this change keep the previous fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

#185887 introduced a shared standing-instructions renderer and used it in embedded preparation. CLI preparation still consumed only the current request's extra prompt. This change uses that renderer at the CLI boundary and avoids repeating the role already supplied on launch. Main sessions, side questions, control operations and isolated completions keep their existing behavior.

The spawn mode used to come only from the retained run record. The registry sweeps completed session-mode records after `SUBAGENT_SESSION_RUN_TTL_MS` while the child session stays available. Follow-ups omit or force the cleanup flag, so a swept persistent child fell back to run mode. The spawn owner now records `spawnMode` on the child's session entry next to `spawnDepth`, `subagentRole` and `subagentControlScope`. Reset, rollover and lineage, capability facts and reserved plugin slot keys preserve it. A re-spawn on a reused key rewrites it. CLI and embedded preparation read the entry, or the stored row when the caller has no entry. They fall back to the run record and then the cleanup flag only for entries created before this change. `sessions.patch` cannot set the field.

## Evidence

**Refresh onto `main` `1108290d41` (2026-11-26), current head `7145755dfa82273a0cc1a25e384bb476bf440b64`:**
- `75c6349a46` merges `main`. The only conflict was the import block in `cli-runner/prepare.ts`: `main` now imports `resolveCliModelCapabilities` and `prepare-hook-context`. This PR's single `prepareCliChildInstructions` import is added to `main`'s block.
- `7145755dfa` is a test-only follow-up. Since #197535, a manual `/compact` control operation rebuilds the full session prompt instead of an empty one. The "does not add a child role to control operations" case therefore no longer asserts an empty prompt. All three cases assert what this PR owns: no `# Subagent Context`, no standing role, and the caller's addition is kept.
- At this head: `tsgo:core` passes. The changed test files plus `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare*` pass, 14 files and 113/113 (WSL Ubuntu, Node 24.19.0, pnpm 12.15.0).
- The author's own Gateway has run this change continuously since 2026-11-02; today's build includes this head on `1108290d41`.
- The live and upgrade proofs below were recorded on `90c2702`/`297ddb9` and were not rerun on this head.

Head before the 2026-11-26 refresh: `297ddb9c845994a987f954efcb518a0a394e6c03`: patch commit `90c2702ea58bc20784c8e05c5312af313a7279d9` plus a merge of `main` at `8088fcd`. The merge conflict was in a test file only, and the diff against `main` is unchanged. The live proof and the before/after runs below used `90c2702` on base `9f3da25c107e88380e84f8a70f8f703422ba5995` (earlier qualified head `3360f06`). After the merge, the focused files, `tsgo:core`, the core test type shards, lint, format and the test-line ratchet were rerun.

- **Before:** the launch/follow-up regression fails at final system-prompt equality. The new swept-persistent regressions fail on the previous production code:
  - CLI preparation with no run record;
  - the embedded `persistent-swept` follow-up, which shows "Ephemeral";
  - spawn entry write and clear.
- **After:**
  - continuity, spawn-patch and embedded-prompt files: 57 pass;
  - capability-store, reconciliation, `sessions_send` authority, fast-path and policy consumers: 110 pass;
  - reset/rollover with `spawnMode` in the owned-child fixture: 7 pass.
  - These runs overlap with the earlier 102-test qualification, so the counts are not additive. That qualification covered the standing-instructions renderer, prefix stability and the synthetic Anthropic native-stdio boundary.
- **Static checks:** `tsgo:core`, the core test type shards, focused type-aware lint, formatting, test-line, max-lines, line-cap and assertion-safety ratchets pass (test-line allocation 173). A fresh independent review returned ready with no mandatory findings. Its one coverage note (rollover fixture) is applied.
- **CI:** the earlier red `checks-node-changed-compact-large-25` job was an inherited fixture failure in `subagent-spawn.production-boundary.test.ts` ("Gateway SDK resource host is not bound", #189317). #189329 fixed it on `main` after this PR's first CI run. The same failure appeared on unrelated PRs in that window. The later red `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)` on `90c2702` was a stale sidebar badge expectation in `boot-module-boundaries.e2e.test.ts`, fixed on `main` by #189641 (test-only). This PR changes no UI files.
- **Live proof (attached `claude-live-evidence-297ddb9.zip`, which supersedes `claude-live-evidence-90c2702.zip`):** both cases use the real Claude CLI native login. The persistent case was repeated on this exact head `297ddb9` with the same result (`live-proof.md` section 3).
  - **Run-mode child, `openclaw agent` on an isolated Gateway.** The child is followed up with `sessions_send`. The child's binding `extraSystemPromptHash` changes on base `9f3da25` (`a6f79a73…` → `84a5df93…`) and stays `a6f79a73…` on this head, with the same native Claude session resumed in both.
  - **Persistent thread-bound child, QA Matrix lane on a local homeserver.** After a 7-minute wait the child's run records go from 1 to 0, and the follow-up resumes the same native session. A pass-through observation of the `appendSystemPrompt` sent to Claude shows the difference. At `3360f06` the follow-up prompt contains "Ephemeral: termination after completion is normal." At this head it does not, and the entry carries `spawnMode: "session"`.
- **Upgrade from stable 2026.10.9 (`upgrade-proof.md`):** the published `openclaw@2026.10.9` ran a run-mode child that was then followed up. The same state was upgraded to this head with the documented `openclaw doctor --fix` (agent database schema 25 to 39).
  - **Stored data:** parent and child keep their OpenClaw sessions, and the model, runtime and `subagents.maxSpawnDepth` settings are preserved.
  - **Legacy child:** on 2026.10.9 its follow-up lacked `# Subagent Context`; after the upgrade it has it. Entries from before this change have no `spawnMode` and use the pre-existing fallback. On a `sessions_send` follow-up that fallback renders persistent wording, the same as at `3360f06` without any upgrade (control run).
  - **Legacy native session:** the changed prompt starts a fresh native Claude session once for such a legacy child. Its OpenClaw history remains.
  - **New child after the upgrade:** it records `spawnMode: "run"`, keeps its native session and code word, and gets run-mode instructions.

The tests use actual CLI admission, prompt preparation, binding hashes, native-session reuse resolution and the real session store with no run record. They are not a paid-provider cache or billing measurement. Restart and upgrade continuity is covered only by the single-process runs above. Broad platform coverage remains with PR CI.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction, scope and test cost</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.command-continuity.test.ts src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn-session-patch.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-system-prompt.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-models.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
```

To reproduce the failures, restore the production files to the previous head and keep the new tests. Verification used Windows, Node 24.22.1 and pinned pnpm 12.15.0 through the repository wrappers. The three-file run took about 5.5 minutes including worker preparation.

Scope: 21 files, +305/-19. Production is +127/-14: the CLI consumer plus the spawn-mode owner, preservation sites and store reader. Tests are 173 net lines with a matching allocation. The shared ceiling is unchanged. The existing renderer remains the single role owner, and no cache is introduced.

</details>

prs.title: fix: preserve native child work during Codex context rotation
prs.body:
Related: #165808

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native child work losing its parent ownership when token pressure makes OpenClaw start a new Codex thread.

## User Impact

Token-pressure rotation preserves the existing child assignments, and a failed successor start leaves the original parent binding available. No configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The token-pressure helper currently clears the saved parent before the normal replacement owner can preserve its children. Carry the selected predecessor to that existing replacement path instead, validate it against the current thread/client identity under the lease, and commit through the existing compare-and-swap operation. Do not add a new postcommit unsubscribe step; existing child protection and idle retirement retain their responsibility for the physical subscription.

This is the pressure producer path. It reuses the normal preservation introduced by #160952 and does not import the restricted-continuation changes in #156651 or broaden the completion-delivery authorization proposed in #165809/#169320. Ordinary claimed/protected rotation controls remain unchanged; saved-rollout byte rotation was later removed on `main` by #194902.

## Evidence

**Refresh onto `main` `1108290d41` (2026-11-26), current head `191af7d1a0f2bc54d261c857771dbe49ced9d383`:**
- `1d13fd5c5f` merges `main`. `main` (#202074) extracted the same local-execution placement predicate as `ownsLocalExecution`, so this branch's equivalent `ownsLocalProcess` helper (`70587487a9`) is dropped in favor of `main`'s. The pressure-rotation change itself is unchanged.
- `64c5f8d4b1`: after #194902 removed saved-rollout byte rotation, the token-pressure path was the last caller of the startup-binding `clearBinding` helper. This PR hands that path the predecessor instead, so the helper is removed as dead code.
- `191af7d1a0`: two `startup-binding.test.ts` cases added by #194902 asserted the old clear-on-token-pressure behavior that this PR intentionally changes. They now assert the retained predecessor (`expectPredecessorRetained`), matching the other token-pressure cases.
- At this head: `tsgo:extensions` passes. The changed test files plus `run-attempt-connection*` pass, 3 files and 49/49 (WSL Ubuntu, Node 24.19.0, pnpm 12.15.0).
- The author's own Gateway has run this change continuously since 2026-11-02; today's build includes this head on `1108290d41`.
- The built-Gateway comparison below was recorded on `c16048229a` and was not rerun on this head.

Pinned upstream base: `fa3e272e21361300a538c2ee1e21502ec5cd1e15`. Node 24.19.0, frozen dependencies, separate baseline/candidate installations and isolated state.

Published candidate: `c16048229a3a2c4c0350d530665ebf7fe80b35ba`. All 12 committed file hashes match the source used for the tests, builds, review and live comparison below. Publishing the commit did not change the tested source; these are the recorded local results, not a claim about later upstream revisions or hosted CI.

Built-Gateway comparison with real native Codex 0.160.0 and local `qwen3.8-27b-mtp-highest`, using synthetic input and fresh persistent state:

| Case | Actual initial tokens / native window | Pressure rotations | Child command and final | Gateway result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline, no pressure | 13,855 / 62,259 | 0 | Completed, exit 0 | Delivered once; observed at 3.059 s |
| Baseline, startup pressure | 13,738 / 31,129 | 1 | Completed, exit 0 | None during 90.927 s |
| Candidate, startup pressure | 14,176 / 31,129 | 2 | Completed, exit 0 | Delivered once; observed at 10.118 s |

All four helper hashes and the native binary hash match across these three runs. The reviewed source hashes match the built/executed candidate. All 20 provider calls returned HTTP 200; actual child and successor turns completed. The observed failure is lost delivery after rotation, not a model-unload or inference-timeout result.

The child executes real native shell work held on a FIFO. Only after the exact successor turn finishes does the controller release a unique nonce. The proof joins that nonce to the exact child's command item, exit zero and final marker. The successor must emit only its exact marker, with no tool items, so it cannot recover or terminate the child. Successful delivery is joined to its own Gateway-selected writer, native turn-start/completion, persisted final, Gateway lifecycle end and assistant history entry. The native client and physical requester session remain the same across rotation.

The candidate's small context triggers a **second** pressure rotation at announcement time; the result reaches the third/current writer. All distinct parent writers have zero native compactions. The successful cases show no duplicate in an additional five-second observation. The baseline's successful harness exit means the expected bounded non-delivery was observed, not that the product passed.

**Live-proof limits:** all three cases use the same disclosed test-only adapter to flatten/reverse five native delegation tool names for LM Studio, and a normal read/write client without admin scope. The adapter changes no model decisions, arguments, call IDs, results, usage or native RPC; it is not part of this production patch. This does not establish stock LM Studio namespace interoperability or repair the separate admin-client catalog/protected-parent failure found during setup. Child completion is released after successor restoration. One run per row is not a reliability or latency benchmark; the observation is not an unbounded exactly-once claim.

Source checks cover the additional pressure/failure paths:

- **Before:** the same entry-point regression has 3 failures and 1 pass. Startup pressure, projected-input pressure and failed successor start all lose the predecessor binding; the no-pressure control passes. Wall time: 43.242 s.
- **After:** 4/4 entry-point cases pass. Wall time: 58.598 s. The final affected suite passes **53 tests across five files**, including stale selection, changed connection, revoked authority, compare-and-swap conflict, claimed/protected predecessor controls, warm cleanup and subscription recovery. Wall time: 86.404 s. These counts overlap and are not additive.
- Baseline and candidate QA runtime builds pass. Targeted formatting, all three lint scopes, extension production/test types and script types pass.
- Independent Sol 6.1 High autoreview found no actionable P0-P2 issues in the exact diff and supplied unchanged ownership/retirement code. The reviewer did not run the tests.

The entry-point fixture uses real SQLite session/current-generation authority and production ownership logic, but its Codex binding store has an in-memory backing, native RPC is substituted, and completion reaches a substituted sink after restoration. The separate built-Gateway comparison above supplies real process/persistence/delivery evidence. Live coverage is startup pressure; projected-input pressure and failed successor start have source-regression evidence only.

The sanitized evidence bundle retains all 18 attempts, including unsuccessful ContextPilot controls, unadapted Qwen tool routing, corrected phase/live-process assertions, a separate admin-catalog failure and an initial native-home placement that did not activate pressure. These are setup findings, not additional defect reproductions. No model response, usage event or native RPC was fabricated to obtain a pass. The final comparison receipt is `main-live-final-comparison.json`; each final case includes its summary, provider receipts, native observations and source/helper/binary hashes. Reproduction helpers and their export transformations accompany the evidence.

prs.title: fix(codex): enable discovery for eligible restricted turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Restricted local Codex turns publish full dynamic-tool schemas even when the selected native model can discover deferred tools. This bypasses the existing searchable-loading setting and adds the complete schema surface to those turns.

## User Impact

Eligible restricted turns can use deferred schemas with the existing `codexDynamicToolsLoading` setting, whose default is `searchable`; explicit `direct` remains the opt-out. The model receives the complete qualified tool-name inventory and retrieves schemas through its native discovery mechanism. Tool execution still passes through the existing OpenClaw policy checks. Unlisted models, unavailable catalogs and the existing direct-loading exclusions keep direct declarations. Existing immutable thread catalogs and successor rules keep their current owners.

## Why This Change Was Made

The loading decision must use the selected model from `model/list` on the connection that will execute the turn. The patch acquires and retains that startup lease before preparing declarations, checks the native model identity, and preserves the existing ownership rules when acquisition fails or is cancelled.

A process replacement repeats connection-specific discovery but keeps the logical run's first context-engine assembly outcome, including an ordinary rejection. Reassembling there could substitute a different history after admission. Current-attempt authority and projection checks remain in their existing owners.

For these newly deferred restricted turns, the complete deferred-name inventory is admitted against the existing catalog-budget convention. Other searchable turns and retained native catalogs keep their existing admission. Overflow fails before native startup and tells the user to enable fewer tools, use a larger context window, or set `codexDynamicToolsLoading` to `"direct"`; count, size and limit stay in the diagnostic. It does not drop names or silently publish full schemas. Guidance follows the actual native calling surface, including Code Mode. There is no new configuration, SDK export, persistent cache or stored-data migration.

## Evidence

**Refresh onto `main` `1108290d41` (2026-11-26), current head `40747b72175a511a3133b8b0d8345f2f043c6603`:**
- `5de24e26d3` merges `main`. The only conflict was an import list in `thread-prompt.test.ts`; both imports are kept. The production diff against `main` is unchanged in substance.
- `40747b7217` is a test-only follow-up. #191830 raised the previous owner's unload-confirmation bound to `CODEX_THREAD_UNLOAD_CONFIRMATION_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000`, but the three settled-error client-replacement cases in `run-attempt.restricted-context-continuity.test.ts` advanced fake time by only 2 s. The replacement client never started, so they timed out deterministically on any merge with `main` after #191830. The test now mirrors the production bound by name, as `thread-lifecycle-policy-refresh.test-support.ts` does.
- At this head: `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:extensions` pass, and the 7 changed test files pass 89/89 (`--maxWorkers=1`, WSL Ubuntu, Node 24.19.0, pnpm 12.15.0).
- The author's own Gateway has run this change continuously since 2026-11-02, on builds 2026.10.9 through 2026.11.10. Today's build combines this head with #189348 and #172232 on `1108290d41`; its 28 carried test files pass 431/431.
- The upgrade and live-proof results below were recorded on the earlier heads named there and were not rerun on this head.

- Base: `9f3da25c107e88380e84f8a70f8f703422ba5995`. Head before the 2026-11-26 refresh: `d31deab6e9017a7d3190574ca1a300d0de037a46`, which is `9ab1559` plus a test-only commit. Earlier qualified head: `42ca0174d05b7545f0df08b73b4ce5d625eb6fa8`. Results below are for the earlier head unless marked as a review follow-up or an upgrade.
- **Upgrade from stable 2026.10.9 (attached `codex-discovery-evidence-d31deab.zip`, `upgrade-proof.md`):** a real isolated Gateway with the published `openclaw@2026.10.9` and `@openclaw/codex@2026.10.9`. The restricted agent (`tools.deny: ["group:runtime", "group:fs"]`) ran a `session_status` turn there. The same state was then switched to the upgrade target, with the documented `openclaw doctor --fix` (agent database schema 25 to 39).
  - **Stored data:** on every target, the existing session keeps its OpenClaw session and history and recalls the earlier tool result. `codexDynamicToolsLoading`, `tools.deny` and the model setting are unchanged.
  - **`searchable`:** the released 2026.10.9 already deferred 45 of 55 tools for this agent. After an upgrade to this head, the existing and new sessions defer 48 of 61 and call the tool. After an upgrade to base `9f3da25` they defer 0 of 61, because #175903 forces direct declarations when native discovery is unavailable.
  - **`direct`:** stays direct before and after an upgrade to this head.
  - This PR therefore keeps the released deferred behavior across the upgrade instead of switching restricted searchable agents to direct.
  - This PR adds no persisted field.
- **Review follow-up (`9ab1559fb125743ee3dc1143bf6798a7db73c81e`):** inventory admission now runs only for restricted turns whose model is listed on the executing connection, and the overflow `userMessage` names supported next actions. The overflow regression covers both paths at a 100-token window. The restricted turn fails before `thread/start`. The ordinary searchable turn starts and completes without a `model/list` probe; it fails with `TOOL_INVENTORY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` on the earlier head. `run-attempt.dynamic-tools` and `tool-inventory-budget` pass 24/24. Format, type-aware lint, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, max-lines, assertion-safety, test-mock-export, timeout-race and test-line ratchets pass. In `d31deab`, the redundant unrestricted catalog case is removed, as the review suggested. The overflow table's unrestricted row covers it. `run-attempt.dynamic-tools` passes 21/21, and the allocation is now 711. The self-referential catalog hash test and its fixture are removed. A fresh independent review returned ready with no blocking findings; the one wording note it raised is applied. The fixture-admission native acceptance below ran on the earlier head.
- **Shipped-entry live proof (`9ab1559`, attached `codex-discovery-evidence-9ab1559.zip`):** each run used a real isolated Gateway, two `openclaw agent` turns and a remote model through the Codex harness, on a turn restricted by `tools.deny: ["group:runtime", "group:fs"]`. With `searchable` configured, base `9f3da25` deferred 0 of 61 dynamic tools. This head deferred 48, and the model called the deferred `openclaw__session_status` after a native `ALL_TOOLS` search. Explicit `direct` at this head deferred 0. Each follow-up turn recalled the tool result without another call, in the same native thread. Limits: one model, tool and session per mode; prompts request discovery; no restart, upgrade, overflow or cache/billing claim.
- Baseline reproduction: the listed-model regression fails on the base after successful tool dispatch; the unlisted/direct control passes. With the patch, both pass.
- Focused candidate run: 301 passing tests in 16 files, six platform skips and one existing guarded-collector shell failure. The same unchanged `echo allowed` test fails on base production on Windows; its other two collector controls pass. No expected-failure exception was added. Coverage includes catalog fallback, exact native identity, inventory boundaries, client cleanup, startup-replacement recovery, and retained successful/rejected context assembly.
- Independent review found a borrowed-client abandonment defect in the initial port. The corrected fixture discriminates it: five borrowed-client regressions fail with the earlier helper while three owned-client controls pass; all 17 helper tests pass with the corrected helper. A separate fixture setup failure is retained in the evidence and is not counted as reproduction.
- Full `pnpm build` passes (15m56s), as do Codex packaged-entry types, the canonical extensions-test TypeScript graph, focused type-aware lint/format and line/environment ratchets. Node 24.22.1, pinned pnpm 12.15.0, Windows repository test wrapper with its supported Node fallback.
- Scope at the current head: 21 files, +1123/-63; production +363/-40, net test growth 711 lines with an exact allocation. No shared budget ceiling changes. The port keeps upstream prompt materialization and existing lifecycle owners instead of adding a parallel manager.
- Native acceptance on the earlier head passes with pinned Codex 0.164.0 in searchable and explicit-direct modes: two synthetic turns per mode, one actual tool execution, returned executor-only receipt, then same-thread recall without another call. Declaration exposure differs as expected. The probe uses production harness tool authority and real native/model I/O with isolated test admission/storage; it does not claim deployed-Gateway, durable-store or restart coverage. Prompts explicitly request discovery and forward the entire Code Mode result.

`model/list` membership is a conservative compatibility proxy, not a native capability flag. The supported source assumptions were inspected at Codex 0.164.0 (`6aaac694803004a63c6f393d153c96d22521a6b9`) and are recorded in the attached evidence; refreshed native metadata can drift. This patch does not repair Code Mode image projection or establish provider cache/billing savings.

prs.title: fix: stabilize prompt-cache fingerprint across transcript reloads
prs.body:
Fixes #150081 — Prompt cache fingerprint destabilizes when messages are reloaded from the transcript database.

## Problem

When messages are reloaded from the transcript database (session resume, queued/steered messages, mid-turn transcript reloads), fresh message objects are created with different references even though their content is identical. The reference-based divergence check (`message !== history[index]`) caused false-positive history rewrite detections that dropped the prompt cache from ~90k tokens to ~3k, forcing full recomputation.

Additionally, the `timestamp` field was included in the envelope fingerprint despite being persistence metadata that does not appear in the prompt sent to the LLM. For user messages, the timestamp prefix is already captured in the content hash. For toolResult messages, the timestamp is purely persistence metadata. Including it caused false-positive cache drops when messages were reloaded with slightly different timestamps (persistence time vs original creation time).

## Fix

This PR makes two changes to stabilize the fingerprint:

1. **Omit `timestamp` from the envelope fingerprint**: Add `"timestamp"` to `MESSAGE_ENVELOPE_OMITTED_FIELDS` in `prompt-cache-history.ts`. This prevents persistence-only metadata from triggering cache drops.

2. **Use fingerprint identity comparison instead of reference comparison**: In `prompt-cache-observability.ts`, change the divergence check from `message !== history[index]` to a comparison that also checks the packed fingerprint identity (`message.packed.slice(0, message.identityLength) !== history[index]?.packed.slice(0, history[index]?.identityLength)`). This means content-identical messages with different object references will NOT be detected as divergent.

## Testing

Added regression tests that verify:
- `timestamp` is in the `MESSAGE_ENVELOPE_OMITTED_FIELDS` set
- The code uses `identityLength` and `packed.slice` instead of pure reference comparison
- Changing only the timestamp does NOT trigger a history rewrite detection
- The existing test for timestamp field changes was removed (it is no longer a cache-affecting change)

## Impact

This fix is critical for local LLM providers (Ollama, llama.cpp) where prompt cache misses cause multi-second regressions. It also benefits cloud providers by avoiding unnecessary cache invalidations on session resume.

prs.title: fix(agents): stabilize system-prompt suffix across normal and announce/yield turns
prs.body:
Fixes #150081 — Ollama prompt cache drops when transitioning between normal main turns and `sessions_yield`/announce turns.

## Problem

When a session transitions between normal main turns and announce/yield turns, five volatile fields in the system-prompt suffix change values, causing Ollama's `prompt_eval_cached_count` to drop from ~25k to ~14k tokens. This increases prompt evaluation time from ~11s to ~123-203s on large local models.

The volatile fields are:
1. **Silent Replies section** — gated on `silentReplyPromptMode !== "none"`, which differs between normal and announce/yield turns
2. **Completion event guidance** — branched on `suppressSilentTokenGuidance`, producing different wording
3. **Assistant output directives** — gated on `(!sourceMessageToolOnly || messageToolAvailable)`, which differs by turn type
4. **Control UI Embed section** — gated on `(!sourceMessageToolOnly || messageToolAvailable)`, same issue
5. **Owner list fallback** — `command.ownerList` is empty during announce/yield turns, producing a different owner count

## Fix

This PR makes the suffix digest constant regardless of turn type by:

- **Silent Replies section**: Remove the `silentReplyPromptMode !== "none"` gate. The section is now always included when not in minimal mode (subagent isolated contexts), keeping the suffix stable across normal and announce/yield turns.
- **Completion event guidance**: Always use the full guidance wording (with `SILENT_REPLY_TOKEN` reference) instead of branching on `suppressSilentTokenGuidance`.
- **Output directives**: Simplify the gate from `(!sourceMessageToolOnly || messageToolAvailable)` to `messageToolAvailable`, since `messageToolAvailable` is stable across turn types.
- **Control UI Embed**: Same simplification for the embed section gate.
- **Owner list fallback**: When `command.ownerList` is empty, fall back to `resolveConfiguredCommandOwners()` which produces a stable result regardless of turn type.

## Testing

Added regression tests in `system-prompt-cache-stability.test.ts` that verify:
- `SILENT_REPLY_TOKEN` is a stable constant
- Silent Replies section is not gated on `silentReplyPromptMode`
- Completion-event guidance does not branch on `suppressSilentTokenGuidance`
- Owner list fallback uses `resolveConfiguredCommandOwners` when empty
- Output directives are not gated on `sourceMessageToolOnly`

## Impact

This is particularly important for local LLM providers (Ollama, llama.cpp) that rely on prompt caching for performance. Cloud providers with fast KV cache (Claude, OpenAI) are less affected but still benefit from stable suffixes.

prs.title: fix(plugins): release idle workers after preparing bundled state operations
prs.body:
Refs #192547

## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway that prepares bundled state operations can keep a JavaScript worker alive until the plugin registration closes. In a one-CPU ARM64 Gateway with the default memory plugin, the preparation worker held nine callable handles and had no pending calls at readiness, in the first chat handler, and at acknowledgement. The worker remained alive through the following 60-second soak. Its physical V8 heap was 32.5 MiB in the 2 GiB reference service. That figure measures the worker heap. The 768 MiB service has a separate first-reply test. [Gateway measurements](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192547#issuecomment-7180444727)

## User Impact

The Gateway can retire the last preparation worker before the first late state operation. Registered operations continue using their admitted code and dependencies after installed files change or disappear. An independent borrower keeps the shared worker until it releases its own capture. An in-place edit to an already loaded bundled export still requires a Gateway restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

The preparation worker owned the final copy of the selected operation graph. The host now transfers the same captured file facts, module lookups and native leases, and makes that final copy directly into an independent recovery claim. It releases the source worker after the transfer completes. Failed replies and synchronous binding cleanup both join physical resource disposal. The change applies to immutable bundled state-operation captures. External-plugin preparation retains its existing ownership and timing. [Related external-plugin experiment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177141)

## Evidence

- On stock `ee4061ce`, both async loader cases observed a live preparation worker at first use. Both synchronous controls passed. On `b6e51224`, seven focused suites passed all 90 tests, including first invocation after file removal, replacement registration, scoped and unscoped capture, native files, recovery, unexpected worker exit, and final teardown. The lost-reply and pending-close controls each failed independently on the respective pre-fix implementation. The plugin-platform TypeScript check and typed lint passed. [Linux x64 proof host](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45892060422)
- Forty synthetic registrations ran in stock/fixed/fixed/stock order on the same host, with 10 samples per dependency shape and revision. Every relative-dependency registration selected 115 original bytes and copied 230 logical bytes. Every package-import registration selected 218 and copied 436. Both revisions recorded two captures and two receipt passes. Registration p50/p95 was 239/509 ms on stock and 245/524 ms on the fix for relative dependencies, and 244/273 ms versus 250/272 ms for package imports. The two late exports together took 2.16/3.09 ms versus 2.10/2.79 ms and 1.52/2.34 ms versus 1.34/1.59 ms respectively.
- Independent lifecycle review covered native lease transfer, the bundled restart guard and both error paths. Local ClawSweeper completed the exact committed range `ee4061ce..b6e51224` with no listed risks or open questions. The signed successor `2417dad8` moves one existing ownership comment immediately above its type assertion. Executable source lines match the tested `b6e51224` exactly. The repository’s assertion guard counted 0 uncovered assertions on `ee4061ce`, 1 on `b6e51224`, and 0 on `2417dad8`. Local ClawSweeper also completed the successor range. Production changes add 137 lines and remove 45. Tests add 183 and remove 8.
- The matched ARM64 test used one CPU, a 768 MiB service cgroup, a 1 GiB outer cgroup and zero swap. Stock and patched images reached readiness at 33.206 s and 33.876 s, and acknowledged the first chat at 37.418 s and 37.488 s, respectively. Both peaked at 768 MiB and both lost the Gateway before the mock inference endpoint received a request. The first service OOM kill fell in 35.499–35.763 s on stock and 39.979–40.245 s on the patch, with three and two local kills in total. This single pair establishes that the 768 MiB first reply still fails. The external sampler did not measure worker ownership or a successful state operation in that run. [ARM64 comparison and limits](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192547#issuecomment-7180444727)

prs.title: fix(apple): preserve recalled draft spelling across session switches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In Apple chat, press Up to recall a message, replace `é` with `e` followed by a combining acute accent, then switch sessions. On return, the composer restores the draft from before recall and loses the edit. The two spellings look alike, but their UTF-8 bytes differ. This can happen without sending a message.

## Why This Change Was Made

Input history now compares the UTF-8 bytes of the edited text with the recalled entry. An edit that changes those bytes exits recall, so the existing draft-saving path receives the text the user typed. Re-entering identical bytes keeps recall active and preserves the user's prior working draft.

## User Impact

The edited spelling survives switching away, returning to the session, and reopening the stored draft. This follows the separate fix for a send accepted during history recall. [Predecessor PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206117)

## Evidence

Before the fix, both composed-to-decomposed and decomposed-to-composed edits saved the older working draft. With the fix, both cases recovered the exact edited bytes after an explicit save, a session round trip and a fresh model opening the SQLite store. The identical-byte control recovered the working draft, and an ordinary replacement recovered the replacement text.

The focused native SwiftPM run on the composed source passed 24 tests in three suites, including both four-case regression groups. The view model and SQLite store were exercised directly. A shipped-app keyboard recording was not collected.

On the signed head, all 2,730 OpenClawKit tests in 246 suites passed in 211.046 seconds. The four recalled-spelling cases passed in 0.352 seconds, and the four accepted-send cases from the predecessor passed in 0.214 seconds. [Hosted Swift package job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45890584120/job/140152513454)

prs.title: agents: let the sessions tool clear a thinking override
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The agent `sessions` tool could set a session thinking override with `action: "patch"` and `thinkingLevel`, but could not clear one. The reset words the rest of OpenClaw accepts (`default`, `inherit`, `inherited`, `clear`, `reset`, `unpin`) were forwarded to `sessions.patch` as level names and rejected as `invalid thinkingLevel`. `sessions.patch` only clears the override for `null`, and the tool parameter is a string, so a model had no way to send it. The same tool already clears a model override with `model: "default"`.

Closes #204998.

## Changes

- `src/agents/tools/sessions-tool-patch.ts`: `readSessionsToolPatch` maps `thinkingLevel` through `isSessionDefaultDirectiveValue` (the helper `/think` uses) and sends `null` for reset words. Explicit levels, including `off`, pass through unchanged, and unknown words are still rejected by the gateway. The single-session patch and the `targets` batch both build their patch through this function.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-tool.response.test.ts`: four cases (`default`, `inherit`, `clear`, `reset`) expecting `sessions.patch` to receive `thinkingLevel: null`, plus one case that `off` passes through unchanged.

## Evidence

Direct call of `readSessionsToolPatch` from source (`node --import tsx/esm`), same inputs on current `main` and on this branch:

| input `thinkingLevel` | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `high` | `"high"` | `"high"` |
| `off` | `"off"` | `"off"` |
| `default` | `"default"` | `null` |
| `inherit` | `"inherit"` | `null` |
| `reset` | `"reset"` | `null` |

On `main`, the string `"default"` is what reaches `sessions.patch`, which is what the issue shows being rejected.

Tests: `pnpm vitest run src/agents/tools/sessions-tool.response.test.ts` passes (9 tests, including the 5 new ones). With the one-line change reverted, the four reset-word cases fail and the `off` case passes. Repo formatter reports both touched files correctly formatted.

What was not tested: no live agent turn through the embedded runner (the issue's loopback-model run was not repeated), and `sessions.patch` itself was not exercised end to end; its `null` handling is read from the code and unchanged. `sessions-tool.test.ts` and `sessions-tool.batch.test.ts` were started but did not finish in my environment's time limit, so they were not confirmed. The full repo-wide `check:changed` was not run.

## Checklist

- [x] I understand what this code does: the tool passed the raw string to `sessions.patch`, which clears only on `null`; the change translates the shared reset words to `null` at the tool boundary, like the `model` line above it.
- [x] Local validation: the targeted vitest file passes and the formatter is clean; see the untested items above.
- [ ] Review-flow doc read; will follow up on Barnacle/ClawSweeper feedback

prs.title: feat: show mentioned people by name when an agent reads Slack
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent reads Slack history, people who are @mentioned show up as raw IDs like `<@U0AT23VB65A>`. #205621 named message authors, but a Learn from Slack scribe still wrote action items such as "U0AT23VB65A: give detailed candidate feedback" into Knowledge, because nothing told it who a mentioned ID was.

## User Impact

- A Slack `read` now also returns `userProfiles`: the names of users the messages mention, by user ID, whether the mention is in the text or in a rich-text user element. Message text stays exactly as Slack sent it.
- Learn from Slack writes mentioned people by name in Knowledge pages and claims. Its transcripts show `@Name` in message text, thread titles and reply quotes. Different people who share a display name stay apart (`@Sam#U2`, `@Sam#U3`).
- No new scopes: lookups use the same `users:read` as author names. A mention whose lookup fails keeps its ID, and the read still succeeds.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mentions reuse the author-name path from #205621: one `users.info` per distinct uncached user, through the cache keyed by account, token and workspace, so a person who writes and is mentioned costs one lookup. Names go in a separate map rather than rewritten text. That keeps Slack's raw text, and the Knowledge snapshot hashes built from it, independent of name lookups. The ingest normalizer records the names as an unhashed label next to `author_name`, and the transcript renders them.

Not covered: user-group mentions (`<!subteam^…>`), which need another API and scope, and channel links.

## Evidence

- Live, on a test Gateway with this change on top of #205614: a `read` of a channel with six @mentions returned `userProfiles` for all six. A forced Learn from Slack run read 10 channels and 211 messages, wrote 17 pages and 8 claims, and none of what it published contains a raw Slack ID. Example claim: "Vincent Koc set a fixed $7k OpenClaw reimbursement toward …".
- That run left 47 raw `<@U…>` lines in its transcript, all in thread titles and reply quotes. This branch names those too. Re-run on the same saved reads, 2 remain: thread titles cut off at 60 characters in the middle of a mention.
- Tests: the Slack read and action tests pass (72). They cover text and block mentions, a shared lookup with authors, a failed lookup keeping its ID, and unchanged text. The Knowledge normalizer and transcript tests cover names in text, thread titles and quotes, an unchanged row hash, and same-named users kept apart.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint, oxfmt and the line-cap ratchet are clean.
- A separate pre-PR review found that a mentioned user sharing a display name with an author was relabeled as that author in transcripts. It's fixed, with a test.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)
