prs.title: refactor: QQ Bot leaves core for the official qqbot plugin (installed by default, auto-migrated)
prs.body:
## What this does, in plain words

QQ Bot (Tencent QQ's official Bot API v2, as a Hermes messaging platform) leaves Hermes core. It becomes the official `qqbot` plugin in [NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/tree/main/qqbot), maintained by Nous Research, and like Weixin it is **installed by default on every Hermes home** (catalog `default: true`), idle until a QQ App ID and secret are set.

**Existing users do nothing:** the first `hermes update` (or the next agent/gateway start) sees that the profile ran QQ Bot and installs the plugin from the catalog once, and that same gateway start serves it. Same `QQ_*` / `QQBOT_*` env vars (legacy `QQ_HOME_CHANNEL` included), same `platforms.qqbot` config, same `QQBOT_HOME_CHANNEL`. **New users** already have it: the existing default-plugin installer (`hermes_cli/default_plugins.py`) puts it on every home once, and with no QQ credentials the gateway never starts the adapter (zero qqbot log lines). Whichever installer runs first, each home gets exactly one automatic install, and a later `hermes plugins remove qqbot` sticks.

## Round 17 (head `a6f9ca44b9c0`)
- Rebased onto origin/main. Main's newer hot-start suite listed `Platform.QQBOT` among the named profile's fresh platforms; it now names `discord` (`b3e418368eea`).
- **Silent off after removing the default copy** (Greptile on #159641): a home that ran QQ Bot in core and removed the idle copy the default installer placed was skipped quietly after the upgrade. `5b609cf830f8` (same `_pending` hunk as #159651 `443284d0addb`, equal `git patch-id`) keeps the removal and says the existing "…so it is off. Run `hermes plugins install qqbot`" line on the install backoff. Test `test_a_qqbot_the_default_installer_placed_and_the_user_removed_stays_removed_and_is_said_off` is red on the old head (1 failed), green here. The docs page says the same.
- Review threads: `d31fbbfa076a` (the later of `qqbot` / `qqbot-platform` replaces the other, as the gateway reads them; 2 tests red → green); `e485f9960ac0` (a non-list `requires_env` / `optional_env` reads as no env names, so one bad manifest cannot stop plugin discovery; shared with #159651); `66f891f77f0c` (cron reports a destination skipped because its platform left core, also beside a delivered one and for a saved `origin`; shared); `304de8b2a9ea` + `a6f9ca44b9c0` (an automatic install keeps a `plugins.disabled` entry the home already lists; shared). The `/reload` env thread is answered inline: core's existing rule for its own names, unchanged.
- Local: the PR's touched test files + left-core / default-plugins / catalog-platform / platform-plugin / hot-start / held-route suites + `tests/cron/`: 2,760 passed, 0 failed, 15 skipped. `scripts/check --only health`, boundary lint, no-tmp-literals, doc links ok.

### Live, round 17 (real `gateway run --force`, fake HOME, endpoints behind a closed proxy)
Trees: `v0.23.4` (stamped `0.23.4` by `deb_version.py --release-version v0.23.4` → `write_install_stamp.py`), and the removal heads stamped `0.23.4+canary.20261127T024356Z` by the same producer for `canary.20261127T024356Z-v0.23.4`. The fixture catalog pins qqbot `7e8bc4e` / feishu `2c8be75`, `default: true`. Each home had creds in `.env`, then ran v0.23.4's real `default_plugins.install_defaults` (the `hermes update` step): both plugins were placed idle and recorded in `_default_plugins_installed`.

| Leg | QQ Bot | Feishu |
|---|---|---|
| removed the idle copy (`hermes plugins remove <x>` on v0.23.4), then upgrade: new head | not reinstalled; logs `⚠ QQ Bot moved out of core into the 'qqbot' plugin, which this profile does not have, so it is off. Run `hermes plugins install qqbot`.`; one kept notice | not reinstalled; same line for `feishu`; one kept notice (logged twice on this first start, because the toolset-scope conversion changes the settings fingerprint and the start re-passes; the kept-notice queue dedupes) |
| same, old head (80868f4 / 99beefcc) | silent, not reinstalled | silent, not reinstalled |
| existing user (idle copy kept), upgrade | plugin adapter `hermes_plugins.qqbot` connects in the same start (refused at the closed proxy); `_left_core_installed: [qqbot]` | `hermes_plugins.feishu` `✓ feishu connected` in the same start; `_left_core_installed: [feishu]` |

Real `~/.hermes/config.yaml` md5 `c72b5ba9…` before and after.

## Round 16: staged transition instead of a version floor

The `>=0.23.5` floor is gone. Stable and canary both report 0.23.4 today (canary payloads read `0.23.4+canary.<stamp>`), so that floor locked every shipping build out, including a canary that has already dropped core's adapter. Both plugins now install on **Hermes 0.23.4 or later**. They do nothing while the running core still bundles the same platform. The check is whether core's files are present: `plugins/platforms/qqbot/` for QQ Bot; `plugins/platforms/feishu/` or `tools/feishu_doc_tool.py` for Feishu. On such a core `register()` registers nothing and logs one DEBUG line (`... the plugin stays inactive until core drops it`), and core's own adapter and tools keep serving. The first core without them gets the plugin's adapter, with the same settings and tool names.

- Feishu's `plugin.yaml` now ships `provides_tools: []`. `hermes plugins validate` fails any declared name that collides with a built-in, and core still ships `feishu_doc_read` / `feishu_drive_*`. On that core the plugin registers none of them, so it validates cleanly on main. **Follow-up after the core removal merges:** put the five names back in `provides_tools`. Until then, validate on the post-removal core reports "undeclared tools registered" for `feishu` only. Runtime is unaffected, because user plugins load eagerly and register the tools from `register()`. The catalog entry keeps listing the five tools.
- Seam used: the plugin's own presence check, which already existed. Main has no registry rule that prefers one side cleanly. Platforms are last-writer-wins, so the user plugin would replace core's adapter. Tools are core-wins, and the plugin's `register_tool` returns `None` with a WARNING on every start. Staying inactive avoids both.
- Cost on a core that still ships the platform: the package import, measured on a 0.23.4 CLI process at +0.08 s (qqbot) and +0.17 s (feishu).

**Rollout order:** fixed plugin PR merged → catalog entry re-pinned to the plugin's MERGED sha → check that the published catalog (`hermes plugins browse` / a catalog fetch from main) returns the entry → core removal merges LAST (→ Feishu only: the `provides_tools` follow-up).

### Live probe (real version strings, real installs, real `gateway run --force`)

Version strings came from the real producers. The `v0.23.4` worktree goes through git (`0.23.4`). The `canary.20261126T064809Z-v0.23.4` worktree got its stamp from `scripts/termux/deb_version.py --release-version <tag>`, then `scripts/write_install_stamp.py` with the Termux build's arguments (`0.23.4+canary.20261126T064809Z`). The removal heads ran twice: once stamped by the same producer for `canary.20261127T024356Z-v0.23.4` (`0.23.4+canary.20261127T024356Z`), and once through git (`0.23.4`, display `0.23.4+777`). The fixture catalog in each tree pins the pushed plugin commit (qqbot `7e8bc4e`, feishu `2c8be75`) with `requires_hermes: ">=0.23.4"` and `default: true`. Endpoints sat behind a closed proxy; each home had creds in `.env`.

| Leg | Core (reported version) | QQ Bot | Feishu |
|---|---|---|---|
| Existing profile, default install on the old core | v0.23.4 (`0.23.4`) | installed + enabled; core adapter `hermes_plugins.platforms__qqbot` serves; plugin `tools []` + DEBUG stand-down | installed + enabled; core adapter `platforms__feishu` connects; plugin `tools []`; no shadow warnings |
| Same | canary.20261126 (`0.23.4+canary.20261126T064809Z`) | same | same |
| Upgrade of that home | removal head, git (`0.23.4`) | plugin adapter `hermes_plugins.qqbot` attempts the token in the same start; no reinstall (plugin dir mtime unchanged) | plugin adapter `hermes_plugins.feishu` connects; 5 tools from `hermes_plugins.feishu.feishu_doc_tool`; no reinstall |
| Upgrade of that home | removal head, canary-stamped (`0.23.4+canary.20261127T024356Z`) | same | same |
| Existing profile, no plugin (left-core migration) | removal head, canary-stamped | installed once (`_left_core_installed: [qqbot]`) + plugin adapter in the same start | `✓ Installed the 'feishu' plugin…` + connects in the same start |
| Same | removal head, git | same | same |
| hermes-tag profile: stable, then removal head ×2 | v0.23.4, then canary-stamped removal head | — | stable: `Hermes Tag` serves Feishu over core, official plugin inactive. First removal start: one `⚠ The community 'hermes-tag' plugin…` line, also kept in `left-core-notices.jsonl` for the next attended turn, and the official plugin connects. Second start: no repeat |

Cross-check from the same runs: on the Feishu removal head, the default-installed qqbot plugin stays inactive (core still ships QQ Bot), and the reverse holds too. `hermes plugins validate` passes for both plugins on main, v0.23.4, the canary and the QQ removal head. Feishu on the Feishu removal head reports "undeclared tools registered" until the follow-up above. The real `~/.hermes/config.yaml` md5 was the same before and after (`c72b5ba9…`).

**Round 16: no code change in this PR.** The floor lived only in the plugin and catalog: official#520 `7e8bc4e`, catalog #159641 `7cd30f6`. The live table above ran this head (`80868f4d77c1`) as a git checkout and canary-stamped. Shared commits with #159651 keep the same patch-id: `dd3669581f63` = `f9be92efa16b` (predicate factory) and `80868f4d77c1` = `d561c62ce397` (empty `requires_env`).

_Round 16 supersedes the sections below wherever they mention a `>=0.23.5` floor, a probe tree stamped `0.23.5`, or a different merge order. The rollout order above is the current one._

## Slate (merge order)

1. **This PR** (core removal + LEFT_CORE row)
2. NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#520, the `qqbot` plugin (history kept: 157 commits; replaces the closed Labs PR NousResearch/hermes-labs-plugins#110)
3. Data-only catalog entry: NousResearch/hermes-agent#159641 (`tier: official`, `default: true`, `requires_hermes: ">=0.23.5"`; `hold`, re-pinned to the merged plugin sha)

Until 3 lands, a migrating home logs "cannot find in the plugin catalog yet" plus the notice and retries with backoff; a release never sees the gap if all three land before it.

## Changes

- **Removed:** `plugins/platforms/qqbot/**` and its 8 test files (moved to the plugin), `Platform.QQBOT` (`Platform("qqbot")` resolves once the plugin registers), `toolsets.py` `hermes-qqbot` and its `hermes-gateway` include, the `hermes_cli/platforms.py`, `tools_config`, `dump`, setup home-channel and web-messaging rows, the `QQ_*` `OPTIONAL_ENV_VARS` / env-key list entries, webhook deliver set, startup allowlist list, `/update`'s built-in list entry (the plugin's entry keeps `allow_update_command=True`), the shipped `qqbot: [hermes-qqbot]` row in `cli-config.yaml.example`, the compat required-name rows for the deleted folder (as the Yuanbao/HA moves), and the qqbot boundary-baseline lines. Shared tests drop only their qqbot cases.
- **Migration** (`hermes_cli/left_core_migration.py`): a `LEFT_CORE` row `qqbot` whose `in_use` is one `platform_in_use("qqbot", ...)` call replicating core's gate on main (`register.is_connected` + the `EnvCred` row): `app_id` + `client_secret` from the merged `platforms.qqbot` block (extra or top level; a top-level `qqbot:` block bridged), else `QQ_APP_ID` + `QQ_CLIENT_SECRET` in the home's env layers / secret scope; `platforms.qqbot` on; or `hermes-qqbot` selected for another platform (the Home Assistant precedent). `enabled: false`, or `plugins.disabled` naming `platforms/qqbot` / core's manifest name `qqbot-platform`, is not use. The row:
  - `plugin_key="platforms/qqbot"`, `plugin_names=("qqbot-platform",)`: core's old disable keeps holding over the plugin;
  - `secret_env=QQ_CLIENT_SECRET`, `private_env` = the other manifest names: `_HERMES_PROVIDER_ENV_BLOCKLIST`, `_ALWAYS_STRIP_KEYS` and `_ADAPTER_SECRET_ENV` are **identical to main** (checked by importing both trees; 14 QQ_/QQBOT_ names). `QQ_CLIENT_SECRET` joins `QQ_STT_API_KEY` on `local_env_policy`'s short adapter-secret list because `gateway_restart_env` reads that set directly;
  - no toolsets/off_platforms/legacy_toolsets: `hermes-qqbot` carried only core tools and the plugin registers none; Yuanbao's derived `off_platforms` now lists `qqbot`;
  - `platform="qqbot"`, `enable_env`, and `_qqbot_notice`: no placement sentence (official rows carry none, as Feishu's), only what changed for the home: a bare `qqbot` in `plugins.disabled` now turns it off, and `plugins.isolation: host` keeps a catalog platform adapter off. Yuanbao keeps its own Labs notice unchanged.
  - Profile-gate detection now takes every LEFT_CORE platform as a gate prefix, so `QQBOT_*_ALLOWED_*` stays a profile gate without `Platform.QQBOT`. This also makes `YUANBAO_*` / `HOMEASSISTANT_*` gate names count again, as they did before those platforms left the enum. `QQ` stays in `_EXTRA_GATE_ENV_PREFIXES`.
- **One automatic install per plugin and home** comes from main (#160177: left-core `_pending` + `_DEFAULT_INSTALLED_KEY`, default_plugins `_recorded`); the QQ Bot row only joins it. Held routes for a late-registering platform also come from main (#160253); this PR no longer carries its own copy of either.
- **Kept:** the shared own-policy helpers (comments only), cron's home-target order and the `QQ_HOME_CHANNEL` legacy alias, doctor's rename warning, the `QQ_` prefix alias for profile channel ownership, the `session_rules` route enum, desktop/TUI source lists. `hermes-qqbot` stays valid as a retired telemetry toolset value (`RETIRED_TOOLSET_NAMES`; the contract file is 1,982 lines).
- **Docs:** `messaging/qqbot.md` (+ zh-Hans) is now a short "moved to the official qqbot plugin, installed by default" page; toolsets reference, messaging index and other mentions say the same.

## Live migration probe

Real `gateway run --force` processes (own PID, killed after ~45 s) in a fake `HOME` + `HERMES_HOME` + `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` + `HERMES_GATEWAY_LOCK_DIR`, on a `git archive` of this head `2d034b04c21`. The catalog fixture's `qqbot` entry is `tier: official`, `default: true`, pinned to plugin PR #520 head `20a9a52ed021`. All outbound HTTP goes through a proxy on a closed loopback port (QQ's token URL is not env-overridable; `NO_PROXY` exempts the git/package hosts), so the connect is refused after the adapter is created. The md5 of the real `~/.hermes/config.yaml` was equal before and after (`d57827e7…`).

| Leg | Home | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 first start | `QQ_APP_ID`+`QQ_CLIENT_SECRET` in `.env` | `✓ QQ Bot moved out of core — installed the 'qqbot' plugin from the catalog (QQ_*/QQBOT_* settings … unchanged).` once; 0 lines with "not supported"/"Labs"; the **plugin's** adapter (`hermes_plugins.qqbot.adapter`) fetches a token (refused) in the SAME start; `_left_core_installed: [qqbot]`, enabled |
| 2 second start | same home | no install line; plugin tree mtime unchanged; plugin adapter connects again |
| 3 fresh, no creds | `install_defaults(home)` (fixture default) then a gateway start | `✓ Installed default plugin 'qqbot'`, enabled, `_default_plugins_installed: [qqbot]`; the gateway logs **zero** qqbot lines (no warning, no error), `No messaging platforms enabled.`, no connection opened |
| 4a install-once | creds; `migrate_home` → `install_defaults` → `migrate_home`, then `hermes plugins remove qqbot`, then both again | exactly 1 install (left-core), `install_defaults -> {'installed': [], 'owed': []}`; after remove neither reinstalls (dir stays gone) |
| 4b install-once | creds; `install_defaults` → `migrate_home` → `install_defaults`, remove, both again | exactly 1 install (default), `left_core -> []`; after remove neither reinstalls |

Earlier legs on the previous head (base creds = core adapter; no catalog entry = "cannot find in the plugin catalog yet"; multiplex secondary with creds only in `profiles/b/.env` = installed only into b and connects there) are unchanged by this placement change. First start also logs that the plugin's `qrcode` dependency was installed after the process started (setup-only; harmless).

## Round-12 rebase onto the merged enablers (head `1ee397fc8c24`)

Rebased onto main after #160253 / #160177 / #160180 / #160183 / #160200. Dropped this PR's own copies for main's: every `gateway/session.py` / `session_lifecycle.py` / `session_persistence.py` hunk and `tests/gateway/test_unparsed_route_survives_save.py` (main's `test_held_route_late_platform.py` covers the same cases), and the `_pending` / `default_plugins` one-install hunks. `git diff origin/main -- gateway/session*.py hermes_cli/default_plugins.py` is empty. The predicate factory and the off-platforms/cron/webhook commit are unchanged (same patch-ids), so other move PRs can carry them byte-identically.

Live, real `gateway run --force` on a `git archive` of this head, fake `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/lock dir, fixture catalog `qqbot` (official, `default: true`) pinned to #520 head `20a9a52ed021`, all other HTTP through a closed loopback proxy. Real `~/.hermes/config.yaml` md5 equal before/after (`d57827e7…`).

| Leg | Setup | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A existing user | `QQ_APP_ID`+`QQ_CLIENT_SECRET` in `.env`, no plugin | one `✓ Installed the 'qqbot' plugin from the catalog for QQ Bot…` line; `hermes_plugins.qqbot.adapter` fetches a token (refused) in the same start and retries; `_left_core_installed: [qqbot]`, enabled |
| B creds added live | fresh home, gateway running ~60 s (no qqbot dir), then `hermes config set QQ_APP_ID …` and `QQ_CLIENT_SECRET …` | 2nd `config set` prints "Running gateway is installing the plugin this platform needs…"; the live reconcile installs `qqbot` and the plugin adapter starts in the same process ~10 s later, no restart |
| C setup listing | `available_catalog_platforms()` | fresh home lists `qqbot` (`official`, installable); the leg-B home (installed) does not |

The probe tree carries an install stamp with `baseVersion 0.23.5` because #520 declares `requires_hermes: ">=0.23.5"` and main currently reports 0.23.4; without it the install is refused with the version message.

## Composite-round fixes (same hunk in #159640 and #159651)

- **Off-platforms come from the rows.** A row whose tools lived only in its own platform's bundle (Yuanbao, Feishu) sets `own_platform_only`, and `_derive_off_platforms` gives it every platform core knows plus every platform any LEFT_CORE row moved out. The hand lists `_YUANBAO_OFF_PLATFORMS` / `_FEISHU_OFF_PLATFORMS` are gone, so whichever of QQ Bot / Feishu merges second cannot leave `qqbot` off Feishu's list (or either off Yuanbao's). Test: `tests/hermes_cli/test_left_core_off_platforms.py` (stand-in rows + the shipped rows).
- **Saved routes to a platform that left core behave the same for QQ Bot and Feishu.** Webhook route load accepts any LEFT_CORE platform (no hand-kept `qqbot` entry), so a route a secondary profile's plugin serves is not skipped. Cron `deliver: <platform>:<chat>` delivers through the plugin's sender once it is loaded; without the plugin the delivery error and the preflight message name `hermes plugins install <plugin>` instead of "no delivery target resolved". Test: `tests/cron/test_cron_left_core_platform_route.py` (red on the previous head: the no-plugin cases and the webhook load of the other left-core platforms).

## Tests

- Round 12 (this head): touched tests + `test_left_core_*`, `test_default_plugins*`, `test_held_route_late_platform`, `test_platform_hot_start`, `tests/cron/`, catalog-platform/reconcile files via `scripts/run_tests.sh`: 234 files, 2,581 passed, 0 failed, 9 skipped (Windows-only). CI 16 passed / 20 skipped.
- New `tests/hermes_cli/test_left_core_qqbot.py` (21 cases): `in_use` true for `.env` creds, config-only extras, `platforms.qqbot` on, a top-level `qqbot:` block, `hermes-qqbot` on another platform; false for a fresh home, half a credential set, `enabled: false` with env creds, `plugins.disabled` `platforms/qqbot` / `qqbot-platform`; install once with no placement notice; a plugin the default installer placed and the user removed is not reinstalled by left-core, and vice versa; gate-env and strip-set parity. **Red on base** `70634248084b` (15 failed, 4 passed: the parity and fresh-home cases hold there by design), green on head.
- 78 touched/related files through `scripts/run_tests.sh` (fake HOME): 1,566 passed, 0 failed, 16 skipped (previous head); after this placement change the left-core + default-plugin files: 131 passed, 0 failed.
- `scripts/check --only health`, `boundary_lint.py --check`, ruff on touched files, `check_no_tmp_literals.py`, `check_doc_links.py`: ok.
- Plugin suite against a `git archive` of this branch (QQ Bot dir and enum member gone): 116 passed; `hermes plugins validate` passed; `scan_plugin` `safe` on main and `v0.23.4`.

## Not covered

- Version gate: #520 needs Hermes >= 0.23.5. On a main checkout that still reports 0.23.4, a QQ Bot home gets "requires hermes >=0.23.5" and retries at the next start; it resolves once the release ships.

- The QQ backend itself: every connect is refused at loopback once the adapter exists.
- The multiplexed-secondary leg uses creds in the secondary's `.env`, not an external secret source (that path is the shared Yuanbao code, unit-tested there).
- `required_names.py` rows dropped as in the Yuanbao move: an update swap from v0.22.3–v0.23.2 no longer finds the QQ folder during the swap scan.
- Open PRs touching the old `plugins/platforms/qqbot` path are not ported here; they belong in hermes-official-plugins now.

prs.title: fix(gateway-migrate): refuse macOS system LaunchDaemons in preflight and make launchd rollback steps state-aware
prs.body:
## Summary

Refuse automatic backend migration for macOS system-wide `launchd` LaunchDaemons (`/Library/LaunchDaemons`, `scope="system"`) in preflight (exit 6, zero mutations) with `sudo launchctl` manual steps, matching Linux `systemd-system` parity, and make `launchd` manual rollback steps privilege-, stage-, filesystem-, and shell-quoting-aware.

Refs https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/160209 (BM-14)
Credit: reported by `@deyil` on https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/160209.

## ELI5

Linux already stops before changing anything when the old Hermes backend runs as a root-owned system service, printing user-level instructions plus one `sudo` line. On macOS, a root-owned system LaunchDaemon slipped past that check, failed unprivileged partway through stopping the old backend, and printed broken manual rollback commands missing `sudo` and referencing a `.disabled` plist that was never created. Now macOS system LaunchDaemons are refused up front with one `sudo launchctl` step, and launchd rollback instructions shell-quote paths/labels, handle missing plists and partial restores, and only print `sudo`, `mv .disabled`, `enable`, or `bootstrap` when the host state actually requires them.

## Root cause & fix

**Root cause**
- `hermes_cli/gateway_migrate_backends_plan.py` (`_supervisor_kind`) separated `systemd` user units from `systemd-system`, but returned `"launchd"` for all launchd jobs regardless of whether `scope` was `"system"` (or `unit_path` sat under `/Library/LaunchDaemons/`). Automatic migration therefore accepted root-owned system LaunchDaemons, wrote config and installed the gateway service, then failed unprivileged at `stop_old_backend` (`Operation not permitted`) and failed automatic rollback.
- `hermes_cli/gateway_migrate_backends_apply.py` (`_manual_rollback_steps`) always emitted unquoted `mv <unit_path>.disabled <unit_path>; launchctl enable ...; launchctl bootstrap ...` for `launchd`, omitting `sudo` for system daemons, emitting `mv .disabled` even when `old_disable` never ran or restore already renamed the plist back, splitting paths containing spaces, and failing to handle missing `unit_path` or ambiguous legacy-manifest disable state cleanly.

**Fix** (+147/-12 prod lines, +324/-0 test lines)
- `hermes_cli/gateway_migrate_backends_plan.py`: add `"launchd-system"` to `_UNSUPPORTED`, add `_is_user_launchd_scope` / `_is_system_launchd` / `_launchd_manual_stop`, and route non-user launchd scopes (e.g. `scope="system"`) and `/Library/LaunchDaemons/` or `/System/Library/LaunchDaemons/` plists to `"launchd-system"` in `_supervisor_kind()`. Per-user LaunchAgents (`gui/<uid>`, `user/<uid>`) continue migrating automatically.
- `hermes_cli/gateway_migrate_backends_plan.py`: build launchd stop/disable (`_launchd_manual_stop`) and restart hint (`_restart_hint`) commands via `shlex.join()` with `sudo` for system LaunchDaemons, and populate missing `HERMES_DASHBOARD_*` env key names for `launchd-system` (falling back to `plist_environment(unit_path)` when root process env is unreadable, without printing values).
- `hermes_cli/gateway_migrate_backends_apply.py`: record `old_backend_stopped` and `old_backend_disabled` progress around `old_stop` / `old_disable` and update them in `_restore_old_backend()` during `_undo()` (skipping `old_enable` if `old_disable` never ran). Delegate launchd manual rollback commands to `_launchd_stop_progress()` + `_launchd_manual_rollback_step()`:
  - build all printed launchd commands (`mv`, `launchctl enable`, `launchctl bootstrap`, `launchctl kickstart`) with `shlex.join()` so paths/labels with spaces stay intact while clean paths remain unquoted;
  - add `sudo` for system LaunchDaemons;
  - omit `mv .disabled` when `old_disable` never ran OR when `Path(unit_path).exists()` and `<unit_path>.disabled` is already absent (partial restore where rename succeeded before `launchctl enable` failed), while preserving `mv` for non-existent paths when disabled;
  - keep explicit `old_backend_disabled=False` free of `mv`/`enable`, while including `launchctl enable` for legacy manifests with ambiguous `stop_old_backend` failure so a disabled job can come back up;
  - when `unit_path` is absent and the job was booted out (or stop state is unknown), instruct the operator to locate the original plist and run `[sudo ]launchctl bootstrap <scope> <plist-path>` instead of emitting an unusable `launchctl kickstart`.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_migrate_backends_launchd.py`: add regression and control tests (34 total in file) covering system LaunchDaemon preflight refusal (`--dry-run`, `--apply`, `--detach`), plist env-key discovery with unreadable root process env, scope/path detection edge cases, `user/<uid>` LaunchAgent automatic-migration preservation, `shlex.join` quoting for spaces in plist paths/labels, legacy-manifest ambiguous disable recovery, missing `unit_path` bootstrap guidance, and partial-restore `mv` omission.

prs.title: [Catalog] Add Ruse — bounded browser authority for Hermes
prs.body:
# Ruse — bounded browser authority for Hermes

## One-line summary
Ruse grants Hermes a temporary, owner-approved capability lease over a dedicated
authenticated browser profile (one origin, exact pages, one frozen write,
commit budget, expiry, revocation) and enforces it at the browser's network
boundary — denied requests never reach the application.

## Why this entry
Hermes lets agents drive real browsers using the user's authenticated sessions
(`browser_exec`/raw CDP, `browser_vault` credentials). Those are unrestricted
surfaces: nothing stops an agent from touching other records, deleting data, or
exfiltrating information inside the account. Ruse is the missing bounded-action
manifest — the browser equivalent of `computer_use.permission_mode: bounded`,
which Hermes already has for desktop control.

## Product promise
> Your agent can use the tools you approve. A page cannot change what those
> tools can do.

The owner grants a lease; Ruse enforces it request-by-request at the network
boundary (navigation, form submit, page fetch, XHR). Nothing is sent unless
prepared and committed exactly once; expired/revoked leases refuse everything;
fail closed on broker/policy failure.

## Evidence package
- 32 decision-matrix unit tests (`tests/test_lease.py`) — pure logic, no browser
  - Includes same-key/different-value body tampering, None-body attacks, query
    string in commit path
- 45 plugin surface tests (`tests/test_plugin_surface.py`) — all 10 tools
  register through Hermes' `ctx.register_tool()` contract, plus lease-name
  containment tests (`../x`, `/abs/x`, absolute paths, overlong names) and
  `HERMES_HOME`-derived data-dir scoping
- 24 real-Chrome end-to-end tests (`tests/test_e2e.py`) against a real local CRM
  fixture whose **server-side audit log** is the judge: blocked requests never
  appear in it
- Attack proof: a hostile page script attempts `DELETE`, wrong-record write, and
  cross-origin exfiltration — all three blocked, zero mutating requests arrived

## Catalog admission
- `repo: https://github.com/HillaryIkhais/Ruse.git`
- `sha: df34949ec5e16eef7c078690a01eb8d0114a7c22`
- `requires_hermes: ">=0.23.0"` in both the entry and `plugin.yaml`;
  `manifest_version: 2` in `plugin.yaml`
- Privileged capabilities: none (`tools.override`, `llm.*`, etc.). The catalog
  entry declares exactly the 10 `ruse_*` tools the plugin registers via
  `ctx.register_tool()`; no hooks and no middleware
- No core overrides — plugin registers its own toolset via documented
  `ctx.register_tool()`; middleware untouched
- stdout stays Hermes-protocol-only; broker diagnostics to stderr
- `playwright` dependency declared with upper bound; launches Chrome via the
  Playwright `chrome` channel; Playwright may fetch its browser on first use
- Honest framing: "not a sandbox" — governs the session Ruse owns; co-enabled
  unrestricted network/browser surfaces are documented as unsafe deployments;
  a compromised owner is trusted

## Rule 13 disclosures (catalog)
- Network: only to `browser.allowed_origins` (owner-declared); Playwright
  itself downloads Chromium on first broker start
- Shell/subprocess: none from the plugin; broker spawns one Playwright browser
  process
- Telemetry: none
- Self-update: none
- Writes: lease/receipt files under `plugin-data/ruse/` (derived from the active
  `HERMES_HOME`); dedicated browser profile under
  `plugin-data/ruse/browser-profiles/`. The profile persists the owner's
  sign-in session across runs so auto-login can be skipped; it is Ruse-owned
  and is never the user's everyday browser profile.
- Stored credentials: none in the plugin data dir. The login password comes
  from Hermes' secret scope (`RUSE_CRM_PASSWORD`); the profile's session cookie
  is the only persisted authentication state.
- Background: one broker daemon thread for the life of the session, owning one
  headless Chrome process. No telemetry and no self-update.

## Disclosure: YOLO / `approvals.mode: off`
Like any Hermes tool surface, Ruse's tools respect the session's approval mode.
With `approvals.mode: off` (YOLO), Ruse's tools would run without owner prompts —
that is a Hermes-wide bypass, not Ruse-specific, and is disclosed here honestly.

## Honest enforcement boundary disclosures
Playwright's `page.route()` does not intercept every possible browser egress path.
Ruse mitigates the known gaps:

- Context-level routes registered alongside page-level routes (popups, service workers)
- WebSocket connections denied by default via `route_web_socket`
- Redirect chains: handler fires only for first URL — `allowed_origins` should
  list only origins the owner fully trusts
- Body values compared exactly (not just keys); same-key/different-value denied
- No model-controlled lease paths — lease selected by name only from owner-provisioned files

## Review fixes since e81a230e (v2.0.1)
- `ruse_connect` now accepts only `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}` and verifies with
  `os.path.realpath`/`commonpath` that the lease stays inside the leases dir.
  `../x` and `/abs/x` are rejected; regression tests added.
- The default data dir now derives from `HERMES_HOME` (per-profile leases,
  receipts and browser profiles) instead of a hardcoded `~/.hermes` path.
- Auto-login no longer reads a plaintext `credentials.json`. The password is
  resolved via `agent.secret_scope.get_secret("RUSE_CRM_PASSWORD")` (declared
  as a `type: secret` config field). If the secret is unset, auto-login is
  skipped and the owner signs in once in the persistent profile. Login username
  and selectors are owner-authored under `browser.login` in the lease.
- Removed the unsupported README claim that Ruse detects co-enabled
  browser/network tools; the limitation is now stated honestly.
- `ruse_inspect` blanks password-field values before returning form fields.
- Catalog entry brought in line with the documented entry schema: quoted
  `version`, `maintainer`, `docs_url`, `category: tools`, `platforms: []`, and
  an explicit `capabilities:` block listing the 10 registered tools with no
  hooks/middleware/env requirements. Rule 13 disclosures expanded to cover the
  Ruse-owned persistent profile, the broker thread and secret handling.

prs.body:
Bumps the vector-platform catalog pin to the v0.6.2 release commit (following review on v0.6.1). The description is unchanged. Declared tools and hooks match what the plugin registers (`8` Concord admin tools + `pre_tool_call` approval hook).

- sha: `5b2e4b244076413139a4c8781047bf1dde138303` → `58a42f9d74e11ddc636f68fe452dabb8b2cd1909` (annotated tag `v0.6.2`)
- version: 0.6.0 → 0.6.2
- full range: https://github.com/BonesGit/hermes-vector-platform/compare/5b2e4b244076413139a4c8781047bf1dde138303...58a42f9d74e11ddc636f68fe452dabb8b2cd1909
- review delta (`v0.6.1` → `v0.6.2`): https://github.com/BonesGit/hermes-vector-platform/compare/b55029d13b127b2c5ee2aa17d4ba7d210b9dfdbb...58a42f9d74e11ddc636f68fe452dabb8b2cd1909

Later CI-only commits on `master` (updating the plugin repo's GitHub Actions workflow) are not in this pin.

## What 0.6.1 → 0.6.2 adds

A new sidecar with Concord community administration and `v0.6.2` security hardening. The plugin registers:

- `vector_community_inspect`
- `vector_community_moderate`
- `vector_community_channels`
- `vector_community_categories`
- `vector_community_roles`
- `vector_community_settings`
- `vector_community_invites`
- `vector_community_defense`
- hook: `pre_tool_call` (prompts for human approval on irreversible/high-impact actions)

Calls are enforced against the active Hermes session context (`HERMES_SESSION_PLATFORM`, `HERMES_SESSION_CHAT_TYPE`, `HERMES_SESSION_CHAT_ID`, `HERMES_SESSION_ACTOR_ID`) and fail closed if session context is unavailable. Local CLI/TUI stays off unless `vector.communities.admin_cli` is on. Public invite links stay off unless `vector.communities.allow_public_invites` is set. Admin tool schemas are gated behind a `@no_cache_check_fn` availability check. Community icon/banner updates accept base64 image payloads only (magic-byte validated for PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP; no host filesystem path reads).

## Disclosure

`hermes gateway setup` still downloads a prebuilt `vector-bridge` from `github.com/BonesGit/hermes-vector-platform` release `v0.6.2`, checks it against that release's `SHA256SUMS`, and falls back to building the bundled Rust source when `vector.prebuilt.download` is false. Re-run setup after this update so the sidecar binary refreshes. Setup merges `vector:` into `~/.hermes/config.yaml`, writes `VECTOR_*` to `~/.hermes/.env`, and publishes a public bot profile (kind-0, `bot: true`) to Nostr discovery relays. The admin tools act on a Concord community only when the bot has been given those powers.

## Test plan

- [x] `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/vector-platform.yaml` → OK
- [x] `hermes plugins validate` on `58a42f9d` → passed (declared tools + `pre_tool_call` hook match)
- [ ] Catalog CI `pinned-source-validate` clones `58a42f9d` and runs `hermes plugins validate --install-deps`

prs.title: fix(checkpoints): anchor runtime-cache excludes and skip the desktop release build
prs.body:
## Problem

`DEFAULT_EXCLUDES` in `agent/checkpoints/manager.py` is written into the checkpoint store's `info/exclude`, so it is matched with **gitignore semantics**, not by Python. Two consequences:

1. **An unanchored `cache/` excludes too much.** It matches *any* directory named `cache/` anywhere in the tree — including a user's `src/cache/` — silently dropping their source files from every snapshot. Same for `e2e-sandboxes/` and `hermes-e2e/`.
2. **`apps/desktop/release/` is not excluded at all.** It is the Electron build output inside the source tree (~429 MB in a working install) and is not covered by `dist/`, so `git add -A` inside the store hit the 60s timeout and every snapshot failed:

```
ERROR tools.checkpoint_manager: git timed out after 60s
```

## Fix

Anchor the three runtime/sandbox rules with a leading `/` so they only match at the project root, and add `/apps/desktop/release/`.

```python
"/cache/",
"/e2e-sandboxes/",
"/hermes-e2e/",
"/apps/desktop/release/",
```

10 added lines, no behaviour change for anyone who does not have these directories.

## Verification

Behaviour, not diff review. Temporary `git init`, rules copied into `.git/info/exclude`, then `git check-ignore -q --no-index`:

- root-level `cache/` → ignored (positive path)
- `apps/desktop/release/…` → ignored (positive path)
- `src/cache/x.py` → **not** ignored (anti over-exclusion; this is the regression the anchor fixes)
- `./cache/…` form → ignored

Also confirmed the checkpoint store's `info/exclude` SHA changes after `_init_store()` and that a snapshot completes without the 60s timeout on a tree containing the 429 MB release directory.

Note: `_write_default_excludes` rewrites `store/info/exclude` in full, and the list is applied at **store initialisation**, not at process start — so existing stores pick this up on next `_init_store()`, not merely on restart. That is pre-existing upstream behaviour and is not changed here.

prs.title: Saved GPT Image 1.5 picks keep working after OpenAI's Dec 1 shutdown (image_gen)
prs.body:
Saved `fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5` picks keep working after OpenAI shuts GPT Image 1.5 and 1 Mini down on **2026-12-01**: they now run on GPT Image 2 instead of breaking or quietly switching to Klein.

## Why

OpenAI's [deprecations page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations) (notice dated 2026-06-02, page updated 2026-10-22) shuts down `gpt-image-1-mini`, `gpt-image-1.5` and `chatgpt-image-latest` on **Dec 1, 2026**. Hermes still lists two of them:

- `fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5` in the FAL image catalog (fal only proxies OpenAI, so it dies the same day)
- `openai/gpt-image-1-mini` in the OpenRouter Image API list, where it is the only model offering `background=transparent`

## Changes

- Removed `fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5` from `FAL_MODELS`, plus the `gpt_literal` size style that only this model used.
- New `RETIRED_FAL_MODELS = {"fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5": "fal-ai/gpt-image-2"}`. A config that still has the old id is read as GPT Image 2 by both `_read_configured_image_model` (managed dispatch), `_resolve_fal_model` (config or `FAL_IMAGE_MODEL`), and `managed_backend_for_model` (router + `nous_subscription` status). No config migration needed.
- OpenRouter: replaced `openai/gpt-image-1-mini` with `openai/gpt-image-2.5-flare`, and a saved Mini pick (kwarg, `OPENROUTER_IMAGE_MODEL`, `image_gen.openrouter.model` or `image_gen.model`) resolves to Flare via `_RETIRED_IMAGE_API_MODELS` in `_resolve_model_chain`. Flare keeps `background=transparent`; its params come from OpenRouter's live `GET /api/v1/images/models` (9 ratios incl. 16:9, quality auto…max, n≤10, 16 refs).
- Docs (en + zh-Hans): removed the 1.5 rows and aspect column, and added a note about the remap.

## Before / after (stored `image_gen.provider: nous`, `image_gen.model: fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5`)

| | resolved model | managed route | after Dec 1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | `fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5` | FAL | upstream 4xx, generation fails |
| removing the entry with no successor map | Klein fallback (FAL path) | **`portal`**: the dead id is sent to the Portal gateway | wrong backend / failure |
| **this PR** | `fal-ai/gpt-image-2` | FAL | works |

## Validation

- **Live (real managed Nous gateway, runtime interpreter, worktree code):** stored `fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5` + provider `nous`. `_resolve_fal_model()` → `fal-ai/gpt-image-2`. Real `image_generate_tool("a red apple…", "square")` returned `success: True` with a fal.media PNG. On main the same config resolves to `fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5`.
- Clearing the map on head makes `managed_route("nous", "fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5")` return `portal`. That routing bug is why the map is needed, not just the deletion.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_image_generation.py tests/tools/test_image_generation_managed.py tests/plugins/image_gen/ tests/hermes_cli/test_tools_config.py tests/tools/test_managed_media_gateways.py tests/hermes_cli/test_nous_subscription.py`: **343 passed, 0 failed**.
- New invariant tests: `test_retired_saved_pick_resolves_to_successor` (OpenRouter) and `TestRetiredModels`, which also covers the `FAL_IMAGE_MODEL` path: each retired id is gone from the catalog, its successor is present, and the retired id resolves to the successor on the FAL path and the managed router. It fails on main, which has no `RETIRED_FAL_MODELS`.
- ruff clean, `scripts/check --only health` ok, `check_doc_links` ok, `check_no_tmp_literals` ok.

## Notes

- Pricing: GPT Image 2 medium costs $0.04–0.06/image on fal, up from 1.5's $0.034. It is already metered on the managed gateway (`_PORTAL_DUPLICATE_OF` maps it), so no portal work is needed.
- Not touched: `x-ai/grok-imagine-image-quality` (retires Nov 2), which is already covered by open #128430. `openai/gpt-image-1` shut down Oct 23 and was never in Hermes's curated list.
- Timing: the replacement models are live today, so this can merge now or any time before Dec 1.

prs.title: fix(gateway): allow Matrix /sessions and /resume to see completed sessions
prs.body:
## Bug Description

Matrix `/sessions` and `/resume` silently hide completed sessions whose origins have been garbage-collected. After a session finishes and its `SessionSource` origin is evicted from the in-memory registry, `_same_matrix_room()` receives `target_origin=None` and returns `False` — causing:

1. `/sessions` listing to omit the session entirely
2. `/resume <id>` to return `matrix_blocked_no_origin`

Users can no longer see or resume their own completed sessions on Matrix.

## Root Cause

Three code paths treat a missing origin (`target_origin is None`) as a cross-origin access attempt and block it, without checking whether the caller actually owns the session via the DB.

The origin registry is ephemeral — it only tracks *active* sessions. Completed sessions lose their origin, making the origin-based room check permanently fail.

## Fix

Three targeted changes in `gateway/slash_commands_session.py`, all preserving the IDOR guard:

**1. `_resume_access_denied_reply` (line ~1206)**
When `target_origin is None`, fall through to `_resume_target_allowed()` — a DB-level ownership check that proves the caller owns the session. Only allow if ownership is proven; otherwise keep the `matrix_blocked_no_origin` error to prevent cross-user enumeration.

**2. `_list_titled_sessions` (line ~1142)**
Skip the `_resume_row_visible` filter when the SQL query is scoped by `session_key`. The origin filter is an enumeration net for an *unscoped* query only: a falsy `session_key` drops the SQL clause entirely (the sessions store's `_session_filter_where`, `persistence/sqlite/conversation/_store/sessions.py` since the storage-interface refactor), so the filter stays for that case; admin widen keeps its `allow_all` pass-through. For a scoped query the SQL already proved ownership — applying the origin filter would incorrectly hide GC'd sessions. (`build_session_key` embeds `chat_id`, so a `session_key`-scoped query is chat/room-scoped and the skipped filter cannot widen the result.)

**3. `_handle_sessions_command` (line ~1364)**
Same net: apply `_resume_row_visible` only for an unscoped query (falsy `session_key`) outside admin cross-origin. A `session_key`-scoped query already proved ownership, and filtering admin `all` would defeat the cross-chat listing that flag exists for.

## How to Verify

1. Start a session on Matrix, send a few messages
2. Let the session complete / trigger origin GC (or manually evict the origin)
3. Run `/sessions` — the completed session should now appear
4. Run `/resume <id>` — should succeed and load the transcript
5. From a *different* Matrix room, `/resume <id>` should still be blocked (`matrix_blocked_other_room` or `matrix_blocked_no_origin` with DB check failure)
6. Admin `all` (cross-chat listing) keeps showing cross-origin rows; a non-admin caller with an unresolvable `session_key` still gets the origin-filter net on unscoped queries

## Test Plan

- [x] `tests/gateway/test_resume_command.py` (37 passed)
- [x] `tests/gateway/test_telegram_observe_resume_ownership.py` (5 passed)
- [x] `tests/gateway/test_session_list_allowed_sources.py` (1 passed)
- [x] Out-of-tree repro harness on storage-interface fixtures (4 passed: owner fall-through, cross-room IDOR block, scoped `/resume` listing, `/sessions` search)
- [ ] Manual verification on Matrix (see above)

## Risk Assessment

**Low** — each change is scoped: the IDOR guard is preserved (DB ownership check before allowing access), and the filter is skipped only where the SQL query already proved ownership via `session_key` (or the caller is a configured admin using `all`). The enumeration net stays in place for unscoped queries; cross-origin enumeration remains blocked.

## Maintenance notes (2026-11-27)

- Rebased onto `main` @ `ab7e19a` after the storage-interface refactor landed upstream: gateway session reads now go through `persistence.aio` / `SessionQuery`, and `_session_filter_where` moved from `hermes_state_sessions` to `persistence/sqlite/conversation/_store/sessions.py`. Its falsy-`session_key` clause-widening is unchanged (`if values:` skips the clause), so the fix's premise still holds; hunks 2–3 were re-resolved onto the new `list_sessions()` reader and the search path's `exclude_sources=["tool", "cron"]` extension is preserved.
- Re-verified on the new base: the `/resume` fall-through lands in `_resume_target_allowed` → `_persisted_row_proves_owner`, which fails closed (blank/legacy rows, alt-keyed callers, other threads all deny), so it cannot widen access. Full suite subset green per Test Plan.
- CI on this head still sits behind the fork-PR approval gate — no runs have executed; a maintainer approving the workflow run is enough.

## Maintenance notes (2026-10-27)

- Rebased onto `main` @ `198f6ad` (the branch carried one commit against a September base). No conflicts; the three hunks were re-verified in their new context — `_resume_target_allowed`, `_resume_row_visible`, `hermes_state_sessions._session_filter_where` and `build_session_key` are semantically unchanged since the PR was opened, and the `matrix_blocked_no_origin` behavior this fixes is still present on `main`.
- The three red workflow runs on the previous head (`33210ae`, dated 2026-09-25) never executed a single job — they were fork-PR approval-gate runs that expired after 30 days (`check-suites: latest_check_runs_count: 0`, no logs). Nothing failed; a maintainer approving the new head's runs is enough.

Supersedes #100558 (upstream refactored `slash_commands.py` into `slash_commands_session.py`)

prs.title: Agents can make hand-inked SVG character animations and videos (line-art-animation, optional, upstream stub)
prs.body:
Agents had no way to make hand-drawn style character animation: there was no skill for little ink-drawn people walking around a scene. Now `hermes skills install official/creative/line-art-animation` installs a well-liked one from its author's repo, and an agent following it built a new animated scene and rendered it to video in six minutes.

Adds [JDhruv14/line-art-animation](https://github.com/JDhruv14/line-art-animation) (MIT, ~1.3k stars, one release commit `c43d698` from Nov 10, 16 days old) to the optional creative catalog as an **upstream stub**.

**Depends on two open PRs (both rebased onto current main this run):**
- #133691: lets a stub point at a skill that lives at the repo root (`path: .`). This repo's root is the skill directory.
- #132602: lets a skill whose SKILL.md names a support directory (`examples/village`) install. Without it the hub rejects the fetch.

On main alone the install fails with `Rejected non-regular referenced file in skill bundle: examples/village`. This PR only adds the catalog entry, so it can merge after those two.

## What the skill does

It builds animated line-art components: one thin pen line on warm paper, drawn live in SVG from TypeScript. It ships four small library modules with no dependencies:
- drawing primitives, with limbs drawn as two open pen strokes
- a walk/run solver that keeps the feet planted
- springs and pendulums for scarves, bags and lanterns
- a day/night palette

It also comes with a ~150-line single-figure example, a full canal-street scene to copy from, and a capture script that steps through frames deterministically for MP4 export.

| | Before (main) | This PR (on the #133691 + #132602 stack) |
|---|---|---|
| Hand-inked character animation | no skill (p5js is procedural canvas art, manim-video is maths) | `line-art-animation` |
| `hermes skills install official/creative/line-art-animation` | entry does not exist | installs 36 files, scan `safe`, trust `trusted` |

## Validation (all run on this host)

- **Install:** scratch `HERMES_HOME`, worktree code at `sys.path[0]`, `hermes skills install official/creative/line-art-animation --yes`. Result: `Decision: ALLOWED — Allowed (trusted source, safe verdict)` and `Installed: creative/line-art-animation`. Findings were MEDIUM `traversal` only (the examples' `../../lib/*.ts` imports) plus a LOW 7.4 MB total size, mostly the README media.
- **Upstream workflow:** `npm ci` (0 vulnerabilities; dev deps only: typescript, vite, @types/node), `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `vite preview`, then `node scripts/capture.ts …/examples/walker/index.html?debug out 90 30 960 540` (`done: 90 frames in 4.5s`) and ffmpeg to MP4. A contact sheet of frames 0.13 s apart was vision-checked: the legs go through the contact, passing and stride poses. The village scene at night was checked in a real browser: no errors, and lit windows, lanterns and the boatman all render.
- **Cold agent test:** a fresh subagent with only the installed skill built a new scene from scratch (a baker carrying steaming bread past a bakery window) and rendered a 4 s MP4 in about 6 minutes, costing about $0.82. Its contact sheet was vision-checked as a correct walk cycle with planted feet and no broken frames.

Friction the cold run found is upstream's to fix (this stub vendors nothing, so the agent reads upstream's SKILL.md):
- step 2 says to copy `lib/` but later steps also need `scripts/capture.ts`
- the repo's `package.json` and `tsconfig.json` reference the examples and have to be trimmed for a new project
- `__step(1/fps)` rounds to 1/60 s ticks, so frame rates that don't divide 60 play fast (24 fps runs 1.25×)
- the references hard-code `/tmp` and `localhost:5173`

The stub's Prerequisites/Pitfalls section on the docs page records the host-side traps.

## Cost / trust

- Free and local. Needs Node ≥ 22.18, ffmpeg and Chrome/Chromium. No API keys, network, telemetry or credentials.
- Live third-party content, installed at `trusted` (not `builtin`), so a dangerous scan verdict would still block it.

## Host note (not a skill bug)

On this machine, headless Chrome launched from a cron/service context hangs on every network load while `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` points at the session bus. `env -u DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` fixes it. The stub's pitfalls list this.

## Infographic

![line-art-animation skill](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab41d4b/Oa1Y_U2JkoKKt6TZmRRGR_0T9alfEr.png)

prs.title: feat(optional-skills): ffmpeg-skill — local FFmpeg editing from natural language, upstream-kept; stubs can point at a repo-root skill (salvage #132056)
prs.body:
`hermes skills install official/creative/ffmpeg-skill` installs kajisho5/ffmpeg-skill — 42 local-FFmpeg editing scripts driven from natural language — as an upstream-kept catalog stub, and the stub pointer can now express a repo-root skill (`path: .`), which also lands @ljluestc's vlog-auto-edit stub (#132056, salvaged with authorship intact).

## What it is

- **ffmpeg-skill** ([kajisho5/ffmpeg-skill](https://github.com/kajisho5/ffmpeg-skill), MIT, 1.8k★, 150 forks, created Sep 3): probe → plan (`--dry-run --json`) → cut/join/fit/caption/overlay/sync/loudness/export → `check.py --platform` → verify, all standard-library Python over a local `ffmpeg`. No cloud, no keys. Hermes had footage *generators* (`ascii-video`, `manim-video`, `ai-presenter-video`) but no general-purpose editor for footage the user already has.
- **Why a stub, not a port:** upstream publishes several releases a week (v2.3.1 → v2.5.1 in 10 days, 101 npm versions), so a vendored copy would be stale on arrival and could never meet the ≥2-week pin rule. The `metadata.hermes.upstream` stub (archify/reladraw/geo-sleuth shape) vendors zero bytes and pins the live tree SHA at install.
- **Resolver fix (salvaged from #132056):** upstream keeps `SKILL.md` at the repo root. `_upstream_pointer_from_content` rejected `path: .` (collapsed to no parts), so such a stub silently degraded to a vendored 40-line SKILL.md. Now `path: .` means repo root (an omitted path is still rejected on purpose) and the bundle is named after the catalog entry. Contributor commit cherry-picked as-is; one follow-up commit reworded its `/tmp` prose for the new `check_no_tmp_literals` gate.

## Changes

- `optional-skills/creative/ffmpeg-skill/SKILL.md` — stub, `upstream: {repo: kajisho5/ffmpeg-skill, path: .}`
- `optional-skills/creative/vlog-auto-edit/SKILL.md` — stub (@ljluestc, from #132056; closes #11036)
- `tools/skills_hub_official.py` — `path: .` → repo root; upstream bundle named after the catalog entry (@ljluestc)
- `tests/tools/test_skill_bundle_provenance.py` — 1 invariant test (`test_optional_source_upstream_stub_with_repo_root_skill`), **red on base, green here**
- Docs: 2 generated pages, 2 catalog rows, 2 `sidebars.ts` lines

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `OptionalSkillSource().fetch("official/creative/ffmpeg-skill")` (real resolver, worktree) | 315 files, 19.25 MB, tree `008333aa…`, trust `trusted`, `upstream_path=''`, ~2.5 min |
| Fetched scripts, FFmpeg 9.0.1, synthetic 1280x720 clip | `probe` → `cut --start 1 --end 4` (hybrid re-encode, 3.023 s) → `fit --aspect 9:16` → `check --platform tiktok` 13 checks, loudness FAIL correctly flagged at −21.8 LUFS |
| **Cold live test** (fresh subagent, upstream SKILL.md only, no references opened) | "6 s vertical Reel from s3, burn caption, normalise for Instagram": `render.py` project with 5 stages → `reel.mp4` 6.10 s, 1080x1920, 30 fps, −14.0 LUFS, TP −9.7 dBTP; `check --platform reels` 13/13, 0 FAIL. Verdict **SHIP**; 2 wording nits folded into the stub (fetch wall time, `instagram` alias) |
| `skills_guard.scan_skill` | stub `safe`; fetched upstream tree `caution` (315 files > 50, prose `sudo apt install ffmpeg`, `os.environ` in upstream tests — informational; `trusted` tier still blocks only `dangerous`) |
| `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/skills/ tests/tools/test_skill_bundle_provenance.py` | 1771 passed, 0 failed |
| Base A/B for the resolver test | `git show origin/main:tools/skills_hub_official.py` swapped in → `test_optional_source_upstream_stub_with_repo_root_skill` FAILED; head → passed |
| `check_no_tmp_literals.py`, `check_doc_links.py`, `audit_pr_attribution.py` | clean |

Not exercised: `hermes skills update ffmpeg-skill` re-pin path (the cold test was forbidden from running the CLI updater; `do_update` exists in `hermes_cli/skills_hub.py`). vlog-auto-edit's own workflow (Whisper + vision model + zh narration) was not live-run; the stub's prerequisites and `path: .` fetch are what this PR verifies.

## Cost / trust

- ffmpeg-skill: free, local; no network at run time. Upstream `bin/install.js` (npm installer) and `mcp/server.py` are unused by Hermes; `.github/`, `tests/`, `evals/` ride along in the fetch (the stub says so). No telemetry, no update-check step (unlike archify).
- vlog-auto-edit: needs `openai-whisper`/FunASR + an OpenAI-compatible vision model; Linux/macOS only (platform font paths). Disclosed in the stub.
- Nothing in either stub phones home from the Hermes side.

## Credit

- @kajisho5 — ffmpeg-skill (MIT).
- @ljluestc — vlog-auto-edit stub + the `path: .` resolver fix (#132056); @znyupup — ai-video-editing-skill (MIT, #11036).

## Infographic

![ffmpeg-skill stub](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aad40d2/nh3USC9yGrZXkl-m6t7GN_P7DoAqcW.png)

Supersedes #132056 (its single commit carried as-is, authorship preserved). Closes #11036.

prs.title: Skills hub installs a GitHub skill whose SKILL.md links a support directory (was rejected as a symlink escape)
prs.body:
A skill whose `SKILL.md` links a support **directory** (`references/clues/`) now installs from GitHub instead of being rejected as a symlink escape.

## Symptom

`hermes skills install` of a GitHub skill whose SKILL.md says, in prose, "rules live in `references/clues/`" (a plain directory holding three markdown files) returned nothing but

```
Rejected non-regular referenced file in skill bundle: skills/geo-sleuth/references/clues
```

## Root cause

`GitHubSource._collect_tree_files` (`tools/skills_hub_github.py`) builds its `symlinked` set from `_tree_members`, which reported **every** non-blob tree entry as "non-regular" — git `tree` entries (directories) included. A SKILL.md-referenced path that resolved to a directory was then treated as the escape shape the check exists for (a linked **symlink**, mode `120000`).

## Change

- `_tree_members` yields blobs only; symlinks keep `is_regular_blob=False` so a linked symlink still rejects the bundle. Directories and submodules are skipped — their blobs are listed on their own.
- A referenced path that prefixes bundled files (`references/clues` → `references/clues/global.md`) no longer logs a misleading "referenced support file is missing".
- `OptionalSkillSource` (the other `_tree_members` caller) already skipped non-regular entries; behaviour unchanged.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/tools/test_skills_hub.py::TestGitHubSourceFetchMissingReferencedFile::test_fetch_keeps_a_skill_that_links_a_support_directory` (new; directory installs, symlink still rejects) | **red on `origin/main`** (bundle `None`), green on this branch |
| `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_skills_hub.py tests/tools/test_skills_hub_browse_sh.py` | 112 passed, 0 failed |
| Live: `OptionalSkillSource().fetch("research/geo-sleuth")` → `Oldcircle/geo-sleuth:skills/geo-sleuth` (the stub in #132603) | base: rejected; fixed: 40 files, 1.09 MB, pinned to `e753bb3a`, `skills_guard` verdict `caution` |

Surfaced while cataloging `Oldcircle/geo-sleuth` (companion PR adds the `optional-skills/research/geo-sleuth` stub and carries this commit so its live install works; it drops out on rebase once this lands).

## Infographic

![A directory is not a symlink](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aacfd40/pa5flCk1pq_vDHdOo72hc_CLM2vpOs.png)

Opened by the agent-tools scout (cron). Awaiting review — not merged.

prs.title: plugin-catalog: add syncky (two-way Apple Health over an end-to-end encrypted relay)
prs.body:
Adds `plugin-catalog/syncky.yaml` for [Syncky](https://github.com/syncky/syncky-open/tree/main/plugins/syncky), submitted by the repository owner.

**What it does.** With the Syncky Health iPhone app, Hermes reads the Apple Health types the user chooses and can write entries back to Apple Health for the types the user allows for writing on the iPhone. Health data is end-to-end encrypted (HPKE) between the iPhone and the local Syncky agent. No account and no public URL: the agent connects out over HTTPS.

**Hermes surfaces used.** Portable Agent Plugins v1 only: `plugin.json`, `mcp.json` with one stdio server (`npx -y @syncky/agent@0.2.3 mcp`, tools `syncky_status`, `syncky_inbox`, `syncky_skill`, `syncky_send`, `syncky_ack`) and one skill, `skills/syncky`. No Python entrypoint, hooks, middleware, Desktop code or core overrides.

**Disclosures (rule 13).**
- Network: on first use, `npx` can download the pinned `@syncky/agent@0.2.3` package from npm. The agent sends and receives sealed messages over HTTPS to Syncky Relay (`relay.syncky.app`), operated by the plugin's author; the relay sees delivery metadata, not health values.
- Data to the model: Health data the user chooses appears in tool results and command output, so the model provider the Hermes session uses sees it.
- Writes: `syncky_send` sends Health write commands. The skill instructs Hermes to send a write only when the user asks for that entry or approves a standing rule. The iPhone checks write permissions and does not prompt for each entry; it applies a write only for types allowed for writing and records the requesting agent in the entry's metadata.
- Local files: `~/.syncky-agent` holds keys and received records. The receiver deletes records older than 30 days when it runs.
- Shell commands: the skill runs `npx -y @syncky/agent@0.2.3` commands (`init`, `pair`, `status`, `receive`, `inbox`).
- Background process: if the user chooses continuous receive, the skill installs the receiver locally and configures it to start at login and restart after a failure.
- Credentials: no Hermes credentials or user-supplied API key are required. The agent stores its private key locally and registers its public key with the relay.
- No self-updater: the npm version is pinned in `mcp.json` and in the skill, and updates arrive only through a sha-bump PR here. The agent contains a signed skill-text update path, but this release pins no signing key, so it fails closed and never fetches or replaces skill files. No binary downloads.
- Daily version report: by default, the receiver reports its agent version and operating-system family to Syncky Relay once a day. You can turn this off with `SYNCKY_HEARTBEAT=off`. The report contains no health values.

**Validation.** `hermes plugins validate plugins/syncky --install-deps` at the pinned commit: passed; security scan: safe; `hermes plugins install` without `--force` enables the plugin (Hermes v0.23.2).

prs.title: fix(acp): scope Buzz launch credentials to gateway terminal turns
prs.body:
## Problem

`hermes acp` delegates tool execution to the shared gateway. A Buzz ACP worker has its own Buzz credentials in its launch environment, but the gateway's terminal scrub does not see that launch environment. The `buzz` CLI can then fall back to a different ambient identity.

## Fix

- Carry a validated `acp_launch_env` envelope over the same-user private control socket, using the one-use, profile-bound bootstrap ticket. The generic bridge and gateway don't special-case Buzz. A reviewed producer policy selects the inherited namespace; `buzz-acp` supplies the first policy. The receiver rejects unknown producers, names outside the selected namespace, and Desktop ownership stamps.
- Exclude the selected launch namespace from the auto-started daemon's inherited environment.
- Keep the credentials in memory on the owning ACP session and bind them to its admitted turns. Only the opaque binding ID goes into the durable queue. Local terminal children receive the bound values after the normal scrub, and shell snapshots exclude them.
- Keep the platform as ACP so editor toolsets and approval handling continue to work. The dedicated turn context does not use Buzz Desktop's process-ownership marker. A queued turn whose binding was lost on restart fails closed.

## Verification

On Linux, `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/acp_adapter/test_gateway_buzz_terminal_env.py` exercises the ordinary ACP entry point, private bootstrap, shared gateway and real terminal children against a loopback model fixture. It fails on the base and passes with the fix: two concurrent Buzz ACP sessions get their own values, and an ordinary ACP session and a CLI session get none.

Also ran focused ACP, gateway bootstrap and terminal environment tests, including rejection of unregistered producers, arbitrary environment variables, and Desktop's ownership marker at the control socket, plus `scripts/check`.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add feishu (official, installed by default; Feishu / Lark leaves core)
prs.body:
## Round 16: staged transition instead of a version floor

The `>=0.23.5` floor is gone. Stable and canary both report 0.23.4 today (canary payloads read `0.23.4+canary.<stamp>`), so that floor locked every shipping build out, including a canary that has already dropped core's adapter. Both plugins now install on **Hermes 0.23.4 or later**. They do nothing while the running core still bundles the same platform. The check is whether core's files are present: `plugins/platforms/qqbot/` for QQ Bot; `plugins/platforms/feishu/` or `tools/feishu_doc_tool.py` for Feishu. On such a core `register()` registers nothing and logs one DEBUG line (`... the plugin stays inactive until core drops it`), and core's own adapter and tools keep serving. The first core without them gets the plugin's adapter, with the same settings and tool names.

- Feishu's `plugin.yaml` now ships `provides_tools: []`. `hermes plugins validate` fails any declared name that collides with a built-in, and core still ships `feishu_doc_read` / `feishu_drive_*`. On that core the plugin registers none of them, so it validates cleanly on main. **Follow-up after the core removal merges:** put the five names back in `provides_tools`. Until then, validate on the post-removal core reports "undeclared tools registered" for `feishu` only. Runtime is unaffected, because user plugins load eagerly and register the tools from `register()`. The catalog entry keeps listing the five tools.
- Seam used: the plugin's own presence check, which already existed. Main has no registry rule that prefers one side cleanly. Platforms are last-writer-wins, so the user plugin would replace core's adapter. Tools are core-wins, and the plugin's `register_tool` returns `None` with a WARNING on every start. Staying inactive avoids both.
- Cost on a core that still ships the platform: the package import, measured on a 0.23.4 CLI process at +0.08 s (qqbot) and +0.17 s (feishu).

**Rollout order:** fixed plugin PR merged → catalog entry re-pinned to the plugin's MERGED sha → check that the published catalog (`hermes plugins browse` / a catalog fetch from main) returns the entry → core removal merges LAST (→ Feishu only: the `provides_tools` follow-up).

### Live probe (real version strings, real installs, real `gateway run --force`)

Version strings came from the real producers. The `v0.23.4` worktree goes through git (`0.23.4`). The `canary.20261126T064809Z-v0.23.4` worktree got its stamp from `scripts/termux/deb_version.py --release-version <tag>`, then `scripts/write_install_stamp.py` with the Termux build's arguments (`0.23.4+canary.20261126T064809Z`). The removal heads ran twice: once stamped by the same producer for `canary.20261127T024356Z-v0.23.4` (`0.23.4+canary.20261127T024356Z`), and once through git (`0.23.4`, display `0.23.4+777`). The fixture catalog in each tree pins the pushed plugin commit (qqbot `7e8bc4e`, feishu `2c8be75`) with `requires_hermes: ">=0.23.4"` and `default: true`. Endpoints sat behind a closed proxy; each home had creds in `.env`.

| Leg | Core (reported version) | QQ Bot | Feishu |
|---|---|---|---|
| Existing profile, default install on the old core | v0.23.4 (`0.23.4`) | installed + enabled; core adapter `hermes_plugins.platforms__qqbot` serves; plugin `tools []` + DEBUG stand-down | installed + enabled; core adapter `platforms__feishu` connects; plugin `tools []`; no shadow warnings |
| Same | canary.20261126 (`0.23.4+canary.20261126T064809Z`) | same | same |
| Upgrade of that home | removal head, git (`0.23.4`) | plugin adapter `hermes_plugins.qqbot` attempts the token in the same start; no reinstall (plugin dir mtime unchanged) | plugin adapter `hermes_plugins.feishu` connects; 5 tools from `hermes_plugins.feishu.feishu_doc_tool`; no reinstall |
| Upgrade of that home | removal head, canary-stamped (`0.23.4+canary.20261127T024356Z`) | same | same |
| Existing profile, no plugin (left-core migration) | removal head, canary-stamped | installed once (`_left_core_installed: [qqbot]`) + plugin adapter in the same start | `✓ Installed the 'feishu' plugin…` + connects in the same start |
| Same | removal head, git | same | same |
| hermes-tag profile: stable, then removal head ×2 | v0.23.4, then canary-stamped removal head | — | stable: `Hermes Tag` serves Feishu over core, official plugin inactive. First removal start: one `⚠ The community 'hermes-tag' plugin…` line, also kept in `left-core-notices.jsonl` for the next attended turn, and the official plugin connects. Second start: no repeat |

Cross-check from the same runs: on the Feishu removal head, the default-installed qqbot plugin stays inactive (core still ships QQ Bot), and the reverse holds too. `hermes plugins validate` passes for both plugins on main, v0.23.4, the canary and the QQ removal head. Feishu on the Feishu removal head reports "undeclared tools registered" until the follow-up above. The real `~/.hermes/config.yaml` md5 was the same before and after (`c72b5ba9…`).

**Round 16 (`2073082`):** re-pinned to NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins@2c8be75 (image 200 at that sha), `requires_hermes: ">=0.23.4"`; `hermes plugins validate` on that sha passes on main (it failed on all OSes before: declared tool names collided with core's built-ins). The hermes-tag cap stays `<0.23.5` (its pin imports core's Feishu adapter). Its comment now names the one-time notice its users get from core #159651. A version cap cannot catch a canary built after the removal (it still reads 0.23.4+canary), and that is the case the notice covers. `python scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/`: OK.
The plugin PR's head is now `ff13054`, a tests-only change on top of `2c8be75`. This entry stays at `2c8be75` until the re-pin to the merged sha.

The Feishu / Lark messaging platform is leaving Hermes core for an official plugin that is installed by default on every Hermes home. It stays idle until that home sets a Feishu App ID and App Secret: no adapter starts, and its five `feishu_*` tools are not offered to the model. Once set up, the tools default on for the Feishu platform only.

- **Entry:** `plugin-catalog/feishu.yaml`, `tier: official`, **`default: true`**, `maintainer: NousResearch`, repo `NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins`, subdir `feishu`. Same shape as Weixin (#159643) and QQ Bot (#159641).
- **Existing Feishu users:** migrated automatically (core's LEFT_CORE row in #159651). **New homes:** get the plugin once from the default-plugin installer; it does nothing until configured. Removing it sticks (one automatic install per home across both installers).
- **Why default is safe now:** plugin #517 `098aaeb` gates the tools' `check_fn` on the profile's App ID + App Secret (the adapter's own reader: scoped `FEISHU_APP_ID` / `FEISHU_APP_SECRET`, else `platforms.feishu` `app_id` / `app_secret`). Unconfigured, the model's `tools[]` carries zero Feishu names; before, all five were listed in the tool_search catalog. Configured: #517 `18add6c` registers them with `default_platforms=("feishu",)` (core #159651), so CLI / Telegram / other platforms get none unless the user turns them on in `hermes tools`.
- **hermes-tag cap (round 12):** `plugin-catalog/hermes-tag.yaml` now reads `requires_hermes: ">=0.22.5,<0.23.5"`. Its pin `75e1931` imports `plugins.platforms.feishu.adapter` when it registers, and that module leaves core with #159651. On 0.23.5+ the import raises, and the plugin registers nothing, its Slack and DingTalk parts included. An install by name on 0.23.5+ is now refused with that reason until a pin that loads the Feishu adapter from the plugin is listed. A home that has hermes-tag keeps Feishu through this official plugin, which the left-core migration installs. `validate_plugin_catalog.py` passes for both files.
- **Description:** "Installed by default on every home; it stays idle, with no adapter and no tools offered to the model, until you set a Feishu App ID and App Secret, and then offers its tools on the Feishu platform only. Formerly built into Hermes core; existing users are migrated automatically." No "not supported" wording.
- **Disclosure** (read from the code):
  - messages, media, documents and comment threads travel between Feishu / Lark's servers (`open.feishu.cn` / `open.larksuite.com`) and the user's own gateway, using the user's own app ID and secret;
  - webhook mode opens a local HTTP port;
  - image and file URLs that appear in replies are downloaded (SSRF-checked).
- **Pin:** `27e4756` (manifest declares FEISHU_ENCRYPT_KEY / FEISHU_VERIFICATION_TOKEN as labelled password fields, so the Channels card masks them), the head of NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#517 for now. **Hold:** this gets re-pinned to the merged sha before merge.
- **Release floor:** `requires_hermes: ">=0.23.5"`, in this entry and in the plugin's `plugin.yaml`. 0.23.4 still bundles Feishu with its built-in `feishu_*` tools, so 0.23.5 is the first release without it. If the removal ships later, the floor moves with it at the re-pin.
- **Image:** `assets/feishu.jpg` at the pin (curl 200). `validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/feishu.yaml`: OK.

Merge order: NousResearch/hermes-agent#159651 (core removal, migration row, default-install docs) → NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#517 → this PR (re-pinned).

Expected red: `pinned-source-validate` runs `hermes plugins validate` against core main, so it stays red on the built-in `feishu_doc_read` / `feishu_drive_*` name clash until #159651 merges.







## Infographic

Same move as #159651 (core side):

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): retry bridge spawn without CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB on WinError 5
prs.body:
## Problema
En Windows, si el gateway corre dentro de un job object que prohíbe breakaway (p. ej. Hermes Desktop/Electron), `_spawn_bridge_process` falla con `PermissionError: [WinError 5] Access is denied` porque `windows_detach_flags()` incluye `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB`. El bridge de WhatsApp no arranca y el backend queda "down", aunque el emparejamiento exista. Desde una terminal normal funciona.

## Cambio
En `plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py`, `_spawn_bridge_process` reintenta el spawn sin `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` (`windows_detach_flags_without_breakaway()`, que ya existe en `_subprocess_compat`) solo cuando el primer intento lanza `PermissionError`. En POSIX no cambia nada.

## Verificación
- `py_compile` del archivo: OK.
- Reproducido en Windows 11: el gateway lanzado desde Hermes Desktop falla con WinError 5; lanzado desde terminal, el bridge arranca.
- Pendiente: prueba con Hermes Desktop tras aplicar el cambio (no ejecutada en CI).

## Notas
Cambio de 10 líneas, sin nuevas dependencias.
