prs.title: catalog: bump livetalk to v2.3.0 (three providers, rule 9/11 compliant)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

SHA bump for **livetalk** — `34f4ebb` (v2.0.0) → `d86f517` (v2.3.0). Rule 4: the pin is the only thing that moves, so the adopted range is spelled out below for review.

Entry fields refreshed alongside the pin: `sha`, `version`, `requires_hermes` (`>=0.23.0`), `image` (now points at the new commit), `description` (three providers, credential route, disclosures), and `capabilities.requires_env` (three keys).

Diff: `v2.0.0...v2.3.0` — 7 files, +1,484 / −346.

## What changed in the adopted range

- **Three providers behind one REST surface**: Gemini Live (ephemeral 1-use token mint), ElevenLabs Realtime (`client_secret` mint, semantic VAD), Grok Voice (xAI realtime, server VAD). The renderer never learns which provider is upstream; the provider lives in runtime state, not in settings.
- **`recall` tool + warm start**: a second declared tool searches earlier turns of the plugin's dedicated agent session; last-five-messages + a topic digest seed the provider's system instruction.
- **Resumption fixes**: the Gemini handle is stored with model *and* voice, so a voice change opens a fresh session instead of replaying the old `speechConfig` (issue cruzlxyz/livetalk#3, reported with mean-F0 measurements); a handle rejected for a stale model configuration (close `1007`) is dropped and redialled clean; Grok resume uses `?conversation_id=` with a 30-minute replay window.
- **ElevenLabs setup resilience**: mint+dial retried twice in a 25 s window with a `session.update` nudge.
- **Delegation/polling**: delegations are a serialised queue (no drops), `response.create` is spaced after `conversation_item.create`, `/poll` recall offset fixed.

## Catalog rules

- **Rule 11** — credentials come from `agent.secret_scope.get_secret()` only. The hand-rolled `.env` reader (three roots, quotes, `op://`) was **removed** in this range; `requires_hermes` moves to `>=0.23.0` because the credential scope is installed per plugin route. `requires_env` declares `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `XAI_API_KEY`; only the selected provider's key is required at runtime, and a missing one produces a path-free error pointing at Settings → Providers.
- **Rule 9** — settings are read with `load_config_readonly()` and written with `save_config(merge_existing=True)` on `plugins.entries.livetalk.settings`. No private core helpers remain (the previous version imported `hermes_cli.plugins._plugin_settings_entry` and `plugins_state.save_plugin_setting`); the private-import warning is gone from `hermes plugins validate`.
- **Rule 3** — no self-updating code: the plugin never fetches or replaces its own files. Updates arrive through this catalog entry + `hermes plugins update`.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- **Microphone audio** is captured while a session runs and streamed from the local backend to the selected provider only: `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`, `api.elevenlabs.io`, or the xAI realtime endpoint. Nothing is sent anywhere else.
- **Transcripts** (input and output) are held in backend memory for the session and are **not** written to disk.
- **Local files written** inside the plugin's install directory: `.resume.json` (Gemini resumption handle) and `.resume-grok.json` (xAI conversation id). Settings live in `config.yaml` under `plugins.entries.livetalk.settings`.
- **Network**: the backend owns the upstream WebSocket; the desktop UI only talks to localhost. The plugin registers **no** agent tools, hooks or middleware, and creates/reuses one agent chat session titled "Livetalk" for delegations.
- **Delegation**: the voice model can ask the agent to do work (`talk`) and read earlier turns (`recall`); those requests are visible in the transcript, and the Hermes agent's own approval policy still applies.
- **Security hardening in this range**: provider key moved out of the models-list URL (header auth), `/tool_response` accepts only an id queued by the provider (once), missing-key errors no longer print filesystem paths, `/status` reports the active provider's key state.

## Validation

Both gates run locally at the pinned commit:

- `hermes plugins validate . --install-deps` → **Validation passed**, 16 checks, 0 warnings (private-core-imports warning gone).
- `python scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/livetalk.yaml` → `{"ok": true, "errors": [], "warnings": []}`.
- Functional checks on a throwaway `HERMES_HOME`: settings round-trip preserves unrelated config sections; key resolution covers scoped/env; forged tool-call ids are rejected; `/status` is provider-aware.

Thanks!

Version strings came from the real producers. The `v0.23.4` worktree goes through git (`0.23.4`). The `canary.20261126T064809Z-v0.23.4` worktree got its stamp from `scripts/termux/deb_version.py --release-version <tag>`, then `scripts/write_install_stamp.py` with the Termux build's arguments (`0.23.4+canary.20261126T064809Z`). First removal start: one `⚠ The community 'hermes-tag' plugin…` line, also kept in `left-core-notices.jsonl` for the next attended turn, and the official plugin connects. Second start: no repeat |

prs.title: fix(cli): add --archived-only to sessions prune
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`hermes sessions prune` could not target archived sessions alone: `--include-archived` only widened the candidate set and still needed an age filter, so there was no safe bulk way to delete archived sessions. This adds `--archived-only`, which maps to the already tri-state `archived` filter in `SessionDB` (`True` = archived only), rejects the contradictory `--include-archived` combination, and keeps the existing time bounds composable (`--archived-only --older-than 30d`, `--archived-only --before 2026-10-01`). The confirmation prompt now says `archived only`.

The optional `--archived-before` from the issue is not added: the existing `--older-than`/`--before` flags already cover that case when combined with `--archived-only`.

## Related Issue

Fixes #156674

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/subcommands/sessions.py`: new `--archived-only` flag; prune flags extracted into `_add_prune_flags()` to respect the 300-line code-health cap on `build_sessions_parser`.
- `hermes_cli/session_filters.py`: `build_prune_filters()` maps `archived_only` to `archived=True`; `describe_filters()` labels the selection as `archived only`.
- `hermes_cli/sessions_cmd.py`: conflict with `--include-archived` is refused; `archived_only` counts as a filter so bare `--archived-only` does not inherit the 90-day default cutoff.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_session_filters.py`: two invariant tests for the flag mapping and the default.

## How to Test

1. On unmodified `main`, `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_session_filters.py -k archived` fails with `KeyError: 'archived'` (2 tests).
2. With this patch, the same tests pass (13/13 in the file).
3. CLI smoke with the real parser: `sessions prune --archived-only --dry-run` → `archived=True`, description `archived only`; adding `--older-than 7d` keeps both filters.

prs.title: feat(prompt): inject current wall-clock time via ephemeral_system_prompt
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds ambient temporal awareness to Hermes Agent by injecting the current wall-clock time into every API call via the existing `ephemeral_system_prompt` mechanism.

**Key design decisions:**
- Uses `ephemeral_system_prompt` (not the stable system prompt) so prefix-cache KV stability is **unaffected**
- Injected **per-API-call** so the time is always current, even in multi-turn sessions
- Uses `hermes_time.now()` for timezone awareness (respects `HERMES_TIMEZONE` env var and `config.yaml timezone`)
- Existing `Conversation started:` date-only line in volatile tier is preserved unchanged

## Related Issue

Fixes #693

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `agent/prompt_builder.py` — Added `build_temporal_context_prompt()` function
- `agent/conversation_loop.py` — Ephemeral injection point: prepends current time before user's ephemeral prompt
- `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` — Same injection in the max-iterations summary path
- `tests/agent/test_prompt_builder.py` — 3 tests for the new function

## How to Test

1. Start a Hermes session: `hermes -q "What time is it?"`
2. The agent should respond with the current time (within a few minutes)
3. Verify the existing `Conversation started:` line still appears correctly
4. Run `pytest tests/agent/test_prompt_builder.py::TestBuildTemporalContextPrompt -v`

prs.title: feat(discord): hand a $<profile> message to that profile's session
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

**TL;DR for reviewers:** Adds `$<profile>` mention-dispatch for Discord — when one gateway multiplexes several Hermes profiles behind one bot, typing `$agent-one <text>` anywhere in a message runs a normal turn in `agent-one`'s own session and labels the reply with its name. Opt-in is per-profile (`discord.mentionable`/`mention_handle` in that profile's own `config.yaml`), fails closed, and reuses the existing session-identity seam — no new routing or authority system. Implements issue #159776.

**Why this is safe to review quickly:** a small, bounded feature (not a re-attempt at the long-stalled #89995 "Bot Mode room" effort — see the issue's Alternatives Considered). 9 self-driven remediation rounds closed an independent review's 2 critical + 4 warning findings, plus 2 further bugs a purpose-built end-to-end test rig found on its own (duplicate dispatch across multiple bots; a gateway session-binding refusal that blocked the feature's main path entirely). 76 feature tests plus a reusable e2e harness (`tests/plugins/platforms/discord_gateway_rig.py`); locally verified against the full repo test suite (8652 files / 95,597 tests) with zero PR-caused regressions — see [Local CI-lane verification](#local-ci-lane-verification-final).

**Known, deliberate limitations (not bugs — documented + pinned by a tripwire test each):** a skill-triggering slash command's handle stays as plain text, never re-routed; the profile that owns the bot process needs a restart to pick up its *own* opt-in flag turning off, only in the uncommon case where a *different* profile owns the bot.

**Status: ready for review.** CI has not run yet — this is a fork PR, so a maintainer needs to approve the Actions workflow run before any check appears on this PR. Full round-by-round detail follows below for anyone who wants the audit trail.

---

> **Review status:** every 🔴 critical (2) and ⚠️ warning (4) finding from the [independent review](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/159794#pullrequestreview-6053238814) is addressed (see [Review follow-ups](#review-follow-ups-review)). **Round 9 fixed the round-8 🔴 open issue:** a `$<profile>` prompt was refused by the gateway itself (`profile_mismatch` from the session binding), so the feature did not work end to end. Round 9 first added a real end-to-end rig (`tests/plugins/platforms/discord_gateway_rig.py`: real `DiscordAdapter` → multiplexed `GatewayRunner` → session-authority admission and binding → turn and reply), re-ran every case of the feature through it (15 of 32 failed, all with that refusal), then fixed the binding (`3965bd32d7`) and a second bug the rig found with two bots (a profile's conversation got paused, `b20201476f`). All 33 end-to-end cases now pass. No 🔴 is open. The 💡 suggestions are not done. Gates on `b20201476f` (on `main` at `76b55a4679`): the full suite and every CI lane this diff triggers were run locally, see [Local CI-lane verification](#local-ci-lane-verification-final); no failure is caused by this PR. Targeted set: 258 files, 2295 passed, 0 failed, 9 skipped; 22 checks ok, code health 0 blocking (13 files vs 76b55a4679).

A single Discord bot under `gateway.multiplex_profiles` can hand a message to a specific profile by name. A message that names one (`$agent-one what's the status?`, anywhere in the text) runs **one normal turn in that profile's own session**, and the reply is labelled with the profile's name.

**Each profile opts itself in, in its own `config.yaml`.** No profile is reachable by default:

```yaml
# ~/.hermes/profiles/agent-one/config.yaml
discord:
  mentionable: true      # a YAML boolean; "true"/1 do not count
  mention_handle: a1     # optional; defaults to the profile name
```

You can also set it at creation time with `hermes profile create agent-one --discord-mention[=a1]`.

### Revision 2: opt-in moved from the host's config to each profile's own config

The first revision used a central `discord.profile_mentions` list in the config of the profile that owns the bot. To make a new profile reachable you had to edit *another* profile's config. That was flagged as too much friction. Auto-enrolling every profile was rejected as a security regression: every profile would silently become reachable by anyone the bot already accepts. That breaks the gateway's fail-closed, explicit-allowlist model (`profile_routes`, Bot Mode's per-profile `bot.enabled` from #100758). The opt-in now lives in each profile's own config instead, following the per-profile `bot.enabled` precedent. **`discord.profile_mentions` is removed entirely**, not kept alongside.

How the bot computes its `{handle: profile}` map (`adapter_profile_mentions.py`):
- It enumerates the profiles this gateway **serves** (`served_profile_names()`, the hot-serve reconcile's live record) and reads each one's own `discord:` block:
  - **The bot's own profile:** from `adapter.config.extra`. `mentionable`/`mention_handle` are added to the existing live allowlist refresh keys (`adapter_live_gates.py`), so editing its config.yaml applies on the next message.
  - **Every other served profile:** from `runner._profile_configs[name]`, the config the hot-serve reconcile (`gateway/run_profile_reconcile.py`) loaded for it. The reconcile already re-loads a served profile whose `config.yaml` changed (30 s watcher, plus an immediate rescan on profile create/delete through the control socket) and drops a deleted one. A flag flip therefore applies live with **no new reconcile or polling logic**.
- Fails closed: a profile that is not served, did not opt in, has a non-boolean flag or an invalid handle, or claims a handle another profile also claims (WARNING naming both) is unreachable.
- Known gap (documented, pinned by a test): when the bot belongs to a *secondary* profile, the profile the gateway was **started from** re-reads its own flag only on restart. The reconcile never rebuilds the launch profile, and the bot's live refresh only covers the bot's own profile. **Switching that flag off keeps the launch profile reachable until the gateway process restarts**; the docs say so in a warning box.

### Unchanged from revision 1
- **No new routing or session authority, and one narrow session-binding rule (round 9).** Each dispatched copy is the event's own `SessionSource` with `profile` stamped, the same shape `build_source` produces for a `profile_routes` match. The session authority's binding accepts that profile only for a copy the receiving bot marked in process and still vouches for (see the round-9 row). Keying, authorization and delivery all go through the existing identity seam (`resolve_identity`):
  - runtime: the named profile;
  - transport and authorization: the bot that received the message;
  - delivery: that bot.
- **Labelling reuses the runtime-footer seam.** A wire-invisible `SessionSource.profile_mention` flag makes `_hmwa_runtime_footer_line` lead with `— <profile>`. Nothing is serialized.
- **`$`, not `@`**, so real users and roles are never pinged. Multiple handles fan out as independent turns with no ordering. Unknown handles produce an INFO line with counts only (no message text at INFO+). There is no turn loop and no room state (#89995's scope).

## Review follow-ups ([review](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/159794#pullrequestreview-6053238814))

Current head: `b20201476f`, on `main` at `76b55a4679`. All 6 findings are addressed, plus two post-review checks (the 🔎 rows) and the round-8 issue (fixed in round 9, with a second bug the round-9 rig found). Nothing is open. The commit SHAs below are the ones after the rebase onto `76b55a4679`; older thread replies and the round-9 gate record cite pre-rebase SHAs.

| Finding | Status |
|---|---|
| 🔴 Duplicate dispatch: with several bots, every bot dispatched the same `$handle` | **Fixed** in `133e1b8189`. A gateway-wide `(platform, message id, profile)` claim means one bot dispatches. Tests: `test_two_bots_in_one_channel_dispatch_a_mention_once`, `test_a_dispatch_claim_outlives_the_bot_that_made_it`. |
| 🔴 Prompt whitespace destroyed (`" ".join(prompt.split())`) | **Fixed** in `9ae8d3edc5`. Only the handle tokens are removed, together with the spaces flanking them, a `:`/`,`/`;` right after a leading handle, and a line that held only handles. Tests: `test_a_code_block_after_the_handle_reaches_the_profile_intact`, `test_multi_paragraph_prompts_keep_their_lines_and_spacing`, `test_stripping_a_handle_touches_only_the_text_around_it`. |
| ⚠️ Slash commands (`MessageType.COMMAND`) are re-homed too | **Fixed** in `bea8076beb`. A slash command is never dispatched: `addresses_profile` ignores text starting with `/` (so the `require_mention` gate treats `/reset $agent-one` like any command), and `mention_events` passes a `COMMAND` event through unchanged, arguments intact, in the channel's own session. Native slash interactions never reached dispatch. Test: `test_a_slash_command_is_never_rerouted_by_a_handle`. Docs: new slash-command row in the `#profile-mentions` table. |
| ⚠️ Case 6 with default `history_backfill` dispatches an empty-text turn (docs say "Ignored") | **Clarified (docs + test, no runtime change)** in `73ece792ca`. A reproduction with backfill at its default (on) shows a bare `$agent-one` and a bare `@bot` producing the same turn: empty text and the same backfilled `channel_context`. With no channel activity, neither one dispatches. This is the existing bare-@mention "catch me up" rule, so the docs row now says so. Test: `test_a_bare_handle_with_default_backfill_behaves_like_a_bare_at_mention[channel-activity\|no-activity]` (backfill left at its default). Gates: `just test` 129 files, 1101 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped; `just check` 22 checks ok, code health 0 blocking. |
| ⚠️ The gate reads `raw_content` but dispatch reads `event.text`, which includes inlined attachment text | **Fixed** in `d2be0f2af0`. The adapter passes the typed text (`normalized_content`, what the gate checks, minus the bot's own `<@id>`) to `dispatch_event`. Planning, the slash-command check and handle stripping all run on that text only. `_rebuild_prompt` swaps only the typed suffix of `event.text` for its stripped form, so an inlined document reaches the profile byte for byte, and a `$handle` inside it never routes. Tests: `test_a_handle_inside_an_attached_document_never_routes_or_gets_stripped`, `test_a_typed_handle_routes_while_the_attached_documents_text_stays_intact`, `test_attached_document_handles_with_every_discord_default_left_alone` (require_mention/auto_thread/history_backfill at defaults), `test_the_prompt_rebuild_never_edits_text_it_cannot_place_as_typed`. Docs: new attachment row in the `#profile-mentions` table. Gates: `just test` (mention files) 2 files, 33 passed; full sweep 209 files, 1885 passed, 0 failed, 9 skipped; `just check` 22 checks ok, code health 0 blocking. |
| ⚠️ The launch profile's off-switch takes effect only after a restart (fails open); not documented or pinned by a test | **Addressed (docs + test, no runtime change)** in `f37d56bca9`. `#profile-mentions` now lists what applies live (the bot's own profile on its next message, every other served profile on the rescan, on and off alike), plus a warning box for the one exception: when another profile owns the bot, turning the launch profile's flag **off** keeps it reachable until the gateway process restarts. Restarting only the bot's profile is not enough, and turning it on waits for a restart too. Test: `test_pin_known_gap_launch_profile_flag_needs_a_restart_when_another_profile_owns_the_bot` runs the real `reconcile_served_profiles` and pins the gap. Its docstring marks it as a tripwire to update once the gap is closed, and a hypothetical live re-read makes exactly this test fail. Not fixed in code: a live re-read of the launch profile needs a second launch-config loader outside the reconcile (loading the launch home bridges YAML into the process env), which is new infrastructure. Gates: 210 files, 1894 passed, 0 failed, 9 skipped; 22 checks ok, code health 0 blocking. |
| 🔎 Post-review check (not a review finding): does a skill slash command (`/some-skill $agent-one do X`) get `$<profile>`-dispatched once the gateway rewrites it into a prompt? | **Answered: no. Documented + pinned, no runtime change** in `d679e4c0d0`. Traced and reproduced end to end (real `DiscordAdapter` → real `GatewayRunner` + session authority): dispatch runs in the adapter (`dispatch_event`, before `handle_message`), the skill rewrite runs later in the gateway (`_hm_dispatch_idle_commands` → `_hm_skill_slash_rewrite`). So the message is still `/some-skill …` when dispatch sees it, the round-3 slash rule passes it through untouched, and the skill runs in the channel's own session with `$agent-one` left in its prompt as text. Not changed in code: the plugin cannot reach the slash-command resolver (`agent.skill_commands`/`agent.skill_bundles` are not published plugin API), what `/<name>` resolves to depends on the profile that runs the turn, and the disk-bound skill scan was moved off the adapter's loop on purpose (#111091). Reordering would mean re-homing a `COMMAND` event, which undoes round 3. Docs: new skill-command row in the `#profile-mentions` table (ask the profile in words instead). Test: `test_pin_known_gap_a_skill_slash_command_keeps_its_handle_as_text`, a tripwire; a hypothetical fix that routes `/demo` makes only this test fail (29 others pass). Gates: `just test` (mention files) 2 files, 35 passed; full sweep 227 files, 2038 passed, 0 failed, 9 skipped; `just check` 22 checks ok, code health 0 blocking. |
| 🔎 Post-review check, round 8: does a handle in FRONT of a slash command (`$agent-one /new`) bypass the round-3 slash exclusion? | **Yes, a real bypass. Fixed** in `5dc6af163d`. Reproduced end to end on a really multiplexed gateway (round 7's rig had no multiplexed authority): real `DiscordAdapter` → real `GatewayRunner(multiplex_profiles=True)`, `set_multiplex_active(True)`, a session authority per served profile in a multiplexed `SessionAuthorities`, reserved runtime homes. Before the fix, `$agent-one /new` was handed over as a `TEXT` event with text `/new` stamped for `agent-one`, and the real `_handle_reset_command` ran in `agent-one`'s home ("New session started!"). Why: round 3 checked only whether the typed text starts with `/`, and the gateway tells a command by its **text** (`MessageEvent.is_command`), not by the adapter's `MessageType`. Commands also skip the authority FIFO admission, so nothing downstream stopped it. Fix: a message is not dispatched (and does not count as addressing the bot for `require_mention`) when its typed text, or its prompt after the handles are stripped, is a command by the gateway's own classifier (which also catches `$agent-one @file:x` + a `/new` line). It stays plain text in the channel's own session, like `/new $agent-one`. A `/` later in the prompt still dispatches. Docs: new `$agent-one /new` row in the `#profile-mentions` table. Tests: `test_a_handle_in_front_of_a_slash_command_never_reroutes_it[6 shapes]`, `test_a_slash_later_in_the_prompt_still_dispatches[3]`, `test_a_handle_prefixed_slash_command_never_runs_in_that_profiles_session` (end to end; it first proves the rig really runs `/new` in `agent-one` for such a copy). Gates: `just test` (mention files) 2 files, 45 passed; full sweep 227 files, 2048 passed, 0 failed, 9 skipped; `just check` 22 checks ok, code health 0 blocking. |
| 🔴 Found in round 8, **fixed in round 9**: the multiplexed ingress binding refused every re-homed `$<profile>` prompt | **Fixed** in `3965bd32d7`. Round 8 found that `$agent-one <text>` was dispatched correctly and then refused by the gateway: `_hm_authority_admission` → `admit_native` → `capture_provenance` → `session_ingress_context._binding` raised `AuthorityRefusal('profile_mismatch')` ("Something went wrong" in the channel). `_binding` derives the runtime profile only from `profile_routes`, a `/p/<profile>/` producer or the relay. **Why a new rule and not an existing channel:** none of the three fits a per-message address (routes are per channel, the `/p/` prefix belongs to HTTP producers on the shared listener, the relay seal to the relay connector). So the binding gets one narrow rule, `_mention_profile`: it accepts `source.profile` only when (1) the source carries the in-process `profile_mention` marker, which only the receiving adapter sets and which is never serialized, so no wire field, relay frame or stored row can mint it; (2) it is not a relay delivery; (3) the profile is a reserved served home; and (4) the receiving bot vouches for it right now (`profile_mention_targets()`: served and opted in through its own config; a new `DiscordProfileMentionsMixin`). It is not a blanket trust of a caller-stamped profile: a stamped profile without the marker, or a marked one the bot does not vouch for, is still `profile_mismatch` (tested). The rig also showed a second half of the bug: the FIFO re-runs the binding on a `SessionSource.from_dict` copy (`restore_provenance`) on **every** drain, where the marker is gone. So the binding records `profile_mention` in the provenance it captures, and `restore_provenance` re-arms the marker only from that record and re-runs the same check (a restored turn is re-validated against the current opt-in, as a route is re-matched against the current config). The restored source keeps the marker, so the reply keeps its `— <profile>` label. An explicit `$<profile>` wins over a `profile_routes` route for its own message (docs updated). Tests: the end-to-end file below. |
| 🧪 Round 9: real end-to-end rig (durable test artifact) | Added in `47b1b6045f`. `tests/plugins/platforms/discord_gateway_rig.py`: `async with discord_gateway_rig(tmp_path, monkeypatch, profiles={...}, bots=(...)) as rig`, then `out = await rig.send("$agent-one hi")`. It runs the real path (`DiscordAdapter._handle_message` → the runner's real message handler → `GatewayRunner._handle_message` → the authority FIFO: `admit_native`, `capture_provenance`/`_binding`, `restore_provenance` → real turn setup, reply shaping, label and delivery) on a really multiplexed gateway (process latch, reserved runtime homes, one authority per served home, each profile's own `config.yaml` through the real loader). Only the model call (`_run_agent`), the Discord wire (`send`) and the profile directory lookup are stand-ins. `out` records the events handed over, every turn (profile, runtime home, session key/id, prompt), every reply, every `AuthorityRefusal` the gateway raised (also ones it turned into a notice) and escaped errors. It also drives several bots, a secondary profile's bot, held (busy) turns, missed-message recovery and hand-over of a hand-built event. `test_discord_profile_mentions_e2e.py` (33 cases) uses it; the two earlier end-to-end tests moved there onto the shared rig. Use it (not `resolve_identity`) to test any change here. |
| 🔴 Found in round 9 by the rig, **fixed**: with two bots, a profile's conversation got paused at random | **Fixed** in `b20201476f`. Every bot in the channel receives each message, and round 1 let the first bot to reach dispatch hand it over. But the gateway binds a session lane to the bot that carried its first turn (`SessionEntry.transport_profile`) and pauses the lane when a later turn arrives through another bot (`check_native_route` → `not_found`: "This conversation is paused: a queued message could not be re-authorized"). Which bot sees a message first is a race, so this hit real multi-bot channels. `_claim` now lets only the bot the gateway recorded for the copy's lane dispatch to it; a lane with no record yet is claimed in memory by the first bot (so a second message cannot race the first one's lane creation), and the persisted record governs after a restart. Tests: `test_two_bots_in_one_gateway_run_the_turn_once` (both bot orders, and after the in-memory claims are cleared), `test_two_bots_racing_on_a_new_lane_keep_it_on_one_bot`. Docs: the multi-bot bullet in `#profile-mentions`. |
| 💡 Suggestions (`replace_source` comment, `_owner_profile`, INFO log level, auto-thread, label position) | Not done (optional, outside the 6 findings) |

#### Round 9: every case through the real end-to-end rig

Before = `5dc6af163d` (round 8's head) with the new rig and tests; after = this head. Every ❌ was the same refusal: `AuthorityRefusal('profile_mismatch')` raised in `session_ingress_context._binding` and a "Something went wrong" reply, except where noted. 33 test cases in `test_discord_profile_mentions_e2e.py` (some rows group parametrized cases).

prs.title: fix(credential-pool): bench a spent Claude plan window for every model and rotate on its first 429
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A Claude subscription (OAuth) account whose weekly or five-hour window is spent keeps receiving requests from `fill_first`, so sessions sit on its 429. Three code paths cause it; this PR fixes all three.

1. **The bench covers one model.** `_is_model_scoped_failure` treats every non-billing Anthropic 429 as a per-model limit (#111769, correct for API-key per-minute limits), so a spent `seven_day` window benches only the model that asked. The next request for any other model goes straight back to the spent account.
2. **The first 429 waits instead of rotating.** `_recover_rate_limit` rotates on the first 429 only when the reason or message contains a usage-limit token. Anthropic's message (`This request would exceed your account's rate limit.`) has none, so the session sleeps `min(Retry-After, RETRY_AFTER_CAP_S)` = 600 s on the spent account, retries it, and only then rotates.
3. **The auxiliary path drops the reset.** `_recover_provider_pool` (titles, compression) rebuilt the error context as `{"message": str(exc)}`, discarding the response headers. Its bench therefore lasted the default one hour instead of until the provider's reset, and the spent account came back into rotation every hour.

The 429 already says which case it is. Anthropic sends `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-status: rejected` and names the refusing window in `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-representative-claim` (headers captured in #147070 and #149112). With this change:

- `extract_api_error_context` records that claim as `subscription_window`, and uses `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-reset` as `reset_at` when no earlier header set one.
- A spent account-wide window (`five_hour`, `seven_day`) benches the credential for every model until the reset, and the first such 429 rotates.
- A family claim (`seven_day_opus`, …) and a 429 without the unified headers keep today's per-model cooldown and single retry.
- The auxiliary path builds its context with `extract_api_error_context`, as the main loop does.

## Related Issue

Fixes #149112

Two open PRs overlap with this one; I'm crediting them here so maintainers can choose:

- #130459 by @devseunggwan covers the account-wide bench and first-429 rotation. It also benches on 200 responses and for env tokens. It currently conflicts with `main`.
- #131360 by @kokhlo (draft) sizes the auxiliary bench from the provider's reset window.

This PR is the smaller change, built on today's `main`, and covers the three paths together. If maintainers prefer #130459 plus #131360, this PR can close in their favour and its tests can move over.

This PR also removes the 600 s wait from #147070 for subscription windows, the case that issue's field reports describe. #155714, #130458, #78274, #117941 and #142792 change the general retry-versus-rotate decision. This PR leaves that decision alone and acts only on the provider's explicit "this account is spent" signal, so it composes with whichever of them lands.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/credential_pool_model_cooldowns.py`: new functions `record_plan_window` (reads the unified headers), `account_window_spent` and `usage_allowance_spent`. The two usage-limit token lists and their check move here from `agent_runtime_helpers.py`, beside the scope decision they feed. `_is_model_scoped_failure` takes the error context and returns `False` for a spent account-wide window.
- `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`: `extract_api_error_context` calls `record_plan_window`, and `_recover_rate_limit` asks `usage_allowance_spent`. Net −7 lines.
- `agent/credential_pool.py`: `mark_exhausted_and_rotate` passes the error context to the scope check (one line).
- `agent/auxiliary_client.py`: `_recover_provider_pool` uses `extract_api_error_context(exc)`. It is imported lazily because importing `auxiliary_client` does not load `agent_runtime_helpers` today. The dropped `status_code` key was never read: `_normalize_error_context` keeps only `reason`, `message` and `reset_at`.
- `tests/agent/test_anthropic_plan_window_scope.py`: behaviour contracts against a real pool in a temp `HERMES_HOME`, driven by a real `anthropic.RateLimitError` that carries the unified headers.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_anthropic_plan_window_scope.py`: 6 passed. On `main` (04be1bc0) 4 of them fail. The two controls pass on both: a family claim stays per-model, and a plain 429 keeps its one retry.
2. Sabotage run, undoing one fix at a time:
   - Scope check reverted: the `seven_day` and `five_hour` cases and the auxiliary test fail.
   - Usage-allowance check reverted: only the first-429 test fails.
   - Auxiliary context reverted: only the auxiliary test fails.
3. Standalone repro (two seats, spent `seven_day` 429 on the first one), on `main` vs this branch:

```
main 04be1bc0:
[1] error context: reason='rate_limit_error' reset_in=63.0h subscription_window=None
[2] after a claude-fable-5-2 429 on the spent seat: rotated_to=spare-seat spent.last_status=None spent.model_cooldowns=['claude-fable-5-2']
    next claude-opus-5-5 request goes to: spent-seat
[3] first 429: recovered=False has_retried_429=True rotated=[]
[4] aux (title/compression) 429: rotated=True spent.last_status=None bench_ends_in=1.0h (provider reset in 63.0h)

this branch:
[1] error context: reason='rate_limit_error' reset_in=63.0h subscription_window='seven_day'
[2] after a claude-fable-5-2 429 on the spent seat: rotated_to=spare-seat spent.last_status=exhausted spent.model_cooldowns=[]
    next claude-opus-5-5 request goes to: spare-seat
[3] first 429: recovered=True has_retried_429=False rotated=['rate limit']
[4] aux (title/compression) 429: rotated=True spent.last_status=exhausted bench_ends_in=63.0h (provider reset in 63.0h)
```

4. `scripts/check`: 22 checks pass; code health reports 0 blocking and 0 advisory findings for the 5 files against 04be1bc0. No file over the line cap grows.
5. Every test file that references the credential pool, rate-limit recovery or error context (231 files): 4,340 passed, 12 failed. The failures are all in 4 files (`test_marked_home_env_values`, `test_delegate_resumable`, e2e `test_catalog_oauth`, `test_tui_gateway_server`) that fail identically on unpatched `main`: 658 passed, 11 failed on both sides, the same test IDs. The 12th did not recur in either rerun.

**Field symptom (v0.23.4, macOS, two Claude subscriptions on `fill_first`, several profiles sharing one root pool).** The first account's weekly window was spent (`/api/oauth/usage`: `weekly_all` 100%, reset in 2.2 days) while the second sat at 1%.

- An auxiliary title-generation 429 benched the first account for `claude-fable-5-2` only, and for exactly one hour.
- When the hour lapsed, live sessions went back to the first account and logged `HTTP 429 … Retrying API call in 600.0s (attempt 1/3)` within minutes of each other, while the second account was idle.

The model picker showed the account as "Limited until Nov 28" throughout, because it reads the usage endpoint and not the pool.

**Risk.** Only a 429 that carries `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-status: rejected` with an account-wide claim changes behaviour. API-key per-minute 429s, family-scoped claims, billing and entitlement paths are untouched. A spent sole credential is now benched for every model until the reset; before this change each model took one failing request to learn the same. Rollback: revert the commit.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)

- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 27.0.1 (arm64)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

prs.body:
## Rollout order

Fixed plugin PR merged → this catalog entry re-pinned to the plugin's **merged** sha → verify the published catalog (`hermes plugins browse` / catalog fetch from main) returns the entry → core removal #159649 merges **last**. Since round 16 only homes that ran wecom in core are installed automatically; a profile that sets it up later is told `hermes plugins install wecom` (or uses the platform card's install route), so the entry is never fetched unasked.

---

## What this does, in plain words

This adds the `wecom` catalog entry: WeCom (Enterprise WeChat) as a Hermes Labs plugin, built by Nous Research and not supported. It is `tier: community`, maintainer NousResearch, with no `default`, so it is opt-in. This is the catalog half of moving WeCom out of Hermes core. Homes that already used WeCom are migrated automatically through the core PR's LEFT_CORE rows; everyone else installs it with `hermes plugins install wecom`.

Teknium re-placed WeCom: it was official + `default: true`, and is now non-default Hermes Labs. This entry now points at NousResearch/hermes-labs-plugins, and the description carries the "A Hermes Labs plugin: built by Nous Research, not supported" sentence, like yuanbao and dingtalk.

- **Data only:** `plugin-catalog/wecom.yaml`.
- **Pin:** `repo: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-labs-plugins`, `subdir: wecom`, `sha: 1de1d0c` (the labs PR head). The `image` URL at that sha returns 200, and `docs_url` points at hermes-labs-plugins.
- **Validation:** `python scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/wecom.yaml` gives `OK: 1 file(s) valid`.
- **Live:** the core PR's probe used this exact file as its catalog fixture. A home with WeCom creds got the plugin installed from hermes-labs-plugins at `1de1d0c`. A fresh home got nothing, and `default_plugins.default_entries()` was `[]`.
- **First sentence carries the disclosure** (review): Desktop's install confirmation shows only the description's first sentence. That sentence now names the bot mode's WebSocket reply/attachment destination (openws.work.weixin.qq.com, or `WECOM_WEBSOCKET_URL`), the inbound media downloads, the callback endpoint (local port 8645) and qyapi.weixin.qq.com. The labs and migration sentences are unchanged.
- **Hold:** this PR stays on `hold` and gets re-pinned to the merged plugin sha before merge.

## The slate (merge order)
1. Core removal: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/159649
2. Plugin: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-labs-plugins/pull/111 (replaces the closed hermes-official-plugins#510)
3. This catalog entry, re-pinned to the merged sha of step 2

prs.title: fix(desktop): keep pinned session singular across /compress tip rotation
prs.body:
Closes #105507

## Problem

Running `/compress` in a pinned Desktop session left the sidebar showing **two rows for the same conversation**: the stale pre-compression row under *Pinned* (with cost) and a raw, unpinned, cost-less duplicate of the rotated tip under *Sessions*.

The rotation itself is by design — `publish_compression_child` moves the conversation onto a new `parent_session_id`-chained row, and title/pin projection live on the new tip. The bug was display-state: three gaps let a raw (lineage-less) tip row coexist with the stale cached ancestor in the renderer's lineage-keyed store.

## Root cause (three gaps)

1. **`GET /api/sessions/{id}` served raw rows** — no `_lineage_root_id` / `_lineage_ids` / projected pin, unlike every list path (`list_sessions_rich`, search, the sidebar endpoint). The Desktop's dedupe (`mergeSessionPage`) and pin identity (`sessionPinId`) are lineage-keyed, so a raw payload cannot be linked to the stale cached row. (`hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py`, `get_session_detail`)
2. **`upsertResolvedSession` replaced rows wholesale** — a raw detail payload *downgraded* an already-projected tip, silently dropping it out of Pinned. (`apps/desktop/src/.../use-session-actions/utils.ts`)
3. **`/compress` never refreshed the sidebar** — the stale keep-set row lingered next to the duplicate until an unrelated refresh. (`apps/desktop/src/.../use-prompt-actions/slash.ts`)

Display-state only: the DB holds one conversation; any projected list page healed the sidebar. The exact ingestion call site for the raw payload is not proven — the candidate paths are the by-id resolution/upsert paths (`resolveStoredSession` → `getSession` → `upsertResolvedSession`, runtime-info seeds); the fix covers the class, not just one call site.

## The fix

- **Backend** (`get_session_detail`): project the compression lineage tip-only (`sid == chain[-1]`), same semantics as `_project_compression_tips` — root id, full id chain, lineage-wide pin OR'd across the chain (pruned chain members tolerated). Ancestor GETs deliberately stay raw-shape so a stale root payload can never evict the live tip.
- **Renderer `upsertResolvedSession`**: payload AND cached rows get symmetric nullish→undefined normalization (JSON producers emit explicit `null`); a raw-shape payload preserves the cached lineage projection instead of downgrading it, while projected values win outright; eviction keys on the **merged** row's lineage root; raw ancestor payloads that would evict the live tip are refused.
- **Renderer `/compress`**: coalesced `refreshSessions()` after success — on both the `session.compress` RPC path and the legacy slash-worker fallback.

## Known limitation

A raw tip payload arriving when the tip is not cached cannot be linked to a stale ancestor client-side (nothing in the payload carries the link). The post-compress refresh delivers the projected tip on the real path, and every projected payload evicts by lineage.

## Test plan

- 5 new FastAPI endpoint tests (`tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server.py`): tip projection, ancestor-stays-raw, unpinned-lineage-stays-false, childless-row-unchanged, plus real-rotation fixtures via `publish_compression_child`.
- 9 new renderer tests (`use-session-actions/utils.test.ts`): raw-shape preservation, projected-wins overwrite, lineage eviction of a distinct ancestor row (fails on the pre-fix code — the false-green trap), ancestor-payload suppression (root + intermediate), cold-arrival ingestion, explicit-null payload, explicit-null cached row.
- 1 new renderer test (`use-prompt-actions/index.test.tsx`): `refreshSessions` called after successful compress.
- All new tests verified RED before their fix, GREEN after (5 fix→test cycles during review).
- Full desktop suite: 9479 passed / 3 pre-existing environment failures (verified failing identically on clean main). Backend file: 190 passed / 2 pre-existing (same verification). `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint` clean on all touched files.

## Notes

**Open question:** the ancestor-guard's UX edge — a warm deep-link to an *old ancestor id* resolves to the cached tip (so the guard's suppression is invisible), but a user explicitly opening a root id with nothing cached sees the raw row. Suppressing only lineage-linked raw payloads keeps every observed path correct; if maintainers would rather ancestors deep-link to the live tip server-side (301-style via `latest-descendant`), that's a clean follow-up.

prs.title: feat(feishu): add ignore_at_all config to opt out of @everyone triggering the bot
prs.body:
Closes #33723

## Problem

In Feishu group chats, the bot always responds to `@所有人`/`@everyone` mentions because `_mentions_self()` in `plugins/platforms/feishu/adapter.py` short-circuits to `True` whenever `@_all` appears in the raw message content. In announcement-heavy groups this produces unwanted bot responses that can't be disabled.

## Solution

Adds an opt-in config so `@_all` alone no longer triggers the bot:

- **Env var:** `FEISHU_IGNORE_AT_ALL=true`
- **YAML:** `feishu.ignore_at_all: true` (bridged to the env var via the plugin's `apply_yaml_config_fn` hook; env wins when both are set)
- **Default:** `false` — behavior is unchanged for every existing user

When enabled, the `@_all` short-circuit in `_mentions_self()` is skipped and only explicit bot mentions trigger the bot (both the raw `mentions[]` path and the post/rich-text `is_self` ref path remain fully intact — an `@_all` ref never sets `is_self`, so the two paths don't interact).

Precedence chain: explicit env var → `feishu.ignore_at_all` YAML key → default `false`.

## Naming note

The issue proposed `FEISHU_IGNORE_MENTION_ALL` / `feishu.ignore_mention_all`. This PR uses `FEISHU_IGNORE_AT_ALL` / `feishu.ignore_at_all`, the name that 3 of the 5 prior PRs for this issue converged on. Happy to rename if maintainers prefer.

## Docs

Documented in English and zh-Hans: `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/feishu.md` (prose + table row), `website/docs/reference/environment-variables.md`, and both zh-Hans mirrors.

## Test plan

- `python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_feishu.py tests/gateway/test_feishu_bot_admission.py -q` → 89 passed, 18 skipped
- Full Feishu suite (`test_feishu.py`, `test_feishu_bot_admission.py`, `test_feishu_bot_auth_bypass.py`, `test_feishu_approval_buttons.py`) → 104 passed, 18 skipped
- New tests cover: settings wiring (unset/false/true, extra-config override, env-wins-over-extra), `_mentions_self` gating (all-only gated when enabled, explicit bot mention still triggers when enabled), admission-level rejection/admission, YAML→env bridge (bridge set, env wins, key absent leaves env untouched), and `_to_boolean` edge pins (`"TRUE"`/`"1"` → `False`)
- `git diff --check` clean

## Notes

**Open question:** the read path for `require_mention` in `_load_settings` uses the same `extra.get(..., os.getenv(...))` ordering that makes extra-config override the env var (contradicting the `apply_yaml_config_fn` docstring "Env vars take precedence over YAML"). This PR fixes the ordering for the new key only, following the narrowest-patch approach — whether `require_mention` (and other keys using the same pattern) should be fixed too is a maintainer call.

prs.title: fix(model_switch): dedupe self-duplicate provider views in typed-model routing
prs.body:
## Problem

Bare `/model <name>` hard-fails for a model that is declared by exactly **one** configured endpoint:

```
Model 'my-model' is declared by multiple configured providers (relay-lb, custom:Relay LB East).
Pass --provider to disambiguate.
```

Callers such as the gateway `/model` path (`gateway/slash_commands.py`) pass both `cfg["providers"]` (as `user_providers`) **and** `get_compatible_custom_providers(cfg)` (as `custom_providers`) into typed-model resolution. `get_compatible_custom_providers()` re-exposes every `providers`-dict entry as a legacy custom-provider row, so `_configured_provider_matches()` counts the **same physical endpoint twice** — once as `providers.<slug>`, once as `custom:<display name>` — and the #45006 multi-provider ambiguity guard rejects a perfectly unambiguous name. The only workaround is to always type `--provider`, which defeats the point of the guard.

## Change

Dedupe at the match-collection altitude: before recording a `custom:<name>` match, recognize when the entry is merely a legacy *view* of a `providers.<slug>` block and attribute the match to that slug instead. Identity checks, strongest first:

1. **`provider_key`** — stamped by `_normalize_custom_provider_entry()` with the originating `providers`-dict key when the view is built by `providers_dict_to_custom_providers()`.
2. **Display name + base_url** — a view whose `name` equals a `providers` entry's display name AND targets the same endpoint (trailing-slash/case-insensitive URL compare) *is* that entry; this covers hand-rolled views that lack the `provider_key` stamp.

## Correctness notes

- The dual exposure in `get_compatible_custom_providers()` is deliberately left intact — it is load-bearing for the legacy `custom_providers` consumers (runtime provider resolution, credential pool, pickers). Only the match *accounting* changes.
- Genuine ambiguity still errors: two **different** endpoints declaring the same model — including a display-name collision on different `base_url`s — keep tripping the `--provider` guard. Both cases are pinned by new tests.
- A match attributed to the slug resolves the entry's `base_url`/key via the explicit-provider user-config credential path, identical to `/model <name> --provider <slug>`.

## Tests

`tests/hermes_cli/test_model_switch_configured_provider_routing.py` gains 5 dedupe cases:

- dual-exposed user provider counts as one match (bare `/model` routes, no ambiguity error) — **fails before the fix**
- the dedup'd match resolves the provider's endpoint and key — **fails before the fix**
- a legacy view without `provider_key` dedupes by display name + base_url (trailing slash tolerated) — **fails before the fix**
- two different endpoints with the same model still error (guard intact)
- display-name collision on different base_urls still errors (guard intact)

Full file (15 tests) plus the adjacent model-switch suites pass with the fix.

prs.title: fix(picker): show all tool-capable OpenRouter models, not just curated 39
prs.body:
## Summary

The OpenRouter model picker only showed the curated entries from a hand-maintained whitelist (~39 at the
time of writing; 49 of the manifest's 59 entries survive today), while the live catalog has hundreds of
tool-capable models (378 as of 2026-09-19). Other providers (Nous Portal, Codex, Copilot) already fetch
their full live catalogs. This made models like Laguna S 2.1 invisible in search even though they support
tool calling on OpenRouter.

Changes `fetch_openrouter_models()` to return all tool-capable models from the live catalog, with curated
entries first (keeping their descriptions). Also guards the OpenRouter rung of the provider-detection
ladder against overriding custom providers — with the expanded catalog, bare model names like `laguna-s-2.1`
now match OpenRouter entries, which would silently redirect users away from their explicitly-configured
endpoints.

## Changes

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `hermes_cli/models.py` | `fetch_openrouter_models()`: after building curated list, append all remaining tool-capable live models. `_detection_candidates()`: skip the OpenRouter rung when the current provider is `custom` or `custom:*`, so a bare-name collision cannot pull a session off a user's own endpoint. |
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_models.py` | New `test_includes_non_curated_tool_capable_models` (verifies non-curated models appear, curated first). New `test_custom_provider_not_overridden_by_live_openrouter` (verifies both `custom` and `custom:*` protected). New `test_explicit_prefix_still_resolves_on_a_custom_endpoint` (verifies the guard skips the OpenRouter rung and nothing else). |

The guard's comment was also reworded (comment-only): the previous wording read as if the generator
continued past the `return`, when an explicit `vendor/model` prefix actually resolves through
`detect_provider_for_model`'s trailing `_resolve_provider_prefix` fallback.

## Before/After

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| OpenRouter models exposed by `fetch_openrouter_models()` | 39 (curated only, 2026-08-20) | 378 (all tool-capable, 2026-09-19) |
| Laguna S 2.1 visible | No | Yes on the searchable pickers, selectable by name everywhere — see "Picker surfaces" below |
| Custom provider overridden | No (static catalog only) | No (live catalog too) |

## Validation

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_models.py`: 83/83 passed
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_model_catalog.py`: 21/21 passed
- Mutation check: with the guard removed, `test_custom_provider_not_overridden_by_live_openrouter` fails
  with `('openrouter', 'poolside/laguna-s-2.1')`; restoring it returns the file to 83 passed.
- Live verification: `fetch_openrouter_models(force_refresh=True)` returns 378 models, curated first
  (live catalog: 447 models, 378 advertising `tools`).

## Notes

**Picker surfaces (verified 2026-09-19, current head).** Most of the interactive surfaces that consume this
list filter or window it rather than rendering it flat; the two exceptions are noted in the table.

| Surface | Effect |
|---|---|
| Interactive CLI `/model` picker | Uncapped; fuzzy filter + scroll panel |
| TUI picker (`ui-tui`) | Uncapped; fuzzy filter + windowed rows |
| Desktop picker dialog | Uncapped; search box, renders the full list on an empty query |
| Desktop model menu | Curated default-visible set via `featured_models` (newest 5 per vendor lab) |
| Dashboard `/api/model/options` | Uncapped; searchable |
| `hermes setup` / provider key-flow model selection | Uncapped; searchable curses list |
| Messaging-gateway inline pickers (Telegram/Discord/Slack/Matrix) | Pre-existing `max_models=50` slice in `list_picker_providers`; the tail of the row is not in the inline grid |
| Auxiliary-task pickers (vision, compression, …) | Pre-existing `max_models=40` cap |

On the capped surfaces a specific model is still selectable by name: `/model poolside/laguna-s-2.1`
resolves through `detect_provider_for_model`, which reads this same expanded list. Those caps predate this
PR and this PR does not change them.

**Open question:** The curated list still contains stale entries (e.g. `poolside/laguna-m.1:free` no longer
exists on OpenRouter — the live models are `poolside/laguna-s-2.1` and `poolside/laguna-xs-2.1`). These are
silently skipped by the live-catalog intersection, so they don't cause errors, but the curated manifest at
`website/static/api/model-catalog.json` could use a cleanup pass.

**Deliberate trade-off on custom providers:** the guard skips the OpenRouter rung of
`_detection_candidates()` when the current provider is `custom` or `custom:*`. A bare model name that
matches an OpenRouter slug therefore no longer resolves to OpenRouter on a custom endpoint — the point of
the guard, since with hundreds of live slugs the collision rate against a user's own endpoint names goes
from occasional to constant. Nothing else changes: an explicit `vendor/model` prefix naming a declared
provider still resolves as a selection through `detect_provider_for_model`'s trailing
`_resolve_provider_prefix` fallback. The same ladder already treats `custom` and `openrouter` as providers
that need an explicit model name in the static path (`detect_static_provider_for_model()`), so this keeps
the live-catalog path consistent with the static one.

Fixes #78470

prs.title: test: home_io_guard exempts both spellings of the interpreter prefix
prs.body:
**What**

`tests/home_io_guard.py` exempted only the *resolved* interpreter prefixes. A PM-managed runtime exposes the interpreter through a version symlink (`cpython-<minor> -> cpython-<full-version>`), so imports and traceback formatting read stdlib sources under the **unresolved** `sys.base_prefix` spelling. On a linked worktree — whose repo root is not the home checkout the repo-inside-home exemption covers — the guard then refused the interpreter's own files: the first test failed with `TEST BUG: file I/O against the REAL hermes home: …/zoneinfo/__init__.py`, and the run aborted while formatting that failure, exiting on a `tmp_path` stash `KeyError` with zero tests reported.

This exempts both spellings of every interpreter prefix (`sys.prefix` / `sys.base_prefix` / exec prefixes, plus sys.path site-packages entries), with regression tests for both spellings and a negative test proving non-interpreter paths under the same root are still refused. The change grants no new reach: anything readable through the symlink spelling was already readable through its exempted target.

**Why it matters**

Any worktree run of the suite on a default-layout install crashes instead of reporting — a red run looks like pytest infrastructure breakage, and the real failure (and its identity) is never shown.

**Evidence**

- RED before the fix (on this machine's symlinked runtime): `test_unresolved_interpreter_prefix_paths_are_exempt` fails at `home_io_guard.py:107` refusing `…/cpython-3.11-macos-aarch64-none/lib/os.py`.
- GREEN after: `tests/test_home_io_guard.py` → `3 passed`. The tests construct their own symlinked prefix under `tmp_path` (fresh guard-module load with `sys.base_prefix` pointed at the fixture link), so the unresolved-spelling test discriminates against the base guard on every machine: base guard source → `1 failed, 2 passed` (that test refusing the fixture link), fixed → `3 passed`.
- End-to-end: the previously-crashing command (`pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_skills_config.py -q`, real env, clean-main worktree) → `11 passed in 1.05s`.
- Control: clean `origin/main` in a plain worktree reproduces the crash (`KeyError: <_pytest.stash.StashKey …>`, exit 1, zero tests).

**Notes**

- Adjacent to #129455 (also `home_io_guard` on default installs) — different trigger: that one is import-time PM probes at collection; this one is the interpreter's own stdlib paths during execution/reporting. This PR does not address that issue's probes.

Fixes #129510

prs.title: feat(desktop): execute slash commands with attachments for prompt-taking dispatches
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Implements the split-by-command-class design from #131233: instead of blanket-blocking every slash command that carries an attachment (the warning shipped in #81833 to stop #81798's silent data loss), Desktop now classifies the command's surface and only refuses the ones an attachment can never ride.

- **Prompt-taking dispatches** (`send`/`skill`, plus `prefill`) execute with their attachments: the composer attachments thread through `executeSlashCommand` into `submitPromptText`, so `/moa <prompt>` with a screenshot finally works — the case #81798 asked for. `prefill` re-homes its attachments silently alongside the prefilled draft so the next non-slash send carries both.
- **Known no-payload surfaces** (`action`/`picker`/`rpc`/`unavailable`, e.g. `/stop`, `/status`, pickers) keep today's warn-and-refuse — nothing has executed, so the caller's restore path puts the draft back intact.
- **Unknown/backend commands** reach dispatch; a post-dispatch check merges anything unconsumed back into the composer (merge-by-id with staged-rows winning — never an overwrite of files the user staged mid-dispatch) and warns. Only a rejected send returns `false`, delegating restore to the caller.
- **Queue**: both slash+attachment refusals narrow to known no-payload commands, drains bypass the refusal (a catalog sync between enqueue and drain can no longer livelock the queue), and `queueKickoffIfSessionBusy` carries attachments instead of dropping them.

The entry guards in all three submit paths (`use-prompt-actions/index.ts`, the busy branch in `use-composer-submit.ts`, `session-tile-actions.ts`) share the new `isNoPayloadSlashCommand` classifier, which reuses the existing desktop command registry after stripping leading composer attachment refs. Tile surfaces execute text-only with an explicit warning — threading them would consume against the primary composer's scope and duplicate against the tile's.

## Related Issue

Fixes #131233

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/lib/desktop-slash-commands.ts` — new `isNoPayloadSlashCommand` classifier (registry surfaces `action`/`picker`/`rpc`/`unavailable`; strips leading `@ref` lines like `isSlashCommandText`).
- `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/index.ts` — guard narrows to the classifier (queue drains bypass it); attachments + `fromQueue` forwarded to `executeSlashCommand`, which now returns the send-rejection boolean.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/slash.ts` — `SlashActionCtx.attachments` threading (including alias re-dispatch); `send`/`skill` dispatches pass attachments to `submitPromptText`; `prefill` flags silent re-home; queued kickoffs consume-later; post-dispatch tail merges unconsumed attachments back with a warning; returns `false` only on rejected send.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/queue-if-busy.ts` — `QueueIfBusyInput.attachments` so queued entries carry their attachments to drain.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-submit.ts` — busy-path guard narrows to the classifier; busy slash submissions clone+clear like the idle path so consumption/re-home stay symmetric.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-queue.ts` — enqueue and queued-edit refusals narrow to known no-payload commands (unknown commands drain via the post-dispatch check).
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/session-tile-actions.ts` — classifier guard; unknown commands execute text-only with an explicit warning.
- Tests: `desktop-slash-commands.test.ts` (+5 classifier cases), `index.test.tsx` (guard/threading/re-home/prefill/sendRejected/alias), `use-composer-queue.test.tsx` (refusal narrowing, harness attachment override).

## How to Test

1. Attach an image, type `/moa <prompt>`, send — the command executes and the image rides into the prompt (previously: "Command not sent" warning). Same for skill commands and `/goal <text>`.
2. Attach an image, type `/status` (or `/stop`, `/new`) — the existing warning appears, nothing executes, and the draft + attachment remain in the composer.
3. Attach an image, type an output-only command (e.g. a skill that prints) — the command executes, the attachment returns to the composer with a warning (nothing silently dropped).
4. Attach an image while a send is in flight / queue a slash command with an attachment — the staged file is preserved (merge, not overwrite) and queued entries drain without livelocking.

Verification: `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean; `eslint` 0 errors (warnings identical to baseline); vitest 1509 passed with the only failures pre-existing on clean `main` (voice-prefs + electron build-script suites, same-lane baseline-verified); targeted suites for the touched files pass 200/200. Backend `pytest` not run — this change touches `apps/desktop` only.

prs.title: fix(agent): honor "retry shortly (after N s)" capacity hints in the retry wait
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

OpenCode Go answers a per-model capacity refusal with HTTP 429 and puts the wait only in the message text:

```
Upstream request failed: [ttft_admission_refused] the cell is at capacity; retry shortly (after 42 s)
```

There is no `Retry-After` header and no `retry_after` field. On current `main` (`2506f5b0`) both `reset_delay_from_message(msg)` and `provider_retry_after_seconds(err)` return `None` for this error, so `compute_error_backoff` waits a jittered 2–3 s and the turn falls back to another (often paid) provider within seconds, although the server asked for 42 s.

This PR fixes half (1) of #145899. Half (2), the `overloaded` fallback threshold, is #130273 and does not overlap with this diff.

- `_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS_RE` also accepts `retry shortly (after N s)`. The existing `retry N s` and `retry after N s` forms still parse. `ms` and words that start with `s` (`42 samples`) do not match.
- `provider_retry_after_seconds` uses that explicit retry hint from the error text as a last resort, after the `Retry-After` header and the `retry_after` body field. `resets in …` quota windows stay out, because they are not a request to wait before retrying. Zero and negative values still return `None`.

All callers of `provider_retry_after_seconds` get the same value: the main retry wait, the auto-recovery ladder, the free-tier cooldown check and the auxiliary same-credential backoff. Each one already treats it as a provider-declared cooldown and applies its own cap.

This supersedes #145927 by @akhilraija, which took the same approach and was closed by its author without review. The commit credits them with a `Co-authored-by:` trailer.

## Related Issue

Fixes #145899

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/retry_utils.py`: widen `_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS_RE`; text-hint fallback in `provider_retry_after_seconds`.
- `tests/agent/test_capacity_retry_delay.py`: new regression tests. They drive `compute_error_backoff` with a real `openai.RateLimitError` and cover precedence (header > body field > text) and inputs that are not a wait.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_capacity_retry_delay.py`: 14 passed.
2. Red check: with only `agent/retry_utils.py` reverted, 6 of the 14 fail: the four capacity cases, plus `retry after 2 seconds` and `retry 7 secs`, which `main` parses for the credential pool but never feeds into the retry wait. The header and body-field precedence cases and the inputs that are not a wait still pass.
3. Neighbouring suites: `test_retry_utils`, `test_retry_delay_parsers_shared`, `test_stream_retry_backoff`, `test_retry_status_buffer`, `test_image_shrink_recovery`, `test_rate_limit_reset_hint`, `test_reasoning_disable_recovery`, `test_turn_recovery_autorecover`, `test_welcome_tier_recovery` and `tests/e2e/core/providers/test_openai_responses.py`, together with the new file: 109 passed, 8 skipped, 0 failed.

prs.title: fix(terminal): break exact retries after timeouts
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A terminal timeout does not prove that the command had no side effects. Retrying the exact call automatically can repeat a partially completed deployment, write, or remote operation.

This change records a profile-local HMAC fingerprint only after a terminal command was actually dispatched and timed out. For 15 minutes, an unchanged retry in the same session is blocked with an explicit `UNKNOWN` side-effect warning. The fingerprint uses the final middleware-mutated arguments; raw commands and session IDs are not persisted.

Queued calls, pre-tool-hook timeouts, guardrail blocks, and start-gate-abandoned calls are not recorded. Natural process exit code 124 is kept distinct from a real timeout.

This is adjacent to, but does not duplicate:

- #69346, which handles repeated pre-dispatch hardline blocks within one conversation. This PR handles real post-dispatch timeouts with unknown side effects and can survive process restarts when secure POSIX persistence is available.
- #72500, which prevents several internal timeout surfaces from freezing the turn. It does not prevent replay of a terminal call that may already have produced side effects.

## Related Issue

Related: #69346, #72500

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- Add `agent/tool_timeout_circuit.py` with HMAC fingerprints, a 15-minute TTL, and bounded state. Raw commands and session IDs are not persisted.
- Keep a process-local circuit on all platforms. Persist profile-local state on supported POSIX systems with owner-only storage, atomic replacement, and cross-process locking; fall back to memory when secure persistence or locking is unavailable.
- Check the final middleware-mutated arguments at the dispatch boundary and record explicit post-dispatch timeouts. Keep pre-dispatch abandonment distinct from a dispatched operation with unknown side effects.
- Preserve natural exit code 124 as distinct from an explicit execution timeout and propagate structured timeout markers through terminal and environment result paths.
- Add integration coverage for private fingerprints, storage fallbacks, middleware argument rewrites, dispatch races, and abandonment snapshots.

## Validation for the current revision

Current head: `78c18130c4201cbff7b27b6a7a30d7ff42eebbf6`.

The commands below have been updated to paths present at this head. They are **commands to run, not new passing results**. Tests, lint, and compilation were not rerun as part of this description-only update. Previously reported pass counts and root E2E results belong to earlier validation and must not be treated as evidence for this head.

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/run_agent/test_timeout_retry_circuit_integration.py tests/run_agent/test_sequential_tool_timeout.py tests/run_agent/test_start_order_gate.py tests/tools/test_managed_modal_environment.py tests/tools/test_terminal_timeout_output.py tests/tools/test_terminal_tool.py
```

prs.title: fix(persistence): uniquify tool-call ids after provider-id digest normalization
prs.body:
## Problem

Turns abort with `session_persistence_failed` (user-facing: "Hermes couldn't save this conversation, so it stopped rather than lose your messages") because the session-DB flush raises:

```
sqlite3.IntegrityError: UNIQUE constraint failed: messages.session_id, messages.tool_call_id
```

## Root cause

Chat-completions gateways mint tool-call ids with the `chatcmpl-tool-*` prefix. In `validate_tool_calls()` the pipeline is:

1. `uniquify_tool_call_ids(tool_calls, taken=taken)` — dedupe on RAW ids; `taken` holds ids from earlier turns (already digest-normalized `call_<sha256[:12]>` strings)
2. `normalize_provider_tool_call_ids(tool_calls)` — deterministic digest `chatcmpl-tool-X` → `call_<sha256(X)[:12]>`

If the provider re-mints the SAME raw `chatcmpl-tool-X` in a later turn of the same session, step 1 sees a raw string not present in `taken` (which holds digests), so no rename happens; step 2 maps it to the same digest that is already persisted → the UNIQUE constraint fails, the whole flush batch is rejected, and the turn is aborted. Observed in production against the Nous inference gateway (both claude-opus and glm routes).

## Fix

- Re-run `_uniquify_tool_call_ids(tool_calls, taken=taken)` AFTER normalization in `validate_tool_calls()`, so an id colliding with an already-persisted digest gets the deterministic `<id>_d<n>` suffix (the existing scheme in `uniquify_tool_call_ids`).
- Same guard in `turn_tool_round.py` after batch filtering, since filtering can make a mixed batch normalization-eligible right before staging.

Everything stays deterministic (no uuid4) so prompt-cache prefixes are preserved; `normalize` remains idempotent for already-normalized ids.

## Testing

- New regression test: a re-used provider id across turns is renamed to `call_<digest>_d2` (deterministic suffix), no collision; within-batch duplicates and the third re-use (`_d3`) are covered too.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_provider_id_mint_normalization.py tests/agent/test_agent_guardrails.py` → 40 passed, 0 failed.

prs.title: plugin-catalog: add github-locker
prs.body:
Adds **GitHub.Locker** (`github-locker`) to the plugin catalog.

## What does this PR do?

Adds one file, `plugin-catalog/github-locker.yaml`, pointing to [zer0person/github-locker-mcp](https://github.com/zer0person/github-locker-mcp) pinned at [`cfdbe54c9760b85c3eb1253a80f33ceb5d574baf`](https://github.com/zer0person/github-locker-mcp/tree/cfdbe54c9760b85c3eb1253a80f33ceb5d574baf) (version `1.0.0`). I own GitHub.Locker (https://github.locker) and the plugin repository and am its sole contributor (Rule 5).

- **Format:** Agent Plugins v1 (`plugin.json` + `mcp.json` + `skills/github-locker/SKILL.md`), configuration only: no runtime code, no Python dependencies.
- **Hosted MCP endpoint:** `https://github.locker/mcp` (`streamable-http`, stateless, free, no authentication or keys).
- **Tools (3, all read-only):**
  - `search_projects`: catalog projects matching every word of a query, sorted by stars or by stars gained in a day, week or month.
  - `trending_projects`: the projects that gained the most stars on the last GitHub day, week or month.
  - `get_project`: one project as markdown: summary, questions and answers, license, similar projects, topics, start of the README.

## Disclosure (Rule 13)

- **Network:** every tool call goes over HTTPS to `https://github.locker/mcp` with only the arguments the agent passes (search words, a period, an `owner/repo` name). Nothing from the user's machine is read or sent.
- **Read-only & server trust:** all tools are annotated `readOnlyHint: true`, `destructiveHint: false`, `idempotentHint: true`. `plugin.json` marks the server `trust: "untrusted"` under `extensions.com.nousresearch.hermes`. The tool set is served by github.locker at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.
- **Local footprint:** `plugin.json`, `mcp.json`, `skills/github-locker/SKILL.md`, README, LICENSE and manifests for other clients. No binaries, hooks, env vars, stored credentials, telemetry or self-updater. The server logs only the tool name and response time.

## Testing

Live server at the time of submission:

```text
$ tools/list
search_projects  readOnly=true destructive=false
trending_projects  readOnly=true destructive=false
get_project  readOnly=true destructive=false

$ tools/call search_projects {"query":"self-hosted notes","limit":2}
8 GitHub.Locker projects match "self-hosted notes"; most-starred first:

1. usememos/memos — 64.6K stars · +177 this week · Go · MIT · last push 2026-11-18
   Memos is an open-source, self-hosted app for capturing short-form notes—daily notes, links, work logs, and snippets—into a chronological Markdown timeline you can revisit by search, tag, or date.
   https://github.locker/usememos/memos · https://github.com/usememos/memos
2. TriliumNext/Trilium — 39K stars · +111 this week · TypeScript · AGPL-3.0 · last push 2026-11-18
   Trilium Notes is a free, open-source, cross-platform hierarchical note-taking app built for creating large personal knowledge bases.
   https://github.locker/TriliumNext/Trilium · https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium
```

The same endpoint is checked with the official MCP TypeScript SDK client (`StreamableHTTPClientTransport`: initialize, tools/list, tools/call). It is also listed in the official MCP Registry as `locker.github/catalog`.

prs.title: fix(tool_search): resolve Anthropic OAuth wire tool aliases in tool_call and tool_describe
prs.body:
## Summary
Resolves Anthropic OAuth wire tool aliases (`chat_history_lookup` -> `session_search`, `context_notes` -> `memory`) inside deferred `tool_call` and `tool_describe` validation/dispatch.

## Problem
On Anthropic OAuth, `agent/anthropic_adapter.py` aliases `session_search` -> `chat_history_lookup` and `memory` -> `context_notes` (`_OAUTH_TOOL_NAME_ALIASES`) in tool schemas and prose (including compaction hints). While direct calls are reverse-mapped in `agent/transports/anthropic.py`, if the model invokes `chat_history_lookup` (or `context_notes`) through `tool_call` or `tool_describe`, `tools/tool_search_validation.py` only checks internal tool names and rejects it as an unknown tool name instead of resolving the alias / guiding the model to call it directly.

## Changes
- Resolve `_OAUTH_TOOL_NAME_REVERSE_ALIASES` in `tools/tool_search_validation.py` and `tools/tool_search.py` for `tool_call` and `tool_describe`.
- Add unit tests in `tests/tools/test_tool_search.py` covering OAuth wire aliases (`chat_history_lookup`, `context_notes`).

## Verification
- Passed targeted `tool_search` and Anthropic OAuth alias pytest suites (114 tests).

### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

main at 9774cb596, with #4274 applied (@types/bun 1.4.4)

### Host platform

macOS

### What happened?

The container typecheck fails once `@types/bun` moves to 1.4.4 (Dependabot PR #4274):

`container/agent-runner/src/test-utils/run-bun.ts(27,37): error TS2322: Type 'number | Signals | null' is not assignable to type 'Signals | null'.`

In 1.4.4, `Subprocess.signalCode` can be a number. Our test helper `runBun` returns it in a field typed `NodeJS.Signals | null`. Every CI job on #4274 is red because of this one line.

### What did you expect?

The container typechecks with both `@types/bun` 1.3 and 1.4, so #4274 can merge.

### How can we reproduce it?

1. Check out #4274 (head ff68121b6).

Development checkout

Not provider-specific

```shell
##[error]container/agent-runner/src/test-utils/run-bun.ts(27,37): error TS2322: Type 'number | Signals | null' is not assignable to type 'Signals | null'.
```

`@types/bun` 1.3.12 (main today).

issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

v2026.11.0 (also main 080bd7809)

### Host platform

macOS

### What happened?

`/update-nanoclaw` stops at `prepare` with a raw git failure (see logs) when the install is not on a branch. This happens after `git checkout v2026.11.0`, and on installs made by the e2e tools, which check out the commit under test detached.

The updater has a clearer message for this case, "Update requires a named branch, not detached HEAD", but never reaches it. `git symbolic-ref --quiet` exits 1 on a detached HEAD, so the call throws first (`currentBranch` in `scripts/update/transaction.ts`).

When the detached commit is newer than the latest release, the default stable channel fails even earlier with `ahead-of-release` and asks the user to pick a channel. The branch problem only shows up on the next run.

### What did you expect?

A plain error, before any channel question, that says HEAD is detached, where (the tag or commit), and the one command that fixes it. For example:

`Update needs a branch, but HEAD is detached at tag v2026.11.0. Make one here, then run the update again: git switch -c nanoclaw`

### How can we reproduce it?

1. `git clone https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw.git && cd nanoclaw`
2. `git checkout v2026.11.0`
3. Run `/update-nanoclaw` (or, after `pnpm install`: `pnpm exec tsx scripts/update-nanoclaw.ts prepare --project-root "$PWD" --remote origin`)
4. See the `git symbolic-ref` error in the logs below.

### OS version and CPU architecture

macOS 26.6.1, arm64

### Install or update path

Something else

### Docker version

_No response_

### Channel or interface

Not channel-specific

### Agent provider

Not provider-specific

_No response_

```shell
{
  "schema": "nanoclaw-update-error/v1",
```
