prs.title: fix(templates): read restamp's live files without following or blocking
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Restamp now reads the agent-writable files it compares through one descriptor that cannot follow a symlink or wait on a named pipe.

- **Problem**: restamp's plan checked a context file or a skill overlay file, then read it by path. Both folders are container-writable, so the agent could swap in a named pipe between the two calls, and the read would wait on the host's event loop (the hang in GHSA-j5mj-3gjr-xpwj). `statSync` also followed a symlinked context file to its target.
- **Fix**: one helper, `readRegularFile`, opens with `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`, checks `fstat` on the descriptor, and takes the bytes and the mode from it. Anything else reads as absent, and so does an overlay entry that the container removes or replaces after the listing. A symlinked context file now plans as `create` and is never removed, the rule `readGroupPersona` already uses for the persona file.
- **Out of scope**: a symlinked parent folder is still followed by the compare, as before. The compare cannot block, and the writes already refuse that folder through `AnchoredDir`.

## Related work

Closes #4521

Follow-up to #4440 (GHSA-j5mj-3gjr-xpwj), suggested by @amit-shafnir while reviewing that fix. His other follow-up, a refused provider spawn file that names itself, already shipped in #4440.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [x] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- 4 new tests in `src/templates/restamp.test.ts`, all failing on main: a symlinked context file plans as absent; a context file or overlay file that turns into a FIFO at the moment of the open does not block the plan; overlay entries that change after the listing do not abort it.
- Removing `O_NONBLOCK`, `O_NOFOLLOW`, the `fstat` check, the mode compare, the listing fix, or either new read fails at least one test.
- The FIFO tests cannot hang: a helper process frees a stuck read after 3 s, so a regression fails instead.
- `vitest run src`: 2503 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed. `tsc`, `prettier` and `eslint` on the changed files: clean.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Restamp no longer follows symlinks or waits on named pipes when it compares an agent's files with its template.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Untrusted input: context files in the group folder and the skill overlay, which the agent container can write. Restamp's reads there now refuse anything that is not a regular file, without blocking. No change to writes, permissions, credentials, mounts or containers.

## Skill delivery

- [x] Not a skill
- [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

## AI assistance

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change

<!-- Required. -->
- [x] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

## Summary

prs.title: fix(update): say where a detached HEAD is and how to fix it
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

`/update-nanoclaw` on a detached HEAD now says where HEAD is and how to fix it, instead of failing with a raw `git symbolic-ref` error.

- **Problem**: `git symbolic-ref --quiet` exits 1 on a detached HEAD, so `prepare` threw "Command failed: git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD" before reaching its own branch message. When the detached commit was newer than the latest release, the stable channel failed even earlier with `ahead-of-release` and asked a channel question instead.
- **Fix**: read the branch with `git branch --show-current` (empty when detached) and refuse with `Update needs a branch, but HEAD is detached at tag v2026.11.0. Make a branch here with a name that is not taken yet, then run the update again. For example: git switch -c nanoclaw` (or `at commit <sha>`). CLI `prepare` runs this check before channel resolution, so `prepare` fetches nothing and no channel question comes first.
- **Reach**: the skill runs the controller from upstream `main`, so every install gets the new message on its next `/update-nanoclaw` after merge.
- **Out of scope**: updating while detached (the updater still needs a branch), and a checkout detached by hand between `prepare` and `cutover`, which main does not check either.

## Related work

Closes #4525

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- New test in `scripts/update/transaction.e2e.test.ts`: `prepare` on a checkout detached at an annotated tag, then at a bare commit, names each one and creates no transaction, backup branch or tag. Fails on main with the raw error.
- New test in `scripts/update/channel.test.ts` runs the real controller CLI on a checkout detached at a commit newer than the latest release. It gets the branch message, not `ahead-of-release`, and fetches nothing. Fails on main, and fails again with only the CLI check removed.
- `scripts/update` tests: 131/131 pass. Prettier clean.
- Codex adversarial review, 3 rounds: 3 findings fixed (check order, stderr parsing, fetch proof in the test). The rest were refuted or left as minor: the cutover gap above is on main too, and `nanoclaw.sh` already needs git 2.22 for `--show-current`.
- E2E on a fresh exe.dev VM: headless install of main 080bd7809 (Claude, OneCLI, `PING: ok`), which leaves the checkout detached. Ran `prepare` with the controller archived from main and from this branch, the way the skill does:

  | Checkout | main | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | Detached as installed, newer than v2026.11.0 | `ahead-of-release` | `detached at commit 110a625d` |
  | Same, `--channel edge` | raw `git symbolic-ref` error | `detached at commit 110a625d` |
  | `git checkout v2026.11.0` | raw `git symbolic-ref` error | `detached at tag v2026.11.0` |

  After `git switch -c nanoclaw`, this branch's `prepare` reached `prepared` (already on v2026.11.0), and `abandon` cleaned up.

prs.title: fix(update): check snapshot space before cutover stops the service
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Update cutover now checks free space for the snapshot before it stops the service, and validate shows the numbers first.

- **Problem**: cutover stopped the service and killed the agents before it checked free space (in `createSnapshot`). A short disk meant downtime and lost turns, with nothing updated.
- **Fix**: cutover runs the check before `stopService` and refuses with the service and agents untouched. `createSnapshot` keeps its check after the drain as the last guard. One shared measure.
- **Before cutover**: validate saves `snapshotSpace` (needed, free, fits, summary) and the update skill shows it. It never fails validation; cutover enforces.
- **Error**: needed and free (`need 260 MiB ... have 120 MiB free`), how much to free, and a `prune --dry-run` command from the running controller (checkouts older than v2.3.0 have no `prune`).
- **Live state**: the early walk runs while agents write; an entry that vanishes or changes type counts as zero. A crashed copy's space counts as free; cutover clears it first.
- **Full disk after the drain**: if saving state fails too, the old service still restarts (before, that write threw first).
- **Reach**: the controller comes from upstream `main`, so every install gets this on its next update after merge.
- **Not covered**: image rebuild space. It depends on Docker's cache, and a failed build rolls back.
- **Follow-up, not counted**: a rollback stages a second snapshot copy. Counting it would double the need and block updates that work today. A short rollback fails safe: live files untouched, manual steps printed.
- **Out of scope**: what the snapshot copies (#4479), and the estimate (file sizes plus 256 MiB).

## Related work

Closes #4478

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- 5 new tests: refusal before any stop, drain, reset or build, then cutover once freed; a disk that fills after the drain (refuses, restarts the service even when state cannot be saved); validate's report (fits, short, unmeasured); a crashed copy; vanished entries. Each fails without its fix.
- `vitest run scripts/update setup/lib/setup-commit.test.ts scripts/update-skills.test.ts src/memory-migration-contract.test.ts`: 170 pass. `tsc`, `prettier --check`, `skill-pins:check` clean.
- The archived controller loads under tsx 4.21.0 (v2.2.0, v2.3.0) and 4.23.15; an `import.meta.dirname` draft crashed under 4.21.0.
- Live, fresh Debian 13 LXC on Proxmox, installed from `main` (0097da64a), disk filled to 120 MiB free:
  - `main`'s controller stopped the service, killed the running agent, failed on space, then restarted.
  - This branch refused at once: same service PID, agent still up, no stop in the journal, HEAD unchanged.
  - Freed, the same transaction cut over and finished; the agent replied. Repeated on the final commit after a `rollback`.

prs.title: feat(channels): add native Proton Mail adapter via Proton Mail Bridge
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

The adapter half of #3726, moved to the `channels` registry branch as review asked; #3726 keeps the skill (`/add-proton-mail`) and the Bridge container on `main`.
- **What**: a native IMAP/SMTP adapter (`src/channels/proton-mail.ts`) for a local Proton Mail Bridge, its tests, a faithful fake IMAP server for them (`src/test-utils/fake-imap.ts`), the barrel import, and six exact-pinned deps.
- **Sender identity**: a mail counts as from its `From:` address only when Proton vouches for it. Mail from outside Proton needs exactly one `mail.protonmail.ch` DMARC verdict, `pass`, for the From domain. Mail from another Proton account (which carries no verdict) needs exactly one `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, no Proton DMARC verdict, and a From domain that is Proton's own (`proton.me`, `protonmail.com`, `protonmail.ch`, `pm.me`, or a subdomain) or listed exactly in `PROTON_MAIL_INTERNAL_DOMAINS` (Proton custom domains, the Bridge account's own included: a Proton account can send from a connected Gmail address, so its domain is not trusted on its own; entries must be whole domains, and the adapter warns at startup when the account's own non-Proton domain is unlisted). Addresses are compared with the domain in ASCII (punycode) and the address in NFC, so one mailbox is one sender; at startup the adapter names any `proton-mail` messaging group stored in another form (it would never match mail). The `From:` must be one plain address on one `From:` line. Mail from the Bridge account's own address is never delivered. Refused mail stays unread; internal mail from a domain not trusted is also flagged `$NanoClawFailed`, since it is almost always a real Proton user on an unlisted custom domain.
- **Approval cards**: each card mail carries an `[NC-…]` token in its subject. An answer counts only from the card's approver, quoting the token, `In-Reply-To` the card mail (or the one reminder the adapter sent the approver about it), with an option command on the first line. Every option gets a distinct command. Cards persist across restarts; `onAction` gets the card's Message-ID and address. A card core has closed, or no longer holds, refuses later replies with core's reason when it gave one. Unanswered cards are never pruned before their 7-day TTL; at 1000 open cards a new one is refused rather than pushing one out. Answers to an open card are not held by the hourly sender limit (a held answer would let a gateway approval time out); mail on a card's thread that turns out not to be an answer is counted. While a card waits, its approver's reply to it without a command ("Approve" without the slash) gets one notice listing the commands instead of reaching the agent, and later ones stay unread and flagged `$NanoClawFailed`; a bottom-posted command is read below the quote. Card lines show a label the command doesn't say, and options sharing a label (two agents with one name) show their value.
- **Confirmations**: none of the adapter's own for gateway approvals (`deferResolution`): core's card edit is the confirmation, threaded onto the card; other cards get a neutral "Reply received".
- **Transport**: IMAP STARTTLS required; certificate verification on except on loopback; `PROTON_MAIL_TLS_CA_FILE` pins Bridge's own certificate so loopback is verified too, and an unreadable pin stops the adapter.
- **Delivery**: no mail is read until core's `onHostStart` has run (the host releases inbound first), so nothing is marked read while the host still holds routing. The callback only sets a flag; an adapter set up after host start reads at once, and one still waiting after 5 minutes logs that it is still waiting (mail stays unread on the server). The inbound id is the adapter's (UIDVALIDITY plus UID), never the sender's Message-ID. A reply that keeps the conversation's subject, or arrives on a card's thread, reaches core as its bare body, so core's free-text prompts get just the answer. Failures inside the adapter are retried with back-off up to five times, then left unread and flagged `$NanoClawFailed`; routing failures inside the host are not retried (the mail is already handed over). Mail over 40 MB is flagged without being fetched. State is written atomically with a backup (`state.json.bak`); with both unreadable the adapter does not start, so no mail is skipped.
- **Reading mail**: parsing and HTML conversion run in worker threads with timeouts and a heap ceiling, so crafted mail cannot stall the host. When a mail has both bodies the HTML is read. html-to-text runs with no word wrap and no upper-casing. HTML hidden from a mail-client reader (`display:none`, `hidden`, zero-size, transparent text, `<template>`, …) is kept but marked `[hidden CODE: … /hidden CODE]` with a per-mail random code, and invisible or direction characters are marked too (a lone direction mark beside Hebrew/Arabic letters, or a zero-width space between Thai/Lao/Khmer/Myanmar letters, is ordinary text and left alone); when the body the agent gets carries any mark, a note tells it to treat marked text as suspect. Quoted history and signatures are cut; a forward keeps the forwarded mail (a forward's subject prefix, or a "Forwarded message" / "Begin forwarded message:" line before any quoted history), with a coded `[forwarded CODE: …]` line where the forwarded mail begins, since its From:/Date: lines are the sender's claim; the header block is recognised in the common European languages, Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Greek, Hebrew, Turkish and Hungarian, and in a forward-subject mail any "label: name <address>" line followed by two more label lines (indented continuations skipped). A mail that opens with such a block gets the same line whatever its subject. A forward sent as an attachment (`message/rfc822`) is read into the body under the same line. A coded `[end of forwarded text CODE]` line follows the sender's text, and the note says instructions inside a forward are not the sender's request. Every bracketed line the channel adds carries the code (the attachments held back, `[… truncated by the mail channel CODE, …]`, the HTML-cut and "HTML body not converted" lines, and the notes, which open `[Note from the mail channel CODE: …`); the notes come last, after the shown subject, and are decided on the text as cut. Any "[Note from the mail channel" the sender typed is rewritten as theirs, also with invisible or control characters inside it (best effort: the code is what holds). Attachment names are cleaned, made unique per mail and given extensions from their MIME type. A non-ASCII sender domain is shown in ASCII with its Unicode spelling beside it. The body is capped at 50k characters, the subject at 300.
- **Limits**: attachments go through only once the sender's DM is wired to an agent, up to 15 MB each and 25 MB per mail. Bounces, auto-replies (`Auto-Submitted`, `X-Loop`, no-reply senders, …) and mailing-list mail (`List-Id`, `List-Post`, `Precedence: list`) are skipped before the router; list mail is left unread and tagged `$NanoClawList`, since list headers can be forged. `PROTON_MAIL_POLL_SECONDS` must be 10–3600.
- **Hourly limits and the hold queue**: at most 20 mails an hour from one sender reach the host; beyond that, mail waits unread (in the state's retry list) and is handed over as the hour frees up. **This is a throttle, not a loop breaker**: two agents mailing each other are slowed to about 20 mails an hour each, not stopped. Bridge drops every loop marker on outgoing mail (below), and core has no loop handling for any channel yet, so that risk stays open project-wide. New addresses not yet approved are limited to 10 an hour, 200 in any 7 days, and 20 per registrable domain (subdomains share their parent's) in the same 7 days, freed early when core settles (approves or denies) an address; a denied address takes no slot. A new address over its domain's share waits, re-checked hourly, while the hold queue has room for it. Held mail is capped at 200. Senders not yet approved may use 100 of it between them, whichever limit held their mail (their own hourly figure too), any one domain 20 and any one new address 5, so approved senders' over-limit mail always has room. A denied address's mail over the hourly limit is not held or even fetched (core drops it). A retry is checked against the limit unless the mail was already counted (entries saved by earlier versions are read by their old rule), so a failure never lets mail past it, a held mail's first read may still retry a slow HTML conversion, and someone a card was mailed to (within its 7 days) counts as approved. Past a cap, mail is left unread and flagged `$NanoClawFailed`.
- **Headers that cannot be sent**: Bridge builds each outgoing mail from a draft template and drops custom headers, so `Auto-Submitted` (RFC 3834) and our `X-NanoClaw-Agent` loop marker never arrive. The own-address check, the inbound auto-reply filter and the hourly throttle are what remain.
- **Message kinds**: a `/command` by email is a command; `send_card` goes out as its fallback text plus links; an edit goes out as a correction on the edited mail's thread.
- **Out of scope**: shared email helpers (sender check, reply-card store) for `/add-resend` and #3743, a follow-up once their home is agreed; a generic IMAP/SMTP channel (maintainers' call); loop handling in core; laying out HTML tables row by row (#4257, stacked on this); an HTML alternative for agent Markdown in outbound mail (a follow-up).

<details>
<summary>Why the sender check counts verdicts, not their position</summary>

Review asked for `Authentication-Results` "only as added by the trusted receiving server". Bridge adds no verdict of its own; it serves the headers Proton's inbound servers recorded. A position rule (only verdicts above the first `Received:`) was tried and dropped: across 60 real inbox mails, Bridge rebuilds every message with the whole `Received:` chain first, then Proton's verdicts, then `X-Pm-Origin`, so position says nothing about who added a verdict. A forged `mail.protonmail.ch` verdict beside Proton's makes two and is refused; all 60 external mails carried exactly one.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Why X-Pm-Origin: internal can be trusted, and why only for some domains (probes on Bridge 3.27.0)</summary>

Proton-to-Proton mail carries no Authentication-Results, so the DMARC rule alone refused all of it. Three probes:
1. **External mail with forged Proton headers.** A mail from Gmail carried a forged `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, `X-Pm-Content-Encryption`, `X-Pm-Internal-Id` and `mail.protonmail.ch; dmarc=pass`. Every one was stripped. What arrived carried Proton's own single `X-Pm-Origin: external` and Proton's real verdicts only.
2. **A separate Proton account to the Bridge account.** One `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, `X-Pm-Content-Encryption: end-to-end`, and no Authentication-Results.
3. **The Bridge account to itself.** The same as probe 2.

A Proton sender cannot set headers: Bridge's SMTP draft template drops them. The rule fails closed: a forged `internal` that ever survived would sit beside Proton's `external` and be refused as two values. Since a Proton account can also send as an address outside Proton's domains (a custom domain, or a connected external address), and nothing Proton adds says which, `internal` is trusted only for the domains above. On a real inbox, every internal mail without a verdict came from a Proton domain or a subdomain (`notify.proton.me`).
</details>

## Related work

Split from #3726 (skill half stays there; it copies these files from `channels`, so this lands first). Purely additive on `channels`: new files, one barrel line, six deps.

Native IMAP/SMTP adapter; mail counts as from its sender only on Proton's DMARC pass (or Proton-internal mail from a trusted domain), and approval cards are answered by replying to the card email itself. Proton custom domains, the Bridge account's own included, go in `PROTON_MAIL_INTERNAL_DOMAINS`.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- Inbound email is untrusted. For outside mail, sender identity rests on Proton's DMARC verdict, which is domain-level, so the owner's domain must stop its users sending as each other: someone who can get a DMARC-aligned pass for the owner's domain (a shared ESP in its SPF record, a relay that doesn't enforce From) can write as the owner. Only card answers carry the extra token. For Proton-to-Proton mail it rests on Proton's `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, trusted only for the domains above; anyone with a free Proton account is verified as their own address, and unknown senders still go through the approval card.
- Hidden HTML and invisible characters are marked for the agent, not removed, with a code the sender cannot predict, so a mark without the code was written by the sender.
- Attachments from a sender who is not yet approved are held back, and new addresses are limited per hour, per 7 days and per domain, so strangers cannot fill `pending_channel_approvals` or the cards the owner's approvals need.
- Loops: throttled, not stopped (see Hourly limits); stated here and in SKILL.md (#3726).
- Credentials: the bridge password is read from `.env` only; IMAP requires STARTTLS and SMTP requires TLS; Bridge's certificate is pinned when `PROTON_MAIL_TLS_CA_FILE` is set (the skill sets it).
- Deps pinned exactly — `imapflow@1.7.8`, `mailparser@3.9.47`, `nodemailer@10.1.7` (past the addressparser advisories below 10.1.4), `html-to-text@10.0.1`, `@types/mailparser@3.4.6`, `@types/nodemailer@8.0.1` — all past the 3-day `minimumReleaseAge`; no build-script approvals added.

prs.title: fix(router): await session write turn before backfill and wake context
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Serializes cross-session backfill and wake-context gathering inside the session write turn so concurrent arrivals cannot reorder context ahead of earlier messages.
- **Problem**: `deliverToAgent` awaited `turn.previous` only after `backfillSession` and `gatherWakeContext`, allowing a fast concurrent message on the same session (e.g. a second chat on an `agent-shared` session while a slash command's backfill is in flight) to write wake-context rows ahead of the earlier message.
- **Fix**: Moves `await turn.previous` to the top of the `try` block in `deliverToAgent` before `backfillSession` and `gatherWakeContext` (zero overhead when no wake-context providers are registered because `takeWriteTurn` returns a no-op).
- **Out of scope**: Changing `WAKE_CONTEXT_BUDGET_MS` or late-arriving block writes.

## Related work

No linked issue; isolated 2-line router ordering fix with a deterministic regression test in `src/wake-context.test.ts`.

prs.title: fix(dsh): recover profile reloads and transient desktop connections
prs.body:
## Changes

- Restore profile hot reload in Electron by using its exposed module binding when the upstream bootstrap realm is unavailable. The patch is scoped to DSH `0.2.2-rc.5`.
- Set the desktop gateway heartbeat interval to 10 seconds. A short main-thread stall can otherwise disconnect an active tool stream. Detecting a silent peer can now take longer.
- Retry a read of `session/projections` once on `ECONNRESET`. This lets the subagent list refresh its cached status on the first request. Turn submissions keep their existing semantics.

## Windows Electron acceptance

- Playwright/CDP with a Windows ASAR layout recorded three HMR errors at startup and across two profile edits before the patch, and zero after. Both updated settings took effect on the same host PID.
- During a real shell task, a 7.6 s injected pause disconnected three active streams with close code 1006 on the original heartbeat. The patched run remained connected. A separate TCP reset during a child task recovered with one persisted user message. A reset of a catalog read returned stale `running` before the change and the correct `done` on the first refresh after it.
- With 20,000 synthetic rows the default 400,000-token window reached 366,230 tokens and completed automatic compaction. Three staging scenarios completed three automatic and three manual compactions. The reported HTTP 500 did not recur. The two external MCP cases were deferred.

24 targeted tests, changed-file ESLint, main-process type checking, the DSH upgrade gate and runtime verification passed. Windows DSH E2E passed after making the temporary Git fixture's read-only objects writable for cleanup.

prs.title: feat(migration): clean up legacy experimental DSH configs and dead IPC
prs.body:
## Summary

- Add a one-shot, non-blocking cleanup module (`src/main/migration/legacyExperimentalDshCleanup.ts`) that surgically removes obsolete `lobsterai-*` provider routes, dangling `agent-default-model` overrides, and stale writer locks from legacy experimental DSH homes (`~/.dsh` and `<userData>/dsh`), while preserving user-defined routes, `!!js` expressions, credentials, plugins, and session histories.
- Wire cleanup into DSH bootstrap / app startup (`dshBootstrap.ts`, `main.ts`), legacy OpenClaw migration (`legacyOpenClawMigrator.ts`), and cross-machine backup restore sanitization (`postRestoreSanitizer.ts`).

prs.title: fix(installer): elevate process stop on demand when access is denied
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes the Windows first-overwrite install failure where the installer aborted with:

> `The LobsterAI update stopped before replacing the previous version because the old application processes could not be confirmed stopped. Please close LobsterAI and retry.`

### Root Cause
1. Switching the Windows NSIS installer from `RequestExecutionLevel admin` to `RequestExecutionLevel user` (`asInvoker`) meant `stopLobsterAIProcesses` ran unelevated (Medium Integrity). When an existing `LobsterAI.exe` (or child process under `$INSTDIR`) was running elevated (High Integrity), `Stop-Process -Force` failed with Win32 `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` (5), was silently swallowed by `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue`, burned all 30 poll rounds (~29s), and aborted with `exit=3`.
2. In `app-builder-lib`'s `installSection.nsh`, `CHECK_APP_RUNNING` was guarded by `${ifNot} ${UAC_IsInnerInstance}`, which skipped `customCheckAppRunning` (process stop, Skills backup, fast-path rename) for per-machine (`HKLM`) upgrades that elevated via `UAC_RunElevated` before entering `Section "install"`.

### Changes
- **`scripts/nsis-installer.nsh`** (`stopLobsterAIProcesses`):
  - Deduplicate matched processes by PID in both the stop loop and survivor logger.
  - Inspect locale-independent Win32 `NativeErrorCode == 5` / `UnauthorizedAccessException` on `Stop-Process` failure.
  - When all remaining processes fail with access denied for 2 consecutive rounds, fail fast instead of burning 30 rounds:
    - In interactive unelevated installs, elevate the current PowerShell binary (`Process.GetCurrentProcess().MainModule.FileName`, avoiding 32-bit WOW64 `Sysnative` inside 64-bit PowerShell) on demand via hidden `ProcessStartInfo` (`Verb = "runas"`, `ProcessWindowStyle::Hidden`, Base64 `-EncodedCommand`). Exits `6` on elevated stop success, `1223` on UAC decline.
    - In silent (`/S`) installs, never trigger UAC and exit `5` (`status=access-denied`) with survivor diagnostics.
  - Log survivor details for `exit=3`, `exit=5`, and `exit=1223`.
- **`patches/app-builder-lib+24.13.3.patch`** (`installSection.nsh`):
  - Remove `${ifNot} ${UAC_IsInnerInstance}` around `!insertmacro CHECK_APP_RUNNING` so per-machine elevated upgrades run the full `customCheckAppRunning` lifecycle.
- **`tests/windowsInstallerContract.test.ts`**:
  - Add contract assertions for locale-independent error 5 detection, `MainModule.FileName` elevated helper launch, silent-mode zero-UI guard, survivor logging on `3/5/1223`, and inner-instance `CHECK_APP_RUNNING`.

### Electron / Packaging Impact
- Windows NSIS installer (`scripts/nsis-installer.nsh`) and `app-builder-lib` NSIS template patch (`patches/app-builder-lib+24.13.3.patch`). No IPC, SQLite, renderer, or main-process runtime changes.

### Verification
- `npm run verify:installer-patches` (57/57 tests passed)
- `npx eslint --ext ts,tsx --report-unused-disable-directives --max-warnings 0 --no-warn-ignored tests/windowsInstallerContract.test.ts` (0 warnings)
- `npx tsc` (0 errors)
- Packaged real Windows NSIS installer (`LobsterAI-Setup-x64-2026.11.16-official.exe`, `asInvoker`) and verified on Windows:
  - **Before fix (repro):** overwriting elevated `LobsterAI.exe` (12 procs) aborted at 29.2s with `exit=3` and the exact error popup.
  - **After fix — `/S` silent over elevated `LobsterAI.exe`:** no UAC prompt, failed fast in 4.7s with `status=access-denied exit=5` and 12 deduplicated survivor lines, old install untouched.
  - **After fix — interactive `--updated` over elevated `LobsterAI.exe`:** on-demand elevated stop succeeded in 7.4s (`status=success exit=6`), 0 popups, full overwrite install completed (`ExitCode=0`, `phase=install-complete`).
  - **After fix — interactive `--updated` over unelevated `LobsterAI.exe`:** zero-elevation fast stop in 2.6s (`status=success exit=0`), full overwrite install completed (`ExitCode=0`).
  - **Playwright/CDP real-machine Electron check:** connected to freshly overwrite-installed `LobsterAI.exe` over CDP, confirmed UI rendered and DSH host reached `phase=ready` (`0.2.2-rc.5`, `lastError=null`).

prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes feedback items tracked on `migrate-openclaw-to-dsh`:

1. **Model selector clipped when right sidebar / native preview is open**
   - Marks the chat pane root (`CoworkSessionDetail`) with `data-popover-boundary="true"`, right-aligns the session composer's model selector dropdown, and introduces `resolvePortalDropdownPlacement` in `ModelSelector.tsx` so the portal dropdown and its cascaded hover / thinking / context-window popovers stay strictly left of the right sidebar boundary (avoiding occlusion by native Electron `WebContentsView` panels such as Agent Browser and Word).
   - Observes the boundary element with `ResizeObserver` while open so resizing or toggling the sidebar updates placement immediately.
2. **Mid-turn auto-compaction splitting one turn into two assistant messages**
   - Keeps `ContextCompactionMode.Auto` system messages inside the active `ConversationTurn` in `buildConversationTurns` (preserving turn splitting only for manual `/compact` dividers), keeps empty-content auto-compaction markers renderable inside the expanded process, and folds auto-compaction rows into process chunks in `getTurnAnswerStartIndex` so only a single assistant reply and a single footer (with turn usage credits) render.
3. **Image editor stuck on "正在跟随修改请求" after a failed, stopped, or superseded turn**
   - Tracks `observedRunning` on active `ImageEditJob` records in `imageEditorSlice` / `ImageEditProgress`, checks `sessionStatus === 'error'`, `observedRunning && !running`, and `hasLaterUserMessage` in `imageEditJobStatus`, and surfaces `system` error message text as the failure reason so the editor exits preparing state instead of spinning indefinitely. (The original `already owned by an active write handle` root cause from 2026-11-25 logs was addressed by PR #3204.)
4. **IM permission approval timeout extended from 90s to 300s**
   - Confirmed PR #3210 only disabled `ask_user_question` in IM/scheduled sessions and left `ImApprovalRelay` active for tool/sandbox approvals. Raised `DEFAULT_IM_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_MS` in `src/main/im/imApprovalRelay.ts` from `90_000` (90s) to `300_000` (5 minutes), well within `DshImInboundHandler`'s 10-minute turn timeout.

- **Windowing / native `WebContentsView` layering**: Portal popovers in `ModelSelector` now respect the chat column's `[data-popover-boundary="true"]` right edge so menus do not extend beneath native `WebContentsView` sidebars.
- **Main process IM relay**: `DEFAULT_IM_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_MS` increased from 90s to 300s (`src/main/im/imApprovalRelay.ts`).

prs.title: feat(auth): enforce forced login gate for fresh installations
prs.body:
## Summary

Enforces a forced-login authentication gate for fresh installations while preserving guest/optional login behavior for legacy installations and enterprise deployments that hide login (`ui.login === 'hide'`).

## Key Changes

- **Durable Auth Access Policy (`src/main/libs/authAccessPolicy.ts`, `src/shared/auth/constants.ts`)**:
  - Detects legacy installations from SQLite KV keys, business tables, and userData markers before startup writes default keys, persisting `auth_access_policy` (`legacy_optional` vs `login_required`) in SQLite `kv`.
  - Backfills `legacy_optional` during backup restore sanitization (`postRestoreSanitizer.ts`) when restoring legacy data.
- **IPC & Preload (`src/main/ipcHandlers/authGate/`, `src/main/preload.ts`)**:
  - Adds `auth:getAccessState` and `auth:accessStateChanged` IPC channels and `window.electron.auth.getAccessState` / `onAccessStateChanged`.
  - Guards mutating/runtime IPC handlers (`dshHost`, `mcp`, `scheduledTask`, `skills`) with `isAuthGateBlocked`.
- **Runtime Startup, Suspension & Windowing (`src/main/libs/authGateLifecycle.ts`, `src/main/libs/dsh/dshBootstrap.ts`, `src/main/main.ts`, `src/main/desktopCompanion/`, `src/main/trayManager.ts`)**:
  - Adds `AuthGateLifecycleCoordinator` to serialize service startup/suspension across login, logout, and session expiration transitions.
  - Adds non-destructive `DshBootstrap.suspend()` with lifecycle generation guards so active sessions, scheduler polling, IM gateways, and DSH host cleanly suspend on logout/expiry and resume on re-login.
  - Defers Desktop Companion orb/shortcuts/selection hook and simplifies the tray menu while auth-gated.
- **Renderer Gate UI (`src/renderer/services/authGate.ts`, `src/renderer/App.tsx`, `src/renderer/components/login/FirstRunLoginIntroduction.tsx`, `src/renderer/components/LogoutConfirmDialog.tsx`)**:

prs.title: feat(discord): ingest inbound document attachments
prs.body:
## Summary

Discord handled voice notes (STT) and images (multimodal), but every other attachment (PDF, text, Office files, archives, video…) was dropped: the agent saw the caption, or an empty body, and never got the file.

- Attachments that are neither audio nor a still image are downloaded concurrently through the existing SSRF-checked `DiscordInboundMediaDownloader`, capped at 25 MB, saved with `ChannelEventSink::save_channel_attachment`, and passed to the agent through `ChannelMessageMeta.documents`, like Telegram and WhatsApp.
- Each document adds a `[Document: name (mime)]` label after the caption; a message can mix images and documents (the image still goes through the multimodal path).
- Oversized files are rejected from Discord's reported size, before any download.
- Too large / download failed / save failed: the sender gets a message naming the file and the reason, and the agent body says the file was not received. A message made only of unreadable documents gets the notice and is not dispatched.
- Stored filenames: `<attachment id>_<name reduced to [A-Za-z0-9._-]>`, stem capped at 160 chars, extension kept. MIME types are normalized to a bare `type/subtype` with an extension fallback. Display names drop control characters, brackets and backticks before reaching the prompt or the reply.
- The CDN download and attachment classification helpers move to `handler/attachments.rs`; ingestion lives in `handler/documents.rs` (`implementation.rs` goes from 1482 to 1350 lines).
- A voice note without speech-to-text no longer drops the documents sent with it, and `video/webm` clips are saved as documents instead of being transcribed (Greptile review).
- Docs: new "Inbound Attachments" section in `docs/src/discord.md`, capability column in `docs/src/channels.md`.

Telegram's document helpers are not copied: Discord builds `ChannelDocumentFile` inline. Text/PDF content is not inlined in the body; the agent opens the saved file with its tools. In sandboxed sessions `Read` cannot extract PDF text today, tracked in #1328.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    M[Discord message from approved sender] --> R[resolve voice / image]
    R --> D[ingest documents: non-audio, non-image]
    D -->|size > 25 MB| F[failure]
    D -->|download error| F
    D -->|save_channel_attachment None| F
    D -->|saved| S[ChannelDocumentFile]
    F --> N[reply to sender: which file, why]
    S --> B[body = caption + document labels]
    F --> B
    B --> C{only failed docs, no text?}
    C -->|yes| X[stop after notice]
    C -->|no| G[dispatch_to_chat with meta.documents]
```

## Validation

### Completed
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (all checks below re-run on 6cd9524d)
- [x] `cargo clippy -p moltis-discord --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p moltis-discord` (149 passed)
- [x] `./scripts/check-file-size.sh`
- [x] `just lint` (macOS: workspace clippy plus `moltis-providers` and `moltis-gateway` with `local-llm-metal`, `-D warnings`)
- [x] `taplo fmt --check crates/discord/Cargo.toml`
- [x] Deployed on a NixOS host and tested over Discord DM (see Manual QA), before the Greptile fixes; those are covered by unit tests only

### Remaining
- [ ] `./scripts/local-validate.sh <PR_NUMBER>`

## Manual QA

Done on a live deployment:

1. PDF with a caption in a DM: dispatched as `inferred_kind=Document` with the caption and a `[Document: rapport-test.pdf (application/pdf)]` label; the file is saved as `<attachment id>_rapport-test.pdf` in session media and the agent answered from its content.
2. PDF and `.zip` in one message: one dispatch with both labels; the agent read both files.
3. `.md` with no caption: dispatched with the document label only (previously an empty body).
4. Voice note: still transcribed and answered as before.

Still to check:

5. A file over 25 MB (Nitro account): the bot replies "I couldn't read `file`: the file exceeds the 25 MB limit." and does not call the agent.
6. An image and a document in one message: the image reaches the model as a multimodal attachment, the document is saved and labelled (covered by `image_and_document_in_one_message_are_both_handled`, not yet checked live).

prs.title: fix(signal): accept signal-cli's empty health check body
prs.body:
## Summary

signal-cli's daemon answers `GET /api/v1/check` with `200 OK` and an empty body. `SignalClient::check` decoded that body as JSON, so every call failed with `signal-cli check json: error decoding response body`. As a result:

- the Signal account never started: `failed to start channel account: channel operation failed: signal-cli check json: error decoding response body`;
- the channel health snapshot reported the daemon as unreachable even though it was up.

`check` now reads the body and only decodes it when it is not blank. An empty (or whitespace-only) body counts as healthy and returns `Value::Null`; a non-empty body is still parsed, and malformed JSON is still an error.

Seen with signal-cli in `daemon --http` mode on NixOS:

```
$ curl -si 127.0.0.1:<port>/api/v1/check
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-length: 0
```

## Validation

### Completed

- [x] `just release-preflight` (macOS: workspace clippy `-D warnings`, `moltis-providers` and `moltis-gateway` with `local-llm-metal`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`)
- [x] `cargo test -p moltis-signal` (16 passed, including 3 new unit tests for `parse_check_body`: empty/whitespace body, JSON body, malformed body)
- [x] `bash scripts/check-changelog-guard.sh upstream/main HEAD`
- [x] `bash scripts/check-file-size.sh`
- [x] Live check against a real daemon (`signal-cli 0.14.9 daemon --http`, no account needed for `/api/v1/check`), through `SignalClient::check` from a throwaway integration test:
  - before (upstream `main`): `Err(External { context: "signal-cli check json", source: reqwest::Error { kind: Decode, source: Error("EOF while parsing a value", line: 1, column: 0) } })`
  - after: `Ok(Null)`

### Remaining

- None.

## Manual QA

1. Run `signal-cli -a <number> daemon --http 127.0.0.1:<port>` and check that `curl -si 127.0.0.1:<port>/api/v1/check` returns `200` with an empty body.
2. Configure a `[channels.signal.<id>]` account with `http_url` pointing at it and start Moltis.
3. Before: the account fails to start with `signal-cli check json: error decoding response body`. After: the account starts and the channel health shows "signal-cli daemon reachable".

issues.title: Repeated identical tool calls are never interrupted: the doom-loop gate records at most one call per reply
issues.body:
## What happens

With `QWENPAW_SHELL_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB=128`, a 400 MB probe process is terminated
correctly and the tool result reads:

```
exit code 15. [resource protection] Shell memory limit exceeded (RSS 134881280 bytes > 134217728 bytes)
```

The same `Bash` invocation was then approved **14 times** between `09:09:10`
and `09:10:22` — one every 6–7 seconds — and the user had to press stop twice.
Nothing in the agent loop noticed that the same call was repeating.

## Correction to the earlier report

The first version of this issue claimed the model never received the result and
therefore retried. That is wrong, and I am correcting it here rather than
leaving a misleading cause in place.

The result did reach the model. The stored turn at `09:11:01` ends with the tool
result carrying the full text shown above plus `state=error`. Draining the same
tool response directly returns it as a normal tool response as well.

So the retries were not caused by a missing result. They were caused by nothing
stopping them.

## Why nothing stopped them

`loop/gates/doom_loop.py` is enabled in the default mode — `window_size=3`,
`similarity_threshold=0.5`, `stop` after 4 hits — but the gate has never fired.
`_auto_record_from_ctx` de-duplicates on the **message** id:

```python
last_msg = context[-1]
if last_msg.id == state.last_recorded_msg_id:
    return
```

Inside a single reply, every assistant message is written with the same
`state.reply_id`: `agentscope` creates one `ReplyContext(reply_id=…)` per reply,
and `AgentState.append_context` either extends the existing message or appends a
new one **with that same id**. From the second iteration onwards `last_msg.id`
already equals `state.last_recorded_msg_id`, the function returns before
recording anything, and the history never grows past **one** entry.

| iteration within one reply | message id | recorded calls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `reply_id` | 1 |
| 2 | `reply_id` | 1 |
| 3 … 14 | `reply_id` | 1 |

A three-entry window can never fill, so `_detect_repetition` cannot return true
and no stage is ever reached.

Reproduced against the real `DoomLoopGate` with two synthetic contexts:

| context shape | history after 8 iterations | fired |
| --- | --- | --- |
| same message id every iteration (actual behaviour) | stays at 1 | never |
| distinct message id per iteration (hypothetical) | reaches 3 on iteration 3 | on iteration 4 |

Production logs agree: `qwenpaw.log` since 11-13 contains no `DoomLoopGate` and
no `Doom loop` line at all.

## Scope

This is not specific to resource-protection terminations. **Any** tool invoked
repeatedly with identical arguments inside a single reply is invisible to the
gate. The shell case only made it visible because each attempt was expensive
and the user was watching.

## Expected

Repeating the same tool call with the same arguments past the configured window
should reach the configured stage, instead of running until the user stops it.

## Proposed direction

Record per tool-call block rather than per message: make the de-duplication key
something that differs between two calls inside the same reply — the tool-call
block id, or `(reply_id, block_id)` — and scan the blocks appended since the
last observation instead of only `context[-1]`.

I am explicitly **not** proposing a change to `_with_shell_guard`. Overriding the
result state with `ERROR` is a separate question, it is not the cause of the
repetition, and changing it would not make the gate work.

## Second observation — explained, not a defect

While reproducing, a bare script that set `QWENPAW_SHELL_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB=96`
before importing `qwenpaw` still ended up with `ShellGuard.from_environment`
returning `None`, and a 300 MB process ran to completion.

The cause is `load_bootstrap_envs()`: at import time it replays
`$QWENPAW_HOME.secret/envs.json` over `os.environ` with `overwrite=True`, and
that file contained `"0"` for this key, so the value set by the script was
replaced (96 → 0). Setting the variable **after** the import creates the guard
as expected (96 MB, kills a 300 MB process).

That is documented behaviour — "persisted values override existing
process/system values" — and the Console path writes through the same store, so
a limit configured there is applied correctly. I am recording it only so the
reproduction in this issue can be run; it is not a defect.

issues.title: test: 12 plugin-install tests fail on Windows (symlink privilege, slow package init vs 5s budgets, venv launcher pids)
issues.body:
## Summary

12 tests under `tests/unit/plugins` fail on a plain Windows checkout (Windows 10 build 19045, Python 3.11.6 venv, the documented `pip install -e ".[dev,test,full]"`). All twelve stem from three environment assumptions that hold on the Linux CI but not on Windows. No product code is implicated — in every case the tests make an assumption about the environment or about process identity that Windows breaks.

### 1. Symlink creation privilege — 5 tests

`OSError: [WinError 1314] 客户端没有所需的特权` — creating symlinks on Windows needs admin or Developer Mode. The tests create symlinks themselves while arranging fixtures:

- `test_provision_create.py::test_api_preserves_absolute_symlink_location` (2 params), `::test_publish_does_not_replace_a_target_created_after_the_check[dangling-link]`
- `test_install_lock.py::TestEnvironmentIdentity::test_site_aliases_share_one_cross_process_lock[reader-symlink]` and `[writer-symlink]`

Fix: probe symlink creation and `pytest.skip` when unavailable, mirroring the file's existing `pytest.skip("requires a case-insensitive filesystem")` precedent.

### 2. A 5 s readline budget vs ~11.5 s of package-import work — 3 tests

`test_install_lock.py::test_reader_admission_waits_for_publication` spawns `python -I -c "<script>"` whose script does `from qwenpaw.plugins import dependency_maintenance as m`. Importing the package runs the environment custody in `qwenpaw/__init__.py`, which measured **11.25–11.80 s per fresh interpreter on this machine** (both `-I` and plain). The parent reads the child's first line with `asyncio.wait_for(peer.stdout.readline(), 5)` — five seconds — so the test can never pass here, regardless of the lock behavior it wants to verify.

Fix: load the stdlib-only `dependency_maintenance` module directly by path (`importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`), exactly like the sibling child-custody test in the same file already does. The child then starts in well under a second, and the budgets (now `WAIT_TIMEOUT` from `tests/unit/plugins/timing.py`, "bounds hangs, not performance") only ever see a hang.

### 3. venv launcher pid ≠ interpreter pid — 4 tests

After fixing 1 and 2, the remaining failures are pid assertions comparing `peer.pid` with pids recorded by the child. On a Windows venv, `python.exe` is a launcher that starts the real interpreter as its own child:

```
peer.pid      = 30340
child getpid  = 3336   (same spawn, measured)
```

Reproduced 4/4 combinations (Popen and asyncio, parent with and without `import qwenpaw`) — `peer.pid` never equals the child's `os.getpid()` on this venv. Lease filenames record the interpreter's `os.getpid()`, so `live_readers()` can never return `peer.pid` here. Affected: `test_reader_admission_waits_for_publication[success]` and `test_observation_child_custody_is_temporary` (4 params). The product is unaffected: lease liveness is decided by OS file locks, and in-process pid comparisons stay consistent.

Fix: on `_WINDOWS`, assert the lease count (the meaningful part: exactly the child holds it) and keep the exact pid equality on POSIX.

## Evidence

- WinError 1314 tracebacks for all five symlink tests (captured in per-file runs).
- Import timing: `python -I -c "import qwenpaw"` → 11.80 / 11.28 / 11.25 s across three runs; plain (no `-I`) → 11.43 / 12.07 / 11.51 s.
- pid matrix: both spawners × both parent contexts → 4/4 mismatch.
- After the fixes (commit in the linked PR): `pytest tests/unit/plugins/test_install_lock.py tests/unit/plugins/test_provision_create.py -q` → `33 passed, 20 skipped`, reproduced across three consecutive runs.

AI assistance disclosure: this investigation and report were prepared with the assistance of an AI coding tool; all commands above were executed locally on the reporter's machine.

issues.title: [Feature]: Console 缺少「查看被压缩归档的历史轮次」入口，压缩后早期对话在 UI 上不可达

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
## Summary

会话经历过上下文压缩后，Console 上只能看到「压缩摘要占位消息 + 压缩点之后的轮次」。被逐出活动窗口、写入归档的早期原始轮次，在界面上没有任何入口可以查看，用户会直接理解为「历史对话丢了」。

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Problem / Motivation

1. 会话触发上下文压缩后，被逐出的轮次会从 `agent.state.context` 中移除，替换为一条标注 `[context compressed]` 的索引消息；原始消息写入归档表 `conversation_history`。
2. `GET /api/chats/{chat_id}` 的返回值来自 `agent.state.context`（即当前活动窗口），不会读取归档表。因此前端拿到的历史 = 活动窗口 + 压缩索引。
3. 结论：压缩前的原始对话在 UI 上不可达。数据完整保存在归档里，但缺少只读读取路径；Agent 侧有 recall 类工具可检索归档，Console 侧没有对等能力。
4. 用户侧表现是「昨天的对话后半段看不到了」，且没有任何提示说明这些内容仍可找回，容易被误判为数据丢失。

## Expected Behavior

- 打开会话时，除活动窗口外，允许继续向前加载归档轮次（分页，按需触发）。
- 或在压缩索引消息上提供「查看被压缩的历史」入口，点击后拉取对应区间。
- 默认行为保持不变，对现有客户端向后兼容。

## Suggested Approach

- 后端：在 `GET /api/chats/{chat_id}` 上增加可选参数（例如 `include_archived=true`、`before=<cursor>`、`limit=<n>`），命中时从归档表按序分页读取，返回结构与活动窗口一致，并给出 `has_more`/`total`。或另开一个只读端点，避免污染现有返回体。
- 前端：消息列表顶部提供「加载更早消息」；压缩索引消息渲染为可展开卡片。
- 隔离：归档读取沿用现有会话归属/权限校验，不提供跨会话读取。
- 不改写、不回填：归档只读，不因查看而修改会话状态或再次进入上下文。

## Related

- **#3915** [Feature]: Introduce virtual scrolling for Console WebUI — 同属 Console 长会话体验，但该 issue 解决的是渲染性能（虚拟滚动/分页渲染），不涉及归档轮次可见性。
- **#3923** [Bug] Chat API returns all messages without pagination + no virtual scrolling — 同样聚焦分页与内存占用。
- **#7049** feat(chats): add limit/before pagination to GET /chats/{chat_id} — 曾提交的分页 PR（已关闭未合并）。本 issue 的分页诉求与之部分重合，但核心差异在于：分页解决的是「一次拉太多」，本 issue 解决的是「压缩后根本取不到」。若 #7049 的方向被采纳，本 issue 可收敛为在其上追加 `include_archived`。

## Environment

- QwenPaw: 2.3.0
- OS: Linux
- Channel: Console (WebUI)

issues.title: Console: markdown tables overflow the message bubble with no horizontal scroll
issues.body:
## Summary Markdown tables inside assistant messages are wider than the message bubble, are painted past the edge of the message list, and cannot be scrolled horizontally. The overflowing columns are effectively invisible, although the text can be selected. ## Environment - QwenPaw 2.3.0.post1, QwenPaw Desktop (Tauri webview) - Windows 10 Home 22H2 (build 19045), WebView2 / Chromium 126 - Viewport 1366 x 705 ## Steps to reproduce 1. Ask the agent for a response containing a markdown table with a few wide columns (a two-column table with a long first column is enough). 2. Look at the table in the rendered message. ## Expected The table either fits the bubble, or is horizontally scrollable inside it. ## Actual The table extends beyond the bubble and beyond the right edge of the message list. There is no horizontal scrollbar, and the columns that fall outside are not readable (but remain selectable/copyable). ## Measurements From the live DOM for one such table: | Element | Value | | --- | --- | | `` width | 1007 px | | `.qwenpaw-bubble-content-wrapper` width | 898 px (overflow 109 px) | | list right edge | 1299 px | | table right edge | **1377 px** | | list `clientWidth` / `scrollWidth` | 930 / 930 (no horizontal scroll available) | Ancestor chain of the table: ``` table .x-markdown.qwenpaw-markdown overflow-x: visible .HostBubbles-module__quoteResponse__ overflow-x: visible .qwenpaw-bubble-content-wrapper overflow-x: visible, 898 px wide .qwenpaw-bubble.qwenpaw-bubble-start overflow-x: visible .qwenpaw-bubble-list-scroll overflow-x: auto, scrollWidth == clientWidth .qwenpaw-bubble-list-wrapper overflow-x: hidden ``` ## Root cause The Console stylesheet applies the overflow rule directly to the table: ```css [class*=bubble-assistant] .x-markdown table { max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto; } ``` `overflow-x: auto` has no effect on a `
` element, because a table box is not a scroll container. The same rule works on `
`, which is why code blocks scroll correctly and tables do not.

## Suggested fix

Wrap rendered tables in a block-level scroll container, for example in the markdown component:

```jsx
…
``` ```css .qwenpaw-table-scroll { max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto; } ``` The same treatment is worth applying to wide standalone images and to `
` wrappers for consistency.

issues.title: [Bug]: [Console] Single `~` parsed as a strikethrough delimiter: numeric ranges (e.g. `600~1500 t/s`) get struck through and the `~` characters are swallowed

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### 问题描述 / Problem Description [中文] QwenPaw Web 控制台的**聊天消息**渲染会把单个波浪号 `~` 当作删除线定界符：正文中任意两个 `~` 之间的内容被渲染为 `` 删除线，且 `~` 字符本身从显示中消失。 Agent 回复中很常用 `~` 表示数字区间（且 `~` 紧贴数字，如 `64~128G`、`600~1500 t/s`）。一条回复里只要出现 2 个以上这样的区间，就会两两配对，导致区间之间横跨大段正文被划掉、`~` 全部丢失（如显示为 "6001500"、"170220"）。 经核对，后端持久化的消息原文完整（`~` 与 `**` 标记均在），**纯前端渲染问题**。 **已定位的根因（headless 浏览器 + 真实 DOM 验证）：** 聊天消息走的是内嵌 **marked** 解析器（bundle：`console/assets/index-BBME4Plt.js`，渲染容器 class 为 `x-markdown qwenpaw-markdown`）。marked 的 GFM `del` 规则为： ```js del: /^(~~?)(?=[^\s~])((?:\\.|[^\\])*?(?:\\.|[^\s~\\]))\1(?=[^~]|$)/ ``` 其中 `(~~?)` 允许**单个** `~` 作为删除线定界符，而 GFM 规范的 strikethrough 要求 `~~…~~`（双波浪）。实测 DOM 中每个单波浪配对区间都对应一个 `` 元素。 另发现同一 marked `del` 规则的变体副本存在于 `console/assets/editor-vendor-*.js`： `del:/^(~~?)(?=[^\s~])([\s\S]*?[^\s~])\1(?=[^~]|$)/`（代码编辑/预览管线），同样支持单波浪，需一并修复。 注意：console 里另有 `markdown-vendor-*.js`（micromark/remark 管线，用于文档/预览类组件），其 `micromark-extension-gfm-strikethrough` 的 `singleTilde` 默认值同样为 `true`，但**聊天消息不走该管线**——修复时请勿改错管线。 [English] The QwenPaw Web Console's **chat message** rendering treats a single tilde `~` as a strikethrough delimiter: the content between any two `~` characters is rendered as a `` strikethrough, and both `~` characters disappear from the rendered output. Agent replies frequently use `~` for numeric ranges (usually adjacent to digits, e.g. `64~128G`, `600~1500 t/s`). As soon as a reply contains two or more such ranges, they pair up and everything spanning between them is struck through, dropping all `~` characters (e.g. "6001500", "170220"). The persisted message content is intact (verified in storage: `~` and `**` markers are all present), so this is purely a frontend rendering issue. **Root cause (verified with a headless browser + real DOM):** Chat messages are rendered by an embedded **marked** parser (bundle: `console/assets/index-BBME4Plt.js`; rendered container has classes `x-markdown qwenpaw-markdown`). marked's GFM `del` rule is: ```js del: /^(~~?)(?=[^\s~])((?:\\.|[^\\])*?(?:\\.|[^\s~\\]))\1(?=[^~]|$)/ ``` where `(~~?)` allows a **single** `~` to open a strikethrough, while the GFM spec requires `~~…~~` (double tilde). In the real DOM, every single-tilde pair range corresponds to a `` element. A variant of the same `del` rule also exists in `console/assets/editor-vendor-*.js`: `del:/^(~~?)(?=[^\s~])([\s\S]*?[^\s~])\1(?=[^~]|$)/` (code editor/preview pipeline) — it also accepts a single tilde and should be fixed together. Note: the console also ships `markdown-vendor-*.js` (micromark/remark pipeline, used by doc/preview components) whose `micromark-extension-gfm-strikethrough` `singleTilde` option also defaults to `true`, but **chat messages do not use that pipeline** — do not fix the wrong pipeline. --- ### 实际渲染 DOM 证据 / Actual Rendered DOM (evidence) [中文] 触发文本（Agent 回复原文节选）： `参考机配置 64~128G 内存…关键区间如下：**上下文 ~128K（262K 理论可行但吃紧）、prefill 600~1500 t/s（llama.cpp）/ ~5K t/s（Strata）、decode 30~50 t/s（llama.cpp）/ 170~220 t/s（Strata，MTP 再 +30~70%）**` 实际渲染 HTML： ```html

渲染自测 A（2026-11-27 新消息）：参考机配置 64128G 内存、单卡 3248G 显存。 关键区间如下：上下文 128K（262K 理论可行但吃紧）、prefill 6001500 t/s（llama.cpp）/ 5K t/s（Strata）、decode 3050 t/s（llama.cpp）/ 170220 t/s（Strata，MTP 再 +3070%）。…

``` [English] Trigger text (excerpt of the agent reply as stored): `参考机配置 64~128G 内存…关键区间如下：**上下文 ~128K（262K 理论可行但吃紧）、prefill 600~1500 t/s（llama.cpp）/ ~5K t/s（Strata）、decode 30~50 t/s（llama.cpp）/ 170~220 t/s（Strata，MTP 再 +30~70%）**` Actually rendered HTML: ```html

渲染自测 A（2026-11-27 new message）: 参考机配置 64128G 内存、单卡 3248G 显存。 关键区间如下：上下文 128K（262K 理论可行但吃紧）、prefill 6001500 t/s (llama.cpp) / 5K t/s (Strata)、decode 3050 t/s (llama.cpp) / 170220 t/s (Strata, MTP 再 +3070%. …

``` --- ### 具体痛点 / Pain Points - [中文] Agent 回复常用 `~` 写数字区间，一条消息 2~4 个区间非常常见，触发频率高 [English] Agent replies (especially in Chinese) commonly use `~` for numeric ranges; 2–4 ranges per message is routine - [中文] 划掉的文字与丢失的 `~` 直接造成数据误读（"6001500"、"170220"），用户必须查原文才能确认真实数值 [English] The struck-through text and missing `~` make the data misreadable ("6001500", "170220"); users must inspect the raw content to recover the real values - [中文] 后端原文完好、仅显示损坏，问题不可见，用户难以自行定位到前端渲染层 [English] The stored content is fine and only the display is corrupted, so the issue is invisible and hard to attribute to the rendering layer --- ### 期望效果 / Desired Behavior [中文] - 单个 `~` 渲染为字面波浪号，不作为删除线定界符（尤其紧贴数字/单位时） - 删除线仅在 `~~…~~`（双波浪）时生效，与 GFM 规范一致 - 修复建议（二选一；方案 1 已在本地对两份副本实测验证）： 1. 将两份 marked 副本的 `del` 规则中 `(~~?)` 均收紧为 `(~~)`（聊天渲染 `index-BBME4Plt.js` + 编辑/预览 `editor-vendor-*.js`）；或在 marked 配置层禁用/替换该 tokenizer 2. 若长期方案是换渲染器，则保证新管线 strikethrough 仅识别 `~~` - 回归验证： 1. 回复文本 `range A 600~1500 t/s, range B 170~220 t/s, RAM 64~128G` 应原样显示，无 ``、无字符丢失 2. `~~strikethrough~~` 仍应正常渲染为删除线 [English] - A single `~` should render as a literal tilde, never as a strikethrough delimiter (especially adjacent to digits/units) - Strikethrough should only apply for `~~…~~` (double tilde), matching the GFM spec - Suggested fix (either; option 1 locally tested on both copies): 1. Tighten `(~~?)` to `(~~)` in the `del` rule of both marked copies (chat rendering `index-BBME4Plt.js` + editor/preview `editor-vendor-*.js`); or disable/replace that tokenizer at the marked config level 2. If the long-term plan is to swap the renderer, ensure the new pipeline only recognizes `~~` - Regression checks: 1. A reply reading `range A 600~1500 t/s, range B 170~220 t/s, RAM 64~128G` must display verbatim — no ``, no missing characters 2. `~~strikethrough~~` must still render as strikethrough --- ### 复现步骤 / Reproduction [中文] 1. 在任意会话中让 agent 回复一段包含至少两个 `~` 数字区间的文字（例如："性能上限大致是：prefill 600~1500 t/s，decode 170~220 t/s，参考配置 64~128G 内存"） 2. 查看控制台消息气泡：区间之间的文字被 `` 划掉，`~` 字符消失（如 "6001500"、"170220"） [English] 1. In any session, have the agent reply with text containing at least two `~` numeric ranges (e.g. "the ceiling is roughly: prefill 600~1500 t/s, decode 170~220 t/s, reference config 64~128G RAM") 2. In the console message bubble, the text between the ranges is struck through with `` and the `~` characters vanish (e.g. "6001500", "170220") --- ### 环境 / Environment - QwenPaw 版本 / Version: 2.3.0.post1 - 界面 / UI: Web Console (chat message rendering) - 浏览器 / Browser: headless Chromium 159 已验证 / verified with headless Chromium 159 - 操作系统 / OS: Ubuntu 24.04

issues.title: [Bug] Windows: orphaned llama-server.exe processes accumulate across backend restarts, exhausting memory and preventing local model startup
issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows, `llama-server.exe` launched by QwenPaw for a local model is **not terminated when the backend exits abnormally** (crash / forced kill / restart). Every subsequent backend start spawns *another* `llama-server.exe` on a fresh random port instead of adopting the one that is already running. After a few restarts the machine runs out of RAM commit, the next server dies silently during `load_model`, and the user only sees:

```
{"detail":"llama.cpp server exited before becoming ready"}
```

## Environment

- QwenPaw **2.3.0.post1**, `pip` install in venv, started with `qwenpaw app`
- Windows 10 (AMD64)
- Local model: `AgentScope/Piccolo-4B-Q8_0` (4.48 GB GGUF)
- Server argv: `llama-server.exe --host 127.0.0.1 --port <random> --model ...gguf --alias AgentScope/Piccolo-4B-Q8_0 --log-file ... --gpu-layers auto --ctx-size 8192 --batch-size 8192 --ubatch-size 8192 --parallel 1 --no-cache-prompt --cache-ram 0 --no-context-shift`
- Machine: 32 GB RAM (commit limit 48.88 GB)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Enable a local model so `llama-server.exe` is running and healthy.
2. Restart / hard-kill the QwenPaw backend (the `atexit` path does not run).
3. `Get-Process llama-server` shows the old process still alive and still `LISTENING` on its old port; the new backend start adds one more process.
4. Repeat a few times: each process holds ~5.18 GB working set.

## Observed

Four successful starts, none reclaimed:

| start time | port | pid |
|---|---|---|
| 08:42:29 | 50442 | 11148 |
| 08:50:12 | 50669 | 13756 |
| 08:52:44 | 50694 | 2412 |
| 08:54:32 | 50711 | 4408 |

Then every subsequent start fails (each on a new port: 50765, 52777, 52782, 52798):

```
INFO | local_models\llamacpp.py:833 | llama.cpp health check returned 503 while waiting for http://127.0.0.1:50765/health
INFO | local_models\llamacpp.py:840 | llama.cpp health check failed for http://127.0.0.1:50765/health:
WARNING | providers\provider_manager.py:1244 | Failed to restore local model server for AgentScope/Piccolo-4B-Q8_0: llama.cpp server exited before becoming ready
```

`local_models/logs/llama-server.log` (446 bytes, overwritten per attempt) ends with **no error at all**:

```
0.00.049.730 I srv    load_model: loading model 'C:\...\Piccolo-4B-Q8_0.gguf'
```

i.e. the child is killed while loading, and the exit reason is lost. Commit charge at that moment: 48.88 GB limit, 6.81 GB free, ~20.7 GB held by the four orphaned servers.

Killing the four orphans (`taskkill /IM llama-server.exe /F`) makes the local model start again immediately — confirming resource exhaustion, not a corrupt model.

## Expected

- When the backend exits (including crash / forced kill), its `llama-server` child should be terminated too.
- At startup, restore should **adopt** an already-running server for the same model instead of spawning a new one.
- When the health check sees a dead child, the error should carry the exit code and the tail of `llama-server.log` instead of a bare "exited before becoming ready".

## Code pointers

- `qwenpaw/local_models/llamacpp.py:266-282` — reuse check is purely in-instance (`self._server_process` / `self._server_port`); no pid/port file, no scan for an existing `llama-server`.
- `qwenpaw/local_models/llamacpp.py:783` `_resolve_server_port()` → `_find_free_port()` — always allocates a **new** port, so old servers are never reused and never conflict. (With a fixed port it would at least fail loudly: `Requested llama.cpp port is unavailable`, `:797`.)
- `qwenpaw/local_models/llamacpp.py:826` — `raise RuntimeError("llama.cpp server exited before becoming ready")` when `returncode is not None`.
- `qwenpaw/local_models/llamacpp.py:301-303` — `start_new_session=True` is applied **only on non-Windows**; on Windows there is no Job Object, so children survive the parent.
- `qwenpaw/local_models/llamacpp.py:85, :890` — cleanup relies on `atexit` + `shutdown_server_sync`, which never runs on a hard kill.
- `qwenpaw/providers/provider_manager.py:1234-1250` — `_resume_local_model()` calls `setup_server(model_id)` unconditionally; on failure it only logs a warning and clears `qwenpaw-local` (`base_url: ""`, `extra_models: []`).

## Suggested fixes

1. On Windows, put `llama-server` in a Job Object with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` so it cannot outlive the backend.
2. Persist runtime state (`local_models/run/llama-server.json`: pid, port, model alias, start time) and, at startup, adopt the running instance if it matches and is healthy; otherwise kill it before spawning a new one.
3. As a cheap pre-flight, stop any `llama-server.exe` whose `--model` matches the one about to be loaded.
4. Improve the error: on `returncode is not None`, include the exit code and the last ~20 lines of the child's log.

## Workaround

```powershell
taskkill /IM llama-server.exe /F
```

then re-enable the local model in the UI.

issues.title: [Bug]: Local model list suggests an unavailable download command
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

`main` at `2b4e13e3`

## Description

After local model management was extracted into a plugin, the legacy `download`, `local`, and `remove-local` CLI commands are no longer registered. However, `qwenpaw models list` still tells users with no downloaded local models to run `qwenpaw models download`.

**Related PR(s):** #8499

**Security considerations:** None. This is a CLI guidance issue.

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [x] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** `2b4e13e3`
- **OS:** macOS
- **Install method:** from source
- **Python version (if applicable):** 3.12

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure or load a local provider that has no downloaded models.
2. Run `qwenpaw models list`.
3. Follow the displayed suggestion and run `qwenpaw models download <repo_id>`.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** The list command suggests `qwenpaw models download`, but invoking it exits with `Error: No such command 'download'.`

Usage: qwenpaw models [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
