issues.title: [Bug]: Feishu table cards treat lines inside code blocks as tables and headings
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

`main` at 879d07d (`qwenpaw 2.3.1b2`).

## Description

When a Feishu reply contains a line that starts with `|`, the channel sends it as an interactive card built by `build_interactive_content_chunks()`. That builder does not know about fenced code blocks:

1. `|` lines inside a code block are treated as table rows. A table example in a code block becomes a native table element. A shell pipeline (`cat app.log` / `  | grep ERROR`) splits the code block into several card elements. Each element then shows a broken fence.
2. `_convert_md_headings_to_bold()` also rewrites lines inside code blocks. A shell or Python comment such as `# count errors` turns into `**count errors**` inside the code.
3. The check in `_send_text()` uses the same pattern. A reply whose only `|` lines are inside code goes to the card path instead of the normal `post` message.

Root cause: in `plugins/channel/feishu/qwenpaw_channel_feishu/utils.py`, `_convert_md_headings_to_bold()` (line 387) and `_build_elements()` (lines 395-440) match `^\s*\|` and `^#{1,6}\s+` on every line, including lines inside code. In `plugins/channel/feishu/qwenpaw_channel_feishu/platform.py`, `_send_text()` (lines 1207-1211) uses the same table check.

**Related PR(s):** #8946

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** `main` at 879d07d
- **OS:** Windows 11
- **Install method:** from source
- **Python version:** 3.12

## Steps to Reproduce

Run from the repository root:

```python
import json
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "plugins/channel/feishu")
from qwenpaw_channel_feishu.utils import build_interactive_content

FENCE = "`" * 3
table_example = "\n".join([
    "Example table markdown:", "",
    FENCE + "markdown", "| Name | Age |", "| --- | --- |", "| Bob | 3 |", FENCE,
    "", "That's it.",
])
shell = "\n".join([
    "Run:", FENCE + "bash", "# count errors", "cat app.log",
    "  | grep ERROR", "  | wc -l", FENCE,
])
for text in (table_example, shell):
    for el in json.loads(build_interactive_content(text))["elements"]:
        print(el["tag"], json.dumps(el.get("content", el.get("rows"))))
    print()
```

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** 3 elements for each input. The code blocks are split, and the comment is now bold.

````
markdown "Example table markdown:\n\n```markdown"
table [{"col0": "Bob", "col1": "3"}]
markdown "```\n\nThat's it."

markdown "Run:\n```bash\n**count errors**\ncat app.log"
markdown "  | grep ERROR\n  | wc -l"
markdown "```"
````

- **Expected:** each code block stays whole and unchanged in one markdown element. A reply whose only `|` lines are inside code goes out as a `post` message, like other text.

````
markdown "Example table markdown:\n\n```markdown\n| Name | Age |\n| --- | --- |\n| Bob | 3 |\n```\n\nThat's it."

markdown "Run:\n```bash\n# count errors\ncat app.log\n  | grep ERROR\n  | wc -l\n```"
````

## Additional Notes

Fix idea: mark fence lines and the lines between them. A fence is a run of 3 or more backticks or tildes, and it closes with the same character and at least the same length. Skip table detection and heading conversion on those lines, and use the same check in `_send_text()`.

issues.title: [Design] Reference-counted archival for long-term memory: stale entries as status changes, not deletions

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
### Context

The README promises "Never forgets", and #7571 (8 comments) reports the user-facing symptom: the agent "keeps forgetting" what matters while stale entries pile up. Both symptoms share a root: distilled long-term memory entries have no TTL, no reference tracking, and no decay. The only cleanup paths are session-file expiry by mtime (`as_agent_wrapper.py:237`) and proactive topic expiry (`steps/evolve/proactive/utils.py:242-254`) — neither touches distilled long-term memory.

### Consequence

Memory only grows: stale facts and conflicting entries accumulate, and retrieval quality degrades over time — "forgets what matters, remembers everything else".

### Proposal (direction, not spec)

1. **Reference tracking**: refresh a last-referenced timestamp when an entry is retrieved and actually used in a response.
2. **Archival, not deletion**: entries unreferenced for N days (e.g., 90) transition to an `archived` status — a status change, not a delete; a later session can re-promote an archived entry with a fresh reference.
3. **Placement TBD**: reme is an external dependency (reme-ai 0.4.2.0), so the fix may belong in the QwenPaw wrapper layer or upstream in the reme repo — happy to follow the maintainers' view on where this fits best.

This mirrors a pattern discussed in the DeepSeek Harness community (cross-session memory with reference-counted archival) and would complement the existing proactive expiry rather than replace it.

issues.title: [Feature]: WebRouter as a web_search provider
issues.body:
Hi, I'm Yogev, one of the maintainers of [WebRouter](https://github.com/Nimbleway/webrouter), an open-source (Apache 2.0) Python library that puts one interface in front of many search APIs.

## Summary

Add WebRouter as a fourth `web_search` provider next to Tavily, AnySearch and Firecrawl. It works with no API key, and when one search backend fails it falls back to the next. I'd build and maintain it.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [x] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [x] Scripts / Deploy

## Problem / Motivation

Each built-in provider is a single service, so when its free quota runs out or it is down, `web_search` fails until the user switches provider by hand. WebRouter tries the keyless search backends in turn and returns the first good answer, so a user with no key still gets results when one of them is out of quota.

## Proposed Solution

Follow the layout of the Firecrawl provider:

- `WebRouterProvider` in `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/websearch/webrouter.py`, mapped to the same `title` / `url` / `snippet` / `content` shape. It uses each result's short snippet (at most 500 characters), not the page body.
- The `webrouter` option in the factory, the router `options` list and the Console modal.
- WebRouter takes no key from the Console, so the API key field is disabled for it and a short hint (in all seven Console languages) explains why.
- Docs in `mcp.en.md` and `mcp.zh.md`, and unit tests.

This needs one new dependency, `webrouter>=0.16,<1` (pure Python; it brings `pydantic`, `httpx`, `nimble-python` and `tavily-python`). It is imported only when a search runs, so QwenPaw's startup does not change. The desktop PyInstaller spec gets `collect_submodules("web_router")` and `collect_data_files("web_router")`, because WebRouter loads backends by name and reads its routing tables from package data. AnySearch stays the default.

One behaviour to know about: WebRouter also reads provider keys from the process environment. If QwenPaw's environment holds one (for example `TAVILY_API_KEY` for the Tavily MCP client), WebRouter adds that provider to its routing and the searches it serves are billed to that key. The docs and the Console hint say so.

## Alternatives Considered

- An optional extra (`qwenpaw[webrouter]`) instead of a core dependency. Desktop and Docker users can't add extras, so the Console option would fail for them. Happy to switch if you prefer it.
- A WebRouter MCP server (WebRouter ships one). The built-in provider needs no MCP setup and no key.

## Additional Context

I have the change built and tested on a branch and can open the PR once you're fine with the direction, including the new dependency. @rayrayraykk @cuiyuebing

## Willing to Contribute

- [x] I am willing to open a PR for this feature (after discussion).

issues.title: [Bug]: ToolCallBudgetGate counts earlier tool calls again on every iteration
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

`main` at 879d07d (`qwenpaw 2.3.1b2`), agentscope 2.0.10.

## Description

`ToolCallBudgetGate` (the "Tool-call budget" gate for custom loop modes) counts a tool call again on every later iteration of the same reply. A budget of N calls stops the turn after about √(2N) calls.

Root cause: `src/qwenpaw/loop/gates/limits.py`, `ToolCallBudgetGate.check()` and `_latest_tool_names()` (lines 185-234). On each new iteration, the gate adds every tool call in the latest message that has calls. agentscope 2.0 `AgentState.append_context()` appends each iteration's blocks to the same assistant message (its id is `reply_id`). So iteration k adds calls 1..k again. The text-only final step also adds the earlier calls again, because that message is still the latest one with calls.

This is the same root cause that #8700 / #8701 fixed for `DoomLoopGate`.

**Related PR(s):** #8944

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** `main` at 879d07d
- **OS:** Windows 11
- **Install method:** from source
- **Python version:** 3.12

## Steps to Reproduce

The script builds the context the way `append_context()` does: one assistant message, with one tool call added per iteration.

```python
import asyncio
from types import SimpleNamespace
from qwenpaw.loop.gates.limits import ToolCallBudgetGate


async def main():
    gate = ToolCallBudgetGate(max_calls=5)
    gate.reset_turn()
    message = SimpleNamespace(id="reply-1", role="assistant", content=[])
    agent = SimpleNamespace(state=SimpleNamespace(context=[message]))
    for i in range(1, 5):
        message.content.append(
            {"type": "tool_call", "id": f"call-{i}", "name": "search", "input": "{}"},
        )
        result = await gate.check({"iteration": i, "agent": agent})
        print(f"calls made={i} counted={gate._state().total} action={result.action.value}")


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:**

```
calls made=1 counted=1 action=bypass
calls made=2 counted=3 action=bypass
calls made=3 counted=6 action=terminate
calls made=4 counted=10 action=terminate
```

  A mode with `max_calls=5` stops after 3 calls. With `per_tool={"search": 2}`, one `search` call followed by a text answer also reports "Tool 'search' call budget reached".
- **Expected:** `counted` equals the number of calls made. The gate stops only when the budget is really used.

## Additional Notes

Fix idea: count each tool call id once per turn, as `DoomLoopGate` now does. Keep the ids in the gate's per-turn state, so `reset_turn()` clears them.

issues.title: [Bug] Runtime blocks image input (explicitly not multimodal) while catalog/prober says supports_multimodal=true (mimo-v2.6-flash, glm-5.3-flash)
issues.body:
# Title: [Bug] Runtime blocks image input ("explicitly does not support multimodal") for models whose probed/catalog capability says supports_multimodal=true

## Summary

Images sent to the agent never reach the model: `view_image` logs
`view_image was called but the active model explicitly does not support multimodal input ... the model cannot see it`,
even though the same model's capability record in QwenPaw itself says
`supports_multimodal=true, supports_image=true` (probe_source: "probed", probe passed ok earlier).
The multimodal gate in the runtime appears out of sync with the provider/model capability data.

## Environment

- QwenPaw Desktop **2.2.2-beta.4** (Windows 10, AMD64)
- Backend: `qwenpaw-backend.exe` (same install), channel: Feishu + QQ
- Providers/models where observed:
  1. `mimo` / **mimo-v2.6-flash** (base_url https://api.xiaomimimo.com/v1)
  2. `workbuddy` / **glm-5.3-flash** (OpenAI-compatible local relay)
- Multi-modal prober history (from logs, 2026-09-26):
  - `Video probe done: model=mimo-v2.6-flash ok=True(color)`
  - `Image probe done: model=mimo-v2.6-pro result=True`
  - `Image probe done: model=cn:glm-5.3-flash result=True`

## Evidence from local catalog (GET /api/models, trimmed)

```json
{
  "id": "mimo",
  "extra_models": [{
    "id": "mimo-v2.6-flash",
    "supports_multimodal": true,
    "supports_image": true,
    "supports_video": true,
    "probe_source": "probed",
    "availability_status": "unverified"
  }]
}
```

A scan over all 36 providers in `/api/models` found **zero** entries with
`supports_multimodal=false` — yet the runtime rejects images for both active models.

## Reproduction

1. Configure the `mimo` provider with a valid API key, add `mimo-v2.6-flash`.
2. Ensure the prober has marked it `supports_multimodal=true` (see log excerpt above).
3. Send an image to the bot on Feishu/QQ.
4. Agent calls `view_image`.
5. Backend log:

```
WARNING | qwenpaw\agents\tools\view_media.py:643 | view_image was called but the active
model explicitly does not support multimodal input. The image at 'C:\...\.jpg' will be
shown to the user but the model cannot see it.
```

The image is displayed to the user but **never attached to the model context** — the model
answers as if no image exists. Observed repeatedly on 2026-10-03 15:14 (mimo-v2.6-flash)
and 15:31 (glm-5.3-flash), both sessions of the same agent.

## Expected behavior

When the active model's effective capability (`supports_multimodal`/`supports_image`) is
true — per catalog or prober — `view_image` should attach the image block to the model
request. If the runtime intentionally overrides catalog capability (e.g. per-request-family
limits), the decision and its reason should be logged with the exact source of the override,
so users can see *which* flag made it "not supported".

## Suspected cause

The runtime's "active model supports multimodal" check reads a different capability source
(static model template / provider default / session snapshot) than the one the prober writes
to (`/api/models` entry). Possibly a stale session-scoped snapshot: the Feishu session was
built with `model=mimo/mimo-v2.6-flash` and a later `/model switch` in that session did not
re-evaluate capabilities either. A restart of the backend is being tested by the reporter;
if that fixes it, the capability snapshot is likely cached per session/process and not
invalidated after probing or model switching.

## Workaround verified locally

None for real vision (image never enters context). OCR-based fallback (Windows.Media.Ocr)
works for text-only screenshots but loses layout/graphics. Also note the separate 2 MB
image-size limit rejected a 12.3 MB photo earlier (`exceeds the 2097152-byte image limit`)
— worth documenting/auto-compressing instead of hard-failing.

issues.title: classify_model_error misclassifies 400+quota as bad_request, blocking fallback when primary model quota exhausted
issues.body:
## 问题描述

当主模型（primary model）的额度（quota）耗尽时，部分 provider（如 dots）返回的不是标准的 HTTP 429，而是 **HTTP 400 + "quota exceeded" 错误消息**。`classify_model_error()` 将其归类为 `bad_request`，而 `bad_request` 的 `fallback_eligible = False`，导致 `FallbackChatModel` 不会自动切换到备用模型，最终报 "Internal error"。

## 复现步骤

1. 配置一个主模型（如 dots3-note-prev）和一个备用模型（如 agnes-3.0-flash）
2. 将主模型额度耗尽（或使用已耗尽的账号）
3. 发送任意消息触发模型调用
4. 观察：返回 "Internal error"，备用模型未被尝试

## 根因分析

`qwenpaw/providers/model_error_policy.py` 的 `classify_model_error()` 函数中：

```python
elif status == 429 or _is_sdk_rate_limit(exc):
    kind = "rate_limited"
# ...
elif status is not None and 400 <= status < 500:
    kind = "bad_request"  # ← 400 + quota 落到这里
```

`fallback_eligible` 的计算逻辑：
```python
fallback_eligible = retryable or kind == "model_not_found"
```
对于 `bad_request`，`retryable = False`，所以 `fallback_eligible = False`。

## 证据

1. **`convert_model_exception()` 能识别 quota**：`qwenpaw/exceptions.py` 中有：
   ```python
   if any(kw in error_message for kw in ["rate limit", "quota", "too many requests"]):
       return ModelQuotaExceededException(...)
   ```
   但这个逻辑在 `ErrorNormalizeHook` 中执行，**晚于** `FallbackChatModel` 的判断，所以 fallback 判断时用的是原始 SDK 异常，未经过 quota 识别。

2. **dots provider 确认返回 400**：当额度耗尽时，dots 返回 400 状态码（非 429），错误消息中包含 "quota" 关键词。

## 建议修复

在 `classify_model_error()` 中，400→`bad_request` 分支之前，增加 quota/rate-limit 关键词判断：

```python
elif status == 429 or _is_sdk_rate_limit(exc):
    kind = "rate_limited"
elif any(kw in message for kw in ("quota", "rate limit", "too many requests")):
    kind = "rate_limited"  # ← 新增：400 + quota 也按 rate_limited 处理
elif status is not None and 400 <= status < 500:
    kind = "bad_request"
```

这样 400 + quota 也能触发 fallback，切到配置的备用模型。

## 影响

不修复此问题时，任何主模型额度耗尽的用户都会得到 "Internal error" 而不是自动 fallback 到备用模型，严重影响多模型 fallback 链路的可用性。

---

*由 QwenPaw 用户 w1tv 提交*

---

## 附录：相关源码位置

- `qwenpaw/providers/model_error_policy.py` — `classify_model_error()` 函数
- `qwenpaw/providers/fallback_chat_model.py` — `FallbackChatModel`，`_can_try_next()` 方法
- `qwenpaw/exceptions.py` — `convert_model_exception()`，已有 quota 识别逻辑
- `qwenpaw/hooks/error/error_hook.py` — `ErrorNormalizeHook`，在 fallback 之后执行

issues.title: [Bug]: /model 在渠道内无法切换会话级钉住模型（只改 agent 默认），钉住模型故障时无法自救
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0

## Description

### 现象

在渠道（飞书 / 钉钉等）对话框里，对**已经钉住了会话级模型**的会话执行 `/model <provider>:<model>`，命令返回 "Model Switched" 成功，但**当前会话实际使用的模型不变**，再发 `/model` 查看也仍显示原来钉住的模型。用户无法在渠道内把当前会话切换到别的模型——即使钉住的那个模型已经故障、整条会话无法对话。

### 实际复现案例（生产实测）

- 某飞书会话此前通过 Console 模型选择器钉住了会话级模型 `provider-b:model-b`（写入 `chats.json` 的 `meta.runtime_context.model`）。
- 该模型所属网关整体连接失败（`Connection error`），会话无法正常对话。
- 在飞书对话框发 `/model provider-a:model-a`：
  - 服务日志出现 `/model switch: agent=default provider=provider-a model=model-a`（命令执行成功）；
  - `agent.json` 的 `active_model` 确实被持久化为 `provider-a:model-a`；
  - 回执为 "Model Switched"，附带一句英文提示 "This conversation keeps its session override: provider-b:model-b ..."。
- 紧接着发普通消息，builder 日志仍为 `built agent for session=... model=provider-b/model-b`——会话依旧用钉住的故障模型。
- 再发 `/model` 查看，显示的仍是 `provider-b:model-b`（session override）。
- 期间还发了 `/new`：会话重建后**仍用** `provider-b/model-b`（`/new` 不清会话级钉住）。
- 关键：slash command 本身不经过 LLM（模型故障时 `/model` 依然能执行成功），所以这本该是模型故障时的自救通道，但因为改不动会话钉住而失效。

### 期望行为

在渠道对话框内，`/model <provider>:<model>` 应能切换**当前会话**实际使用的模型；或至少提供一个命令（如 `/model reset` / `/model unpin`）能清除当前会话的会话级模型钉住，让会话回落到 agent 默认，从而在钉住模型故障时用户能在渠道内自救。

### 实际行为

`/model <provider>:<model>` 只更新 **agent 级默认**（`agent.json` 的 `active_model`），完全不触碰当前会话的会话级模型钉住（`chats.json` 的 `meta.runtime_context.model`）。由于会话级优先级更高，当前会话的显示与实际调用都不变。`/model reset` 同样只清 agent 级、不清会话钉住。渠道内没有任何命令能设置 / 清除会话级模型。

### 根因分析（源码链路）

1. **模型选择优先级**：`qwenpaw/services/session_thinking.py` 的 `select_chat_model()` = 请求级 override > 会话级 override（`session_model(meta)` 读 `meta.runtime_context.model`）> 无。会话级钉住优先于 agent 默认。
2. **`/model` 显示与实际调用都走会话级优先**：`qwenpaw/runtime/commands/control/model_handler.py` 的 `_current_model()` 先调 `_conversation_model()`（读会话 override），有则直接返回；builder 构建普通消息时同样应用会话 override。
3. **`/model <spec>` 只写 agent 级**：`_switch_model()` 仅 `agent_config.active_model = new_slot` + `update_agent_config_async(...)` 持久化到 `agent.json`，**不调用** `set_session_model()`，不改 `meta.runtime_context.model`。成功回执里的 `_override_notice()` 只是"提示"会话仍用旧 override，并不改变它。
4. **`/model reset` 同样只清 agent 级**：`_reset_model()` 把 `agent_config.active_model = None`，也不触碰会话 override。
5. **会话级模型的唯一写入入口不在渠道命令**：`qwenpaw/app/chats/manager.py` 的 `set_session_model(chat_id, model)` 只被 `qwenpaw/app/chats/api.py` 的 `PUT /{chat_id}/model`（Console）与 `qwenpaw/app/routers/console.py` 调用。渠道侧 control 命令（/model /stop /skills /checkpoint /approval）与渠道命令（/new /compact）均无法设置 / 清除会话级模型。

**结果**：一旦某会话在 Console 钉住了模型，渠道内就再也无法用命令改它的模型；钉住模型故障时，用户在渠道内无自救手段，只能回到 Console（或直连 API）处理。

## 与既有 issue 的关系

- **#8464（已修复 / completed）**：`/compact` 无视会话级模型、固定用 agent 级默认——官方已让 `/compact` 继承会话当前模型。本 issue 是**同族互补缺口**：`/model` 作为"模型管理"命令，却反而**无法管理当前会话的模型**（只能改 agent 默认）。两者都源于"slash command 与 `meta.runtime_context.model` 会话级 override 的交互不完整"。
- 区别于 #8310（Console 切换弹窗 UX / 思考控制），本 issue 专指**渠道内 `/model` 命令无法切换 / 清除会话级模型**。

## 修复建议

让 `/model` 在渠道会话内使用时作用于**当前会话**，任选其一或组合：

- 选项 A：`/model <provider>:<model>` 在有会话上下文时，同时调用 `set_session_model(chat_id, new_slot)` 更新当前会话 override（与 Console `PUT /{chat_id}/model` 同源），使显示与实际调用立即一致。
- 选项 B：赋予 `/model reset`（或新增 `/model unpin`）会话语义——清除当前会话的 `meta.runtime_context.model`（`set_session_model(chat_id, None)`），回落到 agent 默认。当前 `/model reset` 只清 agent 级，建议区分会话级。
- 无论哪种，成功回执应明确说明"当前会话已切换 / 已清除钉住"，而不是仅提示 "This conversation keeps its session override"。

## 影响

- 模型故障时渠道内无法自救，只能回 Console，违背"slash command 不经过 LLM、模型挂了也能用"的兜底设计初衷。
- "Model Switched" 成功回执与实际行为不符，易误导用户以为已切换。

## Environment

- QwenPaw 2.3.0（Docker 部署）
- 渠道：飞书（其他渠道同理，凡支持会话级模型钉住 + slash command 的均受影响）

issues.title: [Bug][feishu] extract_json_key() crashes with AttributeError on valid non-object JSON message content
issues.body:
## Describe the bug
`plugins/channel/feishu/qwenpaw_channel_feishu/utils.py::extract_json_key()` catches `json.JSONDecodeError` and returns `None`, but assumes `json.loads(content)` returns a `dict`:

```python
    try:
        data = json.loads(content)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return None
    for k in keys:
        v = data.get(k) or data.get(k.replace("_", "").lower())
```

Inbound Feishu message content is passed directly into `extract_json_key()` from `platform.py`. When `content` is valid non-object JSON (e.g. `"[1, 2]"`, `""text""`, `"42"`, `"true"`, `"null"`), `data.get(...)` raises `AttributeError`.

Note: `_extract_structured_text()` later in the same file already guards with `if not isinstance(data, dict): return None`.

## To reproduce
```python
from qwenpaw_channel_feishu.utils import extract_json_key

extract_json_key("[1, 2]", "text")  # AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'
```

## Expected behavior
Return `None` when `data` is not a `dict`.

prs.title: feat(console): support runtime base-path deployment
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #8714.

Related context only: #1853, #8177, and #8316. This PR does not reopen, comment on, or close those older issues or pull requests.

Add an optional `QWENPAW_BASE_PATH` runtime setting for serving the standard prebuilt Console and API below a reverse-proxy prefix such as `/app/qwenpaw/web`.

#8316 covers custom builds through `VITE_CONSOLE_BASENAME`. This PR covers the complementary runtime case: pip/uv/Docker users should not need to rebuild the Console or have a proxy rewrite minified JavaScript. Uvicorn `root_path` alone cannot solve the absolute URLs already present in that prebuilt output.

### What changed

- Add a validated base-path ASGI middleware using standard `root_path` semantics for HTTP, mounted static files, and WebSockets. The bare prefix redirects to a trailing slash; requests outside the prefix return 404.
- Set the deployment prefix via `<base href>` in the prebuilt `index.html`. Current builds do not require inline JavaScript to bootstrap, so `script-src 'self'` works without `unsafe-inline`. The server still recognizes the old token for older Console bundles; it does not rewrite JavaScript or CSS responses.
- Build default Console entry and module URLs relative to the document base; resolve public assets, API calls, router/login navigation, and chunk-readiness probes against the same runtime prefix.
- Preserve the existing root and `/console` behavior when the setting is empty or `/`. Existing build-time `VITE_CONSOLE_BASENAME` and desktop behavior remain separate.
- Document runtime proxy configuration in English and Chinese. Proxies must preserve rather than strip the configured prefix.

The current login flow uses a Bearer token in `localStorage`, so no authentication-cookie path change is needed.

### Review follow-up (`286c6556`)

prs.title: fix(loop): record every tool call appended during a reply so the doom-loop gate can fire
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`DoomLoopGate` is enabled in the default mode (`window_size=3`,
`similarity_threshold=0.5`, `stop` after 4 hits) but it has never fired. A reply
that repeats the same tool call with the same arguments — the case in #8712,
where one `Bash` invocation was approved 14 times in 70 seconds — ran until the
user pressed stop twice.

The gate's auto-recording path de-duplicated on the **message** id:

```python
last_msg = context[-1]
if last_msg.id == state.last_recorded_msg_id:
    return
```

Inside a single reply, every assistant message is written with the same
`state.reply_id`: `agentscope` creates one `ReplyContext(reply_id=…)` per reply,
and `AgentState.append_context` either extends the existing message or appends a
new one with that same id. From the second iteration on, `last_msg.id` already
equalled `state.last_recorded_msg_id`, so the function returned before recording
anything and the history never grew past one entry. A three-entry window can
never fill, `_detect_repetition` can never return true, and no stage is reached.

This is not specific to shell calls: no tool, in any reply, could trip the gate.

## Scope

Type: B (state machine / dedup)

One file of production code plus one test file. `agents/tools/shell.py` is not
touched: the earlier revision of this PR changed `_with_shell_guard` to stop
overriding the result state with `ERROR`, on the theory that the tool result
never reached the model. That theory was wrong — the result does reach the
model — so that change is reverted, and this PR fixes the layer that actually
dropped the repetition.

## Self-review

1. Failure — a block with an unexpected shape cannot raise: the scan skips any
   block whose type is not `tool_call`/`tool_use`, and reads fields defensively
   for both block objects and plain dicts.
2. Timeout — not applicable: the gate has no timeout path; it runs synchronously
   inside `check()`.
3. Skipped — a text-only iteration (`has_tool_calls is False`) records nothing;
   an empty or non-list `content` returns early.
4. Concurrency — one iteration that carries several parallel tool calls records
   every block it contains (`test_blocks_of_one_iteration_are_all_recorded`).

## Evidence

Recorded against the real `DoomLoopGate` with synthetic contexts that mirror
what the agent writes:

| context | history after 8 iterations | gate fired |
| --- | --- | --- |
| same message id every iteration (before) | stays at 1 | never |
| same message id, blocks appended (after) | 8 | iteration 4 |

Production logs agree: `qwenpaw.log` since 13 November contains no
`DoomLoopGate` and no `Doom loop` line at all.

The concrete case from #8712 — 14 identical `Bash` calls inside one reply — now
reaches the configured stop stage instead of running to completion.

## Test scope

- Target: `tests/unit/loop/test_doom_loop_auto_record.py` — **7 passed**.
- Red/green: with the `src` change reverted the same file gives **2 failed**
  (including the three-iteration stop case), and **7 passed** once restored.
- Adjacent: `tests/unit/loop` — **99 passed**.
- Adjacent: `tests/unit/modes` + `tests/unit/agents/tools/test_shell_resources.py`
  — **196 passed, 4 skipped** (the skips are the platform-gated resource tests).
- Lint: `pre-commit run --files` — all hooks passed.

Fixes #8712.

prs.title: test(plugins): make the install-lock and provision tests pass on Windows
prs.body:
## Description

Twelve tests in `tests/unit/plugins` fail on a plain Windows checkout for three environment reasons; a Linux CI never sees any of them. This PR makes the two affected files green on Windows without weakening anything on POSIX. Filed with evidence in #8931 (to be filed alongside).

1. **Symlink privilege (`WinError 1314`)** — five tests create symlinks while arranging fixtures, which needs admin or Developer Mode on Windows. Probe-and-skip now mirrors the file's existing `pytest.skip("requires a case-insensitive filesystem")` precedent (`test_install_lock.py`) and a small helper in `test_provision_create.py`.

2. **5 s readline budget vs ~11.5 s of package-import work** — `test_reader_admission_waits_for_publication` spawns `python -I -c` whose script imported `qwenpaw.plugins.dependency_maintenance` through the package, running environment custody at import time (measured 11.25–11.80 s per fresh interpreter on this machine), while the parent waited five seconds for the child's first line. The child now loads the stdlib-only module directly by path — the same pattern its sibling child-custody test in the same file already uses — and the readline/communicate budgets use `WAIT_TIMEOUT` from `tests/unit/plugins/timing.py`, which is documented as bounding hangs, not performance.

3. **venv launcher pid ≠ interpreter pid** — on a Windows venv, `python.exe` is a launcher and `peer.pid` never equals the child's `os.getpid()` (measured 4/4 across Popen/asyncio and parent-import combinations), while lease filenames record the interpreter's pid. The two `live_readers` pid-equality assertions now check the lease count on `_WINDOWS` and keep the exact pid equality on POSIX. Product code is unaffected: lease liveness is decided by OS file locks, and in-process pid comparisons stay consistent.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8941

prs.title: fix(agents): retry generic media bad requests without media
prs.body:
Historical tool results from `view_video` can reintroduce video into later
model requests. When the provider returns a generic `400 Invalid request
parameters`, the existing fallback does not recognize it, so follow-up
messages in the same session keep failing.

Retry once without media only if the failed request actually sent media and
the response does not identify a specific invalid parameter. The retry does
not modify stored history, affect file delivery, or cache a model capability
change. If the retry also fails, propagate the error.

prs.title: fix(video_memory): coerce root themes to str & guard null in merged_graph_payload
prs.body:
Fixes #8931

## What Problem This Solves
In `plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/backend/vendor/media_toolkit/video_memory/merge.py::merged_graph_payload()`:

```python
all_themes.update(root.get("themes", []))
all_entities.update(str(e) for e in root.get("key_entities", []))
```

`root` comes from LLM/VLM-generated JSON via `json.loads`. While `key_entities` coerces elements via `str(e)`, `themes` does not—causing `TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict'` or `TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'int'` during `sorted(all_themes)`. Neither line handles explicit JSON `null` (`"themes": null` / `"key_entities": null`), which raises `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable`.

## Change
Normalize both fields consistently with `or []` and `str(...)`:

```python
all_themes.update(str(t) for t in (root.get("themes") or []))
all_entities.update(str(e) for e in (root.get("key_entities") or []))
```

*(Note: this file is vendored from Qwen-MM-Plugins; happy to adjust or defer if maintainers prefer syncing upstream first.)*

1. Added regression test `test_merged_graph_payload_tolerates_bad_root_fields` in `plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/backend/tests/vendored/test_video_memory_toolkit.py` covering `themes=None`, `key_entities=None`, nested dict entries, and mixed `int`/`str` themes across multiple sources.

prs.title: fix(video_memory): cap folded short-tail segments at max_scene_sec in plan_segments
prs.body:
Fixes #8930

## What Problem This Solves
In `plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/backend/vendor/media_toolkit/video_memory/segmentation.py::plan_segments()`, the middle loop and the `last_dur > max_scene_sec` branch both enforce `max_scene_sec` by splitting over-length spans. However, the trailing short-tail absorption branch:

```python
elif final_segments and last_dur < min_scene_sec:
    s, _ = final_segments.pop()
    final_segments.append((s, end_sec))
```

folds the trailing remainder into the previous segment without re-checking `max_scene_sec`. When the previous segment was already near `max_scene_sec`, the merged `(s, end_sec)` segment exceeds the cap (for example, returning `(0, 310)` when `max_scene_sec=300.0`).

## Change
Re-check `absorbed_dur = end_sec - s` in that `elif` branch and split using the same `max(2, round(absorbed_dur / (max_scene_sec * 0.7)))` helper logic when `absorbed_dur > max_scene_sec`.

*(Note: this file is vendored from Qwen-MM-Plugins; happy to adjust or defer if maintainers prefer syncing upstream first.)*

## Evidence
1. Added regression test `test_plan_segments_short_tail_fold_respects_max_scene_sec` in `plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/backend/tests/vendored/test_video_memory_toolkit.py` covering both auto-threshold and explicit-threshold over-max cases (`end_sec=310, max=300`, `end_sec=320, max=300`, `end_sec=188, max=100`).

prs.title: fix(utils): skip empty text blocks in _first_text_in_list
prs.body:
## Description
`_first_text_in_list()` in `src/qwenpaw/utils/model_response.py` returned on `isinstance(got, str)` without checking non-emptiness. When a structured response contains a leading empty text block (`{"type": "text", "text": ""}`) followed by the actual answer block, `extract_response_text()` returned `""` and discarded the answer.

This PR updates `_first_text_in_list()` to require `isinstance(got, str) and got:` (matching the scalar `.text` check in the same module) and adds regression tests in `tests/unit/utils/test_model_response.py` while preserving the no-fallback invariant when content blocks contain only thinking or empty text.

prs.title: fix(creator/json_pointer): enforce RFC 6901 array-index tokens to prevent wrong-element writes
prs.body:
## Description
`plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/backend/services/project_files/json_pointer.py` parsed array-index reference tokens with bare `int(token)` in `value_at`, `_parent_and_token`, and `apply_changes`. Because `_parent_and_token` did not guard against negative indices while `value_at` returned `MISSING`, a pointer like `/items/-1/name` bypassed the CAS read check and silently mutated the last element of the list. Bare `int()` also accepted non-RFC-6901 forms (`+1`, `01`, whitespace, underscores, Unicode digits).

This PR adds `_parse_array_index(token)` enforcing RFC 6901 §4 (`0` or `[1-9][0-9]*` ASCII digits) and applies it across all three sites, plus regression tests in `test_json_pointer_and_jq.py`.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8904

prs.title: fix(console): clarify confirmation and approval interactions
prs.body:
## Description

This PR updates confirmation dialogs, approval cards, and destructive actions across the QwenPaw Console. It addresses two problems: generic labels often hid what users were about to authorize, and several workflows reported success too early, displayed stale state, or lost the context needed to retry.

### Tool and application approvals

- Replace misleading “just once” and “always allow” labels for `exact` and `similar` with descriptions of the actual authorization scope. The approval card now distinguishes a single call, a session-scoped target or pattern, strict-mode confirmation, and requests whose scope is unknown.
- Carry `approval_behavior` through backend display data and SDK approval snapshots. Preserve the effective execution level so the UI can describe strict-mode requests correctly, including those from mail F1 exploration.
- Update the bundled Computer Use plugin to distinguish allow or deny decisions for the current session from persistent, installation-wide application access. Clarify what revoking persistent access does and rebuild the bundled frontend.
- Preserve in-flight submission state when switching between approval cards in Chat. Display expired, unavailable, rejected, and unconfirmed decisions separately, and let users recheck whether a request is still pending before retrying. Dismissing an expired Inbox notice no longer sends a denial.
- Limit desktop quick actions to known single-call approvals. Other requests open the matching Inbox card. A late deep-link response can no longer put a resolved request back into the shared approval list. `404` and `409` remove unavailable notifications; network and server failures leave **Review request** instead of re-enabling the quick actions.

### Backups, restore, and deletion

- Make the pre-restore choices explicit: cancel, skip the backup, or back up before continuing. Let users close the dialog and choose again if the pre-restore backup fails. Keep the three choices usable in narrow layouts.
- Prevent a failed pre-restore backup request from adopting another window’s active job and treating that job’s completion as success. Ordinary backup resumption is unchanged.
- Show backup cancellation as in progress until the job reaches a terminal state. Distinguish creating, exporting, overwriting, and restoring backups, and use separate trust confirmations for import and restore.
- Show the backup name and ID before deletion, and report success only when the server confirms that the requested backup ID was deleted.
- Update the shared inline delete control used for backups and custom environment variables. Keep confirmations within the viewport, improve keyboard focus, prevent duplicate submissions, and keep failed actions available for retry.
- Wait for Inbox batch deletion to finish, report partial failures, and deselect only successful items so the failed items can be retried directly.

### Other Console workflows

| Area | Changes |
| --- | --- |
| Workspace and Git | Clarify discarding unsaved file edits before switching, and treat closing that dialog as cancellation. Name the directory creation action for assistive technology. Localize using a volume root, reverting a commit, discarding file changes, and creating and switching branches. |
| Agents, sessions, and jobs | Name agent enable, disable, copy, and delete actions; session and group deletion; cron job deletion and import approval; and MCP client and ACP integration deletion. Prefer Cancel as the initial focus in selected destructive dialogs, including checkpoint actions. |
| Channels and mail | Distinguish allowlist removal, blocklist removal, approval, blocking, and dismissal. Show the relevant target or selection count. Keep the mail processing resume dialog open if the request fails. |
| Skills and security | Distinguish importing, transferring, overwriting, renaming, syncing, updating, broadcasting, and deleting skills in the workspace and skill pool. Distinguish removing file protection from deleting a file. Report when a skill was removed from the allowlist but could not be disabled, and keep scan-history clearing retryable. |
| Models, providers, and apps | Clarify opening or cancelling OAuth authorization versus closing its dialog. Distinguish clearing a local provider key from revoking remote credentials or deleting the provider. Name model switching, local model deletion, and engine updates. Report that download cancellation was requested, and distinguish uninstalling an app from uninstalling a plugin. |
| Environment, Community, imports, and Hub | Distinguish restoring an inherited environment value from deleting a custom variable. Clarify publishing edits, deleting posts and drafts, and retrying selected import items. Name Hub runtime, registration, credential, invitation, and password-reset actions explicitly. |

**Security considerations:** This PR does not broaden authorization or change the underlying approval policy. It exposes the existing scope more accurately, distinguishes an accepted decision from successful execution, and avoids offering an immediate desktop retry when the server outcome is unknown.

prs.title: feat(chat): add append-only session storage, paginated history and native Turn forks
prs.body:
## Description

This PR adds a durable conversation timeline for QwenPaw and updates the Console to consume it incrementally. The main work is organized around four capabilities: per-session transcript persistence, bounded history loading, Turn-level fork, and in-run steering.

## Main work

### 1. Durable per-session conversation storage

- Store each conversation in its own SQLite transcript database instead of treating mutable session JSON as display history.
- Keep append-only conversation facts separate from rebuildable message/runtime projections.
- Persist Turn status, messages and content blocks, context revisions, usage, provider boundaries, and steering receipts.
- Import legacy JSON sessions and history data into the new storage when needed.
- Connect the transcript lifecycle to clear/new, compaction, Scroll/Recall, checkpoints, backup/restore, statistics, cloning, and PawApp/SDK session access.
- Finalize covered failure and cancellation paths so history does not normally remain in a running state after the request terminates.

### 2. Paginated history and bounded Console rendering

- Read history by stable snapshot cursor with Turn, content-block, and byte budgets rather than loading the full conversation.
- Return page-owned fork capability and steering receipt data together with history messages.
- Add incremental older/newer history loading, scroll anchoring, bottom-follow behavior, a user-message directory, and route-safe session switching.
- Keep live streaming and reconnect replay available while the user is viewing historical messages.
- Preserve the continuation cursor until an oversized user message is complete so forward navigation does not skip fragments.
- Window large message lists, Markdown tables, code blocks, and rendered rows to reduce full-DOM work.

### 3. Turn-level fork

- Fork from a persisted Turn boundary instead of copying only the latest mutable session state.
- Report fork availability from the actual stored boundary and hide the action when no usable snapshot exists.
- Use native provider fork/reset state for Codex and Qoder when available; do not silently replace a failed native restore with a fresh provider context.
- Persist parent/child lineage and show the fork boundary in the child conversation, with navigation back to the parent when it is still available.
- Track native forks after an external provider ID is returned so local-registration failures can be recovered without creating a second provider branch.

### 4. In-run steering

- Accept steering input while a QwenPaw Console Turn is running and apply accepted inputs at the next agent reasoning boundary.
- Reuse the normal message attachment conversion path for steering attachments.
- Support consecutive steering inputs with durable accepted/applied/failed receipts and stable client message IDs.
- Render applied steering inputs as user messages in the live timeline and after history reload or fork.
- Include steering receipts and conversation sync state in history pages, and poll only while local or server state remains unsettled.

The Console message queue remains disabled. A busy composer submission uses the steering path directly and does not create a persistent queued item.

## Consistency and recovery hardening

The current HEAD also closes the storage consistency cases found during adversarial review:

- Staged deletion recovery remains owned by the mutating catalog; statistics opens the catalog read-only and cannot restore an in-progress deletion.
- Logical deletion records pending physical cleanup, backup refuses incomplete cleanup, and a later delete can retry cleanup after a transient failure.
- Legacy migration initializes transcript identity before publishing the catalog mapping.
- Failed session deletion restores the catalog mapping instead of leaving a dangling row.
- Empty conversations can be checkpointed without a runtime database, while non-empty conversations still require valid runtime state.
- Deleted or unavailable chat routes preserve the 404 meaning and show a specific unavailable/deleted message.

Earlier review findings covered by the code include ephemeral ACP handling on fork-capable backends, Recall purge carry-forward across historical forks, stream cancellation ordering, failed Turn finalization, and sequenced live-delta batching.

## Current boundaries

The description intentionally does not make delivery commitments for:

- A hard 8 MiB limit for one Turn accumulated from multiple fragments.
- A specific browser-memory reduction or a measured result for the exact datasets in the linked reports.
- Re-enabling the Console queue or defining queue/steer arbitration.
- Background retention beyond the lifecycle currently wired by the implementation.
- Zero loss of output that was never committed before forced process termination.
- Recovery when a native provider creates a branch but the process terminates before the provider returns its external ID.
- Fresh real-provider browser E2E, network-disconnect injection, or Windows extended-path testing beyond the automated checks below.

The current 8 MiB Console history budget is a best-effort multi-Turn retention budget, not a hard per-Turn or process-memory guarantee.

## Related issues

The following issues describe motivation and functional overlap. They are listed as related work, not automatic closure claims or promises to reproduce every reported measurement:

- #3915 — incremental history loading, measured rendering, scroll anchoring, and bottom follow.
- #3923 — bounded page reads and windowed rendering, subject to the limits above.
- #8134 — durable display history independent of compacted model context.
- #6542 — persistence of completed Turns and their committed final state.
- #8744 — access to durable history after context compaction.
- #1775 — Console steering allows users to supplement a running Turn at the next reasoning boundary; channel-side intent classification and automatic interrupt/queue routing are outside this PR.
- #8774 — overlaps with mid-turn injection and durable steering receipts in Console; this PR does not implement the issue's all-channel routing, steering switches, or queue fallback.
- #7461 — accepted Console steering inputs can arrive during tool execution and apply at the next reasoning boundary; draining channel queues and priority-based interruption are not included.
- #8288 — paginated history, windowed rendering, and session-switch handling address full-history rendering work; no result is claimed for the report's exact dataset or timings.
- #7514 — incremental history loading reduces the amount of history loaded for the initial view; this does not establish resolution across the reported mobile and remote-network scenarios.
- #8816 — per-session storage and recoverable deletion cleanup overlap with the storage lifecycle proposal; user-facing recycle-bin restore, automatic retention, and scheduled cleanup are not included.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Refactoring
- [x] Breaking change (session storage representation changes; legacy data is imported)
- [ ] Documentation

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend
- [x] Console
- [x] Console streaming/reconnect
- [x] Tests
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Testing

Local verification for HEAD `c296f7d33e6badd117fce25482bd38e030806bcb`:

- Backend targeted unit tests: 132 passed, 1 skipped.
- Console targeted Vitest tests: 79 passed.
- Pre-commit, Prettier, and diff checks: passed.
- Real-page validation covered deletion, backup, checkpoint behavior, native fork continuation, refresh/history rendering, and oversized-message forward pagination.

GitHub checks for the new HEAD are running. The checks page below is the source of truth for their final status; passing checks are evidence only for the scenarios they cover.

## Evidence

- Current checks: https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8532/checks
- Review that prompted the consistency follow-up: https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8532#issuecomment-7157911438
- Earlier lifecycle and pagination review: https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8532#issuecomment-6813471058
- Earlier fork/ACP/finalization review: https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8532#issuecomment-7029349334

## Security Considerations

Session ownership and active-session deletion checks remain part of history access. Provider contexts remain provider-owned. This PR does not include local databases, conversation exports, screenshots, profiling dumps, or environment credentials.

## Additional Notes

This remains a large PR covering storage, migration, pagination, replay, fork, and steering. Historical runtime reconstruction can only be as exact as the legacy data that was previously persisted. This description records the current implementation and its observed boundaries without promising follow-up scope or dates.

prs.body:
## Description Custom providers already let users mark a model as a decision model, but selecting it as the default failed because the resolver accepted only TypeSafe and the managed local runtime. Users can now add or edit a custom decision model under Settings → Models. Each model uses its provider's base URL, API key and headers, and can use System One or OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions with JSON object output. The model can be selected globally or for an agent. Testing the connection sends a typed question through the selected protocol. Changing the protocol clears the previous probe result. The Chat Completions adapter maps model-reported probabilities to AgentScope binary, choice and score answers. It validates labels, probability ranges and distributions and rejects truncated completions. A failed tool assessment falls back to user approval. English and Chinese setup instructions are included. prs.title: feat(desktop): add Linux deb and AppImage packaging to the Tauri build
prs.body:
## Description

Linux currently has no desktop artifact. `desktop-build.yml` builds only Windows and macOS, `tauri.conf.json` declares `"targets": ["app", "nsis"]` with `.icns`/`.ico` icons only, and `RELEASING.md` documents the desktop apps as "Windows + macOS" — so Linux users must run the Docker image or build from source.

Related issues: **#8442** — the Linux parity umbrella; this PR lands its packaging half (deb + AppImage), while Computer Use and Chrome Native Messaging follow in separate PRs. **#5668** — the x86_64 AppImage request; the AppImage build is added here, and release publishing plus the updater follow in the next PR.

The packaging chain was already platform-neutral, which is why this is a packaging shell rather than a port:

| Piece | Already handled |
|---|---|
| Resource lookup | `backend/command.rs` resolves `python/bin/python3`, `node-runtime/bin/node`, `qwenpaw-backend` (no `.exe`) for every non-Windows target |
| Python runtime | `stage_python_runtime.py` maps Linux to `{arch}-unknown-linux-gnu` |
| Node runtime | `stage_node_runtime.py` maps Linux to `linux-{arch}` |
| Backend build | `build_pyinstaller.sh` is a generic unix script; macOS signing lives in its own wrapper |
| PyInstaller spec | platform branches exist only for darwin codesign and win32 executable names |
| Icons | generated from `scripts/pack/assets/icon.svg` |

### What this PR does

**Bundle configuration** (`console/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`)

- add `deb` and `appimage` to `bundle.targets`, keeping `app` and `nsis` untouched
- list the existing 512×512 `icons/icon.png` so Linux bundlers have a PNG
- add `bundle.publisher` and `bundle.copyright` (the deb `Maintainer` field is mandatory)
- declare `bundle.linux.deb.depends` explicitly: `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0`, `libgtk-3-0t64 | libgtk-3-0`, `libayatana-appindicator3-1`

**Build entry point** (`scripts/pack-tauri/build_linux_pyinstaller.sh`)

Mirrors the macOS orchestration without signing: `npm ci` → version sync → console build → `build_pyinstaller.sh` (PyInstaller backend plus bundled Python/Node runtimes) → `tauri build --bundles deb,appimage` → collect both artifacts into `dist/`. `QWENPAW_SKIP_BACKEND_BUILD=1` retries packaging without rebuilding the backend.

**Five build-host defects this exposed, each fixed in place**

1. **Python series came from the bootstrap interpreter.** On a 3.14 host the staged runtime left the `requires-python` range and dependency installation failed. `stage_python_runtime.py` now uses the host series only when it is supported (3.11–3.13) and otherwise falls back to 3.13 with a printed notice.
2. **The bundle carried the CUDA stack.** `whisper` pulls torch, and the default Linux wheel declares the CUDA runtime through `DT_NEEDED` on `libtorch_cpu.so` itself (`libcudart.so.13`), so `nvidia-*` plus `triton` added ~4 GB and could not be stripped after the fact. Linux builds now install torch from the CPU index first, so the requirement is already satisfied and the CUDA payload never enters the bundle.
3. **The product name broke `linuxdeploy`.** A space in `productName` puts a space in the AppDir and resource paths (`usr/lib/<productName>/`), which splits the `ldd` invocation linuxdeploy performs for every ELF; `ldd` exits 1 and bundling aborts with the unhelpful `failed to run linuxdeploy`. Linux now uses the space-free `QwenPawDesktop` (the window title still comes from `app.windows[0].title`; data remains under `~/.qwenpaw`).
4. **A failed run poisoned the next one.** Tauri merges into an existing AppDir, so leftovers under the previous product name survived; the bundle directories are now removed before bundling.
5. **linuxdeploy cannot infer dependencies for a bundled runtime.** It walks every ELF in the AppDir — thousands of files inside the Python runtime — and aborts on the first unresolved name, which is pure overhead for a tree that ships its own dependencies. When bundling fails, the script now deduplicates the resource tree that Tauri emits under two names (one real copy plus a symlink), points `.DirIcon` at the icon named by the desktop entry, and packs the AppDir with `appimagetool`.

**Packaging hygiene** — a single build left ~20 GB of intermediates behind (`target/release/binaries` 9.7 GB, `target/release/bundle/appimage_deb` 9.7 GB). They are now removed after the artifacts are collected (`QWENPAW_DESKTOP_KEEP_STAGING=1` keeps them).

**CI** (`desktop-build.yml`, new `build-tauri-linux` job on `ubuntu-24.04`)

Installs the Linux packaging dependencies, builds both formats, verifies the launched app with Playwright through a new `.github/actions/verify-tauri-linux` action (plus `scripts/verify/launch_tauri_linux.sh`, which runs the AppImage under Xvfb, waits for `~/.qwenpaw/desktop_port`, and exports `BASE_URL`), records checksums, and uploads the deb, the AppImage and the verify logs. `desktop_verify.py` gains the `tauri-linux` UI mode (Playwright WebKit).

**Docs** — a Linux section in `website/public/docs/desktop.{en,zh}.md` (requirements, deb vs AppImage install, first-run data paths, updates, uninstall) and the release support matrix.

### Evidence

Environment: Ubuntu 26.04 (GNOME 50, Wayland-only), rustc 1.99.1, webkit2gtk-4.1 2.52.6, node v24.21.0, host Python 3.14.

```text
$ bash scripts/pack-tauri/build_linux_pyinstaller.sh
== Checking prerequisites ==
  [INFO] python3 3.14 is outside 3.11-3.13; the bundled runtime will be staged as 3.13
== Step 2: PyInstaller backend + bundled runtimes ==
== Installing CPU-only torch ==
...
== Step 3b: tauri bundling failed; packing the AppDir with appimagetool ==
    deduplicating usr/lib/QwenPaw Desktop -> symlink to QwenPawDesktop
-rwxr-xr-x 976M  dist/QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b1-linux-x86_64.AppImage
-rw-r--r--  1.3G dist/QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b1-linux-x86_64.deb
```

```text
$ dpkg-deb -I dist/QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b1-linux-x86_64.deb
 Package: qwen-paw-desktop
 Version: 2.3.0-beta.1
 Architecture: amd64
 Installed-Size: 3489035
 Maintainer: QwenPaw Contributors
 Depends: libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0, libgtk-3-0t64 | libgtk-3-0, libayatana-appindicator3-1, ...
```

```text
$ dpkg-deb -c dist/...deb | grep -oE "usr/lib/[^/]+" | sort -u
usr/lib/QwenPawDesktop            # single resource tree

$ apt-get install --dry-run ./dist/...deb | tail -3
The following NEW packages will be installed:
  qwen-paw-desktop
0 upgraded, 1 newly installed
```

Installed and launched on the target machine:

```text
$ sudo apt install ./dist/QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b1-linux-x86_64.deb && qwenpaw-desktop
[backend] packaged command: /usr/lib/QwenPaw Desktop/binaries/qwenpaw-backend/qwenpaw-backend
[backend] bundled python runtime: .../python-runtime/python/bin/python3
[backend] bundled node runtime: .../node-runtime
[backend] shared runtime 2.3.0-beta.1 connected after 9534ms (launched=true)
```

The window renders, the sidecar connects, and `~/.qwenpaw` is created on first launch.

### Open items (separate changes)

- Release plumbing (`desktop-publish.yml` / `desktop-promote.yml`, OSS paths, `linux-x86_64` in the updater manifest) and the AppImage updater client branch — PR2.
- Arm64 (`ubuntu-24.04-arm`) — follow-up once x86_64 is green.
- The AppImage has been built, structurally verified (valid AppImage, correct desktop entry, deduplicated payload) and **launched successfully on the target machine**; CI covers the launch on every build.

### 描述

Linux 目前没有桌面产物：`desktop-build.yml` 只构建 Windows 与 macOS，`tauri.conf.json` 的 `targets` 只有 `["app","nsis"]`，图标只有 `.icns`/`.ico`，`RELEASING.md` 也写着「Windows + macOS」——Linux 用户只能跑 Docker 或从源码构建。

相关 issue：**#8442** —— Linux 对齐的总 issue，本 PR 落地其中的打包部分（deb + AppImage），Computer Use 与 Chrome Native Messaging 由后续 PR 完成；**#5668** —— x86_64 AppImage 提案，本 PR 补上 AppImage 构建，发布与自动更新由下一个 PR 完成。

打包链本来就是平台中立的，所以这是补一个打包壳，而不是移植：

| 部分 | 已就绪 |
|---|---|
| 资源查找 | `backend/command.rs` 对所有非 Windows 目标已按 `python/bin/python3`、`node-runtime/bin/node`、无 `.exe` 的 `qwenpaw-backend` 查找 |
| Python runtime | `stage_python_runtime.py` 已映射 Linux 到 `{arch}-unknown-linux-gnu` |
| Node runtime | `stage_node_runtime.py` 已映射 Linux 到 `linux-{arch}` |
| 后端构建 | `build_pyinstaller.sh` 是通用 unix 脚本，macOS 签名单独封装 |
| PyInstaller spec | 平台分支只有 darwin 签名与 win32 可执行名 |
| 图标 | 由 `scripts/pack/assets/icon.svg` 生成 |

### 本 PR 做了什么

**打包配置**（`console/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`）

- `bundle.targets` 追加 `deb` 与 `appimage`，保留原有 `app`、`nsis`
- 列入已有的 512×512 `icons/icon.png`，供 Linux 打包器使用
- 补 `bundle.publisher` 与 `bundle.copyright`（deb 的 `Maintainer` 是必填项）
- 显式声明 `bundle.linux.deb.depends`：`libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0`、`libgtk-3-0t64 | libgtk-3-0`、`libayatana-appindicator3-1`

**构建入口**（`scripts/pack-tauri/build_linux_pyinstaller.sh`）

照抄 macOS 编排、去掉签名：`npm ci` → 版本同步 → console 构建 → `build_pyinstaller.sh`（PyInstaller 后端 + 内嵌 Python/Node runtime）→ `tauri build --bundles deb,appimage` → 两个产物归集到 `dist/`。`QWENPAW_SKIP_BACKEND_BUILD=1` 可在不重建后端的情况下重试打包。

**这次暴露并修复的五个构建机缺陷**

1. **Python 版本跟随引导解释器**：3.14 宿主会让内嵌运行时越出 `requires-python` 范围、装依赖失败。现在宿主 3.11–3.13 直接用宿主版本，否则回退 3.13 并打印提示。
2. **包里带上 CUDA 栈**：`whisper` 引入 torch，而 Linux 默认 wheel 通过 `libtorch_cpu.so` 的 `DT_NEEDED`（`libcudart.so.13`）硬依赖 CUDA runtime，`nvidia-*` 与 `triton` 合计约 4GB 且**事后删不掉**。改为 Linux 先装 CPU 版 torch，依赖需求即被满足，CUDA 载荷根本不进包。
3. **产品名里的空格打断 `linuxdeploy`**：AppDir 与资源路径（`usr/lib/<productName>/`）都带空格，linuxdeploy 对每个 ELF 调用的 `ldd` 会被拆参，`ldd` 退出码 1，整体报 `failed to run linuxdeploy` 且无细节。Linux 改用无空格的 `QwenPawDesktop`（窗口标题仍来自 `app.windows[0].title`，数据仍在 `~/.qwenpaw`）。
4. **一次失败会污染下一次**：Tauri 合并而非重建 AppDir，旧产品名的残留会留下；现在打包前先清空 bundle 目录。
5. **linuxdeploy 对内嵌 runtime 做依赖推导没有意义**：它会遍历 AppDir 里每个 ELF（内嵌 Python runtime 有数千个），任一解析失败即整体中止；而我们的树自带全部依赖。现在失败时自动去重 Tauri 的双份资源（一份真身 + 一个软链）、修正 `.DirIcon`、改用 `appimagetool` 直接压 AppDir。

**打包卫生**：一次构建会残留约 20GB 中间产物（`target/release/binaries` 9.7GB、`target/release/bundle/appimage_deb` 9.7GB），现在归集产物后自动清理（`QWENPAW_DESKTOP_KEEP_STAGING=1` 可保留）。

**CI**（`desktop-build.yml` 新增 `build-tauri-linux`，`ubuntu-24.04`）

安装 Linux 打包依赖、构建两种格式、用新增的 `.github/actions/verify-tauri-linux` 通过 Playwright 验证启动后的应用（配套 `scripts/verify/launch_tauri_linux.sh` 在 Xvfb 下运行 AppImage、等 `~/.qwenpaw/desktop_port`、导出 `BASE_URL`），记录校验和并上传 deb/AppImage/验证日志。`desktop_verify.py` 增加 `tauri-linux` 模式（Playwright WebKit）。

**文档**：`website/public/docs/desktop.{en,zh}.md` 增加 Linux 章节（系统要求、deb/AppImage 安装、首启数据目录、更新与卸载），并更新发布支持矩阵。

### 证据

环境：Ubuntu 26.04（GNOME 50，仅 Wayland），rustc 1.99.1，webkit2gtk-4.1 2.52.6，node v24.21.0，宿主 Python 3.14。

```text
$ bash scripts/pack-tauri/build_linux_pyinstaller.sh
  [INFO] python3 3.14 is outside 3.11-3.13; the bundled runtime will be staged as 3.13
== Installing CPU-only torch ==
== Step 3b: tauri bundling failed; packing the AppDir with appimagetool ==
    deduplicating usr/lib/QwenPaw Desktop -> symlink to QwenPawDesktop
976M  dist/QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b1-linux-x86_64.AppImage
1.3G  dist/QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b1-linux-x86_64.deb
```

```text
$ dpkg-deb -I dist/...deb
 Package: qwen-paw-desktop | Version: 2.3.0-beta.1 | Architecture: amd64
 Installed-Size: 3489035 | Maintainer: QwenPaw Contributors
 Depends: libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0, libgtk-3-0t64 | libgtk-3-0, libayatana-appindicator3-1, ...

$ dpkg-deb -c dist/...deb | grep -oE "usr/lib/[^/]+" | sort -u
usr/lib/QwenPawDesktop            # 只有一份资源树

$ apt-get install --dry-run ./dist/...deb | tail -3
The following NEW packages will be installed: qwen-paw-desktop
```

真机安装并启动：

```text
$ sudo apt install ./dist/...deb && qwenpaw-desktop
[backend] packaged command: /usr/lib/QwenPaw Desktop/binaries/qwenpaw-backend/qwenpaw-backend
[backend] bundled python runtime: .../python-runtime/python/bin/python3
[backend] bundled node runtime: .../node-runtime
[backend] shared runtime 2.3.0-beta.1 connected after 9534ms (launched=true)
```

窗口正常渲染、sidecar 连接成功、首启生成 `~/.qwenpaw`。

### 未完成项（独立 PR）

- 发布链（`desktop-publish.yml` / `desktop-promote.yml`、OSS 路径、updater manifest 增加 `linux-x86_64`）与 AppImage 自更新的客户端分支 —— PR2。
- arm64（`ubuntu-24.04-arm`）——x86_64 绿了之后跟进。
- AppImage 已构建、通过结构核验（有效 AppImage、desktop 条目正确、载荷已去重），并已在真机**成功启动**；CI 每次构建都会覆盖启动验证。

## Release Notes

- New: the desktop app now builds and ships for Linux (x86_64) as a `.deb` and an AppImage, alongside the existing Windows and macOS artifacts.
- New: on Linux, `apt install ./QwenPaw-*.deb` resolves the runtime dependencies (WebKitGTK 4.1, GTK 3, AppIndicator); the AppImage is a single portable file.

## Release Notes

- 新增：桌面版开始为 Linux（x86_64）构建并发布 `.deb` 与 AppImage，与现有 Windows/macOS 产物并列。
- 新增：Linux 上 `apt install ./QwenPaw-*.deb` 会自动补齐运行时依赖（WebKitGTK 4.1、GTK 3、AppIndicator）；AppImage 为单文件便携版。

prs.title: feat(local-models): add llama.cpp GPU controls and runtime auto-update
prs.body:
## Relationship

These three PRs form one feature, in merge order:

| Order | PR | Scope | Base / dependency |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **#8649 (this PR)** | llama.cpp GPU + auto-update | `main`; merge first |
| 2 | #8647 | managed MLX + auto-update | stacked on #8649 |
| 3 | #8648 | Console engine/GPU/MLX UI + auto-update | depends on #8649 + #8647; merge last |

Relates to #8646.

This PR is self-contained: it does **not** add MLX and does not depend on the other two.

## Description

QwenPaw Local currently tells users that CPU is used by default, even though the shipped macOS runtime already includes Metal. This PR exposes the detected accelerator and lets users control GPU offload for llama.cpp.

It builds on the plugin-owned local model manager introduced by #8499 (`plugins/provider/local-llamacpp/`): the accelerator probe, the GPU setting, the runtime auto-update loop and the management API all live in the plugin now, so the host `lifespan` no longer touches local-model state.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8646

**Security Considerations:** Auto-update adds outbound downloads from the existing QwenPaw runtime release endpoint and verifies the published checksum/manifest. No new inbound listeners or credentials are introduced.

## Summary

- Detect `Metal` / `CUDA` / `CPU` and the device name via `llama-server --list-devices`.
- Return `accelerator`, `device_name`, and runtime `version` from `GET /api/local-models/server`.
- Persist `gpu_acceleration`: `--gpu-layers auto` when enabled, `--gpu-layers 0` when disabled.
- Cache the accelerator and version, and invalidate both when the runtime is replaced.
- Add an `auto_update` setting (on by default) and a plugin-owned background loop that installs a newer llama.cpp runtime only when no local server is running. A running server defers the update — including one that starts while the release check is in flight — an in-flight download is left alone, and a missing runtime is never auto-installed.
- Expose `gpu_acceleration` and `auto_update` through `PUT /api/local-models/config`.
- Treat unsupported device backends (for example custom Vulkan builds) as CPU so the API/UI never claims an accelerator they cannot represent.
- Update the model docs and add backend/manager/API tests.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Tests

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests

## Testing

Manual verification on macOS 27.3 / Apple M5 Max:

- `llama-server --list-devices` reports `MTL0: Apple M5 Max`; a 3B GGUF offloads **29/29 layers** to Metal.
- With GPU acceleration off, the launched process contains `--gpu-layers 0`.
- The status endpoint returns `accelerator=metal`, `device_name=Apple M5 Max`, and the runtime version.

Automated coverage (all on this head):

- `tests/plugins/local_model` — accelerator detection (Metal, unknown backend, no runtime), `--gpu-layers 0` vs `auto`, version caching, the auto-update outcomes (started / deferred / disabled / up-to-date / active download, and deferral when a server starts during the release check), config persistence, and the management API round-trip.

## Evidence

Verified on macOS 27.3 / Apple M5 Max, including Metal offload and the CPU-forcing path.

Real run against the installed macOS runtime on this machine (Apple M5 Max, build 0.9.0-dev), driving the actual plugin code path (`LlamaCppBackend` pointed at the installed `bin/`):

```text
$ llama-server --list-devices
Available devices:
  BLAS: Accelerate (0 MiB, 0 MiB free)
  MTL0: Apple M5 Max (110100 MiB, 110100 MiB free)

$ llama-server --version
version: 0.9.0-dev (build 1, commit cd959ba)

>>> LlamaCppBackend(data_dir=...).get_accelerator_info()
{'accelerator': 'metal', 'device_name': 'Apple M5 Max'}
>>> LlamaCppBackend(data_dir=...).get_version()
'0.9.0-dev'
# second get_accelerator_info() call reuses the cache (no extra subprocess)
```

```text
$ python -m pytest tests/plugins/local_model tests/unit/plugins/test_local_model_migration.py -q
374 passed in 76.97s

$ python -m pytest tests/plugins/local_model/integration/test_local_models_router.py -q
8 passed in 6.26s

$ pre-commit run --files <changed files>
check python ast................................................Passed
check docstring is first.......................................Passed
fix python encoding pragma.....................................Passed
detect private key..............................................Passed
trim trailing whitespace........................................Passed
Add trailing commas.............................................Passed
mypy............................................................Passed
black...........................................................Passed
flake8..........................................................Passed
pylint..........................................................Passed
```

The console GPU switch, auto-update toggle, and MLX UI are in #8648.

## Additional Notes

- The branch is based on `main` and builds on the plugin-owned local model manager from #8499. The change itself is three commits: the feature, the model docs, and the follow-up that keeps a server started during the release check running.
- The runtime auto-update loop is owned by the plugin (`LocalProvider.activate` starts it, `close()` cancels it), so `src/qwenpaw/app/_app.py` is untouched.
- Cancelling an in-flight runtime download on shutdown is already covered by the plugin close path (`LocalModelManager.close()` closes both download controllers), so no separate host-lifespan hook is needed.
- The published runtime pin stays `piccolo-v1`; the shipped macOS bundle already includes Metal, so no runtime release is required for this change.
- The change is backwards compatible: clients that omit the new config fields keep GPU acceleration and auto-update enabled, and a stored `config.json` without the new keys loads with both defaults.

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [x] Ready for review

prs.title: feat(plugins): expose the semantic colour roles to plugin themes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#8071 asks for a plugin theme extension point. #8422 landed the first slice:
six roles (`bg`, `surface`, `surface-raised`, `border`, `text`,
`text-secondary`). Those cover the page frame, but not the semantic colour
surface a theme actually has to touch — a plugin that wants its own accent,
status colours, or the lower-contrast text and border tiers still has to reach
into raw `--app-*` names, which this closed API deliberately rejects.

This PR widens the closed set to the 31 semantic colour roles that
`console/src/styles/tokens.css` already defines and the console already
consumes, and keeps the compatibility story honest:

- the original six roles keep their current minimum SDK version, so plugins
  that already call `overrideTokens` are unaffected;
- the new roles sit behind `sdk.version >= 1.2.0` plus a `themeTokens`
  capability, so a plugin cannot silently depend on a role that an older host
  does not know.

Group 2 from #8071 (fifteen shape and layer roles: radius, shadow,
focus-ring, scrollbar, fill) stays out of this PR and is left for a separate
discussion, as requested.

## Evidence

Every role below is already read by the console. No component was changed and
no new colour was invented — this only opens roles that exist.

| family | role | representative consumer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| surface | `surface-subtle` | `layouts/index.module.less:324` |
| surface | `surface-sunken` | `components/RenderableCodeBlock/index.module.less:122` |
| surface | `shell-bg` | `layouts/dockableSidebar.module.less:13` |
| text | `text-tertiary` | `layouts/dockableSidebar.module.less:36` |
| text | `text-quaternary` | `layouts/index.module.less:254` |
| border | `border-subtle` | `layouts/index.module.less:53` |
| border | `border-strong` | `layouts/sidebarA.module.less:99` |
| accent | `accent` | `App.tsx:421` |
| accent | `accent-hover` | `App.tsx:422` |
| accent | `accent-soft` | `App.tsx:423` |
| status | `success-bg` | `components/LoopInput/index.module.less:57` |
| status | `warning-border` | `components/Chat/ToolCards/shared/offloadBanner.module.less:11` |
| status | `error-text` | `tauri/BackendLoadingPage.module.less:52` |

Both schemes are exercised rather than assumed: `themeTokens.test.ts` asserts
each role lands in the `:root` block with its light value and in the
`html.dark-mode` block with its dark value.

## Self-review

1. Overlapping registrations — `install.test.ts` keeps the existing
   "stacks per token and falls back on dispose" case, and the new semantic
   roles go through the same stacking path.
2. Switching scheme or preset while an override is active —
   `themeTokens.integration.test.ts` keeps "wins over the preset's inline
   `--app-surface` in both schemes" and "restores the preset when the plugin is
   unloaded".
3. Cleanup — "removes the element once every override is gone" and
   `disposeAll(pluginId)` both still clear the new roles.
4. Invalid input — a role missing one scheme and a genuinely unknown name both
   still throw; the unknown-name case now uses `not-a-role` so it does not
   accidentally test a role that became valid in this PR.
5. Backward compatibility — `sdk.version: 1.0.0` stays valid for the original
   six roles; `1.1.0` with `themeTokens` is rejected with a clear message;
   `1.2.0` with `themeTokens` is accepted.

## Test scope

- Console: `src/plugins` — 34 files, 459 passed, including the
  capability-gate cases, the out-of-order catalog regression and the PEP 440
  epoch case.
- Python: `tests/unit/app/routers` 1114 passed, 17 skipped, 2 failed and
  `tests/unit/plugins/test_sdk_entry_contract.py` passed. Both failures are
  `test_config_router.py` cases that need `src/qwenpaw/official_channels/`
  `index.json`; that path is generated, is not tracked in the checkout, and
  the two cases raise `FileNotFoundError` before reaching anything this PR
  touches.
- `tsc -b --noEmit`, eslint, prettier and pre-commit on the touched files.
- Browser: `python scripts/verify_theme_tokens.py` from `console/` (values in
  the follow-up section below).

## Coordination with #8764

#8764 also moves `SDK_VERSION` to `1.2.0` and touches
`src/qwenpaw/plugins/frontend/index.d.ts`. This PR needs the same version slot.
Whichever lands first, the other rebases onto it — the two changes are additive
and share only that version line, so the rebase is mechanical. If #8764 lands
first, this PR moves to 1.2.1; the gate reads `>= 1.2.0`, so the bump changes
no behaviour.


## Review follow-up

Five rounds are folded into `48fb8f1b`.

**One compatibility decision on both list paths.** The loader rejects an
incompatible SDK declaration before a plugin loads, but `/frontend_plugin`'s
disk fallback forwarded the manifest verbatim, so the console became the only
judge. `1.2.0rc1` and `1.2.0.dev1` are below 1.2.0 under PEP 440 and may not
carry `themeTokens`, yet the console's numeric comparison read them as 1.2.0
and accepted the extended roles. Both paths now call `_sdk_declaration()`,
which runs `validate_sdk()` and reports "not declared" when the declaration is
invalid. A pre-release without `themeTokens` is still forwarded unchanged, and
the six original roles need no declaration at all. Covered by
`test_frontend_list_rejects_incompatible_prerelease_on_disk[1.2.0rc1|1.2.0.dev1]`,
`test_frontend_list_keeps_a_prerelease_without_extended_capabilities` and
`test_frontend_list_applies_the_same_check_when_loaded`.

**The gate covers undeclared usage.** `validate_sdk` used to run only when a
plugin declared `themeTokens`, so a plugin could use a new role while declaring
nothing at all. `/frontend_plugin` now carries `sdk_version` and
`sdk_capabilities`, and `chat.theme.overrideTokens` consults that declaration
for every extended role: no declaration, an older version, or a missing
capability each throw with the role, the plugin, what is required and what was
declared. A manifest that cannot be read is treated as undeclared, so the check
fails closed. The original six roles keep their 1.0.0 minimum and need no
declaration.

**Components demonstrate it through the public API.** `themeVerify/main.tsx`
registers through `chat.theme.overrideTokens()` and disposes the handle it
returns; the internal store is not touched on the success path. Playwright
reads `getComputedStyle` for nine roles in both schemes — `bg`, `surface`,
`border`, `text`, `accent`, `error-text`, `success-bg`, `warning-border`,
`info-text` — plus the card, button and text probes: 23 expectations, no
failures. The harness also writes the user preset inline on `<html>` the way
`App.tsx` does, applies an override, changes the preset while it is active and
then disposes: the override keeps winning during the change, and after dispose
the page shows the *new* preset (`rgb(42, 42, 42)`), not the earlier one.
Stacked registrations still walk back across two disposes, and the same public
call with an undeclared plugin throws in the browser too.

Third-party scope is documented in `plugins/frontend/README.md`: this is a
colour surface, not a full UI theme. Only the listed roles participate, and
layout, spacing, typography, iconography, chart palettes and markup that
hardcodes `rgb()`/`rgba()` do not follow the override.

**A stale plugin list no longer clears a fresh declaration.** `fetchFrontendPlugins()`
stamps each list request with a monotonic id and only lets the newest request
rewrite the shared registry; an older response that resolves late is still
returned to its own caller but no longer overwrites newer declarations.
`executePluginScript()` additionally writes the `sdk_version` /
`sdk_capabilities` of the record it is about to evaluate back into the
registry before the entry script runs, so a load is bound to the record it came
from even if the shared map changed while the script was in flight. Covered by
`keeps the newest SDK declaration when an older list arrives late`, which
drives a deferred stale response and asserts the fresh plugin keeps
`themeTokens`; removing the request-id guard turns it red.

**The frontend no longer re-decides the SDK version.** `meetsMinVersion()` is
gone: `chat.theme.overrideTokens` now asks only whether the declaration carries
the `themeTokens` capability, which is the decision the backend already made
under PEP 440. `accepts a PEP 440 epoch version the backend already validated`
pins `0!1.2.0` as accepted, and the backend side of that premise is asserted in
`test_theme_tokens_capability_gates_on_sdk_version`. Re-introducing a raw-string
version comparison turns the epoch case red.

prs.title: fix(feishu): keep fenced code intact in table cards
prs.body:
## Description

**Problem.** The Feishu table-card path does not know about fenced code blocks. It parses `|` lines inside code as table rows. A table example in a code block becomes a native table. A shell pipeline splits the code block into broken card elements. The heading-to-bold step also turns comments inside code, such as `# count errors`, into `**count errors**`. `_send_text()` uses the same check. A reply whose only `|` lines are inside code takes the card path.

**Change.**
- `utils.py`: the new `_code_line_flags()` marks fence lines and the lines between them. A fence is `` ``` `` or `~~~` with up to 3 spaces of indent. It closes with the same character, at least the same length, and no info string.
- `_build_elements()` starts a table only on `|` lines outside code. `_convert_md_headings_to_bold()` skips lines inside code.
- The new `has_md_table_row()` uses the same rule. `platform._send_text()` now calls it instead of the raw `^\s*\|` search, so a reply with pipes only inside code goes out as a normal `post` message. This change also removes the unused `import re` from `platform.py`.
- `normalize_feishu_md()` (used for `post` messages and final stream cards) now uses the same fence state. It adds a newline before a fence only on lines outside code. It no longer splits a 4-backtick fence or a literal triple backtick inside code. Review feedback found this case.

Tables outside code blocks are parsed and sent as before.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8945
