prs.title: fix(loop): count each tool call once in ToolCallBudgetGate
prs.body:
## Description

**Problem.** `ToolCallBudgetGate` counts a tool call again on every later iteration of the same reply. agentscope 2.0 appends each iteration's blocks to one assistant message, and the gate adds all calls in that message on each new iteration. A `max_calls=5` budget stops the turn after 3 calls (counted 1, 3, 6). The text-only final step also counts the earlier calls again.

**Change.** The gate now keeps the ids of the tool calls it has counted in its per-turn state, and counts only ids it has not seen. This is the approach #8701 used for `DoomLoopGate`. Blocks without an id fall back to the block object, so checking the same snapshot again is still a no-op. The `iteration` cursor is no longer needed and is removed. `reset_turn()` clears the ids with the rest of the state.

The change depends on unique call ids. `OpenAIChatModelCompat` restarted the ids of tool calls recovered from text (`text_call_0`, `think_call_0`) for each model response. So it now adds a short random tag per response (`text_call_<tag>_<n>`). Review feedback found this case.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #8093 

The original issue described a mismatch between raw provider model records and resolved catalog/discovery capabilities. Since the first revision of this PR, upstream changes have fixed the main request-formatting and model-selection paths. The remaining problem is narrower: `view_image` can still add a misleading `"the model cannot see this image"` notice even when the resolved image capability is `true` and the formatter sends the image.

Add Platform-backed Web App access to local QwenPaw. Users connect a cloud account from Console, scan a QR code to sign in on their phone, and switch between cloud and connected workspaces.

The phone loads the selected Runtime's own versioned Console, including its existing model, thinking, and mode controls. A shared workspace menu and refresh action are available across Console pages. prs.body:
…g control (#8439)

feat(jobs): add thinking_level to JobRuntimeSpec for per-job reasoning control  Close #8439

## Description

Adds per-job reasoning control to cron jobs by introducing `thinking_level` (and optional `thinking_budget`) on `JobRuntimeSpec`.

Today every cron job inherits the agent-level thinking configuration. Users running many pipeline-style jobs (data collection, report generation, format conversion) must create a separate lightweight agent for every job just to turn reasoning off, which is error-prone and hard to maintain. This change lets each job choose:

- `inherit` (default): keep the existing agent/session behavior.
- `off`: disable reasoning for this job.
- `minimal` / `low` / `medium` / `high` / `xhigh` / `max`: force an effort level for this job.
- `budget`: use an explicit token budget via `thinking_budget`.

The value uses the existing `ThinkingLevel` enum instead of inventing a new `enabled` string. `CronExecutor` passes it through `request_context`, and `AgentBuilder` applies it to a request-scoped copy of `agent_config` after session-level thinking resolution and before model construction. It is never persisted to the shared chat/session.

Backward compatibility:
- New jobs default to `inherit`.
- Existing `jobs.json` files without the new fields load as `inherit`.
- Replacement requests from older clients that omit the fields preserve the stored values.
- `inherit` adds no `request_context` keys and leaves the agent config unchanged.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8439

**Security Considerations:** No authentication, channel, or secret-handling changes. The override is request-scoped and never written to the shared session or persisted agent config, so `share_session=True` cannot leak per-job reasoning settings into another conversation. `runtime` is authoritative in `CronExecutor`; stale or hand-written `cron_thinking_*` keys in the passthrough payload are removed. Invalid hand-written `request_context` overrides are ignored with a warning rather than reaching model construction. `off` remains best-effort, matching existing agent-level behavior: models without a disable control keep their defaults. `thinking_budget` is clamped by the existing model-card resolver.

prs.title: fix(runtime): reject chats until background startup completes (#8746)
prs.body:
## Description

During background startup, a chat submitted before the runtime is fully initialized was accepted (HTTP 200), but the agent was built against a half-projected workspace (`tools=1` in the logs) and the run hung before its first LLM call — no error, no timeout, no log. The stall was process-wide: every subsequent chat (new sessions, different models, Console and Feishu) was swallowed the same way until the process restarted. Fixes #8746.

This PR fixes the issue in four layers, so the user-visible failure mode is gone regardless of which internal wait was poisoned:

1. **Runtime readiness gate** — new `qwenpaw.utils.runtime_readiness`, a lifespan-bound, process-wide gate. The existing `startup_ready` only covers core agents; this gate is published only after the *entire* background startup (plugins, workspace projection, provider sync, skill pool) completes. Failures wake all waiters with a concrete reason. CLI/embedded callers that never run the lifespan are unaffected (inert gate).
2. **HTTP admission** — `POST /console/chat` (new sends, not reconnects) and `POST /console/chat/task` wait up to 5s for readiness (`QWENPAW_RUNTIME_READY_HTTP_TIMEOUT`) and then return **503 + `Retry-After: 5`** instead of admitting into a half-initialized runtime. Reconnects still attach to an existing stream as before.
3. **Single entry-point gate** — `AgentBuilder.build()` awaits runtime readiness (`QWENPAW_RUNTIME_READY_TIMEOUT`, default 180s), covering Console, all channels, cron and sub-agents in one shared point.
4. **No more silent stalls**:
   - `MultiAgentManager.get_agent()` no longer returns a workspace in the window between publication and the plugin `workspace_created` hooks (the half-projected toolkit behind the `tools=1` build).
   - Pre-model watchdog (`QWENPAW_AGENT_PRE_MODEL_TIMEOUT`, default 180s): if a built agent produces no non-heartbeat event before its first model call, the run ends with a visible `AGENT_PRE_MODEL_STALL` error and a task-stack dump. Heartbeats deliberately do **not** disarm it (they prove the transport is alive, not that the model call started).
   - Rate-limiter registry hardening: the module-level `asyncio.Lock` (which could become a no-wait process-wide wait if its lazily-created loop went stale) is replaced by a thread lock, and each limiter is bound to its event loop — cross-loop reuse now raises an immediate `RuntimeError` instead of deadlocking, and closed-loop limiters are replaced.

`/healthz` now additionally reports `runtime_ready` and `runtime_startup_error`, so monitoring can distinguish "core agents loaded" from "background startup finished".

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8746

**Security Considerations:** The task-stack dump logs only `file:line` and coroutine names — no prompt content, message bodies or credentials. The readiness gate does not touch authentication/channel-trust logic. New environment-variable reads reject non-numeric and negative values and fall back to defaults.

## Additional Notes

- Deliberate behavior choice worth highlighting: **channels/cron/sub-agents wait up to 180s for readiness instead of failing fast** (messages may be delayed but must not be lost), while the HTTP chat entry point fails fast with a 503 after 5s (holding a browser connection open through a 90s+ cold start is worse). Both budgets are configurable.
- `QWENPAW_AGENT_PRE_MODEL_TIMEOUT` defaults to 180s to match the channel-side wait budget, so a run waiting out startup is not misreported as stalled.
- The readiness gate lives in a standalone module rather than as an `app.state` field so non-HTTP entry points (channels, cron, sub-agents) can consult it without importing the FastAPI application.

prs.title: fix(channels): decode Slack upload file names from locators
prs.body:
## Description

Files sent to Slack with `send_file_to_user` show up under their percent-encoded names when the name has non-ASCII characters or spaces: `附件 报告.docx` is uploaded as `%E9%99%84%E4%BB%B6%20%E6%8A%A5%E5%91%8A.docx`, `my report.docx` as `my%20report.docx`. This is the Slack side of #8752 / #8753: the tool-result part has only the `file://` locator (which `URLSource` percent-encodes) and no `filename`, and `_send_file` took `os.path.basename(url)` without decoding. The file itself was found because `_resolve_local_file_path` already decodes; only the name passed to `files.getUploadURLExternal` and the title were wrong.

`_send_file` now takes the name from the decoded local path, and for remote URLs from the unquoted basename of the URL path (so a query string is no longer part of the name either). An explicit `filename` on the part still wins.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8752 (same bug, fixed for Feishu in #8753)

**Security Considerations:** None. Only the display name changes; which file is read is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(providers): allow fallback for 4xx quota errors
prs.body:
## Summary

Some providers return HTTP 400 with a quota or rate-limit message instead of
HTTP 429 when the primary model's quota is exhausted. The shared error policy
classified these responses as `bad_request`, which made them ineligible for
cross-model fallback.

This change recognizes structured provider error codes and narrowly scoped
quota and rate-limit messages on 4xx responses before the generic
`bad_request` fallback, allowing `FallbackChatModel` to try the next
configured model without retrying an exhausted quota.

## Changes

- Read normalized provider `code` and `type` values from structured error
  payloads (both nested `error` objects and top-level payloads), with complete
  semantic phrases (including `quota_exceeded` and `too_many_requests`) as the
  message fallback.
- Classify non-429 quota exhaustion as `quota_exceeded`, allowing fallback
  without retrying the same model.
- Preserve retry behavior for standard HTTP 429 and explicit rate-limit
  errors, along with the existing priority of authentication,
  model-not-found, request-size, context-overflow, and content-safety
  classification.
- Add negative tests proving that unrelated quota and rate-limit parameter
  errors remain `bad_request`, plus regression tests covering top-level
  structured `code` payloads and `AsyncOpenAI` HTTP 400 string-valued
  `{"error": "quota_exceeded"}` responses.
- Add a production-style `FallbackChatModel` to `RetryChatModel` regression
  test proving that the primary and fallback models are each called once.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest tests/unit/providers/test_model_error_policy.py tests/unit/providers/test_fallback_chat_model.py -q`
  - 77 passed.
- `pre-commit run --files src/qwenpaw/providers/model_error_policy.py tests/unit/providers/test_model_error_policy.py`
  - All applicable hooks passed (`mypy`, `black`, `flake8`, `pylint`, etc.).

Fixes #8776

prs.title: fix(models): scope /model changes to the current conversation
prs.body:
## Description

In channels, `/model <provider>:<model>` previously updated the agent default. Conversations with a pinned model kept using it, so users could not recover through the channel when that model became unavailable.

- Persist `/model <provider>:<model>` on the current chat. A valid switch sent as the first channel message creates the chat before saving the selection.
- Make `/model reset` clear the chat's model and thinking overrides, matching Console's restore action. The chat then inherits the agent default or, if unset, the global default.
- Update command and TUI help to describe the conversation scope.

Fixes #8725.

Model writes are scoped to the current workspace, channel, session, and user. The slash command now changes the chat's model. Agent defaults can be edited under Runtime Configuration → Primary Model.

The `qwenpaw cron` commands built their base URL as `http://{host}:{port}`. prs.title: fix(crons): persist cron and heartbeat token usage to turn records
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron and heartbeat runs drive `workspace.stream_query` directly instead of going through `Channel.consume_one`, so their token usage was never committed to the session's turn records. The console usage panel undercounts all scheduled task consumption: cron jobs (daily digests, reminders) and heartbeat runs make model calls whose usage never lands in the persisted turn records, even though the session data model already distinguishes cron sessions from chat turns.

Failed runs had a second, subtler problem: staged usage was never dropped, so a failed run's tokens could leak into the next run on the same reused session.

Fixes #8705

## Description

- Extract `commit_turn_usage` / `discard_turn_usage` into `qwenpaw.token_usage.turn_usage`:
  - `commit_turn_usage` resolves and persists one finished turn's usage, never raises
  - `discard_turn_usage` drops staged usage when a run does not finish normally
- `Channel._commit_turn_usage` and `_clear_session_turn_usage` now reuse the shared helpers (no behavior change)
- Cron executor: commit usage after a successful run; discard on timeout / cancel / error
- Heartbeat: same treatment for all three `stream_query` sites
- New e2e regression: `e2e/tests/test_cron_usage.py` (auto-skips without a model API key via `requires_llm`)

prs.title: refactor(runtime): unify session configuration for ACP and native execution
prs.body:
ACP and native execution now use the same session configuration snapshot. Two sessions of one agent can select different settings without changing saved defaults or other processes.

- Define session settings once in `SessionConfig`, inherited by `AgentProfileConfig`. Core `RuntimeParameters` merges global defaults, agent settings, startup defaults, and session overrides, preserving omitted fields and explicit `false`, `null`, and empty lists. ACP inherits the constructor and translates protocol inputs; new session fields require no ACP mapping.
- Support workspace/project directories, models, permissions, coding mode, goal, mission, and loop gates. Keep existing ACP flags, metadata, model/permission setters, and load/resume behavior. Resetting `qwenpaw.config` clears that layer without confusing it with retained legacy metadata.
- Let registered modes declare configuration or entry commands. Resolve saved mode state and Mission's pinned directories before constructing the execution snapshot. Remove duplicated Builder precedence, ACP-specific runtime hooks, the global stop-handler bridge, and obsolete state-loading entry points.
- Keep gate state and resource ownership session-local. Workspace replacements are prepared before publication; failed service or MCP preparation preserves the previous owner. Switching modes replaces derived defaults rather than accumulating them.
- Use one effective iteration limit throughout QwenPaw. Positive limits may exceed 500; disabling the iteration gate removes the fallback limit while cancellation and other enabled stopping conditions remain effective.

Validation: concurrent session and separate-process isolation, legacy restore semantics, no override persistence, failed resource replacement, restored mode switching, Mission directory consistency, ACP stdio lifecycle, and real execution beyond 100 iterations with cancellation. Existing regressions were extended and obsolete helper/forwarding tests removed. English and Chinese documentation matches the final behavior.

Results: 4,031 regression tests passed and 14 were skipped. The three frozen-worker tests needed the ignored official-channel bundle generated by the existing build hook, then passed on rerun. After the final parameter API cleanup, all 32 affected configuration/ACP tests passed again. Pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed.

issues.title: [Bug]: Chat message box doesn't get focus back when a turn ends after the page reconnected
issues.body:
### Affected component

web dashboard

### Severity

S3 - minor issue

### Current behavior

This is the operator reconnect case raised on #11661, which returns focus to the chat message box when a turn ends. It's outside that PR's scope, so I'm filing it separately, as a reviewer suggested there. It applies with #11661 merged; on `master` today the box never gets focus back after a turn.

Since #12376 (merged after the capture on #11661), a reconnect during a turn shows the turn as running, so the original steps now give the first sequence below; the order described on #11661, where the turn ends before the reconnect, is covered after it.

On the operator dashboard (no pairing), if the chat's socket closes during a turn, the page reconnects, sees from `/state` that the turn is still running (#12376), and shows it as running. When the turn ends and the answer loads, the box is enabled and the status reads "Connected", but focus stays on `body`. Text typed without clicking goes nowhere.

A focus log from the browser shows why. Each reload of the conversation clears `hydratedSessionId` ([`AgentContext.tsx` L560](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/74ba6e9647877be8edcb65514d185975d88dd31d/web/src/contexts/AgentContext.tsx#L560)), which disables the box until the reload finishes. Twice, #11661's effect focuses the box right after the update that starts such a reload, disarms, and then loses the focus when the reload disables it:

1. When the socket reopens, the page is connected again and the transcript from before the close still counts as loaded, so the box is briefly enabled. The refocus effect focuses it and disarms. The reconnect's reload ([L1121-L1123](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/74ba6e9647877be8edcb65514d185975d88dd31d/web/src/contexts/AgentContext.tsx#L1121-L1123)) then disables the box, which drops the focus. That reload finds the turn still running (#12376), which re-arms the refocus, so this one is harmless.
2. When the watched turn ends, `AgentContext` clears `typing` and starts the reload that loads the answer, in the same update ([L719-L721](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/74ba6e9647877be8edcb65514d185975d88dd31d/web/src/contexts/AgentContext.tsx#L719-L721)). The render after that update has `typing` false and the box still enabled. The effect focuses the box and disarms, and the reload disables it again. This time nothing re-arms the refocus, so when the reload finishes and the box is enabled, focus stays on `body`.

Log from reproducing the steps below, in Chromium (milliseconds since page load; Firefox shows the same sequence):

```text
25140  close requested (code 4000)
26170  focusin   TEXTAREA
26178  focusout  TEXTAREA (disabled)      <- socket reopened, then the reload locks the box
44284  focusin   TEXTAREA
44287  focusout  TEXTAREA (disabled)      <- turn ended, then the answer's reload locks the box
       (box enabled, "Connected"; focus on body; typed text lost)
```

The order raised on #11661, where the turn ends before the page reconnects, loses focus the same way, at the reconnect. The box is focused when the socket reopens and disabled by the reload, as in step 1. That reload finds no running turn and loads the answer, so nothing re-arms the refocus. To test this, the browser was kept offline after the close until the turn had ended on the server. Chromium (Firefox shows the same sequence):

```text
46448  close requested (code 4000), browser offline
71509  browser back online (the turn ended on the server meanwhile)
77498  focusin   TEXTAREA
77506  focusout  TEXTAREA (disabled)      <- socket reopened, then the reload locks the box
       (answer loaded; box enabled, "Connected"; focus on body; typed text lost)
```

### Expected behavior

When the turn ends and the box is usable again, it has focus, as it does after a turn on a socket that stayed open (#11661). The same rules apply: it isn't focused if the pane is hidden or the user focused another control in the meantime.

One possible approach: keep the refocus armed until focus actually lands in an enabled box. For example, re-arm when the box loses focus because it was disabled (focus goes to `body`), or don't treat the box as usable while the answer's reload is pending.

### Steps to reproduce

```text
1. Operator dashboard (no pairing), SQLite sessions, a model that replies slowly.
2. Open the chat, send a prompt, and while the turn is running close the
   page's chat socket (the test closes it through a Playwright WebSocket
   route with code 4000, which the page sees as a close from the server).
   The page reconnects within about a second and shows the turn as running.
3. Wait for the answer, then type without clicking.
4. The box is enabled and the status is "Connected", but focus is on body and
   the typed text doesn't appear.

For the turn ending before the reconnect: in step 2, keep the page from
reconnecting until the turn has ended (the test sets the browser offline just
before the close and back online 25 s later); then do steps 3 and 4.
```

### Impact

After a reconnect, the next keystrokes are lost until the user clicks the message box.

### Logs / stack traces

The focus log is above. Tested on `master` with #11661 applied (see the version below). The test records focus with `focusin`/`focusout` listeners and `document.activeElement`.

### ZeroClaw version

#11661's head (`dbdceaa03`) merged with `master` at `74ba6e964`, built as a slim daemon with the embedded dashboard. Tested with Playwright 1.52 in headless Chromium 136 and Firefox 137.

### Rust version

_No response_

### Operating system

Linux (amd64); headless Chromium and Firefox

### Regression?

No, first-time setup

### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I reproduced this on the latest master branch or latest release.
- [x] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

issues.body:
### Affected component

web dashboard

### Severity

S3 - minor issue

### Current behavior

In an agent chat in the web dashboard, the message box loses focus while the agent replies and does not get it back when the reply finishes, so continuing the conversation needs a click on the box. Pressing Tab reaches it only after cycling through the other controls on the page (more than ten presses).

In `web/src/pages/AgentChat.tsx`, `handleSend` focuses the textarea, but the textarea is then disabled for the whole turn (`disabled={!connected || typing || !hydrated}`), which drops its focus. Nothing re-focuses it when `typing` returns to false; the only other `focus()` calls are after an image upload and after choosing a slash command.

This started with #6220 (first released in v0.7.5), which added the input lock during a turn. Before that, the textarea stayed enabled and kept the focus `handleSend` gave it.

### Expected behavior

When a turn ends (a completed reply, an error, or the Stop button), focus returns to the message box of the visible chat, so the user can keep typing. It should not take focus from a control the user deliberately moved to during the turn (another chat tab, the model picker, a dialog), so it should only re-focus when nothing else has focus (the document body). Chat tabs that are open but hidden keep running turns, so a turn ending in a hidden tab should not move focus.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# 1. Open the gateway web dashboard and an agent chat (seen in Firefox).
# 2. Type a message and press Enter.
# 3. Wait for the reply to finish.
# 4. Start typing: nothing goes into the message box until it is clicked.
```

Affected users: everyone using the web dashboard chat.

issues.body:
### Tracker kind

roadmap / epic tracker

### Purpose

This is ZeroClaw's roadmap to v1.0.0: the order of releases, their target dates, and what each one is for. It replaces the version plan in [FND-001 §6](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.html), which stays as the architectural direction. I'll update it after each release.

**How versions work until 1.0.** A release that needs a config migration, a plugin rebuild or a changed CLI command is a minor release (0.9.x → 0.10.0). Everything else, new features included, is a patch release (0.9.x → 0.9.x+1). The rule is in [FND-001 §4.4.1](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.html).

**Releases, in order.** The dates are targets. Work that isn't ready moves to the next release, and this issue will say so.

**v0.10.0 happens only if it's needed.** It exists only if something that needs a migration, a plugin rebuild or a changed CLI command is merged before 1.0. If nothing like that is merged by 2026-12-09, there is no v0.10.0, and the next release after v0.9.x is v1.0.0-rc.1.

| Release | Target | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| v0.9.1 | week of 2026-11-30 | Fixes and features merged since v0.9.0, with no config migration. [Milestone](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/milestone/33) |
| v0.9.x | as needed | Fixes, and changes that need no migration. Candidates: the refactors #12444, #12445 and #12446, once reviewed. |
| v0.10.0 (only if needed) | 2026-12-16 | The last chance to break compatibility before 1.0: config schema changes, removals from the default binary, CLI renames. The main candidate is the provider registry with the V5 config schema (#12448, #12454, #12455, #12456, #12457, #12450, #12452, #12453). It ships in v0.10.0 if its review is complete with no open change requests and its upgrade paths are tested. Otherwise it is reconsidered after 1.0. |
| v1.0.0-rc.1 | 2027-01-06 | Fixes only. The config schema, the plugin interface (WIT) and the RPC protocol are frozen from here, or from v0.10.0 if there is one. |
| v1.0.0 | 2027-01-27 | The first stable release, once the checklist below is complete. |

**v1.0.0 checklist (proposed; comments welcome here):**

- [ ] The config schema, CLI, plugin interface (WIT) and RPC and relay protocols are stable, with no breaking change before 2.0.
- [ ] A stability-tiers page says which crates, channels and tools are Stable, Beta or Experimental (FND-001 Phase 4, D5).
- [ ] The plugin SDK docs are good enough for someone outside the team to build and install a plugin.
- [ ] CI tracks the release binary's size against a target.
- [ ] Built-ins that should leave the default binary have left, or are deprecated with upgrade notes.
- [ ] Release branches run CI, so 1.0.x patch releases can ship from a release branch.

FND-001 also plans every channel and about 60 tools as plugins (Phase 4), and a separate gateway binary (Phase 3). I'm proposing that those follow in 1.x where they don't break anything, rather than holding 1.0 for them.

### Scope and non-goals

In scope: the order of releases, their target dates, what each one is for, and the v1.0.0 checklist.

Out of scope: progress on individual PRs (each PR and tracker carries its own), design decisions (RFCs and #8692), the architectural direction (FND-001), and anything after 1.0. A new roadmap issue replaces this one when v1.0.0 ships.

### Linked work

- **Agreed designs and where they are being implemented:** #10330
- **Designs still being decided:** #8692
- **Everything in flight:** [open trackers](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues?q=is%3Aopen+label%3Atype%3Atracker)
- **Not scheduled yet:** #9600 (session persistence), #8600 (choosing any of a provider's models per chat), #6489 (moving channels and tools to plugins), #7432 (runtime, dashboard sign-in and gateway delivery)
- **Earlier roadmap requests this answers:** #3839, #4365
- **Getting something onto the roadmap:** open an issue, or an RFC if the change crosses one of the triggers in [FND-003 §8](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/foundations/fnd-003-governance.html). For a large agreed change that lands as stacked PRs, ask here for an integration slot at the start of a release cycle, and a maintainer will review and queue the layers in order.

### Routing evidence and next decision

Reason to stay open: this is the roadmap until v1.0.0.

Next decision: by 2026-12-09, whether v0.10.0 is needed and what's in it, so that every change in it can ship with upgrade notes.

Owner: @JordanTheJet. Updated after each release.

prs.title: fix(providers): carry the paired tool name on recovered tool results
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The damaged-envelope recovery branch added in #12188 restored `tool_call_id` but still constructed the `NativeMessage` with `name: None`.
  - Groq rejects every role-tool message without `name` (`Tools should have a name!`), so replaying an already-damaged conversation on Groq kept failing even after the id was restored.
  - The recovery branch now resolves `name` through the same `tool_name_map` lookup the whole-envelope branch uses, keyed by the raw id recovered from the leading envelope.
- **Scope boundary:** only the partially-parseable-envelope branch of `OpenAiCompatibleModelProvider::convert_messages_for_native()`. No channel normalization, no contract/id-rewrite behavior, no change to the whole-envelope path; undamaged conversations serialize exactly as before (`name` stays unset there).
- **Blast radius:** strict OpenAI-compatible providers that require `name` on role-tool messages (Groq class), and only sessions already carrying the pre-#12188 corrupted form; new corruption is prevented by the channels half of #12188.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12665. Depends on #12188 — the first three commits on this branch are that PR's head `c36b3c068`; only the last commit `24a0cced8` is new.

prs.title: fix(channels/discord): retry gateway connect failures instead of parking
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The supervised Discord listener parks (stops restarting until a config change or daemon restart) when its error is classified non-retryable. For Discord, that classification falls back to `zeroclaw_providers::reliable::is_non_retryable`, whose text heuristic treats any status-shaped 4xx number in the message as an HTTP client error.
  - A failed gateway reconnect produces `TCP connect to gateway-us-east1-b.discord.gg:443` (context added by `ws_connect_with_proxy`). The heuristic reads the port `443` as an HTTP 4xx status, so a single transient network drop during a reconnect parks the listener and the bot stays offline until someone restarts the daemon. The health endpoint keeps reporting `channel:discord.main` as `error` the whole time.
  - This PR classifies any error whose cause chain contains an `std::io::Error` (DNS, TCP connect, TLS, socket I/O) as retryable before the text heuristic runs. Those are transport failures; none of them is the HTTP preflight failure the parking was introduced for.
- **Scope boundary:** `DiscordListenerFatalError` still parks first. HTTP preflight failures (typed `reqwest` status errors, or text-only errors such as `401 Unauthorized`, with no transport cause) keep exactly the classification they had. The shared provider heuristic in `reliable.rs` is not changed, so provider retry behavior is untouched. No other channel is affected (only Discord uses this classifier). No config surface.
- **Blast radius:** Discord listener supervision only: transport failures now back off through the existing retry path (`reliability.channel_initial_backoff_secs` / `channel_max_backoff_secs`) instead of parking. The worst case for a genuinely permanent transport failure (for example a firewall that always rejects the gateway) is a reconnect attempt per backoff interval, which is the behavior every other channel already has.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #6834 (introduced parking for fatal gateway preflight failures; this narrows it back to that intent).

### What this does, simply

A ZeroClaw Discord bot is supposed to reconnect on its own after a network hiccup. In one case it gives up for good: when the reconnect fails while opening the TCP connection to Discord's gateway. The error message contains the gateway address `...discord.gg:443`, and an error classifier built for HTTP responses mistakes the port number 443 for an HTTP "client error" status, decides retrying is pointless, and stops the Discord channel until the daemon is restarted. The process stays alive, so supervisors that restart on exit do not notice, and the bot just shows as offline.

With this change, network-level failures are always retried with the normal backoff, so the bot comes back by itself once the network does. Real configuration problems, such as a rejected token, still stop the channel as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `discord`
- **Setup / preconditions:** A working Discord channel on Linux with root (for `iptables`). Find the gateway addresses with `getent ahostsv4 gateway.discord.gg`; the `discord.com` REST API resolves to different addresses and must stay reachable.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Start the daemon and wait until `/health` shows `channel:discord.main` with `"status":"ok"`.
  2. Reject TCP 443 to the gateway addresses only: `iptables -I OUTPUT -p tcp -d <gateway-ip> --dport 443 -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset` for each.
  3. Wait until the next heartbeat drops the socket and the reconnect attempt fails (about one minute).
  4. Remove the rules and watch `/health` for three minutes.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the listener backs off and retries; after the rules are removed it resumes and `/health` returns to `"status":"ok"`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the trace records `channel listener hit non-retryable error; waiting for config change or shutdown` with `error: "TCP connect to gateway-...discord.gg:443"`, and `/health` stays at `"status":"error"` after the rules are removed until the daemon is restarted.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI` clippy and `cargo nextest` cover the classifier and the supervised-listener tests added here; the existing supervised-listener tests for Discord parking keep covering the fatal paths.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI cannot drop a live Discord gateway connection; the manual A/B below covers that.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  Run on macOS (aarch64), `rustc 1.99.1`, at the PR head on top of `master` d4a5d2a.

  ```text
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check
  (no output)

  $ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets -- -D warnings
      Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 47s

  $ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- discord_listener_ supervised_listener_
  test orchestrator::tests::discord_listener_fatal_error_stays_non_retryable ... ok
  test orchestrator::tests::discord_listener_retries_network_failures_that_name_a_port ... ok
  test orchestrator::tests::discord_listener_still_parks_on_a_text_only_client_error ... ok
  test orchestrator::tests::supervised_listener_does_not_restart_on_non_retryable_discord_http_error ... ok
  test orchestrator::tests::supervised_listener_enters_retry_path_on_discord_gateway_connect_failure ... ok
  test orchestrator::tests::supervised_listener_enters_retry_path_on_discord_gateway_rate_limit ... ok
  test orchestrator::tests::supervised_listener_does_not_restart_on_fatal_discord_gateway_close_code ... ok
  test result: ok. 17 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 2098 filtered out

  # Same test with the fix removed (red check):
  $ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib discord_listener_retries
  a failed gateway connect must be retried, not parked
  test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed

  $ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs
  Comment hygiene gate passed.

  $ bash scripts/check-pr-title.sh "fix(channels/discord): retry gateway connect failures instead of parking"
  (exit 0)
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Found and A/B-tested on a real deployment (a v0.9.0 build on an aarch64 Linux device, Discord channel with a live bot; the classifier is identical on `master`).

  The original outage, from the runtime trace (UTC): Discord closed the gateway normally, the resume connect failed, and the listener parked; it stayed down for about six hours until the daemon was restarted by hand.

  ```text
  23:54:55 Channel discord exited unexpectedly; restarting
  23:55:01 connecting to gateway... (resume: true)
  23:55:31 ERROR channel listener hit non-retryable error; waiting for config change or shutdown
           error: "TCP connect to gateway-us-east1-b.discord.gg:443"
  ```

  Reproduction (steps in "How you can test": TCP 443 rejected to the five gateway addresses only, REST API left reachable, then unblocked), same device, same config, only the binary swapped:

  ```text
  BEFORE (without this fix)
  11:44:38 connected: status=ok
  11:44:38 gateway blocked
  11:46:15 during block: status=error
  11:46:16 gateway unblocked
  11:49:25 3 min after unblock: status=error restart_count=1, 1 new "non-retryable error" trace event  (parked)

  AFTER (with this fix)
  11:49:46 connected: status=ok
  11:49:46 gateway blocked
  11:51:24 during block: status=error
  11:51:24 gateway unblocked
  11:51:30 6 s after unblock: status=ok restart_count=5, no "non-retryable" event
  ```

  Listener timeline from the trace for the AFTER run (UTC), showing the same error now going through the backoff path:

  ```text
  06:50:20 Channel discord exited unexpectedly; restarting
  06:50:23 channel listener error; restarting | TCP connect to gateway-us-east1-c.discord.gg:443
  06:50:27 channel listener error; restarting | TCP connect to gateway-us-east1-c.discord.gg:443
  06:50:36 channel listener error; restarting | TCP connect to gateway-us-east1-c.discord.gg:443
  06:50:53 channel listener error; restarting | TCP connect to gateway-us-east1-c.discord.gg:443
  06:51:25 connecting to gateway...
  06:51:26 discord RESUMED received
  ```

  Blocking all of Discord (API included) does not reproduce the bug: the reconnect then fails at the HTTP preflight, whose error text has no port and is already retried. The bug needs the preflight to succeed and the gateway TCP connect to fail, which is what a brief route or DNS hiccup to the gateway host looks like.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no interface change; the observable effect is the health status and the bot's presence).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Unit and gate evidence at the PR head (one commit on `master` d4a5d2a). Manual A/B on a v0.9.0 build with the same one-function change applied; interface `channel` = `discord`, evidence from `/health` and the runtime trace.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Exact log output above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** See the manual A/B above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The full workspace suite and `--features ci-all` clippy are left to CI; locally I ran clippy on the changed crate and the Discord supervision tests.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** repeated `channel listener error; restarting` events for Discord with a transport error, at the configured backoff, when the gateway is unreachable for a long time (expected; previously the channel parked silently).

prs.title: feat(skills): pass literal arguments to executables without a shell
prs.body:
## Summary

Related #12625. Base: `master`.

- A `shell` or `script` skill can declare a fixed executable and an `argv` array in `SKILL.toml`. Audit and loading use the same declaration rules: choose `argv` or `command`, not both.
- Each array element binds once and stays one OS argument. The native executor checks the named executable, arguments, runtime and selected sandbox before starting the process; unsupported configurations refuse the call instead of falling back to a shell.
- Scope: core enablement only. This does not add a vendor tool, publish a registry skill, or supersede the built-in fallback in #11076. Existing `command` manifests retain their shell path. Shared command-policy checks and runtime tool registration are the main areas to review for regressions.

### What this does, simply

A skill that hands a paragraph to a CLI shouldn’t have to turn it into a shell command. With `argv`, line breaks and quotes are part of the argument the program reads. The skill author still chooses the program and its options; the manifest does not grant permission to run it.

## Testing

### How you can test

**Reviewer testing requested:** Yes. On native Linux, run the two commands below from the checkout. These are runtime-level tests with a disposable recorder: no provider credentials, installed skill or live settings needed. On the pre-feature revision, an `argv`-only manifest was rejected at audit for lacking `command`. On the draft, both registered tool kinds should return the recorder’s exact argument bytes. Changing only the executable allowlist should produce a policy denial and no startup marker; restoring it should make the same recorder run.

### How I tested

On `9491a15e9`, the unchanged `dependency_boundary` test passed against the updated checkout (standalone fixture, using Cargo metadata). `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and diff hygiene passed. No dependency exception was added.

The following registered literal/legacy runtime results were recorded on the **previous head**, `a24505039`:

```text
cargo test --offline --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --test skill_literal_argv
test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

cargo test --offline --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tools::skill_tool::tests::skill_shell_
test result: ok. 12 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 6326 filtered out
```

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` passed. No full-workspace suite or cross-platform run is claimed. Visual evidence: N/A (manifest/runtime behavior; no rendered interface change). The positive fixture uses an explicit no-OS-sandbox backend; its result proves argument transport and refusal before startup, not OS containment.

**Before marking this ready:**

- [ ] Repeat the registered allow/deny pair under real OS isolation. Verify the selected sandbox reaches the direct executor.
- [ ] Review executable resolution and the authority of allowed CLIs that can invoke other programs. A literal argument is not a restriction on what the receiving CLI can do.
- [ ] Review the remaining runtime registration and process supervision under ADR-016. The declaration and literal-argument binder now live in the existing `zeroclaw-tools` crate; the runtime takes no new normal dependency.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- New capability: **Yes** — opt-in direct execution, with a fixed executable and an exact allowlist entry. A supervised operation requiring per-command approval is refused; a manifest is not operator approval.
- New external network calls: **No**. Changes to secret or credential handling: **No**. Personal data in diff, fixtures or docs: **No**.
- Untrusted text handling: **Yes** — free-form input is passed as an argument without shell evaluation. The receiving program still interprets its own arguments.

## Compatibility

Existing manifests need no migration. **Manifest surface change:** `argv` is an alternative to `command` for `shell` and `script`; see `docs/book/src/tools/skills.md`. No new CLI flag, environment variable or toolchain floor.

## Rollback

Stop invoking or remove the new `argv` declaration from the affected skill; there is no global feature flag. Do not interpolate untrusted text into a shell command as a workaround. If merged, revert this PR through the normal revert path. Regression signals: an existing `command` skill fails, the recorder receives different bytes, or a denied recorder creates its startup marker.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** The memory-policy decorator now forwards the full write options and the agent UUID to the underlying backend after applying the existing content and write policy. - **Scope boundary:** No changes to the SQLite schema, type extraction, consolidation prompts, memory scope, or config defaults. No backfill of missed entries.
- **Blast radius:** Agent-attributed writes through `ScannedMemory`, including WebUI turn-end consolidation. Other backend capabilities and write policy are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

When typed memory is enabled, a WebUI chat can finish successfully even though its summary and durable facts were never saved. The wrapper that checks writes for unsafe content didn't pass the complete combination of type and agent attribution into SQLite. This change passes both through, without skipping those checks.

prs.title: fix(zerocode): show temporary local file-write diffs
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions).
- **What changed and why:**
  - Eligible local ZeroCode `file_write` calls show red removed lines and green added lines from a bounded observation before a successful write. Overwrite cards show `Overwrote existing file`, and six-row previews offer Show all when rows are omitted.
  - Previous text uses a private local notification outside ordinary tool results, model messages and saved history. The private inbox and view share a five-minute deadline. The runtime drops the entire pair if `scrub_credentials` changes either the previous or written text, so ZeroCode falls back to the labelled preview.
  - Direct ACP clients stop constructing creation diffs from write input across live events, restored history and approval requests. Capture admission uses the executor's canonical live resolver, native provenance, exclusions and read-approval policy.
- **Scope boundary:** Capture requires existing native read authority, workspace containment and supported readable text. It adds no durable diff history or remote/direct-ACP diff transport. The pre-write observation cannot guarantee the exact inode contents replaced by a concurrent external writer. ACP separation, Unicode format-character handling and tab presentation are outside this revision.
- **Blast radius:** File-write observation, transient native RPC events, local ZeroCode Chat/Code cards and ACP write presentation. File authorization and atomic replacement remain in force. No new dependency, configuration or durable schema is introduced. Runtime adapters stay in the owners covered by the temporary file-write diff exception approved in [#11436](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11436#pullrequestreview-5474715854).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10294. Remote and direct ACP diffs remain unavailable, so this PR does not close the issue.
- **Release notes:** ZeroCode can show temporary local file-write diffs when existing read authority permits capture and credential scrubbing leaves both sides unchanged. ACP clients, including Zed, no longer get a `file_write` creation-diff preview. Base64 writes now put raw base64 in `rawInput.content`, with `rawInput.encoding` preserved.

### What this does, simply

An agent can replace an existing file with `file_write`. Showing only the new text as green additions makes a replacement look like a creation. ZeroCode can now show what was removed and added when the agent already has permission to read that workspace file. Old text disappears from this view after five minutes and is not saved with the conversation. Reopening shows the saved write summary. If private evidence is unavailable or would require credential redaction, the card uses the supplied-content preview instead of a diff. Recognized overwrite results still have an overwrite heading.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, with disposable synthetic files.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, local native ZeroCode Chat and Code through RPC (`channel=rpc`). Direct ACP presentation also has adapter-level automated coverage; interactive ACP client verification remains pending.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Build daemon and client from the same revision. Use an agent with native `file_write` and `file_read`, no read exclusion and no pending read approval. Use an English tool-result catalog for compact-summary recognition. Start a fresh conversation with a disposable workspace file. A write-only profile intentionally receives the fallback preview.
- **Steps to run:** On both `master` and this branch, ask the agent to use `file_write` to create `write-demo.txt` with eight numbered lines, then overwrite it with three different numbered lines. Inspect the six-row preview, choose Show all, then wait five minutes or disconnect and reopen the conversation. Repeat with read authority disabled or an allowed path outside the workspace. Rewrite a file with identical content. For the scrub cases, put a synthetic labelled credential in the previous file, then separately in the written content. Check `file_edit` independently for its existing diff behavior.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Eligible overwrites show `Overwrote existing file`, red removals, green additions, `Changes · temporary local view` and Show all when rows are omitted. An identical rewrite says `Content unchanged`. Expired, restored, unsupported or credential-scrubbed overwrites show the recorded size summary and `Content preview · diff unavailable`. Pending and unknown calls acquire no success claims. Direct ACP preserves original write arguments without synthesizing a creation diff.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Results report bytes written and path. Write previews look like additions regardless of previous contents, without execution-time overwrite evidence.

### How I tested

The new focused runtime regressions are `agent::tool_execution::tests::local_file_diff_executor_drops_previous_credentials` and `agent::tool_execution::tests::local_file_diff_executor_drops_written_credentials`. Each drives a real filesystem overwrite through the production executor with admitted native read authority and synthetic `token=supersecretvalue` on one side. They assert a successful write, the ordinary correlated result and no `LocalFileDiff` event. Both pass on the current head (results below).

The earlier PR body reported 79 selected API/tools/runtime/ZeroCode tests and a matched daemon/client build. Those reports predate this revision and are not validation of the merge resolution or scrub gate. Existing coverage includes read exclusion and approval, foreign and write-only roots, binary/control text, credential filenames, hard links, size limits, failed writes, nonlocal transport, revoked grants, full queues, inbox retirement, expiry, reused IDs and restored history.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Current head `fec6191343ff6724004fb65a48a9700ef8508cbb`: [`CI Required Gate`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/42236668504) and [`Security`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/42236668504) **failed** on this SHA (gate reported one or more jobs failed/cancelled; not treated as green). Historical green: [`CI Required Gate`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40996117315) on `b06b42f8b`; [run 39022116522](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39022116522) on `a95e2d235f11`. Do not treat those older greens as exact-head clearance for `fec619134`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Exact-head CI is currently red (see above). Local focused scrub regressions below are historical relative to this body refresh unless re-run. Earlier master-merge conflict resolution in `crates/zeroclaw-api/src/jsonrpc.rs` (kept `try_send_raw` next to master's `reserve_frame`) is already in the ancestry of `fec619134`; this update does not merge master again.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  Run on head `9fccb917a` (master merge `4f3ca7c38` into `b06b42f8b`), `zc-cargo-narrow`, `-j2`:

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                                   ok
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zerocode -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings   ok
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-api                  324 passed; 0 failed
  cargo test -p zerocode                      lib 54 passed; bin 1614 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib          1390 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib        6036 passed; 2 failed; 10 ignored
  ```

  Both new regressions pass: `agent::tool_execution::tests::local_file_diff_executor_drops_previous_credentials` and `agent::tool_execution::tests::local_file_diff_executor_drops_written_credentials`. The three failures also fail on clean master `5a51398dd` on this machine and are not touched by this PR: `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` (zerocode), and `relay::local_dial_tests::a_closed_route_releases_a_dial_parked_on_a_stalled_listener` / `a_dial_that_never_connects_ends_on_its_own_budget` (macOS loopback backlog never fills).

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source review checked the canonical resolver, native provenance, read approval, scrub-before-event gate, ordinary-result fallback and master API initializers. Standalone Rust formatting and the docs quality and links gates passed. A live ZeroCode run on `b06b42f8b` captured the new-file and overwrite views (see Visual interface evidence).
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real screenshots of the `file_write` diff view are in [this comment](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11463#issuecomment-6537009304): a new file, then an overwrite of the same file.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Exact head for this body: `fec6191343ff6724004fb65a48a9700ef8508cbb`. Existing screenshots in the linked comment were built from `b06b42f8b` (macOS Terminal.app 150×45, `screencapture -l`) and show only a four-line creation and a four-line overwrite—they are **not** complete evidence for current rendering details after later `render_tool_entry_with_diff` changes, and they do not cover the outstanding states listed under "If any command was intentionally skipped".
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** New file: `Changes · temporary local view` with four `+` lines and `result: Wrote 23 bytes · file previously absent.` Overwrite: `Overwrote existing file`, then `alpha` and `gamma` unchanged, `- beta` / `+ BETA`, `- delta` / `+ epsilon`, and `result: Wrote 24 bytes · file previously 23 bytes.`
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Asked the agent to create a file with `file_write`, then overwrite it. The first card showed only additions; the second showed what was removed and added.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Workspace-wide tests were not run for this body refresh. Outstanding real-interface captures still required (and still not present): (1) 8→3 overwrite with red/green rows plus Show all collapsed and expanded; (2) expiry/reopening showing recorded summary and `Content preview · diff unavailable`; (3) write-only / outside-workspace fallback; (4) identical rewrite showing `Content unchanged`. Existing comment screenshots only cover a short creation and a short overwrite.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes, an authorized write can make a bounded previous-text observation for local display using existing native read authority, readable-path policy and workspace containment. Tool names or model arguments grant no native trust or new read permission.
- New external network calls? No. Private evidence goes only to the trusted local native RPC connection. Remote RPC, direct ACP, gateway and channel adapters do not receive it.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes. Before emitting `TurnEvent::LocalFileDiff`, the runtime drops the entire pair if the existing credential scrubber changes either side. It preserves exact diffs for admitted text rather than rendering partially redacted pairs. Filename and pattern exclusions are not a general secret detector.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Test content is synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Successful results gain pre-write existence and byte counts. Captured previous text stays outside ordinary output, model messages, hooks, observers, receipts, checkpoints and saved history. Rendering escapes terminal controls.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Each snapshot is limited to 16 KiB and 1,024 lines. Capture rejects unsupported text, listed credential filenames/key extensions and Unix files with multiple hard links. Capture is a read that does not count toward the `file_read` rate limit and emits no observer or audit read event. Existing written-content exposure through `ToolCall` arguments is unchanged by the scrub gate.

The inbox and view each cap raw pairs at 64 KiB and 16 entries per session. The inbox tracks at most 16 sessions and each pane at most eight. The generic notification ring holds only opaque tokens. Delivery rechecks live read grants under an authority lease and drops evidence if the writer queue is full. Expiry, disconnect, retirement and history replacement clear owned payloads and derived rendering, selection and copy caches. Explicit copies, terminal scrollback, screenshots and operating-system memory remain outside that lifetime guarantee; memory is not cryptographically erased. Capture or delivery failure does not fail an authorized write.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for ACP consumers that relied on synthesized `file_write` creation diffs or `rawInput.newText`. Tool arguments and durable history remain compatible. Successful human-readable result text changes, and matched-version native RPC gains an optional local-only notification.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: Build daemon and ZeroCode together. ACP clients must read original `rawInput.path`, `rawInput.content` and optional `rawInput.encoding`; base64 content remains raw base64. They must not treat write input as a creation diff. No configuration migration is needed. Compact summaries recognize saved English results with a matching argument path. Unknown or localized results keep their original display. Historical results without pre-write evidence remain unknown.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's commits, then rebuild daemon and ZeroCode together.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** No new toggle. Exclude native `file_read` or require read approval for the agent to prevent capture and use the fallback preview.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Missing temporary diffs despite eligible read authority, old lines appearing after expiry or in restored history, incorrect overwrite headings, credential-bearing private diff events, or failed write cards. ACP clients lose the creation-diff preview as a deliberate compatibility change. The labelled fallback remains available when private capture or delivery is unavailable.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A - no Supersedes

- Superseded PRs + authors (`#<pr> by @<author>`, one per line): N/A, this PR supersedes no other PR.
- Scope materially carried forward: N/A, no superseded work is incorporated.
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? No.
- If `No`, why (inspiration-only, no direct code/design carry-over): N/A, no superseded contributor work is incorporated.

---

**Labels** live in the GitHub label UI, not in the body. The PR path labeler owns path/scope labels from `.github/labeler.yml`, and the PR size labeler owns canonical `size:*` labels. Maintainers and reviewers with label permissions still set `risk:*` and any missing manual labels via the sidebar. Contributors without label permission can note obvious label mismatches in a comment. Canonical colon-scoped labels use no-space spelling; during migration, copy exact live label spelling from the GitHub UI.

**Do not add bot/AI attribution footers** such as `Co-authored-by: Claude ...`
or `Created with Claude Code` to the PR body or commit-message tail. Human
co-author trailers are appropriate only for incorporated contributor work under
the supersede-attribution section and privacy contract.

**Privacy contract** (`docs/book/src/contributing/privacy.md`) is a merge gate. Never commit real identities, secrets, personal emails, or PII in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): reopen open sessions when zerocode restarts
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - zerocode's sidebar list of open sessions lived only in memory. The daemon keeps every transcript, but quitting zerocode lost which sessions were open, so each launch started from an empty sidebar.
  - The list (session ids, agent aliases, order, focus, and the last Chat/Code pane on screen) is now saved whenever it changes, as an owner-only JSON file per connection target under `<config-dir>/open-sessions/`.
  - At launch the saved list goes to the existing reconnect resume path (`set_resume_sessions`), so restored sessions reattach by id exactly as they do after a daemon reconnect: focused first, the rest in the background.
  - On by default (`[sidebar] restore_sessions = true`). `zerocode --fresh` starts one launch with an empty sidebar and still saves its own list.
  - Each zerocode window on a daemon keeps its own list in a numbered slot, held by an OS file lock. A window takes the lowest free slot, so closing a second window and opening it again while the first runs reopens the second window's sessions. At restore, sessions another running window has in its list are skipped with a notice. Without that, two windows would reattach the same live session, and either window could cancel the other's turn. That stale-session and multi-tab hazard is why #8911 (silent auto-resume, for #8653) was closed in favour of the #8922 picker. The lock is released when the owning window exits, including on a crash.
  - Each window publishes the list it is about to reopen before its panes start (an empty list on `--fresh`), so other windows never judge by the previous occupant's stale list.
  - Saved Code sessions the daemon no longer lists, and saved Chat sessions with no stored history (for example deleted), are dropped with one notice.
  - When the daemon refuses to reattach a restored session because this terminal's environment differs from the one the session started in (FORBIDDEN `-32012`, "Session environment differs" or "Session retains a local operator environment"), the entry stays where it was, with the same order and focus. Its pane shows a translated notice that the saved session can't be reattached from this terminal environment and that the daemon still keeps the old conversation, plus an explicit "start a new conversation" action (the existing new-session key, Ctrl+N by default). Only that action opens a fresh session in the same slot, with the same agent and mode, and the saved list then tracks the new id. If creating it fails, the refused entry and its notice stay. Switching from the notice to another session moves the refused entry to the background, and closing it while a live session is focused closes only that row, so the live session stays on screen. Nothing is replaced automatically, other errors behave as before, and the daemon's environment check is unchanged.
  - Fully resuming the old conversation in that case is left to upstream #11921 (history persistence so tasks can resume after restart).
  - Local daemon connections only. Over WSS the daemon admits a resume only from the client identity that owns the session (`capture_session_access`), and a relaunched window connects with a new one, so a saved remote list could only produce failed rows. Reclaiming a remote identity per window slot is a follow-up.
- **Scope boundary:** Local connections only; remote (`--connect`) windows are unchanged. Client only (`apps/zerocode`); no daemon, RPC or runtime change. Queued messages, unsent drafts and attachments are not saved. A turn that was running when zerocode quit is not resumed or rerun.
- **Blast radius:** zerocode startup (one extra `session/list-acp` call and/or one `session/messages` probe per saved Chat session on a local connection when a saved list exists) and the per-frame sidebar derivation (a cheap comparison; the file is written only when the list changes, and never while disconnected).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8653, #8911, #8922.

### What this does, simply

When you quit zerocode and start it again, the sessions you had open in the sidebar come back: same order, same one focused, on the pane you were using. The conversations themselves were always kept by the daemon. What was lost was the list of which ones you had open. If a saved session has since been deleted, it is skipped with a short notice. If a saved session can't be reattached from the terminal you relaunched in, it stays in its place with a notice and an option to start a new conversation there. Each zerocode window keeps its own list: close a second window and open it again, and it gets its own sessions back. A session already open in another window is not opened twice. Use `zerocode --fresh` to start one launch with an empty sidebar, or set `restore_sessions = false` under `[sidebar]` to turn the feature off.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `tui` (zerocode Chat and Code panes)
- **Setup / preconditions:** A local daemon with at least two agents.
- **Steps to run:** Open two Code sessions and one Chat session from the sidebar, focus the second Code session, quit zerocode, start it again. Then quit and start once more with `zerocode --fresh`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** With one `zerocode` open, open a second window, add a session there, close it and reopen it: it comes back with that session, and the first window is unchanged. The second launch opens on the Code pane with the same three sidebar rows in the same order and the second Code session focused, transcripts loaded. The `--fresh` launch starts with an empty sidebar.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Every launch starts with an empty sidebar (or the recent-session picker); the previous launch's open sessions must be reopened one by one.

### How I tested

- **Current head:** `214a73cc5` (`8628b342c` plus the fix for Greptile 4429702542: if switching from a refused restore notice to another retained session fails, the refused entry stays focused, so its notice and "start a new conversation" still work). Linux x86_64, rustc 1.98.0, in its own target dir (the log shows zerocode compiled from this tree): `cargo test --locked -p zerocode --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4` → library 52 passed; binary 1,599 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored, including the new `chat::tests::a_failed_switch_from_a_refused_notice_keeps_the_refused_entry_focused` (Chat and Code panes). `cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` are clean.
- **Previous head:** `8628b342c` (the fix for Greptile 4429144032: closing a refused restore row after switching to a live session no longer replaces that session; test `closing_a_refused_entry_after_switching_away_keeps_the_working_session`).
- **Previous head:** `b8f816f436`, a merge of master `1c1cd118a` into `d05cdf055c`. The merge conflicted only in `apps/zerocode/src/chat.rs`: master added `cleanup_notice` to `ResumeEntry` and this branch added `environment_refused`, so the struct and its constructors keep both fields. On a Linux x86_64 build host (rustc 1.99.1): `cargo test --locked -p zerocode -- --test-threads=4` → library 52 passed; binary 1,596 passed, 1 failed (the known `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`); `cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passed.
- **Previous tested revision:** `d05cdf055cb2a9a61f343643619abe730dc78b4c` on the Mac mini, with the results below.
- **Formatting:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passed.
- **Clippy:** `cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
- **Package suite:** `cargo test -p zerocode`, through `zc-cargo-narrow` with `-j2` for compilation and two test threads: library 54 passed; binary 1,600 passed, 1 failed (the known failure below). The TestBackend evidence-frame tests were removed in this revision; the behaviour tests stay.
- **Deleted-Chat regressions (new or updated, all pass):** `open_sessions::tests::deleted_chat_session_is_skipped_at_restore`, `open_sessions::tests::chat_sessions_survive_startup_without_a_complete_daemon_listing`, `open_sessions::tests::chat_restore_drops_only_the_specific_missing_session_refusal`, `open_sessions::tests::mixed_restore_prunes_code_by_list_and_chat_by_history_in_order`. Each saved Chat entry is probed with `session/messages` (limit 1): no stored history, or the daemon's "Session not found or not owned by this principal" refusal, drops it with the existing notice; any other error keeps it for the normal resume path. I ran the first test against `409b7725ef` and it fails there (`dropped` is 0, expected 1), because that head kept every saved Chat ID.
- **Environment-refusal regressions (all pass):** `chat::tests::focused_restored_environment_refusal_keeps_slot_focus_and_notice`, `chat::tests::background_restored_environment_refusal_keeps_slot_and_opens_notice_on_focus`, `chat::tests::restored_environment_refusal_new_conversation_replaces_only_the_selected_slot`, `chat::tests::failed_refused_session_replacement_keeps_saved_id_and_notice`, `chat::tests::unrelated_forbidden_restore_keeps_existing_error_behaviour`, `chat::tests::session_picker_environment_refusal_keeps_selected_entry_and_notice`, `chat::tests::chat_entry_retry_adopts_restored_environment_refusal_action`, `chat::tests::restored_environment_refusal_requires_typed_code_and_specific_message`. On `c4f45eb508` the focused-refusal case promotes the background session over the refused one and shows no notice, so the first test's focus and notice assertions fail there.
- **Known failures:** `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` also fails on clean master `f2b432db` on this Mini (it passes when run alone). `app::tests::input_wait_returns_early_for_pending_transport_events` is a known timing flake (it passed in this run).
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** That both guards are load-bearing: with the local-only gate removed, `remote_connections_neither_save_nor_restore` fails; with the early publish removed, both `*_publishes_*` tests fail; with the live-window check removed, `sessions_open_in_another_running_window_are_not_restored` fails. Real launches against a live daemon are captured in https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11727#issuecomment-6536921024 (on `8628b342cb`) and https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11727#issuecomment-6546062078 (on `214a73cc5143`); see Screenshots below.
- **Intentionally skipped:** Full workspace tests; this change is confined to `apps/zerocode` and its docs page.

### Screenshots

Real screenshots: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11727#issuecomment-6536921024 (relaunch and `--fresh`, on `8628b342cb`) and https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11727#issuecomment-6546062078 (dragged cross-pane order after restart, per-window lists, and the environment-refusal notice followed by an explicit new conversation, on `214a73cc5143`). Those are the evidence revisions. The current head `f91c108057acef4e287283d446955a41dcf6e95e` is a later master merge; CI Required Gate passed there. The screenshots were not recaptured on it.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes: zerocode writes one new file plus an empty lock file per window slot and connection target under its own config directory. It is written owner-only (`0600`) and atomically, through the same `secure_file::write_private_atomic` funnel as `zerocode-config.toml`.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. The file holds session ids, agent aliases and the connection label (socket path or WSS URL). The label is already shown on the dashboard. Credentials are not stored.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: see the first item.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. A config file without `restore_sessions` restores (default on); a missing, damaged or newer-format list file is ignored.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: `[sidebar] restore_sessions` (env `ZEROCODE_sidebar__restore_sessions`) and the `--fresh` flag. Documented in `docs/book/src/zerocode/config.md`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: nothing to do on upgrade. To keep the old behavior, set `restore_sessions = false` under `[sidebar]`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revert the squash commit. Without a revert, set `[sidebar] restore_sessions = false` or launch with `--fresh`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `[sidebar] restore_sessions`, `--fresh`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a launch that reopens sessions the user closed, or the toast "Could not save the open-session list".

prs.title: feat(zerocode): configure per-pane session cap
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A ZeroCode pane could track at most 8 sessions (focused, background, and retained reconnect entries), fixed by a compile-time constant. Workloads that keep one session per worktree hit it quickly, and the daemon's own ACP `max_sessions` setting does not affect it.
  - A new `[sessions].max_tracked_per_pane` setting replaces the constant. The default stays 8; valid values are 1 through 32, so two panes at the maximum still fit the daemon's 64-session store.
  - The value is resolved once at startup. An out-of-range or malformed value stops startup with an error naming `[sessions]` instead of being silently normalized, as the issue asks for validation. The `ZEROCODE_sessions__max_tracked_per_pane` env override goes through the same check.
  - Every admission path uses it: the sidebar "+", Change directory, opening an existing session, and reconnect resume. The `zc-chat-session-cap` notice shows the configured value. The entry-retry pane carries the value so a retry does not reset it to 8.
  - The three per-session result channels are sized by the configured cap, as they were by the constant.
- **Scope boundary:** no daemon, RPC or runtime change; no Config-pane control yet (file and env only, documented as such); no sidebar UI change.
- **Blast radius:** `apps/zerocode` only (config loading, the two chat-like panes, the config reference page). Existing config files load unchanged; without `[sessions]` the limit is 8 as before.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10665. Supersedes #11729 (same feature as `[chat].max_sessions_per_pane` with clamping; closed in favour of this one).

### What this does, simply

Each ZeroCode window side can keep a limited number of conversations open at once. That limit was fixed at 8. This adds a setting for it. Nothing changes unless you set it: the default is still 8 and the highest allowed value is 32. A value outside that range is reported at startup rather than quietly changed.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface`: `tui`
