prs.title: feat(browser): scope username/password and TOTP access independently
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Depends on #12517, #12438 and the bounded runtime placement record #12266. RFC #12422 remains the scope decision owner.
- **What changed and why:** add independent browser grants to username/password and TOTP catalog records, an operator Permissions panel, and the `submit_credential` action on the existing agent-browser backend. The agent passes an alias; resolved values travel on child stdin and only a fixed localized result returns to the model.
- **Scope boundary:** this PR is draft. The action is implemented and becomes usable when an operator grants an origin. It does not yet isolate browser sessions by task or suppress generic snapshots, screenshots and evaluation on credential-bearing pages. It is not ready for upstream deployment until these acceptance gaps and the RFC/dependencies are settled.
- **Blast radius:** grant mutation API, encrypted catalog revisions, browser release, form selectors, HTTP Basic admission, and credential-use audit metadata. Underlying SSH/HTTP layers remain reviewed in their own PRs.

### Behavior and review repairs

- Match the saved encrypted record before and after an awaited lookup. Replacement, revocation and deletion refuse release.
- Require `expected_revision` for every permission mutation, including legacy `http_allowed` and `browser.origin` forms. Stale or missing revisions return 409.
- Clear browser and HTTP grants when replacement changes the suggested service. Rotation for the same service preserves them.
- A named OTP field must match `autocomplete="one-time-code"` or `name="otp"`; segmented controls must each accept one character. Ordinary text/search selectors cannot receive a code.
- Reject HTTP Basic grants for colon-bearing usernames; the HTTP consumer also refuses them before resolving a password.
- Log one browser-use result with validated alias, HTTPS origin, stage, refusal phase and bounded status. Never log values, seeds, selectors, scripts or raw backend errors.
- Run the form-script boundary tests in CI and include the design contract in the book.

An origin grant also authorizes later password-confirmation prompts on that origin, including sensitive actions. A submission acknowledgement is not proof of authentication. An unconfirmed result can follow a page-handled submission: inspect page state before retrying.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

Use a disposable HTTPS login and synthetic records. Grant password and TOTP independently; exercise staged forms, a same-origin iframe and segmented OTP. Try an ordinary text selector, another origin/window, multiple submitters and fields from different forms. Pause an external lookup, then rotate, revoke or delete its record. From two operator tabs, change grants and submit the stale tab. Change the suggested service and confirm both grant lists clear.

### How I tested

- `node --test crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/browser_credential_form.test.mjs`: **19 passed, 0 failed** on the repaired source.
- Added Rust regressions for lookup replacement/revocation/deletion, early denial, service-change grant clearing, legacy revision enforcement and colon-bearing Basic usernames. [Linux Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45824802280/job/139926130632), Lint and Security passed on **7a2acc241c**. The main test log records PASS for service replacement, stale-tab, colon-username and shared sandbox regressions. The browser lookup regression runs in [Test (opt-in tools)](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45824802280/job/139926130637), which passed and records its PASS. [Repository Structure](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45824802280/job/139926129896) passed with the Node script tests.
- Earlier reviewer and production results apply only to the revisions named in their comments.
- **Known coverage gaps:** managed session isolation and observation suppression, final-interface Permissions-panel screenshot on this head, and independent browser acceptance against disposable HTTPS fixtures remain open. The script fixture is not real-browser acceptance evidence.
- **Visual interface evidence:** pending, which is one reason this stays draft.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities/file scope? **Yes:** independent browser origin grants, denied by default, authorized only by the config operator.
- New external network calls? **Yes:** the authorized browser submits to the granted HTTPS origin; vault resolution uses the existing provider adapter.
- Secrets handling changed? **Yes:** values are resolved just in time, revalidated and sent on stdin; the current browser's session/observation limitations above remain a release blocker.
- PII/real identities in the diff? **No.** Tests use synthetic identities and values.
- Prompt-injection/untrusted input changed? **Yes:** page content and model selectors are untrusted. Origin, form, frame, field and current-record checks bound release. They do not prevent a same-origin page script from observing its own form values.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No for unversioned permission writes:** older clients must GET the catalog and include its `permission_revision` as `expected_revision` on every edit. Refresh the dashboard bundle after upgrade.
- Config/env/CLI surface changed? **Yes:** additive browser grants and action parameters; no grant is inferred from an alias or page prompt.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast path:** revoke browser grants, stop affected tasks and close the browser session; deploy the previous integrated binary with a protected compatible state backup.
- **Toggle:** empty browser-grant lists disable release. There is no claim of task-isolated browser profiles in this implementation.
- **Symptoms:** `browser_credential_use` reports `refused_or_unconfirmed` with a bounded phase; stale editors get 409. Do not automatically retry a page-handled submission.

## Documentation

The browser consumer design page is linked from the book. Environment-specific probes have been removed from that contract; historical evidence stays in the PR discussion. English Markdown is canonical; generated translations are omitted from this maintenance change.

prs.body:
## Summary

The initial HTTP credential PR #12408 is limited to locally encrypted API keys and Basic credentials bound to one HTTPS origin. The native broker PR #12438 is limited to existing SSH-agent authentication. This draft preserves the additional catalog implementation removed from those review slices.

Depends on #12408 and #12438. Related #12422 and #12373. Approval and merge are conditional on acceptance of RFC #12422 and any requested changes to its credential ownership, consumer grants and record model.

The preserved features include TOTP, SSH key records and destination grants, non-HTTP service descriptors, external secret references, the permissions WebUI, OpenBao-backed native SSH authentication and the existing provider-reference adapters. OpenBao provisioning and the other provider writers remain in #12481 and #12482.

These features are used on our company's Jarvis production server for live testing with actual operational workloads. OpenBao-backed credentials and the associated skills are in active use. That deployment supplies operator feedback and does not imply upstream acceptance. We will adjust this draft as RFC #12422 evolves.

The operator-managed service credential stays hidden from the model. Consumers resolve the configured alias under explicit grants. Unsandboxed same-UID shell processes retain the service user's OS authority, including access to catalog state and signer sockets. Destination constraints provide defense in depth.

## Testing

The HTTP redaction production function passed four focused regressions for quote-bearing secrets, decoded JSON strings/keys, numeric secrets and large integer preservation. Native broker lifecycle tests are being refreshed for process-group cleanup and pre-bound socket refusal. Prior operator acceptance covers OpenBao credential creation and real HTTP and managed SSH use. Full CI on this draft must be reviewed independently.

Reviewer testing requested when the RFC scope is accepted. On an isolated deployment, register a synthetic credential, grant its consumer and exact destination, verify use succeeds, revoke it and verify denial, then rotate the secret and verify the new value reaches the protected endpoint.

## Security

Secret values are encrypted locally or referenced from the configured external store. New HTTP grants remain denied by default. Host and consumer authorization continue at use time. The draft documents the same-UID security boundary and remains subject to the RFC.

## Compatibility

This draft preserves the implemented record shapes used by the integrated Jarvis build. The RFC may require schema migration before upstream release. Apply the integrated feature set when testing existing external-source catalogs.

## Rollback

Use a protected state backup and the corresponding integrated binary. A binary supporting only the reduced local HTTP slice cannot consume the extended catalog. Downgrades require an explicit state migration.

## Documentation

The credential and SSH guides describe the retained implementation. RFC #12422 is the decision owner. The separate drafts #12481 and #12482 retain their provider-specific setup and validation.
## Updated validation and dependencies

Depends on #12490 for the Authorization Token header, retained here so the extended catalog can represent existing Token credentials. The live Jarvis build combines both slices.

The final extended broker passed ten tests in the real zeroclaw-tools crate on Linux, including an actual ssh-keygen fixture and a prebound fake-agent listener which received no connection or key. The reduced broker passed six tests in the same crate. HTTP response redaction passed all four focused regressions in the real crate.

Python-runtime retirement is tracked in #12518. The existing Python helper remains a separate predecessor during upstream review. The production Jarvis deployment uses the Rust broker.

## Shared security prerequisite

#12552 has merged into master as 3773cae2d7288f9e6af1ad8414e6d2cd33e90451. This branch incorporates that revision. Hosted CI is rerun on the refreshed head; no separate SMTP policy change is carried in this feature diff.

## Managed credential RPC placement

Depends on #12563, the separately reviewed bounded Core Team exception record for the generic-RPC credential write guard. The guard stays enabled; this feature does not approve its own placement. The record must land before this feature merges.

prs.body:
<!-- replay-cache-fix-20261110 -->
## TLS replay cache follow-up

Revision `f5b5735eb` classifies new TLS-only message IDs at insertion and evicts only that class. Older and encrypted markers remain in the shared replay table, preserving cross-mode deduplication and reviewed inbox release. The private store recognizes the exact legacy and classified schemas.

The old query reproduces a missing encrypted replay marker after exceeding the TLS retention limit. The new regression drives the real private store and offline review/release command through TLS eviction; fresh TLS-to-OMEMO initialization and earlier socket deadline regressions also pass. Integrated XMPP, formatting and all-target Clippy passed locally. Fresh hosted CI remains authoritative.

<!-- control-write-fix-20261110 -->
## Control-write deadline follow-up

Revision `5e1f62ae7` includes `adbc57d18` and master `a4beef9a6`. Control stanzas now have a 60-second write deadline. A stalled or failed control write returns an error from the connection writer, which releases queued replies and lets the existing listener supervisor reconnect. The writer does not replay uncertain sends.

A regression driving the real writer with a stalled sink fails before the fix and passes after it. Healthy and broken control writes are also covered. Integrated XMPP, HTTP-cache and runtime tests, formatting and all-target Clippy passed locally. Fresh hosted CI on this revision remains authoritative.

<!-- review-fix-20261110:start -->
## Review follow-up (2026-11-10)

Published head: 1d062fc50eb74070a6267b4d838875edf763e892. Updated with master 6877da56d.

Atomic peer-device index cleanup for reviewed offline OMEMO session reset, with index-bound review tokens and an actual encrypted send to the surviving device.

Local integration regression tests, formatting and all-target Clippy passed. Hosted CI for this exact head is pending; earlier CI/approval does not validate the new revision. Detailed boundary evidence is in the reply to the corresponding review thread.
<!-- review-fix-20261110:end -->

## Summary



Base branch: `master`.



Implement feature-gated native Rust XMPP with optional Linux legacy OMEMO. Related #9814. The #12015 dependency merged into master as d4a5d2afd and is included in this branch.



### What this does, simply



The native channel owns encrypted receipts independently of the socket. Reconnect reuses the exclusive store; completed runtime and control receipts can be recorded while offline. First-contact key publication explicitly requests readable public nodes.



<!-- jarvis-validation-update:start -->
## Validation update (2026-11-10)

Updated to master a11a5ce5b at f120f8722. Retained scoped-chat authorization and XMPP policy coverage. Canonical API generation, npm run test:auth (including xmppPolicy.test.ts), and the production build passed. Native XMPP/OMEMO validation remains covered by the published commit's CI. The dependency on #12015 remains.

CI results and maintainer decisions on the published revision remain authoritative.
<!-- jarvis-validation-update:end -->

## Testing (required)



### How you can test (when useful)



Run the `xmpp` and `native_ingress_` channel-library filters with `--no-default-features --features channel-xmpp`; then run `crates/zeroclaw-channels/tests/xmpp_native/managed_server.py` using the documented disposable loopback-only fixture.



### Earlier validation (historical)



Current-head CI Required Gate and all executed checks pass at 47f16954424bcc3787379e5e1d2c21df52daf100, including every source-image build. The inherited master root-fixture packaging fix is confirmed across the current Dockerfile/Containerfile source matrix. Integrated validation passed 69 XMPP tests (4 separately marked ignored), 5 shared-ingress tests, all four real encrypted interoperability scenarios and strict channel/test and root binary Clippy. Fresh-account scenarios remove pre-created bot nodes and verify public key discovery without roster subscription. Offline receipt completion, explicit publication policy/refusal, live admission filtering, queue overflow and deferred authorized ping ordering are covered. Human changes-requested review has not been dismissed; re-review is requested.



Visual interface evidence: this follow-up changes integration, lifecycle or tests; prior feature UI evidence remains linked in the review discussion. No new presentation claim is made from source inspection. Remaining platform/integration gaps are those not covered by current-head hosted CI and the named local checks.



## Security & Privacy Impact (required)



OMEMO identity keys, signed prekeys and ratchet state are stored as JSON in the private omemo.sqlite3 database with mode 0600 and exclusive ownership; they are not encrypted at rest by the vault. The vault is required for new identity creation and encrypts queued ingress payloads. The account password uses the existing secret configuration field. Uncertain admitted work remains unreleasable. Public device lists and bundles request open access; these contain public keys, while live peer allowlists and fingerprint pins still gate message admission. Server publication refusal fails explicitly. No private deployment information, real identities, credentials, or messages are included.



- New permissions/capabilities/filesystem scope: Yes â€” the optional channel owns a private mode-0600 OMEMO database and existing-vault access for identity creation and ingress sealing.

- New external network calls: Yes â€” configured XMPP service and bounded protocol exchanges.

- Secrets/credentials handling changed: Yes â€” the account password is a secret field; queued ingress uses vault ciphertext, while long-term OMEMO keys and ratchet state use the private database described above. Fingerprint pins authorize peer devices; they do not encrypt the local key store.

- PII, real identities or private messages in the diff/tests/docs: No.

- Untrusted model-visible content changed: No â€” protocol content remains inside the existing shared dispatch/policy boundary.



## Compatibility (required)



Feature-gated XMPP; encrypted operation is Linux-only. Legacy OMEMO remains distinct from OMEMO v2. The existing migration and replay-protection boundaries remain documented. Offline administration requires stopping the channel owner, including while its socket is disconnected. Existing nodes with incompatible publication policy require owner reconciliation. No toolchain-floor change.



## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)



Disable the XMPP feature/configuration or revert the code subject to documented state compatibility. Preserve newer ratchets, replay markers and uncertain admitted records. Stop the channel owner before supported offline inspection/release. Observe explicit publication errors, refused admission and unreleasable completed receipts.



## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)



None. Incorporated maintainer commits retain their original authorship.


SQLite scope correction: #12322 remains draft pending a published Matrix storage dependency (matrix-org/matrix-rust-sdk#7456). Its workspace-only bridge was removed from this PR; registry compatibility is preserved and #12320 remains the shared advisory tracker. No SQLite waiver is added here.


<!-- followup-20261110-b:start -->
## Additional review follow-up
The discovery exchange now waits for outbound queue capacity inside its existing 10-second budget; queue admission and response share one deadline. Peer timeout remains a typed inbound rejection. Added regressions cover full queue admission, the shared deadline, and cancellation without a late IQ. Integrated validation: 76 XMPP tests pass (4 lab-only ignored).

Local evidence above is from the integrated candidate. Fresh hosted CI will run on the published branch commit; maintainer architecture/merge decisions remain unchanged.
<!-- followup-20261110-b:end -->

## Security maintenance — remove the XMPP chrono dependency

This PR includes the parser correction directly in its branch, commit f7e041a. The XMPP dependency path is now tokio-xmpp → the locally patched xmpp-parsers → time. Its resolved dependency subtree contains neither chrono nor chrono-tz.

The motivation is RustSec RUSTSEC-2026-0543 and the security-maintenance work tracked in #12505. The former Utc::now()/timestamp() calls are supported APIs. The advisory identifies chrono as unmaintained. This change removes that dependency from the new XMPP transport.

The patch preserves the parser's MPL-2.0 license, copyright notices, source commit and original registry checksum. The imported parser is about 1 MB. Functional changes cover its date/time APIs, corresponding parser tests and manifests, plus rejection of unsupported CID algorithms and panic-free handling of malformed CSS declarations and nested unknown XHTML tags. PATCH.md documents the public type changes, source provenance, test commands and eventual removal of the local override. Upstream xmpp-rs currently declines AI-assisted contributions, so this correction is carried in this PR.

Validation on Windows / Rust 1.98.1

- Default parser suite passed 640 tests, with 8 existing ignored tests.
- Strict XML (pedantic) suite passed 669 tests, with 8 existing ignored tests.
- cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --no-default-features --features channel-xmpp --tests passed.
- cargo fmt --all -- --check passed.
- Dependency-tree inspection confirmed the tokio-xmpp subtree has no chrono or chrono-tz.
- A channel regression test parses delayed-delivery XML and checks nanosecond precision, negative sub-hour offsets and rejection of malformed dates.

The security gate still audits existing workspace dependencies. Other chrono/chrono-tz consumers and the separate ZIP advisory retain their existing tracking. Production deployment of this parser update remains pending.

## Shared security prerequisite

#12552 has merged into master as 3773cae2d7288f9e6af1ad8414e6d2cd33e90451. This branch incorporates that revision. Hosted CI is rerun on the refreshed head; no separate SMTP policy change is carried in this feature diff.

Depends on #12323 for the shared Tokio-runtime HTTP pool ownership repair. That repair is intentionally kept in its dedicated approved PR rather than copied into this feature diff. The integrated test deployment composes that PR separately and retains the fix. If master-based pooled-dispatch tests fail before #12323 lands, report/rerun that shared prerequisite failure rather than restoring unrelated cache changes here.

prs.title: feat(web): provision catalog credentials in external cloud vaults
prs.body:
## Summary

- Base branch: `master`. Depends on #12481. Related #12422 and #12373.
- Provide operator-only create and rotate for 1Password Connect, Azure Key Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, and Google Secret Manager.
- Reuse the external reference form and provider-scoped editable defaults. Retain explicit linking, blank preservation on replacement, and catalog-only deletion.
- Use verified HTTPS, per-operation write authorization, and configured vault or name scope. Store only encrypted references. Existing read adapters still use their own identity.

### What this does, simply

An operator can provision a value from the same Secrets form regardless of which configured vault holds it. Azure and 1Password check for a name collision before creating. Their APIs provide no atomic conditional create by name, so configure a dedicated single-writer namespace. Google may create a resource before its first version fails. The UI directs the operator to check, link, and replace in that case.

## Testing

### How you can test

Enable one provider with a disposable prefix according to the WebUI guide. Use a scoped test identity. Add a synthetic value, verify the reference, replace it and confirm it advances, then delete the catalog alias. A blank replacement preserves the external value. Repeat with an existing name to see the conflict.

### How I tested

Added mock HTTP tests for all four providers. Tests cover expected request bodies, routes, AWS signing headers, scope validation, collision handling, 1Password IDs, and Google's partial-create recovery. `cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib cloud_vault_write::tests` passed all five tests. The integrated WebUI passed TypeScript build and Vite production bundling. Real accounts are not available in this environment.

## Security and privacy

- New capability and external calls: yes, opt-in operator-only writes to a configured scope via verified HTTPS. Redirects and proxy environment routing are disabled.
- Secrets: transient write authority and value. Neither is included in catalog responses, audit output or persistent configuration.
- Personal data and untrusted model inputs: none added. Provider responses are never forwarded to the model.

## Compatibility and rollback

Remove the writer prefix to disable writes while preserving existing references. Reverting the code restores link-only behavior for these four providers. No migration is required. To remove an external resource, manage it in the vault.


### Integrated smoke test

The Linux release built with XMPP enabled. A disposable OpenBao KV v2 instance over verified TLS and an isolated gateway passed create, path denial, collision, versioned replacement, blank preservation, deletion of the alias and catalog-response redaction through the shared mutation route. After deployment to the Jarvis lab, the gateway, WebUI, OIDC and XMPP were healthy and the SSH helper remained Rust. The four cloud writers remain opt-in and unconfigured in that environment.

### Review and dependencies update

The branch inherits the catalog and manifest-validation corrections from #12408 and #12402 through the OpenBao work in #12481. The four cloud adapters are covered by mocked provider HTTP tests. The real OpenBao smoke test covers the shared mutation route. Live provider validation remains open for contributors with access.

### OpenBao managed authentication and live validation

The OpenBao form uses the server's configured identity and never asks the operator for a vault write token. It preserves the editable reference suggested from the mount, prefix, alias and field. Add writes the value through the gateway. Link existing saves only the reference and performs no vault write. The server can use the existing OpenBao Agent token sink from BAO_TOKEN_PATH or a dedicated ZEROCLAW_OPENBAO_WRITE_TOKEN_FILE.

Validated on the integrated Jarvis build 0504477e9. The operator confirmed a real WebUI save without a token field after the OpenBao policy was scoped to the configured credential prefix. A synthetic OpenBao API test with the Jarvis identity verified create, read and rotation; the fixture was removed. Validation here covers OpenBao. The other cloud providers retain their own authorization flows.


## RFC scope and deployment status

Depends on #12517. Approval and merge are conditional on acceptance of RFC #12422. This remains a draft. The OpenBao implementation is in actual operational use on our company's Jarvis production server for live testing, with existing secrets and skills. Provider-specific claims retain their documented test coverage. We will adapt these features as the RFC evolves.


## Shared security prerequisite

#12552 has merged into master as 3773cae2d7288f9e6af1ad8414e6d2cd33e90451. This branch incorporates that revision. Hosted CI is rerun on the refreshed head; no separate SMTP policy change is carried in this feature diff.

## Managed credential RPC placement

Depends on #12563, the separately reviewed bounded Core Team exception record for the generic-RPC credential write guard. The guard stays enabled; this feature does not approve its own placement. The record must land before this feature merges.

## Summary

Base branch `master`. Depends on #12408. Related #12422 and #12373.

The external credential editor separates **Add**, **Link existing secret**, **Replace**, and **Delete**. OpenBao KV v2 writes support existing catalog credential types, including TOTP. An operator-configured mount and prefix supply an editable default identifier. The other external providers keep the same reference editor while their write adapters are pending.

### How to test

1. Configure an HTTPS OpenBao origin, a disposable KV v2 prefix and a server-side OpenBao identity scoped to that prefix. Sign in to the dashboard as an operator.
2. Add a synthetic TOTP entry. Check the prefilled identifier, save, and verify the remote KV entry and local metadata.
3. Try to add to the same destination. Confirm the CAS rejection.
4. Replace at the same path and verify its new version. Leave the value blank on a second replacement and verify the version stays the same.
5. Delete the catalog entry and verify the vault still owns its data.

### Validation

- `git diff --check` passed. Includes a regression test for prefix enforcement.

The gateway authorizes the operator and config mutation before contacting OpenBao. It uses verified HTTPS with redirects disabled, a constrained prefix, CAS zero for create, and a versioned patch for rotation. For OpenBao, the gateway uses the server-configured token file. The gateway persists only the encrypted reference. No credentials or personal data are included in fixtures. Remote failures are reported without printing response bodies. Agent-side vault access continues through the existing resolver.

Additive opt-in gateway configuration. Existing link-only requests remain supported. Unset `ZEROCLAW_OPENBAO_WRITE_PREFIX` to disable writes or revert the change to roll back. Manage existing remote secret versions in the vault.

### How you can test

New-head CI will validate this revision.

It verifies that two concurrent requests for the same pool key attempt setup once, return a setup error to the first caller and the cached failure to the second, and leave zero active leases. The test uses no network.

prs.title: feat(web): manage scoped HTTP credentials
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** add write-only, locally encrypted HTTP Basic and API-key aliases, bound to one HTTPS origin and a separate explicit HTTP Request grant. Reject catalog changes through generic gateway/RPC config writers.
- **Scope boundary:** local Basic, Bearer and X-API-Key only. SSH, TOTP, directory destinations and external resolvers remain in draft #12517 behind RFC #12422; Token is the separate #12490 increment. Plugin TLS management is inherited from #12402.
- **Blast radius:** config admission, dedicated credential API, audit/OpenAPI, Secrets editors and HTTP authentication/redaction.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12402 and #12563. Related RFC #12422 and #12490.

### What this does, simply

An operator registers an alias in Settings → Secrets. Creation starts denied and use requires a separate explicit grant. Every caller already allowed to use HTTP Request at the stored origin can use that alias; there is no separate per-agent selector. Scope binds scheme, host and port, without path or method restrictions.

Same-origin rotation preserves the grant; changing origin clears it. Listings and audits never contain values. Host overrides are refused, redirects disabled, auth headers sensitive, reflected values scrubbed, and truncated authenticated bodies omitted.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, with disposable credentials and an allowed HTTPS endpoint.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** WebUI Secrets, dedicated gateway credential API and HTTP Request execution.
- **Setup / preconditions:** encryption enabled with an existing key, operator access and an origin allowed by network policy.
- **Steps to run:** create a denied alias; grant and use it; rotate at an equivalent origin and then a different origin; revoke/delete; attempt generic property, section and map-key mutations with a broad HTTP editor.
- **Expected on this branch:** explicit grant required, same-origin grant retained, cross-origin grant cleared, no secret listing, and generic mutations refused without changing persisted config.
- **Prior behavior on master:** no managed scoped HTTP catalog or dedicated editor.

### How I tested

The current follow-up is e3a5aa5267. Focused rustfmt checks and git diff checks passed. Existing route, rotation, generic gateway/RPC write and redaction regressions are retained. Fresh CI on the published revision is authoritative; pending checks are not a passing result.

Both optional review suggestions are addressed: the shared enum is `CredentialOperation`, and the origin regression includes `https://evil-example.com` and `https://example.com.evil.test`.

[Desktop/narrow HTTP captures](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/tree/0fbb8fcbae826d7f62d9042efdcdfe66713b7671/pr-12408) and [inherited TLS captures](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/tree/e96bc6ba9c12544962e6a9a50afd0567d1507869/pr-12408/tls) render the actual components at 391cce0 with synthetic data and a mocked catalog API. Those component files are unchanged here. The captures cover desktop/narrow empty, encryption-disabled, denied, grant/revoke, replace and delete states where applicable. They remain component-harness evidence, not a new full-gateway deployed exact-head validation. Earlier broader deployment evidence is historical.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** Operator-only mutations and default-denied HTTP grants, shared by callers already authorized for HTTP Request at that origin.
- New external network calls? **Yes.** Opt-in authenticated HTTPS requests use the existing HTTP transport and network policy. No external vault resolver or new process execution is added.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** Locally encrypted values, write-only API, value-free audit and authenticated-response redaction; generic catalog mutation is rejected.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Synthetic fixtures and evidence.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** HTTP responses remain untrusted data and convey no new execution authority.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes.** Empty catalogs preserve the existing HTTP workflow.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** Adds scoped credential config, the dedicated API and an optional tool credential-alias argument. Enrollment and grants are explicit.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revoke grants, remove feature aliases through the dedicated API, preserve an encrypted backup, then revert the feature or restore the previous binary.
- **Feature flags/config toggles:** empty catalog or revoked per-alias grants disables use; existing network policy remains authoritative.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** unexpected credential refusal, grant loss during same-origin rotation, generic-write acceptance, catalog validation errors or reflected secret material.

## Landing prerequisites

Merge #12402 and the independently approved placement record #12563 before this feature, then #12490. This feature grants itself no runtime exception. Both prerequisite merges and outstanding human implementation reviews remain required. Shared SMTP, URL/Ruma and cookie remediation comes from master; no advisory waiver is introduced by this feature.

<!-- full-ui-evidence-20261126:start -->
## Full-application interface evidence (2026-11-26)

Tested feature source: `284104bdbaf3b85c386d90285c7ba54a895194a0`.

[42 desktop/narrow captures, setup and manifest](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/1e145fea0dbbc5b59bf4eac605cad900df43eced/README.md), with [reviewer follow-up](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12408#issuecomment-7199611252). The unchanged full dashboard runs through its normal App/router and real authenticated configuration handlers with encrypted temporary-file persistence. A published test-only local fixture supplies bootstrap and synthetic plugin state; this is neither the earlier isolated component harness nor a production/external-service acceptance claim.

Both widths (1280×900 / 390×844) cover Settings, API token, username/password and inherited Plugin TLS. Captures include empty HTTP catalogs, encryption-disabled editing, default-denied creation, grant/revoke, blank-secret replacement and delete confirmation. TLS captures cover admitted unset/configured slots and lifecycle; no no-plugin-catalog image or executed TLS connection is claimed.

The actual gateway tests `scoped_http_rotation_preserves_only_same_origin_grants` and `scoped_http_catalog_refuses_generic_gateway_writes` were repeated successfully on this source: **2 passed, 0 failed**. The test-only helper was removed afterward; the feature checkout remains clean. #12402 and #12563 remain landing prerequisites, with human re-review still required.

## Summary

- Base branch is `master`.
- Add a write-only operator panel under Config → Storage → Secrets for credentials already referenced by a plugin TLS profile.
- Reuse the canonical encrypted plugin configuration and existing host-mediated TLS authorization. The catalog returns instance, property, destinations and configured state.
- This is the first implementation slice of Related #12373. The broader catalog, reversible disable, and references usable by other consumers are open design work. This PR leaves the issue open.

### What this does, simply

An authenticated operator can provision a PEM value for a configured plugin TLS profile without putting the value in a chat. Rotation and deletion use the existing configuration commit path. New connections continue to use the existing instance and destination checks.

## Testing

### How you can test

- Reviewer testing requested. Surface is web.
- Pair the dashboard, enable encryption with an initialized key, and configure a plugin TLS profile referencing a schema-declared secret.
- Open Storage → Secrets → Plugin TLS credentials. Set, replace, refresh and delete a synthetic PEM value. Inspect the responses and verify they contain only metadata or configured state.
- On master, the dedicated panel is absent.

### How I tested

- `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --tests -j2` completed successfully.
- Web TypeScript type checking passed. The four existing read-only configuration UI regression tests passed.
- Rust formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Added a real config-router test for scoped-principal rejection, missing key, encrypted persistence, duplicate creation, replacement and deletion. The gateway test exposed a deletion failure. The follow-up persists only the selected credential and tests that neighboring ciphertext and the TLS profile survive. The current-head gateway test is pending CI. A Chrome walkthrough of the real WebUI with a synthetic API passed create, replace, refresh, delete, and draft clearing on cancel. This browser test did not use a live gateway.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The new route requires a current authenticated administrator. It accepts only existing TLS binding slots.
- New external network calls? No.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** retain completed tool results across channel deadlines/failures and reuse bounded turn-local recovery through model switches; interrupted calls receive abandonment and terminal card events before a detector error propagates.
- **Scope boundary:** no SSH owner, progress ticker, HTTP cache or dependency-policy implementation.
- **Blast radius:** shared tool-loop cancellation hooks and channel session history.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11909. Depends on #12267. Related #11868, #11869, #11874 and #12323; these are independent changes, not merge prerequisites.

### What this does, simply

A channel can time out after an operation finishes. Completed results enter retained history before awaited notifications, so the next turn can inspect them without blindly repeating the operation. Recovery shares the original deadline; no automatic crash-resumable job or exactly-once external side-effect guarantee is added.

## Testing

### How you can test

Use an isolated channel fixture to complete one tool, then interrupt via cancellation/deadline, a blocked completion hook or a model switch. Verify completed pairs survive session reload and no interrupted card remains pending. Exercise an unguarded batch where a completed call triggers detector Break at the same time cancellation interrupts other calls; each interrupted context must receive one abandonment and one terminal ToolResult.

### How I tested

Current source validation results and exact commit IDs are recorded in the follow-up comment below. Historical evidence is explicitly labeled and is not acceptance of a later revision. Hosted CI on the published head remains authoritative for the full workspace.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.**
- New external network calls? **No.**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Completed tool output is untrusted and now survives timeout, cancellation and failure in durable history and may be replayed on a later turn. Existing `keep_tool_context_turns` retention and tool authorization remain authoritative; retained text conveys no new execution authority.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes.**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No.**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- The additive recovery entrypoints require #12267 to merge first. Tool rows retained before the outbound hook remain stored even when that hook cancels reply delivery.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback:** revert the recovery/caller changes, preserving durable records already written.
- **Feature flags/config toggles:** existing `keep_tool_context_turns` controls tool-context retention; no new toggle.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** missing or duplicate completed pairs, pending interrupted tool cards, missing abandonment hooks or a deadline extended by model switching.

  - Adds operator grant fields `PluginEntryConfig::{dispatch_agents, dispatch_rate_per_min}` in `zeroclaw-config` (default-closed `[]` and `30`/min, strict alias/padding/bounds validation), `InternalPrincipal::PluginTool` in `zeroclaw-api`, and `manifest_owns_instance_state` row seeding so `agent_dispatch`-only manifests receive a `[[plugins.entries]]` row on install.
  - Implements `RuntimeAgentWakeBackend` in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/plugin_wake.rs` and wires `plugin_host_services_with_wake` / `register_plugin_tools` in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/mod.rs` under the ADR-016 exception approved in #12417: live-config target authorization, `MAX_PLUGIN_WAKE_DEPTH = 2`, per-instance continuous token bucket, per-`(instance, target)` wake coalescing, `AgentExecutionCapability` admission, `TaskKind::PeerInbox` durable `TaskRecord` registration/settlement, and `CostTracker` scoping.
  - **CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`):** Increments the hardcoded `wit/v0/` input-inventory assertion in `Check (plugins cranelift runtime)` (`Run runtime plugin admission regressions`, line 1241) from `17` to `18` to account for the new `wit/v0/dispatch.wit`, matching the `expected_inputs` update in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/r5_namespace_tests.rs`. Appends `--test dispatch_plugin_e2e` to the existing `Run plugin component tests` step and adds a `Run runtime plugin wake dispatch tests` step to the cranelift runtime leg (`cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib tools::plugin_wake`). No workflow triggers, runner labels, permissions, pinned actions, or secrets changed.
  - Adds `tool-dispatch-fixture` WASM guest + `dispatch_plugin_e2e`, unit tests across all touched crates, and documentation (`plugin-protocol.md`, `plugin-manifest-fields.md`, `writing-a-tool-plugin.md`, `CHANGELOG-next.md`).
- **Scope boundary:** `tool-plugin` world only; `channel-plugin` and `memory-plugin` do not import `dispatch`. No synchronous plugin-to-agent RPC, no ambient target grants, no edits to `send_message_to_peer.rs`. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` changes only the `len(inputs) != 18` inventory count and the two test selections above. A dispatch-granted `WasmTool` reports `requires_unrestricted_principal`, so restricted (non-admin) principals never receive it. `wit/v0` remains experimental (no `.frozen` marker); `@unstable(feature = plugins-wit-v0-dispatch)` keeps existing `wit/v0` plugins linking unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Additive WIT import, optional `PluginEntryConfig` fields, `InternalPrincipal::PluginTool`, runtime adapter wiring, and the `wit/v0/dispatch.wit` inventory entry in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` / `r5_namespace_tests.rs`. Default-closed (`dispatch_agents = []`) until an operator explicitly grants target aliases for an `agent_dispatch` plugin.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12416, Related #12417

### What this does, simply

Tool plugins run in a fresh store per call with no network listener or access to the agent loop. This adds a gated `dispatch.wake(target-agent, prompt)` host import so an operator-authorized tool plugin can nudge a target agent into an asynchronous turn—coalescing burst wakes onto at most one queued follow-up turn, capping recursion at 2 hops, and enforcing live per-instance rate limits and target allowlists. It also updates the runtime plugin admission step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (and its matching `r5_namespace_tests.rs` list) to expect 18 WIT input files instead of 17 now that `wit/v0/dispatch.wit` exists.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; automated WASM component E2E (`dispatch_plugin_e2e`) and runtime mock-provider coalescing/panic/cost tests (`plugin_wake`) exercise the full boundary directly.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required CI runs workspace format, clippy (with CI's pinned toolchain), `zeroclaw-api`, `zeroclaw-config`, `zeroclaw-plugins`, `zeroclaw-runtime` (including the `r5_namespace_tests` fixture-receipt proof), architecture runner-label checks, and docs/links checks.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None after this head. Earlier revisions had one: required CI selected neither `dispatch_plugin_e2e` nor the runtime `tools::plugin_wake` tests, because the default-feature Test job does not enable `plugins-wasm-cranelift` and the cranelift runtime leg selects modules explicitly. This head adds both selections to the plugin backend job.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - Verified compiled `tool-dispatch-fixture` (`wasm32-wasip2`) end-to-end through both `WasmTool` (`dispatch_plugin_e2e`) and `RuntimeAgentWakeBackend` (`wasm_tool_dispatch_reaches_the_runtime_backend_end_to_end`).
  - Verified under local `rustc 1.99.0` that `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --all-targets -- -D warnings` surfaces only pre-existing lints in untouched files (`crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs`, `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/{upload,dispatch}.rs`, `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/turn/stream_guard.rs`) and zero warnings in `plugin_wake.rs` or `tools/mod.rs`.

- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no UI or terminal presentation changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Head `f20b7dd83b` (lease fix on top of `e51b8e968c`, which merges upstream master `9111460994`). Locally on this head: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins -p zeroclaw-runtime --features zeroclaw-runtime/plugins-wasm-cranelift,zeroclaw-plugins/plugins-wasm-cranelift --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean); `zeroclaw-plugins` lib with `plugins-wasm-cranelift` (485 passed, 1 ignored); `dispatch_plugin_e2e` (5 passed); `zeroclaw-runtime --lib tools::plugin_wake` (22 passed, stable across 3 repeated runs on `f20b7dd83b`, including the HTTP-mock cases, the principal regression, the accepted-wake-loss and SOP step-scope regressions, the revoked-grant-while-waiting regression, the two follow-up registration-retry regressions, and the lifecycle-lease regression on the real coordinator); `zeroclaw-runtime --lib agent::plugin_live_config` (3 passed, including the bounded-delegate attribution guard); docs quality and links gates. The principal regression was confirmed to fail with the override removed; the two accepted-wake-loss regressions and the step-scope regression were written first and failed on `5229d4395a`; `accepted_wake_survives_a_transient_followup_registration_failure` fails with the requeue disabled, and `registration_backoff_releases_the_finished_turns_lifecycle_lease` fails (`active_turns` = 1) without the lease release. Earlier command tails above are from `f72f78a8ff`. Interface: WIT `zeroclaw:plugin/dispatch` + `PluginEntryConfig` + `RuntimeAgentWakeBackend`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Granted `dispatch.wake` schedules a coalesced `PeerInbox` turn attributed to `InternalPrincipal::PluginTool` with target cost scoping; ungranted/padded/oversized/rate-limited/deep wakes fail closed with the closed `dispatch-error` variants.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full `zeroclaw-runtime` / full workspace test suite deferred to CI after verifying all targeted suites above locally.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes: adds `PluginPermission::AgentDispatch` (`agent_dispatch`) gating the `tool-plugin` world's `dispatch` import. Mitigated by default-closed `PluginEntryConfig::dispatch_agents = []`, live config evaluation on every call, `MAX_PLUGIN_WAKE_DEPTH = 2`, per-instance token-bucket rate limiting (`dispatch_rate_per_min`), host-owned `caller_alias` attribution, `ToolExecute`-only frame gating, and withholding dispatch-granted tools from restricted principals (`requires_unrestricted_principal`), since a wake does not carry the caller's live agent/tool selectors into the target turn. A wake issued from a headless SOP step carries that step's tool scope into the woken turn (per wake, coalesced follow-ups included), and a wake is accepted onto a slot only once a worker owns it, so a failed setup never drops a wake that already returned success; a follow-up whose durable registration fails transiently is requeued and retried with capped backoff, re-checking the live grant and target before each attempt; the finished turn's lifecycle lease is released before draining, so an idle target stays deletable during that wait.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. A granted tool plugin supplies a prompt the target agent sees. Operator target grants, the 1024-byte bound, and the target agent's risk profile limit its reach; the prompt remains untrusted input.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes (`wit/v0` is experimental and `@unstable(feature = plugins-wit-v0-dispatch)` leaves existing `wit/v0` components unaffected; new `PluginEntryConfig` fields default to empty/`None`).
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes (`[[plugins.entries]].dispatch_agents` and `[[plugins.entries]].dispatch_rate_per_min`, both optional with fail-closed defaults).
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: No action required for existing installs; operators enabling an `agent_dispatch` plugin explicitly configure `plugins.entries.<key>.dispatch_agents` (and optionally `dispatch_rate_per_min`) to allow target wakes.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Set `dispatch_agents = []` on the affected `[[plugins.entries]]` rows in live config; new plugin wakes are denied without a rebuild. For a code rollback after merge, revert the merged PR commit.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `plugins.entries[].dispatch_agents = []` (default) disables all wake targets; WIT surface is gated behind `plugins-wit-v0-dispatch`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Wakes return `dispatch-error::access-denied` (`dispatch_agents` empty/missing) or `rate-limited` / `unavailable`, logged via `zeroclaw_runtime::tools::plugin_wake` with `action = Reject` or `Dispatch`.

prs.title: feat(mcp): route declared MP4 resources into Qwen video input
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Materialize MCP `resource.blob` items explicitly declaring `video/mp4` as MP4 files and register existing `MarkerKind::Video` attachments, so the provider receives video rather than a document-path description.
  - Reuse the existing materializer, aggregate/item budgets, metadata preservation, and tool-carrier grammar. Resource URIs remain provenance and are never fetched.
  - Pass only declared, current-turn videos to Qwen; preserve tool text, mixed images/documents, native tool-result attribution, and XML external-tool headers. Stop replaying tool videos after a new user turn.
  - Add full MCP HTTP → tool wrapper → native/XML Agent → provider HTTP tests, plus an ignored real-Qwen smoke test.
- **Scope boundary:** Explicit MP4 embedded resources. Other video formats retain document handling. No new MCP tool/content type, camera integration, remote URI fetch, Responses transport, client frame extraction, or shared ACP document-format change.
- **Blast radius:** MCP embedded-resource formatting, shared MP4 header identification, Qwen declared-attachment normalization, and compatible-provider media relocation. Existing image tests remain part of regression coverage.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12578. Related #11383 for tool-body marker trust-boundary concerns.

This is the child of #12578 and is intentionally a draft while the parent is reviewed. Both PRs target `master` as required. The full diff currently includes the parent commits; the child-only comparison is [`71ad5da9a...eb022f04d`](https://github.com/wenhaozhao/zeroclaw/compare/71ad5da9abeb0734f91ac151b5b3e1fe8e44c7cd...eb022f04d8a4a7c96f9a152fee58b2a0af26b054). Refresh and revalidate this branch after the parent lands.

### What this does, simply

A tool can return an MP4 using the existing MCP embedded-resource format. ZeroClaw saves it in the workspace and passes the declared video to a supported Qwen model. The tool's descriptive text stays text, including any VIDEO examples it contains. The video remains available during later tool rounds of that user request, and is removed from media replay when another user request begins.

```json
{"type":"resource","resource":{"uri":"evidence://event/clip.mp4","mimeType":"video/mp4","blob":"<base64 MP4 bytes>"}}
```

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; automated end-to-end tests use real MCP HTTP intake, the production tool wrapper and Agent, and captured provider HTTP. The ignored live test provides optional paid provider reproduction.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Quality Gate on `eb022f04d`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45923363032) passed, including Security and CI Required Gate. The [previous Quality Gate on `63f79e8c5`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45314505315) passed after integrating #12694. This branch includes the parent recall filter in `71ad5da9a`. The parent remains under review.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Ordinary CI ignores paid inference. The native/XML boundary test explicitly needs `test-util`. Local platform is macOS/aarch64, rustc 1.97.1; upstream CI owns its platform/MSRV matrix.
- **Commands run and tail output:** On `eb022f04d` the normal, isolated command below ran both native and XML tool paths and checked the default paid-test selection.

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features test-util --test mcp_video --test live --config 'profile.test.package.zeroclaw-runtime.opt-level=2'
mcp_video: 1 passed
live: 1 ignored (explicit paid opt-in)
```

The three provider MCP video tests also passed on this commit (`cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib mcp_video_tests`), including a missing sibling attachment, the original tool-result body, and video expiry. Formatting and the child-only diff check passed.

Previous verification at `63f79e8c5` follows.

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers -- --test-threads=1
lib: 2033 passed; 0 failed; 4 ignored
integration: 1 passed; 60 passed; 3 ignored

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib mcp_video_tests
3 passed; 0 failed

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib embedded_resource::video_tests
3 passed; 0 failed

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features test-util --test mcp_video --test live --config 'profile.test.package.zeroclaw-runtime.opt-level=2'
mcp_video: 1 passed; 0 failed
live: 0 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored (requires explicit Qwen credentials and a local MP4; makes paid model requests)
No compiler/linker warnings.

cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime --features zeroclaw-runtime/test-util --all-targets -- -D warnings
Finished dev profile; no warnings

cargo fmt --all -- --check
git diff --check
BASE_SHA=github/master DOCS_FILES=$'docs/book/src/providers/catalog.md\ndocs/book/src/tools/mcp.md' scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
BASE_SHA=github/master DOCS_FILES=$'docs/book/src/providers/catalog.md\ndocs/book/src/tools/mcp.md' scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
0 Markdown errors; local link checks passed
```

The full provider run preceded one additional missing-sibling assertion; the focused three-test rerun covers that final edit. An initial tools filter `embedded_video_tests` matched zero tests; the corrected module filter above ran all three. Docs lint uses the existing temporary npm cache after a network-limited initial attempt; lychee is unavailable for optional HTTP link checks.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The integration uses real local MCP HTTP, the production wrapper and `Agent::turn`, then captures actual Qwen-shaped HTTP for native and XML modes. The first continuation contains byte-identical MP4; a new user turn contains no replayed tool video. Provider tests mix a valid MP4, a missing MP4 and an image; only the bad attachment degrades. Tool body examples remain literal and external provenance survives.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no rendered interface changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `eb022f04d`, including parent memory fix `71ad5da9a`. Evidence: `compatible_mcp_video_tests.rs`, `embedded_video_tests.rs`, `tests/mcp_video.rs`, and retained `tests/live/`/`tests/support/` layout.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** The native/XML HTTP assertions require one video only in the tool continuation, string-only native tool messages, preserved XML `[Tool results]` attribution and no tool-video replay in the next user turn. Ordinary `--test live` reports the paid smoke ignored.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** User and declared tool video share the parent's newest-first raw-video budget; preparation failures are per attachment. Native serialization consumes prepared content instead of reconstructing raw video declarations. Resource URIs are provenance and are never fetched.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No paid Qwen call was made for this revision. Historical live smoke on `f1b5ac448` succeeded with Qwen3.8-Flash (7.58s), but is not evidence for this head. No full workspace/platform/MSRV claim; optional HTTP link checking needs lychee. After #12578 merges, merge latest master, confirm the diff is MCP-only and repeat focused checks before leaving Draft.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes:** declared MP4 resources gain model-video delivery. Workspace writes use the existing materializer; provider reads use the parent's current-turn policy and bounded no-follow loader. Allowed filesystem roots are unchanged.
- New external network calls? **Yes:** existing Qwen inference requests may include the tool-declared video. No URI dereference, new external endpoint, or extra fetch/upload request is introduced.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No:** runtime authentication is unchanged; the ignored test reuses explicit `ZEROCLAW_TEST_QWEN_*` variables.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No:** committed media fixtures are synthetic; live video and credentials are uncommitted.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes:** explicitly declared external video becomes evidence. The fixed-position carrier separates attachments from untrusted body text; native relocation retains result ordinals and XML retains its tool-result header.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: An untrusted MCP server can supply video evidence, but cannot promote a VIDEO example in its body or trigger a fetch of its resource URI. Existing 10 MiB per-file/aggregate and 64-item limits remain in force, plus the parent's smaller Qwen dispatch budget. Only current-turn declared videos are delivered; stale/invalid/unsupported attachments degrade without replacing sibling text.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes, additive media support:** explicit MP4 resources intentionally gain video-attachment behavior. Other video formats, shared ACP document behavior, existing text/images, and non-Qwen provider request formats are retained.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No:** no new runtime configuration/CLI fields or MCP tool/content types; the live test uses the parent's explicit test variables.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: N/A. MCP producers opt in through the existing `resource.blob` shape with `mimeType: "video/mp4"`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's eventual merge commit first. The child-only comparison above separates the MCP implementation, retained live-test layout and merge adaptation from #12578. The parent's independent user-file video input can remain.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added. Producers can return text/image evidence while video delivery is investigated.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Video remains a path description, Qwen returns a video-input error, or a tool-video unavailable notice appears. The MCP Agent capture test exposes missing bytes, lost provenance, and stale-video replay. Saved files remain under the existing workspace upload lifecycle.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A. This child depends on #12578 and does not supersede another contribution.

prs.title: feat(providers): support Qwen MP4 video-file input
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Send supported Qwen MP4 video references as `video_url` parts containing `data:video/mp4;base64,...`, across streaming, non-streaming, history, and native-tool Chat Completions requests.
  - Scope local file reads to the current Agent turn's filesystem policy, with no-follow directory/file opens, regular-file checks, and a request-wide raw-video budget below 7,000,000 bytes.
  - Preserve mixed image/video requests and separate system text. Unavailable, unsupported and over-budget user videos retain their literal markers; history cannot stop later chat. Successful loads consume the shared budget newest message first. Tool-result bodies and system/assistant video examples remain literal.
  - Exclude recalled notes with a video marker in their key or body before rendering the memory preamble. Plain notes still supply context.
  - Add factory-to-HTTP, Agent-turn, filesystem-boundary, and opt-in live Qwen tests.
- **Scope boundary:** Chat Completions MP4 files and inline MP4 Data URLs. MCP attachment promotion is tracked in the dependent draft #12579. Responses, remote video fetching, frame extraction, audio-track interpretation, and codec validation are outside this change.
- **Blast radius:** Qwen/Qwen Code compatible-provider request shaping, the shared compatible message-part enum, current-turn filesystem-policy propagation, and provider documentation. The shared Agent memory renderer omits video-bearing notes for all providers.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12671 for the separately reviewed, Core Team-approved runtime exception record required before this feature merges. Related #11383 for the earlier video-input discussion and tool-body marker trust-boundary concerns. This is Qwen-specific and carries no code from that MiniMax PR.

### What this does, simply

A Qwen user can supply `[VIDEO:/absolute/path/clip.mp4]` or an inline MP4 Data URL and have the actual file reach the model. Previously the video reference reached Qwen as text. Files are read only when the current Agent policy permits them; low-level provider callers without a policy scope can use inline bytes but cannot open local paths. The service samples the video using its default settings.

The supported model families and dated snapshots are enumerated in `qwen_video::supports_model`. Only Qwen3.8-Flash was exercised against a real service; the other documented IDs have transport validation coverage.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; deterministic factory/HTTP and Agent-turn tests cover the changed boundary. The ignored provider live test documents optional paid reproduction; no paid run was made for this revision.

### How I tested

- **Commands run and tail output:** On `71ad5da9a`, ran the following focused checks.

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib qwen_video_tests --config 'profile.test.package.zeroclaw-runtime.opt-level=1'

The text-only question sends zero videos, and the question supplying a file sends one video whose decoded bytes match that file. The runtime test binary emits the previously documented macOS linker size warning. Clippy passed without warnings.

Earlier verification on `28a00b928` follows.

```text

integration: 1 passed; 60 passed; 3 ignored

The initial parallel provider run had two OpenAI failures: a runtime proxy-config test received an extra request, and a streaming fixture decoded that proxy's JSON instead of a Chat response. The complete serial run above passes without filtering. The Agent policy test passed at opt-level=1 and opt-level=2, but both emitted macOS ld's compact-unwind table size warning. It is recorded as a platform limitation, not a zero-warning run; Clippy remains warning-free. Diagnostics are not disabled. An initial docs-lint attempt lacked npm network/cache access; the successful rerun uses the existing temporary npm cache. Optional HTTP link checking is unavailable because lychee is not installed.

The directory-replacement negative control changes only `open_dir_nofollow(name)` to `open_dir(name)`: `video_open_rejects_intermediate_directory_replacement` must fail with the relative `private` symlink. The original source is restored in `finally`; the same test and all Qwen tests then pass. The normal and private targets contain different bytes.

Deleted history falls back; two 4 MB clips in different turns send the newer clip and retain the older marker as text. Valid inline MP4 makes tool-body non-promotion tests sensitive to a removed carrier guard.

Automated assertions live in `compatible_qwen_video_tests.rs`, `qwen_video.rs::tests`, and `agent/qwen_video_tests.rs`. No runtime/config/channel public types change in this follow-up.

No full workspace or local Linux/Windows/MSRV claim.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes:** an additive video-input capability can read and transmit MP4 files referenced in eligible user-role messages. It uses the current turn's existing read policy and does not enlarge allowed roots.
- New external network calls? **Yes:** the existing authenticated Qwen Chat request can now carry video bytes. No separate fetch/upload endpoint is added.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No:** runtime authentication is unchanged. The ignored live test reads explicitly supplied test-only environment variables.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No:** committed fixtures are synthetic; live media is external and uncommitted.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes:** the provider scans eligible user-role text. The shared memory renderer filters an entire recalled note when its key or body contains `[VIDEO:`. Tool-result bodies, system messages and assistant messages retain literal markers. Two other sources can place generated text in the user role: the optional link enricher (off by default) prepends fetched page text, and an SOP step can include previous-step output. Video references in either can be promoted under the same model, budget and file-policy checks. Neither source establishes explicit user selection. These paths were identified by code inspection.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: File disclosure is constrained by lexical and resolved read-policy checks, per-component no-follow opens, nonblocking regular-file checks, and bounded reads. Only successfully validated video bytes become media; failed references remain literal text and do not abort dispatch. Container-header checks do not guarantee valid codecs; the service owns decoding.

- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes:** additive handling of the existing VIDEO marker syntax for supported Qwen models and `ZEROCLAW_TEST_QWEN_*` opt-in test variables. No runtime configuration field or CLI flag is added.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: Existing deployments need no migration. To opt in, use a supported Qwen model and an allowed MP4 reference. Direct provider consumers reading paths must use `with_video_read_policy`; the Agent turn supplies this automatically. The live test documents its explicit credential, endpoint, model, and fixture variables.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's eventual merge commit. The recall fix is `71ad5da9a` and the channel fallback fix is `28a00b928`; the branch also includes the original feature commit and an upstream merge. Revert the dependent MCP PR first if both have landed.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The date filter recognizes a bare date in a daily Markdown filename. When the filename also has a suffix, such as a session label or time of day, the entry is treated as undated and can appear outside the requested window.
  - Use the leading calendar date for daily filenames with dash or underscore suffixes, both of which memory hygiene already recognizes.
- **Scope boundary:** Recall time bounds for Markdown entries with dated filenames.
- **Blast radius:** When callers provide time bounds, daily Markdown entries with a date suffix now appear only in the applicable day range.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related to #7192, which added since and until support to Markdown recall.

### What this does, simply

When you search memory for a particular day, a daily file named 2026-01-02-0800.md belongs to January 2. Recall now uses that date, while core notes in MEMORY.md remain available in the same search.

wall=0.77 s status=0

It kept the January 2 daily entry and the core entry. Local validation covered keyword recall in a Linux Markdown workspace. Recent recall, other memory backends and cross-agent reads were outside this check.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The wrapper retained only Cargo's status from the pipeline. If tee could not write the log, a successful Cargo run looked like a successful wrapper run and the wrapper tried to build its report from the unusable log.

- **Scope boundary:** The change covers exit status and summary generation when the Clippy log cannot be written.
- **Blast radius:** The required Lint job, the Windows tools Clippy job, and the scheduled or manually dispatched cross-platform Clippy jobs use this wrapper.
- **Linked issue(s):** Follow-up to the shared runner introduced in #10039.

### What this does, simply

The Clippy job now signals when it cannot save the diagnostic log. When the lint run itself fails too, CI still receives Cargo's exit code.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Lint runs the shared wrapper fixture suite before running workspace Clippy. The Windows tools and cross-platform jobs call the same wrapper with their target parameters. Upstream checks are pending until the PR is opened.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The real log write used the local Linux Bash and tee. The fixture supplies a short Cargo output and exit status. Hosted Windows and macOS runners were outside this local check.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ LC_ALL=C bash scripts/ci/run_clippy.test.sh
Base: FAIL: expected a failure when the Clippy log could not be written
Base: exit 1
Head: shared Clippy runner tests: pass
Head: exit 0 (0.39 s wall)

Base, Cargo exit 0: tee: blocked.log: Is a directory
Base: wrapper exit 0, summary written
Head, Cargo exit 0: tee: blocked.log: Is a directory
Head: Clippy log capture failed (tee exited 1).
Head: wrapper exit 1, summary empty
Head, Cargo exit 17: wrapper exit 17, summary empty

It returned 0 for a successful Cargo run and 17 for a failed Cargo run on both revisions. The real log write used the local Linux Bash and tee. The fixture supplies a short Cargo output and exit status. Hosted Windows and macOS runners were outside this local check.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text output from the wrapper and tee with the temporary directory prefix removed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `788fa5723523`, bash scripts/ci/run_clippy.sh --scope workspace --summary-title Fixture --log-name blocked.log. The before and after observations are below.

prs.title: fix(ci): release inactive swap files after failed setup
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The exit handler always tries swapoff, even if mkswap or file allocation failed before swapon ran. swapoff fails on the inactive file and cleanup returns before deleting it. This can leave a partially or fully allocated swapfile behind on a failed build.
  - Record when activation is first attempted and skip swapoff only for earlier failures. Check the file identity and confirm inactivity before removing the file.
- **Scope boundary:** The guarded cleanup of an owned temporary swapfile when Linux distribution build memory preparation fails.
- **Blast radius:** The Linux ARM64 distribution build preparation used by release and Docker workflows.
- **Linked issue(s):** None filed for this behavior.

### What this does, simply

The build runner allocates a temporary swapfile before enabling it. If setup fails before enabling swap, the runner can remove the unused file once it verifies ownership and inactivity. If enabling swap was attempted, the cleanup still calls swapoff before removing the file.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The regression below runs the before and after cases.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The stable-release, cross-platform-build, and Docker image workflows call this helper. The failure branch is exercised by the focused local script suite. Upstream checks are pending until the PR is opened.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No real swap, sudo, disk allocation, or ARM64 build was run. The test uses ordinary files in a temporary directory. It represents kernel state and ownership in command fixtures and reads the resulting file and receipt state from disk.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ bash -n scripts/ci/dist_runner_memory.sh
(exit 0)

$ LC_ALL=C python3 scripts/ci/dist_runner_memory.test.py -v
test_failed_activation_still_deactivates_before_removal (__main__.DistRunnerMemoryTests.test_failed_activation_still_deactivates_before_removal) ... ok
test_failed_mkswap_removes_the_owned_inactive_file (__main__.DistRunnerMemoryTests.test_failed_mkswap_removes_the_owned_inactive_file) ... ok
test_successful_setup_still_cleans_up_from_its_receipt (__main__.DistRunnerMemoryTests.test_successful_setup_still_cleans_up_from_its_receipt) ... ok
Ran 3 tests in 0.682s
OK
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The mkswap failure case counts 0 swap files and 0 swapoff calls. A simulated partial activation and a normal receipt-based cleanup each make 1 swapoff call and remove the file. The normal prepare case also reads 1 real file path from its receipt before cleanup. No real swap, sudo, disk allocation, or ARM64 build was run. The test uses ordinary files in a temporary directory. It represents kernel state and ownership in command fixtures and reads the resulting file and receipt state from disk.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text output (LC_ALL=C).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `32a34dd56219`, bash scripts/ci/dist_runner_memory.sh prepare on a Linux runner. The before and after observations are below.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** In the failing base run, the inactive file remains on disk after `Swapfile retained: guarded release could not be completed`. The corresponding head test reports `ok` after verifying the runner directory is empty.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** the prepare command still exited 31 without a receipt, left 0 swap files in the runner directory, and did not call swapoff. Both activation controls passed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The setup and cleanup paths are independent of Cargo. The small Linux fixture reproduces command failure and verifies the temporary runner directory without modifying kernel swap state.

- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any Yes, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: None.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the squash commit for this PR.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Failed runner memory setup leaves an unused zeroclaw-dist-swap file behind or guarded cleanup stops removing the file after successful activation.

This PR does not supersede another contribution.
